recipes.title: change the email on an account
recipes.name: change-the-email-on-an-account
recipes.goal: Change the primary email address on an online account without losing access or leaving the old address as a recovery path.

steps.action: **Sign in from a trusted device.** Use the official website or app and avoid public computers for the change.
steps.expect: the account dashboard opens normally.

steps.action: **Open account identity settings.** Go to profile, account, login, or email settings.
steps.expect: the current email address is visible.

steps.action: **Check recovery methods first.** Confirm a recovery phone, recovery email, passkey, or recovery codes are active.
steps.expect: you have a way back in if email verification stalls.

steps.action: **Add the new email.** Enter the new address carefully, checking spelling and domain.
steps.expect: the service sends a verification message to the new address.

steps.action: **Verify the new address.** Open the new inbox directly, not from a forwarded message, and click or enter the verification code.
steps.expect: the service marks the new email as verified.

steps.action: **Handle old-email confirmation.** If the service asks the old address to approve the change, open that inbox and confirm only the change you started.
steps.expect: the old inbox message names the same account and new address.

steps.action: **Make the new email primary.** Select make primary, use for login, or preferred email.
steps.expect: the account shows the new email as primary.

steps.action: **Update recovery addresses.** Remove the old email from recovery if you no longer control it, and add a separate recovery email if possible.
steps.expect: recovery settings no longer point only to the old address.

steps.action: **Check notification settings.** Make sure security alerts, receipts, and password reset emails go to the new address.
steps.expect: notification preferences show the new email.

steps.action: **Sign out and test.** Sign out, then sign in using the new email and current password or passkey.
steps.expect: login succeeds with the new email.

steps.action: **Confirm old email behavior.** Try the old email only if the service supports username checks, or inspect settings for aliases.
steps.expect: the old email is absent or listed only as a non-login alias you intentionally kept.

steps.action: **Save proof of the change.** Keep the confirmation message or account activity entry until the next successful billing cycle or important transaction.
steps.expect: you have a dated record of the email update.

recipes.verification: After signing out, you can sign in with the new email, receive a security alert there, and see the old email removed from login and recovery unless intentionally kept as an alias.

recipes.title: create an online account
recipes.name: create-an-online-account
recipes.goal: Hold a working account on a target website or app: you can sign out, sign back in, and reach the service's logged-in home surface.

steps.action: **Open the service's official site or app.** Type the URL directly or use an app store — avoid links from unsolicited messages.
steps.expect: the landing page shows the service's name and a "Sign up" / "Create account" / "Register" affordance.

steps.action: **Start registration.** Click "Sign up". [BRANCH: email signup | single-sign-on (Google/Apple)] SSO is faster but couples this account to the identity provider; email signup keeps them independent.
steps.expect: a form asking for email/username and password, or a provider chooser.

steps.action: **Enter identity fields.** Provide email and any required profile fields. Give only what is marked required.
steps.expect: no validation errors on the form.

steps.action: **Set a strong unique password.** Generate it in a password manager and save the entry before submitting.
steps.expect: the password field accepts it (meets the site's stated rules).

steps.action: **Submit the form.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some services bind a username permanently — confirm the username is the one you want before submitting.
steps.expect: a "verify your email" notice, or direct entry into the logged-in state.

steps.action: **Verify your email or phone.** Open the verification message and click the link or enter the code within its validity window.
steps.expect: the site confirms verification; the account is active.

steps.action: **Log out and log back in once.**
steps.expect: your saved credentials work; you land on the logged-in home surface.

recipes.verification: A full sign-out → sign-in cycle succeeds with the stored credentials, and the account shows as verified (no pending-verification banner).

recipes.title: delete an account
recipes.name: delete-an-account
recipes.goal: An account you no longer want is permanently deleted (or confirmed scheduled for deletion), with your data exported first and nothing still depending on it.

steps.action: **Inventory dependencies.** List active subscriptions, SSO uses ("Sign in with this account" elsewhere), and data to keep (photos, documents, purchase history).
steps.expect: a short written list; empty list → proceed directly.

steps.action: **Export your data.** Use the service's export/takeout tool (Settings → Privacy/Data → Download your data).
steps.expect: an export archive downloaded and opened once to confirm it's readable.

steps.action: **Detach dependencies.** Cancel subscriptions; switch SSO logins on other services to email+password; migrate anything pointing at this account's email.
steps.expect: the dependency list from step 1 is fully struck through.

steps.action: **Find the deletion flow.** Settings → Account → "Delete account" / "Close account"; some services hide it behind help pages or require contacting support.
steps.expect: a deletion page stating what will be deleted and any grace period.

steps.action: **Read the terms of deletion.** Note the grace period (often 14–30 days where logging in cancels deletion) and what is retained (invoices, legal records).
steps.expect: you can state the grace period and retention before confirming.

steps.action: **Confirm deletion.** Re-enter the password / 2FA as demanded. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* after the grace period, data and the username are gone — this is the point of no return; confirm the export from step 2 is safe first.
steps.expect: on-screen and email confirmation that deletion is scheduled or complete.

steps.action: **Do not log in during the grace period** (it usually cancels deletion). Optionally set a calendar note for the grace-period end.
steps.expect: after the period, login fails with "account not found" or equivalent.

steps.action: **Clean up local traces.** Delete the password-manager entry (or mark deleted), remove the app from devices.
steps.expect: no active references to the account remain.

recipes.verification: Login attempts fail after the grace period, the confirmation email is archived, the exported data archive is stored and readable, and no other service still authenticates through the deleted account.

recipes.title: enable two factor authentication
recipes.name: enable-two-factor-authentication
recipes.goal: The account requires a second factor at login, and you hold working recovery codes stored safely.

steps.action: **Open the account's security settings.** Usually Account → Settings → Security → "Two-factor authentication" / "2-step verification".
steps.expect: a 2FA section showing status "off".

steps.action: **Choose the factor type.** [BRANCH: authenticator app (recommended) | hardware key (strongest) | SMS (weakest — SIM-swap risk)]
steps.expect: the setup flow for the chosen factor starts; the site may re-ask your password.

steps.action: **For an authenticator app: scan the QR code.** Open the app → add account → scan.
steps.expect: the app shows a 6-digit code for this service, refreshing every 30 s.

steps.action: **Enter the current code to confirm pairing.**
steps.expect: the site accepts it and 2FA flips to "on".

steps.action: **Save the recovery codes — do not skip.** Copy every code into the password manager entry (or print). ⚠️ *Irreversible:* losing both your factor and these codes can permanently lock the account; this step is the insurance.
steps.expect: codes stored and readable outside this device.

steps.action: **Test the full loop.** Log out, log in, complete the 2FA challenge.
steps.expect: login succeeds through the new challenge.

steps.action: **Review trusted devices and fallback factors.** Remove stale devices; delete the SMS fallback if you chose app/key and the service allows it.
steps.expect: only intended devices and factors remain listed.

recipes.verification: A fresh logout/login requires and accepts the second factor, and the recovery codes exist in storage independent of the enrolled device.

recipes.title: log in
recipes.name: log-in
recipes.goal: You are authenticated on a service where you already hold an account, at its logged-in home surface.

steps.action: **Open the service's official login page.** Type the URL, use a bookmark, or the app — never a login link from an unexpected email or message.
steps.expect: the domain in the address bar is the service's real domain; a login form is shown.

steps.action: **Choose the login method.** [BRANCH: username + password | SSO ("Sign in with Google/Apple") | passkey] Use the method the account was created with.
steps.expect: the corresponding prompt appears.

steps.action: **Enter credentials.** Autofill from the password manager where possible — autofill refusing to fill is itself a phishing warning (domain mismatch).
steps.expect: fields populated; no manager warning.

steps.action: **Submit.**
steps.expect: either the logged-in home surface, or a 2FA challenge.

steps.action: **Complete 2FA if challenged.** Enter the app/SMS code, or approve the push prompt *only if you initiated this login seconds ago*. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* approving a push you didn't initiate hands your account to an attacker — deny unexpected prompts.
steps.expect: challenge accepted.

steps.action: **Confirm you are logged in.**
steps.expect: your account name/avatar visible; the URL is a logged-in surface, not the login page.

recipes.verification: The logged-in home surface shows your identity, and a page refresh keeps you logged in.

recipes.title: manage your subscriptions
recipes.name: manage-your-subscriptions
recipes.goal: You have a complete inventory of every recurring charge tied to your cards and app-store accounts, have cancelled the ones you do not want, and have calendar reminders set so no renewal surprises you again.

steps.action: **Pull the last 12 months of statements, not just last month.** Annual subscriptions only appear once a year and are the ones people forget.
steps.expect: a full year of transactions open or exported for every card and payment account.

steps.action: **Scan for recurring merchants.** Search statements for the same merchant name at a regular interval; flag anything monthly or yearly. Watch for cryptic descriptors (a media brand may bill as its parent company).
steps.expect: a written list of merchant, amount, and cadence for each recurring charge.

steps.action: **Check the app-store hubs separately.** Apple: Settings > your name > Subscriptions. Google Play: Payments & subscriptions. These bill many apps under one line and are invisible on the merchant's own website.
steps.expect: the store's subscription list reconciled against your statement list, no orphans.

steps.action: **Decide keep / cancel / downgrade for each row.** Mark trials whose free period is about to convert.
steps.expect: every inventory row tagged with a decision.

steps.action: **Cancel through the same channel that bills you.** If Apple bills it, cancel in Apple, not on the merchant site (the merchant cannot stop an app-store charge).
steps.expect: you are in the correct cancellation surface for each item.

steps.action: **Complete the cancel flow to the final confirmation, resisting the dark patterns.** Retention flows bury the real cancel button, offer "pause" instead, or push a discount. Keep clicking the option that actually ends billing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some cancellations forfeit remaining paid time immediately; read whether access runs to period end before confirming.
steps.expect: an on-screen "your subscription is cancelled" state plus a cancellation email.

steps.action: **Save the confirmation email and note the access-until date.**
steps.expect: each cancellation has a dated proof stored.

steps.action: **Add a calendar reminder 2-3 days before every renewal you kept.** Title it with the amount so you re-decide before the charge, not after.
steps.expect: one reminder per kept subscription on the calendar.

recipes.verification: Every recurring charge on 12 months of statements maps to a keep-or-cancel decision; each cancelled item has a dated confirmation and no charge after its access-until date; each kept item has a pre-renewal calendar reminder.

recipes.title: recover a password
recipes.name: recover-a-password
recipes.goal: Regain access to an existing account whose password you cannot produce, and leave it with a new stored password.

steps.action: **Go to the official login page.** Type the URL or use a stored bookmark — never a link from an email claiming your account has a problem.
steps.expect: the service's normal login form.

steps.action: **Trigger the reset flow.** Click "Forgot password?" and enter the account's email or username.
steps.expect: a notice that reset instructions were sent (services deliberately say this even for unknown addresses).

steps.action: **Open the reset message.** Find the email/SMS; check spam after ~2 minutes. Confirm the sender domain matches the service exactly.
steps.expect: a reset link or one-time code with a validity window.

steps.action: **Set the new password.** Follow the link, generate a new unique password in your password manager, and save the entry *before* submitting.
steps.expect: "password changed" confirmation.

steps.action: **Log in with the new password.**
steps.expect: you reach the logged-in home surface.

steps.action: **Review account security.** Check active sessions and recent-activity pages if offered; sign out unknown sessions. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* "sign out all devices" will disconnect legitimate devices too — reconnect them afterward.
steps.expect: only your devices remain listed.

recipes.verification: A fresh login with the new stored password succeeds, and no unknown active sessions remain on the account.

recipes.title: reset 2fa when you lose your phone
recipes.name: reset-2fa-when-you-lose-your-phone
recipes.goal: Regain access to an account after losing the phone that held your two-factor authentication method.

steps.action: **Stop automatic retries.** Do not keep guessing codes or passwords after two failed attempts, because some services lock recovery for a cooling-off period.
steps.expect: you are still on a normal sign-in or recovery screen, not a lockout message.

steps.action: **Open the official recovery path.** Use the service's sign-in page, choose lost device, try another way, or account recovery.
steps.expect: the page offers recovery codes, backup device, email, phone, or identity verification options.

steps.action: **Try recovery codes first.** Find the saved one-time recovery codes in your password manager, printed emergency sheet, or offline vault.
steps.expect: you have an unused code that matches the service name.

steps.action: **Submit one recovery code.** Paste or type a single unused code and mark it used in your storage only after it works.
steps.expect: the account accepts the code and lets you continue to security settings.

steps.action: **Use a backup device if no code works.** [BRANCH: authenticator synced to another device | hardware security key | trusted signed-in session] approve the sign-in from that device.
steps.expect: the service confirms your identity without the lost phone.

steps.action: **Use account recovery if backups fail.** Start the official recovery flow and provide only requested facts such as previous password, recovery email, billing details, or ID.
steps.expect: you receive a case number, email, or waiting-period notice from the service.

steps.action: **Wait through enforced delays.** Leave recovery messages in place and do not restart the flow unless the service tells you to.
steps.expect: the next message references the same account and same recovery request.

steps.action: **Enter security settings immediately after access returns.** Go to two-factor authentication or sign-in methods.
steps.expect: the lost phone is listed as a factor, device, authenticator app, or push method.

steps.action: **Remove the lost factor.** Delete the old authenticator, push device, or phone prompt after adding a working replacement. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* removing the only working factor can lock you out, so confirm the replacement signs in first.
steps.expect: the old phone no longer appears as an approved sign-in method.

steps.action: **Add at least two new factors.** Enroll a passkey or hardware key plus an authenticator app or recovery phone.
steps.expect: the account shows more than one active recovery or two-factor method.

steps.action: **Regenerate recovery codes.** Create a fresh set because any code you found may have been exposed during the emergency.
steps.expect: a new dated set of codes is displayed or downloaded.

steps.action: **Store the new codes safely.** Save them in an encrypted password manager note and one offline place such as a printed sheet in a locked drawer.
steps.expect: you can retrieve the codes without using the lost phone.

steps.action: **Review active sessions.** Sign out unknown sessions and revoke app passwords or OAuth grants you do not recognize.
steps.expect: only current devices and expected connected apps remain.

recipes.verification: You can sign out, sign back in on a separate device, satisfy two-factor authentication without the lost phone, and see fresh recovery codes stored in two safe places.

recipes.title: review account security
recipes.name: review-account-security
recipes.goal: An annual (or post-incident) sweep of your important accounts: sessions, factors, recovery paths, connected apps, and passwords are verified current and yours — the hygiene that makes account takeover boring to attempt.

steps.action: **Start with the email account — it outranks everything.** Whoever holds your email holds your password resets; it gets the fullest version of every step below.
steps.expect: the sweep order acknowledges email as the root of the tree.

steps.action: **Review active sessions/devices and evict strangers.** Security settings → "your devices" / "where you're logged in": recognize each entry (device, location, last active). Unknown or stale → sign it out; anything *suspicious* (a country you've never been) → sign out all + change the password now.
steps.expect: the session list reads as a biography of your actual devices.

steps.action: **Audit sign-in methods and factors.** 2FA still on, and on the strongest available method (`accounts/enable-two-factor-authentication`)? Phone number current? Passkeys offered — enroll. Old factors (a previous phone, SMS-when-you-have-app) removed.
steps.expect: factors current, minimal, and strongest-available.

steps.action: **Verify recovery paths — the forgotten backdoor.** Recovery email and phone: still yours, still active? (A recycled old number is an open door.) Recovery codes: located, and re-generated if you can't find them. Security questions (legacy accounts): answers rotated to non-guessable strings stored in the manager.
steps.expect: every recovery channel points at something you currently control.

steps.action: **Prune third-party access.** "Connected apps"/"apps with account access": that quiz from 2019, the service you stopped using — revoke by default; keep only what you recognize *and* still use. Same for OAuth "sign in with" grants.
steps.expect: the connected-apps list is short and current.

steps.action: **Handle the password itself on evidence, not ritual.** Check the account against breach-notification services (haveibeenpwned-class, or the manager's built-in audit): breached or reused → change it now to a generated unique one; strong-unique-unbreached → leave it (forced rotation without cause breeds weak patterns).
steps.expect: no reused or breached passwords among tier-1 accounts.

steps.action: **Log the sweep and calendar the next.** A one-line note per account ("2026-07: sessions clean, passkey added, 3 apps revoked") and a recurring annual reminder — plus triggers: run this after any breach news, lost device, or breakup involving shared devices.
steps.expect: the review is a system, not a mood.

recipes.verification: For each tier-1 account: sessions recognized, strongest 2FA active, recovery paths verified yours, connected apps pruned, password unique and unbreached — and the log line + next-year reminder exist. The email account got all of it first.

recipes.title: save your 2fa recovery codes
recipes.name: save-your-2fa-recovery-codes
recipes.goal: Generate and store two-factor authentication recovery codes so a lost phone or broken authenticator does not lock you out.

steps.action: **Open security settings.** Go to account settings, security, two-step verification, or two-factor authentication.
steps.expect: the page lists current two-factor methods.

steps.action: **Find recovery codes.** Select backup codes, recovery codes, emergency codes, or generate codes.
steps.expect: the service warns that each code works once.

steps.action: **Reauthenticate if prompted.** Enter your password, passkey, authenticator code, or hardware key touch.
steps.expect: the recovery-code generation screen opens.

steps.action: **Generate a fresh set.** Create new codes if none exist or if you are unsure who has seen the old set. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* generating new codes often invalidates old codes, so confirm you can save the new set now.
steps.expect: a full set of codes appears with a date or download option.

steps.action: **Count the codes.** Note how many codes were issued and whether they are one-time use.
steps.expect: your storage note can later show how many remain.

steps.action: **Save to a password manager.** Put the codes in the account's password-manager item or a secure note labeled with the service name and date.
steps.expect: the saved item is encrypted and searchable by account name.

steps.action: **Create an offline backup.** Print or handwrite the codes and place them in a locked drawer, safe, or sealed emergency folder.
steps.expect: you have one copy that does not depend on your phone, laptop, or cloud account.

steps.action: **Avoid unsafe storage.** Do not leave screenshots in camera roll, downloads, chat messages, or plain email.
steps.expect: temporary files containing the codes are deleted.

steps.action: **Test one code if the service allows.** Sign in from a private window and use a single recovery code, then mark that code used.
steps.expect: the login succeeds and one code is crossed out or deleted.

steps.action: **Regenerate after a test if needed.** If the service provides few codes or the test consumed one you want back, generate a new full set and replace all copies.
steps.expect: only the latest set remains in storage.

steps.action: **Label the storage clearly.** Include service name, username, date generated, and "one-time codes" without adding the account password to the same paper sheet.
steps.expect: you can identify the right codes under stress.

steps.action: **Schedule a review.** Add a reminder to check recovery methods after phone replacement, job change, or moving password managers.
steps.expect: the codes will not sit forgotten after major changes.

recipes.verification: You can retrieve the current recovery-code set from one encrypted location and one offline location, and at least one tested sign-in or visible settings page confirms the codes are valid.

recipes.title: set up a password manager
recipes.name: set-up-a-password-manager
recipes.goal: A password manager installed, protected by one strong memorized passphrase, seeded with your important accounts, and wired into your browsers and phone — retiring the reused-password habit that underlies most personal account takeovers.

steps.action: **Create the vault with a master passphrase you can actually memorize.** Four to five random common words (the dice-and-wordlist method or your manager's generator), typed a few times until fluent. This is now one of the two secrets you memorize forever (the other unlocks your phone); it is never reused anywhere else.
steps.expect: a passphrase you can type from memory, unlike anything you've used before.

steps.action: **Immediately store the emergency kit.** The manager's recovery/secret key and recovery codes printed or written, stored where you keep passports (`accounts/enable-two-factor-authentication` step 5's insurance logic: losing both the passphrase and this kit can mean losing the vault, which is the design).
steps.expect: a physical recovery artifact in a safe place, tested readable.

steps.action: **Protect the vault account itself with 2FA.** The manager's own account gets your strongest second factor.
steps.expect: the vault behind passphrase + factor; the keys to the kingdom guarded like it.

steps.action: **Install everywhere you type passwords.** Browser extension(s), phone app, and enable it as the phone's autofill provider (settings → passwords/autofill); disable the old browser's built-in saving to end the two-systems confusion.
steps.expect: one autofill system answering everywhere; test on any login (`accounts/log-in` step 3's autofill-as-phishing-detector now works for you).

steps.action: **Seed tier-1 accounts tonight, by logging in and updating.** Email first (the master key: `accounts/review-account-security` step 1's ordering), then banking, then the manager's list of your most-used: for each, log in, generate a new unique password in the manager, save. Eight to twelve accounts is a complete first night.
steps.expect: tier-1 all on generated-unique passwords stored in the vault.

steps.action: **Migrate the long tail opportunistically, and let the audit nag.** Every login over the coming weeks: save-on-use, upgrade-on-touch; run the manager's built-in audit (reused/breached/weak lists) monthly until it quiets (`accounts/review-account-security` step 6 now automated).
steps.expect: the vault growing to match your real account surface; the audit's red numbers shrinking weekly.

recipes.verification: The master passphrase types from memory, the emergency kit physically exists, the vault has 2FA, one autofill system answers on desktop and phone, tier-1 runs on unique generated passwords, and the monthly audit trend points at zero reused.

recipes.title: set up account recovery options
recipes.name: set-up-account-recovery-options
recipes.goal: Your important account has a working recovery email, a recovery phone, and backup codes stored safely, and you have proven at least one recovery path actually works, so a lost password or lost phone does not lock you out permanently.

steps.action: **Open the account's security or recovery settings.** Usually under Security, Sign-in, or Recovery.
steps.expect: fields for recovery email, phone, and backup/recovery codes are visible.

steps.action: **Set a recovery email on a different provider.** If the account is a Gmail account, do not use another Gmail as recovery; one provider outage or breach should not take both.
steps.expect: the recovery email shows "verify" and a verification message arrives at that inbox.

steps.action: **Verify the recovery email.** Open the message, click or enter the code.
steps.expect: the setting flips to "verified", not "pending".

steps.action: **Add a recovery phone number and verify the SMS code.** Prefer a number that will not change soon.
steps.expect: phone shows verified; a test code was received.

steps.action: **Generate backup/recovery codes and save them offline.** These are the fallback when both phone and email fail. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* generating a new set invalidates any old printed codes, so replace your stored copy every time.
steps.expect: a list of one-time codes displayed; you have copied all of them.

steps.action: **Store the codes where you can reach them without the account.** Password manager entry, or printed and kept with important documents. Do not store them only inside the same account they unlock.
steps.expect: codes saved in at least one out-of-account location.

steps.action: **Record recovery contacts in your password manager entry for this account.**
steps.expect: the entry notes which email and phone recover it.

steps.action: **Test one recovery path now, while you still have full access.** Log out, choose "forgot password" or "try another way", and confirm a code reaches your recovery email or phone, then log back in.
steps.expect: the recovery challenge delivers a working code and you regain access.

steps.action: **Set a reminder to re-check yearly.** Numbers and backup emails go stale.
steps.expect: a recurring calendar reminder exists.

recipes.verification: Recovery email and phone both show "verified", a current set of backup codes sits in an out-of-account location, and a live test of at least one recovery path returned a working code and let you back in.

recipes.title: set up passkeys
recipes.name: set-up-passkeys
recipes.goal: Add a passkey to an account so you can sign in with a device unlock method instead of typing a reusable password code.

steps.action: **Open the official account settings.** Sign in through the service's official website or app and go to security, sign-in, or passkeys.
steps.expect: a page lists current sign-in methods.

steps.action: **Check the existing fallback.** Confirm a recovery email, recovery phone, authenticator app, or recovery codes are already usable.
steps.expect: at least one fallback method is active before you add the passkey.

steps.action: **Choose passkey enrollment.** Select add passkey, create passkey, or security key.
steps.expect: the browser or app opens a system prompt for where to save the passkey.

steps.action: **Pick the storage location.** [BRANCH: synced passkey | device-bound passkey | hardware security key] choose the option that matches your backup plan.
steps.expect: the prompt names the platform, password manager, device, or security key that will hold the passkey.

steps.action: **Approve with device unlock.** Use face unlock, fingerprint, PIN, password, or touch the hardware key when prompted.
steps.expect: the service reports that the passkey was created.

steps.action: **Name the passkey clearly.** Use a label such as work laptop July 2026 or YubiKey blue.
steps.expect: the passkey list shows a name you can recognize later.

steps.action: **Record how it is backed up.** Note whether the passkey syncs through your account, lives only on one device, or sits on a physical key.
steps.expect: you know what would happen if this device were lost.

steps.action: **Test in a private window.** Open a private browser window or another device and start sign-in with the passkey.
steps.expect: the service offers the new passkey and asks for the expected unlock method.

steps.action: **Complete the test sign-in.** Use the passkey once, then return to the security settings.
steps.expect: the account signs in without an SMS or authenticator code.

steps.action: **Add a second passkey if possible.** Enroll another phone, laptop, password manager, or hardware key.
steps.expect: the account has at least two passkeys or one passkey plus another strong fallback.

steps.action: **Keep password and recovery sane.** If the account still has a password, keep it unique in a password manager and keep recovery codes current.
steps.expect: losing one device does not mean losing the account.

steps.action: **Remove only obsolete methods.** Delete old passkeys or devices you no longer control. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* removing the only passkey or fallback can block access, so complete a fresh test sign-in first.
steps.expect: active methods match devices you control.

recipes.verification: A new private-window sign-in succeeds using the passkey, and account security settings show at least one fallback method that does not depend on the same device.

recipes.title: verify your identity online
recipes.name: verify-your-identity-online
recipes.goal: Complete an online identity verification request while limiting the chance of sending identity documents to the wrong party.

steps.action: **Confirm the request is legitimate.** Navigate to the service from a bookmark or typed address and look for the same verification notice after signing in.
steps.expect: the verification prompt appears inside the official account.

steps.action: **Read what they need.** Check the document types, country rules, selfie or liveness requirement, and review time.
steps.expect: you know exactly which document and photos are required.

steps.action: **Prepare the document.** Use an unexpired ID, remove it from sleeves, and place it on a plain surface with good light.
steps.expect: all edges and text are visible to your eye.

steps.action: **Reduce unrelated exposure.** Cover nearby papers, close other tabs, and turn off screen sharing.
steps.expect: only the verification page and ID are visible.

steps.action: **Start the upload inside the official flow.** Choose the correct issuing country and document type.
steps.expect: the form asks for front, back, passport page, or camera capture as appropriate.

steps.action: **Capture the ID clearly.** Take the photo straight on, without glare, blur, cut-off corners, or fingers over text.
steps.expect: the preview is sharp enough to read the name, birth date, document number, and expiration date.

steps.action: **Complete the liveness selfie.** Follow the prompt to look at the camera, turn your head, blink, or record a short video if required.
steps.expect: the app accepts the selfie capture without a retry warning.

steps.action: **Review before submitting.** Confirm the service name, account email, document images, and privacy notice are still the expected ones.
steps.expect: the final submit button belongs to the same official flow.

steps.action: **Submit the verification.** Send the documents only after confirming the destination. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* identity documents cannot be made secret again once uploaded, so stop if the site or request looks wrong.
steps.expect: the service shows a submitted, pending, or under review status.

steps.action: **Save the receipt.** Record the case number, timestamp, and official sender address for follow-up.
steps.expect: you can find the submission record without reopening the upload page.

steps.action: **Watch for the result.** Check the account status and inbox over the stated review window.
steps.expect: the service either approves, rejects with a reason, or asks for a specific retry.

steps.action: **Delete local temporary copies.** Remove ID photos from downloads, desktop, camera roll, and trash if you created them outside the secure capture flow.
steps.expect: no loose identity-document images remain on the device.

recipes.verification: The official account status shows identity verified, or the service provides a dated pending case number tied to the correct account and document submission.

recipes.title: a b test an email subject line
recipes.name: a-b-test-an-email-subject-line
recipes.goal: Run an A/B test comparing two email subject lines for the same campaign audience.

steps.action: **Open campaign testing.** [BRANCH: Mailchimp | generic] choose A/B Test or subject-line test in Mailchimp, or enable the platform's email experiment feature.
steps.expect: a test setup screen is open.

steps.action: **Define variants.** Enter subject line A and subject line B while keeping sender, content, and audience unchanged.
steps.expect: only the subject line differs between variants.

steps.action: **Choose audience split.** Set the test percentage or equal split according to campaign size.
steps.expect: each variant receives a comparable sample.

steps.action: **Select winning metric.** Choose open rate, click rate, conversion, or manual review based on campaign goal.
steps.expect: the platform knows how to pick a winner.

steps.action: **Set test duration.** Choose a duration long enough for recipients to open but short enough to send the winner on time.
steps.expect: test timing fits the campaign schedule.

steps.action: **Check compliance and previews.** Confirm subject lines are truthful, not misleading, and render correctly.
steps.expect: both variants pass preview and compliance checks.

steps.action: **Launch or schedule the test.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before launching, confirm audience consent, split, subject lines, and winner rules because test emails will send to real recipients.
steps.expect: the test shows scheduled, running, or sent status.

steps.action: **Record the result.** After completion, note winner, metric, sample size, and learning.
steps.expect: future campaigns can use the result.

recipes.verification: The test sends or schedules two approved subject variants to eligible recipients with a defined split, metric, duration, and recorded result.

recipes.title: add a lead to a crm
recipes.name: add-a-lead-to-a-crm
recipes.goal: Create a new CRM lead record with enough accurate information for follow-up and routing.

steps.action: **Open the lead creation flow.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] in Salesforce, open Leads and select New; in HubSpot, open Contacts and select Create contact; in another CRM, open the lead or contact create form.
steps.expect: a blank lead or contact form is visible.

steps.action: **Enter core identity fields.** Add first name, last name, company, email, phone, title, and website when available.
steps.expect: required identity fields are populated.

steps.action: **Record the lead source.** Choose the source value that matches how the prospect entered the pipeline.
steps.expect: source is visible on the record.

steps.action: **Add routing context.** Set owner, territory, lifecycle status, product interest, and campaign if those fields are used.
steps.expect: the lead can be assigned and reported correctly.

steps.action: **Save the record.** Select Save or Create and wait for the CRM to load the new record page.
steps.expect: the lead record has a CRM ID or URL.

steps.action: **Add a next action.** Create a follow-up task or sequence enrollment only if outreach is appropriate.
steps.expect: the record shows the next action and owner.

recipes.verification: The CRM contains one lead or contact record with the prospect's identity, source, owner or queue, and a visible next action if follow-up is permitted.

recipes.title: add a product to an online store
recipes.name: add-a-product-to-an-online-store
recipes.goal: Create a complete product listing in an online store without publishing incorrect price, inventory, or customer-facing details.

steps.action: **Open product creation.** [BRANCH: Shopify | generic] choose Products > Add product in Shopify, or open the store platform's new product form.
steps.expect: a blank product editor is open.

steps.action: **Enter product basics.** Add title, description, vendor or brand, product type, and tags or collections.
steps.expect: the listing can be found and categorized.

steps.action: **Upload media.** Add approved images or video and set alt text if supported.
steps.expect: product media displays in the intended order.

steps.action: **Set pricing.** Enter price, compare-at price if approved, cost if tracked, and taxable status.
steps.expect: checkout pricing matches the approved amount.

steps.action: **Add variants.** Create size, color, format, or bundle variants with unique SKUs.
steps.expect: each purchasable option has a SKU and price.

steps.action: **Set inventory and fulfillment.** Enter stock quantity, inventory tracking, weight, shipping profile, and fulfillment location.
steps.expect: the store can sell and ship the item correctly.

steps.action: **Preview the listing.** Review desktop and mobile product pages before publishing.
steps.expect: copy, images, price, variants, and availability look correct.

steps.action: **Publish or save.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before publishing, confirm price, inventory, shipping, and legal claims because customers may purchase immediately.
steps.expect: the product is active or saved as an approved draft.

recipes.verification: The product page or draft has correct title, media, price, variants, SKU, inventory, shipping settings, and publish status.

recipes.title: apply a late fee
recipes.name: apply-a-late-fee
recipes.goal: Apply a late fee to an overdue invoice according to agreed terms and record the fee clearly for the customer.

steps.action: **Open the overdue invoice.** Locate the unpaid invoice and confirm due date and open balance.
steps.expect: the invoice shows overdue status or a past due date.

steps.action: **Check fee authority.** Review the contract, invoice terms, or customer agreement for late-fee language.
steps.expect: you can cite the basis for the fee.

steps.action: **Calculate the fee.** Apply the fixed amount or percentage only to the eligible overdue balance after any grace period.
steps.expect: the fee amount is documented.

steps.action: **Add the fee line.** Add a late-fee item, finance charge, or adjustment with a clear description and date.
steps.expect: the invoice total increases by the calculated fee.

steps.action: **Save the updated invoice.** Save the revised invoice or finance charge.
steps.expect: the customer balance reflects the late fee.

steps.action: **Notify the customer.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* sending the updated invoice changes the collection request, so confirm the fee is allowed and accurate before sending.
steps.expect: the activity log shows the updated invoice or notice sent.

recipes.verification: The overdue invoice or finance charge shows the allowed late fee amount, clear description, updated balance, and customer notification record.

recipes.title: approve a time off request
recipes.name: approve-a-time-off-request
recipes.goal: Review and approve or decline a time-off request consistently with policy, coverage needs, and leave balance.

steps.action: **Open the request.** Review employee name, leave type, dates, hours, and submission notes.
steps.expect: the requested absence details are visible.

steps.action: **Check eligibility.** Confirm the leave type, notice period, and balance or entitlement according to policy.
steps.expect: the request is eligible, ineligible, or needs HR review.

steps.action: **Check coverage.** Compare team calendar, deadlines, shifts, and blackout periods.
steps.expect: coverage impact is clear.

steps.action: **Decide consistently.** [BRANCH: approve | decline | ask for changes] approve if policy and coverage allow, decline with reason if not, or request date adjustments.
steps.expect: the selected action matches policy.

steps.action: **Submit the decision.** Click approve, decline, or request changes in the HR system.
steps.expect: the request status updates.

steps.action: **Notify affected owners.** If needed, tell scheduling, payroll, or project owners about approved coverage changes.
steps.expect: downstream teams know the absence dates.

recipes.verification: The HR system shows the correct approval status, leave dates appear on the relevant calendar, and payroll or scheduling owners have any required notice.

recipes.title: approve an invoice for payment
recipes.name: approve-an-invoice-for-payment
recipes.goal: Approve a vendor invoice for payment after confirming the charge is authorized, accurate, and ready to be paid.

steps.action: **Open the invoice awaiting approval.** Find the vendor bill in pending, awaiting approval, or inbox status.
steps.expect: invoice details and attachments are visible.

steps.action: **Verify vendor identity.** Confirm vendor name, remittance details, invoice number, and tax ID if used.
steps.expect: the invoice belongs to an approved vendor.

steps.action: **Match support.** Compare invoice lines to purchase order, receipt, contract, timesheet, or service acceptance.
steps.expect: quantity, price, and work received match support.

steps.action: **Check coding and due date.** Review expense category, project, department, tax, payment terms, and due date.
steps.expect: the bill will post to the correct accounts and payment cycle.

steps.action: **Resolve exceptions.** Hold the invoice if there are price differences, duplicate invoice numbers, missing receipt, or suspicious bank changes.
steps.expect: only valid invoices continue to approval.

steps.action: **Approve for payment.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* approval may release payment in automated workflows, so confirm vendor, amount, and bank details before approving.
steps.expect: the invoice status changes to approved or ready to pay.

steps.action: **Add approval note.** Record any exception resolution, partial approval, or payment instruction.
steps.expect: the audit trail shows why the invoice was approved.

recipes.verification: The invoice status is approved or ready to pay, with matched support, correct coding, verified vendor details, and an approval note or audit trail.

recipes.title: archive a completed project
recipes.name: archive-a-completed-project
recipes.goal: Archive a completed project so active views stay clean while the project record remains retrievable.

steps.action: **Open the project.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] open the project, board, initiative, or workspace project page.
steps.expect: project settings and task lists are accessible.

steps.action: **Confirm completion state.** Check that tasks are done, moved, or intentionally left open elsewhere.
steps.expect: no active work will be hidden by archiving.

steps.action: **Add closeout notes.** Record outcome, final links, owner, and where follow-up work lives.
steps.expect: future readers can understand why the project ended.

steps.action: **Check access and exports.** Save any required reports, files, or audit links before archiving.
steps.expect: required records remain available.

steps.action: **Archive the project.** Use Archive, Close, Complete, or equivalent project setting.
steps.expect: the project leaves active lists and shows archived or completed status.

steps.action: **Notify stakeholders.** Share that the project was archived and where to find records or follow-up work.
steps.expect: stakeholders know the project is no longer active.

recipes.verification: The project is marked archived or completed, active work has been moved or closed, and closeout notes identify final records and follow-up locations.

recipes.title: assign a lead to a rep
recipes.name: assign-a-lead-to-a-rep
recipes.goal: Assign a lead to the correct sales rep or queue so follow-up ownership is clear.

steps.action: **Open the lead record.** Search by name, email, company, or lead ID.
steps.expect: the lead owner field is visible.

steps.action: **Review routing signals.** Check region, segment, account ownership, product interest, source, and language if relevant.
steps.expect: the correct owner or queue can be determined.

steps.action: **Check for existing account ownership.** Search matching company or domain for an active owner.
steps.expect: assignment will not bypass an existing account owner.

steps.action: **Update the owner.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] change Lead Owner in Salesforce; change Contact owner or Lead owner in HubSpot; in another CRM, update owner or assignee.
steps.expect: the selected rep or queue appears as owner.

steps.action: **Set the follow-up task.** Create or transfer the next outreach task to the assigned owner.
steps.expect: the assignee has a dated action.

steps.action: **Notify if needed.** Use CRM notification, mention, or routing workflow only when the rep will not otherwise see the assignment.
steps.expect: the owner knows the lead is assigned.

recipes.verification: The lead record shows the correct owner or queue, a follow-up task assigned to that owner, and no unresolved duplicate or account-owner conflict.

recipes.title: assign a task
recipes.name: assign-a-task
recipes.goal: Assign an existing task to the person responsible for moving it forward.

steps.action: **Open the task.** Go to the task, issue, or card that needs an owner.
steps.expect: the task detail view is visible.

steps.action: **Check the task context.** Confirm the title, description, acceptance criteria, and attachments are sufficient.
steps.expect: the assignee will not need basic context before starting.

steps.action: **Set the assignee.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] use Assignee in Jira or Linear, Assignee in Asana tasks, or Owner/Assigned to in a generic tracker.
steps.expect: the intended person's name appears as the assignee.

steps.action: **Set timing if needed.** Add or confirm the due date, sprint, milestone, or priority.
steps.expect: the owner can see when the work is expected.

steps.action: **Notify the assignee.** Add a short comment naming the assignment and any immediate next action.
steps.expect: the assignee receives a visible notification.

recipes.verification: The task detail view shows one accountable assignee, and the activity log or comment stream records the assignment.

recipes.title: book a conference room
recipes.name: book-a-conference-room
recipes.goal: Reserve an appropriate conference room for an in-person or hybrid meeting.

steps.action: **Confirm headcount.** Count required in-room attendees and likely visitors.
steps.expect: a minimum room capacity is known.

steps.action: **List room needs.** Note video, screen, whiteboard, phone, privacy, accessibility, or catering needs.
steps.expect: room filters match the meeting requirements.

steps.action: **Search available rooms.** Open the room calendar or booking tool for the meeting time.
steps.expect: available rooms appear for the correct date and duration.

steps.action: **Choose the best fit.** Select a room with enough capacity and required equipment without overbooking a much larger room.
steps.expect: the room matches the meeting size and purpose.

steps.action: **Add the room to the invite.** Reserve the room resource or complete the booking form.
steps.expect: the room shows as accepted, reserved, or pending.

steps.action: **Include access details.** Add floor, building, visitor instructions, or hybrid equipment notes to the invite.
steps.expect: attendees know where to go and what to expect.

steps.action: **Check confirmation.** Verify the room did not decline because of a conflict or approval rule.
steps.expect: the booking status is confirmed or a clear next action is shown.

recipes.verification: The room booking is confirmed for the correct time, capacity, location, and equipment needs.

recipes.title: build a prospect list
recipes.name: build-a-prospect-list
recipes.goal: Build a targeted prospect list from approved sources for lawful sales outreach or research.

steps.action: **Define list criteria.** Specify industry, company size, geography, technology, buying role, trigger, and exclusions.
steps.expect: list scope is narrow enough to search.

steps.action: **Select approved sources.** Use CRM reports, data providers, event scans, website leads, or public business directories allowed by policy.
steps.expect: the data source is permitted.

steps.action: **Search and filter accounts.** Apply company-level filters and remove customers, competitors, partners, and poor-fit accounts.
steps.expect: target accounts match the campaign criteria.

steps.action: **Identify contacts.** Find relevant business roles and verified work contact details from approved sources.
steps.expect: each prospect has a role-based reason for inclusion.

steps.action: **Check suppression and ownership.** Remove opt-outs, do-not-contact records, active opportunities owned by others, and restricted accounts.
steps.expect: the list is eligible for use.

steps.action: **Import or save the list.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] create a Campaign or report in Salesforce; create a list in HubSpot; in another CRM, save the segment or import with source labels.
steps.expect: prospects are grouped in the CRM or approved tool.

steps.action: **Add source and purpose labels.** Tag list source, campaign, date, owner, and intended use.
steps.expect: list provenance is visible.

steps.action: **Review sample quality.** Inspect a small sample for fit, duplicates, consent status, and bad data.
steps.expect: obvious quality problems are found before outreach.

recipes.verification: The saved prospect list contains target-fit records from approved sources, excludes suppressed and owned-conflict records, and includes source and purpose labels.

recipes.title: categorize a transaction
recipes.name: categorize-a-transaction
recipes.goal: Assign a bank or card transaction to the correct accounting category so reports and reconciliation stay accurate.

steps.action: **Open the transaction.** Go to banking, transactions, or bank feed and select the unmatched item.
steps.expect: transaction date, description, amount, and account are visible.

steps.action: **Check for a match first.** Look for an existing invoice payment, bill payment, expense, transfer, or deposit that has the same amount and date.
steps.expect: you know whether to match or categorize.

steps.action: **Choose the transaction type.** [BRANCH: expense | income | transfer | owner contribution] select the type that reflects what happened economically.
steps.expect: the form shows fields appropriate to that type.

steps.action: **Assign the category.** Choose the account category, customer, project, class, or location if used.
steps.expect: the transaction will appear under the correct reporting line.

steps.action: **Add memo and receipt.** Enter a short business purpose and attach support if needed.
steps.expect: a reviewer can understand the transaction later.

steps.action: **Confirm the categorization.** Save, add, or approve the transaction.
steps.expect: the bank feed item changes to categorized, added, or matched status.

recipes.verification: The transaction is no longer unmatched and shows the correct type, category, amount, date, account, memo, and attachment or review note.

recipes.title: chase an overdue invoice
recipes.name: chase-an-overdue-invoice
recipes.goal: Follow up on an overdue invoice with a structured escalation path that seeks payment, resolves blockers, and preserves evidence.

steps.action: **Review the account.** Open the customer record and confirm invoice number, amount due, due date, prior reminders, and payment history.
steps.expect: you know the exact overdue balance and timeline.

steps.action: **Check for blockers.** Look for disputes, missing purchase order, wrong billing contact, failed payment link, or unapplied payment.
steps.expect: any nonpayment reason is identified or ruled out.

steps.action: **Send a firm written follow-up.** State invoice number, amount, days overdue, payment link, and a specific response deadline.
steps.expect: the customer receives a clear request with next action.

steps.action: **Call or message the right contact.** If no response, contact accounts payable or the buyer and ask what is needed to release payment.
steps.expect: you get a payment date, blocker, or escalation contact.

steps.action: **Record every contact.** Log dates, names, promises to pay, disputes, and documents sent.
steps.expect: the customer record has a complete collection trail.

steps.action: **Offer a controlled resolution.** [BRANCH: pay now | payment plan | dispute resolution] accept immediate payment, document a payment plan, or pause collection while resolving a valid dispute.
steps.expect: there is a concrete next step and owner.

steps.action: **Escalate if needed.** Send final notice, suspend service if contract allows, or refer to owner, attorney, or collection agency after approval. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* formal escalation can damage the relationship and may create legal duties, so confirm approval and documentation first.
steps.expect: escalation status and approval are recorded.

recipes.verification: The overdue invoice has a current collection note showing contact history, blocker status, next action date, responsible contact, and payment, payment plan, dispute path, escalation, or write-off recommendation.

recipes.title: close out a sprint
recipes.name: close-out-a-sprint
recipes.goal: Close a sprint so completed work is recorded, unfinished work is handled, and the next planning cycle can start cleanly.

steps.action: **Open the active sprint.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] open the active sprint, project section, cycle, or iteration view.
steps.expect: all sprint work items are visible.

steps.action: **Review incomplete work.** Filter or scan for tasks not marked done.
steps.expect: unfinished work is identified.

steps.action: **Confirm completed work.** Check that done items meet the team's definition of done.
steps.expect: only truly complete work is closed.

steps.action: **Move unfinished work.** Send unfinished tasks to the next sprint, backlog, or explicit follow-up milestone.
steps.expect: no open task is stranded in the closed sprint.

steps.action: **Record sprint notes.** Capture carryover, scope changes, notable wins, and blockers.
steps.expect: the sprint history explains the outcome.

steps.action: **Close the sprint.** Use Complete sprint, Close cycle, or equivalent.
steps.expect: the sprint status changes to closed or completed.

steps.action: **Share the closeout.** Post summary metrics, carryover, and follow-up items to the team.
steps.expect: the team has a shared record.

recipes.verification: The sprint is closed, done work remains recorded, unfinished work appears in the next sprint or backlog, and a summary is posted.

recipes.title: collect interview feedback
recipes.name: collect-interview-feedback
recipes.goal: Collect structured interview feedback from interviewers before the hiring decision meeting.

steps.action: **Open the interview record.** Locate the candidate, role, interview stage, and assigned interviewers.
steps.expect: the feedback status for each interviewer is visible.

steps.action: **Send feedback reminders.** Ask interviewers to submit feedback by the agreed deadline before group discussion.
steps.expect: interviewers receive a clear reminder.

steps.action: **Check rubric completion.** Review whether ratings, evidence notes, and recommendation fields are filled in.
steps.expect: each submitted form contains structured feedback.

steps.action: **Request missing evidence.** Ask interviewers to replace vague labels with job-related observations from the interview.
steps.expect: notes support the rating with examples.

steps.action: **Lock or mark complete.** When all required forms are submitted, mark feedback collection complete if the system supports it.
steps.expect: the candidate record shows feedback ready for review.

steps.action: **Prepare decision summary.** Summarize submitted ratings, strengths, concerns, and unresolved questions without adding unsupported opinions.
steps.expect: the hiring team has a neutral overview.

recipes.verification: All required interviewers have submitted rubric-based feedback, missing forms are accounted for, and the candidate record is ready for a hiring decision.

recipes.title: conduct a reference check
recipes.name: conduct-a-reference-check
recipes.goal: Complete a candidate reference check using job-related questions and document the result.

steps.action: **Confirm authorization.** Verify the candidate approved contacting the reference and any timing restrictions.
steps.expect: permission is documented.

steps.action: **Schedule or place the call.** Contact the reference using the approved phone number or email.
steps.expect: the reference is reached or a message is left.

steps.action: **Verify relationship.** Ask how the reference knows the candidate, dates, role, and reporting relationship.
steps.expect: the reference context is clear.

steps.action: **Ask job-related questions.** Cover responsibilities, strengths, development areas, reliability, collaboration, and eligibility for rehire where lawful.
steps.expect: responses relate to the target role.

steps.action: **Avoid prohibited topics.** Do not ask about protected traits, health, family status, religion, age, national origin, disability, or other non-job-related matters.
steps.expect: the conversation stays within lawful employment criteria.

steps.action: **Record factual notes.** Summarize the reference's statements, date, caller, and any unanswered questions.
steps.expect: the candidate record has concise reference notes.

steps.action: **Update recruiting status.** Mark the reference check complete, pending, or needs review.
steps.expect: the hiring team can see the reference status.

recipes.verification: The candidate record shows reference permission, reference identity, call date, job-related notes, and a complete or pending status.

recipes.title: create a project in a tracker
recipes.name: create-a-project-in-a-tracker
recipes.goal: Create a project in a tracker so work has a named home, owner, scope, and starting workflow.

steps.action: **Open the project area.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] open Projects in Jira, Teams or Portfolios in Asana, Projects in Linear, or the workspace project list in a generic tracker.
steps.expect: the project list or project creation button is visible.

steps.action: **Start a new project.** Choose New project, Create project, or Add project.
steps.expect: a project setup form opens.

steps.action: **Enter the project identity.** Add the project name, short description, owner, team, and key if the tool asks for one.
steps.expect: the form identifies the project clearly.

steps.action: **Choose the workflow.** Select a template, board type, issue status set, or default task workflow.
steps.expect: the project has statuses or sections for tracking work.

steps.action: **Set access.** Add the people or groups who should view or edit the project.
steps.expect: only intended members are listed.

steps.action: **Create the project.** Save or create the project.
steps.expect: the new project opens with an empty board, list, or issue view.

steps.action: **Add a starter task.** Create one task for kickoff, planning, or backlog capture.
steps.expect: the project can accept work items.

recipes.verification: The tracker shows a project whose name matches the filename-level request, with an owner, workflow, intended access list, and at least one starter task.

recipes.title: create a runbook
recipes.name: create-a-runbook
recipes.goal: Create a runbook that gives an operator repeatable steps for handling a business workflow, support process, or operational incident.

steps.action: **Open the runbook location.** Create a document in the approved knowledge base, wiki, or shared folder.
steps.expect: a blank runbook draft is available.

steps.action: **Name the scope.** Write the process name, when to use it, and when not to use it.
steps.expect: readers know the runbook's boundary.

steps.action: **List prerequisites.** Add required access, tools, inputs, dashboards, and permissions.
steps.expect: operators can check readiness before starting.

steps.action: **Write ordered steps.** Describe each action, expected observation, and handoff point.
steps.expect: the workflow can be followed without relying on memory.

steps.action: **Add decision points.** Include branches for common conditions, severity levels, or customer states.
steps.expect: operators know how to choose paths.

steps.action: **Add recovery paths.** Document common failures, detection signals, and escalation contacts.
steps.expect: operators can recover or escalate.

steps.action: **Review with an owner.** Ask the process owner or experienced operator to verify the runbook.
steps.expect: obvious gaps are corrected before use.

steps.action: **Publish and link it.** Save the runbook in the official location and link it from relevant tickets, trackers, or dashboards.
steps.expect: the runbook is findable during work.

recipes.verification: The runbook has scope, prerequisites, ordered steps, decision points, failure recovery, owner review, publish location, and links from relevant work surfaces.

recipes.title: create a sales pipeline report
recipes.name: create-a-sales-pipeline-report
recipes.goal: Create a CRM report that shows open sales pipeline by stage, owner, amount, and expected close date.

steps.action: **Open the report builder.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] choose Reports and New Report in Salesforce; open Reports or Custom Report Builder in HubSpot; in another CRM, open analytics or reporting.
steps.expect: a report configuration screen is visible.

steps.action: **Select the deal object.** Choose Opportunities, Deals, or the equivalent pipeline object.
steps.expect: the report is based on sales deals.

steps.action: **Filter to open pipeline.** Exclude closed-won, closed-lost, deleted, test, and duplicate records; set close-date range if needed.
steps.expect: only active pipeline rows remain.

steps.action: **Add key columns.** Include deal name, account, owner, stage, amount, probability, close date, and next step.
steps.expect: the table contains fields needed for inspection.

steps.action: **Group and summarize.** Group by stage and owner, then summarize amount and weighted amount if available.
steps.expect: totals show pipeline value by stage and rep.

steps.action: **Add visual output.** Create a funnel, bar chart, or table summary appropriate for the audience.
steps.expect: the report is readable without exporting data.

steps.action: **Save and share.** Name the report, save it in the approved folder, and set access for the intended users.
steps.expect: authorized users can open the report.

recipes.verification: The saved report shows only open pipeline, grouped by stage or owner, with correct amount totals and access limited to the intended audience.

recipes.title: create an invoice
recipes.name: create-an-invoice
recipes.goal: Create a complete invoice for goods or services so the customer can review what they owe and pay through the agreed channel.

steps.action: **Open a new invoice.** Go to the invoices area and choose the option to create a new invoice.
steps.expect: a blank invoice form is visible.

steps.action: **Select the customer.** Choose an existing customer or add the customer name, email, billing address, and tax details.
steps.expect: the invoice shows the correct billing recipient.

steps.action: **Enter invoice dates and terms.** Set the invoice date, due date, payment terms, and invoice number if the system does not assign one.
steps.expect: the header shows a due date and unique invoice number.

steps.action: **Add line items.** Enter each product or service with description, quantity, rate, discount, and taxable status.
steps.expect: subtotals match the agreed prices.

steps.action: **Review taxes and totals.** Confirm sales tax, VAT, shipping, credits, deposits, and rounding.
steps.expect: the total due equals the amount you intend to bill.

steps.action: **Add payment instructions.** Include online payment, bank transfer, check, or other accepted methods.
steps.expect: the customer has at least one clear way to pay.

steps.action: **Save as a draft.** Save without sending so you can check the final preview.
steps.expect: the invoice exists in draft or unsent status.

recipes.verification: The invoice is saved as draft or unsent with the correct customer, invoice number, due date, itemized charges, tax, total due, and payment instructions.

recipes.title: dedupe crm contacts
recipes.name: dedupe-crm-contacts
recipes.goal: Identify and merge duplicate CRM contact records while preserving the best data, history, and associations.

steps.action: **Open duplicate candidates.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] use matching rules or duplicate jobs in Salesforce; use Manage duplicates in HubSpot; in another CRM, open the duplicate detection tool or search results.
steps.expect: possible duplicate contact records are visible.

steps.action: **Confirm they are the same person.** Compare email, phone, company, title, location, activity, and source.
steps.expect: duplicates are confirmed or rejected.

steps.action: **Choose the primary record.** Select the record with the best owner, activity history, consent status, and system associations.
steps.expect: one record is identified as the survivor.

steps.action: **Review field values.** Choose the most accurate values for email, phone, title, company, lifecycle stage, owner, and consent fields.
steps.expect: important data will not be overwritten accidentally.

steps.action: **Merge records.** Use the CRM merge action and confirm the selected primary and retained values.
steps.expect: one contact record remains after the merge.

steps.action: **Check associations and activity.** Verify account, deals, tickets, campaigns, tasks, emails, and meetings carried over.
steps.expect: history and relationships are intact.

steps.action: **Add a cleanup note if useful.** Note the merge reason when the CRM timeline does not show it clearly.
steps.expect: future users understand why the duplicate disappeared.

recipes.verification: Only one contact record remains for the person, with correct key fields, preserved consent state, and expected activities and associations.

recipes.title: add an upsell at checkout
recipes.name: add-an-upsell-at-checkout
recipes.goal: Add a relevant checkout upsell that increases order value without surprising the customer or degrading checkout completion.

steps.action: **Pick a product that fits the cart context.** Choose an accessory, refill, warranty, gift wrap, or expedited service that is useful for the items already in cart.
steps.expect: one upsell candidate with a clear reason to appear.

steps.action: **Set eligibility rules.** Limit the offer by cart contents, order value, inventory, destination, and customer type.
steps.expect: the upsell appears only where it is relevant and fulfillable.

steps.action: **Price the offer and check margin.** Include product cost, extra packaging, fees, and any shipping impact before setting a discount.
steps.expect: the upsell remains profitable after all incremental costs.

steps.action: **Write concise offer text.** State the item, price, and benefit plainly; avoid countdown pressure or hidden recurring charges.
steps.expect: the customer can understand the offer without leaving checkout.

steps.action: **Configure the checkout placement.** Add the upsell in the approved checkout extension, post-purchase page, or cart drawer.
steps.expect: the admin shows the offer enabled with the intended placement and rules.

steps.action: **Test accepting and declining.** Use a test cart to accept, remove, and decline the upsell across desktop and mobile. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not publish until the customer can complete checkout either way.
steps.expect: totals, taxes, shipping, and order contents update correctly.

steps.action: **Publish with a measurement window.** Set a review date and monitor attach rate, checkout conversion, refunds, and support contacts.
steps.expect: the upsell is live and performance can be compared against the baseline.

recipes.verification: In a test checkout, the eligible upsell appears, can be accepted or declined, updates the order total correctly, and a completed test order contains the exact upsell line item.

recipes.title: add product tags for discovery
recipes.name: add-product-tags-for-discovery
recipes.goal: Add product tags that improve filtering, merchandising, automation, and search discovery without creating misleading labels.

steps.action: **Review existing tag conventions.** Check capitalization, separators, category tags, seasonal tags, and automation rules.
steps.expect: new tags will match the store's existing system.

steps.action: **Select useful discovery attributes.** Choose tags for product type, use case, material, style, size range, season, audience, or merchandising campaign.
steps.expect: each proposed tag supports search, filtering, or collection logic.

steps.action: **Avoid misleading or temporary claims.** Do not tag products with unsupported terms such as organic, handmade, clearance, or bestseller unless true.
steps.expect: all tags are accurate and defensible.

steps.action: **Add tags to the product.** Enter the approved tags in the product admin or bulk editor.
steps.expect: the product record shows the new tags.

steps.action: **Check automated collections and filters.** Confirm the tags place the product in intended collections and not unintended ones.
steps.expect: merchandising changes match the plan.

steps.action: **Save and preview live discovery.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* tags can immediately change storefront placement, so confirm collection effects before saving bulk edits.
steps.expect: the product appears in the correct filters and collections.

steps.action: **Document new controlled tags.** Update the tag list or merchandising notes if a new reusable tag was created.
steps.expect: future products can use the same tag consistently.

recipes.verification: The product has the approved tags, appears in intended filters or collections, avoids unintended placements, and uses the store's canonical tag naming convention.

recipes.title: approve a high value order
recipes.name: approve-a-high-value-order
recipes.goal: You approve a high-value ecommerce order for fulfillment only after confirming payment, risk, inventory, and delivery requirements.

steps.action: **Confirm the order qualifies for review.** Check subtotal, total, product type, shipping speed, and customer type against the high-value policy.
steps.expect: the order is correctly in the approval queue.

steps.action: **Verify payment status.** Confirm authorization or capture status, processor risk score, AVS/CVV outcome, and whether funds can still fail.
steps.expect: payment risk is understood before fulfillment.

steps.action: **Review fraud signals.** Check billing/shipping mismatch, IP geography, proxy indicators, prior chargebacks, account age, and order velocity.
steps.expect: no unresolved high-risk signal remains.

steps.action: **Confirm inventory and allocation.** Verify the ordered units are available, reserved, and not promised to another order.
steps.expect: inventory can cover the order without backorder surprise.

steps.action: **Validate fulfillment details.** Check address deliverability, signature requirement, insurance, packaging needs, and carrier restrictions.
steps.expect: the shipment plan matches the order value and product risk.

steps.action: **Contact customer if policy requires it.** Confirm order intent using approved contact channels and neutral wording.
steps.expect: customer confirmation is documented or the lack of response is handled by policy.

steps.action: **Record approval evidence.** Add an internal note with payment, risk, inventory, shipping controls, reviewer, and timestamp.
steps.expect: the approval decision is auditable.

steps.action: **Release the order.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once fulfilled, recovery may be difficult, so confirm payment, risk review, and shipping safeguards first.
steps.expect: the order status changes from hold/review to approved or ready to fulfill.

steps.action: **Monitor until carrier acceptance.** Confirm tracking, signature, insurance, and carrier scan.
steps.expect: the shipment is traceable and protected after release.

recipes.verification: The high-value order has documented approval evidence, confirmed payment status, reserved inventory, and a fulfillment plan with tracking, insurance, and signature controls appropriate to the value.

recipes.title: ask a happy customer for a review
recipes.name: ask-a-happy-customer-for-a-review
recipes.goal: You ask a satisfied customer for an honest review in a compliant way that does not pressure them, manipulate ratings, or expose private data.

steps.action: **Identify eligible customers.** Filter for delivered orders, enough time to use the product, no open return/dispute, and no recent complaint.
steps.expect: a list of customers likely to have a fair post-purchase opinion.

steps.action: **Check consent and channel rules.** Confirm the customer can receive transactional or review-request messages under platform and email/SMS rules.
steps.expect: only permitted recipients remain.

steps.action: **Write a neutral request.** Ask for an honest review, avoid asking only for positive ratings, and do not condition benefits on review content.
steps.expect: message copy complies with review rules.

steps.action: **Include the correct review link.** Use the product or order-specific review URL from the platform/tool.
steps.expect: the customer can reach the review form with minimal friction.

steps.action: **Disclose any incentive if allowed.** If offering a coupon or loyalty points, state that it is for any honest review and confirm platform rules allow it.
steps.expect: incentive terms are transparent and compliant.

steps.action: **Send the review request.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before sending, confirm recipient list, message text, incentive terms, and unsubscribe/compliance settings because customers receive it immediately.
steps.expect: the review request is sent or scheduled.

steps.action: **Monitor responses.** Track review submissions, replies, unsubscribes, and complaints.
steps.expect: you know whether the request generated reviews without compliance issues.

steps.action: **Respond appropriately.** Thank reviewers or route negative feedback to support without asking them to change ratings improperly.
steps.expect: customer feedback is handled professionally.

recipes.verification: The review request was sent only to eligible customers through an allowed channel, with neutral honest-review language, compliant incentive handling if any, and recorded delivery or schedule status.

recipes.title: audit a marketplace payout
recipes.name: audit-a-marketplace-payout
recipes.goal: Reconcile a marketplace payout against orders, fees, refunds, reserves, and adjustments so missing or incorrect money is identified.

steps.action: **Download the payout statement.** Export the payout summary and transaction-level detail for the exact payout ID.
steps.expect: a report listing every order, fee, refund, adjustment, and reserve movement.

steps.action: **Match the bank deposit.** Compare payout ID, date, currency, and net amount to the bank transaction.
steps.expect: the marketplace net payout equals the bank deposit or has a documented transfer delay.

steps.action: **Reconcile gross order revenue.** Sum included order payments and compare to order reports.
steps.expect: every paid order in the payout period is accounted for.

steps.action: **Reconcile deductions.** Check commissions, payment fees, fulfillment fees, shipping labels, refunds, chargebacks, ads, and taxes withheld.
steps.expect: each deduction has a category and order or adjustment reference.

steps.action: **Review reserves and holds.** Identify unavailable balances, rolling reserves, dispute holds, and pending settlements.
steps.expect: withheld funds have stated release criteria or dates.

steps.action: **Investigate differences.** For any variance above the tolerance, open the underlying order or fee detail.
