steps.expect: every variance is either explained or ready for a support claim.

steps.action: **File disputes for errors.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* submit claims only with exact evidence, because false or duplicate disputes can delay support.
steps.expect: marketplace support receives a claim with payout ID, transaction IDs, and variance amount.

recipes.verification: The payout net amount ties to the bank deposit within the stated tolerance, and every variance has an explanation, carry-forward entry, or submitted support case ID.

recipes.title: bundle products to raise order value
recipes.name: bundle-products-to-raise-order-value
recipes.goal: Create a product bundle that increases average order value while still giving the customer a clear, fair reason to buy the items together.

steps.action: **Choose products that solve one buyer need together.** Pair items customers naturally use in the same session, such as a device plus case or skincare cleanser plus moisturizer.
steps.expect: a bundle concept that is easy to explain in one sentence.

steps.action: **Check inventory and fulfillment constraints.** Confirm every bundled SKU has enough stock and can ship together without special handling surprises.
steps.expect: no component has low stock, restricted shipping, or incompatible fulfillment rules.

steps.action: **Calculate the standalone total and unit cost.** Add current selling prices, product costs, packaging cost, payment fees, and expected shipping subsidy.
steps.expect: a baseline revenue, cost, and gross margin for the unbundled items.

steps.action: **Set the bundle price above your margin floor.** Offer a modest discount only if the bundle remains profitable after fees and shipping.
steps.expect: a bundle price that beats the standalone total and still meets the margin target.

steps.action: **Create the bundle product or offer.** Use the platform's bundle app, kit SKU, or discount rule so inventory decrements correctly for each component.
steps.expect: the admin shows the bundle with all component SKUs linked.

steps.action: **Write the bundle copy around the outcome.** Name what the customer gets, list each included item, and state the savings without exaggeration.
steps.expect: the product page makes the included items and final price unambiguous.

steps.action: **Test the cart and checkout.** Add the bundle, change quantity, apply common discounts, and estimate shipping. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not publish until the cart total and inventory behavior are correct.
steps.expect: cart price, taxes, shipping, and inventory changes match the intended rules.

steps.action: **Publish and monitor the first orders.** Watch conversion rate, average order value, refund reasons, and stock levels for the bundle components.
steps.expect: the bundle is live and early orders can be fulfilled without manual correction.

recipes.verification: The bundle is live, adding it to cart charges the intended bundle price, every component SKU decrements correctly, and the calculated gross margin is at or above the stated minimum.

recipes.title: calculate a product margin
recipes.name: calculate-a-product-margin
recipes.goal: Calculate a product's gross and contribution margin so pricing, discounts, and ads can be judged against real profitability.

steps.action: **Collect the selling price.** Use the actual customer-paid item price after automatic discounts but before taxes collected on behalf of authorities.
steps.expect: one net item revenue value.

steps.action: **Collect product and packaging costs.** Include landed cost, duties, inbound freight allocation, inserts, and packaging.
steps.expect: a complete unit cost before selling fees.

steps.action: **Add transaction and platform fees.** Include payment processing, marketplace commission, app fees per order, and currency conversion if relevant.
steps.expect: variable selling fees are assigned to the unit.

steps.action: **Add fulfillment costs.** Include pick-pack, postage, shipping subsidy, and expected reshipment or return cost.
steps.expect: fulfillment cost per sold unit is estimated.

steps.action: **Calculate gross margin.** Subtract product and packaging cost from net item revenue, then divide by net item revenue.
steps.expect: a gross margin percentage.

steps.action: **Calculate contribution margin.** Subtract all variable costs from net item revenue, then divide by net item revenue.
steps.expect: a contribution margin percentage and dollar contribution.

steps.action: **Compare against the target.** Decide whether the product can support discounts, ads, bundles, or free shipping.
steps.expect: the product is classified as above target, near target, or below target.

recipes.verification: The product has a documented gross margin and contribution margin using actual selling price and all relevant variable costs, and the result is compared to the target margin.

recipes.title: calculate a reorder point
recipes.name: calculate-a-reorder-point
recipes.goal: You calculate the inventory level at which a product should be reordered so stock arrives before expected demand consumes the remaining units.

steps.action: **Choose the SKU and unit of measure.** Confirm whether the calculation is per each, case, bundle, or variant.
steps.expect: one unambiguous SKU and inventory unit.

steps.action: **Calculate average daily demand.** Use a representative sales period and exclude documented stockout days, launch spikes, or one-off promotions unless they will repeat.
steps.expect: an average units-sold-per-day figure.

steps.action: **Determine realistic lead time.** Add supplier processing, production, shipping, customs, receiving, and inspection days.
steps.expect: a lead-time estimate in days.

steps.action: **Set safety stock.** Use an existing buffer or calculate it from demand variability and lead-time uncertainty.
steps.expect: a safety stock quantity in the same unit as the SKU.

steps.action: **Compute the reorder point.** Multiply average daily demand by lead time, then add safety stock.
steps.expect: a reorder point: `(daily demand x lead time) + safety stock`.

steps.action: **Compare to current inventory.** Include on-hand, committed, inbound, and backordered units according to the inventory system's rules.
steps.expect: current available inventory is either above or at/below reorder point.

steps.action: **Create an alert or purchase draft.** Configure an inventory alert, replenishment task, or draft purchase order at the calculated threshold.
steps.expect: the system will prompt reorder before stock drops too low.

steps.action: **Review after each cycle.** Compare forecasted demand and lead time to actual results.
steps.expect: the reorder point is adjusted when demand or supplier reliability changes.

recipes.verification: The SKU has a documented reorder point equal to average daily demand times lead time plus safety stock, and an alert or purchasing trigger is set at that inventory level.

recipes.title: compare supplier quotes
recipes.name: compare-supplier-quotes
recipes.goal: You compare supplier quotes on total landed value, not just unit price, and choose the quote that best meets cost, quality, timing, and risk constraints.

steps.action: **Normalize the requested item.** Confirm each quote covers the same SKU, specification, packaging, certification, warranty, and quantity.
steps.expect: differences that affect comparability are visible.

steps.action: **Record base commercial terms.** Capture unit price, minimum order quantity, volume tiers, currency, payment terms, quote expiration, and lead time.
steps.expect: each quote has the same core fields in a comparison sheet.

steps.action: **Add logistics and import costs.** Include freight, insurance, duties, brokerage, handling, storage, and last-mile costs.
steps.expect: each quote has an estimated landed cost per sellable unit.

steps.action: **Adjust for quality and defect risk.** Include sample results, defect allowance, returns process, replacement policy, and inspection costs.
steps.expect: lower-quality offers are not treated as equal to validated suppliers.

steps.action: **Account for cash-flow impact.** Compare deposit, payment timing, credit terms, and currency exposure.
steps.expect: the quote's working-capital burden is visible.

steps.action: **Score non-price factors.** Rate reliability, communication, references, compliance, lead time, and ability to scale.
steps.expect: a weighted score or written ranking beyond price.

steps.action: **Identify negotiation points.** Mark the biggest cost or risk drivers: MOQ, freight, payment term, warranty, or tier discount.
steps.expect: a short list of asks for each supplier.

steps.action: **Select the preferred quote.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* issuing a purchase order or deposit commits money, so confirm landed cost, terms, and approval authority first.
steps.expect: a recommended supplier and backup are documented.

recipes.verification: The comparison includes normalized specs, total landed cost per unit, lead time, payment terms, quality risk, and a documented preferred supplier that meets the stated constraints.

recipes.title: flag a suspicious order
recipes.name: flag-a-suspicious-order
recipes.goal: You mark a suspicious ecommerce order so it cannot be fulfilled accidentally while the team reviews fraud, payment, or policy risk.

steps.action: **Open the exact order.** Match order number, customer name, email, amount, and creation time before taking action.
steps.expect: you are viewing the intended order record.

steps.action: **Identify the suspicious signal.** Record the payment warning, unusual address, velocity issue, high-risk item, duplicate order, or customer report.
steps.expect: the reason for concern is specific and visible.

steps.action: **Apply a visible fraud-review tag or hold.** Use the platform's hold, tag, or internal status such as `fraud-review` or `do-not-ship`.
steps.expect: the order list and order detail show the review marker.

steps.action: **Pause fulfillment.** Cancel pending warehouse release, hold the fulfillment request, or notify the fulfillment team according to workflow.
steps.expect: the order cannot be picked, packed, shipped, or digitally delivered automatically.

steps.action: **Add an internal note.** Include the risk signal, source, timestamp, and next reviewer or queue.
steps.expect: the note explains why the order is flagged without exposing unnecessary personal data.

steps.action: **Notify the responsible reviewer.** Send the order link through the approved internal channel, not a public customer thread.
steps.expect: the fraud or operations owner has the order and expected next action.

steps.action: **Confirm the flag persists.** Refresh the order and check any automation rules that might remove holds.
steps.expect: the order remains held after refresh and no fulfillment event is queued.

recipes.verification: The target order has a visible internal suspicious-order marker, an explanatory private note, and an active fulfillment hold or equivalent control preventing shipment or delivery.

recipes.title: forecast demand for a product
recipes.name: forecast-demand-for-a-product
recipes.goal: You forecast expected product demand for a defined future period so purchasing, staffing, and marketing decisions have a measurable baseline.

steps.action: **Define the forecast scope.** Select SKU, channel, geography, and date range.
steps.expect: one forecast target with a clear horizon and unit of measure.

steps.action: **Clean the historical data.** Remove canceled orders, test orders, stockout-constrained periods, and one-time anomalies unless they will repeat.
steps.expect: a usable historical demand series.

steps.action: **Establish a baseline.** Calculate average demand over comparable recent periods, adjusting for day-of-week or seasonality.
steps.expect: a baseline units-per-period estimate.

steps.action: **Account for known drivers.** Add expected effects from promotions, price changes, email campaigns, holidays, ad spend, or product-page changes.
steps.expect: documented upward or downward adjustments.

steps.action: **Check supply constraints.** Note current inventory, inbound stock, supplier lead time, and maximum fulfillable units.
steps.expect: the forecast distinguishes unconstrained demand from sellable supply.

steps.action: **Create low, expected, and high scenarios.** Use conservative, most-likely, and aggressive assumptions.
steps.expect: a demand range rather than a single fragile number.

steps.action: **Compare to purchasing needs.** Translate forecast into reorder quantity, safety stock, or production requirement.
steps.expect: a replenishment recommendation tied to the forecast.

steps.action: **Share and timestamp the forecast.** Save assumptions, data source, owner, and creation date.
steps.expect: stakeholders can audit why the forecast was made.

steps.action: **Reconcile actuals after the period.** Compare forecast to real demand and record error.
steps.expect: future forecasts improve from measured variance.

recipes.verification: The product has a timestamped demand forecast for a defined period with low, expected, and high unit estimates, documented assumptions, and a resulting purchasing or inventory recommendation.

recipes.title: fulfill a dropship order
recipes.name: fulfill-a-dropship-order
recipes.goal: You send a customer order to a dropship supplier, confirm fulfillment details, and update the customer-facing order with accurate tracking.

steps.action: **Review the customer order.** Confirm payment captured or authorized, fraud status acceptable, SKU, quantity, shipping method, and customer address.
steps.expect: the order is ready to fulfill.

steps.action: **Confirm supplier availability.** Check supplier stock, cost, handling time, shipping options, and any variant mapping.
steps.expect: supplier can ship the exact item within the promised window.

steps.action: **Compare margin before purchase.** Include supplier cost, dropship fee, shipping, payment fees, and expected store revenue.
steps.expect: the order remains profitable or is flagged for approval.

steps.action: **Create the supplier order.** Enter customer shipping address, SKU, quantity, shipping speed, and blind-shipping/gift-message requirements.
steps.expect: a supplier checkout or draft order matches the customer order.

steps.action: **Submit payment to supplier.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before placing the supplier order, confirm SKU, address, shipping method, cost, and cancellation window.
steps.expect: supplier order number is issued.

steps.action: **Record supplier order details.** Save supplier order ID, cost, estimated ship date, and expected tracking source in the customer order notes.
steps.expect: support can trace fulfillment without asking the supplier again.

steps.action: **Update customer status.** Mark the order in progress or fulfilled only according to platform rules; do not add tracking until real tracking exists.
steps.expect: the customer sees an accurate status.

steps.action: **Upload tracking when available.** Verify carrier, tracking number, destination, and movement before notifying the customer.
steps.expect: customer receives valid tracking for the shipment.

steps.action: **Monitor delivery and exceptions.** Watch for supplier cancellations, out-of-stock notices, split shipments, or carrier delays.
steps.expect: problems are caught before the customer has to chase them.

recipes.verification: The supplier order is confirmed for the correct SKU/address, supplier details are recorded on the customer order, and valid tracking is uploaded once the supplier ships.

recipes.title: handle a lost package claim
recipes.name: handle-a-lost-package-claim
recipes.goal: You investigate a customer's lost-package claim, choose a fair resolution, and file any carrier or insurance claim with the necessary evidence.

steps.action: **Open the order and tracking.** Confirm order status, address, carrier, service, tracking events, and delivery scan.
steps.expect: a timeline from shipment to the claimed problem.

steps.action: **Classify the loss scenario.** [BRANCH: no movement | delayed in transit | marked delivered | returned to sender] Identify which carrier process applies.
steps.expect: the claim path matches the tracking state.

steps.action: **Verify address and fulfillment evidence.** Check label address, package weight, pickup/drop-off scan, packing photo if available, and any signature/GPS proof.
steps.expect: evidence shows whether shipment was sent correctly.

steps.action: **Ask the customer for practical checks.** For delivered scans, ask them to check household members, mailroom, neighbors, parcel lockers, and delivery photo/location.
steps.expect: simple misdelivery possibilities are ruled out.

steps.action: **Contact the carrier or open a trace.** Submit tracking number, shipper details, package description, and delivery issue through the carrier process.
steps.expect: carrier trace or case number is created.

steps.action: **Choose customer resolution.** Based on policy and evidence, offer replacement, refund, wait for trace, or denial for unsupported claims.
steps.expect: customer has a clear next step and timeline.

steps.action: **Issue replacement or refund if approved.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before reshipping or refunding, confirm order number, address, claim evidence, amount, and whether insurance/carrier recovery is separate.
steps.expect: customer resolution is recorded.

steps.action: **File insurance or carrier claim.** Upload invoice, label, tracking, proof of value, photos, and customer statement within deadline.
steps.expect: claim submission confirmation and case number are saved.

steps.action: **Close the loop.** Update order notes, fraud/risk flags if needed, and prevention settings such as signature for high-value shipments.
steps.expect: order history shows final outcome and prevention action.

recipes.verification: The lost-package case has a documented tracking investigation, customer resolution, and carrier/insurance claim number when eligible, with no duplicate refund or replacement left unresolved.

recipes.title: handle a marketplace suspension
recipes.name: handle-a-marketplace-suspension
recipes.goal: Respond to a marketplace account or listing suspension with a factual appeal and corrective action plan that maximizes reinstatement chances.

steps.action: **Read the suspension notice exactly.** Identify whether the issue is account-level, listing-level, payment, performance, intellectual property, safety, or verification.
steps.expect: the cited policy and requested action are known.

steps.action: **Stop risky activity.** Pause affected listings, ads, or fulfillment actions that could worsen the violation.
steps.expect: no new orders are accepted for disputed or noncompliant items.

steps.action: **Collect evidence.** Gather invoices, photos, tracking, customer messages, safety documents, authorization letters, and process logs.
steps.expect: evidence directly addresses the stated issue.

steps.action: **Find the root cause.** Determine what failed: listing content, supplier verification, late shipments, counterfeit complaint, restricted product, or account identity mismatch.
steps.expect: a clear cause without blaming the marketplace or customer.

steps.action: **Write the corrective action plan.** State what happened, what was fixed immediately, and what process prevents recurrence.
steps.expect: the appeal is concise, factual, and tied to policy.

steps.action: **Submit the appeal.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm all evidence is attached and the appeal answers the exact notice before submission, because repeated weak appeals can reduce review quality.
steps.expect: the marketplace confirms receipt or shows appeal under review.

steps.action: **Track and respond once.** Wait for a decision, answer any specific follow-up, and avoid duplicate tickets unless the platform instructs it.
steps.expect: all communication is in one documented case thread.

recipes.verification: The marketplace appeal is submitted under the correct case or appeal flow with required evidence attached, affected listings paused or corrected, and a case ID or review status recorded.

recipes.title: handle a price match request
recipes.name: handle-a-price-match-request
recipes.goal: Evaluate a customer's price-match request and either issue an approved adjustment or decline with a clear policy-based explanation.

steps.action: **Capture the request details.** Record customer identity, product SKU, requested competitor price, date, and source URL.
steps.expect: a complete ticket or note with the claimed lower price.

steps.action: **Verify product equivalence.** Compare model, size, color, condition, warranty, seller, shipping, and taxes.
steps.expect: either an exact match or a documented mismatch.

steps.action: **Check policy eligibility.** Confirm the competitor, sale type, time window, stock status, and exclusions.
steps.expect: the request is classified as eligible or ineligible under policy.

steps.action: **Calculate the true comparable price.** Include competitor shipping, required memberships, coupons, and tax treatment where policy allows.
steps.expect: a final comparable price difference.

steps.action: **Choose the adjustment method.** [BRANCH: pre-purchase coupon | post-purchase partial refund | store credit | decline] Match the remedy to policy and payment status.
steps.expect: the next action is approved and documented.

steps.action: **Apply the adjustment if approved.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm SKU, amount, and order before issuing money or credit.
steps.expect: the customer receives the promised discount, refund, or credit.

steps.action: **Reply with the decision.** Explain the outcome, amount, and any remaining steps in plain language.
steps.expect: the customer has a clear answer tied to the policy.

recipes.verification: The request has a recorded eligibility decision, any approved adjustment has the exact authorized amount applied to the correct order or customer, and the customer has been notified.

recipes.title: handle a stockout
recipes.name: handle-a-stockout
recipes.goal: You stop overselling a stocked-out item, communicate realistic options to customers, and preserve demand without making false promises.

steps.action: **Confirm the stockout.** Check physical stock, reserved units, pending returns, 3PL inventory, and open orders.
steps.expect: a verified shortage quantity by SKU/variant.

steps.action: **Stop new oversells.** Set available inventory to zero, disable oversell, pause affected ads, or mark the variant unavailable.
steps.expect: customers can no longer buy stock you cannot fulfill unless preorder is intentional.

steps.action: **Prioritize open orders.** Sort orders by payment time, service level, fraud status, and promised ship date.
steps.expect: a fulfillment priority list and a count of orders needing action.

steps.action: **Find recovery supply.** Check incoming purchase orders, supplier stock, transfers, substitutions, or returned sellable units.
steps.expect: a realistic earliest fulfillment date or confirmation that none is available.

steps.action: **Choose customer options.** [BRANCH: restock soon | restock uncertain] Offer wait/backorder if ETA is credible; otherwise offer substitution, cancellation, or refund.
steps.expect: a policy-consistent option for every affected order.

steps.action: **Notify affected customers.** Send clear messages with apology, new ETA or options, response deadline, and refund path.
steps.expect: customers know what will happen and how to choose.

steps.action: **Process cancellations or refunds.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before refunding or canceling, confirm order number, customer choice, amount, and whether inventory should be released.
steps.expect: canceled/refunded orders are updated correctly.

steps.action: **Capture future demand.** Enable back-in-stock alerts or preorder only with accurate timing and payment disclosure.
steps.expect: interested customers can opt in without being misled.

steps.action: **Fix the cause.** Update reorder points, safety stock, feed sync, promotion rules, or supplier monitoring.
steps.expect: a specific prevention change is recorded.

recipes.verification: The stocked-out SKU cannot be newly oversold, every affected order has a documented fulfill/wait/substitute/refund outcome, and the product page or alert mechanism shows accurate availability.

recipes.title: handle an order dispute
recipes.name: handle-an-order-dispute
recipes.goal: You respond to an ecommerce order dispute with evidence, policy-aligned resolution, and no duplicate refund or missed deadline.

steps.action: **Record the dispute deadline.** Open the case and note response due date, reason code, disputed amount, and required evidence type.
steps.expect: a clear deadline and case scope.

steps.action: **Freeze duplicate actions.** Check whether refunds, replacements, or return requests are already open and avoid separate compensation outside the dispute.
steps.expect: one coordinated resolution path.

steps.action: **Gather order evidence.** Collect order confirmation, billing/shipping match, IP/device fraud checks if available, fulfillment record, tracking, delivery proof, and customer messages.
steps.expect: an evidence packet tied to the disputed order.

steps.action: **Match evidence to reason code.** [BRANCH: item not received | not as described | unauthorized | duplicate charge] Select proof relevant to the specific claim rather than uploading everything.
steps.expect: the response directly answers the dispute reason.

steps.action: **Decide contest or accept.** Compare evidence strength, customer history, cost, policy, and likelihood of winning.
steps.expect: a documented decision to fight, refund, or settle.

steps.action: **Submit the response or resolution.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before submitting, confirm case ID, amount, evidence files, customer, and whether accepting creates a refund or fee.
steps.expect: the dispute portal shows a submitted response or accepted liability.

steps.action: **Message the customer only if appropriate.** Keep communication factual and avoid pressuring them to withdraw a chargeback.
steps.expect: any customer message is logged and consistent with platform rules.

steps.action: **Monitor outcome.** Track provisional credit, processor decision, fees, and order status until the case closes.
steps.expect: the dispute is resolved, won, lost, or awaiting processor review.

steps.action: **Update prevention controls.** Adjust fraud filters, shipping signature rules, product descriptions, or support workflows based on the root cause.
steps.expect: one specific change reduces repeat disputes.

recipes.verification: The dispute case has a submitted response or accepted resolution before the deadline, evidence is stored with the order, no duplicate refund is pending, and the final outcome is tracked.

recipes.title: issue a partial refund
recipes.name: issue-a-partial-refund
recipes.goal: You issue a partial refund for a specific order reason without refunding too much, duplicating compensation, or losing the dispute evidence trail.

steps.action: **Open and verify the order.** Confirm customer, payment status, fulfillment status, item, quantity, and prior refunds or chargebacks.
steps.expect: you are working on the correct paid order with no duplicate open compensation.

steps.action: **Validate the refund reason.** Review evidence for damage, late delivery, missing accessory, price adjustment, service failure, or negotiated resolution.
steps.expect: a documented reason that supports a partial refund.

steps.action: **Calculate the refund amount.** Include item portion, tax adjustment, shipping if applicable, discounts, and maximum allowed goodwill amount.
steps.expect: a precise refund amount and what it covers.

steps.action: **Confirm customer agreement when needed.** For negotiated settlements, state the amount and whether it resolves the issue.
steps.expect: customer acceptance is recorded in the order thread.

steps.action: **Check inventory impact.** Decide whether any item is returned, kept, replaced, or written off.
steps.expect: refund action will not incorrectly restock inventory.

steps.action: **Enter the partial refund.** Select the item or custom amount, reason code, tax/shipping treatment, and internal note.
steps.expect: the refund preview matches the intended amount.

steps.action: **Submit the refund.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before confirming, verify order number, customer, refund amount, payment method, inventory action, and that no duplicate refund exists.
steps.expect: payment processor records a partial refund transaction.

steps.action: **Notify the customer.** Send the amount, expected posting time, and any remaining action required.
steps.expect: the customer has clear confirmation of the refund.

recipes.verification: The order shows a partial refund transaction for the correct amount and reason, no duplicate refund or inventory error exists, and the customer has been notified of the posting timeline.

recipes.title: issue store credit
recipes.name: issue-store-credit
recipes.goal: Issue store credit to a customer for an approved reason and record it so the customer can spend it and the business can reconcile it.

steps.action: **Confirm the reason and amount.** Review the order, return, support ticket, or promotion that authorizes the credit.
steps.expect: a documented amount and reason code.

steps.action: **Verify the customer account.** Match the email, order number, and shipping or billing details before adding value.
steps.expect: the correct customer profile is open.

steps.action: **Choose the credit mechanism.** [BRANCH: account credit | gift card | coupon code] Use the option your platform tracks best for liabilities and redemption.
steps.expect: a credit type selected that the customer can actually use.

steps.action: **Set restrictions and expiration.** Apply currency, product exclusions, expiration date, and one-time-use rules if policy requires them.
steps.expect: the credit terms match the approval.

steps.action: **Create the credit.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm customer, amount, currency, and expiration before issuing because store value may be immediately spendable.
steps.expect: the platform generates a credit balance, gift card, or code.

steps.action: **Notify the customer.** Send the amount, how to redeem it, expiration, and any restrictions without exposing internal notes.
steps.expect: the customer receives usable redemption instructions.

steps.action: **Record the action.** Add an internal note with reason, approver, amount, and reference number.
steps.expect: support and finance can audit why the credit exists.

recipes.verification: The correct customer has the approved store-credit amount available, the customer has redemption instructions, and the credit record includes amount, currency, reason, and reference ID.

recipes.title: launch a new product
recipes.name: launch-a-new-product
recipes.goal: You publish a new ecommerce product with accurate content, inventory, pricing, fulfillment, and launch checks so customers can buy it without avoidable errors.

steps.action: **Create the product record in draft.** Add the name, SKU, product type, vendor, status, and sales channels without publishing yet.
steps.expect: a draft product exists in the catalog.

steps.action: **Add accurate variant data.** Enter sizes, colors, bundles, barcodes, weights, inventory quantities, and option names exactly as they should appear to buyers.
steps.expect: each sellable variant has a unique SKU and inventory value.

steps.action: **Upload product media.** Add clear images or videos showing the product, scale, included items, and important details.
steps.expect: the gallery communicates what the buyer will receive.

steps.action: **Write the purchase-critical content.** Add description, specifications, care instructions, compatibility, ingredients/materials, warranty, and restrictions as applicable.
steps.expect: the page answers the main pre-purchase questions.

steps.action: **Set price and margins.** Enter price, compare-at price if truthful, cost, tax category, and any launch discount.
steps.expect: the expected gross margin is known before launch.

steps.action: **Configure fulfillment.** Assign warehouse/location, shipping profile, package weight, delivery promise, and backorder behavior.
steps.expect: checkout can calculate shipping for the product.

steps.action: **Run a test purchase path.** Preview the product, add each key variant to cart, apply intended discounts, and proceed to the payment step without submitting a real order unless using test mode.
steps.expect: product, price, tax, shipping, and inventory behave as intended.

steps.action: **Publish the product.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before setting live, confirm price, inventory, shipping, legal claims, images, and sales channels because customers can purchase immediately.
steps.expect: the product page is live and buyable on intended channels.

steps.action: **Monitor the first orders.** Watch analytics, search, payment authorization, inventory decrement, and fulfillment queue for the first hour or first several orders.
steps.expect: orders flow through without catalog or checkout errors.

recipes.verification: The product is live on the intended sales channel, at least one variant can reach checkout with correct price/shipping/tax, inventory decrements correctly, and no launch-blocking admin errors remain.

recipes.title: launch a referral program
recipes.name: launch-a-referral-program
recipes.goal: Launch a referral program that gives existing customers a reason to invite real new buyers while limiting self-referral and discount abuse.

steps.action: **Define the qualified referral.** Specify first purchase, minimum order value, excluded products, return window, and reward timing.
steps.expect: a written rule for when rewards are earned.

steps.action: **Set reward economics.** Calculate advocate reward, friend discount, margin impact, and maximum monthly payout.
steps.expect: reward cost stays below the acquisition-cost cap.

steps.action: **Configure fraud controls.** Block self-referrals, duplicate accounts, same payment instruments, and reward issuance before the return window if needed.
steps.expect: obvious abuse paths are disabled.

steps.action: **Create referral links and landing copy.** Explain the offer, eligibility, expiration, and privacy terms.
steps.expect: customers can share a trackable link with accurate terms.

steps.action: **Test the full flow.** Use separate test accounts to share, purchase, refund, and qualify or disqualify a referral. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not launch until rewards do not issue for refunded or self-referred orders.
steps.expect: qualified purchases trigger rewards and invalid ones do not.

steps.action: **Launch to a controlled segment.** Start with recent satisfied customers or loyalty members before broad promotion.
steps.expect: referral invites are sent only to the intended audience.

steps.action: **Monitor quality and cost.** Track referred conversion, fraud flags, reward liability, refund rate, and customer complaints.
steps.expect: the program produces new qualified customers within the target cost.

recipes.verification: A test advocate can generate a referral link, a separate eligible buyer can complete a qualifying order, and only after qualification the configured rewards appear for both parties.

recipes.title: launch a social media ad campaign
recipes.name: launch-a-social-media-ad-campaign
recipes.goal: Launch a paid social campaign for an ecommerce offer with clear targeting, creative, budget limits, and conversion measurement.

steps.action: **Define the campaign objective.** Choose sales, leads, traffic, or retargeting based on the intended measurable outcome.
steps.expect: one objective tied to a conversion event.

steps.action: **Confirm tracking and catalog setup.** Test pixel, conversion API, product catalog, and event deduplication if used.
steps.expect: test events appear in the ad platform diagnostics.

steps.action: **Build the target audience.** Select geography, age limits, interests, lookalikes, or retargeting pools without sensitive or discriminatory targeting.
steps.expect: the estimated audience is large enough and policy-compliant.

steps.action: **Upload creative and copy.** Use product-visible images or video, a direct offer, price or discount terms, and a matching landing page.
steps.expect: each ad preview accurately represents the product and offer.

steps.action: **Set budget, schedule, and bid controls.** Enter the approved spend cap and a start date; use a lifetime budget for fixed promotions.
steps.expect: the campaign cannot exceed the approved budget settings.

steps.action: **Review compliance and publish.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* ads can spend money once approved, so confirm budget, audience, destination URL, and conversion event.
steps.expect: campaign status is published, scheduled, or in review.

steps.action: **Monitor early delivery.** Check spend, CPM, CTR, conversion events, comments, and rejected ads within the first day.
steps.expect: the campaign spends toward the intended audience and reports usable metrics.

recipes.verification: The campaign is published or scheduled with the approved objective, audience, creative, destination URL, conversion event, and budget cap visible in the ad manager.

recipes.title: launch a waitlist for a drop
recipes.name: launch-a-waitlist-for-a-drop
recipes.goal: You publish a waitlist for a limited product drop, collect consented buyer interest, and have a clean export or segment ready for launch notifications.

steps.action: **Define the waitlist promise.** State what subscribers get: early access, restock notice, private link, or first notification only.
steps.expect: a one-sentence promise that does not overstate guaranteed access.

steps.action: **Set the drop constraints.** Record launch date, time zone, quantity, purchase limits, eligible countries, and any maximum price or shipping constraints.
steps.expect: internal notes that support consistent copy and customer support answers.

steps.action: **Create the waitlist capture form.** Ask only for necessary fields such as email, optional phone, preferred variant, and marketing consent checkbox.
steps.expect: a form that submits successfully and stores each field.

steps.action: **Write the confirmation message.** Tell users they joined, when to expect updates, and that joining does not reserve inventory unless that is true.
steps.expect: a post-submit page or email with the exact waitlist status.

steps.action: **Connect the form to a tagged audience.** Apply a tag or segment such as `drop-waitlist-product-date` in the email/SMS system.
steps.expect: a test signup appears in the correct audience segment.

steps.action: **Add the waitlist entry point to the storefront.** Place the form on the product page, homepage module, or dedicated landing page.
steps.expect: shoppers can reach the waitlist without checkout access to the unavailable product.

steps.action: **Test the full signup flow.** Submit a test address, confirm consent fields, verify tags, and check the confirmation email.
steps.expect: the test contact has the right attributes and receives the intended message.

steps.action: **Publish the waitlist page.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once promoted publicly, customers may rely on the wording, so confirm dates, limits, and privacy text first.
steps.expect: the waitlist URL is live and accepts real signups.

steps.action: **Monitor quality and exportability.** Review signup count, bounce rate, duplicate rate, and segment export.
steps.expect: a usable audience count and a retrievable list for launch messaging.

recipes.verification: The waitlist page is live, a test signup is stored in the correct tagged audience with consent metadata, and the current signup count or export is visible to the operator.

recipes.title: negotiate a bulk supplier price
recipes.name: negotiate-a-bulk-supplier-price
recipes.goal: You negotiate a bulk supplier price or term improvement that lowers landed cost while preserving quality, delivery, and supplier reliability.

steps.action: **Set your walk-away economics.** Calculate target unit price, maximum landed cost, acceptable MOQ, and cash-flow limit.
steps.expect: a private negotiation range and walk-away point.

steps.action: **Identify tradable variables.** List price, quantity, payment terms, lead time, packaging, warranty, freight, exclusivity, and reorder commitment.
steps.expect: multiple negotiation levers beyond demanding a lower price.

steps.action: **Prepare evidence.** Gather competing quotes, historical order volume, forecasted demand, and reasons the supplier should value the account.
steps.expect: a credible basis for the ask.

steps.action: **Open with a specific proposal.** Ask for a price tier or term tied to quantity, reorder schedule, or prompt payment.
steps.expect: the supplier receives a concrete offer they can accept or counter.

steps.action: **Trade concessions deliberately.** [BRANCH: supplier lowers price, protect quality and delivery terms | supplier refuses, ask for freight, payment, or defect allowance improvement]
steps.expect: each concession is exchanged for something measurable.

steps.action: **Request the revised quote in writing.** Include unit price, MOQ, validity date, lead time, payment terms, freight terms, and quality obligations.
steps.expect: the supplier sends an updated written quote.

steps.action: **Recalculate landed cost.** Include any changed freight, payment fee, defect allowance, or inventory carrying cost.
steps.expect: the revised offer is confirmed to meet or miss the target.

steps.action: **Accept or walk away.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not issue a purchase order, deposit, or payment until the written quote matches the approved terms.
steps.expect: either a documented accepted quote or a clear decision to continue sourcing.

recipes.verification: A revised written supplier quote meets the target landed cost or documented alternative term, stays within MOQ and cash-flow limits, and is approved before any purchase order or payment is sent.

recipes.title: onboard a new supplier
recipes.name: onboard-a-new-supplier
recipes.goal: You qualify a new supplier, collect the required business and payment information, and make them ready for purchase orders without exposing the business to preventable fraud or quality risk.

steps.action: **Define the supply requirement.** Specify SKU, quantity, quality standard, lead time, packaging, certifications, and target landed cost.
steps.expect: a clear requirement the supplier can confirm or decline.

steps.action: **Verify business legitimacy.** Check company registration, website, references, address, and whether contact email matches the business domain.
steps.expect: evidence that the supplier is a real operating business.

steps.action: **Request onboarding documents.** Collect tax form, banking instructions through a secure channel, insurance or compliance certificates, catalog, and price list as applicable.
steps.expect: required documents are received or missing items are listed.

steps.action: **Review product fit and quality risk.** Compare samples, specifications, photos, certifications, and warranty terms against your requirement.
steps.expect: the supplier's offering meets the minimum standard or gaps are documented.

steps.action: **Agree on commercial terms.** Confirm unit price, minimum order quantity, payment terms, incoterms or shipping responsibility, lead time, returns, defects, and chargeback process.
steps.expect: terms are written in a quote, contract, or supplier profile.

steps.action: **Set up the supplier record.** Enter legal name, contact, addresses, tax status, payment terms, currency, and approved SKUs in the purchasing system.
steps.expect: the supplier appears in the system but is not yet paid without approval.

steps.action: **Verify payment instructions independently.** Call a known supplier phone number or use an approved vendor-verification process before activating bank details.
steps.expect: payment account details are confirmed outside the original email thread.

steps.action: **Approve initial purchasing.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* purchase orders and deposits commit money, so confirm supplier identity, terms, and approval authority first.
steps.expect: supplier status changes to approved for a limited first order or pilot.

steps.action: **Document first-order controls.** Set sample inspection, smaller initial quantity, deposit cap, or pre-shipment photos.
steps.expect: the first purchase has defined acceptance checks.

recipes.verification: The supplier has a complete approved profile, independently verified payment details, documented commercial terms, and first-order controls before any purchase order or deposit is released.

recipes.title: optimize a product title for search
recipes.name: optimize-a-product-title-for-search
recipes.goal: Rewrite a product title so shoppers and marketplace search can identify the product without keyword stuffing or policy violations.

steps.action: **Identify the core product terms.** List the words a buyer would use for the item type, brand, model, and essential attributes.
steps.expect: a short prioritized keyword list.

steps.action: **Check platform title rules.** Review character limits, prohibited claims, punctuation rules, and brand usage policy.
steps.expect: title constraints are known before editing.

steps.action: **Remove weak or risky wording.** Delete stuffing, subjective claims, competitor trademarks, ALL CAPS, and unverifiable superlatives.
steps.expect: only accurate, policy-safe terms remain.

steps.action: **Draft the title in natural order.** Use a readable pattern such as brand, product type, model, key attribute, size or count.
steps.expect: a title that communicates the product at a glance.

steps.action: **Validate against the product page.** Confirm every title claim is supported by images, specs, and inventory variant data.
steps.expect: no title term misrepresents the item.

steps.action: **Save the title update.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* title changes can affect rankings and ad relevance, so confirm spelling, SKU, and policy compliance first.
steps.expect: the admin stores the new title.

steps.action: **Check search and listing display.** View the live page, collection pages, marketplace search result, and mobile truncation.
steps.expect: the important terms appear before truncation.

recipes.verification: The live product title is readable, within platform limits, includes the most important accurate search terms, and displays correctly in search or collection results.

recipes.title: pause an underperforming ad
recipes.name: pause-an-underperforming-ad
recipes.goal: Pause an ad that is missing its performance target while preserving enough data to diagnose or relaunch it later.

steps.action: **Open the campaign report.** Filter to the relevant date range, attribution setting, campaign, ad set, and ad.
steps.expect: performance metrics for the exact ad being evaluated.

steps.action: **Compare against the stop rule.** Check spend, conversions, revenue, CPA, ROAS, CTR, and frequency against the target.
steps.expect: the ad clearly passes or fails the rule.

steps.action: **Check tracking before acting.** Confirm conversion tags and revenue reporting are working so the ad is not falsely blamed.
steps.expect: tracking status is healthy or the issue is identified.

steps.action: **Record the current state.** Save or export metrics, creative, audience, budget, and learning status.
steps.expect: there is a snapshot for later analysis.

steps.action: **Pause the ad.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* pausing can disrupt learning and delivery, so confirm the selected entity is the underperforming ad, not the whole account.
steps.expect: the ad status changes to paused and spend stops for that ad.

steps.action: **Check related budgets.** Confirm the budget does not simply shift to an equally poor ad unless that is intended.
steps.expect: remaining spend is assigned to acceptable campaigns or held.

steps.action: **Document the next test.** Note whether to revise creative, audience, landing page, bid, or offer before relaunch.
steps.expect: the paused ad has a clear follow-up action.

recipes.verification: The specific underperforming ad status is paused, its spend is no longer increasing after platform reporting delay, and its metrics snapshot is saved with the reason for pausing.

recipes.title: print a shipping label
recipes.name: print-a-shipping-label
recipes.goal: You buy and print the correct shipping label for an ecommerce order, then attach tracking to the order without address or service errors.

steps.action: **Open the order to fulfill.** Confirm payment status, fraud status, items, quantities, shipping address, and requested shipping method.
steps.expect: the order is eligible for shipment.

steps.action: **Pack and measure the package.** Include the correct items, packing slip if used, protective materials, final weight, and box dimensions.
steps.expect: package details reflect the actual parcel.

steps.action: **Validate the address.** Use the platform or carrier validator and resolve apartment, postal code, or country-format warnings.
steps.expect: the label destination is deliverable or flagged for customer confirmation.

steps.action: **Select carrier service.** Match or exceed the customer's paid shipping speed while considering tracking, insurance, signature, and cost.
steps.expect: selected service satisfies the order promise.

steps.action: **Review label cost and details.** Confirm origin, destination, package weight/dimensions, service, insurance, and ship date.
steps.expect: the label preview is accurate.

steps.action: **Purchase the label.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before buying, confirm order number, address, weight, dimensions, service, and label cost because void windows may be limited.
steps.expect: a label and tracking number are generated.

steps.action: **Print and inspect the label.** Print at the correct size and verify barcode clarity, address readability, and no cutoff edges.
steps.expect: the carrier can scan the label.

steps.action: **Attach label and mark fulfilled.** Affix label flat, cover old barcodes, upload tracking if not automatic, and send customer notification.
steps.expect: the order shows fulfilled/shipped with tracking.

steps.action: **Handoff to carrier.** Drop off or schedule pickup and keep acceptance scan or manifest when possible.
steps.expect: tracking shows carrier possession or a documented handoff.

recipes.verification: The package has a scannable label for the correct order/address/service, the order record contains tracking, and the carrier has received or is scheduled to receive the parcel.

recipes.title: process a return request
recipes.name: process-a-return-request
recipes.goal: You evaluate a customer's return request, issue the correct authorization, and set conditions so the refund is accurate after the item is received.

steps.action: **Open the order record.** Verify customer, items, delivery status, payment status, and prior refunds or disputes.
steps.expect: the request is tied to the correct order.

steps.action: **Check return eligibility.** Compare request date, item category, condition, final-sale status, and reason against policy.
steps.expect: a decision on whether the item qualifies for return.

steps.action: **Inspect evidence if needed.** For damage, wrong item, or defect, request photos, serial numbers, packaging images, or troubleshooting results.
steps.expect: enough evidence to choose standard return, replacement, or denial.

steps.action: **Choose the return outcome.** [BRANCH: eligible return | ineligible return | damaged/wrong item] Approve with instructions, deny with policy explanation, or offer replacement/refund path.
steps.expect: a policy-backed outcome.

steps.action: **Create the return authorization.** Select items, quantities, return reason, expected condition, restocking fee if allowed, and refund destination.
steps.expect: an RMA or return record exists.

steps.action: **Send label and instructions.** Provide deadline, packaging requirements, included accessories, label, and tracking if the store pays return shipping.
steps.expect: the customer knows exactly how to send the item back.

steps.action: **Receive and inspect the return.** Compare the received item, serial number, condition, and included parts against the authorization.
steps.expect: the return is accepted, partially accepted, or escalated.

steps.action: **Issue the refund or exchange.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before refunding, confirm order number, item received, amount, fees, tax, shipping refund, and payment method.
steps.expect: the refund/exchange is recorded and customer is notified.

steps.action: **Update inventory disposition.** Restock sellable items, quarantine damaged goods, or mark unsellable.
steps.expect: inventory reflects the actual returned condition.

recipes.verification: The return request has a documented approve/deny/exchange outcome, any received item has been inspected, and the final refund or replacement record matches policy and order details.

recipes.title: read an ad performance report
recipes.name: read-an-ad-performance-report
recipes.goal: Read an ad performance report and decide whether the campaign is profitable, needs adjustment, or should be paused.

steps.action: **Set the reporting window.** Choose a date range long enough for attribution delay and matching the campaign objective.
steps.expect: report data covers the intended evaluation period.

steps.action: **Confirm metric definitions.** Check attribution window, conversion event, revenue source, currency, and whether refunds are included.
steps.expect: metrics are comparable to the business target.

steps.action: **Review spend and delivery.** Read impressions, reach, frequency, clicks, CPM, CPC, and total spend.
steps.expect: you know whether the campaign is getting enough traffic.

steps.action: **Review conversion outcomes.** Read orders, revenue, CPA, ROAS, conversion rate, and average order value.
steps.expect: sales performance is visible for each campaign or ad.

steps.action: **Calculate contribution profit.** Subtract ad spend, product cost, payment fees, fulfillment, and expected returns from attributed revenue.
steps.expect: each campaign is classified as profitable, break-even, or losing money.

steps.action: **Segment by useful dimensions.** Compare creative, audience, product, placement, device, region, and new-versus-returning customers.
steps.expect: the strongest and weakest segments are identifiable.

steps.action: **Decide the action.** [BRANCH: scale | hold | revise | pause] Tie the action to the target metric and confidence level.
steps.expect: every campaign has a documented next action.

recipes.verification: The report identifies spend, revenue, CPA or ROAS, contribution profit, and a documented scale, hold, revise, or pause decision for each evaluated campaign.

recipes.title: reduce cart abandonment
recipes.name: reduce-cart-abandonment
recipes.goal: You identify why shoppers leave checkout and implement a measured fix that increases completed orders without creating misleading or risky pressure.

steps.action: **Measure the baseline.** Record cart additions, checkout starts, completed orders, device split, and top abandoned products for a recent normal period.
steps.expect: a baseline rate and the step where the largest drop-off occurs.

steps.action: **Inspect the checkout path.** Walk through product page, cart, shipping, payment, and confirmation on desktop and mobile.
steps.expect: a list of visible friction points such as surprise shipping, account requirement, or payment errors.

steps.action: **Check total-cost surprises.** Compare advertised price, shipping, taxes, fees, and delivery promise at cart and checkout.
steps.expect: customers see costs early enough to avoid a late surprise.

steps.action: **Fix the highest-confidence blocker first.** [BRANCH: shipping shock, show free-shipping threshold or lower-cost option | payment friction, add trusted payment methods | form friction, simplify required fields]
steps.expect: one concrete checkout change is live or ready to publish.

steps.action: **Configure cart recovery.** Create a reminder email or message with item details, support link, and honest availability, sent only to eligible contacts.
steps.expect: abandoned carts receive a compliant recovery message after the chosen delay.

steps.action: **Test recovery links.** Trigger an abandoned cart with a test account and click the recovery link.
steps.expect: the cart reopens with the correct items and current prices.

steps.action: **Set a measurement window.** Compare abandonment and completed orders for a defined period after the change against the baseline.
steps.expect: a date range and success threshold are documented.

steps.action: **Publish the change.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* if sending a discount or policy promise, confirm margin, expiration, and eligibility before enabling automation.
steps.expect: the recovery flow or checkout fix is active for real shoppers.

steps.action: **Review impact and side effects.** Check conversion, revenue per visitor, support tickets, refund rate, and coupon dependency.
steps.expect: the change either improves the target metric without unacceptable side effects or is rolled back.

recipes.verification: The store has a documented baseline, one abandonment-reduction change live, a tested abandoned-cart recovery path if used, and a post-change report comparing checkout completion against the baseline.

recipes.title: reprice inventory dynamically
recipes.name: reprice-inventory-dynamically
recipes.goal: You adjust product prices using inventory, demand, competitor, and margin signals while enforcing a hard price floor and audit trail.

steps.action: **Define repricing rules.** Set the business goal, such as clearing aging stock, protecting margin, matching market price, or slowing sales of scarce inventory.
steps.expect: a written repricing objective for each SKU group.

steps.action: **Calculate price floors and ceilings.** Include full cost, marketplace fees, shipping, returns allowance, and any brand or legal price limits.
steps.expect: every SKU has a minimum and maximum allowed price.

steps.action: **Segment inventory.** Group SKUs by stock level, age, seasonality, sales velocity, and replacement lead time.
steps.expect: products with similar pricing logic are grouped together.

steps.action: **Gather market signals.** Review competitor all-in prices, buy-box status, conversion rate, ad cost, and cart abandonment.
steps.expect: current demand and competition data for each group.

steps.action: **Choose price changes.** Apply conservative increments, such as lowering slow movers within floor limits or raising scarce fast movers within ceiling limits.
steps.expect: proposed prices that satisfy the rule set.

steps.action: **Preview margin and order impact.** Model expected gross margin, inventory depletion date, and customer-facing totals after discounts.
steps.expect: the change does not create loss-making or misleading prices.

steps.action: **Apply the repricing update.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before saving live, confirm SKU mapping, floor/ceiling, currency, sale badges, and channel because customers can order at the new price.
steps.expect: live prices update only for intended SKUs.

steps.action: **Monitor results.** Track conversion, revenue, margin, buy-box status, stockout risk, and customer complaints after the change.
steps.expect: evidence that repricing moved the target metric without breaking constraints.

steps.action: **Roll back or iterate.** Restore prior price if performance worsens or if a rule violation appears.
steps.expect: each SKU has a current price and reason recorded.

recipes.verification: The intended SKUs have live prices within approved floor/ceiling bounds, the repricing reason is recorded, and monitoring confirms no unintended SKU, currency, or discount-stack violation.

recipes.title: respond to a buyer message
recipes.name: respond-to-a-buyer-message
recipes.goal: Respond to a buyer message accurately, safely, and within marketplace or store service expectations.

steps.action: **Read the full thread and order record.** Check the buyer's question, order status, shipping details, and prior promises.
steps.expect: the buyer's issue and context are clear.

steps.action: **Classify the message.** Identify whether it is a product question, shipping issue, return request, complaint, scam attempt, or policy-sensitive topic.
steps.expect: the response path is known.

steps.action: **Verify facts before replying.** Check inventory, tracking, delivery estimate, return window, sizing, compatibility, or warranty terms.
steps.expect: the answer is based on current records.

steps.action: **Draft a concise response.** Address the buyer by issue, answer directly, and state the next action or timeline.
steps.expect: the message is clear and does not overpromise.

steps.action: **Keep the conversation on-platform.** Decline requests for external payment, private links, gift cards, or moving the dispute elsewhere.
steps.expect: the reply complies with platform protection rules.

steps.action: **Send or escalate.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before sending, confirm order number, amount, and promises because messages become part of the dispute record.
steps.expect: the buyer receives the response or the ticket is assigned to the right team.

steps.action: **Set a follow-up reminder if needed.** Track promised shipping updates, refunds, replacements, or supplier answers.
steps.expect: unresolved buyer issues have an owner and due time.

recipes.verification: The buyer has received an accurate on-platform reply, any promised action is recorded with an owner, and no prohibited off-platform payment or private data exchange occurred.

recipes.title: restock a low inventory item
recipes.name: restock-a-low-inventory-item
recipes.goal: You reorder a low-inventory ecommerce item in the right quantity and update systems so sales can continue without overspending or overselling.

steps.action: **Confirm true available inventory.** Check on-hand, reserved, damaged, returned, and incoming quantities.
steps.expect: an accurate available-to-sell number.

steps.action: **Estimate demand through the next lead time.** Use recent sales velocity, seasonality, campaigns, and safety stock.
steps.expect: a forecasted quantity needed before the next restock can arrive.

steps.action: **Calculate reorder quantity.** Subtract available and incoming units from forecasted need, then respect minimum order quantity and cash constraints.
steps.expect: a proposed reorder amount with cost.

steps.action: **Check supplier terms.** Confirm unit cost, lead time, payment terms, shipping cost, minimums, and substitution rules.
steps.expect: a purchase option that matches budget and timing.

steps.action: **Create or approve the purchase order.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before sending, confirm SKU, quantity, cost, delivery address, payment terms, and cancellation policy.
steps.expect: supplier receives a correct order or purchase order.

steps.action: **Record incoming inventory.** Add expected quantity, ETA, supplier order number, and receiving location in the inventory system.
steps.expect: staff can see incoming stock without making it prematurely sellable.

steps.action: **Adjust selling controls.** [BRANCH: enough stock until arrival | stockout likely] Keep sales open if stock is sufficient; if stockout is likely, cap quantity, enable preorder with clear date, or pause ads.
steps.expect: customer-facing availability matches realistic supply.

steps.action: **Track shipment and receive stock.** Monitor supplier updates, inspect received units, and reconcile quantity/condition against the purchase order.
steps.expect: inventory is increased only for sellable units actually received.

recipes.verification: A supplier order or purchase order is confirmed for the correct SKU and quantity, incoming inventory is recorded with ETA, and customer-facing availability is adjusted to prevent overselling.

recipes.title: run a discount promotion
recipes.name: run-a-discount-promotion
recipes.goal: You create a discount promotion with controlled eligibility, margin protection, and a verified customer checkout experience.

steps.action: **Define the promotion objective.** Choose whether the goal is inventory clearance, first purchase, average-order-value lift, retention, or campaign attribution.
steps.expect: a measurable objective and target audience.

steps.action: **Select eligible products and customers.** Include only SKUs, collections, customer segments, or channels that fit the objective.
steps.expect: a precise eligibility list.

steps.action: **Calculate margin impact.** Model discount amount, shipping subsidy, platform fees, returns, and ad spend against the floor margin.
steps.expect: a maximum safe discount and expected contribution margin.

steps.action: **Create the discount rule.** Configure code or automatic discount, value, minimum order, usage limits, start/end time, customer eligibility, and stacking rules.
steps.expect: a draft or saved promotion with bounded rules.

steps.action: **Write customer-facing terms.** State eligible items, expiration, exclusions, minimums, and whether the discount combines with other offers.
steps.expect: the offer terms match the actual rule.

steps.action: **Test checkout scenarios.** Try eligible and ineligible products, minimum order edge cases, existing coupons, and mobile checkout.
steps.expect: the discount applies only where intended.

steps.action: **Launch the promotion.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before activation, confirm dates, timezone, discount value, eligibility, usage caps, and stacking because customers can redeem immediately.
steps.expect: the promotion is active and visible to the intended audience.

steps.action: **Monitor redemptions and margin.** Track code usage, order values, inventory, customer segment, and net margin during the promotion.
steps.expect: redemptions stay within budget and inventory constraints.

steps.action: **End and review.** Disable or let the promotion expire, then compare results against the objective.
steps.expect: the discount is no longer redeemable and performance is recorded.

recipes.verification: The promotion is active only for the intended products/customers/time window, test carts show the correct discount behavior, and redemption/margin tracking is in place.

recipes.title: run a flash sale
recipes.name: run-a-flash-sale
recipes.goal: You run a time-limited ecommerce flash sale with controlled inventory, tested checkout, and a clean shutdown at the advertised end time.

steps.action: **Define sale constraints.** Set start/end time, timezone, eligible products, inventory cap, customer limit, and revenue or sell-through target.
steps.expect: the sale has measurable boundaries.

steps.action: **Check inventory and fulfillment capacity.** Confirm sellable units, warehouse staffing, packaging, carrier pickup, and backorder settings.
steps.expect: sale volume can be fulfilled within the promised window.

steps.action: **Configure the discount.** Create automatic sale prices or coupon rules with eligibility, usage limits, stacking prevention, and exact schedule.
steps.expect: the discount exists but is bounded.

steps.action: **Prepare customer-facing messaging.** Update banners, email, ads, product pages, and terms with the same start/end time and exclusions.
steps.expect: public messaging matches the backend rule.

steps.action: **Load-test critical paths if traffic will spike.** Check home page, product page, cart, checkout, payment, and inventory decrement behavior.
steps.expect: the store can handle expected demand or the plan is scaled down.

steps.action: **Test checkout before launch.** Use an eligible cart and ineligible cart to verify price, shipping, tax, stock limits, and discount stacking.
steps.expect: sale pricing appears only where intended.

steps.action: **Launch the flash sale.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before activation or campaign send, confirm time, products, discount, inventory caps, links, and rollback plan because customers can buy immediately.
steps.expect: sale is live and traffic reaches the correct products.

steps.action: **Monitor during the sale.** Watch orders, payment failures, site errors, inventory depletion, coupon abuse, and customer support volume.
steps.expect: problems are detected while there is still time to intervene.

steps.action: **End the sale cleanly.** Disable discounts, remove banners, stop ads/emails, and verify product prices return to normal.
steps.expect: customers can no longer redeem the flash-sale offer after the end time.

steps.action: **Review results.** Compare revenue, margin, sell-through, new customers, refunds, and operational issues against the target.
steps.expect: sale outcome is documented for the next campaign.

recipes.verification: The flash sale starts and ends at the intended times, eligible carts receive the correct discount during the window only, inventory stays within cap or is handled by sold-out logic, and post-sale prices return to normal.

recipes.title: run a google shopping ad
recipes.name: run-a-google-shopping-ad
recipes.goal: Launch a Google Shopping campaign for eligible products with a controlled budget, valid feed, and measurable conversion tracking.

steps.action: **Confirm product-feed health.** Open Merchant Center diagnostics and resolve disapprovals for the products you want to advertise.
steps.expect: selected products are approved and eligible for Shopping ads.

steps.action: **Verify landing pages and policies.** Check price, availability, returns, contact information, and checkout security.
steps.expect: feed data matches the live site and policy issues are absent.

steps.action: **Confirm conversion tracking.** Test purchase or checkout events in Google Ads and analytics.
steps.expect: a recent test conversion or tag assistant event appears correctly.

steps.action: **Create the campaign.** Choose Shopping or Performance Max with Merchant Center products, target locations, language, and bidding strategy.
steps.expect: the campaign draft contains the intended product source and market.

steps.action: **Set budget and exclusions.** Enter the daily budget cap, excluded products, negative keywords where available, and brand-safety settings.
steps.expect: spend cannot exceed the planned daily cap by configuration.

steps.action: **Review and publish.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* ads can spend money once enabled, so confirm budget, products, geography, and conversion action first.
steps.expect: the campaign status changes to enabled or under review.

steps.action: **Check after launch.** Review impressions, clicks, spend, product status, and conversion tracking after the first traffic arrives.
steps.expect: spend and traffic appear only for the intended products and regions.

recipes.verification: The Shopping campaign is enabled or under review, uses approved products from Merchant Center, has conversion tracking selected, and has a daily budget at or below the approved cap.

recipes.title: run a limited time coupon
recipes.name: run-a-limited-time-coupon
recipes.goal: You create a coupon with a defined discount, eligibility, and expiration, then verify customers can redeem it only within the intended limits.

steps.action: **Set the promotion target.** Choose the exact goal: clear inventory, acquire first-time buyers, recover carts, or reward loyal customers.
steps.expect: a written target and success metric such as orders, revenue, or units moved.

steps.action: **Calculate the discount guardrails.** Check product margin, shipping subsidy, payment fees, and return risk before choosing percent, fixed amount, or free shipping.
steps.expect: a discount that does not push the order below the allowed profit floor.

steps.action: **Create the coupon code.** Enter a memorable code, discount type, eligible products or collections, customer segment, redemption limit, and per-customer limit.
steps.expect: the draft coupon shows the intended amount and restrictions.

steps.action: **Set the time window.** Use the store's business time zone and include both start and end timestamp.
steps.expect: the promotion has a precise active period, not an open-ended coupon.

steps.action: **Exclude conflicting discounts.** Disable stacking with subscriptions, wholesale pricing, gift cards, or other promotions unless intentionally allowed.
steps.expect: the rules show whether the code can combine with other offers.

steps.action: **Test checkout before launch.** Add eligible and ineligible products, apply the code, and verify taxes, shipping, and totals.
steps.expect: eligible carts receive the right discount and ineligible carts show a clear rejection.

steps.action: **Publish the code to the chosen channel.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once sent to customers, the code can spread, so confirm limits, expiration, and margin first.
steps.expect: the coupon is active and the announcement contains the same terms as the platform rule.

steps.action: **Monitor redemption and margin.** Review orders using the code, average order value, refund rate, and remaining redemption count.
steps.expect: performance is visible and any unexpected use is caught early.

steps.action: **End or archive the coupon.** After the window closes, disable the code or confirm automatic expiration.
steps.expect: new checkout attempts no longer receive the discount.

recipes.verification: The coupon is active only for the intended products, customers, redemption count, and time window, and a test checkout shows the exact expected discount before any public announcement.

recipes.title: set a break even price
recipes.name: set-a-break-even-price
recipes.goal: Set the minimum price at which a product breaks even after variable costs, fees, and any required advertising or overhead allocation.

steps.action: **Define the break-even scope.** Choose variable-cost break-even, contribution break-even with ads, or fully loaded break-even with overhead.
steps.expect: the calculation scope is explicit.

steps.action: **List all per-unit costs.** Include landed cost, packaging, payment fees, platform fees, shipping subsidy, returns, and support allowance.
steps.expect: each variable cost has a value and source.

steps.action: **Convert percentage fees into a formula.** Separate fixed fees from percentage fees so the price solves correctly.
steps.expect: the price formula accounts for fee percentages.

steps.action: **Calculate the break-even price.** Divide fixed per-unit costs by one minus the total percentage-fee rate, then add required profit or ad allowance if included.
steps.expect: a minimum price before rounding.

steps.action: **Check market and policy constraints.** Compare the break-even price to competitor prices, minimum advertised price, and marketplace rules.
steps.expect: you know whether the product can compete profitably.

steps.action: **Set or record the price floor.** Save the floor in the pricing sheet, repricer, or product admin. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not lower live price below the floor unless leadership approves a planned loss.
steps.expect: the system or team has a clear minimum price.

steps.action: **Test promotions against the floor.** Apply common coupons, bundles, and free-shipping thresholds to make sure they do not go below break-even.
steps.expect: planned discounts stay above the floor or are blocked.

recipes.verification: A documented break-even price exists for the product and channel, and live pricing rules or promotion checks prevent selling below that price without explicit approval.

recipes.title: set a minimum order for free shipping
recipes.name: set-a-minimum-order-for-free-shipping
recipes.goal: You set a free-shipping threshold that encourages larger carts while protecting margin, then verify checkout applies it correctly.

steps.action: **Calculate the current economics.** Record average order value, average gross margin, average shipping cost, and contribution margin by order size.
steps.expect: a minimum order value that can absorb shipping without wiping out profit.

steps.action: **Choose the threshold.** Set it slightly above average order value or at a bundle-friendly amount that customers can reasonably reach.
steps.expect: a target threshold with a margin rationale.

steps.action: **Define eligible regions and products.** Exclude oversized, hazardous, wholesale, subscription, or international orders if they do not fit the economics.
steps.expect: a clear eligibility list.

steps.action: **Create the shipping rule.** Add a free-shipping rate with minimum subtotal, eligible zones, and product exclusions as supported by the platform.
steps.expect: the shipping settings show free shipping only above the threshold.

steps.action: **Add cart messaging.** Show progress such as "Add X more for free shipping" using subtotal rules that match checkout.
steps.expect: the cart message updates as items are added or removed.

steps.action: **Test below, at, and above the threshold.** Use representative carts and addresses in eligible and excluded zones.
steps.expect: free shipping appears only when the subtotal and destination qualify.

steps.action: **Publish the threshold.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once advertised, customers may rely on it, so confirm exclusions and dates before promoting.
steps.expect: product, cart, and policy pages state the same free-shipping terms.

steps.action: **Monitor order mix.** Track average order value, shipping cost as a percent of revenue, conversion, and support tickets.
steps.expect: the threshold improves cart value without excessive shipping subsidy.

recipes.verification: Checkout grants free shipping for an eligible cart at or above the threshold and rejects it for below-threshold or excluded carts, with matching terms visible in cart and shipping policy text.

recipes.title: set a product price
recipes.name: set-a-product-price
recipes.goal: You set a product price that covers costs, fits market positioning, and is entered correctly in the ecommerce system.

steps.action: **Calculate landed unit cost.** Include product cost, freight, duties, packaging, payment fees, platform fees, fulfillment labor, and expected returns.
steps.expect: a per-unit cost number that reflects selling reality.

steps.action: **Choose the margin target.** Set minimum gross margin and preferred gross margin based on category, cash needs, and acquisition costs.
steps.expect: a minimum viable price and a target price.

steps.action: **Map the market range.** Compare direct competitors, substitutes, brand positioning, review strength, and shipping terms.
steps.expect: a realistic price band customers already understand.

steps.action: **Select the list price.** Choose a price that meets the minimum margin and supports the product's positioning.
steps.expect: a final list price with a documented rationale.

steps.action: **Decide discount boundaries.** Define the lowest promotional price, coupon exclusions, wholesale price, and bundle impact.
steps.expect: a floor price that protects margin during promotions.

steps.action: **Enter pricing fields.** Add price, compare-at/reference price only if truthful, cost field, tax category, and variant-specific prices.
