steps.expect: the admin record reflects the intended price for each variant.

steps.action: **Preview checkout totals.** Add the product to cart and check tax, shipping, discounts, and currency conversion if relevant.
steps.expect: the customer-facing total matches expectations.

steps.action: **Publish the price.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before saving live, confirm SKU, channel, price, discount eligibility, and currency because customers can place orders immediately.
steps.expect: the live product page and checkout show the correct price.

steps.action: **Monitor early performance.** Track conversion, abandoned carts, margin, ad spend, and support questions after the price changes.
steps.expect: data showing whether the price is sustainable.

recipes.verification: The live product price and checkout total match the documented list price, each variant meets or intentionally flags the minimum margin, and discount rules cannot push the item below its floor price.

recipes.title: set a safety stock level
recipes.name: set-a-safety-stock-level
recipes.goal: You set a safety stock quantity that buffers demand spikes and supplier delays without holding excessive inventory.

steps.action: **Select the SKU and planning period.** Use one product or variant and a demand period that matches how often you replenish.
steps.expect: the safety stock calculation is scoped to a specific SKU.

steps.action: **Measure demand variability.** Review daily or weekly sales swings, excluding known one-off anomalies unless likely to recur.
steps.expect: a range or standard deviation of demand.

steps.action: **Measure lead-time variability.** Compare promised versus actual supplier lead times across recent orders.
steps.expect: a normal and worst-case lead-time range.

steps.action: **Choose the service target.** Decide how often you are willing to avoid stockouts, such as 90%, 95%, or 98%.
steps.expect: a service level that fits product importance and carrying cost.

steps.action: **Calculate initial safety stock.** Use a simple max-average method or a statistical method supported by your planning tool.
steps.expect: a proposed buffer quantity in sellable units.

steps.action: **Check business constraints.** Compare the buffer against cash tied up, warehouse space, shelf life, and markdown risk.
steps.expect: the buffer is feasible or adjusted downward with documented tradeoff.

steps.action: **Enter the safety stock level.** Add it to inventory software, purchasing spreadsheet, or replenishment rule.
steps.expect: replenishment calculations reserve the buffer instead of treating it as available to consume.

steps.action: **Review exceptions monthly.** Check stockouts, excess stock, supplier delays, and demand spikes.
steps.expect: the safety stock level is increased, decreased, or confirmed based on actual performance.

recipes.verification: The SKU has a documented safety stock quantity entered in the replenishment system, with assumptions for demand variability, lead-time variability, service level, and carrying-cost constraints.

recipes.title: set an ad budget and cap
recipes.name: set-an-ad-budget-and-cap
recipes.goal: Set an ad budget and cap so a campaign can run without exceeding the business's approved spend limit.

steps.action: **Identify the control level.** Locate account spend limits, campaign budgets, ad-set budgets, and billing thresholds.
steps.expect: you know which setting actually limits spend.

steps.action: **Translate the approved budget.** Convert the total cap into daily or lifetime values using the campaign schedule.
steps.expect: a numeric budget that matches the approved cap.

steps.action: **Set campaign or ad-set budget.** Enter the daily or lifetime budget in the appropriate field and confirm currency.
steps.expect: the campaign shows the intended budget value.

steps.action: **Set an account-level cap if available.** Add a secondary spend limit for the billing account or campaign group.
steps.expect: a hard stop or alert exists above the campaign budget.

steps.action: **Check pacing and overspend rules.** Read how the platform may spend above the daily average and compensate later.
steps.expect: you understand the maximum possible short-term spend.

steps.action: **Save the settings.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* active ads may spend immediately under the new cap, so confirm currency, schedule, and budget before saving.
steps.expect: the new budget is active or scheduled.

steps.action: **Set monitoring alerts.** Create platform, analytics, or finance alerts at 50%, 80%, and 100% of the cap.
steps.expect: someone will be notified before the budget is exhausted.

recipes.verification: The active campaign and any account-level control show budget values that keep maximum spend at or below the approved cap, and alerting is configured for spend thresholds.

recipes.title: set up a loyalty program
recipes.name: set-up-a-loyalty-program
recipes.goal: Launch a loyalty program that rewards repeat customers while keeping reward liability and discount cost under control.

steps.action: **Define the reward economics.** Choose points per currency spent, redemption value, exclusions, expiration, and a monthly liability cap.
steps.expect: a written rule set with an estimated reward cost per order.

steps.action: **Choose eligible actions.** Decide whether customers earn for purchases only or also for account creation, reviews, birthdays, and referrals.
steps.expect: each earn action has a fraud risk and reward value assigned.

steps.action: **Configure the loyalty tool.** Set earning rules, redemption rules, customer account requirements, and excluded products or discounts.
steps.expect: the admin shows the program rules saved and inactive or in test mode.

steps.action: **Add customer-facing explanations.** Update account pages, checkout messaging, and help content with plain terms.
steps.expect: customers can see how points are earned, redeemed, and expired.

steps.action: **Test earn and redeem flows.** Place test orders, cancel one, refund one, and redeem points on a new cart. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not launch until refunds and cancellations reverse points correctly.
steps.expect: point balances change exactly as the policy says.

steps.action: **Launch to a limited audience first.** Enable for staff, VIP customers, or a small segment before full rollout.
steps.expect: real accounts earn and redeem points without support intervention.

steps.action: **Monitor cost and abuse.** Review redemption rate, liability balance, suspicious account creation, and margin impact weekly.
steps.expect: the program stays within the planned reward budget.

recipes.verification: The loyalty program is live for the intended audience, a test customer earns and redeems points under the published rules, and the estimated reward cost per order is within the configured cap.

recipes.title: set up a preorder
recipes.name: set-up-a-preorder
recipes.goal: Set up a preorder product so customers can buy or reserve it with clear timing, payment, cancellation, and fulfillment expectations.

steps.action: **Confirm supply and timeline.** Verify purchase order, production status, expected arrival, and quantity available for preorder.
steps.expect: a realistic ship window and preorder quantity cap.

steps.action: **Choose payment timing.** [BRANCH: charge now | authorize later | deposit] Match the method to platform capability and local rules.
steps.expect: the customer payment flow is defined.

steps.action: **Configure preorder inventory.** Set the product to accept preorders only up to the approved quantity and prevent oversell beyond the cap.
steps.expect: available preorder units match committed supply.

steps.action: **Write transparent product messaging.** State preorder status, expected ship window, payment timing, cancellation policy, and what happens if delayed.
steps.expect: the product page clearly differs from in-stock items.

steps.action: **Set checkout and order tags.** Add preorder labels to cart, checkout, confirmation email, and fulfillment workflow.
steps.expect: customers and operations can identify preorder orders.

steps.action: **Test the full purchase path.** Place a test preorder and inspect payment, confirmation, inventory, taxes, and fulfillment hold. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not launch until customers cannot mistake the item for immediate shipment.
steps.expect: the test order is marked as preorder and not released for immediate fulfillment.

steps.action: **Publish and monitor.** Track units sold, payment status, customer questions, supplier updates, and delay risk.
steps.expect: preorder sales remain within cap and customers receive updates.

recipes.verification: The live product clearly shows preorder terms, checkout and confirmation label the order as preorder, sales cannot exceed the quantity cap, and a test order is held for later fulfillment.

recipes.title: set up a shipping rate
recipes.name: set-up-a-shipping-rate
recipes.goal: You configure an ecommerce shipping rate that charges customers accurately and appears only for eligible products, destinations, and order conditions.

steps.action: **Define the rate purpose.** Decide whether the rate is flat, free over threshold, weight-based, carrier-calculated, local delivery, or pickup.
steps.expect: one shipping rule with a clear use case.

steps.action: **Choose eligible destinations.** Select countries, regions, postal codes, or local delivery radius where the rate should appear.
steps.expect: the rate will not show for unsupported locations.

steps.action: **Assign products or profiles.** Link the rate to the correct product group, warehouse, vendor, or fulfillment location.
steps.expect: only eligible items can use the rate.

steps.action: **Set price and conditions.** Enter shipping price, free-shipping threshold, weight/order-value limits, handling fee, and delivery estimate.
steps.expect: the rule reflects both customer promise and cost coverage.

steps.action: **Check margin impact.** Test representative carts to compare charged shipping against expected carrier/fulfillment cost.
steps.expect: the rate does not routinely create unintended losses.

steps.action: **Save the shipping rate.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before enabling, confirm destinations, products, price, conditions, and delivery promise because customers can select the rate at checkout.
steps.expect: the rate appears in shipping settings as active.

steps.action: **Test checkout edge cases.** Try eligible/ineligible addresses, light/heavy carts, threshold just below/above, and mixed product carts.
steps.expect: the rate appears and disappears exactly as intended.

steps.action: **Document the customer-facing promise.** Update shipping policy pages, product pages, or FAQ if the new rate changes timing or eligibility.
steps.expect: public wording matches checkout behavior.

steps.action: **Monitor first orders.** Compare charged shipping, label cost, delivery time, and support contacts.
steps.expect: real orders validate the rate or reveal needed adjustments.

recipes.verification: Checkout shows the new shipping rate only for intended products, destinations, and cart conditions, with a charge and delivery promise matching the configured rule.

recipes.title: track a conversion rate
recipes.name: track-a-conversion-rate
recipes.goal: You measure the percentage of visitors who complete a defined ecommerce action, using a consistent event, time window, and denominator.

steps.action: **Choose one conversion event.** Define the exact success action and avoid mixing purchases with softer events.
steps.expect: a named event such as `purchase_completed` or `email_signup`.

steps.action: **Define the audience denominator.** Choose sessions, users, product-page visitors, or campaign clicks depending on the question.
steps.expect: a clear formula: conversions divided by the selected visitor count.

steps.action: **Set the measurement window.** Pick dates, time zone, and attribution lookback, excluding abnormal outages if documented.
steps.expect: all reports use the same date range and time zone.

steps.action: **Verify event firing.** Complete a test action or inspect recent events to confirm the conversion event fires once per success.
steps.expect: the analytics event appears with correct timestamp and revenue or item metadata if relevant.

steps.action: **Filter internal and invalid traffic.** Exclude staff IPs, test orders, bot traffic, and duplicate transactions where the platform supports it.
steps.expect: the dataset reflects real customer behavior.

steps.action: **Calculate the rate.** Divide conversions by the selected denominator and record the raw counts beside the percentage.
steps.expect: a conversion rate with both numerator and denominator visible.

steps.action: **Segment the result.** Compare by channel, device, landing page, product, or new/returning customer.
steps.expect: at least one segment reveals where performance differs materially.

steps.action: **Create a recurring report.** Save a dashboard, scheduled email, or spreadsheet tab with the formula and source.
steps.expect: the same metric can be refreshed without redefining it.

steps.action: **Annotate changes.** Record promotions, site releases, pricing changes, and tracking updates that affect comparability.
steps.expect: future rate changes have operational context.

recipes.verification: The report shows a conversion rate for a named event, date range, time zone, numerator, denominator, and data source, and the conversion count reconciles with the underlying order or event log within an accepted tolerance.

recipes.title: update a product photo
recipes.name: update-a-product-photo
recipes.goal: Replace or add product photos so the listing accurately shows the item and improves buyer confidence.

steps.action: **Audit the current images.** Check whether photos are outdated, blurry, misleading, missing variants, or hiding flaws.
steps.expect: a clear list of images to replace or add.

steps.action: **Prepare compliant images.** Crop, resize, name files, and remove unsupported overlays or watermarks.
steps.expect: images meet platform dimensions and policy.

steps.action: **Confirm image rights and accuracy.** Use only owned, licensed, supplier-authorized, or platform-permitted photos.
steps.expect: every image can legally represent the product.

steps.action: **Upload the new photos.** Add images to the product media library and assign them to the correct product or variant.
steps.expect: uploaded images appear in the admin preview.

steps.action: **Set the image order and alt text.** Put the clearest main image first and add descriptive alt text for accessibility and search.
steps.expect: the product page preview has the intended primary image and labels.

steps.action: **Preview before publishing.** Check desktop, mobile, zoom, thumbnails, and variant switching. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* publishing misleading images can create disputes, so confirm the photos match the shipped item.
steps.expect: the buyer-facing preview is accurate and usable.

steps.action: **Save and verify live page.** Publish the update and refresh the live listing.
steps.expect: customers see the new product photo set.

recipes.verification: The live product page displays the intended new photo set, with the correct primary image, variant mapping, and no rejected or misleading media.

recipes.title: verify an order for fraud
recipes.name: verify-an-order-for-fraud
recipes.goal: You review a flagged ecommerce order and decide whether to fulfill, hold, cancel, or request verification using evidence that reduces chargeback and customer harm.

steps.action: **Open the order risk summary.** Review AVS, CVV, IP location, billing/shipping mismatch, proxy indicators, order velocity, and payment processor score.
steps.expect: a list of specific risk signals, not just a generic label.

steps.action: **Compare customer and order history.** Check account age, prior successful orders, chargebacks, returns, and recent address changes.
steps.expect: context showing whether this behavior is normal for the customer.

steps.action: **Assess item and fulfillment risk.** Note high-resale goods, expedited shipping, freight forwarding, gift cards, or digital delivery.
steps.expect: an order-level risk rating tied to what could be lost.

steps.action: **Look for benign explanations.** Identify legitimate reasons such as traveling customer, gift shipment, corporate card, or recent move.
steps.expect: possible low-risk explanations are documented.

steps.action: **Contact the customer through trusted channels if needed.** Use the email or phone already on the order; do not ask for full card numbers or sensitive documents unless policy requires secure upload.
steps.expect: the customer confirms or fails to confirm key order details.

steps.action: **Decide the action.** [BRANCH: low risk, release fulfillment | uncertain, hold and request verification | high risk, cancel and void/refund]
steps.expect: the order status reflects the chosen action.

steps.action: **Document the review.** Record evidence, customer response, decision, reviewer, and timestamp in the order notes.
steps.expect: another staff member can understand why the order was approved or stopped.

steps.action: **Release or stop fulfillment.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once shipped or digitally delivered, recovery may be impossible, so confirm payment status and risk decision first.
steps.expect: fulfillment is either released with tracking or the order is canceled/refunded according to policy.

recipes.verification: The flagged order has a documented fraud review with a final action, and no physical or digital fulfillment occurs until the payment and risk decision support release.

recipes.title: write a product description that converts
recipes.name: write-a-product-description-that-converts
recipes.goal: You write and publish a product description that helps qualified buyers decide while reducing returns, disputes, and misleading claims.

steps.action: **Collect verified product facts.** Use supplier specs, measurement, testing notes, and customer-service questions rather than guesses.
steps.expect: a fact sheet with claims you can support.

steps.action: **Define the buyer and job-to-be-done.** Identify who buys the product, what problem it solves, and what would make it a poor fit.
steps.expect: the description has a specific audience and use case.

steps.action: **Lead with the concrete benefit.** Write an opening sentence that connects the product's main feature to the buyer's practical outcome.
steps.expect: the first line explains why the product matters.

steps.action: **Add scannable purchase details.** Include bullets for specifications, included items, compatibility, sizing, materials, setup, and care.
steps.expect: a buyer can answer key fit questions quickly.

steps.action: **Handle limitations honestly.** State exclusions, size constraints, color variation, maintenance, region compatibility, or use restrictions.
steps.expect: the page prevents predictable misunderstandings.

steps.action: **Remove unsupported claims.** Delete exaggerations, medical/legal claims, fake urgency, or comparisons you cannot substantiate.
steps.expect: remaining claims are defensible and compliant.

steps.action: **Align description with media and variants.** Confirm photos, variant names, alt text, and description all refer to the same product configuration.
steps.expect: no contradiction between text, images, and options.

steps.action: **Publish or submit for approval.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before saving live, confirm price-sensitive claims, warranty terms, and compliance language because customers may rely on them.
steps.expect: the product page shows the approved description.

steps.action: **Check conversion and return signals.** Review add-to-cart rate, search queries, support questions, and return reasons after traffic arrives.
steps.expect: evidence of whether the description is reducing friction or creating confusion.

recipes.verification: The live or approved product description includes verified benefits, specifications, limitations, and included items, with no unsupported claims or contradictions against photos and variants.

recipes.title: enrich a contact record
recipes.name: enrich-a-contact-record
recipes.goal: Improve a CRM contact record with verified business information that supports routing, segmentation, and sales context.

steps.action: **Open the contact record.** Search by email, name, or company.
steps.expect: the existing contact fields are visible.

steps.action: **Review current data quality.** Check blank, outdated, conflicting, or low-confidence fields.
steps.expect: enrichment targets are identified.

steps.action: **Verify business identity.** Confirm current company, title, location, website, phone, and role from approved sources.
steps.expect: updates are based on a reliable source.

steps.action: **Update CRM fields.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] edit Contact fields in Salesforce; edit contact properties in HubSpot; in another CRM, update the equivalent profile fields.
steps.expect: enriched values appear on the record.

steps.action: **Record source or confidence.** Add source notes, last-enriched date, or data provider confidence if the CRM supports it.
steps.expect: future users can judge data reliability.

steps.action: **Review ownership and segments.** Update account association, owner, lifecycle stage, persona, or segment if enrichment changes routing.
steps.expect: the contact fits the right operational bucket.

steps.action: **Save and refresh.** Save changes and reload if needed to confirm automations finished.
steps.expect: the record shows updated fields and any triggered changes.

recipes.verification: The contact record contains verified business fields, source or confidence context, correct account association, and no unauthorized personal data.

recipes.title: escalate a support ticket
recipes.name: escalate-a-support-ticket
recipes.goal: Escalate a support ticket to the right specialist or incident path with enough context for fast handling.

steps.action: **Confirm escalation criteria.** Compare the ticket impact, urgency, and symptoms to the support escalation policy.
steps.expect: the reason for escalation is explicit.

steps.expect: the specialist has enough information to begin.

steps.expect: the escalation context is visible in the ticket.

steps.action: **Set escalation fields.** [BRANCH: Zendesk | generic] choose the Zendesk group, macro, problem link, or escalation tag; in a generic helpdesk, choose the specialist queue, status, and escalation reason.
steps.expect: routing metadata matches the escalation path.

steps.action: **Assign or route the ticket.** Move the ticket to the correct specialist, engineering, billing, or incident queue.
steps.expect: the new owner or queue is shown.

steps.action: **Update the customer if needed.** Send a brief reply that the issue is being reviewed by the appropriate team and state the next update window.
steps.expect: the customer knows what happens next.

recipes.verification: The ticket shows an escalation reason, evidence summary, specialist owner or queue, and customer update status if a reply was required.

recipes.title: export transactions for your accountant

recipes.title: forecast monthly sales
recipes.name: forecast-monthly-sales
recipes.goal: Produce a monthly sales forecast from CRM pipeline using close dates, stages, forecast categories, and rep judgment.

steps.action: **Classify forecast categories.** Set commit, best case, pipeline, omitted, or local equivalents based on evidence.

steps.action: **Calculate totals.** Summarize closed-won, commit, best case, weighted pipeline, and gap to target.

steps.action: **Add rep or manager judgment.** Adjust commentary for risk, upside, timing, procurement, and known blockers without changing source data inaccurately.

steps.action: **Save or export the forecast.** Save the CRM forecast/report or export only if policy allows.
steps.expect: stakeholders can access the monthly forecast.

recipes.verification: The forecast shows current-month closed-won, commit, best-case, pipeline, and gap totals, with material deals reviewed for stage, amount, close date, and next step.

recipes.title: fulfill and ship an order

steps.expect: the order shows fulfilled or shipped with tracking.

recipes.verification: The order is fulfilled with correct items, carrier label, tracking number, shipment status, and customer notification if required.

recipes.title: generate a profit and loss report
recipes.name: generate-a-profit-and-loss-report
recipes.goal: Generate a profit and loss report for a defined period so revenue, expenses, and net income can be reviewed.

steps.action: **Open reports.** Go to reports and choose Profit and Loss, Income Statement, or Statement of Activity.
steps.expect: a report setup screen or default P&L appears.

steps.action: **Set the date range.** Choose the month, quarter, year, or custom period being reviewed.
steps.expect: the report header shows the intended period.

steps.action: **Choose accounting basis.** [BRANCH: cash | accrual] select cash basis for paid transactions or accrual basis for earned and incurred activity.
steps.expect: the report basis is visible in settings or header.

steps.action: **Apply filters.** Add class, location, project, department, customer, or comparison columns if needed.
steps.expect: the report scope matches the review purpose.

steps.expect: onboarding receives the handoff and can acknowledge it.

recipes.verification: An onboarding-owned record exists with sold scope, documents, stakeholders, commitments, risks, owner, due dates, and notification to the onboarding team.

recipes.title: handle a chargeback
recipes.name: handle-a-chargeback
recipes.goal: Review a chargeback and either accept it or submit evidence by the deadline.

steps.action: **Open the dispute.** Find the chargeback in the payment processor or store dispute center.
steps.expect: reason code, amount, deadline, and status are visible.

steps.action: **Match the order.** Identify the order, payment, customer, fulfillment, refund, and communication records.
steps.expect: the disputed transaction is tied to one order.

steps.action: **Assess the reason.** Determine whether the claim is fraud, not received, not as described, duplicate, canceled, or credit not processed.
steps.expect: evidence needs are clear.

steps.action: **Decide response.** Choose to accept the chargeback or contest it based on policy, evidence strength, amount, and customer history.
steps.expect: the dispute has a documented strategy.

steps.action: **Gather evidence.** Collect receipt, billing match, delivery proof, tracking, product description, refund policy, and customer messages.
steps.expect: evidence directly addresses the reason code.

steps.action: **Prepare the response.** Write a brief factual statement and attach evidence in the required format.
steps.expect: the submission is complete and readable.

steps.action: **Submit or accept before deadline.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before submitting or accepting, confirm amount, order, evidence, and policy because missed or accepted chargebacks usually cannot be reopened.
steps.expect: the processor shows submitted or accepted status.

steps.action: **Record the outcome.** Note dispute status, deadline, expected decision date, and any order account action.
steps.expect: the business can track financial impact and follow-up.

recipes.verification: The dispute record shows accepted or submitted status before the deadline, with order-linked evidence or a documented acceptance reason.

recipes.title: hold a project retrospective
recipes.name: hold-a-project-retrospective
recipes.goal: Hold a project retrospective that produces a short set of improvement actions for future project work.

steps.action: **Define the retro scope.** Name the project period, milestone, or delivery event being reviewed.
steps.expect: participants discuss the same body of work.

steps.action: **Prepare prompts.** Use prompts such as what worked, what did not, what surprised us, and what to change.
steps.expect: feedback is structured.

steps.action: **Collect input silently.** Give participants time to write notes before discussion.
steps.expect: quieter participants can contribute.

steps.action: **Group themes.** Combine similar points and separate facts from interpretations.
steps.expect: the discussion focuses on patterns.

steps.action: **Discuss top themes.** Ask what caused each theme and what would improve future work.
steps.expect: the team moves from complaint to cause.

steps.action: **Choose actions.** Select one to three improvements with owners and due dates.
steps.expect: actions are small enough to complete.

steps.action: **Publish the summary.** Share themes, decisions, actions, owners, and follow-up date.
steps.expect: the project record includes the retrospective outcome.

recipes.verification: The retrospective summary contains themes, one to three improvement actions, owners, due dates, and a follow-up date.

recipes.title: issue a refund
recipes.name: issue-a-refund
recipes.goal: Issue a customer refund for a valid return, overpayment, cancellation, or service credit and record it against the correct sale.

steps.action: **Find the original sale.** Locate the invoice, receipt, order, or payment being refunded.

steps.action: **Send confirmation.** Provide the customer with amount, method, timing, and reference number.
steps.expect: the customer has written confirmation of the refund.

steps.action: **Check accounting impact.** Confirm the refund reduced revenue, tax liability, accounts receivable, or customer credit as intended.
steps.expect: reports no longer show the refunded amount as collectible revenue.

recipes.verification: The refund record links to the original sale, shows the approved amount and method, has submitted or completed status, and the customer balance and reports reflect the refund.

recipes.title: issue a store coupon code

recipes.title: log a bug report
recipes.name: log-a-bug-report
recipes.goal: Log a bug report that gives the owning team enough evidence to reproduce, prioritize, and fix the issue.

steps.action: **Open issue creation.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] choose Create issue in Jira, Add task in Asana, New issue in Linear, or New bug in a generic tracker.

recipes.title: log a meeting note in the crm

recipes.title: log a sales call

recipes.title: log a sick day

steps.expect: the leave code matches the reported absence.

steps.action: **Enter date and hours.** Add the sick day date, partial-day hours if applicable, and pay code.
steps.expect: the entry reflects the actual absence.

steps.action: **Add minimal notes.** Record only operational details such as "reported sick" or "manager notified."
steps.expect: no unnecessary medical details are stored.

steps.action: **Submit or save.** Save the leave entry or submit it for approval if required.
steps.expect: the system shows saved, pending, or approved status.

steps.action: **Confirm calendar impact.** Check that schedule, payroll, or team calendar reflects the absence if integrated.
steps.expect: downstream systems show the sick day or pending sync.

recipes.verification: The employee's time record shows the correct sick leave date, hours, status, and leave code with no unnecessary medical details.

recipes.title: mark a deal won or lost
recipes.name: mark-a-deal-won-or-lost
recipes.goal: Close a CRM deal as won or lost with accurate reason, amount, date, and handoff context.

steps.action: **Open the deal.** Find the opportunity or deal to close.
steps.expect: current stage, amount, and close date are visible.

steps.action: **Confirm the outcome evidence.** Check contract, purchase order, email confirmation, cancellation, or loss reason.
steps.expect: the close outcome is supported by evidence.

steps.action: **Update final fields.** Enter final amount, close date, products, primary competitor, loss reason, or win reason as applicable.
steps.expect: required close fields are complete.

steps.action: **Set the close stage.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] choose Closed Won or Closed Lost in Salesforce; move to Closed Won or Closed Lost in HubSpot; in another CRM, set the terminal won or lost stage.
steps.expect: the deal shows a closed status.

steps.action: **Add a closing note.** Summarize the outcome, reason, and any customer commitments.
steps.expect: the timeline explains why the deal closed.

steps.action: **Trigger next process.** For won deals, start onboarding or order processing; for lost deals, set nurture or closed-lost analysis if appropriate.
steps.expect: the correct post-close workflow begins.

recipes.verification: The deal is in a terminal won or lost stage with final amount, close date, required reason fields, closing note, and appropriate post-close action.

recipes.title: move a deal to the next stage
recipes.name: move-a-deal-to-the-next-stage
recipes.goal: Advance a CRM deal to the next pipeline stage only when the buyer evidence matches the stage criteria.

steps.action: **Open the deal.** Search for the opportunity or deal by account, contact, or deal name.
steps.expect: the current stage and deal details are visible.

steps.action: **Check stage criteria.** Compare the deal evidence against the next stage requirement, such as qualified need, discovery complete, proposal sent, or verbal agreement.
steps.expect: there is a clear reason to move or hold the deal.

steps.action: **Update required fields.** Enter amount, close date, next step, decision process, competitor, or probability fields required by the next stage.
steps.expect: no required-stage fields are blank.

steps.action: **Move the stage.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] select the next Opportunity Stage in Salesforce; drag or set Deal Stage in HubSpot; in another CRM, update the pipeline stage field.
steps.expect: the deal displays the new stage.

steps.action: **Log the reason.** Add a brief note or activity explaining the evidence behind the stage change.
steps.expect: reviewers can see why the deal advanced.

steps.action: **Save and confirm automation.** Save the record and review any created tasks, approvals, or notifications.
steps.expect: the CRM accepts the stage change and related workflow actions appear.

recipes.verification: The deal is in the intended next stage, required fields are complete, and the timeline contains evidence supporting the move.

recipes.title: offboard a departing employee
recipes.name: offboard-a-departing-employee
recipes.goal: Complete a departing employee's offboarding tasks so access, property, payroll, benefits, and knowledge transfer are handled.

steps.action: **Open the employee record.** Confirm legal name, employee ID, manager, location, and final work date.
steps.expect: the offboarding record matches the departing employee.

steps.action: **Create offboarding tasks.** Assign HR, IT, payroll, benefits, facilities, and manager tasks with due dates.
steps.expect: each required owner has a task.

steps.action: **Coordinate access removal.** Schedule account deactivation, badge removal, device return, and system ownership transfer.
steps.expect: access actions are queued for the right time.

steps.action: **Confirm final pay inputs.** Verify final hours, PTO payout, deductions, expenses, and severance if applicable.
steps.expect: payroll has the information needed for final pay.

steps.action: **Arrange knowledge transfer.** Ask the manager to capture projects, files, contacts, deadlines, and handoff owners.
steps.expect: active work has a successor or status note.

steps.action: **Send exit information.** Provide return instructions, benefits notices, final pay timing, and contact information.
steps.expect: the employee knows next steps.

steps.action: **Complete deprovisioning.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm final date, legal hold, and manager approval before disabling accounts or wiping devices.
steps.expect: access is disabled according to schedule.

steps.action: **Close the record.** Mark tasks complete and store required documentation.
steps.expect: the HRIS shows the employee as terminated or inactive.

recipes.verification: The HRIS shows the correct departure status, access is disabled or scheduled, property and payroll tasks are tracked, and required offboarding documents are stored.

recipes.title: onboard a new hire
recipes.name: onboard-a-new-hire
recipes.goal: Prepare a new hire for day one by completing HR setup, logistics, and manager handoffs.

steps.action: **Create the employee profile.** Enter legal name, preferred name, role, manager, department, location, start date, and employment type in HRIS.
steps.expect: the new hire has an HR record.

steps.action: **Launch onboarding tasks.** Assign tax, direct deposit, handbook, policy, benefits, and emergency contact tasks as applicable.
steps.expect: the new hire sees required tasks in the onboarding portal.

steps.action: **Coordinate equipment.** Request laptop, badge, workspace, shipping, and required tools.
steps.expect: each logistics task has an owner and due date.

steps.action: **Notify stakeholders.** Send start details to manager, IT, payroll, facilities, and recruiting.
steps.expect: each team knows the start date and dependencies.

steps.action: **Prepare day-one schedule.** Add orientation, manager check-in, team introduction, and required training.
steps.expect: the new hire has a first-day agenda.

steps.action: **Confirm documentation status.** Check completion of identity, tax, work authorization, and payroll forms according to local rules.
steps.expect: missing items are visible before start.

steps.action: **Send welcome information.** Share start time, location or login details, contact person, agenda, and what to bring.
steps.expect: the new hire knows how to start.

recipes.verification: The new hire profile exists, onboarding tasks are assigned, first-day logistics are scheduled, and all owners can see their required actions.

recipes.title: post a job opening
recipes.name: post-a-job-opening
recipes.goal: Publish an approved job opening with accurate role details, fair hiring language, and a traceable posting record.

steps.action: **Open the requisition.** Sign in to the recruiting system and select the approved requisition or create one from the approved template.
steps.expect: the role record is visible with the correct hiring manager.

steps.action: **Enter core details.** Add title, department, employment type, location, work arrangement, compensation range if required, and application deadline.
steps.expect: the posting fields match the approved role.

steps.action: **Paste the job description.** Add responsibilities, required qualifications, preferred qualifications, benefits, and EEO statement.
steps.expect: the preview reads clearly and avoids unnecessary exclusionary criteria.

steps.action: **Set application questions.** Add only job-related screening questions and required documents.
steps.expect: applicants are asked for information needed to evaluate the role.

steps.action: **Choose posting channels.** Select internal board, external careers page, and approved paid boards.
steps.expect: each intended channel is checked or scheduled.

steps.action: **Review compliance fields.** Confirm equal opportunity language, pay transparency, location eligibility, and data retention notices.
steps.expect: required compliance fields show complete.

steps.action: **Publish the opening.** Submit the posting for publication after final review.
steps.expect: the system shows a posted, pending, or scheduled status.

steps.action: **Notify stakeholders.** Send the posting link to the hiring manager, recruiter, and approvers.
steps.expect: stakeholders can open the live or scheduled posting.

recipes.verification: The job has a live, pending, or scheduled posting status, the posting link opens correctly, and the requisition record contains approved role details and compliance text.

recipes.title: prioritize a backlog
recipes.name: prioritize-a-backlog
recipes.goal: Prioritize a backlog so the most valuable and time-sensitive work is visible at the top.

steps.action: **Open the backlog.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] open the backlog, project list, Linear backlog, or generic unscheduled work view.
steps.expect: unplanned work items are visible.

steps.action: **Remove obvious noise.** Close duplicates, archive stale items, and flag unclear items for refinement.
steps.expect: the backlog contains active candidates.

steps.action: **Group by outcome.** Cluster items by goal, customer impact, product area, or milestone.
steps.expect: related work can be compared together.

steps.action: **Assess value and urgency.** Consider customer impact, revenue, risk reduction, deadlines, and strategic fit.
steps.expect: each high item has a reason.

steps.action: **Assess effort and dependency.** Note size, blockers, sequencing, and required teams.
steps.expect: priority accounts for feasibility.

steps.action: **Rank the top items.** Move the highest-priority items to the top or assign priority fields.
steps.expect: the top backlog reflects the next likely work.

steps.action: **Document priority rationale.** Add short notes for major choices, tradeoffs, and deferred items.
steps.expect: stakeholders can understand the order.

recipes.verification: The backlog has a clear top set, each top item has a priority reason, and blocked or stale items are marked rather than silently ranked.

recipes.title: process a purchase order
recipes.name: process-a-purchase-order
recipes.goal: Process a purchase order so an approved vendor order is recorded, trackable, and ready to match against receipt and invoice.

steps.action: **Open a new purchase order.** Go to purchases, procurement, or expenses and choose purchase order.
steps.expect: a blank PO form is visible.

steps.action: **Select the vendor.** Choose the vendor and verify contact, payment terms, and delivery details.
steps.expect: the PO is addressed to the correct supplier.

steps.action: **Enter requested items.** Add item descriptions, quantities, unit prices, tax, shipping, project, and delivery date.
steps.expect: the PO total matches the approved request.

steps.action: **Attach approval support.** Link the request, quote, budget approval, or contract.
steps.expect: the PO file shows why the purchase is authorized.

steps.action: **Submit for approval if required.** Route the PO to the approver or mark the approval already received.
steps.expect: the PO status is pending approval or approved.

steps.action: **Send the approved PO to the vendor.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* sending may authorize the vendor to fulfill the order, so confirm vendor, quantities, price, and delivery address first.
steps.expect: the PO status shows sent or issued.

steps.action: **Prepare for matching.** Note how receipts and vendor invoices should be matched to the PO.
steps.expect: the PO remains open for receiving and billing.

recipes.verification: The PO is approved and sent to the correct vendor with matching items, quantities, prices, delivery details, approval support, and open status for receipt or billing.

recipes.title: process an online order
recipes.name: process-an-online-order
recipes.goal: Review an online order and move it to the correct next status for fulfillment, hold, cancellation, or refund.

steps.action: **Open the order.** [BRANCH: Shopify | generic] open the order in Shopify Orders, or search the order number in the order system.
steps.expect: the full order record is visible.

steps.action: **Check payment status.** Confirm paid, authorized, pending, refunded, or failed status.
steps.expect: payment readiness is clear.

steps.action: **Review fraud and risk signals.** Check risk score, billing-shipping mismatch, high-value items, and unusual notes.
steps.expect: the order is safe to fulfill or needs review.

steps.action: **Verify inventory and fulfillment status.** Confirm items are in stock and not already fulfilled.
steps.expect: the order can move forward without duplication.

steps.action: **Check customer and shipping details.** Review address validation, delivery method, and customer messages.
steps.expect: fulfillment has a usable address and instructions.

steps.action: **Choose the next action.** [BRANCH: fulfill | hold | cancel] send to fulfillment, place a review hold, or cancel according to policy.
steps.expect: the order status matches the decision.

steps.action: **Notify the customer if needed.** Send a concise update for holds, address questions, cancellations, or delays.
steps.expect: the customer knows any required next step.

recipes.verification: The order has a documented next status, valid payment decision, usable fulfillment information, and customer communication if action is required.

recipes.title: provision accounts for a new hire
recipes.name: provision-accounts-for-a-new-hire
recipes.goal: Request and confirm the correct system accounts for a new hire before their start date.

steps.action: **Confirm access template.** Match the new hire's role, department, location, and worker type to the approved access profile.
steps.expect: required systems and permission levels are identified.

steps.action: **Create the provisioning request.** Enter employee name, start date, manager, title, email format, and access template in the ticket or IAM system.
steps.expect: the request has a ticket or workflow ID.

steps.action: **Add special access needs.** Include approved exceptions such as admin tools, finance systems, or regulated data access.
steps.expect: exceptions are documented with approver names.

steps.action: **Set activation timing.** Schedule accounts to activate on or just before the start date according to policy.
steps.expect: activation timing is visible in the request.

steps.action: **Notify approvers.** Route manager, system owner, security, or data owner approvals as required.
steps.expect: approval tasks are assigned.

steps.action: **Confirm completion.** Check that email, SSO, core apps, groups, and device enrollment are provisioned.
steps.expect: account status shows active or scheduled.

steps.action: **Share access instructions.** Send first-login guidance through the approved channel.
steps.expect: the new hire or manager has secure onboarding instructions.

recipes.verification: The provisioning ticket lists approved systems, account activation timing, required approvals, and completed or scheduled account status for the correct new hire.

recipes.title: publish a blog post
recipes.name: publish-a-blog-post
recipes.goal: Publish an approved blog post with correct formatting, metadata, links, and visibility.

steps.action: **Create or open the post draft.** Open the CMS and start a new post or edit the approved draft.
steps.expect: the post editor is open.

steps.action: **Add title and body.** Paste approved title, headings, body copy, and calls to action.
steps.expect: the post content is present and structured.

steps.action: **Add media and alt text.** Upload approved images and add descriptive alt text.
steps.expect: images display correctly and are accessible.

steps.action: **Set metadata.** Add slug, excerpt, category, tags, author, featured image, and SEO fields if used.
steps.expect: listing and search previews are complete.

steps.action: **Check links.** Click or preview internal, external, download, and CTA links.
steps.expect: every link opens the intended destination.

steps.action: **Preview the post.** Review desktop and mobile preview for formatting, media, and embedded content.
steps.expect: the post is readable and visually correct.

steps.action: **Publish or schedule.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before publishing, confirm approvals, date, slug, claims, and links because the page may become public and indexed.
steps.expect: the post is live or scheduled.

steps.action: **Record the URL.** Add the final URL to the editorial calendar or campaign tracker.
steps.expect: stakeholders can find the post.

recipes.verification: The post is live or scheduled with approved content, correct URL, metadata, images, alt text, and working links.

recipes.title: qualify a lead
recipes.name: qualify-a-lead
recipes.goal: Assess whether a lead is worth active sales pursuit and record the qualification outcome in the CRM.

steps.action: **Open the lead record.** Review source, company, title, activity, and existing notes.
steps.expect: the available qualification evidence is visible.

steps.action: **Check account fit.** Compare industry, company size, geography, use case, and technology fit against the ideal customer profile.
steps.expect: fit is marked strong, partial, or poor.

steps.action: **Assess buying intent.** Review inquiry type, content viewed, meeting request, reply quality, or stated project.
steps.expect: intent level is clear.

steps.action: **Assess authority and timing.** Identify role, decision influence, urgency, and likely buying window.
steps.expect: the lead has a documented buyer role and timing estimate.

steps.action: **Update qualification fields.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] update Lead Status and rating in Salesforce; update Lifecycle Stage, Lead Status, or fit properties in HubSpot; in another CRM, update qualification status and score fields.
steps.expect: the CRM reflects the qualification decision.

steps.action: **Choose the next action.** Convert, route, nurture, disqualify, or ask for more information.
steps.expect: the lead has a next path, not just a score.

steps.action: **Document the rationale.** Add a short note naming the evidence and any uncertainty.
steps.expect: another rep can audit the decision.

recipes.verification: The lead record has qualification status, fit or score evidence, documented rationale, and a routed, nurtured, disqualified, or research-next action.

recipes.title: reconcile a bank statement
recipes.name: reconcile-a-bank-statement
recipes.goal: Reconcile an accounting account to a bank or credit-card statement so the cleared balance matches the statement ending balance.

steps.action: **Open reconciliation.** Choose the bank, credit-card, or payment account to reconcile.
steps.expect: the reconciliation screen asks for statement details.

steps.action: **Enter statement details.** Add statement ending date, ending balance, and service charges or interest if the tool asks.
steps.expect: the system shows a list of unreconciled transactions.

steps.action: **Mark cleared deposits and credits.** Compare each statement credit to accounting records and mark matches only.
steps.expect: cleared deposits match the statement amounts.

steps.action: **Mark cleared payments and charges.** Compare checks, card charges, fees, withdrawals, and transfers to the statement.
steps.expect: cleared payments match the statement amounts.

steps.action: **Investigate differences.** Review missing transactions, duplicates, reversed signs, timing differences, and bank fees.
steps.expect: the difference moves toward zero for valid records.

steps.action: **Finish the reconciliation.** Complete only when the difference is exactly zero.
steps.expect: the system generates a completed reconciliation or report.

steps.action: **Save the report.** Store the reconciliation report with the statement period.
steps.expect: the reconciled period can be reviewed later.

recipes.verification: The reconciliation difference is zero, the account shows reconciled through the statement ending date, and the saved reconciliation report matches the official statement ending balance.

recipes.title: reconcile a payout report
recipes.name: reconcile-a-payout-report
recipes.goal: Match a payment processor payout report to orders, refunds, fees, and the bank deposit.

steps.action: **Open the payout.** Find the processor payout by date, amount, currency, and bank account.
steps.expect: payout summary and transaction list are visible.

steps.action: **Export transaction detail.** Download orders, refunds, disputes, fees, taxes, and adjustments for the payout.
steps.expect: a detail report is available for reconciliation.

steps.action: **Match gross sales.** Compare order sales in the payout to store order reports for the same period.
steps.expect: sales totals match or differences are listed.

steps.action: **Match deductions.** Compare refunds, chargebacks, processor fees, reserves, and adjustments.
steps.expect: net payout calculation explains deductions.

steps.action: **Match bank deposit.** Compare processor net payout to the bank deposit amount and settlement date.
steps.expect: the bank deposit equals the payout or has a documented timing difference.

steps.action: **Investigate variances.** Drill into missing orders, duplicate refunds, currency conversion, pending settlements, or fees.
steps.expect: every variance has a cause or owner.

steps.action: **Record reconciliation.** Enter the matched totals, variance notes, and supporting report links in accounting records.
steps.expect: the payout is marked reconciled or pending with reasons.

recipes.verification: The payout net amount matches the bank deposit or has documented variances with owners, and supporting reports are attached or linked.

recipes.title: record a customer payment
recipes.name: record-a-customer-payment
recipes.goal: Record a customer payment against the correct invoice so the customer balance and deposits are accurate.

steps.action: **Open receive-payment.** Go to sales, invoices, customers, or payments and choose receive or record payment.
steps.expect: a payment form is visible.

steps.action: **Select the customer.** Choose the paying customer and review open invoices.
steps.expect: the relevant unpaid invoice is listed.

steps.action: **Enter payment details.** Add payment date, amount, method, reference number, and deposit account.
steps.expect: the payment details match the bank, check, card, or gateway record.

steps.action: **Apply to invoice.** Select the invoice or invoices the payment covers and allocate partial amounts if needed.
steps.expect: the applied amount equals the received payment.

steps.action: **Handle overpayment or short payment.** [BRANCH: exact | partial | overpayment] close exact payments, leave partial balance open, or record customer credit for overpayment.
steps.expect: customer balance reflects the remaining amount correctly.

steps.action: **Save the payment.** Save the record without duplicating any payment imported from the bank feed.
steps.expect: the invoice status changes to paid or partially paid.

steps.action: **Match deposit if needed.** Match the saved payment to the bank feed or deposit batch.
steps.expect: the bank transaction links to the payment record.

recipes.verification: The customer payment is linked to the correct invoice, the invoice status and remaining balance are correct, and the payment is matched or ready to match to the deposit account.

recipes.title: record an expense
recipes.name: record-an-expense
recipes.goal: Record a business expense with the correct vendor, amount, category, date, payment method, and receipt so books and reports stay accurate.

steps.action: **Open the expense entry form.** Go to expenses, bills, purchases, or transactions and choose new expense.
steps.expect: a blank expense form is visible.

steps.action: **Enter the vendor and date.** Select or add the vendor and use the transaction or receipt date.
steps.expect: the expense has the correct payee and date.

steps.action: **Enter the payment details.** Add amount, currency, payment account, payment method, and reference number if available.
steps.expect: the total matches the source document.

steps.action: **Choose the category.** Pick the expense account that best matches the business purpose.
steps.expect: the expense will appear in the correct report line.

steps.action: **Attach the receipt.** Upload or link the receipt, bill, or invoice image.
steps.expect: the source document is attached to the record.

steps.action: **Mark billable or reimbursable if needed.** Assign the customer, project, employee, or reimbursement flag.
steps.expect: the expense can be billed or reimbursed later.

steps.action: **Save the expense.** Save the entry and leave it unmatched if a bank feed transaction still needs to be matched.
steps.expect: the expense appears in the expense list or ledger.

recipes.verification: The expense record shows the correct vendor, date, amount, payment account, category, receipt attachment or note, and billable/reimbursable status if applicable.

recipes.title: record and share a meeting
recipes.name: record-and-share-a-meeting
recipes.goal: Record a meeting with consent and share the recording only with the intended audience.

steps.action: **Confirm recording need.** Decide whether recording is necessary or whether notes are enough.
steps.expect: the recording has a clear business purpose.

steps.action: **Check policy and consent rules.** Review company policy and local consent requirements for participants.
steps.expect: you know whether explicit verbal consent is needed.

steps.action: **Tell attendees before recording.** State that you intend to record and why.
steps.expect: attendees have a chance to object or leave.

steps.action: **Start recording.** Use the meeting tool's record button after consent is handled.
steps.expect: the tool shows a recording indicator.

steps.action: **Pause for sensitive segments.** Stop or pause recording before confidential, personal, or off-record discussion.
steps.expect: sensitive content is not captured unnecessarily.

steps.action: **Stop and save.** End recording when the meeting ends or the recordable portion is complete.
steps.expect: the recording is processing or saved.

steps.action: **Set sharing permissions.** Limit access to attendees or the approved group before sending the link.
steps.expect: only intended viewers can open it.

steps.action: **Share the link with context.** Send the recording link with notes, action items, and any retention expectations.
steps.expect: recipients can find the useful part and know how long it remains available.

recipes.verification: The recording link opens for intended viewers only, and attendees were notified before recording began.

recipes.title: reject a candidate gracefully
recipes.name: reject-a-candidate-gracefully
recipes.goal: Send a respectful candidate rejection and update the recruiting record with an appropriate status.

steps.action: **Open the candidate record.** Confirm candidate name, role, stage, email, and decision status.
steps.expect: the correct candidate and requisition are visible.

steps.action: **Confirm disposition reason.** Select the approved job-related reason or category in the ATS.
steps.expect: the record has a compliant disposition.

steps.action: **Choose the rejection template.** Use the appropriate template for application, post-screen, post-interview, or final-stage rejection.
steps.expect: the message tone matches the candidate stage.

steps.action: **Personalize carefully.** Add a brief thank-you or role reference without giving unsupported feedback or promises.
steps.expect: the message is respectful and accurate.

steps.action: **Send the rejection.** Send the message through the ATS or approved recruiting channel.
steps.expect: the communication is marked sent.

steps.action: **Update candidate status.** Move the candidate to rejected, archived, or talent pool status as appropriate.
steps.expect: the workflow no longer shows the candidate as active.

steps.action: **Log follow-up limits.** Record any referral, reapply timing, or talent community note if approved.
steps.expect: future recruiters can see the intended next step.

recipes.verification: The ATS shows the candidate rejected or archived with an approved disposition reason, sent communication, and no remaining active interviews.

recipes.title: request a customer referral
recipes.name: request-a-customer-referral
recipes.goal: Ask a satisfied customer for a referral in a respectful, specific, and compliant way.

steps.action: **Confirm customer readiness.** Review health score, recent support issues, renewal risk, stakeholder sentiment, and value achieved.
steps.expect: the customer is an appropriate referral candidate.

steps.action: **Coordinate internally.** Check with account owner, customer success manager, or partner owner before asking.
steps.expect: the request will not conflict with account strategy.

steps.action: **Choose the referral ask.** Decide whether to request an introduction, named account referral, testimonial path, or permission to mention your company internally.
steps.expect: the ask is specific and low-friction.

steps.action: **Draft the message.** Thank the customer, name the outcome, make one specific ask, and offer a simple way to decline.
steps.expect: the message is respectful and clear.

steps.action: **Review incentives and compliance.** Confirm whether referral rewards, disclosures, or procurement restrictions apply.
steps.expect: the request follows policy.

steps.action: **Send through an approved channel.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] send and log email from Salesforce; send and log email from HubSpot; in another CRM, send through the approved email or task workflow.
steps.expect: the request is sent or logged on the account.

steps.action: **Track the response.** Create a task or campaign status to follow up, thank, or close the loop.
steps.expect: the referral request has a visible status.

recipes.verification: The CRM account shows a sent or scheduled referral request with internal alignment, specific ask, compliance review, and follow-up status.

recipes.title: request a status update
recipes.name: request-a-status-update
recipes.goal: Request a status update that gets a useful answer without creating unnecessary interruption or ambiguity.

steps.action: **Check existing status.** Open the tracker, ticket, document, or channel where updates are normally posted.
steps.expect: you know what information is already available.

steps.action: **Choose the recipient.** Identify the person responsible for the next update or decision.
steps.expect: the request goes to the right owner.

steps.action: **Write a specific ask.** State the item, what status you need, and why you need it.
steps.expect: the recipient understands the requested information.

steps.action: **Include a response deadline.** Name when the update is needed and whether a short answer is acceptable.
steps.expect: urgency is clear.

steps.action: **Send in the right channel.** Use the task comment, ticket note, email, or team chat where the work is tracked.
steps.expect: the request is visible in the work context.

steps.action: **Record any reply.** Update the tracker or document if the answer arrives outside the system of record.
steps.expect: the status is captured for others.

recipes.verification: The status request names the work item, specific information needed, deadline, recipient, and location where the answer will be recorded.

recipes.title: respond to a customer review
recipes.name: respond-to-a-customer-review
recipes.goal: Post a professional response to a customer review without exposing private customer information.

steps.action: **Read the full review.** Note rating, issue, date, product or location, and tone.
steps.expect: the customer's main point is clear.

steps.action: **Check internal context.** Look up the order or visit only if policy allows and access is needed.
steps.expect: you know whether a specific recovery path exists.

steps.action: **Choose response type.** [BRANCH: positive | negative | inaccurate] thank, apologize and route to support, or correct facts briefly.
steps.expect: the response matches the review.

steps.action: **Draft a public reply.** Keep it short, respectful, and free of private account or order details.
steps.expect: the reply can stand in public.

steps.action: **Offer a support path.** For unresolved issues, invite the customer to contact an official support channel.
steps.expect: the customer has a next step outside the public thread.

steps.action: **Post the response.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before posting, confirm tone, facts, and privacy because public replies may be screenshotted or indexed.
steps.expect: the reply appears under the review.

steps.action: **Log follow-up if needed.** Create a support task for issues that require internal action.
steps.expect: public response and private resolution are connected.

recipes.verification: The public response is posted, addresses the review's main point, contains no private data, and routes unresolved issues to an official support channel.

recipes.title: run a background check
recipes.name: run-a-background-check
recipes.goal: Initiate an authorized background check for a candidate or employee and track it through compliant completion.

steps.action: **Confirm eligibility.** Verify role, jurisdiction, timing, and check package are appropriate.
steps.expect: the check type matches the role and location.

steps.action: **Confirm authorization.** Check that required consent, disclosure, and identity information are complete.
steps.expect: the record shows authorization before ordering.

steps.action: **Open the vendor workflow.** Select the candidate or employee and the approved background package.
steps.expect: the vendor form displays the correct person and package.

steps.action: **Review submitted data.** Confirm legal name, email, location, and required identifiers are correct.
steps.expect: the order data has no obvious mismatch.

steps.action: **Submit the order.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm consent and package before submission because the vendor may begin processing immediately.
steps.expect: the vendor shows the check as ordered or in progress.

steps.action: **Monitor status.** Track pending items, candidate action requests, and estimated completion.
steps.expect: blockers are visible.

steps.action: **Record completion.** Save pass, review, or adjudication-needed status according to policy without copying unnecessary report details.
steps.expect: the HR or ATS record reflects the outcome.

recipes.verification: The vendor shows the check ordered with valid authorization, current status is tracked, and the HR or ATS record contains only the necessary outcome.

recipes.title: run a daily standup
recipes.name: run-a-daily-standup
recipes.goal: Run a short daily standup that surfaces progress, priorities, and blockers without turning into a full planning meeting.

steps.action: **Open the work board.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] open the sprint board, project list, Linear team view, or generic task board.
steps.expect: current work is visible.

steps.action: **Start on time.** State the focus: yesterday or last update, today's priority, and blockers.
steps.expect: participants know the format.

steps.action: **Go person by person or work item by work item.** Ask for brief updates and keep discussion to facts.
steps.expect: progress and plans are heard quickly.

steps.action: **Capture blockers.** Record each blocker with an owner and follow-up action.
steps.expect: blockers do not disappear after the meeting.

steps.action: **Park deep discussions.** Move detailed design, debugging, or planning topics to follow-up conversations.
steps.expect: the standup stays within the timebox.

steps.action: **Confirm next actions.** Repeat owners for blockers, handoffs, and urgent tasks.
steps.expect: everyone knows what happens after standup.

steps.action: **Update the board.** Move tasks, adjust owners, or add notes discovered during standup.
steps.expect: the tracker matches the team's current state.

recipes.verification: After the standup, the board reflects current work and every blocker has an owner, next action, and follow-up path.

recipes.title: run payroll
recipes.name: run-payroll
recipes.goal: Process a scheduled payroll run accurately so employees are paid and required records are updated.

steps.action: **Open the payroll run.** Select the correct company, pay group, pay period, and pay date.
steps.expect: the payroll batch matches the scheduled run.

steps.action: **Import approved inputs.** Pull approved time, PTO, commissions, bonuses, deductions, reimbursements, and employee changes.
steps.expect: payroll inputs load without unresolved errors.

steps.action: **Review exceptions.** Check missing timecards, negative net pay, unusual hours, bank changes, tax errors, and terminated employees.
steps.expect: exceptions are listed and assigned for resolution.

steps.action: **Correct approved issues.** Make only documented corrections or send unresolved items to the proper owner.
steps.expect: the batch has no blocking errors.

steps.action: **Preview payroll.** Generate gross-to-net, tax, deduction, employer cost, and variance reports.
steps.expect: totals are available for review.

steps.action: **Obtain approval.** Route the preview to the payroll approver or finance reviewer.
steps.expect: approval is recorded.

steps.action: **Submit payroll.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm pay date, bank funding, employee count, and approval before submission because funds and filings may initiate.
steps.expect: the system shows payroll submitted or processing.

steps.action: **Save reports.** Store required payroll reports and confirmation numbers in the approved location.
steps.expect: audit records are complete.

recipes.verification: Payroll status is submitted or processed for the correct pay period, approval is recorded, confirmation numbers exist, and payroll reports are saved.

recipes.title: schedule a meeting across time zones
recipes.name: schedule-a-meeting-across-time-zones
recipes.goal: Find and propose a meeting time that works for participants in different time zones.

steps.action: **List participant zones.** Record each attendee's city or time zone and normal working hours.
steps.expect: every required attendee has a time zone and availability window.

steps.action: **Set the meeting length.** Choose the shortest duration that can achieve the meeting purpose.
steps.expect: the calendar search uses a specific duration.

steps.action: **Compare overlapping hours.** Use a calendar availability view or world-clock planner to find times inside shared working hours.
steps.expect: at least one candidate slot is visible, or the conflict is clear.

steps.action: **Check calendar conflicts.** Review required attendees' free/busy calendars for the candidate slots.
steps.expect: the best slot has no required-attendee conflicts.

steps.action: **Prefer fair inconvenience.** If no slot fits everyone cleanly, rotate the burden away from the same person or region.
steps.expect: the chosen slot is defensible and not repeatedly unfair.

steps.action: **Send the proposed time with zones.** Include the time in your zone plus the main attendee zones or use the calendar tool's timezone conversion.
steps.expect: attendees can see the meeting time in their local calendar.

steps.action: **Hold alternatives briefly.** If approval is needed, mention one backup option and set a response deadline.
steps.expect: people know when the time will be finalized.

recipes.verification: The selected slot appears on required attendees' calendars at the intended local time and does not conflict with known required-attendee events.

recipes.title: schedule a one on one
recipes.name: schedule-a-one-on-one
recipes.goal: Schedule a one-on-one meeting with the right participant, cadence, agenda space, and calendar details.

steps.action: **Check availability.** Compare calendars for both participants and select a workable time.
steps.expect: an open time slot is identified.

steps.action: **Create the event.** Add the participant, title, date, time, duration, and recurrence if needed.
steps.expect: the calendar invite draft has the correct basics.

steps.action: **Add location or link.** Include a room, video link, phone number, or office location.
steps.expect: attendees know how to join.

steps.action: **Add agenda space.** Include a shared agenda document or brief description of topics to maintain.
steps.expect: both participants have a place to add topics.

steps.action: **Set visibility.** Use appropriate privacy settings if the meeting may include personnel, performance, or health topics.
steps.expect: calendar details are visible only as intended.

steps.action: **Send the invite.** Send the calendar invitation to the participant.
steps.expect: the invite appears on both calendars or awaits response.

steps.action: **Confirm acceptance.** Check the attendee response or follow up if needed.
steps.expect: attendance is accepted, tentative, or clearly pending.

recipes.verification: The calendar shows the one-on-one with correct participant, time, recurrence if needed, join details, and appropriate visibility.

recipes.title: schedule a sales follow up
recipes.name: schedule-a-sales-follow-up
recipes.goal: Schedule a timely follow-up after a sales interaction and record it where the owner will act on it.

steps.action: **Open the CRM record.** Find the relevant lead, contact, account, or deal.
steps.expect: the record and recent activity are visible.

steps.action: **Choose the follow-up type.** Select task, email, call, meeting, or sequence based on what was agreed.
steps.expect: the action matches the buyer expectation.

steps.action: **Set owner and due time.** Assign the responsible rep and choose a due date or meeting slot.
steps.expect: the follow-up has an accountable owner and deadline.

steps.action: **Write the action detail.** Add a short subject and notes that explain what to say or send.
steps.expect: the owner can execute without reopening all prior context.

steps.action: **Use the right tool path.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] create a Task or Event in Salesforce; create a Task, Meeting, or Sequence step in HubSpot; in another CRM, create the equivalent reminder or activity.
steps.expect: the follow-up appears in the CRM task or calendar view.

steps.action: **Send or save as appropriate.** If sending an email now, review and send; if scheduling future outreach, save the task.
steps.expect: the CRM shows either sent outreach or a pending follow-up.

recipes.verification: The CRM record shows a pending or sent follow-up with owner, due date, channel, and clear action detail.

recipes.title: schedule a social media post
recipes.name: schedule-a-social-media-post
recipes.goal: Schedule an approved social media post to publish at the intended time and channel.

steps.action: **Open the scheduler.** Select the correct brand account and channel.
steps.expect: the composer is tied to the intended account.

steps.action: **Add copy and media.** Paste approved text, upload images or video, and add alt text where supported.
steps.expect: the preview matches the approved post.

steps.action: **Check links and tags.** Verify URLs, UTM parameters, mentions, hashtags, and product tags.
steps.expect: links open correctly and tags point to the right accounts.

steps.action: **Set publish time.** Choose the date, time, and time zone.
steps.expect: the scheduled time displays correctly.

steps.action: **Review platform preview.** Check cropping, character limits, thumbnails, and link cards.
steps.expect: the post is readable and visually intact.

steps.action: **Schedule the post.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before scheduling, confirm account, time, copy, and media because the post may publish automatically.
steps.expect: the post appears in the scheduled queue.

steps.action: **Record the schedule.** Add the post to the campaign calendar or tracker.
steps.expect: stakeholders can see when it will publish.

recipes.verification: The post is in the scheduled queue for the correct account, channel, date, time zone, copy, media, and link.

recipes.title: schedule an interview panel
recipes.name: schedule-an-interview-panel
recipes.goal: Coordinate an interview panel with the right interviewers, times, format, and evaluation coverage.

steps.action: **Confirm interview plan.** Verify panel members, interview focus areas, duration, format, and target date range.
steps.expect: the interview loop has clear coverage and owners.

steps.action: **Check interviewer availability.** Compare calendars or scheduling links for the panel and recruiter.
steps.expect: at least one workable time block is identified.

steps.action: **Check candidate availability.** Use existing availability or request time windows from the candidate.
steps.expect: candidate availability overlaps with panel availability.

steps.action: **Reserve rooms or meeting links.** Book physical rooms, video links, or phone bridges for each segment.
steps.expect: every interview segment has a location or link.

steps.action: **Create calendar holds.** Add events with candidate name, role, interview focus, resume link if appropriate, and feedback deadline.
steps.expect: interviewers receive calendar invitations.

steps.action: **Update the ATS.** Record the interview schedule, panel assignments, and candidate status.
steps.expect: recruiting records match the calendar.

steps.action: **Send internal prep.** Share rubric, interview plan, and candidate materials with interviewers.
steps.expect: interviewers know what they are evaluating.

recipes.verification: All interviewers and the candidate have matching calendar invitations, the ATS shows the scheduled panel, and each segment has an assigned evaluation area.

recipes.title: screen a resume
recipes.name: screen-a-resume
recipes.goal: Evaluate one candidate resume against job-related criteria and record a fair, consistent screening decision.

steps.action: **Open the candidate record.** Review the resume, application answers, and source in the applicant tracking system.
steps.expect: the candidate materials are visible in one record.

steps.action: **Check minimum qualifications.** Compare education, certifications, experience, location, and work authorization only where job-related and lawful.
steps.expect: each required criterion is marked met, not met, or unclear.

steps.action: **Assess relevant experience.** Look for evidence of responsibilities, tools, scope, outcomes, and progression that match the role.
steps.expect: the resume has a concise job-related evidence summary.

steps.action: **Ignore protected traits.** Do not use age, race, gender, disability, family status, national origin, religion, or other protected characteristics.
steps.expect: notes avoid protected-class assumptions.

steps.action: **Apply the rubric.** Score or categorize the candidate using the same rubric used for comparable applicants.
steps.expect: the decision is tied to documented criteria.

steps.action: **Choose the next status.** [BRANCH: advance | hold | reject] move qualified candidates forward, hold unclear cases for recruiter review, and reject clear nonmatches.
steps.expect: the candidate has the correct workflow status.

steps.action: **Write neutral notes.** Record factual reasons such as "missing required certification" or "matches required payroll experience."
steps.expect: another reviewer can understand the decision.

recipes.verification: The candidate record has a documented screen result, rubric-based notes, and no selection rationale based on protected traits or non-job-related assumptions.

recipes.title: send a calendar invite
recipes.name: send-a-calendar-invite
recipes.goal: Create and send a calendar invite with the correct attendees, time, location, and meeting context.
