steps.action: **Open a new event.** Start a calendar event on the intended calendar, not a personal or test calendar.
steps.expect: a blank event editor is open.

steps.action: **Enter the title.** Use a specific title that identifies the topic or decision.
steps.expect: the event is recognizable on a busy calendar.

steps.action: **Set date and time.** Enter the confirmed start, end, and time zone.
steps.expect: the event duration matches the planned meeting.

steps.action: **Add attendees.** Add required participants and mark optional attendees if the tool supports it.
steps.expect: the invitee list contains the intended people only.

steps.action: **Add location or link.** [BRANCH: virtual | in-person | hybrid] add video link, room, or both as appropriate.
steps.expect: attendees know where to join.

steps.action: **Write the description.** Include the agenda, preparation links, and owner for follow-up.
steps.expect: attendees understand why they are invited.

steps.action: **Check notifications.** Confirm default reminders are suitable and avoid noisy extra reminders.
steps.expect: reminders are present but not excessive.

steps.action: **Send the invite.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before sending, confirm attendees, time zone, and external recipients because invitations may notify everyone immediately.
steps.expect: the calendar event shows as sent or saved with guests.

recipes.verification: The event appears on the intended calendar with the correct attendees, time, location or join link, and description.

recipes.title: send a customer satisfaction survey
recipes.name: send-a-customer-satisfaction-survey
recipes.goal: Send a customer satisfaction survey to an appropriate customer group and collect responses.

steps.action: **Open the survey tool.** Create a new survey or open the approved survey template.
steps.expect: survey questions are editable or ready.

steps.action: **Confirm questions.** Check rating scales, required fields, free-text prompts, and thank-you page.
steps.expect: the survey asks only necessary questions.

steps.action: **Set audience.** Upload or select the approved customer segment and suppress unsubscribed or ineligible contacts where required.
steps.expect: recipient count matches the plan.

steps.action: **Write the invitation.** Add clear purpose, estimated completion time, privacy note, and survey link.
steps.expect: customers know what they are being asked to do.

steps.action: **Test the survey.** Submit a test response and verify routing, scoring, and confirmation.
steps.expect: the response appears in results.

steps.action: **Send or schedule.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before sending, confirm audience, consent basis, survey link, and privacy language because customer messages cannot be recalled reliably.
steps.expect: the survey invitation is sent or scheduled.

steps.action: **Monitor responses.** Check delivery, bounce, response count, and any urgent negative feedback.
steps.expect: responses are being collected and routed.

recipes.verification: The approved survey invitation is sent or scheduled to the intended eligible audience, and a test response appears in the results.

recipes.title: send a job offer letter
recipes.name: send-a-job-offer-letter
recipes.goal: Send an approved job offer letter to the selected candidate with accurate terms and acceptance instructions.

steps.action: **Open the candidate record.** Confirm candidate identity, role, requisition, and offer approval status.
steps.expect: the offer workflow is ready for drafting.

steps.action: **Enter offer terms.** Add title, salary or hourly rate, bonus or equity if applicable, benefits summary, location, start date, reporting manager, and employment status.
steps.expect: the offer fields match approvals.

steps.action: **Add contingencies.** Include background check, work authorization, reference, drug screen, or credential requirements only if approved and lawful.
steps.expect: contingencies are visible in the letter.

steps.action: **Review legal language.** Confirm at-will or local employment terms, expiration date, confidentiality, and signature requirements.
steps.expect: the letter uses the current approved template.

steps.action: **Get final approval.** Route the offer for recruiter, compensation, HR, finance, or legal approval as required.
steps.expect: all required approvals show complete.

steps.action: **Send the offer.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm recipient, terms, and approvals before sending because the candidate may rely on the written offer.
steps.expect: the offer is sent to the candidate.

steps.action: **Log the deadline.** Record the response deadline and follow-up task in the ATS.
steps.expect: the recruiting team can track acceptance status.

recipes.verification: The candidate record shows an offer sent to the correct candidate, with approved terms, required contingencies, expiration date, and a follow-up task.

recipes.title: send a payment reminder
recipes.name: send-a-payment-reminder
recipes.goal: Send a polite payment reminder for an unpaid invoice while preserving the customer relationship and keeping a record in the billing system.

steps.action: **Open the unpaid invoice.** Find the invoice by customer, invoice number, or unpaid status.
steps.expect: the invoice detail page shows an open balance.

steps.action: **Check the payment status.** Confirm no payment, credit, refund, or dispute is pending.
steps.expect: the amount due is still accurate.

steps.action: **Review the contact.** Confirm the reminder will go to the billing contact or accounts-payable address.
steps.expect: the recipient is the person responsible for payment.

steps.action: **Choose a reminder template.** Use a short message that names the invoice number, amount, due date, and payment link.
steps.expect: the reminder text is specific and professional.

steps.action: **Send the reminder.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* sending contacts the customer, so confirm amount, recipient, and tone before clicking send.
steps.expect: the system records the reminder as sent.

steps.action: **Schedule the next follow-up.** Add a reminder, task, or note for the next follow-up date if payment does not arrive.
steps.expect: there is a visible follow-up plan.

recipes.verification: The invoice activity log shows a reminder sent to the correct billing contact for the current open balance, and a next follow-up date exists if payment remains unpaid.

recipes.title: send a price quote
recipes.name: send-a-price-quote
recipes.goal: Send a clear price quote that tells a prospective customer what is included, what it costs, and how long the offer is valid.

steps.action: **Open a new quote or estimate.** Go to quotes, estimates, sales, or proposals and create a new record.
steps.expect: a blank quote form is visible.

steps.action: **Select the customer.** Choose or add the customer and quote recipient.
steps.expect: the quote is addressed to the correct person or business.

steps.action: **Define the scope.** Add concise descriptions of products, services, deliverables, exclusions, and assumptions.
steps.expect: the customer can see what is and is not included.

steps.action: **Enter pricing.** Add quantities, rates, discounts, tax treatment, shipping, deposits, and payment terms.
steps.expect: the quoted total matches your intended offer.

steps.action: **Set validity and next step.** Add expiration date, acceptance instructions, and whether approval converts to an invoice.
steps.expect: the customer knows how and when to accept.

steps.action: **Preview the quote.** Review customer, scope, totals, dates, and terms.
steps.expect: no draft notes or internal-only fields are visible.

steps.action: **Send the quote.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* sending may create a commercial offer, so confirm pricing, scope, and recipient first.
steps.expect: the system records the quote as sent.

recipes.verification: The quote is marked sent with the correct customer, scope, exclusions, pricing, tax, expiration date, and acceptance instructions.

recipes.title: send a quote for approval
recipes.name: send-a-quote-for-approval
recipes.goal: Submit a sales quote for internal approval with complete pricing, discount, customer, and deal context.

steps.action: **Open the quote.** Navigate from the deal to the quote, CPQ record, or quoting tool.
steps.expect: quote lines and approval controls are visible.

steps.action: **Validate quote details.** Check account, billing entity, products, quantities, currency, term dates, taxes, and expiration date.
steps.expect: commercial fields match the intended offer.

steps.action: **Check pricing policy.** Compare discount, margin, payment terms, and nonstandard terms against approval rules.
steps.expect: approval requirement is clear.

steps.action: **Add approval context.** Write the business case, competitor context, customer deadline, discount rationale, and any legal or finance notes.
steps.expect: approvers have enough context to decide.

steps.action: **Submit for approval.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] use Submit for Approval in Salesforce or CPQ; use HubSpot quote approval workflow if enabled; in another CRM, start the configured approval workflow.
steps.expect: quote status changes to pending approval.

steps.action: **Notify the deal team.** Mention or message the owner, manager, or deal desk if separate notification is expected.
steps.expect: relevant internal owners know the quote is pending.

steps.action: **Track approval status.** Review workflow status and respond to approver questions.
steps.expect: the quote has a visible pending, approved, or rejected state.

recipes.verification: The quote is in pending, approved, or rejected approval status with complete quote details, rationale, and approver trail.

recipes.title: send an employee survey
recipes.name: send-an-employee-survey
recipes.goal: Send an employee survey with the correct audience, questions, anonymity settings, and response deadline.

steps.action: **Create the survey draft.** Add title, introduction, questions, response scale, and estimated completion time.
steps.expect: the survey content is visible in draft mode.

steps.action: **Set privacy options.** Configure anonymous or confidential settings, reporting thresholds, and data access permissions.
steps.expect: privacy settings match the approved plan.

steps.action: **Upload the audience.** Select employees by department, location, tenure, or other approved filters.
steps.expect: recipient count matches the target population.

steps.action: **Preview the survey.** Test the employee view, mobile layout, branching, and required questions.
steps.expect: the survey can be completed without errors.

steps.action: **Schedule communications.** Add launch message, deadline, reminders, and support contact.
steps.expect: communications are queued with correct dates.

steps.action: **Send the survey.** Release the survey to the selected audience.
steps.expect: the survey tool shows sent or active status.

steps.action: **Monitor response rate.** Track responses without identifying individuals beyond approved reporting rules.
steps.expect: aggregate participation is visible.

recipes.verification: The survey is active for the approved audience, privacy settings match the communication, and response reporting follows the defined threshold.

recipes.title: send an interview invite
recipes.name: send-an-interview-invite
recipes.goal: Send a candidate a clear interview invitation with time, format, preparation details, and contact information.

steps.action: **Open the candidate record.** Confirm candidate name, email address, role, and interview stage.
steps.expect: the invite will go to the correct person.

steps.action: **Select the invite template.** Use the approved interview invitation template for the stage and format.
steps.expect: the message includes standard recruiting language.

steps.action: **Add schedule details.** Insert date, time zone, duration, interviewer names, meeting link or location, and check-in instructions.
steps.expect: the candidate can tell when and where to attend.

steps.action: **Add preparation guidance.** Include agenda, materials to bring, portfolio expectations, or assessment instructions if applicable.
steps.expect: the candidate knows how to prepare.

steps.action: **Include support contact.** Provide recruiter contact details and accommodation request language.
steps.expect: the candidate has a path for questions or access needs.

steps.action: **Send the invitation.** Send the email or ATS message and attach the calendar invite if supported.
steps.expect: the message is marked sent.

steps.action: **Record the communication.** Confirm the invite appears in the ATS activity log.
steps.expect: the recruiting record shows the invitation timestamp.

recipes.verification: The candidate received an invitation with correct date, time zone, format, location or link, preparation notes, and recruiter contact information.

recipes.title: set a deal reminder
recipes.name: set-a-deal-reminder
recipes.goal: Create a reminder on a deal so the responsible person follows up before momentum is lost.

steps.action: **Open the deal.** Search for the deal by name, account, or owner.
steps.expect: the deal record and activity controls are visible.

steps.action: **Choose reminder timing.** Pick a due date based on buyer commitment, close date, or internal review cadence.
steps.expect: the reminder timing supports the next sales action.

steps.action: **Create the task.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] create a Task in Salesforce; create a Task in HubSpot; in another CRM, add the equivalent reminder or activity.
steps.expect: a task editor opens.

steps.action: **Enter task details.** Add owner, due date, subject, priority, and a short instruction.
steps.expect: the task clearly states what to do.

steps.action: **Associate the task to the deal.** Link the task to the opportunity, company, contact, or related account as supported.
steps.expect: the reminder appears on the deal timeline.

steps.action: **Save the reminder.** Save and confirm it appears in the owner's task list.
steps.expect: the owner can see the pending task.

recipes.verification: The deal timeline and owner's task list show a pending reminder with due date, owner, subject, and action detail.

recipes.title: set a meeting agenda
recipes.name: set-a-meeting-agenda
recipes.goal: Create a focused meeting agenda that makes the purpose, topics, owners, and desired outcomes clear.

steps.action: **Define the outcome.** Write the decision, alignment, review, or handoff the meeting must produce.
steps.expect: the meeting has a clear end state.

steps.action: **List topics.** Add only topics that need discussion with this group.
steps.expect: the agenda excludes items that can be handled asynchronously.

steps.action: **Assign topic owners.** Name the person leading each topic or decision.
steps.expect: no agenda item is ownerless.

steps.action: **Estimate timing.** Allocate minutes to each topic and leave time for wrap-up.
steps.expect: the agenda fits the meeting length.

steps.action: **Add preparation links.** Include pre-reads, documents, dashboards, or decisions needed before the meeting.
steps.expect: attendees know what to review.

steps.action: **Place the agenda where attendees will see it.** Add it to the calendar invite or link a shared document.
steps.expect: the agenda is visible before the meeting starts.

steps.action: **Confirm with key owners.** Ask topic owners to verify their item and timing.
steps.expect: owners are prepared to lead their sections.

recipes.verification: The invite or shared document contains the outcome, agenda items, owners, timing, and preparation links before the meeting.

recipes.title: set a project milestone
recipes.name: set-a-project-milestone
recipes.goal: Create or update a project milestone so a major delivery point has a name, target date, and linked scope.

steps.action: **Open the project plan.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] open Versions or Releases in Jira, Milestones or Goals in Asana, Project milestones in Linear, or the project roadmap in a generic tracker.
steps.expect: milestone or release controls are visible.

steps.action: **Create the milestone.** Choose New milestone, Add release, or similar.
steps.expect: a milestone form opens.

steps.action: **Enter milestone details.** Add the name, target date, owner, and short outcome statement.
steps.expect: the milestone describes a concrete delivery point.

steps.action: **Link relevant work.** Attach tasks, issues, epics, or sections that make up the milestone scope.
steps.expect: the milestone shows related work items.

steps.action: **Save the milestone.** Commit the milestone or release record.
steps.expect: the milestone appears on the project timeline, roadmap, or milestone list.

steps.action: **Share the update.** Post a brief note in the project channel or tracker comments.
steps.expect: stakeholders know the milestone exists and what it covers.

recipes.verification: The project shows a milestone with a name, target date, owner or responsible team, and linked work items.

recipes.title: set a task due date
recipes.name: set-a-task-due-date
recipes.goal: Set a due date on a task so the owner and stakeholders know when the work is expected.

steps.action: **Open the task.** Go to the relevant task, issue, or card.
steps.expect: the task detail view is visible.

steps.action: **Find the date field.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] use Due date, Target date, Cycle date, or a custom date field depending on the tracker.
steps.expect: a calendar picker or date input is visible.

steps.action: **Select the due date.** Enter the approved date and time if the tool supports time.
steps.expect: the chosen date appears on the task.

steps.action: **Check related schedule fields.** Confirm sprint, milestone, dependency, or reminder fields do not contradict the due date.
steps.expect: scheduling fields are consistent.

steps.action: **Save and comment if needed.** Save the task and add a short note when the date changed materially.
steps.expect: the task activity shows the updated due date.

recipes.verification: The task displays the intended due date in its detail view and activity history.

recipes.title: set up a lead scoring rule
recipes.name: set-up-a-lead-scoring-rule
recipes.goal: Create or update a lead scoring rule that helps prioritize leads using clear fit and intent signals.

steps.action: **Open scoring settings.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] open scoring automation or Einstein/lead score configuration in Salesforce; open Score properties or lead scoring in HubSpot; in another CRM, open scoring or workflow rules.
steps.expect: scoring rules can be viewed or edited.

steps.action: **Define positive fit signals.** Add points for approved attributes such as target industry, company size, role, territory, and product fit.
steps.expect: good-fit leads receive fit points.

steps.action: **Define intent signals.** Add points for approved behaviors such as demo request, pricing-page visit, event attendance, reply, or high-value form submission.
steps.expect: active interest raises the score.

steps.action: **Define negative signals.** Subtract points for student, vendor, competitor, bad email, out-of-market geography, or low-fit company.
steps.expect: poor-fit leads are deprioritized.

steps.action: **Set thresholds and actions.** Define MQL, sales-ready, nurture, or disqualify thresholds and any routing workflow.
steps.expect: score changes map to an operational action.

steps.action: **Test with sample records.** Apply the rule to known good, weak, and bad leads.
steps.expect: sample scores match sales judgment.

steps.action: **Publish the rule.** Save or activate the rule after review by sales and marketing owners.
steps.expect: new or updated scores calculate in the CRM.

steps.action: **Monitor early results.** Review routed leads and false positives after initial use.
steps.expect: scoring quality can be adjusted with evidence.

recipes.verification: The active scoring rule applies documented positive, negative, and threshold logic, and sample records score according to agreed sales and marketing expectations.

recipes.title: set up a performance review cycle
recipes.name: set-up-a-performance-review-cycle
recipes.goal: Launch a performance review cycle with the correct participants, timeline, forms, and calibration steps.

steps.action: **Create the cycle.** Enter cycle name, review period, launch date, due dates, and eligible employee population.
steps.expect: the draft cycle appears in the performance system.

steps.action: **Select review forms.** Attach self-review, manager review, peer review, goals, or competency forms as approved.
steps.expect: each participant type has the correct form.

steps.action: **Configure workflow.** Set routing for employee, manager, second-level manager, HR, and calibration if applicable.
steps.expect: the process order is visible.

steps.action: **Check participant list.** Review inclusions, exclusions, recent hires, leaves, transfers, and terminated employees.
steps.expect: the roster matches eligibility rules.

steps.action: **Add communications.** Prepare launch, reminder, and deadline messages with links and support contacts.
steps.expect: scheduled messages are ready.

steps.action: **Test the cycle.** Preview the employee and manager experience using a test or admin view.
steps.expect: forms, deadlines, and routing work as intended.

steps.action: **Launch the cycle.** Start the review cycle after confirming configuration and roster.
steps.expect: participants receive tasks or notifications.

recipes.verification: The review cycle is launched with the approved roster, forms, due dates, routing, and participant notifications.

recipes.title: set up a recurring task
recipes.name: set-up-a-recurring-task
recipes.goal: Set up a recurring task so repeated operational work is created or reminded on a predictable schedule.

steps.action: **Open task creation.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] create a task, issue, cycle item, or recurring template depending on the tracker.
steps.expect: a task form is visible.

steps.action: **Define the task.** Add a clear title, description, owner, checklist, and acceptance criteria.
steps.expect: each occurrence will be understandable.

steps.action: **Set the first due date.** Choose when the first occurrence should be completed.
steps.expect: the first deadline appears on the task.

steps.action: **Configure recurrence.** Set the repeat interval, weekdays, monthly rule, or custom schedule.
steps.expect: the task shows a recurrence rule or automation.

steps.action: **Choose completion behavior.** Confirm whether the next occurrence appears after completion, on a fixed schedule, or as separate future tasks.
steps.expect: future task behavior is predictable.

steps.action: **Save and test visibility.** Save the task and check the calendar, board, or upcoming view.
steps.expect: the recurring task or next instance is visible.

recipes.verification: The task shows the correct owner, due date, recurrence rule, and expected next occurrence or upcoming reminder.

recipes.title: set up a sales tax rate
recipes.name: set-up-a-sales-tax-rate
recipes.goal: Set up a sales tax rate so taxable sales calculate the correct tax for a jurisdiction, item type, and effective date.

steps.action: **Open tax settings.** Go to taxes, sales tax, VAT, or rates in the accounting system.
steps.expect: existing tax agencies or rates are visible.

steps.action: **Confirm jurisdiction and agency.** Identify the country, state, province, city, county, or tax agency receiving the tax.
steps.expect: the rate will be tied to the correct authority.

steps.action: **Create or update the rate.** Enter the rate name, percentage, agency, effective date, and filing frequency if required.
steps.expect: the rate appears in the tax-rate list.

steps.action: **Assign taxability rules.** Link the rate to taxable products, services, customer locations, or item codes as the system supports.
steps.expect: taxable sales can use the rate automatically or by selection.

steps.action: **Test on a draft invoice.** Create a draft sale with a taxable item and customer address in the jurisdiction.
steps.expect: calculated tax equals the expected rate times taxable amount.

steps.action: **Save tax setup notes.** Record source, effective date, registration number, and who verified the rate.
steps.expect: the tax setup has audit support.

recipes.verification: A draft invoice for a taxable item in the jurisdiction calculates the expected tax, and tax settings show the correct agency, rate, effective date, and taxability rules.

recipes.title: set up an abandoned cart email
recipes.name: set-up-an-abandoned-cart-email
recipes.goal: Set up an abandoned cart email that reminds eligible shoppers to complete checkout.

steps.action: **Open automation setup.** [BRANCH: Shopify | Mailchimp | generic] open Shopify abandoned checkout automation, Mailchimp Customer Journey, or the platform's abandoned cart workflow.
steps.expect: an automation builder or template is open.

steps.action: **Choose the trigger.** Set the trigger to cart or checkout abandoned for the intended store.
steps.expect: the workflow starts only after abandonment.

steps.action: **Set delay and exit rules.** Choose wait time and stop sending when the customer purchases or unsubscribes.
steps.expect: buyers and opted-out contacts are excluded.

steps.action: **Build the email.** Add approved subject, copy, product/cart merge content, support contact, and unsubscribe link if required.
steps.expect: the email renders with cart context.

steps.action: **Add offer rules if used.** Include coupon code, expiration, and eligibility restrictions.
steps.expect: the offer cannot be misused beyond approved terms.

steps.action: **Test the workflow.** Use a test customer or preview data to check content, links, and cart recovery URL.
steps.expect: the email opens the intended cart or checkout.

steps.action: **Activate the automation.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before activation, confirm consent rules, audience exclusions, timing, and unsubscribe handling because customers may receive messages automatically.
steps.expect: the workflow shows active status.

steps.action: **Monitor first sends.** Check early send counts, revenue attribution, errors, and unsubscribe rate.
steps.expect: automation behavior matches expectations.

recipes.verification: The active automation triggers after cart abandonment, excludes purchasers and unsubscribed contacts, includes compliant content, and passes a recovery-link test.

recipes.title: set up an email campaign
recipes.name: set-up-an-email-campaign
recipes.goal: Prepare a compliant marketing email campaign for an approved audience.

steps.action: **Choose the campaign type.** [BRANCH: Mailchimp | generic] create a regular email campaign in Mailchimp, or create a standard marketing email in the platform.
steps.expect: a draft campaign exists.

steps.action: **Select the audience.** Choose the approved list or segment and exclude unsubscribed, suppressed, or ineligible contacts.
steps.expect: the recipient count matches the campaign plan.

steps.action: **Set sender details.** Enter the from name, reply-to address, and subject line.
steps.expect: inbox preview shows the intended sender and subject.

steps.action: **Build the email.** Add approved copy, images, buttons, footer, and required unsubscribe link.
steps.expect: the email preview matches the approved creative.

steps.action: **Check links and tracking.** Test each link and confirm tracking parameters if required.
steps.expect: every link opens the intended destination.

steps.action: **Send a test email.** Send to internal reviewers and check desktop, mobile, and plain-text rendering if available.
steps.expect: reviewers receive a usable test.

steps.action: **Schedule or prepare send.** Choose send time and time zone, or leave as draft for final approval.
steps.expect: the campaign is ready for approval or scheduled send.

steps.action: **Send or schedule the campaign.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before sending or scheduling, confirm audience consent, unsubscribe link, sender, subject, and recipient count because mass email cannot be recalled reliably.
steps.expect: the platform shows sent, scheduled, or queued status.

recipes.verification: The campaign has the approved audience, sender, subject, content, working links, unsubscribe mechanism, and sent or scheduled status.

recipes.title: set up recurring billing
recipes.name: set-up-recurring-billing
recipes.goal: Create a recurring billing schedule that automatically drafts or sends invoices for repeat work on the agreed cadence.

steps.action: **Open recurring billing settings.** Go to recurring invoices, repeating invoices, subscriptions, or templates.
steps.expect: a recurring billing setup form is visible.

steps.action: **Select the customer.** Choose the customer and billing contact.
steps.expect: the schedule is tied to the correct customer.

steps.action: **Enter recurring line items.** Add services, products, quantities, rates, discounts, and taxable status.
steps.expect: each future invoice will contain the right charges.

steps.action: **Set the cadence.** Choose start date, frequency, end date or number of occurrences, due terms, and invoice send timing.
steps.expect: the schedule preview shows the intended billing dates.

steps.action: **Choose collection behavior.** [BRANCH: auto-charge | auto-send | draft-only] charge saved payment automatically, send invoices automatically, or create drafts for review.
steps.expect: the schedule behavior matches the customer agreement.

steps.action: **Add customer-facing notes.** Include contract reference, service period, cancellation terms, and support contact.
steps.expect: future invoices explain the recurring charge.

steps.action: **Activate the schedule.** Save and enable the recurring billing rule.
steps.expect: the schedule shows active status and next invoice date.

recipes.verification: The recurring billing schedule is active with the correct customer, line items, cadence, collection behavior, next invoice date, and authorization status if auto-charge is enabled.

recipes.title: share meeting notes and action items
recipes.name: share-meeting-notes-and-action-items
recipes.goal: Share meeting notes that preserve decisions, owners, and deadlines after a meeting.

steps.action: **Collect raw notes.** Gather the agenda, chat, transcript, whiteboard, and personal notes.
steps.expect: all meeting outputs are in one place.

steps.action: **Separate facts from commentary.** Keep decisions, open questions, and action items; remove side comments and unclear claims.
steps.expect: the draft is concise and factual.

steps.action: **Write action items.** For each task, name the owner, deliverable, and due date.
steps.expect: every task can be assigned and checked.

steps.action: **Record decisions.** State what was decided, who approved it, and any known constraints.
steps.expect: readers can distinguish decisions from discussion.

steps.action: **Flag open questions.** List unresolved items with an owner for getting the answer.
steps.expect: ambiguity is visible instead of buried.

steps.action: **Share with attendees.** Send the notes or link to attendees and relevant stakeholders.
steps.expect: recipients can access the notes.

steps.action: **Ask for corrections.** Give a short window for factual corrections before treating the notes as final.
steps.expect: people know how to fix inaccuracies.

recipes.verification: Shared notes include dated decisions, action items with owners and due dates, and access works for the intended recipients.

recipes.title: split an invoice into milestones
recipes.name: split-an-invoice-into-milestones
recipes.goal: Create milestone invoices so a project is billed in agreed stages instead of as one full invoice.

steps.action: **Review the billing schedule.** List each milestone, trigger, amount, due date, and remaining balance.
steps.expect: the total across milestones equals the contract amount.

steps.action: **Open the project or original quote.** Find the source estimate, project, or customer record.
steps.expect: project billing context is visible.

steps.action: **Create the first milestone invoice.** Add line items for the milestone deliverable, percentage, deposit, tax, and payment terms.
steps.expect: the invoice total matches the first milestone.

steps.action: **Label the milestone clearly.** Include milestone number, service period, acceptance trigger, and remaining schedule in notes.
steps.expect: the customer can identify what the invoice covers.

steps.action: **Save or send based on readiness.** [BRANCH: draft | send] save as draft if approval is pending, or send if the milestone is earned and approved. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* sending requests payment, so confirm milestone completion and amount before sending.
steps.expect: the invoice is draft or sent with the correct status.

steps.action: **Create future milestone records.** Draft future invoices or set reminders for later milestones without sending early.
steps.expect: the remaining billing schedule is tracked.

steps.action: **Update the project balance.** Record billed, paid, and remaining amounts in the project or customer notes.
steps.expect: the project shows what has been billed and what remains.

recipes.verification: Milestone invoices or drafts total the contract amount, each milestone has a clear description and due trigger, and the project balance shows billed, paid, and remaining amounts.

recipes.title: tag and route a ticket
recipes.name: tag-and-route-a-ticket
recipes.goal: Tag and route a support ticket so it reaches the correct queue and can be found in reports.

steps.action: **Open the ticket.** [BRANCH: Zendesk | generic] open the Zendesk ticket or generic helpdesk case.
steps.expect: ticket content and metadata fields are visible.

steps.action: **Identify the issue type.** Read the customer request and determine product area, problem type, urgency, and language or region if relevant.
steps.expect: the routing target is clear.

steps.action: **Apply required tags.** Add approved tags for product, issue type, plan, region, or campaign.
steps.expect: tags appear on the ticket.

steps.action: **Set routing fields.** Choose the group, queue, category, form, or assignment rule target.
steps.expect: the ticket points to the intended support path.

steps.action: **Add an internal note if helpful.** Summarize why the ticket was routed there.
steps.expect: the receiving team can see the routing reason.

steps.action: **Save or submit the update.** Apply changes to the ticket.
steps.expect: the ticket remains in or moves to the expected queue.

recipes.verification: The ticket displays the approved tags, routing fields, and expected queue or group after saving.

recipes.title: tag and segment contacts
recipes.name: tag-and-segment-contacts
recipes.goal: Apply tags or segment membership to CRM contacts so they can be filtered, routed, reported, or messaged appropriately.

steps.action: **Define the segment rule.** Write the exact inclusion and exclusion criteria, such as persona, product interest, lifecycle stage, region, or event source.
steps.expect: membership can be checked objectively.

steps.action: **Find matching contacts.** Use CRM filters, reports, or list builder to identify contacts that meet the rule.
steps.expect: candidate contacts are visible.

steps.action: **Review exclusions.** Remove duplicates, opt-outs, restricted accounts, wrong owners, and contacts that fail the criteria.
steps.expect: the segment contains only eligible contacts.

steps.action: **Apply the tag or segment.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] update a campaign, field, or list in Salesforce; create a static or active list in HubSpot; in another CRM, apply the tag, saved segment, or property.
steps.expect: selected contacts show the tag or membership.

steps.action: **Name and document the segment.** Use a clear name and description with owner, date, source, and purpose.
steps.expect: future users understand why the segment exists.

steps.action: **Test membership.** Open several included and excluded contacts to confirm the rule behaves correctly.
steps.expect: sample contacts match the intended logic.

recipes.verification: The CRM segment or tag has documented criteria, correct sample membership, required exclusions, and a clear owner or purpose.

recipes.title: track pto balances
recipes.name: track-pto-balances
recipes.goal: Review and reconcile paid time off balances so employee accruals, usage, and corrections are accurate.

steps.action: **Open the PTO report.** Select the employee group, leave plan, and date range.
steps.expect: current balances and activity are visible.

steps.action: **Check accrual rules.** Confirm accrual rate, service date, employment status, and eligibility.
steps.expect: each balance follows the applicable rule.

steps.action: **Compare usage.** Match approved PTO requests against deductions from balances.
steps.expect: taken PTO is reflected correctly.

steps.action: **Review exceptions.** Look for negative balances, missing accruals, duplicate deductions, carryover issues, or terminated employees.
steps.expect: anomalies are listed for review.

steps.action: **Make approved corrections.** Enter corrections only with policy support or manager or HR approval.
steps.expect: corrected balances show an audit note.

steps.action: **Notify stakeholders.** Inform payroll, HR, manager, or employee when a correction affects pay or scheduling.
steps.expect: impacted parties know the updated balance.

steps.action: **Save the report.** Export or archive the reconciliation report in the approved location.
steps.expect: the audit trail is retained.

recipes.verification: The PTO report shows reconciled balances, exceptions are resolved or assigned, and any manual corrections have documented approval and audit notes.

recipes.title: triage a support ticket
recipes.name: triage-a-support-ticket
recipes.goal: Triage a support ticket so it has the right urgency, category, owner, and next action.

steps.action: **Open the ticket.** [BRANCH: Zendesk | generic] open the ticket in Zendesk or the helpdesk queue in a generic support tool.
steps.expect: the customer message, status, and metadata are visible.

steps.action: **Read the latest customer request.** Identify the problem, affected product, customer impact, and requested outcome.
steps.expect: the ticket can be summarized in one sentence.

steps.action: **Check account and history.** Review plan level, open related tickets, recent incidents, and prior replies.
steps.expect: repeated or high-impact issues are visible.

steps.action: **Set priority.** Choose the urgency and impact level according to the support policy.
steps.expect: the ticket priority reflects business impact.

steps.action: **Categorize the issue.** Add the product area, issue type, and relevant tags.
steps.expect: routing and reporting fields are complete.

steps.action: **Assign the owner or queue.** Send the ticket to the right agent, team, or specialist queue.
steps.expect: the ticket has a responsible next handler.

steps.action: **Record the next action.** Add an internal note with the summary, evidence, and next step.
steps.expect: another agent can continue without rereading everything.

recipes.verification: The ticket has a priority, category or tags, owner or queue, internal triage note, and a clear next action.

recipes.title: update a project timeline
recipes.name: update-a-project-timeline
recipes.goal: Update a project timeline so dates, dependencies, and stakeholder expectations reflect current reality.

steps.action: **Open the timeline view.** [BRANCH: Jira | Asana | Linear | generic] open Timeline, Roadmap, Project milestones, or the generic schedule view.
steps.expect: project dates and dependencies are visible.

steps.action: **Review current status.** Compare completed, in-progress, blocked, and not-started work against the existing dates.
steps.expect: schedule gaps are visible.

steps.action: **Update task dates.** Adjust start dates, due dates, milestone dates, or target dates for affected work.
steps.expect: the visual timeline reflects current estimates.

steps.action: **Check dependencies.** Move dependent tasks or mark dependency conflicts caused by date changes.
steps.expect: downstream effects are visible.

steps.action: **Add a change note.** Document what changed, why, and who approved or requested it.
steps.expect: the timeline history explains the update.

steps.action: **Notify stakeholders.** Share the revised dates and any decision needed.
steps.expect: stakeholders know the updated schedule.

recipes.verification: The project timeline shows updated dates, dependency impacts, and a written explanation or notification for the change.

recipes.title: update store inventory
recipes.name: update-store-inventory
recipes.goal: Update store inventory so customers can only buy quantities the business can fulfill.

steps.action: **Find the SKU.** [BRANCH: Shopify | generic] search Products or Inventory in Shopify, or search the SKU in the inventory system.
steps.expect: the correct item and variants are visible.

steps.action: **Confirm the location.** Select the warehouse, store, or fulfillment location being updated.
steps.expect: the adjustment applies to the intended stock pool.

steps.action: **Compare current quantity.** Review available, committed, incoming, and reserved counts if shown.
steps.expect: the system quantity difference is understood.

steps.action: **Enter the adjustment.** Change the quantity or add/subtract the approved amount with a reason note.
steps.expect: the new available quantity is previewed or saved.

steps.action: **Save the change.** Confirm the inventory update in the platform.
steps.expect: the SKU shows the updated quantity.

steps.action: **Check storefront availability.** Open the product page or admin availability view.
steps.expect: customers see in-stock, low-stock, or sold-out status correctly.

steps.action: **Record the reason.** Add a note, tag, or tracker entry for receiving, damage, cycle count, or correction.
steps.expect: the adjustment is auditable.

recipes.verification: The correct SKU and location show the approved available quantity, and the storefront availability matches that quantity.

recipes.title: void an invoice
recipes.name: void-an-invoice
recipes.goal: Void an invoice that should no longer be collectible while preserving an audit trail of the original invoice number and reason.

steps.action: **Open the invoice.** Locate the invoice by number, customer, or date.
steps.expect: the invoice details and current status are visible.

steps.action: **Check linked activity.** Review payments, credits, tax, reminders, and customer communications tied to the invoice.
steps.expect: you know the downstream impact of voiding.

steps.action: **Confirm void is the right action.** Compare voiding against editing, issuing a credit memo, or writing off the balance.
steps.expect: voiding is appropriate for an invoice that should not exist as collectible.

steps.action: **Add a reason note.** Record the reason, replacement invoice number if any, and approval.
steps.expect: the audit trail explains the void.

steps.action: **Void the invoice.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* voiding may permanently cancel the invoice and preserve its number, so confirm customer, invoice number, and reason before proceeding.
steps.expect: the invoice status changes to voided.

steps.action: **Notify affected parties.** Tell the customer or internal team if they received, approved, or were chasing the invoice.
steps.expect: no one continues trying to pay or collect the voided invoice.

recipes.verification: The invoice status is voided, the balance is no longer collectible, the reason and approval are documented, and any replacement invoice or linked payment is handled.

recipes.title: write a cold outreach email
recipes.name: write-a-cold-outreach-email
recipes.goal: Draft a compliant cold outreach email that is relevant, concise, and ready for review or sending.

steps.action: **Confirm outreach eligibility.** Check consent, opt-out status, geography, suppression lists, and account ownership.
steps.expect: the prospect is allowed to receive outreach.

steps.action: **Identify one relevant reason.** Use a business trigger, role responsibility, company initiative, or known pain point.
steps.expect: the email has a specific reason for contacting this person.

steps.action: **Write the subject line.** Keep it short, accurate, and non-deceptive.
steps.expect: the subject matches the body and sender.

steps.action: **Draft the opening.** Name the relevant reason in one sentence without exaggerated familiarity.
steps.expect: the first line could not be sent unchanged to every prospect.

steps.action: **State the value and proof.** Explain one business outcome and include a credible proof point if approved.
steps.expect: the recipient can understand why the message matters.

steps.action: **Ask for one action.** Request a brief reply, meeting, referral to the right owner, or permission to send more detail.
steps.expect: the call to action is simple.

steps.action: **Add compliance elements.** Include sender identity, company, physical mailing address or approved footer, and opt-out language where required.
steps.expect: the email meets policy and legal footer requirements.

steps.action: **Save or send through the CRM.** [BRANCH: Salesforce | HubSpot | generic] use Salesforce email composer or sequence; use HubSpot email or sequence; in another CRM, use the approved outreach tool.
steps.expect: the draft or sent email is logged to the contact.

recipes.verification: The outreach email has a lawful recipient, accurate subject, relevant opening, clear value, single call to action, required compliance footer, and CRM log.

recipes.title: write a handoff doc
recipes.name: write-a-handoff-doc
recipes.goal: Write a handoff document that lets another person continue project or support work without losing context.

steps.action: **Open the handoff destination.** Create or open the document, ticket note, project update, or shared template.
steps.expect: the handoff can be edited.

steps.action: **State the scope.** Name the project, ticket, customer, or workstream being handed off.
steps.expect: the reader knows what the document covers.

steps.action: **Summarize current status.** Describe what is done, what is in progress, and what is unresolved.
steps.expect: the work state is clear.

steps.action: **List next actions.** Add each next action with owner, due date, and required input.
steps.expect: the receiver knows what to do first.

steps.action: **Capture blockers and decisions.** Note open questions, risks, dependencies, and escalation paths.
steps.expect: unresolved items are not hidden.

steps.action: **Add links and evidence.** Include tracker items, tickets, docs, files, dashboards, and relevant messages.
steps.expect: the receiver can verify context.

steps.action: **Share with the receiver.** Send the handoff and ask for confirmation or questions.
steps.expect: the receiver acknowledges access or raises gaps.

recipes.verification: The handoff document names the scope, current status, next actions, owners, blockers, links, and receiver confirmation path.

recipes.title: write a status report
recipes.name: write-a-status-report
recipes.goal: Write a concise project status report that tells stakeholders what changed, what is blocked, and what decisions are needed.

steps.action: **Open the reporting destination.** Open the document, project update field, email draft, or status tool.
steps.expect: the report can be edited.

steps.action: **State the overall status.** Choose a simple status such as on track, at risk, blocked, or complete.
steps.expect: the reader can understand the project state at a glance.

steps.action: **Summarize progress.** List the most important completed work since the last update.
steps.expect: accomplishments are concrete and recent.

steps.action: **Name risks and blockers.** Describe each blocker, owner, and needed decision or dependency.
steps.expect: unresolved issues are actionable.

steps.action: **Update timeline and scope.** Note changes to milestones, due dates, deliverables, or assumptions.
steps.expect: stakeholders see what changed.

steps.action: **List next steps.** Add the next one to five actions with owners and dates.
steps.expect: the report points to future work.

steps.action: **Publish or send the report.** Share it in the agreed channel.
steps.expect: stakeholders can access the same status record.

recipes.verification: The report includes overall status, recent progress, risks or blockers, timeline changes, next steps, owners, and publication location.

recipes.title: write off a bad debt
recipes.name: write-off-a-bad-debt
recipes.goal: Write off an uncollectible customer balance so accounts receivable and reports no longer show it as expected cash.

steps.action: **Open the unpaid invoice.** Locate the customer invoice and confirm the open balance.
steps.expect: the receivable amount is visible.

steps.action: **Review collection history.** Check reminders, disputes, payment plans, returned mail, bankruptcy notices, or collection notes.
steps.expect: the record supports treating the balance as uncollectible.

steps.action: **Confirm approval.** Get owner, manager, or accountant approval for the write-off.
steps.expect: approval is documented in the customer or invoice notes.

steps.action: **Create the write-off entry.** [BRANCH: credit memo | bad-debt expense | allowance] create a credit memo or journal entry using the approved bad-debt account.
steps.expect: the entry amount equals the balance being written off.

steps.action: **Apply the entry to the invoice.** Apply the credit or write-off against the unpaid invoice.
steps.expect: the invoice open balance becomes zero.

steps.action: **Save supporting notes.** Add the reason, approval, date, and whether collection may resume later.
steps.expect: a reviewer can understand why the receivable was removed.

recipes.verification: The invoice has zero open balance, the write-off entry is linked to it, the approved reason is documented, and accounts receivable no longer includes the written-off amount.

recipes.title: ask a coworker for help
recipes.name: ask-a-coworker-for-help
recipes.goal: Ask a coworker for help in a way that is specific, respectful of their time, and easy for them to answer without taking ownership of your whole problem.

steps.action: **Define the exact help needed.** Decide whether you need a pointer, review, decision, debug session, context, approval, or introduction.
steps.expect: your ask has a shape smaller than "help me."

steps.action: **Show what you tried.** Gather links, error messages, options considered, and the point where you got stuck.
steps.expect: the coworker can start from your work instead of repeating it.

steps.action: **Choose the right channel.** Use chat for quick pointers, a ticket or doc comment for trackable work, and a meeting only when live back-and-forth is needed. [BRANCH: quick question | deeper help] ask in chat for quick context; send a short agenda for deeper help.
steps.expect: the medium fits the effort.

steps.action: **Write the ask with constraints.** Include context, the specific question, deadline, and what answer format would help.
steps.expect: they can answer yes, no, or with a pointer.

steps.action: **Respect their time.** Offer a bounded option: "Could you spend 10 minutes pointing me to the right owner?" or "If you are not the right person, who should I ask?"
steps.expect: the request does not silently claim their afternoon.

steps.action: **Offer reciprocity or cleanup.** Say you will document the answer, take the next step, or return the favor on something you can help with.
steps.expect: the exchange feels collaborative, not extractive.

steps.action: **Use the help well.** Listen, take notes, confirm next actions, and do the follow-through yourself. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* forwarding blame or exposing a coworker's informal advice can damage trust, so ask before quoting them in a wider thread.
steps.expect: the coworker sees their help turned into progress.

steps.action: **Thank and close the loop.** Send a quick thanks and, later, the result: "Your pointer to the cache key fixed it."
steps.expect: they know the time was useful.

recipes.verification: The coworker received a specific bounded ask, saw what you already tried, and got a thank-you or outcome update after helping.

recipes.title: ask for a deadline extension
recipes.name: ask-for-a-deadline-extension
recipes.goal: You have secured a realistic new deadline from the person who owns the original one, through a request that owns the delay honestly, proposes a specific new date, and protects the relationship, and then you deliver by that date.

steps.action: **Decide early, the moment you doubt the date.** The value of an extension request drops fast as the deadline nears; a week out is a planning conversation, an hour out is an apology.
steps.expect: you are raising this while the owner still has room to adjust.

steps.action: **Estimate the real new date, then add buffer.** Pick the date you can hit even if one more thing goes wrong, not your best case.
steps.expect: a specific date you would bet on, not a hopeful one.

steps.action: **Choose the channel to match the stakes.** [BRANCH: routine or internal → a short written message | high-stakes, client, or a date others depend on → a call or in-person, followed by written confirmation]
steps.expect: the owner hears it through a channel that signals you take it seriously.

steps.action: **Lead with the ask and the new date, not the backstory.** Open with "I need to move the X deadline to [date]" so they can react to the concrete request.
steps.expect: the owner immediately knows what you want and by when.

steps.action: **Own the reason in one honest line, without over-explaining.** State the cause plainly; do not manufacture drama or bury it in excuses.
steps.expect: the reason is credible and brief; you have not shifted blame onto others without cause.

steps.action: **Show what they get for the delay.** Offer a partial deliverable now, a status detail, or a scope trade so the extension buys quality, not just time.
steps.expect: the owner sees the new date as protecting the outcome, not just your comfort.

steps.action: **Get the new date confirmed in writing.** A verbal yes on a call must be echoed in a message. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not treat silence as agreement; an unanswered request means the old deadline still stands.
steps.expect: an explicit written acknowledgment of the new date.

steps.action: **Deliver on the new date, or earlier.** The whole request is only worth making if you hit the date you asked for.
steps.expect: the work arrives by the agreed date; your next extension request, if ever, is still credible.

recipes.verification: The deadline owner has explicitly agreed in writing to a specific new date, and you delivered the committed work on or before that date.

recipes.title: ask for a mental health day
recipes.name: ask-for-a-mental-health-day
recipes.goal: Ask for a mental health day professionally while protecting privacy, work continuity, and trust.

steps.action: **Check the leave channel.** Confirm whether your workplace requires a manager message, HR system entry, calendar block, or sick line.
steps.expect: you know where the request must go.

steps.action: **Decide how much to disclose.** Use a simple line such as "I need to take a sick day today" or "I need a mental health day and will be offline."
steps.expect: your privacy boundary is clear.

steps.action: **Send the request early.** Message your manager before your workday starts if possible.
steps.expect: your absence is visible before others depend on you.

steps.action: **Cover urgent work.** Name what is blocked, what can wait, and who can answer urgent questions.
steps.expect: the team can keep critical work moving.

steps.action: **Set an offline boundary.** [BRANCH: fully offline | limited availability] state you will be offline; if limited availability is required, define one short check-in window.
steps.expect: people know whether they can contact you.

steps.action: **Update systems.** Enter leave in HR, mark calendar as unavailable, and adjust meeting responses.
steps.expect: the absence appears in official and practical calendars.

steps.action: **Use a short return note.** When back, say "I'm back today and catching up; please flag anything urgent."
steps.expect: colleagues know you have returned.

steps.action: **Review recurring causes.** If mental health days are becoming frequent, consider workload discussion, benefits, employee assistance, or medical support.
steps.expect: the absence is not the only intervention.

recipes.verification: Your manager or required system has the leave notice, your calendar shows unavailable, urgent work has a coverage note, and your privacy-sensitive details are not broadly shared.

recipes.title: ask for a raise
recipes.name: ask-for-a-raise
recipes.goal: Ask for a raise with a documented business case, market context, clear number, and professional response to the answer.

steps.action: **Collect accomplishments.** List outcomes from the last 6 to 12 months, including revenue, savings, quality, speed, risk reduction, or leadership.
steps.expect: evidence focuses on results, not effort alone.

steps.action: **Map work to role scope.** Show how your responsibilities match or exceed the current role expectations.
steps.expect: the case explains why pay should change now.

steps.action: **Gather market data.** Use several sources for comparable title, level, location, industry, and company size.
steps.expect: you have a realistic pay range, not one outlier.

steps.action: **Choose the ask.** Pick a specific salary, hourly rate, or percentage increase and know the minimum acceptable outcome.
steps.expect: the request is clear enough to approve or counter.

steps.action: **Book the meeting.** Ask for time to discuss compensation and growth, rather than surprising your manager in a busy hallway.
steps.expect: a focused conversation is scheduled.

steps.action: **Present the case briefly.** Explain role growth, outcomes, market range, and the specific ask in a calm sequence.
steps.expect: the manager understands the business reason.

steps.action: **Listen to constraints.** [BRANCH: yes | no | later] ask about process, budget cycle, criteria, and timeline.
steps.expect: the next step is explicit.

steps.action: **Confirm in writing.** Send a short recap with the ask, evidence summary, and agreed timeline or decision.
steps.expect: there is a written record.

steps.action: **Handle the answer.** If approved, confirm effective date; if delayed or denied, ask what measurable changes would reopen the discussion.
steps.expect: you leave with decision, date, or criteria.

recipes.verification: You made a specific compensation request supported by documented impact and market data, then saved the decision, timeline, or criteria in writing.

recipes.title: ask for a reference
recipes.name: ask-for-a-reference
recipes.goal: Ask someone to serve as a professional or academic reference in a way that is clear, respectful, and easy for them to accept.

steps.action: **Choose the right person.** Pick someone who can speak to relevant work, reliability, judgment, or growth.
steps.expect: the person has direct experience with you.

steps.action: **Ask early.** Contact them before listing their name, ideally at least 1 to 2 weeks before a deadline.
steps.expect: they have time to decide and prepare.

steps.action: **Make the request direct.** Ask whether they would be comfortable giving a positive reference for this opportunity.
steps.expect: they can say yes, no, or not this time.

steps.action: **Give the context.** Include the role, organization, deadline, and what the reference may be asked to do.
steps.expect: they understand the commitment.

steps.action: **Provide supporting material.** Send your resume, job description, key projects, and 2 or 3 points they might mention.
steps.expect: they do not need to reconstruct your history from memory.

steps.action: **Confirm contact details.** Ask which email, phone number, title, and organization they prefer you to list.
steps.expect: the application information is accurate.

steps.action: **Thank them either way.** Reply promptly with appreciation, whether they accept or decline.
steps.expect: the relationship stays respectful.

steps.action: **Notify before each use.** Tell them when you submit their name and what timeline to expect.
steps.expect: they are not surprised by a call or email.

steps.action: **Update after the result.** Share the outcome and thank them again.
steps.expect: they know their help mattered and are not left wondering.

recipes.verification: The reference has explicitly agreed, has the opportunity details and materials, and you have confirmed their preferred contact information.

recipes.title: ask for an informational interview
recipes.name: ask-for-an-informational-interview
recipes.goal: Ask someone for a short informational interview in a way that is warm, specific, respectful of their time, and likely to produce useful advice.

steps.action: **Start with the warmest path.** Use a mutual introduction, alumni directory, event follow-up, or prior connection when possible.
steps.expect: the recipient can place you or the context quickly.

steps.action: **Write the ask in one short paragraph.** Include who you are, why them, what you want to learn, and the time limit.
steps.expect: the message is understandable without scrolling.

steps.action: **Respect their time explicitly.** Ask for 15 to 20 minutes, offer two or three windows, and make it easy to decline.
steps.expect: saying yes feels bounded.

steps.action: **Make the questions specific.** Ask about decisions, skills, transitions, day-to-day work, and what they wish they had known. Avoid "Can I pick your brain?"
steps.expect: they can see the conversation will be focused.

steps.action: **Avoid disguising a job ask.** Do not ask for a referral, opening, or internal contact in the first request. [BRANCH: student or career changer | peer in field] emphasize learning if exploring; emphasize targeted perspective if already in the field.
steps.expect: the meeting is informational, not a hidden transaction.

steps.action: **Send a polished message.** Example: "I am exploring product roles in health tech and saw your path from nursing operations to product. Would you be open to 20 minutes next week so I can ask how you made that transition?"
steps.expect: the recipient knows exactly why they were chosen.

steps.action: **Prepare before they answer.** Make a short agenda, read their public work, and decide which questions matter most.
steps.expect: if they say yes, you are ready.

steps.action: **Thank and update.** After the conversation, send a same-day thank-you with one useful takeaway. Later, send a brief update if their advice helped. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* burning someone's time with an unprepared call damages trust, so prepare before booking.
steps.expect: the relationship ends warmer than it began.

recipes.verification: The request states why this person, asks for a bounded 15 to 20 minute conversation, includes focused topics, and makes declining easy.

recipes.title: ask someone for a recommendation letter
recipes.name: ask-someone-for-a-recommendation-letter
recipes.goal: A recommender is asked early, respectfully, and given enough material to write a specific letter by the deadline.

steps.action: **Ask early.** Aim for at least three to four weeks before the deadline, more for busy seasons.
steps.expect: the person has real time to say yes and write.

steps.action: **Ask in person or live if appropriate.** [BRANCH: in person | email] Ask in person or on a call when the relationship is active; use email when distance, schedule, or formality makes that better.
steps.expect: the ask feels personal and easy to answer.

steps.action: **Make yes or no safe.** Say "Would you feel comfortable writing a strong recommendation for me?" rather than assuming.
steps.expect: they can decline without damaging the relationship.

steps.action: **Give the core details.** Include opportunity name, deadline, submission link, recipient, and whether the letter is confidential.
steps.expect: logistics are not hidden in follow-up messages.

steps.action: **Provide useful material.** Send your resume, draft statement, relevant work, achievements, and a short note reminding them what you did together.
steps.expect: they can write with specific examples.

steps.action: **Suggest focus areas lightly.** Mention two or three qualities the opportunity values, without scripting praise.
steps.expect: the recommender knows what would help.

steps.action: **Send reminders respectfully.** Check in one week before the deadline, then two days before if there is still no confirmation.
steps.expect: the deadline stays visible without pestering.

steps.action: **Do not submit their name casually.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some systems email recommenders immediately, so get consent before entering their contact information.
steps.expect: no one receives a surprise automated request.

steps.action: **Thank them and update them.** Send a thank-you after submission and later share the outcome.
steps.expect: the relationship is maintained beyond the transaction.

recipes.verification: The recommender agreed, has the deadline and submission instructions, received supporting material, and was thanked after submitting.

recipes.title: conduct a job interview
recipes.name: conduct-a-job-interview
recipes.goal: Conduct a structured job interview that gathers role-relevant evidence and gives the candidate a respectful, consistent experience.

steps.action: **Review the scorecard.** Identify the competencies this interview owns, such as technical judgment, collaboration, leadership, or domain knowledge.
steps.expect: you know what evidence to collect.

steps.action: **Prepare questions.** Write consistent behavioral or work-sample questions tied to the scorecard.
steps.expect: candidates are evaluated on comparable prompts.

steps.action: **Open professionally.** Introduce yourself, confirm timing, explain the structure, and leave space for candidate questions.
steps.expect: the candidate knows what to expect.

steps.action: **Ask for concrete examples.** Use prompts like "Tell me about a time you had to change a stakeholder's mind."
steps.expect: answers include situation, action, and result.

steps.action: **Probe fairly.** Ask follow-ups about tradeoffs, ownership, conflict, measurement, and lessons learned.
steps.expect: you get evidence beyond rehearsed claims.

steps.action: **Avoid protected or irrelevant topics.** [BRANCH: candidate volunteers personal information | no personal information] redirect to role requirements if personal information appears; continue with prepared questions otherwise.
steps.expect: the interview stays job-related.

steps.action: **Leave time for questions.** Answer honestly about role, team, process, and next steps without overselling.
steps.expect: the candidate can evaluate fit.

steps.action: **Submit notes promptly.** Record evidence against the scorecard before discussing with other interviewers.
steps.expect: feedback reflects your observations, not group influence.

recipes.verification: The submitted interview feedback includes role-relevant evidence for each assigned competency, a recommendation, and no prohibited personal information.

recipes.title: decline a job offer gracefully
recipes.name: decline-a-job-offer-gracefully
recipes.goal: Decline a job offer promptly and professionally while preserving goodwill with the recruiter, hiring manager, and future version of the opportunity.

steps.action: **Make the decision cleanly.** Confirm you are declining, not negotiating, stalling, or waiting for another answer you still need.
steps.expect: you know whether the next message is a decline or a request for more time.

steps.action: **Respond promptly.** Decline as soon as the decision is firm, ideally before the deadline.
steps.expect: the employer can move to another candidate without unnecessary delay.

steps.action: **Use the right channel.** If the relationship was mostly email, email is enough; if a recruiter invested heavily, a brief call plus written confirmation may be kinder. [BRANCH: email only | call then email] choose call for close relationships or senior roles; choose email for standard processes.
steps.expect: the decline is clear and documented.

steps.action: **Lead with gratitude.** Thank them for the offer, time, conversations, and specific thing you appreciated about the team or role.
steps.expect: the tone recognizes their effort.

steps.action: **Give a brief reason.** Keep it simple: accepted another role, timing, compensation, location, scope, or fit. Do not litigate every concern.
steps.expect: they understand the category without receiving a teardown.

steps.action: **State the decision plainly.** Use "I have decided to decline the offer" rather than soft language that invites confusion. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once you decline, the role may be offered to someone else immediately, so confirm before sending.
steps.expect: there is no ambiguity about acceptance.

steps.action: **Keep the door open if true.** Say you hope to stay in touch or would welcome future paths crossing, but only if you mean it.
steps.expect: the relationship closes with respect.

steps.action: **Send written confirmation.** After any call, send a short email restating the decision and thanks.
steps.expect: both sides have a record and no one is left guessing.

recipes.verification: The employer receives a prompt written decline that includes gratitude, a clear decision, a brief reason, and no ambiguous acceptance language.

recipes.title: decline a meeting invite
recipes.name: decline-a-meeting-invite
recipes.goal: Decline a meeting invite while preserving the work relationship and, when useful, offering a better way to handle the topic.

steps.action: **Check the purpose.** Read the title, notes, attendees, and any attached agenda.
steps.expect: you know whether the meeting needs you specifically.

steps.action: **Decide the response path.** [BRANCH: decline | tentative | propose new time] Choose decline when you cannot or should not attend.
steps.expect: your calendar action matches your actual availability.

steps.action: **Respond quickly.** Decline as soon as you know, especially for small meetings.
steps.expect: the organizer has time to adjust.

steps.action: **Keep the reason optional.** Give a brief reason only if it helps, such as conflict, focus block, or not the right owner.
steps.expect: message stays concise and does not overexplain.

steps.action: **Offer an alternative when needed.** Suggest async notes, a delegate, a decision doc, or one alternate time.
steps.expect: the organizer has a next step besides losing your attendance.

steps.action: **Protect focus respectfully.** If declining for priority work, say you are preserving time for a committed deadline.
steps.expect: the message frames the decline around work impact.

steps.action: **Use the calendar response.** Click decline and add a note if the tool allows it.
steps.expect: the event is removed or marked declined on your calendar.

steps.action: **Follow up separately if important.** Send a short chat or email if the calendar note may be missed.
steps.expect: the organizer sees the context before the meeting.

recipes.verification: The calendar shows the invite as declined or tentative as intended, and the organizer has either a short reason or a practical alternative.

recipes.title: decline extra work without burning bridges
recipes.name: decline-extra-work-without-burning-bridges
recipes.goal: Decline or renegotiate extra work while preserving trust, making tradeoffs visible, and keeping relationships intact.

steps.action: **Clarify the request.** Ask what outcome is needed, by when, why it matters, and who is requesting it.
steps.expect: you know the actual size and urgency.

steps.action: **Check your capacity.** Compare the request against current commitments and deadlines.
steps.expect: your response is based on tradeoffs, not mood.

steps.action: **Decide your response.** [BRANCH: decline | defer | trade] decline if it does not fit; defer if timing is the issue; trade if something else must move.
steps.expect: you have a constructive alternative.

steps.action: **Use a clear script.** Say, "I cannot take this on by Friday without delaying the client report. I can help next Tuesday or review a draft for 20 minutes."
steps.expect: the no includes useful options.

steps.action: **Name the tradeoff.** Explain which priority, deadline, or quality bar would be affected.
steps.expect: the requester sees the cost.

steps.action: **Offer a narrower contribution.** Suggest a template, quick review, referral, later slot, or partial deliverable if appropriate.
steps.expect: the relationship gets support without full ownership.

steps.action: **Escalate priority conflicts.** If the requester insists, ask your manager or decision owner to choose between competing commitments.
steps.expect: prioritization moves to the right authority.

steps.action: **Confirm in writing.** Send a short recap of what you declined, deferred, or agreed to do instead.
steps.expect: expectations are documented.

recipes.verification: The requester has a clear answer, the tradeoff is visible, any alternative help is bounded, and changed commitments are documented.

recipes.title: delegate a task clearly
recipes.name: delegate-a-task-clearly
recipes.goal: Delegate a task so the recipient understands the outcome, authority, constraints, deadline, and check-in rhythm.

steps.action: **Define the outcome.** Write the desired end state in one sentence, such as "Create a two-page vendor comparison for Friday's decision."
steps.expect: the task is described by result, not activity.

steps.action: **Explain the context.** State why the task matters, who will use the output, and what decision it supports.
steps.expect: the recipient can make sensible tradeoffs.

steps.action: **Set boundaries.** Clarify budget, tools, people to consult, quality bar, and decisions they can make alone.
steps.expect: authority and limits are explicit.

steps.action: **Agree on deadline and checkpoints.** [BRANCH: routine task | high-risk task] use a final deadline for routine work; add interim checkpoints for high-risk or unfamiliar work.
steps.expect: progress will surface before it is too late.

steps.action: **Provide resources.** Share files, examples, contacts, and prior decisions.
steps.expect: the recipient can start without hunting for basics.

steps.action: **Ask for playback.** Say, "Can you tell me what you understand the deliverable and deadline to be?"
steps.expect: mismatches are caught immediately.

steps.action: **Document the handoff.** Send a short written note with outcome, owner, deadline, resources, and check-in plan.
steps.expect: both sides have the same record.

steps.action: **Follow up without taking over.** Ask about blockers and decisions, not every detail of execution.
steps.expect: ownership stays with the delegatee.

recipes.verification: The delegated task has one owner, a written outcome, deadline, constraints, resources, authority level, and agreed checkpoint cadence.

recipes.title: facilitate a retrospective
recipes.name: facilitate-a-retrospective
recipes.goal: Facilitate a retrospective that turns recent work into specific improvements without blaming individuals.

steps.action: **Set the scope.** Define the time period, event, or project the retrospective covers.
steps.expect: participants evaluate the same work.

steps.action: **Choose prompts.** Use prompts like "What worked?", "What did not?", "What surprised us?", and "What should change next time?"
steps.expect: input is structured.

steps.action: **Collect input privately.** Give people quiet writing time before discussion.
steps.expect: candid points are captured before group pressure shapes them.

steps.action: **Discuss patterns.** Group repeated themes and ask for facts, examples, and impact.
steps.expect: the team focuses on system patterns.

steps.action: **Separate facts from judgments.** Convert "handoff was careless" into "handoff lacked owner, date, and acceptance criteria."
steps.expect: issues become fixable.

steps.action: **Pick improvement actions.** [BRANCH: many issues | few issues] prioritize the top one to three issues when there are many; assign action directly when there are few.
steps.expect: the retro does not create an impossible list.

steps.action: **Assign owners.** Give each action one owner, one deliverable, and one due date.
steps.expect: accountability is clear.

steps.action: **Share the retro summary.** Send themes, actions, owners, and follow-up date to participants.
steps.expect: the record is transparent and usable.

recipes.verification: The retro notes contain themes, decisions, 1-3 improvement actions, owners, deadlines, and a follow-up date to check whether actions happened.

recipes.title: follow up after a job interview
recipes.name: follow-up-after-a-job-interview
recipes.goal: Send a professional follow-up after a job interview that thanks the interviewer, reinforces fit, and asks about timing when appropriate.

steps.action: **Send within 24 hours.** Draft the note the same day if possible, or the next morning.
steps.expect: the follow-up arrives while the conversation is still fresh.

steps.action: **Use a clear subject.** Reply to the existing thread or use a subject like `Thank you - [Role] interview`.
steps.expect: the recipient can identify the interview quickly.

steps.action: **Open with thanks.** Thank them for their time and name the role.
steps.expect: first line is direct and professional.

steps.action: **Reference something specific.** Mention a project, challenge, team goal, or detail from the conversation.
steps.expect: the note does not read like a template.

steps.action: **Reinforce one fit point.** Connect your experience to one need they described.
steps.expect: the message adds useful context without repeating your whole resume.

steps.action: **Ask about timeline only if needed.** If no timeline was given, ask when they expect next steps. If they gave one, acknowledge it.
steps.expect: the timing question is polite and not pushy.

steps.action: **Keep it short.** Limit the message to one or two brief paragraphs.
steps.expect: the note can be read in under a minute.

steps.action: **Proofread and send.** Check name spelling, company name, and role title before sending.
steps.expect: no copied or incorrect details remain.

steps.action: **Wait before a second follow-up.** If the stated timeline passes, wait 1 to 2 business days before checking in again.
steps.expect: you have a date for the next reasonable follow-up.

recipes.verification: The follow-up was sent within 24 hours, includes a specific interview reference, and either acknowledges or politely asks about the hiring timeline.

recipes.title: give a short presentation
recipes.name: give-a-short-presentation
