steps.expect: either full function confirmed or a clean diagnosis that only data is down.

steps.action: **Set the APN manually if data fails.** Settings > mobile network > access point names: add the carrier's APN (name, APN string, sometimes username/password; the values are on the packaging or the carrier's site, and counter staff know them). Reboot after saving.
steps.expect: mobile data works after reboot with the new APN selected.

steps.action: **Learn the top-up mechanism before you leave.** Ask: carrier app (may need a local payment method), USSD code (like *123#), scratch cards from convenience stores, or online with a foreign card. Install the carrier app and check your balance once.
steps.expect: you can read your remaining balance and data, and know one top-up method that works with your payment options.

recipes.verification: With Wi-Fi off, a fresh website loads over mobile data; a test call connects; the carrier app or USSD code shows your balance and data remaining; you know the plan's expiry date and can state your top-up method; your home SIM is physically accounted for.

recipes.title: buy a ticket from a machine
recipes.name: buy-a-ticket-from-a-machine
recipes.goal: Buy the correct machine-issued ticket and leave with the ticket, change, card, and receipt if needed.

steps.action: **Read the first screen before paying.** Look for language, ticket type, destination, zones, date, and passenger category.
steps.expect: the machine shows options that match your trip or purchase.

steps.action: **Choose the product.** [BRANCH: transit | parking | event] select ride fare, parking duration, or event ticket category.
steps.expect: the screen shows a price before payment.

steps.action: **Check restrictions.** Look for off-peak, single-use, return, transfer, senior, child, or timed-entry rules.
steps.expect: the ticket will be valid when you plan to use it.

steps.action: **Select quantity carefully.** Set number of adults, children, bikes, bags, or vehicles if relevant.
steps.expect: total price updates to the intended count.

steps.action: **Choose payment method.** [BRANCH: exact change | card] use exact change if the machine says no change given; use card if cash acceptance is limited.
steps.expect: the machine prompts for coins, bills, tap, insert, or swipe.

steps.action: **Pay only after reviewing the summary.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* many machines cannot refund wrong tickets; confirm destination, date, quantity, and price first.
steps.expect: payment is accepted and printing begins.

steps.action: **Wait for all items.** Do not walk away at the first sound.
steps.expect: ticket, card, change, and receipt slots finish dispensing.

steps.action: **Take the ticket and change.** Check every slot, including low change cups and side receipt trays.
steps.expect: nothing paid for remains in the machine.

steps.action: **Verify the printed ticket.** Compare destination, date, time window, zone, and count against your plan.
steps.expect: the printed ticket matches the trip or purchase.

steps.action: **Keep the receipt if reimbursement or disputes matter.** Store it separately from the ticket so you do not hand it over by mistake.
steps.expect: proof of purchase is available later.

recipes.verification: You hold the correct printed ticket, your card is back, change is collected, and the receipt is kept or intentionally declined.

recipes.title: buy flowers for an occasion
recipes.name: buy-flowers-for-an-occasion
recipes.goal: You hand over (or have delivered) a bouquet that fits the occasion and the recipient's culture, arrives fresh, and comes with what the recipient needs to keep it alive.

steps.action: **Decode the occasion.** Common codes: red roses read as romance almost everywhere (avoid them for colleagues); white lilies and white chrysanthemums are funeral flowers in much of Europe and East Asia; yellow roses mean friendship in some cultures and jealousy or infidelity in others; bright mixed seasonal bouquets are the safe congratulations/birthday default. When unsure, tell the florist the occasion and relationship and let them steer.
steps.expect: a flower-and-color direction that cannot be misread as romantic, funereal, or accusatory.

steps.action: **Check the number rules.** Stem-count customs are real: in Russia and much of Eastern Europe, even counts are strictly for funerals, so give odd numbers; in parts of East Asia the number 4 is avoided (homophone of death) and 8 is favored; a dozen red roses is the Western romantic standard. When the recipient's culture is unknown, an odd count under ten offends nobody.
steps.expect: a stem count that is deliberate, not accidental.

steps.action: **Choose the source.** [BRANCH: hand delivery today → local florist (best quality and advice) or supermarket (cheaper, fine for casual occasions) | remote recipient → a delivery service or, better, phone a florist local to the recipient directly, which skips relay markups | peak date → order 3+ days ahead and expect surge pricing on roses]
steps.expect: a source that can meet the deadline at your budget.

steps.action: **Select for freshness, not fullest bloom.** Buy blooms one-third to half open: fully open flowers are at peak now and fade in days. Freshness tells: firm upright heads, green (not slimy or brown) stem ends, no translucent or dropping petals, buds with color showing. Sniff the water in the bucket; sour means old stock.
steps.expect: a bouquet that looks slightly "young", which is correct.

steps.action: **Have it finished for the occasion.** Ask for a hand-tied wrap for casual gifting, an arrangement in wet foam or a vase if the recipient will not have one (hospitals, offices), and a written card; dictate the message and check the spelling of names.
steps.expect: wrap or vessel matched to where the flowers will sit, card attached and correct.

steps.action: **Attach or request the care card.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* skipped care halves vase life and cannot be recovered. The card (most florists include one, or write it yourself): recut stems 2 cm at an angle under running water, use the food sachet in clean water, refresh water every 2 days, keep away from direct sun, heaters, and the fruit bowl (ripening fruit emits ethylene, which ages flowers fast).
steps.expect: care instructions and a food sachet physically with the bouquet.

steps.action: **Transport flat and cool, deliver on time.** Lay the bouquet flat in the car, out of sun; in hot weather go directly, no errands en route. For services, confirm the delivery window lands when someone is there to receive.
steps.expect: flowers handed over unwilted, at the planned moment.

recipes.verification: The bouquet reached the recipient on time and unwilted, its flowers, colors, and stem count fit the occasion and culture (or were florist-vetted for it), the card carries the intended message with names spelled right, and the food sachet plus care instructions traveled with it.

recipes.title: buy groceries
recipes.name: buy-groceries
recipes.goal: A grocery run that returns home with what the week actually needs — within budget, cold chain respected, nothing crushed, nothing forgotten.

steps.action: **Build the list by category, and eat something first.** Group list items the way stores are laid out: produce / meat-dairy / pantry / frozen / household. Shopping hungry measurably worsens every decision ahead.
steps.expect: a categorized list; you, not starving.

steps.action: **Route the store perimeter-first, frozen-last.** Classic layout: produce → bakery → meat/dairy along the walls, pantry aisles as needed, frozen at the very end so it travels warm-side the least.
steps.expect: cart filling in list order; frozen still in the store's freezer, not your cart, until the end.

steps.action: **Pick produce and dates deliberately.** Produce: firmness/smell over cosmetic perfection; ripeness matched to *when you'll eat it* (bananas for Friday can be green today). Dated goods: reach for dates that outlive your meal plan — and know "best before" is quality, "use by" is safety.
steps.expect: items that survive until their planned meal.

steps.action: **Compare by unit price, not sticker price.** The shelf tag's per-kg/per-100g figure is the honest number; bigger packs win only if you'll finish them.
steps.expect: choices justified by unit price or genuine need, not package theater.

steps.action: **Load the cart with physics in mind.** Heavy/rigid below (cans, bottles), crushables on top (bread, eggs, chips, berries). Same rule again at bagging.
steps.expect: nothing fragile under anything heavy at any stage.

steps.action: **Sweep the list before the checkout line.** One scan of unchecked items — the missing ingredient discovered *now* costs one aisle walk; at home it costs the meal.
steps.expect: every list line checked or consciously dropped.

steps.action: **Check out and bag by destination.** (`daily/pay-at-a-cashier` or `daily/use-a-self-checkout`.) Bag cold-with-cold (they insulate each other), heavy-below again, and chemicals/soaps away from food.
steps.expect: paid, bagged in a scheme that unpacks logically.

steps.action: **Go home reasonably directly and put cold things away first.** Perishables have been out of refrigeration since step 7; frozen and chilled unpack before anything else.
steps.expect: fridge/freezer loaded within the safe window; pantry at leisure; bags stored for next time.

recipes.verification: Home with every list item or a conscious substitute, cold chain unbroken (cold items in the fridge/freezer promptly), nothing crushed, spend within budget, and the next trip's list already collecting what ran out.

recipes.title: buy medicine at a pharmacy
recipes.name: buy-medicine-at-a-pharmacy
recipes.goal: The right over-the-counter medicine for a minor complaint, bought with the pharmacist's free expertise actually used, dosed correctly at home, and escalated to a doctor when the complaint outranks the shelf.

steps.action: **Ask the pharmacist instead of browsing blind.** The counter consult is free expertise most people walk past: state the symptom, its duration, who it is for, and your other medications.
steps.expect: a targeted recommendation, often cheaper than your guess, sometimes the advice that no medicine is needed, occasionally the advice to see a doctor, which is the consult's most valuable output.

steps.action: **Answer the screening questions honestly.** Pregnancy, blood pressure, liver issues, other medicines: these change what is safe (decongestants and hypertension, paracetamol ceilings, drowsy antihistamines and driving).
steps.expect: a recommendation filtered through your actual situation, not the shelf's default.

steps.action: **Choose generic where offered.** The pharmacy's own ibuprofen is the branded one minus the marketing budget; the active ingredient line on the box is the truth (`daily/food/read-food-labels` discipline, medical edition).
steps.expect: the same active ingredient at a fraction of the price, unless a formulation difference genuinely matters.

steps.action: **Confirm the dosing at the counter.** How much, how often, with or without food, for how many days, and what "if it persists" means in days.
steps.expect: a dosing sentence you can repeat back, and the maximum daily dose named aloud for anything containing paracetamol/acetaminophen (the quiet overdose champion because it hides in multi-symptom products).

steps.action: **At home: read the leaflet's three lines that matter and dose as agreed.** Dose, maximum per day, interactions/warnings. One symptom, one product: multi-symptom combos stack duplicate ingredients. ⚠️ *Irreversible in effect:* doubled paracetamol across a "cold & flu" combo plus painkiller tablets is the classic accidental harm; check every box's active ingredients before combining anything.
steps.expect: a single-ingredient regimen you can name, inside the daily maximum.

steps.action: **Set the escalation tripwire when you start.** "If this isn't clearly better by day three, I book the doctor" (`healthcare/book-a-doctors-appointment`), written where you will see it; store the medicine in its box with the leaflet, away from children.
steps.expect: a dated tripwire, and the medicine cabinet holding boxes, not loose foil mysteries.

recipes.verification: The complaint matched the pharmacy's league, the pharmacist's screen shaped the choice, one product with a named active ingredient came home, dosing follows the counter sentence inside the daily maximum, and the escalation tripwire has a date on it.

recipes.title: buy stamps
recipes.name: buy-stamps
recipes.goal: You buy the right postage stamps for mail you plan to send, choosing domestic or international postage and the quantity needed.

steps.action: **Sort the mail destination.** Separate domestic letters from international letters and anything large, thick, or valuable.
steps.expect: each item has a postage category.

steps.action: **Choose a buying channel.** [BRANCH: post office | grocery or pharmacy counter | postal website or kiosk]
steps.expect: you know where you will buy and whether help is available.

steps.action: **Ask for current rates if unsure.** Say the destination and whether it is a standard letter.
steps.expect: the clerk or website shows the current domestic or international amount.

steps.action: **Pick forever or denomination stamps.** For ordinary domestic letters, buy forever stamps if available; for exact-rate needs, buy stated-value stamps.
steps.expect: the stamp value covers the letter at mailing time.

steps.action: **Choose sheet, booklet, or singles.** Buy a sheet or booklet for future use, or singles when you only need one or two international stamps.
steps.expect: quantity matches your likely mail volume.

steps.action: **Pay and inspect the stamps.** Check that the stamps are unused, not torn, and match what you requested.
steps.expect: you receive stamps and a receipt or transaction record.

steps.action: **Store them flat.** Keep stamps dry, away from heat, and in the booklet or envelope they came in.
steps.expect: adhesive and barcodes remain intact.

steps.action: **Apply only when ready to mail.** Put the correct postage in the top right corner and add extra postage if the letter is heavy.
steps.expect: the envelope is ready for a mailbox or counter drop.

recipes.verification: You have unused stamps with enough value for the intended mail class and destination, and any stamped envelope has the postage placed in the top right corner.

recipes.title: change a flat tire
recipes.name: change-a-flat-tire
recipes.goal: Replace a flat tire with the spare tire using the vehicle jack and lug wrench without putting yourself under an unstable car.

steps.action: **Choose the safest stopping place.** Pull well off the road, avoid soft shoulders and slopes, and call roadside help if the location is unsafe.
steps.expect: the car is stable and traffic is not passing close to your body.

steps.action: **Secure the vehicle.** Shift to park or gear, set the parking brake, and place a wheel chock or heavy object opposite the flat if available.
steps.expect: the car does not roll when gently rocked.

steps.action: **Find the jack point.** Use the owner's manual or the notched reinforced point near the flat tire.
steps.expect: the jack saddle lines up with reinforced metal, not plastic trim or a floor pan.

steps.action: **Loosen lug nuts before lifting.** Turn each lug nut counterclockwise about a half turn while the tire is still on the ground.
steps.expect: each nut breaks free without the wheel spinning.

steps.action: **Raise the car only enough.** Jack slowly until the flat tire clears the ground by about 1 inch. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a slipping jack can crush or kill; never put any part of your body under the car.
steps.expect: the jack stands vertical and the tire spins free.

steps.action: **Remove the flat tire.** Finish removing the lug nuts, keep them together, and pull the wheel straight off.
steps.expect: the hub is exposed and no lug nut is missing.

steps.action: **Mount the spare.** Lift the spare onto the studs, then hand-thread all lug nuts with the tapered side facing the wheel.
steps.expect: every nut turns several threads by hand without cross-threading.

steps.action: **Snug in a star pattern.** Tighten the nuts lightly across from each other while the wheel is still raised.
steps.expect: the spare sits flat against the hub.

steps.action: **Lower and tighten firmly.** Lower the car until the tire touches ground, tighten in a star pattern, then lower fully and remove the jack.
steps.expect: the wheel is secure and the car rests normally.

steps.action: **Check pressure and limits.** Read the spare's speed and distance limit, then get the lug torque checked with a torque wrench soon.
steps.expect: you know the temporary spare limit and the flat is stored safely.

recipes.verification: The spare tire is mounted flush, all lug nuts are tightened in a star pattern, the jack is removed, and the car can roll slowly without wobble or scraping.

recipes.title: check tire pressure
recipes.name: check-tire-pressure
recipes.goal: Set each tire to the vehicle maker's recommended cold pressure so the car handles predictably and tires wear evenly.

steps.action: **Find the correct PSI.** Open the driver's door and read the tire placard on the door jamb, not the maximum pressure molded into the tire sidewall.
steps.expect: front and rear PSI targets are known.

steps.action: **Remove the first valve cap.** Put the cap in a pocket or cup holder so it cannot roll away.
steps.expect: the valve stem is exposed and the cap is not on the ground.

steps.action: **Press the gauge on squarely.** Push firmly until the hiss stops and the gauge locks a reading.
steps.expect: one clear PSI number appears without continued air leakage.

steps.action: **Compare to the placard.** [BRANCH: low | high | correct] low needs air, high needs a brief bleed, correct moves to the next tire.
steps.expect: you know the needed adjustment for that tire.

steps.action: **Top up low tires in short bursts.** Add air for a few seconds, then recheck with the gauge instead of guessing by tire shape.
steps.expect: the reading rises toward the placard PSI.

steps.action: **Bleed high tires carefully.** Press the valve pin briefly with the gauge nub or a small tool, then recheck.
steps.expect: the reading drops slowly and stays near target.

steps.action: **Replace the valve cap.** Screw it on finger tight only.
steps.expect: the valve is covered and the cap threads are not crossed.

steps.action: **Repeat for all tires, including the spare if accessible.** Note any tire that was much lower than the rest.
steps.expect: all checked tires match the placard within about 1 PSI.

recipes.verification: Each tire's cold pressure matches the door-jamb placard within about 1 PSI, valve caps are installed, and no valve is hissing.

recipes.title: check your engine oil
recipes.name: check-your-engine-oil
recipes.goal: You confirm the engine oil level is between the minimum and maximum marks and top up with the correct grade if it is low.

steps.action: **Park safely and let the engine cool.** Use level ground, set the parking brake, turn the engine off, and wait several minutes after driving.
steps.expect: the car is stable and the engine bay is not dangerously hot.

steps.action: **Open the hood and locate the dipstick.** Look for a colored loop or handle labeled engine oil; check the manual if unsure.
steps.expect: the dipstick is identified, not the transmission dipstick.

steps.action: **Pull and wipe the dipstick.** Remove it fully and wipe oil off with the rag.
steps.expect: the metal blade is clean enough for a fresh reading.

steps.action: **Reinsert and seat the dipstick fully.** Push it all the way back into its tube, then wait a moment.
steps.expect: the dipstick is seated at its normal depth.

steps.action: **Pull it again and read the level.** Hold it horizontal and look where the oil film reaches relative to Min and Max, Low and Full, or the crosshatched zone.
steps.expect: the oil level is visibly between, below, or above the marks.

steps.action: **Decide whether to top up.** [BRANCH: between marks | below minimum | above maximum] leave it alone if in range, add oil if low, and do not drive hard if overfilled or very low.
steps.expect: the next action matches the reading.

steps.action: **Add small amounts only if low.** Open the oil-fill cap, add the manual-specified grade in small pours, wait, and recheck with the dipstick.
steps.expect: the level moves toward the middle or upper part of the safe range.

steps.action: **Close everything cleanly.** Tighten the oil cap, seat the dipstick, remove the rag, close the hood, and wipe spills.
steps.expect: no tools or rags remain in the engine bay.

recipes.verification: With the engine off, cool, and the vehicle level, the dipstick oil film reads between the Min and Max marks after a wipe, reinsert, and reread.

recipes.title: clean your cars interior
recipes.name: clean-your-cars-interior
recipes.goal: Clean a car interior so trash, dust, crumbs, fingerprints, and odors are reduced without damaging electronics or trim.

steps.action: **Declutter first.** Remove trash, receipts, cups, toys, and loose gear from seats, pockets, and the floor.
steps.expect: only items that belong in the car remain.

steps.action: **Sort personal items.** Put registration, insurance cards, keys, and electronics somewhere safe before using cleaners.
steps.expect: documents and devices are not mixed with trash.

steps.action: **Pull out mats.** Shake mats away from the car and set them aside for vacuuming or washing.
steps.expect: floor carpet and mat surfaces are exposed.

steps.action: **Vacuum high to low.** Vacuum seats, console gaps, floor, under pedals, and trunk areas before wiping surfaces.
steps.expect: crumbs and grit are removed from fabric and crevices.

steps.action: **Brush the vents.** Use a soft brush while vacuuming near the vent slats.
steps.expect: dust lifts from vents without bending slats.

steps.action: **Wipe hard surfaces.** Spray cleaner onto a cloth, not directly onto screens or switches, then wipe dash, console, handles, and cup holders.
steps.expect: surfaces look even and not wet.

steps.action: **Clean buttons and seams.** Wrap the cloth over a fingertip or soft brush for knobs, seams, and cup holder edges.
steps.expect: sticky spots are gone without liquid pooling.

steps.action: **Treat upholstery lightly.** [BRANCH: cloth | leather | vinyl] use the material-appropriate cleaner and avoid soaking seams.
steps.expect: stains lift without dark wet patches.

steps.action: **Clean glass last.** Spray glass cleaner on a cloth and wipe inside windows, mirrors, and windshield.
steps.expect: fingerprints and haze are removed after other dust is finished.

steps.action: **Air out and replace mats.** Let damp areas dry with doors open, then reinstall dry mats securely.
steps.expect: mats are clipped or flat and pedals move freely.

recipes.verification: The cabin has no loose trash, no wet electronics, clear interior glass, dry secured mats, and pedals that move without obstruction.

recipes.title: deal with a car that wont start
recipes.name: deal-with-a-car-that-wont-start
recipes.goal: Diagnose the likely reason a car will not start and choose a safe next action.

steps.action: **Make the location safe.** Shift to park or neutral, set the parking brake, turn on hazard lights if near traffic, and stay visible.
steps.expect: the vehicle will not roll and other drivers can see it.

steps.action: **Check the dashboard and lights.** Turn the key or press start and watch whether interior lights, headlights, and warning lights work.
steps.expect: you know if electrical power is present.

steps.action: **Listen during start.** [BRANCH: rapid clicks | one click | silence | cranks normally but will not start] use the sound to guide the next check.
steps.expect: the symptom category is clear.

steps.action: **Check simple lockouts.** Confirm the transmission is in park or neutral, clutch is pressed if manual, brake pedal is pressed if required, and steering wheel is not locked.
steps.expect: start interlocks are satisfied.

steps.action: **Check the key or fob.** Hold the fob near the start button or use the backup key method from the manual.
steps.expect: the car recognizes the key if fob battery was weak.

steps.action: **Treat dim lights or rapid clicks as a battery problem.** Jump-start only with correct polarity and a safe donor battery or jump pack.
steps.expect: the engine starts or cranks stronger after the jump.

steps.action: **Treat one solid click as possible starter trouble.** Do not keep trying repeatedly if the battery seems strong.
steps.expect: you avoid overheating wiring or draining the battery.

steps.action: **Treat normal cranking as fuel, ignition, or engine-management trouble.** Check fuel level and warning messages, then stop extended cranking.
steps.expect: the battery is preserved for diagnosis or towing.

steps.action: **Call for help when the quick checks fail.** Contact roadside assistance, a mechanic, or emergency services if stopped in a dangerous location.
steps.expect: a jump, tow, or traffic protection is arranged.

recipes.verification: The car starts and can be moved safely, or the likely failure category is identified and roadside assistance, a mechanic, tow, or emergency service has been contacted.

recipes.title: defog a windshield
recipes.name: defog-a-windshield
recipes.goal: You clear interior fog from the windshield quickly and maintain visibility before driving or while driving.

steps.action: **Use the defrost mode.** Turn airflow to the windshield defrost icon.
steps.expect: air starts blowing at the base of the windshield.

steps.action: **Turn on the AC with heat.** Use warm or hot temperature, AC on, and medium-to-high fan. AC dries the air while heat warms the glass.
steps.expect: fog begins thinning from the vent area outward.

steps.action: **Use fresh air, not recirculation.** Turn recirculation off so humid cabin air is replaced with drier outside air.
steps.expect: clearing speeds up instead of fog returning.

steps.action: **Clear side windows and mirrors.** Aim side vents toward front side glass and turn on rear defogger or mirror heat if equipped.
steps.expect: blind-spot visibility improves.

steps.action: **Wait until you can see.** [BRANCH: parked | already driving] stay parked if visibility is poor; if already driving, slow down and keep both hands ready.
steps.expect: the forward view is safe enough for the speed.

steps.action: **Handle exterior frost separately.** If ice or frost is outside the glass, scrape it off before driving; defog settings alone are too slow.
steps.expect: exterior glass is physically clear.

steps.action: **Maintain the setting until stable.** Keep AC, heat, and fresh air on until passengers, wet clothes, or weather stop re-fogging the glass.
steps.expect: the windshield stays clear after the first clearing.

recipes.verification: The windshield and front side windows are clear enough to see lanes, vehicles, pedestrians, signs, and mirrors before normal driving resumes.

recipes.title: donate blood
recipes.name: donate-blood
recipes.goal: Complete a blood donation appointment safely and know what aftercare and deferral rules apply.

steps.action: **Check eligibility before booking.** Review the donor center's current rules for age, weight, illness, pregnancy, tattoos, travel, medications, and prior donations.
steps.expect: no obvious deferral applies, or you know what to ask about.

steps.action: **Schedule the appointment.** [BRANCH: whole blood | platelets or plasma] choose the donation type, time, and location you can complete without rushing.
steps.expect: you have a confirmed slot and estimated visit length.

steps.action: **Prepare your body.** Hydrate well, eat iron-rich food, sleep enough, and avoid arriving hungry.
steps.expect: you feel steady and have urinated normally before leaving.

steps.action: **Check in honestly.** Present ID and answer the health history questions truthfully and privately.
steps.expect: staff either clears you or explains a deferral.

steps.action: **Complete the mini-physical.** Let staff check temperature, pulse, blood pressure, and hemoglobin.
steps.expect: your readings pass the center's thresholds or donation stops.

steps.action: **Donate while still.** Sit or lie back, keep the arm relaxed, and tell staff immediately if you feel dizzy, hot, nauseated, or anxious.
steps.expect: blood flows into the collection bag while staff monitors you.

steps.action: **Recover before leaving.** Keep the bandage on, drink fluids, eat the snack, and sit until staff says you can stand.
steps.expect: you can stand and walk without lightheadedness.

steps.action: **Follow aftercare.** Avoid heavy lifting with that arm, intense exercise, and alcohol for the advised period. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once donated blood leaves your body, you cannot undo the temporary fluid and iron loss.
steps.expect: the puncture site stays dry and you feel normal.

recipes.verification: You have completed check-in, screening, donation or documented deferral, and can leave the site alert with aftercare instructions.

recipes.title: donate used goods
recipes.name: donate-used-goods
recipes.goal: Usable things you no longer need reach an organization that can actually use them, in the condition and manner that helps rather than burdens, and the donate-pile leaves your life for good.

steps.action: **Sort by destination, not just by "donate".** Wearable clothes to the shop pile; ragged textiles to the textile bank pile; books, kitchenware, toys per the venue's accepted list (posted on their sites; many refuse electronics, cots, helmets, and mattresses for safety and law).
steps.expect: piles matched to venues that accept them, and a small honest trash pile that stops pretending.

steps.action: **Prepare the goods like they matter.** Clothes washed (`daily/home/do-the-laundry`) and folded; sets complete and bagged together (game pieces counted, cables with their device); pockets checked (`daily/home/organize-a-closet`'s pocket rule: keys and cards retire with coats constantly).
steps.expect: bags a stranger would be pleased to open.

steps.action: **Check the venue's intake mode before hauling.** Shop drop-off hours, donation-bin locations, or booked collections for furniture; food banks post current-needs lists (they drown in pasta and starve for toiletries, typically).
steps.expect: a confirmed destination, open hours, and for big items a booking.

steps.action: **Deliver during staffed hours where possible.** Hand bags to staff rather than stacking them at a closed door: doorstep dumping is fly-tipping in law and in effect, whatever the intention.
steps.expect: goods handed over, and for taxed jurisdictions a receipt where deductions apply (ask; `us` itemizers especially).

steps.action: **Big furniture and appliances: let collectors come.** Charity furniture services collect free or cheaply and refuse honestly (fire-safety labels on sofas matter legally in some countries); give-away boards move the rest with a "collection only" post and a doorstep handover.
steps.expect: the item leaving through a door you did not carry it through alone.

steps.action: **Close the loop the same day.** The car unloads at the venue, not back into the garage; the give-away post gets deleted once collected; the receipt files where receipts live.
steps.expect: the donate pile extinct, not migrated.

recipes.verification: Every pile reached a venue that accepts its kind, in cleaned complete condition, during staffed hours or by booked collection, with receipts where relevant, and by nightfall the house, the car, and the hallway hold none of it.

recipes.title: drive safely in heavy rain
recipes.name: drive-safely-in-heavy-rain
recipes.goal: You reduce crash risk in heavy rain by slowing down, increasing visibility and following distance, and responding correctly if the car hydroplanes.

steps.action: **Turn on headlights and wipers.** Use low beams, not high beams, and choose a wiper speed that keeps the windshield clear.
steps.expect: other drivers can see you and you can see lane edges.

steps.action: **Slow down below normal speed.** Reduce speed for visibility, standing water, tire condition, and traffic.
steps.expect: you have more time to react and less hydroplaning risk.

steps.action: **Increase following distance.** Leave at least several extra seconds behind the vehicle ahead, more at highway speed.
steps.expect: spray and sudden braking are less dangerous.

steps.action: **Use smooth inputs.** Accelerate, brake, and steer gently; avoid cruise control in heavy rain.
steps.expect: tires keep better contact with the road.

steps.action: **Watch for pooled water.** [BRANCH: shallow spray | deep standing water] drive through shallow water slowly if unavoidable; avoid deep water because depth is hard to judge.
steps.expect: you avoid the deepest water and lane-edge puddles.

steps.action: **Recover from hydroplaning correctly.** If steering feels light or the car floats, ease off the accelerator, keep the wheel pointed where you want to go, and do not brake hard.
steps.expect: tire grip returns gradually.

steps.action: **Pull over when visibility is unsafe.** Use a safe parking lot or far-off-road area if possible; avoid stopping in a travel lane or under a bridge shoulder unless truly necessary.
steps.expect: the car is out of traffic with hazards on if stopped.

steps.action: **Restart only when conditions allow.** Wait for rain, flooding, or visibility to improve before rejoining traffic.
steps.expect: you can see and be seen before moving again.

recipes.verification: You are driving at a rain-appropriate speed with headlights on, extra following distance, clear glass, and no hard braking or abrupt steering.

recipes.title: drive through a roundabout
recipes.name: drive-through-a-roundabout
recipes.goal: You enter, travel through, and exit a roundabout predictably while yielding correctly and protecting pedestrians, cyclists, and nearby drivers.

steps.action: **Slow on approach.** Read lane arrows, destination signs, and crosswalks before the yield line.
steps.expect: you know which lane and exit you need.

steps.action: **Choose the correct lane early.** [BRANCH: right or first exit | straight or later exit] use the lane markings; do not change lanes inside unless markings clearly permit it.
steps.expect: your vehicle is positioned in the proper approach lane.

steps.action: **Yield to pedestrians and cyclists first.** Stop before the crosswalk if anyone is crossing or about to cross.
steps.expect: the crosswalk is clear before you reach the yield line.

steps.action: **Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.** Look left in right-side-driving countries, or toward circulating traffic in your locale. Enter only when there is a safe gap.
steps.expect: you do not make circulating traffic brake for you.

steps.action: **Enter smoothly and keep lane discipline.** Maintain a low steady speed and follow your lane around the circle.
steps.expect: your path is predictable and within lane markings.

steps.action: **Signal before exiting.** Turn on the exit signal after passing the exit before yours, or as local rules require.
steps.expect: waiting drivers and pedestrians can read your intention.

steps.action: **Check the exit crosswalk.** Watch for pedestrians, cyclists, and scooters at the exit, where drivers often accelerate too soon.
steps.expect: the exit path is clear.

steps.action: **Exit without stopping inside.** Leave the roundabout in your lane and cancel the signal.
steps.expect: you are on the intended road and traffic flow remains smooth.

recipes.verification: You exited onto the intended road without forcing circulating traffic to brake, crossing lane markings improperly, or failing to yield to pedestrians.

recipes.title: drop off a prescription
recipes.name: drop-off-a-prescription
recipes.goal: A prescription is handed to a pharmacy, entered with insurance and contact details, and queued for pickup or delivery.

steps.action: **Choose the pharmacy.** Confirm hours, location, and whether it accepts your insurance or discount card.
steps.expect: you know where the prescription will be filled.

steps.action: **Go to the drop-off counter.** Hand the script to pharmacy staff or give the electronic prescription details.
steps.expect: staff can find or scan the prescription.

steps.action: **Verify patient identity.** Provide name, date of birth, phone number, and address if requested.
steps.expect: the pharmacy profile matches the intended patient.

steps.action: **Provide insurance or discount details.** Hand over the insurance card or ask for cash price and available savings programs.
steps.expect: staff can estimate coverage or price.

steps.action: **Confirm medication basics.** Listen for drug name, strength, quantity, and prescriber; correct any mismatch immediately.
steps.expect: the order matches the prescription.

steps.action: **Ask for wait time.** [BRANCH: wait in store | return later | delivery or text notice]
steps.expect: you know when and how pickup will happen.

steps.action: **Leave contact instructions.** Make sure the phone number for questions or pickup texts is correct.
steps.expect: the pharmacy can reach you if insurance or stock is a problem.

steps.action: **Keep the pickup proof.** Save any ticket, app notice, or estimated ready time.
steps.expect: you have a way to identify the pending prescription.

recipes.verification: The pharmacy confirms the prescription is entered for the correct patient with a ready time, pickup method, and price or insurance status.

recipes.title: drop off hazardous waste
recipes.name: drop-off-hazardous-waste
recipes.goal: Dispose of household hazardous waste through an approved facility or collection event without spilling it or putting it in regular trash.

steps.action: **Sort the waste by type.** Separate chemicals, paint, batteries, electronics, bulbs, oil, and sharps if present.
steps.expect: incompatible items are not mixed in one loose pile.

steps.action: **Find the correct program.** [BRANCH: permanent facility | one-day event] use the local waste authority site or phone line to confirm location, hours, residency rules, and quantity limits.
steps.expect: you have an address, date, and accepted-item list.

steps.action: **Keep original labels.** Leave waste in original containers when possible, and label unknown containers with what you believe they contain.
steps.expect: staff can identify each item without opening it.

steps.action: **Seal and contain.** Tighten lids, tape weak caps if needed, and place containers upright in a lined box or tray.
steps.expect: nothing tips or leaks when the box is gently moved.

steps.action: **Load safely.** Put the box in a ventilated cargo area away from passengers, pets, food, and direct sun.
steps.expect: containers remain upright and separated during the drive.

steps.action: **Follow site instructions.** Stay in the directed lane, keep children and pets inside the vehicle, and let staff unload if required.
steps.expect: staff accepts the items or directs you to the right station.

steps.action: **Never abandon rejects.** If an item is refused, ask for the correct disposal route before leaving. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* dumping hazardous waste can contaminate drains, soil, and workers' equipment.
steps.expect: every refused item has a next destination.

steps.action: **Clean up the transport area.** Remove liners, ventilate the vehicle, and wash hands after the drop-off.
steps.expect: there is no residue, odor, or loose debris left behind.

recipes.verification: All accepted hazardous items have been handed to the approved program and no hazardous item was placed in a regular bin.

recipes.title: file a car insurance claim
recipes.name: file-a-car-insurance-claim
recipes.goal: Open a car insurance claim with accurate crash information, a claim number, and a clear next step for repair or payout.

steps.action: **Make the scene safe first.** Move to a safe location if possible, turn on hazards, and call emergency services for injuries, blocked lanes, suspected impairment, or major damage.
steps.expect: people are safer than the vehicles.

steps.action: **Exchange required information.** Get names, phone numbers, driver licenses, plate numbers, insurance details, vehicle descriptions, and witness contacts.
steps.expect: you can identify every involved party.

steps.action: **Document the scene.** Photograph vehicle positions, damage, plates, road signs, signals, skid marks, debris, weather, and injuries if appropriate.
steps.expect: photos show context before vehicles are moved or repaired.

steps.action: **Avoid admitting fault.** Stick to facts with drivers, police, tow operators, and insurers.
steps.expect: you have not guessed blame or accepted private pressure.

steps.action: **Contact your insurer.** [BRANCH: app or web | phone] report the date, time, location, vehicles, people, police report number if any, and what happened.
steps.expect: the insurer opens or prepares a claim.

steps.action: **Record the claim number.** Save the claim number, adjuster contact, repair instructions, rental rules, and upload link.
steps.expect: you can refer to one claim record in later calls.

steps.action: **Ask about deductible and coverage.** Confirm whether collision, comprehensive, liability, uninsured motorist, rental, towing, or glass coverage applies.
steps.expect: you know what costs may come out of pocket.

steps.action: **Follow repair and inspection steps.** Use approved estimates, photos, repair shops, or adjuster appointments as instructed. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* settling or signing a release can close rights, so read payout and injury documents before accepting.
steps.expect: the next claim action is scheduled or submitted.

recipes.verification: The insurer has issued a claim number and you have documented the next required action, deductible status, and contact channel.

recipes.title: fill a propane tank
recipes.name: fill-a-propane-tank
recipes.goal: Get a propane cylinder safely refilled or exchanged, then transport it home upright without leaks.

steps.action: **Inspect the cylinder.** Check for rust, dents, bulges, damaged threads, an expired date stamp, or a missing collar.
steps.expect: the tank looks intact and the date is acceptable to the attendant.

steps.action: **Choose refill or exchange.** [BRANCH: refill | exchange] refill if your tank is in good shape and you want to keep it, or exchange if it is expired, nearly empty, or inconvenient to refill.
steps.expect: you know which counter or cage to use.

steps.action: **Keep ignition sources away.** Turn off cigarettes, grills, heaters, and vehicle engines near the filling area. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* propane can ignite explosively, so do not create flames or sparks around the tank.
steps.expect: the area around the cylinder has no open flame.

steps.action: **Hand the tank to staff.** Let trained staff fill, weigh, or swap the cylinder instead of opening fill valves yourself.
steps.expect: the attendant controls the filling equipment or unlocks the exchange cage.

steps.action: **Confirm the fill limit.** Know that portable cylinders are filled to about 80 percent liquid capacity so vapor has expansion space.
steps.expect: the tank is weighed or filled by an overfill prevention device, not topped to full liquid volume.

steps.action: **Check the valve and leak screen.** Make sure the valve is closed, the outlet is capped if provided, and no hissing or propane smell is present.
steps.expect: the cylinder is quiet and odor-free at the valve.

steps.action: **Pay and get the receipt.** Confirm the price, any exchange deposit, and the cylinder size before paying.
steps.expect: the receipt matches the service and tank size.

steps.action: **Transport upright and ventilated.** Place the tank upright, secure it from tipping, open a window if inside the cabin, and drive directly home.
steps.expect: the cylinder stays vertical and does not roll or heat up.

recipes.verification: The cylinder is upright, valve closed, leak-free by smell and sound, and ready to connect only when outdoors at the appliance.

recipes.title: find a reliable tradesperson
recipes.name: find-a-reliable-tradesperson
recipes.goal: Select a reliable tradesperson for home work by comparing scope, reputation, licensing where relevant, schedule, and payment terms before money changes hands.

steps.action: **Define the job.** Write the issue, location, desired result, and known constraints.
steps.expect: every contractor hears the same scope.

steps.action: **Collect candidate names.** Ask neighbors, building managers, local groups, or trade directories.
steps.expect: at least five possible contacts before filtering.

steps.action: **Screen basics.** Check website, reviews, years in business, photos of similar work, and contact information.
steps.expect: obvious bad fits are removed.

steps.action: **Check license and insurance where relevant.** Search the local license database or ask for license and insurance proof.
steps.expect: regulated trades can be matched to a current credential.

steps.action: **Request three quotes.** Send the same scope and photos to at least three candidates.
steps.expect: responses can be compared on the same job.

steps.action: **Ask for written scope.** Require materials, labor, cleanup, exclusions, timeline, and warranty in writing.
steps.expect: quote details are not just a single price.

steps.action: **Compare more than price.** Weigh responsiveness, clarity, reviews, schedule, and deposit terms.
steps.expect: the best choice is defensible, not only cheapest.

steps.action: **Limit deposits.** Avoid large upfront payments before materials or work begin. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* money sent by cash, wire, or instant transfer may be hard to recover.
steps.expect: payment schedule matches visible progress or material purchase.

steps.action: **Confirm access and logistics.** Agree on date, arrival window, parking, pets, shutoffs, and cleanup.
steps.expect: both sides know how the workday will run.

steps.action: **Keep records.** Save messages, quote, license proof, receipts, and photos before work starts.
steps.expect: there is a paper trail if the job changes.

recipes.verification: You have chosen one tradesperson with a written scope, checked reputation and license where relevant, compared at least three quotes or documented why fewer were available, and agreed to payment terms.

recipes.title: get a car safety inspection
recipes.name: get-a-car-safety-inspection
recipes.goal: Complete a required or voluntary vehicle safety inspection and know what to do if the car passes or fails.

steps.action: **Check the inspection rules.** Confirm timing, approved stations, fees, and whether emissions testing is separate.
steps.expect: you know the correct inspection type and deadline.

steps.action: **Book or choose a station.** [BRANCH: appointment | walk-in] schedule a slot if required, or pick an approved station with posted inspection service.
steps.expect: the station can inspect your vehicle class.

steps.action: **Do a quick pre-check.** Test headlights, brake lights, turn signals, horn, wipers, tire tread, mirrors, and seat belts.
steps.expect: obvious simple failures are found before paying.

steps.action: **Bring documents and arrive clean enough.** Take registration, insurance, ID if required, and remove clutter blocking belts or inspection points.
steps.expect: the inspector can access the vehicle and paperwork.

steps.action: **Authorize only the inspection first.** Ask what is included and whether repairs require separate approval.
steps.expect: you understand the inspection fee and repair consent process.

steps.action: **Review checked systems.** Expect checks of brakes, steering, suspension, lights, tires, glass, wipers, horn, emissions equipment where applicable, and safety restraints.
steps.expect: the station performs the required checklist.

steps.action: **Handle the result.** [BRANCH: pass | fail] accept the sticker or certificate if it passes, or get a written failure report and retest rules if it fails.
steps.expect: you leave with proof of pass or a repair list.

steps.action: **Complete retest if needed.** Repair required items, keep receipts, and return within any retest window. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* driving an unsafe or expired-inspection vehicle can create legal and crash risk, so confirm the allowed window.
steps.expect: the vehicle is reinspected or scheduled before the deadline.

recipes.verification: The vehicle has a valid inspection sticker, certificate, or electronic pass record for the required inspection period.

recipes.title: get a document notarized
recipes.name: get-a-document-notarized
recipes.goal: Your document carries a valid notarial certificate (stamp/seal and the notary's signature), executed correctly for the certificate type the receiving party requires, and it is accepted on submission.

steps.action: **Confirm the document actually needs notarization and which type.** Read the receiving party's instructions or the document's pre-printed certificate wording. Many forms only need a witness or a certified copy, which are different services.
steps.expect: you can name the required act (acknowledgment, jurat/affidavit, certified copy, or signature witnessing).

steps.action: **Do not sign the document yet.** [BRANCH: jurat required → the signature must happen in the notary's presence, full stop | acknowledgment required → pre-signing is technically allowed in many places, but signing in front of the notary is always safe] The universal rule: arrive with it unsigned.
steps.expect: signature lines still blank when you leave home.

steps.action: **Find a notary and confirm scope before traveling.** Options: your bank (often free for account holders), shipping/office stores, courthouses and law offices, mobile notaries (they come to you, at a travel premium), or remote online notarization where the receiving party accepts it. Call ahead: confirm they can handle your document type, all signers can attend, and the fee.
steps.expect: an appointment or confirmed walk-in window, quoted fee, and confirmation they will notarize this document class (some refuse wills or immigration forms).

steps.action: **Bring every required signer, their IDs, and the whole document.** All signers appear in person with unexpired photo ID; bring all pages, not just the signature page, since the notary may need to see what is being signed.
steps.expect: everyone present, IDs in hand, complete document on the table.

steps.action: **Present ID and sign exactly as the document names you.** The notary checks each ID against the document. Sign in the notary's presence, matching the printed name form (middle initial included if the document prints one).
steps.expect: signatures placed while the notary watches; names on ID, document, and signature consistent.

steps.action: **The notary completes the certificate, seals, and records the act.** They fill the certificate block (venue, date, names, act type), sign, apply the stamp or embossed seal, and log it in their journal. Verify the certificate wording matches what the receiving party specified and that the date and names are correct before you leave. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an executed and submitted notarization cannot be quietly amended; errors caught after submission mean redoing the document.
steps.expect: legible seal, notary signature, correct date and names, and the certificate type you needed.

steps.action: **Pay and take copies.** Fees are commonly per signature or per seal and are capped by law in many jurisdictions; mobile travel fees are separate. Photograph or scan the executed document before submitting the original.
steps.expect: receipt, plus a scan of the sealed document in your files.

recipes.verification: The document bears a legible notary seal and signature, a fully completed certificate block of the type the receiving party specified, dates and all names are correct and consistent with the IDs shown, every signer signed in the required manner, and you hold a scan plus the fee receipt.

recipes.title: get a flat tire repaired
recipes.name: get-a-flat-tire-repaired
recipes.goal: Have a flat tire inspected and repaired safely, or replaced if the damage cannot be repaired.

steps.action: **Avoid driving on the flat.** Stop before the sidewall is crushed or the rim is damaged, and use a spare or tow if needed.
steps.expect: the tire is not being destroyed by continued driving.

steps.action: **Locate the suspected puncture.** Look for a nail, screw, cut, sidewall bulge, or slow leak, but do not remove objects before the shop sees it.
steps.expect: you can tell the shop what happened.

steps.action: **Call or visit a tire shop.** Ask whether they repair punctures, expected wait, cost, and whether appointment or walk-in is better.
steps.expect: the shop can inspect the tire.

steps.action: **Explain temporary driving.** Tell the shop if you drove on it flat, used sealant, or installed a spare.
steps.expect: the technician knows what hidden damage to check.

steps.action: **Ask plug versus patch.** [BRANCH: patch-plug repair | replacement] prefer an internal patch-plug for repairable tread punctures, or replace if damage is unsafe.
steps.expect: the shop explains the repair method.

steps.action: **Confirm repairability.** Make sure the puncture is in the tread area, not the sidewall or shoulder, and not too large or near another repair.
steps.expect: the technician either approves repair or shows why it cannot be repaired.

steps.action: **Authorize the work.** Approve repair, replacement, balancing, valve stem, or rotation only after price and tire match are clear. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* removing and discarding a tire ends any chance to reuse it, so confirm it is unrepairable first.
steps.expect: the work order matches your decision.

steps.action: **Reinstall and check pressure.** Have the repaired or replacement tire installed, torqued, inflated, and the spare stored properly.
steps.expect: the car drives normally and the tire-pressure warning clears or is explained.

recipes.verification: The repaired or replacement tire holds recommended pressure, is mounted and torqued, and the spare or damaged tire is accounted for.

recipes.title: get a flu shot at a pharmacy
recipes.name: get-a-flu-shot-at-a-pharmacy
recipes.goal: Receive a seasonal flu vaccine at a pharmacy and leave with a record that can be used for school, work, or medical files.

steps.action: **Choose walk-in or appointment.** [BRANCH: walk-in | appointment] check the pharmacy website or call for vaccine hours, or book a time online.
steps.expect: you know when the immunizing pharmacist is available.

steps.action: **Bring documents.** Pack ID, insurance card, and any vaccine form from school or work.
steps.expect: documents are easy to reach at check-in.

steps.action: **Wear accessible clothing.** Choose a short sleeve or loose sleeve that exposes the upper arm.
steps.expect: the shoulder can be uncovered without undressing in the pharmacy.

steps.action: **Check in at the pharmacy counter.** Say you are there for a flu shot and give your name or appointment time.
steps.expect: staff provide a consent form or direct you to a waiting area.

steps.action: **Complete screening honestly.** List allergies, illness today, pregnancy status if relevant, and past reactions.
steps.expect: the pharmacist confirms whether vaccination can proceed.

steps.action: **Confirm cost before the shot.** Ask what insurance covers or what the cash price is.
steps.expect: you know whether payment is due before vaccination.

steps.action: **Choose the arm.** Pick the non-dominant arm unless you prefer the other side for sleeping or work.
steps.expect: the pharmacist has a clear injection site on the upper arm.

steps.action: **Receive the shot.** Relax the shoulder and let the arm hang loose.
steps.expect: a quick pinch, then a bandage or cotton on the site.

steps.action: **Wait if instructed.** Stay nearby for 10 to 15 minutes if the pharmacy asks, especially after prior reactions.
steps.expect: no immediate dizziness, breathing trouble, or rash.

steps.action: **Get the record.** Ask for printed or digital proof showing vaccine name and date.
steps.expect: you leave with documentation or know where it appears online.

steps.action: **Do aftercare.** Move the arm normally, drink water, and use usual pain relief only if appropriate for you.
steps.expect: soreness is mild and improves over 1 to 2 days.

recipes.verification: You received the flu shot, have no urgent reaction before leaving, and possess a dated vaccination record from the pharmacy.

recipes.title: get a haircut
recipes.name: get-a-haircut
recipes.goal: You leave a barbershop/salon with a haircut you asked for, having communicated it well enough that "what you asked for" and "what you wanted" were the same thing.

steps.action: **Arrive on time (appointment) or check in and take the queue (walk-in).** Give your name at the desk; waiting is `daily/wait-in-line` with magazines.
steps.expect: you're in the system; rough wait known.

steps.action: **Brief the cutter before any water or clippers touch you.** The three-part brief: overall goal ("shorter but still combable"), the numbers/lengths where you know them ("2 on the sides, scissor top"), and the photo if you have one. State the *don'ts* too ("keep the fringe long enough to sweep").
steps.expect: they play it back or ask sharpening questions ("skin fade or leave weight?") — a cutter who asks questions is a good sign.

steps.action: **Answer the process questions honestly.** Wash first? Product you normally use? How long since the last cut? These calibrate them.
steps.expect: brief agreed; cape on.

steps.action: **Stay still, and speak up early — not at the end.** Head where they place it; phone down (it tilts your head). If something looks shorter/different than briefed *say it at the first sign*: "That's about the shortest I'd want on the sides." Mid-cut corrections are cheap; end-state ones are haircuts you wear for a month.
steps.expect: course corrections absorbed while they still matter.

steps.action: **Use the mirror check as a real checkpoint, not a formality.** When shown the back with the hand mirror: actually look — back hairline, sideburn evenness, the blend. Request touch-ups now: "Could you square the neckline a bit more?"
steps.expect: touch-ups done; you've approved the actual cut, not performed approval.

steps.action: **Pay and tip per local custom, and log the result.** Note (in your phone, honestly) what you asked for in whose language it worked: "Maria — 3 side, finger-length top, thinned."
steps.expect: paid; the successful spec recorded so next time starts from a known-good state.

recipes.verification: The mirror check was a genuine approval, the result matches the brief (or the agreed mid-cut revision), payment and tip are settled, and the spec that worked is written down for next time.

recipes.title: get a suit tailored
recipes.name: get-a-suit-tailored
recipes.goal: Have a suit adjusted so the jacket and trousers fit cleanly for your body and intended shoes.

steps.action: **Wear the right base layers.** Put on the dress shirt, shoes, and belt or suspenders that match the suit use.
steps.expect: the tailor measures the suit in the same setup you will wear.

steps.action: **State the fit goal.** Tell the tailor whether you want classic, slim, conservative business, wedding, or comfort-first fit.
steps.expect: the tailor understands the target silhouette and deadline.

steps.action: **Ask what is adjustable.** Confirm likely changes such as trouser hem, waist, seat, taper, sleeve length, jacket waist, collar roll, and button stance limits.
steps.expect: the tailor explains what can and cannot be altered cleanly.

steps.action: **Stand naturally for measurements.** Keep feet flat, arms relaxed, and posture normal while the tailor measures and marks.
steps.expect: pins or chalk reflect your usual stance rather than a posed one.

steps.action: **Test movement while pinned.** Sit, reach forward, button the jacket, put hands in pockets, and walk.
steps.expect: pinned fabric looks clean without pulling, twisting, or restricting normal movement.

steps.action: **Approve the alteration plan.** [BRANCH: simple hem | major tailoring] confirm each change, cost, and pickup date before leaving. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cutting fabric cannot be fully undone, so confirm length and taper before work starts.
steps.expect: the ticket lists the agreed alterations.

steps.action: **Pick up and re-check.** Try on the suit at pickup with the same shoes and shirt, not over casual clothes.
steps.expect: hems, sleeves, waist, and jacket shape match the pinned plan.

steps.action: **Request corrections immediately.** Point out puckers, uneven hems, tightness, or loose areas before taking the suit away.
steps.expect: the tailor either fixes it on the spot or writes a follow-up ticket.

recipes.verification: The suit lies smooth while standing, permits sitting and walking, and the tailor ticket is closed with no unresolved fit issue.

recipes.title: get car insurance quotes
recipes.name: get-car-insurance-quotes
recipes.goal: Collect comparable car insurance quotes and identify the best value for the coverage you actually need.

steps.action: **Gather current coverage.** Pull your declarations page or write down liability limits, collision, comprehensive, uninsured motorist, medical coverages, deductibles, and extras.
steps.expect: you have a baseline policy to match.

steps.action: **Prepare driver and vehicle information.** Collect VIN, mileage, use type, annual distance, parking location, safety features, and driver histories.
steps.expect: each quote can be entered consistently.

steps.action: **Choose quote sources.** [BRANCH: direct insurers | broker or comparison site] use at least three sources and include one human agent if your situation is complex.
steps.expect: you have multiple legitimate quote channels.

steps.action: **Compare like for like.** Set the same liability limits, deductibles, excess, rental coverage, roadside assistance, and optional endorsements across quotes.
steps.expect: price differences are not caused by hidden lower coverage.

steps.action: **Test deductible tradeoffs.** Raise or lower collision and comprehensive deductibles only to amounts you could pay after a claim.
steps.expect: you can see how excess affects premium.

steps.action: **Check discounts and terms.** Ask about bundling, mileage, telematics, student, defensive driving, anti-theft, and paid-in-full discounts.
steps.expect: each quote includes applicable discounts and policy fees.

steps.action: **Review claim reputation.** Look at complaint indexes, repair network rules, rental limits, and customer service reputation.
steps.expect: the cheapest quote is not evaluated on price alone.

steps.action: **Save quote details.** Keep quote numbers, effective dates, coverage pages, and expiration times before deciding. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not cancel an old policy until the new policy is bound and active.
steps.expect: you can bind coverage without a gap.

recipes.verification: You have at least three quote records with matching core coverages, clear deductibles or excess, total premium, and effective dates.

recipes.title: get keys copied
recipes.name: get-keys-copied
recipes.goal: You leave the shop with a working duplicate key that has been proven in the actual lock it is meant to open.

steps.action: **Identify what kind of key you have.** [BRANCH: standard house/padlock key (plain brass/nickel, no electronics) → any hardware store or kiosk | car key with a plastic head → likely contains a transponder chip; a plain metal copy will turn the door but not start the engine, see Decision points | key stamped "DO NOT DUPLICATE" or a patented/restricted profile → locksmith with your authorization, see Decision points | USPS cluster mailbox key → cannot be legally duplicated; replacements go through the postal service]
steps.expect: you know which counter to walk to before leaving home.

steps.action: **Go to the cutting station and hand over the original.** At a hardware store, ask staff; at a kiosk (MinuteKey, KeyMe and similar), insert the key as prompted.
steps.expect: the machine or clerk finds a matching blank; "we don't have that blank" means a locksmith trip instead, not a "close enough" blank.

steps.action: **Choose the blank.** Plain brass is fine; decorated blanks work identically. If offered a thickness or headshape choice, match the original.
steps.expect: blank and original side by side with identical profile (the ridged silhouette along the blade).

steps.action: **Have it cut.** Duplication takes about a minute per key: the original guides a stylus while a wheel cuts the blank.
steps.expect: a freshly cut key, warm, with visible burrs on the teeth.

steps.action: **Ask for deburring.** Most cutters brush the key automatically; if the teeth feel sharp or gritty, ask for a pass on the wire wheel. Burrs are the top cause of a new key sticking.
steps.expect: teeth smooth to the thumb.

steps.action: **Pay, then test immediately in the real lock.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* discovering a bad copy at your door at midnight is the failure this whole recipe prevents; do not skip the test. Insert fully, turn both directions, repeat three times, and also re-test the original. [BRANCH: lock is at home → test the same day before you need the key | lock is nearby → test before leaving the area]
steps.expect: the copy turns as smoothly as the original.

steps.action: **Label and distribute.** Mark the copy (tag or paint pen, never the address it opens) and hand it to its intended holder.
steps.expect: copy identifiable in a drawer six months from now, and not traceable to your door if lost.

recipes.verification: The duplicate has been inserted and turned in the target lock at least three times without force, the original still works, and the copy is labeled without revealing what address it opens.

recipes.title: get shoes repaired
recipes.name: get-shoes-repaired
recipes.goal: Your shoes are assessed, left with a cobbler under an agreed price and pickup date, and come back wearable for another season, or you have made an informed decision to replace them instead.

steps.action: **Triage repairability at home.** Repair-friendly: leather or suede uppers, stitched (welted) soles, worn heel tips, broken zippers on boots, stretched or loose stitching, detached but intact soles. Repair-hostile: crumbling foam midsoles (hydrolyzed PU turns to powder with age), fast-fashion shoes where glue is the only thing holding them together, knit sneaker uppers torn at the flex point.
steps.expect: a genuine candidate, or an early honest decision to replace.

steps.action: **Do the cost math before you go.** Rules of thumb: heel tips are cheap and always worth it; half-soles and heels cost a mid-double-digit amount; a full resole on welted shoes can approach half the price of new. Repair is usually rational when the uppers are sound and the quote lands under about half of replacement cost.
steps.expect: a walk-away price in your head before anyone quotes you.

steps.action: **Brief the cobbler specifically.** Point at each problem and say what outcome you want: "new heel tips", "restitch this seam", "resole, keep the leather sole" (or "switch to rubber"). Also ask what *they* see; a good cobbler will flag the failing counter or dried-out sole you missed.
steps.expect: a per-item quote and their read on whether the shoe is worth it. A cobbler who says "not worth repairing" is giving you free, reliable advice.

steps.action: **Agree the full terms before handing them over.** Price, pickup date, and any materials choice (leather vs rubber sole, hardware color). [BRANCH: quote under your walk-away price → proceed | over it → thank them and take the shoes; no partial commitments]
steps.expect: one number, one date, no "we'll see when we open it up" without a cap.

steps.action: **Get the claim ticket.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* many shops release shoes only against the physical ticket, and unclaimed pairs are disposed of or donated after a posted period (often 30 to 90 days). Photograph the ticket immediately.
steps.expect: ticket in hand and photographed, pickup date written on it.

steps.action: **Pick up on time and inspect at the counter.** Check the specific repairs, flex the sole, verify heel tips are seated flush, look inside for stray nails on heel work. Raise anything before paying, while the shoes are still their responsibility.
steps.expect: the briefed items visibly fixed; pairs match in color after any refinishing.

steps.action: **Pay and break them back in gently.** Resoled shoes are stiff for the first few wears; wear them dry days first.
steps.expect: payment done, shoes home, first wear planned indoors or on a short day.

recipes.verification: The specific faults you briefed are fixed and pass a counter inspection (flush heel tips, continuous sole bond, matching finish), you paid the pre-agreed price, and the shoes survive their first full day of wear without the repair lifting.

recipes.title: handle a tire blowout
recipes.name: handle-a-tire-blowout
recipes.goal: Keep control of the vehicle during a tire blowout and stop in a safe location.

steps.action: **Grip the wheel firmly.** Hold the vehicle straight and resist the pull toward the failed tire.
steps.expect: the vehicle stays in its lane as much as possible.

steps.action: **Do not brake hard.** Ease off the accelerator and avoid sudden steering.
steps.expect: speed begins dropping without weight shifting abruptly.

steps.action: **Keep the vehicle pointed straight.** Make only small corrections to stay in the lane.
steps.expect: swerving is minimized.

steps.action: **Let the car coast down.** Allow speed to fall before changing lanes or pulling over.
steps.expect: the vehicle becomes easier to control.

steps.action: **Signal when you have control.** Turn on hazard lights and signal toward a shoulder or safe exit.
steps.expect: nearby drivers can see you are slowing.

steps.action: **Move off the travel lane gradually.** Steer to a wide shoulder, exit ramp, parking lot, or other safe area.
steps.expect: the car leaves traffic without a sharp maneuver.

steps.action: **Stop on level ground if possible.** Park away from traffic, set the parking brake, and keep wheels turned away from the road if on a slope.
steps.expect: the vehicle is stable.

steps.action: **Exit only if safe.** Leave from the side away from traffic, or stay buckled with hazards on if the roadside is unsafe.
steps.expect: people are not standing next to traffic.

steps.action: **Call roadside assistance if needed.** Request a tow or tire change, especially on highways, narrow shoulders, or bad weather.
steps.expect: help is arranged without roadside exposure.

recipes.verification: The vehicle is stopped out of traffic or emergency help is called, hazard lights are on, passengers are protected from traffic, and the failed tire is handled by a safe change or tow.

recipes.title: inspect a used car before buying
recipes.name: inspect-a-used-car-before-buying
recipes.goal: Inspect a used car enough to decide whether to walk away, negotiate, or pay for a mechanic pre-purchase inspection.

steps.action: **Match identity documents.** Compare the VIN on the dashboard, door jamb, title or registration, listing, and history report.
steps.expect: all VIN records match exactly.

steps.action: **Review history and title status.** Check accident history, branded title, mileage records, ownership gaps, recalls, and service records.
steps.expect: the story is consistent with the odometer and seller claims.

steps.action: **Inspect panels and paint.** Look for uneven gaps, overspray, mismatched paint, rust, cracked glass, water stains, and repaired structural areas.
steps.expect: body condition matches the price and history.

steps.action: **Check tires and brakes visually.** Look for uneven tread wear, old date codes, mismatched tires, curb damage, and visible brake rotor scoring.
steps.expect: tire and brake condition does not hide immediate major cost.

steps.action: **Open the hood cold.** [BRANCH: cold engine | already warm] prefer cold start; check oil, coolant, belts, hoses, battery, leaks, and smells before running.
steps.expect: fluids look plausible and no fresh leak is obvious.

steps.action: **Start and observe.** Watch for smoke, rough idle, warning lights, delayed engagement, unusual exhaust smell, and overheating.
steps.expect: warning lights turn off and the idle stabilizes.

steps.action: **Test drive deliberately.** Drive varied roads and test steering, braking, acceleration, transmission shifts, suspension noise, cruise, climate, and electronics.
steps.expect: the car behaves consistently under normal use.

steps.action: **Book a mechanic inspection.** If still interested, arrange an independent pre-purchase inspection before paying. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* buying without title and mechanical checks can leave you with unrecoverable repair costs.
steps.expect: a mechanic can inspect or you decide to walk away.

recipes.verification: VIN, title story, visible condition, cold start, test drive, and mechanic inspection plan all support either a walk-away or a justified offer.

recipes.title: join a gym
recipes.name: join-a-gym
recipes.goal: You hold an active gym membership whose real monthly cost, commitment length, and exact cancellation procedure you understood before signing.

steps.action: **Visit at the hour you will actually train.** A gym at 2pm tells you nothing about the 6pm squat-rack queue. Walk in and ask for a tour; any decent gym gives one free.
steps.expect: a tour granted during your real workout window.

steps.action: **Run the tour checklist.** Count people waiting for the equipment you care about; check machines for out-of-order tags and frayed cables; inspect locker rooms and showers for cleanliness; note ventilation and whether staff are on the floor.
steps.expect: mental notes on crowding, maintenance, and hygiene; more than one or two dead machines is a maintenance-budget signal.

steps.action: **Ask for a trial pass before any contract talk.** [BRANCH: free day/week pass offered → train once at your normal hour before deciding | no trial at all → treat as a yellow flag and raise your contract scrutiny]
steps.expect: either a trial workout completed or a conscious decision to proceed without one.

steps.action: **Get the full price in writing, itemized.** Monthly fee, joining/initiation fee, any "annual maintenance fee" (the classic hidden charge, often billed in month 3), and class or towel add-ons.
steps.expect: a single total figure for year-one cost, not just the headline monthly rate.

steps.action: **Read the cancellation clause before anything else in the contract.** How many days' notice, from what date, delivered how (many chains still require certified mail or an in-person form, not email), and what an early exit from a fixed term costs.
steps.expect: you can state the exact steps and cost of leaving; if the rep cannot show you the clause, do not sign today.

steps.action: **Check the other standard traps.** Auto-renewal into a new fixed term versus rolling monthly; price-increase clauses; whether "freeze" (pause) options exist for travel or injury; transfer rules if you move.
steps.expect: each answered from the contract text, not from the rep's verbal assurances.

steps.action: **Negotiate before signing.** Initiation fees are waived routinely near month-end when reps chase quotas; ask directly. Month-to-month at a slightly higher rate usually beats a 12-month commitment unless you have trained consistently for a year already.
steps.expect: at least one concession, or confirmation the price is genuinely fixed.

steps.action: **Sign, keep the counter-signed copy, and confirm billing.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a fixed-term direct-debit agreement commits real money; verify the amount and the term on the paper matches the verbal offer before signing.
steps.expect: your own copy of the contract, membership card or app access active, and first billing date noted in your calendar.

recipes.verification: You can enter the gym with your card or app, your contract copy states the same monthly price and term you agreed verbally, the exact cancellation procedure is written in your notes or calendar, and the first billing matches the itemized total from step 4.

recipes.title: jump start a car
recipes.name: jump-start-a-car
recipes.goal: Start a car with a weak battery using another car or jump pack without reversing polarity, sparking at the battery, or touching moving parts.

steps.action: **Position the power source.** Park the good car close enough for cables to reach, but keep the vehicles from touching.
steps.expect: both batteries are reachable and the cable path avoids belts, fans, and hot exhaust.

steps.action: **Turn everything off.** Switch off ignitions, lights, climate controls, radios, and chargers in both cars.
steps.expect: dashboards are dark except any unavoidable security indicators.

steps.action: **Identify terminals and bare metal.** Find dead positive, good positive, good negative, and an unpainted metal ground on the dead car away from the battery.
steps.expect: plus and minus marks are visible and the ground point is solid engine or chassis metal.

steps.action: **Connect red to dead positive.** Clamp the red cable to the dead battery positive terminal.
steps.expect: the clamp grips clean metal and does not touch any other part.

steps.action: **Connect red to good positive.** Clamp the other red end to the good battery positive terminal.
steps.expect: both red clamps are on positive terminals only.

steps.action: **Connect black to good negative.** Clamp the black cable to the good battery negative terminal.
steps.expect: the black clamp is secure on the good car negative post.

steps.action: **Connect black to dead-car metal ground.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* wrong cable order or polarity can damage electronics or ignite battery gas; confirm red is on positive before placing this final black clamp.
steps.expect: the final black clamp is on bare metal away from the dead battery.

steps.action: **Start the good car, then the dead car.** Run the good car for 2 to 5 minutes, then crank the dead car for no more than 5 seconds at a time.
steps.expect: the dead car starts or the starter sound improves after each rest.

steps.action: **Remove cables in reverse order.** Remove black from dead-car metal, black from good negative, red from good positive, then red from dead positive.
steps.expect: no clamp touches another clamp or loose metal during removal.

steps.action: **Keep the revived car running.** Drive or idle it in a safe place for at least 20 minutes, then arrange a battery and charging-system check.
steps.expect: the engine keeps running after cables are removed.

recipes.verification: The revived car starts, cables are removed in reverse order, all clamps are clear of metal, and both vehicles show no warning smoke, smell, or exposed cable damage.

recipes.title: mail a letter
recipes.name: mail-a-letter
recipes.goal: A letter or document is correctly addressed, stamped, and entered into the postal system toward its recipient.
