steps.action: **Fold and insert the contents; seal the envelope.** Fold to fit without bulging; moisten or peel-and-stick the flap.
steps.expect: envelope flat, sealed on all edges, contents not shifting the shape.

steps.action: **Write the recipient's address in the addressee zone.** Front of the envelope, centered-to-lower-right, in this line order: name / street address + number (apartment on the same or next line) / city + postal code (order varies by country) / COUNTRY in capitals for international. Legible ink, no cursive flourishes on the postal code.
steps.expect: address complete per that structure; postal code present and correct — verify it, misdirected codes are the top delivery failure.

steps.action: **Write your return address in the sender zone.** Top-left corner (or the back flap, in some countries).
steps.expect: a deliverable return path exists if delivery fails.

steps.action: **Determine required postage.** Standard-size letter under the weight limit (~20 g/1 oz) inside the country: one standard stamp. [BRANCH: heavier/rigid/oversized → weigh at a post office | international → international rate]
steps.expect: you know the rate class; when unsure, the post-office counter is the authority.

steps.action: **Affix the stamp(s) in the top-right corner.** Total face value ≥ the required rate.
steps.expect: stamps flat and firmly stuck in the corner.

steps.action: **Enter it into the postal stream.** [BRANCH: public mailbox (check the collection-time plate — a drop after today's last collection goes out tomorrow) | post-office counter (required for weighing, international customs forms, or tracked options)] ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a mailbox drop cannot be retrieved — confirm the address and contents before the slot.
steps.expect: letter through the slot, or a counter receipt.

steps.action: **For anything that matters, get proof.** Tracked/registered mail at the counter yields a tracking number — the only way to later prove sending.
steps.expect: receipt with tracking number stored, if chosen.

recipes.verification: The letter is in the postal stream (slot dropped after checking the collection time, or counter receipt in hand), addressed with verified postal code and return address, with tracking recorded when it mattered.

recipes.title: merge onto a highway
recipes.name: merge-onto-a-highway
recipes.goal: You use the entrance ramp to match highway speed, choose a safe gap, and merge smoothly without surprising highway traffic.

steps.action: **Read the ramp early.** Check signs, curve, ramp length, and whether the lane becomes an exit-only or add lane.
steps.expect: you know how much space you have to accelerate.

steps.action: **Signal before the merge area.** Turn on the signal while still on the ramp, not after drifting toward traffic.
steps.expect: highway drivers can see your intent.

steps.action: **Accelerate to match traffic.** Use the ramp to approach the speed of the lane you will enter, within weather and legal limits.
steps.expect: your speed is close enough that only a small adjustment is needed.

steps.action: **Find the gap, not the car.** Look for open space between vehicles, then adjust speed to arrive beside that space.
steps.expect: a specific gap is selected.

steps.action: **Check mirrors and blind spot.** [BRANCH: clear gap | blocked gap] merge if clear; if blocked, adjust speed and choose the next gap.
steps.expect: no vehicle is hidden beside your rear quarter.

steps.action: **Commit smoothly.** Steer gently into the lane while maintaining speed, then center the vehicle in the lane.
steps.expect: the merge is one controlled movement, not a hesitation across the line.

steps.action: **Cancel the signal and rebuild space.** Once fully in the lane, leave a following gap and match traffic flow.
steps.expect: you are established in the highway lane with safe space ahead.

steps.action: **Use the shoulder only as an emergency escape.** If the ramp ends and no safe gap exists, avoid stopping in the lane; use available escape space only if needed to prevent a collision.
steps.expect: the vehicle remains controlled and visible.

recipes.verification: You are fully in the highway lane at a speed close to traffic, with your signal canceled and safe space ahead and behind.

recipes.title: negotiate a used car price
recipes.name: negotiate-a-used-car-price
recipes.goal: Negotiate a used car price using market value, inspection findings, and an out-the-door number you are willing to pay.

steps.action: **Research fair value.** Compare guide values, sold listings where available, dealer listings, private listings, mileage, options, and title status.
steps.expect: you have a realistic price range, not one number.

steps.action: **List leverage items.** Note tires, brakes, fluids, warning lights, cosmetic damage, missing keys, accident history, overdue services, and inspection findings.
steps.expect: every price objection is tied to evidence.

steps.action: **Decide your walk-away number.** Include purchase price, taxes, dealer fees, registration, immediate repairs, insurance, and financing cost.
steps.expect: you know the highest out-the-door price you will accept.

steps.action: **Ask for the seller's best basis.** Have the seller explain their price and included fees before making your offer.
steps.expect: hidden costs or confidence in pricing become visible.

steps.action: **Make a calm lower offer.** [BRANCH: private seller | dealer] start below your target with evidence, while staying polite and specific.
steps.expect: the seller counters, accepts, or refuses without confusion.

steps.action: **Negotiate out-the-door.** Focus on the final total including taxes, document fees, add-ons, delivery, registration, and required repairs.
steps.expect: the number you compare is the total amount due.

steps.action: **Use inspection results carefully.** Ask for a price reduction, repair before sale, or credit for mechanic-confirmed issues.
steps.expect: the seller addresses concrete defects rather than vague complaints.

steps.action: **Pause before committing.** Leave or take time if the seller pressures you, changes terms, or asks for a rushed deposit. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing purchase documents or paying a nonrefundable deposit can lock the deal, so verify title, price, and conditions first.
steps.expect: any agreement is written and matches your walk-away number.

recipes.verification: The agreed written out-the-door price is at or below your maximum and accounts for title status, condition, fees, and known repairs.

recipes.title: parallel park
recipes.name: parallel-park
recipes.goal: Park a car parallel to the curb inside a street space without touching another vehicle or blocking traffic.

steps.action: **Choose a forgiving space.** Pass spaces shorter than 1.5 car lengths or beside fire hydrants, driveways, bus stops, or corners.
steps.expect: a legal space with a clear entry angle and no hidden curb obstruction.

steps.action: **Signal and stop beside the front car.** Pull even with the parked car ahead of the space, about 2 to 3 feet away, with rear bumpers roughly aligned.
steps.expect: your right side mirror is near the other car's left mirror and traffic can see your signal.

steps.action: **Check all directions before reversing.** Look over both shoulders, then use mirrors and the backup camera if present.
steps.expect: no cyclist, pedestrian, or car is entering your path.

steps.action: **Reverse with the wheel turned toward the curb.** Back slowly until your rear inside corner points toward the curb and the rear car appears in the outside mirror.
steps.expect: your car sits at about a 45 degree angle into the space.

steps.action: **Straighten while continuing back.** Turn the wheel back to center and reverse until your front bumper clears the rear bumper of the front car.
steps.expect: the front bumper can swing inward without clipping the car ahead.

steps.action: **Turn away from the curb to tuck in.** Rotate the wheel fully away from the curb and ease back.
steps.expect: the front end swings into the space and the car becomes parallel to the curb.

steps.action: **Center the car with small moves.** [BRANCH: too far from curb | too close to curb] if too far, pull forward with wheel toward curb; if too close, pull forward with wheel away, then straighten.
steps.expect: tires are 6 to 12 inches from the curb and bumpers have space at both ends.

steps.action: **Secure the parked car.** Straighten the wheels unless parking on a hill, shift to park or gear, and set the parking brake.
steps.expect: the car is still, legal, and not sticking into the lane.

recipes.verification: The car is parallel to the curb, 6 to 12 inches from it, fully inside the marked or legal space, and has visible bumper clearance front and rear.

recipes.title: park in a parking garage
recipes.name: park-in-a-parking-garage
recipes.goal: A car parked in a multi-story garage, its location retrievable hours later, and the exit paid and cleared without holding a queue at the barrier.

steps.action: **Enter and take the ticket, or badge in.** Pull close to the machine, take the ticket (or tap the card/app the garage uses), wait for the barrier to fully rise before moving.
steps.expect: barrier up, ticket in hand; the ticket goes with you, never stays in the car (payment machines and some exit checks need it, and thieves read tickets as receipts).

steps.action: **Drive the ramps at walking-pace caution.** Headlights on, hard lefts and rights around blind pillars, yield to reversing cars and pedestrians surging from stairwells.
steps.expect: steady progress upward; no surprises at the ramp bends.

steps.action: **Choose a spot for the return trip, not just the entry.** Near a stair or lift core beats near the entrance ramp; wider spots beat tight pillar-side ones (door dings live by pillars); note lighting if returning late.
steps.expect: a spot you can reverse out of and find again.

steps.action: **Park straight, fold mirrors where tight, and record the location.** Photo of the level marker and row sign (or drop a pin in the garage's app); valuables out of sight or with you.
steps.expect: a photo or note that answers "level, color, row" hours later; a cabin showing nothing worth breaking a window for.

steps.action: **Before leaving the garage: find and pay at the machine (pay-on-foot systems).** Most garages want payment at the walk-in machine *before* returning to the car; the ticket validates for a short exit window. [BRANCH: pay-on-foot machine → pay now, keep the validated ticket | pay-at-exit barrier → pay when leaving | app/plate-recognition → nothing to do]
steps.expect: the system's mode identified on the way in or at the machine, and a validated ticket where that mode applies.

steps.action: **Return, load, and exit within the window.** Retrieve the car (the photo does its work), reverse out with a full look for walkers, follow exit arrows, insert the validated ticket or tap at the barrier.
steps.expect: barrier up on the first try; no reversing against one-way ramps.

recipes.verification: The car sits straight in a findable, exit-friendly spot recorded by photo; payment matched the garage's mode; and the exit barrier rose on the first presentation with no queue collected behind you.

recipes.title: pick up a package from the post office
recipes.name: pick-up-a-package-from-the-post-office
recipes.goal: Collect a held package from a post office or postal pickup point using the delivery notice, ID, and any required authorization.

steps.action: **Read the notice.** Check pickup address, available date, carrier, and any barcode or item number.
steps.expect: you know where the package is held and when it is ready.

steps.action: **Check the hold window.** Look for the last pickup date before return to sender.
steps.expect: the deadline is clear and still in the future.

steps.action: **Gather ID.** Bring photo ID and proof of address if the ID address may not match.
steps.expect: your name or address can be matched to the package.

steps.action: **Bring authorization if needed.** If collecting for another person, have their signed slip or carrier-approved authorization.
steps.expect: staff can release the item without guessing.

steps.action: **Choose counter or locker.** [BRANCH: staffed counter | parcel locker] follow the notice for counter pickup or use the locker code or QR code.
steps.expect: you are in the correct pickup line or at the correct locker bank.

steps.action: **Present the slip or tracking.** Hand over the notice or show the barcode on your phone.
steps.expect: staff can scan or type the item number.

steps.action: **Show ID when asked.** Keep the ID visible until staff finish matching it.
steps.expect: staff accept the identity check or explain what is missing.

steps.action: **Inspect the package label.** Confirm recipient name and address before accepting.
steps.expect: the package is yours or clearly authorized.

steps.action: **Sign if required.** Sign the handheld device or paper form only after confirming the item. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signature may mark delivery complete, so verify the package first.
steps.expect: the carrier record shows pickup completed.

steps.action: **Carry it out securely.** Use both hands for heavy packages and keep small parcels zipped in a bag.
steps.expect: package leaves with you undamaged.

recipes.verification: You leave the pickup location with the correct package, and tracking or the receipt shows the item was picked up or delivered.

recipes.title: refuel a car
recipes.name: refuel-a-car
recipes.goal: The car's tank is filled with the *correct* fuel, paid for, and you drive off with the cap closed and nothing on fire.

steps.action: **Pull up with the filler side toward the pump; engine off.** No smoking, and leave the phone call for later — attention, not radiation, is the real reason.
steps.expect: filler flap within hose reach; engine and cabin ignition sources off.

steps.action: **Open the fuel door and uncap.** Release lever/button inside the car if it has one; hang or rest the cap per its tether.
steps.expect: open filler neck.

steps.action: **Authorize payment.** [BRANCH: card/phone at the pump → follow the screen | prepay inside → tell the cashier the pump number and amount | attended station → state fuel + amount and let them work]
steps.expect: pump display resets to zero and shows "ready"/lifts to live.

steps.action: **Select the correct fuel and lift that nozzle.** Diesel nozzles are usually larger and color-coded differently — the *label*, not the hose color, is the truth. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* pumping the wrong fuel (especially petrol into diesel) means do-not-start-the-engine and a drained tank — triple-check the label against the flap sticker.
steps.expect: nozzle in hand matching the car's required fuel exactly.

steps.action: **Insert the nozzle fully into the filler neck and squeeze; latch if fitted.**
steps.expect: fuel flowing, counter running; stay at the nozzle — this is not the moment to wander inside.

steps.action: **Stop at the auto-click.** The first click means full — do not round up with extra squeezes ("topping off" floods the vapor system and spills).
steps.expect: flow stopped by itself; counter shows the final amount.

steps.action: **Return the nozzle, cap the tank until it clicks, close the flap.**
steps.expect: cap clicked (a loose cap triggers the check-engine light later); flap flush.

steps.action: **Collect the receipt and depart.** Prepay-inside stations: settle up if you pumped an open amount.
steps.expect: paid in full; receipt if wanted; pump area left as found.

recipes.verification: The pumped fuel type matches the flap sticker, the auto-click ended the fill with no topping-off, the cap clicked shut, payment is settled, and the gauge reads full as you pull away.

recipes.title: register as an organ donor
recipes.name: register-as-an-organ-donor
recipes.goal: Record your organ donor decision in the official registry and make sure your family knows your preference.

steps.action: **Find the official registry.** Use a government health, motor vehicle, or recognized donation organization site for your location.
steps.expect: the page clearly identifies the registry authority.

steps.action: **Review what registration means.** Read which organs and tissues may be donated and when donation decisions are considered.
steps.expect: you understand that donation is evaluated only after death or for specific living donation programs.

steps.action: **Enter your identity details.** Provide the required name, birth date, address, ID number, or account login.
steps.expect: the form accepts your identity information.

steps.action: **Select your donor preference.** [BRANCH: register broadly | limit donation] choose the default donor option or any allowed limits for organs, tissues, research, or transplant use.
steps.expect: the selected preference is shown before submission.

steps.action: **Submit the registration.** Confirm the details before final submission. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* this records a legal medical preference until you update it, so verify your identity and choice first.
steps.expect: the registry shows a confirmation page, email, card, or app status.

steps.action: **Save proof accessibly.** Add the donor status to your license, wallet card, health app, or personal records if offered.
steps.expect: you can find evidence of your donor status quickly.

steps.action: **Tell your family.** Tell your next of kin or emergency contact that you registered and what you want.
steps.expect: at least one person likely to be contacted knows your decision.

steps.action: **Note how to change it.** Save the registry link or account method for updating or withdrawing later.
steps.expect: you know where to edit the preference if your decision changes.

recipes.verification: The official registry, license record, donor card, or app shows your current donor preference and a family contact has been told.

recipes.title: renew a library book
recipes.name: renew-a-library-book
recipes.goal: A borrowed library item has its due date extended, or you learn why renewal is blocked and what to do next.

steps.action: **Check the due date.** Look at your receipt, account, app, or reminder email.
steps.expect: you know which item needs renewal and when it is due.

steps.action: **Open a renewal channel.** [BRANCH: website | mobile app | phone | service desk]
steps.expect: you reach a place that can access your loans.

steps.action: **Sign in or identify yourself.** Enter card number and PIN, or give the staff member your card and name.
steps.expect: your borrowed items list is visible or read back.

steps.action: **Select the item.** Choose the book or other material you want to renew, not the whole account unless that is intended.
steps.expect: the item shows a renewal option or a block reason.

steps.action: **Request renewal.** Click renew, tap renew, or ask staff to renew it.
steps.expect: the system accepts the request or explains the denial.

steps.action: **Read the new date.** Write down, screenshot, or save the updated due date.
steps.expect: the item now has a later due date.

steps.action: **Handle blocked renewals.** If a hold, renewal limit, billed status, or overdue rule blocks it, ask for the return deadline and options.
steps.expect: you know whether to return, pay, or talk to staff.

steps.action: **Set a reminder.** Put the new due date in a calendar or reminder app.
steps.expect: you will be warned before the next deadline.

recipes.verification: The library account or staff confirmation shows the exact item title with a due date later than the previous due date.

recipes.title: renew your car registration
recipes.name: renew-your-car-registration
recipes.goal: Renew your vehicle registration before the deadline and place any new sticker or document where required.

steps.action: **Read the renewal reminder.** Check the plate number, VIN, expiration date, fee, and any missing requirement listed.
steps.expect: you know the deadline and what blocks renewal.

steps.action: **Gather documents.** Have registration notice, plate number, VIN, odometer if requested, insurance proof, inspection result, emissions result, and payment.
steps.expect: the renewal form can be completed without searching mid-process.

steps.action: **Choose the renewal channel.** [BRANCH: online | mail or in-person] use online if eligible, or choose a licensing office, kiosk, or mail option if documents need review.
steps.expect: you are using an accepted channel for your vehicle.

steps.action: **Confirm vehicle and owner details.** Verify name, address, plate, VIN, and vehicle description before paying.
steps.expect: the renewal shows the correct vehicle and mailing address.

steps.action: **Pay the fees.** Submit the required fee and save the receipt or confirmation number. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* renewal fees and penalties may not be refundable, so confirm the plate and VIN first.
steps.expect: payment is accepted and a confirmation appears.

steps.action: **Receive the proof.** Download, print, or wait for the registration card, sticker, decal, or electronic record.
steps.expect: you have temporary or final proof of renewal.

steps.action: **Install the sticker correctly.** Clean the plate or windshield area and apply the new sticker exactly where local rules specify.
steps.expect: the displayed month or year matches the renewed period.

steps.action: **Store the document.** Put the registration card in the vehicle or approved digital wallet, and discard old copies that could confuse a stop.
steps.expect: the vehicle carries current proof.

recipes.verification: The vehicle record, registration card, or sticker shows a current expiration date for the correct plate and VIN.

recipes.title: replace a key fob battery
recipes.name: replace-a-key-fob-battery
recipes.goal: Replace a weak key fob battery while preserving the case, buttons, and battery orientation.

steps.action: **Remove the mechanical key if present.** Press the release and slide the key blade out of the fob.
steps.expect: the hidden seam or pry slot is easier to access.

steps.action: **Find the case seam.** Look for a notch, slot, or split line instead of prying at a random edge.
steps.expect: you know where the case is designed to open.

steps.action: **Pry the case gently.** Twist a coin or plastic pry tool in the slot while supporting both halves.
steps.expect: the case begins to separate without cracking.

steps.action: **Open over the table.** Lift the cover slowly so buttons, gasket, or circuit board pieces do not fall.
steps.expect: the inside layout remains in place.

steps.action: **Note the battery type.** Read the printed code, such as CR2032 or CR2025, before removing it.
steps.expect: the replacement type is confirmed.

steps.action: **Record the orientation.** Check whether the plus side faces up or down.
steps.expect: you know exactly which face of the new battery should be visible.

steps.action: **Swap the battery.** Slide the old cell out and insert the new one with the same orientation.
steps.expect: the battery sits flat under the contact tabs.

steps.action: **Snap the case shut.** Align the halves and press around the edges until clips seat.
steps.expect: the seam is even and no buttons are trapped.

steps.action: **Reinstall the mechanical key.** Slide it back until it clicks.
steps.expect: the key blade is locked into the fob.

steps.action: **Test close and at range.** Press lock or unlock near the car, then from several parking spaces away.
steps.expect: the car responds reliably at both distances.

recipes.verification: The fob locks or unlocks the vehicle from normal walking distance and the case is fully closed with all buttons moving freely.

recipes.title: replace a windshield wiper
recipes.name: replace-a-windshield-wiper
recipes.goal: Replace a worn windshield wiper blade with the correct size so it clears water without streaking or scratching the glass.

steps.action: **Measure or confirm the blade size.** Check the owner's manual, parts lookup, or the old blade length before opening the package.
steps.expect: each side's blade length is known and the new blades match.

steps.action: **Lift one wiper arm carefully.** Raise it until it holds itself away from the windshield, then lay a folded towel under the bare arm path.
steps.expect: the arm is stable and the glass is protected.

steps.action: **Find the release tab.** Rotate the blade slightly and look for the tab, latch, or button where the blade meets the arm.
steps.expect: the locking point is visible before you pull.

steps.action: **Release the old blade.** [BRANCH: tab | button | clip] press the tab, push the button, or open the clip while sliding the blade off the arm.
steps.expect: the blade separates without bending the arm.

steps.action: **Keep control of the arm.** Hold the metal arm with one hand while the blade is off. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a dropped bare arm can crack or scratch the windshield, so do not let it snap down.
steps.expect: the arm stays raised and controlled.

steps.action: **Install the new blade.** Slide or click the new blade into the same connector path until the lock seats.
steps.expect: you hear or feel a firm click and the blade cannot slide free with a light tug.

steps.action: **Lower the blade onto the towel.** Guide the arm down slowly, then remove the towel after the rubber rests on the glass.
steps.expect: the rubber edge sits flat against the windshield.

steps.action: **Repeat on the other side.** Match the second blade to its side because left and right lengths may differ.
steps.expect: both new blades are installed and locked.

steps.action: **Test with washer fluid.** Turn the key to accessory mode if needed and run the washers with one wipe cycle.
steps.expect: both blades sweep smoothly without chatter or hitting trim.

steps.action: **Do the smear check.** Look through the cleaned area in daylight or with headlights on glass.
steps.expect: no broad streaks, missed arcs, or oily smears remain.

recipes.verification: Both wiper blades are locked to the arms, sweep the windshield without contact or chatter, and leave a clear view after one washer cycle.

recipes.title: return an item without a receipt
recipes.name: return-an-item-without-a-receipt
recipes.goal: Attempt a store return without the original receipt, using alternate proof where available and accepting the realistic outcome if only store credit is offered.

steps.action: **Check the return policy.** Look online or call before traveling.
steps.expect: you know the return window, excluded items, and no-receipt rule.

steps.action: **Gather proof alternatives.** Bring the payment card, loyalty number, order email, gift giver details, or bank statement.
steps.expect: at least one clue can help staff find the purchase.

steps.action: **Restore the package.** Put accessories, manuals, tags, and boxes together.
steps.expect: the item looks complete and resellable if it is unused.

steps.action: **Inspect condition honestly.** Note damage, missing parts, or use before reaching the counter.
steps.expect: you can describe the item without surprise.

steps.action: **Go to customer service.** Bring ID and say you would like to return or exchange without a receipt.
steps.expect: staff ask for proof, ID, or the item barcode.

steps.action: **Offer lookup options.** [BRANCH: card lookup | loyalty lookup | order lookup] provide the method that most likely matches the purchase.
steps.expect: staff either find the transaction or confirm they cannot.

steps.action: **Ask for the available outcome.** If no receipt is found, ask whether exchange or store credit is possible.
steps.expect: staff state the refund amount and form.

steps.action: **Decide before accepting.** Compare store credit, exchange, or keeping the item. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once processed, the return may void warranties or promotional pricing.
steps.expect: you choose knowingly before the item is taken.

steps.action: **Complete the return.** Provide ID or signature only if you accept the policy.
steps.expect: you receive store credit, exchange item, refund, or denial explanation.

steps.action: **Keep the return proof.** Save the receipt, gift card slip, or email.
steps.expect: you have a record showing value and date.

recipes.verification: The store has either processed the return with documented value and form, or clearly denied it under policy while you still have the item.

recipes.title: return deposit bottles
recipes.name: return-deposit-bottles
recipes.goal: Accumulated deposit bottles and cans go back through a return machine (or counter), and the deposit comes back to you as cash or store credit.

steps.action: **Sort eligible from ineligible at home.** Deposit logo/mark present, barcode intact, container empty and roughly rinsed (machines and their rooms smell of everyone who skips this).
steps.expect: a bag of machine-ready containers; juice cartons and unmarked glass left out.

steps.action: **Find the return machine.** Usually near the store entrance or a dedicated room.
steps.expect: a machine with a round feed hole, a display, and a receipt button; note any posted limits (some cap counts or accept only what the store sells).

steps.action: **Feed containers one at a time, barcode roughly along the roller.** The machine rotates and scans each; rhythm beats speed.
steps.expect: per-container beep + count/value ticking up on the display; rejected ones come back — set them aside, keep feeding (F1 handles the rejects after).

steps.action: **Retry rejects once, correctly oriented and un-dented.** Gently reshape a dented can's barcode zone; a second rejection means the machine doesn't take it (foreign barcode, non-deposit, unreadable) — into your recycling stream instead (`daily/home/sort-recycling`).
steps.expect: every container either counted or consciously reclassified.

steps.action: **Press the receipt/finish button.** ⚠️ *Irreversible-ish:* walking away without pressing it donates your total to the next person.
steps.expect: a printed voucher showing the total.

steps.action: **Redeem the voucher at the checkout.** Cash out, or apply it against your groceries (`daily/errands/buy-groceries` synergy: bring bottles, leave with dinner partially paid). Vouchers often expire and are store-specific — redeem today.
steps.expect: deposit value in hand or off your bill.

recipes.verification: Every container is counted, redeemed, or reclassified to recycling; the voucher's total made it into cash or your grocery bill; and no crushed rejects went back home with you.

recipes.title: sell your car privately
recipes.name: sell-your-car-privately
recipes.goal: Sell your car privately with an honest listing, safer buyer screening, scam-aware payment, and proper title transfer.

steps.action: **Clean and document the car.** Wash it, remove personal items, gather service records, title status, manuals, keys, and take clear photos.
steps.expect: the car can be represented accurately.

steps.action: **Price with evidence.** Compare similar mileage, trim, condition, accident history, and local listings.
steps.expect: your asking price has a defensible range.

steps.action: **Write an honest listing.** Include VIN if comfortable, mileage, title status, maintenance, defects, tire condition, features, and reason for sale.
steps.expect: serious buyers can pre-screen the car.

steps.action: **Screen inquiries.** [BRANCH: serious buyer | suspicious buyer] answer normal questions, reject overpayment, shipping-agent, code-verification, and rushed-payment messages.
steps.expect: you schedule only plausible buyers.

steps.action: **Meet safely.** Use a public lot, police exchange zone, or bank, bring another person if possible, and verify license before any test drive.
steps.expect: the meeting location and driver identity feel controlled.

steps.action: **Handle test drives.** Ride along or set clear terms, keep possession of your keys and documents, and avoid leaving the buyer alone with the car.
steps.expect: the car returns and no documents are missing.

steps.action: **Use scam-safe payment.** Prefer verified bank cashier process, in-bank transfer, or cleared electronic payment before releasing title and keys. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing over title before verified payment can permanently lose the car.
steps.expect: funds are verified by your bank, not just a screenshot or email.

steps.action: **Transfer title and notify authorities.** Complete bill of sale, odometer statement, lien release if needed, plates, release of liability, and registration cancellation as local rules require.
steps.expect: ownership and liability are no longer tied to you.

recipes.verification: Payment is verified, title transfer paperwork is complete, release of liability is filed if required, and copies of sale documents are saved.

recipes.title: take a dog for a walk
recipes.name: take-a-dog-for-a-walk
recipes.goal: Take a dog outside for exercise, toileting, and enrichment while keeping the dog, other people, and other animals safe.

steps.action: **Fit the gear.** Attach the leash to a secure collar or harness, check that the dog cannot back out, and confirm ID is on the dog.
steps.expect: the leash connection holds with gentle tension.

steps.action: **Pack the basics.** Bring poop bags, keys, phone if needed, and water for heat, long routes, puppies, seniors, or flat-faced breeds.
steps.expect: you can clean up and handle delays without returning immediately.

steps.action: **Check heat and pavement.** Touch the pavement with the back of your hand for several seconds and choose shade, grass, booties, or a shorter walk if it is too hot.
steps.expect: the route will not burn paws or overheat the dog.

steps.action: **Start with attention.** Ask for a simple cue or pause at the door so the dog exits without bolting.
steps.expect: the first movement outside is controlled.

steps.action: **Use loose-leash basics.** Keep the leash short enough for safety but slack when possible, reward the dog near your side, and stop or change direction when pulling hard begins.
steps.expect: the dog learns that slack leash movement keeps the walk going.

steps.action: **Allow sniffing breaks.** Build in safe sniff stops away from traffic, yards, and hazards.
steps.expect: the dog gets mental enrichment without dragging you.

steps.action: **Follow greeting rules.** [BRANCH: greeting allowed | greeting skipped] ask the other handler before dog-to-dog contact, keep leashes loose, and pass by if either dog stiffens, stares, barks, or pulls.
steps.expect: greetings happen only with mutual permission and calm bodies.

steps.action: **Clean up promptly.** Pick up feces with a bag, tie it closed, and carry it to a trash bin.
steps.expect: the sidewalk or grass is left clean.

steps.action: **Return and check the dog.** Offer water, check paws for cuts or debris, and remove gear after the dog is indoors.
steps.expect: the dog settles with no limping, coughing, or heat distress.

recipes.verification: The dog returns home safely exercised or toileted, waste is disposed of, and no heat, paw, leash, or greeting problem remains unresolved.

recipes.title: take a pet to the vet
recipes.name: take-a-pet-to-the-vet
recipes.goal: The pet has been examined by a veterinarian, you leave with a clear diagnosis or plan, written care instructions, and a booked follow-up if one is needed.

steps.action: **Start carrier acclimation days ahead, not the morning of.** Leave the carrier open in the living space with bedding and treats inside so it stops predicting doom. A carrier that only appears for vet trips guarantees a fight.
steps.expect: the pet enters the carrier voluntarily at least once before the appointment day.

steps.action: **Write symptom notes with dates and specifics.** When it started, frequency, appetite, water intake, stool/urine changes, current medications with doses. Film any intermittent behavior (limping, coughing, seizure-like episodes) on your phone; symptoms hide in exam rooms.
steps.expect: a dated note and any video ready on your phone.

steps.action: **Confirm pre-visit instructions when booking.** Ask whether to withhold food (possible bloodwork or sedation) and whether to bring a fresh stool sample.
steps.expect: fasting yes/no and sample yes/no explicitly answered.

steps.action: **Load and secure the pet for transport.** Cat: into the carrier rear-first or lowered in top-down, door latched, a towel over the carrier to cut visual stress. Dog: harness clipped, carrier or seat-belt tether in the car.
steps.expect: carrier latched and seat-belted flat on the seat or footwell; no loose animal in the car.

steps.action: **Check in and keep the pet contained in the waiting room.** Carrier stays closed and off the floor if possible; keep dogs at leash length from other animals, many of whom are sick or scared.
steps.expect: checked in; pet contained and reasonably settled until called.

steps.action: **During the exam, restrain only as the staff direct.** Trained staff handle the actual restraint; your job is a calm voice and steady hands where asked. Never grab a panicking animal's scruff or muzzle on your own initiative.
steps.expect: the vet completes the exam; you have relayed the symptom notes and shown any video.

steps.action: **Ask the closing questions before anyone reaches for the door.** What is the diagnosis or the differential? What does this medication do, dose and duration, and key side effects? What signs mean come back immediately? What is the total cost of the proposed plan?
steps.expect: answers you could repeat back; written or printed instructions in hand.

steps.action: **Pay, book the follow-up, and get records.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* consenting to surgery, euthanasia, or other major procedures cannot be walked back; ask for the estimate in writing and take time to decide unless it is a true emergency.
steps.expect: receipt, follow-up date if needed, and copies of new records or vaccine certificates.

recipes.verification: The pet is back home and settled, you hold written instructions you can act on (or a clean bill of health), any medication schedule is understood with first dose timed, and a follow-up appointment exists if the vet said one was needed.

recipes.title: test drive a car
recipes.name: test-drive-a-car
recipes.goal: Evaluate a car on a varied route without sales pressure and decide whether it deserves further consideration.

steps.action: **Request a cold start.** Ask that the car not be warmed up before you arrive, then start it yourself if allowed.
steps.expect: the engine starts cleanly without smoke, long cranking, or warning lights.

steps.action: **Set the route.** [BRANCH: dealer route | your route] include stop-and-go traffic, turns, bumps, braking, parking, and higher-speed driving if allowed.
steps.expect: the seller agrees to enough variety for evaluation.

steps.action: **Check controls before moving.** Adjust seat, mirrors, steering wheel, climate, visibility, infotainment basics, and driver assists.
steps.expect: you can sit comfortably and see safely.

steps.action: **Listen at low speed.** Drive slowly with the radio off and note clunks, squeaks, steering play, brake noise, or transmission hesitation.
steps.expect: the car moves smoothly without obvious mechanical complaints.

steps.action: **Test acceleration and braking.** Accelerate moderately, brake progressively, and check whether the car pulls, shudders, or smells hot.
steps.expect: power and braking feel predictable.

steps.action: **Drive at speed.** On a safe road, hold steady speed and feel for vibration, wind noise, tracking issues, or gear hunting.
steps.expect: the car tracks straight and feels settled.

steps.action: **Park and inspect again.** Try reverse, tight turns, parking sensors, camera, and look underneath for new drips.
steps.expect: parking systems work and no fresh leak appears.

steps.action: **Leave without pressure.** Tell the seller you need time to review notes and compare options. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not place a nonrefundable deposit from test-drive excitement until price, inspection, title, and financing are checked.
steps.expect: you leave with notes, not an impulse commitment.

recipes.verification: You have driven the car on varied roads, checked cold-start behavior, and recorded any concerns before discussing purchase terms.

recipes.title: tip a delivery driver
recipes.name: tip-a-delivery-driver
recipes.goal: Leave a fair delivery tip using cash or the app, with adjustments for effort and conditions.

steps.action: **Check whether a service fee is not a tip.** Look at the checkout or receipt line items before assuming the driver receives the fee.
steps.expect: tip amount is a separate line or still unset.

steps.action: **Start from a normal percentage.** Use about 15% to 20% for standard food delivery, with a practical floor for small orders.
steps.expect: the calculated amount is not tiny just because the order was cheap.

steps.action: **Bump for extra effort.** Add more for bad weather, long distance, heavy bags, many drinks, stairs, parking difficulty, or late-night delivery.
steps.expect: the tip reflects driver effort, not only food price.

steps.action: **Choose cash or app.** [BRANCH: cash | app] cash works well at the door if you have bills. app works when contactless or pre-tipping is required.
steps.expect: you have a clear way to hand off or submit the tip.

steps.action: **Set the app tip before delivery when needed.** Some drivers see expected payout before accepting.
steps.expect: the order is less likely to sit unaccepted.

steps.action: **Keep cash visible and ready.** If tipping cash, separate it before the driver arrives.
steps.expect: the handoff does not make the driver wait.

steps.action: **Adjust after delivery only for real service issues.** Missing restaurant items are often not the driver's fault; unsafe behavior or ignored instructions may be.
steps.expect: any change is tied to driver-controlled behavior.

steps.action: **Confirm the final amount.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once submitted or handed over, a tip may not be recoverable; check decimal placement and currency first.
steps.expect: the receipt or cash handoff matches your intended amount.

steps.action: **Save the receipt.** Keep the app receipt or note the cash amount if you track spending.
steps.expect: the total cost is visible later.

recipes.verification: The driver receives a separate tip amount you intentionally chose, and the receipt or cash handoff confirms it.

recipes.title: top up windshield washer fluid
recipes.name: top-up-windshield-washer-fluid
recipes.goal: You fill the windshield washer reservoir with the correct washer fluid and confirm the sprayers work.

steps.action: **Park and open the hood safely.** Stop on level ground, turn the engine off, set the parking brake, and use the hood prop if needed.
steps.expect: the hood stays open securely.

steps.action: **Find the washer reservoir.** Look for the cap with a windshield spray symbol, often blue. Do not use the coolant reservoir, brake fluid reservoir, or oil fill.
steps.expect: the washer-fluid fill neck is identified.

steps.action: **Confirm it is not coolant.** Coolant reservoirs often have warning labels, pressure caps, colored coolant, and hot-system warnings. Washer fluid is usually a simple flip cap.
steps.expect: you are certain the blue-cap reservoir is for windshield washer fluid.

steps.action: **Open the cap and pour slowly.** Use a funnel if the neck is narrow, and keep dirt out of the reservoir.
steps.expect: fluid enters the washer reservoir without spilling into the engine bay.

steps.action: **Fill to the line or near full.** Stop at the marked fill line if present; otherwise stop before overflowing.
steps.expect: the reservoir is filled without liquid running out.

steps.action: **Close the cap and hood.** Snap the cap shut, remove the bottle and funnel, and close the hood securely.
steps.expect: nothing is left loose under the hood.

steps.action: **Test the washer spray.** [BRANCH: front windshield | rear window] activate the sprayer briefly and check that fluid reaches the glass.
steps.expect: spray hits the windshield or rear window and wipers clear it.

recipes.verification: The washer reservoir is filled with season-appropriate washer fluid, the cap is closed, and the washer spray reaches the windshield when tested.

recipes.title: use a coin or air pump
recipes.name: use-a-coin-or-air-pump
recipes.goal: Inflate car tires at a coin or station air pump to the correct cold tire pressure without overinflating.

steps.action: **Find the correct PSI.** Read the door jamb sticker, not the maximum PSI molded on the tire sidewall.
steps.expect: you know the front and rear target pressures.

steps.action: **Park near the pump.** Pull close enough for the hose to reach all tires and set the parking brake.
steps.expect: the car is stable and the hose reaches at least the nearest tire.

steps.action: **Set the pump if digital.** [BRANCH: preset pump | manual gauge] enter the target PSI on a preset pump, or keep your own gauge ready for manual filling.
steps.expect: the pump is ready to inflate to the chosen pressure.

steps.action: **Remove the valve cap.** Unscrew the cap and place it in a pocket or safe spot.
steps.expect: the valve stem is exposed and the cap is not lost.

steps.action: **Attach the chuck firmly.** Press the air chuck straight onto the valve stem until leaking air stops.
steps.expect: the hose connection seals with little or no hiss.

steps.action: **Inflate in bursts.** Add air for short bursts, then pause for the gauge or pump reading.
steps.expect: pressure rises gradually toward the target.

steps.action: **Check and adjust.** Remove the chuck, check PSI, add more air or press the valve pin briefly to release excess. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* driving on badly overinflated or underinflated tires can reduce control, so correct pressure before leaving.
steps.expect: the tire reads at the recommended PSI.

steps.action: **Replace the cap and repeat.** Screw the cap back on and repeat for each tire, including the spare if accessible.
steps.expect: every checked tire has a cap and target pressure.

recipes.verification: Each tire you intended to inflate reads the door-jamb PSI and has its valve cap installed.

recipes.title: use a coinstar
recipes.name: use-a-coinstar
recipes.goal: Loose coins are converted at a Coinstar-style kiosk into a cash voucher, gift card, or donation receipt.

steps.action: **Pre-sort obvious junk.** Spread coins on a tray or table and remove anything that is not a valid local coin.
steps.expect: no sharp, sticky, or foreign objects are mixed in.

steps.action: **Find a working kiosk.** Check the screen, coin tray, reject slot, and printer area before starting.
steps.expect: the kiosk is on and not showing out-of-service.

steps.action: **Choose the payout type.** [BRANCH: cash voucher with fee | gift card with no fee if offered | charity donation]
steps.expect: the screen shows the fee or no-fee terms before counting.

steps.action: **Accept the terms.** Read the percentage fee and redemption instructions, then continue only if acceptable.
steps.expect: the machine is ready for coins.

steps.action: **Pour slowly.** Tip coins into the tray at a steady rate instead of dumping the whole container at once.
steps.expect: coins feed without backing up or spilling.

steps.action: **Check rejects.** Pull rejected coins from the return slot, wipe dirty coins, and feed valid ones once more.
steps.expect: only unreadable, foreign, or damaged coins remain rejected.

steps.action: **Finish counting.** Tap done only after the tray and return slot are empty.
steps.expect: the final total appears on screen.

steps.action: **Print and redeem.** Take the voucher or gift-card code and redeem it at the register or keep it as instructed. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once printed or donated, payout type usually cannot be changed; confirm the total and option first.
steps.expect: you receive cash, a gift card claim, or a donation receipt.

recipes.verification: You leave with cash, a valid gift-card claim, or a donation receipt matching the kiosk's printed final total after any stated fee.

recipes.title: use a drive through
recipes.name: use-a-drive-through
recipes.goal: Food or drink is ordered, paid for, received, and checked without holding up the line or leaving with the wrong items.

steps.action: **Enter the correct lane slowly.** Follow arrows, clearance signs, and lane markings.
steps.expect: your vehicle is aligned with the menu board and not blocking cross traffic.

steps.action: **Review the menu before the speaker.** Decide main items, sizes, drinks, sauces, and substitutions while waiting.
steps.expect: you can order in a clear sequence.

steps.action: **Pull to the speaker.** Stop with your window near the microphone and turn down music or fans.
steps.expect: you can hear the greeting and be heard.

steps.action: **Order clearly.** Say each item with size, quantity, modifications, and drink, pausing for confirmation.
steps.expect: the screen or employee repeats the order accurately.

steps.action: **Fix errors before moving.** [BRANCH: screen correct | screen wrong] proceed, or politely correct the item, size, sauce, or quantity.
steps.expect: the final total matches the intended order.

steps.action: **Have payment ready.** Put card, cash, phone wallet, coupon, or app code within reach before the window. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* submitting payment finalizes the order in many systems, so confirm the total before paying.
steps.expect: payment can be handed over without searching.

steps.action: **Collect drinks and food securely.** Place drinks in cup holders and hot bags on a flat surface or passenger's hands.
steps.expect: nothing spills when the vehicle moves.

steps.action: **Check the bag before leaving the lot.** Pull into a safe spot if needed and verify main items, drinks, sauces, utensils, and receipts.
steps.expect: mistakes are found while the restaurant can still fix them.

recipes.verification: Before driving away from the restaurant area, the bag and drinks match the receipt and requested sauces, utensils, or substitutions are present.

recipes.title: use a laundromat
recipes.name: use-a-laundromat
recipes.goal: Laundry washed and dried at a laundromat, machines claimed and released by the local etiquette, and the two hours spent rather than lost.

steps.action: **Scout on arrival.** Find free washers of the right size (bigger drums cost more, take duvets), check posted prices and any house rules, locate carts and folding tables.
steps.expect: a machine chosen, price known, cart nearby if hauling between machines.

steps.action: **Inspect the drum before loading.** A quick look and sniff: strangers' left socks, bleach puddles, or a gasket full of grime move you one machine over.
steps.expect: a clean, empty drum.

steps.action: **Load, dose, and pay.** Clothes in loosely (the home three-quarters rule), detergent in the drawer or drum per the machine's marking, select cycle and temperature, feed the payment, start.
steps.expect: door locked, cycle running, and the end time noted on your phone.

steps.action: **Stay close or come back on time.** The cardinal etiquette: machines are shared infrastructure and a finished load squatting in a washer blocks everyone. Set an alarm for the cycle end.
steps.expect: you at your machine within minutes of the beep.

steps.action: **Move wet laundry to a dryer promptly.** Shake pieces out (`daily/home/do-the-laundry` step 7), clean the dryer's lint filter first, load loosely, choose medium heat unless the labels say low, pay and start. Overloaded dryers run twice for the same money.
steps.expect: lint screen cleaned, drum loose, alarm reset for the dry time.

steps.action: **Check dryness before hauling home.** Waistbands and seams are the last dry; damp means one more short paid cycle beats mildew at home.
steps.expect: genuinely dry clothes.

steps.action: **Fold at the tables, claim everything, and leave the station clean.** Folding warm at the venue (`embodied/household/fold-a-tshirt`) beats a wrinkled bag; sweep the drum and gasket with a hand for strays (fitted sheets eat socks), take your detergent, wipe your table.
steps.expect: folded bags, empty machines, nothing of yours left behind.

recipes.verification: Everything that arrived leaves washed, dried through at seams, folded, with the lint screen cleaned, machines emptied promptly, and no sock left in a drum or on a table.

recipes.title: use a parcel locker
recipes.name: use-a-parcel-locker
recipes.goal: Your parcel is out of the locker and in your hands, the compartment is closed behind you, and the pickup is registered as complete before any storage deadline expires.

steps.action: **Check the deadline the moment the notification arrives.** Find the "pick up by" date in the message; if none is stated, assume 48 hours.
steps.expect: a pickup slot planned before expiry, with a margin.

steps.action: **Retrieve the code before you travel.** Open the notification and confirm the PIN or QR loads; screenshot it. Locker banks are often in garages and lobbies with poor signal, and a code you cannot load is the classic stranding.
steps.expect: code or QR visible offline on your phone.

steps.action: **Locate the correct terminal.** Sites often host lockers from several carriers side by side; match the brand and the location name in your notification exactly.
steps.expect: terminal brand matches the notification.

steps.action: **Authenticate at the screen.** [BRANCH: PIN → type it at the touchscreen | QR/barcode → hold it to the scanner window, adjusting brightness up | app-driven → stand at the locker, press the in-app open button with Bluetooth on]
steps.expect: screen confirms your parcel and a compartment door pops ajar somewhere in the bank; watch and listen for it, the open door can be at ankle height or above your head.

steps.action: **Empty the compartment completely.** Reach in and sweep the full depth; multi-parcel orders can mean two boxes in one compartment, and small padded envelopes hide at the back.
steps.expect: compartment visibly empty on a final look.

steps.action: **Inspect before the door closes.** Check the label is yours and the box is not crushed or leaking. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once the door shuts, most systems mark the pickup complete and the code dies; you cannot reopen it to put a wrong or damaged parcel back. Wrong parcel or serious damage → photograph it in the open compartment and use the terminal's help/support option before touching the door.
steps.expect: your name on the label, box intact.

steps.action: **Close the door firmly until it latches.** An unlatched door keeps the transaction open and can flag the compartment as faulted.
steps.expect: door flush with the bank, a click, and the screen (or app) showing pickup complete.

recipes.verification: The parcel with your name on it is in your possession, the compartment door is latched flush, and the carrier app or a follow-up message shows the delivery status as picked up or complete.

recipes.title: use a parking meter
recipes.name: use-a-parking-meter
recipes.goal: Parking time is paid for the correct space or license plate, within the posted rules, so the vehicle is less likely to receive a ticket or tow.

steps.action: **Read the curb signs first.** Check days, hours, time limits, permits, loading zones, street cleaning, tow-away rules, and accessible-space restrictions.
steps.expect: you know parking is allowed right now.

steps.action: **Find the correct meter or zone.** Match the space number, stall marker, curb zone, or app zone code to your vehicle.
steps.expect: the meter or app identifier matches where the car is parked.

steps.action: **Check payment options.** [BRANCH: meter | mobile app] use coins or card at the meter, or open the app and enter the zone and plate.
steps.expect: the payment screen or meter display is ready for time selection.

steps.action: **Choose enough time.** Add time for the errand plus walking and checkout delays, staying within the posted maximum.
steps.expect: the display shows an expiration later than your expected return.

steps.action: **Confirm before paying.** Review plate, space, zone, duration, fee, and any convenience charge. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once submitted, parking payments often cannot be moved to another plate or zone, so check identifiers before paying.
steps.expect: the details match the actual car and curb.

steps.action: **Complete payment.** Insert coins, tap or swipe card, or submit in the app.
steps.expect: the meter shows paid time, or the app shows an active session.

steps.action: **Display proof if required.** Put the receipt on the dashboard only if the machine or sign says pay-and-display.
steps.expect: the receipt is visible from outside, or no display is required.

steps.action: **Set a return reminder.** Set an alarm 5 to 10 minutes before expiration and note whether extensions are allowed.
steps.expect: you have time to return, extend, or move the car.

recipes.verification: The meter or app shows an active paid session for the correct plate, space, or zone, and the expiration time is later than your planned return.

recipes.title: use a public library
recipes.name: use-a-public-library
recipes.goal: You hold a library card, can find and borrow materials (physical and digital), and return them on time — unlocking the most underused free institution in most towns.

steps.action: **Register once.** At the desk (or online-start): ID + address proof → a library card and a PIN/password. Ask the two questions that unlock everything: "What's my loan limit and period?" and "Which apps do you use for e-books/audiobooks?"
steps.expect: a card in hand, online account credentials, and the digital-app names written down.

steps.action: **Find things via the catalog, not wandering (unless wandering is the point).** The catalog terminal/website/app: search title/author/topic → note the call number and shelf area, or the item's status (on loan → place a hold).
steps.expect: a call number in hand or a hold placed with a pickup notification promised.

steps.action: **Read the shelf logic once and it works everywhere.** Fiction: alphabetical by author. Non-fiction: numbered by subject (Dewey-style) — the call number walks you to the shelf, the range labels on shelf-ends do the navigation.
steps.expect: the item found at its call number, or a librarian asked (they *enjoy* being asked; it's the job).

steps.action: **Borrow at the desk or self-checkout kiosk.** Card + items, kiosk scans and prints/emails the due-date slip.
steps.expect: items on your account with known due dates — calendar them or turn on the library's email/app reminders now.

steps.action: **Use the digital branch from your sofa.** Install the apps from step 1 (Libby/OverDrive-class), sign in with the card number + PIN, borrow e-books/audiobooks/magazines instantly — they return *themselves* at expiry.
steps.expect: a working digital shelf; the no-late-fees-ever tier of library use unlocked.

steps.action: **Return physical items on or before the due date.** The returns slot/bin (any branch, usually, and 24/7 slots exist) — or renew online *before* the date if nobody's waiting.
steps.expect: account back to zero items overdue; holds for others honored.

recipes.verification: Card active, one physical item successfully borrowed-and-returned on time, the digital app signed in with something checked out, due-date reminders on, and you know your library's answer to "what else does my card do?"

recipes.title: use a self checkout
recipes.name: use-a-self-checkout
recipes.goal: Your basket of items is scanned, paid, and bagged at a self-checkout kiosk without triggering the attendant more than the system inherently demands.

steps.action: **Start the transaction.** Tap the screen's start button; answer the opening prompts (own bags? loyalty card? — scan the loyalty code *now*, most kiosks won't add it later).
steps.expect: scanning screen active; your bag placed *in the bagging area* if prompted, and acknowledged by the kiosk.

steps.action: **Scan items one at a time, and place each in the bagging area immediately.** Barcode toward the glass/laser; listen for the beep; then set it down in the bagging zone *before* scanning the next — the scale there is watching, and rhythm is what keeps it happy.
steps.expect: beep → item on screen with price → placed → no complaint. A red-screen "unexpected item / please place item" → F1.

steps.action: **Handle barcode-less items via lookup.** Produce: place on the scale, tap Lookup, find the item (or type its code from the sticker/shelf—PLU), confirm the weight-price. Bakery/bulk similar.
steps.expect: item added at a plausible weight and price.

steps.action: **Handle restricted items by design, not surprise.** Alcohol and similar flag for age verification — the light will summon the attendant; have ID ready and just wait.
steps.expect: attendant tap-in, ID glance, transaction resumes.

steps.action: **Verify the item count and total before paying.** Screen list vs. basket-now-empty; kiosks double-beep or miss in ways cashiers don't.
steps.expect: list matches what's bagged; total plausible.

steps.action: **Pay.** Tap/insert card or feed cash; take the receipt (some exits check it).
steps.expect: approval, receipt printed, screen resets to idle.

steps.action: **Take everything.** Bags, receipt, card, and the phone you set down at step 3.
steps.expect: bagging area and shelf empty of your belongings.

recipes.verification: Everything from the basket is in your bags, each listed exactly once on a receipt in your hand, the payment cleared, and nothing of yours is left at the kiosk.

recipes.title: use a self service car wash
recipes.name: use-a-self-service-car-wash
recipes.goal: Wash a car in a coin or card-operated self-service bay without scratching paint, wasting paid time, or leaving soap residue.

steps.action: **Read the control panel before paying.** Note the order of modes, timer behavior, and any minimum charge.
steps.expect: you know how to switch between rinse, soap, brush, wax, and stop.

steps.action: **Prepare the car quickly.** Remove loose trash, fold mirrors only if needed, and place towels where they will stay dry.
steps.expect: nothing loose will blow away or block the wash hose.

steps.action: **Start with pre-rinse.** Spray from top down, keeping the nozzle 1 to 2 feet from paint and farther from loose trim.
steps.expect: grit, mud, and loose debris run off before anything touches the paint.

steps.action: **Apply soap.** Switch to soap and cover roof, glass, panels, wheels, and bumpers in that order.
steps.expect: the car is wet with visible foam before it starts drying.

steps.action: **Use the brush only after rinsing it.** Spray the brush head first, then brush top down with light pressure; skip it if the bristles hold grit.
steps.expect: dirt lifts without dragging visible grit across paint.

steps.action: **Watch the timer.** [BRANCH: enough time | time nearly out] continue the wash if enough; if nearly out, switch to rinse immediately.
steps.expect: soap will not dry on the car.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly.** Work top down, including mirrors, grille, wheel wells, door handles, and lower panels.
steps.expect: water sheets off with no foam hiding in seams or trim.

steps.action: **Dry outside the bay if allowed.** Move to the drying area and use clean towels on glass first, then paint, then dirty lower panels.
steps.expect: the bay is clear for the next user and the car has fewer water spots.

recipes.verification: The car has no visible soap foam, grit, or heavy water spots, and the bay floor is clear of your towels, trash, and equipment.

recipes.title: use a tire pump
recipes.name: use-a-tire-pump
recipes.goal: Use an air pump to bring a vehicle tire to the manufacturer's recommended pressure without overinflating it.

steps.action: **Find the PSI target.** Open the driver's door and read the tire placard on the door jamb, not the tire sidewall maximum.
steps.expect: the correct front and rear PSI values are known.

steps.action: **Park close enough to the pump.** Position the car so the hose reaches the tire without stretching across a walkway or traffic lane.
steps.expect: the hose reaches the valve comfortably.

steps.action: **Remove the valve cap.** Put it in a pocket or cup holder so it does not roll away.
steps.expect: the valve stem is uncovered and the cap is secure.

steps.action: **Attach the chuck squarely.** Press or clamp the pump chuck straight onto the valve until the loud hiss stops.
steps.expect: the chuck stays seated and air is not leaking around it.

steps.action: **Read the current pressure.** [BRANCH: built-in gauge | handheld gauge] use the pump gauge or briefly remove the chuck and check with your own gauge.
steps.expect: you know how far the tire is from target.

steps.action: **Inflate in short bursts.** Add air for 3 to 5 seconds at a time, then pause.
steps.expect: the pressure rises gradually instead of jumping past the target.

steps.action: **Check after each burst.** Re-seat the gauge if the reading seems unstable or the hose hissed during inflation.
steps.expect: the reading approaches the door-jamb PSI.

steps.action: **Stop at the target.** Do not keep adding air for a cushion above the placard value.
steps.expect: the tire is at the listed PSI or within about 1 PSI.

steps.action: **Bleed if needed.** If the tire is high, press the valve pin briefly and recheck.
steps.expect: pressure drops slowly back to target.

steps.action: **Replace the cap and repeat.** Screw the cap on finger tight, then move to the next tire.
steps.expect: all adjusted valves are capped.

recipes.verification: Every serviced tire matches its door-jamb PSI target within about 1 PSI, has a valve cap installed, and is not audibly leaking.

recipes.title: use a vending machine
recipes.name: use-a-vending-machine
recipes.goal: The item you wanted drops, you retrieve it plus any change, and you walk away — even the stuck-spiral scenario handled correctly.

steps.action: **Survey the machine's state before paying.** Item in stock (visible product, or the slot not flagged "sold out"), price noted, payment types listed on the reader.
steps.expect: your item visibly available at a known price; a payment path you can satisfy.

steps.action: **Pay.** [BRANCH: coins/notes → feed them flat and unwrinkled | contactless → tap when the reader wakes | QR/app → scan and authorize]
steps.expect: credit displayed on screen equal to what you provided, or reader showing approval.

steps.action: **Select the item by its code.** Punch the letter-number (e.g., "B4") exactly as labeled *under* the item you want — not the neighbor's. Verify the display echoes it.
steps.expect: display shows your code; the spiral/pusher for that slot begins turning.

steps.action: **Watch the drop.**
steps.expect: item falls to the retrieval bin. Wobbling-but-hanging → F1; nothing moved at all → F2.

steps.action: **Retrieve the item and your change.** Push the flap, take the item; check the coin-return cup.
steps.expect: item in hand; change matches (paid − price).

recipes.verification: You hold the item you selected, correct change (if cash), and the machine shows an idle display ready for the next person.

recipes.title: use an atm
recipes.name: use-an-atm
recipes.goal: Cash is withdrawn from your bank account at an ATM (or a balance/deposit operation completed), with card, cash, and receipt all retrieved.

steps.action: **Choose the machine and give it one glance of inspection.** Prefer bank-branch ATMs over standalone ones. Wiggle-check: a loose or bulky card slot or keypad overlay suggests a skimmer — walk away if anything shifts or looks glued on.
steps.expect: card slot and keypad are solid, flush, and match the machine's design.

steps.action: **Insert or tap the card.** Chip cards go in chip-first, face up (a diagram is printed by the slot); contactless: tap and hold.
steps.expect: screen leaves the idle state and prompts for language or PIN.

steps.action: **Enter the PIN with your other hand shielding the keypad.**
steps.expect: dots appear per digit; screen advances to the menu. Three wrong attempts usually swallow the card — after two failures, stop and verify the PIN elsewhere.

steps.action: **Select the operation and amount.** Withdrawal → amount from the quick list or "other amount" in the machine's dispensable denominations.
steps.expect: a confirmation screen; fees, if any, are disclosed here — decline if the surcharge is unacceptable.

steps.action: **Confirm and wait without walking off.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* dispensed cash left in the tray is rarely recoverable — stay at the machine until everything is out.
steps.expect: whirring, then cash presented in the tray.

steps.action: **Take cash, card, and receipt — all three, in whatever order the machine returns them.** Many machines return the card *before* the cash to prevent forgotten cards; don't leave after the first item.
steps.expect: you hold cash, card, and receipt; the screen returns to idle.

steps.action: **Count the cash discreetly and put it away before stepping aside.**
steps.expect: count matches the withdrawal amount.

recipes.verification: You possess the card, the correct counted cash, and the receipt; your banking app (checked later, not at the machine) shows exactly one debit for the expected amount plus disclosed fees.

recipes.title: wash a car by hand
recipes.name: wash-a-car-by-hand
recipes.goal: The car's exterior is clean and dried spot-free, with no new swirl marks in the paint, and the wash gear is rinsed and stored.

steps.action: **Stage in shade and let the panels cool.** Sun-heated paint flash-dries soap and water into etched spots.
steps.expect: panels cool to the back of your hand; car out of direct sun.

steps.action: **Set up the two buckets.** Bucket A: soap solution per the bottle's dilution. Bucket B: plain rinse water. Keep them a step apart so you never dunk into the wrong one.
steps.expect: one sudsy bucket, one clear bucket, grit guards seated at the bottoms.

steps.action: **Do the wheels first with dedicated tools.** Wheel brush and its own water; wheels carry brake dust and grit that must never touch the paint mitt.
steps.expect: wheel faces and barrels clean; wheel brush set aside, out of the paint workflow.

steps.action: **Pre-rinse the whole car top-down.** Loosen and float off loose dirt before anything touches the paint.
steps.expect: visible dirt sheeting off; standing water on all panels.

steps.action: **Wash top-down in sections: roof, glass, hood and trunk, upper sides, lower sides last.** Load the mitt in bucket A, wash one section with straight-line strokes (not circles), then dunk and scrub the mitt against the grit guard in bucket B before reloading.
steps.expect: rinse-bucket water getting dirty while the soap bucket stays clean; lower panels always done last.

steps.action: **Rinse each section before its soap dries.** In warm weather work panel-by-panel: wash one, rinse it, move on.
steps.expect: no dried soap haze anywhere; water sheeting cleanly off rinsed sections.

steps.action: **Final rinse with a gentle free-flowing stream (nozzle off).** A low-pressure sheet of water pulls most droplets off the panel and halves the drying work.
steps.expect: water sheeting off in a film, leaving only scattered droplets.

steps.action: **Dry immediately with clean microfiber towels, top-down.** Blot or drag lightly; swap to a dry towel once one is saturated. Do not let the car air-dry.
steps.expect: glass and dark panels streak-free and spot-free when viewed at a low angle.

steps.action: **Empty buckets and machine-wash the mitt and towels (no fabric softener).** Softener ruins microfiber absorbency.
steps.expect: gear clean and drying; buckets empty and stored.

recipes.verification: Walk around the car at a low viewing angle in good light: no dirt lines at panel bottoms or behind wheels, no soap residue, no water spots on glass or dark paint, and the wash mitt never touched the ground or the wheel gear.

recipes.title: what to do after a minor car accident
recipes.name: what-to-do-after-a-minor-car-accident
recipes.goal: Handle a minor car accident safely, document the facts, and start police or insurance reporting when needed.

steps.action: **Check for injuries and danger.** Look for pain, bleeding, smoke, fire, traffic exposure, or leaking fuel.
steps.expect: urgent medical or fire risks are identified.

steps.action: **Call emergency services if anyone is hurt or danger remains.** Give location, lane, vehicle count, and hazards.
steps.expect: responders are dispatched when needed.

steps.action: **Move to safety if vehicles are drivable.** Use hazard lights and pull to a shoulder, parking lot, or side street.
steps.expect: people are away from moving traffic.

steps.action: **Stay at the scene.** Do not leave until information is exchanged and any required report is handled.
steps.expect: you remain reachable and legally present.

steps.action: **Exchange information.** Share name, phone, license plate, driver's license details as locally required, insurance company, and policy number.
steps.expect: each driver has enough information to file a claim.

steps.action: **Document with photos.** Photograph vehicle positions, damage, plates, road signs, skid marks, weather, and insurance cards if offered.
steps.expect: factual evidence is saved.

steps.action: **Get witness and police details.** Ask witnesses for contact information and record the responding officer or report number if police attend.
steps.expect: independent references are available.

steps.action: **Avoid admitting fault.** Stick to facts like direction, lane, signals, and what happened.
steps.expect: no speculative or blame statement is made.

steps.action: **Notify your insurer.** Report the accident promptly, even if damage seems small.
steps.expect: the insurer gives claim instructions.

recipes.verification: Everyone is safe, required emergency or police calls are made, driver and insurance information is exchanged, photos are saved, and your insurer has been notified.

recipes.title: bake a loaf of bread
recipes.name: bake-a-loaf-of-bread
recipes.goal: A basic yeasted loaf is mixed, kneaded, risen, shaped, baked with steam, cooled, and checked for doneness.

steps.action: **Mix the dough.** Stir 500 g flour, 325 g warm water, 7 g yeast, and 10 g salt until no dry flour remains.
steps.expect: a shaggy, sticky mass that pulls loose from the bowl in patches.

steps.action: **Rest before kneading.** Cover for 15 minutes so the flour hydrates.
steps.expect: dough feels less sandy and stretches farther before tearing.

steps.action: **Knead to build gluten.** Knead 8-10 minutes by hand, pushing and folding, or 5-6 minutes on low in a mixer.
steps.expect: dough becomes smoother, elastic, and tacky rather than wet.

steps.action: **Check the gluten.** Pinch off a piece and stretch it thin. [BRANCH: thin sheet forms | tears instantly]
steps.expect: a translucent window, or a clear need for 2 more minutes of kneading.

steps.action: **First rise.** Put dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise at room temperature 1-2 hours.
steps.expect: dough roughly doubles and a fingertip dent fills back slowly.

steps.action: **Shape the loaf.** Pat into a rectangle, fold thirds like a letter, roll tight, and pinch the seam.
steps.expect: a taut log with surface tension and the seam underneath.

steps.action: **Second rise.** Place in a greased pan or seam-down on parchment, cover, and proof 45-75 minutes.
steps.expect: dough looks puffy and springs back slowly when touched.

steps.action: **Preheat and prepare steam.** Heat oven to 220 °C with an empty metal tray on the lower rack.
steps.expect: oven fully hot and tray ready before the loaf goes in.

steps.action: **Slash and bake with steam.** Score the top, load the loaf, pour 1 cup hot water into the lower tray, and close the door. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* steam burns skin fast; keep face back and use a long-spouted cup.
steps.expect: an immediate burst of steam and the loaf beginning to expand.

steps.action: **Finish the bake.** Bake 30-40 minutes, lowering to 200 °C after 15 minutes if browning too fast.
steps.expect: deep golden crust and an internal temperature near 93 °C.

steps.action: **Tap-test and cool.** Tip loaf out and tap the bottom; cool on a rack at least 1 hour before slicing.
steps.expect: a hollow sound, dry base, and no gummy crumb when cut.

recipes.verification: The cooled loaf sounds hollow when tapped, has a browned crust, and slices with an open, set crumb rather than raw dough.

recipes.title: bake a potato
recipes.name: bake-a-potato
recipes.goal: A baked potato with crisp, salty, edible skin and a fluffy interior that yields completely to a fork, ready to split and top.

steps.action: **Scrub under running water.** Russets grow in dirt and the skin is part of the dish; scrub with a brush or rough sponge, then dry completely with a towel. A wet skin steams and stays leathery.
steps.expect: visibly clean skin, no dirt in the eyes, surface dry to the touch.

steps.action: **Pierce each potato 6-8 times with a fork.** Space the holes around the whole surface. This vents steam; an unpierced potato can genuinely burst in the oven and coat it in starch.
steps.expect: shallow fork marks all around; no need to stab deep.

steps.action: **Oil and salt the skin.** Rub a thin coat of oil over the whole potato, then roll or sprinkle with coarse salt. The oil crisps the skin; the salt seasons it and draws surface moisture out.
steps.expect: a thin even sheen with salt clinging to it.

steps.action: **Bake hot and unwrapped, directly on the rack.** 220 °C (425 °F), potatoes straight on the oven rack or on a wire rack over a sheet for airflow all around. Never wrap in foil: foil traps steam and gives you a boiled texture with soggy skin.
steps.expect: oven at temperature before the potatoes go in; a sheet on the rack below to catch salt and drips.

steps.action: **Bake 50-70 minutes without opening the oven early.** Medium russets take about 55 minutes; large ones over an hour.
steps.expect: the kitchen smells of baked potato in the last third; skin looks dry, wrinkled at the shoulders, and slightly puffed away from the flesh.

steps.action: **Run the done test.** Squeeze with an oven mitt: a done potato gives easily under gentle pressure. Confirm with a skewer or thin knife: it should glide to the center with zero resistance. A thermometer reading 95-99 °C in the center is the precise version.
steps.expect: effortless skewer, soft squeeze. Any firmness at the center means 10 more minutes.

steps.action: **Split immediately and fluff.** Cut a cross in the top, push the ends toward each other so it blossoms open, and rough up the interior with a fork so steam escapes. Waiting keeps steam inside and turns fluffy flesh dense.
steps.expect: steam rising, interior white and fluffy; add butter and salt while hot so they melt in.

recipes.verification: A skewer passes to the center of every potato with no resistance (or center reads 95-99 °C), the skin is dry and crisp enough to eat, and the split interior is steaming, fluffy, and separates into flakes under a fork.

recipes.title: bake chocolate chip cookies
recipes.name: bake-chocolate-chip-cookies
recipes.goal: A batch of chocolate chip cookies with crisp edges and soft centers, evenly baked, cooled enough to hold their shape.
