steps.action: **Preheat the oven to 180 °C / 350 °F, rack in the middle.** Start this first; a cold oven ruins spread and texture.
steps.expect: preheat indicator confirms temperature before any tray goes in.

steps.action: **Cream the softened butter with both sugars for a full 2-3 minutes.** Beat until the mixture is visibly lighter in color and fluffy, not just combined. This aeration is what the leavening builds on; undercreamed dough bakes into dense pucks.
steps.expect: pale, fluffy mixture that has grown in volume, no butter streaks.

steps.action: **Beat in the egg and vanilla.** Mix just until uniform.
steps.expect: smooth, glossy batter with no liquid pooling at the bowl edge.

steps.action: **Add flour, baking soda, and salt; mix until the last flour streak disappears, then stop.** Overmixing develops gluten and toughens the cookie.
steps.expect: a cohesive soft dough; no dry pockets, no long beating after they vanish.

steps.action: **Fold in the chocolate chips with a few strokes.**
steps.expect: chips distributed through the dough, dough still soft.

steps.action: **Portion onto the parchment-lined tray with 5 cm / 2 in between balls.** Roughly golf-ball size, 8-12 per standard tray. Cookies spread to 2-3x their raw diameter; crowding welds them into one sheet.
steps.expect: evenly spaced balls with clear gaps on all sides.

steps.action: **Bake 9-12 minutes and pull when the centers still look slightly underdone.** Edges set and golden, centers pale and puffy. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overbaking. Carryover heat finishes the centers on the hot tray; a cookie that looks fully done in the oven is dry once cooled.
steps.expect: golden edges, soft-looking middles that seem one minute early.

steps.action: **Rest the cookies on the tray 5 minutes, then move to a rack.** They are too soft to lift at first.
steps.expect: cookies firm enough to slide off intact with a spatula.

steps.action: **Repeat with remaining dough on a cooled tray.** [BRANCH: second tray ready and cool → load it | only one tray → wait until it is cool to the touch] A hot tray melts the dough before baking starts and causes overspreading.
steps.expect: second batch spreads the same as the first.

recipes.verification: Cookies are uniformly golden at the edges, centers soft but set (a cooled cookie bends slightly before breaking), no cookies fused together, none burnt underneath, and the oven is off.

recipes.title: blanch vegetables
recipes.name: blanch-vegetables
recipes.goal: Vegetables are briefly cooked in salted boiling water, then chilled so they stay bright, tender-crisp, and ready to eat, freeze, or finish later.

steps.action: **Cut evenly.** Trim tough ends, peel only if needed, and cut pieces to a matching thickness so they finish together
steps.expect: pieces look uniform, with no woody stems mixed in.

steps.action: **Prepare the ice bath.** Fill a bowl with cold water and enough ice to keep it cold after hot vegetables go in
steps.expect: the bowl feels very cold and has room for the vegetables.

steps.action: **Boil and salt the water.** Bring a large pot to a rolling boil, then salt it until it tastes lightly seasoned, not seawater-level salty
steps.expect: large bubbles break the surface continuously and the salt has dissolved.

steps.action: **Cook in a small batch.** Add vegetables and stir once so the water returns to a boil quickly [BRANCH: tender greens | dense roots]
steps.expect: the water resumes bubbling within about 30 seconds.

steps.action: **Taste early.** Start checking thin vegetables at 30 seconds and dense pieces after 2 minutes
steps.expect: the vegetable is brighter and barely tender at the center.

steps.action: **Shock immediately.** Lift vegetables into the ice bath as soon as they are done
steps.expect: steam stops rising within seconds and the color stays vivid.

steps.action: **Drain when cold.** Remove the vegetables once fully chilled, then drain well in a colander
steps.expect: the vegetables feel cold all the way through and no longer cook from carryover heat.

steps.action: **Dry before storing or finishing.** Spread on a towel and pat dry, especially before sauteing or freezing
steps.expect: surfaces look matte rather than wet.

recipes.verification: A test piece is bright, cold, and tender enough to bite through while still holding its shape.

recipes.title: blind bake a pie crust
recipes.name: blind-bake-a-pie-crust
recipes.goal: A pie crust is baked empty so it stays crisp and holds its shape for wet or no-bake fillings.

steps.action: **Dock and chill.** Prick the base lightly with a fork and chill the lined pie plate 20 minutes.
steps.expect: dough feels firm and cold.

steps.action: **Preheat the oven.** Heat oven to 190 °C with a baking sheet inside.
steps.expect: oven is fully hot before dough enters.

steps.action: **Line with parchment.** Press parchment into the crust and fill to the rim with weights.
steps.expect: sides are supported and parchment touches the corners.

steps.action: **Bake weighted.** Put pie plate on the hot sheet and bake 15-20 minutes.
steps.expect: edge looks set and just starting to color.

steps.action: **Remove weights.** Lift parchment and weights out carefully. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* hot weights burn and spill easily; lift slowly with dry mitts.
steps.expect: crust base looks pale and slightly damp.

steps.action: **Finish baking.** Return crust to oven 8-15 minutes for partial bake or 15-25 minutes for full bake. [BRANCH: custard filling later | no-bake filling]
steps.expect: base is dry for partial bake or golden for full bake.

steps.action: **Cool before filling.** Set crust on a rack until warm or room temperature as the filling requires.
steps.expect: crust firms and releases steam.

recipes.verification: Crust sides hold their shape, base is dry, color matches the intended partial or full bake, and no raw dough patches remain.

recipes.title: boil corn on the cob
recipes.name: boil-corn-on-the-cob
recipes.goal: Corn on the cob is hot, sweet, tender-crisp, and ready for butter and salt.

steps.action: **Check freshness.** Choose ears with green husks, moist silk, and plump kernels under the tip.
steps.expect: kernels look full, not shriveled.

steps.action: **Decide when to husk.** [BRANCH: husk before boiling for clean water | husk after a 1-minute blanch if silk is stubborn]
steps.expect: the chosen workflow fits your cleanup space.

steps.action: **Bring plain water to a boil.** Fill the pot with enough water to cover the ears, but do not salt it.
steps.expect: water reaches a rolling boil with room for corn.

steps.action: **Add corn carefully.** Lower ears into the water with tongs and cover until the boil returns.
steps.expect: the water bubbles again within 1 to 2 minutes.

steps.action: **Time 3 to 5 minutes.** Cook fresh sweet corn briefly once the boil returns.
steps.expect: kernels brighten and smell sweet.

steps.action: **Test doneness.** Lift one ear and pierce a kernel with a fork tip.
steps.expect: the kernel is tender but still pops with juice.

steps.action: **Drain and season.** Move corn to a platter, spread butter while hot, then salt at the table.
steps.expect: butter melts across the kernels and salt sticks.

steps.action: **Serve promptly.** Keep covered with foil or a towel if waiting a few minutes.
steps.expect: ears stay hot without continuing to boil.

recipes.verification: At least one kernel from the thickest ear is hot, juicy, and tender when pierced, with no raw starchy center.

recipes.title: boil water
recipes.name: boil-water
recipes.goal: A container of water is brought to a full boil and is available for use (tea, cooking, sterilizing) without spills or burns.

steps.action: **Choose the method for the amount needed.** [BRANCH: electric kettle (fastest, ≤ its max line) | stovetop pot (any volume) | microwave (single cup only — see Variations for the superheating precautions)]
steps.expect: container capacity ≥ needed volume with ≥ 2 cm headroom.

steps.action: **Fill with cold tap water to the needed level.** Kettle: between MIN and MAX marks. Pot: no more than 2/3 full.
steps.expect: water level within the safe marks; outside of the container is dry.

steps.action: **Start heating.** Kettle: seat it on its base, close the lid, press the switch. Stovetop: pot centered on the burner, lid on, burner to high.
steps.expect: kettle switch light on / burner flame or coil visibly on; faint heating sound builds within ~1 min.

steps.action: **Wait, staying within earshot.** Do not leave the building with a stove on.
steps.expect: progression of sound: quiet → hissing → rolling rumble; steam appears from the spout or lid edge.

steps.action: **Recognize the boil.** Kettle: clicks off automatically. Pot: large bubbles break the surface continuously (a "rolling boil"); lid may rattle.
steps.expect: kettle switch has flipped off, or the pot shows a sustained rolling boil.

steps.action: **Turn off the heat (stovetop) and move the container safely.** Use the handle; for a pot, lift the lid tilted *away* from your face to vent steam away. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* boiling-water scalds — never carry a full open pot across the room; bring the destination (cup, pan) near the kettle/pot instead.
steps.expect: heat source off; container resting on the dry stable surface.

steps.action: **Use or pour the water at once.** Pour slowly, spout close to the target vessel.
steps.expect: target vessel filled without splash; remaining water left in the container, not in your path.

recipes.verification: The water reached a sustained rolling boil (or the kettle auto-clicked off), the heat source is now off, and the hot container sits on a stable dry surface — no water on the floor or stovetop, no one scalded.

recipes.title: brew french press coffee
recipes.name: brew-french-press-coffee
recipes.goal: Full-bodied french press coffee with no technique anxiety and no mud in the cup, plus a press that gets cleaned instead of becoming the kitchen's guilt object.

steps.action: **Preheat the press with a swirl of hot water, then discard it.** Cold glass steals brewing heat.
steps.expect: warm empty press.

steps.action: **Add the coffee, then all the water, and give one gentle stir.** Make sure no dry island of grounds floats unwetted.
steps.expect: all grounds saturated; a crust forming on top is normal.

steps.action: **Rest the lid on with the plunger pulled all the way up, and steep four minutes.** The lid holds heat; the timer holds you back.
steps.expect: four untouched minutes.

steps.action: **Press slowly and only halfway-firmly.** Steady pressure over ten seconds or so; the plunger should meet mild resistance. ⚠️ Forcing a stuck plunger can blast hot coffee out of the spout; if it resists hard, pull up slightly and press again slower.
steps.expect: the mesh gliding down, grounds pinned below, no eruption.

steps.action: **Pour all the coffee out immediately.** Coffee left standing on the grounds keeps extracting into bitterness; decant the whole press into cups or a carafe now.
steps.expect: press emptied within a minute of pressing; the last few sips left behind if you dislike sediment.

steps.action: **Clean the press today.** Grounds into the bin or compost (not the sink drain; `daily/home/unclog-a-drain` exists because of habits like that), then rinse and wash the beaker and mesh.
steps.expect: a clean press drying, mesh free of packed grounds.

recipes.verification: Four-minute steep, slow successful press, entire brew decanted immediately, cups carry body without mud, and the press is clean with the grounds in the bin rather than the drain.

recipes.title: brew iced tea
recipes.name: brew-iced-tea
recipes.goal: A pitcher of clear, full-flavored iced tea, properly chilled and not watered down, ready to pour over ice.

steps.action: **Choose the method.** [BRANCH: hot-brew double strength (ready in ~30 min) | cold-brew (smoothest, near-zero bitterness, needs 8-12 h)] Cold-brew: skip to step 6.
steps.expect: method matched to the deadline.

steps.action: **Brew at double strength.** Use twice the tea per volume of water, not double the steeping time: e.g. 4 bags per 500 ml where you would use 2 for hot tea. The ice in step 5 will dilute it back to normal. Longer steeping extracts bitterness, more leaf extracts flavor.
steps.expect: correct leaf-to-water ratio measured before pouring.

steps.action: **Pour water just off the boil over the tea and steep 3-5 minutes.** Black tea: boiling water, 4-5 min. Green tea: let the water cool ~2 min first (80 °C) and steep 2-3 min, or it turns bitter. Set a timer; "a few extra minutes" is the classic bitterness mistake.
steps.expect: deep-colored concentrate at the timer, bags/leaves removed promptly, not squeezed hard (squeezing wrings out tannin).

steps.action: **Cool the concentrate 10-15 minutes at room temperature.** If sweetening, stir sugar in now while it is hot; sugar will not dissolve in cold tea (or use simple syrup later).
steps.expect: concentrate warm, not steaming; sugar fully dissolved if added.

steps.action: **Pour the concentrate over a pitcher packed with ice.** The melting ice performs the dilution to drinking strength; stir until the ice stops melting fast. Top up with cold water if it still tastes strong.
steps.expect: tea at drinking strength and cold, roughly doubling the volume; proceed to step 8.

steps.action: **Cold-brew: combine tea and cold water at normal strength in the pitcher.** Regular ratio (1 bag or 1 tsp loose leaf per 250 ml), cold water, lid on.
steps.expect: leaves submerged, pitcher lidded and in the fridge.

steps.action: **Steep refrigerated 8-12 hours, then strain.** Cold water never extracts the harsh tannins, so overshooting to 12+ hours is forgiving.
steps.expect: smooth, clear, aromatic tea; remove bags or strain leaves.

steps.action: **Serve over fresh ice and refrigerate the rest.** Lemon or syrup to taste at the glass.
steps.expect: clear (not cloudy) tea in the glass; pitcher back in the fridge, best within 2-3 days.

recipes.verification: The tea tastes at drinking strength after the ice melt (not sharp, not watery), is clear in the glass, cold throughout, and the leaves/bags are out of the liquid so it will not keep extracting.

recipes.title: brew pour over coffee
recipes.name: brew-pour-over-coffee
recipes.goal: A clean, sweet cup of pour-over coffee from a cone dripper, with the two variables that matter (grind and ratio) under control and the ritual under five active minutes.

steps.action: **Rinse the paper filter with hot water, then dump the rinse water.** This washes papery taste out and preheats the dripper and mug.
steps.expect: wet seated filter, warm vessel, rinse water discarded.

steps.action: **Add the ground coffee and level the bed.** A gentle shake flattens it.
steps.expect: a level bed; scale zeroed with everything on it if you use one.

steps.action: **Bloom: pour about twice the coffee's weight in water (30 g water for 15 g coffee) and wait 30 to 45 seconds.** The bed swells and bubbles as gas escapes; skipping this makes sour, uneven cups.
steps.expect: visible blooming and a swelling bed; all grounds wetted, none dry at the edges.

steps.action: **Pour the remaining water in slow circles, in two or three stages.** Spiral from the center outward and back, keeping the water level steady rather than flooding to the rim; pause between stages to let it draw down. Avoid pouring directly on the filter walls.
steps.expect: controlled pours reaching the target weight; the slurry never near overflow.

steps.action: **Let it draw down completely.** Total brew time from bloom to final drip should land around 2.5 to 3.5 minutes for a mug.
steps.expect: a flat bed of grounds and a finished drip inside that window. Much faster means too coarse; much slower means too fine (see F1 and F2).

steps.action: **Remove the dripper, swirl the cup, and taste before adjusting anything.** ⚠️ hot vessel and dripper: set the dripper on a saucer, not the tablecloth.
steps.expect: a cup you can already evaluate: sour and thin, bitter and harsh, or balanced.

recipes.verification: Bloom happened and the bed swelled, total brew time landed in the window, the bed finished flat, and the cup tastes balanced or you know which single variable you are changing next brew.

recipes.title: brine a chicken
recipes.name: brine-a-chicken
recipes.goal: Chicken is seasoned by wet or dry brining, then dried so it cooks juicy with browned skin.

steps.action: **Choose wet or dry.** [BRANCH: wet: dissolve salt in water | dry: salt directly on meat]
steps.expect: method fits your space and desired skin texture.

steps.action: **Use the right salt ratio.** Wet brine: 50-60 g salt per 1 L water; dry brine: 1-1.5% salt by chicken weight.
steps.expect: measured salt, not a random handful.

steps.action: **Add optional flavor.** Add sugar at half the salt weight for browning, plus herbs or spices if desired.
steps.expect: seasoning is dissolved or evenly scattered.

steps.action: **Submerge or coat.** Wet brine chicken fully under liquid; dry brine salt evenly over all sides and under loose skin if possible.
steps.expect: all thick parts contact salt.

steps.action: **Refrigerate by size.** Pieces need 1-4 hours; a whole chicken needs 8-24 hours.
steps.expect: chicken stays below 4 °C the whole time.

steps.action: **Remove from brine.** Lift chicken out and discard wet brine. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* used brine contains raw chicken juices; do not reuse it for sauce.
steps.expect: contaminated liquid is poured away safely.

steps.action: **Rinse only if needed.** If wet-brined heavily, rinse briefly; dry-brined chicken usually should not be rinsed.
steps.expect: surface is not crusted with excess salt.

steps.action: **Dry thoroughly.** Pat very dry and rest uncovered in the refrigerator 1-12 hours if time allows.
steps.expect: skin feels tacky-dry, not wet.

steps.action: **Cook with less added salt.** Season other components lightly because the chicken is already salted.
steps.expect: final dish is seasoned through, not salty on the surface only.

recipes.verification: Chicken has been salted by measured ratio, kept refrigerated, removed from brine, and dried before cooking.

recipes.title: brown butter
recipes.name: brown-butter
recipes.goal: Cook butter until its milk solids turn nutty brown, then stop the carryover heat before the solids burn.

steps.action: **Melt evenly.** Put butter in the light pan over medium heat
steps.expect: butter melts and pale solids are visible

steps.action: **Cook through foam.** Stir while the butter foams and crackles
steps.expect: sound is wet and lively as water cooks off

steps.action: **Watch the bottom.** Scrape constantly where milk solids settle
steps.expect: specks move from pale to tan

steps.action: **Lower at nutty.** When the smell turns nutty, lower heat or lift the pan
steps.expect: color keeps deepening from carryover

steps.action: **Stop at brown.** Remove from heat at chestnut brown. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* black milk solids cannot be fixed, so stop slightly early
steps.expect: specks are brown, not black

steps.action: **Pour out.** Scrape butter and solids into a cool bowl unless using immediately
steps.expect: color stops darkening

steps.action: **Use with solids.** Spoon or measure the butter with the brown bits included
steps.expect: flavor is toasted and nutty

recipes.verification: The butter smells nutty, contains evenly browned milk solids, and has no black specks or harsh smoke smell.

recipes.title: build a balanced plate
recipes.name: build-a-balanced-plate
recipes.goal: A meal plate is assembled with satisfying portions of vegetables or fruit, protein, starch or grain, fat, and flavor.

steps.action: **Start with produce.** Fill about half the plate with vegetables, fruit, or both.
steps.expect: plate has color, volume, and fiber-rich food.

steps.action: **Add protein.** Fill about one-quarter with beans, tofu, eggs, dairy, fish, poultry, meat, or another protein.
steps.expect: portion is palm-size or otherwise adequate for the eater.

steps.action: **Add starch or grain.** Fill about one-quarter with rice, bread, pasta, potatoes, corn, oats, or another staple.
steps.expect: meal has an energy source that fits appetite and activity.

steps.action: **Add fat and sauce.** Include oil, nuts, avocado, cheese, dressing, or sauce in a moderate amount.
steps.expect: food tastes rounded and not dry.

steps.action: **Check flavor contrast.** Add acid, herbs, spice, crunch, or salt if needed.
steps.expect: each bite tastes intentional rather than bland.

steps.action: **Adjust for the eater.** [BRANCH: child | athlete | medical diet] Change portions according to hunger, activity, and professional guidance.
steps.expect: plate fits the person rather than a rigid diagram.

steps.action: **Serve safely.** Keep hot foods hot and cold foods cold until eating.
steps.expect: meal is appetizing and perishable items have not sat out over 2 hours.

recipes.verification: The plate includes produce, protein, starch or grain, some fat or sauce, and is portioned for the eater's needs while perishable food remains safely held.

recipes.title: caramelize onions
recipes.name: caramelize-onions
recipes.goal: Onions are cooked low and slow into a deeply browned, sweet, jammy pile without scorching or pretending it takes 10 minutes.

steps.action: **Slice evenly.** Cut onions pole to pole into 3 to 5 mm slices so pieces cook at the same pace.
steps.expect: a loose pile of similar-width onion strips.

steps.action: **Use a wide pan.** Set a heavy skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat and add enough oil or butter to coat the bottom.
steps.expect: fat shimmers or butter foams without browning hard.

steps.action: **Load and salt.** Add onions with a pinch of salt and stir to coat.
steps.expect: the pan looks crowded at first, then onions begin to soften and shed water.

steps.action: **Cook off moisture.** Stir every few minutes while steam rises and the pile collapses.
steps.expect: onions turn translucent and reduce to less than half their starting volume.

steps.action: **Lower the heat.** When browning begins, reduce to medium-low or low.
steps.expect: sizzling becomes quiet and steady rather than sharp.

steps.action: **Let color build slowly.** Stir every 3 to 5 minutes, scraping the bottom each time.
steps.expect: pale gold becomes tan, then brown, with no black flakes.

steps.action: **Deglaze when fond sticks.** Add 1 to 2 tablespoons water, stock, wine, or vinegar and scrape until the browned film dissolves.
steps.expect: dark sticky spots lift into the onions and the pan bottom looks clean.

steps.action: **Repeat patiently.** Continue cooking and deglazing as needed until 45 to 60 minutes have passed for a full pan.
steps.expect: onions are soft, glossy, and deep brown throughout.

steps.action: **Finish seasoning.** Taste and adjust salt; add a small splash of vinegar only if the onions taste flat.
steps.expect: sweetness is balanced and not greasy.

steps.action: **Use or store.** Move onions to a dish or jar. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once onions scorch, bitterness cannot be removed, so reduce heat at the first black specks.
steps.expect: pan is off heat and onions are ready for burgers, soup, toast, or storage.

recipes.verification: The onions are uniformly soft, glossy, sweet, and brown, with no acrid smell or black scorched pieces.

recipes.title: caramelize sugar
recipes.name: caramelize-sugar
recipes.goal: Melt sugar into smooth amber caramel while avoiding crystallization, burning, and molten-sugar burns.

steps.action: **Choose method.** [BRANCH: dry method | wet method] dry uses sugar only; wet uses water to dissolve sugar
steps.expect: method is chosen

steps.action: **Load pan.** Spread sugar evenly, or stir wet sugar only before heating
steps.expect: pan sides are clean

steps.action: **Heat still.** Use medium heat and avoid stirring once boiling
steps.expect: syrup bubbles clear

steps.action: **Control crystals.** Brush wet-method crystals from the sides with water
steps.expect: syrup stays smooth

steps.action: **Watch color.** Cook from pale gold to amber, knowing color equals flavor
steps.expect: smell turns toasted

steps.action: **Stop early.** Remove at target amber. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* hard-crack dark caramel burns fast and cannot be fixed
steps.expect: color deepens slightly off heat

steps.action: **Finish safely.** Add cream off heat from arm length or pour onto a heatproof mat
steps.expect: violent bubbling settles glossy

recipes.verification: caramel is smooth amber with no crystals or black streaks

recipes.title: carve a roast
recipes.name: carve-a-roast
recipes.goal: A rested roast carved into clean slices across the grain, with juices retained and portions cut to the right thickness.

steps.action: **Rest the roast first.** Move it to the board and tent loosely with foil for 10 to 30 minutes depending on size.
steps.expect: juices settle and the roast feels firm, not actively steaming hard.

steps.action: **Find the grain.** Look for the direction muscle fibers run across the cut face.
steps.expect: you can point to long lines that need to be cut across.

steps.action: **Anchor with the fork.** Set the carving fork into the roast lightly, tines angled down and away from the slicing path.
steps.expect: the roast stays put without being crushed.

steps.action: **Trim ties or bones.** [BRANCH: boneless | bone-in] Remove twine on boneless roasts; for bone-in, separate the meat from bone in one long cut first.
steps.expect: the knife has a clear slicing path.

steps.action: **Slice against the grain.** Use long strokes with a sharp knife, letting the blade length do the work.
steps.expect: slices show short muscle fibers, not long stringy strands.

steps.action: **Control thickness.** Cut 1/4 inch slices for tender roasts and thinner slices for tougher cuts.
steps.expect: slices bend without shredding.

steps.action: **Transfer neatly.** Slide the knife or spatula under slices and move them to a warm platter.
steps.expect: slices stay intact and juices remain on the board or platter.

steps.action: **Spoon juices back.** Pour resting juices over sliced meat or into sauce.
steps.expect: carved meat looks glossy, not dry. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cutting before the rest dumps juices; confirm the rest time is complete before carving.

recipes.verification: Slices are even, carved across the grain, still juicy, and served at the planned thickness.

recipes.title: clean as you cook
recipes.name: clean-as-you-cook
recipes.goal: The kitchen finishes the meal in near-serving condition, because cleaning was woven into the cooking's dead time instead of stacked into a post-dinner mountain.

steps.action: **Set up the stations before heat.** A "garbage bowl" or the bin pulled near the board for scraps, hot soapy water standing in the sink or a basin, and a damp wipe-cloth parked at the counter's edge.
steps.expect: trash, wash, and wipe each have a destination within arm's reach.

steps.action: **Practice: every wait is a wash.** Water coming to a boil, onions sweating, oven preheating: those minutes wash the knife, the board, the measuring cups. Small items go straight into the standing hot water and take seconds each.
steps.expect: dead time consumed by two-minute cleaning bursts; no idle staring at pots.

steps.action: **Practice: done-with-it means dealt-with-it.** The moment a tool or bowl finishes its last job, it goes to the dishwasher or the soak, not to the counter. The counter is workspace, not storage.
steps.expect: the counter holding only what the meal still needs.

steps.action: **Practice: wipe spills at commission time.** Splatter, flour, and drips wipe off in one pass while fresh and cook onto surfaces if left (`embodied/kitchen/wipe-down-a-countertop` at micro scale).
steps.expect: each spill's lifespan under a minute.

steps.action: **Practice: pots start soaking the moment they are empty.** Serve, then immediately fill the pan with hot water (never cold water into a screaming-hot pan; warping and spitting) and a drop of soap.
steps.expect: by the first bite, every pan is soaking rather than setting.

steps.action: **Close the loop after eating.** With steps 1 to 5 done, the aftermath is ten minutes: plates and soaked pans into the wash flow (`daily/home/wash-dishes-by-hand` or the machine), surfaces wiped, sink emptied and rinsed.
steps.expect: the kitchen at baseline the same evening, and tomorrow-you not negotiating with a sink mountain.

recipes.verification: At serving time the counter holds only serving items, every pan is soaking, spills died young, and the post-meal close-out took ten minutes rather than an evening.

recipes.title: cook a burger
recipes.name: cook-a-burger
recipes.goal: Cook a juicy burger with a browned outside, safe interior temperature, and a patty that stays flat enough to fit the bun.

steps.action: **Portion the meat.** Divide cold ground beef into loose 115 g to 170 g portions without kneading or squeezing it smooth.
steps.expect: each portion holds together but still has a rough, craggy surface.

steps.action: **Shape gently.** Pat each portion into a disk slightly wider than the bun and about 2 cm thick.
steps.expect: the patty looks even, with edges that are not cracked apart.

steps.action: **Dimple the center.** Press a shallow thumbprint into the middle of each patty so it will not dome while cooking.
steps.expect: the center is lower than the rim by about 5 mm.

steps.action: **Salt the outside only.** Season both faces with salt and pepper right before cooking, not while mixing the meat.
steps.expect: seasoning is visible on the surface and the meat has not been overworked.

steps.action: **Heat the cooking surface.** [BRANCH: skillet or griddle | grill] heat to medium-high until a drop of water sizzles hard, or the grill grate is hot and brushed clean.
steps.expect: the surface is hot enough to brown within the first minute.

steps.action: **Cook the first side.** Set the patty down and leave it alone for 3 to 5 minutes, depending on thickness.
steps.expect: the bottom develops a deep brown crust and releases with a thin spatula.

steps.action: **Flip once.** Turn the patty one time and do not press it flat with the spatula.
steps.expect: juices stay in the burger and the browned side faces up intact.

steps.action: **Cook to doneness.** Use temperature if possible: 63 C for medium with a rest, or 71 C for well done and food safety for ground beef.
steps.expect: the thermometer tip in the center reads the chosen target.

steps.action: **Add cheese if using.** Place cheese on during the last minute and cover briefly with a lid or metal bowl.
steps.expect: cheese softens and droops without burning.

steps.action: **Rest the burger.** Move the patty to a plate for 3 to 5 minutes before putting it on the bun.
steps.expect: juices settle and the bun does not immediately turn soggy.

recipes.verification: The burger has a browned crust, rests at least 3 minutes, and the center reaches the chosen doneness temperature.

recipes.title: cook a steak
recipes.name: cook-a-steak
recipes.goal: A steak with a deep brown crust and an evenly cooked interior at your target doneness, rested so it stays juicy when cut.

steps.action: **Salt early and dry the surface.** Salt both sides generously, then leave the steak uncovered on a rack, in the fridge for 1-24 hours if you planned ahead, or at room temperature for 30-45 minutes if not. Just before cooking, pat every surface bone-dry with paper towels. A wet surface steams instead of searing; drying is the single highest-leverage step.
steps.expect: paper towels come away nearly dry on the final pat; the surface looks tacky, not glossy.

steps.action: **Heat the pan properly.** Empty pan over medium-high for 3-4 minutes, then add a thin film of oil.
steps.expect: the oil shimmers and shows first wisps of smoke. If the oil smokes heavily on contact, the pan is too hot; pull it off heat for 30 seconds.

steps.action: **Lay the steak in, away from you.** Place it down and leave it alone. Moving it early tears the developing crust.
steps.expect: an immediate loud, sustained sizzle. A quiet pan means it was not hot enough; take the steak out, reheat, and restart.

steps.action: **Sear undisturbed, then flip once.** 2-4 minutes per side depending on thickness. Peek by lifting one corner; flip only when the crust releases and is deep brown.
steps.expect: a mahogany crust on the first side; the steak releases without sticking.

steps.action: **Optionally baste after the flip.** Add a knob of butter, smashed garlic, and thyme; tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steak for the last 1-2 minutes.
steps.expect: foaming (not blackening) butter; the crust darkens and smells nutty.

steps.action: **Pull by thermometer, not by clock.** Probe horizontally into the center. Pull at 48-50 °C for rare, 52-54 °C for medium-rare, 57-60 °C for medium; carryover adds roughly 3 °C while resting. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overcooking cannot be undone; when in doubt pull early, you can always return it to the pan.
steps.expect: thermometer reads your pull target in the thickest part.

steps.action: **Rest as long as you cooked.** Steak to a warm plate or rack, loosely tented, for about as many minutes as it spent in the pan (5-10 minutes). Cutting immediately dumps the juices onto the board.
steps.expect: only a small puddle on the plate after resting; slices stay juicy.

steps.action: **Slice across the grain and serve.** Identify the direction of the muscle fibers and cut perpendicular to them.
steps.expect: short fibers in each slice; tender chew even on cheaper cuts.

recipes.verification: Crust is deep brown on both faces, the center reads the target doneness on a thermometer (or shows the target color when cut), the steak rested at least as long as it seared, and slices are cut across the grain with juice retained in the meat rather than pooled on the board.

recipes.title: cook bacon
recipes.name: cook-bacon
recipes.goal: Bacon is cooked to the target crispness with rendered fat managed safely and no grease sent down the drain.

steps.action: **Choose the cooking method.** [BRANCH: stovetop for 2-8 slices with close control | oven tray for a full package or hands-off batch]
steps.expect: the pan or tray size matches the bacon volume without tight stacking.

steps.action: **Separate the strips.** Peel slices apart while cold, keeping torn pieces grouped by thickness.
steps.expect: strips lie flat and similar-thickness pieces are ready to cook together.

steps.action: **Start stovetop bacon in a cold pan.** Lay strips in the cold skillet with slight gaps, then set heat to medium-low.
steps.expect: fat begins to look glossy before loud sizzling starts.

steps.action: **Render before browning.** Let the bacon slowly release fat for 5-8 minutes, moving curled edges flat with tongs.
steps.expect: a shallow pool of clear fat forms and the meat shrinks evenly.

steps.action: **Turn and adjust heat.** Flip when the underside is lightly browned; reduce heat if fat spits hard or edges darken before centers firm.
steps.expect: steady sizzle, not smoke, and both sides color gradually.

steps.action: **Use the oven-tray method when batching.** Line a rimmed tray, arrange strips in one layer, and bake at 400°F until browned.
steps.expect: bacon renders into the lined tray and cooks evenly in about 15-22 minutes.

steps.action: **Pull just before final crispness.** Transfer strips to paper towels when they look one shade paler than the target.
steps.expect: carryover heat crisps the bacon as surface grease drains.

steps.action: **Save or dispose of grease correctly.** Pour warm, not smoking, grease into a heat-safe container. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* grease down a sink can clog plumbing; confirm the drain path is avoided before pouring.
steps.expect: grease is contained off the pan and no liquid fat enters the sink.

steps.action: **Degrease after cooling.** Wipe the cooled skillet or tray with paper towel before washing with hot soapy water.
steps.expect: only a thin film remains before the item reaches the sink.

steps.action: **Store leftovers promptly.** Refrigerate cooked bacon once it is no longer steaming.
steps.expect: leftovers are in a covered container, not sitting warm on the counter.

recipes.verification: Bacon is cooked to the desired crispness, the heat source is off, and all rendered grease is cooling in a container or solidified in trash rather than in the drain.

recipes.title: cook dried beans
recipes.name: cook-dried-beans
recipes.goal: A pot of dried beans cooked through to uniform creaminess in a seasoned broth, portioned for immediate use and storage.

steps.action: **Sort and rinse.** Spread the beans on a tray, pick out stones, dirt clods, and shriveled or broken beans, then rinse in a colander. Small stones are genuinely common in dried beans and cost a tooth.
steps.expect: clean beans, a small reject pile, clear rinse water.

steps.action: **Choose a soak.** [BRANCH: overnight soak: cover with 5+ cm of water, 8-15 h on the counter | quick soak: boil 2 minutes, lid on, off heat 1 h | no soak: proceed directly, add ~50% simmering time] All three produce good beans; soaking mainly buys time and evenness.
steps.expect: soaked beans visibly swollen to roughly double; no-soak path proceeds with dry beans and more patience.

steps.action: **Salt the soak or the pot from the start.** About 1 tablespoon per liter in the soak water, and season the cooking water too. The old rule that salt toughens beans and must wait until the end is a myth; brined beans cook up with better-seasoned, more intact skins. What genuinely slows softening is acid (tomato, vinegar), which waits until the beans are tender.
steps.expect: cooking water that tastes pleasantly salty, like weak soup; no acidic ingredients in the pot yet.

steps.action: **Bring to a boil, then drop to a bare simmer.** Fresh water to 3-4 cm over the beans, aromatics in, boil, then reduce until only a few lazy bubbles rise, lid ajar. For kidney beans (and other red beans), hold a hard rolling boil for the first 10 minutes before reducing; see Safety.
steps.expect: an occasional slow bubble, not a churn; hard-boiling churns beans into split skins and cloudy broth.

steps.action: **Skim, then leave it mostly alone.** Skim the gray-white foam in the first 15 minutes, top up with hot water if beans breach the surface, stir rarely.
steps.expect: beans staying submerged, broth clearing after the skim.

steps.action: **Start testing at 1 hour, then every 15 minutes.** Blow on a spooned bean (thin skin wrinkles when done), then eat it: creamy to the center with no chalky core. Age, variety, and hard water swing the total anywhere from 1 to 2.5+ hours. Judge by texture, never by the clock.
steps.expect: five tested beans in a row all creamy; one chalky bean means keep going.

steps.action: **Finish in the broth.** Off heat, adjust salt, add any acid now if the recipe calls for it, and let the beans rest 15-30 minutes in their liquid; they season and firm slightly as they cool. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* draining the broth discards the best part; it is the base for the soup or the storage liquid, so decide before the colander.
steps.expect: seasoned beans resting submerged in tasty broth.

steps.action: **Store submerged.** Refrigerate beans in their broth (4-5 days) or freeze in portions with enough broth to cover (3+ months). Beans stored dry of liquid crack and stale.
steps.expect: containers with beans fully under liquid, labeled and dated.

recipes.verification: Five consecutive sampled beans are creamy to the center with intact skins, the broth tastes seasoned, no acid was added before tenderness, kidney beans got their 10-minute hard boil, and all stored portions sit submerged in liquid.

recipes.title: cook frozen dumplings
recipes.name: cook-frozen-dumplings
recipes.goal: Frozen dumplings are cooked through without thawing, either tender from boiling or crisp-bottomed by the potsticker steam-fry method.

steps.action: **Choose the cooking style.** [BRANCH: boil for soft dumplings | steam-fry for potstickers] pick boiling for soups and delicate wrappers, or steam-fry for crisp bottoms.
steps.expect: pan or pot choice matches the texture you want.

steps.action: **Keep dumplings frozen.** Take out only the amount you will cook and return the rest to the freezer.
steps.expect: dumplings are firm and separate, not thawed or sticky.

steps.action: **Boil option: start rolling water.** Fill a pot with enough water for dumplings to move freely and bring it to a boil.
steps.expect: large bubbles break the surface continuously.

steps.action: **Boil option: add and stir.** Slide dumplings in, stir gently once, and simmer 6 to 10 minutes depending on size.
steps.expect: dumplings float, wrappers turn slightly translucent, and filling feels firm.

steps.action: **Potsticker option: oil the cold skillet.** Add 1 tablespoon neutral oil, arrange dumplings flat-side down with space between them, then heat over medium.
steps.expect: bottoms sizzle within 2 minutes.

steps.action: **Potsticker option: steam then crisp.** Add 1/3 cup water, cover immediately, cook 6 to 8 minutes, uncover, then cook until water evaporates and bottoms brown. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* hot oil and water splatter when combined, so add water from the side and cover right away.
steps.expect: wrappers are tender and bottoms release golden and crisp.

steps.action: **Serve with sauce.** Mix soy sauce with vinegar and chili oil or sesame oil, then plate dumplings while hot.
steps.expect: dumplings hold shape and sauce is ready before they cool.

recipes.verification: At least one dumpling cut open has a steaming-hot, fully opaque filling, and the batch has either tender boiled wrappers or crisp browned potsticker bottoms.

recipes.title: cook frozen vegetables
recipes.name: cook-frozen-vegetables
recipes.goal: Cook frozen vegetables so they are hot, seasoned, and not waterlogged.

steps.action: **Keep them frozen until cooking.** Do not thaw unless the package specifically says to.
steps.expect: vegetables go from freezer to heat while still icy.

steps.action: **Choose the method.** [BRANCH: roast | steam | saute] Roast for browned edges, steam for tender plain vegetables, or saute for fast seasoning.
steps.expect: method matches the texture you want.

steps.action: **Use high heat for roasting.** Heat oven to 220 C and preheat the sheet pan if safe for the pan.
steps.expect: vegetables sizzle when they hit the pan.

steps.action: **Spread or contain properly.** Roast in one layer, steam in a basket over simmering water, or saute in a wide skillet with a little oil.
steps.expect: vegetables are not piled into a wet mound.

steps.action: **Cook without early stirring.** Let roasting or sauteing vegetables sit for a few minutes before moving them.
steps.expect: moisture cooks off and browning begins.

steps.action: **Drain if steaming.** Stop steaming when vegetables are hot and bright, then shake off water.
steps.expect: vegetables are tender but not sitting in liquid.

steps.action: **Season after moisture leaves.** Add salt, pepper, butter, lemon, sauce, or herbs near the end.
steps.expect: seasoning sticks to the vegetables instead of dissolving into water.

steps.action: **Serve immediately.** Move vegetables to a warm plate or bowl.
steps.expect: texture stays firm enough to bite and color remains bright.

recipes.verification: The vegetables are hot through, free of standing water, seasoned after cooking moisture is gone, and still have visible structure.

recipes.title: cook lentil dal
recipes.name: cook-lentil-dal
recipes.goal: Lentils are rinsed, simmered with aromatics, and finished with tempered spices for a soft, flavorful dal.

steps.action: **Pick and rinse lentils.** Check 250 g lentils for stones, then rinse until water is mostly clear.
steps.expect: no grit and less foaming in the pot.

steps.action: **Choose water by lentil.** [BRANCH: red or yellow split: 750 ml water | whole brown or green: 1 L water]
steps.expect: enough water for a soft stew, not a dry pilaf.

steps.action: **Start aromatics.** Simmer lentils with water, turmeric, sliced onion, garlic, and ginger.
steps.expect: foam rises during the first few minutes.

steps.action: **Skim and simmer.** Skim foam, lower heat, and cook partly covered.
steps.expect: gentle bubbles, not violent boiling.

steps.action: **Cook until soft.** Red lentils take 15-25 minutes; split pigeon peas and whole lentils may take 35-60 minutes.
steps.expect: lentils collapse or mash easily against the pot.

steps.action: **Adjust body.** Mash some lentils with a spoon and add hot water if too thick.
steps.expect: dal pours slowly and thickens as it sits.

steps.action: **Salt after softening.** Add salt and acid only after lentils are tender.
steps.expect: flavor wakes up without toughening undercooked lentils.

steps.action: **Temper spices.** Heat ghee or oil in a small skillet, bloom cumin, mustard seed, chili, garlic, or curry leaves for 30-60 seconds.
steps.expect: spices sizzle and smell fragrant, not burnt.

steps.action: **Pour tempering into dal.** Stir hot spiced fat through the pot or spoon it over bowls. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* wet curry leaves can spit in hot oil; dry them and keep your face back.
steps.expect: aroma intensifies immediately.

recipes.verification: The lentils are fully tender, the dal has a spoonable stew texture, and the tempered spices smell fragrant without burnt bitterness.

recipes.title: cook lentils
recipes.name: cook-lentils
recipes.goal: Lentils are cooked without soaking until tender, with the type of lentil matched to the dish and the salt managed for good texture.

steps.action: **Sort and rinse.** Spread lentils briefly to check for stones, then rinse under cool water
steps.expect: rinse water runs mostly clear and no grit remains.

steps.action: **Choose the cooking goal.** [BRANCH: red for soft puree | green or brown for intact grains] match the lentil to soup, salad, curry, or side dish
steps.expect: the selected lentil type fits the desired final texture.

steps.action: **Add liquid.** Put lentils in a pot with about 3 parts water or stock to 1 part lentils
steps.expect: lentils are covered by at least 2 cm of liquid.

steps.action: **Add aromatics if using.** Add bay leaf, garlic, onion, or herbs, but keep acidic ingredients out for now
steps.expect: aromatics are submerged and easy to remove later.

steps.action: **Simmer gently.** Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer with small bubbles
steps.expect: lentils move slightly without violently bouncing.

steps.action: **Salt at the right time.** Salt early for seasoned lentils if they are fresh, or halfway through if you are worried they are old and tough
steps.expect: the cooking liquid tastes lightly seasoned.

steps.action: **Check doneness.** Taste red lentils after 10 minutes and green or brown lentils after 18 minutes
steps.expect: lentils are tender at the center with the texture your dish needs.

steps.action: **Drain or hold.** Drain lentils for salad, or keep them in their liquid for soup and stew
steps.expect: the finished lentils are not sitting in unwanted excess liquid.

recipes.verification: Three lentils from different parts of the pot are tender at the center and match the intended texture: creamy for red, intact for green or brown.

recipes.title: cook pasta
recipes.name: cook-pasta
recipes.goal: Pasta cooked to al dente, seasoned from the water, married to its sauce, and on the table without a starch-glued colander disaster.

steps.action: **Boil abundant water.** Roughly a liter per 100 g of pasta; crowded pasta cooks unevenly and glues. Lid on for speed (`daily/food/boil-water`).
steps.expect: a full rolling boil before any pasta enters.

steps.action: **Salt the water generously.** About a tablespoon per few liters, into the boil. Salted water is the only chance to season the pasta itself; the old line is it should taste like the sea.
steps.expect: visibly salted, briefly calmer, then boiling again.

steps.action: **Add the pasta and stir within the first minute.** Long shapes fan into the pot and soften down; the first-minute stir is what prevents sticking, more than any oil (oil in the water mostly coats the drain).
steps.expect: pasta fully submerged and moving freely after the stir.

steps.action: **Cook at a lively boil, stirring occasionally, and set a timer for two minutes under the packet time.** The packet number lands soft; the check starts early.
steps.expect: timer running; occasional stirs; foam managed by lowering heat slightly or resting a spoon across the pot.

steps.action: **Test by biting.** From the timer's ring, fish a piece every minute: al dente means tender with a slight firm core, no white chalky center.
steps.expect: the bite test, not the clock, makes the call.

steps.action: **Reserve a cup of the cooking water, then drain.** Cup first, always, because the colander move is irreversible. Drain promptly; do not rinse (the surface starch is what lets sauce cling; rinsing is only for cold pasta salads). ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the pour is a steam-and-boiling-water moment; pour away from yourself, face back from the steam.
steps.expect: pasta in the colander, starchy water saved, nobody steamed.

steps.action: **Marry pasta and sauce in the pan, loosening with the reserved water.** Pasta into the sauce (never sauce ladled onto naked pasta on plates, ideally), a splash of the starchy water, and a minute of tossing over heat until the sauce coats and clings.
steps.expect: glossy, coated pasta; the water's starch visibly binding sauce to noodle.

steps.action: **Serve immediately.** Pasta continues softening as it sits; the table waits for pasta, not the reverse.
steps.expect: plates out within minutes, cheese and pepper at the table.

recipes.verification: The pasta passes the bite test at al dente, tastes seasoned on its own, wears its sauce glossily thanks to the reserved water, reached the table promptly, and the stove shows no boil-over archaeology.

recipes.title: cook quinoa
recipes.name: cook-quinoa
recipes.goal: Quinoa is rinsed, cooked, rested, and fluffed into tender separate grains without bitterness or a soggy bottom.

steps.action: **Measure quinoa.** Use the serving amount needed, commonly 1 cup dry quinoa for about 3 cups cooked.
steps.expect: dry quinoa is measured before rinsing.

steps.action: **Rinse away bitterness.** Put quinoa in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse under cool running water for 30-60 seconds while rubbing lightly.
steps.expect: runoff looks clearer and the grains smell less grassy.

steps.action: **Drain thoroughly.** Shake the strainer and let excess water drip off.
steps.expect: quinoa is damp, not carrying a pool of rinse water.

steps.action: **Toast if desired.** Warm drained quinoa in the dry saucepan for 1-2 minutes, stirring.
steps.expect: grains smell nutty and no longer hiss with moisture.

steps.action: **Add liquid at the right ratio.** Use 1 3/4 to 2 cups liquid per 1 cup rinsed quinoa, plus a pinch of salt.
steps.expect: liquid level covers the grains evenly.

steps.action: **Bring to a boil, then reduce.** Heat uncovered until bubbling, then cover and lower to a gentle simmer.
steps.expect: lid is on and only faint steam escapes.

steps.action: **Cook without stirring.** Simmer for 12-15 minutes until most liquid is absorbed.
steps.expect: small steam holes appear and the pan sounds quieter.

steps.action: **Rest off heat.** Turn off the burner and let the covered pot sit 5-10 minutes.
steps.expect: remaining steam finishes hydration without scorching.

steps.action: **Check doneness.** Look for translucent grains with tiny white germ rings visible.
steps.expect: grains are tender with a slight pop, not chalky.

steps.action: **Fork-fluff.** Gently lift and separate the grains with a fork, scraping the bottom lightly.
steps.expect: quinoa loosens into separate grains and steam escapes.

recipes.verification: Quinoa is tender, has visible germ rings, tastes clean rather than bitter, and separates when lifted with a fork.

recipes.title: cook rice in a rice cooker
recipes.name: cook-rice-in-a-rice-cooker
recipes.goal: Rice is rinsed, cooked in a rice cooker, rested, and fluffed without scorching or wet pockets.

steps.action: **Measure rice.** Add rice with the cooker cup or a standard cup, noting the amount.
steps.expect: rice quantity matches a cooker water line or known ratio.

steps.action: **Rinse in the inner pot or bowl.** Swirl with cold water and drain 2-4 times.
steps.expect: water changes from milky to lightly cloudy.

steps.action: **Add water.** Fill to the matching line for that rice type, or use the package ratio. [BRANCH: white rice | brown rice]
steps.expect: rice is level and water sits at the correct mark.

steps.action: **Seat the pot.** Dry the outside of the inner pot and place it flat in the cooker.
steps.expect: pot contacts the heating plate and no water drips into the cooker body.

steps.action: **Start cooking.** Close the lid and press the cook or rice setting.
steps.expect: indicator shows cooking and steam begins later in the cycle.

steps.action: **Let it switch and rest.** When the cooker changes to warm, wait 10 minutes without opening.
steps.expect: steam settles and the top grains look plump.

steps.action: **Fluff gently.** Open away from your face and fold rice with a paddle.
steps.expect: grains separate or cling as intended with no crunchy center.

steps.action: **Hold or store.** Keep warm only for serving time, or refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours.
steps.expect: rice is either hot for service or cooling quickly below 4 °C.

recipes.verification: Rice is tender through the center, evenly hydrated from top to bottom, not burnt, and leftovers are cooled or held safely.

recipes.title: cook rice
recipes.name: cook-rice
recipes.goal: A batch of rice cooked to fluffy, separate (or intentionally sticky) grains — not burnt, crunchy, or gluey.

steps.action: **Measure the rice.** ~¾ cup dry per hungry person.
steps.expect: rice in a bowl or the cooker pot, quantity known in "cups".

steps.action: **Rinse until the water runs mostly clear.** Cover with cold water, agitate with fingers, pour off the cloudy water; repeat 2–3×.
steps.expect: rinse water goes from milky to nearly clear — this is what prevents gluey rice.

steps.action: **Add water by ratio.** Long-grain white: 1 : 1.5 (rice : water). Rice cooker: fill to the matching numbered line instead.
steps.expect: correct water level; a pinch of salt in if desired.

steps.action: **Bring to a boil uncovered, then drop to the lowest heat and lid on.** [BRANCH: rice cooker → press cook and skip to step 6]
steps.expect: brief visible boil, then a quiet simmer under a closed lid.

steps.action: **Simmer ~15 min without lifting the lid.** The trapped steam is doing the cooking; every peek costs it.
steps.expect: faint hissing that quiets near the end; no burnt smell (burnt smell → F2).

steps.action: **Rest 10 minutes off the heat, lid still on.** Rice cooker: after it clicks to "keep warm", same rest.
steps.expect: untouched pot; the rest lets moisture equalize so the bottom isn't wet and the top isn't dry.

steps.action: **Fluff with a fork or paddle and serve.** Gentle folding, not stirring.
steps.expect: grains separate and tender all the way through.

recipes.verification: Grains are tender through the center, distinct (unless sticky was intended), nothing is burnt to the pot beyond a light film, and quantity matches the plan.

recipes.title: cook salmon
recipes.name: cook-salmon
recipes.goal: Cook a skin-on salmon fillet with crisp skin, moist flesh, and doneness that is easy to confirm.

steps.action: **Dry the fish.** Pat the skin and flesh very dry with paper towels, especially along the skin edges.
steps.expect: the skin feels tacky rather than wet.

steps.action: **Season just before cooking.** Salt the flesh and skin lightly and let the fillet sit only while the pan heats.
steps.expect: salt is visible and no liquid pools on the fish.

steps.action: **Heat the pan.** Add a thin film of oil to a skillet over medium-high heat until the oil shimmers.
steps.expect: the oil moves quickly and a corner of fish would sizzle on contact.

steps.action: **Start skin down.** Place the fillet skin-side down, laying it away from you to avoid splatter.
steps.expect: the skin sizzles immediately.

steps.action: **Press flat briefly.** Hold the fillet down with a spatula for 10 seconds so the skin does not curl.
steps.expect: the skin stays in full contact with the pan.

steps.action: **Cook 70 percent skin-side down.** Leave it mostly undisturbed for 4 to 7 minutes, lowering heat if the skin darkens too fast.
steps.expect: the opaque cooked band climbs about two thirds up the side.

steps.action: **Flip briefly.** Turn the fillet and cook the flesh side for 30 to 90 seconds.
steps.expect: the top surface turns lightly opaque but does not dry out.

steps.action: **Check doneness.** [BRANCH: thermometer | flake test] aim for 50 C to 52 C for medium, 63 C for fully cooked, or flesh that flakes with slight translucency in the center.
steps.expect: the thickest part matches the chosen doneness.

steps.action: **Rest skin up.** Move the fish to a plate skin-side up for 2 minutes.
steps.expect: carryover heat finishes the center and the skin stays crisp.

steps.action: **Serve promptly.** Plate with sauce beside the skin, not poured over it.
steps.expect: the skin remains crisp when served.

recipes.verification: The salmon skin is browned and crisp, and the thickest part reaches the chosen temperature or flakes cleanly.

recipes.title: cook shrimp
recipes.name: cook-shrimp
recipes.goal: Shrimp are thawed, cleaned, and cooked quickly until juicy, opaque, and curled into a loose C shape.

steps.action: **Thaw safely.** [BRANCH: overnight in refrigerator | sealed bag under cold running water for 10 to 20 minutes]
steps.expect: shrimp bend easily and have no icy core.

steps.action: **Peel if needed.** Remove shells, leaving tails on only if wanted for serving.
steps.expect: flesh is exposed and shells are set aside for disposal or stock.

steps.action: **Devein.** Cut a shallow line along the back and lift out the dark vein with a knife tip.
steps.expect: the back is clean or only a harmless clear line remains.

steps.action: **Dry thoroughly.** Pat shrimp on both sides with paper towels.
steps.expect: surfaces feel tacky, not wet.

steps.action: **Heat the pan.** Warm a skillet over medium-high heat, then add a thin film of oil.
steps.expect: oil shimmers and a shrimp sizzles immediately on contact.

steps.action: **Cook briefly.** Add shrimp in one layer, salt lightly, and cook 1 to 2 minutes per side.
steps.expect: the first side turns pink and opaque around the edges.

steps.action: **Stop at C shape.** Flip once and remove shrimp when curled like a C, not a tight O.
steps.expect: centers are opaque and the curve is relaxed.

steps.action: **Rest off heat.** Move shrimp to a plate and season with lemon, butter, herbs, or sauce.
steps.expect: carryover heat finishes them without a rubbery texture.

recipes.verification: Every shrimp is opaque through the thickest part and curled into a C shape, with no translucent raw gray areas.

recipes.title: cut a mango
recipes.name: cut-a-mango
recipes.goal: A mango is cut away from its flat pit into clean pieces with minimal waste and safe knife control.

steps.action: **Find the pit direction.** Stand the mango stem-end up and notice the wider, flatter sides.
steps.expect: the flat pit runs parallel to the broad cheeks.

steps.action: **Slice off the first cheek.** Cut about 1/4 inch from center along one broad side, following the pit.
steps.expect: a thick oval cheek comes away with little hard white pit.

steps.action: **Slice off the second cheek.** Repeat on the other broad side.
steps.expect: two cheeks and a pit strip remain.

steps.action: **Trim the pit strip.** Cut narrow side pieces from around the pit.
steps.expect: most usable flesh is removed from the hard center.

steps.action: **Choose a cutting method.** [BRANCH: hedgehog scoring for cubes | peel-the-strip method for slices]
steps.expect: the method matches how ripe and soft the mango is.

steps.action: **Score cheeks for cubes.** Cut a grid through the flesh but not the skin, then turn the cheek inside out.
steps.expect: cubes stand up like a hedgehog pattern.

steps.action: **Remove the pieces.** Slice cubes off the skin, or peel a strip and slice flesh directly from it.
steps.expect: edible pieces drop cleanly onto the board.

steps.action: **Clean up sticky surfaces.** Wipe the board and knife before they get slick.
steps.expect: knife handle and board are no longer slippery.

recipes.verification: The pit is mostly bare, the edible mango is in bite-size pieces or slices, and no large hard pit fragments remain.

recipes.title: cut a pineapple
recipes.name: cut-a-pineapple
recipes.goal: A pineapple trimmed, peeled, eyes removed, cored, and cut into spears or chunks.

steps.action: **Trim top and base.** Lay pineapple on its side and cut off the crown and bottom.
steps.expect: two flat ends make the fruit stand stable.

steps.action: **Stand it upright.** Put the broad flat base on the board and hold the top with a claw grip.
steps.expect: pineapple does not wobble.

steps.action: **Cut down the skin.** Slice from top to bottom following the curve, removing peel in strips.
steps.expect: yellow flesh shows with some brown eyes remaining.

steps.action: **Remove the eyes.** Use a paring knife to cut shallow diagonal channels following the spiral rows of eyes.
steps.expect: tough brown spots are gone with minimal flesh loss.

steps.action: **Quarter lengthwise.** Cut the peeled pineapple from top to bottom into four wedges.
steps.expect: each wedge has a strip of pale core at the inner edge.

steps.action: **Cut out the core.** Lay each wedge flat and slice away the firm inner core.
steps.expect: only tender yellow flesh remains.

steps.action: **Choose final shape.** [BRANCH: spears | chunks] Leave long wedges as spears, or cut crosswise into bite-size pieces.
steps.expect: pieces are even for serving.

steps.action: **Collect juice and clean.** Move pieces to a bowl and wipe the board before it gets slippery.
steps.expect: fruit is ready and the work surface is safe. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* deep peel cuts waste fruit; follow the curve and remove eyes separately.

recipes.verification: Pineapple pieces have no tough skin, eyes, or core, and are cut evenly into the chosen shape.

recipes.title: cut a watermelon
recipes.name: cut-a-watermelon
recipes.goal: A watermelon cut safely into wedges, batons, or rindless cubes with stable flat surfaces throughout.

steps.action: **Wash the rind.** Rinse and dry the outside before cutting through it.
steps.expect: dirt from the rind will not drag into the flesh.

steps.action: **Trim a small base.** Slice a thin piece from one side if the melon rolls badly.
steps.expect: melon sits more steadily.

steps.action: **Halve the melon.** Cut through the center with long steady strokes, keeping the other hand clear.
steps.expect: two halves expose the red flesh.

steps.action: **Place flat side down.** Put one half cut-side down before any smaller cuts.
steps.expect: the half is stable and safe to cut.

steps.action: **Choose the cut.** [BRANCH: wedges | batons | cubes] Pick wedges for hand eating, batons for parties, or rindless cubes for bowls.
steps.expect: the cut plan is set before slicing.

steps.action: **Make wedges or batons.** Slice the half into wide slabs, then cut slabs into wedges or stick-like batons.
steps.expect: pieces have rind handles if desired.

steps.action: **Make rindless cubes.** For cubes, cut the half into slabs, remove rind from each slab, then crosscut into cubes.
steps.expect: cubes are bite-size and rind-free.

steps.action: **Chill or serve.** Move pieces to a tray and wipe juice from the board.
steps.expect: melon is portioned and the board is no longer slick. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once rind is removed, pieces lose their handle; decide serving style first.

recipes.verification: Watermelon is cut into the chosen shape, pieces are stable and even, and no cutting was done on a rolling surface.

recipes.title: cut an onion
recipes.name: cut-an-onion
recipes.goal: An onion cut into even dice (or slices) with all fingers intact, minimal tears, and the board clear.

steps.action: **Cut the onion in half pole-to-pole (through the root).** Stem end to root end, not around the equator.
steps.expect: two halves, each with the root intact at one end.

steps.action: **Peel each half.** Trim the stem (non-root) tip, lift the papery skin plus the first leathery layer from that corner. Leave the root on — it holds the layers together for every following cut.
steps.expect: naked halves, roots still attached.

steps.action: **Place a half flat-side down.** The flat face on the board is your stability; never cut a rounded, rocking piece.
steps.expect: half sits dead stable under light pressure.

steps.action: **Make horizontal cuts toward the root (for a dice), stopping short of it.** Knife parallel to the board, 1–2 cuts through the half's height, fingertips of the holding hand *on top*, well above the blade path.
steps.expect: layered half, still hinged together at the root.

steps.action: **Make vertical lengthwise cuts toward the root, again stopping short.** Spacing = your dice size. Holding hand in the **claw**: fingertips curled under, knuckles forward guiding the flat of the blade.
steps.expect: a fan of strips, root hinge intact, knuckles — not fingertips — nearest the blade.

steps.action: **Slice across the fan to produce dice.** Claw hand walks backward; the blade's flat rides against the knuckles; rock the knife, tip staying low.
steps.expect: even dice falling away; the hand retreats ahead of every cut.

steps.action: **Discard the root nub, sweep dice aside with the knife's *spine*** (edge-sweeping dulls it).
steps.expect: board holding a pile of even dice and one root nub for the compost.

recipes.verification: Dice are even at roughly the intended size, the root nub is discarded, all ten fingertips are accounted for, and the knife is cleaned and stored edge-safe (block/rail/sheath — never loose in a drawer).

recipes.title: debone a chicken thigh
recipes.name: debone-a-chicken-thigh
recipes.goal: A chicken thigh deboned cleanly, kept flat for even cooking, with skin left on or removed as needed.

steps.action: **Set skin side down.** Place the thigh on the board with the bone side facing up.
steps.expect: the bone is visible or easy to feel through the meat.

steps.action: **Locate the bone.** Run fingers along the center ridge and identify both ends.
steps.expect: you know the exact line to cut.

steps.action: **Cut along one side.** Use short strokes against the bone, keeping fingertips curled back.
steps.expect: one side of the bone is exposed.

steps.action: **Cut along the other side.** Repeat tight to the bone without cutting through the skin.
steps.expect: the bone stands free along both edges.

steps.action: **Scrape under the bone.** Angle the blade against bone and scrape meat away in small strokes.
steps.expect: meat releases while staying in one flat piece.

steps.action: **Free the ends.** Cut around cartilage at each end and lift the bone out.
steps.expect: the thigh opens boneless with minimal meat on the bone.

steps.action: **Trim and flatten.** [BRANCH: skin-on | skin-off] Leave skin for crisping, or peel it off; trim knobs, then open the thigh flat.
steps.expect: thickness is even for cooking.

steps.action: **Save or discard bones.** Move bones to stock or trash and sanitize the board.
steps.expect: raw poultry scraps are contained. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* removing skin changes browning and moisture; confirm skin-on or skin-off before trimming.

recipes.verification: The thigh is boneless, mostly even in thickness, and the chosen skin status matches the cooking plan.

recipes.title: deep fry safely at home
recipes.name: deep-fry-safely-at-home
recipes.goal: Food is deep-fried in a pot with controlled oil temperature, safe loading, and clear fire response.

steps.action: **Choose the pot.** Use a heavy pot and fill oil no more than halfway.
steps.expect: at least 8 cm empty space remains above the oil.

steps.action: **Dry the food.** Pat food dry and shake off excess marinade, ice, or loose flour.
steps.expect: surface is damp at most, with no dripping water.

steps.action: **Set up landing zone.** Place a rack or towels on a tray beside the stove.
steps.expect: cooked food has a clear destination before oil is hot.

steps.action: **Heat oil slowly.** Warm oil to the recipe temperature, usually 165-190 °C.
steps.expect: thermometer rises steadily and oil shimmers without smoking.

steps.action: **Load small batches.** Lower food away from your body with tongs or a spider. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* dropped food can splash hot oil; lower pieces gently and do not crowd.
steps.expect: bubbling surrounds food and oil level stays safely below the rim.

steps.action: **Control temperature.** Adjust heat to keep oil in range. [BRANCH: oil too cool | oil too hot]
steps.expect: food bubbles actively without smoking.

steps.action: **Cook to doneness.** Fry until exterior is browned and interior reaches its safe temperature, such as chicken at 74 °C.
steps.expect: coating is crisp and meat juices run clear when applicable.

steps.action: **Drain and season.** Lift food out, let oil drip back, then move to rack and salt while hot.
steps.expect: food crackles lightly and excess oil drains away.

steps.action: **Cool oil before handling.** Turn off heat and leave oil uncovered until fully cool.
steps.expect: oil is room temperature before straining or disposal.

recipes.verification: Oil stayed below smoke point, food is crisp and fully cooked to safe internal temperature, no water contacted hot oil, and cooled oil was handled only after reaching room temperature.

recipes.title: defrost frozen food
recipes.name: defrost-frozen-food
recipes.goal: Frozen food is thawed by one of the three safe methods and cooked on the right timeline, without ever taking a bath in the danger zone on the counter.

steps.action: **Choose the method by lead time.** [BRANCH: cooking tomorrow → fridge | cooking within the hour or two → cold water bath | cooking right now → microwave defrost, or cook straight from frozen where the food allows]
steps.expect: a method matched to the clock, chosen before anything leaves the freezer.

steps.action: **Fridge method: transfer to a plate or container on a low shelf.** The plate catches drips; the low shelf protects everything below (`embodied/kitchen/store-groceries`'s raw-meat-below rule). Allow roughly 12 to 24 hours for typical portions, a full day per couple of kilos for large items.
steps.expect: food thawing slowly at safe temperature; thawed items then keep a day or two in the fridge, which makes this the most forgiving method.

steps.action: **Cold water method: submerge in a sealed bag in cold tap water, changing the water every 30 minutes.** Sealed matters (waterlogged food and contaminated water both ruin things); cold matters (warm water is the counter problem with extra steps). Small portions thaw in under an hour.
steps.expect: water refreshed on schedule; food pliable within the hour; **cook immediately after**.

steps.action: **Microwave method: use the defrost setting with the weight entered, turning and separating as prompted.** Edges will start cooking slightly; that is the method's tradeoff.
steps.expect: thawed, possibly part-warm food; **cook immediately after**, because parts of it just visited warm temperatures.

steps.action: **Cook-from-frozen where it works.** Vegetables, dumplings, thin fish fillets, burger patties, and most prepared foods cook honestly from frozen with a few extra minutes; packaging often says so. Large roasts and whole poultry do not.
steps.expect: the packet's from-frozen instructions followed, core cooked through (juices clear, or steaming-hot centers per `daily/food/use-a-microwave`'s standard).

steps.action: **Verify the thaw before cooking normally.** Flexible, no ice crystals in the center, a knife meets no frozen core.
steps.expect: fully thawed texture, then straight into the planned cooking.

recipes.verification: The method matched the timeline, nothing proteinaceous ever sat at room temperature, water-bath and microwave thaws went straight into cooking, drips stayed on the catch plate, and the cooked result reached steaming-hot centers.

recipes.title: deglaze a pan
recipes.name: deglaze-a-pan
recipes.goal: Turn browned fond in a pan into a concentrated sauce base without burning it or washing flavor down the sink.

steps.action: **Pause the heat.** Move the pan off heat if the fond is very dark or the fat is smoking; pour off excess fat, leaving a thin film
steps.expect: sizzling calms and browned bits remain on the pan

steps.action: **Choose the liquid.** [BRANCH: wine or cider for acidity | stock for savory body | water for neutral flavor] measure 2 tablespoons to 1/2 cup
steps.expect: liquid is ready before the hot pan needs it

steps.action: **Add liquid safely.** Return to medium heat and pour liquid in from the side. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* alcohol vapor can flare, so turn gas off briefly for wine or spirits
steps.expect: steam rises and the fond starts loosening

steps.action: **Scrape thoroughly.** Drag the spoon across the bottom and corners while the liquid bubbles
steps.expect: brown bits dissolve into the liquid

steps.action: **Reduce.** Simmer until the liquid is glossy and slightly syrupy
steps.expect: volume drops and bubbles look tighter

steps.action: **Taste late.** Taste after reducing, then add salt, acid, or a small knob of butter
steps.expect: flavor is roasted and balanced

steps.action: **Use the base.** Pour into a sauce, spoon over food, or continue with cream or butter
steps.expect: pan is mostly clean and sauce tastes browned, not burnt

recipes.verification: The fond has dissolved into a reduced liquid that tastes savory and roasted without burnt bitterness.

recipes.title: devein shrimp
recipes.name: devein-shrimp
recipes.goal: Shrimp cleaned of the dark digestive tract, with shells left on or removed as the recipe needs.

steps.action: **Keep shrimp cold.** Work from the refrigerator in small batches, leaving the rest chilled.
steps.expect: shrimp feel cold and firm, not warm or limp.

steps.action: **Choose shell status.** [BRANCH: shell-on | peeled] For shell-on shrimp, leave the shell attached and slit through it; for peeled shrimp, pull off shell segments and legs first.
steps.expect: each shrimp is ready for a shallow cut along the back.

steps.action: **Expose the back line.** Hold the shrimp curved-side up, fingers curled in a claw away from the blade.
steps.expect: the dark line along the outer curve is visible or traceable.

steps.action: **Make a shallow back slit.** Use the tip of a sharp knife to cut 1/8 inch deep from head end toward tail, following the curve.
steps.expect: the flesh opens slightly without cutting the shrimp in half.

steps.action: **Lift the vein.** Slide the knife tip, skewer, or fingertip under the dark tract and pull it out in one piece when possible.
steps.expect: the groove is clear or only tiny fragments remain.

steps.action: **Rinse briefly.** Pass the slit under cold water and wipe out fragments with a fingertip.
steps.expect: no gritty dark line remains in the back cut.

steps.action: **Butterfly when wanted.** [BRANCH: normal | butterfly] Stop after the shallow slit for normal prep, or deepen the cut almost to the belly for butterflied shrimp.
steps.expect: butterflied shrimp open flat but remain hinged.

steps.action: **Dry before cooking.** Pat shrimp dry on towels before seasoning or searing.
steps.expect: surfaces are dry enough to brown instead of steam. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a deep butterfly cut cannot be undone; confirm the recipe wants flattened shrimp first.

recipes.verification: Each shrimp has a clean back groove with no gritty dark tract, stays cold, and is dry before cooking.

recipes.title: dice a tomato
recipes.name: dice-a-tomato
recipes.goal: A tomato diced cleanly into even pieces, with seeds kept for juiciness or removed for drier dishes.

steps.action: **Wash and dry.** Rinse the tomato and dry the skin so it does not slide.
steps.expect: tomato feels clean and less slippery.

steps.action: **Core the stem.** Use a paring knife to cut a shallow cone around the stem scar.
steps.expect: tough core lifts out with minimal flesh.

steps.action: **Create a stable side.** Halve the tomato through the core line and set cut-side down.
steps.expect: each half sits flat on the board.

steps.action: **Choose seed handling.** [BRANCH: seeds-in | seeds-out] Keep seeds for salsa or salad; scoop them out for bruschetta or omelets.
steps.expect: tomato moisture matches the dish.

steps.action: **Cut planks.** With a serrated knife, saw gently into even slices while holding a claw grip.
steps.expect: skin cuts cleanly without crushing flesh.

steps.action: **Cut sticks.** Stack one or two planks and cut into strips the width of your dice.
steps.expect: strips stay aligned and even.

steps.action: **Cut crosswise.** Rotate strips and cut into cubes using short saw strokes.
steps.expect: dice fall cleanly with limited juice loss.

steps.action: **Drain if needed.** Move dice to a sieve or towel for very wet tomatoes.
steps.expect: excess juice drains without smashing the dice. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* squeezing seeds out crushes texture; decide seeds-in or seeds-out before dicing.

recipes.verification: Tomato dice are roughly even, core is removed, and seed level matches the intended use.

recipes.title: ferment sauerkraut
recipes.name: ferment-sauerkraut
recipes.goal: Cabbage is salted and fermented under brine into crisp, sour sauerkraut.

steps.action: **Weigh cabbage.** Remove dirty outer leaves, core the cabbage, and weigh the shredded edible cabbage.
steps.expect: a known cabbage weight in grams.

steps.action: **Salt at 2 percent.** Add 20 g salt per 1000 g cabbage and toss thoroughly.
steps.expect: salt is evenly distributed and cabbage begins to look glossy.

steps.action: **Massage for brine.** Squeeze and knead 5-10 minutes until liquid pools in the bowl.
steps.expect: cabbage bends without snapping and releases enough brine to drip from a handful.

steps.action: **Pack the jar.** Press cabbage tightly into a clean jar, leaving at least 3 cm headspace.
steps.expect: no large air pockets and brine rises above the cabbage.

steps.action: **Submerge everything.** Place a weight or clean folded cabbage leaf on top so solids stay below brine.
steps.expect: cabbage is fully covered by brine.

steps.action: **Ferment at room temperature.** Cover loosely or use an airlock and set the jar on a tray for 5-21 days. [BRANCH: mild | sour]
steps.expect: bubbles appear after 1-3 days and aroma turns pleasantly sour.

steps.action: **Burp if sealed.** Open a tight lid daily to release gas. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* pressure can crack glass; do not let a sealed jar build pressure.
steps.expect: gas escapes and brine remains over the cabbage.

steps.action: **Taste and refrigerate.** When sour enough, remove any harmless surface kahm yeast, cap, and refrigerate.
steps.expect: kraut is pale, crisp, salty-sour, and cold storage slows fermentation.
