recipes.verification: Sauerkraut is fully submerged during fermentation, tastes cleanly sour, remains crisp, and has no fuzzy mold, pink color, rotten smell, or slimy brine.

recipes.title: fillet a fish
recipes.name: fillet-a-fish
recipes.goal: A whole fish broken into clean fillets, with pin bones removed and skin kept on or taken off as needed.

steps.action: **Dry and position the fish.** Pat the fish dry and lay it belly facing you, head to your non-knife side.
steps.expect: the fish grips the board instead of skating.

steps.action: **Cut behind the gill plate.** Angle the knife behind the gill and pectoral fin until you touch the backbone.
steps.expect: a clean diagonal cut reaches bone without sawing through it.

steps.action: **Turn onto the spine.** Rotate the blade flat toward the tail and make short strokes along the backbone.
steps.expect: the top edge of the fillet starts releasing in one sheet.

steps.action: **Ride the rib cage.** Keep the blade flexible and close to bone, lifting the fillet with your claw hand as you cut.
steps.expect: ribs show cleanly with little flesh left on them.

steps.action: **Finish through the tail.** Keep the blade flat and slice out through the tail end.
steps.expect: one attached fillet comes free with even thickness.

steps.action: **Repeat the second side.** Flip the fish and repeat behind the gill, along the spine, over the ribs, and out the tail.
steps.expect: two fillets and one mostly clean frame.

steps.action: **Remove pin bones.** Run fingertips from head end to tail, then pull bones in their natural angle with tweezers.
steps.expect: no sharp pin bones catch your fingertip.

steps.action: **Skin off if desired.** [BRANCH: skin-on | skin-off] For skin-off, start at the tail, grip skin with a towel, and slide the knife flat between skin and flesh.
steps.expect: skin separates in one strip and flesh remains smooth. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once skinned, the crisp-skin option is gone; confirm the cooking method first.

recipes.verification: Fillets are free of pin bones, trimmed cleanly from the frame, and either skin-on or skin-off to match the intended cooking method.

recipes.title: frost a layer cake
recipes.name: frost-a-layer-cake
recipes.goal: Cake layers are filled, crumb-coated, chilled, and frosted into a stable, even layer cake.

steps.action: **Level layers.** Trim domed tops with a serrated knife if needed.
steps.expect: layers sit flat without rocking.

steps.action: **Anchor the first layer.** Smear a dab of frosting on the board and place the first layer on it.
steps.expect: cake grips the board and does not slide.

steps.action: **Add filling.** Spread an even layer of frosting or filling, keeping it inside the edge.
steps.expect: filling thickness is even and not spilling down the sides.

steps.action: **Stack layers.** Place the next layer centered over the first.
steps.expect: sides line up and stack looks vertical.

steps.action: **Apply crumb coat.** Spread a thin coat over top and sides to trap crumbs.
steps.expect: cake is lightly covered and crumbs are sealed in the thin layer.

steps.action: **Chill to set.** Refrigerate 20-30 minutes until the crumb coat firms.
steps.expect: surface feels cool and no longer sticky.

steps.action: **Apply final coat.** Add frosting to top and sides, then smooth with spatula or scraper.
steps.expect: cake has even coverage and clean edges.

steps.action: **Finish decorations.** Pipe, texture, or garnish while frosting is workable. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cut fruit and perishable garnishes shorten safe holding time; add them near service.
steps.expect: decorations adhere and cake remains stable.

recipes.verification: Cake stands level, layers are aligned, crumbs are sealed, final frosting covers top and sides evenly, and perishable fillings are held safely.

recipes.title: froth milk for coffee
recipes.name: froth-milk-for-coffee
recipes.goal: Turn cold milk into glossy microfoam that pours with coffee instead of sitting as dry bubbles.

steps.action: **Start cold.** Fill pitcher or jar no more than halfway with cold milk
steps.expect: milk has room to expand

steps.action: **Choose method.** [BRANCH: steam wand | frother | jar method] use clean equipment
steps.expect: tool is ready

steps.action: **Add air early.** Keep wand or frother near the surface, or shake jar before heating
steps.expect: volume increases

steps.action: **Texture.** Sink the tip deeper and swirl; microwave shaken jar with lid off
steps.expect: foam turns glossy

steps.action: **Stop warm.** Stop around 140 to 150 F or when pitcher is hot but holdable
steps.expect: milk smells sweet

steps.action: **Polish.** Tap and swirl to pop large bubbles
steps.expect: surface looks like wet paint

steps.action: **Pour now.** Pour steadily into coffee. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overheated milk tastes cooked and will not become sweet again
steps.expect: foam flows with milk

recipes.verification: milk is warm, glossy, and made of fine bubbles

recipes.title: fry an egg
recipes.name: fry-an-egg
recipes.goal: An egg fried to your chosen doneness — runny sunny-side-up through fully-set over-hard — with an intact yolk (unless scrambled was the plan) and no burnt edges.

steps.action: **Heat the pan on medium, not high.** Add a small knob of butter or ~1 tsp oil.
steps.expect: butter foams gently without browning / oil shimmers without smoking. Smoking pan → too hot, F1.

steps.action: **Crack the egg.** Tap firmly once on a *flat* surface (not the pan edge — drives shell in), part the shell with thumbs close to the pan or into a bowl first, and slide it in low.
steps.expect: yolk intact, white contained, no shell fragments (fragment → fish out with a shell half, it attracts the piece).

steps.action: **Let it set undisturbed on medium-low.** Salt and pepper the top.
steps.expect: white turning opaque from the edges inward within a minute; gentle sizzle, not violent sputtering.

steps.action: **Choose the finish.** [BRANCH: sunny-side-up → cover with a lid 1 min so steam sets the top | over-easy → flip gently when the white is set, 20–30 s on side two | over-hard → flip and press yolk to break, cook till firm]
steps.expect: whites fully set (no clear slime) in every finish; yolk state per choice.

steps.action: **Slide onto the plate.** Spatula fully under before lifting; tilt the pan to help.
steps.expect: egg lands intact; runny yolk unbroken until you break it on purpose.

steps.action: **Kill the heat and move the pan off the burner.**
steps.expect: stove off; pan cooling on an idle burner.

recipes.verification: Whites fully opaque and set, yolk in the chosen state, no burnt frill, egg intact on the plate, and the burner is off.

recipes.title: hard boil eggs
recipes.name: hard-boil-eggs
recipes.goal: Cook eggs in the shell until the whites are fully set and the yolks reach the texture you want, then cool them so they peel cleanly.

steps.action: **Choose the start method.** [BRANCH: cold start | boiling-water drop] Use cold start for fewer cracked shells and boiling-water drop for slightly easier peeling.
steps.expect: one method chosen before heat is turned on.

steps.action: **Load the eggs in one layer.** Put eggs in a saucepan without stacking them.
steps.expect: each egg touches the pan bottom or sits in a single layer.

steps.action: **Add or heat the water.** Cold start: cover eggs with 2 to 3 cm of cold water. Boiling-water drop: bring enough water to a gentle boil first.
steps.expect: water depth can cover the eggs fully.

steps.action: **Start the timer at the right moment.** Cold start: when water reaches a full boil, turn off heat, cover, and time covered rest. Boiling-water drop: lower eggs into boiling water, reduce to a steady simmer, and time immediately.
steps.expect: timer is running only after the chosen trigger.

steps.action: **Use the texture chart.** Time 6 min for jammy yolks, 8 min for mostly set, 10 min for firm yellow yolks, or 12 min for extra firm yolks.
steps.expect: timer length matches the yolk texture you want.

steps.action: **Prepare an ice bath while eggs cook.** Fill a bowl with ice water deep enough to cover the eggs.
steps.expect: the cooling bowl is ready before the timer ends.

steps.action: **Chill the eggs immediately.** Move eggs into the ice bath for at least 5 min, or 10 min for easy handling.
steps.expect: shells feel cool enough to hold.

steps.action: **Peel under water if serving now.** Crack the wide end first, roll gently, then peel under running water or in the bowl.
steps.expect: the membrane loosens and the shell lifts off in larger pieces.

steps.action: **Store unpeeled eggs if saving.** Dry the shells and refrigerate in a covered container.
steps.expect: eggs are cold, labeled if needed, and not left at room temperature.

recipes.verification: One cooled test egg peels without large white tears, and when cut open the white is fully opaque and the yolk matches the selected timing.

recipes.title: juice a lemon
recipes.name: juice-a-lemon
recipes.goal: Maximum clean lemon juice extracted, with seeds caught and zest saved first when needed.

steps.action: **Zest before cutting.** If zest is needed, grate only the yellow peel before juicing.
steps.expect: zest is fluffy and has no bitter white pith.

steps.action: **Warm the lemon.** Microwave 10 to 15 seconds or place in warm water for a few minutes.
steps.expect: lemon feels slightly warm, not hot.

steps.action: **Roll firmly.** Press the lemon under your palm and roll on the counter to break internal membranes.
steps.expect: fruit softens and gives under pressure.

steps.action: **Cut crosswise.** Use a sharp knife and stable board to halve the lemon around its equator.
steps.expect: two juicy halves expose the segments.

steps.action: **Choose a tool.** [BRANCH: fork | reamer] Use a fork for quick work, or a reamer or press for higher yield.
steps.expect: tool fits into the cut face.

steps.action: **Juice over a strainer.** Twist the fork or reamer while squeezing the lemon half.
steps.expect: juice flows and seeds stay out of the bowl.

steps.action: **Scrape membranes.** Rotate and press the half until the flesh looks collapsed.
steps.expect: little juice remains in the pulp.

steps.action: **Measure and use.** Pour juice through the strainer and use soon for brightest flavor.
steps.expect: clean juice is seed-free and fragrant. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once juiced, zesting is awkward and low-yield; zest first if there is any chance you need it.

recipes.verification: Juice is seed-free, zest is saved if needed, and the squeezed halves are mostly collapsed.

recipes.title: knead bread dough
recipes.name: knead-bread-dough
recipes.goal: Bread dough is developed until elastic enough to trap gas, with hydration handled by feel instead of drowning it in bench flour.

steps.action: **Assess stickiness before adding flour.** Touch the dough with a clean finger and pull away slowly.
steps.expect: tacky dough stretches slightly; soupy dough coats the finger.

steps.action: **Set the dough on the bench.** Use minimal flour for standard dough or wet hands for high-hydration dough.
steps.expect: the dough releases from the bowl in one mass.

steps.action: **Push with the heel.** Press the dough away from you using the heel of one hand.
steps.expect: the dough elongates without tearing into crumbs.

steps.action: **Fold back.** Fold the far edge toward you over the center.
steps.expect: the dough stacks on itself and traps a little tension.

steps.action: **Turn a quarter turn.** Rotate the dough 90 degrees and repeat the push-fold-turn rhythm.
steps.expect: each cycle works a new side of the dough.

steps.action: **Use the scraper, not handfuls of flour.** If the dough sticks, scrape it up and keep moving.
steps.expect: the bench clears and the dough gradually sticks less.

steps.action: **Rest if it fights.** If the dough snaps back hard, cover it for 5 minutes.
steps.expect: the dough relaxes and stretches farther after the pause.

steps.action: **Check texture at 8 to 10 minutes.** Gather the dough into a ball and feel the surface.
steps.expect: the surface is smoother, elastic, and slightly tacky.

steps.action: **Perform the windowpane test.** Pinch off a small piece and stretch it thin between fingers.
steps.expect: it forms a translucent membrane before tearing, or it tears cleanly after a little more kneading.

steps.action: **Shape for proofing.** Tuck the dough into a taut ball and place it seam-side down in a lightly oiled bowl.
steps.expect: the dough holds a rounded shape and springs back slowly when poked.

recipes.verification: The dough is smooth, elastic, slightly tacky, and passes a windowpane test or stretches thin before a clean tear.

recipes.title: make a baked egg
recipes.name: make-a-baked-egg
recipes.goal: A ramekin-baked egg with set whites, a jammy yolk, cream, seasoning, and toast for dipping.

steps.action: **Heat the oven.** Set oven to 375 °F.
steps.expect: oven preheats while the ramekin is prepared.

steps.action: **Butter the ramekin.** Grease the inside lightly with butter or oil.
steps.expect: bottom and sides have a thin sheen.

steps.action: **Add cream.** Pour 1 tbsp cream or milk into the ramekin.
steps.expect: a shallow layer covers the bottom.

steps.action: **Crack in the egg.** Add one egg without breaking the yolk.
steps.expect: yolk sits intact in the center or slightly off-center.

steps.action: **Season lightly.** Add a pinch of salt, pepper, and optional herbs or cheese.
steps.expect: seasoning sits on top without burying the egg.

steps.action: **Use a water bath.** Place ramekin in a baking dish and add hot water halfway up the ramekin sides.
steps.expect: ramekin is stable and surrounded by hot water.

steps.action: **Bake until just set.** Bake 10 to 14 minutes, checking early.
steps.expect: whites are opaque at the edges and yolk still jiggles slightly.

steps.action: **Rest and serve.** Remove carefully, rest 2 minutes, and serve with toast soldiers. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an overbaked yolk turns firm, so pull the egg while the center still jiggles.
steps.expect: spoon breaks into creamy white and jammy yolk.

recipes.verification: The baked egg has opaque set whites, a yolk that is still soft or jammy, and toast ready for dipping.

recipes.title: make a cheese board
recipes.name: make-a-cheese-board
recipes.goal: A cheese board with three contrasting cheeses at full room-temperature flavor, arranged with accompaniments so guests can serve themselves without instructions.

steps.action: **Take the cheese out of the fridge 45-60 minutes before serving.** This is the step that matters most and the one most often skipped. Cold cheese is muted and waxy; fat needs room temperature to carry flavor. Leave wrappers on while tempering so surfaces do not dry out.
steps.expect: soft cheese yields under a gentle press; hard cheese has lost its fridge chill.

steps.action: **Choose for contrast, not theme.** Three is the sweet spot: enough variety, no crowding, one knife each. Confirm the trio spans soft/semi-firm/hard and ideally mixes milk types (cow, goat, sheep).
steps.expect: three cheeses that differ visibly in color and texture on the counter.

steps.action: **Anchor the board with the cheeses first.** Place them spaced apart (roughly a triangle), each with its own knife. Pre-cut a third of the hard cheese into shards and break the first wedge; an untouched board intimidates guests, a started one gets eaten.
steps.expect: three stations, each knifed, hard cheese partially cut, first cuts made.

steps.action: **Fill in accompaniments around the anchors.** Bowls for wet items (honey, jam, olives) so nothing bleeds across the board; crackers in a fan or a separate basket so they stay crisp; grapes in small snippable clusters; sweet things nearer the blue/strong cheese, briny near the rich soft one.
steps.expect: no bare wood showing, wet items contained, every cheese has a natural pairing within reach.

steps.action: **Label anything unusual.** A small flag or card for the blue and anything pungent spares guests a surprise.
steps.expect: strong cheeses identified at a glance.

steps.action: **Serve, and hold back reserves.** Put out about two-thirds of everything; refill from the fridge-tempered reserve as the board wears down rather than crowding it all on at once.
steps.expect: the board still looks composed an hour in.

recipes.verification: Each cheese yields correctly for its type at a touch (soft gives, hard shears clean), every cheese has its own knife and a reachable pairing, wet items are in bowls with no run-off on the board, and strong cheeses are labeled.

recipes.title: make a cheese sauce
recipes.name: make-a-cheese-sauce
recipes.goal: A smooth cheese sauce is built from roux, warm milk, and cheese melted off heat.

steps.action: **Warm the milk.** Heat 500 ml milk until warm but not boiling.
steps.expect: milk steams lightly and will blend into roux faster.

steps.action: **Make the roux.** Melt 30 g butter, whisk in 30 g flour, and cook 1-2 minutes.
steps.expect: paste smells nutty and loses raw flour smell without browning much.

steps.action: **Add milk gradually.** Whisk in warm milk a splash at a time at first, then in larger additions.
steps.expect: sauce stays smooth and thickens after each addition.

steps.action: **Simmer to thicken.** Cook 3-5 minutes, whisking, until it coats a spoon.
steps.expect: no floury taste and bubbles rise slowly.

steps.action: **Turn off heat.** Remove pan from burner before adding cheese.
steps.expect: sauce is hot enough to melt cheese but not boiling.

steps.action: **Melt cheese gently.** Stir in 150-200 g grated cheese by handfuls.
steps.expect: each handful disappears before the next is added.

steps.action: **Season last.** Add salt, pepper, mustard, hot sauce, or nutmeg to taste after cheese is in.
steps.expect: sauce tastes balanced, not flat or overly salty.

steps.action: **Adjust texture.** [BRANCH: too thick: whisk in warm milk | too thin: simmer plain sauce before more cheese]
steps.expect: sauce flows slowly from a spoon.

steps.action: **Hold warm, not hot.** Keep over very low heat or a warm water bath.
steps.expect: sauce remains glossy and does not split.

recipes.verification: The sauce is smooth, glossy, seasoned, and coats a spoon without visible oil separation or flour lumps.

recipes.title: make a compound butter
recipes.name: make-a-compound-butter
recipes.goal: Seasoned butter blended with herbs, garlic, citrus zest, or spices, chilled into a sliceable log.

steps.action: **Soften the butter.** Leave butter out until it dents easily but is not greasy.
steps.expect: fork presses through with light resistance.

steps.action: **Prepare flavorings finely.** Mince herbs, grate garlic, zest citrus, or measure spices.
steps.expect: pieces are small enough to distribute evenly.

steps.action: **Mash butter smooth.** Work the butter in a bowl before adding flavorings.
steps.expect: texture is pliable and lump-free.

steps.action: **Fold in seasonings.** For 1 stick butter, add 1 to 2 tbsp herbs, 1 small grated garlic clove, zest, and salt to taste.
steps.expect: color and aromatics are evenly streaked through.

steps.action: **Taste and adjust.** Spread a little on bread or a warm spoon to check salt and intensity.
steps.expect: flavor is slightly stronger than plain butter because it will be used sparingly.

steps.action: **Shape into a log.** Spoon onto parchment, roll tightly, and twist the ends.
steps.expect: butter forms an even cylinder without large air pockets.

steps.action: **Chill until firm.** Refrigerate 1 hour or freeze 20 minutes for quick slicing.
steps.expect: log holds its shape when unwrapped.

steps.action: **Slice and use.** Cut coins for steak, vegetables, toast, pasta, or rice. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* raw garlic gets stronger as it sits, so do not overload it for long storage.
steps.expect: slices melt evenly over hot food.

recipes.verification: The compound butter is evenly seasoned, firm enough to slice, and melts into food without gritty pockets of seasoning.

recipes.title: make a dessert sauce
recipes.name: make-a-dessert-sauce
recipes.goal: A simple dessert sauce, either chocolate ganache or berry coulis, with pourable consistency.

steps.action: **Choose the sauce.** [BRANCH: ganache | coulis] use chocolate and cream for rich sauce, or berries and sugar for fruit sauce.
steps.expect: ingredients match one path.

steps.action: **Set the ratio.** For ganache, use equal weights chocolate and cream; for coulis, use 2 cups berries to 2 to 4 tbsp sugar.
steps.expect: sauce base is measured before heating.

steps.action: **Make ganache gently.** Heat cream until steaming, pour over chopped chocolate, wait 2 minutes, then stir from the center.
steps.expect: chocolate melts into a glossy sauce.

steps.action: **Make coulis gently.** Simmer berries, sugar, and 1 tsp lemon juice for 5 to 8 minutes.
steps.expect: berries collapse and release syrup.

steps.action: **Adjust consistency.** Thin ganache with warm cream, or reduce coulis by simmering; strain coulis if smoothness matters.
steps.expect: sauce coats a spoon but still pours.

steps.action: **Taste warm.** Add a pinch of salt to ganache or more lemon to coulis if flavor tastes flat.
steps.expect: sweetness has contrast and does not taste dull.

steps.action: **Serve at the right temperature.** Serve ganache warm or room temperature; serve coulis warm, room temperature, or cold.
steps.expect: texture flows over cake, ice cream, pancakes, or fruit.

steps.action: **Store and rewarm.** Refrigerate covered and rewarm ganache gently. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overheated chocolate can split or scorch, so use gentle heat and stop early.
steps.expect: leftover sauce is covered and labeled.

recipes.verification: The dessert sauce is smooth enough for its use, tastes balanced, and pours or drizzles without running like water.

recipes.title: make a frittata
recipes.name: make-a-frittata
recipes.goal: A tender frittata is cooked through, lightly browned on top, and released from the pan in one piece.

steps.action: **Heat the finish source.** [BRANCH: oven at 350 F | broiler on low or with rack 6 inches from heat]
steps.expect: the oven or broiler is hot before the eggs go into the pan.

steps.action: **Prep the fillings.** Slice vegetables thin, grate cheese, and pat wet items dry.
steps.expect: fillings are bite-size and no puddle of moisture sits on the board.

steps.action: **Saute the fillings.** Cook raw vegetables, potatoes, or meats in oil until tender; season them before adding eggs.
steps.expect: fillings smell cooked and any released liquid has boiled off.

steps.action: **Mix the eggs.** Whisk 6 large eggs with 1/4 cup dairy or water, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and pepper.
steps.expect: mixture is uniform yellow with no streaky whites.

steps.action: **Set the bottom.** Lower heat to medium-low, spread fillings evenly, pour eggs over them, and nudge edges inward for 2 to 4 minutes.
steps.expect: edges thicken while the center still jiggles.

steps.action: **Finish gently.** Move the skillet to the oven or broiler. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an overheated handle burns skin, so mark it with a towel or mitt before anyone touches it.
steps.expect: top is just set, with faint browning if broiled.

steps.action: **Check doneness.** Insert a thin knife near the center and tilt the pan slightly.
steps.expect: no loose liquid egg runs into the cut.

steps.action: **Slide out.** Rest 2 minutes, loosen the edge with a silicone spatula, and slide onto a plate.
steps.expect: frittata moves as one round without tearing badly.

recipes.verification: A center cut shows fully set egg, the underside is not blackened, and a slice lifts cleanly enough to hold its shape.

recipes.title: make a grilled cheese
recipes.name: make-a-grilled-cheese
recipes.goal: A grilled cheese sandwich has crisp browned bread, fully melted cheese, and no scorched butter.

steps.action: **Choose cheese that melts.** Use American, cheddar, Monterey Jack, Swiss, mozzarella, or a mix; grate firm cheese if the slices are thick.
steps.expect: cheese pieces are thin enough to soften before the bread burns.

steps.action: **Butter the outside faces.** Spread butter all the way to the corners on one side of each bread slice.
steps.expect: each outside face has a thin even butter coat with no dry corners.

steps.action: **Build the sandwich cold.** Put cheese between the unbuttered faces, keeping fillings thin and dry.
steps.expect: butter is on the outside, cheese is centered, and no wet filling touches the pan.

steps.action: **Preheat low-medium.** Set the skillet over low-medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
steps.expect: a butter crumb sizzles gently instead of smoking.

steps.action: **Start covered.** Place the sandwich in the pan, cover with a lid, and cook 2 to 4 minutes.
steps.expect: the bottom turns golden while trapped heat starts melting the cheese.

steps.action: **Flip once.** Slide the spatula fully under the sandwich, flip in one motion, and cover again.
steps.expect: the first side stays intact and evenly browned.

steps.action: **Finish uncovered if needed.** Remove the lid for the last 30 to 60 seconds if the bread needs more crispness.
steps.expect: both sides are crisp and the cheese looks glossy at the edge.

steps.action: **Rest and cut.** Move to a plate, wait 1 minute, then cut with a serrated knife.
steps.expect: cheese stretches or oozes lightly without flooding the plate.

recipes.verification: The bread is golden and crisp on both outside faces, and the cheese is melted across the center when the sandwich is cut.

recipes.title: make a latte at home
recipes.name: make-a-latte-at-home
recipes.goal: A hot latte is made with espresso or strong coffee, warmed milk, and a foam layer that tastes balanced instead of watery.

steps.action: **Warm the mug.** Fill the mug with hot tap water while you prepare the coffee, then dump it out.
steps.expect: the mug feels warm and will not cool the drink immediately.

steps.action: **Brew the coffee base.** Use 1 double espresso shot, about 2 oz, or 3 to 4 oz of very strong coffee.
steps.expect: the coffee smells concentrated and has no grounds floating in it.

steps.action: **Measure the milk.** Use about 6 oz milk for a classic 1:3 espresso-to-milk latte, or 4 oz for a stronger drink.
steps.expect: the milk amount fits the mug with at least 1 inch of headroom.

steps.action: **Heat and texture the milk.** [BRANCH: steam wand | handheld frother | jar-and-microwave] steam until hot but not boiling, froth after warming with a handheld frother, or shake cold milk in a half-full jar, remove the lid, then microwave 30 to 45 seconds.
steps.expect: milk is hot, lightly foamy, and still smells sweet, not cooked.

steps.action: **Tap and swirl the milk.** Tap the pitcher or jar once, then swirl until the foam and milk look glossy.
steps.expect: large bubbles shrink and the surface looks smooth.

steps.action: **Pour milk into coffee.** Hold back the foam with a spoon at first, pour the hot milk into the coffee, then spoon foam over the top.
steps.expect: the drink is pale brown with a thin cap of foam.

steps.action: **Taste and adjust.** Add sweetener or a pinch of cocoa only after tasting the plain latte. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once syrup or sugar is stirred in, the sweetness cannot be removed, so add half the amount first.
steps.expect: the latte tastes balanced, warm, and not scorched.

recipes.verification: The mug contains hot coffee mixed with roughly 2 to 3 parts textured milk to 1 part espresso or strong coffee, with a smooth foam layer and no scorched flavor.

recipes.title: make a margarita
recipes.name: make-a-margarita
recipes.goal: A bright shaken margarita with tequila, fresh lime, orange liqueur, salt, and enough ice dilution.

steps.action: **Chill the glass.** Put the glass in the freezer or fill it with ice while preparing the drink.
steps.expect: glass is cold by the time the cocktail is strained.

steps.action: **Salt the rim selectively.** Rub a lime wedge around half the rim, dip that side in salt, and shake off excess.
steps.expect: salt sticks in a thin band, with an unsalted side for control.

steps.action: **Juice fresh lime.** Squeeze 1 oz lime juice and strain seeds if needed.
steps.expect: juice smells sharp and fresh, not bottled or dull.

steps.action: **Measure the base.** Add 2 oz blanco tequila, 1 oz lime juice, and 3/4 oz orange liqueur to the shaker.
steps.expect: the ratio is tart before dilution.

steps.action: **Adjust sweetness if needed.** [BRANCH: dry | sweeter] keep as is for dry, or add 1/4 oz agave syrup for sweeter.
steps.expect: sweetness choice is made before ice melts.

steps.action: **Shake hard with ice.** Fill shaker with ice, seal, and shake 10 to 15 seconds.
steps.expect: shaker frosts or gets very cold and the drink sounds lighter.

steps.action: **Strain immediately.** Strain into the prepared glass, either up or over fresh ice.
steps.expect: cold, slightly cloudy drink with no spent shaker ice shards unless desired.

steps.action: **Garnish and serve.** Add a lime wheel or wedge. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* extra salt or syrup cannot be removed cleanly once mixed, so add lightly.
steps.expect: aroma is lime-forward and the first sip is tart, cold, and balanced.

recipes.verification: The margarita is very cold, tart first, lightly orange-sweet, and the salt rim accents the drink without dominating it.

recipes.title: make a marinade
recipes.name: make-a-marinade
recipes.goal: Make a balanced marinade that seasons food without making it mushy or unsafe to cook.

steps.action: **Start with a ratio.** Mix about 3 parts oil, 1 part acid, 1 percent salt by food weight if measuring, and aromatics to taste.
steps.expect: marinade tastes bright, salty, and rounded rather than harsh.

steps.action: **Choose the acid.** [BRANCH: vinegar | citrus | yogurt | wine] Pick one main acidic ingredient so the flavor stays focused.
steps.expect: acid is present but does not dominate the bowl.

steps.action: **Add salt intentionally.** Use kosher salt, soy sauce, fish sauce, or miso, counting salty liquids as part of the seasoning.
steps.expect: a small taste of marinade is noticeably seasoned.

steps.action: **Use the bag method for coverage.** Put food and marinade in a zip-top bag, press out air, seal, and set the bag in a bowl.
steps.expect: marinade contacts most surfaces and the bowl catches leaks.

steps.action: **Refrigerate during marinating.** Place the covered bowl or sealed bag in the refrigerator, not on the counter.
steps.expect: food stays cold until cooking.

steps.action: **Respect time limits.** Marinate fish 15 to 30 min, shrimp 15 to 20 min, chicken 2 to 12 h, pork or beef 2 to 24 h, vegetables 15 min to 2 h.
steps.expect: timer or reminder matches the food type.

steps.action: **Remove food and pat if needed.** Lift food out, let excess drip off, and pat dry for browning.
steps.expect: surface is seasoned but not dripping heavily.

steps.action: **Discard used marinade.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once marinade has touched raw meat, poultry, or seafood, throw it away unless boiled hard as a sauce.
steps.expect: used marinade is not served raw.

steps.action: **Cook promptly.** Move marinated food to the grill, pan, oven, or broiler.
steps.expect: food starts cooking while still cold and safely handled.

recipes.verification: The food has been marinated under refrigeration for an appropriate time, excess marinade is removed, and any marinade that touched raw protein is discarded or boiled.

recipes.title: make a meringue
recipes.name: make-a-meringue
recipes.goal: Egg whites and sugar are whipped into a stable foam with the right peak texture for topping, folding, or baking.

steps.action: **Clean the bowl.** Wipe bowl and whisk with vinegar or lemon juice if greasy.
steps.expect: surfaces feel clean and dry.

steps.action: **Separate eggs.** Place whites in the bowl with no yolk.
steps.expect: whites are clear and free of yellow streaks.

steps.action: **Foam the whites.** Beat on medium until bubbly, then add a pinch of cream of tartar if using.
steps.expect: foam covers the surface with small bubbles.

steps.action: **Add sugar slowly.** Sprinkle in sugar 1 tbsp at a time while beating.
steps.expect: foam thickens and looks glossy instead of grainy.

steps.action: **Whip to target peaks.** [BRANCH: soft peaks | stiff peaks] Continue until peaks curl softly or stand upright.
steps.expect: meringue holds the chosen peak shape.

steps.action: **Check sugar dissolution.** Rub a little meringue between fingers.
steps.expect: texture feels mostly smooth, not sandy.

steps.action: **Use promptly.** Spread, pipe, fold, or bake according to the dessert. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overwhipped dry foam collapses when folded; stop as soon as target peaks appear.
steps.expect: meringue is glossy, cohesive, and holds volume.

recipes.verification: Meringue is glossy, smooth, holds the required peak, has no liquid pooling, and is baked or made with pasteurized whites when served uncooked.

recipes.title: make a milkshake
recipes.name: make-a-milkshake
recipes.goal: Make a cold, thick milkshake that pours slowly, tastes like the chosen flavor, and does not become watery from overblending.

steps.action: **Soften the ice cream slightly.** Let it sit 5 minutes until a scoop presses in without bending the spoon.
steps.expect: the ice cream is soft at the edges but not melted.

steps.action: **Load ice cream first.** Add 2 to 3 large scoops per serving to the blender.
steps.expect: the jar is mostly filled with ice cream, not liquid.

steps.action: **Add minimal milk.** Start with 30 ml to 60 ml milk per serving.
steps.expect: milk sits around the ice cream but does not cover it.

steps.action: **Add flavoring.** Add syrup, vanilla, fruit, cookies, or malt powder in small amounts.
steps.expect: flavoring is in the jar before blending starts.

steps.action: **Pulse instead of running.** Blend in short pulses, stopping to tamp or stir with the blender off if needed.
steps.expect: the mixture moves without turning thin.

steps.action: **Check thickness.** Stop as soon as no large ice cream chunks remain.
steps.expect: the shake mounds briefly on a spoon.

steps.action: **Fix texture.** [BRANCH: too thick | too thin] add a splash of milk for too thick, or add more ice cream for too thin.
steps.expect: the correction changes thickness without diluting flavor.

steps.action: **Blend once more briefly.** Pulse 1 to 3 times after any correction.
steps.expect: the shake is smooth but still cold and thick.

steps.action: **Serve cold.** Pour into the chilled glass immediately.
steps.expect: the shake slides slowly and frost forms on the glass.

steps.action: **Finish and clean.** Add whipped cream or toppings if using, then rinse the blender before residue dries.
steps.expect: the shake is ready and the jar rinses clean quickly.

recipes.verification: The milkshake is smooth, cold, and thick enough to coat a spoon before being served.

recipes.title: make a mug cake
recipes.name: make-a-mug-cake
recipes.goal: A single-serving cake mixed and cooked in a mug, tender rather than rubbery or overflowing.

steps.action: **Choose a large mug.** Use a straight-sided mug no more than half full after mixing.
steps.expect: plenty of headroom for the batter to rise.

steps.action: **Mix dry ingredients first.** In the mug, stir 4 tbsp flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp cocoa or 1/2 tsp vanilla later, 1/4 tsp baking powder, and a pinch of salt.
steps.expect: no pockets of white flour or cocoa remain.

steps.action: **Add wet ingredients.** Stir in 3 tbsp milk and 1 tbsp neutral oil or melted butter until just combined.
steps.expect: batter is glossy and spoonable, not dry paste.

steps.action: **Scrape the bottom corners.** Drag the spoon around the mug base where flour hides.
steps.expect: no dry streaks come up on the spoon.

steps.action: **Stop mixing early.** Do not beat once the batter is uniform.
steps.expect: batter still looks slightly loose and not elastic.

steps.action: **Microwave in short timing.** Cook on high 60 seconds in a standard microwave.
steps.expect: top rises and looks mostly set with a tiny damp spot in the center.

steps.action: **Rest and check.** Wait 1 minute; carryover heat finishes the center.
steps.expect: cake pulls slightly from the sides and the center is fudgy, not liquid.

steps.action: **Add 10-second bursts only if needed.** [BRANCH: wet center | set center] cook wet batter briefly, or stop if set. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overcooked mug cake turns rubbery and cannot be softened except with sauce.
steps.expect: spoon meets tender cake with a moist crumb.

recipes.verification: The mug cake is risen, set at the edges, slightly moist in the center, and can be spooned without raw batter pooling.

recipes.title: make a pan sauce
recipes.name: make-a-pan-sauce
recipes.goal: Build a glossy sauce in the searing pan with fond, aromatics, deglazing liquid, reduction, and cold butter.

steps.action: **Assess fond.** Remove the cooked item and pour off excess fat, leaving 1 to 2 teaspoons
steps.expect: brown fond remains without deep grease

steps.action: **Soften aromatics.** Add shallot, garlic, or herbs over medium-low heat
steps.expect: aromatics smell sweet, not scorched

steps.action: **Deglaze.** Add wine, stock, or water and scrape the pan
steps.expect: fond dissolves into the liquid

steps.action: **Reduce.** Simmer until slightly syrupy
steps.expect: spoon leaves a short trail

steps.action: **Add juices.** Pour in resting juices from the plate
steps.expect: sauce tastes more like the main food

steps.action: **Mount butter.** Turn heat low or off and whisk in cold butter. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* boiling after butter can break the sauce
steps.expect: sauce turns glossy

steps.action: **Season and serve.** Add salt or acid, then spoon over food
steps.expect: sauce coats rather than floods

recipes.verification: sauce is glossy and tastes like the seared food

recipes.title: make a party dip
recipes.name: make-a-party-dip
recipes.goal: Make a party dip that tastes balanced, holds its texture on the table, and works with sturdy dippers.

steps.action: **Pick the base.** [BRANCH: creamy base | bean base] use sour cream or softened cream cheese for cool dips, or mashed beans for a thicker savory dip.
steps.expect: the base is smooth enough to stir.

steps.action: **Loosen only if needed.** Add a spoonful of milk, lime juice, salsa, or olive oil if the base is too stiff.
steps.expect: a chip can scoop it without snapping.

steps.action: **Season in layers.** Stir in salt, acid, spice, and aromatics such as garlic powder, scallions, herbs, cumin, or hot sauce.
steps.expect: seasoning is evenly distributed with no dry pockets.

steps.action: **Add texture.** Fold in grated cheese, chopped vegetables, herbs, beans, or cooked bacon if using.
steps.expect: mix-ins are small enough to fit on a chip.

steps.action: **Taste and adjust.** Try the dip with the actual dipper, not a plain spoon.
steps.expect: it tastes slightly bold because cold dips dull flavor.

steps.action: **Control thickness.** Add more base if too salty or spicy, or add a small amount of liquid if too dense.
steps.expect: the dip mounds softly and does not run.

steps.action: **Chill to meld.** Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes when time allows.
steps.expect: flavors taste more blended and harsh raw notes soften.

steps.action: **Stir before serving.** Recheck thickness and taste after chilling.
steps.expect: any separated liquid is mixed back in.

steps.action: **Serve with sturdy dippers.** Choose thick chips, pita, crackers, celery, carrots, or toasted bread.
steps.expect: dippers can scoop without breaking.

steps.action: **Refresh safely.** Put out a small bowl and refill from the refrigerator rather than leaving the whole batch out.
steps.expect: the serving bowl stays neat and cool.

recipes.verification: The dip can be scooped with the chosen dipper, tastes balanced, and has chilled at least 30 minutes if served cold.

recipes.title: make a quesadilla
recipes.name: make-a-quesadilla
recipes.goal: Make a crisp tortilla filled with melted cheese and optional fillings that stays together when cut and eaten.

steps.action: **Choose the build style.** [BRANCH: folded tortilla | two-tortilla stack] Use folded for easier flipping and two-tortilla for a larger serving.
steps.expect: the tortilla size and portion match the skillet.

steps.action: **Warm the pan.** Heat a skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 min.
steps.expect: a drop of water sizzles and evaporates within a few seconds.

steps.action: **Choose dry pan or light oil.** Use a dry pan for a flexible tortilla, or wipe in a thin film of oil for a crisper surface.
steps.expect: pan surface is evenly hot and not puddled with oil.

steps.action: **Lay down cheese as glue.** Put cheese on the tortilla first, then add small amounts of fillings, then a little more cheese.
steps.expect: cheese touches both tortilla and filling so the layers can bind.

steps.action: **Cook the first side.** Place the quesadilla in the pan and press lightly with the spatula.
steps.expect: the bottom shows golden spots and the cheese at the edge starts to melt.

steps.action: **Flip confidently.** Slide the spatula under the center, support the top with fingertips or another spatula if needed, then turn it over in one motion.
steps.expect: filling stays inside and the browned side faces up.

steps.action: **Finish melting.** Cook the second side over medium or medium-low heat until the tortilla browns and the cheese fully melts.
steps.expect: edges look sealed and the center feels soft when pressed.

steps.action: **Rest before cutting.** Move to a board and wait 1 to 2 min before slicing.
steps.expect: cheese firms slightly so the filling does not slide out.

steps.action: **Cut and serve.** Slice with a knife or pizza wheel and serve with salsa, crema, or hot sauce.
steps.expect: wedges hold together when lifted.

recipes.verification: The tortilla is browned on both sides, the cheese is melted through the center, and a cut wedge can be lifted without the filling falling out.

recipes.title: make a quiche
recipes.name: make-a-quiche
recipes.goal: A quiche with a crisp crust and just-set custard is baked, cooled slightly, and sliced cleanly.

steps.action: **Chill the lined crust.** Fit dough into the pan, trim, dock lightly, and chill 20-30 minutes.
steps.expect: firm dough that does not slump when touched.

steps.action: **Blind-bake weighted.** Line with parchment, fill with weights, and bake at 190 °C for 15 minutes.
steps.expect: edges set and bottom no longer raw-looking.

steps.action: **Finish the empty crust.** Remove weights and bake 8-12 minutes more until pale golden.
steps.expect: dry, lightly colored bottom that resists sogginess.

steps.action: **Prepare fillings.** Cook watery vegetables, bacon, or mushrooms first and cool them.
steps.expect: fillings are flavorful and not leaking liquid.

steps.action: **Mix custard ratio.** Whisk 1 large egg per 120 ml dairy, using 3 eggs plus 360 ml cream or milk for a standard pie.
steps.expect: smooth custard with no streaks.

steps.action: **Fill the shell.** Scatter cheese and fillings in the crust, then pour custard to just below the rim.
steps.expect: solids are evenly distributed and not mounded above liquid.

steps.action: **Bake gently.** Bake at 175 °C for 30-40 minutes.
steps.expect: edges puff slightly while the center still has a small wobble.

steps.action: **Stop at just-set.** Remove when a knife 2 cm from the edge comes out mostly clean.
steps.expect: center jiggles like soft gelatin, not liquid.

steps.action: **Rest before slicing.** Cool 15-30 minutes on a rack.
steps.expect: custard firms enough for neat wedges.

recipes.verification: The cooled quiche slices cleanly, with a crisp bottom crust and custard set to the center without watery seepage.

recipes.title: make a quick tomato sauce
recipes.name: make-a-quick-tomato-sauce
recipes.goal: A bright weeknight tomato sauce is made in about 20 minutes from garlic, olive oil, canned tomatoes, salt, and basil.

steps.action: **Open and check the tomatoes.** Pour tomatoes into a bowl if you need to crush them by hand.
steps.expect: tomatoes smell sweet and acidic, not metallic or fermented.

steps.action: **Warm the oil.** Add 2 tablespoons olive oil to a saucepan over medium-low heat.
steps.expect: oil shimmers lightly but does not smoke.

steps.action: **Soften the garlic.** Add 2 thin-sliced or minced garlic cloves and cook 30 to 60 seconds.
steps.expect: garlic smells fragrant and stays pale gold.

steps.action: **Add tomatoes carefully.** Pour in the canned tomatoes and their juice, then crush large pieces with a spoon. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* garlic turns bitter once burned, so if it browns hard before the tomatoes go in, discard and restart the oil and garlic.
steps.expect: sauce bubbles gently after the first minute.

steps.action: **Season and simmer.** Add 1/2 teaspoon salt, lower heat, and simmer uncovered 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often.
steps.expect: sauce thickens enough to coat the spoon.

steps.action: **Finish with basil.** Tear in fresh basil at the end, or rub in a pinch of dried basil during the last 5 minutes.
steps.expect: sauce smells fresh and no longer tastes flat.

steps.action: **Adjust for pasta.** Taste, then add salt, olive oil, or a splash of pasta water if using with noodles.
steps.expect: sauce clings to pasta instead of pooling as watery tomato juice.

recipes.verification: The sauce tastes seasoned, coats a spoon, and has simmered long enough that garlic, tomato, oil, salt, and basil taste integrated.

recipes.title: make a roux
recipes.name: make-a-roux
recipes.goal: A smooth cooked mixture of fat and flour is prepared as a thickening base for sauce, gravy, soup, gumbo, or stew.

steps.action: **Measure the fat and flour.** Use a 1:1 weight ratio, or equal tablespoon volumes for a quick home sauce.
steps.expect: flour is measured before the pan gets hot.

steps.action: **Melt or warm the fat.** Heat butter until foaming subsides, or warm oil until it shimmers lightly.
steps.expect: fat coats the pan and is hot but not smoking.

steps.action: **Add flour all at once.** Sprinkle flour over the fat while whisking or stirring firmly.
steps.expect: the mixture becomes a thick paste with no dry flour islands.

steps.action: **Cook out raw-flour taste.** Stir constantly over medium-low heat for at least 2-3 minutes for a pale roux.
steps.expect: the paste smells nutty instead of dusty or cereal-like.

steps.action: **Choose the color stage.** [BRANCH: white roux for milk sauces | blond roux for gravy | brown roux for darker stews | dark roux for gumbo]
steps.expect: color matches the intended dish before liquid is added.

steps.action: **Control darker roux carefully.** For brown or dark roux, stir without stopping and lower heat as color deepens.
steps.expect: color changes evenly with no black flecks.

steps.action: **Prevent lumps before adding liquid.** Use hot roux with cool liquid, or cooled roux with hot liquid, and add the first liquid slowly.
steps.expect: the first splash forms a smooth paste instead of floating clumps.

steps.action: **Whisk in liquid gradually.** Add liquid in several pours, fully smoothing after each addition.
steps.expect: sauce loosens evenly and thickens as it simmers.

steps.action: **Simmer to finish thickening.** Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer for 1-3 minutes after all liquid is added.
steps.expect: spoon coating improves and no floury taste remains.

steps.action: **Adjust final texture.** Thin with more liquid or reduce gently if too loose.
steps.expect: sauce flows at the thickness needed for the dish.

recipes.verification: The roux or sauce is smooth, smells toasted rather than raw, has no black flecks, and thickens liquid without visible flour lumps.

recipes.title: make a salad
recipes.name: make-a-salad
recipes.goal: A salad that people actually want to eat: washed and dried greens, balanced components, and a dressing applied at the right moment so nothing arrives wilted or swimming.

steps.action: **Wash the greens properly.** Separate leaves, submerge in a bowl of cold water, agitate, lift the greens out (grit sinks; pouring the bowl back over them re-grits everything). Repeat for sandy greens like spinach.
steps.expect: no grit at the bowl's bottom on the final pass.

steps.action: **Dry the greens completely.** Spinner, or rolled loosely in a clean towel and patted. This is the least glamorous and most important step: dressing slides off wet leaves and pools at the bottom.
steps.expect: leaves dry to the touch.

steps.action: **Tear or cut into fork-sized pieces.** Bite-sized beats knife-and-fork wrestling at the table.
steps.expect: pieces that fit on a fork without folding engineering.

steps.action: **Build the body.** Crunch (cucumber, peppers, carrots, radish), something sweet or juicy (tomato, apple, orange segments), something rich (cheese, avocado, nuts, seeds), and the protein for meal salads (eggs, beans, chicken, tuna). Aim for three to five components beyond the greens; more becomes compost-drawer roulette.
steps.expect: a bowl with contrast in texture, color, and richness.

steps.action: **Make the dressing in the ratio 3:1 oil to acid.** Three spoons oil, one spoon vinegar or lemon, salt, pepper, and optionally a dab of mustard or honey to bind. Shake in a jar or whisk in the bowl's bottom before the greens go in.
steps.expect: a dressing that tastes slightly too sharp alone; it mellows across the leaves.

steps.action: **Dress at the last minute, less than you think, and toss thoroughly.** Half the dressing, toss with hands or two spoons from the bottom up, taste a leaf, add more only if needed. ⚠️ *Irreversible in effect:* overdressing cannot be undone; underdressing takes ten seconds to fix.
steps.expect: every leaf lightly coated, nothing pooling below.

steps.action: **Finish and serve immediately.** Delicate toppings (croutons, seeds, cheese shavings) go on after the toss so they stay crisp and visible.
steps.expect: salad on the table within minutes of dressing.

recipes.verification: Leaves are dry-crisp with no grit, the components cover crunch, sweetness, and richness, every leaf carries a light coat with no pool at the bottom, and delicate toppings arrived crisp on top at serving time.

recipes.title: make a sandwich
recipes.name: make-a-sandwich
recipes.goal: A structurally sound, tasty sandwich — fillings stay in, bread isn't soggy, and it's cut and ready to eat or pack.

steps.action: **Lay out both bread slices and audit the fillings.** Everything sliced/ready before assembly. Wet things (tomato, pickles) get patted dry with a paper towel.
steps.expect: all components staged; wet items visibly drier.

steps.action: **Apply the moisture barrier.** Spread butter/mayo edge-to-edge on *both* inner faces — the fat layer is what keeps juicy fillings from soaking the bread.
steps.expect: full coverage to the crusts, thin and even.

steps.action: **Build in stability order.** Cheese or large leaf flat on the base → protein → wet/slippery items (tomato, cucumber) in the *middle* of the stack → lettuce/greens on top. Keep the footprint inside the bread's edges.
steps.expect: a level stack, nothing overhanging, wet items sandwiched between dry layers.

steps.action: **Season the inside.** Salt/pepper directly on the tomato layer; condiment accents (mustard, hot sauce) go on now, not pooled on the bread.
steps.expect: seasoning where the flavor lives, bread still dry.

steps.action: **Cap, and compress gently with a flat palm.**
steps.expect: layers seat together; nothing squirts out the sides.

steps.action: **Cut with a sharp knife, decisively.** Diagonal or half; a serrated blade *saws* soft bread rather than pressing (pressing ejects fillings). Claw grip on the holding hand.
steps.expect: clean cut faces, stack intact in both halves.

steps.action: **Serve or wrap.** Eating later: wrap snugly in paper/wrap and refrigerate if it contains meat, egg, or dairy (`daily/food/store-leftovers` windows apply).
steps.expect: sandwich plated, or wrapped tight enough to hold its build.

recipes.verification: The sandwich holds together through a bite test at the cut face, the bread is dry to the touch outside, fillings are inside the footprint, and the board and knife are cleaned.

recipes.title: make a simple gravy
recipes.name: make-a-simple-gravy
recipes.goal: A smooth pan gravy thickened with a fat-flour roux and seasoned from drippings or stock.

steps.action: **Separate usable fat.** Spoon 2 tbsp fat from drippings, or use butter if there is not enough.
steps.expect: fat is measured apart from watery juices.

steps.action: **Keep the flavorful liquid.** Deglaze browned bits with stock or pour pan juices into a cup.
steps.expect: you have about 2 cups liquid total.

steps.action: **Cook the roux.** Heat 2 tbsp fat, whisk in 2 tbsp flour, and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
steps.expect: paste smells nutty and no longer raw-floury.

steps.action: **Whisk in liquid gradually.** Add warm stock a splash at a time at first, whisking smooth before adding more.
steps.expect: paste loosens without lumps.

steps.action: **Simmer to thicken.** Bring to a gentle simmer for 3 to 5 minutes.
steps.expect: gravy coats a spoon and bubbles lazily.

steps.action: **Season after thickening.** Taste, then add salt, pepper, and any reserved pan juices.
steps.expect: savory flavor is clear without harsh salt.

steps.action: **Fix texture before serving.** [BRANCH: too thick | too thin] whisk in stock to loosen, or simmer longer to reduce.
steps.expect: gravy pours in a ribbon.

steps.action: **Strain if needed.** Pour through a fine strainer for a smoother finish. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* heavy salt cannot be removed except by dilution, so season in small pinches.
steps.expect: hot gravy ready in a warm boat or saucepan.

recipes.verification: The gravy is smooth, hot, savory, and thick enough to coat a spoon while still pouring easily.

recipes.title: make a simple white sauce
recipes.name: make-a-simple-white-sauce
recipes.goal: A smooth bechamel-style white sauce is made from butter, flour, and milk, ready for pasta, vegetables, casseroles, or cheese sauce.

steps.action: **Measure the base ratio.** Use 2 tablespoons butter, 2 tablespoons flour, and 1 cup milk for medium sauce.
steps.expect: ingredients are measured before heat is on.

steps.action: **Melt the butter.** Heat butter in a saucepan over medium-low until foamy, not browned.
steps.expect: butter is liquid with small bubbles.

steps.action: **Cook the roux.** Whisk in flour and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
steps.expect: paste smells lightly nutty and no raw flour dust remains.

steps.action: **Add milk gradually.** Pour in a small splash of warm milk while whisking hard, then add the rest in several additions.
steps.expect: each addition smooths out before the next one goes in.

steps.action: **Simmer to thicken.** Keep whisking over medium heat until bubbles break slowly at the surface.
steps.expect: sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.action: **Choose thickness.** [BRANCH: thin sauce, add 2 to 4 tablespoons milk | thick sauce, simmer 1 to 3 minutes longer]
steps.expect: sauce runs, ribbons, or mounds according to the target use.

steps.action: **Season.** Add salt, pepper, and a small pinch of nutmeg if wanted.
steps.expect: sauce tastes savory rather than flat.

steps.action: **Add cheese off heat.** Remove from heat and stir in grated cheese a handful at a time.
steps.expect: cheese melts smoothly without oily separation.

recipes.verification: The sauce is smooth, hot, and thick enough to coat a spoon while leaving no floury taste.

recipes.title: make a smoothie
recipes.name: make-a-smoothie
recipes.goal: A drinkable, balanced smoothie from whatever fruit is on hand, blended in the right order, with the blender cleaned in the thirty seconds when cleaning is still easy.

steps.action: **Load in the blending order: liquid first, then soft, then frozen on top.** A cup or so of liquid (milk, plant milk, juice, water) at the blades, then yogurt or banana, then greens, then frozen fruit and ice last. Liquid-first is what lets the vortex form instead of the blades spinning in a jam.
steps.expect: jar loaded bottom-light to top-heavy, filled no more than two-thirds.

steps.action: **Lid on, hand on the lid, start low.** Low speed until a vortex forms and pulls the top layers down, then ramp to high.
steps.expect: a visible vortex; contents circulating rather than a frozen island spinning above the blades.

steps.action: **Blend on high for 30 to 60 seconds until visually smooth.** Green flecks disappearing is the sign the greens are actually blended rather than confetti.
steps.expect: uniform color and texture, no chunks knocking.

steps.action: **Check the consistency and adjust once.** Too thick: splash more liquid, pulse. Too thin: a handful more frozen fruit or ice, pulse.
steps.expect: pourable but spoon-coating, or whatever your target is, reached in one adjustment.

steps.action: **Taste and balance.** Too tart: half a banana, a date, or a small drizzle of honey. Too sweet or flat: a squeeze of citrus.
steps.expect: balanced flavor before it leaves the jar.

steps.action: **Pour and rinse-blend immediately.** Serve, then put warm water and a drop of dish soap in the jar, run it 20 seconds, rinse. ⚠️ Blade jars are the cut-risk moment of the kitchen sink; the self-clean cycle exists so hands never chase residue around the blade.
steps.expect: clean jar drying, hands never inside with the blade.

recipes.verification: The vortex formed, the result is smooth with no flecks or chunks, consistency and taste were adjusted once each, and the jar was self-cleaned before the smoothie was finished.

recipes.title: make a stir fry sauce
recipes.name: make-a-stir-fry-sauce
recipes.goal: A balanced stir-fry sauce is mixed with salt, sweetness, acidity, aromatics, and starch so it coats food without becoming watery.

steps.action: **Choose a salty base.** Add 3 tbsp soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, or tamari to a bowl.
steps.expect: sauce base tastes clearly salty.

steps.action: **Add liquid.** Stir in 3 tbsp water or stock.
steps.expect: saltiness is diluted enough to coat a full pan of food.

steps.action: **Balance with sugar and acid.** Add 1-2 tsp sugar and 1 tbsp rice vinegar, Shaoxing wine, or citrus juice.
steps.expect: sauce tastes salty first, then slightly sweet and bright.

steps.action: **Add aromatics.** Stir in minced garlic, ginger, chile, sesame oil, or white pepper as desired.
steps.expect: aroma is vivid but not muddy.

steps.action: **Make a slurry.** Mix 1-2 tsp cornstarch into the cold sauce until smooth.
steps.expect: no dry starch lumps remain.

steps.action: **Use at the end.** Stir-fry ingredients first, then pour sauce around the hot pan edge and toss.
steps.expect: sauce bubbles immediately and coats food.

steps.action: **Adjust final texture.** [BRANCH: too thick: splash water | too thin: simmer 30-60 seconds]
steps.expect: sauce lightly glazes the food with little pooling.

recipes.verification: Finished stir-fry has a glossy coating, balanced salty-sweet-acid flavor, no starch lumps, and little loose liquid in the pan.

recipes.title: make a stir fry
recipes.name: make-a-stir-fry
recipes.goal: A stir-fry with seared (not steamed) protein and crisp-tender vegetables, glazed in sauce, served over rice or noodles within minutes of finishing.

steps.action: **Prep every single ingredient before the burner goes on.** Slice protein thin against the grain; cut vegetables bite-size, grouped hard vs. soft; mince aromatics; stir the sauce together in a bowl; mix the slurry. Once the pan is hot there is zero time to chop.
steps.expect: all ingredients in separate bowls arranged in cooking order beside the stove, sauce mixed, empty plate staged for the protein.

steps.action: **Heat the dry pan until it is screaming hot.** High heat, 1-2 minutes empty, then add oil and swirl. Water flicked on the surface should bead and skitter, not sit and sizzle.
steps.expect: oil shimmers and runs thin immediately; the first wisp of smoke is the go signal.

steps.action: **Sear the protein in a single layer and leave it alone for 30-60 seconds.** Then toss until just cooked. Crowding drops the pan temperature and boils the meat in its own juices; cook in two batches if needed.
steps.expect: browned edges and a sear crust; protein removed to the staged plate at barely-done.

steps.action: **Re-heat the pan, add oil, then the hard vegetables.** Carrots, broccoli, peppers first; toss every 15-20 seconds, letting them sit briefly between tosses to char. A tablespoon of water with a quick lid, 30 seconds, steams dense broccoli through.
steps.expect: blistered spots on the vegetables, colors brightened, still snappy.

steps.action: **Add soft vegetables and aromatics late.** Snow peas, leafy greens, then garlic and ginger for the final 30-60 seconds only; burnt garlic is bitter and unfixable.
steps.expect: greens just wilted, aromatics fragrant and golden, not brown.

steps.action: **Return the protein, pour the sauce around the pan's edge, and toss.** Pouring down the hot pan wall sizzles off raw sauce taste.
steps.expect: everything reunited, sauce bubbling hard within seconds.

steps.action: **Thicken with the slurry and kill the heat.** Re-stir the slurry (cornstarch settles), add half, toss 15 seconds; add the rest only if the glaze is still thin. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* over-thickening turns the sauce to gravy-glue; you can always add more slurry but never remove it.
steps.expect: sauce clings to each piece with a glossy coat; no pool of liquid in the pan bottom.

steps.action: **Serve immediately over the rice or noodles.** A stir-fry degrades by the minute; steam softens the sear.
steps.expect: plated and eaten hot, wok soaking in the sink.

recipes.verification: Protein shows sear color and is cooked through, vegetables retain a slight snap and bright color, the sauce coats as a glossy glaze with no watery pool, and the dish hit the table within ~2 minutes of the heat going off.

recipes.title: make a wrap
recipes.name: make-a-wrap
recipes.goal: Make a tidy wrap that rolls tightly, holds its filling, and stays firm enough to eat by hand.

steps.action: **Warm the tortilla.** Heat it in a dry pan for 10 to 20 seconds per side or microwave it under a damp towel for 10 seconds.
steps.expect: the tortilla bends without cracking.

steps.action: **Place it on a dry board.** Set the warm tortilla flat with the best-looking side facing down.
steps.expect: the side that will show outside is clean and unbroken.

steps.action: **Make a sauce barrier.** Spread sauce in a thin stripe through the center, leaving 5 cm bare at the edges and avoiding watery puddles.
steps.expect: the sauce is controlled and not soaking the tortilla.

steps.action: **Layer dry ingredients first.** Put lettuce, rice, cheese, or other dry pieces over the sauce before wet fillings.
steps.expect: wet ingredients are buffered from the tortilla.

steps.action: **Add the main filling.** Keep the mound in a narrow horizontal band below center and use less than you think.
steps.expect: the tortilla still has clear side flaps and a top flap.

steps.action: **Choose the fold.** [BRANCH: closed-end wrap | open-end wrap] fold both sides in for a sealed wrap, or fold only one side for a deli-style open top.
steps.expect: the filling is contained before rolling.

steps.action: **Fold and tuck.** Pull the bottom edge up over the filling, tuck it back under the mound with your fingertips, and keep tension as you roll.
steps.expect: the first turn is snug and the filling is compressed, not squeezed out.

steps.action: **Finish the roll.** Continue rolling away from you until the bare top edge seals against the outside.
steps.expect: the wrap forms a firm cylinder.

steps.action: **Set seam side down.** Rest the wrap on its seam for 1 minute, or toast that side briefly in a dry pan.
steps.expect: the seam stays closed when released.

steps.action: **Cut cleanly if needed.** Use a sharp knife and gentle sawing motion through the middle.
steps.expect: the halves show compact layers without filling falling out.

recipes.verification: The wrap rests seam side down and can be lifted with one hand without unrolling or dripping.

recipes.title: make an old fashioned
recipes.name: make-an-old-fashioned
recipes.goal: A balanced Old Fashioned with whiskey, sugar, bitters, cold dilution, and citrus oil.

steps.action: **Chill the serving glass.** Put the rocks glass in the freezer or fill it with ice while you build the drink.
steps.expect: the glass feels cold before the cocktail goes in.

steps.action: **Dissolve the sweetener.** Add 1 tsp simple syrup, or 1 sugar cube with a few drops of water, to the mixing glass.
steps.expect: syrup is fluid, or the cube is crushed into a wet paste.

steps.action: **Add bitters.** Dash in 2 to 3 dashes aromatic bitters and stir into the sugar.
steps.expect: the sugar smells spiced and no dry sugar sits in the glass.

steps.action: **Measure whiskey.** Add 2 oz bourbon or rye.
steps.expect: the drink base is strong and slightly sweet before dilution.

steps.action: **Add ice and stir.** Fill the mixing glass with solid ice and stir 20 to 30 seconds; do not shake.
steps.expect: the outside chills and the drink loosens without becoming cloudy or foamy.

steps.action: **Serve over one large cube.** Empty any chilling ice from the rocks glass, add a large cube, and strain or pour the cocktail over it.
steps.expect: clear amber drink around cold fresh ice.

steps.action: **Express the peel.** Hold orange peel skin-side down over the glass, squeeze to spray oils, rub the rim, then drop it in or discard.
steps.expect: orange aroma rises before the first sip.

steps.action: **Taste once.** If too hot, stir 5 more seconds with ice; if too sweet, add 1 more dash bitters. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once extra sugar or bitters are added, balance can only be diluted, not removed.
steps.expect: whiskey leads, with sugar and bitters supporting it.

recipes.verification: The drink is cold, clear, lightly sweetened, aromatic from orange oil, and not foamy or watered down.

recipes.title: make an omelette
recipes.name: make-an-omelette
recipes.goal: An omelette is softly set, folded cleanly, and filled without raw egg or cold filling pockets.

steps.action: **Warm the fillings first.** Heat mushrooms, onions, meat, or greens separately and keep cheese ready.
steps.expect: fillings are warm and not watery.

steps.action: **Beat the eggs.** Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt until yolks and whites are fully combined.
steps.expect: the mixture pours as one yellow liquid with no clear streaks.

steps.action: **Heat the pan gently.** Put the pan over medium heat, add butter, then drop to low once the butter foams.
steps.expect: butter is melted and quiet, not brown or smoking.

steps.action: **Add eggs and pause.** Pour eggs into the pan and wait 10 seconds for the bottom to start setting.
steps.expect: a pale rim appears around the edge.

steps.action: **Push and tilt.** Push set egg from the edge toward the center while tilting raw egg into the empty space.
steps.expect: curds form while loose egg keeps flowing to the pan surface.

steps.action: **Stop while glossy.** Spread the top gently and stop stirring before it looks dry.
steps.expect: the omelette is mostly set with a slightly shiny top.

steps.action: **Add filling to one side.** Place warm fillings and cheese on the half farthest from the handle.
steps.expect: filling sits in a low mound and the empty half can fold over it.

steps.action: **Fold and slide.** Loosen the edge, fold the empty half over the filling, and slide onto a plate seam-side down.
steps.expect: the omelette lands in one folded piece.

recipes.verification: The omelette is folded, holds together on the plate, and shows no clear raw egg when the thickest part is cut.

recipes.title: make buttercream frosting
recipes.name: make-buttercream-frosting
recipes.goal: Butter and sugar are beaten into a smooth frosting that spreads, pipes, and holds shape.

steps.action: **Soften butter.** Let 225 g butter sit until it dents with gentle pressure.
steps.expect: butter bends but does not look shiny or oily.

steps.action: **Beat butter.** Mix 2-3 minutes until lighter and smooth.
steps.expect: butter looks pale and creamy.

steps.action: **Add sugar gradually.** Beat in 450 g powdered sugar in batches.
steps.expect: frosting thickens without a sugar cloud after each addition.

steps.action: **Add flavor and salt.** Mix in vanilla and a pinch of salt.
steps.expect: sweetness tastes rounded rather than flat.

steps.action: **Adjust consistency.** Add milk or cream 1 tsp at a time. [BRANCH: spreading | piping]
steps.expect: frosting is soft for spreading or firmer with clear ridges for piping.

steps.action: **Beat smooth.** Mix 1-2 minutes, then stir by hand to knock out large air pockets.
steps.expect: frosting is fluffy but not full of large holes.

steps.action: **Use or store.** Use immediately, or cover and refrigerate up to several days.
steps.expect: surface is protected from drying and odors.

recipes.verification: Buttercream is smooth, spreadable or pipeable for its purpose, holds ridges for several minutes, and tastes balanced with no greasy separation.

recipes.title: make caramel sauce
recipes.name: make-caramel-sauce
recipes.goal: Sugar is cooked to amber caramel, loosened with warm cream, finished with butter and salt, and cooled into a pourable sauce.

steps.action: **Warm the cream.** Heat 240 ml cream until steaming, then keep nearby off the burner.
steps.expect: cream is warm enough to reduce seizing.

steps.action: **Start the sugar.** [BRANCH: wet: combine 200 g sugar with 60 ml water | dry: sprinkle 200 g sugar evenly in the pan]
steps.expect: sugar begins melting evenly over medium heat.

steps.action: **Dissolve without crystals.** For wet caramel, swirl rather than stir once boiling; brush pan sides with water if crystals appear.
steps.expect: syrup turns clear before coloring.

steps.action: **Cook to amber.** Watch closely as color shifts from pale gold to honey to amber.
steps.expect: caramel smells nutty, not burnt, and is deep amber.

steps.action: **Stop the heat.** Remove pan from heat before adding dairy. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* caramel above 160 °C causes severe burns and cannot be wiped off safely while hot.
steps.expect: pan is off the burner and tilted away from you.

steps.action: **Add warm cream slowly.** Pour in a small stream while whisking; it will bubble violently and steam.
steps.expect: bubbling rises then settles without overflowing.

steps.action: **Finish with butter and salt.** Whisk in 30-45 g butter and 1/2 tsp salt until glossy.
steps.expect: sauce is smooth and slightly thinner than final texture.

steps.action: **Cool safely.** Pour into a heatproof jar and let cool uncovered until warm, then lid and refrigerate.
steps.expect: sauce thickens as it cools.

steps.action: **Rewarm to serve.** Warm gently in short bursts or a water bath if too thick.
steps.expect: sauce pours from a spoon in a ribbon.

recipes.verification: The cooled sauce is glossy, smooth, amber, lightly salted, and pours from a spoon without grainy crystals.

recipes.title: make carbonara
recipes.name: make-carbonara
recipes.goal: Pasta is coated in a glossy sauce made from eggs, hard cheese, pork fat, and pasta water without scrambling.

steps.action: **Prepare the sauce base.** Whisk 2 whole eggs plus 2 yolks with 80 g finely grated cheese and black pepper.
steps.expect: thick yellow paste with no dry cheese pockets.

steps.action: **Render pork.** Cook diced guanciale or pancetta slowly in a skillet until crisp and fat renders.
steps.expect: golden pieces and clear fat in the pan.

steps.action: **Boil pasta.** Cook pasta in salted water until just shy of al dente.
steps.expect: pasta bends but has a firm center.

steps.action: **Reserve pasta water.** Scoop at least 1 cup starchy water before draining.
steps.expect: cloudy hot water is ready beside the skillet.

steps.action: **Combine off heat.** Add hot pasta to the pork pan, turn off heat, and toss 30 seconds.
steps.expect: pasta is glossy with rendered fat and pan is no longer sizzling hard.

steps.action: **Emulsify egg sauce.** Add egg-cheese paste and splash in pasta water while tossing constantly. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* high heat scrambles eggs; keep the pan off direct heat while adding eggs.
steps.expect: sauce turns creamy and coats strands without curds.

steps.action: **Adjust thickness.** [BRANCH: too thick: add pasta water | too loose: toss over very low residual heat]
steps.expect: sauce clings in a shiny layer.

steps.action: **Serve immediately.** Plate with extra cheese and pepper.
steps.expect: pasta is hot, glossy, and not oily or grainy.

recipes.verification: Pasta is al dente, sauce is glossy and creamy with no scrambled curds, pork is crisp, and the dish is served hot immediately.

recipes.title: make clarified butter
recipes.name: make-clarified-butter
recipes.goal: Butter separated into clear golden butterfat with water cooked off and milk solids left behind.

steps.action: **Cut the butter.** Cube butter so it melts evenly in the pan.
steps.expect: pieces are similar size.

steps.action: **Melt slowly.** Set over low heat and let butter melt without stirring hard.
steps.expect: foam rises and yellow fat separates.

steps.action: **Hold a gentle heat.** Keep heat low enough that bubbling is quiet, not frying.
steps.expect: moisture bubbles off steadily.

steps.action: **Skim the foam.** Spoon white foam from the surface into a discard bowl.
steps.expect: the top looks clearer and more golden.

steps.action: **Watch the layers.** Let milk solids settle to the bottom while the middle layer turns transparent gold.
steps.expect: pale solids sit below clear butterfat.

steps.action: **Pour carefully.** [BRANCH: ladle | pour] Ladle or pour the golden layer through a strainer into the jar, stopping before solids leave the pan.
steps.expect: jar fills with clear butterfat.

steps.action: **Leave the solids.** Keep the last cloudy spoonfuls and browned bits out of the jar.
steps.expect: pan holds milk solids and the jar stays clear.

steps.action: **Cool and store.** Cool uncovered briefly, then cover and refrigerate for longer storage.
steps.expect: clarified butter firms into a clean yellow fat. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* browned solids make ghee-like flavor; stop early for neutral clarified butter.

recipes.verification: The jar contains clear golden butterfat with no visible white foam or milk solids.

recipes.title: make cold brew coffee
recipes.name: make-cold-brew-coffee
recipes.goal: A clean, low-bitterness cold brew concentrate that can be diluted over ice or with milk.

steps.action: **Grind coarse.** Use coffee about as coarse as raw sugar, not espresso or drip-fine.
steps.expect: distinct gritty particles; very little powder at the bottom.

steps.action: **Measure a concentrate ratio.** Combine 1 part coffee by weight with 5 parts cold water, such as 100 g coffee and 500 g water.
steps.expect: all grounds are wet but the mixture is still thick.

steps.action: **Stir until fully saturated.** Scrape the dry clumps from the sides and bottom.
steps.expect: no pale floating islands of dry coffee remain.

steps.action: **Cover and refrigerate.** Steep 12 to 18 hours in the fridge.
steps.expect: the liquid darkens slowly and smells sweet rather than sharp.

steps.action: **Strain the grounds.** Pour through a fine strainer without pressing hard on the bed.
steps.expect: most grounds stay behind and the coffee flows steadily.

steps.action: **Filter for clarity.** Run the strained brew through paper, cloth, or a nut milk bag.
steps.expect: fewer silty particles and a smoother mouthfeel.

steps.action: **Dilute to drink.** Start with 1 part concentrate to 1 part water, milk, or ice, then adjust.
steps.expect: coffee tastes strong but not muddy or harsh.

steps.action: **Store cold.** Transfer concentrate to a clean bottle and refrigerate up to 5 days. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* discard brew left warm for hours or smelling fermented; do not try to rescue it.
steps.expect: sealed cold brew labeled or easy to identify.

recipes.verification: The finished concentrate pours clear enough to leave little grit in the glass, tastes rounded after dilution, and is stored covered in the fridge.

recipes.title: make congee
recipes.name: make-congee
recipes.goal: Rice is simmered with plenty of liquid until it breaks down into a soft, spoonable porridge.

steps.action: **Rinse rice.** Rinse 1 cup rice until water is less cloudy.
steps.expect: loose surface starch is washed off but grains remain intact.

steps.action: **Add liquid.** Combine rice with 8-10 cups water or stock in a heavy pot.
steps.expect: rice is submerged under a large volume of liquid.

steps.action: **Bring to a boil.** Heat uncovered, stirring so grains do not stick.
steps.expect: steady bubbles rise and foam may collect on top.

steps.action: **Lower to a simmer.** Reduce heat and partially cover the pot.
steps.expect: gentle bubbling without boilover.

steps.action: **Stir occasionally.** Cook 60-90 minutes, scraping the bottom every 10-15 minutes.
steps.expect: grains split and porridge thickens from watery to creamy.

steps.action: **Adjust texture.** [BRANCH: too thick: add hot water | too thin: simmer uncovered]
steps.expect: congee flows slowly from a spoon.

steps.action: **Cook additions safely.** Add cooked toppings at the end, or simmer raw chicken pieces to 74 °C and shrimp until opaque.
steps.expect: proteins are fully cooked with no translucent raw centers.

steps.action: **Season and serve.** Add salt, soy sauce, ginger, scallion, or sesame oil to taste.
steps.expect: porridge tastes savory and smooth, with toppings hot.

recipes.verification: Congee is creamy, rice grains are mostly broken, no burnt flavor is present, and any meat or seafood is fully cooked.

recipes.title: make croutons
recipes.name: make-croutons
recipes.goal: Crisp, evenly seasoned croutons from stale bread, suitable for salads, soups, or snacking.

steps.action: **Cut even cubes.** Slice bread into 1/2 to 3/4 inch cubes.
steps.expect: pieces are similar size so they crisp together.

steps.action: **Dry fresh bread if needed.** If bread is soft, leave cubes out 20 minutes or toast briefly at low heat.
steps.expect: surfaces feel dry, not squishy.

steps.action: **Season with fat.** Toss 4 cups bread with 3 tbsp oil or butter, 1/2 tsp salt, pepper, and seasonings.
steps.expect: bread is lightly coated, not soaked.

steps.action: **Choose cooking method.** [BRANCH: oven | pan] use a 375 °F oven for batches, or a skillet over medium heat for small amounts.
steps.expect: one cooking path is set before browning starts.

steps.action: **Cook in one layer.** Spread on a baking sheet or keep cubes moving in the pan.
steps.expect: cubes touch heat directly instead of steaming in a pile.

steps.action: **Turn for even color.** Bake 10 to 15 minutes, stirring once, or pan-toast 6 to 10 minutes.
steps.expect: multiple sides become golden.

steps.action: **Cool completely.** Move croutons to a plate or leave on the sheet off heat.
steps.expect: centers finish drying and the texture crisps as they cool.

steps.action: **Store dry.** Transfer to an airtight container only when fully cool. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* burned garlic powder or blackened bread tastes bitter and cannot be fixed.
