steps.expect: crisp croutons that rattle in the container.

recipes.verification: Croutons are golden on several sides, crisp after cooling, and seasoned enough to taste good alone.

recipes.title: make french toast
recipes.name: make-french-toast
recipes.goal: Slices of bread soaked through with custard and cooked to a golden-brown surface with a soft, set (not wet) center, served hot.

steps.action: **Mix the custard until fully blended.** Per 4 thick slices: 3 eggs, 180 ml milk, 1 tbsp sugar, pinch of salt, splash of vanilla, dusting of cinnamon. Whisk hard until no streaks of white remain; unblended white cooks into rubbery patches on the surface.
steps.expect: a uniform pale custard with cinnamon suspended, not floating in rafts.

steps.action: **Pour the custard into the shallow dish.** It should sit about 1 cm deep so slices can lie flat.
steps.expect: dish wide enough for one or two slices lying fully flat.

steps.action: **Soak each slice on both sides.** Lay a slice in, count to 15-20 per side for properly stale bread (shorter for fresher, up to 40 for very dry). The goal is custard to the center, not a saturated sponge.
steps.expect: slice feels heavy and looks wet through, but still holds its shape when lifted with support under it.

steps.action: **Heat the pan to medium, then medium-low, with butter.** Melt a knob of butter over medium heat until foaming, then back off to medium-low. Medium is the whole game: too hot browns the outside while the center stays raw custard; too cool dries the slice out before it colors.
steps.expect: butter foaming and just fragrant, not browning.

steps.action: **Cook 2-4 minutes per side, flipping once.** Lay slices in without crowding. Lift a corner to check color before flipping.
steps.expect: an even deep golden-brown on the first side; a gentle sizzle throughout, never a hard sear sound.

steps.action: **Press-test the center before plating.** Press the middle lightly with the spatula: it should spring back, not squelch. If it squelches, give each side another minute on lower heat.
steps.expect: springy center, both faces golden, edges set.

steps.action: **Serve immediately, or hold in a low oven.** Straight to plates with butter, syrup, or fruit; for a batch, hold finished slices on a rack in a 100 °C oven, never stacked (stacking steams them limp).
steps.expect: surfaces still slightly crisp at serving; center soft and custardy but fully set.

recipes.verification: Every slice is golden-brown on both faces, the center springs back under a light press with no wet squelch, no slice is burnt or pale, and slices held for serving are still unstacked and slightly crisp.

recipes.title: make fresh breadcrumbs
recipes.name: make-fresh-breadcrumbs
recipes.goal: Turn stale bread into fresh, dried, or toasted crumbs with the right texture for binding or coating.

steps.action: **Inspect bread.** Reject moldy or musty bread
steps.expect: bread smells clean

steps.action: **Choose style.** [BRANCH: fresh crumbs | dried crumbs] match moisture to use
steps.expect: style is chosen

steps.action: **Tear pieces.** Remove tough crusts if fine crumbs are needed
steps.expect: pieces fit the tool

steps.action: **Blitz or grate.** Pulse or grate in short bursts
steps.expect: crumbs form without paste

steps.action: **Dry if needed.** Spread in a skillet or low oven
steps.expect: crumbs feel lighter

steps.action: **Toast if wanted.** Stir until golden. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* burned crumbs taste bitter
steps.expect: crumbs smell toasted

steps.action: **Cool and store.** Cool before sealing
steps.expect: no steam collects in container

recipes.verification: crumbs are even, clean-tasting, and cooled before storage

recipes.title: make fried rice
recipes.name: make-fried-rice
recipes.goal: A plate of fried rice with separate, lightly chewy grains, distinct egg pieces, and a savory toasted-soy edge, made in one pan in under ten minutes of actual cooking.

steps.action: **Break up the cold rice.** Wet your hands and crumble the clumps into loose grains in a bowl. Clumps that go in whole come out as clumps.
steps.expect: mostly individual grains, no fist-sized lumps.

steps.action: **Heat the empty wok until it just smokes, then add oil.** High heat throughout; a timid burner is why home fried rice tastes steamed. Swirl in 1-2 tablespoons of oil.
steps.expect: a wisp of smoke off the bare metal, then oil that shimmers and flows fast.

steps.action: **Cook the egg first and remove it.** [BRANCH: egg-first (default): pour in the beaten egg, scramble 20-30 seconds to barely set, take it out to a bowl | egg-last coating: skip here, see step 6] Egg-first gives distinct golden pieces; leaving egg in for the whole stir-fry overcooks it to rubber.
steps.expect: soft just-set curds out of the pan, still glossy.

steps.action: **Flash the aromatics, then the add-ins.** More oil if the pan is dry; garlic and scallion whites for 10-15 seconds only, then cooked add-ins for ~1 minute.
steps.expect: loud sizzle, fragrant garlic that is not browning past golden.

steps.action: **Add the rice and toss until every grain is hot.** Spread it, let it sit 20-30 seconds to toast, then toss; repeat. Press clumps flat with the spatula back. 2-3 minutes total.
steps.expect: grains hopping loose in the toss, faint toasty smell, no steam-wet sheen.

steps.action: **[BRANCH: egg-last chosen]** Push rice aside, pour beaten egg into the gap, half-set it, then toss so egg coats the grains golden.
steps.expect: rice coated pale gold rather than carrying distinct egg pieces.

steps.action: **Soy sauce at the edge of the wok, not on the rice.** Drizzle 1-2 tablespoons down the hot side wall so it sears and caramelizes on the metal before being tossed through. Poured directly on the pile, it soaks in and makes wet, patchy rice.
steps.expect: an instant sharp sizzle and a toasted-soy smell, then even pale-brown color after tossing.

steps.action: **Return the egg, season, finish.** Egg pieces back in, salt to taste, scallion greens, optional sesame oil off the heat. Toss twice and plate immediately.
steps.expect: separate grains on the plate, egg in visible pieces, nothing pooling.

recipes.verification: Grains fall separately off the spatula, egg appears as distinct pieces (or an even golden coat, if egg-last), color is uniform pale brown with no white wet patches, and the plate shows no liquid after a minute.

recipes.title: make garlic bread
recipes.name: make-garlic-bread
recipes.goal: Bread is toasted with a garlic-butter spread so it comes out either crisp-edged or soft and pull-apart, by deliberate choice.

steps.action: **Choose crisp or soft.** [BRANCH: crisp open-face | soft wrapped loaf] use split bread for crisp edges, or a scored loaf wrapped in foil for soft centers.
steps.expect: bread is cut to match the texture you want.

steps.action: **Make garlic butter.** Mash 4 tablespoons soft butter with 1 minced garlic clove, a pinch of salt, and parsley if using.
steps.expect: garlic is evenly spread through the butter.

steps.action: **Spread to the edges.** Coat the cut sides thinly and evenly, reaching the corners.
steps.expect: no dry patches remain on the eating surface.

steps.action: **Bake for control.** Heat oven or toaster oven to 375 F and bake 8 to 10 minutes for crisp bread or 10 to 12 minutes wrapped for soft bread.
steps.expect: butter melts in and the bread smells toasted.

steps.action: **Broil only to finish.** If you want more browning, broil 30 to 90 seconds while watching constantly. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* garlic bread can go from golden to burnt in seconds under a broiler, so do not walk away.
steps.expect: edges are golden, not black.

steps.action: **Rest briefly.** Move bread to a board and wait 1 minute before slicing.
steps.expect: butter stops bubbling and slices hold together.

steps.action: **Serve hot.** Cut into portions and serve with sauce, soup, or salad.
steps.expect: bread is warm, garlicky, and not greasy on the bottom.

recipes.verification: The bread is hot and evenly seasoned, with the chosen texture: crisp browned edges for open-face bread or soft buttery centers for wrapped bread.

recipes.title: make guacamole
recipes.name: make-guacamole
recipes.goal: A bowl of chunky, well-seasoned guacamole made from properly ripe avocados, bright with lime and salt, protected from browning until served.

steps.action: **Test ripeness before cutting anything.** Cradle the avocado in your palm and press gently with the whole hand, not a thumbtip (thumb-pressing bruises it): ripe yields slightly, like a relaxed muscle. Flick out the small stem nub: green underneath means ripe, brown means overripe, stuck-tight means underripe.
steps.expect: gentle give plus a green stem scar on every avocado you commit to.

steps.action: **Prep the mix-ins first.** Finely dice onion (rinse the dice in cold water for 30 s to tame raw-onion harshness), mince chili (seeds out for mild), chop cilantro, dice tomato if using (seed it first; tomato water makes guac runny).
steps.expect: small even dice staged in the bowl or beside it; hands washed after chili.

steps.action: **Halve, pit, and scoop the avocados.** Cut lengthwise around the pit, twist the halves apart. Remove the pit with a spoon or by prying with fingertips, not by whacking a knife into it (a top cause of home hand injuries). Scoop the flesh into the bowl with a spoon.
steps.expect: all flesh in the bowl; any grey or stringy patches cut away; pits and skins discarded.

steps.action: **Add lime juice and salt before mashing.** Juice of about half a lime and a generous pinch of salt per avocado; the acid coats the flesh immediately and slows browning from the first second.
steps.expect: juice distributed over the flesh, no dry surfaces.

steps.action: **Mash with a fork, deliberately short of smooth.** Press and fold until it holds together but distinct chunks remain; a food processor makes paste, which is a different (worse) food.
steps.expect: creamy base with visible avocado pieces throughout.

steps.action: **Fold in the mix-ins, then season in rounds.** Taste; adjust lime and salt alternately in small additions until the flavor snaps into focus. Under-salted guacamole tastes flat and "missing something"; the answer is nearly always salt or lime, not more chili.
steps.expect: each adjustment tastes brighter; you stop when one more taste makes you keep eating.

steps.action: **Serve now, or seal against air.** [BRANCH: serving immediately → done | holding → press plastic wrap into full contact with the surface (zero air pockets), or float a thin layer of lime juice or water on top and pour it off later; refrigerate] Browning is oxidation: no air contact, no browning. The pit-in-the-bowl trick only shields the area it touches.
steps.expect: surface fully covered, no trapped air bubbles; fridge if held over 30 minutes.

recipes.verification: The guacamole is green throughout (no brown streaks), chunky rather than pureed, tastes bright and salted enough that a plain chip's worth is compelling on its own, and any held portion has an airtight surface seal.

recipes.title: make hot chocolate
recipes.name: make-hot-chocolate
recipes.goal: Proper hot chocolate from real cocoa (or real chocolate), smooth and lump-free, hot but drinkable, and dressed for the occasion — a full tier above the packet, for three minutes more work.

steps.action: **Make the slurry first — this is the anti-lump technology.** In the cold pan or the mug: cocoa, sugar, salt, and just 2 to 3 tablespoons of the milk, stirred into a smooth, thick paste. Cocoa whisked into hot milk directly forms armored lumps; the slurry surrenders instantly.
steps.expect: a glossy, lump-free chocolate paste.

steps.action: **Add the remaining milk gradually, whisking.** Thin the paste with a splash, whisk smooth, then the rest.
steps.expect: uniformly chocolate-colored milk with nothing clinging to the whisk.

steps.action: **Heat on medium, whisking often, to steaming — never boiling.** Milk scorches on the bottom and skins on top when boiled; steaming with small bubbles at the rim is the ceiling (`daily/food/make-oatmeal`'s milk-vigilance applies).
steps.expect: steam rising, tiny rim bubbles, and a bottom the whisk confirms is clean.

steps.action: **Chocolate-bar variant: melt off the heat.** If using chopped chocolate instead of (or with) cocoa: heat the milk first, remove from the stove, add the chocolate and let it sit 30 seconds, then whisk smooth.
steps.expect: fully melted chocolate; the residual heat does it without scorching risk.

steps.action: **Finish with the ten-second froth.** A vigorous final whisk (or a milk frother pulse) aerates the surface into a light foam.
steps.expect: a foamy crown; the difference between hot milk and a beverage.

steps.action: **Pour, top per the occasion, and mind the first sip.** Marshmallows, whipped cream, a dusting of cocoa or cinnamon; the mug is at scald temperature (⚠️ the `daily/food/make-tea` first-sip test doubly applies for kids: an ice cube or a minute's wait for theirs).
steps.expect: a dressed mug, first sip taken cautiously, subsequent sips taken rapidly.

recipes.verification: Smooth to the last sip with a clean pan bottom, steamed-not-boiled, frothed, seasoned with the salt pinch, and the kid-mug tested to drinkable before small hands got it.

recipes.title: make hummus
recipes.name: make-hummus
recipes.goal: A smooth, seasoned chickpea and tahini dip is made with a creamy texture and balanced lemon, salt, garlic, and olive oil.

steps.action: **Soften the chickpeas if needed.** If canned chickpeas feel firm, simmer them in water for 10 minutes, then drain [BRANCH: canned | home-cooked]
steps.expect: a chickpea squashes easily between two fingers.

steps.action: **Decide on peeling.** Peel chickpeas only if you want the smoothest result and have the patience; otherwise use them as-is
steps.expect: you know whether the batch is speed-first or silk-first.

steps.action: **Whip tahini first.** Process tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt before adding chickpeas
steps.expect: the tahini lightens, thickens, and turns paler.

steps.action: **Loosen with ice water.** With the machine running, drizzle in ice water 1 tablespoon at a time
steps.expect: the tahini mixture changes from pasty to fluffy and glossy.

steps.action: **Add chickpeas gradually.** Add chickpeas in two or three additions, scraping the bowl between additions
steps.expect: the paste becomes uniform with no whole chickpeas at the edge.

steps.action: **Blend longer than seems necessary.** Run the processor for 2 to 4 minutes, stopping to scrape as needed
steps.expect: the hummus looks smoother and slightly lighter after each minute.

steps.action: **Adjust seasoning.** Add salt for flatness, lemon for heaviness, tahini for nuttiness, or ice water for looseness
steps.expect: a spoonful tastes bright, savory, and spreadable.

steps.action: **Rest and finish.** Let the hummus sit 10 minutes, then spoon into a bowl and top with olive oil or spices
steps.expect: the flavor settles and the surface holds a shallow swirl.

recipes.verification: A spoonful is smooth enough to spread without tearing bread, tastes seasoned, and leaves no dry chickpea bits on the tongue.

recipes.title: make iced coffee
recipes.name: make-iced-coffee
recipes.goal: Make cold coffee that tastes strong enough after ice, milk, or sweetener are added.

steps.action: **Choose the method.** [BRANCH: hot-bloom-over-ice | cold brew] Use hot-bloom-over-ice for coffee now, or cold brew for a smoother drink prepared 12 to 18 hours ahead.
steps.expect: method fits your timeline.

steps.action: **Plan for dilution.** For hot coffee over ice, brew stronger by using about 1.5 times the usual coffee or replacing half the brew water with ice in the glass.
steps.expect: the recipe accounts for melting ice.

steps.action: **Use good ice.** Fill the serving glass with fresh ice, or use coffee ice cubes if you have them.
steps.expect: glass is cold and ice smells neutral.

steps.action: **Bloom hot grounds if brewing now.** Wet grounds with a small amount of hot water for 30 seconds, then finish brewing directly over ice or brew strong coffee into a separate cup.
steps.expect: coffee aroma opens up and hot liquid starts melting some ice.

steps.action: **Strain cold brew if using it.** Mix coarse grounds with cold water, steep in the fridge, then strain through a filter or fine mesh.
steps.expect: concentrate is clear enough to pour without grit.

steps.action: **Cool before adding milk when possible.** Pour hot-brewed coffee over ice and stir until the glass chills, then add milk or cream.
steps.expect: milk stays smooth and does not taste cooked.

steps.action: **Sweeten in the form that dissolves.** Use syrup in cold coffee, or dissolve sugar in the hot coffee before it hits the ice.
steps.expect: sweetness is even, with no sugar pile on the bottom.

steps.action: **Adjust strength at the end.** Add more coffee concentrate for stronger flavor or more cold water for a lighter drink.
steps.expect: drink tastes balanced after the final stir.

recipes.verification: After stirring, the drink is cold, the coffee flavor is still distinct, and no undissolved sweetener or grit remains at the bottom.

recipes.title: make infused water
recipes.name: make-infused-water
recipes.goal: Cold water lightly flavored with fruit, herbs, cucumber, or citrus without bitterness or mushy solids.

steps.action: **Wash the produce.** Rinse fruit, herbs, and cucumber under cool water.
steps.expect: visible grit is gone and leaves look fresh.

steps.action: **Slice for surface area.** Cut citrus, cucumber, berries, or stone fruit into thin slices or halves.
steps.expect: cut surfaces are exposed without pulverizing the fruit.

steps.action: **Crush herbs lightly.** Clap mint, basil, or rosemary between your hands or press once with a spoon.
steps.expect: herbs smell stronger but are not shredded.

steps.action: **Combine with cold water.** Add about 1 cup produce to 1 quart water.
steps.expect: ingredients move freely and are fully submerged.

steps.action: **Steep cold.** Refrigerate 1 to 4 hours; use citrus-heavy blends closer to 1 hour.
steps.expect: water takes on aroma and faint color while staying clear.

steps.action: **Taste and remove bitter items.** Pull citrus rinds or strong herbs once the flavor is enough.
steps.expect: flavor is refreshing, not pithy or medicinal.

steps.action: **Serve over ice.** Pour gently so soft fruit stays behind if desired.
steps.expect: glass has clean flavored water and a few attractive pieces.

steps.action: **Refill once.** Add more cold water to the same solids one time, then discard after the second batch. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* discard fruit water left warm for more than 2 hours; do not chill it again for later.
steps.expect: second infusion is lighter but still pleasant.

recipes.verification: The water is cold, clean-tasting, lightly aromatic, and the solids are fresh-looking or removed before storage.

recipes.title: make instant noodles
recipes.name: make-instant-noodles
recipes.goal: A serving of instant noodles is cooked to proper texture with its seasoning correctly applied — cup or pot variant — and eaten without a scald.

steps.action: **Read the packet's own instructions once.** Water volume and minutes vary by brand and matter more than habit.
steps.expect: target water amount and time known (typ. 400–500 ml, 3–4 min).

steps.action: **Sort the sachets.** Dry seasoning, oil/paste, dried vegetables — set them aside; note which the instructions add *after* cooking.
steps.expect: sachets out of the packet, not boiled with their plastic.

steps.action: **Cook the noodles.** [BRANCH: pot → noodles into boiling water, simmer per the stated minutes, loosening with chopsticks/fork halfway | cup → fill to the marked line with boiling water, lid on, steep the stated minutes *unopened*]
steps.expect: pot: noodles softening and separating; cup: lid sealed (weight a corner with the sachet), timer running.

steps.action: **Add seasonings at the right stage.** Pot: powder into the broth in the final minute (or into the serving bowl); oil/paste after the heat's off. Cup: per its lid printing, usually after steeping.
steps.expect: fully dissolved seasoning, no dry pockets.

steps.action: **Transfer/open with steam awareness.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the classic instant-noodle injury is a lap scald from carrying an overfull cup or bowl — peel the cup lid *away* from you, carry half-covered, or eat where it cooked.
steps.expect: noodles at the table intact; no splash en route.

steps.action: **Cool the first bites.** Noodles hold heat in their strands — lift, blow, test.
steps.expect: first mouthful hot but not scalding.

recipes.verification: Noodles at intended texture, seasoning dissolved and balanced, sachets' plastic accounted for in the trash (not the broth), and the transit from kettle/stove to mouth happened without a burn.

recipes.title: make jam
recipes.name: make-jam
recipes.goal: Fruit, sugar, acid, and pectin are cooked to a safe set, packed into sterilized jars, sealed, and stored correctly.

steps.action: **Sterilize jars.** Wash jars and keep them hot in simmering water or a low oven.
steps.expect: hot clean jars ready when jam is done.

steps.action: **Prepare fruit.** Wash, trim, pit, and crush or chop fruit evenly.
steps.expect: measured fruit quantity matches the recipe.

steps.action: **Combine by ratio.** For classic jam, use about equal weights fruit and sugar, plus 1-2 tbsp lemon juice per kg fruit; add pectin as directed.
steps.expect: sugar begins dissolving into fruit juices.

steps.action: **Bring to a hard boil.** Use a wide pot and stir until the mixture boils even when stirred. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* boiling sugar sticks to skin and causes deep burns; use long sleeves and keep children away.
steps.expect: large glossy bubbles across the surface.

steps.action: **Cook to setting point.** Boil until 104-105 °C or until the wrinkle test passes.
steps.expect: jam thickens and bubbles become slower and heavier.

steps.action: **Do the wrinkle test.** Drop jam on a chilled plate, wait 30 seconds, then push with a finger.
steps.expect: surface wrinkles instead of flowing like syrup.

steps.action: **Fill jars hot.** Ladle into hot jars, leaving the headspace specified by the recipe, usually about 6 mm.
steps.expect: rims are clean and jars are filled evenly.

steps.action: **Seal and process.** Apply lids fingertip-tight and process in a boiling-water bath for the tested time.
steps.expect: jars are covered by boiling water and processed fully.

steps.action: **Cool undisturbed.** Lift jars out upright and rest 12-24 hours.
steps.expect: lids ping down and do not flex after cooling.

steps.action: **Label and store.** Store sealed jars in a cool dark place; refrigerate any unsealed jar.
steps.expect: jars are dated and failed seals are not shelved.

recipes.verification: Sealed jars have concave non-flexing lids after 12-24 hours, and any unsealed jar is clearly refrigerated.

recipes.title: make kimchi
recipes.name: make-kimchi
recipes.goal: Napa cabbage is salted, seasoned with chile paste, packed, fermented briefly, and refrigerated as kimchi.

steps.action: **Cut the cabbage.** Quarter 1 large napa cabbage lengthwise and cut into bite-size pieces or leave quarters attached at the core.
steps.expect: cabbage pieces are uniform enough to salt evenly.

steps.action: **Salt the cabbage.** Toss with 50-70 g coarse salt, getting salt between thicker leaves.
steps.expect: cabbage is visibly salted and begins to wilt.

steps.action: **Rest and turn.** Let stand 1.5-2 hours, turning every 30 minutes.
steps.expect: stems bend without snapping and liquid collects in the bowl.

steps.action: **Rinse and drain.** Rinse cabbage 2-3 times, then drain 15-30 minutes.
steps.expect: cabbage tastes seasoned but not sharply salty.

steps.action: **Make the paste.** Mix 3-5 tbsp gochugaru, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1-2 tbsp fish sauce, and optional sugar or rice paste.
steps.expect: paste is red, spreadable, and pungent.

steps.action: **Coat cabbage.** Wear gloves and massage paste through cabbage and scallions.
steps.expect: every piece is lightly coated red with no dry white clumps.

steps.action: **Pack the jar.** Press kimchi into a clean jar, leaving 3 cm headspace and pushing liquid above the vegetables.
steps.expect: few air pockets and vegetables sit under their own brine.

steps.action: **Ferment briefly.** Leave at cool room temperature 12-48 hours, opening daily if sealed. [BRANCH: fresh kimchi | sour kimchi] ⚠️ *Irreversible:* gas pressure can crack jars; vent sealed jars.
steps.expect: bubbles rise and aroma turns tangy.

steps.action: **Refrigerate.** Move kimchi to the refrigerator when it tastes right.
steps.expect: fermentation slows and kimchi remains crisp and bright red.

recipes.verification: Kimchi is refrigerated, vegetables are coated and mostly under brine, flavor is salty-sour and chile-forward, and there is no fuzzy mold, rotten smell, or slimy texture.

recipes.title: make lemonade
recipes.name: make-lemonade
recipes.goal: A pitcher of lemonade that is balanced (tart but drinkable), with all sugar fully dissolved and no gritty layer at the bottom, chilled and ready to serve.

steps.action: **Make a simple syrup instead of adding sugar directly.** Combine 1 cup sugar with 1 cup water in a saucepan over medium heat (or microwave 90 seconds), stirring until clear. This is the whole trick: sugar barely dissolves in cold water and otherwise sinks into a sludge you re-stir all afternoon.
steps.expect: liquid goes from cloudy to fully transparent with no grains on the spoon.

steps.action: **Juice the lemons.** Roll each lemon firmly under your palm for 5 seconds first, then halve and juice into a bowl or measuring cup. Fish out seeds; pulp is a taste choice.
steps.expect: about 1 cup of juice from 4-6 lemons; rolled lemons give up noticeably more.

steps.action: **Combine at the 1:1:4 ratio.** In the pitcher: 1 cup lemon juice, 1 cup syrup, 4 cups cold water. Stir.
steps.expect: a uniform pale-yellow mix; nothing settling at the bottom.

steps.action: **Taste and correct before chilling.** [BRANCH: too tart → add syrup 2 tablespoons at a time | too sweet → add lemon juice 1 tablespoon at a time | too strong overall → add water]
steps.expect: a sip that makes you want a second sip, slightly stronger than final target (ice will dilute it).

steps.action: **Chill the pitcher, then add ice only at serving.** Refrigerate 30+ minutes if time allows. Ice melting in the pitcher is the classic failure: an hour later the batch tastes like lemon water. Put ice in the glasses instead.
steps.expect: cold lemonade in the pitcher, ice standing by in glasses, not swimming in the batch.

steps.action: **Serve.** Pour over ice, garnish with a lemon slice if you like.
steps.expect: first glass tastes balanced even after the ice starts to melt.

recipes.verification: The pitcher shows no sediment when tilted, a taste from the top and a taste after stirring are identical (fully dissolved), and a glass poured over ice still tastes of lemon after five minutes.

recipes.title: make mashed potatoes
recipes.name: make-mashed-potatoes
recipes.goal: A bowl of smooth, seasoned mashed potatoes: fluffy, not gluey, hot at serving time, with the dairy fully absorbed.

steps.action: **Peel and cut evenly.** Peel (or leave skins on Yukon Golds if you like texture), cut into chunks of equal size, about 4 cm.
steps.expect: uniform chunks; no piece more than twice the size of another, so they finish together.

steps.action: **Start in cold, well-salted water.** Potatoes into the pot, cold water to cover by 2 cm, salt until the water tastes like the sea (about 1 tbsp per 2 liters). Starting cold cooks them evenly; dropping into boiling water leaves hard centers.
steps.expect: chunks submerged in visibly salted cold water before the burner goes on.

steps.action: **Simmer until knife-tender.** Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Hard boiling batters the outsides apart before the centers cook. Check at 15 minutes.
steps.expect: a paring knife slides into the largest chunk with no resistance, typically 15-20 minutes.

steps.action: **Warm the milk and butter while they simmer.** Milk to steaming (not boiling) with the butter melting into it. Cold milk drops the potatoes' temperature and they absorb it badly.
steps.expect: steaming, buttery milk standing by when the potatoes are done.

steps.action: **Drain thoroughly, then dry the potatoes in the hot pot.** Drain in the colander, return potatoes to the empty pot over low heat for 1-2 minutes, shaking. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the drain is the scald hazard of this recipe: pour away from your body, colander seated in the sink first.
steps.expect: visible steam leaving the chunks; surfaces look chalky-dry. Wet potatoes make wet, bland mash.

steps.action: **Mash off the heat, dairy in stages.** [BRANCH: ricer for the smoothest result | hand masher for rustic texture] Mash first, then fold in the warm milk-butter in two or three additions, stirring just until absorbed. Overworking ruptures starch and turns the mash to glue.
steps.expect: smooth mash that holds a soft peak; each milk addition disappears before the next.

steps.action: **Season and taste.** Salt in pinches, taste after each; black pepper if wanted.
steps.expect: it tastes seasoned, not flat; a final knob of butter on top for serving is optional but correct.

recipes.verification: The mash is smooth (or intentionally rustic), holds a soft peak on a spoon without weeping liquid, tastes distinctly seasoned, and is steaming hot at serving. No hard lumps on a fork drawn through the center of the bowl.

recipes.title: make meatballs
recipes.name: make-meatballs
recipes.goal: Tender meatballs are mixed with a panade, shaped evenly, cooked by searing and simmering or baking, and checked for doneness.

steps.action: **Make the panade.** Soak 60 g breadcrumbs or torn bread in 120 ml milk for 5 minutes.
steps.expect: bread becomes a soft paste that keeps meatballs tender.

steps.action: **Season the binder.** Mix egg, salt, garlic, herbs, cheese, and pepper into the panade before adding meat.
steps.expect: seasoning is evenly dispersed.

steps.action: **Add meat gently.** Add 500 g ground meat and fold with fingers or fork just until combined.
steps.expect: mixture holds together without becoming smeared and pasty.

steps.action: **Cook a test bite.** Fry a teaspoon of mixture and taste for salt.
steps.expect: seasoning can be corrected before shaping all of it.

steps.action: **Shape evenly.** Roll 30-45 g portions with damp hands.
steps.expect: meatballs are similar size and cook evenly.

steps.action: **Choose cooking path.** [BRANCH: sear-then-simmer | bake] Sear in oil before simmering in sauce, or bake on a rimmed tray at 220 °C.
steps.expect: browned exterior or firm set surface.

steps.action: **Cook through.** Simmer 15-25 minutes or bake 15-20 minutes depending on size.
steps.expect: centers reach 71 °C for beef, pork, or mixed meat; 74 °C for poultry.

steps.action: **Rest briefly.** Let meatballs sit 5 minutes in sauce or on the tray.
steps.expect: juices settle and texture firms.

steps.action: **Serve or store.** Serve hot, or cool quickly and refrigerate.
steps.expect: leftovers are packed within 2 hours.

recipes.verification: Meatballs are evenly shaped, tender when cut, and cooked to the safe internal temperature for the meat used.

recipes.title: make microwave popcorn
recipes.name: make-microwave-popcorn
recipes.goal: Microwave popcorn is popped with minimal burning, safe steam handling, and an option for a plain-paper-bag DIY version.

steps.action: **Read the bag direction.** Place the commercial bag correct-side up, or add 1/4 cup kernels to a plain paper bag and fold the top twice.
steps.expect: bag lies flat and can expand.

steps.action: **Set time generously, then listen.** Use the popcorn button only if it works well on your microwave, otherwise set 2 to 3 minutes.
steps.expect: popping starts after a short delay.

steps.action: **Listen for the gap.** Stop when pops slow to about 2 seconds between pops.
steps.expect: most kernels have popped and there is no burnt smell.

steps.action: **Wait before opening.** Let the bag sit closed for 15 to 30 seconds.
steps.expect: steam settles and popping stops.

steps.action: **Open away from your face.** Tear or unfold the bag with the opening pointed away from hands and eyes. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* steam burns happen instantly, so vent the first puff away from skin.
steps.expect: hot steam escapes without hitting you.

steps.action: **Pour into a bowl.** Shake gently so unpopped kernels stay near the bottom of the bag.
steps.expect: popped corn moves to the bowl and hard kernels are visible before serving.

steps.action: **Season lightly.** Add salt, melted butter, or oil in small amounts and toss.
steps.expect: seasoning sticks without soaking the popcorn.

recipes.verification: The bowl contains mostly popped kernels, no active smoke, no scorched smell, and the bag was opened away from the body after popping slowed to 2-second gaps.

recipes.title: make nachos
recipes.name: make-nachos
recipes.goal: Nachos come out crisp, evenly cheesy, and topped in the right order so hot toppings stay hot and cold toppings stay fresh.

steps.action: **Preheat the oven.** Set it to 400 F or 205 C and line a sheet pan.
steps.expect: the oven is hot before chips go in.

steps.action: **Sort toppings by temperature.** [BRANCH: hot toppings like beans, meat, peppers | cold toppings like salsa, crema, avocado, cilantro]
steps.expect: cold toppings are held back.

steps.action: **Spread one chip layer.** Arrange chips in a shallow layer instead of a tall pile.
steps.expect: most chips touch the pan and remain visible.

steps.action: **Cheese every chip.** Scatter grated cheese over the layer, reaching edges and corners.
steps.expect: each cluster has visible cheese.

steps.action: **Add hot toppings lightly.** Spoon warm beans or meat in small dots, then add a little more cheese to glue them down.
steps.expect: toppings are distributed without burying the chips.

steps.action: **Bake, do not microwave.** Bake 5 to 8 minutes until cheese melts and edges toast.
steps.expect: cheese bubbles and chips stay crisp.

steps.action: **Finish with cold toppings.** Add salsa, sour cream, avocado, herbs, and lime after baking.
steps.expect: cold toppings look fresh and do not soak the whole pan.

steps.action: **Serve immediately.** Put the pan on a trivet and eat while cheese is stretchy.
steps.expect: chips lift with toppings attached.

recipes.verification: At least five random chips across the pan have melted cheese, and the center chips are still crisp when lifted.

recipes.title: make nut butter
recipes.name: make-nut-butter
recipes.goal: Smooth nut butter made from roasted nuts, with enough patience to pass through the crumbly stage.

steps.action: **Roast for flavor.** Spread raw nuts and roast at 325 °F for 8 to 12 minutes, stirring once.
steps.expect: nuts smell toasted and are lightly darker inside.

steps.action: **Cool briefly.** Let nuts cool 5 minutes so they are warm, not scorching.
steps.expect: nuts can be handled and still feel slightly warm.

steps.action: **Load the processor.** Add at least 2 cups nuts so the blade has enough volume to work.
steps.expect: nuts sit above the blade line.

steps.action: **Blitz to meal.** Process until nuts become coarse crumbs.
steps.expect: mixture looks sandy and climbs the bowl sides.

steps.action: **Scrape and keep going.** Stop, scrape sides, then process through the dry clumpy phase.
steps.expect: crumbs clump, then start releasing oil.

steps.action: **Process to smooth.** Run in 1-minute bursts, resting the motor if hot.
steps.expect: texture changes from paste to glossy flowing butter.

steps.action: **Season at the end.** Add 1/4 tsp salt per 2 cups nuts, then blend and taste.
steps.expect: nuttiness is clearer without tasting salty.

steps.action: **Jar and store.** Spoon into a clean jar and refrigerate for longer storage. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a burned-out motor or scorched nuts cannot be fixed, so pause if the machine smells hot.
steps.expect: jarred butter with oil either incorporated or ready to stir later.

recipes.verification: The nut butter is spreadable, glossy after stirring, and tastes toasted with salt balanced to the nut flavor.

recipes.title: make oatmeal
recipes.name: make-oatmeal
recipes.goal: A bowl of oatmeal at the consistency you actually like, cooked without a boiled-over pot or a cement-lined microwave, topped and on the table in minutes.

steps.action: **Measure oats, liquid, and the salt pinch into the pot.** Half a cup of rolled oats to one cup of liquid feeds one person. Starting everything cold together (rather than adding oats to boiling liquid) gives a creamier result.
steps.expect: pot loaded, ratio known, salt in.

steps.action: **Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring now and then.** Milk-based pots scorch and boil over more readily than water; medium heat and presence are the deal.
steps.expect: small bubbles at the edges rising to a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil.

steps.action: **Simmer 5 to 7 minutes for rolled oats, stirring occasionally.** More stirring means creamier (the starch releases); less stirring keeps flakes more distinct. Steer by preference.
steps.expect: visible thickening; flakes softening; the spoon starting to leave a brief trail.

steps.action: **Judge doneness by texture, slightly early.** Oatmeal keeps thickening off the heat, so pull it a shade looser than target.
steps.expect: the consistency you like, minus a little.

steps.action: **Rest one minute off the heat, then bowl it.**
steps.expect: final texture landing on target as it sits.

steps.action: **Top with intent.** A fat or protein (nut butter, yogurt, nuts, seeds), a fruit (banana, berries, apple), and a flavor accent (cinnamon, honey, maple, jam). Sweeteners measured after tasting, not before.
steps.expect: a bowl that holds you until lunch, not a sugar delivery system.

steps.action: **Fill the pot with water immediately.** Dried oat residue sets like plaster; a soaking pot cleans itself (`daily/home/wash-dishes-by-hand` will thank you).
steps.expect: pot soaking before the first spoonful.

recipes.verification: The bowl hits your chosen consistency after the one-minute rest, tastes seasoned before sweeteners, carries a fat or protein alongside the fruit, and the pot is already soaking rather than fossilizing.

recipes.title: make overnight chia pudding
recipes.name: make-overnight-chia-pudding
recipes.goal: Chia pudding thickened overnight with an even gel texture and toppings added at serving.

steps.action: **Measure the ratio.** Use 3 tbsp chia seeds to 1 cup milk for spoonable pudding.
steps.expect: seeds are measured before liquid hydrates them.

steps.action: **Mix liquid first.** Stir milk with 1 to 2 tsp sweetener, a pinch of salt, and vanilla if using.
steps.expect: sweetener dissolves evenly.

steps.action: **Add chia while stirring.** Sprinkle seeds into the liquid rather than dumping them in one clump.
steps.expect: seeds disperse throughout the jar.

steps.action: **Stir again after 10 minutes.** Break up any seed clusters along the sides and bottom.
steps.expect: mixture looks evenly speckled, not clumped.

steps.action: **Chill overnight.** Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, preferably overnight.
steps.expect: seeds swell and suspend in a thick gel.

steps.action: **Check texture.** Stir before serving.
steps.expect: pudding mounds softly on the spoon.

steps.action: **Fix if needed.** [BRANCH: too thick | too thin] loosen with milk, or stir in 1 tsp chia and wait 30 minutes.
steps.expect: texture returns to spoonable.

steps.action: **Top and serve.** Add fruit, nuts, granola, jam, or yogurt just before eating. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* soggy crunchy toppings cannot be made crisp again, so add them last.
steps.expect: pudding is cold with fresh toppings.

recipes.verification: The pudding is cold, evenly gelled, spoonable, and has no dry seed clumps at the bottom or edges.

recipes.title: make overnight oats
recipes.name: make-overnight-oats
recipes.goal: Rolled oats are soaked in a jar until tender, with toppings timed so the final breakfast has the intended texture.

steps.action: **Choose the base ratio.** Use 1 part rolled oats to 1 part liquid for spoonable oats, or add 1/4 part yogurt for creamier oats
steps.expect: the jar has enough headroom for stirring and toppings.

steps.action: **Season the dry oats.** Add a pinch of salt and any dry spices before the liquid
steps.expect: spices are dispersed instead of clumped on top.

steps.action: **Add liquid and dairy.** Pour in milk, plant milk, or water, then add yogurt if using
steps.expect: oats are fully wet with no dry pockets at the bottom.

steps.action: **Stir thoroughly.** Scrape the corners and sides of the jar with a spoon
steps.expect: the mixture looks even from top to bottom.

steps.action: **Time the toppings.** [BRANCH: soft toppings overnight | crunchy toppings morning] add dried fruit now, but keep nuts, granola, and crisp fruit separate
steps.expect: toppings that should soften are submerged and crunchy items stay dry.

steps.action: **Refrigerate.** Seal the jar and chill for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight
steps.expect: the jar is cold and the oats have absorbed most liquid.

steps.action: **Fix the texture.** Stir before eating, then add liquid for thick oats or extra oats/chia for loose oats
steps.expect: the spoon moves easily and the mixture is not soupy unless desired.

steps.action: **Finish cold or warm.** Eat cold, or microwave in a microwave-safe bowl with extra liquid if you prefer warm oats
steps.expect: the final bowl is creamy and evenly mixed.

recipes.verification: After chilling and stirring, the oats are hydrated throughout, cold, and thick enough to hold on a spoon.

recipes.title: make pancakes
recipes.name: make-pancakes
recipes.goal: A stack of fluffy pancakes from scratch, with the batter rested, the first-pancake sacrifice understood, and the bubble-reading skill that makes every flip land golden.

steps.action: **Mix dry and wet separately, then combine *briefly*.** Whisk the dry ingredients; whisk egg, milk, and melted butter in another bowl; pour wet into dry and stir just until no dry streaks remain. Lumps are correct. Overmixing develops gluten and makes rubber frisbees — the single most important sentence in pancake literature.
steps.expect: a thick, pourable, visibly lumpy batter.

steps.action: **Rest the batter 5 to 10 minutes while the pan heats on medium.** The rest hydrates the flour and lets the baking powder start; the pan wants medium, not hot (`fry-an-egg` step 1's smoking-pan rule applies).
steps.expect: batter slightly puffed; a water-drop on the pan dances rather than instantly vanishing.

steps.action: **Grease lightly and pour the first pancake — the designated sacrifice.** A small knob of butter wiped around with a paper towel; pour about a third-cup from a low height into the center. The first pancake calibrates pan temperature and is traditionally eaten standing up by the cook.
steps.expect: a slowly spreading round; gentle sizzle, not a sear.

steps.action: **Read the bubbles for the flip.** Wait for bubbles to form across the surface *and begin popping and staying open*, with the edges looking set and slightly dry — typically 2 to 3 minutes. This visual, not a timer, is the flip signal.
steps.expect: open bubble holes across the middle; an edge lifted with the spatula shows golden brown.

steps.action: **Flip once, decisively, and cook the second side briefly.** Slide the spatula fully under, one confident wrist turn, no height ambitions. Side two takes half the time. Do not press the pancake down; the fluff you squash never comes back.
steps.expect: an even golden second side in 60 to 90 seconds; the pancake puffing, not hissing flat.

steps.action: **Stack, hold, and repeat with adjusted heat.** Finished pancakes stack on a plate (in a low oven or under a towel if serving all at once); re-grease lightly every second or third pancake; nudge the heat down as the pan accumulates warmth.
steps.expect: colors converging batch by batch on uniform gold; the stack growing faster than the audience can be restrained.

steps.action: **Serve warm with the toppings ceremony.** Butter melting between layers, syrup or the household's ruling toppings; pancakes wait for no one — the eaters assemble before the last flip.
steps.expect: a warm stack meeting an assembled table.

recipes.verification: The batter went lumpy-and-rested, the bubbles called every flip, no pancake was pressed, the stack runs uniform gold, and the cook got the first pancake plus the last word on when they were ready.

recipes.title: make pasta from scratch
recipes.name: make-pasta-from-scratch
recipes.goal: Fresh egg pasta dough is mixed, kneaded, rested, rolled thin, cut, and cooked quickly.

steps.action: **Measure the ratio.** Use 100 g flour per large egg, plus a pinch of salt per egg.
steps.expect: one serving per egg for a main course.

steps.action: **Make the well.** Mound flour, dig a wide crater, and crack eggs into the center.
steps.expect: walls high enough to hold the eggs.

steps.action: **Beat eggs inward.** Use a fork to whisk the eggs while slowly pulling flour from the inner wall.
steps.expect: a thick slurry forms before the wall breaks.

steps.action: **Bring dough together.** Scrape loose flour into the paste and press until a rough ball forms.
steps.expect: most flour is absorbed, with only dry crumbs left aside if not needed.

steps.action: **Knead firmly.** Push, fold, and rotate for 8-10 minutes.
steps.expect: dough changes from rough to smooth, dense, and slightly springy.

steps.action: **Rest wrapped.** Wrap tightly or cover with an inverted bowl for 30 minutes.
steps.expect: dough softens and rolls without snapping back.

steps.action: **Roll in stages.** [BRANCH: pasta machine | rolling pin] Start thick, fold and reroll a few times, then go thinner one setting at a time.
steps.expect: a long sheet with even thickness and no wet patches.

steps.action: **Cut the pasta.** Dust the sheet, fold loosely, and slice into ribbons, or run through a cutter.
steps.expect: strands separate when tossed with a little flour.

steps.action: **Cook fast.** Boil in well-salted water for 60-120 seconds, stirring immediately.
steps.expect: pasta floats, tastes tender with slight bite, and does not clump.

steps.action: **Sauce immediately.** Transfer with tongs into warm sauce with a splash of cooking water.
steps.expect: sauce coats the pasta instead of pooling underneath.

recipes.verification: Cooked pasta is tender, separate, lightly springy, and coated with sauce within two minutes of draining.

recipes.title: make pesto
recipes.name: make-pesto
recipes.goal: A bright green basil pesto is made with balanced herb, nut, cheese, garlic, and oil flavors without unnecessary bruising or browning.

steps.action: **Pick and inspect basil.** Remove thick stems, wilted leaves, and gritty pieces.
steps.expect: leaves are fragrant, dry or lightly damp, and free of dirt.

steps.action: **Prevent early browning.** Pat basil dry and chill the bowl or blade if the kitchen is hot.
steps.expect: basil stays green before chopping.

steps.action: **Toast nuts only if wanted.** Warm pine nuts, walnuts, or almonds lightly, then cool fully.
steps.expect: nuts smell sweet and are not dark or oily.

steps.action: **Start with garlic, nuts, and salt.** Pulse or pound them first to break down hard pieces.
steps.expect: a coarse paste forms before basil is added.

steps.action: **Add basil gently.** Pulse in short bursts or pound with a twisting motion instead of grinding continuously.
steps.expect: basil breaks down without turning hot, blackened, or watery.

steps.action: **Balance cheese and oil.** Add grated Parmesan or Pecorino, then drizzle olive oil until the pesto loosens.
steps.expect: sauce looks glossy and spoonable, not dry or swimming.

steps.action: **Taste for salt, sharpness, and bitterness.** Add more cheese for savoriness, oil for softness, lemon for brightness, or nuts for body.
steps.expect: no single ingredient dominates.

steps.action: **Use the no-processor method if needed.** Mince basil with a sharp knife, then fold with crushed garlic, chopped nuts, cheese, and oil.
steps.expect: texture is rustic but cohesive.

steps.action: **Cover against air.** Press pesto into a jar and cover the surface with a thin oil layer.
steps.expect: exposed green surface is sealed from oxygen.

steps.action: **Serve or store quickly.** Refrigerate for short storage or freeze in small portions.
steps.expect: pesto remains bright and aromatic.

recipes.verification: Pesto is green, cohesive, spoonable, and balanced enough that a small taste shows basil first with supporting garlic, nut, cheese, salt, and oil.

recipes.title: make pie dough
recipes.name: make-pie-dough
recipes.goal: Flour, fat, salt, and water are mixed into a flaky pie dough that rolls without cracking or greasing.

steps.action: **Measure ingredients.** Use 300 g flour, 225 g cold butter, 5 g salt, and 90-120 ml ice water for a double crust.
steps.expect: fat is cold and ingredients are measured before mixing.

steps.action: **Cut in fat.** Rub or cut butter into flour until pieces range from pea-size to flat flakes.
steps.expect: mixture has visible butter pieces, not a uniform paste.

steps.action: **Add water gradually.** Sprinkle in ice water while tossing with a fork or fingers.
steps.expect: dough clumps when squeezed but still looks shaggy.

steps.action: **Gather the dough.** Press crumbs together on the counter with a bench scraper.
steps.expect: dough holds together with dry streaks but no loose flour pile.

steps.action: **Divide and shape.** Split into disks, wrap tightly, and flatten to even thickness. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overworking now reduces flakiness; stop once the disk holds.
steps.expect: wrapped disks have smooth edges with butter flecks visible.

steps.action: **Chill before rolling.** Refrigerate at least 30 minutes and up to 2 days.
steps.expect: dough feels firm but not rock hard.

steps.action: **Roll as needed.** Let stand 5-10 minutes if too hard, then roll on a lightly floured surface.
steps.expect: dough bends without cracking and does not smear butter.

recipes.verification: Chilled dough rolls into a sheet without sticking heavily, cracking apart, or losing visible cold fat pieces.

recipes.title: make pizza at home
recipes.name: make-pizza-at-home
recipes.goal: A pizza with a browned, crisp-bottomed crust and just-melted toppings comes out of a home oven, sliced and ready to eat.

steps.action: **Make or temper the dough.** [BRANCH: homemade: mix 500 g flour, 325 g water, 7 g yeast, 10 g salt; knead 8 min; rise covered 1.5-2 h | store-bought: rest the ball on the counter 1 h]
steps.expect: dough roughly doubled (homemade) or soft and stretchable without snapping back hard (either path).

steps.action: **Preheat the oven with the stone or tray inside.** Max temperature, stone/steel/inverted tray on a middle-high rack, for a full 45-60 minutes. This is the step people cut short; a cold surface gives a pale, bendy base.
steps.expect: oven at max for the full soak; a drop of water flicked onto the surface skitters off instantly.

steps.action: **Shape by hand, not with a rolling pin.** Press the ball flat, then stretch from the center outward on a floured surface, leaving a 2 cm rim untouched. Rolling crushes the gas bubbles that become the airy rim.
steps.expect: a 28-30 cm round, thin enough in the center to see light through when lifted, rim intact.

steps.action: **Build on parchment or a floured peel.** Thin sauce layer (2-3 tablespoons, spread with the back of a spoon), cheese, then the few toppings, none stacked. Work fast: a wet dough glued to the peel will not launch.
steps.expect: the built pizza still slides when you shake the peel/board gently.

steps.action: **Launch onto the hot surface.** Open the oven, slide the pizza (with its parchment, or with a confident jerk off the peel) onto the stone/tray. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the stone and rack are at max heat; a hesitant launch folds the pizza onto itself. Commit to the motion and keep forearms clear.
steps.expect: pizza flat on the hot surface, door closed within seconds.

steps.action: **Bake 6-10 minutes, watching from ~5 minutes.** If the oven has a broiler/grill, switching it on for the last 2 minutes browns the top like a real pizza oven.
steps.expect: rim puffed and spotted brown, cheese bubbling, edges of the base lifting slightly.

steps.action: **Retrieve, rest, slice.** Pull it out with a peel or tongs onto a rack or board, wait 2 minutes, then slice. Cutting immediately drags molten cheese off.
steps.expect: bottom shows browning when lifted; slices hold their cheese.

recipes.verification: The underside shows brown spots (lift a slice to check), the rim is puffed and holds its shape when a slice is picked up, cheese is melted without a pool of liquid in the center, and the oven is off.

recipes.title: make pizza dough
recipes.name: make-pizza-dough
recipes.goal: Pizza dough is mixed, developed, fermented, divided into balls, and ready to stretch without tearing.

steps.action: **Choose the schedule.** [BRANCH: same-day: 500 g flour, 325 g water, 7 g yeast, 10 g salt | cold ferment: 500 g flour, 325 g water, 2 g yeast, 10 g salt]
steps.expect: ingredients match the time you actually have.

steps.action: **Mix flour and water first.** Stir flour and water until rough, then rest 15-20 minutes before adding yeast and salt.
steps.expect: dough starts stretchy before kneading.

steps.action: **Add yeast and salt.** Sprinkle yeast and salt over the dough, pinch and fold until evenly distributed.
steps.expect: no visible salt piles or yeast granules.

steps.action: **Knead until elastic.** Work dough 8 minutes by hand or 5 minutes on low speed; add only dustings of flour.
steps.expect: dough is tacky, smooth, and springs back when pressed.

steps.action: **Bulk ferment.** Cover the bowl. Same-day dough rises 1.5-2 hours at room temperature; cold dough rests 30 minutes, then refrigerates 24-72 hours.
steps.expect: dough increases in volume and shows small bubbles.

steps.action: **Divide into balls.** Cut into 2 large or 3 smaller pieces; tuck edges underneath while rotating to make tight balls.
steps.expect: each ball has a smooth top and sealed bottom.

steps.action: **Proof before stretching.** Same-day balls rest 30-60 minutes; refrigerated balls warm covered for 1-2 hours.
steps.expect: dough feels relaxed and does not feel cold in the center.

steps.action: **Flour and press the center.** Dust both sides, press from the middle outward, leaving the rim untouched.
steps.expect: a flat center with a thicker outer ring.

steps.action: **Stretch by gravity.** Lift the dough over knuckles and rotate gently, pausing when it resists.
steps.expect: a thin round that expands without tearing.

steps.action: **Use promptly.** Transfer to parchment or a floured peel and top lightly.
steps.expect: dough still slides and has not stuck to the work surface.

recipes.verification: Each dough ball stretches into a thin center with an intact rim and enough elasticity to transfer without tearing.

recipes.title: make quick pickles
recipes.name: make-quick-pickles
recipes.goal: Make refrigerator pickles with hot vinegar brine, aromatics, cooling, and chilled storage.

steps.action: **Prep vegetables.** Wash, trim, and slice evenly
steps.expect: pieces fit the jar

steps.action: **Pack jar.** Add aromatics and vegetables without crushing
steps.expect: jar is full but loose

steps.action: **Mix brine.** Use equal parts vinegar and water with salt and sugar
steps.expect: seasoning dissolves partly

steps.action: **Heat brine.** Bring just to a simmer
steps.expect: brine is clear and steaming

steps.action: **Pour brine.** Cover vegetables fully. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* hot brine can crack weak glass, so use a heatproof jar
steps.expect: vegetables are submerged

steps.action: **Cool.** Let steaming stop before lidding
steps.expect: jar closes without pressure

steps.action: **Refrigerate.** Chill 2 hours for thin slices or overnight for thick pieces
steps.expect: pickles taste tangy

recipes.verification: vegetables are submerged in cold tangy brine

recipes.title: make risotto
recipes.name: make-risotto
recipes.goal: Rice is cooked into a creamy risotto with distinct grains, warm stock added gradually, and a loose wave on the plate.

steps.action: **Warm the stock.** Heat stock until steaming, then keep it just below a simmer
steps.expect: stock is hot enough that it does not cool the rice when ladled in.

steps.action: **Sweat aromatics.** Cook onion or shallot gently in butter or oil until translucent, not browned
steps.expect: the pan smells sweet and the pieces look glossy.

steps.action: **Toast the rice.** Add dry rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until the edges look translucent
steps.expect: grains feel hot and sound faintly glassy against the pan.

steps.action: **Deglaze if using wine.** Add wine and stir until the pan is almost dry [BRANCH: wine | no wine]
steps.expect: the sharp alcohol smell fades.

steps.action: **Ladle stock gradually.** Add enough warm stock to barely cover the rice, stirring often until mostly absorbed
steps.expect: the spoon leaves a temporary trail across the pan.

steps.action: **Keep stirring.** Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly enough to release starch and prevent sticking
steps.expect: the mixture gets creamier while the grains stay visible.

steps.action: **Taste for doneness.** Start tasting around 16 minutes and stop when the center has a small firm point
steps.expect: rice is tender but not mushy.

steps.action: **Check the wave.** Shake the pan; add stock if the risotto sits stiff, or cook briefly if it floods the pan
steps.expect: the surface flows slowly like a soft wave.

steps.action: **Finish with mantecatura.** Off heat, beat in cold butter and grated cheese until glossy
steps.expect: risotto looks shiny and loose, not oily or clumpy.

recipes.verification: When spooned onto a warm plate, the risotto spreads slowly into a shallow pool while the rice grains remain distinct.

recipes.title: make salad dressing
recipes.name: make-salad-dressing
recipes.goal: A balanced vinaigrette is emulsified, seasoned, and tested on an actual leaf so it tastes right on salad, not just on a spoon.

steps.action: **Start with the ratio.** Measure 3 parts oil to 1 part acid for a classic vinaigrette.
steps.expect: the base tastes bright but not harsh once mixed.

steps.action: **Add binder.** Add a small spoon of Dijon or other prepared mustard.
steps.expect: the mustard disappears into the acid and gives the dressing body.

steps.action: **Season the acid first.** Stir salt and pepper into the vinegar or lemon before adding oil.
steps.expect: salt dissolves instead of sitting as grains.

steps.action: **Add optional flavorings.** Mix in shallot, garlic, herbs, honey, or zest in small amounts.
steps.expect: the dressing smells seasoned but not dominated by one raw ingredient.

steps.action: **Emulsify slowly.** Whisk while drizzling oil, or shake everything in a jar for 15 seconds.
steps.expect: the dressing turns cloudy and slightly thick.

steps.action: **Taste on a leaf.** Dip a lettuce leaf or salad ingredient into the dressing and eat it.
steps.expect: acid, salt, and oil taste balanced on the food.

steps.action: **Adjust deliberately.** [BRANCH: too sharp → add oil or honey | too flat → add acid or salt | too oily → add acid and mustard]
steps.expect: the next leaf tastes better, not just stronger.

steps.action: **Dress lightly.** Toss salad with part of the dressing, then add more only if needed.
steps.expect: leaves are glossy, not dripping.

steps.action: **Hold leftovers.** Store extra dressing in a covered jar and shake before reuse.
steps.expect: dressing is contained, labeled if needed, and can re-emulsify.

recipes.verification: The dressing coats salad ingredients lightly, tastes balanced on a leaf, and can be shaken back together if it separates.

recipes.title: make salsa
recipes.name: make-salsa
recipes.goal: Fresh or cooked salsa is chopped or blended, balanced with acid, heat, and salt, rested, and ready to serve.

steps.action: **Choose fresh or cooked.** [BRANCH: fresh: raw tomatoes and lime | cooked: roasted or simmered tomatoes or tomatillos]
steps.expect: style matches the flavor and storage time wanted.

steps.action: **Prep ingredients.** Core tomatoes, peel onion, stem chiles, and wash herbs.
steps.expect: tough stems and bruised spots are removed.

steps.action: **Control chile heat.** Remove seeds and ribs for milder salsa, or keep them for more heat.
steps.expect: chile quantity is intentional, not accidental.

steps.action: **Dice or blitz.** Dice by hand for chunky salsa, or pulse in short bursts for smoother salsa.
steps.expect: texture is even and not watery puree unless desired.

steps.action: **Balance acid.** Add lime juice or vinegar a teaspoon at a time.
steps.expect: tomato sweetness tastes brighter.

steps.action: **Salt correctly.** Add salt, stir, wait 2 minutes, then taste again.
steps.expect: flavors become distinct and less flat.

steps.action: **Rest the salsa.** Let sit 10-20 minutes so onion mellows and juices mingle.
steps.expect: salsa tastes more integrated than when first mixed.

steps.action: **Adjust before serving.** [BRANCH: too sharp: add tomato | too hot: add tomato or avocado | dull: add salt and lime]
steps.expect: acid, heat, and salt are in balance.

steps.action: **Store cold.** Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container.
steps.expect: salsa is chilled within 2 hours.

recipes.verification: Salsa has an even texture, tastes balanced for acid, heat, and salt, and has rested at least 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: make scrambled eggs
recipes.name: make-scrambled-eggs
recipes.goal: A plate of soft, glossy scrambled eggs in small creamy curds: fully set but not dry, rubbery, or weeping liquid.

steps.action: **Beat the eggs thoroughly with salt.** Crack into a bowl, add a pinch of salt per two eggs, and beat until fully homogeneous, no ribbons of clear white remaining. Salting now (not in the pan) dissolves evenly and slightly tenderizes.
steps.expect: a uniform pale-yellow liquid with no streaks.

steps.action: **Melt butter over low heat.** A generous knob in the pan on low. Low heat is the entire method: eggs set at around 63-70 °C and high heat blows straight past that.
steps.expect: butter melted and foaming gently, never browning. Browning butter means the pan is too hot; pull it off and let it cool 30 seconds.

steps.action: **Add the eggs and start stirring immediately.** Pour in and stir slowly but constantly with the spatula, scraping the bottom and edges where the eggs set first. Constant motion is what makes small creamy curds; leaving them alone makes an omelet.
steps.expect: nothing happens for the first 30-60 seconds. This is correct; do not raise the heat.

steps.action: **Keep stirring as curds form.** Continue steady scraping as the mixture thickens from liquid, to thick cream, to soft curds. If it ever starts setting faster than you can stir, lift the pan off the heat and keep stirring; the pan's stored heat keeps cooking.
steps.expect: gradual thickening over 3-5 minutes; small moist curds forming without any browning.

steps.action: **Pull off the heat early, while still glossy and slightly underdone.** Remove when the eggs look about 80 percent done: mostly set but still visibly wet on top. Carryover heat from the pan finishes them. This off-heat finish is the difference between creamy and rubbery.
steps.expect: eggs continue to visibly set in the pan over the next 30-60 seconds with no burner under them.

steps.action: **Stir once more and plate immediately.** A final fold off heat, then straight onto the warm plate; do not let them sit in the hot pan. Add pepper, chives, or a small knob of cold butter folded in for gloss.
steps.expect: soft, glossy curds that hold their shape but jiggle slightly; no browned bits, no pooled liquid.

recipes.verification: Eggs on the plate are fully set with no translucent raw patches, show no browning, form soft distinct curds rather than one dry mass, and no free liquid pools on the plate within a minute of serving.

recipes.title: make simple syrup
recipes.name: make-simple-syrup
recipes.goal: Sugar and water are dissolved into a clear simple syrup for drinks, desserts, or cocktails.

steps.action: **Choose the ratio.** [BRANCH: 1:1 by volume for standard syrup | 2:1 sugar to water for rich cocktail syrup]
steps.expect: measured sugar and water match the drink recipe.

steps.action: **Combine sugar and water.** Add both to a small saucepan or heatproof jar.
steps.expect: sugar is fully wetted with no dry mound.

steps.action: **Warm gently.** Heat over low to medium heat, or add hot water to the jar and stir.
steps.expect: liquid warms without a hard boil.

steps.action: **Dissolve, not reduce.** Stir until the liquid turns clear.
steps.expect: no sugar grains scrape under the spoon.

steps.action: **Stop heating.** Remove from heat as soon as dissolved.
steps.expect: volume has not noticeably boiled away.

steps.action: **Cool uncovered.** Let syrup cool until no steam rises.
steps.expect: bottle will not trap pressure or condensation.

steps.action: **Bottle cleanly.** Pour into a clean labeled bottle.
steps.expect: syrup is clear and the lid closes tightly.

steps.action: **Refrigerate.** Store 1:1 syrup chilled and use within about 1 month.
steps.expect: bottle sits cold and dated.

recipes.verification: The syrup is clear, fully liquid, labeled with its ratio, and has no visible sugar crystals after cooling.

recipes.title: make soup from scratch
recipes.name: make-soup-from-scratch
recipes.goal: A pot of well-seasoned soup built from raw ingredients: aromatics, a main vegetable or protein, and liquid, finished either blended-smooth or chunky.

steps.action: **Prep everything before heat.** Dice the aromatics small and uniform; cut the main ingredient into even bite-size pieces so they cook at the same rate.
steps.expect: all cutting done, board cleared, pot empty on the stove.

steps.action: **Sweat the aromatics in fat over medium heat, 5-10 minutes.** Onion first with a pinch of salt to draw moisture; garlic only in the last minute (it burns fast and burnt garlic ruins the pot). Do not brown unless you want a darker, roastier soup.
steps.expect: onions translucent and soft, glossy, fragrant, not colored.

steps.action: **Add hardy ingredients and stir 2-3 minutes.** Root vegetables, dried spices, tomato paste if using; a short fry in the aromatic fat wakes them up.
steps.expect: spices fragrant, paste darkened a shade, nothing sticking hard.

steps.action: **Add liquid to cover by 2-3 cm and bring to a boil, then drop to a simmer.** Scrape the pot bottom as the liquid goes in; those browned bits are flavor.
steps.expect: contents submerged, first boil reached, then lazy bubbles only.

steps.action: **Simmer, lid ajar, until the slowest ingredient is tender.** Roughly 20-30 min for vegetables, 45+ for dried legumes (pre-soaked), longer for tough meat cuts. Skim any grey foam early on.
steps.expect: a knife slides through the largest piece with no resistance.

steps.action: **Choose the finish.** [BRANCH: blend smooth → next step | leave chunky → skip to step 8]
steps.expect: a decision matched to the ingredients (silky for squash or tomato, chunky for minestrone-style).

steps.action: **Blend.** Immersion blender: kill the heat, keep the head fully submerged, work in slow passes. Countertop blender: ⚠️ *Irreversible:* hot liquid erupts in a sealed blender; blend in half-full batches, lid vent open, towel over the top.
steps.expect: uniform velvety texture, no eruption, no splatter burns.

steps.action: **Season late, in rounds.** Now add most of the salt: taste, add, stir, wait 30 seconds, taste again; repeat until flavors pop. Salting fully at the start overshoots because the liquid reduces. Finish with black pepper and a small squeeze of acid.
steps.expect: each round tastes noticeably better; the acid makes it taste brighter, not sour.

steps.action: **Adjust body and serve hot.** Too thick: loosen with hot stock or water. Too thin: simmer uncovered 10 min, or blend a cupful and stir it back.
steps.expect: the soup coats a spoon the way you want; ladled without drips down the pot side.

recipes.verification: The slowest ingredient is fork-tender, the seasoning was tasted and adjusted in at least two rounds, texture matches the intended branch (uniformly smooth or distinct pieces), and the pot is at a servable temperature with the burner off or on low.

recipes.title: make stock from scratch
recipes.name: make-stock-from-scratch
recipes.goal: Extract flavor and body from bones or scraps into a clear stock by starting cold and simmering gently.

steps.action: **Start cold.** Cover bones or scraps with cold water by 1 to 2 inches
steps.expect: solids are submerged

steps.action: **Heat slowly.** Bring toward a simmer over medium
steps.expect: foam rises

steps.action: **Skim.** Remove gray scum with a ladle
steps.expect: surface looks cleaner

steps.action: **Add aromatics.** Add onion, carrot, celery, herbs, or peppercorns
steps.expect: aromatics are submerged

steps.action: **Simmer low.** Hold only a few bubbles at the surface
steps.expect: stock trembles without boiling

steps.action: **Strain gently.** Pour through a strainer without pressing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* pressing spent solids clouds stock
steps.expect: liquid runs clear

steps.action: **Cool quickly.** Use shallow containers and refrigerate or freeze
steps.expect: stock chills promptly

recipes.verification: stock tastes savory and is strained and cooled safely

recipes.title: make sushi rice
recipes.name: make-sushi-rice
recipes.goal: Short-grain rice is cooked, seasoned, cooled, and handled so it is glossy, sticky, and safe for sushi.

steps.action: **Measure rice.** Use 2 cups short-grain rice for about 4 rolls or bowls.
steps.expect: rice quantity is known and matched to cooker capacity.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly.** Wash in cold water, drain, and repeat until water is mostly clear.
steps.expect: water changes from milky to faintly cloudy.

steps.action: **Soak and drain.** Soak rice 20-30 minutes, then drain 10 minutes.
steps.expect: grains look opaque white and slightly swollen.

steps.action: **Cook with measured water.** Add water near a 1:1 rice-to-water ratio by volume, or use the cooker sushi line.
steps.expect: pot or cooker is loaded with level rice and correct water.

steps.action: **Rest after cooking.** Let cooked rice sit covered 10 minutes.
steps.expect: steam equalizes and grains are tender to the center.

steps.action: **Mix seasoning.** Dissolve 60 ml rice vinegar, 25 g sugar, and 8 g salt for 2 cups raw rice.
steps.expect: seasoning is clear with no sugar crystals.

steps.action: **Season and fan.** Spread rice in a wide bowl, drizzle seasoning, and fold while fanning. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* crushing hot rice makes paste; cut and fold instead of mashing.
steps.expect: rice becomes glossy and cools to body temperature.

steps.action: **Cover for use.** Cover with a damp towel and use within a few hours.
steps.expect: rice stays moist, sticky, and not refrigerated-hard.

recipes.verification: Rice is glossy, lightly tangy, sticky enough to clump, tender through the center, and held covered at room temperature for no more than 4 hours.

recipes.title: make tea
recipes.name: make-tea
recipes.goal: A cup or pot of properly steeped tea, at drinking temperature, matched to the tea type.

steps.action: **Match water temperature to the tea.** Black/herbal: fully boiling. Oolong: ~90 °C. Green/white: 70–80 °C (boil, then wait 2–3 min or add a splash of cool water).
steps.expect: water at the right band — boiling water on green tea is the classic bitterness mistake.

steps.action: **Warm the cup/pot (optional but real).** Swirl a little hot water in and dump it.
steps.expect: vessel warm to the touch; the tea won't crash in temperature on contact.

steps.action: **Dose the tea.** One bag or ~1 tsp loose leaf per cup (~250 ml); leaves in the infuser with room to expand.
steps.expect: infuser at most half-full of dry leaf.

steps.action: **Pour the water over the tea and start a timer.** Black: 3–5 min. Green: 1–3 min. Herbal: 5+.
steps.expect: leaves unfurling/bag steeping, color developing; a timer actually running.

steps.action: **Remove the tea at time.** Pull the bag without wringing it (wringing squeezes bitter tannins); lift the infuser and let it drip a moment.
steps.expect: liquor at the expected color; leaves out of the water.

steps.action: **Adjust and serve.** Milk/sugar/lemon per taste (milk pairs with black; lemon curdles milk — pick one). ⚠️ *Irreversible:* it's near-boiling liquid — carry cup-half-full if walking, and test a sip's temperature at the lip first.
steps.expect: drinkable within a few minutes; no scalded tongue.

recipes.verification: The tea's color and strength match its type, it tastes intended (not accidentally bitter), and the steeping tea/bag has been removed rather than left in.

recipes.title: make whipped cream
recipes.name: make-whipped-cream
recipes.goal: Whip cold cream to soft or stiff peaks while stopping before it turns grainy and starts becoming butter.

steps.action: **Chill tools.** Use a refrigerator-cold bowl and whisk, or freeze them for 10 minutes
steps.expect: tools feel cold to the touch

steps.action: **Start slow.** Pour in cold cream and beat on low until foamy
steps.expect: cream bubbles without splashing

steps.action: **Add flavor.** Add sugar and vanilla once cream thickens slightly
steps.expect: flavoring disappears evenly

steps.action: **Increase speed.** Beat on medium while moving around the bowl
steps.expect: whisk tracks briefly hold

steps.action: **Check peaks.** [BRANCH: soft peaks for folding | stiff peaks for piping] lift the whisk often
steps.expect: peak tips slump for soft or stand for stiff

steps.action: **Stop smooth.** Slow down near the target. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* separated butter grains will not become silky whipped cream again
steps.expect: surface is satin-smooth

steps.action: **Hold cold.** Serve now or refrigerate covered for a few hours
steps.expect: cream holds shape without weeping

recipes.verification: The cream holds the chosen peak stage, remains smooth, and has no butter grains or watery separation.

recipes.title: make yogurt at home
recipes.name: make-yogurt-at-home
recipes.goal: Milk is heated, inoculated with live yogurt culture, incubated until tangy and set, then chilled safely.

steps.action: **Clean the equipment.** Wash the pot, jar, spoon, and thermometer with hot soapy water and rinse well.
steps.expect: no visible food residue and equipment is air-drying or freshly dried.

steps.action: **Heat the milk.** Warm 1 L milk to 82-85 °C, stirring to prevent scorching.
steps.expect: steam rises, small bubbles form at the edge, and the thermometer reads at least 82 °C.

steps.action: **Hold the heat.** Keep milk at 82-85 °C for 5 minutes.
steps.expect: milk smells sweet, not scorched, and stays below a rolling boil.

steps.action: **Cool to inoculation temperature.** Set the pot in cool water or leave it uncovered until milk reaches 43-46 °C.
steps.expect: milk feels warm but not hot, and the thermometer is under 46 °C.

steps.action: **Add starter.** Whisk a ladle of warm milk into the yogurt, then stir that mixture back into the pot.
steps.expect: starter disappears smoothly with no large yogurt clumps.

steps.action: **Incubate undisturbed.** Pour into the clean jar, cover, and hold at 40-45 °C for 6-10 hours. [BRANCH: mild yogurt | tangier yogurt]
steps.expect: surface sets like soft custard and smells cleanly sour.

steps.action: **Chill promptly.** Move the jar to the refrigerator when set. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not taste yogurt that smells rotten, moldy, or alcoholic; discard it.
steps.expect: yogurt cools below 4 °C within a few hours and firms further.

steps.action: **Save starter if desired.** Reserve a clean spoonful before serving from the jar.
steps.expect: starter is separated in a clean container without crumbs or saliva contact.

recipes.verification: After chilling, the yogurt is below 4 °C, smells cleanly tangy, holds a spoon mark, and has no mold, discoloration, or off gas.

recipes.title: mince garlic
recipes.name: mince-garlic
recipes.goal: Garlic peeled and minced evenly, with an optional salt paste for sauces, dressings, and marinades.

steps.action: **Separate cloves.** Pull the needed cloves from the head and leave skins on for the smash.
steps.expect: loose cloves are ready on the board.

steps.action: **Smash and peel.** Lay the flat of the knife over one clove, heel of your hand on top, and press firmly.
steps.expect: skin cracks and slips off easily.

steps.action: **Trim rough ends.** Cut away hard root nubs with fingers in a claw grip.
steps.expect: peeled cloves have no dry root bits.

steps.action: **Slice first.** Cut each clove lengthwise into thin slices so the mince starts even.
steps.expect: slices lie flat instead of rolling.

steps.action: **Rock-chop.** Gather slices, place your free hand flat on the knife spine, and rock the tip through the pile.
steps.expect: garlic becomes small, even pieces.

steps.action: **Scrape and repeat.** Use the knife spine to gather garlic, then chop again until fine.
steps.expect: no large chunks remain.

steps.action: **Make paste if needed.** [BRANCH: mince | salt-paste] Sprinkle a pinch of kosher salt and drag the blade flat across the garlic to smear it.
steps.expect: salted garlic turns sticky and smooth.

steps.action: **Add late to heat.** Put minced garlic into hot fat only when other ingredients are ready.
steps.expect: garlic sizzles briefly and smells sweet, not bitter. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* burnt garlic turns harsh quickly; remove it and restart rather than trying to hide the flavor.

recipes.verification: Garlic pieces are evenly minced or pasted, skins and root nubs are removed, and the garlic has not browned before the recipe needs it.

recipes.title: open a coconut
recipes.name: open-a-coconut
recipes.goal: A mature coconut drained, cracked open, and separated into usable water and flesh without unsafe chopping.

steps.action: **Find the soft eye.** Inspect the three eyes and press each with a skewer or screwdriver.
steps.expect: one eye gives more easily than the others.

steps.action: **Open the eye.** Twist through the soft eye and widen the hole.
steps.expect: a clean drain hole reaches the hollow center.

steps.action: **Drain the water.** Invert the coconut over a bowl and shake until flow stops.
steps.expect: coconut water collects without shell pieces.

steps.action: **Check the water.** Smell and taste a small amount if it looks clear.
steps.expect: it smells fresh and mildly sweet, not sour or fermented.

steps.action: **Crack the equator.** Wrap in a towel or hold firmly, then tap around the middle line with a hammer or heavy pan.
steps.expect: a crack forms around the coconut.

steps.action: **Split the shell.** Continue tapping along the crack until the halves separate.
