recipes.verification: After two flushes, tank water stops at the fill mark or about 1 inch below the overflow tube, and the toilet is silent for five minutes.

recipes.title: anchor furniture to the wall
recipes.name: anchor-furniture-to-the-wall
recipes.goal: A dresser, bookcase, TV stand, or similar furniture is secured to wall studs with anti-tip hardware so it cannot tip forward easily.

steps.action: **Empty and stabilize.** Remove heavy loose items, close drawers, and push the furniture near its final position.
steps.expect: it can be moved without tipping.

steps.action: **Read the kit rating.** Confirm the strap or bracket is intended for furniture anti-tip use, not light picture hanging.
steps.expect: hardware is suitable for the furniture size.

steps.action: **Find a stud.** Use a stud finder behind the furniture and mark the stud center above the furniture top or through the back gap.
steps.expect: a stud location is clearly marked.

steps.action: **Choose attachment points.** [BRANCH: strap kit | L-bracket] straps usually connect high on the furniture; brackets connect the furniture back or top rail to the wall.
steps.expect: the anchor point is high and solid.

steps.action: **Mark holes.** Hold the wall bracket on the stud mark and the furniture bracket on a solid rail, not thin backer board.
steps.expect: screw marks are aligned with strong material.

steps.action: **Drill pilots.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the furniture location and avoid hidden wiring or plumbing before drilling.
steps.expect: pilot holes match the screw size.

steps.action: **Fasten to the wall stud.** Drive the wall screws into the stud, not just drywall.
steps.expect: the bracket or strap mount cannot pull out by hand.

steps.action: **Fasten to furniture.** Attach the furniture-side hardware into a solid rail or manufacturer-marked point.
steps.expect: screws bite firmly without splitting.

steps.action: **Set strap tension.** Move the furniture back and tighten the strap so it is snug but not bowing the furniture.
steps.expect: the furniture sits flush and restrained.

steps.action: **Check the tip resistance.** Pull gently from the top front while another adult steadies the piece.
steps.expect: the anchor prevents forward tip movement.

recipes.verification: With drawers closed and shelves loaded normally, the furniture cannot tip forward during a gentle top-front pull because the anti-tip strap or bracket holds it to the wall.

recipes.title: assemble flat pack a bookshelf
recipes.name: assemble-flat-pack-a-bookshelf
recipes.goal: The flat-pack bookshelf is assembled square, shelves are secure, and any tall unit is anchored to prevent tip-over.

steps.action: **Inventory every part.** Lay panels, cams, dowels, screws, shelf pins, back panel, and anchors against the parts list.
steps.expect: no part count is short before assembly begins.

steps.action: **Read the instructions fully.** Identify panel orientation, finished edges, and steps that require two people.
steps.expect: front, back, top, and bottom are clear.

steps.action: **Start cam-lock hardware correctly.** Insert dowels and cam bolts straight, then align cams with their openings facing the bolt path.
steps.expect: panels draw together when cams turn.

steps.action: **Build the frame loosely.** Join side, top, bottom, and fixed shelves before final tightening. [BRANCH: cam locks | screws] snug cams by rotation, snug screws by hand pressure.
steps.expect: the frame stands in the intended shape.

steps.action: **Square with the back panel.** Measure diagonals or align corners before fastening the back panel.
steps.expect: the diagonals match and shelves sit parallel.

steps.action: **Fasten the back panel.** Nail, screw, or slide the panel as instructed, keeping edges flush. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the unit is square before driving nails or staples.
steps.expect: the frame becomes rigid and square.

steps.action: **Install shelves and caps.** Add adjustable shelf pins at matching heights and press covers into exposed holes.
steps.expect: shelves sit level and do not rock.

steps.action: **Anchor tall units.** Attach the anti-tip bracket to the unit and a stud, masonry anchor, or rated hollow-wall anchor.
steps.expect: the top cannot be pulled forward by hand.

recipes.verification: The bookshelf is square, shelves sit on matched supports, and any tall unit is anchored so the top cannot tip forward under a firm hand pull.

recipes.title: assemble flat pack furniture
recipes.name: assemble-flat-pack-furniture
recipes.goal: The furniture item is fully assembled, square, and stable in its final position, with every fastener accounted for and no panel installed backwards.

steps.action: **Unbox onto the flattened cardboard and inventory everything.** Lay panels out, tip hardware into a bowl, and count every fastener type against the manual's parts list before starting.
steps.expect: every listed part present in the listed quantity; missing parts discovered now, not at step 9 of the build.

steps.action: **Read the entire instruction booklet before touching a screw.** Note which panels look alike but differ (hole patterns, edge finishing) and where the build direction matters.
steps.expect: you can say in one sentence what order the major panels join and which face of each panel points out.

steps.action: **Sort hardware by step.** Group fasteners as the manual numbers them; cam locks with cam locks, dowels with dowels.
steps.expect: each build step's hardware reachable without searching.

steps.action: **Orient the first panels by their holes, not by guesswork.** The rule that saves rebuilds: pre-drilled holes face inward or toward mating panels; the unbroken finished face is the visible side.
steps.expect: panel orientation matches the manual's little arrows and hole diagrams exactly.

steps.action: **Insert dowels and cam bolts before mating panels.** Cam-lock logic: the metal cam bolt screws into one panel, the round cam nut drops into the large hole of the other, arrow on the cam facing the incoming bolt.
steps.expect: dowels seated halfway, cam bolts standing perpendicular, cam nuts loose in their sockets with arrows toward the bolt holes.

steps.action: **Mate panels and turn each cam nut about a half turn clockwise to lock.** Stop at firm resistance. Cam nuts strip their particleboard sockets if forced further, and a stripped socket is close to unrepairable.
steps.expect: panels pulled tight together; cam slot roughly perpendicular to the bolt.

steps.action: **Assemble the full frame with screws only hand-tight.** Leave every screwed joint a quarter turn loose until all frame parts are connected.
steps.expect: a complete but slightly floppy frame that can still be racked by hand.

steps.action: **Square the frame, then do the final tightening pass.** Push the frame square (equal diagonals, or against a known-square wall corner), then tighten every fastener fully in the same order they were installed.
steps.expect: diagonal measurements equal within a few millimeters; frame rigid.

steps.action: **Fit the back panel and nail or screw it in square.** The thin back panel is what actually holds most flat-pack cabinets square; align its edges flush to the frame before fixing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* nails through the back panel into the wrong line miss the shelf edge and are visible from inside; mark the nail line first.
steps.expect: back panel flush on all four edges, nails biting panel edges, unit no longer rackable.

steps.action: **Add doors, drawers, shelves, and level in final position.** Adjust hinge screws so door gaps are even; anchor tall units to the wall with the included bracket.
steps.expect: doors close flush, drawers run smoothly, unit does not rock.

recipes.verification: Diagonals of the main frame are equal, no leftover fasteners remain beyond the manual's declared spares, all doors and drawers open and close without rubbing, and the unit stands without rocking (anchored to the wall if tall).

recipes.title: attract pollinators to a garden
recipes.name: attract-pollinators-to-a-garden
recipes.goal: Create a garden area that offers nectar, pollen, shelter, and clean water for bees, butterflies, moths, flies, and other useful pollinators across the growing season.

steps.action: **Map bloom gaps.** Note what flowers in spring, summer, and fall, including trees, herbs, vegetables, and ornamentals.
steps.expect: missing bloom seasons are visible on a short list.

steps.action: **Choose region-suitable plants.** Select mostly native or well-adapted flowers with varied shapes, including early, midseason, and late blooms.
steps.expect: the plant list offers pollen or nectar for multiple months.

steps.action: **Plant in clusters.** Group three or more of the same plant where space allows so pollinators can forage efficiently.
steps.expect: blooms form visible patches rather than scattered single plants.

steps.action: **Include host plants.** Add plants that feed caterpillars or specialist insects, such as milkweed where appropriate or native grasses and herbs.
steps.expect: the garden supports life stages beyond adult nectar feeding.

steps.action: **Provide shallow water.** Set a shallow dish with stones or keep a small muddy patch damp during dry weather.
steps.expect: insects can land and drink without drowning.

steps.action: **Leave shelter.** Keep some hollow stems, leaf litter, bare soil patches, or brushy edges where they do not create hazards.
steps.expect: nesting and overwintering sites remain available.

steps.action: **Avoid pesticide exposure.** Hand-pick pests, use barriers, and never spray flowers when pollinators are active.
steps.expect: blooming plants are not coated with insecticide.

steps.action: **Observe and adjust.** Watch visits at different times of day and replace unused or failing plants with better-adapted choices.
steps.expect: pollinator visits increase over the season.

recipes.verification: The garden has overlapping bloom periods, clustered flowering plants, a safe shallow water source, some shelter habitat, and no insecticide applied to open flowers.

recipes.title: balance radiators
recipes.name: balance-radiators
recipes.goal: Radiators heat more evenly across rooms by slowing the hottest radiators at their lockshield valves and giving colder radiators more flow.

steps.action: **Bleed air first.** With heating off and cool, bleed radiators that have cold tops, then close the bleed valve.
steps.expect: water appears steadily and trapped air is gone.

steps.action: **Open valves fully.** Open each thermostatic valve and remove lockshield caps to open each lockshield fully.
steps.expect: all radiators can receive full flow.

steps.action: **Turn heating on.** Let the system warm from cold and note which radiators heat first.
steps.expect: faster radiators reveal where flow is strongest.

steps.action: **Throttle the fastest radiator.** Close its lockshield fully, then reopen about a quarter to half turn.
steps.expect: that radiator still heats but warms more slowly.

steps.action: **Move through the house.** Adjust each early-hot radiator in small increments, waiting several minutes between changes.
steps.expect: colder rooms begin warming closer to the rest.

steps.action: **Leave cold rooms more open.** Keep lockshields more open on radiators that heat last. [BRANCH: one cold radiator | whole zone cold] one radiator suggests valve or air, a zone suggests pump or controls.
steps.expect: heat distribution becomes more even.

steps.action: **Replace caps and record settings.** Note approximate lockshield turns for each room.
steps.expect: settings can be restored if someone changes a valve.

recipes.verification: After one full warm-up, all occupied rooms reach usable heat without one radiator becoming hot much earlier than the rest.

recipes.title: bathe a dog
recipes.name: bathe-a-dog
recipes.goal: Wash a dog safely with dog shampoo, rinse completely, and dry the coat without causing fear, skin irritation, or ear and eye problems.

steps.action: **Brush first.** Remove loose fur, burrs, and small tangles before water tightens them.
steps.expect: the coat parts more easily and mats are visible before washing.

steps.action: **Prepare the calm setup.** Put a mat in the tub or shower, lay towels within reach, and run water before bringing in a nervous dog if the sound worries them.
steps.expect: the space is ready and you do not need to leave the wet dog unattended.

steps.action: **Check the water.** Test lukewarm water on your inner wrist and keep pressure gentle.
steps.expect: the water feels warm but not hot, with no startling blast.

steps.action: **Wet from neck down.** Soak the coat slowly, avoiding eyes, ear canals, and the inside of the nose.
steps.expect: the body coat is wet while the face remains controlled and dry enough to manage.

steps.action: **Apply dog shampoo.** Massage shampoo into the coat from shoulders to tail and down the legs, using the label amount and skipping the eyes and ears.
steps.expect: dirt lifts into light suds without stinging or strong perfume exposure.

steps.action: **Clean the face carefully.** Use a damp cloth around muzzle wrinkles, chin, and forehead rather than spraying the face.
steps.expect: the face is cleaner without water running into eyes or ears.

steps.action: **Rinse fully.** Rinse until water runs clear and the coat no longer feels slippery, checking belly, armpits, tail, and between toes.
steps.expect: no shampoo residue remains when you part the fur.

steps.action: **Dry in stages.** Squeeze water from the coat, towel dry, and use a cool or low dryer only if the dog tolerates the sound and heat.
steps.expect: the dog is damp or dry enough to stay warm and not drip across the floor.

steps.action: **Reward and reset.** Offer praise, treats, and a quiet place, then clean the tub and wash your hands.
steps.expect: the dog recovers calmly and the bathing area is safe again.

recipes.verification: The dog's coat is clean, fully rinsed, warm enough, and free of obvious shampoo residue, with eyes and ears not irritated.

recipes.title: bleed a radiator
recipes.name: bleed-a-radiator
recipes.goal: Trapped air is released from a hot-water radiator so it heats evenly top to bottom, and the boiler system pressure is restored to its normal cold reading afterwards.

steps.action: **Turn the heating off and let the system go cold.** Wait at least 30-60 min after shutoff. Bleeding a hot system sprays scalding water and the running pump drags air around the circuit so it never collects at the valve.
steps.expect: radiators cool to the touch, pump silent.

steps.action: **Note the boiler's cold pressure before starting.** Read the gauge. Typical sealed-system cold pressure is 1.0-1.5 bar.
steps.expect: a baseline reading written down or remembered.

steps.action: **Find the bleed valve.** It is at one top corner of the radiator: a small square-socket screw inside a round nut, sometimes under a plastic cap.
steps.expect: the key seats snugly on the square socket.

steps.action: **Open the valve a quarter to half turn counterclockwise.** Hold the cloth under the valve and the cup below that. Do not open more than one full turn; the screw can come all the way out and is miserable to reseat against escaping water.
steps.expect: a steady hiss of escaping air.

steps.action: **Wait through the hiss.** The hiss may run from a few seconds to a minute on a badly aired radiator.
steps.expect: hiss weakens, then water starts to sputter.

steps.action: **Close the valve when water runs in a steady dribble.** Sputtering means air is still mixed in; a solid dribble means the air is out. Turn clockwise until snug, not forced.
steps.expect: water flow stops completely; valve body dry after a wipe.

steps.action: **Repeat for other cold-topped radiators.** [BRANCH: one problem radiator → done after it | whole-system bleed → work from the lowest floor outward from the boiler, ending with the highest and farthest radiator, where air collects most]
steps.expect: every bled radiator ends on a steady dribble, valve closed.

steps.action: **Check and restore boiler pressure.** Bleeding removes water volume; the gauge will read lower than your baseline. On a sealed system, open the filling loop valves slowly until the gauge reaches 1.0-1.5 bar cold, then close both loop valves fully.
steps.expect: gauge steady in the green zone; filling loop closed and not hissing.

steps.action: **Run the heating and re-check.** Turn heating on, wait 20-30 min, feel each bled radiator top and bottom.
steps.expect: radiators hot across their full height, no gurgling, no drips at any bleed valve.

recipes.verification: With the heating running for 30 min, every treated radiator is hot over its entire surface, no bleed valve shows moisture, and the boiler gauge reads within its normal band (typically 1.0-1.5 bar cold, up to about 2 bar hot).

recipes.title: brush a dogs teeth
recipes.name: brush-a-dogs-teeth
recipes.goal: Clean a dog's outer tooth surfaces with pet-safe toothpaste while making the routine tolerable enough to repeat.

steps.action: **Let the dog taste the paste.** Offer a pea-sized amount from your finger or brush.
steps.expect: the dog sniffs, licks, or accepts the flavor without gagging.

steps.action: **Lift the lip, not the jaw.** Touch the muzzle and lift one side lip briefly while praising calm behavior.
steps.expect: the outer teeth and gumline are visible for a second or two.

steps.action: **Brush the front teeth.** Use small circles along the gumline on the outside of the incisors and canines.
steps.expect: paste spreads over the teeth and the dog stays relaxed enough for a short pass.

steps.action: **Move to cheek teeth.** Slide the brush under the cheek and brush the outside surfaces on each side; do not force the mouth open.
steps.expect: the back outer teeth get contact from the brush.

steps.action: **End with a reward.** Stop after 30 to 60 seconds at first, then praise and give water.
steps.expect: the dog disengages calmly and the brush can be cleaned.

recipes.verification: Pet toothpaste has contacted the outer gumline surfaces without distress, no painful mouth problem was ignored, and the dog accepts the routine better or at least no worse than before.

recipes.title: brush a long haired cat
recipes.name: brush-a-long-haired-cat
recipes.goal: Brush a long-haired cat to remove loose coat, prevent mats, and find skin problems without pulling painfully.

steps.action: **Start with calm contact.** Pet the cat in favorite areas and offer treats before brushing.
steps.expect: the cat stays relaxed or signals a clear limit.

steps.action: **Comb in sections.** Work from shoulders to tail, then chest, belly, armpits, and hind legs only as tolerated.
steps.expect: loose hair lifts out and the comb moves through small areas.

steps.action: **Support the skin.** Hold fur near the base while easing through tangles from the ends inward.
steps.expect: tangles loosen without yanking the skin.

steps.action: **Stop at tight mats.** Do not cut close mats with scissors; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* skin can tent into a mat and be cut accidentally.
steps.expect: dangerous mats are left for a groomer or vet.

steps.action: **Reward breaks.** Pause often and let the cat change position.
steps.expect: the session continues without biting, swatting, or escape panic.

steps.action: **Check skin and hygiene.** Look for fleas, dandruff, redness, lumps, fecal soiling, or painful areas.
steps.expect: grooming also becomes a health check.

recipes.verification: The coat has fewer loose hairs and surface tangles, the cat is not injured or distressed, and any tight mats or skin concerns are identified for professional care.

recipes.title: build a raised garden bed
recipes.name: build-a-raised-garden-bed
recipes.goal: Build a stable raised bed in a sunny, accessible spot and fill it with safe growing soil.

steps.action: **Choose and measure the site.** Pick a level area with 6 or more hours of sun for vegetables and leave paths wide enough for a wheelbarrow or child helper.
steps.expect: the bed footprint is marked and accessible.

steps.action: **Prepare the ground.** Remove rocks and aggressive weeds, then lay overlapping plain cardboard if building over lawn.
steps.expect: the base is flat and weed-suppressed.

steps.action: **Cut or arrange materials.** Use rot-resistant boards, kits, blocks, or untreated cedar; avoid railroad ties or unknown treated wood for food beds. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* saws and drills can injure hands and permanently cut materials, so clamp boards and confirm measurements before cutting.
steps.expect: pieces match the planned bed size.

steps.action: **Assemble the frame.** Fasten corners squarely with exterior screws or brackets, checking diagonals for alignment.
steps.expect: the frame sits solidly without wobbling.

steps.action: **Set the bed level.** Place the frame, shim low spots with soil or gravel, and confirm it does not rock.
steps.expect: water will not pool heavily at one end.

steps.action: **Fill in layers.** Add quality raised-bed mix or compost blended with mineral soil; avoid burying fresh manure or uncomposted woody chunks in the root zone.
steps.expect: soil is loose, moist, and a few inches below the rim.

steps.action: **Water and settle.** Soak the bed, top up low spots, and label the bed if multiple crops or kids will use it.
steps.expect: soil settles evenly and the bed is ready for planting.

recipes.verification: The bed is level, stable, filled with appropriate soil below the rim, drains after watering, and can be reached without stepping into the planting area.

recipes.title: build a trellis
recipes.name: build-a-trellis
recipes.goal: Build and install a sturdy garden trellis that supports climbing crops or vines without collapsing, shading the wrong plants, or damaging roots.

steps.action: **Match design to crop.** Choose a teepee, A-frame, panel, or vertical trellis based on crop weight and height.
steps.expect: the structure is sized for mature vines.

steps.action: **Place the trellis before roots spread.** Set it at planting time or while plants are still small.
steps.expect: supports do not crush established roots.

steps.action: **Anchor the main supports.** Drive stakes or posts deep enough to resist wind and wet soil movement.
steps.expect: uprights stand firm when pushed.

steps.action: **Add crosspieces or mesh.** Attach horizontal supports, netting, twine, or panel securely with plant-safe spacing.
steps.expect: vines have reachable places to climb.

steps.action: **Check sun and access.** Position tall trellises on the north or shaded side of lower crops where appropriate.
steps.expect: the trellis will not unnecessarily shade sun-loving plants.

steps.action: **Guide young vines.** Tie stems loosely or weave tendrils onto the support without tightening around growth.
steps.expect: plants begin climbing in the intended direction.

steps.action: **Reinforce under load.** Add guy lines, extra stakes, or braces before heavy fruit develops.
steps.expect: the trellis remains stable as weight increases.

steps.action: **Inspect through the season.** Tighten loose fasteners and cut off ties that begin to constrict stems.
steps.expect: support remains secure without girdling plants.

recipes.verification: The trellis is anchored, sized for the crop, provides climbable surfaces, does not block necessary access, and supports vines without tight ties or leaning.

recipes.title: build an emergency supply kit
recipes.name: build-an-emergency-supply-kit
recipes.goal: A household emergency kit is assembled, stored accessibly, and scheduled for regular checks.

steps.action: **Choose kit locations.** Pick accessible spots for home, vehicle, and go-bag if needed.
steps.expect: supplies can be reached in darkness or evacuation.

steps.action: **Store water.** Add enough sealed water for drinking and basic hygiene for each person and pet.
steps.expect: water is present and dated.

steps.action: **Add shelf-stable food.** Pack ready-to-eat food, manual can opener, and food for dietary needs.
steps.expect: meals can be eaten without power.

steps.action: **Pack light and power.** Add flashlights, headlamps, batteries, power banks, and charging cables.
steps.expect: the kit works during an outage.

steps.action: **Add first aid and hygiene.** Include first aid supplies, masks, sanitizer, soap, wipes, menstrual products, diapers, and trash bags.
steps.expect: basic care and sanitation are covered.

steps.action: **Add medications and medical items.** Include copies of prescriptions, spare glasses, hearing aid batteries, and essential supplies where safe and legal.
steps.expect: critical health needs are represented.

steps.action: **Add communication documents.** Include emergency contacts, paper maps, copies of key documents, and cash in small bills.
steps.expect: information and payment still work offline.

steps.action: **Add warmth and tools.** Pack blankets, clothing, gloves, whistle, wrench or pliers, duct tape, and multipurpose tool.
steps.expect: basic shelter and utility tasks are possible.

steps.action: **Label and date items.** Mark expiration dates and create a replacement calendar.
steps.expect: stale supplies are easy to find.

steps.action: **Review every six months.** Replace expired food, water, batteries, medications, and outgrown clothing.
steps.expect: the kit stays usable.

recipes.verification: The kit contains water, food, light, power, first aid, hygiene, medications or medical supports, documents, cash, warmth, and tools, and each expiring item has a review date.

recipes.title: catch a spider humanely
recipes.name: catch-a-spider-humanely
recipes.goal: A house spider relocated outdoors alive via the glass-and-card method, with the household's arachnophobe calmed and the whole operation over in two minutes.

steps.action: **Track, don't chase.** Keep the spider in sight while you fetch the tools; a spider lost behind the bookcase is tonight's suspense. Announce your plan to any distressed observers — narration genuinely calms rooms.
steps.expect: spider stationary or slow, tools in hand, audience upgraded from screaming to supervising.

steps.action: **Place the glass over the spider in one smooth motion.** Approach slowly from behind its heading, then decisive placement, rim flush with the surface. Speed matters more at the end than the start; spiders bolt at looming shadows.
steps.expect: spider enclosed under the glass, unharmed, probably annoyed.

steps.action: **Slide the card under the rim.** Ease one edge of the card under the glass, sliding slowly along the surface; the spider will step onto the card or up the glass wall as it advances.
steps.expect: the card fully underlapping the rim, forming a sealed floor; the spider contained between glass and card.

steps.action: **Invert and carry with the card held firmly against the rim.** One hand pressing card to glass, walk to the door or window. Ceiling captures: same moves overhead with the glass pushed up and the card slid across — brace your forearm.
steps.expect: a portable spider observatory; children en route may inspect the passenger through the glass, which converts fear to biology in one generation.

steps.action: **Release properly: outside, at ground level, near shelter.** A bush, woodpile, or wall base a few meters from the door; tip the glass and let it walk off — don't fling.
steps.expect: spider off into cover; glass and card retrieved.

steps.action: **Debrief and wash the glass.** A rinse for the glass (or dishwasher), and the traditional closing statement to the household that the spider "was more scared of you."
steps.expect: equipment restored to drinking duty, household peace restored to baseline.

recipes.verification: The spider left alive under its own power near outdoor shelter, no legs were harmed in the containment, the glass is washed, and the household's next spider encounter starts from a calmer baseline — the recipe's compounding return.

recipes.title: caulk a bathtub
recipes.name: caulk-a-bathtub
recipes.goal: The joint between bathtub and wall is sealed with a clean mildew-resistant bead that cures before water reaches it.

steps.action: **Confirm the joint is dry.** Stop using the tub and wipe the seam before starting.
steps.expect: no water beads appear when pressed with a dry towel.

steps.action: **Remove old caulk.** Cut along both edges, peel strips away, and scrape residue without gouging tile or tub.
steps.expect: the joint is open with loose caulk removed.

steps.action: **Clean the seam.** Vacuum debris, wipe with rubbing alcohol, and let it evaporate.
steps.expect: surfaces look dull-clean and dry.

steps.action: **Mask straight edges.** Apply painter's tape parallel to the joint, leaving the desired bead width exposed.
steps.expect: two clean tape lines frame the gap.

steps.action: **Cut the nozzle small.** Slice the caulk tip at a 45-degree angle slightly smaller than the joint.
steps.expect: test squeeze makes a controlled bead.

steps.action: **Apply a continuous bead.** Push or pull the gun steadily along the seam, filling the gap without stopping mid-run.
steps.expect: wet caulk bridges both surfaces with no hollow breaks.

steps.action: **Tool the bead promptly.** Smooth once with a damp finger or caulk tool, pressing caulk into the joint.
steps.expect: bead is concave or gently rounded and fully adhered.

steps.action: **Remove tape before skin forms.** Pull tape back over itself at a low angle. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cured silicone is difficult to correct cleanly; inspect the line before it sets.
steps.expect: edges are sharp and excess caulk leaves with the tape.

steps.action: **Clean small smears now.** Wipe stray wet caulk with the solvent recommended on the tube.
steps.expect: surrounding tile and tub are free of haze or blobs.

steps.action: **Let it cure before water.** Keep the seam dry for the label cure time, often 24 hours.
steps.expect: the tub remains unused until the caulk is firm and non-tacky.

recipes.verification: The cured bead is continuous, adhered to both sides of the joint, non-tacky, and has had no water exposure before the stated cure time.

recipes.title: change a lightbulb
recipes.name: change-a-lightbulb
recipes.goal: A dead bulb is replaced with a working one of the correct type, and the fixture lights normally.

steps.action: **Turn the light switch off and, ideally, leave the bulb to cool for a few minutes.** Incandescent/halogen bulbs burn skin for minutes after going out.
steps.expect: switch down/off; bulb cool to a near-touch hover.

steps.action: **Set up stable access.** Place the step stool directly under the fixture, all feet flat.
steps.expect: you can reach the bulb with your elbow bent, not at full stretch.

steps.action: **Remove any cover/shade.** Most twist counterclockwise or unclip; support it with one hand as you release it.
steps.expect: cover off and set somewhere it can't be stepped on.

steps.action: **Remove the old bulb.** Screw base: turn counterclockwise until free. Bayonet: push in gently, quarter-turn counterclockwise, release. Pin (halogen capsule): pull straight out — with a cloth, not bare fingers.
steps.expect: bulb comes free without forcing; socket looks clean and intact.

steps.action: **Check the new bulb against the old one.** Same base and size; wattage ≤ the fixture's marked max (LED equivalents are far under old limits).
steps.expect: bases match; markings within limits.

steps.action: **Install the new bulb.** Screw: clockwise until snug — *snug, not cranked*; over-tightening breaks bulbs and seizes bases. Bayonet: push, quarter-turn clockwise. Halogen pins: push straight in via cloth (skin oil shortens halogen life).
steps.expect: bulb seats firmly with light resistance at the end.

steps.action: **Switch on and observe.**
steps.expect: the bulb lights steadily. If not, F1.

steps.action: **Replace the cover, climb down, and dispose of the old bulb properly.** Incandescent: household trash (wrapped). CFL: hazardous/recycling point — contains mercury. LED: e-waste recycling where available.
steps.expect: fixture reassembled; old bulb routed to the right waste stream.

recipes.verification: The fixture lights steadily from its own switch, the cover is back on, the ladder is put away, and the old bulb is in the correct waste stream — trash, or hazardous collection for CFLs.

recipes.title: change an air filter
recipes.name: change-an-air-filter
recipes.goal: An HVAC or furnace air filter is found, sized correctly, installed in the right airflow direction, and scheduled for regular replacement.

steps.action: **Turn the system off.** Set the thermostat mode to off before opening any grille or slot.
steps.expect: fan noise stops or does not start during the change.

steps.action: **Find the filter location.** Check return air grilles, the furnace side slot, or the air handler cabinet.
steps.expect: a rectangular filter or empty filter track is visible.

steps.action: **Read the old filter size.** Look at the printed edge for dimensions such as 16x20x1.
steps.expect: replacement size matches all three numbers.

steps.action: **Note the airflow arrow.** Identify which way air moves, usually from room return toward furnace or blower.
steps.expect: arrow direction is understood before removal.

steps.action: **Remove the old filter carefully.** Slide it out without shaking dust into the room.
steps.expect: dirty side faces the incoming air side.

steps.action: **Inspect the slot.** Look for collapse, heavy dust, or a missing cover.
steps.expect: filter track is clear and ready.

steps.action: **Insert the new filter.** Align the printed arrow with airflow toward the equipment.
steps.expect: filter slides fully into place without bending.

steps.action: **Close the grille or cover.** Latch panels and covers securely.
steps.expect: no open gap lets air bypass the filter.

steps.action: **Restart the system.** Turn the thermostat back to the previous mode.
steps.expect: air flows normally with no rattling filter noise.

steps.action: **Record the cadence.** Write the date on the filter edge or set a reminder for 1-3 months, adjusted for pets, smoke, dust, or allergy needs.
steps.expect: next replacement date is visible or scheduled.

recipes.verification: The new filter is fully seated with its airflow arrow pointing toward the HVAC equipment, the cover is closed, and a replacement date is recorded.

recipes.title: change device batteries
recipes.name: change-device-batteries
recipes.goal: A battery-powered device (remote, clock, toy, smoke detector, scale) is back in service with fresh batteries of the right type, correctly oriented, and the dead cells routed to battery recycling — not the trash.

steps.action: **Open the compartment.** Sliding latch, press-tab, or small screws (keep screws in a cup, not on the carpet). Smoke detectors: twist the unit off its base plate first.
steps.expect: compartment open without forced plastic; screws accounted for.

steps.action: **Read the compartment before removing anything.** Battery type and the +/− orientation diagram are molded/printed inside; note (or photo) the current orientation — especially in multi-cell devices where cells alternate direction.
steps.expect: you know the type, count, and the orientation pattern.

steps.action: **Remove the old batteries.** Pry from the negative (spring) end; check for corrosion — white/green crust means leakage. [BRANCH: clean → continue | crusted → F2 before inserting anything]
steps.expect: old cells out and set *apart* from the fresh ones (mixing them up is the classic self-own).

steps.action: **Insert fresh batteries per the diagram.** Flat end (−) against the spring, matching every cell to its molded symbol; never mix old-with-new or different brands/chemistries in one device (the weakest cell drains and leaks).
steps.expect: each cell seated firmly, orientation matching the diagram cell-by-cell.

steps.action: **Test before closing.** Power the device — remote blinks, clock ticks, detector's test button sounds. No response → recheck orientation (the #1 cause) before doubting the batteries.
steps.expect: the device demonstrably works.

steps.action: **Close up and route the dead cells.** Compartment latched/screwed, device remounted (smoke detector twisted back until it clicks); old batteries into the recycling jar — terminals of 9V and coin cells taped (they short against each other and other metals; this is a real fire path in a jar of loose cells).
steps.expect: device in service, dead cells taped-and-jarred, nothing in the household trash.

recipes.verification: The device works (tested before closing), orientation matched the diagram, no old/new or mixed-chemistry combinations were installed, the compartment is properly closed, and the dead cells sit taped in the recycling jar rather than the bin.

recipes.title: childproof a fireplace
recipes.name: childproof-a-fireplace
recipes.goal: Reduce a child's access to fireplace heat, tools, ash, sharp edges, and ignition controls while keeping fire safety equipment ready.

steps.action: **Cool and clear the area.** Confirm there are no hot embers, hot glass, or active flames before working.
steps.expect: the fireplace can be touched safely around the exterior.

steps.action: **Choose a stable barrier.** Select a gate or guard that surrounds the hearth and cannot be tipped by a child.
steps.expect: the barrier fits the fireplace width and floor layout.

steps.action: **Install the gate or guard.** Anchor or brace it according to the product instructions.
steps.expect: the guard stays in place when pushed lightly.

steps.action: **Block hot access.** Keep the guard closed whenever the fireplace is hot or cooling. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* burns can happen in seconds, so no child should have access to hot glass, metal, or embers.
steps.expect: a child cannot reach the hot surface from the room side.

steps.action: **Use the screen correctly.** Close the mesh or glass screen when the fireplace is in use.
steps.expect: sparks and rolling logs are contained behind the screen.

steps.action: **Move tools away.** Store pokers, shovels, brushes, and log holders behind a locked barrier or in an adult-only area.
steps.expect: sharp and heavy tools are out of reach.

steps.action: **Secure ignition items.** Move matches, lighters, starter blocks, remote controls, and gas keys to locked storage.
steps.expect: a child cannot start the fireplace.

steps.action: **Check hearth edges.** Add edge padding only if it is heat-safe and placed where it will not contact hot surfaces.
steps.expect: sharp corners are reduced without creating a fire hazard.

steps.action: **Test alarms.** Press the test button on smoke and carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping and living areas.
steps.expect: alarms sound and batteries or power are working.

steps.action: **Set the house rule.** Teach that the fireplace area is adult-only and supervise even when barriers are installed.
steps.expect: the barrier is treated as backup, not the only protection.

recipes.verification: A child cannot reach the fireplace opening, hot glass, tools, fuel, ignition controls, or sharp hearth edges, and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms pass their tests.

recipes.title: childproof a room
recipes.name: childproof-a-room
recipes.goal: One room is made safe for an unsupervised-for-seconds crawler or toddler: nothing tippable, strangling, shocking, sharp at head height, or swallowable is reachable, verified from the child's own eye level.

steps.action: **Survey at crawl level.** Get on hands and knees and cross the whole room slowly. Note everything graspable, every cord, every gap, every glinting small object under furniture. This one step finds hazards no standing walkthrough does.
steps.expect: a written list of 10+ items; fewer usually means the survey was done standing.

steps.action: **Clear the floor and low zone of swallowables.** Anything that fits through the toilet-paper tube is a choking hazard: coins, button batteries, magnets, pen caps, beads. Button batteries and high-powered magnets are medical emergencies if swallowed, so hunt for them specifically (remotes, tea lights, greeting cards).
steps.expect: nothing tube-sized reachable below 1 m; remote battery doors taped or screwed shut.

steps.action: **Anchor every tippable furniture piece.** Dressers, bookcases, and shelving over 60 cm tall get anti-tip straps into wall studs (find studs with the stud finder; drywall anchors alone will not hold a climbing child). TVs strap to the wall or their stand. Test by pulling hard on an open top drawer. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* tip-over injuries are a leading cause of child furniture deaths; do not defer this step to "when they start climbing", they start without notice.
steps.expect: no piece moves when an adult pulls on it; straps taut, screwed into studs.

steps.action: **Cover outlets and manage cords.** Replace reachable outlet plates with sliding self-closing covers (loose plastic plug caps are themselves a choking hazard once pried out). Shorten or hide appliance cords; a dangling kettle or iron cord pulls the appliance down.
steps.expect: no open outlet slots; no cord hangs within reach or crosses the floor as a pull-line.

steps.action: **Eliminate blind and curtain cord loops.** Looped window-covering cords are a strangulation hazard. Fit cordless blinds, or cut loops and fit cleats above 1.5 m and wind cords fully after every use.
steps.expect: no loop of any cord hangs below 1.5 m anywhere in the room.

steps.action: **Guard corners and edges.** Fit corner guards on hard furniture at toddler head height (roughly 40-90 cm): coffee tables, hearths, low sills. Glass-topped tables either get guards and a stability check or leave the room.
steps.expect: running a hand along low furniture finds no bare hard corner.

steps.action: **Lock away chemicals, medicines, and sharp items.** Anything in this room that cleans, medicates, or cuts goes above 1.5 m or behind a latched door. Handbags and visitor coats (which carry pills and coins) get a designated high hook.
steps.expect: latches click shut on their own; the visitor-bag hook is in use.

steps.action: **Secure doors, windows, and heavy swinging things.** Window stops limit opening to under 10 cm on above-ground floors; door pinch guards on hinge sides where fingers get crushed; doorstops without removable rubber caps.
steps.expect: windows open only to the stop; doors cannot slam a finger flat at the hinge.

steps.action: **Re-survey at crawl level.** Repeat step 1 against the original list.
steps.expect: every listed item resolved; nothing new found.

recipes.verification: An adult at crawl level can cross the room and find no reachable swallowable, no unanchored tippable furniture (pull-test passes), no open outlet, no cord loop below 1.5 m, no bare hard corner at head height, and all latched storage self-closes.

recipes.title: choose pet insurance
recipes.name: choose-pet-insurance
recipes.goal: Choose a pet insurance policy or decide not to buy one after comparing coverage, exclusions, costs, and the pet's likely needs.

steps.action: **List the pet's risk profile.** Write age, breed risks, chronic conditions, lifestyle, and prior diagnoses.
steps.expect: pre-existing conditions and likely exclusions are visible before comparing prices.

steps.action: **Compare policy types.** Separate accident-only, accident-and-illness, wellness add-ons, reimbursement rates, deductibles, annual limits, and waiting periods.
steps.expect: plans are compared on the same terms.

steps.action: **Read exclusions.** Check bilateral conditions, dental disease, hereditary conditions, exam fees, prescriptions, rehab, and alternative care.
steps.expect: you know what the policy will not pay for.

steps.action: **Estimate real cost.** Calculate monthly premium, deductible, copay share, annual limit, and expected premium increases.
steps.expect: the plan's best and worst routine cost is understandable.

steps.action: **Check claim logistics.** Confirm vet choice, reimbursement timing, records required, and cancellation rules.
steps.expect: you know how money returns after a vet bill.

steps.action: **Choose or decline deliberately.** Pick the best fit or keep a dedicated emergency fund instead; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not enroll until policy documents match the quote and pet details.
steps.expect: the decision is documented with policy name, price, and reasons.

recipes.verification: A selected policy or no-insurance decision is supported by written comparisons of premium, deductible, reimbursement, annual limit, waiting periods, exclusions, and emergency budget.

recipes.title: clean a bathroom
recipes.name: clean-a-bathroom
recipes.goal: The bathroom's four zones — toilet, sink/mirror, shower/tub, floor — are cleaned and disinfected in the right order, with chemicals never mixed and the room left dry and aired.

steps.action: **Ventilate, glove up, and clear the surfaces.** Window open/fan on; bottles, toothbrushes, and towels off the counters; bath mat out (to `daily/home/do-the-laundry`).
steps.expect: airflow moving, surfaces bare, gloves on.

steps.action: **Start the soak timers first.** Toilet-bowl cleaner around the bowl's rim, brush later; spray the shower/tub surfaces with cleaner. Dwell time is the active ingredient — let both sit while you do the sink zone.
steps.expect: two zones soaking; you're not scrubbing anything yet.

steps.action: **Clean the sink zone.** Spray and wipe the basin, taps, and counter (cloths A); scrub the drain collar and the tap bases where grime rings.
steps.expect: basin and taps gleaming; hair and paste residue gone.

steps.action: **Do the mirror and glass.** Glass cleaner, wipe in one direction with a dry-side finish.
steps.expect: streak-free at an angle to the light.

steps.action: **Return to the shower/tub and scrub with the grain of the grime.** Walls top-down, fixtures, then the basin/tray; a brush for grout lines; rinse everything down with the shower head.
steps.expect: soap scum yields after its soak; water sheets off surfaces rather than beading on film.

steps.action: **Finish the toilet — outside first, bowl last, its own cloths (B).** Wipe tank, lid, seat top, seat underside, rim exterior, base and the floor around it; then brush the soaked bowl under the rim and flush with the lid down.
steps.expect: every touched surface disinfected; bowl clean under the rim; brush rinsed in the flush and drip-dried in its holder.

steps.action: **Floor last, door-to-corner logic reversed.** Sweep/vacuum hair first, then mop from the far corner to the door (`daily/home/sweep-and-mop-a-floor`), including behind the toilet base.
steps.expect: floor uniformly clean, you exiting over wet floor's edge, not across it.

steps.action: **Reset the room.** Cloths to a hot wash (A and B still segregated), gloves washed then off, hands washed anyway; fresh towels/mat back once the floor dries; fan running until the room is dry.
steps.expect: dry, aired, restocked bathroom; cleaning kit stored with the toilet cloths marked.

recipes.verification: All four zones pass a look-and-touch check (no film, no rings, no hair), the bowl is clean under the rim, cloths A/B went to the wash still segregated, no two chemicals ever shared a surface or a session, and the room is drying with air moving.

recipes.title: clean a burnt pot
recipes.name: clean-a-burnt-pot
recipes.goal: Burnt food is loosened from a pot without gouging the surface or damaging nonstick coating.

steps.action: **Let the pot cool.** Move it off heat and wait until it is warm, not hot.
steps.expect: water added to the pot will not flash into steam.

steps.action: **Soak with soap.** Add warm water and a few drops of dish soap, then soak 15 to 30 minutes.
steps.expect: loose food softens and the water darkens.

steps.action: **Scrape gently.** Use a wooden spoon, nylon scraper, or plastic spatula to lift softened bits.
steps.expect: some residue releases without scratching.

steps.action: **Boil baking soda water.** Add enough water to cover the burnt area and 2 tablespoons baking soda, then simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
steps.expect: residue bubbles and loosens from the base.

steps.action: **Cool and scrub.** Turn off heat, let the pot cool, then scrub with a non-scratch pad. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* metal tools can permanently scratch nonstick and enamel, so do not use steel wool or a knife on coated surfaces.
steps.expect: burnt film thins or lifts.

steps.action: **Use vinegar for stainless.** For stainless steel only, add a splash of vinegar after baking soda treatment, then rinse well.
steps.expect: mineral haze and brown stains lighten.

steps.action: **Wash normally.** Finish with dish soap, rinse, and dry.
steps.expect: pot feels smooth and has no cleaner residue.

recipes.verification: The cooking surface is smooth to the touch after washing, with no loose burnt food, no gritty cleaner, and no new scratches from metal tools.

recipes.title: clean a coffee grinder
recipes.name: clean-a-coffee-grinder
recipes.goal: Clean coffee oils and grounds from a blade or burr grinder without wetting the motor or leaving cleaner in the grind path.

steps.action: **Unplug the grinder.** Remove the plug before touching blades, burrs, or the hopper.
steps.expect: the grinder cannot start accidentally.

steps.action: **Empty loose beans and grounds.** Pour out beans and remove the grounds bin or catcher.
steps.expect: the grind chamber is mostly clear.

steps.action: **Remove safe parts.** [BRANCH: burr grinder | blade grinder] take out removable burrs or hopper parts only if the manual allows it; leave fixed parts in place.
steps.expect: cleanable areas are exposed without forcing parts.

steps.action: **Brush burrs or blades.** Use a dry brush to loosen packed grounds from teeth, blades, corners, and chute openings.
steps.expect: dry grounds fall free.

steps.action: **Vacuum loose debris.** Use a small vacuum nozzle near the chamber without touching delicate parts.
steps.expect: loosened grounds are removed.

steps.action: **Use tablets or rice if suitable.** Run grinder-cleaning tablets, or a small amount of dry uncooked rice only if the manufacturer allows it.
steps.expect: oils and fine residue are absorbed into the powder.

steps.action: **Discard the cleaning powder.** Empty the bin and brush away remaining tablet or rice dust.
steps.expect: no visible cleaning residue remains in the chamber.

steps.action: **Wipe removable plastic parts.** Use a barely damp cloth on removable bins or lids, then dry fully before reassembly.
steps.expect: parts are clean and completely dry.

steps.action: **Keep the motor dry.** Never rinse, soak, or spray the motor base. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* water inside the motor can ruin the grinder or create shock risk, so clean it only with a dry or barely damp cloth.
steps.expect: the base exterior is clean and dry.

steps.action: **Reassemble and purge.** Put parts back, plug in, and grind a small spoonful of beans to clear residue.
steps.expect: the grinder runs normally and first purge grounds can be discarded.

recipes.verification: The grinder is dry, reassembled, free of visible grounds or cleaning residue, and runs normally during a short purge grind.

recipes.title: clean a coffee maker
recipes.name: clean-a-coffee-maker
recipes.goal: Clean and descale a drip coffee maker so water flows normally and brewed coffee no longer tastes stale or sour.

steps.action: **Empty removable parts.** Remove old grounds, paper filters, and leftover coffee from the basket and carafe.
steps.expect: no loose grounds or stale coffee remain.

steps.action: **Wash the basket and carafe.** Clean them with warm soapy water, rinse well, and set them back in place.
steps.expect: oily residue and coffee film are gone.

steps.action: **Mix descaling solution.** Fill the reservoir with equal parts white vinegar and water unless the manual says otherwise.
steps.expect: the reservoir is filled below its max line.

steps.action: **Run half a brew cycle.** Start brewing until about half the solution has moved into the carafe, then stop the machine.
steps.expect: hot vinegar-water is in the carafe and the reservoir is partly full.

steps.action: **Let it soak.** Wait 20 minutes so scale loosens inside the heater and lines.
steps.expect: the machine sits idle with solution in the system.

steps.action: **Finish the brew cycle.** Turn the machine back on and let the rest of the solution run through.
steps.expect: the reservoir is empty and the carafe contains used solution.

steps.action: **Discard and rinse.** Pour the hot solution down the sink and rinse the carafe.
steps.expect: no vinegar-water remains in the carafe.

steps.action: **Run first rinse cycle.** Fill the reservoir with plain water and brew a full cycle.
steps.expect: the water smells less like vinegar.

steps.action: **Run second rinse cycle.** Repeat with another full reservoir of plain water.
steps.expect: the brewed water smells neutral.

steps.action: **Dry and reassemble.** Wipe the exterior, leave the lid open briefly, and return clean parts.
steps.expect: the machine is clean, dry at the edges, and ready to brew.

recipes.verification: A full plain-water brew cycle runs through at normal speed and the output has no vinegar smell.

recipes.title: clean a dishwasher filter
recipes.name: clean-a-dishwasher-filter
recipes.goal: The dishwasher filter is free of food debris, the spray arms are unobstructed, and the filter is locked back in place.

steps.action: **Remove the lower rack.** Slide it out and set it on a towel or stable floor space.
steps.expect: the filter assembly at the bottom is easy to reach.

steps.action: **Unlock the cylindrical filter.** Turn the handle in the marked direction and lift it out. [BRANCH: twist-lock | lift-out] follow the printed arrows or manual for your model.
steps.expect: the main filter is loose without force.

steps.action: **Lift the flat filter plate.** Remove the lower mesh or plate if your model has one.
steps.expect: the sump area is visible.

steps.action: **Rinse debris away.** Rinse food from the filters under warm water, keeping solids out of the sink drain.
steps.expect: the mesh openings are visible.

steps.action: **Brush the mesh gently.** Use dish soap and a soft brush for greasy film, then rinse clean.
steps.expect: water flows through the filter without pooling.

steps.action: **Check the sump and spray arms.** Wipe loose debris from the bottom and clear spray arm holes with a toothpick if blocked.
steps.expect: spray arms spin freely and holes are open.

steps.action: **Refit and lock the filter.** Replace the flat plate, seat the cylinder, and twist until it locks.
steps.expect: the filter does not lift out when tugged lightly.

steps.action: **Run a rinse cycle.** Start a short rinse with no dishes and listen for abnormal grinding.
steps.expect: water drains cleanly and no error appears.

recipes.verification: The filter is clean, locked, spray arms spin freely, and a rinse cycle drains without grit or error.

recipes.title: clean a dishwasher
recipes.name: clean-a-dishwasher
recipes.goal: A dishwasher is cleaned so the filter, spray arms, seals, and interior can move water effectively without odor or grit redepositing on dishes.

steps.action: **Empty and inspect.** Remove dishes and pull out the lower rack
steps.expect: the tub bottom, filter area, and spray arm are visible.

steps.action: **Remove the filter.** Unlock and lift out the filter assembly according to the manual [BRANCH: removable filter | self-cleaning filter]
steps.expect: the filter comes free without force or cracking.

steps.action: **Wash the filter.** Rinse under warm water and brush away grease, labels, seeds, and grit
steps.expect: water passes through the mesh easily.

steps.action: **Clear the sump area.** Wipe food pieces from the filter well without pushing debris deeper
steps.expect: no loose scraps remain around the drain opening.

steps.action: **Check spray-arm jets.** Spin each arm and clear blocked holes with a toothpick or small wire
steps.expect: arms rotate freely and jets are open.

steps.action: **Wipe seals and edges.** Clean the door gasket, detergent cup area, and lower door lip with a damp cloth
steps.expect: black residue, crumbs, and slime are removed.

steps.action: **Run a cleaning cycle.** Place a cup of vinegar upright on the top rack or use dishwasher cleaner, then run a hot empty cycle
steps.expect: steam and hot water circulate through an otherwise empty machine.

steps.action: **Reassemble and air out.** Reinstall the filter, slide racks back, and leave the door cracked after the cycle
steps.expect: parts sit flush and odor is reduced.

recipes.verification: After cleaning, the filter is locked in place, spray arms spin freely by hand, and a hot empty cycle completes without odor, leaks, or standing debris.

recipes.title: clean a dogs ears
recipes.name: clean-a-dogs-ears
recipes.goal: Clean a dog's outer ear canal with a vet-approved ear cleaner without pushing debris deeper or hurting the ear.

steps.action: **Inspect both ears.** Look and smell before adding cleaner.
steps.expect: you can tell whether wax is mild or whether pain, odor, redness, or discharge suggests a vet visit.

steps.action: **Position calmly.** Hold the ear flap upright and steady the head without pinning the dog hard.
steps.expect: the ear canal opening is visible and the dog can still breathe and stand normally.

steps.action: **Fill with cleaner.** Place the bottle tip near the opening without touching skin and squeeze in the label amount.
steps.expect: cleaner pools in the canal entrance.

steps.action: **Massage the base.** Rub the base of the ear for 20 to 30 seconds.
steps.expect: a soft squishing sound indicates cleaner is loosening wax.

steps.action: **Let the dog shake.** Step back with the towel ready.
steps.expect: loosened fluid and debris move outward.

steps.action: **Wipe only what you can see.** Use cotton pads on the ear flap and canal entrance; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not push tools down the canal where they can damage the eardrum.
steps.expect: visible wax is removed without scraping or pain.

recipes.verification: Visible outer-ear wax is reduced, no tool entered deep into the canal, and the dog has no increased pain, head tilt, discharge, or persistent shaking afterward.

recipes.title: clean a dryer vent
recipes.name: clean-a-dryer-vent
recipes.goal: The dryer vent path is cleared from the machine outlet to the outside flap so air can move freely and lint cannot build into a fire hazard.

steps.action: **Power down the dryer.** Unplug the dryer, or switch off the dedicated breaker if the plug is inaccessible.
steps.expect: the dryer display is dark and the drum will not start.

steps.action: **Pull the dryer forward carefully.** Move it just far enough to reach the duct, keeping hoses, cords, and any gas line unstressed.
steps.expect: the vent connection is visible and nothing is kinked or taut.

steps.action: **Disconnect the duct.** Loosen the clamp or tape at the dryer outlet and at the wall if needed. [BRANCH: flexible duct | rigid duct] flex duct may compress, rigid duct may need a gentler straight pull.
steps.expect: the duct end is open and lint is visible.

steps.action: **Vacuum the dryer outlet.** Vacuum loose lint from the dryer port without pushing debris deeper into the machine.
steps.expect: the outlet lip and first few inches are clear.

steps.action: **Brush the duct.** Run the vent brush through the duct in short passes, then vacuum the loosened lint.
steps.expect: the brush comes back with less lint on each pass.

steps.action: **Check the outside flap.** Go outside, clear lint from the hood, and make sure the flap opens and closes freely.
steps.expect: the flap moves without sticking and the hood is not blocked by nests, leaves, or screens packed with lint.

steps.action: **Reconnect with a smooth path.** Refit the duct, tighten clamps, replace damaged foil tape, and keep the run as short and uncrushed as possible.
steps.expect: both ends are secure and the duct has no sharp folds.

steps.action: **Run an air test.** Restore power and run air-only for two minutes while watching the outside flap.
steps.expect: strong airflow opens the flap and no lint smell, rattle, or leak appears indoors.

recipes.verification: With the dryer running on air-only, the outside flap opens strongly and no duct joint leaks lint or warm air indoors.

recipes.title: clean a grill
recipes.name: clean-a-grill
recipes.goal: A grill is burned off, brushed, degreased, emptied, inspected, and lightly seasoned so it is clean enough for the next cook and safer from flare-ups.

steps.action: **Heat the grill for burn-off.** Run burners high or let charcoal heat the grates for 10-15 minutes with lid closed.
steps.expect: stuck food turns brittle and ashy.

steps.action: **Brush hot grates safely.** Wearing gloves, brush grates front to back while hot.
steps.expect: carbon flakes off and grate bars look exposed.

steps.action: **Shut down and cool partly.** Turn off gas or close vents, then wait until parts are warm but not dangerously hot.
steps.expect: cleaning can continue without burn risk.

steps.action: **Remove grates and flavorizer parts.** Lift out grates, plates, or charcoal grate according to the grill type.
steps.expect: grease tray and firebox are visible.

steps.action: **Scrape the firebox.** Push loose carbon and grease toward the tray or ash catcher.
steps.expect: heavy buildup is removed from the bottom.

steps.action: **Degrease removable parts.** [BRANCH: greasy grates | lightly soiled grates] wash greasy parts with hot soapy water; wipe light soil with damp cloths.
steps.expect: sticky grease is gone.

steps.action: **Empty the tray or ash catcher.** Remove cool grease liners or fully cold ash and dispose safely.
steps.expect: flare-up fuel is removed.

steps.action: **Dry and season the grates.** Dry parts fully, reinstall, then wipe grates with a thin film of cooking oil.
steps.expect: grates are clean, dry, and lightly protected.

recipes.verification: The grates are brushed and lightly oiled, grease tray or ash catcher is empty, loose carbon is removed, and no soap, bristles, or heavy grease remain.

recipes.title: clean a keyboard
recipes.name: clean-a-keyboard
recipes.goal: A keyboard is powered off, cleared of crumbs and dust, wiped or keycap-cleaned, and fully dried before reconnecting.

steps.action: **Power off and disconnect.** Shut down or unplug the keyboard, and remove batteries if wireless.
steps.expect: no keypresses register while cleaning.

steps.action: **Photograph the layout.** Take a picture before removing any keycaps.
steps.expect: key positions can be restored correctly.

steps.action: **Shake out loose debris.** Hold the keyboard upside down over a trash bin and tap gently.
steps.expect: crumbs and grit fall out without tools.

steps.action: **Blow between keys.** Use short bursts of air at an angle, not straight down.
steps.expect: dust moves out from under keys instead of deeper inside.

steps.action: **Clean key surfaces.** Wipe keys with a cloth lightly dampened with alcohol.
steps.expect: oils lift and no liquid drips between keys.

steps.action: **Remove keycaps only if appropriate.** [BRANCH: removable keycaps | laptop or fragile keys] pull removable caps carefully; wipe around fixed keys with swabs.
steps.expect: access improves without breaking scissor switches.

steps.action: **Treat sticky keys.** Work a barely damp alcohol swab around the sticky key edge, pressing and releasing it repeatedly.
steps.expect: key movement improves without flooding the switch.

steps.action: **Dry before reconnecting.** Let everything air-dry fully, reinstall keycaps from the photo, then reconnect power.
steps.expect: keys are dry, seated, and responsive.

recipes.verification: The keyboard is dry, debris-free, all removed keycaps are back in place, and every commonly used key registers normally after reconnecting.

recipes.title: clean a mattress
recipes.name: clean-a-mattress
recipes.goal: The mattress surface is vacuumed, spot-treated, deodorized, dried fully, and protected without soaking the interior.

steps.action: **Strip and inspect the bed.** Remove sheets, protector, and pillows, then check the label for cleaning limits.
steps.expect: bare mattress and known fabric warnings.

steps.action: **Vacuum slowly.** Use the upholstery tool over the top, sides, seams, and tufting in overlapping passes.
steps.expect: dust, hair, and grit are removed from seams.

steps.action: **Spot-treat stains lightly.** Blot with a barely damp cloth and a small amount of cleaner. [BRANCH: protein stain | general soil] use enzyme cleaner for protein, mild soap for general soil.
steps.expect: stain transfers to the cloth without spreading.

steps.action: **Rinse the spot with a damp cloth.** Blot with plain cold water, then press dry towels over the area.
steps.expect: no visible suds and the spot feels only slightly damp.

steps.action: **Deodorize with baking soda.** Sprinkle a thin, even layer over the surface and brush it lightly into fabric texture.
steps.expect: powder sits dry across the mattress, not clumped into wet patches.

steps.action: **Let it sit.** Leave baking soda for at least 1 hour, longer for odor, with a fan or open window.
steps.expect: the room smells fresher and the surface stays dry.

steps.action: **Vacuum again thoroughly.** Remove all baking soda from the top, sides, and seams.
steps.expect: no powder puffs when you pat the mattress.

steps.action: **Dry fully before covering.** Leave the mattress uncovered until cool dampness is gone, then add a clean protector and bedding.
steps.expect: fabric feels dry and bedding is not trapping moisture.

steps.action: **Rotate if the mattress allows it.** Turn head-to-foot unless the maker says not to.
steps.expect: wear pressure is redistributed.

recipes.verification: The mattress is dry, vacuumed clean, has no loose baking soda, stains are reduced without wet patches, and a clean protector is installed.

recipes.title: clean a refrigerator
recipes.name: clean-a-refrigerator
recipes.goal: The refrigerator is emptied, purged of expired stowaways, wiped clean shelf by shelf, and restocked in the zone layout that keeps food safe, with the cold chain respected throughout.

steps.action: **Empty one zone at a time, triaging as you go.** Everything out to the counter in its shelf-groups; meat, dairy, and delicate perishables into the cool bag. Each item passes the gate: expired, unrecognizable, or three-olives-left → bin or compost; keeper → its counter group.
steps.expect: an emptying fridge and an honest bin bag; the `daily/food/read-food-labels` date rules (use-by vs best-before) doing the judging.

steps.action: **Remove shelves and drawers that lift out, and wash them at the sink.** Warm soapy water; glass shelves get five minutes to reach room temperature first, because hot water on cold glass is a cracking risk.
steps.expect: shelves and crisper drawers washed, rinsed, and drying on a towel.

steps.action: **Wipe the interior top-to-bottom.** Walls, fixed shelves, door seals (fold the gasket open gently; crumbs live in its pleats), and the drip channel at the back if visible. Baking-soda water handles odors; nothing harsh, it is a food box.
steps.expect: interior surfaces clean and rinsed of any cleaner taste; the gasket pleats grit-free.

steps.action: **Deal with the drain hole and any ice or puddle.** The small drain at the back wall clogs with crumbs and creates the mystery puddle; a cotton swab or the fridge's little cleaning tool clears it.
steps.expect: drain open, puddle history explained.

steps.action: **Reassemble and restock by zones.** Shelves back dry; then the layout that `embodied/kitchen/store-groceries` teaches: raw meat lowest (drip containment), dairy and eggs mid, ready-to-eat up, vegetables in crispers, condiments in the door, older stock in front of newer.
steps.expect: everything back with a logic a stranger could read, the cool-bag items first.

steps.action: **Finish the outside and the metadata.** Handle and door front wiped (the handle is the kitchen's most-touched surface), the temperature checked at 4 °C or below, and a dated note or phone reminder for the next round in two to three months.
steps.expect: clean touchpoints, verified temperature, next cycle scheduled.

recipes.verification: The interior is clean including gasket and drain, nothing expired went back in, zones match the layout, the temperature reads at or below 4 °C, the handle is clean, and the next session has a date.

recipes.title: clean a washing machine filter
recipes.name: clean-a-washing-machine-filter
recipes.goal: The washer pump filter is drained, cleared of lint and objects, and resealed so the machine can drain properly.

steps.action: **Switch the washer off.** Unplug it or turn it off at the breaker if the outlet is hidden.
steps.expect: the panel is dark and the drum is stopped.

steps.action: **Open the pump access flap.** Locate the small lower door and place towels under it. [BRANCH: drain hose present | no drain hose] use the hose first if present, otherwise drain slowly through the filter cap.
steps.expect: the filter cap and drain path are visible.

steps.action: **Drain the trapped water.** Pull the small hose plug or crack the cap slowly into the tray, emptying the tray as needed.
steps.expect: water flow slows to drips.

steps.action: **Remove the filter cap.** Turn the cap counterclockwise while keeping towels in place.
steps.expect: the filter comes free without a rush of water.

steps.action: **Clear debris.** Remove coins, hair pins, lint, buttons, and fabric scraps from the filter and cavity.
steps.expect: the impeller area is visible and clear.

steps.action: **Brush and inspect the seal.** Rinse the cap, brush lint from threads, and check the rubber seal for grit.
steps.expect: the seal sits clean and undamaged.

steps.action: **Reseal the filter.** Thread the cap by hand until snug, close the drain hose plug, and wipe the area dry.
steps.expect: the cap is straight and the flap closes.

steps.action: **Run a leak check.** Restore power and run a short drain or rinse cycle while watching the flap area.
steps.expect: the pump drains and no water appears at the cap.

recipes.verification: A short drain or rinse cycle completes with no pump error and no leakage from the filter access area.

recipes.title: clean a washing machine
recipes.name: clean-a-washing-machine
recipes.goal: The washing machine is free of detergent scum, mold, and drain debris: the drum smells of nothing, the drawer and gasket are visibly clean, and future laundry stops coming out with a musty edge.

steps.action: **Run an empty hot maintenance cycle.** No laundry, hottest cycle available (60-90 °C), with either a commercial machine cleaner (follow its packet) or ~250 ml white vinegar in the drum. Modern cool-wash habits are exactly why machines grow smelly biofilm; the hot empty cycle is the cure.
steps.expect: cycle completes; water may come out visibly grey the first time.

steps.action: **Remove the detergent drawer completely and scrub it.** Most drawers release via a tab or by pressing the softener siphon while pulling. Soak in hot water, scrub every channel with the toothbrush; the fabric-softener compartment hides the worst gunk under its siphon cap, so pop the cap off.
steps.expect: drawer white/clear again, siphon cap clean inside.

steps.action: **Scrub the drawer housing in the machine.** The roof of the drawer slot grows black mold where the water jets enter. Toothbrush and rag as far as fingers reach.
steps.expect: no black or slimy residue on a rag wiped through the slot.

steps.action: **Wipe the door gasket, inside the fold.** [BRANCH: front-loader → pull back each fold of the rubber gasket and wipe the hidden channel all the way around, where water, lint, coins, and black mold collect | top-loader → wipe under the top rim and around the agitator instead] Stubborn black spots: rag soaked in diluted bleach laid on the spot for an hour, then rinse. Note that established black mold stains the rubber permanently even once the growth is dead.
steps.expect: the gasket channel wipes clean; trapped debris (hair pins, coins, socks) recovered.

steps.action: **Clean the drain-pump filter (front-loaders).** Behind the small hatch at the bottom front: lay down the towel, hold the shallow tray under the hatch, open the little drain hose or unscrew the filter slowly; up to a litre of standing water comes out, so drain in stages. Remove lint, coins, and debris from the filter, rinse, screw back firmly.
steps.expect: filter clear; cap screwed tight (a loose cap leaks on the next wash).

steps.action: **Wipe the drum, door glass, and exterior.** Vinegar-damp rag over the drum interior and the inside of the door glass, where scum films build.
steps.expect: glass squeak-clean, drum smells neutral or faintly of vinegar.

steps.action: **Run a short empty rinse cycle.** Flushes loosened residue and any bleach or vinegar traces before the next real load.
steps.expect: rinse water runs clean.

steps.action: **Leave the door and drawer ajar.** From now on, after every wash: door open a hand's width, drawer cracked open, gasket wiped dry weekly. A machine that dries out between loads cannot grow mold; this habit matters more than any deep clean.
steps.expect: interior dry to the touch within a day.

recipes.verification: With the cycle history done: the drum and door glass are film-free, the drawer and its housing show no residue, the gasket fold wipes clean and dry, the pump filter is empty and tight, and a sniff of the closed drum after ten minutes yields no musty smell.

recipes.title: clean an oven
recipes.name: clean-an-oven
recipes.goal: An oven with baked-on grime is cleaned by paste-and-patience chemistry (or its own self-clean cycle, used correctly), racks included, and finishes ready to bake without smoking.

steps.action: **Empty the oven and start the racks soaking.** Racks, trays, and thermometer out; racks into a tub or sink of hot water with a good squirt of dish soap (the bathtub lined with a towel works for full-size racks).
steps.expect: bare oven; racks beginning their long soak.

steps.action: **Scrape the loose debris first.** Plastic scraper on carbonized lumps and flakes; sweep or vacuum the crumbs out of the box. Dry removal first makes the paste's job possible.
steps.expect: only bonded grime remains, no loose char.

steps.action: **Paste the interior.** Baking soda mixed with just enough water to make a spreadable paste; coat the walls, floor, and door interior, avoiding heating elements and the door gasket.
steps.expect: a white paste layer over every grimy surface, elements bare.

steps.action: **Wait hours; overnight is the real recipe.** The paste browns as it lifts grease. Do something else; the chemistry does not need supervision.
steps.expect: hours later, a browned, dried paste layer.

steps.action: **Wipe out, spray, wipe again.** Damp cloth removes the paste and the grime it captured; stubborn patches get a vinegar spray onto the soda residue (it foams, loosening the last film) and another wipe. The scraper returns for any softened islands.
steps.expect: bare enamel emerging; cloths rinsed repeatedly; the vinegar pass leaving no white haze.

steps.action: **Scrub and rinse the racks.** After their hours of soaking, a scouring pad takes the softened grime; rinse and dry.
steps.expect: racks clean enough to touch without gray fingers.

steps.action: **Do the door glass and reassemble.** Paste or a glass-safe scrub on the door window (a razor scraper held flat works on glass only, carefully); wipe the gasket gently with plain water. Racks back in, and run the empty oven at medium heat for ten minutes with the fan on or a window open.
steps.expect: clear-ish glass, everything reassembled, and the burn-off run producing faint steam but no billowing smoke.

recipes.verification: The interior wipes clean with no paste haze, racks slide in clean, the door shows its food through the glass again, the gasket is intact and untouched by harsh chemistry, and the ten-minute burn-off runs without smoke.

recipes.title: clean and store leather boots
recipes.name: clean-and-store-leather-boots
recipes.goal: Leather boots are cleaned, conditioned if appropriate, dried, and stored so the leather keeps its shape.

steps.action: **Remove laces and loose dirt.** Take out laces and brush mud from seams, welt, and sole edges.
steps.expect: dry debris is gone before moisture is added.

steps.action: **Wipe with a damp cloth.** Clean the leather surface using light pressure.
steps.expect: surface grime transfers to the cloth.

steps.action: **Use leather cleaner sparingly.** Apply a small amount to the cloth and work on one panel at a time.
steps.expect: leather looks clean without becoming soaked.

steps.action: **Wipe residue away.** Use a clean damp cloth to remove cleaner from stitching and creases.
steps.expect: no soap film remains.

steps.action: **Dry slowly.** Stuff boots with paper or insert boot trees and air dry at room temperature.
steps.expect: boots hold shape while moisture leaves.

steps.action: **Condition lightly.** Rub a thin layer of leather conditioner into dry leather if it feels dry or stiff.
steps.expect: leather looks even and supple, not greasy.

steps.action: **Buff the surface.** Use a clean cloth or horsehair brush after conditioner absorbs.
steps.expect: excess product is removed and the finish is even.

steps.action: **Store upright.** Keep boots in a cool dry place with trees or paper support.
steps.expect: shafts and toe boxes do not collapse.

recipes.verification: Boots are dry to the touch, clean at seams and soles, lightly conditioned without residue, and standing in shape in breathable storage.

recipes.title: clean grout
recipes.name: clean-grout
recipes.goal: Grout lines are cleaned without damaging tile, and the surface is evaluated for sealing or mold treatment.

steps.action: **Identify dirt versus mold.** Dirt is usually tan or gray and wipes lighter; mold is spotty black, green, or pink and returns in damp zones.
steps.expect: the stain type has a likely cause.

steps.action: **Dry sweep or vacuum.** Remove loose grit before wet cleaning.
steps.expect: grout lines are free of sand that could scratch tile.

steps.action: **Mix a mild paste.** Combine baking soda with enough water to make a spreadable paste.
steps.expect: paste clings to vertical grout without running.

steps.action: **Apply and dwell.** Press paste into grout lines and let it sit 10-15 minutes.
steps.expect: paste remains damp and begins lifting surface soil.

steps.action: **Brush along the grout.** Scrub in short strokes along the line, then cross it lightly at stubborn spots.
steps.expect: soil releases into the paste without tile scratching.

steps.action: **Boost if needed.** Mist hydrogen peroxide onto the paste for stained grout, avoiding incompatible stone surfaces.
steps.expect: mild bubbling or lightening appears at stains.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly.** Wipe with clean water until no gritty cleaner remains.
steps.expect: tile feels smooth and grout lines are visible.

steps.action: **Dry completely.** Use towels and ventilation to remove moisture.
steps.expect: grout color can be judged without wet darkening.

steps.action: **Seal porous grout.** Apply grout sealer after cleaning and full drying if water soaks in quickly.
steps.expect: sealer wets the grout line, then excess is wiped from tile.
