steps.action: **Set a moisture habit.** Squeegee showers or dry splash zones after use.
steps.expect: cleaned grout stays dry longer between uses.

recipes.verification: After drying, grout lines are visibly cleaner, free of gritty residue, and any porous cleaned grout is sealed or scheduled for sealing.

recipes.title: clean out gutters
recipes.name: clean-out-gutters
recipes.goal: Remove leaves, grit, and blockages from gutters and downspouts so roof water drains away from the house.

steps.action: **Inspect from the ground.** Look for sagging gutters, wasp nests, power lines, and downspout outlets before setting the ladder.
steps.expect: hazards and work zones are identified.

steps.action: **Set the ladder safely.** Place it on firm level ground at a proper angle, extending above the gutter if using an extension ladder. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* ladder falls can cause serious injury, so move the ladder often instead of overreaching.
steps.expect: the ladder does not shift when weighted.

steps.action: **Scoop debris by hand or tool.** Wear gloves and remove leaves, seed pods, roof grit, and twigs into a bucket or tarp.
steps.expect: the gutter channel is visible for several feet at a time.

steps.action: **Flush toward the downspout.** Use a hose to rinse remaining dirt and watch water flow.
steps.expect: water moves freely toward the outlet.

steps.action: **Clear downspout clogs.** [BRANCH: water drains | water backs up] if water backs up, flush from the bottom or use a plumber's snake gently.
steps.expect: water exits at the downspout base.

steps.action: **Check drainage away from the foundation.** Reattach elbows or extensions so water discharges several feet away from the house.
steps.expect: runoff points away from basement walls, paths, and garden beds.

steps.action: **Clean the work area.** Bag debris, rinse siding splashes, and store the ladder flat or secured.
steps.expect: walkways are not slippery and tools are put away.

recipes.verification: Water poured or hosed into each gutter flows to the downspout and away from the foundation, with no standing debris, visible overflow, or unsafe debris left on walkways.

recipes.title: clean suede
recipes.name: clean-suede
recipes.goal: Dry surface dirt and light marks are removed from suede while preserving the nap.

steps.action: **Dry completely.** Let wet suede air dry away from heat before brushing.
steps.expect: the nap feels dry and no damp dark patches remain.

steps.action: **Stuff for support.** Place paper inside shoes or under bags to support the surface.
steps.expect: suede does not collapse under brushing.

steps.action: **Brush with the nap.** Use a suede brush in one direction to lift loose dirt.
steps.expect: dust and flattened fibers loosen.

steps.action: **Erase small marks.** Rub a suede eraser gently over scuffs or dry stains.
steps.expect: marks lighten and eraser crumbs appear.

steps.action: **Brush crumbs away.** Brush again to remove eraser debris and reset nap direction.
steps.expect: surface texture looks even.

steps.action: **Treat edges carefully.** Use light strokes around seams, welts, and trim.
steps.expect: dirt lifts without fraying stitching.

steps.action: **Let rest and reassess.** Leave the item for 10 minutes, then inspect in natural light.
steps.expect: cleaned and uncleaned areas blend.

recipes.verification: The suede is dry, the nap is raised evenly, loose dirt is gone, and no new water rings or pale rubbed patches are visible.

recipes.title: clean up a pet accident
recipes.name: clean-up-a-pet-accident
recipes.goal: Remove pet urine, feces, or vomit from a household surface with odor control and hygiene while watching for signs of illness.

steps.action: **Check the pet first.** Look for repeated vomiting, blood, straining, weakness, or toxin exposure before focusing on the mess.
steps.expect: urgent health concerns are either absent or routed to a vet.

steps.action: **Remove solids.** Wearing gloves, pick up feces or vomit without rubbing it into the surface.
steps.expect: bulk material is bagged and the stain is not spread.

steps.action: **Blot liquids.** Press towels into urine or liquid vomit until no more transfers easily.
steps.expect: moisture is reduced before cleaner is added.

steps.action: **Apply enzymatic cleaner.** Saturate the affected area according to the label and allow the required contact time.
steps.expect: odor-causing residue is being broken down rather than perfumed.

steps.action: **Dry and block access.** Let the area air-dry fully and keep pets away until dry.
steps.expect: the pet cannot lick cleaner or reuse the damp spot.

steps.action: **Wash hands and tools.** Launder washable items and dispose of waste securely.
steps.expect: hygiene is restored and supplies are not cross-contaminated.

recipes.verification: The visible mess is removed, the area smells neutral after drying, the pet is blocked from cleaner exposure, and any repeated or abnormal symptoms have a veterinary plan.

recipes.title: clean window blinds
recipes.name: clean-window-blinds
recipes.goal: Window blinds are dusted on both faces, spot-cleaned or washed as appropriate, and dried before being raised or stacked.

steps.action: **Lower the blinds fully.** Close the slats in one direction without forcing the tilt wand or cord.
steps.expect: one continuous face is exposed.

steps.action: **Dust the closed face.** Wipe from top to bottom with a microfiber cloth or vacuum brush.
steps.expect: loose dust is removed instead of falling onto already-clean slats.

steps.action: **Reverse the slats.** Tilt them closed the other way.
steps.expect: the opposite dusty edges face you.

steps.action: **Dust the second face.** Repeat the top-to-bottom pass.
steps.expect: both sides look evenly clean in daylight.

steps.action: **Use the sock trick for grime.** Put a damp sock over your hand, pinch one slat at a time, and slide from center to edge.
steps.expect: finger oils and gray lines transfer to the sock.

steps.action: **Deep-wash removable vinyl or aluminum slats if needed.** [BRANCH: removable washable blinds | wood or fabric] wash washable blinds in a tub with mild soap; spot-clean wood or fabric only.
steps.expect: sticky residue lifts without soaking delicate material.

steps.action: **Rinse and dry.** Wipe soap with clean water, then towel each wet slat before raising.
steps.expect: no drips, no soap film, and cords stay dry.

steps.action: **Reset the blinds.** Raise or open them only after the slats are dry.
steps.expect: slats stack cleanly without trapping moisture.

recipes.verification: With blinds lowered and tilted both ways, slats show no dust lines, sticky spots, drips, or damp stacking.

recipes.title: clean windows
recipes.name: clean-windows
recipes.goal: Windows cleaned streak-free on both reachable sides, frames and sills included, without anyone leaning out of anything to reach the unreachable.

steps.action: **Start dry: vacuum or brush the frames, tracks, and sill.** Wet cleaning over grit makes mud and scratches glass. Sliding-window tracks give up their debris to a vacuum crevice tool or a dry brush.
steps.expect: dry dust and dead flies gone before any liquid appears.

steps.action: **Wash the frames and sill first with the separate rag.** Frames drip dirty water; doing them after the glass undoes the glass.
steps.expect: clean frames, with drips landing on still-dirty glass where they cost nothing.

steps.action: **Apply cleaner to the glass modestly.** A few sprays, or a wrung-out cloth of the vinegar mix; pooling liquid is what runs into streaks and frame corners.
steps.expect: a thin even film across the pane.

steps.action: **Squeegee top-to-bottom in overlapping strokes, wiping the blade between strokes.** No squeegee: wipe in one deliberate pattern (say, horizontal), then buff with the dry second cloth in the perpendicular pattern. The two-direction trick makes any remaining streak announce which pass caused it.
steps.expect: glass clearing behind each stroke; blade or cloth wiped each pass.

steps.action: **Detail the edges and corners.** A dry cloth-wrapped finger along the pane's perimeter picks up the liquid the main strokes pushed there.
steps.expect: no drying pool at any corner.

steps.action: **Repeat on the other side where reachable, then step back in raking light.** Streaks hide straight-on and show at an angle.
steps.expect: both reachable faces clear; any streak found gets one buff with the dry cloth.

recipes.verification: Glass reads clear in raking light from both reachable sides, corners are dry, frames and tracks hold no mud lines, and no part of the job involved a body further out of a window than a forearm.

recipes.title: clear a clogged showerhead
recipes.name: clear-a-clogged-showerhead
recipes.goal: A showerhead with weak or uneven spray is cleared of mineral buildup and reinstalled without leaks.

steps.action: **Turn the shower off.** Confirm both hot and cold flow are fully closed.
steps.expect: no water drips from the head except residual drops.

steps.action: **Bag-soak the head.** Fill a bag with enough vinegar to cover the spray face, secure it around the showerhead, and wait 30 to 60 minutes.
steps.expect: mineral deposits soften.

steps.action: **Remove the bag carefully.** Hold the bag upright and pour the vinegar down the drain.
steps.expect: vinegar does not splash onto eyes or stone surfaces.

steps.action: **Brush the jets.** Scrub rubber nozzles and holes with a toothbrush, flicking soft nozzles if present.
steps.expect: loosened scale falls away.

steps.action: **Flush the spray.** Run warm water for 30 seconds.
steps.expect: debris rinses out and spray pattern improves.

steps.action: **Remove the head if still clogged.** [BRANCH: hand-loose | wrench-needed] unscrew by hand or use a cloth-wrapped wrench on the flats.
steps.expect: the head separates from the shower arm.

steps.action: **Backflush and soak again.** Rinse water backward through the inlet, remove loose screen debris, and soak the head again if needed.
steps.expect: water passes through more freely.

steps.action: **Refit the head.** Replace the washer if damaged, wrap shower-arm threads with plumber's tape only if required, and screw the head on straight.
steps.expect: the connection is snug and aligned.

steps.action: **Spray test.** Turn the shower on gradually and inspect the joint and spray face.
steps.expect: spray is even and no water leaks at the threads.

recipes.verification: With the shower running, most jets spray evenly, the pattern is centered, and the showerhead connection stays dry for one minute.

recipes.title: clear a dishwasher that wont drain
recipes.name: clear-a-dishwasher-that-wont-drain
recipes.goal: A dishwasher with standing water is cleared of common filter, sump, air-gap, or drain-hose blockages.

steps.action: **Stop power at the control.** Cancel the cycle and turn the dishwasher off before reaching inside.
steps.expect: spray arms and pump are inactive.

steps.action: **Remove standing water.** Scoop water into a bucket and sponge the bottom.
steps.expect: the filter and sump area are visible.

steps.action: **Clean the filter.** Remove the lower rack and filter assembly, then rinse debris from the screen.
steps.expect: water can pass through the filter mesh.

steps.action: **Check the sump.** Remove food, glass, labels, or bones from the sump without forcing pump parts.
steps.expect: the sump is clear of visible debris.

steps.action: **Inspect the air gap.** If present, remove the cap and clear buildup from the air-gap body.
steps.expect: the air gap is open and not packed with debris.

steps.action: **Check the disposal inlet.** Confirm the garbage disposal knockout plug is removed if the dishwasher hose was recently connected.
steps.expect: the hose path into the disposal is open.

steps.action: **Run a drain test.** Reassemble the filter, restore normal control power, and start a drain or cancel cycle.
steps.expect: water pumps out through the sink drain path.

steps.action: **Watch for leaks.** Check under the sink and around the dishwasher toe area during the drain.
steps.expect: hoses and connections stay dry.

recipes.verification: After a drain cycle, the dishwasher tub has no standing water above the sump screen and all visible drain connections remain dry.

recipes.title: clip a dogs nails
recipes.name: clip-a-dogs-nails
recipes.goal: Trim a dog's nails in small, controlled cuts while avoiding the quick, keeping the dog calm, and knowing when to stop or get professional help.

steps.action: **Set up a calm station.** Place the dog on a non-slip floor or low table, keep treats within reach, and let the dog sniff the clippers before you begin.
steps.expect: the dog notices the tools but can still take a treat and remain near you.

steps.action: **Hold one paw lightly.** Lift a paw only as high as the dog's body comfortably allows, supporting the toe rather than squeezing the whole foot.
steps.expect: the paw is steady enough to see the nail, and the dog is not twisting hard away.

steps.action: **Find the safe cutting zone.** On light nails, look for the pink quick and plan to cut below it; on dark nails, trim only the very tip and watch for a pale chalky center.
steps.expect: you have chosen a shallow cut that removes nail without approaching live tissue.

steps.action: **Make the first small cut.** Clip straight across the tip with one decisive squeeze, not a crushing half-cut. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cutting into the quick causes pain and bleeding, so confirm the cut is tiny before closing the clippers.
steps.expect: a small nail tip comes off and the dog stays recoverable with praise or a treat.

steps.action: **Check the nail face.** Stop cutting that nail if you see a darker dot, a moist center, or the dog suddenly pulls from pain.
steps.expect: each nail ends with a dry cut surface and no blood.

steps.action: **Reward between nails.** Give a treat, release the paw for a moment, and reset the light grip before moving to the next toe.
steps.expect: the dog learns that each nail is brief and followed by something good.

steps.action: **Handle dewclaws separately.** Look for the thumb-like nail higher on the leg and trim it only if it is long enough to curl or snag.
steps.expect: no hidden nail is left growing into the skin.

steps.action: **Stop early if needed.** [BRANCH: finish all nails | do one paw today] choose the shorter session if the dog stiffens, pants hard, growls, or stops taking treats.
steps.expect: the session ends before fear escalates.

steps.action: **Smooth and clean up.** Use a grinder or nail file only if the dog tolerates it, then collect nail pieces and put clippers away.
steps.expect: the dog can walk normally and the trimmed nails do not scrape sharply.

recipes.verification: All trimmed nails are shorter without bleeding, the dog is walking normally, and no nail has a sharp snag or curl toward the pad.

recipes.title: collect rainwater
recipes.name: collect-rainwater
recipes.goal: Collect roof runoff in a rain barrel or cistern for garden watering while managing overflow, mosquito prevention, and local rules.

steps.action: **Confirm rules and use.** Check that rainwater collection is allowed and plan to use it for ornamental or soil-level garden watering.
steps.expect: collection is permitted for the intended use.

steps.action: **Choose a safe location.** Place the barrel near a downspout on compact level ground that can hold heavy water weight.
steps.expect: the barrel will not tip or sink.

steps.action: **Build a stable base.** Set concrete blocks, pavers, or a stand level under the barrel.
steps.expect: the spigot is accessible and the barrel sits solidly.

steps.action: **Fit the inlet screen.** Keep all openings covered with fine mesh or a sealed lid.
steps.expect: leaves and mosquitoes cannot enter easily.

steps.action: **Connect the downspout.** Cut or redirect the downspout into the barrel or diverter following the kit instructions.
steps.expect: roof runoff enters the screened inlet.

steps.action: **Set overflow away from the foundation.** Attach an overflow hose that drains to a safe area or existing storm path.
steps.expect: excess water will not pool near the building.

steps.action: **Test with hose water or rain.** Run water into the inlet and watch the spigot, seams, base, and overflow.
steps.expect: water flows in and out without leaks or tipping.

steps.action: **Use and maintain the barrel.** Water at soil level, clean screens, drain before freezing, and empty stagnant water if unused.
steps.expect: stored water remains contained and usable for the garden.

recipes.verification: The rain barrel is legal for the location, sits level on a stable base, has screened openings, directs overflow away from the foundation, and releases water through the spigot.

recipes.title: compost kitchen scraps
recipes.name: compost-kitchen-scraps
recipes.goal: Kitchen scraps are composted with the right balance of greens, browns, air, and moisture, while meat, dairy, and pest-attracting materials are kept out.

steps.action: **Separate compostable scraps.** Collect fruit and vegetable peels, coffee grounds, tea leaves, eggshells, and small plant trimmings.
steps.expect: acceptable greens are separated from trash.

steps.action: **Skip problem foods.** Keep meat, fish, dairy, grease, oily food, pet waste, and glossy packaging out.
steps.expect: the bucket contains no strong pest attractors.

steps.action: **Chop large pieces.** Cut corn cobs, melon rinds, and stems smaller before adding.
steps.expect: scraps have more surface area and break down faster.

steps.action: **Add browns with every deposit.** Cover kitchen greens with dry leaves, shredded paper, or cardboard.
steps.expect: scraps are hidden and the pile does not smell like garbage.

steps.action: **Balance moisture.** [BRANCH: too dry | too wet] add water if dusty; add browns if slimy.
steps.expect: compost feels like a wrung-out sponge.

steps.action: **Turn for air.** Mix the pile weekly or when it smells sour.
steps.expect: fresh air reaches the center and heat or decomposition resumes.

steps.action: **Keep the lid and site managed.** Close the bin, bury fresh scraps, and wipe the countertop container.
steps.expect: fewer flies, rodents, and kitchen odors.

steps.action: **Harvest when ready.** Use compost when it is dark, crumbly, earthy, and original scraps are no longer recognizable.
steps.expect: finished compost smells like soil, not food.

recipes.verification: New kitchen scraps are covered with browns, the pile is moist but not slimy, excluded foods are absent, and finished material is dark, crumbly, and earthy.

recipes.title: crate train a puppy
recipes.name: crate-train-a-puppy
recipes.goal: Teach a puppy to rest calmly in a crate that is safe, comfortable, and associated with predictable good things.

steps.action: **Set up the crate safely.** Remove collars or dangling tags, add washable bedding, and place the crate away from heat vents, cords, and direct sun.
steps.expect: the puppy can enter without snagging or overheating.

steps.action: **Build curiosity with the door open.** Toss treats inside and let the puppy walk in and out freely.
steps.expect: the puppy enters voluntarily at least once.

steps.action: **Feed near or inside the crate.** Move meals gradually from the doorway to the back of the crate.
steps.expect: the puppy eats without bracing or backing away.

steps.action: **Close the door briefly.** Close it while the puppy chews or eats, then open it before distress escalates.
steps.expect: the puppy notices the door but can stay engaged.

steps.action: **Add short absences.** Step away for 30 seconds, return calmly, and release during a quiet moment.
steps.expect: the puppy learns quiet behavior opens the door.

steps.action: **Extend time after needs are met.** [BRANCH: sleepy puppy | restless puppy] crate after potty and play for naps, or shorten the session if the puppy is not ready.
steps.expect: the puppy settles or at least remains recoverable.

steps.action: **Use a consistent cue.** Say the same cue, reward entry, and keep departures low-key.
steps.expect: the puppy starts entering on cue.

steps.action: **Keep nights practical.** Place the crate close enough to hear potty needs and take young puppies out calmly when needed.
steps.expect: nighttime crying is interpreted as either adjustment or potty need.

recipes.verification: The puppy enters the crate willingly, can stay with the door closed for an age-appropriate short period after potty and exercise, and leaves calmly when released.

recipes.title: darn a hole in a sock
recipes.name: darn-a-hole-in-a-sock
recipes.goal: A sock hole is reinforced with woven thread so the patch is smooth enough to wear and strong enough for laundering.

steps.action: **Inspect the hole.** Trim loose lint but leave sound loops around the edge.
steps.expect: the weak area and solid fabric boundary are visible.

steps.action: **Place the form inside.** Stretch the sock lightly over a darning egg or rounded object.
steps.expect: the hole lies flat without being stretched wide.

steps.action: **Thread the needle.** Use yarn close to the sock thickness and knot only if the inside lump will not bother you.
steps.expect: needle passes through fabric without forcing.

steps.action: **Anchor beside the hole.** Make small running stitches in solid fabric 1/4 inch from the edge.
steps.expect: thread is secured outside the weak area.

steps.action: **Lay warp threads.** Stitch parallel strands across the hole, catching solid fabric on both sides.
steps.expect: the opening is bridged by evenly spaced threads.

steps.action: **Weave cross threads.** Turn the sock and weave over-under through the first strands.
steps.expect: a small woven patch fills the hole.

steps.action: **Secure the end.** Stitch several tiny backstitches in solid fabric and trim excess thread.
steps.expect: no loose thread tails snag inside the sock.

steps.action: **Check the inside.** Remove the form and feel the patch with fingertips.
steps.expect: the repair is flat enough to wear comfortably.

recipes.verification: The hole is fully covered by woven thread, the surrounding fabric is not puckered, and the inside patch feels flat under light finger pressure.

recipes.title: deadhead flowers
recipes.name: deadhead-flowers
recipes.goal: Remove spent flowers at the correct point so plants look tidy, direct energy away from seed production, and may bloom again.

steps.action: **Identify spent blooms.** Look for faded petals, browning heads, or seed pods forming after flowers finish.
steps.expect: only finished flowers are targeted.

steps.action: **Find the next cut point.** Trace the flower stem to the first healthy leaf, bud, branching point, or basal foliage.
steps.expect: cuts will not leave long bare stems.

steps.action: **Use clean sharp snips.** Cut just above the chosen leaf or bud without crushing the stem.
steps.expect: the cut is neat and angled slightly away from buds.

steps.action: **Pinch soft annuals.** For tender stems such as petunias or marigolds, pinch spent blooms with fingertips if easier.
steps.expect: the old flower and seed base are removed.

steps.action: **Leave useful seed heads.** Skip flowers you want for seed, bird food, winter interest, or self-sowing.
steps.expect: selected heads remain on the plant.

steps.action: **Remove diseased material.** Put mildewed or spotted blooms in trash rather than compost.
steps.expect: disease pressure is not spread through compost.

steps.action: **Water or feed if needed.** After heavy deadheading, water dry plants and fertilize repeat bloomers only as appropriate.
steps.expect: plants have resources for new buds.

steps.action: **Repeat during bloom season.** Check weekly for new spent flowers.
steps.expect: the display stays tidy and rebloomers keep producing buds.

recipes.verification: Spent flowers and seed bases are removed to appropriate leaf or bud points, desired seed heads are intentionally left, and the plant has no crushed stems or diseased debris left beneath it.

recipes.title: deal with fleas on a pet
recipes.name: deal-with-fleas-on-a-pet
recipes.goal: Reduce fleas on a pet and in the home using species-safe treatment, cleaning, and veterinary guidance when infestation or illness is present.

steps.action: **Confirm fleas.** Part the coat near the neck, tail base, and belly, looking for moving fleas or black flea dirt that reddens when wet.
steps.expect: evidence of fleas is found or another skin problem is suspected.

steps.action: **Choose a species-safe product.** Read the label for species, weight, age, dose, and repeat interval; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never put dog-only permethrin products on cats.
steps.expect: the treatment matches the pet exactly.

steps.action: **Apply or give the treatment as labeled.** Follow the product directions and prevent licking or contact between pets until dry if topical.
steps.expect: the pet receives the full correct dose without cross-exposure.

steps.action: **Clean the environment.** Wash bedding on hot if fabric allows and vacuum carpets, cracks, furniture, and sleeping areas.
steps.expect: eggs, larvae, and flea dirt are physically reduced.

steps.action: **Repeat cleaning and prevention.** Vacuum frequently and maintain the product schedule for all household pets.
steps.expect: new flea sightings decline over several weeks.

steps.action: **Watch health signs.** Check for pale gums, weakness, skin infection, hair loss, tapeworm segments, or severe itching.
steps.expect: illness triggers veterinary care instead of more home treatment.

recipes.verification: The pet has received a correct species-safe flea treatment, bedding and floors have been cleaned, all household pets are accounted for, and flea sightings decrease without signs of illness.

recipes.title: deal with garden pests naturally
recipes.name: deal-with-garden-pests-naturally
recipes.goal: Reduce garden pest damage using identification, monitoring, barriers, hand removal, plant health, and least-toxic controls before stronger interventions.

steps.action: **Identify the pest and damage.** Look for insects, eggs, frass, chewed edges, stippling, slime trails, or webbing before acting.
steps.expect: the likely pest and affected plants are named.

steps.action: **Decide whether action is needed.** Compare damage to plant vigor, crop stage, and predator presence.
steps.expect: minor damage is monitored and serious damage is targeted.

steps.action: **Remove pests by hand.** Pick large caterpillars, beetles, and eggs into soapy water, or prune heavily infested shoots.
steps.expect: visible pest numbers drop immediately.

steps.action: **Use water and barriers.** Blast aphids with water, install row cover, collars, netting, or copper barriers where suited.
steps.expect: new damage slows without spraying.

steps.action: **Improve growing conditions.** Water consistently, mulch, thin crowded plants, and remove diseased debris.
steps.expect: plants recover with better airflow and less stress.

steps.action: **Invite beneficial insects.** Keep flowering herbs and small blooms nearby and avoid broad-spectrum insecticides.
steps.expect: lady beetles, lacewings, hoverflies, wasps, or spiders are not harmed.

steps.action: **Apply least-toxic products only if needed.** Use insecticidal soap, horticultural oil, Bt, or iron phosphate according to the label and pest type.
steps.expect: the treatment matches the pest and avoids open flowers when possible.

steps.action: **Recheck after several days.** Inspect the same leaves and new growth to confirm damage is slowing.
steps.expect: pest activity is reduced or the plan is adjusted.

recipes.verification: The pest is identified, plant damage is no longer increasing rapidly, chosen controls match the pest, and pollinators or beneficial insects are not being exposed to broad sprays.

recipes.title: deep clean a microwave
recipes.name: deep-clean-a-microwave
recipes.goal: The microwave interior, door, and turntable are clean, deodorized, and free of loosened food debris.

steps.action: **Make a steam bowl.** Mix 1 cup water with 2 tablespoons white vinegar in a microwave-safe bowl.
steps.expect: the bowl is no more than half full.

steps.action: **Heat until steamy.** Microwave 3 to 5 minutes, stopping when the window fogs heavily.
steps.expect: steam coats the walls and door.

steps.action: **Let it sit closed.** Leave the door shut for 5 minutes so grime softens.
steps.expect: dried splatters look wet or swollen.

steps.action: **Remove hot items carefully.** Take out the bowl and turntable with a dry towel.
steps.expect: the cavity is open and safe to wipe.

steps.action: **Wash the turntable.** Clean it in the sink with dish soap, then dry it.
steps.expect: the glass plate has no grease film.

steps.action: **Wipe top to bottom.** Wipe ceiling, sides, floor, and door gasket with a damp cloth.
steps.expect: softened food lifts without hard scraping.

steps.action: **Treat stuck spots.** Press the warm damp cloth on stuck food for 30 seconds, then wipe again.
steps.expect: residue releases without scratching.

steps.action: **Dry and deodorize.** Dry surfaces, reinstall the turntable, and leave the door open 5 minutes.
steps.expect: vinegar smell fades and no damp puddles remain.

recipes.verification: The microwave has a dry clean interior, a seated turntable, and no visible food splatter on the ceiling, walls, or door.

recipes.title: defrost a freezer
recipes.name: defrost-a-freezer
recipes.goal: The freezer is ice-free, dry, running again at temperature, and restocked, with no food thawed past safety and no water on the floor or damage to the cooling lining.

steps.action: **Run stocks down first, then stage the cooler.** Plan the defrost for when the freezer is emptiest; load the cool box with ice packs 30 minutes ahead.
steps.expect: cool box cold inside before any food moves.

steps.action: **Move all food to the cooler, triaging as you go.** Pack tightly (a full cooler holds cold far longer), most perishable items deepest against the ice packs. Toss anything freezer-burned beyond use or of unknown age.
steps.expect: freezer empty; cooler closed and kept shut.

steps.action: **Switch off and unplug the freezer, door propped open.** Remove shelves and drawers to wash separately in the sink. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* food safety clock starts now; a packed cooler buys roughly 4-6 hours, so the defrost must finish inside that window.
steps.expect: freezer off, interior starting to warm, shelves soaking.

steps.action: **Lay the towel and tray defenses.** Towels across the floor in front of and under the freezer edge; the baking tray under the door lip or beneath the drain outlet if the model has one at the back/bottom. Locate the internal drain channel and check it is not iced shut.
steps.expect: every path meltwater can take ends in a towel or tray.

steps.action: **Speed the melt, gently.** [BRANCH: bowls of steaming (not boiling) water set inside on trivets, door shut, swapped every 15 minutes | a fan blowing room air into the open freezer, surprisingly effective and hands-off | patience only, 2-4 hours] Never chip at ice with a knife, screwdriver, or any sharp tool; one puncture of the wall lining hits a refrigerant line and writes off the whole appliance. A hairdryer only on low, kept moving, hands and cord clear of standing water.
steps.expect: sheets of ice loosening at the edges within 20-30 minutes.

steps.action: **Remove ice as slabs, not shards.** As sheets loosen, ease them off whole with fingers or a plastic scraper and drop them in the sink; wring towels as they saturate and re-lay dry ones.
steps.expect: walls progressively bare; meltwater volume dropping.

steps.action: **Drain and dry completely.** Sponge out the remaining water, clear the drain channel and drain hole (a straw of paper towel wicks the last of it), wipe the interior with a mild bicarbonate solution, then dry every surface. A wet interior refrosts instantly and puddles ice on the floor of the compartment.
steps.expect: interior bone dry to the touch, drain clear, no smell.

steps.action: **Restart and wait for temperature before restocking.** Plug in, thermostat to normal, door shut. Wait until the compartment is properly cold: 30 minutes minimum, ideally until an interior thermometer reads near -18 °C.
steps.expect: compressor running; interior frosty-cold to the hand.

steps.action: **Restock from the cooler, checking each item.** Anything fully thawed and warm does not go back in; fully-thawed-but-cold raw meat gets cooked today, not refrozen raw. Log the restock as the date of this defrost.
steps.expect: food back in, still hard-frozen or refrigerator-cold at worst; cooler empty.

recipes.verification: Interior walls are bare metal/plastic with no ice, the drain is clear, the floor around the appliance is dry, an interior thermometer reads at or near -18 °C, and all restocked food was still frozen or cold when it went back in.

recipes.title: deodorize a room
recipes.name: deodorize-a-room
recipes.goal: A room smells neutral because the odor source is removed first, then air, surfaces, and absorbent materials are refreshed.

steps.action: **Find the source.** Check trash, laundry, drains, pet areas, food, shoes, damp fabrics, and hidden spills.
steps.expect: the strongest smell has an identifiable location or category.

steps.action: **Remove the source.** Take out trash, wash fabric, clean spills, or move damp items to dry.
steps.expect: the room smells better within a few minutes.

steps.action: **Ventilate.** Open windows if outdoor air is acceptable, or run exhaust and a fan.
steps.expect: stale air moves out and fresh air enters.

steps.action: **Clean contact surfaces.** Wipe hard surfaces near the source with appropriate cleaner and dry them.
steps.expect: sticky or dusty residue is gone.

steps.action: **Absorb remaining odor.** Place bowls of baking soda or activated charcoal near the odor zone for several hours.
steps.expect: smell fades without perfume covering it.

steps.action: **Avoid masking only.** Use sprays only after cleaning, and choose light amounts. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* heavy fragrance can soak into fabric and create a second odor problem, so do not saturate upholstery or carpets.
steps.expect: room smells clean rather than perfumed.

steps.action: **Recheck next day.** Close the room for 1 hour, then re-enter and smell near likely sources.
steps.expect: odor does not rebound strongly.

recipes.verification: After the room has been closed for 1 hour, re-entering produces no strong odor source, and the air smells neutral without relying on heavy fragrance.

recipes.title: deodorize smelly shoes
recipes.name: deodorize-smelly-shoes
recipes.goal: Shoes are dried, aired, and treated so odor is reduced without damaging the uppers or insoles.

steps.action: **Remove insoles and laces.** Open the shoes fully so air can reach the inside.
steps.expect: the interior is exposed.

steps.action: **Dry the shoes.** Stuff with newspaper or place near airflow away from heat.
steps.expect: interiors feel dry rather than clammy.

steps.action: **Brush out debris.** Shake out grit, lint, and loose sock fibers.
steps.expect: no loose material remains under the toes or heel.

steps.action: **Apply odor absorber.** Put baking soda in sachets or thin socks and place one inside each shoe overnight.
steps.expect: powder stays contained while absorbing odor.

steps.action: **Air out.** Remove sachets and let shoes ventilate for several hours.
steps.expect: stale smell is noticeably reduced.

steps.action: **Treat insoles.** Wipe washable insoles with mild soap or spray with shoe-safe disinfectant and dry fully.
steps.expect: insoles smell cleaner and are dry before reinsertion.

steps.action: **Restart with dry socks.** Wear clean moisture-wicking socks and rotate shoes between wears.
steps.expect: odor does not immediately return after one use.

recipes.verification: After overnight treatment and airing, the shoes and insoles are dry, have no loose powder inside, and have no strong odor when smelled at the opening.

recipes.title: descale a kettle
recipes.name: descale-a-kettle
recipes.goal: The kettle's limescale is dissolved with a mild acid, rinsed away completely, and the appliance boils clean again, faster and without white flakes in the tea.

steps.action: **Prepare the solution in the kettle.** Vinegar: half water, half white vinegar to cover the scale. Citric acid: one to two tablespoons in half a kettle of water. Commercial: its packet's word is law.
steps.expect: solution covering all visible scale; the warning note on the kettle.

steps.action: **Heat, but do not necessarily boil.** Bring it near-boiling (vinegar especially turns the kitchen sharp when boiled), then switch off.
steps.expect: hot solution; audible fizzing from the scale is the reaction working.

steps.action: **Let it sit 20 to 30 minutes.** Heavy crusts can take an hour or a second round; patience does what scrubbing cannot reach.
steps.expect: scale visibly thinning, dissolving, or detaching in flakes.

steps.action: **Empty, and rub off any loosened remnants.** Pour the solution away (it is drain-safe and even mildly helpful to drains), then a soft cloth or sponge on any softened patches. No metal scouring on the element or coating.
steps.expect: interior surfaces smooth to the touch.

steps.action: **Rinse, then boil-and-dump twice with fresh water.** ⚠️ This is the step that keeps the next cup from tasting of vinegar and, more importantly, ensures nobody drinks descaler: two full boil-discard cycles minimum, three for commercial products.
steps.expect: boiled water that smells and tastes of nothing.

steps.action: **Remove the note, and clean the outside while you are there.** A damp cloth for the body, and the limescale ring on the spout mesh (many kettles have a removable spout filter that rinses under the tap).
steps.expect: kettle back in service, filter re-seated, no note left to cry wolf.

recipes.verification: The element and floor show bare metal or clean coating, the boil is quiet and quick again, water boiled afterward tastes of nothing, the spout filter is clean and seated, and the warning-note discipline held for the whole soak.

recipes.title: descale a showerhead
recipes.name: descale-a-showerhead
recipes.goal: Mineral scale is loosened from a showerhead so water sprays evenly through the jets again.

steps.action: **Check the spray pattern.** Run the shower briefly and note blocked jets or sideways spray.
steps.expect: the clogged areas are identified before cleaning.

steps.action: **Fill a bag with vinegar.** Add enough white vinegar to cover the face of the showerhead without overflowing.
steps.expect: the bag can surround the spray plate with liquid over the jets.

steps.action: **Tie the bag over the head.** Lift the bag around the showerhead and secure it tightly with a rubber band or twist tie.
steps.expect: the jet face is submerged and the bag hangs without slipping.

steps.action: **Soak the scale.** Leave it for 30 to 60 minutes, shorter for delicate finishes. [BRANCH: chrome or plastic | delicate finish]
steps.expect: white crust softens and the vinegar may turn cloudy.

steps.action: **Remove and brush.** Take the bag off, dip the toothbrush in vinegar, and scrub each jet face gently.
steps.expect: loosened flakes come away without scratching the finish.

steps.action: **Work stubborn jets.** Rub rubber nozzles with a thumb or brush across mineral plugs.
steps.expect: blocked holes open visibly.

steps.action: **Flush hot water.** Run the shower on warm or hot for 1 to 2 minutes while standing clear of spray.
steps.expect: grit and vinegar rinse out, then water runs clear.

steps.action: **Wipe dry.** Dry the fixture and surrounding wall so vinegar does not sit on metal or stone.
steps.expect: the showerhead is clean, dry, and free of vinegar smell.

recipes.verification: After flushing, water exits most jets in a straight even pattern, with no vinegar dripping from the fixture and no new leak at the shower arm.

recipes.title: desensitize a dog to nail trims
recipes.name: desensitize-a-dog-to-nail-trims
recipes.goal: Teach a dog to tolerate nail-trim handling gradually, so future trims can happen with less fear and less restraint.

steps.action: **Pick a calm marker.** Use a clicker or short word followed by a treat.
steps.expect: the dog looks for food after the marker.

steps.action: **Reward paw-adjacent touch.** Touch shoulder, leg, then paw for one second, staying below the dog's fear threshold.
steps.expect: the dog keeps eating and does not pull away hard.

steps.action: **Introduce the tool at a distance.** Show the clipper or grinder, mark calm looking, and put it away.
steps.expect: the tool predicts food instead of restraint.

steps.action: **Pair tool sound with food.** Click clippers in the air or run the grinder far away, then feed.
steps.expect: the dog hears the sound and remains able to eat.

steps.action: **Touch nail without cutting.** Tap the tool to one nail, mark, feed, and stop.
steps.expect: brief nail contact is tolerated.

steps.action: **Trim one tiny tip only when ready.** Clip or grind a minimal amount; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not cut deeper to make up for missed sessions.
steps.expect: one nail changes slightly and the dog recovers immediately.

recipes.verification: The dog can calmly accept the current training step, such as paw touch, tool sound, nail tap, or one tiny trim, while still taking treats and recovering quickly.

recipes.title: divide perennials
recipes.name: divide-perennials
recipes.goal: Divide overcrowded perennial plants into healthy sections that can be replanted at the right depth with reduced transplant stress.

steps.action: **Choose the right season.** Divide spring bloomers after flowering or in fall, and divide late bloomers in spring when possible.
steps.expect: the plant is not stressed by peak bloom or heat.

steps.action: **Water the plant.** Water the day before if soil is dry.
steps.expect: roots are hydrated and soil releases more cleanly.

steps.action: **Cut back excess foliage.** Trim tall stems by about one-third if they will wilt or get in the way.
steps.expect: the plant is easier to handle.

steps.action: **Lift the clump.** Dig around the drip line and pry from several sides to keep roots intact.
steps.expect: the clump comes up with a usable root mass.

steps.action: **Separate healthy divisions.** Pull, slice, or saw the clump into sections with roots and several growing points.
steps.expect: each division can grow independently.

steps.action: **Discard weak centers.** Remove dead, woody, diseased, or hollow center material.
steps.expect: only vigorous outer growth is replanted.

steps.action: **Replant promptly.** Set divisions at the original soil depth with compost-enriched backfill and firm gently.
steps.expect: crowns are level with the surrounding soil.

steps.action: **Water and mulch.** Soak the new plantings and mulch around, not over, crowns.
steps.expect: soil settles around roots and moisture is conserved.

recipes.verification: Each replanted division has roots, growing points, original planting depth, firm moist soil contact, and mulch that does not cover the crown.

recipes.title: do the laundry
recipes.name: do-the-laundry
recipes.goal: A load of dirty clothes is washed, dried, and put away — clean, undamaged, un-shrunk, and nothing dyed pink.

steps.action: **Sort the pile.** Split by color: darks / lights-whites; pull out anything labeled hand-wash/dry-clean, and anything new and deeply dyed (new red items bleed — first washes go alone or with darks).
steps.expect: two or more piles; delicates and bleed-risks separated.

steps.action: **Prep the garments.** Empty every pocket (a tissue ruins a load; a pen ruins a machine), zip zippers, turn prints and dark jeans inside out.
steps.expect: pockets flat-empty; zips closed.

steps.action: **Load the drum loosely.** Fill at most ~¾ — clothes need tumble room to get clean.
steps.expect: a hand fits flat between the load and the drum top.

steps.action: **Dose detergent per its cap markings and the load size.** Into the drawer's main compartment (or pod straight into the drum, *under* the clothes). More detergent ≠ cleaner; excess leaves residue.
steps.expect: dose at or below the cap's line for a normal load.

steps.action: **Choose the cycle and temperature.** Default: normal/cotton cycle, 30–40 °C. Care label overrides: the tub symbol's number is the max temperature; a hand in the tub = hand-wash cycle.
steps.expect: cycle set consistent with the most delicate item in the load.

steps.action: **Start, and note the finish time.**
steps.expect: door locks, water sound begins; you know when to come back — wet clothes left sitting sour within hours.

steps.action: **Move to drying promptly at cycle end.** [BRANCH: dryer — medium heat, clean the lint filter *first*, no items with elastic/wool that the label bans | rack/line — shake each piece out, hang with air space] ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a hot dryer shrinks wool and elastic permanently — when in doubt, rack-dry it.
steps.expect: lint filter cleaned; load drying by the chosen path.

steps.action: **Fold or hang while just-dry (or slightly warm).** This is when wrinkles surrender (`embodied/fold-a-tshirt` for the fold). Put everything away.
steps.expect: empty basket, stocked drawers, no chair-mountain of clean laundry.

recipes.verification: Clothes are clean (spot-check former stains), fully dry, correctly sized (nothing shrunk), sorted into their storage, the lint filter is clean, and the machine door is ajar to dry.

recipes.title: drain a radiator
recipes.name: drain-a-radiator
recipes.goal: A radiator is drained without flooding the room, then the heating system is refilled and bled so it can run normally again.

steps.action: **Turn heating off and wait.** Let the radiator and pipework cool fully before touching valves.
steps.expect: metal and water are safe to handle.

steps.action: **Close both radiator valves.** Turn the thermostatic or hand valve off and close the lockshield, counting turns.
steps.expect: the radiator is isolated and settings are noted.

steps.action: **Protect the floor.** Lay towels, position a tray or hose at the drain point, and keep a bucket nearby.
steps.expect: any first spill lands on protection.

steps.action: **Open the bleed valve.** Crack the top bleed valve to admit air once draining starts.
steps.expect: air can enter so water will leave smoothly.

steps.action: **Open the drain or loosen the union.** [BRANCH: drain cock | valve union] use the drain cock if fitted, otherwise loosen the lower union carefully.
steps.expect: water begins flowing into the tray, hose, or bucket.

steps.action: **Catch and empty water patiently.** Keep draining until flow stops, tightening briefly when swapping buckets.
steps.expect: the radiator is light enough or empty enough for the next task.

steps.action: **Close and reseal.** Close the drain, retighten the union, close the bleed valve, and reopen radiator valves to their noted positions.
steps.expect: joints are closed and dry.

steps.action: **Refill and rebleed.** Repressurize the system if needed, bleed the radiator, and top pressure back up.
steps.expect: the radiator refills without gurgling.

recipes.verification: After refilling, the radiator heats evenly, the boiler pressure is in range, and all disturbed joints remain dry for 10 minutes.

recipes.title: dust a room
recipes.name: dust-a-room
recipes.goal: A room dusted top-to-bottom in the order that means dust is removed once, not relocated twice, including the surfaces everyone skips.

steps.action: **Top of the room first, always.** Ceiling corners and cobwebs, light fixtures (switched off, and cool if they were on), the tops of tall furniture, curtain rails, and the ceiling fan (an old pillowcase slipped over each blade wipes and *catches* instead of raining).
steps.expect: the high layer done; whatever fell is now the lower surfaces' problem, which is exactly why order matters.

steps.action: **Work down through the mid-layer.** Shelves, picture frames (`daily/home/hang-a-picture`'s survivors, held steady with the free hand), window sills, the TV and its stand (dry microfiber only on screens, no sprays), lamps and shades. Lift objects, wipe under them, replace; wiping around things is the signature of fake dusting.
steps.expect: each surface cleared under its objects, not just in front of them.

steps.action: **Hit the invisible standards.** Skirting boards, door tops and frames, radiator tops and fins (a damp cloth over a ruler slides between fins), light switches and door handles (the touched-surfaces get a damp pass), and vents.
steps.expect: the zones that make a "clean" room smell dusty are actually clean.

steps.action: **Refold or swap the cloth as it loads.** A saturated cloth deposits; fold to a fresh face every few surfaces, and switch cloths when no faces remain.
steps.expect: always wiping with a face that looks cleaner than the surface.

steps.action: **Electronics get the gentle version.** Screens: dry microfiber, light pressure. Keyboards and vents: a soft brush or air blower rather than a wet cloth. Cables and power strips behind furniture: unplug nothing, but the dust bunnies there are fuel for step 6.
steps.expect: electronics dust-free with zero moisture near them.

steps.action: **Finish with the floor.** Everything that fell now gets vacuumed or swept (`daily/home/vacuum-a-room` or `daily/home/sweep-and-mop-a-floor`), including under the furniture edges you dusted above.
steps.expect: the room's dust actually in a bin or bag, not resettled by morning.

recipes.verification: High, mid, and invisible layers all wiped under-not-around, screens dry-wiped, cloth faces retired as they loaded, and the floor vacuumed last so the room passes the sunbeam test: light through the window showing air, not a snow globe.

recipes.title: empty and clean a lint trap
recipes.name: empty-and-clean-a-lint-trap
recipes.goal: The dryer lint trap is cleared for the next load, and the screen is washed when softener film blocks airflow.

steps.action: **Remove the screen before every load.** Pull the lint trap straight out without bending the frame.
steps.expect: the mesh screen is fully exposed.

steps.action: **Peel the lint mat off.** Start at one corner and roll the lint into itself, then put it in the bin.
steps.expect: the mesh looks open instead of fuzzy.

steps.action: **Check for softener film.** Run a little water over the screen. [BRANCH: water beads | water passes through] beading means the screen needs washing, passing water means it can go back dry.
steps.expect: you know whether residue is blocking airflow.

steps.action: **Wash the screen if needed.** Use warm water, dish soap, and a soft brush on both sides.
steps.expect: water sheets through the mesh evenly.

steps.action: **Dry the screen completely.** Pat it with a towel and let it air-dry until no droplets remain.
steps.expect: the screen is dry, straight, and free of soap.

steps.action: **Clear the slot lip.** Pick or vacuum loose lint from the trap slot entrance without dropping tools inside.
steps.expect: the screen path is unobstructed.

steps.action: **Refit the screen.** Slide it back along its rails until it sits flush.
steps.expect: the trap is seated and the dryer door or top closes normally.

recipes.verification: The lint screen is clean, dry, intact, fully seated, and water can pass through the mesh after any wash.

recipes.title: escape a house fire safely
recipes.name: escape-a-house-fire-safely
recipes.goal: Everyone who can evacuate leaves a house fire quickly, calls emergency services from outside, and stays out.

steps.action: **React immediately.** Treat alarms, smoke, or fire as real and start leaving without collecting belongings.
steps.expect: evacuation begins without delay.

steps.action: **Alert others while moving.** Shout "fire" and wake household members on your route out.
steps.expect: others are warned without stopping evacuation.

steps.action: **Stay low under smoke.** Crawl or crouch where smoke is present.
steps.expect: breathing air is clearer near the floor.

steps.action: **Check doors before opening.** Feel the door and knob with the back of your hand and look for smoke around edges.
steps.expect: you know whether that route may be dangerous.

steps.action: **Use the safest exit.** [BRANCH: door cool and clear | door hot or smoky] open slowly and leave if clear; use another exit or shelter if heat or smoke is present.
steps.expect: you avoid moving into intense fire or smoke.

steps.action: **Close doors behind you.** Close each door you pass through if safe.
steps.expect: fire and smoke spread may slow.

steps.action: **Go to the meeting place.** Move to the planned outdoor location away from the building.
steps.expect: people can be accounted for safely.

steps.action: **Call emergency services from outside.** Give the address, fire location, trapped people, and hazards such as gas cylinders.
steps.expect: firefighters are dispatched with useful information.

steps.action: **Stay out.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* re-entering can be fatal; confirm firefighters have been told about anyone missing instead of going back inside.
steps.expect: no one re-enters before firefighters say it is safe.

steps.action: **Signal if trapped.** If you cannot escape, close doors, block smoke gaps with cloth, call emergency services, and signal from a window.
steps.expect: rescuers know where to find you.

recipes.verification: People who escaped are outside at the meeting place, emergency services have the address and missing-person information, and no one re-enters until firefighters declare it safe.

recipes.title: find a lost pet
recipes.name: find-a-lost-pet
recipes.goal: Run an immediate, organized search for a lost pet while notifying the right people and making it easy for the pet to return safely.

steps.action: **Secure the escape point.** Leave a safe entry open only if it does not endanger other pets or people, and place familiar bedding or scent nearby.
steps.expect: the pet has a clear return route.

steps.action: **Search the immediate area quietly.** Check closets, garages, sheds, under decks, bushes, and nearby hiding spots with a flashlight.
steps.expect: close hiding places are ruled out before the search radius expands.

steps.action: **Alert nearby people.** Tell neighbors, building staff, postal workers, and local groups with a photo, name, and contact method.
steps.expect: more eyes are watching without chasing the pet.

steps.action: **Contact shelters and vets.** File lost reports with animal control, shelters, microchip registry, and nearby veterinary clinics.
steps.expect: found-pet intake points can match the pet to you.

steps.action: **Post clear notices.** Use large readable flyers and online posts with area, date, photo, and one contact number.
steps.expect: sightings can be reported quickly.

steps.action: **Follow sightings carefully.** Go to sightings with food, carrier or leash, and calm voices; do not run after a scared pet.
steps.expect: the pet is approached slowly or the location is marked for trapping help.

recipes.verification: The pet is physically recovered and checked for injury, or all local shelters, vets, microchip registry, neighbors, flyers, and online lost-pet channels have current reports and contact information.

recipes.title: find a water leak
recipes.name: find-a-water-leak
recipes.goal: Locate likely water leak sources and decide whether to shut off water or call a professional.

steps.action: **Look for urgent hazards.** Check for water near outlets, breaker panels, ceilings, or sagging drywall.
steps.expect: hazards are identified before touching plumbing.

steps.action: **Stop using water.** Turn off faucets, appliances, irrigation, humidifiers, and ice makers.
steps.expect: no intentional water use is happening.

steps.action: **Check the water meter.** Watch the low-flow indicator or record the meter reading for 10 to 15 minutes.
steps.expect: movement with all water off suggests an active supply-side leak.

steps.action: **Inspect visible fixtures.** Wipe supply valves and trap joints under sinks, then look for new droplets.
steps.expect: wet joints show the likely leak location.

steps.action: **Check toilets with dye.** Put dye in the tank, wait 10 minutes without flushing, then inspect the bowl.
steps.expect: colored bowl water indicates a leaking flapper or flush valve.

steps.action: **Check appliances.** Inspect water heater, washing machine hoses, dishwasher base, refrigerator line, and HVAC condensate drain.
steps.expect: pooling, corrosion, or damp flooring points to a source.

steps.action: **Trace stains and sounds.** Follow ceiling stains, wall dampness, musty smells, or hissing toward the nearest plumbing line.
steps.expect: the likely source area narrows.

steps.action: **Shut off water if the leak is active.** Close the fixture valve or the water main if water is escaping continuously.
steps.expect: flow slows or stops.

steps.action: **Call a professional when the source is hidden or damage is spreading.** Contact a plumber, building maintenance, or water mitigation company.
steps.expect: the issue is handed to someone equipped to open walls or dry structures.

recipes.verification: The suspected leak source is identified or isolated, water flow has stopped or been shut off, and a professional has been called for hidden, electrical, structural, or continuing leaks.

recipes.title: fix a cracked tile
recipes.name: fix-a-cracked-tile
recipes.goal: A single cracked ceramic or porcelain tile is removed and replaced with a matching tile, fresh adhesive, grout, and sealer.

steps.action: **Protect the area.** Cover nearby surfaces and tape the edges of adjacent tiles.
steps.expect: surrounding tile and fixtures are shielded.

steps.action: **Clear the grout.** Rake grout from all sides of the cracked tile without cutting into neighboring tile edges.
steps.expect: the tile is isolated by open joints.

steps.action: **Break the damaged tile.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the replacement fits, then crack the bad tile inward from the center with light hammer taps.
steps.expect: fragments loosen away from adjacent tiles.

steps.action: **Chip out pieces.** Use the chisel at a shallow angle and remove tile fragments from the center outward.
steps.expect: the old tile is gone and neighboring tiles remain intact.

steps.action: **Scrape the substrate.** Remove old adhesive until the surface is flat and vacuum dust.
steps.expect: the new tile can sit level.

steps.action: **Dry-fit the tile.** Place the new tile with spacers and check height and joint width.
steps.expect: the face is flush with nearby tiles.

steps.action: **Set the tile.** Spread thinset or adhesive, press the tile in, wiggle slightly, and insert spacers.
steps.expect: the tile is aligned and supported evenly.

steps.action: **Grout the joints.** After adhesive cures as directed, pack grout into the joints and tool them smooth.
steps.expect: joints are full and even.

steps.action: **Clean and seal.** Wipe haze after grout firms, then seal when the grout cure time allows.
steps.expect: the repair is clean and protected.

recipes.verification: After cure, the replacement tile is flush, firmly bonded, evenly grouted, sealed if required, and does not rock or sound hollow.

recipes.title: fix a drawer slide
recipes.name: fix-a-drawer-slide
recipes.goal: A drawer slide is cleaned, realigned, or reattached so the drawer opens and closes smoothly without falling off track.

steps.action: **Empty the drawer.** Remove contents and set them aside.
steps.expect: the drawer is light enough to handle safely.

steps.action: **Remove the drawer.** Pull out fully and release tabs or lift the front depending on slide type.
steps.expect: the drawer separates from the cabinet tracks.

steps.action: **Clean the slides.** Vacuum debris and wipe tracks, rollers, and drawer sides.
steps.expect: dirt and loose objects are gone.

steps.action: **Inspect hardware.** Check for loose screws, bent rails, broken rollers, or missing stops.
steps.expect: the cause of binding or sagging is identified.

steps.action: **Tighten or replace screws.** Drive loose screws snugly and replace missing screws with matching length screws.
steps.expect: slides are fixed firmly to wood.

steps.action: **Realign the slide.** Loosen screws slightly, square the rail, and retighten.
steps.expect: both slides sit parallel and level.

steps.action: **Reinstall the drawer.** Align rails and push until release tabs or rollers engage.
steps.expect: the drawer travels on both slides.

steps.action: **Test under load.** Reload lightly and open and close several times.
steps.expect: the drawer moves smoothly and stays level.

recipes.verification: The drawer opens fully, closes flush, stays on both slides, and does not bind after being loaded with normal contents.

recipes.title: fix a drooping hemline
recipes.name: fix-a-drooping-hemline
recipes.goal: A loose or drooping hem is temporarily or permanently secured so the garment hangs evenly again.

steps.action: **Find the loose area.** Turn the garment inside out and trace where stitches or adhesive failed.
steps.expect: the drooping section and secure section are clearly identified.

steps.action: **Realign the fold.** Fold the hem back to the original crease and clip or pin it in place.
steps.expect: the outside hemline looks even.

steps.action: **Choose the repair.** Use [BRANCH: hand stitch | fusible tape | temporary tape or pins] based on time and fabric.
steps.expect: the repair method fits the garment and event.

steps.action: **Secure the hem.** Stitch tiny catch stitches, fuse tape with a pressing cloth, or place temporary tape inside the fold. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* iron heat and adhesive can mark fabric; test before fusing.
steps.expect: the loose fold stays against the inside of the garment.

steps.action: **Remove visible pins.** Take out alignment pins or replace emergency pins with hidden ones.
steps.expect: no sharp pins show on the outside.

steps.action: **Press or smooth lightly.** Use label-safe pressing or hand smoothing to settle the hem.
steps.expect: the hem edge hangs flat.

steps.action: **Inspect while hanging.** Hang or wear the garment and check the hem all around.
steps.expect: the repaired section matches the rest of the hemline.

recipes.verification: With the garment hanging naturally, the repaired hem stays level, does not gape, and has no visible stitches, pins, or adhesive on the outside.

recipes.title: fix a gap under a door
recipes.name: fix-a-gap-under-a-door
recipes.goal: A gap under a door is reduced with an adjusted threshold, door sweep, or draft seal so light, air, and insects are limited.

steps.action: **Measure the gap.** Close the door and measure the largest space between door bottom and threshold or floor.
steps.expect: the needed seal height is known.

steps.action: **Check door swing.** Open and close the door while watching the floor clearance.
steps.expect: you know whether a sweep will drag.

steps.action: **Adjust the threshold.** If adjustable, turn threshold screws upward evenly until the gap narrows.
steps.expect: the door closes without rubbing hard.

steps.action: **Size the sweep.** Mark the sweep to door width and trim it to fit.
steps.expect: the sweep spans the door without hitting jambs.

steps.action: **Position the sweep.** Hold it against the closed door so the flexible fin touches the threshold lightly.
steps.expect: no daylight shows under the fin.

steps.action: **Fasten the sweep.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* drill pilot holes only after confirming height and door swing.
steps.expect: screws hold the sweep straight and snug.

steps.action: **Test operation.** Open, close, and latch the door several times.
steps.expect: the sweep seals without blocking the latch.

steps.action: **Check from outside.** Look for daylight or air movement along the bottom edge.
steps.expect: the visible gap is closed.

recipes.verification: With the door latched, no continuous daylight is visible under the door and the door opens and closes without scraping hard.

recipes.title: fix a leaky faucet
recipes.name: fix-a-leaky-faucet
recipes.goal: A dripping sink faucet stops leaking after the worn washer, cartridge, or O-ring is identified and replaced without flooding the cabinet.

steps.action: **Shut off the water.** Turn both under-sink valves clockwise, then open the faucet to drain pressure.
steps.expect: water slows to drips and stops.

steps.action: **Protect the drain and finish.** Plug the drain, lay a towel in the basin, and wrap shiny parts before using a wrench.
steps.expect: dropped screws cannot fall into the drain.

steps.action: **Remove the handle.** Pry off the cap if present, remove the set screw, and lift the handle straight up.
steps.expect: the valve stem or cartridge top is visible.

steps.action: **Identify the valve type.** [BRANCH: compression | cartridge] compression faucets have a threaded stem and rubber washer at the bottom; cartridge faucets pull out as a plastic or brass cartridge.
steps.expect: you know which replacement path to use.

steps.action: **Service a compression stem.** Unscrew the packing nut, remove the stem, replace the bottom washer, and replace the O-ring if it is flattened or cracked.
steps.expect: fresh rubber sits flat with no splits.

steps.action: **Service a cartridge valve.** Note the cartridge orientation, remove the retaining clip or nut, pull the cartridge straight out, and match it exactly at the store if needed.
steps.expect: the new cartridge matches length, tabs, and ports.

steps.action: **Lubricate seals lightly.** Apply a thin film of plumber's grease to O-rings only, not to ceramic discs or threaded seats unless the maker says so.
steps.expect: seals slide without bunching.

steps.action: **Reassemble in order.** Reinstall the stem or cartridge, retaining hardware, handle, and cap without forcing cross-threaded parts.
steps.expect: the handle moves normally through its range.

steps.action: **Restore water slowly.** Open the shutoff valves a quarter turn at a time while watching the faucet and cabinet.
steps.expect: no spray, seep, or sudden cabinet leak.

steps.action: **Test hot and cold.** Run each side, close the faucet firmly, and wait two minutes.
steps.expect: the spout and handle base stay dry.

recipes.verification: With the faucet closed after a full hot and cold test, no drip forms at the spout, handle base, supply valves, or cabinet connections for five minutes.

recipes.title: fix a loose cabinet hinge
recipes.name: fix-a-loose-cabinet-hinge
recipes.goal: A loose cabinet hinge is tightened or re-anchored so the door swings cleanly and lines up with neighboring doors.

steps.action: **Support the door.** Hold the cabinet door level or place a folded towel under it.
steps.expect: hinge is not carrying extra twisting weight while you work.

steps.action: **Tighten obvious screws.** Use the correct driver and turn hinge screws clockwise until snug.
steps.expect: screws stop wobbling and hinge plate sits flat.

steps.action: **Test movement.** Open and close the door slowly.
steps.expect: door moves without clunking or pulling away.

steps.action: **Repair stripped holes.** If a screw spins, remove it, dip toothpicks in wood glue, pack the hole, snap flush, and reinstall after the glue begins to grab.
steps.expect: screw bites into wood again.

steps.action: **Realign the door.** Adjust hinge position or European hinge screws in small turns until gaps are even.
steps.expect: top and side gaps look parallel.

steps.action: **Snug, do not crush.** Tighten final screws by hand for the last turns. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overtightening can strip particleboard or split the stile, so stop when the hinge is firm.
steps.expect: hinge does not shift under gentle pressure.

steps.action: **Clean up and recheck.** Wipe glue squeeze-out and open the door several times.
steps.expect: door stays aligned after repeated movement.

recipes.verification: The cabinet door opens and closes five times without sagging, rubbing, or hinge movement, and the visible gaps remain even.

recipes.title: fix a loose door hinge
recipes.name: fix-a-loose-door-hinge
recipes.goal: A loose door hinge is tightened or anchored so the door swings cleanly and the hinge no longer pulls from the jamb or door edge.

steps.action: **Find the loose side.** Open the door halfway and watch whether the hinge leaf moves on the jamb or door.
steps.expect: the loose screw locations are identified.

steps.action: **Tighten intact screws.** Drive each loose screw clockwise by hand or with a low-torque driver.
steps.expect: screws pull the hinge leaf flat.

steps.action: **Test the swing.** Open and close the door slowly.
steps.expect: the latch side no longer drops or rubs.

steps.action: **Replace a jamb screw.** If a top hinge screw spins, remove one jamb screw and install a 3 inch screw angled slightly toward the framing stud.
steps.expect: the screw bites firmly and pulls the hinge tight.

steps.action: **Patch a stripped hole.** [BRANCH: toothpick-glue | longer screw] fill a stripped door-edge hole with glue-coated toothpicks or use a longer same-diameter screw where solid wood is available.
steps.expect: the screw tightens without spinning.

steps.action: **Trim the patch.** Let glue set enough to hold, cut toothpicks flush, and reinstall the screw.
steps.expect: the hinge leaf sits flat over the repair.

steps.action: **Check hinge alignment.** Make sure hinge barrels form a straight vertical line and screws are seated flat.
steps.expect: the hinge pin is not binding.

steps.action: **Tighten remaining hinges.** Repeat only for screws that are loose, one at a time.
steps.expect: the door stays supported throughout.

steps.action: **Final swing test.** Open, close, and latch the door several times.
steps.expect: the door swings freely and latches without lifting.

recipes.verification: The hinge leaves stay flush, no screw spins, and the door opens, closes, and latches three times without rubbing caused by hinge movement.

recipes.title: fix a loose grout line
recipes.name: fix-a-loose-grout-line
recipes.goal: A narrow loose grout line between tiles is cleaned out, refilled, and cured so water and dirt cannot enter the joint.

steps.action: **Identify the loose line.** Press nearby tiles lightly and mark only the crumbling grout section.
steps.expect: tiles stay fixed and only grout flakes move.

steps.action: **Remove weak grout.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* saw out loose grout to at least half the tile thickness without scratching tile edges.
steps.expect: the joint contains firm edges and no powdery grout.

steps.action: **Clean the joint.** Vacuum dust and wipe with a barely damp sponge.
steps.expect: the joint is open, dust-free, and not wet.

steps.action: **Mix grout.** Mix a small batch to peanut-butter consistency and let it slake if directed.
steps.expect: grout holds on the float without running.

steps.action: **Pack the joint.** Force grout diagonally across the line until the gap is filled.
steps.expect: the joint is full with no visible voids.

steps.action: **Shape the surface.** Wipe diagonally with a damp sponge after the grout firms slightly.
steps.expect: grout is level with neighboring joints and tile faces are mostly clean.

steps.action: **Buff haze.** After haze forms, polish tile faces with a dry cloth.
steps.expect: tiles look clean while grout remains undisturbed.

steps.action: **Cure and protect.** Keep the area dry and unused for the grout maker's cure time.
steps.expect: the repaired line hardens without cracking.

recipes.verification: After curing, the grout line is hard, flush with adjacent grout, free of cracks, and does not crumble when rubbed with a dry cloth.

recipes.title: fix a noisy radiator
recipes.name: fix-a-noisy-radiator
recipes.goal: A noisy hot-water or steam radiator is checked and corrected for common air, pitch, or valve issues.

steps.action: **Identify the system.** Look for a small bleed screw on hot-water radiators or a side air vent on steam radiators.
steps.expect: the radiator type is clear.

steps.action: **Let it cool enough to touch.** Wait until surfaces are warm rather than hot before working near valves.
steps.expect: you can touch controls safely with gloves.

steps.action: **Open the supply valve fully.** Turn the radiator supply valve fully open, not halfway.
steps.expect: valve chatter from partial opening is eliminated.

steps.action: **Bleed hot-water air.** For hot-water radiators, hold a cup under the bleed valve and open it slowly until water appears.
steps.expect: air hisses first, then a steady water trickle appears.

steps.action: **Close the bleed valve.** Tighten the bleed valve gently when water flows.
steps.expect: no water drips from the bleeder.

steps.action: **Check steam radiator pitch.** For one-pipe steam, slope the radiator slightly toward the supply valve using a level.
steps.expect: condensate can drain back toward the pipe.

steps.action: **Inspect the steam vent.** Replace a spitting, stuck, or paint-clogged steam air vent with the same style.
steps.expect: the vent admits air quietly and closes when hot.

steps.action: **Run a heat cycle.** Observe the radiator during the next call for heat.
steps.expect: noise is reduced and no valve or vent leaks.

recipes.verification: During a normal heating cycle, the radiator heats without persistent banging, hissing, or water leakage from the valve, vent, or bleeder.

recipes.title: fix a slow draining sink
recipes.name: fix-a-slow-draining-sink
recipes.goal: A bathroom or kitchen sink drains normally after the stopper, trap, and near-drain buildup are cleared without damaging plumbing.

steps.action: **Clear the basin.** Remove standing water with a cup and bucket, then wipe the drain area.
steps.expect: the basin is empty enough to work without spilling.

steps.action: **Remove the stopper.** Lift out the stopper or loosen the pivot nut under the sink to release a pop-up stopper.
steps.expect: hair and debris around the stopper are visible.

steps.action: **Clean the stopper.** Pull off hair and sludge, wash the stopper with dish soap, and set it aside.
steps.expect: the stopper moves freely and no longer carries buildup.

steps.action: **Snake the drain opening.** Feed a plastic zip tool or small snake into the drain and pull out debris slowly.
steps.expect: hair or soft buildup comes out, or the tool passes freely.

steps.action: **Flush with hot tap water.** Run hot tap water for one minute if the pipe is not fully blocked.
steps.expect: flow improves or the blockage location is confirmed.

steps.action: **Open the trap.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* place a bucket under the P-trap, confirm no chemical cleaner is present, then loosen the slip nuts by hand or with pliers.
steps.expect: water drains into the bucket and the trap comes free.

steps.action: **Clean the trap.** Empty the trap, scrub visible sludge, and check for hard objects.
steps.expect: the trap interior is clear and the washers are intact.

steps.action: **Reassemble and test.** Reinstall washers in the same orientation, tighten slip nuts snugly, then run water while watching joints.
steps.expect: water drains quickly and no trap joints drip.

recipes.verification: A full sink basin drains completely within two minutes, and the P-trap and slip nuts stay dry during and after the test.

recipes.title: fix a sticking drawer
recipes.name: fix-a-sticking-drawer
recipes.goal: A drawer opens and closes smoothly without scraping, jumping its track, or needing excessive force.

steps.action: **Empty the drawer.** Remove contents and check for items jammed behind it.
steps.expect: the drawer is light and moves farther than before.

steps.action: **Find the rub.** Pull slowly and watch where wood, runners, or slides scrape.
steps.expect: the sticking point is visible or audible.

steps.action: **Remove loose debris.** Vacuum crumbs, screws, labels, or splinters from tracks and corners.
steps.expect: tracks look clear.

steps.action: **Tighten hardware.** Snug loose slide screws, knobs, and front-panel fasteners.
steps.expect: parts no longer wiggle under hand pressure.

steps.action: **Wax wood runners.** Rub candle wax or dry bar soap along wooden contact surfaces.
steps.expect: a thin slick film appears on the runners.

steps.action: **Reseat or shim.** [BRANCH: slide is loose | cabinet is racked] tighten screws or add a thin shim behind the low side.
steps.expect: drawer front sits more evenly.

steps.action: **Test with light load.** Slide the empty drawer in and out 5 times.
steps.expect: travel improves without scraping or jumping.

steps.action: **Reload lightly.** Put contents back with heavy items spread evenly.
steps.expect: the drawer still moves with one hand.

recipes.verification: The drawer travels fully open and fully closed 5 times with its normal load and without scraping, binding, or jumping the runner.

recipes.title: fix a sticking lock
recipes.name: fix-a-sticking-lock
recipes.goal: A door lock turns smoothly after the keyway, latch, and strike alignment are cleaned and adjusted.

steps.action: **Inspect the key.** Compare it with a spare and wipe off dirt or burrs.
steps.expect: the key is clean and not visibly bent.

steps.action: **Test with the door open.** Turn the key and thumb turn while the latch is not in the strike.
steps.expect: you know whether the cylinder or door alignment is sticking.

steps.action: **Lubricate the keyway.** Apply a small amount of dry lock lubricant and work the key in and out.
steps.expect: the key enters farther and turns more smoothly.

steps.action: **Tighten hardware.** Snug loose screws on the lock body, latch plate, hinges, and strike plate.
steps.expect: the lock and door no longer shift by hand.

steps.action: **Check latch alignment.** Close the door slowly and watch whether the latch rubs the strike.
steps.expect: rub marks or smooth entry identify the next action.

steps.action: **Adjust the strike.** File a small rub point or loosen and shift the strike plate slightly.
steps.expect: the latch enters the strike without lifting or pushing the door.

steps.action: **Retest locked and unlocked.** Operate the key several times from both sides if accessible.
steps.expect: the bolt extends and retracts without binding.

recipes.verification: With the door closed, the key locks and unlocks the door five times without lifting, pulling, or forcing the door.

recipes.title: fix a stuck zipper
recipes.name: fix-a-stuck-zipper
recipes.goal: A stuck or separated zipper moves again without torn fabric, bent teeth, or a slider mangled beyond repair.

steps.action: **Stop pulling hard.** Hold the fabric near the slider and take tension off the zipper. [BRANCH: jammed fabric | dry teeth | separated teeth] identify the visible problem before adding force.
steps.expect: the slider stops worsening the snag.

steps.action: **Free trapped fabric.** If cloth is caught, pull the fabric gently backward while nudging the slider the opposite direction.
steps.expect: the cloth loosens without a new tear.

steps.action: **Lubricate the teeth.** Rub graphite from a pencil, candle wax, or dry bar soap along both sides of the teeth near the slider.
steps.expect: the teeth look lightly coated, not greasy.

steps.action: **Work the slider gently.** Move it a few millimeters down, then up, repeating small motions instead of one heroic yank.
