steps.expect: travel increases a little each pass.

steps.action: **Realign the slider.** If teeth separate behind the slider, unzip to the bottom, reseat both sides evenly, and zip up while keeping the tape straight.
steps.expect: the teeth interlock behind the slider.

steps.action: **Tighten a loose slider.** For a metal slider that closes but leaves teeth open, squeeze the back plates very slightly with pliers. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* too much pressure can crack or freeze the slider, so make tiny adjustments and test between squeezes.
steps.expect: the slider grips the teeth more firmly.

steps.action: **Clean excess lubricant.** Wipe wax or soap from nearby fabric with a dry cloth.
steps.expect: the zipper moves while the garment looks presentable.

steps.action: **Run a full test.** Zip from bottom to top and back once at normal speed.
steps.expect: smooth motion with no skipped or split section.

recipes.verification: The zipper travels its full useful length twice and the teeth remain interlocked after the slider passes.

recipes.title: fix a toilet that runs intermittently
recipes.name: fix-a-toilet-that-runs-intermittently
recipes.goal: A toilet that refills intermittently is adjusted or fitted with a new flapper so tank water no longer leaks into the bowl.

steps.action: **Remove the tank lid.** Place it flat on a towel away from the toilet.
steps.expect: the flapper, chain, fill valve, and overflow tube are visible.

steps.action: **Check water height.** Let the tank fill and compare water level to the overflow tube.
steps.expect: water stops below the overflow tube rim.

steps.action: **Adjust a high float.** Lower the float if water enters the overflow tube.
steps.expect: the fill valve shuts off below the tube.

steps.action: **Test for flapper leak.** Add food coloring to the tank and wait ten minutes without flushing.
steps.expect: bowl water stays clear, or color reveals leakage.

steps.action: **Shut off water.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* turn the toilet supply valve clockwise before removing the flapper.
steps.expect: the tank does not refill after a flush.

steps.action: **Replace or clean flapper.** Unhook the old flapper, clean the flush valve seat, and attach a matching flapper.
steps.expect: the flapper sits flat over the valve opening.

steps.action: **Set chain slack.** Adjust the chain so it has slight slack when the flapper is closed.
steps.expect: the handle lifts the flapper without holding it open.

steps.action: **Restore water and test.** Open the shutoff, flush twice, and listen after refills.
steps.expect: the tank refills, stops, and remains silent.

recipes.verification: After two flushes and a ten-minute dye test, no color enters the bowl and the toilet does not refill on its own.

recipes.title: fix a toilet that wont flush
recipes.name: fix-a-toilet-that-wont-flush
recipes.goal: A toilet that will not flush is restored by finding whether the problem is the handle chain, flapper, tank water level, or bowl clog.

steps.action: **Stop any overflow risk.** Turn the shutoff valve clockwise if the bowl is rising or the tank is refilling nonstop.
steps.expect: water stops entering the tank.

steps.action: **Open the tank.** Lift the lid with two hands and set it flat on a towel.
steps.expect: the handle arm, chain, flapper, fill valve, and water level are visible.

steps.action: **Check the handle and chain.** Press the handle while watching the chain lift the flapper. [BRANCH: chain slack | chain disconnected] shorten slack to about 1/2 inch or reconnect it to the handle arm.
steps.expect: the flapper lifts fully when the handle is pressed.

steps.action: **Check the flapper seal.** Press the flapper down, then lift it by hand and inspect for warping, slime, or a broken hinge.
steps.expect: the flapper moves freely and seats flat over the drain opening.

steps.action: **Replace a bad flapper.** Turn water off, flush to drain the tank, unhook the old flapper, clip on a matching one, and reconnect the chain.
steps.expect: the new flapper covers the flush valve without twisting.

steps.action: **Check the tank fill line.** Compare the water level with the mark on the overflow tube or tank wall.
steps.expect: water sits about 1 inch below the overflow tube or at the fill mark.

steps.action: **Raise low tank water.** Adjust the float screw or float cup upward a small amount, then let the tank refill.
steps.expect: the next flush has a stronger surge.

steps.action: **Test for a bowl clog.** If the tank flushes but the bowl drains weakly, add enough water to cover the plunger cup and plunge with firm straight strokes.
steps.expect: the bowl water pulls down sharply.

steps.action: **Flush with observation.** Restore water, wait for the tank to fill, flush once, and watch both tank and bowl.
steps.expect: the tank empties quickly and the bowl clears.

recipes.verification: After two flushes, the handle lifts the flapper, the bowl clears fully, the tank refills to the fill line, and no water keeps running.

recipes.title: fix a wobbly ceiling fan
recipes.name: fix-a-wobbly-ceiling-fan
recipes.goal: A ceiling fan runs with minimal wobble after loose hardware, blade alignment, and balance are corrected.

steps.action: **Turn off the fan.** Let the blades stop completely and switch wall power off if tightening near wiring or the canopy.
steps.expect: the fan is still and controls are inactive.

steps.action: **Check the mount.** Gently hold the downrod or motor housing and look for ceiling-box movement.
steps.expect: the mount is solid, or unsafe movement is found.

steps.action: **Tighten visible screws.** Tighten blade bracket screws, blade screws, downrod set screws, and canopy screws.
steps.expect: no hardware turns loosely.

steps.action: **Clean the blades.** Wipe dust from the tops and edges of all blades.
steps.expect: blade weight is not affected by uneven dust.

steps.action: **Measure blade height.** Measure from ceiling to each blade tip at the same point.
steps.expect: blade tips are within about 1/8 inch of each other.

steps.action: **Correct bent brackets.** Gently adjust only a visibly bent bracket or replace a damaged blade.
steps.expect: blade tips sit at similar height.

steps.action: **Use a balance clip.** Run the fan on low, move the kit clip along the wobbliest blade, and find the quietest position.
steps.expect: wobble reduces at one clip location.

steps.action: **Add balance weight.** Stick the matching weight to the blade top at the tested position.
steps.expect: the fan runs smoother without the temporary clip.

recipes.verification: At low and medium speed, the fan runs for five minutes with no loose hardware noise and no visible mount movement at the ceiling.

recipes.title: fix a wobbly chair
recipes.name: fix-a-wobbly-chair
recipes.goal: The chair sits solid on a flat floor with no rock and no frame flex, either by correcting a short leg or by re-securing loose joints, and glides quietly on felt pads.

steps.action: **Diagnose: leg or joint.** Set the chair on the flat test surface and rock it corner to corner, then grip the backrest and seat and twist gently. [BRANCH: chair rocks but frame feels rigid: a short/long leg, go to step 2 | frame flexes, creaks, or a rail shifts in its socket: loose joint, go to step 3 | both: fix joints first, since re-gluing changes the leg geometry]
steps.expect: a clear verdict; mark the offending leg or joint with tape.

steps.action: **Correct a leg-length mismatch.** Identify the gap under one leg on the flat surface and measure it with feeler-style shims (folded paper). Fix by sticking a felt pad or a trimmed hard shim under the short leg. Sanding the three long legs to match is a last resort. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* wood removed cannot go back; sand in tiny passes with the chair re-tested on the flat surface after every pass, and expect to chase it around all four legs if you overdo one.
steps.expect: no rock in any direction on the test surface; skip to step 7.

steps.action: **Tighten mechanical fasteners first.** Flip the chair on a padded table. Snug every visible bolt, screw, and corner-block fastener. Snug means firm, not gorilla-tight; overtorquing strips wood threads.
steps.expect: wobble gone (done, go to step 7) or fasteners tight but a glued joint still moves (continue).

steps.action: **Open the loose glued joint.** Work the loose rail or spindle free with hand pressure and mallet taps on a padded block, opening it just enough to expose the mating surfaces. Only open joints that are actually loose; sound joints stay untouched.
steps.expect: tenon or dowel end visible, joint apart or hinged open.

steps.action: **Remove all old glue.** Scrape and lightly sand dried glue off the tenon and out of the socket down to bare wood. This is the step that decides the repair: new PVA glue does not bond to old cured glue, and gluing over it fails within weeks.
steps.expect: mating surfaces look and feel like bare wood, dry-fit is snug.

steps.action: **Glue, clamp, and square.** Coat both surfaces thinly, reassemble, wipe squeeze-out with a damp rag, and pull the frame tight with the band clamp around all four legs. Before walking away, set the chair upright on the flat surface and check it sits flat and the seat frame diagonals measure equal, then let it cure 24 hours undisturbed.
steps.expect: joints closed with a fine glue line, no rock while clamped, equal diagonals.

steps.action: **Fit felt pads and final-test.** Clean the leg feet, apply felt pads, set the chair on its real floor, rock-test and sit-test with full adult weight and a deliberate lean.
steps.expect: silent, solid seat; no movement under a twist.

recipes.verification: On a verified-flat surface the chair shows no rock in any direction, no frame movement under a firm twist at the backrest, and it holds a full-weight seated adult leaning side to side silently; felt pads are on all four feet.

recipes.title: fix a wobbly table
recipes.name: fix-a-wobbly-table
recipes.goal: The table stands steady under normal use by correcting a short leg, loose glide, or loose joint.

steps.action: **Find the wobble direction.** Press each corner gently and note which leg lifts or taps.
steps.expect: the short corner or loose area is identified.

steps.action: **Check the floor first.** Move the table a few inches and test again. [BRANCH: wobble follows table | wobble stays with floor] table means repair it, floor means shim for that location.
steps.expect: you know whether the problem is table or floor.

steps.action: **Inspect feet and glides.** Look for missing pads, backed-out glides, or damaged caps.
steps.expect: simple foot faults are visible.

steps.action: **Adjust or shim the short leg.** Turn adjustable glides or add thin felt under the short leg.
steps.expect: the tapping corner touches the floor.

steps.action: **Tighten joints.** Tighten bolts, screws, brackets, or apron fasteners a little at a time.
steps.expect: legs no longer twist by hand.

steps.action: **Re-glue loose wood joints.** Open the joint slightly, add wood glue, clamp square, and wipe squeeze-out.
steps.expect: the joint is clamped in alignment.

steps.action: **Retest under light load.** Set the table upright, place hands near opposite corners, and press normally.
steps.expect: the table stays steady.

recipes.verification: On its normal floor, the table does not rock when each corner is pressed and all joints remain tight under light load.

recipes.title: fold a fitted sheet
recipes.name: fold-a-fitted-sheet
recipes.goal: A fitted sheet folded into a flat, stackable rectangle instead of the usual resentful ball, via the corner-nesting technique that everyone claims is impossible and is actually four moves.

steps.action: **Find two adjacent corners along one short edge and put a hand inside each, seams facing you.** The sheet hangs from your hands like a limp puppet, inside-out pockets on your fists.
steps.expect: two cornered fists, elastic edge running between them, the rest of the sheet dangling.

steps.action: **Nest corner one over corner two.** Bring your hands together and flip the corner on your right hand over the one on your left, so one pocket swallows the other; the seam edges align.
steps.expect: one hand now wearing both corners as a single tidy pocket; the visible fold edge is straight.

steps.action: **Repeat for the other short edge, then nest the pairs.** Run your free hand down the elastic to the third corner, scoop it, nest the fourth over it as before; then flip that pair over the pair on your other hand.
steps.expect: all four corners stacked on one hand; the sheet now hangs as a rough half-square with one clean folded edge and one elastic-gathered edge.

steps.action: **Lay it down and square the shape.** On the table, arrange it into an approximate rectangle: the clean folded edge straight, the elastic curve folded inward so the gathered mess hides inside an L-shaped border.
steps.expect: a wobbly but recognizable rectangle with all chaos tucked into one interior curve.

steps.action: **Fold into thirds, then thirds again.** Fold the long sides inward over the elastic first (locking the mess inside), then fold the strip into thirds the other way. Smooth with flat palms between folds (`embodied/household/fold-a-tshirt`'s smoothing habit).
steps.expect: a flat, calm packet that looks indistinguishable from a folded flat sheet.

steps.action: **Store it inside its own pillowcase with the flat sheet.** The bedding-set-in-a-pillowcase trick: the whole set stays together, shelves stay tidy, and future-you grabs one bundle.
steps.expect: one pillowcase parcel per bedding set on the shelf.

recipes.verification: The sheet sits flat and rectangular with no elastic visible, stacks stably, fits inside its pillowcase with its set, and the fold took under two minutes without any negotiation with the fabric.

recipes.title: get a stuck ring off
recipes.name: get-a-stuck-ring-off
recipes.goal: A tight ring is removed from a finger without cutting skin, worsening swelling, or delaying urgent care.

steps.action: **Check circulation.** Look for color, warmth, sensation, and ability to move the fingertip.
steps.expect: finger is pink or normal-colored and responsive.

steps.action: **Reduce swelling.** Raise the hand above heart level for 5 to 10 minutes.
steps.expect: throbbing eases or swelling softens.

steps.action: **Cool the finger.** Run cold water over the hand or apply a cool pack briefly.
steps.expect: finger feels cooler but not numb.

steps.action: **Lubricate well.** Coat the finger and ring with soap, oil, lotion, or petroleum jelly.
steps.expect: ring rotates slightly.

steps.action: **Twist and pull.** Rotate the ring while easing it over the knuckle.
steps.expect: ring advances a little without sharp pain.

steps.action: **Use floss wrap.** Thread floss under the ring toward the hand, then wrap the finger snugly from ring to fingertip.
steps.expect: swollen tissue is compressed evenly.

steps.action: **Unwind through the ring.** Pull the under-ring floss end so the wrap unwinds and walks the ring over the knuckle.
steps.expect: ring moves outward with each turn.

steps.action: **Stop if unsafe.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* delayed care can cost circulation, so seek urgent help if the finger turns blue, numb, or very painful.
steps.expect: either ring is off or medical removal is chosen promptly.

recipes.verification: The ring is off, the finger has normal color and sensation, and any skin irritation is minor and clean.

recipes.title: get gum off a shoe
recipes.name: get-gum-off-a-shoe
recipes.goal: Chewing gum is removed from a shoe sole or tread with minimal residue and without spreading the sticky mess into a larger biography.

steps.action: **Keep the gum contained.** Do not step around on carpets or car mats. [BRANCH: fresh soft gum | old hard gum] chill soft gum first, scrape hard gum carefully.
steps.expect: the gum stays on the sole area you can clean.

steps.action: **Freeze the gum.** Put the shoe in a bag sole-side up in the freezer for 1 to 2 hours, or press an ice pack on the gum for 10 minutes.
steps.expect: the gum becomes firm and less stretchy.

steps.action: **Peel the main piece.** Use fingers, a spoon edge, or a dull scraper to lift the gum from one side.
steps.expect: a large piece comes away instead of smearing.

steps.action: **Pick the tread channels.** Work a toothpick or old toothbrush through grooves where gum remains.
steps.expect: the tread pattern is visible again.

steps.action: **Use oil for residue.** Rub a tiny amount of peanut butter or cooking oil into stubborn gum, wait two minutes, then scrape again.
steps.expect: sticky residue loosens into crumbs or streaks.

steps.action: **Wash the sole.** Scrub with dish soap and warm water to remove oil and sugar.
steps.expect: the sole feels rubbery, not slick.

steps.action: **Dry and inspect.** Pat dry, flex the sole, and check the tread under bright light. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* oil can stain suede, fabric, or porous uppers, so keep it only on the sole.
steps.expect: no gum strings stretch between tread blocks.

steps.action: **Clean the tools.** Wrap gum scraps in paper and discard them.
steps.expect: no sticky residue remains on the work surface.

recipes.verification: The shoe sole is dry, not sticky, and leaves no gum mark when pressed on scrap paper.

recipes.title: get rid of ants
recipes.name: get-rid-of-ants
recipes.goal: Ants are removed by finding the trail, cleaning the scent path, using bait for the colony, and sealing entry points.

steps.action: **Follow the trail.** Watch where ants travel for several minutes before cleaning.
steps.expect: you identify a food source, wall gap, window edge, or pipe opening.

steps.action: **Remove the food source.** Seal sugar, crumbs, pet food, and trash.
steps.expect: no exposed food remains near the trail.

steps.action: **Clean the scent path.** Wipe the trail with soapy water, then dry the surface.
steps.expect: fewer ants follow the exact old line.

steps.action: **Place bait near activity.** Set bait beside the trail but away from children, pets, and food-prep surfaces.
steps.expect: ants find bait without crossing clean counters.

steps.action: **Avoid spraying the trail after baiting.** Let worker ants carry bait back for several days. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* insecticide spray can scatter the colony and contaminate food surfaces, so do not spray where bait needs active foragers.
steps.expect: activity may rise briefly, then fall.

steps.action: **Seal entry points.** Caulk cracks, tighten door sweeps, or tape gaps temporarily after bait has started working.
steps.expect: fewer ants enter from the same point.

steps.action: **Monitor for a week.** Refresh bait as the label allows and keep surfaces clean.
steps.expect: traffic drops steadily or disappears.

recipes.verification: For 48 hours, no active ant trail appears at the original food source or entry point, and bait remains placed or removed according to its label.

recipes.title: get rid of cockroaches
recipes.name: get-rid-of-cockroaches
recipes.goal: Cockroach activity is reduced by removing food and water, using gel bait correctly, sealing entry points, monitoring results, and escalating when infestation signs are heavy.

steps.action: **Confirm the activity.** Look for live roaches, droppings like black pepper, egg cases, shed skins, and odor.
steps.expect: the problem area and severity are clearer.

steps.action: **Remove food access.** Seal pantry goods, wipe counters, clean under appliances, and take out trash nightly.
steps.expect: roaches have less loose food than bait.

steps.action: **Remove water access.** Fix drips, dry sinks at night, and empty pet water if practical.
steps.expect: fewer water sources remain overnight.

steps.action: **Skip repellent spray near bait.** Do not fog or spray baseboards where gel will go.
steps.expect: roaches are not driven away from bait or contaminated by repellent.

steps.action: **Place gel bait in small dots.** Put pea-sized dots in cracks, hinge corners, under sinks, behind appliances, and near droppings.
steps.expect: bait is hidden along travel paths, not smeared in open areas.

steps.action: **Seal entry and harborages.** Caulk cracks, add door sweeps, and pack pipe gaps with steel wool before sealing.
steps.expect: travel routes narrow and hiding spots shrink.

steps.action: **Set monitors.** Place sticky monitors behind appliances and under sinks, then date them.
steps.expect: catches show where activity continues.

steps.action: **Review after 1-2 weeks.** [BRANCH: fewer catches | same or more] refresh bait if fewer; call a pro if activity persists or spreads.
steps.expect: results are measured instead of guessed.

recipes.verification: After two weeks, monitors show sharply reduced or no roach catches, food and water sources are controlled nightly, and any persistent infestation has a professional scheduled.

recipes.title: get rid of fruit flies
recipes.name: get-rid-of-fruit-flies
recipes.goal: Fruit flies are trapped, their breeding source is removed, and the kitchen is set up to prevent a rebound.

steps.action: **Find the source.** Check ripe fruit, trash, recycling, compost, damp cloths, and forgotten potatoes or onions.
steps.expect: at least one feeding or breeding spot is found or ruled out.

steps.action: **Remove spoiled food.** Bag rotten produce and take it outside, not just into an indoor bin.
steps.expect: the strongest smell source leaves the kitchen.

steps.action: **Wash sticky surfaces.** Wipe counters, bin lids, bottle rings, and fruit bowls.
steps.expect: no sweet residue remains where flies land.

steps.action: **Set a vinegar trap.** Add apple cider vinegar and one drop dish soap to a cup, then cover with poked plastic wrap or a paper cone.
steps.expect: flies can enter and cannot easily escape.

steps.action: **Place traps near activity.** Put traps near fruit bowls, sinks, or bins, away from open windows.
steps.expect: flies gather around the trap within hours.

steps.action: **Check drains.** Pour boiling water down suspect drains and scrub the visible rim.
steps.expect: drain slime and odor are reduced.

steps.action: **Repeat for two days.** Refresh traps daily and keep counters dry.
steps.expect: fly count drops each day.

steps.action: **Prevent return.** Refrigerate ripe fruit, empty compost often, and rinse bottles before recycling.
steps.expect: no new swarm forms after traps are removed.

recipes.verification: No fruit flies are visible around fruit, sink, trash, or traps during a 2-minute kitchen check.

recipes.title: get rid of mice humanely
recipes.name: get-rid-of-mice-humanely
recipes.goal: Mice are addressed humanely by removing food access, sealing entry points, using live traps responsibly, and escalating when needed.

steps.action: **Confirm signs.** Look for droppings, gnaw marks, scratching sounds, or greasy rub marks along walls.
steps.expect: you can identify where mice travel.

steps.action: **Remove food access.** Store grains, pet food, and snacks in hard sealed containers and clean crumbs nightly.
steps.expect: counters, floors, and pantry shelves have no exposed food.

steps.action: **Find entry points.** Check gaps around pipes, doors, vents, baseboards, and foundations.
steps.expect: holes the size of a pencil or larger are marked for sealing.

steps.action: **Seal durable gaps.** Pack small holes with steel wool and seal over it; cover larger gaps with hardware cloth.
steps.expect: material cannot be pushed aside by a finger.

steps.action: **Set live traps on travel paths.** Place traps against walls with bait such as peanut butter or oats.
steps.expect: trap entrances face the route mice already use.

steps.action: **Check traps often.** Inspect at least twice daily and follow local release rules for distance and habitat. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* releasing animals in the wrong place may be illegal or fatal to them, so confirm local rules before trapping.
steps.expect: trapped mice are not left without water or exposed to heat or cold.

steps.action: **Escalate if activity continues.** Call a humane pest professional for repeated captures, nests, or building-wide problems.
steps.expect: a plan covers exclusion, sanitation, and monitoring.

recipes.verification: For 7 days, no new droppings, gnaw marks, nighttime scratching, or trap captures appear after food is sealed and entry points are closed.

recipes.title: get wrinkles out without an iron
recipes.name: get-wrinkles-out-without-an-iron
recipes.goal: Wrinkles are relaxed from clothing using steam, moisture, and tension without using an iron.

steps.action: **Check the fabric.** Read the label and inspect for stains before adding heat or moisture.
steps.expect: fabric can tolerate the selected method.

steps.action: **Choose a method.** Use [BRANCH: shower steam | dryer tumble | spray-and-hang] based on fabric and available time.
steps.expect: one wrinkle-release path is selected.

steps.action: **Hang with tension.** Place the garment on a broad hanger and smooth seams, collar, and placket by hand.
steps.expect: the garment hangs straight without folded sections.

steps.action: **Add controlled moisture.** Steam in a bathroom, tumble with a damp towel, or mist lightly from 8-12 inches away.
steps.expect: wrinkled areas become slightly damp or warm, not soaked.

steps.action: **Smooth by hand.** Pull fabric gently along grain lines and flatten collars, cuffs, and hems.
steps.expect: wrinkles visibly soften while the fabric is warm or damp.

steps.action: **Let it dry undisturbed.** Keep the garment hanging with airflow until fully dry.
steps.expect: fabric holds the smoother shape.

steps.action: **Repeat targeted areas.** Re-mist stubborn wrinkles and smooth again rather than soaking the whole garment.
steps.expect: remaining creases are reduced without water spots.

recipes.verification: The garment is fully dry, hangs smoothly from shoulders to hem, and has no visible water spots or heat damage.

recipes.title: give a cat a pill
recipes.name: give-a-cat-a-pill
recipes.goal: Give a cat one prescribed pill safely and confirm it was swallowed, with minimal fear and no dosing mistake.

steps.action: **Verify the dose.** Read the label, cat name, tablet count, and timing before opening the medication.
steps.expect: the pill in your hand matches the prescription.

steps.action: **Try the food method first if allowed.** Hide the pill in a tiny treat or wet food bite before the full meal.
steps.expect: the cat eats the medicated bite completely or refuses it clearly.

steps.action: **Set up gentle restraint.** If needed, place the cat on a stable surface or wrap the body in a towel with the head free.
steps.expect: the cat is contained without chest compression or panic.

steps.action: **Place the pill behind the tongue.** Tilt the head slightly up, open the mouth from the corners, place the pill far back, and close the mouth.
steps.expect: the cat licks the nose or swallows.

steps.action: **Follow with food or water.** Offer wet food, a treat, or the vet-recommended water chaser.
steps.expect: the pill moves down and the cat does not spit it out.

steps.action: **Check the area.** Look on the floor, fur, towel, and food bowl for the pill.
steps.expect: no pill is found and the dose can be recorded.

recipes.verification: The prescribed dose is no longer visible, the cat has swallowed and is breathing normally, and the dose time is recorded.

recipes.title: give a pet a pill
recipes.name: give-a-pet-a-pill
recipes.goal: Give a prescribed pill to a pet reliably, with the least stressful method that is safe for the medication and the animal.

steps.action: **Read the label first.** Confirm pet name, pill count, dose, timing, and whether it must be given with food or on an empty stomach.
steps.expect: the pill in your hand matches the prescription instructions.

steps.action: **Try the food method if allowed.** [BRANCH: hide in food | use direct method] tuck the pill inside a tiny soft treat, wet food ball, or pill pocket so the first bite is small enough to swallow whole.
steps.expect: the pet eats the dose without chewing around it.

steps.action: **Check for leftovers.** Look at the bowl, floor, lips, and cheek area for a spit-out pill before assuming it worked.
steps.expect: no pill or fragments are visible.

steps.action: **Position for the direct method.** If food fails or is not allowed, sit the pet facing away from escape, steady the head gently, and keep your fingers away from the biting surfaces.
steps.expect: the pet is controlled but still breathing easily and not pinned in panic.

steps.action: **Tilt and drop.** Lift the muzzle just enough that the nose points slightly upward, open the lower jaw, and place or drop the pill far back over the tongue.
steps.expect: the pill lands behind the tongue rather than at the front of the mouth.

steps.action: **Hold until swallowed.** Close the mouth gently, lower the head to a natural angle, stroke the throat, and watch for a lick, swallow, or nose lick.
steps.expect: the pet makes a clear swallow motion before you release fully.

steps.action: **Follow with water or food.** Give a small water chaser by syringe into the cheek pouch, or offer a bite of food if the vet allows it, especially for cats.
steps.expect: the pill moves down instead of sitting in the throat.

steps.action: **Use refusal tricks calmly.** If the pet spits it out, try a smaller food wrapper, a pill gun taught by a vet, a second treat immediately after the first, or a compounding pharmacy flavor option.
steps.expect: the retry changes the delivery path without turning into a chase.

steps.action: **Record the dose.** Mark the medication chart, note any vomiting or refusal, and store the remaining pills safely.
steps.expect: the next caregiver can tell whether the dose was given.

recipes.verification: The prescribed pill is no longer visible, the pet has swallowed and taken a water or food follow-up if allowed, and the dose is logged.

recipes.title: grow garlic
recipes.name: grow-garlic
recipes.goal: Plant garlic cloves in fall or the proper local season, grow them through dormancy and spring growth, and harvest cured bulbs for storage.

steps.action: **Choose seed garlic.** Buy seed garlic or locally adapted bulbs and keep cloves intact until planting day.
steps.expect: cloves are firm, large, and disease-free.

steps.action: **Prepare the bed.** Loosen soil, remove weeds, and mix in compost without leaving soggy pockets.
steps.expect: the planting area is loose and drains well.

steps.action: **Separate cloves.** Break bulbs into individual cloves and keep the papery skins on.
steps.expect: each clove has an intact base plate.

steps.action: **Plant point up.** Set cloves 2-3 inches deep and 4-6 inches apart, with the pointed end upward.
steps.expect: rows or clusters are evenly spaced.

steps.action: **Mulch after planting.** Cover with straw, shredded leaves, or similar mulch once soil cools.
steps.expect: cloves are insulated and weeds are suppressed.

steps.action: **Water during active growth.** Keep soil evenly moist in spring, then reduce watering as lower leaves begin yellowing.
steps.expect: plants grow strong leaves before bulbing.

steps.action: **Remove hardneck scapes.** Cut curling scapes when they form and use them in the kitchen.
steps.expect: hardneck plants direct more energy to bulbs.

steps.action: **Harvest and cure.** Lift bulbs when several lower leaves brown, then cure in a dry airy shaded place.
steps.expect: wrappers dry and bulbs store without rotting.

recipes.verification: Garlic cloves are planted point-up at proper spacing in well-drained soil, mulched, watered during spring growth, and harvested when lower leaves brown with bulbs cured dry.

recipes.title: grow microgreens
recipes.name: grow-microgreens
recipes.goal: Grow edible microgreens indoors in a shallow tray and harvest them cleanly at the first true leaf stage.

steps.action: **Sanitize the tray.** Wash reusable trays and tools before planting.
steps.expect: surfaces are clean before seeds touch them.

steps.action: **Prepare the medium.** Add 1-2 inches of moist seed-starting mix or place a moistened grow mat in the tray.
steps.expect: the surface is evenly damp and level.

steps.action: **Sow densely but evenly.** Scatter seeds across the surface without thick piles, then press them gently for contact.
steps.expect: seeds cover the tray in a single even layer.

steps.action: **Cover for germination.** Use a lid, second tray, or towel according to the crop for the first few days.
steps.expect: humidity stays high and seeds begin sprouting.

steps.action: **Move into light.** Remove the cover when seedlings lift it or most seeds germinate, then place under bright light.
steps.expect: shoots turn green and stand upright.

steps.action: **Water from below.** Add water to the bottom tray and pour off excess after the medium absorbs moisture.
steps.expect: stems stay cleaner and roots stay moist.

steps.action: **Harvest at the right stage.** Cut just above the medium when cotyledons are open and first true leaves begin.
steps.expect: greens are tender and flavorful.

steps.action: **Store or use promptly.** Keep harvested greens dry in a covered refrigerator container or eat immediately.
steps.expect: microgreens remain crisp and clean.

recipes.verification: Microgreens are grown from food-safe seed in a clean tray, have green upright shoots, show no mold or sour odor, and are harvested with clean scissors above the medium.

recipes.title: grow potatoes in a bag
recipes.name: grow-potatoes-in-a-bag
recipes.goal: Grow potatoes in a fabric grow bag or large container by planting seed potatoes, hilling gradually, watering evenly, and harvesting clean tubers.

steps.action: **Chit or inspect seed potatoes.** Use firm disease-free seed pieces with at least one strong sprout or eye.
steps.expect: planting pieces are viable and not rotting.

steps.action: **Prepare the bag.** Roll down the sides and add 4-6 inches of moist potting mix.
steps.expect: the bag is stable with a shallow planting layer.

steps.action: **Plant seed pieces.** Place pieces sprout side up about 8-10 inches apart and cover with 3-4 inches of mix.
steps.expect: seed pieces are covered but not buried too deeply.

steps.action: **Water gently.** Moisten the mix evenly without leaving the bag waterlogged.
steps.expect: water drains from the bottom.

steps.action: **Hill as stems grow.** Add mix or compost around stems when they reach about 6-8 inches tall, leaving top leaves exposed.
steps.expect: buried stems have room to form more tubers.

steps.action: **Feed and water consistently.** Fertilize lightly as directed and keep soil evenly moist during tuber formation.
steps.expect: foliage grows steadily without wilting.

steps.action: **Watch for maturity.** Stop hilling when the bag is near full and reduce watering after foliage yellows naturally.
steps.expect: skins begin to set before harvest.

steps.action: **Harvest carefully.** Dump the bag onto a tarp after plants die back, or gently take new potatoes earlier from the side.
steps.expect: potatoes separate from loose mix with minimal bruising.

recipes.verification: The grow bag drains freely, seed potatoes sprout, stems are hilled while leaves remain exposed, soil stays evenly moist, and harvested tubers are firm and not green.

recipes.title: grow tomatoes in a pot
recipes.name: grow-tomatoes-in-a-pot
recipes.goal: Grow a tomato plant in a draining container with enough soil, support, sun, water, and feeding to produce healthy fruit.

steps.action: **Choose the right tomato.** Select a healthy determinate or patio tomato for compact spaces, or a larger indeterminate only if you can support it well.
steps.expect: the plant has sturdy green growth and no obvious pests.

steps.action: **Prepare the container.** Use a clean pot at least 12-18 inches wide with open drainage holes and fill partway with fresh potting mix.
steps.expect: water can leave the pot and the mix is loose.

steps.action: **Plant deeply.** Remove the lowest leaves and bury the stem so only the top leaf clusters remain above the mix.
steps.expect: the seedling sits upright with buried stem ready to root.

steps.action: **Add support early.** Install a cage, stake, or small trellis before roots spread.
steps.expect: the support is firm and does not wobble in the pot.

steps.action: **Water thoroughly.** Soak the mix until water drains from the bottom, then let the top inch dry before watering again.
steps.expect: the whole root zone is moist without standing water.

steps.action: **Mulch the surface.** Add straw, shredded leaves, or compost mulch while keeping it slightly away from the stem.
steps.expect: soil surface is shaded and the stem base remains clear.

steps.action: **Feed on schedule.** Apply tomato fertilizer after planting according to the label, reducing nitrogen if the plant grows leaves but few flowers.
steps.expect: growth is steady and flower clusters form.

steps.action: **Monitor weekly.** Tie loose stems, remove yellow lower leaves, check leaf undersides, and harvest ripe fruit promptly.
steps.expect: the plant stays supported, ventilated, and productive.

recipes.verification: The tomato is in a draining pot of adequate size, receives direct sun, is supported before heavy growth, has evenly moist soil, and produces flowers or fruit without collapse.

recipes.title: hand wash delicate clothes
recipes.name: hand-wash-delicate-clothes
recipes.goal: Delicate clothing is cleaned gently, rinsed fully, and dried flat without stretching, felting, or color transfer.

steps.action: **Read the care label.** Check fiber, water temperature, and drying instructions before wetting the garment.
steps.expect: the label does not say dry clean only or do not wash.

steps.action: **Test dye stability.** Dab an inside seam with a wet white cloth and mild detergent.
steps.expect: no visible dye transfers to the cloth.

steps.action: **Fill cool water.** Add cool water to a clean basin and mix in a small amount of mild detergent.
steps.expect: the water feels slippery but has little foam.

steps.action: **Submerge and soak.** Press the garment under water for 5-10 minutes without twisting.
steps.expect: fibers are fully wet and soil begins to loosen.

steps.action: **Agitate gently.** Swish the garment and squeeze sudsy water through stained areas with open hands.
steps.expect: cloudy water or loosened soil appears without fabric distortion.

steps.action: **Drain and support.** Lift the garment from underneath while draining the basin.
steps.expect: the wet fabric is not hanging from one stretched point.

steps.action: **Rinse repeatedly.** Refill with cool clean water and press out suds until the rinse water stays clear.
steps.expect: no slippery detergent remains in the fabric.

steps.action: **Remove water by rolling.** Lay the garment on a towel, roll it up, and press the roll.
steps.expect: the garment is damp rather than dripping.

steps.action: **Dry flat to shape.** Lay it on a dry towel or mesh rack and reshape seams, cuffs, and hem.
steps.expect: the garment dries in its normal dimensions.

recipes.verification: The garment is clean-smelling, free of visible suds, reshaped to its original outline, and drying flat without dripping.

recipes.title: hang a heavy mirror
recipes.name: hang-a-heavy-mirror
recipes.goal: A heavy mirror is hung level on hardware rated for its weight, anchored into studs or suitable heavy-duty wall anchors.

steps.action: **Weigh or verify the mirror.** Check the label or weigh yourself with and without the mirror.
steps.expect: you have a weight number for hardware selection.

steps.action: **Inspect the hanger.** [BRANCH: D-rings | French cleat | wire] use two D-rings or a cleat for heavy mirrors; avoid light picture wire unless rated by the maker.
steps.expect: the mirror has sound attachment points.

steps.action: **Choose the height.** Mark the desired top edge and centerline with painter's tape.
steps.expect: the placement is visible before drilling.

steps.action: **Find studs.** Use a stud finder, then confirm by measuring likely 16 inch or 24 inch spacing.
steps.expect: at least one stud location is marked.

steps.action: **Choose anchors.** Use screws into studs where possible; use toggle or heavy hollow-wall anchors only if rated for the wall and mirror weight.
steps.expect: selected hardware rating exceeds the mirror weight.

steps.action: **Mark hanger points.** Measure from the mirror top to the D-rings or cleat, transfer points to the wall, and check level.
steps.expect: holes align with the mirror hardware.

steps.action: **Drill pilot holes.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm height, level, and no hidden electrical or plumbing before drilling.
steps.expect: clean holes sized for screws or anchors.

steps.action: **Install mounting hardware.** Drive stud screws or set anchors exactly as directed, leaving screw heads proud only if the hanger requires it.
steps.expect: hardware does not wobble under hand pressure.

steps.action: **Hang with a helper.** Lift the mirror onto both points or the cleat without sliding across the wall.
steps.expect: both sides catch securely.

steps.action: **Level and tug-test.** Adjust if allowed, then apply a gentle downward and outward test.
steps.expect: the mirror stays level and firmly seated.

recipes.verification: The mirror remains level after a gentle tug test, with all weight carried by rated hardware and no visible wall movement.

recipes.title: hang a picture
recipes.name: hang-a-picture
recipes.goal: A picture hangs level, at the right height, on a fixing that matches the wall type and the frame's weight, without a hidden pipe or cable being the surprise.

steps.action: **Choose the spot at the right height.** Gallery convention: the picture's center at about 145 to 152 cm from the floor (eye level); above furniture: 15 to 25 cm above its top edge. Hold the picture up, or cut a paper template, and step back to judge.
steps.expect: a pencil tick marking the picture's intended top-center.

steps.action: **Find the actual fixing point from the hanging hardware.** Pull the wire taut upward as it will hang, or measure D-ring positions; the fixing point sits *below* the frame's top edge by that offset. Transfer the measurement down from your top-center tick.
steps.expect: a pencil cross where the hook or screw actually goes, which is not where the frame's top will be.

steps.action: **Check what is inside the wall before making any hole.** Detector pass, or the heuristics: avoid the vertical and horizontal lines running from sockets and switches, and the zones directly above and beside sinks and radiators. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* drilling into a cable or pipe converts a picture into an electrician or a flood; thirty seconds of checking is the whole insurance.
steps.expect: a clear spot, or a relocated pencil cross.

steps.action: **Install the fixing for the wall type.** Solid masonry: drill the plug's stated diameter, insert plug flush, drive the screw leaving a few millimeters proud. Hollow drywall: appropriate anchor per its instructions. Light frame on wood or plaster: a picture hook nailed at its angle. Two-ring heavy frames: two fixings, leveled against each other with the tape and level.
steps.expect: a fixing that does not wiggle, sized to the frame's weight class.

steps.action: **Hang and level.** Wire or rings onto the fixing, then the level on the frame's top edge, nudging corners until the bubble centers.
steps.expect: level frame; wire-hung frames stay adjustable, ring-hung ones are as level as your two fixings.

steps.action: **Clean up and pressure-test gently.** Pencil marks erased or hidden, dust swept, and a light downward hand-press on the frame.
steps.expect: no shift, no plaster crumbs trickling, wall around the fixing intact.

recipes.verification: The picture hangs level at the planned height, the fixing matches wall and weight, a gentle press moves nothing, no marks remain, and nothing inside the wall objected.

recipes.title: hang a shelf
recipes.name: hang-a-shelf
recipes.goal: A wall shelf is mounted level, fastened to structure or appropriate anchors, and loaded within its safe weight limit.

steps.action: **Estimate the load.** Add the shelf weight and what will sit on it, then include a safety margin.
steps.expect: you have a target load category: light, medium, or heavy.

steps.action: **Find studs or structure.** Use a stud finder, outlet clues, or small test holes where hidden by the bracket.
steps.expect: stud edges or masonry locations are marked.

steps.action: **Choose fasteners by load.** [BRANCH: stud screws for heavy | rated hollow-wall anchors for medium | small anchors for light]
steps.expect: fastener ratings meet or exceed the planned load.

steps.action: **Mark bracket height.** Hold the shelf or rail where it belongs and mark one hole.
steps.expect: the first mark is at the intended height and clear of hazards.

steps.action: **Level the layout.** Use a level to mark the remaining holes from the first mark.
steps.expect: marks line up horizontally and match the bracket spacing.

steps.action: **Check for hidden services.** Avoid drilling directly above outlets, switches, plumbing fixtures, or known pipes.
steps.expect: the drill path is reasonably clear.

steps.action: **Drill pilot holes.** Use a bit sized for the screw or anchor, keeping the drill square to the wall.
steps.expect: holes are clean and at the marks.

steps.action: **Install anchors or screws.** Set anchors flush or drive screws into studs, leaving brackets snug but adjustable.
steps.expect: brackets hold position without spinning.

steps.action: **Level and tighten.** Place the level on the shelf, adjust, then tighten all fasteners.
steps.expect: the bubble is centered and brackets no longer shift.

steps.action: **Load gradually.** Add items in stages, heaviest near brackets. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overloaded anchors can tear drywall, so stop if the shelf sags or fasteners move.
steps.expect: the shelf remains level and quiet under normal load.

recipes.verification: The shelf is level, fasteners are tight, and the planned load sits on it without sagging, shifting, or wall damage.

recipes.title: hang curtains
recipes.name: hang-curtains
recipes.goal: A curtain rod is mounted level and secure, sized and positioned by the standard proportion rules, with panels that hang to the intended length and draw fully clear of the glass.

steps.action: **Measure the window and apply the placement rules.** Width: rod extends 15-25 cm past the frame on each side so open panels stack on wall, not glass. Height: brackets 10-15 cm above the frame top, or two-thirds of the way from frame to ceiling for a taller look. Record rod length, bracket height, and floor-to-bracket drop.
steps.expect: three written numbers; rod length equals frame width plus both side extensions.

steps.action: **Buy to the measurements.** Rod rated for the span (spans over 120 cm need a center support bracket). Panel math: total panel width 1.5-2x the rod span for proper fullness; skimpier looks flat when closed. Length: floor-length panels should kiss the floor or float at most 1 cm above; "high-water" panels ending mid-wall are the classic regret. When between stock lengths, buy long; hemming down is easy, adding length is not.
steps.expect: rod, matching brackets (three for wide spans), and panels totaling 1.5-2x span width.

steps.action: **Mark the first bracket.** Measure up from the floor (not down from the ceiling) to the bracket height at one side of the window, at the planned side-extension distance, and mark.
steps.expect: one pencil mark at the recorded height and offset.

steps.action: **Mark the second bracket level with the first.** Measure the same floor-to-mark height on the other side, then verify by holding the rod with the level across both marks. If the ceiling line is visibly out of level, split the difference between true level and ceiling-parallel; a rod that fights a crooked ceiling looks worse than one that is slightly off-level.
steps.expect: bubble centered (or a deliberate compromise line); marks at equal floor heights.

steps.action: **Check what is behind each mark.** Run the stud finder; also check for hidden pipes and wires near the frame edges (headers above windows often contain a lintel that takes screws well). [BRANCH: mark lands on stud or solid lintel: screws go straight in | hollow drywall: use rated anchors, self-drilling or toggle type, not the flimsy ribbed plugs bundled with cheap rods]
steps.expect: fastening plan per hole; no drilling planned over a suspected cable drop.

steps.action: **Drill pilot holes and mount the brackets.** Hold each bracket to its mark, transfer screw-hole positions, drill pilots (or set anchors), and screw brackets snug. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* holes in the wall; re-measure both marks and re-check the level line once more before drilling.
steps.expect: brackets tight to the wall with no wiggle under a firm tug.

steps.action: **Dress the rod and seat it.** Thread panels (and center bracket ring allocation: split rings evenly each side of a center support) onto the rod on the floor, then seat the rod in the brackets and tighten set screws.
steps.expect: rod seated, finials on, panels sliding freely past everything except the center support.

steps.action: **Hem check after hanging.** Let panels hang 2-3 days so folds and length settle, then pin the hem at kiss-the-floor or 1 cm float and hem (sew, iron-on tape, or a tailor). Steam out packing creases.
steps.expect: even hem line along the full width; no puddling unless deliberately styled.

recipes.verification: The rod passes a level check and a firm downward tug on each bracket; panels drawn open clear the glass entirely; drawn closed they meet with fullness and hem 0-1 cm off the floor evenly across the width.

recipes.title: hang string lights
recipes.name: hang-string-lights
recipes.goal: Hang string lights along a planned path so they are supported safely, powered correctly, and working before final use.

steps.action: **Test the lights first.** Plug them in at ground level, confirm every section works, then unplug them.
steps.expect: bad bulbs or dead strands are found before hanging.

steps.action: **Plan the path.** Lay out the route and mark support points every few feet with enough slack for gentle curves.
steps.expect: the full span reaches the outlet without tight pulls.

steps.action: **Check the rating.** [BRANCH: indoor | outdoor] use outdoor-rated lights and cords outside, and keep indoor-only lights indoors.
steps.expect: the label matches the location.

steps.action: **Calculate the load.** Add the wattage of connected strands and compare it with the product limit and outlet circuit. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overheated wiring can cause fire, so do not exceed listed limits or daisy-chain beyond the label.
steps.expect: the planned connection is within the safe limit.

steps.action: **Install hooks or clips.** Fasten hooks into solid trim, posts, or anchors, not into the electrical cord.
steps.expect: each support point is firm when tugged lightly.

steps.action: **Hang without staples.** Place the cord on hooks or clips and never staple, nail, pinch, or pierce it.
steps.expect: insulation is intact and the cord hangs freely.

steps.action: **Keep plugs protected.** Position plug connections off the ground and away from puddles.
steps.expect: connections are dry and not strained.

steps.action: **Secure loose spans.** Add supports where the strand sags into walking paths or rubs on a sharp edge.
steps.expect: lights stay clear of heads, doors, and abrasion points.

steps.action: **Plug in and inspect.** Turn the lights on and walk the full route.
steps.expect: bulbs light evenly and no plug, cord, or socket feels warm after several minutes.

steps.action: **Set normal use.** Add an outdoor-rated timer if desired and turn lights off when unattended for long periods.
steps.expect: the lights operate from a controlled, accessible switch or timer.

recipes.verification: The lights are supported by hooks or clips, rated for their location, within electrical load limits, and run for 10 minutes without flicker, heat, or tripping.

recipes.title: hang wallpaper
recipes.name: hang-wallpaper
recipes.goal: Wallpaper drops are measured, pasted, hung plumb, smoothed flat, and trimmed neatly at edges.

steps.action: **Plan the first line.** Mark a plumb line near the starting corner rather than trusting the corner itself.
steps.expect: a vertical guide is visible.

steps.action: **Measure and cut with overlap.** Cut the first drop to wall height plus top and bottom overlap.
steps.expect: the drop is long enough for trimming.

steps.action: **Paste the paper or wall.** [BRANCH: paste-the-paper | paste-the-wall] follow the roll label exactly for paste location and soak time.
steps.expect: adhesive is even with dry edges avoided.

steps.action: **Book the paper if required.** Fold pasted sides together without creasing and wait the listed time.
steps.expect: the paper relaxes and expands evenly.

steps.action: **Hang the first drop plumb.** Align one edge to the guide, leaving overlap at ceiling and skirting.
steps.expect: the drop hangs straight with extra at both ends.

steps.action: **Smooth out bubbles.** Brush from the center outward, wiping paste from the face with a damp sponge.
steps.expect: the surface lies flat without trapped air.

steps.action: **Trim edges sharply.** Press into corners with a straightedge and cut with a fresh blade. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the paper has not shifted before cutting.
steps.expect: ceiling and base edges are clean.

steps.action: **Match and hang the next drop.** Align the pattern at eye level first, butt seams without overlap, smooth, and trim.
steps.expect: the seam is tight and the pattern continues.

recipes.verification: The hung drops are plumb, seams are butted, bubbles are smoothed, and trimmed edges are clean after the paste begins to set.

recipes.title: harvest and store vegetables
recipes.name: harvest-and-store-vegetables
recipes.goal: Harvest vegetables at good eating quality and store each crop in conditions that preserve flavor, texture, and safety.

steps.action: **Harvest during the cool part of day.** Pick in the morning or evening when crops are hydrated and heat stress is low.
steps.expect: produce is crisp and not sun-warmed.

steps.action: **Use clean cuts.** Snip stems for greens, herbs, peppers, squash, and tomatoes rather than tearing plants.
steps.expect: plants and harvested vegetables have minimal damage.

steps.action: **Sort as you pick.** Separate bruised, pest-damaged, or diseased produce from sound produce.
steps.expect: storage containers hold only good-quality vegetables.

steps.action: **Brush off soil.** Remove loose dirt outdoors and avoid washing storage crops unless needed.
steps.expect: produce is cleaner without added surface moisture.

steps.action: **Cool perishable crops.** Refrigerate leafy greens, peas, beans, broccoli, cucumbers, and herbs soon after harvest.
steps.expect: tender vegetables stop wilting.

steps.action: **Keep dry-storage crops dry.** Cure onions, garlic, potatoes, winter squash, and sweet potatoes as appropriate before longer storage.
steps.expect: skins or necks are dry enough for storage.

steps.action: **Match storage conditions.** Store tomatoes at room temperature until fully ripe, greens in humid refrigeration, and roots in cool humid conditions.
steps.expect: each crop is placed where it keeps best.

steps.action: **Check stored produce.** Inspect every few days and remove soft, moldy, or leaking items.
steps.expect: one failing vegetable does not spoil the rest.

recipes.verification: Harvested vegetables are cleanly cut, sorted, placed in crop-appropriate storage, labeled if needed, and checked so damaged produce is not mixed with sound produce.

recipes.title: hem trousers with iron on tape
recipes.name: hem-trousers-with-iron-on-tape
recipes.goal: Trouser hems are shortened evenly with fusible hem tape and a crisp fold.

steps.action: **Try on and mark length.** Wear the trousers with shoes and mark the desired finished hem on both legs.
steps.expect: both legs have visible length marks.

steps.action: **Measure both legs.** Lay trousers flat and compare inseam lengths from crotch seam to marks.
steps.expect: marks are even or intentionally adjusted for posture.

steps.action: **Set the fold.** Turn each leg inside out and fold the hem to the marked finished length.
steps.expect: the fold line matches the chosen length around each leg.

steps.action: **Press the crease.** Use label-safe heat and a pressing cloth to crease the fold. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* high heat can scorch or shine fabric; confirm the fiber setting first.
steps.expect: the new hem crease stays in place.

steps.action: **Trim excess if needed.** Leave at least 1-1/2 inches of allowance before cutting bulky extra fabric. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cut fabric cannot be restored; confirm both legs twice before trimming.
steps.expect: each leg has a manageable, even allowance.

steps.action: **Insert hem tape.** Place fusible tape inside the fold, set back from the visible edge.
steps.expect: tape is hidden and does not protrude.

steps.action: **Fuse in sections.** Press with the damp cloth for the tape label time without sliding the iron. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* melted adhesive can mark fabric; test a hidden area first.
steps.expect: the folded allowance bonds to the trouser leg.

steps.action: **Cool flat.** Leave the hem untouched until fully cool.
steps.expect: adhesive sets without lifting.

steps.action: **Check the outside.** Turn trousers right side out and inspect the hem line.
steps.expect: both hems are even with no adhesive bleed-through.

recipes.verification: Both trouser legs measure the same finished inseam, the hems stay bonded after cooling, and no adhesive or scorch marks are visible outside.

recipes.title: install a bidet attachment
recipes.name: install-a-bidet-attachment
recipes.goal: A non-electric bidet attachment is mounted under the toilet seat and connected to the toilet supply without leaks.

steps.action: **Shut off water.** Turn the toilet shutoff valve clockwise, then flush to drain most tank water.
steps.expect: the tank does not refill.

steps.action: **Place a towel.** Put a towel and bucket below the fill-valve connection under the tank.
steps.expect: small spills are contained.

steps.action: **Disconnect the supply at the tank.** Loosen the nut where the supply line meets the toilet fill valve.
steps.expect: the tank inlet threads are exposed.

steps.action: **Install the tee valve.** Fit the tee valve with the correct washer onto the tank inlet and hand-tighten straight.
steps.expect: the tee sits squarely below the tank.

steps.action: **Reconnect the toilet supply.** Attach the existing supply line to the bottom or side of the tee as instructed.
steps.expect: the supply line is not kinked or twisted.

steps.action: **Remove the toilet seat.** Open bolt caps, loosen the seat bolts, and lift the seat away.
steps.expect: the bowl mounting holes are open.

steps.action: **Mount the bidet plate.** Place the attachment brackets over the bolt holes, reinstall the seat, and align the nozzle guard centered in the bowl.
steps.expect: the seat rests flat.

steps.action: **Connect the bidet hose.** Attach one end to the tee and the other to the bidet inlet with washers in place.
steps.expect: both hose nuts thread by hand.

steps.action: **Restore water slowly.** Open the shutoff a quarter turn at a time while watching all connections.
steps.expect: no dripping appears at the tee, hose, or tank.

steps.action: **Adjust and test.** Turn the bidet control briefly while seated aside or with the seat lowered as the manual directs.
steps.expect: spray starts, stops, and aims into the bowl.

recipes.verification: After five minutes under pressure and three short spray tests, the seat is stable, the spray lands in the bowl, and every connection is dry.

recipes.title: install a smart bulb
recipes.name: install-a-smart-bulb
recipes.goal: A smart bulb is installed in a compatible fixture, paired to its app, named clearly, and ready for routine control.

steps.action: **Check compatibility.** Confirm socket size, enclosed-fixture rating, dimmer support, and voltage.
steps.expect: the bulb is safe for this fixture.

steps.action: **Turn off the fixture.** Use the wall switch and let any old bulb cool.
steps.expect: the bulb can be touched safely.

steps.action: **Install the bulb.** Screw the smart bulb in by the base, not the glass or diffuser.
steps.expect: the bulb sits snug without forcing.

steps.action: **Turn power on.** Switch the fixture on and leave it on for pairing.
steps.expect: the bulb lights or blinks in setup mode.

steps.action: **Open the app.** Sign in if required and choose add device or add bulb.
steps.expect: the app begins searching or shows setup instructions.

steps.action: **Choose network band.** [BRANCH: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi | hub or Thread] use 2.4 GHz for most Wi-Fi bulbs, or pair through the required hub or border router.
steps.expect: the bulb appears for pairing.

steps.action: **Pair the bulb.** Follow the app prompts, enter Wi-Fi details if needed, and wait for confirmation.
steps.expect: the app shows the bulb online.

steps.action: **Name and place it.** Give it a room and plain name like "Desk lamp" or "Porch light."
steps.expect: controls are easy to find.

steps.action: **Group if useful.** Add the bulb to an existing room, group, or scene.
steps.expect: grouped controls affect the intended lights only.

steps.action: **Test controls.** Turn the bulb off and on from the app, then adjust brightness or color if supported.
steps.expect: the bulb responds within a few seconds.

recipes.verification: The bulb turns on and off from the app, appears in the correct room or group, and still responds after the wall switch has remained on for one minute.

recipes.title: install a towel rail
recipes.name: install-a-towel-rail
recipes.goal: A towel rail is mounted level, fixed into anchors suited to the wall, and strong enough for normal towel pull.

steps.action: **Choose the location.** Hold the rail at usable height and check clearance for hanging towels.
steps.expect: the rail fits without hitting nearby fixtures.

steps.action: **Scan for pipes and wires.** Use a detector and consider plumbing routes near sinks, showers, and radiators.
steps.expect: the fixing points avoid likely services.

steps.action: **Mark level fixing points.** Use the template or brackets, then check with a level.
steps.expect: marks are level and spaced to match the rail.

steps.action: **Select wall anchors.** [BRANCH: stud | hollow wall | masonry or tile] use screws into studs, cavity anchors for hollow walls, and masonry or tile bits for solid surfaces.
steps.expect: fixings match the wall material.

steps.action: **Drill pilot holes.** Drill straight at the marked points, using tape on tile and the correct bit size. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the marks and service scan before drilling.
steps.expect: holes are clean and correctly spaced.

steps.action: **Set anchors and brackets.** Insert anchors flush and screw brackets tight without cracking tile or plaster.
steps.expect: brackets do not wiggle.

steps.action: **Attach the rail.** Fit the rail onto brackets and tighten grub screws or end caps.
steps.expect: the rail is level and fully seated.

steps.action: **Test the pull.** Pull down and outward with moderate hand force, then hang a towel.
steps.expect: the rail stays firm and the towel hangs clear.

recipes.verification: The towel rail is level, brackets are firm, and it holds a wet towel plus a moderate hand pull without movement.

recipes.title: introduce a cat to a new home
recipes.name: introduce-a-cat-to-a-new-home
recipes.goal: Help a cat settle into a new home gradually, with food, litter, hiding places, and territory introduced before full-house access.

steps.action: **Start in one room.** Place the carrier in the prepared room and close the door before opening it.
steps.expect: the cat can exit into a small safe territory or stay hidden by choice.

steps.action: **Let the cat choose distance.** Sit quietly and avoid pulling the cat from the carrier or hiding spot.
steps.expect: the cat sniffs, hides, or explores without being chased.

steps.action: **Keep essentials predictable.** Put food, water, and litter in stable locations and scoop the box daily.
steps.expect: the cat can find resources without crossing scary open space.

steps.action: **Add gentle interaction.** Offer play, treats, or soft talk only when the cat approaches or relaxes.
steps.expect: the cat shows curiosity, blinking, eating, grooming, or resting.

steps.action: **Expand territory slowly.** Open one additional room after the cat is eating, using the litter box, and moving confidently.
steps.expect: the cat investigates and can retreat to the starter room.

steps.action: **Introduce residents gradually.** Exchange scents before visual meetings with other pets and supervise children calmly.
steps.expect: meetings are brief and end before chasing, swatting, or cornering.

recipes.verification: The cat eats, drinks, uses the litter box, rests in the home, and can retreat to a safe room while new spaces and residents are introduced without forced contact.

recipes.title: introduce a dog to a baby
recipes.name: introduce-a-dog-to-a-baby
recipes.goal: Prepare and manage dog-baby introductions so the dog stays under control and the baby is never exposed to preventable risk.

steps.action: **Practice before arrival.** Reward the dog for settling on a mat, walking beside baby gear, and hearing baby sounds at low volume.
steps.expect: baby-related cues begin to predict calm rewards.

steps.action: **Refresh routines.** Arrange walking, feeding, toileting, and rest so the dog is not ignored or frantic.
steps.expect: basic needs are met before introductions.

steps.action: **Bring home scent first.** Let the dog sniff a baby blanket while calm and then redirect to a treat or mat.
steps.expect: the dog investigates briefly without grabbing or guarding.

steps.action: **Use barriers for first viewing.** Keep the dog leashed or behind a gate while an adult holds the baby at a distance.
steps.expect: the dog can look, sniff the air, and reorient to the handler.

steps.action: **Reward calm proximity.** Feed treats for relaxed body language, soft eyes, and settling away from the baby.
steps.expect: calm distance becomes the default behavior.

steps.action: **Maintain separation rules.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a bite can permanently injure a baby, so never allow unsupervised contact or face-level access.
steps.expect: every dog-baby moment has an awake adult controlling distance.

recipes.verification: The baby and dog are separated by management unless an awake adult is actively supervising, and the dog can remain calm, respond to cues, and disengage near baby-related sights, sounds, and smells.

recipes.title: introduce two pets
recipes.name: introduce-two-pets
recipes.goal: Introduce two pets gradually so they can share a home with lower stress, fewer fights, and clear escape options.

steps.action: **Separate first.** Put the new or visiting pet in a private room before any face-to-face greeting.
steps.expect: both animals know another pet is present but cannot reach each other.

steps.action: **Swap scent.** Trade bedding, toys, or cloths between areas, then reward calm sniffing.
steps.expect: each pet investigates the scent without prolonged hiding, barking, hissing, or lunging.

steps.action: **Feed near the barrier.** Place meals or treats on opposite sides of a closed door or gate at a distance where both can eat.
steps.expect: the other pet's presence predicts good things without blocking appetite.

steps.action: **Allow brief visual contact.** Crack the door, use a gate, or leash both animals with space between them.
steps.expect: they can see each other for seconds without charging or freezing.

steps.action: **Use neutral space when possible.** For dogs, choose a neutral outdoor area; for cats or small pets, use a controlled room neither animal owns strongly.
steps.expect: territory pressure is reduced and movement stays loose.

steps.action: **Run short supervised meetings.** Keep sessions to a few minutes, reward calm glances away, and end before tension builds.
steps.expect: the meeting finishes while both pets are still manageable.

steps.action: **Watch body language.** Look for soft bodies, loose tails, sniffing breaks, and the ability to disengage; treat hard staring, stalking, raised hackles, pinned ears, growling, hissing, or lunging as stop signs.
steps.expect: you respond to early signals rather than waiting for contact.

steps.action: **Separate and slow down.** [BRANCH: continue gradually | return to scent work] move forward only after several calm sessions; otherwise go back to barriers and scent swaps.
steps.expect: progress is based on behavior, not the calendar.

steps.action: **Supervise shared time.** Keep food bowls, high-value toys, litter boxes, and sleeping spots separate until trust is established.
steps.expect: no pet needs to defend a resource during early access.

recipes.verification: Both pets can spend a supervised session in the same area with relaxed body language, no chasing or threats, and easy access to separate exits.

recipes.title: iron a shirt
recipes.name: iron-a-shirt
recipes.goal: A wrinkled shirt is ironed crisp in a fixed order that avoids re-wrinkling what you already did, without scorch marks on the shirt or the board.

steps.action: **Heat the iron to the label's setting with water in the tank.** Test on an inside seam or hem first.
steps.expect: the test patch smooths without any shine, stick, or smell.

steps.action: **Iron the collar first, wrong side then right side, from the points inward.**
steps.expect: flat collar; ironing from points toward center pushes any crease into the invisible middle.

steps.action: **Do the cuffs and sleeves next.** Cuffs open and flat, inside then outside; sleeves laid flat by the seam, ironed from shoulder to cuff. A crisp sleeve crease is a choice: crease along the fold line for formal, or roll the sleeve slightly and iron flat-ish to avoid a crease.
steps.expect: cuffs crisp, sleeves smooth with your chosen crease policy.

steps.action: **Iron the yoke and shoulders over the board's narrow end.** Slide the shoulder over the board's nose.
steps.expect: the upper back panel smooth; this is the section everyone skips and everyone sees.

steps.action: **Do the front panels, button side and buttonhole side.** Point the iron's nose *between* buttons, never over them (buttons crack and their imprint shines through). Work top to bottom alongside the placket.
steps.expect: flat fronts; placket crisp; all buttons intact.

steps.action: **Finish with the back in two overlapping halves.** Lay half the back flat, iron top to bottom, rotate, do the other half over the pleat if there is one.
steps.expect: a smooth back with the box pleat (if any) pressed as a pleat, not flattened randomly.

steps.action: **Hang it immediately, top button closed.** ⚠️ Then the iron: upright on its heel, cord safe, switched off, and cooling somewhere no hand or child will find it; irons stay burn-hot for many minutes after power-off.
steps.expect: shirt cooling into shape on the hanger; iron parked safe and off.

recipes.verification: Collar, cuffs, plackets, and yoke are crisp, panels are smooth with no shine or scorch, the shirt is on a hanger while still warm, and the iron is off, upright, and cooling out of reach.

recipes.title: lag a pipe
recipes.name: lag-a-pipe
recipes.goal: Exposed pipework is insulated with sleeves or wrap so it loses less heat and is less likely to freeze in cold spaces.

steps.action: **Trace the pipe run.** Identify straight sections, elbows, valves, and gaps where cold air reaches the pipe.
steps.expect: you know every section that needs insulation.

steps.action: **Measure the diameter and length.** Measure outside pipe diameter and total length, adding extra for elbows and mistakes.
steps.expect: the insulation size matches the pipe.

steps.action: **Choose the covering.** [BRANCH: foam sleeve | wrap] use sleeves for straight accessible pipe and wrap for awkward elbows or tight spaces.
steps.expect: the material fits without crushing the pipe.

steps.action: **Cut straight sleeves to length.** Cut square ends and open the slit along the pipe.
steps.expect: each sleeve section covers a straight run cleanly.

steps.action: **Cover elbows and bends.** Miter foam pieces or spiral wrap around bends so no bare pipe shows.
steps.expect: elbows have continuous insulation.

steps.action: **Seal the joints.** Tape sleeve seams, butt joints, and wrap ends, leaving service valves usable.
steps.expect: insulation stays closed when touched.

steps.action: **Check clearances.** Keep insulation away from flues, hot appliance cases, and moving parts.
steps.expect: the pipe is covered but hazards and controls remain clear.

recipes.verification: All reachable vulnerable pipe sections, including elbows, are covered with secure insulation while valves and safety clearances remain accessible.

recipes.title: level a fridge
recipes.name: level-a-fridge
recipes.goal: The refrigerator is level side-to-side with a slight backward tilt so the doors close by themselves and seals land evenly.

steps.action: **Check door behavior first.** Open each door halfway and let go gently.
steps.expect: you see whether the door self-closes or drifts open.

steps.action: **Measure side-to-side level.** Place the level on a front shelf or cabinet edge.
steps.expect: the bubble shows any left-right lean.

steps.action: **Find the front adjusters.** Remove the toe grille if needed and identify the feet or roller screws. [BRANCH: threaded feet | roller screws] turn only the adjusters your model provides.
steps.expect: both front adjusters are accessible.

steps.action: **Set side-to-side level.** Raise the low front side in small turns until the bubble centers.
steps.expect: the cabinet no longer leans left or right.

steps.action: **Add slight backward tilt.** Raise both front adjusters evenly until the front is just higher than the back.
steps.expect: doors begin to swing closed from a partly open position.

steps.action: **Check seal contact.** Close the doors on a strip of paper at several points and pull gently.
steps.expect: the paper has light resistance around the gasket.

steps.action: **Reinstall the toe grille.** Clip the grille back without blocking airflow.
steps.expect: the front looks finished and ventilation openings are clear.

recipes.verification: The fridge is level side-to-side, slightly high at the front, and each door self-closes from a partly open position without rocking.

recipes.title: level a washing machine
recipes.name: level-a-washing-machine
recipes.goal: The washing machine stands level and stable so it does not walk, bang, or shake across the floor during spin.

steps.action: **Confirm the cause.** Push each top corner diagonally and listen for rocking before adjusting anything.
steps.expect: one or more feet lifts or taps if the washer is unstable.

steps.action: **Check side-to-side and front-to-back level.** Place the level on the top front edge, then the side edge.
steps.expect: you know which direction needs adjustment.

steps.action: **Loosen the foot lock nuts.** Turn each accessible lock nut upward from the floor. [BRANCH: front feet only | four adjustable feet] adjust the design your washer uses.
steps.expect: the feet can turn independently.

steps.action: **Adjust the low side.** Turn feet to raise the low corner or lower the high corner, working in small half-turns.
steps.expect: the bubble moves toward center.

steps.action: **Stabilize the stance.** Press each corner again and adjust until the washer does not rock.
steps.expect: all feet touch firmly.

steps.action: **Lock the nuts.** Hold each foot still and tighten the lock nut against the washer base.
steps.expect: the feet no longer turn by hand.

steps.action: **Run a spin test.** Run a rinse and spin with a few towels, then watch the first high-speed spin.
steps.expect: vibration is brief and the washer stays in place.

recipes.verification: During a spin test with towels, the washer stays in position and no corner rocks when pressed afterward.

recipes.title: light a charcoal grill
recipes.name: light-a-charcoal-grill
recipes.goal: A charcoal grill is lit outdoors with a chimney starter, coals are brought to ash-gray readiness, and heat zones are arranged safely for cooking.

steps.action: **Open vents and set the chimney.** Put the chimney on the charcoal grate, not on a table or deck.
steps.expect: airflow can feed the fire from below.

steps.action: **Load fuel.** Fill the chimney with the amount of charcoal needed, usually half for small cooks and full for high heat.
steps.expect: charcoal sits contained above the starter space.

steps.action: **Light the starter.** Place a lighter cube or loosely crumpled newspaper under the chimney and light it with a long lighter.
steps.expect: flame pulls upward through the chimney.

steps.action: **Wait for ash-gray coals.** Let coals burn 15-25 minutes until top pieces show gray edges and orange glow below.
steps.expect: smoke drops and coals look mostly ashed over.

steps.action: **Pour coals carefully.** Wearing gloves, lift the chimney by its handle and pour slowly onto the charcoal grate.
steps.expect: coals land where intended without sparks spilling outside the grill.

steps.action: **Arrange heat zones.** [BRANCH: direct grilling | two-zone cooking] spread coals evenly for direct heat, or bank to one side for hot and cooler zones.
steps.expect: cooking area has the heat pattern you need.

steps.action: **Install grate and preheat.** Set the cooking grate on, close the lid briefly, then brush the grate clean.
steps.expect: grate is hot and ready for food.

steps.action: **Control air and keep watch.** Adjust vents for heat and keep the grill attended until coals are fully out after cooking.
steps.expect: fire stays controlled and outdoors.

recipes.verification: The grill is outdoors, coals are ash-gray and glowing, heat zones are arranged, vents work, and no charcoal is burning in an enclosed or poorly ventilated space.

recipes.title: litter train a kitten
recipes.name: litter-train-a-kitten
recipes.goal: Teach a kitten to use a clean, accessible litter box consistently while preventing accidents and stress.

steps.action: **Prepare the box.** Fill a low-sided box with 1-2 inches of unscented litter and place it where the kitten can reach it quickly.
steps.expect: the kitten can step in without climbing or slipping.

steps.action: **Limit the starting area.** Keep the kitten in one kitten-proof room with food, water, bed, toys, and the box.
steps.expect: the box is easy to find from anywhere in the room.

steps.action: **Place the kitten after key moments.** Gently set the kitten in the box after waking, eating, playing, and any sniffing or crouching.
steps.expect: the kitten paws or sniffs the litter without fear.

steps.action: **Reward quiet success.** Praise softly or offer a tiny treat after use, then leave the kitten alone to exit.
steps.expect: the kitten associates the box with relief and calm.

steps.action: **Scoop daily.** Remove waste at least once daily and fully refresh litter as needed.
steps.expect: the box smells mild and has clean digging space.
