steps.action: **Clean accidents correctly.** Use enzyme cleaner and block access to repeated accident spots until dry.
steps.expect: odor cues are removed rather than masked.

steps.action: **Expand territory gradually.** [BRANCH: reliable use | repeated accidents] add access to more rooms after reliable box use, or return to a smaller area and add another box.
steps.expect: the kitten can still find a nearby box.

recipes.verification: The kitten uses a clean, accessible litter box for urine and stool for at least a full day in its current area, with no repeated accidents in the same spot.

recipes.title: lubricate a squeaky lock
recipes.name: lubricate-a-squeaky-lock
recipes.goal: A squeaky or sticky keyed lock turns smoothly after dry lubricant is applied without attracting grit into the cylinder.

steps.action: **Confirm the symptom.** Insert the key and turn gently to feel squeak, drag, or sticking.
steps.expect: the key still operates the lock with effort.

steps.action: **Clean the key.** Wipe the key with a dry paper towel to remove pocket lint and grime.
steps.expect: the key surface is visibly clean.

steps.action: **Choose dry lubricant.** [BRANCH: graphite | dry PTFE] use a small puff of graphite powder or a short burst of dry PTFE labeled for locks.
steps.expect: no wet oil film is introduced.

steps.action: **Apply sparingly.** Aim into the keyway and add a very small amount.
steps.expect: lubricant enters the cylinder without clumps or runoff.

steps.action: **Work the key.** Insert the key fully, remove it, then insert and turn it several times.
steps.expect: movement becomes smoother with each cycle.

steps.action: **Wipe residue.** Clean the key and lock face with a paper towel.
steps.expect: no black powder or spray residue transfers to fingers.

steps.action: **Test from both sides.** If it is a door lock with interior and exterior cylinders, test each side separately.
steps.expect: both sides turn without squeak or drag.

steps.action: **Check the latch alignment.** Open the door and turn the key or thumb turn, then close the door and try again.
steps.expect: the lock is smooth when open and closed.

recipes.verification: The correct key inserts fully, turns the lock three times in a row without squeak or sticking, and comes out clean enough not to mark a paper towel heavily.

recipes.title: make a bed
recipes.name: make-a-bed
recipes.goal: The bed is neatly made — sheets taut, duvet/blanket squared, pillows plumped — ready to be pleasant to get into tonight.

steps.action: **Strip back and air for a moment.** Throw the duvet fully back over the footboard; let the sheet breathe while you do step 2.
steps.expect: bottom sheet exposed end to end.

steps.action: **Re-tension the bottom sheet.** Pull each corner of the fitted sheet back over its mattress corner; smooth wrinkles outward from the center with flat palms.
steps.expect: drum-tight surface, corners seated, no ripples.

steps.action: **Square the top layer.** Spread the duvet/top sheet evenly: equal overhang left and right, top edge where you like it (at the headboard, or folded back a hand's width).
steps.expect: symmetric overhangs; label end at the foot.

steps.action: **Smooth the top layer from center outward.** Long sweeping strokes toward the edges and foot.
steps.expect: flat surface, no trapped lumps of last night.

steps.action: **Plump and place the pillows.** Grab each pillow at both ends, compress-and-release a few times, drop it square against the headboard, open ends outward.
steps.expect: pillows full-looking and aligned, not deflated pancakes.

steps.action: **Final square-up.** Step to the foot of the bed and check symmetry; tug where uneven; fold the throw/blanket across the foot if used.
steps.expect: even lines from the one viewing angle that shows everything.

recipes.verification: From the foot of the bed: bottom sheet invisible and tight, top layer symmetric with smooth surface, pillows plump and square — and tonight-you will find no crumbs or twisted layers inside.

recipes.title: make a family emergency plan
recipes.name: make-a-family-emergency-plan
recipes.goal: A household has a written emergency plan for communication, evacuation, sheltering, reunification, and essential needs.

steps.action: **List household members and needs.** Write names, phone numbers, medications, mobility needs, languages, pets, and key medical information.
steps.expect: the plan reflects who actually needs help.

steps.action: **Choose emergency contacts.** Pick one local contact and one out-of-area contact everyone can reach.
steps.expect: everyone knows who to call or text.

steps.action: **Set meeting places.** Choose one near-home spot and one outside the neighborhood.
steps.expect: the household has reunification locations for different scenarios.

steps.action: **Map exits and routes.** Identify two ways out of each room and two routes out of the neighborhood when possible.
steps.expect: evacuation does not depend on one path.

steps.action: **Assign roles.** Decide who helps children, pets, medication, documents, utilities, and emergency kit when time allows.
steps.expect: responsibilities are clear.

steps.action: **Write communication rules.** Prefer texts when networks are overloaded, leave short status messages, and call emergency services for immediate danger.
steps.expect: contact attempts are coordinated.

steps.action: **Plan sheltering actions.** Identify interior rooms, basement, upper floor, or safe rooms for likely hazards.
steps.expect: shelter locations match local risks.

steps.action: **Record utility shutoffs.** Note gas, water, and electrical shutoff locations and who is allowed or trained to use them. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* shutting off gas may require the utility to restore service; confirm emergency need first.
steps.expect: utility controls are known without unsafe practice shutoffs.

steps.action: **Share and store copies.** Put copies on phones, paper near exits, and with trusted contacts as appropriate.
steps.expect: the plan is accessible during an outage.

steps.action: **Practice and update.** Run a drill and update the plan after moves, new phone numbers, new medications, or household changes.
steps.expect: gaps are found before an emergency.

recipes.verification: Every household member can name the emergency contacts, two meeting places, primary roles, and where the written plan is stored.

recipes.title: mount a tv on the wall
recipes.name: mount-a-tv-on-the-wall
recipes.goal: A TV is mounted level on a wall using hardware rated for the TV weight, wall structure, and VESA pattern, with cables routed safely.

steps.action: **Confirm compatibility.** Match the TV's VESA pattern and weight to the mount rating
steps.expect: the mount manual lists a pattern and weight rating that cover the TV.

steps.action: **Choose viewing height.** Mark the desired screen center and account for where the mount brackets attach to the TV
steps.expect: the wall marks represent final screen height, not just bracket height.

steps.action: **Find structure.** Locate studs or masonry and mark fastener positions [BRANCH: studs | masonry | drywall-only]
steps.expect: marks align with solid structure or rated anchors appropriate for the load.

steps.action: **Plan cable route.** Choose surface raceway, in-wall rated cables, or a recessed power kit installed as allowed locally
steps.expect: power and signal cables have a legal, accessible path.

steps.action: **Attach brackets to TV.** Use the correct VESA screws and spacers so screws do not bottom out or press the panel
steps.expect: brackets sit flat and screws are snug without flexing the TV back.

steps.action: **Drill pilot holes.** Drill at the marked locations using the mount manual's bit size
steps.expect: holes are straight and centered in the marked support.

steps.action: **Fasten wall plate.** Lag into studs or use rated anchors for the wall type; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* drilling holes can hit wires or pipes, so confirm location before drilling
steps.expect: wall plate is tight and level.

steps.action: **Hang with a helper.** Lift the TV onto the wall plate and engage safety screws, locks, or straps
steps.expect: the TV is fully seated and cannot lift off accidentally.

steps.action: **Connect and check.** Connect cables, tilt or swivel gently, and verify clearance
steps.expect: the screen remains level and cables do not pinch.

recipes.verification: The TV remains level, all mount locks are engaged, and a gentle controlled tug does not move the wall plate or lift the TV off the mount.

recipes.title: move heavy furniture safely
recipes.name: move-heavy-furniture-safely
recipes.goal: A heavy furniture item is relocated to its destination with no injury to the movers and no damage to the item, the floors, or the doorframes.

steps.action: **Measure before you move anything.** Measure the item (all three dimensions) and every doorway, hallway pinch point, and stair turn on the route. Compare the smallest opening against the item's smallest two dimensions, since items can travel tilted.
steps.expect: a route where the item fits at every point, or a decision to disassemble first.

steps.action: **Strip the item.** Empty drawers and shelves, remove loose shelves and drawers entirely, take off legs and doors where fittings allow, tape or tie doors that stay on.
steps.expect: item at minimum weight; nothing shifts when you rock it.

steps.action: **Clear the entire path.** Rugs up, cables away, door mats gone, doors propped fully open, children and pets in another room.
steps.expect: an unobstructed corridor from start to destination, walked once to confirm.

steps.action: **Fit sliders under the load points.** Tilt one side just enough for a helper to slip sliders under the feet or corners, then the other side. Felt side down on hard floors; hard smooth side down on carpet.
steps.expect: item slides with a firm push instead of scraping.

steps.action: **Slide, don't carry, wherever the floor allows.** Push low on the item, from a lunge stance, moving it in short controlled shoves; pull only when pushing is impossible.
steps.expect: steady low-effort movement, floor unmarked behind it.

steps.action: **Where lifting is unavoidable, lift with the legs.** Feet shoulder-width, squat with a straight back, grip low on the frame (not handles or trim, which rip off), stand up by straightening the legs, keep the load against your body. Never twist while loaded; turn with your feet.
steps.expect: the load rises with the legs doing the work; no back rounding.

steps.action: **Agree the calls before a two-person lift, then use them.** Decide who walks backwards (the stronger navigator faces forward and steers verbally), then use fixed phrases: "lift on three: one, two, three", "set down on three", "stop" means freeze instantly. The person moving backwards gets continuous guidance: "two steps to the door, curb behind you".
steps.expect: both people lift and set down in the same instant, every time.

steps.action: **Take stairs high-low.** The stronger person takes the low end (it bears most of the weight), item tilted to match the stair angle, one slow step at a time, resting on landings. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a dropped load on stairs injures whoever is below it; never position anyone under a load they cannot hold alone for a few seconds.
steps.expect: controlled descent/ascent with the load never supported by one person alone.

steps.action: **Place, then reassemble.** Set down on the agreed call, remove sliders (tilt method again), refit legs, doors, drawers, shelves, contents.
steps.expect: item in final position, level and stable, route furniture and rugs restored.

recipes.verification: The item stands stable and undamaged at its destination, doorframes, walls, and floors along the route show no new marks, all removed parts and contents are back in place, and nobody is nursing a strain.

recipes.title: mow a lawn
recipes.name: mow-a-lawn
recipes.goal: Cut grass to an even, healthy height while keeping people, pets, windows, and the mower safe.

steps.action: **Walk the yard first.** Pick up sticks, toys, hoses, rocks, dog waste, and fallen fruit that could become projectiles.
steps.expect: the mower path is clear from driveway edge to fence line.

steps.action: **Check the mower.** Set the deck to remove no more than one-third of the blade height, confirm the bag or chute is attached, and inspect the blade area with the mower off.
steps.expect: the mower is intact, stable, and set for the season's grass height.

steps.action: **Protect the work area.** Close windows near the lawn, move cars if gravel is nearby, and keep kids and pets inside.
steps.expect: no bystanders or breakable targets are beside the cutting path.

steps.action: **Start on the perimeter.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* power mower blades can amputate or throw debris, so keep hands and feet away from the deck and stop the blade before clearing jams.
steps.expect: one safe border pass gives room to turn.

steps.action: **Mow in straight overlapping lanes.** Walk at a steady pace, overlap each pass by a few inches, and alternate direction from the last mow when possible.
steps.expect: grass is cut evenly without scalped stripes.

steps.action: **Handle slopes across, not up and down.** [BRANCH: push mower | riding mower] push across gentle slopes; ride up and down only if the manual allows.
steps.expect: wheels stay planted and you do not fight the mower's weight.

steps.action: **Finish edges and cleanup.** Empty clippings into compost or yard waste, blow or sweep clippings off sidewalks, and store the mower cool and dry.
steps.expect: hard surfaces are clear and the lawn has no heavy clumps.

recipes.verification: The lawn is uniformly cut, hard surfaces are swept, the mower is off and stored, and no toys, stones, or clippings remain in walkways.

recipes.title: mulch a garden bed
recipes.name: mulch-a-garden-bed
recipes.goal: Apply mulch to a garden bed to conserve moisture, moderate soil temperature, suppress weeds, and protect soil without smothering plant crowns or stems.

steps.action: **Choose mulch for the bed.** Use fine organic mulch for vegetables and perennials, and coarser wood mulch for paths or ornamental beds.
steps.expect: mulch suits the plants and use area.

steps.action: **Weed first.** Pull weeds by the roots before covering the surface.
steps.expect: the bed starts with low weed pressure.

steps.action: **Water dry soil.** Irrigate before mulching if the root zone is dry.
steps.expect: moisture is sealed in rather than blocked out.

steps.action: **Spread an even layer.** Apply 1-3 inches depending on mulch texture and plant size.
steps.expect: soil is covered without forming a thick mat.

steps.action: **Keep crowns and stems clear.** Pull mulch back a few inches from stems, trunks, and perennial crowns.
steps.expect: plant bases remain visible and dryable.

steps.action: **Feather edges.** Thin mulch near seedlings, self-sowers, and places where bulbs need to emerge.
steps.expect: small plants are not buried.

steps.action: **Water lightly to settle.** Spray or water gently if mulch is dusty or loose.
steps.expect: mulch settles and is less likely to blow away.

steps.action: **Refresh as needed.** Check monthly and add small amounts where soil becomes exposed.
steps.expect: coverage remains consistent through the season.

recipes.verification: The bed is weeded, soil is moist, mulch covers exposed soil evenly, and every plant crown, stem, or trunk has a clear gap around it.

recipes.title: oil a cutting board
recipes.name: oil-a-cutting-board
recipes.goal: A wooden cutting board is cleaned, dried, saturated with food-safe mineral oil, and buffed so it resists drying and cracking.

steps.action: **Clean the board first.** Wash with mild soap and warm water, then rinse quickly.
steps.expect: food residue and odors are gone without soaking the board.

steps.action: **Dry it fully.** Stand the board on edge with air on both faces until it is dry to the touch.
steps.expect: no cool damp patches remain.

steps.action: **Place it on a protected surface.** Lay down a towel or parchment and keep the bottle cap away from the oiled area.
steps.expect: drips will not stain the counter.

steps.action: **Apply mineral oil generously.** Pour a small puddle and spread with the grain over the top, sides, handle cutouts, and end grain.
steps.expect: the wood darkens evenly as it drinks in oil.

steps.action: **Wait for absorption.** Leave the board flat for 20 to 60 minutes. [BRANCH: dry board drinks oil fast | maintained board stays glossy]
steps.expect: dry areas appear where oil has soaked in.

steps.action: **Add a second pass if needed.** Re-oil any pale or dry patches, especially end grain and knife-scarred areas.
steps.expect: the whole surface keeps a slight sheen for several minutes.

steps.action: **Buff off excess.** Wipe firmly with a clean dry cloth until the board no longer feels greasy.
steps.expect: the board feels smooth, not slick, and no oil transfers heavily to a finger.

steps.action: **Set a cadence.** Repeat monthly for regular use, or whenever water no longer beads on the board.
steps.expect: a simple maintenance trigger is chosen.

recipes.verification: The dry board has an even slightly richer color, feels smooth but not greasy, and a few drops of water bead briefly instead of soaking in immediately.

recipes.title: open a bottle without a corkscrew
recipes.name: open-a-bottle-without-a-corkscrew
recipes.goal: A corked still wine bottle is opened without a corkscrew, using the least risky available substitute and accepting that this is a backup plan, not a party trick.

steps.action: **Choose the safer method first.** [BRANCH: screw and pliers | shoe against wall | push-in last resort] prefer screw and pliers when available, because glass impact is harder to control.
steps.expect: one method is chosen before anyone starts improvising.

steps.action: **Remove the foil.** Cut or peel the capsule so the cork top and bottle lip are visible.
steps.expect: the cork can move without snagging foil.

steps.action: **Use screw and pliers if available.** Drive a long screw into the cork center until 2 cm remains above the cork, then pull the screw upward with pliers.
steps.expect: the cork rises slowly and remains mostly intact.

steps.action: **Set up the shoe method safely.** Put the bottle base inside the heel cup of a flat-soled sturdy shoe, keep the bottle horizontal, and choose a solid wall that cannot dent or shatter.
steps.expect: the shoe cushions the bottle base and your hands stay away from the impact point.

steps.action: **Tap, do not smash.** Hit the shoe sole flat against the wall in short controlled taps, checking the cork after every few taps. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* glass can break and wine can spray, so stop immediately if you see cracks, chips, or leakage.
steps.expect: the cork creeps outward a few millimeters at a time.

steps.action: **Pull the cork before it flies.** Once enough cork is exposed to grip, twist and pull it out by hand.
steps.expect: the cork comes free without launching across the room.

steps.action: **Push in only as the last resort.** If extraction fails, use the blunt handle of a wooden spoon to push the cork into the bottle slowly over a sink.
steps.expect: the cork drops in and wine may rise or spill slightly.

steps.action: **Strain the first pour.** Pour through a clean strainer if cork fragments or dust are present.
steps.expect: drinkable wine reaches the glass without grit.

recipes.verification: The bottle is open, no glass is damaged, and the wine can be poured without cork grit after straining if needed.

recipes.title: open a wine bottle
recipes.name: open-a-wine-bottle
recipes.goal: A still wine bottle is opened cleanly, with the cork removed intact and no foil, cork crumbs, or sudden splashes in the glass.

steps.action: **Stand the bottle upright.** Set it on a stable surface and wipe dust from the top. [BRANCH: cork closure | screw cap] use this recipe for cork, twist off screw caps by hand.
steps.expect: the bottle is steady and the capsule is easy to see.

steps.action: **Cut the foil below the lip.** Use the foil cutter around the lower edge of the raised glass lip, then lift the top of the capsule away.
steps.expect: the cork top is fully exposed with no foil where wine will pour.

steps.action: **Center the worm.** Put the corkscrew tip in the exact center of the cork and press lightly.
steps.expect: the screw stands upright, not leaning into the bottle neck.

steps.action: **Twist straight down.** Turn the worm until about one curl remains visible.
steps.expect: the screw is deep enough to grip without punching through the cork bottom.

steps.action: **Use the first lever.** Hook the short notch on the bottle lip and lift the handle smoothly.
steps.expect: the cork rises partway with a soft movement, not a snap.

steps.action: **Use the second lever.** Switch to the longer notch if your corkscrew has one, then lift again.
steps.expect: most of the cork is out and still aligned with the neck.

steps.action: **Ease the last bit by hand.** Grip the cork and wiggle upward while keeping the bottle steady. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a hard sideways pull can break old cork, so slow down once the cork is nearly free.
steps.expect: the cork releases with a small sigh, not a pop.

steps.action: **Wipe and pour.** Wipe the mouth, sniff for obvious cork taint if you know it, and pour a small taste first.
steps.expect: wine flows cleanly with no foil flakes or cork crumbs.

recipes.verification: The cork is out, the bottle mouth is clean, and a test pour lands in the glass without cork pieces.

recipes.title: organize a closet
recipes.name: organize-a-closet
recipes.goal: A closet emptied, honestly purged, and rebuilt into zones you can maintain, with the outgoing clothes actually leaving the house instead of migrating to a bag in the hallway.

steps.action: **Empty it completely, one shelf or rod at a time.** Everything onto the bed by section. A full emptying is what makes the purge honest; sorting in place preserves every hiding spot.
steps.expect: bare closet, clothes staged in rough groups, dust visible where it always was.

steps.action: **Clean the empty closet.** Vacuum the floor, wipe shelves and rods (`daily/home/dust-a-room` logic in a box).
steps.expect: clean surfaces; this two-minute step is why emptying was worth it.

steps.action: **Purge each item with two questions.** Worn in the last year? Would you buy it again today? Two yeses: keep. Two nos: donate or discard (stained, torn beyond repair). One yes: a maybe-box with a date six months out; unopened by then, it donates itself.
steps.expect: real piles forming; the keep pile visibly smaller than what came out.

steps.action: **Rebuild in zones by frequency and kind.** Eye level and easy reach: what you wear weekly. Hanging: things that wrinkle (shirts, dresses, jackets). Folded shelves or drawers: knits and tees (`embodied/household/fold-a-tshirt`, filed vertically so every item shows). High shelves: seasonal and rare (luggage, formal wear). Floor: shoes on a rack or in rows, not a heap.
steps.expect: a layout a half-asleep version of you can navigate.

steps.action: **Group within zones.** By category first (all trousers together), then by color if you enjoy it. One-in-one-out lives or dies on being able to see what you own.
steps.expect: like with like; gaps visible where categories are thin or bloated.

steps.action: **Evacuate the exits today.** Discard to the bin now; donate bag into the car or by the door with a calendar slot this week (`daily/errands/donate-used-goods` is its own errand; schedule it); elsewhere-box distributed. ⚠️ *Irreversible in effect:* the donate bag that lingers three weeks quietly reopens; leaving the house is part of this recipe, not an afterthought.
steps.expect: by tonight, only keep items remain on the premises, staged or shelved.

recipes.verification: The closet holds only keep items in navigable zones, every shelf and rod is clean beneath them, the maybe-box has a date, the discard is in the bin, and the donate bag is in the car or already gone.

recipes.title: organize a junk drawer
recipes.name: organize-a-junk-drawer
recipes.goal: The drawer holds only items that earn their place, sorted into categories, each category in its own container, with a rule in place that keeps it from refilling with clutter.

steps.action: **Stage the sorting surface.** Spread the towel, line up trash bag, recycling bag, and relocate box within arm's reach.
steps.expect: an empty surface bigger than the drawer's contents, three exits ready.

steps.action: **Empty the drawer completely.** Pull it out if the slides allow and dump everything onto the towel. Partial emptying is how junk drawers stay junk drawers.
steps.expect: the drawer holds nothing, not even the crumbs.

steps.action: **Wipe the drawer clean.** Vacuum or brush out debris, wipe with a damp cloth, let it dry.
steps.expect: a clean, dry, empty drawer.

steps.action: **Triage every item with a fast three-way sort.** Keep (used in the last year and belongs at this station), relocate (useful but lives elsewhere), or toss. Duplicates: keep the best one. Dead batteries and expired coupons go straight out. Mystery keys and orphan cables go to a quarantine bag, not back in.
steps.expect: the towel shows only keepers; the other piles are in their bags.

steps.action: **Discard the toss pile now.** Batteries and electronics to their recycling stream, blades wrapped in tape before binning. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* photograph mystery keys and one-of-a-kind small parts before tossing, in case something turns out to have a lock.
steps.expect: trash and recycling bags are out of the room.

steps.action: **Cluster the keepers into categories.** Typical sets: writing tools, tape and adhesives, batteries, small tools, keys and fobs, chargers, coupons and stamps. Five to eight categories is right; twenty means you are keeping too much.
steps.expect: distinct piles with nothing left in a "misc" heap.

steps.action: **Fit containers to the drawer.** Measure the drawer's interior length, width, and depth, then dry-fit trays so every category has a walled home and the drawer still closes.
steps.expect: trays cover most of the floor with no tray taller than the drawer's interior depth.

steps.action: **Load with frequency-based placement.** Most-used categories at the front, rare ones at the back. Anchor sliding trays with rubber shelf liner or museum putty under each.
steps.expect: the drawer opens and closes without trays shifting or contents jamming the slide.

steps.action: **Deliver the relocate box and declare the one-drawer rule.** Walk each relocate item to its real home in one pass. The rule going forward: nothing enters the drawer loose; it goes into a category tray or it does not go in.
steps.expect: relocate box empty; household members told the rule.

recipes.verification: The drawer closes freely; every item inside sits in a category container; the trash, recycling, and relocate piles are gone from the room; opening the drawer and naming where any given item goes takes under three seconds.

recipes.title: organize cables behind a desk
recipes.name: organize-cables-behind-a-desk
recipes.goal: Desk cables are identified, grouped, routed, secured, and reconnected with enough slack for normal movement and no strain on ports.

steps.action: **Photograph the current wiring.** Take a clear picture of ports and power connections before unplugging.
steps.expect: a fallback reference exists.

steps.action: **Power down and unplug.** Shut down computers, switch off the strip, and unplug from the wall before handling the bundle.
steps.expect: no powered cables are being pulled or tied.

steps.action: **Label both ends.** Mark monitor, dock, charger, lamp, speakers, and any similar-looking cables.
steps.expect: each loose cable can be identified from either side.

steps.action: **Remove unused cables.** Pull out old chargers, duplicates, and mystery cords that are not connected to a device.
steps.expect: the bundle is smaller before organizing.

steps.action: **Group by destination.** [BRANCH: power | data | movable device] keep power together, data together, and keyboard or laptop cables separately flexible.
steps.expect: cables follow logical routes instead of one tangled rope.

steps.action: **Mount the power strip.** Attach it under or behind the desk where plugs are reachable and the switch is not kicked.
steps.expect: heavy power cords are off the floor.

steps.action: **Sleeve and tie with slack.** Wrap long runs in a sleeve and use hook-and-loop ties every 20-30 cm, leaving service loops near monitors and the laptop.
steps.expect: cables stay together but can move without port strain.

steps.action: **Reconnect from the photo.** Plug in data first, then power, then turn the strip on and test each device.
steps.expect: everything powers up and the desk can move slightly without tugging.

recipes.verification: All desk devices work, cables are labeled, the floor is clear, and moving the chair, monitor, or desk does not tug a connector.

recipes.title: overwinter potted plants
recipes.name: overwinter-potted-plants
recipes.goal: Keep potted plants alive through winter by matching each plant to dormancy, indoor protection, insulation, or sheltered outdoor storage.

steps.action: **Sort plants by hardiness.** Compare each plant's cold tolerance to expected winter lows and container exposure.
steps.expect: plants are grouped by indoor, sheltered, or outdoor overwintering needs.

steps.action: **Inspect before moving indoors.** Check leaf undersides, stems, and soil surface for insects, eggs, and disease.
steps.expect: pests are found before they spread inside.

steps.action: **Clean and prune lightly.** Remove dead leaves, spent flowers, and diseased growth without forcing heavy new growth.
steps.expect: plants are tidier and less pest-prone.

steps.action: **Transition tropical plants.** Move tender plants indoors before nights are consistently cold, placing them in bright light away from drafts.
steps.expect: tropical plants are protected before chilling injury.

steps.action: **Protect hardy pots outdoors.** Cluster hardy containers, mulch the soil surface, and place them against a sheltered wall or inside an unheated garage if needed.
steps.expect: roots are buffered from freeze-thaw swings.

steps.action: **Reduce watering.** Water dormant or slow-growing plants only when the mix is dry below the surface.
steps.expect: roots stay barely moist and not soggy.

steps.action: **Label dormant plants.** Mark pots that die back so they are not mistaken for empty soil.
steps.expect: dormant plants remain identifiable.

steps.action: **Resume growth gradually.** In late winter or spring, increase light and water slowly and harden outdoor plants off before full exposure.
steps.expect: new growth appears without sudden shock.

recipes.verification: Each potted plant has a winter location matched to its hardiness, pots drain freely, watering is reduced for slow growth, and pests are not spreading among stored plants.

recipes.title: paint a wall
recipes.name: paint-a-wall
recipes.goal: One interior wall carries two even coats of the new color with crisp edges at the ceiling, corners, and trim, and no drips, lap marks, or paint on the floor.

steps.action: **Clear and protect.** Move furniture off the wall, remove outlet and switch plates, lay drop cloths tight against the baseboard.
steps.expect: bare wall, plates in a labeled bag with their screws, floor covered with no gaps at the base.

steps.action: **Wash and repair the wall.** Wipe down with sugar soap or diluted degreaser (kitchen-adjacent walls especially), fill holes and dents, sand repairs flush, dust off.
steps.expect: wall feels smooth and slightly matte; your hand comes away clean.

steps.action: **Tape the borders.** Tape along ceiling line, adjacent walls, and trim; press the tape edge down firmly with a fingernail or card. A loosely pressed edge is the single biggest cause of bleed.
steps.expect: continuous tape lines with the leading edge burnished shiny.

steps.action: **Cut in the edges with the brush.** Load the bottom third of the brush, paint a 5-8 cm band along all taped edges and corners, working one wall section at a time.
steps.expect: an even wet band framing the wall, no drips running from the band.

steps.action: **Roll the field in a W pattern.** Load the roller evenly in the tray, roll a large W in a roughly 1 m square, then fill it in with vertical strokes without reloading; work top to bottom, each square overlapping the last while its edge is still wet.
steps.expect: uniform wet sheen across each square, no thick lines at the roller edges.

steps.action: **Keep the wet edge moving.** Do not stop mid-wall for a break; a dried edge painted over later shows as a lap mark. Finish the full wall in one pass.
steps.expect: whole wall wet-coated in one continuous session.

steps.action: **Let the first coat dry fully.** Follow the can's recoat time (typically 2-4 h for water-based paint), not touch-dry time. Wrap the brush and roller tightly in plastic instead of washing between coats.
steps.expect: coat is dry to firm pressure; first-coat coverage looks streaky and thin, which is normal.

steps.action: **Roll the second coat the same way.** Cut in again, then W-pattern the field.
steps.expect: color reads solid and even; the streaks from coat one are gone.

steps.action: **Pull the tape while the paint is barely wet.** Pull at a 45 degree angle, slowly, back over itself. If the paint has fully dried, score the tape line lightly with a blade first. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* ripping dried paint off with the tape tears the new coat and sometimes the old one; when in doubt, score.
steps.expect: crisp paint lines, tape comes away with no flakes attached.

steps.action: **Clean up.** Water-based: wash brush and roller until water runs clear, spin dry. Reinstall plates after the paint at their edges is dry.
steps.expect: tools clean and reshaped, plates back on, drop cloths folded paint-side-in.

recipes.verification: Under raking light from both sides, the wall shows uniform color and sheen with no thin patches, drips, or lap marks; ceiling and trim lines are straight; plates are reinstalled; no paint is on the floor, trim, or ceiling.

recipes.title: patch a small wall hole
recipes.name: patch-a-small-wall-hole
recipes.goal: A nail, screw, or anchor hole up to about 1.5 cm across is filled, sanded flush, and painted so the repair is invisible from one meter away in normal light.

steps.action: **Prepare the hole.** Pull out any remaining anchor or screw, brush loose debris out of the hole, and press raised paper or plaster edges flat by dimpling them inward with the round end of a screwdriver handle.
steps.expect: nothing proud of the wall surface around the hole; ragged edges pushed slightly below flush.

steps.action: **Wipe the area.** Damp cloth over the hole and 5 cm around it, then let it dry. Filler grips clean matte surfaces, not dust.
steps.expect: clean, dry, dull patch of wall.

steps.action: **Press filler into the hole.** Load the knife, push filler in across the hole from two or three directions so it packs the cavity, not just caps it.
steps.expect: filler visible at full depth in the hole, no air gap at the back.

steps.action: **Overfill slightly and strike off.** Leave the patch a hair proud of the wall (a fraction of a millimeter), then one smooth diagonal pass with the knife nearly flat. Filler shrinks as it dries; a flush-struck patch dries into a dimple.
steps.expect: a thin, slightly raised smear feathering to nothing at the edges.

steps.action: **Let it dry completely.** Follow the tub's time (30 min to a few hours by depth); many spackles change color when dry. Deep holes: fill in two lifts rather than one thick one.
steps.expect: uniform dry color, hard to a fingernail press.

steps.action: **Sand flush.** 220-grit wrapped around a flat block, light circular strokes, feathering outward. Stop as soon as your flat hand cannot find the patch by feel.
steps.expect: patch undetectable by touch with eyes closed; surrounding paint only lightly scuffed.

steps.action: **Dust off and prime the spot.** Wipe with the barely damp cloth, then dab or spray primer just over the patch. Unprimed filler drinks paint and "flashes" as a dull spot through the topcoat.
steps.expect: thin even primer film over the patch only, dry to touch before painting.

steps.action: **Spot paint with feathered edges.** Small brush or mini roller, patch plus 2-3 cm around it, rolling or stippling the edge out to nothing. Two thin coats beat one thick one.
steps.expect: wet paint blends past the patch boundary; after drying, color matches.

steps.action: **Check in raking light.** Hold a flashlight flat against the wall across the repair.
steps.expect: no shadowed dimple, ridge, or sheen halo; if there is, see F1 or F4.

recipes.verification: From one meter away under both overhead light and raking flashlight, the repaired spot cannot be located: no dimple, ridge, color difference, or sheen difference, and a hand run over the area feels only flat wall.

recipes.title: patch a window screen
recipes.name: patch-a-window-screen
recipes.goal: A small tear or hole in a window screen is patched so insects stay out and the screen remains usable.

steps.action: **Remove loose strands.** Trim frayed mesh around the hole without enlarging it.
steps.expect: the damaged area has a neat edge.

steps.action: **Clean the screen.** Wipe both sides around the tear with a lightly damp cloth and let dry.
steps.expect: dust and grease are gone.

steps.action: **Cut the patch.** Cut patch mesh at least 1 inch larger than the hole on all sides.
steps.expect: the patch overlaps sound screen evenly.

steps.action: **Apply the patch.** Press a self-adhesive patch in place or weave aluminum patch wires through the mesh.
steps.expect: the patch lies flat and covers the opening.

steps.action: **Secure the edges.** Add a thin bead of clear outdoor adhesive if needed and smooth it around the patch edge.
steps.expect: the patch edges do not lift.

steps.action: **Let it set.** Keep the screen flat or untouched until adhesive cures.
steps.expect: the patch stays bonded when lightly touched.

steps.action: **Reinstall and inspect.** Put the screen back and check from indoors and outdoors.
steps.expect: no open gap remains around the patch.

recipes.verification: The patched screen has no visible open hole, the patch edge remains attached, and the window opens and closes without catching it.

recipes.title: plane a sticking door
recipes.name: plane-a-sticking-door
recipes.goal: A sticking wood door is trimmed only where it rubs, sealed at the bare edge, and tested so it closes without scraping.

steps.action: **Confirm the rub.** Close the door slowly and slide paper around the top, latch side, and bottom gaps.
steps.expect: the tight area catches the paper.

steps.action: **Mark the high spot.** Rub pencil on the sticking edge or mark shiny scrape points with painter's tape.
steps.expect: the material to remove is clearly bounded.

steps.action: **Check hinges first.** Tighten hinge screws before removing wood.
steps.expect: any hinge-caused sag is corrected or ruled out.

steps.action: **Decide removal method.** [BRANCH: light rub | heavy rub] sand a light rub in place or remove the door and plane a heavier high spot.
steps.expect: the tool choice matches the amount of interference.

steps.action: **Support the door.** If removing it, pull hinge pins with the door blocked and place it on padded supports.
steps.expect: the door edge is stable for work.

steps.action: **Remove small passes.** Plane or sand only the marked area, working with the grain and checking often.
steps.expect: a thin shaving or dust comes off evenly.

steps.action: **Keep the edge square.** Hold the plane flat and avoid rounding the door face.
steps.expect: the edge remains straight and the reveal stays even.

steps.action: **Seal bare wood.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before reinstalling, confirm enough wood has been removed, then seal exposed wood with paint or clear finish.
steps.expect: raw wood is covered against swelling.

steps.action: **Rehang and test.** Reinstall hinge pins, close the door, and repeat only if it still rubs.
steps.expect: the door closes without scraping.

recipes.verification: The door closes and latches from a normal push, with paper sliding through the repaired gap and no exposed raw wood left unsealed.

recipes.title: plant a tree
recipes.name: plant-a-tree
recipes.goal: Plant a young tree at the correct depth and location so roots can establish without trunk rot, girdling, or utility conflicts.

steps.action: **Confirm the planting site.** Check mature height and spread, sun exposure, drainage, and distance from utilities or foundations.
steps.expect: the tree has room to grow without future conflict.

steps.action: **Find the root flare.** Pull soil or nursery mulch away from the trunk until the first major roots begin to widen.
steps.expect: the flare is visible above the root ball.

steps.action: **Dig a wide shallow hole.** Make the hole two to three times wider than the root ball and no deeper than the root flare height.
steps.expect: the tree will sit with the flare at or slightly above grade.

steps.action: **Remove container problems.** Slide off the pot, cut circling roots, and remove burlap, twine, and wire from the top and sides where practical. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* root and wrapping cuts affect establishment, so confirm the flare and root direction before cutting.
steps.expect: roots can grow outward into native soil.

steps.action: **Set and backfill.** Place the tree straight, refill with native soil, and firm gently without stomping hard.
steps.expect: the trunk is vertical and the root flare remains visible.

steps.action: **Water deeply.** Soak the root ball and surrounding soil until water reaches the planting depth.
steps.expect: soil settles without leaving the tree too low.

steps.action: **Mulch correctly.** Spread 2-3 inches of mulch in a wide ring, keeping it several inches away from the trunk.
steps.expect: the mulch looks like a doughnut, not a volcano.

steps.action: **Stake only if needed.** [BRANCH: stable tree | unstable site] skip stakes for a firm tree, or use loose flexible ties and remove them within a year.
steps.expect: the trunk can move slightly but will not fall.

recipes.verification: The root flare is visible at grade, the tree is upright, mulch is not touching bark, and the root zone has been watered deeply.

recipes.title: plant spring bulbs
recipes.name: plant-spring-bulbs
recipes.goal: Plant fall-planted spring bulbs at the correct depth and spacing so they root before winter and bloom reliably in spring.

steps.action: **Inspect the bulbs.** Keep firm bulbs and discard soft, moldy, or badly damaged ones.
steps.expect: only viable bulbs remain for planting.

steps.action: **Choose a draining site.** Pick a bed where winter water will not stand around bulbs.
steps.expect: the planting area is not soggy.

steps.action: **Dig to proper depth.** Make holes about two to three times as deep as the bulb is tall unless the label says otherwise.
steps.expect: holes match bulb size.

steps.action: **Set bulbs point up.** Place pointed ends or shoots upward and root plates downward; set uncertain bulbs sideways.
steps.expect: each bulb is oriented for easy sprouting.

steps.action: **Space for the display.** Plant in clusters or drifts with spacing from the package, avoiding straight single-file rows unless desired.
steps.expect: bulbs have room and a natural-looking layout.

steps.action: **Backfill and firm.** Cover with soil and press gently to remove air pockets without compacting hard.
steps.expect: bulbs are covered at an even grade.

steps.action: **Water once.** Water the planting area thoroughly after backfilling.
steps.expect: soil settles around the bulbs.

steps.action: **Mulch and mark.** Add light mulch and labels so the area is not dug up before spring.
steps.expect: bulbs are protected and their location is known.

recipes.verification: Bulbs are firm, planted in fall at label or size-based depth, oriented correctly, watered in, mulched lightly, and marked for spring emergence.

recipes.title: polish silver
recipes.name: polish-silver
recipes.goal: Tarnished silver is cleaned, rinsed, dried, and stored to slow new tarnish.

steps.action: **Inspect the item.** Look for loose parts, plating wear, stones, or deliberate dark detail.
steps.expect: you know whether a bath or hand polish is safer.

steps.action: **Choose a method.** [BRANCH: foil bath for plain pieces | paste-and-buff for detailed or delicate pieces]
steps.expect: the cleaning method fits the object.

steps.action: **Prepare the foil bath.** Line a bowl with foil, add silver touching the foil, sprinkle baking soda, and pour hot water over it.
steps.expect: faint sulfur smell or bubbling appears.

steps.action: **Wait briefly.** Let the item sit 1 to 3 minutes, turning so tarnished areas contact solution.
steps.expect: tarnish lightens without aggressive rubbing.

steps.action: **Use paste if needed.** Apply silver polish or baking soda paste with a soft cloth, rubbing gently.
steps.expect: black tarnish transfers to the cloth.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly.** Rinse under warm water, avoiding soaking handles or glued parts.
steps.expect: no gritty baking soda or polish remains.

steps.action: **Dry completely.** Buff with a soft lint-free cloth, reaching seams and crevices.
steps.expect: surface is dry and brighter.

steps.action: **Store against tarnish.** Wrap in anti-tarnish cloth or keep dry with low airflow.
steps.expect: silver is protected from moisture and sulfur exposure.

recipes.verification: The silver is visibly brighter, dry to the touch, and leaves no black residue on a clean cloth after final buffing.

recipes.title: potty train a puppy
recipes.name: potty-train-a-puppy
recipes.goal: Teach a puppy where to toilet by using supervision, frequent trips, rewards, and calm cleanup instead of punishment.

steps.action: **Set the schedule.** Take the puppy out after waking, eating, drinking, playing, and at least every few hours.
steps.expect: the puppy reaches the toilet area before most accidents happen.

steps.action: **Go to the same spot.** Walk calmly to the chosen area and wait without play until toileting happens or a few minutes pass.
steps.expect: the location becomes linked with elimination.

steps.action: **Reward immediately.** Mark and treat within seconds after the puppy finishes outside.
steps.expect: the puppy learns that toileting there pays.

steps.action: **Supervise indoors.** Use leash tethering, gates, or a crate sized for resting when you cannot watch.
steps.expect: sniffing, circling, or wandering can be interrupted early.

steps.action: **Clean accidents calmly.** Interrupt only if caught in the act, take the puppy out, and clean with enzymatic cleaner.
steps.expect: odor is removed and the puppy is not frightened.

steps.action: **Track progress.** Record accident times, successful trips, meals, and naps.
steps.expect: the schedule adjusts to the puppy's real bladder and bowel pattern.

recipes.verification: The puppy toilets in the chosen area most of the time, accidents are decreasing on the log, and indoor freedom is increased only after reliable supervised success.

recipes.title: prepare a pet for boarding
recipes.name: prepare-a-pet-for-boarding
recipes.goal: Prepare a pet for boarding with health records, supplies, emergency instructions, and a lower-stress drop-off.

steps.action: **Confirm requirements early.** Ask the facility for vaccines, parasite prevention, exam records, food rules, medication forms, and drop-off windows.
steps.expect: missing requirements are known before the travel week.

steps.action: **Book needed vet care.** Schedule vaccines, refills, or health certificates with enough time for waiting periods.
steps.expect: records will be valid on boarding day.

steps.action: **Prepare written instructions.** List feeding amounts, medication dose and timing, behavior notes, vet contact, and emergency spending authorization.
steps.expect: staff can follow care without guessing.

steps.action: **Pack labeled supplies.** Portion food, medications in original containers, comfort item if allowed, leash or carrier, and records.
steps.expect: every item is labeled with pet name and instructions.

steps.action: **Do a calm drop-off.** Exercise or toilet the pet first, keep goodbye brief, and hand instructions directly to staff.
steps.expect: the pet transfers safely and staff confirm intake.

steps.action: **Stay reachable.** Keep phone access and respond quickly if the facility reports illness or stress.
steps.expect: urgent decisions do not stall.

recipes.verification: The facility has accepted the pet with current records, labeled supplies, written care instructions, emergency contacts, and a reachable decision-maker.

recipes.title: propagate a plant from a cutting
recipes.name: propagate-a-plant-from-a-cutting
recipes.goal: A healthy plant cutting is taken below a node, rooted in water or soil, monitored for weeks, and potted on after roots are ready.

steps.action: **Choose a healthy stem.** Pick non-flowering growth with at least two nodes and several leaves.
steps.expect: cutting material is firm, green, and pest-free.

steps.action: **Cut below a node.** Make a clean cut 1-2 cm below the node using sanitized scissors.
steps.expect: the cutting has a node near the base where roots can form.

steps.action: **Remove lower leaves.** Strip leaves that would sit underwater or under soil.
steps.expect: bare lower stem and leaves only above the rooting zone.

steps.action: **Choose the rooting method.** [BRANCH: water | soil] put the node in clean water for easy viewing, or into moist mix for fewer transition problems.
steps.expect: the node is covered by the rooting medium.

steps.action: **Place in bright indirect light.** Keep it warm and out of harsh sun.
steps.expect: leaves stay firm without scorching.

steps.action: **Maintain moisture and cleanliness.** Change water every few days, or keep soil lightly moist but not soggy.
steps.expect: stem base stays fresh, not slimy.

steps.action: **Wait for roots.** Check weekly and resist tugging soil cuttings.
steps.expect: roots appear in 2-8 weeks depending on plant and season.

steps.action: **Pot on when roots are ready.** Move water cuttings when roots are 3-5 cm long, or soil cuttings when new growth appears.
steps.expect: cutting enters a small draining pot and remains upright.

recipes.verification: The cutting has healthy roots or new growth, is potted in a small draining container, and shows firm leaves after several days.

recipes.title: prune a shrub
recipes.name: prune-a-shrub
recipes.goal: Remove dead, damaged, crossing, or overgrown shrub branches while preserving the plant's natural shape and seasonal bloom.

steps.action: **Identify the shrub's timing.** [BRANCH: spring-blooming | summer-blooming | unknown] prune spring bloomers after flowering, summer bloomers in late winter or early spring, and unknown shrubs lightly.
steps.expect: you avoid removing the season's flower buds.

steps.action: **Clean the tools.** Wipe blades with alcohol or disinfectant before cutting, especially between diseased plants.
steps.expect: blades are sharp-looking and free of sap or soil.

steps.action: **Remove dead or diseased wood first.** Cut back to healthy tissue or the branch collar without leaving long stubs.
steps.expect: dead, brittle, or spotted material is gone.

steps.action: **Thin crossing stems.** Choose one rubbing or inward-growing branch and cut it at its base with bypass pruners or loppers. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* each cut changes growth for the season, so step back and confirm the branch before cutting.
steps.expect: the center has more air and no obvious rubbing pair remains.

steps.action: **Shape with selective cuts.** Shorten long shoots back to a side branch or outward-facing bud, not by shearing the whole face unless it is a hedge.
steps.expect: the shrub looks natural rather than flat-topped.

steps.action: **Limit the session.** Stop after removing about one-quarter of live growth unless rejuvenation pruning is appropriate for that species.
steps.expect: the plant still has enough leaves and structure to recover.

steps.action: **Clean up debris.** Bag diseased material for trash and compost healthy clippings if allowed.
steps.expect: no thorny or diseased cuttings remain underfoot.

recipes.verification: Dead, damaged, crossing, and overlong branches are removed with clean cuts; the shrub keeps a balanced shape; and no wildlife, diseased debris, or sharp cuttings remain.

recipes.title: prune tomato plants
recipes.name: prune-tomato-plants
recipes.goal: Prune tomato plants to improve airflow, reduce soil-borne disease splash, and keep growth supported without removing too much fruiting canopy.

steps.action: **Identify the plant type.** Check the tag or growth habit before cutting.
steps.expect: you know whether to prune lightly or manage ongoing vine growth.

steps.action: **Clean the tool.** Wipe blades with alcohol or wash and dry them before starting.
steps.expect: blades are clean and sharp enough for neat cuts.

steps.action: **Remove lower leaves.** Cut leaves touching soil and lower yellowing leaves below the first flower cluster.
steps.expect: the base has better airflow and less soil contact.

steps.action: **Choose main stems.** For indeterminate tomatoes, keep one to three strong leaders and remove extra small suckers if desired.
steps.expect: growth is easier to support.

steps.action: **Keep determinate plants fuller.** For determinate tomatoes, remove only diseased, crowded, or soil-touching foliage.
steps.expect: fruiting branches remain mostly intact.

steps.action: **Cut small suckers early.** Pinch or snip suckers when they are small and avoid stripping large amounts at once.
steps.expect: cuts are small and the plant keeps enough leaves.

steps.action: **Tie remaining stems.** Secure stems loosely to support below leaf nodes, leaving room for thickening.
steps.expect: stems are upright and not strangled.

steps.action: **Dispose of diseased material.** Remove spotted leaves from the garden rather than composting active disease.
steps.expect: infected foliage is not left under plants.

recipes.verification: The tomato has no leaves touching soil, diseased foliage is removed, main stems are supported, and enough healthy leaf canopy remains to shade fruit.

recipes.title: put out a small kitchen fire
recipes.name: put-out-a-small-kitchen-fire
recipes.goal: Stop a small, contained kitchen fire without spreading it or blocking your escape.

steps.action: **Check your escape path first.** Stand between the fire and an exit, and keep others away from the kitchen.
steps.expect: you can leave in one movement if the fire grows.

steps.action: **Turn off the heat if you can reach the control safely.** Use the knob or switch without leaning over flames.
steps.expect: burner, oven, or appliance heat source is off.

steps.action: **Cover a pan fire.** Slide a metal lid or baking sheet over the pan from the side, then leave it covered.
steps.expect: flames shrink or stop as oxygen is cut off.

steps.action: **Smother a small grease fire only with baking soda if no lid fits.** Use handfuls from a box for a small pan fire. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never pour water on burning oil or grease, because it can explode burning fat across the room.
steps.expect: flames reduce without splashing.

steps.action: **Handle an oven fire by keeping the door closed.** Turn the oven off and do not open the door until fully cool.
steps.expect: flames stay contained and fade.

steps.action: **Handle an appliance fire by cutting power.** Unplug only if the plug is reachable without touching fire, smoke, or water; otherwise shut the circuit breaker.
steps.expect: appliance power is off and you are not in contact with energized equipment.

steps.action: **Use a fire extinguisher only if the fire is still small.** Use a Class B or multipurpose ABC extinguisher for grease, and only from your exit side.
steps.expect: extinguisher stream reaches the base of the fire while the exit remains behind you.

steps.action: **Call the fire service if flames do not go out quickly.** Leave, close the door behind you if possible, and call emergency services from outside.
steps.expect: everyone is out and responders are being dispatched.

steps.action: **Wait before uncovering or moving cookware.** Leave a smothered pan covered until cool.
steps.expect: no re-ignition when the area is monitored from a safe distance.

recipes.verification: The heat source is off, flames are out, smoke is clearing, cookware remains covered until cool, and emergency services have been called if the fire spread, restarted, or could not be controlled within seconds.

recipes.title: quiet a squeaky floor
recipes.name: quiet-a-squeaky-floor
recipes.goal: A localized squeaky floor is quieted by fastening loose subfloor or floorboards without damaging visible flooring.

steps.action: **Locate the squeak.** Walk slowly while a helper marks the loudest spot with tape.
steps.expect: the squeak point is marked.

steps.action: **Find joist direction.** Use a stud finder, floor registers, or basement view to identify joist locations.
steps.expect: the nearest joist line is marked.

steps.action: **Choose access.** [BRANCH: from above | from below] use surface screws from above or shims and adhesive from an exposed basement ceiling.
steps.expect: the least visible repair path is selected.

steps.action: **Drill a pilot from above.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm no radiant heat, wiring, or plumbing is below before drilling into the floor.
steps.expect: the pilot enters solid joist material.

steps.action: **Drive the repair screw.** Use a breakaway squeak screw or trim screw into the joist.
steps.expect: the board pulls tight without dimpling badly.

steps.action: **Shim from below if accessible.** Apply wood glue to a thin shim and tap it lightly between subfloor and joist.
steps.expect: the gap closes without lifting the floor.

steps.action: **Conceal the repair.** Break off special screw heads or fill trim-screw holes with matching filler.
steps.expect: the visible repair is small and flush.

steps.action: **Retest the area.** Walk over the marked spot and nearby boards.
steps.expect: the squeak is gone or significantly reduced.

recipes.verification: The marked floor area no longer squeaks during normal walking, and any fastener hole is flush and stable.

recipes.title: rake and bag leaves
recipes.name: rake-and-bag-leaves
recipes.goal: Collect autumn leaves into bags or yard-waste containers without damaging grass, storm drains, or your back.

steps.action: **Choose the collection route.** Start upwind and uphill, working toward the curb, compost pile, or bagging spot.
steps.expect: leaves move with you instead of being dragged across the whole yard.

steps.action: **Clear drains and beds first.** Pull leaves away from storm drains, window wells, young shrubs, and pet paths.
steps.expect: water can flow and delicate plants are visible.

steps.action: **Rake in small rows.** Use short strokes, switch hands often, and keep the rake close to your body.
steps.expect: leaves form manageable windrows without shoulder strain.

steps.action: **Move piles onto a tarp or into bags.** [BRANCH: bag pickup | compost] scoop dry leaves into paper bags, or drag a tarp to the compost area.
steps.expect: each load can be lifted without tearing or spilling.

steps.action: **Keep bags light.** Fill bags about two-thirds full if leaves are damp, then fold or tie according to local pickup rules.
steps.expect: bags stand upright and can be moved by one person.

steps.action: **Leave useful mulch where appropriate.** Spread a thin leaf layer under shrubs or mow dry leaves into the lawn if local practice allows.
steps.expect: beds are protected without burying crowns or turf.

steps.action: **Stage bags safely.** Place bags at the pickup point away from fire hydrants, sidewalks, bike lanes, and street drains.
steps.expect: the yard is clear and public access remains open.

recipes.verification: Leaves are removed from lawn, drains, walkways, and plant crowns; bags or compost piles are stable; and pickup bags comply with local rules.

recipes.title: re caulk a window
recipes.name: re-caulk-a-window
recipes.goal: Failed window caulk is removed and replaced with exterior-rated sealant so drafts and water intrusion are reduced.

steps.action: **Inspect the joint.** Identify cracked, missing, or separated caulk around the window trim.
steps.expect: the repair area is clear and limited to sealant failure.

steps.action: **Remove old caulk.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cut and scrape failed caulk without gouging trim or siding.
steps.expect: the joint is open and loose material is gone.

steps.action: **Clean and dry.** Brush dust away, wipe bonding surfaces, and let them dry fully.
steps.expect: the joint is clean, dry, and ready for sealant.

steps.action: **Tape neat edges.** Apply painter's tape along both sides of the joint if a crisp bead is needed.
steps.expect: the intended bead width is defined.

steps.action: **Cut the nozzle.** Cut the caulk tip to the joint width and puncture the inner seal.
steps.expect: caulk flows in a controlled bead.

steps.action: **Apply the bead.** Run a continuous bead over the joint with steady pressure.
steps.expect: the gap is filled without skips.

steps.action: **Tool the bead.** Smooth the bead with a wet finger or caulk tool, then pull tape before skin forms.
steps.expect: the sealant bridges both sides with a concave surface.

steps.action: **Let it cure.** Keep the window dry and undisturbed for the product cure time.
steps.expect: the bead firms without cracks or bubbles.

recipes.verification: After curing, the caulk bead is continuous, adhered to both sides, and no draft or water path is visible around the repaired joint.

recipes.title: reattach a loose baseboard
recipes.name: reattach-a-loose-baseboard
recipes.goal: A loose baseboard is refastened to the wall, gaps are closed, and the trim is ready for touch-up.

steps.action: **Inspect the gap.** Pull gently on the baseboard and look behind it with a flashlight.
steps.expect: the loose section and any damage are visible.

steps.action: **Find studs.** Mark studs above the trim with painter's tape.
steps.expect: fastener locations align with framing.

steps.action: **Clean behind trim.** Vacuum loose dust from the gap without prying the board farther out.
steps.expect: the baseboard can sit flat against the wall.

steps.action: **Press the board in place.** Hold or clamp the baseboard tight to the wall and floor line.
steps.expect: the gap closes along the loose section.

steps.action: **Fasten into studs.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* nail through the baseboard into studs after confirming no hidden cable or pipe risk.
steps.expect: nail heads seat close to the trim face.

steps.action: **Set and fill nails.** Use a nail set, then fill nail holes with wood filler.
steps.expect: nail heads are below the surface and holes are filled.

steps.action: **Caulk the top gap.** Apply a thin paintable caulk line where the baseboard meets the wall.
steps.expect: the wall-trim seam is continuous.

steps.action: **Touch up finish.** After filler and caulk dry, sand lightly and paint as needed.
steps.expect: the repair blends with surrounding trim.

recipes.verification: The baseboard does not move when pressed, nail holes are filled, and the top seam has no open gap along the repaired section.

recipes.title: regrout tiles
recipes.name: regrout-tiles
recipes.goal: Old failing grout is removed and replaced with fresh grout that is tooled, cleaned, cured, and sealed where appropriate.

steps.action: **Inspect the field.** Tap tiles and press grout lines to find loose tile or soft areas.
steps.expect: only stable areas are selected for regrouting.

steps.action: **Remove old grout.** Rake out damaged grout to at least half the tile thickness, keeping the tool centered in the joint.
steps.expect: joints are open and tile edges are intact.

steps.action: **Clean the joints.** Vacuum dust and wipe with a damp sponge, then let the joints dry.
steps.expect: no loose powder remains.

steps.action: **Mix grout.** Prepare grout to the maker's consistency and slake if instructed.
steps.expect: grout is smooth and spreadable.

steps.action: **Pack the joints.** Hold the float diagonally and force grout into the lines.
steps.expect: joints are completely filled.

steps.action: **Tool the lines.** Draw the float or sponge lightly over the joints to shape them evenly.
steps.expect: grout sits slightly below the tile face with no voids.

steps.action: **Wipe haze.** [BRANCH: first wipe | final buff] use a barely damp sponge first, then buff dry haze with microfiber after it forms.
steps.expect: tile faces are clean without pulling grout from joints.

steps.action: **Cure undisturbed.** Keep the area dry and avoid scrubbing for the grout's cure time.
steps.expect: grout hardens without cracking.

steps.action: **Seal if needed.** Apply penetrating sealer to cement grout after cure, wiping excess from tile.
steps.expect: grout darkens briefly and then dries protected.

recipes.verification: After curing, grout lines are full, firm, evenly tooled, haze-free, and sealed where the grout type requires sealing.

recipes.title: remove a broken cork from a bottle
recipes.name: remove-a-broken-cork-from-a-bottle
recipes.goal: Remove or manage a broken cork so the bottle can be poured without cork bits in the drink.

steps.action: **Inspect the break.** Look at how much cork remains above or inside the neck.
steps.expect: you can tell whether the cork can be gripped or must be pushed in.

steps.action: **Choose the path.** [BRANCH: extract with screw | push cork in] Extract if a firm cork section remains; push in if the cork is crumbly, too short, or already falling.
steps.expect: the chosen method matches the cork condition.

steps.action: **Extract with a screw.** Twist the corkscrew or clean screw into the cork center, then pull slowly with steady upward pressure.
steps.expect: the cork rises without shredding further.

steps.action: **Push in if extraction fails.** Use the blunt handle of a clean wooden spoon or similar tool to push the cork into the bottle.
steps.expect: the cork drops below the liquid surface.

steps.action: **Strain the pour.** Place a fine strainer, coffee filter, or clean cloth in a funnel over a decanter or clean pitcher.
steps.expect: the receiving container is ready before pouring.

steps.action: **Pour slowly.** Tilt the bottle and pour through the filter, stopping before sediment or large cork pieces rush the neck.
steps.expect: liquid passes through while cork bits stay behind.

steps.action: **Decant for service.** Move the strained drink to a decanter, pitcher, or clean bottle if it will be served at the table.
steps.expect: the serving container has clear liquid with no visible cork pieces.

steps.action: **Discard the damaged cork.** Do not try to reinsert a broken, wet, or crumbly cork.
steps.expect: the bottle is closed with a clean stopper if anything remains.

steps.action: **Prevent the next break.** Store corked bottles on their side when appropriate, use a sharp corkscrew, and pull straight rather than levering sideways.
steps.expect: the next cork has less chance of tearing.

recipes.verification: The drink has been poured or decanted through a filter, and no visible cork bits or glass damage remain in the serving container.

recipes.title: remove a coffee or tea stain
recipes.name: remove-a-coffee-or-tea-stain
recipes.goal: A fresh or set coffee or tea stain is lifted from washable fabric or carpet without spreading it or heat-setting the tannins.

steps.action: **Blot the spill.** Press with a dry white cloth, working from the outside toward the center.
steps.expect: liquid transfers to the cloth without rubbing the stain wider.

steps.action: **Flush with cold water.** Run cold water through the back of washable fabric, or dab cold water onto carpet.
steps.expect: the brown color lightens.

steps.action: **Mix cleaner.** Combine 1 cup cold water, 1 teaspoon dish soap, and 1 tablespoon white vinegar.
steps.expect: solution is slightly soapy and not heavily sudsy.

steps.action: **Test first.** Dab the mix on a hidden area and wait 5 minutes.
steps.expect: no color lifts onto the cloth and the surface texture stays normal.

steps.action: **Treat the stain.** Apply the solution with a cloth, blot, then rinse with cold water. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* heat can set coffee and tea stains, so do not use hot water, a dryer, or an iron until the stain is gone.
steps.expect: stain fades after each blotting pass.

steps.action: **Handle carpet moisture.** Press dry towels over carpet and weigh them down for 10 minutes if needed.
steps.expect: carpet feels damp, not soaked.

steps.action: **Air dry and inspect.** Let the area dry fully before judging the result.
steps.expect: remaining shadow is easier to see once dry.

recipes.verification: After full air drying, the treated area is the same color as the surrounding surface or is clearly lighter with no soap residue or wet ring.

recipes.title: remove a grease stain from clothing
recipes.name: remove-a-grease-stain-from-clothing
recipes.goal: A cooking-oil or grease stain is lifted from washable clothing before heat sets it.

steps.action: **Blot fresh grease.** Press a clean cloth onto the stain without rubbing it wider.
steps.expect: surface oil transfers to the cloth.

steps.action: **Lift solids.** Scrape food residue away with a dull spoon from the outside inward.
steps.expect: no chunks remain on the fabric.

steps.action: **Apply absorbent powder.** Cover the stain with baking soda, cornstarch, or talc for 15 minutes.
steps.expect: powder clumps or darkens as it absorbs oil.

steps.action: **Brush off powder.** Shake or brush powder into the trash.
steps.expect: the stain looks lighter but may still show a shadow.

steps.action: **Pretreat with soap.** Work a drop of dish soap or liquid detergent into the greasy area with fingertips.
steps.expect: the stained fibers are evenly coated.

steps.action: **Rest the pretreatment.** Let the soap sit for 10 minutes without drying completely.
steps.expect: detergent has time to break down the oil.

steps.action: **Rinse from the back.** Flush warm water through the wrong side if the label allows warm water.
steps.expect: loosened grease moves out of the fabric.

steps.action: **Wash normally.** Launder at the warmest label-safe temperature with regular detergent.
steps.expect: the garment finishes a full wash cycle.

steps.action: **Air-dry and inspect.** Do not use dryer heat until the stain is gone.
steps.expect: the damp or dry fabric has no visible greasy outline.

recipes.verification: After air drying, the garment has no translucent grease shadow when viewed from the front and back in bright light.

recipes.title: remove a red wine stain
recipes.name: remove-a-red-wine-stain
recipes.goal: Remove or lighten a fresh red wine stain without spreading it, bleaching the item unexpectedly, or heat-setting the color.

steps.action: **Blot immediately.** Press a clean white cloth onto the stain and lift straight up; do not rub.
steps.expect: wine transfers to the cloth without enlarging the stain.

steps.action: **Move to a protected surface.** Put a towel under fabric or blot carpet from the outside toward the center.
steps.expect: liquid does not spread to clean areas.

steps.action: **Flush with cold water.** Run cold water through the back of washable fabric, or dab cold water onto carpet and upholstery.
steps.expect: some red color loosens and dilutes.

steps.action: **Choose a treatment.** [BRANCH: salt for fresh wet stain | dish-soap plus peroxide for washable colorfast fabric] pick salt when the stain is still wet, or peroxide mix after testing.
steps.expect: the method matches the material risk.

steps.action: **Use salt if fresh.** Cover the damp stain with a thick layer of salt and let it draw wine out for 10 minutes.
steps.expect: the salt turns pink or clumpy.

steps.action: **Test peroxide mix.** Mix 1 part dish soap with 2 parts 3 percent hydrogen peroxide and dab a hidden area first.
steps.expect: the test spot does not lighten after 5 minutes.

steps.action: **Apply treatment gently.** Dab the chosen treatment onto the stain, working from edge to center.
steps.expect: red color lifts onto the cloth or into the salt.

steps.action: **Rinse cold.** Rinse washable fabric in cold water or blot carpets with a clean damp cloth.
steps.expect: cleaner residue and loosened wine are removed.

steps.action: **Check before drying.** Inspect the item in good light before using heat. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* dryer heat or ironing can set remaining red pigment; confirm the stain is gone first.
steps.expect: no visible red remains before any heat is used.

steps.action: **Launder or air dry.** Wash fabric according to its care label or let carpet air dry after blotting.
steps.expect: the treated area dries without a ring.

recipes.verification: The stained area shows no visible red in good light before the item is exposed to dryer heat or ironing.

recipes.title: remove a stain
recipes.name: remove-a-stain
recipes.goal: A fresh stain is treated by type without spreading it, setting it with heat, or damaging the material.

steps.action: **Identify the material.** Check whether the item is washable, dry-clean only, carpet, upholstery, or hard surface.
steps.expect: you know whether water is safe to use.

steps.action: **Blot, do not rub.** Press a clean cloth onto the stain and lift straight up.
steps.expect: color transfers to the cloth without the stain spreading wider.

steps.action: **Remove solids.** Lift food, mud, or wax with a dull edge before adding liquid.
steps.expect: loose material is gone and only the stain remains.

steps.action: **Use cold water first.** Flush from the back of washable fabric when possible.
steps.expect: stain moves out of the fibers instead of deeper into them.

steps.action: **Triage the stain type.** [BRANCH: protein like blood or egg | oil or grease | tannin like coffee or wine | dye or ink] choose the matching treatment.
steps.expect: the next product fits the stain instead of guessing.

steps.action: **Test treatment first.** Apply a tiny amount in a hidden spot and wait a few minutes.
steps.expect: no color loss, ring, or texture change appears.

steps.action: **Apply targeted cleaner.** Use detergent for protein and oils, alcohol for some inks, or oxygen bleach for many tannins on safe fabrics.
steps.expect: the stain lightens from the outside inward.

steps.action: **Rinse and inspect.** Rinse or blot with clean water, then inspect while still wet.
steps.expect: cleaner residue is reduced and remaining stain is visible.

steps.action: **Repeat before drying.** Treat again if color remains. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* dryer heat can permanently set many stains, so do not machine dry until the mark is gone.
steps.expect: the item is held out of heat until clean.

steps.action: **Launder or finish.** Wash according to the care label or air-dry the treated area.
steps.expect: the material dries without a ring or cleaner crust.

recipes.verification: The treated area is dry or ready to launder, with the stain removed or clearly reduced and no new color loss or fabric damage.

recipes.title: remove a stripped screw
recipes.name: remove-a-stripped-screw
recipes.goal: A screw with a damaged drive recess is removed without badly damaging the surrounding material.

steps.action: **Clean the head.** Pick out paint, dirt, or metal crumbs from the recess.
steps.expect: the bit can sit as deep as the damaged recess allows.

steps.action: **Press in the right bit.** Try the correct size screwdriver by hand with firm downward pressure.
steps.expect: the bit catches or clearly slips.

steps.action: **Use the rubber band trick.** Place a wide rubber band over the head and press the bit through it.
steps.expect: the rubber fills gaps and improves grip.

steps.action: **Try a bigger bit.** Move up one bit size or switch from Phillips to a square or Torx bit if it bites.
steps.expect: the bit grabs without camming out.

steps.action: **Back out slowly.** Turn counterclockwise with steady pressure and low speed if using a driver.
steps.expect: the screw rises slightly with each turn.

steps.action: **Grip proud heads.** [BRANCH: head sticks above surface | head is flush] use locking pliers on proud heads, otherwise continue to extraction.
steps.expect: pliers can clamp flat sides if exposed.

steps.action: **Use an extractor.** Drill the pilot side if required, then run the extractor counterclockwise.
steps.expect: the extractor bites and starts turning the screw.

steps.action: **Replace the screw.** Remove debris and install a new screw of the same length and type.
steps.expect: the new screw seats firmly without slipping.

recipes.verification: The stripped screw is fully out, the surrounding material still holds a replacement screw, and no broken tool tip remains in the hole.

recipes.title: remove candle wax
recipes.name: remove-candle-wax
recipes.goal: Candle wax is hardened, lifted, and any oily residue is blotted away from wood, fabric, or carpet.

steps.action: **Let wax harden.** Wait until wax is no longer liquid before touching it.
steps.expect: wax is opaque and firm.

steps.action: **Chill the wax.** Hold bagged ice on the wax for several minutes.
steps.expect: wax becomes brittle and shrinks slightly.

steps.action: **Scrape bulk wax.** Lift hardened pieces with a plastic scraper or spoon.
steps.expect: thick wax flakes off without gouging the surface.

steps.action: **Choose residue treatment.** [BRANCH: wood, use gentle heat and cloth | fabric or carpet, use paper and low iron]
steps.expect: the method protects the material.

steps.action: **Heat and blot.** Place paper over residue and apply warm iron or hair dryer briefly.
steps.expect: wax transfers into the paper.

steps.action: **Move to clean paper.** Repeat with fresh paper until no new wax mark appears.
steps.expect: paper stays mostly clean after heating.

steps.action: **Clean the oily trace.** Dab fabric or carpet with mild dish soap solution, or wipe sealed wood with a barely damp cloth.
steps.expect: greasy shine fades.

steps.action: **Dry and restore.** Blot dry, then polish sealed wood if the finish looks dull.
steps.expect: surface is dry and even-looking.

recipes.verification: No raised wax can be felt, blotting paper no longer picks up wax, and the cleaned area is dry.

recipes.title: remove chewing gum
recipes.name: remove-chewing-gum
recipes.goal: Chewing gum is hardened or loosened, removed from the surface, and cleaned without spreading the sticky residue.

steps.action: **Identify the surface.** [BRANCH: fabric | carpet | hair | hard surface]
steps.expect: the removal method matches the material.

steps.action: **Harden gum when possible.** Hold ice in a sealed bag against the gum, or place a small item in the freezer.
steps.expect: gum turns stiff and less stretchy.

steps.action: **Scrape gently.** Use a spoon edge, dull knife, or plastic scraper to lift the hardened gum.
steps.expect: pieces break away without cutting fibers or scratching finish.
