steps.action: **Repeat cold cycles.** Re-freeze any gum that softens while scraping.
steps.expect: remaining gum stays brittle enough to chip off.

steps.action: **Use oil for hair.** Work cooking oil, peanut butter, or conditioner into hair gum, then slide strands free.
steps.expect: gum loosens and pulls away without cutting hair.

steps.action: **Treat residue.** For fabric or carpet, dab with dish soap solution after bulk gum is gone.
steps.expect: sticky shine fades without spreading.

steps.action: **Rinse and blot.** Use a clean damp cloth, then a dry towel.
steps.expect: soap and loosened residue transfer to the towel.

steps.action: **Dry and inspect.** Let the area dry fully before judging the stain.
steps.expect: no tacky spots remain under a fingertip.

recipes.verification: The surface feels non-sticky when dry, and no visible gum pieces remain in fibers, hair, or surface grooves.

recipes.title: remove hard water stains
recipes.name: remove-hard-water-stains
recipes.goal: Mineral stains from hard water are dissolved and scrubbed off glass, fixtures, tile, or porcelain without damaging stone or plated finishes.

steps.action: **Identify the surface.** Confirm whether the stained area is glass, ceramic, chrome, stainless, plastic, or natural stone
steps.expect: acid-safe and acid-sensitive areas are separated.

steps.action: **Protect stone and delicate finishes.** Keep vinegar and citric acid off marble, limestone, travertine, unsealed grout, and damaged plating
steps.expect: only acid-safe areas remain in the work zone.

steps.action: **Pre-clean soap film.** Wash the area with dish soap and water, then rinse
steps.expect: greasy film is gone and mineral spots are easier to see.

steps.action: **Apply acid dwell.** Lay vinegar-soaked cloths on the stains or spray a citric acid solution [BRANCH: light stains | heavy crust]
steps.expect: the stained area stays wet for 5 to 15 minutes.

steps.action: **Scrub gently.** Use a non-scratch pad or soft brush while the deposit is still wet
steps.expect: white scale starts to smear, powder, or lift.

steps.action: **Repeat for crust.** Reapply acid and dwell again rather than grinding hard
steps.expect: thick deposits soften layer by layer.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly.** Flush the area with clean water and wipe away acidic residue
steps.expect: the surface no longer feels slick or smells strongly of vinegar.

steps.action: **Dry and prevent.** Buff dry, then plan to squeegee or wipe after future use
steps.expect: fewer spots remain once water evaporates.

recipes.verification: After the surface is rinsed and dry, mineral spots are gone or visibly reduced without new dull patches, scratches, or finish damage.

recipes.title: remove limescale from a tap
recipes.name: remove-limescale-from-a-tap
recipes.goal: White limescale is softened and removed from a tap or faucet using a controlled vinegar soak without harming delicate finishes.

steps.action: **Check the finish.** Identify whether the tap is chrome or stainless, or a finish that may dislike acid.
steps.expect: you know whether vinegar is safe to test.

steps.action: **Test a hidden spot.** Dab diluted vinegar on an unseen area for 5 minutes, then rinse and dry.
steps.expect: no discoloration, dulling, or peeling appears.

steps.action: **Prepare the soak.** Use equal parts vinegar and water for routine scale, or plain vinegar for sturdy chrome with heavy scale.
steps.expect: cloth or bag is wet but not dripping across stone or grout.

steps.action: **Wrap the tap.** Press the soaked cloth on the scale, or secure a small vinegar bag around the spout.
steps.expect: scale stays in contact with the wet material.

steps.action: **Let it dwell.** Wait 15 to 30 minutes, checking delicate finishes sooner. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* acid can etch stone and damage some brass, nickel, and coated finishes, so keep vinegar off those surfaces and rinse spills immediately.
steps.expect: white crust softens.

steps.action: **Brush gently.** Remove the cloth and scrub with a soft toothbrush or microfiber cloth.
steps.expect: flakes and chalky residue lift away.

steps.action: **Rinse and dry.** Flush with clean water and buff dry.
steps.expect: tap is shiny and no vinegar smell remains.

recipes.verification: The tap surface and aerator are free of chalky limescale, water flows normally, and the finish is rinsed, dry, and unchanged in color.

recipes.title: remove limescale from a toilet
recipes.name: remove-limescale-from-a-toilet
recipes.goal: Toilet limescale is softened with an acid soak, scrubbed under the rim and waterline, and removed without mixing chemicals or scratching the bowl unnecessarily.

steps.action: **Ventilate and flush.** Turn on the fan, put on gloves, and flush to wet the bowl.
steps.expect: fresh water is in the trap and air is moving.

steps.action: **Lower the waterline if needed.** Push water down the trap with the toilet brush, or turn off supply and flush once.
steps.expect: more scale at the waterline is exposed.

steps.action: **Apply the acid soak.** Pour vinegar or dissolved citric acid onto scale and under the rim, soaking paper towel against vertical deposits if needed.
steps.expect: scale stays wet with acid.

steps.action: **Let it dwell.** Wait 30-60 minutes with the lid open and room ventilated.
steps.expect: crust looks chalky, softened, or easier to scrape.

steps.action: **Scrub under the rim and waterline.** Use the toilet brush firmly, focusing where water exits and where the ring formed.
steps.expect: scale flakes or lightens.

steps.action: **Use pumice only on stubborn ceramic scale.** Wet the pumice and bowl, then rub gently on hard deposits. [BRANCH: porcelain ceramic | colored, plastic, or coated surface] use pumice only on porcelain ceramic.
steps.expect: deposit abrades while the wet surface stays smooth.

steps.action: **Flush and repeat once if needed.** Rinse the bowl, inspect, and repeat the acid soak only if scale remains.
steps.expect: water runs clear and the ring is mostly gone.

steps.action: **Restore and prevent.** Turn water back on if closed, flush twice, and clean more often or treat hard water.
steps.expect: toilet functions normally and new scale has less time to build.

recipes.verification: The bowl and under-rim area are rinsed clean, visible limescale is gone or reduced to non-scratching residue, and no bleach or other cleaner was mixed with acid.

recipes.title: remove mold from shower silicone
recipes.name: remove-mold-from-shower-silicone
recipes.goal: Black or pink surface mold on shower silicone is killed, lifted, rinsed away, and the joint is left dry enough to judge whether it needs re-caulking.

steps.action: **Ventilate and clear the shower.** Turn on the fan, open the door or window, remove bottles, and put on gloves and eye protection.
steps.expect: steady airflow, bare silicone, and no skin contact with cleaner.

steps.action: **Rinse loose soil first.** Wet the silicone with plain water and wipe away soap film so bleach reaches the mold instead of the scum.
steps.expect: the bead looks cleaner but stained areas remain.

steps.action: **Apply bleach gel to the silicone.** Run a thin bead of gel directly along the stained silicone, then press paper towel or cotton onto vertical spots to keep it wet.
steps.expect: cleaner stays in contact with the mold instead of sliding down.

steps.action: **Let it dwell.** Leave the gel for 20-30 minutes with air moving. [BRANCH: stain lightens | stain unchanged] if unchanged, extend once to 45 minutes.
steps.expect: dark spotting fades or turns brown-gray.

steps.action: **Scrub gently along the bead.** Use the brush with light pressure so you do not tear the silicone edge.
steps.expect: loosened mold wipes off without gouging the sealant.

steps.action: **Rinse completely.** Flush the area with plenty of water, then wipe with a clean wet sponge until no slick cleaner remains.
steps.expect: silicone feels clean, not slippery or bleachy.

steps.action: **Dry and inspect.** Towel-dry the joint, keep the fan running, and check for black growth inside the silicone, peeling, gaps, or softness.
steps.expect: surface mold is gone or clearly identified as embedded damage.

steps.action: **Prevent the return.** Squeegee after showers, keep bottles off the bead, run the fan 20 minutes, and leave the curtain or door open.
steps.expect: the joint dries between uses.

recipes.verification: The silicone is rinsed, dry to the touch, free of removable mold, and any remaining embedded staining is marked for re-caulking rather than more scrubbing.

recipes.title: remove pet hair from fabric
recipes.name: remove-pet-hair-from-fabric
recipes.goal: Pet hair is removed from clothing, upholstery, or bedding without grinding it deeper into the fabric.

steps.action: **Dry the fabric fully.** Let damp fabric air dry before hair removal.
steps.expect: hair sits on the surface instead of smearing.

steps.action: **Shake outdoors if possible.** Snap loose washable items away from your face.
steps.expect: loose hair falls off before detailed cleaning.

steps.action: **Use a directional pass.** Drag a lint roller, damp rubber glove, or squeegee in one direction.
steps.expect: hair gathers into lines or clumps.

steps.action: **Collect clumps.** Pick up gathered hair and discard it.
steps.expect: removed hair does not redeposit on the fabric.

steps.action: **Vacuum creases.** Use an upholstery tool along seams, cushions, pockets, and folds.
steps.expect: embedded hair lifts from recessed areas.

steps.action: **Repeat with fresh adhesive or rinsed rubber.** Replace lint sheets or rinse the glove as pickup drops.
steps.expect: each pass continues collecting hair.

steps.action: **Finish before laundering.** Remove visible hair before putting washable fabric in the machine.
steps.expect: less hair transfers to washer and dryer surfaces.

recipes.verification: In bright light, the fabric surface, seams, and folds show no obvious pet-hair clumps after brushing your hand across the grain.

recipes.title: remove pilling from a sweater
recipes.name: remove-pilling-from-a-sweater
recipes.goal: Loose pills are removed from a sweater without cutting the underlying yarns.

steps.action: **Lay sweater flat.** Smooth one small section without stretching the knit.
steps.expect: pills sit above the surface and are easy to see.

steps.action: **Choose the tool.** Use [BRANCH: fabric shaver | sweater comb | scissors] based on knit delicacy.
steps.expect: tool matches the fabric thickness.

steps.action: **Test a hidden area.** Make several light passes on an inside hem or underside.
steps.expect: pills lift without fuzzing or cutting yarn.

steps.action: **Remove pills lightly.** Work in short strokes over one section, keeping the fabric supported.
steps.expect: raised pills detach while intact stitches remain.

steps.action: **Empty or clean the tool.** Clear lint from the shaver head or comb teeth as it fills.
steps.expect: the tool cuts or catches cleanly again.

steps.action: **Brush away debris.** Use hands or a lint brush to remove loose fibers.
steps.expect: the cleaned section looks smoother.

steps.action: **Store folded.** Fold the sweater instead of hanging it by the shoulders.
steps.expect: the knit keeps shape after depilling.

recipes.verification: The sweater surface is visibly smoother, no intact yarn strands are cut, and seams, cuffs, and high-friction areas have been checked.

recipes.title: remove scratches from wood furniture
recipes.name: remove-scratches-from-wood-furniture
recipes.goal: Light scratches in wood furniture are cleaned, color-matched, blended, and protected while deep damage is identified before overworking the finish.

steps.action: **Clean the area gently.** Wipe with a barely damp cloth and mild soap, then dry immediately.
steps.expect: dust and oils are gone, making the scratch edge visible.

steps.action: **Judge the depth.** Run a fingernail across the mark. [BRANCH: nail does not catch | nail catches] treat light scratches; plan repair for deep ones.
steps.expect: a clear light-versus-deep call.

steps.action: **Choose the color fill.** Match a wax stick or marker to the darker grain, not the lightest highlight.
steps.expect: test mark blends on a hidden area after buffing.

steps.action: **Fill light scratches sparingly.** Rub walnut, wax, or marker along the scratch, then wipe across the grain to remove excess.
steps.expect: color settles in the pale line, not smeared over the whole surface.

steps.action: **Buff with a clean cloth.** Use small circles, then finish with the grain.
steps.expect: shine evens out and the repair looks less obvious from standing height.

steps.action: **Protect the finish.** Apply a small amount of compatible wax or polish if the whole area looks dull.
steps.expect: the repaired patch matches the surrounding sheen.

steps.action: **Stop before sanding.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not sand veneer or finished furniture unless you accept changing the surface.
steps.expect: no finish is removed accidentally.

recipes.verification: From normal viewing distance, the scratch is blended in color and sheen, with no sticky residue, haze, or new finish damage.

recipes.title: replace a cabinet door hinge
recipes.name: replace-a-cabinet-door-hinge
recipes.goal: A damaged cabinet door hinge is replaced and the door hangs square, closes cleanly, and matches adjacent doors.

steps.action: **Match the hinge.** Compare overlay, opening angle, cup size, and screw pattern before removal.
steps.expect: the replacement matches the old hinge geometry.

steps.action: **Support the door.** Tape the door closed lightly or hold it with a helper while removing screws.
steps.expect: the door cannot fall when the hinge releases.

steps.action: **Remove the bad hinge.** Unscrew the hinge from the frame and door.
steps.expect: the old hinge comes off without tearing the wood.

steps.action: **Inspect holes.** Check whether screw holes are firm or stripped.
steps.expect: screws can bite, or stripped holes are identified.

steps.action: **Repair stripped holes.** Fill loose holes with wood glue and toothpicks or dowels, then trim flush after set.
steps.expect: the screw holes accept screws tightly.

steps.action: **Install the new hinge.** Fasten the hinge to the door first, then to the cabinet frame or plate.
steps.expect: the hinge sits flat and screws are snug.

steps.action: **Adjust alignment.** Use hinge adjustment screws or loosen and shift the hinge until gaps are even.
steps.expect: the door lines up with neighboring doors.

steps.action: **Test swing and close.** Open and close the door fully several times.
steps.expect: the door clears the frame and stays closed.

recipes.verification: The cabinet door opens fully, closes without rubbing, maintains an even reveal, and the hinge screws remain tight after ten cycles.

recipes.title: replace a cabinet knob
recipes.name: replace-a-cabinet-knob
recipes.goal: A cabinet knob or pull is removed and replaced so the new hardware sits straight, secure, and aligned with the existing hole spacing.

steps.action: **Measure before buying or installing.** For a pull, measure center-to-center distance between the two screw holes.
steps.expect: new hardware matches the existing hole spacing.

steps.action: **Open the cabinet.** Hold the old knob or pull with one hand and access the screw from inside.
steps.expect: screw head is visible and reachable.

steps.action: **Remove old hardware.** Turn the screw counterclockwise and keep the screw if it may fit the new piece.
steps.expect: old knob comes away without tearing the finish.

steps.action: **Clean the contact spot.** Wipe grime or compressed dust around the hole.
steps.expect: surface under the old hardware looks clean and dry.

steps.action: **Install the new knob.** Insert the screw from inside and thread the knob or pull by hand first.
steps.expect: screw catches without cross-threading.

steps.action: **Align and tighten.** Square the knob or pull, then tighten by hand plus a small nudge with the screwdriver. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overtightening can crush the cabinet face or strip the hardware threads, so stop when it no longer twists.
steps.expect: hardware is firm and straight.

steps.action: **Check all matching doors.** Compare height and angle with nearby knobs or pulls.
steps.expect: the replacement visually lines up with the set.

recipes.verification: The new knob or pull is straight, does not rotate under normal hand pressure, and matches the existing cabinet hole spacing without new unwanted holes.

recipes.title: replace a doorbell button
recipes.name: replace-a-doorbell-button
recipes.goal: A broken low-voltage doorbell button is replaced and rings the existing chime reliably.

steps.action: **Turn off doorbell power.** Switch off the doorbell transformer breaker if known, or turn off power before handling unknown wires.
steps.expect: the doorbell cannot ring while wires are separated.

steps.action: **Remove the old button.** Unscrew the button from the wall or trim and pull it out gently.
steps.expect: two low-voltage wires are visible.

steps.action: **Secure the wires.** Tape wires to the trim so they cannot slip into the wall.
steps.expect: both wire ends remain accessible.

steps.action: **Disconnect the old button.** Loosen terminal screws and remove the wires.
steps.expect: the old button is free.

steps.action: **Attach the new button.** Connect one wire to each terminal; polarity usually does not matter for a simple button.
steps.expect: both wires are clamped under terminal screws.

steps.action: **Mount the button.** Tuck wires gently and screw the button to the trim or wall.
steps.expect: the button sits flat without pinched wires.

steps.action: **Restore power and test.** Turn power back on and press the button.
steps.expect: the chime rings once per press.

recipes.verification: The mounted button is secure, does not hum or stick, and the chime sounds correctly on three separate presses.

recipes.title: replace a doorknob
recipes.name: replace-a-doorknob
recipes.goal: A doorknob set is replaced, the latch faces the right way, and the door opens, closes, and latches smoothly.

steps.action: **Open the door.** Keep it open for the whole job and block it from swinging.
steps.expect: both sides of the knob are reachable.

steps.action: **Find interior screws.** Look on the interior rose or under a small cover plate.
steps.expect: mounting screws or a release slot are visible.

steps.action: **Remove old knobs.** Unscrew interior screws and pull both knobs apart.
steps.expect: the spindle and knob halves come free.

steps.action: **Remove the latch.** Unscrew the latch plate on the door edge and slide the latch out.
steps.expect: an empty edge bore remains.

steps.action: **Install new latch.** Insert it with the slanted face toward the strike plate.
steps.expect: the latch plate sits flush and the latch bevel faces closing direction.

steps.action: **Check handedness.** [BRANCH: privacy passage knob | keyed entry knob] orient lock buttons, keyway, and interior side correctly.
steps.expect: the correct side faces the room or hallway.

steps.action: **Attach knobs.** Feed spindle through the latch, align posts, and tighten screws evenly.
steps.expect: knobs sit flat without binding.

steps.action: **Test alignment.** Close the door slowly and turn the knob several times.
steps.expect: latch retracts, enters the strike, and releases cleanly.

recipes.verification: With the door closed, the knob turns freely, the latch catches in the strike, and the door opens again from the intended side.

recipes.title: replace a faucet aerator
recipes.name: replace-a-faucet-aerator
recipes.goal: A clogged or damaged faucet aerator is removed, cleaned or replaced, and refitted so the faucet has an even splash-free stream.

steps.action: **Cover the drain.** Close the stopper or place a towel over the drain opening.
steps.expect: washers and screens cannot disappear.

steps.action: **Try hand removal.** Grip the aerator with a rubber pad and turn it counterclockwise from below.
steps.expect: the aerator loosens without tool marks.

steps.action: **Use padded pliers if stuck.** Wrap the aerator with cloth and turn gently with pliers.
steps.expect: the metal ring moves without scratching the finish.

steps.action: **Keep the parts in order.** Lay out the shell, washer, screen, and flow restrictor in removal order.
steps.expect: reassembly order is clear.

steps.action: **Clean reusable parts.** Soak mineral-crusted parts in vinegar for 20 minutes, then brush the screen and rinse.
steps.expect: holes are open and debris is gone.

steps.action: **Match a replacement.** [BRANCH: male threads | female threads] choose the same diameter and thread direction as the old aerator.
steps.expect: the new aerator starts by hand.

steps.action: **Reinstall by hand.** Seat the washer, thread the aerator clockwise, and stop when snug.
steps.expect: the aerator sits square to the spout.

steps.action: **Flow test.** Turn on cold water slowly, then hot water.
steps.expect: the stream is even with no spray at the threads.

steps.action: **Tighten only if needed.** If the threads seep, add a small padded-plier snug.
steps.expect: seepage stops without crushing the washer.

recipes.verification: With the aerator installed, hot and cold water run in a centered stream and no water beads around the aerator threads.

recipes.title: replace a light fixture
recipes.name: replace-a-light-fixture
recipes.goal: An existing light fixture is replaced with a compatible new fixture that is grounded, mounted securely, and controlled safely by the same switch.

steps.action: **Turn off the breaker.** Switch off the circuit breaker, not just the wall switch.
steps.expect: the fixture no longer turns on.

steps.action: **Test for power.** Use a non-contact tester and, if available, a contact meter at the fixture box.
steps.expect: all fixture conductors test dead.

steps.action: **Remove shade and bulbs.** Take off glass parts and bulbs before loosening the fixture.
steps.expect: the fixture is lighter and safer to handle.

steps.action: **Document wiring.** Photograph wire colors, connectors, and the ground connection before disconnecting anything.
steps.expect: you have a reference image.

steps.action: **Disconnect old fixture.** Support the fixture, remove wire connectors, separate fixture wires, and lower it.
steps.expect: house wires remain accessible in the box.

steps.action: **Inspect the box.** Check that the box is tight, not cracked, and has a grounding path.
steps.expect: the box can safely support the new fixture.

steps.action: **Attach mounting bracket.** Install the new bracket using the screws supplied for the electrical box.
steps.expect: the bracket sits tight and level.

steps.action: **Connect ground first.** Connect green or bare fixture ground to the house ground or grounded metal box as instructed.
steps.expect: ground is mechanically secure.

steps.action: **Connect neutral and hot.** [BRANCH: black-white wiring | marked fixture leads] connect neutral to neutral and switched hot to fixture hot using approved wire connectors.
steps.expect: no copper is exposed below connectors.

steps.action: **Mount the fixture.** Tuck wires carefully, fasten the fixture to the bracket, and install bulbs within wattage rating.
steps.expect: the fixture is secure and clear of pinched wires.

steps.action: **Restore power and test.** Turn the breaker on, then use the switch.
steps.expect: the fixture turns on and off normally with no buzzing, smell, or flicker.

recipes.verification: The breaker stays on, the wall switch controls the fixture reliably, the fixture is firmly mounted, and no conductor is exposed or energized when it should be off.

recipes.title: replace a light switch
recipes.name: replace-a-light-switch
recipes.goal: A like-for-like light switch is replaced safely, with power verified off before touching conductors and the wiring restored correctly.

steps.action: **Identify the switch type.** Remove nothing yet; note whether one switch or multiple switches control the light
steps.expect: you know whether the replacement is single-pole, 3-way, dimmer, or smart.

steps.action: **Turn the breaker off.** Switch off the breaker controlling the circuit; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* touching live wiring can cause serious injury, so do not continue until power is proven off
steps.expect: the light controlled by the switch no longer turns on.

steps.action: **Verify dead.** Test the switch, cover screws, and wires with a voltage tester before touching them
steps.expect: the tester shows no voltage on all conductors in the box.

steps.action: **Remove the cover and photograph wiring.** Take clear photos of wire colors, screw colors, and terminal positions
steps.expect: you have a reference showing every connection.

steps.action: **Label special wires.** Mark common, traveler, line, load, neutral, or ground if present [BRANCH: single-pole | 3-way | smart switch]
steps.expect: wires can be returned to equivalent terminals.

steps.action: **Move wires to the new switch.** Transfer one wire at a time to the matching screw or approved clamp
steps.expect: bare copper is fully under the terminal with no loose strands.

steps.action: **Ground the switch.** Attach the bare or green ground wire to the green screw if present
steps.expect: the metal yoke is grounded when a ground is available.

steps.action: **Mount and restore power.** Fold wires neatly, screw the switch into the box, install the cover, then turn the breaker on
steps.expect: the switch sits straight and the breaker stays on.

steps.action: **Test operation.** Turn the light on and off from every control location
steps.expect: the light works normally and no buzzing, heat, or flicker appears.

recipes.verification: With the cover installed, the switch controls the light correctly from all locations, the breaker stays on, and the switch does not buzz or feel warm after several minutes.

recipes.title: replace a range hood filter
recipes.name: replace-a-range-hood-filter
recipes.goal: The range hood grease or charcoal filter is replaced or refreshed so airflow and odor capture improve.

steps.action: **Turn off the hood.** Switch off fan and light, and let surfaces cool.
steps.expect: the hood is quiet and safe to touch.

steps.action: **Remove the filter.** Slide, unlatch, or push the filter toward the spring side and lower it out.
steps.expect: the filter comes free without bending.

steps.action: **Identify filter type.** Check whether it is washable metal mesh, disposable grease, or charcoal.
steps.expect: you know whether to wash or replace it.

steps.action: **Clean the opening.** Wipe grease from the filter frame and surrounding hood lip.
steps.expect: new filter edges will sit on a clean surface.

steps.action: **Install or wash.** Insert a new disposable or charcoal filter, or wash and dry a metal filter fully before reinstalling.
steps.expect: the filter is clean, dry, and correctly oriented.

steps.action: **Lock it in place.** Seat the filter tabs or latch until the frame is flush.
steps.expect: the filter does not sag or rattle.

steps.action: **Test airflow.** Run the fan on each speed and listen for vibration.
steps.expect: airflow is steady and the filter stays seated.

recipes.verification: The filter sits flush, stays locked while the fan runs on high, and visible grease buildup is removed from the filter area.

recipes.title: replace a refrigerator water filter
recipes.name: replace-a-refrigerator-water-filter
recipes.goal: The refrigerator water filter is replaced with a compatible cartridge, flushed, and reset so dispenser water tastes normal.

steps.action: **Confirm the filter model.** Match the cartridge number to the refrigerator label or manual.
steps.expect: the new cartridge shape and part number match the old one.

steps.action: **Find the filter housing.** Open the grille, upper compartment, or interior filter door.
steps.expect: the old cartridge and release mechanism are visible.

steps.action: **Protect the area.** Place a towel below the housing and remove nearby food if needed.
steps.expect: minor drips will land on the towel.

steps.action: **Remove the old filter.** Press, twist, or pull according to the housing design.
steps.expect: the cartridge releases without forcing the plastic.

steps.action: **Prepare the new filter.** Remove caps, keep seals clean, and align arrows or tabs.
steps.expect: the cartridge is ready to insert without exposed packaging.

steps.action: **Install the new filter.** Push or twist until it seats and locks.
steps.expect: the filter sits flush and cannot be pulled out lightly.

steps.action: **Flush the filter.** Dispense the manual's recommended amount of water, usually several quarts, discarding cloudy first water.
steps.expect: flow becomes steady and water runs clear.

steps.action: **Reset the indicator.** Hold the filter-reset button or menu command until the light changes.
steps.expect: the filter status returns to normal or full.

recipes.verification: The filter is locked in place, no water drips from the housing, dispenser flow is steady, and the filter indicator is reset.

recipes.title: replace a showerhead
recipes.name: replace-a-showerhead
recipes.goal: An old showerhead is removed and a new one seals on the shower arm without leaks or scratched finishes.

steps.action: **Confirm the shower is off.** Close the shower valve fully and let water drip out of the old head.
steps.expect: no active flow remains.

steps.action: **Protect the finish.** Wrap a cloth around the old showerhead nut before using a wrench.
steps.expect: tool jaws do not touch chrome directly.

steps.action: **Unscrew the old head.** Turn the showerhead counterclockwise while supporting the shower arm with your other hand.
steps.expect: the head separates without the wall arm rotating.

steps.action: **Clean the threads.** Remove old tape, mineral crust, and debris from the shower arm threads with fingers or a soft brush.
steps.expect: bare threads are visible all around.

steps.action: **Inspect the shower arm.** Check for cracks, severe corrosion, or looseness at the wall.
steps.expect: the arm feels solid and usable.

steps.action: **Apply new tape.** Wrap plumber's tape clockwise around the male threads two to three turns, keeping the first thread clear.
steps.expect: tape lies flat and tight in the tightening direction.

steps.action: **Install the new showerhead.** Thread it on by hand until snug and square.
steps.expect: it turns smoothly without cross-threading.

steps.action: **Tighten only if needed.** [BRANCH: rubber washer seal | threaded metal seal] hand-tighten washer-style heads; give metal-thread heads a small wrench nudge through a cloth.
steps.expect: the connection is snug without strain.

steps.action: **Leak test.** Turn the shower on gradually and watch the joint for one minute.
steps.expect: water exits only through the spray face.

steps.action: **Adjust spray and final check.** Cycle spray settings and angle the head.
steps.expect: no joint drip appears under normal movement.

recipes.verification: With the shower running for one minute on each spray mode, the showerhead joint and wall escutcheon stay dry except for normal spray splash.

recipes.title: replace a smoke alarm
recipes.name: replace-a-smoke-alarm
recipes.goal: An expired or failed smoke alarm is replaced with the right type, tested, and dated so the household knows when it must be replaced again.

steps.action: **Check the replacement rule.** Read the manufacture date on the old alarm and replace it if it is 10 years old or older.
steps.expect: you have confirmed replacement is needed.

steps.action: **Silence and remove the old unit.** Twist it off the base and disconnect the battery or plug. [BRANCH: battery-only | hardwired] hardwired units require breaker power off before unplugging the harness.
steps.expect: the old alarm is down and no live work is exposed.

steps.action: **Match the alarm type.** Replace like with like where code or system design requires it, such as smoke, heat, photoelectric, ionization, or combination CO.
steps.expect: the new unit matches the location and old function.

steps.action: **Mount the new base.** Use the supplied base and screws, drilling only where you have checked for wires or pipes.
steps.expect: the base is tight and flat.

steps.action: **Connect power or battery.** Plug in the harness or install the battery, then seat the alarm on the base.
steps.expect: the alarm chirps or shows a ready light.

steps.action: **Test the alarm.** Press and hold the test button until it sounds, warning nearby people first.
steps.expect: the alarm sounds clearly and interconnected alarms respond if fitted.

steps.action: **Log the date.** Write the installation date and replacement year on the unit or household maintenance log.
steps.expect: the next 10-year deadline is visible.

recipes.verification: The installed alarm sounds on its test button and has an installation date plus a replacement date no more than 10 years out.

recipes.title: replace a tap washer
recipes.name: replace-a-tap-washer
recipes.goal: A dripping compression tap is opened, its worn washer or O-ring is replaced, and the tap is returned to service without leaks.

steps.action: **Turn the water off first.** Close the isolation valve under the sink or the main shutoff, then open the tap fully.
steps.expect: water flow stops after the pipe drains.

steps.action: **Protect the finish and drain.** Lay a towel in the basin, cover the drain, and wrap chrome parts with cloth before gripping.
steps.expect: the work area catches parts and tools do not bite into visible metal.

steps.action: **Remove the handle cap and screw.** Pry the decorative cap gently, back out the screw, and lift the handle straight up.
steps.expect: the valve stem or bonnet is visible.

steps.action: **Loosen the bonnet or packing nut.** Hold the tap body steady with one hand and turn the nut counterclockwise with the spanner.
steps.expect: the stem assembly begins to unscrew without twisting the whole tap.

steps.action: **Withdraw the stem assembly.** Turn it out slowly and set parts down in removal order.
steps.expect: the washer at the bottom or O-ring on the stem is exposed.

steps.action: **Swap the sealing part.** Remove the retaining screw if present, fit the same-size washer or O-ring, and seat it flat. [BRANCH: flat washer | O-ring]
steps.expect: the new part sits square with no bulge or twist.

steps.action: **Reassemble without over-tightening.** Thread the stem in by hand first, snug the bonnet, reinstall the handle, and leave the tap closed.
steps.expect: the handle turns normally and the bonnet is seated.

steps.action: **Restore water and test.** Open the shutoff slowly, then open and close the tap several times while watching the base and spout.
steps.expect: flow returns, the tap closes cleanly, and no new seep appears.

recipes.verification: With water restored, the tap runs normally when opened, stops completely when closed for 2 minutes, and the handle base and under-sink valves remain dry.

recipes.title: replace a thermostat battery
recipes.name: replace-a-thermostat-battery
recipes.goal: The thermostat batteries are replaced and the display and HVAC commands work normally.

steps.action: **Set the system off.** Move the thermostat mode to Off before opening the faceplate.
steps.expect: heating and cooling calls stop.

steps.action: **Open the battery area.** Slide out the battery tray or pull the faceplate straight from the wall plate.
steps.expect: batteries and polarity marks are visible.

steps.action: **Remove old batteries.** Take out every battery and check for corrosion.
steps.expect: the contacts are clean and intact.

steps.action: **Install new batteries.** Match plus and minus ends to the compartment marks.
steps.expect: the batteries sit firmly in the holder.

steps.action: **Reattach the faceplate.** Align pins and press the thermostat back onto the wall plate.
steps.expect: the faceplate sits flush without bent pins.

steps.action: **Restore settings.** Set the date, time, mode, and schedule if they were lost.
steps.expect: the display shows normal room temperature and settings.

steps.action: **Test a call.** Set heat or cool a few degrees beyond room temperature, then return to normal.
steps.expect: the system responds, then stops when set back.

recipes.verification: The thermostat display is readable, low-battery warning is gone, and a heat or cool test command starts and stops the HVAC system correctly.

recipes.title: replace a toilet fill valve
recipes.name: replace-a-toilet-fill-valve
recipes.goal: A faulty toilet fill valve is removed and replaced so the tank refills quietly to the correct level without leaks.

steps.action: **Shut off water.** Turn the toilet shutoff valve clockwise until it stops.
steps.expect: no new water enters the tank.

steps.action: **Drain the tank.** Flush, hold the handle down, then sponge remaining water into a bucket.
steps.expect: the tank bottom is nearly dry.

steps.action: **Disconnect the supply line.** Place a towel under the tank and loosen the nut below the fill valve.
steps.expect: the supply line hangs free with only a small spill.

steps.action: **Remove the old valve.** Unscrew the mounting nut under the tank and lift the fill valve out from above.
steps.expect: the tank hole is open and the old gasket is removed.

steps.action: **Set the new height.** Adjust the new valve so its critical-level mark sits at least 1 inch above the overflow tube.
steps.expect: the valve height matches the toilet and maker instructions.

steps.action: **Install the new gasket.** Insert the valve through the tank hole with the rubber gasket inside the tank.
steps.expect: the valve stands straight and the gasket lies flat.

steps.action: **Tighten the mounting nut.** Hand-tighten, then snug slightly with a wrench without stressing the tank.
steps.expect: the valve does not wobble.

steps.action: **Connect the refill tube.** Clip the tube to the overflow tube above the water line, not pushed down inside it.
steps.expect: refill water can flow into the overflow opening without siphoning.

steps.action: **Reconnect the supply.** Attach the supply line to the valve shank and tighten until snug.
steps.expect: the connector seats squarely.

steps.action: **Restore and test.** Open the shutoff slowly, let the tank fill, and adjust the float to the fill line.
steps.expect: the tank fills and stops without dripping below.

recipes.verification: With the tank full, the fill valve stops at the marked level and the tank bottom, supply nut, and shutoff stay dry for ten minutes.

recipes.title: replace a toilet flapper
recipes.name: replace-a-toilet-flapper
recipes.goal: A running or weak-flushing toilet gets a matching new flapper so the tank seals, refills, and flushes correctly.

steps.action: **Shut off the toilet water.** Turn the wall valve clockwise until it stops.
steps.expect: the fill valve does not refill after flushing.

steps.action: **Drain the tank.** Flush once and hold the handle down until most water leaves the tank.
steps.expect: only a shallow puddle remains.

steps.action: **Remove the lid safely.** Lift the tank lid with two hands and set it flat on a towel.
steps.expect: the lid cannot slide or crack.

steps.action: **Inspect the old setup.** Note where the flapper ears attach and how much chain slack reaches the handle arm.
steps.expect: you have a clear reference for reassembly.

steps.action: **Unclip the old flapper.** Detach the chain, then pull the rubber ears off the overflow tube posts.
steps.expect: the old flapper is free without bending the flush valve.

steps.action: **Clean the seat.** Wipe the flush valve seat with a cloth to remove slime or mineral grit.
steps.expect: the sealing surface feels smooth.

steps.action: **Match and install the new flapper.** [BRANCH: two-post ears | ring adapter] use the ears on side posts, or slide the ring over the overflow tube only if that is the toilet's style.
steps.expect: the flapper pivots freely and sits centered.

steps.action: **Set chain length.** Clip the chain to the handle arm with about 1/4 to 1/2 inch of slack when closed.
steps.expect: the flapper rests flat and lifts promptly when the handle moves.

steps.action: **Restore water.** Turn the wall valve counterclockwise slowly and let the tank fill.
steps.expect: water reaches the fill line and stops.

steps.action: **Test flushes.** Flush three times while watching the flapper close.
steps.expect: each flush releases fully, then seals without tank refilling.

recipes.verification: After three flushes, the tank reaches its fill line, the fill valve shuts off, and no refill sound occurs for ten minutes.

recipes.title: replace a toilet seat
recipes.name: replace-a-toilet-seat
recipes.goal: An old toilet seat is removed and a matching new seat is installed squarely without rocking or scratching the bowl.

steps.action: **Confirm the shape.** Compare the new seat with the bowl before opening all hardware.
steps.expect: the seat follows the rim shape and bolt spacing.

steps.action: **Open bolt caps.** Flip up the plastic caps behind the seat using a fingernail or flat screwdriver wrapped in cloth.
steps.expect: bolt heads are visible.

steps.action: **Hold the underside nut.** Reach below the bowl rim and grip the nut while turning the bolt from above.
steps.expect: the bolt starts backing out.

steps.action: **Use a rusted-bolt trick.** [BRANCH: plastic nut | metal nut] cut a plastic nut carefully with locking pliers or use penetrating oil on a metal nut, then turn slowly.
steps.expect: the old fastener releases without cracking porcelain.

steps.action: **Remove the old seat.** Lift the seat and bolts away, keeping washers for comparison only.
steps.expect: the hinge deck is bare.

steps.action: **Clean the mounting area.** Scrub around the bolt holes and dry the porcelain.
steps.expect: the new hinges sit flat.

steps.action: **Position the new seat.** Drop the new bolts through the hinge holes and bowl holes with any supplied washers in the correct order.
steps.expect: the seat is centered over the rim.

steps.action: **Tighten evenly.** Alternate sides by hand, then snug with a tool while holding alignment.
steps.expect: both hinges are firm and parallel.

steps.action: **Check for rocking.** Lift, lower, and sit lightly on the closed lid if it is rated for sitting.
steps.expect: the seat does not slide, twist, or rock.

recipes.verification: The seat is centered, both hinge caps close, the lid opens freely, and the seat does not move when pressed side to side.

recipes.title: replace a worn electrical cord end
recipes.name: replace-a-worn-electrical-cord-end
recipes.goal: A damaged plug end on a flexible cord is replaced with a matching rated plug so the appliance or tool can be used safely.

steps.action: **Unplug the cord.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* disconnect the cord from power and confirm the plug cannot be energized while working.
steps.expect: the cord is fully separated from any outlet.

steps.action: **Inspect the cord.** Check the full visible length for cuts, heat damage, or crushed jacket.
steps.expect: damage is limited to the plug end.

steps.action: **Cut off the old end.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cut the cord behind the damaged strain relief or burned insulation.
steps.expect: only clean, flexible cord remains.

steps.action: **Open the new plug.** Disassemble the replacement plug and note terminal colors or markings.
steps.expect: hot, neutral, and ground terminals are identifiable.

steps.action: **Strip the jacket.** Remove only enough outer jacket and conductor insulation to fit the plug terminals.
steps.expect: copper is exposed at the correct length without nicked strands.

steps.action: **Connect conductors.** Attach green to ground, white or ribbed to silver neutral, and black or smooth to brass hot.
steps.expect: each conductor is under the correct terminal with no stray strands.

steps.action: **Secure strain relief.** Clamp the plug body onto the outer jacket, not individual wires.
steps.expect: pulling lightly on the cord does not stress terminals.

steps.action: **Close and test.** Reassemble the plug and test in a GFCI-protected outlet if possible.
steps.expect: the device powers normally without heat, sparks, or flicker.

recipes.verification: The plug strain relief grips the jacket, conductors are on correct terminals, and the device runs for one minute without sparks, odor, flicker, or heat at the plug.

recipes.title: replace a zipper pull
recipes.name: replace-a-zipper-pull
recipes.goal: A broken zipper pull tab is replaced with a functional pull without replacing the zipper slider.

steps.action: **Check the slider.** Move the slider up and down using a temporary paper clip if needed.
steps.expect: the zipper teeth open and close normally.

steps.action: **Remove broken pieces.** Take off any sharp or dangling fragments from the slider loop.
steps.expect: the loop is clear and not cracked through.

steps.action: **Choose the replacement.** Match a metal tab, split ring, or cord pull to the size of the slider loop.
steps.expect: the replacement can pass through the loop without forcing.

steps.action: **Open the connector.** Use fingernails or pliers to open the split ring or jump ring just enough.
steps.expect: the connector gap accepts the slider loop.

steps.action: **Attach the pull.** Thread the connector through the slider loop and rotate or close it fully.
steps.expect: the pull hangs from the slider without falling out.

steps.action: **Close sharp gaps.** Squeeze any jump ring ends flush with pliers.
steps.expect: no edge catches on fabric or skin.

steps.action: **Test under load.** Zip and unzip several times while holding the new pull.
steps.expect: the pull moves the slider smoothly.

recipes.verification: The new pull is securely attached, has no sharp open gap, and opens and closes the zipper through its full travel three times.

recipes.title: replace an outlet
recipes.name: replace-an-outlet
recipes.goal: A worn standard electrical outlet is replaced with a matching rated receptacle after power is shut off and verified dead.

steps.action: **Switch off the breaker.** Turn off the breaker feeding the outlet and tell others not to restore it.
steps.expect: plugged-in lamps or devices at that outlet turn off.

steps.action: **Test the outlet dead.** Use a known-working tester on the outlet slots, then test the tester on a live outlet again.
steps.expect: the target outlet shows no voltage and the tester is proven functional.

steps.action: **Remove the cover.** Unscrew the wall plate and set screws aside.
steps.expect: the receptacle mounting screws are visible.

steps.action: **Pull the receptacle out.** Remove mounting screws and pull the device straight out by the yoke.
steps.expect: wires are visible without stretching.

steps.action: **Test every wire dead.** Check hot, neutral, ground, and each cable entering the box.
steps.expect: no conductor indicates voltage.

steps.action: **Note the wiring.** Photograph the outlet and label hot wires on brass screws, neutral wires on silver screws, and ground on green.
steps.expect: each wire's original terminal is documented.

steps.action: **Transfer one wire at a time.** [BRANCH: side screw | backwire clamp] move each wire to the matching terminal on the new outlet, avoiding push-in backstab holes.
steps.expect: hot, neutral, and ground are on correct terminals.

steps.action: **Mount the outlet.** Fold wires gently, secure the receptacle plumb, and reinstall the cover plate.
steps.expect: the outlet is firm and the cover is not cracked.

steps.action: **Restore and test.** Turn the breaker on and use a receptacle tester.
steps.expect: the tester reports correct wiring and a plug fits snugly.

recipes.verification: With the cover installed and breaker on, a plug-in tester reports correct wiring and the outlet holds a plug firmly without heat, buzz, or movement.

recipes.title: replace furniture feet
recipes.name: replace-furniture-feet
recipes.goal: Damaged or uneven furniture feet are removed, matched by fitting type, replaced, and leveled so the furniture sits stable without wobble.

steps.action: **Empty and protect.** Remove loose items, drawers if practical, and place a blanket on the floor.
steps.expect: the furniture can be moved without scratching floors or spilling contents.

steps.action: **Tip safely.** With help for heavy pieces, tilt or invert the furniture onto padding.
steps.expect: all feet are reachable and the piece is stable.

steps.action: **Identify the fitting.** [BRANCH: screw-in foot | plate-mounted foot | glide] inspect whether the foot threads into an insert, screws to a plate, or presses into a socket.
steps.expect: the attachment type is clear.

steps.action: **Remove one foot.** Unscrew, unbolt, or pry out one damaged foot while supporting the frame.
steps.expect: the mounting point is exposed.

steps.action: **Match size and height.** Compare thread diameter, plate hole spacing, stem length, and foot height.
steps.expect: the replacement matches the old fitting.

steps.action: **Repair minor looseness.** Tighten loose plates or fill small stripped wood screw holes before installing.
steps.expect: the mount holds screws firmly.

steps.action: **Install replacements.** Fit the new foot straight and tighten until snug, repeating for matching feet as needed.
steps.expect: feet sit square to the furniture base.

steps.action: **Set the piece upright.** Lower the furniture gently onto all feet.
steps.expect: weight is carried evenly.

steps.action: **Level and test wobble.** Adjust threaded feet or add suitable glides, then press each corner.
steps.expect: the furniture stays steady without rocking.

recipes.verification: The furniture rests on all feet, does not wobble when each corner is pressed, and moves without scraping or tipping.

recipes.title: repot a houseplant
recipes.name: repot-a-houseplant
recipes.goal: A houseplant is moved into a slightly larger draining pot with fresh mix, loosened roots, and recovery conditions that reduce transplant shock.

steps.action: **Prepare the new pot.** Add fresh mix to the bottom so the plant will sit at its old soil height.
steps.expect: pot has drainage and a shallow base layer of mix.

steps.action: **Slide the plant out.** Tip the old pot, support the stems at soil level, and squeeze or tap the pot rather than pulling leaves.
steps.expect: root ball comes out mostly intact.

steps.action: **Inspect the roots.** [BRANCH: healthy roots | rotten roots] keep firm pale or tan roots; trim black, mushy, smelly roots with clean scissors.
steps.expect: only sound roots remain.

steps.action: **Loosen the root edge.** Tease circling roots outward and roughen the bottom lightly.
steps.expect: roots point into new soil instead of wrapping the old shape.

steps.action: **Set the plant in the new pot.** Center it and keep the crown at the same height it grew before.
steps.expect: stem base is not buried and root ball is not exposed.

steps.action: **Backfill with fresh mix.** Add mix around the sides, firming lightly with fingers, not packing hard.
steps.expect: plant stands upright with small air pockets closed.

steps.action: **Water to settle.** Water slowly until drainage appears, then empty the saucer after 15-20 minutes.
steps.expect: mix settles around roots and no standing water remains.

steps.action: **Give recovery conditions.** Put the plant in bright indirect light and skip fertilizer for 3-4 weeks.
steps.expect: plant has stable moisture and low stress while roots adjust.

recipes.verification: The plant sits upright at its original soil height, water drains freely, no saucer water remains, and the plant is placed in bright indirect light for recovery.

recipes.title: reproof a waterproof jacket
recipes.name: reproof-a-waterproof-jacket
recipes.goal: A waterproof jacket's durable water repellent finish is renewed so water beads on the outer fabric again.

steps.action: **Clean detergent residue.** Rinse the washer detergent drawer or choose a clean basin.
steps.expect: no regular detergent or softener residue remains.

steps.action: **Close hardware.** Zip zippers, close hook-and-loop tabs, and loosen drawcords.
steps.expect: trims are secured and fabric can wash evenly.

steps.action: **Wash with technical cleaner.** Use the product dose and label-safe cycle.
steps.expect: dirt and body oils are removed without fabric softener.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly.** Run an extra rinse if the cleaner label or jacket label recommends it.
steps.expect: no suds remain in the jacket.

steps.action: **Apply DWR.** Use [BRANCH: spray-on | wash-in] according to the product type, coating the outer face evenly.
steps.expect: treatment reaches the shell fabric without puddles.

steps.action: **Remove excess.** Wipe drips, especially on dark panels and inside linings.
steps.expect: the jacket surface is evenly damp, not streaked.

steps.action: **Heat activate if allowed.** Tumble dry low or press with a towel barrier as directed. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* excess heat can delaminate seams or melt trim; confirm the care label first.
steps.expect: the finish cures without scorching or peeling.

steps.action: **Cool and test beading.** Sprinkle water on shoulders and sleeves.
steps.expect: water beads and rolls instead of soaking in immediately.

recipes.verification: After drying, water sprinkled on high-wear outer panels beads for at least 30 seconds without darkening the fabric.

recipes.title: rescue a wet phone
recipes.name: rescue-a-wet-phone
recipes.goal: Reduce damage to a wet phone by powering it down, drying it with air and desiccant, and delaying charging until hidden moisture has had time to leave.

steps.action: **Remove it from liquid.** Pick up the phone, keeping ports pointed downward if water is draining.
steps.expect: the phone is no longer exposed to water.

steps.action: **Power it off.** Shut it down immediately if it is still on; do not test apps or buttons.
steps.expect: the screen is off and the phone is not vibrating or ringing.

steps.action: **Disconnect accessories.** Remove the case, cable, earbuds, and SIM tray if accessible without forcing anything.
steps.expect: trapped water has more paths to evaporate.

steps.action: **Dry the outside.** Blot with a lint-free towel and avoid shaking hard, heating, or blowing into ports.
steps.expect: visible surface water is gone.

steps.action: **Position ports downward.** Stand or lean the phone so charging and speaker openings face down for 30 minutes.
steps.expect: any loose drops can drain out.

steps.action: **Use real desiccant.** Place the phone in a sealed container with silica gel packets or a commercial drying pouch.
steps.expect: desiccant surrounds the phone without touching ports with dust.

steps.action: **Skip rice.** Do not bury the phone in rice; it dries poorly and can leave starch or grains in ports.
steps.expect: the phone stays in clean air or silica, not food.

steps.action: **Wait 48 hours.** Leave the phone powered off and uncharged for two full days. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* charging a wet phone can short components; confirm the wait is complete and ports look dry first.
steps.expect: the phone has had time to dry internally.

steps.action: **Inspect ports.** Check the charging port, speakers, and SIM slot with a flashlight, without inserting metal tools.
steps.expect: no droplets, lint clumps, or corrosion are visible.

steps.action: **Power on carefully.** Try turning it on, then charge only if it boots normally and the port is dry.
steps.expect: the phone starts without heat, smoke, crackling, or repeated shutdowns.

recipes.verification: After at least 48 hours powered off, the phone boots normally and the ports show no visible moisture before charging.

recipes.title: reset a garbage disposal
recipes.name: reset-a-garbage-disposal
recipes.goal: A jammed garbage disposal is safely freed, reset, and tested without putting hands into the grinding chamber.

steps.action: **Turn power off.** Switch off the wall switch and unplug the disposal if it has a cord.
steps.expect: the disposal cannot start accidentally.

steps.action: **Look into the chamber.** Use a flashlight from above without placing fingers inside.
steps.expect: visible objects can be located safely.

steps.action: **Remove loose objects.** Use tongs or pliers to lift out utensils, glass, bones, or other debris.
steps.expect: foreign objects are removed without hand contact.

steps.action: **Insert the hex key.** Put the hex key into the center socket on the bottom of the disposal.
steps.expect: the key seats firmly.

steps.action: **Rock the motor free.** Turn the key back and forth until it rotates more freely.
steps.expect: resistance decreases and the flywheel moves.

steps.action: **Clear remaining debris.** Recheck from above with the flashlight and remove loosened pieces with tongs.
steps.expect: the chamber looks clear.

steps.action: **Press reset.** Push the red reset button on the bottom or side of the disposal.
steps.expect: the button clicks in and stays in.

steps.action: **Restore power.** Plug the disposal back in or prepare to use the wall switch.
steps.expect: power is available only when you choose to test.

steps.action: **Run water first.** Turn cold water on full before starting the disposal.
steps.expect: water flows freely into the drain.

steps.action: **Pulse the disposal.** [BRANCH: normal hum and spin | hum only] if it spins, run briefly; if it only hums, turn it off immediately and repeat freeing once.
steps.expect: the disposal spins without loud grinding.

steps.action: **Flush.** Let cold water run for 20 to 30 seconds after turning the disposal off.
steps.expect: loosened waste clears the drain.

recipes.verification: With cold water running, the disposal starts, spins normally, drains without backing up, and remains off when the switch is off.

recipes.title: reset a gfci outlet
recipes.name: reset-a-gfci-outlet
recipes.goal: A tripped GFCI outlet is identified, reset, and tested so protected outlets work again without ignoring an active electrical fault.

steps.action: **Unplug loads.** Remove appliances or chargers from the dead outlet and nearby protected outlets
steps.expect: nothing is drawing power from the affected receptacles.

steps.action: **Check for obvious danger.** Look for water, scorching, cracked covers, or heat before touching buttons
steps.expect: the outlet face is intact, dry, and cool.

steps.action: **Find the tripped GFCI.** Search bathrooms, kitchen counters, garage, basement, laundry, exterior, and nearby rooms for an outlet with TEST and RESET buttons
steps.expect: you locate the controlling GFCI or confirm none is visible.

steps.action: **Press RESET firmly.** Push RESET until it clicks and stays in [BRANCH: button holds | button pops back out]
steps.expect: the button remains engaged if the fault is cleared.

steps.action: **Test power.** Plug in a lamp or tester at the original dead outlet
steps.expect: the device powers on or the tester shows a normal pattern.

steps.action: **Run the built-in test.** Press TEST on the GFCI, then confirm power shuts off at the protected outlet
steps.expect: the lamp or tester turns off.

steps.action: **Reset again.** Press RESET after the test
steps.expect: power returns and the reset button stays latched.

steps.action: **Reconnect loads one at a time.** Plug devices back in separately so a bad device can reveal itself
steps.expect: power remains on after each device is connected.

recipes.verification: The GFCI TEST button cuts power, RESET restores power, and the original protected outlet powers a tester or lamp afterward.

recipes.title: reset a tripped breaker
recipes.name: reset-a-tripped-breaker
recipes.goal: Power is restored to the dead circuit by resetting the tripped breaker, and the overload or fault that tripped it has been identified so it does not immediately trip again.

steps.action: **Unplug or switch off the suspects first.** On the dead circuit, unplug whatever was running when the power dropped, especially high-draw items (space heater, kettle, microwave, hair dryer, vacuum) and anything that smelled hot or sparked. Resetting into a live fault just trips it again, or worse.
steps.expect: the likely culprits are physically unplugged, not just switched off.

steps.action: **Go to the panel and open the door.**
steps.expect: one or two columns of breaker handles, ideally with a circuit label sheet inside the door.

steps.action: **Identify the tripped breaker.** Scan for the handle that is out of line with its neighbors: most breakers trip to a middle position, some show an orange or red flag window, a few trip fully to OFF. Run a finger lightly across the handles if the light is bad; the tripped one feels loose or springy.
steps.expect: exactly one handle in the middle or flagged position that matches the dead area's label.

steps.action: **Reset with off-then-on.** Push the handle firmly all the way to OFF first (you will feel a click as the mechanism resets), then firmly to ON. A tripped breaker pushed straight toward ON will not latch.
steps.expect: the handle latches solidly at ON and stays there.

steps.action: **Confirm power is back.** Check a light or outlet on the circuit.
steps.expect: the dead area is live again.

steps.action: **Reintroduce loads one at a time.** Plug the suspects back in individually, waiting a minute between each, starting with the least suspicious.
steps.expect: each device runs without the breaker tripping; if one device trips it, you have found the fault.

steps.action: **Fix the root cause.** [BRANCH: overload (too many high-draw devices on one circuit) → redistribute them to outlets on other circuits | one faulty device → retire or repair it, do not plug it in elsewhere | no cause found and no re-trip → note the event and move on]
steps.expect: circuit holds under its normal load.

recipes.verification: The breaker handle sits fully at ON, all normal loads on the circuit are running, and the breaker has held for at least 15 minutes under the circuit's usual load. If it would not hold, the circuit is OFF and an electrician is scheduled: that is also a valid safe end state.

recipes.title: reset a wifi router
recipes.name: reset-a-wifi-router
recipes.goal: Restore a home internet connection by using the right router reset method without accidentally erasing network settings.

steps.action: **Identify the devices.** Find the modem, router, or combined gateway and note which cables go where.
steps.expect: you can tell the power cable from Ethernet or coax/fiber cables.

steps.action: **Choose reset type.** [BRANCH: power-cycle for normal outage | factory reset for forgotten settings or bad configuration] use power-cycle first for most problems.
steps.expect: you know whether settings will be preserved.

steps.action: **Power off cleanly.** Unplug the power from the router and modem, or the combined gateway.
steps.expect: lights turn off within a few seconds.

steps.action: **Wait 30 seconds.** Leave power disconnected long enough for capacitors and sessions to clear.
steps.expect: the devices remain fully dark.

steps.action: **Reconnect modem first.** Plug in the modem or gateway and wait for internet, online, or WAN lights to stabilize.
steps.expect: the service light becomes steady or follows the normal ready pattern.

steps.action: **Reconnect router second.** If separate, plug in the router after the modem is ready.
steps.expect: Wi-Fi lights begin blinking and then settle.

steps.action: **Wait before reconnecting.** Give devices 3 to 5 minutes before judging the result.
steps.expect: your phone or laptop sees the Wi-Fi network again.

steps.action: **Test internet.** Connect to Wi-Fi and open a new website or run a speed test.
steps.expect: pages load without captive portal or DNS errors.

steps.action: **Factory reset only if needed.** Hold the recessed reset button for the manual's required time, often 10 to 15 seconds. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* factory reset erases Wi-Fi name, password, and custom settings; confirm you can reconfigure them first.
steps.expect: lights flash or the router reboots into default settings.

steps.action: **Call the ISP if service stays down.** Contact the provider when modem online lights never stabilize or the outage affects multiple devices.
steps.expect: the ISP can check line status, outages, and provisioning.

recipes.verification: At least one device connects to the Wi-Fi network and loads a fresh external website after the router finishes restarting.

recipes.title: respond to a carbon monoxide alarm
recipes.name: respond-to-a-carbon-monoxide-alarm
recipes.goal: A carbon monoxide alarm triggers immediate evacuation, emergency notification, and no re-entry until professionals declare the space safe.

steps.action: **Leave immediately.** Get everyone outside into fresh air without searching for the source.
steps.expect: exposure begins to stop.

steps.action: **Help vulnerable people.** Assist children, older adults, disabled people, and pets only if it does not trap you inside.
steps.expect: household members are moving out.

steps.action: **Avoid switches and flames if gas is suspected.** Do not light flames or operate unnecessary electrical switches if you also smell gas.
steps.expect: ignition risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Call emergency services from outside.** Report the carbon monoxide alarm, symptoms, address, and fuel-burning appliances.
steps.expect: responders are dispatched or utility help is arranged.

steps.action: **Check symptoms.** Ask everyone about headache, dizziness, nausea, confusion, chest pain, and breathing trouble.
steps.expect: possible poisoning is identified.

steps.action: **Get medical help for symptoms.** [BRANCH: symptoms present | no symptoms] request medical evaluation for anyone symptomatic; keep asymptomatic people outside too.
steps.expect: poisoning is not missed.

steps.action: **Account for everyone.** Use the meeting place and report missing people to responders.
steps.expect: rescuers know if someone may still be inside.

steps.action: **Do not re-enter.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* going back inside can cause collapse and death; confirm clearance from responders before entry.
steps.expect: no one returns to contaminated air.

steps.action: **Ventilate only if instructed.** Let responders or the utility decide when doors and windows should be opened.
steps.expect: investigation and safety are not compromised.

steps.action: **Arrange repair before reuse.** Have fuel-burning appliances, vents, chimneys, and detectors inspected.
steps.expect: the source is corrected before normal occupancy.

recipes.verification: Everyone is outside in fresh air, emergency services or the gas emergency utility has been contacted, symptomatic people are getting medical evaluation, and no one re-enters until professionals clear the building.

recipes.title: restore a flattened pillow
recipes.name: restore-a-flattened-pillow
recipes.goal: A flattened pillow is fluffed, dried, and checked for support so it can be used comfortably or identified for replacement.

steps.action: **Check the label and fill.** Identify [BRANCH: down | polyester | foam] and drying limits.
steps.expect: the pillow type and safe method are known.

steps.action: **Inspect for failure.** Look for clumps, odor, stains, torn seams, or foam crumbling.
steps.expect: pillow is suitable for restoration or marked for replacement.

steps.action: **Hand-fluff corners.** Push fill from edges toward the center and shake the pillow on all sides.
steps.expect: fill redistributes more evenly.

steps.action: **Air it out.** Place the pillow in sun or strong indoor airflow for 30-60 minutes.
steps.expect: moisture and stale odor reduce.

steps.action: **Tumble if allowed.** Dry on no-heat or low heat with dryer balls, checking every 15 minutes.
steps.expect: fill lifts and separates without overheating.

steps.action: **Cool and reshape.** Lay the pillow flat and pat it into an even rectangle.
steps.expect: the pillow holds a fuller shape.

steps.action: **Add protection.** Put on a clean pillow protector and pillowcase.
steps.expect: restored loft is shielded from sweat and oils.

recipes.verification: The pillow is fully dry, evenly filled, free of musty odor, and rebounds after being compressed by hand for 10 seconds.

recipes.title: revive a dying houseplant
recipes.name: revive-a-dying-houseplant
recipes.goal: A struggling houseplant is diagnosed for water, light, pests, and roots, then stabilized with the smallest useful intervention.

steps.action: **Check soil moisture first.** Probe 3-5 cm deep, not just the surface. [BRANCH: dry | wet | evenly moist] match the next action to the reading.
steps.expect: a real moisture diagnosis.

steps.action: **Read the light symptoms.** Look for leggy growth, leaning, scorch, or pale leaves.
steps.expect: light is identified as too low, too harsh, or probably acceptable.

steps.action: **Inspect leaves and stems.** Check undersides, nodes, and soil for pests, webbing, scale, or sticky residue.
steps.expect: pests are found or reasonably ruled out.

steps.action: **Slide out the root ball if soil is wet or sour.** Look for firm pale roots versus black mushy roots.
steps.expect: root health is known before more watering.

steps.action: **Trim only dead material.** Cut crisp brown leaves and mushy stems with clean scissors; leave green tissue that still feeds the plant.
steps.expect: plant is cleaner without losing viable growth.

steps.action: **Correct the main cause.** [BRANCH: underwatered | overwatered | low light | pests] soak and drain dry plants, dry and repot rotten ones, move light-starved plants, isolate and treat pests.
steps.expect: one primary fix is in place.

steps.action: **Stabilize conditions.** Keep temperature steady, avoid fertilizer, and water only when the plant's soil target is reached.
steps.expect: no extra stress is added.

steps.action: **Wait before judging.** Monitor weekly for new growth or firming leaves.
steps.expect: recovery is measured over weeks, not hours.

recipes.verification: The plant has one diagnosed primary problem, dead tissue removed, corrected water or light conditions, and at least one viable green stem, leaf, or root to monitor.

recipes.title: salt an icy walkway
recipes.name: salt-an-icy-walkway
recipes.goal: Improve traction on an icy walkway using the right amount of ice melt, sand, or grit for the surface and temperature.

steps.action: **Remove loose snow first.** Shovel or sweep powder off steps and the path before applying any product.
steps.expect: ice patches are visible and product will reach the slippery surface.

steps.action: **Choose the treatment.** [BRANCH: above product rating | colder than rating] use ice melt within its temperature range, or use sand/grit for traction when melting will not work.
steps.expect: the chosen material matches the weather and walkway.

steps.action: **Apply sparingly and evenly.** Scatter granules by hand with gloves or a cup, focusing on steps, slope changes, and the main walking line.
steps.expect: granules are spaced like light seasoning, not piled.

steps.action: **Wait and scrape.** Give the product time to loosen the bond, then scrape slush away from the walking surface.
steps.expect: ice breaks up and the path exposes pavement or rough traction.

steps.action: **Protect pets and plants.** Keep product away from lawn edges, garden beds, and dog potty spots where possible.
steps.expect: treated areas are limited to necessary walking zones.

steps.action: **Recheck at dusk.** Look for meltwater refreezing before temperatures drop again.
steps.expect: new slick spots are treated or gritted before nighttime use.

recipes.verification: The main walking line has visible traction or exposed surface, steps are treated, excess product is swept from edges, and no meltwater is flowing across the path.

recipes.title: set up a fish tank cycle
recipes.name: set-up-a-fish-tank-cycle
recipes.goal: Establish a biological nitrogen cycle in a new aquarium before adding fish, so ammonia and nitrite can be processed safely.

steps.action: **Set up equipment.** Install substrate, filter media, heater, thermometer, and decor, then fill with dechlorinated water.
steps.expect: the tank runs without leaks and the temperature is stable for the intended species.

steps.action: **Run the filter continuously.** Start the filter and keep media wet and powered.
steps.expect: water circulates through the filter at all times.

steps.action: **Add an ammonia source.** Use a measured aquarium ammonia product or another controlled fishless source; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not add live fish to test unsafe water.
steps.expect: the ammonia test shows a readable starting level.

steps.action: **Test every few days.** Record ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate.
steps.expect: ammonia rises first, then nitrite appears, then nitrate appears.

steps.action: **Wait for conversion.** Keep feeding the cycle until ammonia and nitrite can return to zero after an ammonia dose.
steps.expect: tests show zero ammonia, zero nitrite, and some nitrate.

steps.action: **Change water before stocking.** Do a partial water change to lower nitrate and match temperature with dechlorinated water.
steps.expect: nitrate is in a safe range for the species and temperature remains stable.

recipes.verification: After a controlled ammonia dose, ammonia and nitrite test at zero within the expected interval, nitrate is present but controlled, and the filter has run continuously.

recipes.title: set up a fish tank
recipes.name: set-up-a-fish-tank
recipes.goal: Set up a stable aquarium with conditioned water, filtration, heat if needed, and a cycling plan before adding fish.

steps.action: **Place the tank on a proper stand.** Set it level on a surface designed for the filled weight, leaving room for cords and filter access.
steps.expect: the tank does not rock and all edges are supported.

steps.action: **Rinse substrate and decor.** Rinse gravel, sand, rocks, and decorations with plain water, not soap.
steps.expect: rinse water runs mostly clear and no chemical residue is present.

steps.action: **Install equipment dry.** Add substrate, decor, filter, thermometer, and heater while the tank is empty or partly filled, following equipment instructions.
steps.expect: equipment is secure and reachable.

steps.action: **Add conditioned water.** Fill slowly onto a plate or bag to avoid disturbing substrate, then dose dechlorinator for the full water volume.
steps.expect: the tank is filled, treated, and not cloudy from a hard pour.

steps.action: **Start filter and heater.** Make drip loops in all cords before plugging in equipment.
steps.expect: water circulates, temperature begins stabilizing, and cords dip below outlet height before rising.

steps.action: **Begin cycling.** Add an ammonia source or starter bacteria according to the method chosen and test ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate over time.
steps.expect: the tank has a written cycling log rather than fish added immediately.

steps.action: **Stock only after water tests pass.** [BRANCH: cycled | not cycled] add a small first group only when ammonia and nitrite read zero after processing ammonia, or keep cycling.
steps.expect: fish are not exposed to toxic startup spikes.

recipes.verification: The aquarium is level, filtered, dechlorinated, heated if required, electrically safe with drip loops, and has a cycling test log before fish are added.

recipes.title: set up a home toolkit
recipes.name: set-up-a-home-toolkit
recipes.goal: A single, findable toolkit exists in the home containing the ten tools that cover roughly 90% of household fixes, plus basic consumables, stored so any tool can be found and returned in under a minute.

steps.action: **Buy the container first.** A 40-50 cm toolbox with a lid tray, or a soft tool bag for apartments. The container defines the kit's home; tools without a home scatter.
steps.expect: an empty box or bag sized to hold everything below with some spare room.

steps.action: **Buy the ten essentials.** (1) 16 oz claw hammer, (2) multi-bit ratcheting screwdriver with at least PH1, PH2, and two flat bits, (3) 7.5 m / 25 ft tape measure, (4) adjustable wrench (200 mm), (5) slip-joint pliers, (6) needle-nose pliers with wire cutter, (7) utility knife with snap-off or replaceable blades, (8) torpedo level, (9) LED headlamp or flashlight, (10) hex key set (metric, plus imperial where flat-pack furniture demands it).
steps.expect: all ten in hand; nothing from the "novelty multitool" aisle.

steps.action: **Spend quality money only where it matters.** Cheap is fine for the hammer, level, and pliers. Do not cheap out on: the tape measure (bad locks and floppy blades cause mismeasures), screwdriver bits (soft bits cam out and strip screw heads), and utility blades (dull blades cause the slips that cut people). Mid-tier brand-name versions of those three cost little more.
steps.expect: tape locks firmly and stands out 1 m unsupported; bits are labeled hardened S2 steel or a known brand.

steps.action: **Add the consumables tray.** Assorted wood screws and drywall anchors, picture-hanging hooks, electrical tape, duct tape, super glue, wood glue, a small can of penetrating oil, spare utility blades, spare batteries for the light.
steps.expect: consumables in the lid tray or a zip pouch, not loose among tools.

steps.action: **Stage the kit at its fixed spot and tell the household.** Label the box if others live with you.
steps.expect: everyone can answer "where are the tools" identically.

steps.action: **Shake down the kit on a real task.** Hang a picture or tighten every loose screw and hinge in one room, using only the kit.
steps.expect: the task finishes without leaving the room for a missing tool; gaps found get added to a shopping note, not guessed at in advance.

steps.action: **Adopt the return rule.** A tool leaves the box for a task and returns the same day; the box never migrates to "wherever the last project was".
steps.expect: box back at its spot after the shakedown task.

recipes.verification: All ten tools plus consumables fit in one container at its declared spot; a household member other than the buyer can fetch the screwdriver in under a minute; one real task has been completed start-to-finish from the kit alone.

recipes.title: set up a reptile terrarium
recipes.name: set-up-a-reptile-terrarium
recipes.goal: Set up a reptile enclosure with species-appropriate heat, light, humidity, substrate, hides, and safety before the animal moves in.

steps.action: **Place the enclosure.** Set it away from direct sun, drafts, fumes, and unstable furniture.
steps.expect: the habitat is level, secure, and not overheated by windows.

steps.action: **Install controlled heat.** Connect heat sources through a thermostat and place probes where the animal will experience heat.
steps.expect: the warm side and cool side can be measured separately.

steps.action: **Add light and UVB if needed.** Mount bulbs at the species-appropriate distance and replace old UVB bulbs by schedule.
steps.expect: basking and UV access match the species plan.

steps.action: **Build the interior.** Add safe substrate, at least two hides, water, climbing or basking structures, and humidity support.
steps.expect: the animal will have a warm hide, cool hide, and secure movement.
