steps.action: **Run and measure.** Operate the setup for a full day and record temperature and humidity at several times.
steps.expect: readings stay inside the target range before the reptile arrives.

steps.action: **Move the reptile in calmly.** Transfer the reptile after parameters are stable; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not house incompatible reptiles together or use unregulated heat rocks.
steps.expect: the reptile can hide, thermoregulate, and access water.

recipes.verification: The enclosure holds species-appropriate warm-side, cool-side, basking, nighttime, humidity, hide, water, substrate, and lighting conditions for at least 24 hours before or after move-in.

recipes.title: set up a slow cooker
recipes.name: set-up-a-slow-cooker
recipes.goal: Load and run a slow cooker so food cooks evenly, reaches a safe finish temperature, and stays safe until serving.

steps.action: **Place the cooker safely.** Set it on a flat, heat-safe counter with the cord away from the edge.
steps.expect: the cooker is stable and not crowded by flammable items.

steps.action: **Prep ingredients evenly.** Cut dense vegetables and meat into similar sizes so they cook at a predictable rate.
steps.expect: pieces are ready to layer without large frozen centers.

steps.action: **Layer dense foods first.** Put potatoes, carrots, onions, or other firm vegetables on the bottom near the heat.
steps.expect: dense ingredients sit closest to the insert base.

steps.action: **Add protein and softer items.** Place meat or beans above dense vegetables, with delicate vegetables saved for later if the recipe says so.
steps.expect: ingredients are arranged by cooking speed.

steps.action: **Add the right liquid level.** Pour in the recipe's liquid, usually enough to cover the bottom and partially surround ingredients.
steps.expect: the cooker is not dry and not filled past the max line.

steps.action: **Choose low or high.** [BRANCH: low | high] use low for longer gentle cooking or high for a shorter cook when the recipe allows it.
steps.expect: the setting matches the recipe time.

steps.action: **Keep the lid closed.** Avoid lifting the lid unless adding timed ingredients or checking near the end.
steps.expect: steam stays inside and cooking time remains predictable.

steps.action: **Check finish temperature.** Use a thermometer in the thickest part of meat or the center of the dish.
steps.expect: food reaches the recipe's safe temperature before serving.

steps.action: **Use keep-warm correctly.** Switch to keep-warm after food is fully cooked, not as a cooking setting.
steps.expect: hot food stays above 140 F until served.

steps.action: **Store leftovers promptly.** Portion leftovers into shallow containers within 2 hours.
steps.expect: food cools quickly in the refrigerator.

recipes.verification: The slow cooker is stable, the lid has stayed closed during cooking, and the finished food has reached the safe internal temperature for its ingredients.

recipes.title: set up drip irrigation
recipes.name: set-up-drip-irrigation
recipes.goal: Install a simple drip irrigation system that delivers water slowly to plant roots without overspray, runoff, or frequent hand watering.

steps.action: **Sketch the zones.** Mark beds, containers, plant spacing, water source, and high-water or low-water groups.
steps.expect: tubing routes and zones are planned before cutting.

steps.action: **Attach head assembly.** Install the backflow preventer, filter, pressure regulator, and timer if using one at the faucet.
steps.expect: water supply is protected and pressure is suitable for drip parts.

steps.action: **Lay main tubing.** Run half-inch tubing along bed edges or rows, warming it in sun if it is stiff.
steps.expect: tubing follows the planned route without kinks.

steps.action: **Add emitters or dripline.** Punch holes and insert emitters near root zones, or connect dripline with emitters facing up or sideways as directed.
steps.expect: every plant has a water outlet nearby.

steps.action: **Cap and flush lines.** Open line ends briefly to flush debris, then install end caps or figure-eight closures.
steps.expect: water runs clear before lines are closed.

steps.action: **Test at low flow.** Turn on water and inspect every connector, emitter, and end cap.
steps.expect: emitters drip steadily and fittings do not spray.

steps.action: **Stake and cover.** Pin tubing in place and cover with mulch while keeping emitters findable.
steps.expect: lines stay put and evaporation is reduced.

steps.action: **Set a watering schedule.** Run long enough to wet the root zone, then adjust by digging a small check hole after watering.
steps.expect: soil is moist at root depth without runoff.

recipes.verification: With water running, each plant receives steady drips near its roots, fittings stay dry except at emitters, and soil is moist at root depth after the scheduled run.

recipes.title: sew on a button
recipes.name: sew-on-a-button
recipes.goal: A missing button is sewn back on securely, with the small detail (the thread shank) that makes it last years instead of weeks.

steps.action: **Thread the needle and anchor the thread.** Pass the thread through the eye, double it, and knot the two ends together; doubled thread halves the passes needed.
steps.expect: a doubled strand about forearm length with a solid knot at the end.

steps.action: **Anchor in the fabric at the button's spot.** Two tiny stitches on top of each other on the right side, where the button will hide them.
steps.expect: the thread firmly rooted, knot side hidden under where the button sits.

steps.action: **Sew the button on over a spacer.** Bring the needle up through one buttonhole, lay the toothpick (or a second needle) across the button's top, and stitch over it: down through the opposite hole, up again, six to eight passes total. Four-hole buttons: work two holes at a time in your choice of parallel bars or a cross.
steps.expect: firm, even stitches with the spacer trapped under them, button held but not yet crushed tight to the fabric.

steps.action: **Make the shank.** Remove the spacer, push the needle up through the fabric but *not* through the button, and wind the thread around the stitches between button and fabric five or six times. This thread pillar is what gives the buttoned layer room to sit flat, and its absence is why replacement buttons pop off again.
steps.expect: a short wrapped stem under the button; the button stands slightly proud and wiggles just a little.

steps.action: **Finish underneath.** Needle to the back side, three small stitches over each other into the stitch base, then pass the needle through the loop of the last one and pull snug for a knot. Trim close.
steps.expect: a tidy knot on the underside, no dangling tails.

steps.action: **Test.** Button it.
steps.expect: the button passes through its hole with normal effort, sits flat when closed, and holds under a firm tug.

recipes.verification: The button holds a firm tug, closes and opens with normal effort, sits flat when buttoned thanks to the shank, the underside shows a tidy knot, and the thread color disappears at conversational distance.

recipes.title: sharpen scissors
recipes.name: sharpen-scissors
recipes.goal: Household scissors cut paper or fabric cleanly again by improving the edge and checking the hinge tension.

steps.action: **Clean the blades.** Wipe off tape glue, lint, and old grime before judging sharpness. [BRANCH: sticky blades | truly dull blades] clean sticky blades first, sharpen only if cutting is still poor.
steps.expect: blades close without dragging on residue.

steps.action: **Test on scrap.** Cut plain paper from heel to tip and note where it folds or tears.
steps.expect: the dull section is identified.

steps.action: **Make several sandpaper cuts.** Cut fine sandpaper with the abrasive side facing out, using full strokes through the blade length.
steps.expect: the scissors feel slightly cleaner through paper.

steps.action: **Use foil for light honing.** Fold aluminum foil several times and cut thin strips from heel to tip.
steps.expect: small burrs are knocked down and the cut improves modestly.

steps.action: **Hone on a stone for better results.** Open the scissors, match the existing bevel angle, and stroke the beveled side along the stone from pivot to tip.
steps.expect: a fresh bright line appears along the cutting edge.

steps.action: **Remove the burr.** Close the scissors once or twice, then wipe the blades.
steps.expect: no gritty metal dust remains.

steps.action: **Check screw tension.** Tighten the pivot until blades meet along their length but still open smoothly. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* grinding the flat inner faces can ruin the scissor geometry, so sharpen only the beveled outside edge.
steps.expect: the blades cross with light pressure and no wobble.

steps.action: **Retest on scrap.** Cut paper, thread, or fabric suitable for those scissors.
steps.expect: the cut is clean from heel to tip.

recipes.verification: The scissors cut a clean continuous line through scrap material from the base of the blades to the tip.

recipes.title: shelter during severe weather
recipes.name: shelter-during-severe-weather
recipes.goal: A household moves to the safest available shelter area during severe weather and monitors official instructions.

steps.action: **Check the warning type.** Read or listen for tornado, severe thunderstorm, hurricane, flash flood, or other local alert details.
steps.expect: the immediate hazard is identified.

steps.action: **Bring people inside.** Move household members and pets indoors away from windows.
steps.expect: everyone is out of wind, hail, and lightning.

steps.action: **Choose the safest shelter.** [BRANCH: tornado or extreme wind | flood threat] use basement or lowest interior room for wind; move to higher ground for flooding.
steps.expect: shelter matches the hazard.

steps.action: **Avoid windows and exterior walls.** Stay in an interior room, hallway, closet, or bathroom when wind is the threat.
steps.expect: glass and debris exposure is reduced.

steps.action: **Protect heads and bodies.** Use helmets, mattresses, blankets, sturdy shoes, and coats if available.
steps.expect: impact injury risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Keep emergency supplies nearby.** Bring phone, flashlight, weather radio, shoes, medications, and basic kit.
steps.expect: essentials are reachable if damage occurs.

steps.action: **Monitor official updates.** Use weather radio, local alerts, or emergency management messages.
steps.expect: you know when danger continues or changes.

steps.action: **Stay sheltered until all clear.** Do not leave because weather sounds calmer; wait for official all-clear or warning expiration.
steps.expect: second waves or eyewall calm do not catch you exposed.

steps.action: **Avoid post-storm hazards.** Watch for downed lines, gas smell, flooding, unstable trees, and broken glass.
steps.expect: immediate aftermath risks are recognized.

steps.action: **Call for emergency help if needed.** Report injuries, trapped people, fire, gas leaks, or dangerous flooding.
steps.expect: urgent response is requested for life-safety problems.

recipes.verification: Everyone is in the safest available shelter for the active hazard, official alerts are being monitored, emergency supplies are nearby, and emergency services are called for injuries or immediate life threats.

recipes.title: shine leather shoes
recipes.name: shine-leather-shoes
recipes.goal: Leather shoes are cleaned, conditioned, polished, and buffed to a neat shine without smearing polish onto socks, floors, or cuffs.

steps.action: **Remove loose dirt.** Brush the uppers, seams, welt, and sole edge. [BRANCH: dusty shoes | muddy shoes] dry-brush dust, but let mud dry first and brush it off.
steps.expect: no grit remains to scratch the leather.

steps.action: **Wipe the leather.** Use a barely damp cloth, then let the shoe surface dry.
steps.expect: the leather looks clean and matte.

steps.action: **Condition if thirsty.** Rub a small amount of conditioner into dry or creased leather and wait a few minutes.
steps.expect: the leather darkens slightly and feels less papery.

steps.action: **Apply polish in circles.** Wrap a cloth around two fingers and work a thin layer of polish over the shoe.
steps.expect: color looks even, with no thick clumps in seams.

steps.action: **Let it dry.** Rest the shoes until the polish hazes.
steps.expect: the surface looks duller and no polish lifts easily onto a fingertip.

steps.action: **Buff briskly.** Use a horsehair brush or clean cloth with fast light strokes.
steps.expect: a clear shine appears across the toe and quarters.

steps.action: **Add a water-shine on the toe.** Touch one drop of water to the toe, add a tiny polish dot, and circle gently. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* heavy water or aggressive rubbing can dull delicate finishes, so test on a small area first.
steps.expect: the toe becomes glossier without streaks.

steps.action: **Dry between layers.** Repeat thin toe layers only after the prior layer sets, then give a final buff.
steps.expect: the shoe shines and feels dry, not tacky.

recipes.verification: Both shoes are clean, evenly colored, dry to the touch, and reflect light on the toes after buffing.

recipes.title: shovel snow safely
recipes.name: shovel-snow-safely
recipes.goal: Clear snow from essential walkways and exits while reducing fall, back, and cardiac strain.

steps.action: **Dress and warm up.** Put on traction footwear, layers, and gloves, then do a few minutes of gentle movement indoors.
steps.expect: you are warm, visible, and not starting cold.

steps.action: **Prioritize exits.** Clear the door swing, steps, mailbox path, sidewalk, and a narrow driveway lane before cosmetic areas.
steps.expect: people can leave safely in an emergency.

steps.action: **Push light snow first.** Use the shovel like a plow when snow is fluffy and under a few inches deep.
steps.expect: snow moves to the side without repeated lifting.

steps.action: **Lift small loads correctly.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* snow shoveling can trigger serious injury or heart strain, so keep loads light, bend knees, and stop for chest pain, dizziness, or unusual shortness of breath.
steps.expect: each scoop moves without twisting your torso.

steps.action: **Place snow where it will not refreeze into hazards.** Pile snow downhill from paths, away from drains, vents, fire hydrants, and the street.
steps.expect: meltwater has a route away from walking surfaces.

steps.action: **Take timed breaks.** [BRANCH: light snow | heavy wet snow] pause every 15 minutes for light snow or every 5-10 minutes for wet snow.
steps.expect: breathing and grip recover before the next section.

steps.action: **Treat remaining ice.** Scrape compacted areas and add sand, grit, or ice melt suitable for the surface and pets.
steps.expect: cleared surfaces have traction, not a slick glaze.

recipes.verification: Primary exits, steps, sidewalk, and needed driveway access are clear to the surface or treated for traction, with no snow blocking vents, hydrants, drains, or door swings.

recipes.title: silence a squeaky door
recipes.name: silence-a-squeaky-door
recipes.goal: The door swings through its full arc silently, the hinges are lubricated at the pin (where the squeak actually lives), and no lubricant is left to drip on the floor or stain clothing.

steps.action: **Find the noisy hinge.** Swing the door slowly with a hand resting on each hinge in turn; the squeaking hinge vibrates under your fingers. Most doors have 2-3 hinges and usually only one is guilty.
steps.expect: the squeak localized to a specific hinge.

steps.action: **Stage the area.** Lay cardboard or a towel under the hinge side; drape a rag below the hinge itself.
steps.expect: floor and lower door face protected from drips.

steps.action: **Lift the hinge pin partway.** [BRANCH: pin has a gap under its head → lever it up with a flat-head screwdriver | flush pin → set a nail against its bottom tip through the hole under the hinge barrel and tap upward with a hammer] Raise it 2-3 cm; do not remove it fully or the door sags onto the remaining hinges.
steps.expect: pin standing proud of the barrel; door still hanging normally.

steps.action: **Apply lubricant to the exposed pin and into the barrel.** A thin coat on the pin shaft plus a small amount into the open barrel top. More is not better; excess only migrates out later.
steps.expect: pin visibly coated, no lubricant running down the door face.

steps.action: **Tap the pin back down and seat it.** Hammer or palm until the head sits on the barrel.
steps.expect: pin flush, hinge closed up.

steps.action: **Work the door.** Swing it fully open and closed 10-15 times to carry the lubricant through the barrel.
steps.expect: squeak fades within the first few swings and then disappears.

steps.action: **Wipe all excess.** Rag over the hinge faces, barrel, and any drips on door or frame. Lubricant left on the surface collects dust and marks clothes brushing past.
steps.expect: hinge looks dry to the touch; rag has the residue.

steps.action: **Repeat for any other hinge that still speaks.** Re-run step 1; a second hinge often starts squeaking once the loudest one is silenced.
steps.expect: full silent swing.

recipes.verification: Open and close the door slowly through its full arc: no sound from any hinge, the door neither sags nor rubs, and a finger run over each hinge comes away clean.

recipes.title: snake a drain
recipes.name: snake-a-drain
recipes.goal: A sink, tub, or shower drain blockage is cleared with a hand auger while avoiding pipe damage and unsafe chemical exposure.

steps.action: **Protect the area.** Put on gloves and eye protection, remove standing water with a cup if needed, and place towels nearby.
steps.expect: you can work without splashing dirty water onto floors.

steps.action: **Remove the stopper or strainer.** Unscrew or lift the drain cover and pull out reachable hair or debris first.
steps.expect: the auger has a clear entry point.

steps.action: **Choose the access point.** [BRANCH: sink | tub or shower] for sinks, remove the P-trap if practical and feed into the wall stub; for tubs, feed through the overflow when possible.
steps.expect: the cable enters the pipe without scraping finished surfaces.

steps.action: **Feed cable gently.** Loosen the thumb screw, push cable in a few inches at a time, and stop at resistance.
steps.expect: resistance feels like a clog or bend, not a hard metal stop.

steps.action: **Crank through the obstruction.** Tighten the thumb screw, rotate clockwise while applying light forward pressure, then loosen and feed more cable.
steps.expect: the cable advances or begins to grab material.

steps.action: **Decide break or retrieve.** [BRANCH: break up | retrieve] crank to break soft buildup, or reverse slightly and pull back if hair or wipes catch on the tip.
steps.expect: either water drops or clog material comes out on the cable.

steps.action: **Withdraw slowly.** Pull cable back while rotating, wiping it into a bucket or trash bag as it emerges.
steps.expect: debris is contained and the cable does not whip.

steps.action: **Repeat once if needed.** Feed again until the cable passes the previous resistance with less effort.
steps.expect: the pipe path feels open for several feet.

steps.action: **Reassemble access parts.** Replace the trap, stopper, or overflow cover with washers seated correctly.
steps.expect: fittings are snug and aligned.

steps.action: **Flush the drain.** Run warm water for several minutes while checking any opened joints.
steps.expect: water drains steadily and joints stay dry.

recipes.verification: The fixture drains a full basin or several minutes of running water without backing up, gurgling, or leaking at any disturbed fitting.

recipes.title: socialize a kitten
recipes.name: socialize-a-kitten
recipes.goal: Help a kitten build positive experiences with handling, people, normal home sounds, carriers, and gentle play.

steps.action: **Create a safe base.** Keep the kitten in a kitten-proofed room with hiding, scratching, toys, litter, food, and water.
steps.expect: the kitten can retreat and reappear voluntarily.

steps.action: **Pair people with good things.** Offer treats, meals, play, and soft voices from different calm people.
steps.expect: the kitten approaches or watches with relaxed curiosity.

steps.action: **Handle briefly.** Touch paws, ears, mouth area, tail base, and body for one or two seconds, then reward.
steps.expect: handling predicts food or play instead of restraint.

steps.action: **Introduce normal sounds gently.** Play household sounds at low volume or run appliances at a distance while feeding or playing.
steps.expect: the kitten notices the sound and recovers quickly.

steps.action: **Teach carrier comfort.** Leave the carrier open with bedding and treats inside.
steps.expect: the kitten enters or rests near the carrier without being forced.

steps.action: **Redirect biting and scratching.** Use toys for play and stop hand play calmly when teeth or claws touch skin.
steps.expect: the kitten attacks toys instead of hands.

recipes.verification: The kitten voluntarily approaches familiar people, tolerates brief gentle handling, uses the carrier area calmly, and recovers from normal household sounds.

recipes.title: sort recycling
recipes.name: sort-recycling
recipes.goal: Household waste is separated into the locally correct streams — recyclables clean and sorted, contaminants kept out — and each stream is in its right bin.

steps.action: **Learn the local accept-list once, and post it.** Find your municipality's list; stick a printout by the bins.
steps.expect: you can answer "does this town take greasy pizza boxes / plastic film / glass in the bin?" from the sheet, not vibes.

steps.action: **Sort each item by material.** Paper/cardboard | plastics (check the accepted resin numbers) | metal cans | glass (often its own drop-off) | organics | everything else → general waste.
steps.expect: every item lands in a stream on the list — unlisted items default to general waste, not hopeful recycling ("wishcycling" ruins loads).

steps.action: **Empty and rinse containers.** A quick cold rinse and shake for cans, bottles, tubs — food residue is the #1 contaminant. Caps: follow local rules (often: plastic caps back on the bottle; metal lids inside the can, crimped).
steps.expect: no container with visible food/liquid goes in.

steps.action: **Flatten cardboard; keep paper dry.** Break boxes flat; wet or food-soaked paper (used tissues, greasy box bottoms) is general waste/organics.
steps.expect: cardboard flat-stacked; only clean dry fiber in the paper stream.

steps.action: **Keep the known saboteurs out.** Plastic bags/film (jam sorting machines — return to supermarket collection points instead), batteries and electronics (fire risk — dedicated drop-offs), broken glass/ceramics (wrap, general waste unless a glass point takes it), clothing (textile banks).
steps.expect: none of these in the household recycling bin.

steps.action: **Bag or bin per local convention and set out on the right day.** Some systems want loose recyclables, some want specific bags.
steps.expect: each stream in its container, out on its collection day (`daily/home` calendar note helps).

recipes.verification: Every stream's bin holds only its listed materials, containers are empty-and-rinsed, no bags/batteries/food lurk in the recycling, and the posted list means the next sort needs no guessing.

recipes.title: stake a leaning plant
recipes.name: stake-a-leaning-plant
recipes.goal: Support a leaning garden or house plant so stems stand upright while roots and trunks can still move and grow normally.

steps.action: **Find why the plant leans.** Check for wind, heavy blooms, weak light, loose roots, dry soil, or broken stems.
steps.expect: the cause is understood before staking.

steps.action: **Choose the support.** Use a stake shorter than the mature top for small stems or a stronger post for shrubs and top-heavy plants.
steps.expect: support strength matches plant size.

steps.action: **Insert the stake off-center.** Place it on the windward side or behind the lean, a few inches from the stem.
steps.expect: the stake is firm without piercing the main crown.

steps.action: **Straighten gradually.** Move the plant upright only as far as it bends without cracking.
steps.expect: stems improve position without snapping.

steps.action: **Tie with soft loops.** Use figure-eight ties or flexible plant tape around the stake and stem.
steps.expect: the stem is supported but not tightly bound.

steps.action: **Stabilize the root zone.** Firm loose soil, water deeply if dry, and add mulch if roots were disturbed.
steps.expect: the base no longer rocks easily.

steps.action: **Remove excess weight.** Deadhead heavy flowers or prune broken growth that pulls the plant over.
steps.expect: the plant has less top-heavy stress.

steps.action: **Recheck ties regularly.** Loosen or remove ties as the stem thickens and the plant can stand.
steps.expect: support helps temporarily without girdling.

recipes.verification: The plant stands closer to upright, the stake is firm, ties are soft and loose enough for growth, and the root zone no longer rocks excessively.

recipes.title: start a vegetable garden
recipes.name: start-a-vegetable-garden
recipes.goal: Start a small vegetable garden with suitable crops, prepared soil, and a watering plan that can be maintained through the season.

steps.action: **Pick a small first plot.** Choose a bed or containers you can reach and water easily, such as a 4-by-4-foot bed or a few pots near the kitchen.
steps.expect: the garden size feels maintainable.

steps.action: **Check sunlight and drainage.** Observe whether the site gets 6 or more hours of sun and whether water drains within a few hours.
steps.expect: vegetables will not sit in shade or soggy soil.

steps.action: **Choose seasonal crops.** [BRANCH: cool season | warm season] plant peas, lettuce, radishes, and kale in cool weather; tomatoes, peppers, beans, basil, and squash after frost.
steps.expect: selected crops match the current season.

steps.action: **Prepare the soil.** Loosen compacted soil, remove weeds, and mix in compost without overworking wet clay.
steps.expect: soil is crumbly and roots can enter.

steps.action: **Plant at proper spacing.** Follow seed packet or tag depth and spacing, label rows, and keep tall crops where they will not shade short ones.
steps.expect: each crop has room and a readable label.

steps.action: **Water gently.** Soak seeds or transplants at soil level, avoiding a hard spray that uncovers seeds.
steps.expect: soil is evenly moist but not flooded.

steps.action: **Mulch and protect.** Add straw, shredded leaves, or clean mulch after seedlings emerge, and install cages or netting if pets, kids, rabbits, or birds are likely.
steps.expect: soil stays moist and plants are protected from trampling or browsing.

steps.action: **Schedule care.** Put watering, weeding, and harvest checks on a calendar two or three times per week.
steps.expect: maintenance has a visible routine.

recipes.verification: The garden has season-appropriate crops planted at labeled spacing, soil is moist, water access is practical, and a recurring care schedule exists.

recipes.title: start a windowsill herb garden
recipes.name: start-a-windowsill-herb-garden
recipes.goal: A small windowsill herb garden is planted in draining pots, placed in enough light, watered correctly, and harvested in a way that keeps herbs growing.

steps.action: **Choose herbs for the light you have.** [BRANCH: bright sun | moderate light] use basil, thyme, rosemary for sun; mint, parsley, chives for moderate light.
steps.expect: plant choices match the window.

steps.action: **Prepare draining pots.** Fill pots with fresh mix and set them on saucers or a tray.
steps.expect: excess water has somewhere to drain without damaging the sill.

steps.action: **Plant at the right depth.** Set seedlings at the same soil level, or sow seeds at packet depth.
steps.expect: crowns are not buried and seeds are covered lightly.

steps.action: **Water to settle.** Water until a little drains out, then empty saucers after 15 minutes.
steps.expect: mix is evenly moist, not sitting in water.

steps.action: **Place in strong light.** Put pots close to the glass without leaves touching cold or hot panes.
steps.expect: herbs get direct or bright indirect light for several hours.

steps.action: **Check moisture by touch.** Water when the top 1-2 cm dries for most leafy herbs.
steps.expect: soil cycles from moist to slightly dry, not soaked.

steps.action: **Harvest little and often.** Snip above a leaf pair and never remove more than one-third of a plant at once.
steps.expect: herbs branch instead of being stripped bare.

steps.action: **Fix legginess early.** Rotate pots, pinch tips, and add a grow light if stems stretch toward the window.
steps.expect: growth becomes shorter and leafier.

recipes.verification: Each herb is in a draining pot on a protected sill, receives suitable light, has moist but not waterlogged soil, and can be harvested without removing more than one-third.

recipes.title: start a worm bin
recipes.name: start-a-worm-bin
recipes.goal: Set up a contained worm bin that converts appropriate kitchen scraps into castings without odors, pests, overheating, or drowning worms.

steps.action: **Prepare bedding.** Moisten shredded paper, cardboard, or coir until it feels like a wrung-out sponge.
steps.expect: bedding is damp and fluffy, not dripping.

steps.action: **Set up the bin.** Add bedding 6-8 inches deep and confirm air holes and drainage are open.
steps.expect: worms will have air and moisture control.

steps.action: **Add worms gently.** Place red wigglers on the bedding and leave the lid open briefly under light so they move down.
steps.expect: worms burrow into the bedding.

steps.action: **Feed a small starter amount.** Bury chopped vegetable scraps in one corner and cover completely with bedding.
steps.expect: no food is exposed on the surface.

steps.action: **Place the bin in stable conditions.** Keep it dark, shaded, and away from temperature extremes.
steps.expect: the bin stays within a worm-safe range.

steps.action: **Check moisture weekly.** Add dry bedding if wet or mist lightly if dry.
steps.expect: bedding remains damp but airy.

steps.action: **Feed only what disappears.** Add more scraps when most previous food is partly processed.
steps.expect: food does not accumulate faster than worms can eat it.

steps.action: **Harvest castings when mature.** Move fresh food to one side and collect dark crumbly castings from the other side after worms migrate.
steps.expect: finished castings separate with few worms.

recipes.verification: The bin contains damp airy bedding, composting worms are below the surface, food scraps are buried, temperature is moderate, and there is no rotten odor or standing liquid.

recipes.title: start seeds indoors
recipes.name: start-seeds-indoors
recipes.goal: Start vegetable or flower seeds indoors so they germinate evenly and grow into sturdy transplants ready for hardening off.

steps.action: **Check the sowing date.** Count back from the transplant date using the seed packet timing, usually 4-10 weeks depending on crop.
steps.expect: each crop has a realistic indoor start date.

steps.action: **Moisten the mix.** Add water to seed-starting mix until it feels damp like a wrung-out sponge.
steps.expect: the mix holds together lightly without dripping.

steps.action: **Fill and label containers.** Pack cells gently, level the surface, and label variety and sowing date before seeds are covered.
steps.expect: each row or pot is identifiable.

steps.action: **Sow at the correct depth.** Plant seeds at the packet depth, or press light-needed seeds onto the surface.
steps.expect: seeds are covered or exposed according to their germination need.

steps.action: **Water without washing seeds out.** Mist or bottom-water until the surface is evenly moist.
steps.expect: seeds remain in place and mix is damp.

steps.action: **Provide warmth and humidity.** Cover with a dome or plastic wrap and keep near the crop's germination temperature.
steps.expect: the tray stays humid but not soggy.

steps.action: **Move under strong light.** Remove covers when sprouts appear and place lights 2-3 inches above seedlings for 14-16 hours per day.
steps.expect: seedlings grow upright instead of stretching.

steps.action: **Thin and maintain.** Keep the strongest seedling per cell, water from below when possible, and add airflow.
steps.expect: seedlings have space, firm stems, and no fuzzy soil growth.

recipes.verification: Seedlings are labeled, evenly moist, under strong light after emergence, thinned to suitable spacing, and have compact green growth with no stem collapse.

recipes.title: stop a cat from scratching furniture
recipes.name: stop-a-cat-from-scratching-furniture
recipes.goal: Redirect a cat's scratching from furniture to acceptable surfaces without punishment or declawing.

steps.action: **Identify the preferred texture.** Notice whether the cat scratches vertical fabric, carpet, wood, cardboard, or horizontal surfaces.
steps.expect: the replacement scratcher can match the cat's preference.

steps.action: **Place a better scratcher nearby.** Put a tall stable post or board directly beside the scratched furniture.
steps.expect: the acceptable surface is easier to choose than the furniture.

steps.action: **Make furniture less rewarding.** Cover the target with a washable throw, smooth barrier, or cat-safe double-sided tape.
steps.expect: claws no longer catch satisfyingly on the furniture.

steps.action: **Reward scratcher use.** Add catnip if appropriate, play near the post, and praise or treat when claws touch it.
steps.expect: the cat repeats scratching on the approved surface.

steps.action: **Trim sharp tips if tolerated.** Maintain nail tips separately and gently.
steps.expect: accidental furniture damage is reduced.

steps.action: **Move the scratcher gradually.** After consistent use, shift it a little at a time if you need a different final location.
steps.expect: the cat follows the scratcher instead of returning to furniture.

recipes.verification: The cat uses an approved scratching surface daily, furniture access is protected or no longer attractive, and no paw pain or nail injury is present.

recipes.title: stop a dog from barking
recipes.name: stop-a-dog-from-barking
recipes.goal: Reduce problem barking by identifying the trigger, meeting the dog's needs, and rewarding quiet alternatives instead of punishment.

steps.action: **Log the pattern.** Note time, trigger, location, body language, and duration for several barking episodes.
steps.expect: one or two main causes become visible.

steps.action: **Remove easy triggers.** Close curtains, add white noise, move the dog from fence lines, or block window access during peak times.
steps.expect: barking opportunities decrease immediately.

steps.action: **Teach a quiet alternative.** Cue a mat, recall, hand target, or toy search before the dog explodes.
steps.expect: the dog has a specific behavior to do instead of barking.

steps.action: **Reward quiet seconds.** Mark and treat pauses, looking back at you, or settling after one alert bark.
steps.expect: quiet behavior begins to pay better than continued barking.

steps.action: **Practice below threshold.** Use distant, mild triggers and increase difficulty only when the dog can recover.
steps.expect: the dog notices the trigger and then reorients to you.

steps.action: **Avoid fear tools.** Do not yell, shock, or punish anxious barking; use management, training, and professional help when needed.
steps.expect: barking is not replaced by fear, hiding, or aggression.

recipes.verification: Barking episodes are shorter, less frequent, or easier to interrupt for the logged trigger, and the dog can perform a rewarded quiet alternative in that situation.

recipes.title: stop a running toilet
recipes.name: stop-a-running-toilet
recipes.goal: The toilet stops running between flushes: the tank fills once after a flush, the fill valve shuts off, and no water trickles into the bowl afterwards.

steps.action: **Lift the lid and set it flat on a towel.** Tank lids are unglazed ceramic and crack or shatter if leaned against a wall and knocked over.
steps.expect: lid safe and flat; tank internals visible: fill valve on the left, overflow tube in the middle, flapper at the bottom, chain to the flush handle.

steps.action: **Watch the water and diagnose.** [BRANCH: water pouring into the top of the overflow tube → float set too high or fill valve not shutting off, go to step 3 | water level below the tube top but a trickle runs into the bowl → leaking flapper, go to step 4 | tank silent now but refills every few minutes → slow flapper leak, confirm at step 4]
steps.expect: one of the three patterns clearly identified.

steps.action: **Lower the float.** Turn the adjustment screw on the fill valve (or slide the clip on the float rod, or gently bend a metal float arm down) until the valve shuts off with the waterline about 2-3 cm below the top of the overflow tube. Many tanks have a molded fill line to match.
steps.expect: fill valve goes quiet with water below the tube top; running stops. If it does, skip to step 7.

steps.action: **Confirm the flapper leak with the dye test.** Put 5-10 drops of food coloring in the tank water, do not flush, wait 15 minutes.
steps.expect: colored water appearing in the bowl proves the flapper is leaking; a clean bowl means recheck step 3.

steps.action: **Check the chain and seat before buying anything.** A chain with no slack holds the flapper cracked open; a too-long chain can wedge its tail under the flapper. Set roughly 1 cm of slack and tuck the excess. Also rub a finger around the flapper's seat ring; mineral crust or grit there breaks the seal.
steps.expect: correct slack, clean smooth seat; if the running stops, skip to step 7.

steps.action: **Replace the flapper.** Close the shutoff valve, flush and hold the handle to empty the tank, unhook the old flapper from the overflow tube's side ears and the chain, and take it to the store to match size (typically 2 or 3 inch). Install the new one, reattach the chain with 1 cm slack, and reopen the shutoff valve.
steps.expect: tank refills once, fill valve shuts off, bowl stays still.

steps.action: **Verify a full flush cycle.** Flush normally and watch the whole refill.
steps.expect: strong flush, flapper drops and seals on its own, tank refills to the fill line, valve stops, then silence.

steps.action: **Replace the lid.** Two hands, lower it flat.
steps.expect: lid seated, no grinding.

recipes.verification: Thirty minutes after the last flush the tank is silent, the dye test leaves the bowl clear, the waterline sits at the fill line below the overflow tube top, and the toilet has not refilled by itself.

recipes.title: stop a toilet from overflowing
recipes.name: stop-a-toilet-from-overflowing
recipes.goal: Stop a toilet bowl from overflowing, then clear or isolate the cause without making the spill worse.

steps.action: **Stop new water fast.** Remove the tank lid and lift the flapper closed, or push the flush handle back up if it is stuck.
steps.expect: water stops entering the bowl.

steps.action: **Shut the toilet supply valve.** Turn the small valve near the wall clockwise until it stops.
steps.expect: the tank no longer refills.

steps.action: **Stabilize the spill.** Place towels around the base and keep people from walking through wastewater.
steps.expect: water is contained and the floor is less slippery.

steps.action: **Check the bowl level.** Wait until the water level drops below the rim before plunging.
steps.expect: there is room for plunger movement without more overflow.

steps.action: **Plunge with a toilet plunger.** Seal the flange over the drain and make steady push-pull strokes for 20 to 30 seconds.
steps.expect: water level drops or gurgles as the clog moves.

steps.action: **Test with a small controlled flush.** Reopen the valve partway, let the tank fill, and flush only if the bowl is below half full.
steps.expect: water drains normally without rising toward the rim.

steps.action: **Keep the water off if the toilet still rises.** Close the valve again and stop testing.
steps.expect: no additional water enters the toilet.

steps.action: **Clean and disinfect the area.** Wear gloves and use an appropriate disinfectant on hard surfaces.
steps.expect: contaminated water is removed and surfaces are drying.

recipes.verification: The supply is controlled, the bowl no longer rises, a cautious test flush drains normally, and any wastewater has been cleaned or isolated for professional cleanup.

recipes.title: store seasonal clothes
recipes.name: store-seasonal-clothes
recipes.goal: Store off-season clothing so it stays clean, dry, labeled, and ready to wear next season.

steps.action: **Sort by season and use.** Group coats, sweaters, swimwear, formalwear, and everyday items separately.
steps.expect: each pile has a clear storage purpose.

steps.action: **Inspect for stains and damage.** Check collars, cuffs, underarms, hems, and pockets.
steps.expect: items needing cleaning or repair are separated.

steps.action: **Clean before storing.** Wash or dry-clean clothes according to care labels and dry them fully.
steps.expect: no food, sweat, perfume, or moisture is stored with fabric.

steps.action: **Empty every pocket.** Remove tissues, coins, makeup, receipts, and keys.
steps.expect: pockets are flat and nothing can stain or tear fabric.

steps.action: **Choose breathable storage.** [BRANCH: folded | hanging] use breathable bins or cotton bags for folded items, and garment bags for hanging pieces.
steps.expect: fabric can avoid trapped moisture.

steps.action: **Fold heavy knits.** Fold sweaters and heavy knits instead of hanging them.
steps.expect: shoulders will not stretch during storage.

steps.action: **Add cedar safely.** Place cedar blocks or sachets near clothes, not loose mothballs against skin-contact fabric.
steps.expect: pest deterrent is present without chemical residue on clothing.

steps.action: **Label containers.** Write the season, contents, and date on each bin or bag.
steps.expect: items can be found without opening every container.

steps.action: **Store cool, dry, and dark.** Put containers away from sunlight, damp floors, heaters, and exterior leaks.
steps.expect: storage conditions reduce fading, mildew, and pests.

steps.action: **Check after a week.** Open one container briefly to confirm there is no damp smell.
steps.expect: clothes smell clean and dry.

recipes.verification: All stored clothes are clean, fully dry, labeled by contents, and placed in a cool, dry, dark location using breathable containers.

recipes.title: strip wallpaper
recipes.name: strip-wallpaper
recipes.goal: Old wallpaper is removed without gouging the wall, adhesive residue is washed away, and the surface is left dry for painting or new paper.

steps.action: **Protect the room.** Move furniture, tape plastic at the base, and cover floors with towels or drop cloths.
steps.expect: water and paste scrapings have a landing zone.

steps.action: **Score the surface lightly.** Perforate washable or painted paper without digging into the wall.
steps.expect: moisture can reach adhesive through small holes.

steps.action: **Steam or soak a test patch.** [BRANCH: steamer | soak solution] warm the paper until adhesive softens, keeping water away from outlets.
steps.expect: a corner lifts with moderate pressure.

steps.action: **Scrape at a shallow angle.** Slide the scraper under softened paper, working in strips.
steps.expect: paper releases while the wall face stays intact.

steps.action: **Repeat in small sections.** Wet only what you can strip before it cools or dries.
steps.expect: progress stays controlled and the wall is not saturated.

steps.action: **Wash adhesive residue.** Scrub remaining paste with warm water and a sponge, changing water often.
steps.expect: the wall no longer feels slick or slimy.

steps.action: **Let the wall dry fully.** Ventilate the room and wait before sanding, painting, or repapering.
steps.expect: the wall is dry, dull, and firm.

recipes.verification: No wallpaper or slick paste residue remains, and the wall is dry and firm before any new finish is applied.

recipes.title: sweep and mop a floor
recipes.name: sweep-and-mop-a-floor
recipes.goal: A hard floor (tile, wood, laminate, vinyl) is swept free of debris and mopped clean, drying streak-free with nobody slipping on it.

steps.action: **Clear and prep the area.** Chairs on the table or out; rugs shaken outside and set aside; pick up cables and stray items.
steps.expect: an open floor with reachable corners.

steps.action: **Sweep the whole area toward one collection point.** Work from the far corner toward the exit/center; short overlapping strokes; get under furniture edges and along baseboards where debris drifts.
steps.expect: one debris pile; visibly clear floor elsewhere.

steps.action: **Dustpan the pile.** Brace the pan, sweep in, then *back the pan up a few centimeters and sweep the leftover line again* — the eternal thin line takes two passes.
steps.expect: pile gone including the line; pan emptied to the bin.

steps.action: **Prepare the mop.** Bucket: warm water + cleaner *dosed per its label* (over-dosing causes the sticky/streaky floor). Wring the mop to damp, not dripping — especially over wood/laminate, where standing water is the enemy.
steps.expect: mop damp enough to sheen the floor, not puddle it.

steps.action: **Mop from the far corner toward the exit.** Figure-eight strokes with a string mop / straight overlapping lanes with a flat mop; re-dip-and-wring when the head drags dirty. Don't mop yourself into a corner.
steps.expect: uniform thin wet sheen behind you; visibly dirty water building in the bucket.

steps.action: **Change water when it turns murky.** Mopping with dirty water just relocates soil in an even gray film.
steps.expect: final passes done with clean-ish water.

steps.action: **Block the area and let it dry.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* wet-floor slips hurt real people — keep household members (and yourself) off it for the 10–20 min dry, ventilate to speed it.
steps.expect: floor dries streak-free; no footprints through the wet zone.

steps.action: **Rinse the mop and dustpan, dump the bucket in a toilet/utility drain (not the kitchen sink), and restore the furniture.**
steps.expect: tools clean and drying; room back in order.

recipes.verification: Corners and baseboard lines hold no debris, the dried floor shows neither streaks nor gray film under raking light, tools are rinsed and stored, and furniture is back with no wet-floor incident recorded.

recipes.title: test a smoke alarm
recipes.name: test-a-smoke-alarm
recipes.goal: A smoke alarm is confirmed to sound, have power, be within its service life, and be placed where it can warn people effectively.

steps.action: **Notify people nearby.** Tell occupants you are testing alarms, not reporting a fire.
steps.expect: no one mistakes the test for an emergency.

steps.action: **Locate every alarm.** Check bedrooms, hallways outside sleeping areas, each level, basement, and near living spaces.
steps.expect: all installed units are identified.

steps.action: **Check placement.** Confirm alarms are on the ceiling or high on the wall and not blocked by furniture, vents, or heavy dust.
steps.expect: smoke can reach the sensor.

steps.action: **Read the manufacture date.** Remove or rotate the alarm if needed to see the back label.
steps.expect: the unit is less than 10 years old or marked for replacement.

steps.action: **Press the test button.** Hold the button until the alarm sounds.
steps.expect: a loud pattern starts within a few seconds.

steps.action: **Confirm audibility.** Listen from sleeping areas or ask another person to confirm.
steps.expect: the alarm is clearly audible where people sleep.

steps.action: **Interpret chirps.** Note any single periodic chirp after testing.
steps.expect: silence means normal; repeated chirp indicates low battery or end-of-life.

steps.action: **Replace battery if needed.** Install the correct battery type and close the compartment fully.
steps.expect: the alarm powers up and the chirp stops.

steps.action: **Clean lightly.** Vacuum or wipe dust from vents without spraying cleaner into the alarm.
steps.expect: vents are clear and the test button remains accessible.

steps.action: **Record the monthly test.** Mark the date and replacement due date.
steps.expect: next test and expiration are known.

recipes.verification: Each smoke alarm sounds from its test button, is audible from sleeping areas, is not expired, and is not obstructed.

recipes.title: test your garden soil
recipes.name: test-your-garden-soil
recipes.goal: Collect a representative soil sample and use a home kit or lab test to understand pH, nutrients, and amendment needs before planting or fertilizing.

steps.action: **Choose one testing area.** Sample one bed, lawn, or planting zone at a time rather than mixing unrelated soils.
steps.expect: the test will represent a specific growing area.

steps.action: **Remove surface debris.** Clear mulch, leaves, and compost from each sampling spot.
steps.expect: only mineral soil is sampled.

steps.action: **Take multiple cores.** Collect 6-10 small samples from root depth, usually 6 inches for vegetables and flowers.
steps.expect: the bucket contains soil from across the area.

steps.action: **Mix and remove debris.** Crumble the soil, remove stones and roots, and blend thoroughly in the clean bucket.
steps.expect: the composite sample is uniform.

steps.action: **Dry if required.** Air-dry the sample on clean paper if the kit or lab requests dry soil.
steps.expect: soil is dry enough to package without molding.

steps.action: **Package and label.** Fill the test container or bag with the requested amount and note crop, bed, and date.
steps.expect: the sample can be matched to the garden area.

steps.action: **Run or submit the test.** Follow kit instructions exactly or mail/drop off the lab sample with payment if required.
steps.expect: results are produced or pending from the lab.

steps.action: **Apply recommendations carefully.** Add lime, sulfur, compost, or fertilizer only at the recommended rate for the crop.
steps.expect: amendments match measured soil needs.

recipes.verification: The sample combines multiple root-depth cores from one defined area, is labeled, tested by a kit or lab, and amendments are based on the written result rather than guessing.

recipes.title: tie a tie
recipes.name: tie-a-tie
recipes.goal: A necktie is tied in a neat four-in-hand knot, with the wide end at the belt line and a small dimple under the knot.

steps.action: **Drape the tie around your neck.** Put the wide end on your dominant-hand side and the narrow end on the other side. [BRANCH: standard tie | extra-long tie] start with the wide end about 30 cm lower for standard, farther down for extra-long.
steps.expect: the wide end hangs longer than the narrow end.

steps.action: **Cross wide over narrow.** Lay the wide end across the front of the narrow end just below your collar.
steps.expect: an X shape sits centered at your throat.

steps.action: **Wrap behind and across.** Pass the wide end behind the narrow end, then bring it across the front again.
steps.expect: a horizontal band of fabric covers the front of the knot.

steps.action: **Send wide end up through the neck loop.** Bring the wide end from underneath, up through the opening between collar and tie.
steps.expect: the wide end points upward, with the front band still visible below.

steps.action: **Tuck through the front loop.** Feed the wide end down through the front band you made, keeping the knot loose enough for the fabric to slide.
steps.expect: the wide end emerges flat in front, forming the four-in-hand knot.

steps.action: **Shape the dimple.** Pinch the fabric just below the knot with one finger while pulling the wide end downward.
steps.expect: a clean crease forms under the center of the knot.

steps.action: **Tighten to the collar.** Hold the narrow end and slide the knot upward until it meets the collar.
steps.expect: the knot sits snugly without choking you.

steps.action: **Check the length.** The wide end should touch the top or middle of the belt buckle, hiding the narrow end behind it. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* tugging hard can stretch delicate silk, so loosen and retie instead of yanking.
steps.expect: the tie hangs straight, with no tail peeking out below.

recipes.verification: The knot is centered at the collar, the wide end reaches the belt buckle, and the narrow end stays hidden behind it.

recipes.title: tighten a loose doorknob
recipes.name: tighten-a-loose-doorknob
recipes.goal: A loose doorknob or lever is tightened, aligned with the latch, and tested so it turns and latches without wobble.

steps.action: **Open the door.** Work with the door open and latch visible.
steps.expect: you can test the knob without being locked out.

steps.action: **Find visible screws.** Look on the rose, base plate, or latch-side face for exposed screws.
steps.expect: the main tightening points are identified.

steps.action: **Find a hidden set screw.** Check the underside or neck of the knob or lever for a small slot or hex screw.
steps.expect: the handle retaining screw is located if present.

steps.action: **Expose the base plate.** [BRANCH: snap cover | threaded rose] gently pry or unscrew the cover plate if mounting screws are hidden.
steps.expect: the through-bolts are visible.

steps.action: **Tighten through-bolts.** Hold both sides of the knob aligned and tighten screws evenly.
steps.expect: the knobs pull snug against the door faces.

steps.action: **Tighten the set screw.** Seat the knob fully on the spindle and tighten the set screw.
steps.expect: the handle no longer slides on the spindle.

steps.action: **Align the latch.** Turn the knob and confirm the latch retracts fully and enters the strike plate centered.
steps.expect: the latch moves without scraping.

steps.action: **Adjust the strike if needed.** Tighten strike screws or shift the plate slightly within existing play.
steps.expect: the latch catches without pushing or lifting the door.

steps.action: **Test operation.** Open and close the door several times from both sides.
steps.expect: the knob feels firm and the latch releases cleanly.

recipes.verification: The knob or lever has no side play, retracts the latch fully, and opens and closes from both sides five times without sticking.

recipes.title: tighten a loose faucet handle
recipes.name: tighten-a-loose-faucet-handle
recipes.goal: A loose faucet handle is tightened so it turns the valve cleanly without wobbling or leaking.

steps.action: **Close the drain.** Cover the drain with a stopper or towel to catch small screws.
steps.expect: dropped hardware cannot enter the drain.

steps.action: **Find the set screw.** Look under the handle, behind a cap, or beneath a decorative button.
steps.expect: the fastener location is visible.

steps.action: **Expose the screw.** Remove the cap gently with a fingernail or plastic tool.
steps.expect: the screw head is accessible without scratched finish.

steps.action: **Tighten the handle.** Turn the set screw or handle screw clockwise until snug.
steps.expect: the handle no longer rocks on the stem.

steps.action: **Test movement.** Turn the water on and off through the handle's full range.
steps.expect: the handle moves smoothly and stops firmly.

steps.action: **Reinstall the cap.** Press the decorative cap back into place.
steps.expect: the cap sits flush and covers the screw.

steps.action: **Check for leaks.** Run water and inspect around the handle and under the sink.
steps.expect: no water appears around the handle base or supply connections.

recipes.verification: The faucet handle has no side-to-side wobble, turns water fully on and off, and shows no leak during one minute of running water.

recipes.title: tighten a loose screw
recipes.name: tighten-a-loose-screw
recipes.goal: A loose screw is tightened with the right driver, or its stripped hole is repaired so the screw holds again.

steps.action: **Identify the screw head.** Match Phillips, flat, square, Torx, or hex with a driver that fills the recess.
steps.expect: driver sits deep without wobbling.

steps.action: **Press straight and turn.** Apply inward pressure and tighten clockwise slowly.
steps.expect: screw head moves inward and resistance increases.

steps.action: **Stop at snug.** Quit when the fastened part no longer moves.
steps.expect: surface is secure without dimpling or cracking.

steps.action: **Check for a stripped hole.** If the screw spins without tightening, remove it and inspect the hole.
steps.expect: wood fibers, drywall dust, or enlarged plastic show why it will not grip.

steps.action: **Fix wood holes.** Pack the hole with glue-coated toothpicks, trim flush, then reinstall the screw.
steps.expect: threads bite into the packed wood.

steps.action: **Fix drywall or masonry holes.** Use the correct wall anchor or a larger anchor rated for the load. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overtightening can strip the new anchor or crush the surface, so stop when the fixture is held firm.
steps.expect: anchor stays still while the screw tightens.

steps.action: **Load-test gently.** Wiggle the attached item or apply light downward pressure.
steps.expect: screw and item do not shift.

recipes.verification: The screw sits snugly, the attached part does not wobble under light use, and the head is not stripped or overdriven.

recipes.title: touch up wall paint
recipes.name: touch-up-wall-paint
recipes.goal: Small wall scuffs, chips, or patches blend into the surrounding paint by matching color, sheen, and texture.

steps.action: **Identify the existing finish.** Check whether the wall is flat, eggshell, satin, semi-gloss, or gloss.
steps.expect: the touch-up paint sheen matches the wall.

steps.action: **Confirm the color.** Stir stored paint well or get a store match from a clean chip.
steps.expect: paint color is as close as available.

steps.action: **Clean the area.** Wipe grime with mild cleaner, rinse lightly, and let dry.
steps.expect: paint will stick to a clean dry surface.

steps.action: **Repair tiny defects.** Fill small nail holes if needed, let filler dry, and sand only the patch smooth.
steps.expect: the surface feels even.

steps.action: **Test in a hidden spot.** Apply a small dab where lighting is similar but less visible.
steps.expect: dry color and sheen are acceptable.

steps.action: **Apply a thin coat.** [BRANCH: brush | mini roller] use a brush for chips and a mini roller for textured roller walls.
steps.expect: paint covers the defect without a raised blob.

steps.action: **Feather the edge.** Lightly spread paint outward with less pressure at the perimeter.
steps.expect: there is no hard paint ridge.

steps.action: **Let it dry fully.** Wait the label's recoat time and avoid judging wet paint.
steps.expect: color lightens or darkens to its dry appearance.

steps.action: **Add a second thin coat if needed.** Cover only where the defect still shows and feather again.
steps.expect: coverage improves without building a patch edge.

steps.action: **Check under room lighting.** Look from normal viewing angles in daylight and evening light.
steps.expect: the touch-up is not obvious during normal use.

recipes.verification: After drying under normal daylight and evening lighting, the repaired spot blends with the wall from typical viewing distance without visible ridges or sheen mismatch.

recipes.title: trim a birds nails
recipes.name: trim-a-birds-nails
recipes.goal: Shorten a bird's overgrown nail tips only when it can be done calmly and safely, with bleeding control ready and a vet option preferred for uncertain cases.

steps.action: **Decide if home trimming is appropriate.** Inspect nail length, foot posture, and your confidence.
steps.expect: simple sharp tips can be handled, while curled, cracked, or embedded nails are referred to an avian vet.

steps.action: **Prepare safe restraint.** Wrap the body lightly in a towel while keeping the chest free to expand.
steps.expect: the bird is contained but breathing normally.

steps.action: **Identify the quick.** Use strong light to find the blood supply when visible and plan a tiny tip trim only.
steps.expect: the cut line is well away from living tissue.

steps.action: **Trim one tiny tip.** Clip or file only the point; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a deep cut can bleed seriously in a small bird.
steps.expect: the nail is less sharp and no bleeding starts.

steps.action: **Check breathing and stress.** Pause after each nail and release the bird if panting, weakness, or frantic struggling appears.
steps.expect: the bird remains alert, upright, and breathing comfortably.

steps.action: **Return and monitor.** Put the bird back in the cage with stable perches and observe feet and behavior.
steps.expect: the bird perches normally and no nail is bleeding.

recipes.verification: Only nail tips are shortened, every nail is dry with no bleeding, and the bird is alert, breathing normally, and perching after the session.

recipes.title: trim a cats nails
recipes.name: trim-a-cats-nails
recipes.goal: Trim only the sharp transparent tips of a cat's claws while keeping the cat calm and avoiding the quick.

steps.action: **Choose a quiet moment.** Sit in a calm room after play or a meal, with doors closed and supplies beside you.
steps.expect: the cat stays near you without immediate hiding or struggling.

steps.action: **Handle one paw gently.** Touch a shoulder, then a leg, then one paw, rewarding calm pauses.
steps.expect: the cat allows brief paw contact or recovers quickly after pulling away.

steps.action: **Expose one claw.** Press the toe pad lightly until the claw extends, then locate the narrow sharp hook beyond the quick.
steps.expect: the cutting zone is visible and is only the translucent tip.

steps.action: **Clip a tiny tip.** Hold the clipper perpendicular to the claw hook and remove 1 to 2 mm at a time; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never cut into the pink quick or opaque base.
steps.expect: the sharp point is blunted and the cat does not yelp, bleed, or jerk in pain.

steps.action: **Pause between claws.** Give a treat and release the paw after each claw or each two claws.
steps.expect: the session remains calm enough to continue or stop without a chase.

steps.action: **Stop before panic.** End the session if the cat growls, pants, thrashes, or hides, even if only one paw is finished.
steps.expect: the cat leaves with no injury and can try again later.

recipes.verification: Each trimmed claw has a blunt tip, no nail is bleeding, the cat is walking normally, and the cat can leave the area without being chased.

recipes.title: unclog a drain
recipes.name: unclog-a-drain
recipes.goal: A slow or blocked sink/shower drain flows freely again using mechanical methods first, without chemical injuries or a flooded cabinet.

steps.action: **Diagnose the blockage's neighborhood.** Only this fixture slow → local clog (proceed). Multiple fixtures backing up, or gurgling elsewhere → main-line problem: stop, that's a plumber call.
steps.expect: confirmed single-fixture clog.

steps.action: **Clear the strainer/stopper first.** Pop or unscrew the stopper; pull off surface hair and gunk (the zip-it strip excels here — insert, twist, pull). Shower clogs end at this step surprisingly often.
steps.expect: a satisfyingly disgusting wad removed; test the flow.

steps.action: **Try hot (not boiling into porcelain) water + dish soap for grease clogs.** Kitchen sinks: a kettle of very hot water with a squirt of dish soap, poured in stages.
steps.expect: improvement between pours if it's grease; none → step 4.

steps.action: **Plunge.** Block the overflow hole with a wet cloth (the plunge needs pressure), enough water to cover the cup, seal the plunger over the drain, 10–15 sharp push-pulls, then lift.
steps.expect: water suddenly swirling away = cleared; repeat once or twice before moving on.

steps.action: **Open the P-trap (sink cabinets).** Bucket and towel *under the trap first*; unscrew the two slip nuts by hand or gently with the wrench; drop the trap and empty its contents into the bucket; probe the stub pipes with a finger/wire. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* jewelry lost down this sink lives in this trap — check the sludge before discarding it.
steps.expect: trap off, gunk out, visible clear passage through the trap body.

steps.action: **Snake past the trap if still blocked.** Feed the snake into the wall stub until resistance, crank to bite the clog, pull back and clean the head; repeat until it runs free.
steps.expect: the snake returns with clog material, then meets no resistance.

steps.action: **Reassemble and flush-test.** Trap back on (washers seated, nuts hand-tight plus a nudge), then run *hot* water full-bore for a minute while watching the trap joints.
steps.expect: fast drainage, dry joints under a finger-swipe.

recipes.verification: The fixture drains at full speed with no gurgle, the trap joints stay dry through a one-minute hot flush, tools are cleaned and gloves off with washed hands, and the recovered-valuables check (step 5 ⚠️) is done.

recipes.title: unclog a garbage disposal
recipes.name: unclog-a-garbage-disposal
recipes.goal: A jammed or clogged garbage disposal is cleared, reset, and tested without putting hands near powered blades.

steps.action: **Kill power completely.** Turn the disposal switch off and unplug it under the sink or switch off its breaker. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* moving blades can amputate fingers; never put a hand into a disposal that can receive power.
steps.expect: switch and plug or breaker are both off.

steps.action: **Confirm it is dead.** Flip the wall switch once while standing clear, then return it to off.
steps.expect: no hum, spin, or vibration occurs.

steps.action: **Look into the chamber.** Shine a flashlight through the drain opening and inspect around the grinding plate.
steps.expect: visible food sludge, a stuck object, or a clear chamber.

steps.action: **Remove loose objects with tools.** Use tongs or pliers to lift out glass, metal, bones, or fibrous debris. [BRANCH: object visible | no object visible]
steps.expect: foreign material is out of the chamber or nothing reachable remains.

steps.action: **Free the flywheel from below.** Insert the hex key into the bottom center socket and turn back and forth until it moves freely.
steps.expect: resistance breaks loose and the key can swing both directions.

steps.action: **Press the reset button.** Find the small red or black button on the bottom or side and press it once.
steps.expect: the button clicks in or is already seated.

steps.action: **Flush with cold water.** Restore power only after tools are out, run cold water, and pulse the switch for 1 second.
steps.expect: the disposal spins without humming and water begins to drain.

steps.action: **Clear remaining slow drainage.** Keep cold water running and pulse several short bursts, not one long grind.
steps.expect: water level falls and no object rattles inside.

recipes.verification: With cold water running, the disposal starts instantly, spins smoothly for three short pulses, drains the sink, and remains dry underneath.

recipes.title: unclog a toilet
recipes.name: unclog-a-toilet
recipes.goal: A clogged toilet is cleared without overflow, chemical drain cleaners, or damage to the bowl.

steps.action: **Stop a rising bowl.** If water is climbing, lift the tank lid and close the flapper or turn the wall valve clockwise.
steps.expect: the bowl water stops rising.

steps.action: **Set the water level.** Remove water with a cup if the bowl is near the rim, or add water if the plunger cup will not be covered.
steps.expect: water sits below the rim with the plunger cup submerged.

steps.action: **Use the right plunger.** Pull the flange out from the cup so it can seal inside the toilet outlet.
steps.expect: the rubber flange points downward like a sleeve.

steps.action: **Seat the plunger.** Lower it slowly to burp air out, then press the flange into the outlet.
steps.expect: the cup seals and resists movement.

steps.action: **Plunge with control.** Push gently first, then use firm short strokes without breaking the seal.
steps.expect: water pulses but stays in the bowl.

steps.action: **Pull sharply once.** After 10 to 20 strokes, pull up to create suction.
steps.expect: the water drops, gurgles, or debris moves.

steps.action: **Test with a small flush.** Turn water on if needed and press the handle briefly, ready to stop the flapper.
steps.expect: water drains normally and does not rise toward the rim.

steps.action: **Repeat once if needed.** Re-seat the plunger and run another controlled cycle.
steps.expect: each cycle improves drainage or reveals that plunging is not enough.

steps.action: **Escalate to a toilet auger.** If two good plunging rounds fail, use a closet auger, not chemicals.
steps.expect: the auger meets, hooks, or pushes through the blockage.

steps.action: **Clean up.** Flush twice only after drainage is normal, rinse the plunger in clean bowl water, and disinfect contact surfaces.
steps.expect: toilet refills normally and the floor is dry.

recipes.verification: A full flush drains at normal speed, the bowl refills to its usual level, and no wastewater is on the floor.

recipes.title: unshrink a wool sweater
recipes.name: unshrink-a-wool-sweater
recipes.goal: A shrunken wool sweater is relaxed with conditioner, gently stretched, and reshaped flat so it regains some usable size.

steps.action: **Measure the sweater.** Record chest width, sleeve length, and body length.
steps.expect: target areas for stretching are clear.

steps.action: **Fill a basin.** Use lukewarm water and mix in 1 to 2 tablespoons hair conditioner.
steps.expect: water feels slippery, not hot.

steps.action: **Soak without agitation.** Submerge the sweater for 20 to 30 minutes.
steps.expect: fibers feel relaxed and heavy with water.

steps.action: **Lift carefully.** Support the whole sweater when removing it from the basin.
steps.expect: wet fabric does not stretch unevenly from its own weight.

steps.action: **Press out water.** Roll in a towel and press, without wringing.
steps.expect: sweater is damp but not dripping.

steps.action: **Stretch gradually.** Tug small sections to the target measurements, working side to side and sleeve by sleeve.
steps.expect: fabric gives slightly without ripping or thinning.

steps.action: **Reshape flat.** Lay on a dry towel and square the shoulders, hem, cuffs, and side seams.
steps.expect: sweater matches a wearable outline.

steps.action: **Dry in place.** Leave flat until fully dry, replacing wet towels if needed.
steps.expect: shape holds without hanger marks.

recipes.verification: After drying flat, at least one target measurement is closer to the desired size and the sweater lies evenly without twists.

recipes.title: unstick two glasses stuck together
recipes.name: unstick-two-glasses-stuck-together
recipes.goal: Separate two nested drinking glasses without cracking, chipping, or shattering them.

steps.action: **Move to the sink.** Set the stuck glasses over a towel in the sink or on a towel-lined counter.
steps.expect: any slip would land on a padded surface.

steps.action: **Check for cracks.** Rotate the glasses slowly and inspect the rims and sides. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* forcing cracked glass can shatter it; discard cracked glass instead of separating it.
steps.expect: only intact glass is handled.

steps.action: **Add cold water inside.** Pour cold water or ice water into the inner glass only.
steps.expect: the inner glass cools and contracts slightly.

steps.action: **Warm the outside.** Run warm, not boiling, water over the outside glass while keeping cold water inside the inner glass.
steps.expect: the outer glass warms and expands slightly.

steps.action: **Grip with towels.** Wrap each glass with a dry towel to improve grip and protect your hands.
steps.expect: both glasses can be held without slipping.

steps.action: **Wiggle gently.** Twist the glasses in opposite directions with light pressure, then lift the inner glass straight up.
steps.expect: you feel small movement instead of a hard lock.

steps.action: **Add soap at the rim.** If still stuck, drip a little dish soap where the rims meet and repeat the temperature step.
steps.expect: soap works into the seam between the glasses.

steps.action: **Stop before force.** If the glasses do not move after several gentle tries, set them aside to rest at room temperature and retry later.
steps.expect: no bending, prying, or hard pulling is used.

steps.action: **Dry and store loosely.** After separating, dry both glasses and avoid stacking identical tight glasses while damp.
steps.expect: glasses are separate, dry, and not nested tightly.

recipes.verification: The glasses separate cleanly with no chips, cracks, or sharp fragments, and both are washed before reuse.

recipes.title: use a fire extinguisher
recipes.name: use-a-fire-extinguisher
recipes.goal: Use a portable fire extinguisher on a small fire only when it is safe to attempt.

steps.action: **Decide whether to fight the fire.** [BRANCH: small and contained | growing, smoky, or blocking exit] fight only the first case.
steps.expect: you have chosen evacuation if conditions are unsafe.

steps.action: **Call or assign a call before using the extinguisher.** Tell someone to call the fire service, or call yourself if alone and leaving.
steps.expect: emergency help is on the way if the fire is not instantly controlled.

steps.action: **Confirm the extinguisher class.** Use ABC for most home fires, B for flammable liquids, C for energized electrical equipment, and never use a water extinguisher on grease or live electrical equipment.
steps.expect: the label matches the burning material.

steps.action: **Stand with the exit behind you.** Keep 6 to 8 feet of distance if the extinguisher label allows it.
steps.expect: your path out is clear and the fire is in front of you.

steps.action: **Pull the pin.** Hold the extinguisher upright and break the tamper seal.
steps.expect: the handle can now be squeezed.

steps.action: **Aim at the base.** Point the nozzle or hose where the fuel is burning, not at the top of the flames.
steps.expect: the discharge path targets the source of the fire.

steps.action: **Squeeze the handle.** Discharge a short burst, then continue if the agent is reaching the base.
steps.expect: extinguishing agent flows steadily.

steps.action: **Sweep side to side.** Move across the base until flames are out.
steps.expect: flames shrink and disappear without pushing fire toward you.

steps.action: **Back away and watch.** Do not turn your back on the area until you are clear.
steps.expect: the fire stays out or you leave if it restarts.

recipes.verification: The fire is out, the area is watched for re-ignition from a safe exit path, and the fire service is called for any fire that spread, produced heavy smoke, or required an extinguisher.

recipes.title: vacuum a room
recipes.name: vacuum-a-room
recipes.goal: A room's floors — carpet and/or hard surface — are vacuumed edge to edge, including under and behind the reachable furniture, with the machine left ready for next time.

steps.action: **Pre-flight the machine.** Bin/bag below the full line (empty it now if close), filter seated, correct head/mode for the floor, cord path planned or battery charged.
steps.expect: strong airflow at the head when switched on briefly; no rattle of yesterday's coin.

steps.action: **Pick the floor before the vacuum sees it.** A 60-second sweep for cables, small objects, socks, and string — string and cables wrap the brush roll and end sessions early.
steps.expect: nothing on the floor but dirt and the furniture.

steps.action: **Vacuum in slow, overlapping lanes from the far corner toward the door.** Half-a-head overlap; *slow* is the operative word — dirt pickup happens at walking-backward pace, not scrubbing pace. Carpet: one pass each in two perpendicular directions on the traffic areas.
steps.expect: visible pile-lift lanes on carpet; audible pickup crackle that fades to clean-hum per lane.

steps.action: **Do the edges and corners with the crevice tool.** Baseboards, corners, along furniture feet — where the drift collects (`daily/home/sweep-and-mop-a-floor` knows this too).
steps.expect: the dust lines at edges are gone, not relocated.

steps.action: **Reach the under-zones.** Under beds/sofas with the flat head or by sliding light furniture aside (and back); behind doors. Skip what genuinely can't move — but on a schedule, not forever.
steps.expect: the under-bed dust ecosystem disturbed and collected.

steps.action: **Empty and reset.** Bin emptied into the trash (outside/bagged if dusty), filter tapped clean per the manual's cadence, brush roll checked for hair wrap (scissors along the roll's groove — cut wrap, don't yank), cord/battery restored.
steps.expect: machine stored ready; suction next time == suction this time.

recipes.verification: Lanes covered the full floor including two directions on traffic carpet, edges and reachable unders are done, the bin is emptied and the roll unwrapped, and the machine is stored charged/coiled — verifiably ready for a next session that starts at full suction.

recipes.title: wash a down jacket
recipes.name: wash-a-down-jacket
recipes.goal: A down jacket is washed and dried until the down clusters are clean, separated, and fully lofted.

steps.action: **Inspect and empty.** Close zippers, empty pockets, fasten tabs, and check seams for holes.
steps.expect: jacket is secured and no items remain inside.

steps.action: **Clean the washer.** Remove detergent and softener residue from the dispenser.
steps.expect: only down wash will contact the jacket.

steps.action: **Wash gently.** Use down wash on a gentle cycle with cold or warm water as the label allows.
steps.expect: jacket is wet through and cleaned without regular detergent.

steps.action: **Rinse again.** Run an extra rinse to remove all soap.
steps.expect: rinse water has no visible suds.

steps.action: **Support while moving.** Lift the wet jacket from underneath instead of pulling one sleeve.
steps.expect: heavy wet down does not strain seams.

steps.action: **Dry low and slow.** Tumble dry low with dryer balls, removing and shaking every 30 minutes. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* high heat can melt shell fabric or damage down; confirm low heat before starting.
steps.expect: clumps gradually break apart and loft returns.

steps.action: **Break clumps by hand.** Pinch and separate damp down clusters between dryer checks.
steps.expect: baffles feel less lumpy each cycle.

steps.action: **Confirm full dryness.** Continue drying until cuffs, seams, and thick baffles feel dry and airy.
steps.expect: no cool damp spots remain.

recipes.verification: The jacket has no soap feel, no damp or cool baffles, and the down is evenly lofted across sleeves, body, and collar.

recipes.title: wash dishes by hand
recipes.name: wash-dishes-by-hand
recipes.goal: A sinkful of dishes washed in the efficient order, actually clean rather than rearranged grease, dried and put away, with the sink itself finishing clean.
