steps.action: **Stage: scrape everything, stack by category, start the worst soaking.** Plates scraped to the bin, pots with stuck food filled with hot water and a drop of soap (`daily/food/clean-as-you-cook` step 5 ideally already did this), glasses and cutlery grouped.
steps.expect: no solids heading for the drain; burnt pots soaking; a wash order visible on the counter.

steps.action: **Set up the wash: hot soapy water in the basin, rinse side ready.** Two-basin sinks: wash in one, rinse in the other. Single basin: a washing-up bowl for suds and a thin stream or a filled kettle-pot for rinsing. Water as hot as gloved or bare hands comfortably bear; heat cuts grease.
steps.expect: a suds basin and a rinse plan.

steps.action: **Wash in the cleanest-to-dirtiest order: glasses, cutlery, plates and bowls, serving pieces, then pots and pans last.** The water stays usable longest this way; greasy pans first is the classic self-sabotage.
steps.expect: each category washed inside and out (glass rims, fork tines, the *backs* of plates), then to the rinse.

steps.action: **Rinse off all suds with clean hot water.** Soap film left on dishes is both a taste and a stomach complaint.
steps.expect: squeaky surfaces, no bubbles sliding off into the rack.

steps.action: **Handle knives and the soaked pots deliberately.** Knives washed one at a time, blade away, straight to the rack's safe slot or the towel, never into a crowded caddy edge-up. Pots: their soak has loosened the stuck layer; a brush finishes it, and the baking-soda boil trick (`daily/food/clean-as-you-cook` F3) handles the burnt outliers.
steps.expect: fingers accounted for; pots actually clean, not "dark-bottomed but probably fine".

steps.action: **Dry and put away, then close the sink down.** Air-drying in the rack beats a damp towel for hygiene, but a *clean* towel is fine and faster; either way, put things away when dry (a permanently full rack is storage, not workflow). Then: drain the basin, rinse the sink walls, wring the sponge dry, and hang the cloth to dry.
steps.expect: empty sink, cleared or clearing rack, sponge and cloth drying rather than souring.

recipes.verification: Everything washed in order and soap-rinsed, knives and pots handled by their rules, the rack draining or emptied, grease in the jar rather than the pipes, and the sink, sponge, and cloth left clean and drying.

recipes.title: wash pillows and duvets
recipes.name: wash-pillows-and-duvets
recipes.goal: Pillows or a duvet come out clean, fully dry to the core, and with the filling redistributed and lofted rather than clumped, ready to sleep on without any mildew risk.

steps.action: **Read the care label first.** [BRANCH: machine washable → continue | dry-clean only or "do not wash" (common for wool and some down) → stop, use a professional cleaner | memory foam or latex pillow → never machine wash; see Variations]
steps.expect: a labeled max temperature and drying instruction you will follow.

steps.action: **Inspect seams and fabric before washing.** Check for tears, thin fabric, and open seams; a small hole becomes a machine full of feathers. Spot-repair or hand-stitch any gap first.
steps.expect: no openings anywhere on the shell.

steps.action: **Load the machine with balance in mind.** Pillows: always wash two at a time (or one plus towels) so the drum spins balanced. Duvet: alone, loosely folded, never packed tight.
steps.expect: the item fits with room to shift; the drum turns it, not just vibrates it.

steps.action: **Wash on a gentle cycle, warm (usually 40 °C / warm setting), with about half the normal detergent.** Excess detergent is the main cause of clumped, soap-stiff filling because it never rinses out of down or fiberfill.
steps.expect: cycle running; no over-sudsing visible through the door.

steps.action: **Run an extra rinse and an extra spin.** Filling holds soap and water tenaciously; one added rinse cycle plus a second high spin removes most of both and cuts hours off drying.
steps.expect: item comes out damp, not dripping, with no soap smell.

steps.action: **Dry low and long with tennis balls.** Into the dryer on low heat with 3-4 tennis balls or dryer balls; the balls beat the filling apart as it dries, which is the difference between a lofted pillow and a lumpy one.
steps.expect: rhythmic thumping; item visibly re-lofting over the first hour.

steps.action: **Break up clumps by hand every 30-45 minutes.** Pull the item out, massage apart any wet lumps of filling (they hide in corners and baffles), shake, return.
steps.expect: clumps getting smaller and fewer each check.

steps.action: **Apply the full-dry rule.** Keep drying until the filling is bone dry at the core, not just the shell. Test: squeeze the thickest part hard for ten seconds; any coolness or dampness means keep going. A damp core mildews inside a week and the smell never leaves. Expect 2-3 hours or more for down.
steps.expect: every part of the item warm and weightless, no cool damp spots, no musty smell.

steps.action: **Air, loft, and re-dress.** Let it cool and air for 30 minutes, fluff thoroughly, then back into a clean pillowcase or duvet cover.
steps.expect: item at full loft, smelling of nothing.

recipes.verification: Squeezed hard at its thickest point for ten seconds, the item feels warm and dry with no cool spots; the filling moves freely with no fist-sized clumps; it smells of nothing; and it has returned to something near its original loft.

recipes.title: weatherstrip a door
recipes.name: weatherstrip-a-door
recipes.goal: A drafty door is sealed with weatherstripping that fits the actual gaps while still letting the door close and latch.

steps.action: **Find the draft.** Close the door and feel around edges, or watch smoke movement near the frame.
steps.expect: leaky sides or bottom are identified.

steps.action: **Measure the gaps.** Check top, latch side, hinge side, and bottom separately.
steps.expect: each gap has an approximate width and length.

steps.action: **Choose type by gap.** [BRANCH: foam tape for small even gaps | V-strip for narrow moving edges | rubber bulb for larger gaps | sweep for bottom]
steps.expect: material compresses enough without blocking closure.

steps.action: **Clean the contact surface.** Wipe dust, grease, and loose paint from the frame.
steps.expect: adhesive area is dry and smooth.

steps.action: **Cut pieces to length.** Cut top and side pieces square, leaving no stretched ends.
steps.expect: pieces match the frame sections before backing is removed.

steps.action: **Apply from one end.** Peel backing gradually and press weatherstrip onto the stop or frame where the closed door contacts it.
steps.expect: strip is straight and firmly adhered.

steps.action: **Seal corners carefully.** Butt pieces together without overlapping bulky corners.
steps.expect: light is blocked at corners without bunching.

steps.action: **Install the bottom sweep if needed.** Position it so it touches the threshold lightly, then fasten.
steps.expect: sweep brushes or compresses against the threshold.

steps.action: **Test closure.** Close and latch the door several times.
steps.expect: latch catches without slamming or excessive force.

steps.action: **Paper-test the seal.** Close a sheet of paper in several spots and pull gently.
steps.expect: paper has light resistance where the seal is working.

recipes.verification: The door closes and latches normally, paper has light resistance around sealed edges, and no obvious draft or daylight remains at the treated gaps.

recipes.title: winterize a garden
recipes.name: winterize-a-garden
recipes.goal: Prepare garden beds, tools, containers, and tender plants for freezing weather while preserving soil health and habitat.

steps.action: **Harvest and label.** Pick remaining vegetables, herbs, and seeds worth saving, and label perennials before foliage disappears.
steps.expect: edible crops and plant locations are accounted for.

steps.action: **Remove diseased plants.** Pull blighted tomatoes, mildewed squash, and pest-infested debris for trash, not compost.
steps.expect: obvious disease sources are out of the bed.

steps.action: **Leave useful stems and leaves.** Keep healthy perennial stems or a thin leaf layer where wildlife habitat and local practice allow.
steps.expect: beds are tidy but not stripped bare.

steps.action: **Mulch exposed soil.** Add straw, shredded leaves, compost, or cover crop seed to protect soil from erosion and freeze-thaw cycles.
steps.expect: bare soil is covered without burying plant crowns.

steps.action: **Protect tender plants.** [BRANCH: bring indoors | mulch outdoors] move tender pots inside after checking for pests, or mulch hardy crowns and bulbs.
steps.expect: plants have an appropriate cold plan.

steps.action: **Drain water gear.** Disconnect hoses, drain watering cans, empty ceramic pots that may crack, and shut off outdoor spigots if needed.
steps.expect: no trapped water remains in freeze-prone equipment.

steps.action: **Clean and store tools.** Brush soil from tools, dry metal parts, and oil pruner blades lightly.
steps.expect: tools are dry, sharp, and stored under cover.

recipes.verification: Beds are covered, diseased material is removed, tender plants have a cold plan, hoses are drained, and tools are clean and stored.

recipes.title: blow a big bubble
recipes.name: blow-a-big-bubble
recipes.goal: Make a large soap bubble using a flexible wand, a strong bubble solution, and slow movement in still air.

steps.action: **Mix the solution.** Combine 6 parts water, 1 part dish soap, and either 1 part glycerin or 1 spoon of sugar per cup of water.
steps.expect: the mixture is smooth without heavy foam.

steps.action: **Rest the solution.** Let it sit for at least 15 minutes, longer if possible.
steps.expect: bubbles on the surface settle down.

steps.action: **Build the wand.** Tie string between two sticks or straws to make a loop with a smaller top span and a longer bottom span.
steps.expect: the loop hangs open like a loose triangle.

steps.action: **Wet the wand fully.** Dip the entire string loop into the tray and lift it slowly.
steps.expect: a thin soap film fills the loop.

steps.action: **Find still air.** [BRANCH: outdoors | indoors] Stand where there is a faint breeze or still air; avoid fans and gusts.
steps.expect: the film does not rip immediately.

steps.action: **Open the loop.** Hold the sticks apart gently without snapping the film.
steps.expect: the soap film stretches between the strings.

steps.action: **Pull slowly.** Walk backward or move the wand in one slow steady pull.
steps.expect: a tube of bubble film forms and grows.

steps.action: **Close the bubble.** Bring the sticks together or twist the wand slightly when the bubble is large enough.
steps.expect: the bubble pinches off and floats free.

steps.action: **Adjust one variable.** If bubbles pop quickly, add a little glycerin or sugar; if the film is heavy, add water.
steps.expect: the next bubble lasts longer or opens more easily.

recipes.verification: A soap film stretches from the wand and pinches off into at least one large free-floating bubble.

recipes.title: blow a bubblegum bubble
recipes.name: blow-a-bubblegum-bubble
recipes.goal: A visible bubble (5 cm or larger) is blown from a piece of bubblegum and either popped intentionally or pulled back into the mouth without gum ending up on face or clothes.

steps.action: **Chew the piece until the sugar is mostly gone.** This takes 3 to 5 minutes; two pieces are easier than one for beginners.
steps.expect: the gum is smooth, warm, and stretchy, no longer gritty or intensely sweet.

steps.action: **Flatten the wad against the roof of your mouth with your tongue.** Press it into a rough disc, then move the disc so it sits just behind your front teeth.
steps.expect: a flat pancake of gum you can feel spanning the area behind the teeth.

steps.action: **Make the tongue pocket.** Push the tip of your tongue gently into the center of the flattened disc, stretching a thin cup of gum over the tongue tip (like a sock over a toe).
steps.expect: the tongue tip is wrapped in a thin, translucent-feeling layer of gum; the gum has not torn.

steps.action: **Part your teeth and lips slightly and withdraw the tongue.** Keep the gum sheet anchored by your teeth as the tongue pulls back, leaving a small hollow pocket facing outward.
steps.expect: a small gum membrane sits between slightly open lips.

steps.action: **Blow a slow, steady breath into the pocket.** Use gentle, continuous pressure from the lungs, not a sharp puff. Sharp puffs blow the gum out of your mouth.
steps.expect: the membrane inflates outward and a bubble grows past your lips.

steps.action: **Manage the endgame.** [BRANCH: pop it (bite down and inhale slightly so the film collapses inward onto your lips and teeth) | recover it (stop blowing, suck inward gently, and chew the deflated bubble back into the wad)]
steps.expect: gum is entirely back in the mouth; nothing on skin or clothes.

recipes.verification: A bubble at least the size of your mouth opening was visible to an observer (or in the mirror), and afterward all gum is back in the mouth or in the trash, with none stuck to face, hair, or clothing.

recipes.title: build a blanket fort
recipes.name: build-a-blanket-fort
recipes.goal: A structurally sound blanket fort with standing headroom for its seated occupants, a defensible entrance, and interior lighting, that survives the whole movie without a mid-film roof collapse.

steps.action: **Site survey and frame layout.** Pick a corner or sofa-adjacent zone away from doors and radiators; arrange chairs back-outward in a rough rectangle, or claim the dining table whole. Corners and walls are free structure; use them.
steps.expect: a stable perimeter frame with a planned entrance gap, footprint sized to occupants-plus-snacks.

steps.action: **Engineer the ridge line.** The single biggest upgrade over amateur forts: a spine for the roof. A broom handle bridging two chair backs, a sofa-to-bookshelf cord (taut, tied to something that cannot tip), or the table's underside as a ready-made ceiling.
steps.expect: a high line the roof can drape over, creating pitch instead of sag.

steps.action: **Drape the roof sheets over the ridge and frame.** Lightest sheets on top spans; overlap edges by a hand-width where two sheets meet.
steps.expect: full coverage with pitched sides; the middle clears a seated head.

steps.action: **Anchor every edge with ballast.** Books or cushion weights on the chair seats and floor edges, clips or rubber bands pinching sheet-to-chair joints; the sofa's own cushions clamp that flank.
steps.expect: a tug test on each sheet meets resistance; no edge relies on hope.

steps.action: **Fit out the interior.** Duvet flooring, cushion seating against the hard chair legs, snack corner away from the entrance's traffic, and lighting: LED string lights or a cool lamp *inside a jar or well clear of fabric*.
steps.expect: a habitable interior that a seated adult enters without shoulder-checking a load-bearing chair.

steps.action: **Commission the fort.** Entrance flap test (openable one-handed from inside), full-occupancy wiggle test, and the solemn naming ceremony, which is not optional.
steps.expect: everyone in, roof standing, name declared, movie starting.

recipes.verification: The roof clears seated heads with visible pitch, every edge passes the tug test, the entrance works one-handed, lighting is cool-source and fabric-clear, and the structure outlives the movie including one accidental kick.

recipes.title: build a campfire
recipes.name: build-a-campfire
recipes.goal: A campfire built legally and safely, lit with one or two matches, enjoyed, and then extinguished so thoroughly that the ground is cold to a bare hand, which is the step that defines whether you get to be proud of the rest.

steps.action: **Prepare the site.** Use the existing ring; clear a meter-plus circle down to mineral soil of leaves and debris; overhanging branches disqualify a spot.
steps.expect: a bare-soil circle, water bucket standing by, fuel sorted into its three piles within reach.

steps.action: **Build small and hollow.** A fist-sized tinder nest in the center; kindling around it in a small teepee or lean-to against a thicker stick, with finger-gaps for air. Fire eats oxygen before it eats wood; the classic beginner error is building a woodpile, not an air structure.
steps.expect: a structure you can see through, tinder reachable at its base.

steps.action: **Light the tinder at its base, upwind side.** One match, cupped from the breeze; let flame climb into the kindling.
steps.expect: tinder catching, kindling crackling within a minute; resist rearranging while it establishes.

steps.action: **Feed by size, patiently.** Add kindling until a solid crackle, then fuel wood one piece at a time, laid to preserve airflow. Blowing gently at the base's embers revives hesitation; dumping the big log on early smothers everything.
steps.expect: a self-sustaining fire stepping up through the sizes; flames sized to the ring, never taller than needed.

steps.action: **Run the fire like the custodian you are.** Someone attentive within reach at all times (an unattended campfire is not a thing that exists, only abandonment); shoes on around it; marshmallow radius enforced for kids; new fuel added with placed, not tossed, motions.
steps.expect: a stable, sociable fire with its keeper present and the water still staged.

steps.action: **Extinguish with the full protocol, starting 30+ minutes before leaving.** Let it burn down; spread the coals; water poured on in stages, *stirring* ash and embers with the stick between pours; repeat until no hiss, no steam, no glow. Then the hand test: hover, then touch the ash with a bare hand. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* leaving warm coals is how forests burn down days later; cold-to-the-touch is the only pass grade.
steps.expect: wet, cold, stirred ash; the site cool everywhere a hand checks.

recipes.verification: The fire was legal, ringed, sized modestly, never unattended, and the site you leave passes the bare-hand test on cold wet ash with the surroundings clear of stray embers — the campfire's real final exam.

recipes.title: build a domino run
recipes.name: build-a-domino-run
recipes.goal: A domino run topples from start to finish, including curves and branches, with enough reliability that the final fall feels earned instead of lucky.

steps.action: **Clear the runway.** Sweep crumbs and move chairs, cords, and wobbling objects. [BRANCH: table build | floor build] choose table for short runs, floor for long drama.
steps.expect: the surface is flat and traffic-free.

steps.action: **Use the spacing rule.** Place each domino about half a domino height from the next one.
steps.expect: a falling domino reaches the next near its upper half.

steps.action: **Build straight sections first.** Stand five to ten dominoes in a line, keeping their faces parallel.
steps.expect: the row looks evenly spaced, like tiny patient doors.

steps.action: **Make curves with smaller angles.** Rotate each domino a little, not one big turn.
steps.expect: the curve bends smoothly and every top edge points at the next target.

steps.action: **Add safety gaps while building.** Leave intentional gaps between sections and bridge them only when the section is tested.
steps.expect: one accidental bump cannot destroy the entire route.

steps.action: **Create reset-proof branches.** Aim one falling domino into two slightly offset starters, then leave a removable blocker until the final run.
steps.expect: each branch can be tested without firing the whole machine.

steps.action: **Run a topple test.** Flick the first domino of each section before connecting sections. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the full run spends all setup time at once, so test sections before removing safety gaps.
steps.expect: every tested section reaches its endpoint.

steps.action: **Connect and launch.** Fill the safety gaps, remove blockers, and tap the first domino lightly.
steps.expect: the cascade reaches the final domino.

recipes.verification: One deliberate tap at the start causes the final domino in the planned route to fall.

recipes.title: build a sandcastle
recipes.name: build-a-sandcastle
recipes.goal: Build a freestanding sandcastle with compact towers, carved details, and a moat that survives normal beach wind and a few small waves.

steps.action: **Pick the site.** Choose damp, packed sand above the current wash line.
steps.expect: footprints hold shape and no wave reaches the spot for several minutes.

steps.action: **Make a water source.** Dig a small pit until water seeps in, or carry water in a bucket.
steps.expect: wet sand can be squeezed into a clump that holds.

steps.action: **Mix sand to packing texture.** Use roughly 8 parts sand to 1 part water, adding water until it feels like heavy brown sugar.
steps.expect: a squeezed ball stays intact but does not drip.

steps.action: **Build a compact base.** Pile wet sand in the center and press it down with hands or the shovel back.
steps.expect: the mound feels dense and does not crumble when tapped.

steps.action: **Pack bucket forms.** Fill a bucket in layers, tamping each layer firmly before adding more.
steps.expect: the bucket feels heavy and the top surface is tight.

steps.action: **Flip the bucket.** Place it upside down on the base, tap the sides, then lift straight up.
steps.expect: a tower form releases with clean sides.

steps.action: **Add more forms.** [BRANCH: one large keep | several towers] repeat with larger or smaller containers, pressing each form into the base.
steps.expect: towers touch the base firmly with no gaps at the bottom.

steps.action: **Carve from the top down.** Shape roof points, walls, windows, and stairs before carving lower details.
steps.expect: loose sand falls away without damaging finished lower areas.

steps.action: **Cut clean edges.** Use a stick, shell, card, or finger to scrape doorways and wall lines.
steps.expect: features look intentional, not finger-smeared.

steps.action: **Dig the moat last.** Scoop a ring around the castle and connect it to the water pit only if you want water in it.
steps.expect: the moat has sloped sides and does not undercut the base.

steps.action: **Reinforce weak spots.** Drip wet sand onto cracks and press gently from both sides.
steps.expect: cracks close and the tower no longer sheds dry grains.

recipes.verification: The castle has at least one compact tower, carved visible details, and a moat or boundary trench, and it stands for 5 minutes without hand support.

recipes.title: build a snowman
recipes.name: build-a-snowman
recipes.goal: A stable three-ball snowman, decorated, standing where it can be seen without blocking anyone, built without wrecked backs or lost gloves.

steps.action: **Test the snow.** Squeeze a handful hard. [BRANCH: it compacts into a solid ball → build now | it crumbles → wait for warmer hours or the afternoon sun; a light water mist on the snow surface can rescue marginal snow]
steps.expect: a fist-sized snowball that survives a gentle toss.

steps.action: **Pack a dense starter ball.** Compress a snowball between both hands until it is hard, about melon-core density. A loose starter makes every later layer flaky.
steps.expect: a solid ball roughly 15 cm across that does not crumble under thumb pressure.

steps.action: **Roll the base.** Roll the starter through fresh snow, changing direction every few pushes so it grows round instead of into a cylinder, and pat it firmly every few rolls to bind the new layer. Stop around knee height.
steps.expect: a roughly spherical base you can no longer roll easily; a stripped spiral path behind it.

steps.action: **Seat the base and flatten its top.** Push it to the display spot, then press down and pack a flat platform on top, about two hands wide.
steps.expect: the base does not rock; the top platform is level.

steps.action: **Roll and mount the middle ball.** Roll a second ball to about two-thirds the base diameter. Lift it with your legs, not your back, keeping it close to your body; get a second person for anything heavier than comfortable. Set it on the platform and pack a collar of loose snow into the seam all the way around, pressing hard.
steps.expect: the middle ball sits centered and cannot be slid off by a firm push.

steps.action: **Make and mount the head.** Pack the head by hand at about half the middle ball's size; oversized heads are the number one cause of decapitation. Flatten the middle ball's top, seat the head, and weld the seam with packed snow. For icy or windy days, drive a straight stick down through head and middle as a spine first.
steps.expect: the head stays put when you press its top lightly.

steps.action: **Decorate.** Push stick arms into the middle ball at a slight upward angle, the carrot nose into the head's center, and press stones in firmly for eyes, mouth, and buttons. Add scarf and hat last.
steps.expect: a face readable from 10 m; nothing falls off when the wind gusts.

steps.action: **Clear the site.** Collect tools and any dropped gloves, and note every non-snow item on the snowman for later retrieval.
steps.expect: nothing left on the ground that the melt will not absorb.

recipes.verification: Three balls in decreasing size stand plumb and survive a firm push on the middle ball; face and arms are attached; the site is free of tools and litter; hands are dry and warm again indoors.

recipes.title: carve a pumpkin
recipes.name: carve-a-pumpkin
recipes.goal: A pumpkin with a clean-cut lid, an emptied cavity, and a carved face that reads clearly when lit from inside, achieved without hand injuries.

steps.action: **Wash and dry the pumpkin, then plan the face.** Sketch the design on paper first, or tape a printed template to the flattest side. Chunky shapes survive carving; thin spidery lines break out.
steps.expect: a design where every cutout piece is wider than a finger.

steps.action: **Cut the lid at a 45-degree inward angle.** Draw a hexagon around the stem, add a small notch as a realignment key, and saw with the blade angled toward the center so the lid rests on a ledge. A straight vertical cut makes a lid that falls into the cavity.
steps.expect: the lid lifts out with the stem as a handle and re-seats on its ledge without dropping through.

steps.action: **Scoop the cavity completely.** Scrape seeds and strings out with the spoon, then keep scraping the walls. Thin the wall behind the face area to about 2.5 cm; full-thickness rind is hard to cut and blocks light.
steps.expect: the interior wall feels firm and even; the face wall is noticeably thinner than the back.

steps.action: **Transfer the template.** Poke pinholes along the template lines every few millimeters with a pin or poking tool, then remove the paper and connect the dots with the marker if the holes are hard to see.
steps.expect: the full design visible as a dotted outline on the rind.

steps.action: **Cut the face with short saw strokes, smallest pieces first.** Saw perpendicular to the rind surface, moving the saw, not twisting it. Cut interior details before large outer shapes so the surrounding rind stays rigid. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* every cut is permanent; recheck which side of the line is waste before starting each piece. Always cut away from the hand steadying the pumpkin.
steps.expect: each piece separates along the pinhole line with no cracks radiating past it.

steps.action: **Push cut pieces out from the inside.** Reach into the cavity and press outward with a finger or the spoon handle; prying from the front snaps details off.
steps.expect: pieces pop out cleanly; edges are ragged-free enough to read at a distance.

steps.action: **Light it.** [BRANCH: LED tea light (set inside, switch on, lid on) | real candle (place the candle, light it with a long lighter through the face, then cut a 3 cm chimney hole in the lid before seating it)]
steps.expect: the face glows evenly; with a real candle, no smoke stains forming on the lid underside.

recipes.verification: The lid re-seats on its ledge and the notch key aligns; the cavity is scraped clean; the carved face matches the template with no unintended cracks; a light inside makes the design readable from across the room; all fingers uncut.

recipes.title: crochet a granny square
recipes.name: crochet-a-granny-square
recipes.goal: Crochet a basic granny square with four corners, even clusters, and a secured yarn tail.

steps.action: **Make a center ring.** Chain four stitches and slip stitch into the first chain to form a ring.
steps.expect: a small loop is ready to receive stitches.

steps.action: **Build the first corner round.** Chain three, work two double crochets into the ring, chain two, then make three more double-crochet clusters separated by chain-two corners.
steps.expect: four clusters sit around the center ring.

steps.action: **Join the round.** Slip stitch into the top of the starting chain three.
steps.expect: the first round closes into a tiny square.

steps.action: **Start the next round.** Chain three and work two double crochets into the nearest corner space.
steps.expect: the hook is positioned to grow the square from a corner.

steps.action: **Fill each corner.** In every corner space, make three double crochets, chain two, and three double crochets.
steps.expect: each corner becomes wider and clearly squared.

steps.action: **Work side spaces.** On later rounds, place one three-double-crochet cluster in each side gap between corners.
steps.expect: sides lengthen while corners remain distinct.

steps.action: **Fasten off and weave tails.** Cut the yarn, pull the tail through the final loop, and weave tails through the back.
steps.expect: the square keeps its shape when handled.

recipes.verification: The granny square has four clear corners, straight-ish sides, repeated three-stitch clusters, and woven ends that do not pull free.

recipes.title: deal cards
recipes.name: deal-cards
recipes.goal: Deal cards fairly so each player receives the right count in the right order for the game.

steps.action: **Square the deck.** Tap all four edges and hold the deck face down.
steps.expect: the cards form one clean stack.

steps.action: **Offer the cut.** Place the deck near the player to the dealer's right or according to local custom.
steps.expect: another player lifts part of the deck and completes the cut.

steps.action: **Name the count.** Say how many cards each player gets for this game.
steps.expect: every player hears the target number before the deal starts.

steps.action: **Start with the next player.** Deal one card face down to the player on your left, then continue clockwise.
steps.expect: the dealer receives a card last in each round.

steps.action: **Deal one at a time.** Give one card per player per pass until the count is reached.
steps.expect: all hands grow evenly.

steps.action: **Keep the packet low.** Slide or toss cards gently so faces stay hidden.
steps.expect: no card flips or exposes its value.

steps.action: **Check the count.** Ask players to count their hands without showing faces.
steps.expect: each hand has the correct number.

steps.action: **Apply the deal-again rule.** [BRANCH: clean deal | exposed or wrong count] keep playing if clean, or collect, reshuffle, cut, and redeal if fairness broke.
steps.expect: the table agrees the deal stands or restarts.

recipes.verification: Every player has the required number of face-down cards, no exposed-card dispute remains, and the table agrees play can begin.

recipes.title: do a basic skateboard ollie
recipes.name: do-a-basic-skateboard-ollie
recipes.goal: You can perform a basic skateboard ollie on flat ground: pop the tail, slide the front foot, level the board, and land over the bolts.

steps.action: **Gear up and inspect.** Put on pads and helmet, check wheels, trucks, deck cracks, and shoelaces.
steps.expect: nothing loose, sharp, or likely to catch.

steps.action: **Set the stance.** Back foot on the tail pocket, front foot behind the front bolts, shoulders aligned with the board.
steps.expect: knees bend while weight stays centered.

steps.action: **Practice the pop stationary.** Press the tail sharply down with the back foot while jumping up, letting the board snap against the ground.
steps.expect: a crisp pop sound without leaning backward.

steps.action: **Slide the front foot.** As the board rises, drag the outside edge of the front shoe up toward the nose.
steps.expect: grip tape catches the shoe and lifts the board's front.

steps.action: **Level the board.** Tuck knees, guide the nose forward, and let the back foot rise so the tail can come up.
steps.expect: the deck flattens in the air, even if only briefly.

steps.action: **Land over the bolts.** Bring both feet down above the truck bolts with knees bent and shoulders still aligned.
steps.expect: the board lands flat instead of shooting out.

steps.action: **Try tiny rolling ollies.** [BRANCH: stationary stable | stationary unstable] If stable, roll at walking speed; if unstable, repeat stationary reps and step-offs.
steps.expect: the motion stays the same while moving slowly.

steps.action: **Stop before sloppy reps.** End the session when legs are tired or fear makes you stiff.
steps.expect: practice ends with controlled attempts, not crashes.

recipes.verification: On flat open ground with protective gear, you pop the board, get all four wheels off the ground, land with both feet over the bolts, and roll away.

recipes.title: do a basic yo yo trick
recipes.name: do-a-basic-yo-yo-trick
recipes.goal: A yo-yo is set to the right string length, thrown into a sleeper, returned with a gravity pull, and optionally walked like a tiny obedient wheel.

steps.action: **Set string length.** Stand the yo-yo on the floor and bring the string to your belly button, tying a new finger loop there if needed. [BRANCH: long string | short string] shorten long string, leave short string for now.
steps.expect: the loop reaches about navel height.

steps.action: **Wear the loop correctly.** Slip the loop over your middle finger between the first and second knuckle.
steps.expect: the string tightens on your finger without cutting circulation.

steps.action: **Wind the yo-yo.** Wrap the string neatly until the yo-yo is full.
steps.expect: the yo-yo hangs from your hand without loose loops.

steps.action: **Throw the sleeper.** Hold palm up, snap the yo-yo downward, and let it spin at the end of the string.
steps.expect: the yo-yo spins in place instead of climbing back immediately.

steps.action: **Wake it with a tug.** Flick your wrist upward for a gravity pull.
steps.expect: the yo-yo climbs back to your hand.

steps.action: **Try walk the dog.** Throw a sleeper, lower the spinning yo-yo gently onto smooth floor, and let it roll forward.
steps.expect: the yo-yo creeps ahead while still spinning.

steps.action: **Call it back.** Lift the yo-yo off the floor and tug upward before it slows too much.
steps.expect: it returns to your hand, perhaps with comic dignity.

steps.action: **Reset the wind.** Rewind neatly before the next attempt. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* throwing near breakable objects can convert practice into cleanup, so keep the practice lane clear.
steps.expect: the yo-yo is ready for another clean throw.

recipes.verification: The yo-yo sleeps at the bottom of the string for at least two seconds and returns to your hand on a tug.

recipes.title: do a card fan
recipes.name: do-a-card-fan
recipes.goal: Spread a deck into a clean card fan, close it without dropping cards, and practice the flourish smoothly.

steps.action: **Square the deck.** Tap the cards into a neat block with all edges aligned.
steps.expect: the deck starts compact.

steps.action: **Set the grip.** Hold the deck in the non-dominant hand with the long edge resting across the fingers.
steps.expect: the thumb can move across the top card edges.

steps.action: **Angle the deck.** Tilt the outer corner slightly upward and keep light pressure at the inner corner.
steps.expect: the cards are ready to pivot from one point.

steps.action: **Push with the thumb.** Sweep the thumb across the top edge in a smooth arc.
steps.expect: cards spread one after another instead of in clumps.

steps.action: **Control pressure.** [BRANCH: clumps | gaps] reduce pressure for clumps, or add pressure if cards fly too far apart.
steps.expect: the fan becomes more even.

steps.action: **Support the fan.** Let the fingers underneath hold the curved spread.
steps.expect: the fan stays open without sagging.

steps.action: **Close cleanly.** Push the outer cards back toward the pivot point and square the deck.
steps.expect: the cards return to one packet.

steps.action: **Practice both directions.** Try the fan with the other hand or reverse sweep.
steps.expect: one side feels easier, but both improve.

steps.action: **Add the flourish.** Present the fan briefly, then close it before the spread collapses.
steps.expect: the motion looks intentional and controlled.

recipes.verification: The deck opens into a visible fan with mostly even spacing, then closes back into a squared packet without dropped or bent cards.

recipes.title: do a cartwheel
recipes.name: do-a-cartwheel
recipes.goal: Perform a controlled beginner cartwheel with a hand-hand-foot-foot rhythm and a safe landing.

steps.action: **Choose the direction.** Stand sideways to the travel line and pick the lead leg that feels natural in a lunge.
steps.expect: one foot points forward along the line and the other foot stays behind.

steps.action: **Mark the hand targets.** Imagine two handprints on the line, shoulder-width apart, just past the lead foot.
steps.expect: you know where the first hand and second hand will land.

steps.action: **Practice the rhythm standing low.** Say hand, hand, foot, foot while touching the ground lightly and stepping through.
steps.expect: the sequence feels like a sideways wheel, not a jump straight up.

steps.action: **Start in a deep lunge.** Bend the front knee, raise both arms, and look toward the first hand target.
steps.expect: weight is forward but controlled, with the back leg ready to swing.

steps.action: **Place the first hand.** Reach down with the lead-side hand while the back leg begins to kick up.
steps.expect: first palm lands flat on the line and the hips start to lift.

steps.action: **Place the second hand.** Put the second palm down past the first, keeping arms straight and shoulders strong.
steps.expect: both hands briefly carry weight while legs pass overhead or at a low diagonal.

steps.action: **Land the first foot.** Let the first kicked leg come down on the far side of the line.
steps.expect: the first landing foot touches down before the second foot.

steps.action: **Land the second foot and stand.** Step the second foot down, lift the chest, and finish facing the opposite direction.
steps.expect: the hand-hand-foot-foot rhythm completes without a collapse.

steps.action: **Add height gradually.** Kick a little higher only when the low version stays straight and quiet.
steps.expect: legs rise more without changing the order of contact.

recipes.verification: Hands and feet touch in the order hand, hand, foot, foot, and you finish upright without pain or falling.

recipes.title: do a coin behind the ear trick
recipes.name: do-a-coin-behind-the-ear-trick
recipes.goal: Perform a simple coin trick where a coin appears to come from behind someone's ear.

steps.action: **Choose the coin.** Pick a coin large enough to control but small enough to hide behind curled fingers.
steps.expect: the coin sits flat against your fingers without showing from the front.

steps.action: **Learn the finger palm.** Hold the coin at the base of your middle and ring fingers, lightly curled into the palm.
steps.expect: your hand looks relaxed from the spectator's view.

steps.action: **Practice empty-looking gestures.** Move your hand naturally while keeping the coin hidden in finger palm.
steps.expect: the coin does not flash in the mirror.

steps.action: **Set up the moment.** Hold the hidden coin in the hand closest to the spectator's ear while talking to them.
steps.expect: your loaded hand is near the reveal position.

steps.action: **Use misdirection.** Ask them to look at your other hand, their hat, or a spot in the air while the loaded hand moves near the ear.
steps.expect: attention shifts away from the hidden coin.

steps.action: **Reach behind the ear.** Slide the coin from finger palm to fingertips as your hand passes behind the ear.
steps.expect: the coin is now pinched at the fingertips but still partly hidden.

steps.action: **Reveal slowly.** Pull the coin into view as if it was found behind the ear.
steps.expect: the spectator sees the coin appear from a place they were not watching.

steps.action: **Reset casually.** Drop the coin into a pocket or hand it over before the spectator asks to inspect your hand.
steps.expect: the trick ends cleanly.

steps.action: **Practice in a mirror.** Repeat the whole trick from the spectator's angle until the palm and reveal look natural.
steps.expect: you can perform without looking at your hidden hand.

recipes.verification: In a mirror or recording, the coin stays hidden until the reveal and the hand looks relaxed throughout the trick.

recipes.title: do a coin magic trick
recipes.name: do-a-coin-magic-trick
recipes.goal: You can perform the French Drop (a coin vanish) smoothly enough that a casual spectator believes the coin left one hand when it secretly stayed in the other, followed by a "reappearance" reveal.

steps.action: **Learn the honest action first.** Hold the coin horizontally by its edge in the left hand, between thumb (below) and first two fingertips (above), palm loosely up. With the right hand, reach over, thumb going under the coin and fingers over it, and genuinely take it. Do this 10 times watching what it really looks like.
steps.expect: you can describe the honest take: the right hand closes around the coin, turns, and moves away; the left hand relaxes and drops naturally.

steps.action: **Learn the secret action.** Repeat the same reach, but as the right fingers screen the coin from the spectator's view, relax the left thumb so the coin drops silently into the left fingers' loose curl (finger curl, not a tight fist). The right hand closes on nothing and moves away exactly as before.
steps.expect: coin rests hidden in the loosely curled left hand; the right fist looks like it did in step 1.

steps.action: **Fix the two tells.** First: the left hand must fall naturally to your side or to a rest position, dead relaxed, as if empty, because a hand guarding a coin stiffens. Second: no sound; the drop is a release into flesh, not a toss.
steps.expect: in the mirror, the honest take and the fake take are indistinguishable, and the drop is silent.

steps.action: **Add the misdirection layer: eyes and attention.** Your eyes follow the (empty) right fist; your body turns slightly toward it; your intention says "the coin is here now". Spectators watch where you watch. The left hand becomes uninteresting and is forgotten.
steps.expect: on video, your gaze locks onto the right fist the moment it closes, never flicking to the left hand.

steps.action: **Rehearse the vanish moment.** Hold the right fist up, squeeze slowly, open finger by finger to show it empty. Pause. Let the vanish land before doing anything else.
steps.expect: a clean beat: take, gaze, squeeze, open, empty.

steps.action: **Choose and rehearse a reveal.** [BRANCH: reach up and "pull the coin from" a spectator's ear or collar with the left hand (classic, kid-friendly) | reach into your own pocket with the left hand, ditch or "find" the coin there | simply re-grip and open the left hand after a magical gesture]
steps.expect: the coin's reappearance reads as magic, and the left hand's approach looks motivated (an adjustment, a point, a reach), never like delivering a payload.

steps.action: **Video-test the full routine before performing.** Record from spectator distance, watch for the three killers: left-hand stiffness, gaze flick, audible drop.
steps.expect: three consecutive recorded runs you cannot catch yourself in.

steps.action: **Perform once, small.** One trick, one spectator, no repeat.
steps.expect: a genuine reaction; requests for "do it again" politely declined (see decision points).

recipes.verification: On recorded video from spectator distance, three consecutive full performances show no gaze flick, no left-hand stiffness or flash, and no drop sound; a live spectator reacted to the vanish without pointing at the correct hand.

recipes.title: do a coin roll across your knuckles
recipes.name: do-a-coin-roll-across-your-knuckles
recipes.goal: You can roll a coin from index knuckle to pinky knuckle, catch it with the thumb, and reset for another pass.

steps.action: **Set the hand platform.** Hold your palm down with fingers slightly curled, knuckles forming a shallow ridge.
steps.expect: the coin can rest flat on the index finger segment.

steps.action: **Start at the index.** Place the coin on the first segment of the index finger and pinch it lightly against the thumb to begin.
steps.expect: the coin is controlled but ready to tip.

steps.action: **Tip to the middle finger.** Lift the index finger slightly while lowering the middle finger so the coin rolls over the index knuckle.
steps.expect: the coin lands on the middle finger segment.

steps.action: **Walk finger-to-finger.** Repeat the lift-and-lower motion from middle to ring, then ring to pinky. Move slowly enough to see each handoff.
steps.expect: the coin travels as three small rolls, not one fling.

steps.action: **Catch with the thumb.** When the coin reaches the pinky side, curl the thumb underneath and trap the coin against the side of the index finger or palm.
steps.expect: the coin returns under the hand without falling.

steps.action: **Reset to the index.** Slide or flip the coin back to the starting pinch between thumb and index. [BRANCH: visible reset | hidden reset] Visible is fine for practice; hidden looks smoother later.
steps.expect: another roll can begin immediately.

steps.action: **Drill slow cycles.** Practice sets of five slow rolls, counting only clean finger handoffs and thumb catches.
steps.expect: fewer drops because speed is not hiding the weak point.

recipes.verification: You complete three full coin rolls in a row from index to pinky with thumb catches and resets, without dropping the coin.

recipes.title: do a mind reading card trick
recipes.name: do-a-mind-reading-card-trick
recipes.goal: Perform a simple mind-reading card trick using the key-card principle, where you secretly track the card next to the spectator's chosen card.

steps.action: **Peek the key card.** Secretly look at the bottom card of the deck and remember it without changing your expression.
steps.expect: you know one card the spectator does not know you know.

steps.action: **Invite a selection.** Spread the cards and ask the spectator to pick one, remember it, and show it to others while you look away.
steps.expect: the spectator believes their card is unknown to you.

steps.action: **Cut the deck.** Ask them to place their card on top of the lower half, then place the original bottom half on top.
steps.expect: your key card now sits directly above their chosen card.

steps.action: **Add the patter.** Say you will read tiny clues from their face or from the deck's order while keeping the handling casual.
steps.expect: attention stays on the story, not the method.

steps.action: **Search for the key.** Turn cards face up one by one until you see your key card; the next card is the selection.
steps.expect: the chosen card is identified silently before the reveal.

steps.action: **Reveal cleanly.** [BRANCH: direct | dramatic] Name the card directly or pause on it and ask the spectator to say it aloud.
steps.expect: the named card matches the spectator's memory.

steps.action: **Do not repeat immediately.** Move to another trick or stop while the effect is strong.
steps.expect: no one gets a second identical run to analyze the method.

recipes.verification: The trick is verified when the spectator's selected card is revealed correctly after you locate the card immediately following your remembered key card.

recipes.title: do a simple card trick
recipes.name: do-a-simple-card-trick
recipes.goal: You can reliably perform a key-card trick: a spectator freely picks and returns a card, and you reveal it with confident patter, without exposing the method.

steps.action: **Learn the key-card principle (solo).** Shuffle, then secretly look at the bottom card of the deck. That is your key card. Everything in this trick reduces to placing the key card directly on top of the spectator's card.
steps.expect: you can name the bottom card at any moment without visibly checking.

steps.action: **Practice the secret glimpse.** Natural cover actions: glance at the bottom card while squaring the deck after a shuffle, or while gesturing with the deck as you talk. The glimpse takes half a second and happens while you speak.
steps.expect: in a mirror, the glimpse is invisible; your eyes are on the "audience" when it happens.

steps.action: **Rehearse the pick and return.** Spread the deck face-down, let the spectator take any card and memorize it. Split the deck: spectator's card goes on top of the lower half, then drop the upper half (with your key card on its bottom) on top.
steps.expect: the key card now sits directly on the spectator's card; the cut looked like ordinary handling.

steps.action: **Rehearse the find.** Spread through the deck face-up "looking for a feeling". Find your key card; the spectator's card is the one immediately after it in the spread direction. Do not stop on it yet: note it and keep spreading a few more cards.
steps.expect: you can identify the selection every time; hesitation at the key card is the tell you are training out.

steps.action: **Build the reveal.** [BRANCH: dramatic pull (cut the selection to the top, snap your fingers, flip it) | mind-reading reveal (name it slowly: color, then suit, then rank, reading their face) | spelling reveal (advanced: spell the card name dealing one card per letter)]
steps.expect: one reveal chosen and drilled until smooth; the mind-reading reveal gets the strongest reactions for zero extra skill.

steps.action: **Script your patter.** Patter is not decoration, it is misdirection: while you talk ("squeeze the card, picture it, I want you to project it to me"), nobody watches your hands. Write three sentences and say the same ones every time.
steps.expect: you can run the whole trick while talking continuously, no silent concentrating pauses.

steps.action: **Perform it once.** One spectator, one performance. Take the applause, and put the deck away or move on. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* repeating a trick for the same audience is the one way to burn it; second viewings are watched for method, not magic, and a discovered method cannot be un-discovered.
steps.expect: a reaction, a smile, and a deck back in your pocket while they are still asking "wait, how".

recipes.verification: The spectator confirms the revealed card is theirs, they cannot explain how, and the trick was performed exactly once for that audience.

recipes.title: do a wall handstand
recipes.name: do-a-wall-handstand
recipes.goal: Kick up into a controlled handstand with the feet supported by a wall, hold a hollow body shape briefly, and come down without falling onto the head or neck.

steps.action: **Clear the landing zone.** Move chairs, shoes, toys, and hard objects away from the wall.
steps.expect: open floor where hands, feet, and a sideways bail can land.

steps.action: **Warm wrists and shoulders.** Circle wrists, press palms to the floor, and do a few plank shoulder rocks.
steps.expect: wrists feel warm, not sharp or pinched.

steps.action: **Place the hands.** Set palms shoulder-width on the floor, fingers spread, fingertips 15 to 25 cm from the wall.
steps.expect: index fingers point roughly forward and both hands press evenly.

steps.action: **Set the kick-up stance.** Put one foot forward and one foot back like a short lunge, eyes between the hands.
steps.expect: shoulders stack over hands before the kick starts.

steps.action: **Kick with control.** Swing the back leg up while the front leg pushes the floor, aiming one heel to touch the wall first.
steps.expect: one foot taps the wall softly instead of slamming.

steps.action: **Bring the second foot to the wall.** Join the feet and press through the shoulders, keeping elbows straight.
steps.expect: both heels rest on the wall and arms feel locked but not hyperextended.

steps.action: **Find hollow body.** Squeeze ribs down, belly tight, glutes on, and toes pointed lightly into the wall.
steps.expect: lower back stops sagging and the body feels like one long line.

steps.action: **Hold briefly.** Breathe for 3 to 10 seconds, pressing the floor away.
steps.expect: hands stay rooted and the wall carries only the feet.

steps.action: **Bail safely.** [BRANCH: step down | cartwheel bail] step one foot down if balanced, or turn one hand and let the legs cartwheel sideways if tipping.
steps.expect: feet return to the floor without the head touching down.

steps.action: **Reset before repeating.** Shake out wrists and wait until breathing is calm.
steps.expect: the next attempt starts with steady hands, not panic.

recipes.verification: Both hands stayed planted, both feet touched the wall, the body held for at least 3 seconds, and the exit ended on the feet without head, neck, or shoulder impact.

recipes.title: do a word search
recipes.name: do-a-word-search
recipes.goal: Find all listed words in a word search by scanning systematically in every allowed direction.

steps.action: **Read the rules.** Check whether words can run forward, backward, vertical, horizontal, or diagonal.
steps.expect: every allowed direction is known.

steps.action: **Pick one word.** Start with a word that has an uncommon first letter or unusual letter pair.
steps.expect: the search target is specific.

steps.action: **Scan first letters.** Move row by row looking only for the first letter of that word.
steps.expect: possible start points stand out.

steps.action: **Check all directions.** From each start point, trace the next letters outward in every allowed direction.
steps.expect: most false starts fail within a few letters.

steps.action: **Mark the find.** Circle or highlight the complete word without covering nearby letters.
steps.expect: the found word is visible and still readable.

steps.action: **Cross off the list.** Mark the word on the word list immediately.
steps.expect: completed targets are not searched again.

steps.action: **Sweep systematically.** [BRANCH: by word | by grid] either repeat word by word, or scan each row, column, and diagonal for any listed word.
steps.expect: the number of unmarked words shrinks steadily.

steps.action: **Recheck leftovers.** For remaining words, search by last letter too because words may be backward.
steps.expect: missed reverse words become easier to spot.

steps.action: **Finish the grid.** Inspect crowded intersections and edges one final time.
steps.expect: every listed word is found or clearly not present.

recipes.verification: Every word in the list is crossed off and its full letter path is marked in the grid.

recipes.title: do hand lettering
recipes.name: do-hand-lettering
recipes.goal: Create a hand-lettered word or short phrase with consistent spacing, controlled stroke weight, and a finished layout.

steps.action: **Choose the phrase.** Pick a short phrase and decide which word should be most important.
steps.expect: the lettering has a clear focal word.

steps.action: **Draw light guides.** Pencil a baseline, x-height, and cap height for the main word.
steps.expect: letters have a shared structure to sit on.

steps.action: **Block the layout.** Sketch each word as a simple rectangle or loose shape before drawing letters.
steps.expect: the phrase fits the page with balanced margins.

steps.action: **Pencil the letters.** Draw letter skeletons first, keeping spacing visually even.
steps.expect: the phrase is readable before ink or decoration.

steps.action: **Add weight deliberately.** Thicken downstrokes or shadow one side of each letter consistently.
steps.expect: stroke weight follows one rule across the piece.

steps.action: **Ink the final lines.** Trace slowly and let ink dry before erasing pencil.
steps.expect: clean dark letters remain without smears.

steps.action: **Add small finishing details.** Use dots, lines, flourishes, or color only where they support the words.
steps.expect: decoration frames the lettering without reducing readability.

recipes.verification: The finished lettering is readable at arm's length, has even visual spacing, follows one stroke-weight rule, and shows no major ink smears.

recipes.title: draw a simple face
recipes.name: draw-a-simple-face
recipes.goal: Draw a simple front-facing face with balanced placement of eyes, nose, mouth, ears, and hair.

steps.action: **Draw an oval head.** Sketch lightly and leave room around it for hair and ears.
steps.expect: a soft head shape sits centered on the page.

steps.action: **Place the eye line.** Draw a faint horizontal guide halfway down the head.
steps.expect: the face has a clear center line for features.

steps.action: **Add two simple eyes.** Place almond or oval eyes on the guide with one eye-width between them.
steps.expect: the eyes look evenly spaced.

steps.action: **Mark nose and mouth guides.** Place the nose halfway between eye line and chin, then the mouth halfway between nose and chin.
steps.expect: the lower face has believable proportions.

steps.action: **Draw ears and brows.** Put ears between the eye line and nose line, then add eyebrows above the eyes.
steps.expect: side features align with the central features.

steps.action: **Add hair as a shape.** Draw the hairline and outer hair mass before individual strands.
steps.expect: the hairstyle reads as one clear silhouette.

steps.action: **Darken selected lines.** Strengthen the eyes, nostrils, mouth line, jaw, and hair edges while leaving construction lines light.
steps.expect: the face reads clearly without every guide becoming permanent.

recipes.verification: The drawing shows a recognizable front-facing face with eyes near the halfway line, nose and mouth placed below, ears aligned, and hair attached as a coherent shape.

recipes.title: edit a photo on your phone
recipes.name: edit-a-photo-on-your-phone
recipes.goal: Turn a phone photo into a cleaner finished image using crop, exposure, color, and sharpening adjustments.

steps.action: **Duplicate the photo.** Make a copy before editing if your app allows it.
steps.expect: the original image remains available.

steps.action: **Straighten and crop.** Level obvious horizons, then crop out weak edges without cutting important details.
steps.expect: the subject feels intentionally placed in the frame.

steps.action: **Correct brightness.** Raise exposure if the image is dull or lower highlights if bright areas lack detail.
steps.expect: important parts of the photo are readable without washed-out whites.

steps.action: **Tune contrast gently.** Add a small amount of contrast or black point until the image has shape.
steps.expect: the photo looks clearer without crushed shadows.

steps.action: **Adjust color.** Warm or cool the white balance until skin, paper, or neutral walls look believable.
steps.expect: colors look natural or intentionally stylized.

steps.action: **Add restrained detail.** Apply light sharpening or structure and avoid heavy clarity on faces.
steps.expect: edges look crisp at normal viewing size without gritty texture.

steps.action: **Compare before and after.** Toggle the original view and reduce any adjustment that calls attention to itself.
steps.expect: the edited version improves the photo while still looking credible.

steps.action: **Save or export.** Save a copy at full quality if the app offers that option.
steps.expect: the finished edit appears in the photo library and can be shared.

recipes.verification: The final saved image is level, intentionally cropped, naturally colored or deliberately styled, and visibly improved when compared with the original.

recipes.title: edit a video on your phone
recipes.name: edit-a-video-on-your-phone
recipes.goal: Edit phone video clips into a short finished sequence with clean trimming, logical order, readable sound, and an exported file.

steps.action: **Create a new project.** Import only the clips that support the short video.
steps.expect: the timeline contains usable source clips in one project.

steps.action: **Order the story.** Place context first, action next, and result or reaction last.
steps.expect: the sequence makes sense even before fine trimming.

steps.action: **Trim dead time.** Cut shaky starts, long pauses, and accidental endings from each clip.
steps.expect: each shot begins with purpose and ends before it drags.

steps.action: **Use cutaways.** Place close-up details over jumps or repeated action.
steps.expect: edits feel smoother and the viewer sees useful details.

steps.action: **Balance sound.** Lower music under speech and remove clips with distracting noise if possible.
steps.expect: speech or main sound is understandable.

steps.action: **Add minimal text if needed.** Use short title or label text only where it clarifies the video.
steps.expect: text is readable and does not cover important action.

steps.action: **Watch full-screen once.** Play the whole edit without stopping and note only obvious problems.
steps.expect: pacing, orientation, sound, and text can be judged as a viewer.

steps.action: **Export the final video.** Save at the same orientation and a standard quality setting.
steps.expect: a playable finished video appears in the photo library or files app.

recipes.verification: The exported video plays from start to finish, follows a clear order, has trimmed clips without obvious accidents, and keeps important sound understandable.

recipes.title: finger knit
recipes.name: finger-knit
recipes.goal: Make a simple knitted cord using fingers instead of needles, then bind it off so it does not unravel.

steps.action: **Anchor the tail.** Hold the yarn tail between thumb and palm, leaving about 15 cm free.
steps.expect: the tail stays trapped while the working yarn can move.

steps.action: **Cast on across the fingers.** Weave the working yarn over and under four fingers from index to pinky, then back again.
steps.expect: each finger has one loop sitting near the base.

steps.action: **Make a second row of loops.** Weave across the fingers again above the first row.
steps.expect: each finger has two loops, a lower loop and an upper loop.

steps.action: **Pull over the index loop.** Lift the lower index-finger loop over the upper loop and off the fingertip.
steps.expect: one loop remains on the index finger.

steps.action: **Pull over the remaining fingers.** Repeat the lower-over-upper move on middle, ring, and pinky fingers.
steps.expect: one loop remains on each finger and a cord starts forming behind the hand.

steps.action: **Push loops down.** Slide the remaining loops back toward the base of the fingers without tightening hard.
steps.expect: there is room to weave the next row.

steps.action: **Repeat rows.** Weave a new upper row, then pull each lower loop over again.
steps.expect: the cord grows from the back of the hand.

steps.action: **Keep tension relaxed.** Tug the finished cord gently after every few rows, not the live loops.
steps.expect: stitches look even and fingers do not feel squeezed.

steps.action: **Bind off.** Move the pinky loop to the ring finger, pull the lower ring loop over, then continue moving loops toward the index finger.
steps.expect: one final loop remains.

steps.action: **Secure the final loop.** Cut the yarn with a tail, pass the tail through the final loop, and snug it. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cutting yarn fixes the finished length, so confirm the cord is long enough first.
steps.expect: the cord stays intact when lightly stretched.

recipes.verification: The finished cord has a secured beginning and end, and it does not unravel when lightly pulled.

recipes.title: float on your back
recipes.name: float-on-your-back
recipes.goal: You can settle into a calm back float in shallow supervised water, breathe normally, and recover to standing without panic.

steps.action: **Choose the safe practice spot.** Stand in chest-deep or shallower pool water near the wall, with your supervisor beside you.
steps.expect: you can stand instantly and hold the wall without swimming.

steps.action: **Fill the lungs gently.** Take a comfortable breath in, keep the chest broad, and avoid forcing a giant inhale. Full lungs add buoyancy.
steps.expect: your upper body feels lifted before you lean back.

steps.action: **Let the head go back.** Bend knees, lean back, put ears in the water, and look at the ceiling or sky. The face can stay above water while the ears submerge.
steps.expect: the water supports the back of your head instead of your neck straining.

steps.action: **Open the body shape.** Let hips rise, spread arms slightly, and let legs drift long. [BRANCH: legs sink | body rises] If legs sink, do not kick hard; press the chest slightly upward and relax the knees.
steps.expect: your torso floats first and your legs become lighter.

steps.action: **Scull with quiet hands.** Move hands in small figure-eights beside your hips, palms angled like tiny wings.
steps.expect: gentle pressure on the palms keeps you level without splashing.

steps.action: **Breathe on purpose.** Inhale calmly, exhale slowly, and notice that the body sinks a little on exhale and rises on inhale.
steps.expect: floating feels adjustable rather than fragile.

steps.action: **Practice panic recovery.** Tuck the chin, bring knees toward the chest, sweep hands downward, and put both feet on the bottom.
steps.expect: you can return to standing in one controlled motion.

steps.action: **Repeat shorter floats.** Float for 3 seconds, stand, then 5 seconds, then 10 seconds, always ending before panic takes over.
steps.expect: each repetition ends by choice, not surprise.

recipes.verification: In shallow supervised water, you float on your back for 10 seconds, breathe during it, and recover to standing calmly.

recipes.title: fly a kite
recipes.name: fly-a-kite
recipes.goal: A kite launched without a running start, flown stable at altitude, and landed gently, in a spot chosen so the only thing it can hit is grass.

steps.action: **Read the wind and take your position.** Feel the direction (grass throws, flag checks), then stand with your *back* to the wind; the kite launches downwind of you.
steps.expect: wind on the back of your neck, open space downwind for twice your intended line length.

steps.action: **Assemble and preflight the kite.** Spars seated, bridle untangled, line tied to the bridle point (not a spar), tail attached if the kite has one.
steps.expect: a taut sail, symmetric frame, line running clean off the spool.

steps.action: **Launch from the hand, no running.** Hold the kite up by its bottom edge at arm's length (or have a helper hold it 10 to 20 meters downwind), wait for a gust, release as you pull the line firmly. Running launches teach nothing except falling.
steps.expect: the kite climbing away on the gust as you pull; pumping the line (pull-release-pull) gains altitude in light wind.

steps.action: **Feed line to climb, tension to steer.** Let line out smoothly while the kite pulls; stop feeding when it sits at a stable angle. Pull in to make it climb and gain authority; ease out to descend.
steps.expect: the kite parked in steady wind above the turbulent ground layer, tugging gently, needing only occasional corrections.

steps.action: **Handle trouble by line, not by hope.** Dives and loops: give slack the moment it noses over (slack kills its speed), then re-tension as it settles. Persistent circling: add or lengthen the tail (stability) or the wind is too strong for this kite.
steps.expect: recoveries becoming reflexive; the dive-slack response is the whole pilot's license.

steps.action: **Land deliberately.** Walk toward the kite while winding, or hand-over-hand the line down; in stronger wind, walk the line down with a helper collecting the kite before it can drag. Wind the line properly on the spool as you go — future-you inherits either a spool or a nest.
steps.expect: kite down flat and undamaged, line fully wound, site clear.

recipes.verification: Launched from the hand, flew stable above the ground layer with dive-recovery demonstrated at least once, landed on grass with the line wound on the spool, and the whole session stayed the mandated distance from wires, roads, and trees.

recipes.title: fold a paper fan
recipes.name: fold-a-paper-fan
recipes.goal: You can fold a sheet of paper into even accordion pleats, secure the base, and open it into a handheld fan.

steps.action: **Place the paper landscape.** Lay the long edge left to right so the finished fan has width.
steps.expect: the sheet is oriented wider than tall.

steps.action: **Fold the first pleat.** Fold one short edge over by about 1 to 2 cm and crease firmly.
steps.expect: the first strip sets the pleat width.

steps.action: **Flip and repeat.** Turn the paper over, fold the same width back the other way, and crease.
steps.expect: an accordion pattern begins.

steps.action: **Keep widths even.** Continue flipping and folding, using the previous pleat as a guide. [BRANCH: exact pleats | relaxed pleats] Exact looks crisp; relaxed still works if widths stay close.
steps.expect: a stacked strip with alternating folds.

steps.action: **Compress the pleats.** Run a fingernail or ruler along the stack to sharpen all creases.
steps.expect: the strip springs open slightly but keeps its folds.

steps.action: **Fold the base.** Pinch one end of the strip together and fold the bottom 2 to 3 cm upward to make a handle area.
steps.expect: one end becomes a firm grip.

steps.action: **Secure the base.** Tape, tie, band, or staple the folded base. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* stapling makes holes, so confirm the handle end before pressing.
steps.expect: the base stays closed when released.

steps.action: **Open the fan.** Spread the free end into a semicircle and adjust pleats until the shape looks even.
steps.expect: the fan moves air when waved gently.

recipes.verification: The fan opens into a stable semicircle, stays secured at the base, and moves noticeable air when waved.

recipes.title: fold an origami crane
recipes.name: fold-an-origami-crane
recipes.goal: A square sheet of paper is folded into a classic origami crane using disciplined creases, a square base, and a bird base.

steps.action: **Start color side down.** Place the square like a diamond if using colored paper.
steps.expect: the finished color will show outside.

steps.action: **Fold both diagonals.** Fold corner to corner both ways, creasing sharply, then unfold.
steps.expect: an X crease crosses the center.

steps.action: **Fold both book folds.** Fold edge to edge horizontally and vertically, then unfold.
steps.expect: a plus crease crosses the center.

steps.action: **Collapse the square base.** Bring opposite corners together along the existing creases and flatten into a smaller diamond.
steps.expect: open flaps point downward and the closed corner points upward.

steps.action: **Make kite folds.** Fold the lower left and right edges of the top layer to the center line.
steps.expect: the top layer forms a narrow kite.

steps.action: **Crease the top triangle.** Fold the upper triangle down over the kite folds, crease, then unfold all three folds.
steps.expect: a clear horizontal crease caps the kite.

steps.action: **Petal fold upward.** Lift the bottom top layer and fold it upward while the sides collapse inward.
steps.expect: a long diamond forms cleanly without wrinkles.

steps.action: **Repeat on the back.** Turn the model over and repeat the kite folds, top crease, and petal fold.
steps.expect: the bird base has two long points below and two broad flaps above.

steps.action: **Narrow the legs.** Fold lower outside edges to the center on both front and back.
steps.expect: the two lower points become slim.

steps.action: **Form neck and tail.** Inside-reverse-fold each lower point upward, then inside-reverse-fold a small head on one side.
steps.expect: the crane has a neck, head, and tail.

steps.action: **Fold wings down.** Fold each broad flap downward from the top body line.
steps.expect: wings sit even on both sides.

steps.action: **Open the body.** Hold the wings and pull gently apart, then puff the body from below.
steps.expect: the crane stands with a hollow body and balanced wings.

recipes.verification: The model has a recognizable crane shape with head, tail, two wings, and a puffed body that holds together without tape.

recipes.title: grow an avocado pit
recipes.name: grow-an-avocado-pit
recipes.goal: An avocado pit is started in water, rooted with patience, and moved to soil once it has enough growth to behave like a houseplant.

steps.action: **Find top and bottom.** The pointy end goes up, and the flatter wider end goes down. [BRANCH: obvious point | round pit] if unsure, put the slightly broader end in water.
steps.expect: the pit has an assigned sky side and water side.

steps.action: **Insert toothpicks.** Push three toothpicks around the middle at a slight downward angle.
steps.expect: the pit can rest on a glass rim without falling in.

steps.action: **Suspend over water.** Fill the glass so the bottom third of the pit sits in water.
steps.expect: the lower end is wet and the upper end is dry.

steps.action: **Place in bright indirect light.** Set the glass where it is warm but not baking.
steps.expect: the water stays visible and the pit is not hot to the touch.

steps.action: **Refresh the water.** Change water every few days and top it up between changes.
steps.expect: the submerged end stays wet and the glass does not smell.

steps.action: **Wait for splitting and roots.** Give it 2 to 8 weeks without declaring failure too early.
steps.expect: the pit cracks, then a root appears from the bottom.

steps.action: **Pot when ready.** Once roots are several centimeters long and a shoot has leaves, plant the pit halfway above soil. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* breaking the main root sets the plant back badly, so handle it by the pit, not the root.
steps.expect: roots are covered and the top half of the pit remains visible.

steps.action: **Set expectations.** Keep soil lightly moist and treat fruit as unlikely indoors.
steps.expect: the plant is a leafy experiment, not a guaranteed guacamole farm.

recipes.verification: The potted pit has a visible shoot, intact roots under soil, and new leaves that remain firm for one week.

recipes.title: grow sugar or salt crystals
recipes.name: grow-sugar-or-salt-crystals
recipes.goal: Grow visible sugar or salt crystals from a supersaturated solution on a seed string over several days.

steps.action: **Prepare the seed.** Tie string to a pencil so the string hangs into the jar without touching the bottom.
steps.expect: the string hangs straight in the center.

steps.action: **Make hot water safe.** Have an adult heat water until hot but not dangerously splashing.
steps.expect: the water can dissolve extra solid.

steps.action: **Add solid gradually.** Stir in sugar or salt until no more dissolves and a few grains remain.
steps.expect: the liquid is supersaturated or close to it.

steps.action: **Cool briefly.** Let the solution stop steaming before it goes into the jar.
steps.expect: the jar is warm, not scalding.

steps.action: **Pour and suspend.** Pour the solution into the jar and lay the pencil across the top with the string hanging in.
steps.expect: the string is covered by liquid.

steps.action: **Leave it alone.** Place the jar where it will not be bumped.
steps.expect: evaporation begins slowly.

steps.action: **Check daily.** [BRANCH: crystals forming | no crystals] observe growth if present, or wait another day before changing anything.
steps.expect: small facets appear on the string or jar.

steps.action: **Reveal the crystals.** Lift the string after several days when crystals are large enough to see.
steps.expect: solid crystals cling to the string.

steps.action: **Clean the jar.** Save crystals on paper and dissolve leftover crust with warm water.
steps.expect: the jar is clean and the workspace is dry.

recipes.verification: Visible crystals form on the seed string or jar, and all hot-water equipment is cleaned and put away.

recipes.title: have a picnic
recipes.name: have-a-picnic
recipes.goal: A group has eaten a comfortable outdoor meal at a chosen site and left the spot exactly as found: no trash, no food scraps, no damage.

steps.action: **Pack in reverse order of use.** Blanket on top (first thing out), then plates and drinks, food at the bottom; cold items together against an ice pack. Liquids upright and double-checked for sealed lids.
steps.expect: nothing leaking when the bag is tilted; blanket accessible without unpacking.

steps.action: **Choose the exact spot on arrival.** Look for level ground, partial shade, no ant trails or ground-wasp holes, and reasonable distance from paths, trash bins (wasps), and ponds (mosquitoes). Under a tree beats open sun for food longevity.
steps.expect: a flat, dry, shaded patch with no insect traffic across it.

steps.action: **Lay the blanket and weight the corners.** Waterproof side down; corners held by shoes, the cooler, or bags against gusts.
steps.expect: blanket flat and staying put in the wind.

steps.action: **Set out food in stages, not all at once.** Keep the cooler closed between rounds; put out what will be eaten in the next 20 minutes. Keep lids on or cloths over open dishes.
steps.expect: food stays cool and mostly covered; flies and wasps have no open target.

steps.action: **Eat, with one running rule: trash into the bag immediately.** A dedicated open trash bag from minute one prevents the end-of-picnic scatter hunt. Wind-prone wrappers go straight in.
steps.expect: no loose wrappers on or off the blanket at any point.

steps.action: **Manage sun and time on perishables.** Move the blanket if shade shifts. Perishables out of the cooler for over 2 hours (1 hour above 32 °C) get eaten now or thrown out, not repacked. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* food poisoning from repacked warm perishables; when in doubt, throw it out.
steps.expect: nothing marginal goes back in the cooler.

steps.action: **Break camp with a line sweep.** Pack food first, then shake the blanket downwind away from people, then walk the whole area in a slow pass looking for caps, corks, toys, and micro-trash. Crumbs and food scraps go in the trash bag too: "biodegradable" scraps feed pests and are still littering.
steps.expect: the ground shows no trace the group was there.

steps.action: **Carry trash out unless a proper bin exists.** [BRANCH: park bin present and not overflowing (use it) | bin absent or full (the bag rides home with you)]
steps.expect: sealed trash bag disposed of correctly; hands cleaned.

recipes.verification: Everyone has eaten; the departure sweep found nothing left on the site (including crumbs, caps, and peels); all trash is in a sealed bag in a proper bin or in your possession; the blanket and kit are packed and drier than the ground you left.

recipes.title: hula hoop
recipes.name: hula-hoop
