recipes.goal: A beginner keeps a hula hoop spinning around the waist by choosing a workable hoop size and using rhythmic weight shifts.

steps.action: **Choose a beginner-friendly hoop.** Pick a larger, slightly heavier hoop rather than a tiny toy hoop.
steps.expect: hoop reaches at least the navel when vertical.

steps.action: **Stand inside the hoop.** Hold it against the small of the back with both hands.
steps.expect: hoop is level around the waist.

steps.action: **Set the feet.** Place one foot slightly ahead of the other, knees soft.
steps.expect: body can shift forward and back without leaning.

steps.action: **Start with a flat push.** Push the hoop around the waist strongly and level, not upward.
steps.expect: hoop makes one clean rotation before dropping.

steps.action: **Move with a push, not a circle.** Shift weight forward and back, bumping the hoop each time it touches the belly or back.
steps.expect: hoop speeds up from repeated pulses.

steps.action: **Keep the torso tall.** Look forward and keep shoulders relaxed.
steps.expect: hips move under a steady upper body.

steps.action: **Correct dropping early.** If the hoop slides down, bend knees slightly and pulse faster.
steps.expect: hoop climbs or stabilizes before it reaches the thighs.

steps.action: **Restart efficiently.** When it falls, catch it, reset at the back, and push in the easier direction.
steps.expect: restarts take seconds instead of breaking rhythm.

steps.action: **Practice both directions.** Try clockwise and counterclockwise starts after finding the easier side.
steps.expect: one direction feels natural and the other improves slowly.

steps.action: **Stop with control.** Slow the pulses and catch the hoop with a hand.
steps.expect: hoop stops without hitting nearby objects.

recipes.verification: The hoop completes several waist rotations while the player maintains balance, uses weight shifts, and can catch or restart it safely.

recipes.title: inflate an air mattress
recipes.name: inflate-an-air-mattress
recipes.goal: Inflate an air mattress to comfortable firmness without over-inflating it, then deflate and store it without stressing the valve or seams.

steps.action: **Clear the surface.** Sweep or feel the ground and remove anything sharp before unrolling the mattress.
steps.expect: the mattress rests on a clean, smooth area.

steps.action: **Find the valve.** Open the inflation valve and check whether it has a one-way flap, screw cap, or separate deflation port.
steps.expect: you know which opening takes air in and which releases it.

steps.action: **Attach the pump.** [BRANCH: built-in | external | manual] Turn on the built-in pump, connect an external pump nozzle, or use a hand or foot pump that fits snugly.
steps.expect: air enters without loud leaks around the nozzle.

steps.action: **Inflate gradually.** Add air until the mattress rises and feels supportive but still yields slightly under a hand. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* over-pressure can split seams, so do not keep pumping after the mattress is drum-tight.
steps.expect: the surface is firm, not rock hard.

steps.action: **Cap the valve.** Remove the pump while pinching or closing the valve, then seal the cap firmly.
steps.expect: no hiss continues after the valve is closed.

steps.action: **Top up after settling.** Lie on it for a minute, wait several minutes, and add a small amount of air only if hips or shoulders bottom out.
steps.expect: the mattress feels stable under body weight.

steps.action: **Deflate and store.** Open the deflation valve, press air out gently, fold without sharp creases at the valve, and store dry.
steps.expect: the mattress is flat, dry, capped, and ready for its bag or shelf.

recipes.verification: The mattress is verified when it supports body weight comfortably, the sealed valve is quiet, and the surface is not over-tight.

recipes.title: juggle a soccer ball
recipes.name: juggle-a-soccer-ball
recipes.goal: You can keep a soccer ball in the air for a short streak using controlled laces touches, then build toward alternating feet.

steps.action: **Pick a soft target area.** Stand on grass, turf, or a court with room for bad rebounds.
steps.expect: missed balls roll harmlessly instead of hitting fragile things.

steps.action: **Find the laces surface.** Point the toe slightly down and lock the ankle so the broad top of the foot meets the lower half of the ball.
steps.expect: your foot feels like a small flat paddle.

steps.action: **Start with a bounce.** Drop the ball, let it bounce once, then tap it upward with the laces to waist height. Catch it.
steps.expect: one clean upward touch you can repeat.

steps.action: **Repeat single touches.** Drop, bounce, touch, catch for 20 reps on the stronger foot, then 20 on the other foot.
steps.expect: the ball rises mostly vertical instead of shooting forward.

steps.action: **Add two touches after one bounce.** Bounce, touch, let the ball fall, touch again, then catch. [BRANCH: same foot | alternate feet] Use the same foot for control or alternate to train symmetry.
steps.expect: two intentional contacts before the catch.

steps.action: **Remove the catch gradually.** Let the ball bounce between touches, then reduce the bounce height until the next touch happens before the ground.
steps.expect: the ball spends more time in the air than on the floor.

steps.action: **Count the streak.** Count only laces touches that keep the ball below chest height and within one step. Reset after a wild chase.
steps.expect: a meaningful record, not a lucky ricochet.

steps.action: **Train the weak foot early.** Finish each session with five attempts starting on the weaker foot.
steps.expect: progress feels uneven but the ball stops avoiding one side.

recipes.verification: You complete five controlled juggles in a row, each below chest height and within one step of your starting spot.

recipes.title: juggle three balls
recipes.name: juggle-three-balls
recipes.goal: You can run a three-ball cascade for at least 10 consecutive catches, built from a stable one-ball arc and a clean two-ball exchange.

steps.action: **Set your stance and frame.** Feet shoulder-width, elbows at your sides bent 90°, hands at waist height, palms up. Throws come from waist height; catches return there. Eyes fixed at the peak height, not on your hands.
steps.expect: hands stay in a "tray" plane at your waist; you can see both hands with peripheral vision while looking at eye level.

steps.action: **Drill the one-ball arc (10-15 min).** Throw from one hand to the other in an arc peaking at eye level, crossing your midline. Same height every time, no hand movement to rescue bad throws: let bad ones drop.
steps.expect: 20 consecutive throws landing in the waiting palm without the catching hand chasing; equal quality both directions.

steps.action: **Drill the two-ball exchange (this is the real gatekeeper, often 1-2 sessions).** One ball in each hand. Throw ball A; when A peaks, throw B from the other hand under it; catch A, catch B. Say "throw, throw, catch, catch" out loud.
steps.expect: two distinct throws and two distinct catches, both balls tracing arcs. The classic failure is handing B across instead of throwing it: if B never rises to eye level, you are passing, not juggling.

steps.action: **Mirror the exchange.** Repeat step 3 starting from the other hand until both sides are equal. Almost everyone has a reluctant hand; it gets extra reps.
steps.expect: 10 clean exchanges starting left and 10 starting right.

steps.action: **Add the third ball: the flash.** Two balls in your dominant hand, one in the other. Throw 1 (front ball of the pair), then 2 when 1 peaks, then 3 when 2 peaks; catch all three and stop deliberately.
steps.expect: three throws, three catches, then stillness. Stopping on purpose is the drill; do not chase a fourth throw yet.

steps.action: **Extend the cascade.** Same pattern, keep throwing: every ball is thrown when the incoming ball peaks, always thrown under the incoming arc, always to the same eye-level height. Count catches out loud.
steps.expect: runs lengthening over sessions: 4, then 7, then 10+ catches. Rhythm should sound even, like a slow clock.

steps.action: **Fix forward drift.** [BRANCH: pattern creeps forward and you chase it (throws are slightly outward: practice facing a wall an arm's length away, or juggle over a bed) | pattern stays in plane (continue)]
steps.expect: your feet do not move during a 10-catch run.

recipes.verification: Standing on a mark, you complete a three-ball cascade of at least 10 catches without stepping off the mark, and you can start the pattern from either hand.

recipes.title: knit a scarf
recipes.name: knit-a-scarf
recipes.goal: Knit a simple garter-stitch scarf with even edges, consistent tension, and secured ends.

steps.action: **Cast on the width.** Cast on 18 to 30 stitches depending on yarn thickness and desired scarf width.
steps.expect: the needle holds a flexible row of loops.

steps.action: **Knit the first row.** Insert, wrap, pull through, and slide off each stitch across the row.
steps.expect: all stitches move to the other needle without dropping.

steps.action: **Turn and repeat.** Turn the work and knit every stitch again for garter stitch.
steps.expect: ridges begin forming on both sides of the fabric.

steps.action: **Check edge tension.** Keep the first and last stitch snug but not tight on each row.
steps.expect: the scarf edges stay straight enough to follow.

steps.action: **Measure as you go.** Lay the scarf flat after several inches and check width and length.
steps.expect: the fabric grows evenly without narrowing or widening.

steps.action: **Bind off loosely.** Knit two stitches, pass the first over the second, and repeat across the row.
steps.expect: the final edge is secure and not cinched tight.

steps.action: **Weave in ends.** Thread yarn tails through nearby stitches on the back and trim after a gentle tug.
steps.expect: tails disappear and the scarf does not unravel.

recipes.verification: The scarf is one continuous knitted rectangle with stable stitch count, secure cast-on and bind-off edges, and woven-in ends that stay put after a gentle tug.

recipes.title: learn chess basics
recipes.name: learn-chess-basics
recipes.goal: Set up a chessboard, make legal beginner moves, and understand check, checkmate, castling, and a first opening idea.

steps.action: **Orient the board.** Put a light square in each player's right-hand corner.
steps.expect: "white on right" is true for both players.

steps.action: **Place the pieces.** Put rooks in corners, then knights, bishops, queen on her color, king on the remaining center square, and pawns in front.
steps.expect: both armies mirror each other.

steps.action: **Move pawns.** Move a pawn one square forward, or two from its starting square if both squares are clear.
steps.expect: pawns move straight but capture one square diagonally.

steps.action: **Move the pieces.** Practice rook straight lines, bishop diagonals, queen both, knight L-shapes, and king one square.
steps.expect: each piece follows its own movement pattern.

steps.action: **Respect occupied squares.** Do not move through pieces except with knights, and capture only enemy pieces.
steps.expect: blocked lines stop sliding pieces.

steps.action: **Identify check.** Attack the enemy king and say "check" in practice games.
steps.expect: the checked side must answer the threat.

steps.action: **Escape check.** [BRANCH: move king | block | capture attacker] choose one legal escape.
steps.expect: the king is no longer attacked.

steps.action: **Learn castling.** Move the king two squares toward an unmoved rook, then place that rook beside the king, only if the path and king are safe.
steps.expect: king safety improves in one special move.

steps.action: **Try a first opening idea.** Move a center pawn, develop a knight or bishop, and aim to castle early.
steps.expect: pieces leave the back rank and the king gets safer.

recipes.verification: The learner can set up the board correctly, describe each piece move, and identify a simple checkmate position.

recipes.title: learn four useful knots
recipes.name: learn-four-useful-knots
recipes.goal: Learn four useful knots by purpose: overhand stopper, square knot for light joining, bowline fixed loop, and two half-hitches for tying to a post.

steps.action: **Tie the overhand knot.** Make a loop, pass the working end through it, and pull both sides to make a simple stopper.
steps.expect: one small knot sits near the rope end and is hard to pull through a narrow gap.

steps.action: **Untie and repeat the overhand.** Tie it three more times, each time leaving a longer or shorter tail on purpose.
steps.expect: you can control where the stopper lands.

steps.action: **Tie the square knot.** Cross right over left and tuck, then left over right and tuck, then dress the knot flat.
steps.expect: the two tails lie beside their matching standing parts.

steps.action: **Tie the bowline.** Make the rabbit hole, bring the working end up through it, around the standing part, and back down.
steps.expect: a fixed loop holds its size when pulled by hand.

steps.action: **Tie two half-hitches.** Wrap the rope around a post, make one half-hitch around the standing part, then repeat with a second half-hitch.
steps.expect: the rope grips the post and the two hitches sit neatly beside each other.

steps.action: **Match knot to job.** [BRANCH: stopper | join | fixed-loop | post-tie] Choose overhand for a stopper, square for light same-rope joining, bowline for a fixed loop, or two half-hitches for a post.
steps.expect: each knot is chosen for a clear purpose.

steps.action: **Practice the set.** Tie all four knots in order, inspect them, untie them, and repeat twice more.
steps.expect: the shapes become familiar without needing to force them.

recipes.verification: The practice set is verified when you can tie, name, inspect, and correctly assign a use to all four knots without looking up the steps.

recipes.title: learn morse code basics
recipes.name: learn-morse-code-basics
recipes.goal: You can recognize and send a few basic Morse code letters, including SOS, using clear dot, dash, letter, and word timing.

steps.action: **Learn the timing unit.** Treat a dot as one beat, a dash as three beats, the gap inside a letter as one beat, between letters as three beats, and between words as seven beats.
steps.expect: the rhythm feels measured instead of random.

steps.action: **Send E and T.** Practice E as one dot and T as one dash, tapping or flashing each ten times.
steps.expect: you can make the shortest contrast cleanly.

steps.action: **Add common letters.** Learn A dot-dash, N dash-dot, I dot-dot, M dash-dash, S dot-dot-dot, and O dash-dash-dash.
steps.expect: short words become possible.

steps.action: **Practice SOS.** Send S O S as three dots, three dashes, three dots, with letter gaps between them.
steps.expect: the pattern is recognizable and evenly spaced.

steps.action: **Tap tiny words.** Try "me," "to," "tea," "no," and "sit" using the chart only when stuck.
steps.expect: you hear letters as whole shapes, not counted parts.

steps.action: **Receive before speed.** Have a partner tap one learned letter at a time, or record yourself and play it back. [BRANCH: you recognize it | you count every mark] If counting dominates, slow down and repeat fewer letters.
steps.expect: at least E, T, A, N, S, and O are recognized by sound or flash.

steps.action: **Build practice words.** Mix learned letters into five short words per session, sending slowly with clean spacing.
steps.expect: timing improves more than raw speed.

recipes.verification: You correctly send SOS and recognize at least six learned letters when they are tapped, flashed, or spoken slowly.

recipes.title: learn three guitar chords
recipes.name: learn-three-guitar-chords
recipes.goal: Play three beginner guitar chords cleanly enough to strum a simple progression.

steps.action: **Hold the guitar steady.** Rest the body against you and keep the neck angled slightly upward.
steps.expect: the guitar stays still without the fretting hand gripping it for support.

steps.action: **Form G major.** Place fingers for an open G chord and press just behind the frets.
steps.expect: each string rings or the muted strings match your chord chart.

steps.action: **Check G one string at a time.** Pick from low to high and adjust buzzing or muted notes.
steps.expect: the chord sounds clear across the intended strings.

steps.action: **Form C major.** Move to open C and curve fingertips so they do not touch neighboring strings.
steps.expect: the five intended strings ring with a warm, stable sound.

steps.action: **Form D major.** Move to open D and strum only the top four strings.
steps.expect: the chord sounds bright and avoids the low strings.

steps.action: **Practice slow changes.** Move G to C to D to G, pausing until fingers land together.
steps.expect: each change gets smoother without rushing.

steps.action: **Strum a pattern.** Use four slow downstrokes per chord and count evenly.
steps.expect: the progression stays in time and the chord names match your hand shapes.

recipes.verification: You can play G, C, and D in sequence with four steady strums each, and every chord is recognizable without stopping the rhythm.

recipes.title: make a baking soda volcano
recipes.name: make-a-baking-soda-volcano
recipes.goal: Build a small model volcano and create a foamy eruption using baking soda, dish soap, food color, and vinegar.

steps.action: **Protect the area.** Put the cup or bottle on a tray and keep towels nearby.
steps.expect: spills stay contained.

steps.action: **Build the cone.** Shape paper, clay, or foil around the container without covering the opening.
steps.expect: the model looks like a volcano with a clear crater.

steps.action: **Add baking soda.** Spoon two or three tablespoons of baking soda into the crater.
steps.expect: white powder sits at the bottom.

steps.action: **Add soap and color.** Add a small squirt of dish soap and a few drops of food coloring.
steps.expect: the crater holds a thick, colored mixture.

steps.action: **Predict the reaction.** Ask what will happen when acid vinegar meets base baking soda.
steps.expect: players expect gas bubbles and foam.

steps.action: **Pour vinegar slowly.** Add vinegar a little at a time.
steps.expect: foam rises and flows down the cone.

steps.action: **Repeat with changes.** [BRANCH: more foam | slower flow] add more soap for foam, or pour less vinegar for control.
steps.expect: the eruption changes in visible ways.

steps.action: **Explain the gas.** Point out that carbon dioxide bubbles push the soapy liquid upward.
steps.expect: the eruption connects to a concrete chemistry idea.

steps.action: **Clean up fully.** Rinse the tray and throw away soggy paper after the reaction stops.
steps.expect: the workspace is dry and not sticky.

recipes.verification: The volcano produces visible foam from the crater and the tray, tools, and hands are cleaned afterward.

recipes.title: make a basic balloon animal
recipes.name: make-a-basic-balloon-animal
recipes.goal: A long twisting balloon is inflated and twisted into a basic dog with head, ears, legs, body, and tail.

steps.action: **Inflate with a tail.** Pump the balloon, leaving 3 to 4 inches uninflated at the end.
steps.expect: air has space to move during twisting.

steps.action: **Tie the nozzle.** Pinch the neck, tie a simple knot, and squeeze the balloon gently to soften pressure.
steps.expect: balloon is sealed and slightly flexible.

steps.action: **Twist the snout.** Make a 2-inch bubble at the knotted end.
steps.expect: the bubble holds when pinched.

steps.action: **Make ears.** Twist two more 2-inch bubbles, then fold them together and twist-lock at the base.
steps.expect: snout points forward and two ears sit above it.

steps.action: **Make neck and front legs.** Twist a short neck bubble, then two equal leg bubbles, fold the legs together, and twist-lock.
steps.expect: front legs hang below the neck.

steps.action: **Make body and back legs.** Twist a body bubble, then two equal back-leg bubbles, fold and twist-lock them.
steps.expect: dog stands with four legs.

steps.action: **Leave the tail.** Let the remaining uninflated end act as the tail.
steps.expect: tail has some soft uninflated balloon at the tip.

steps.action: **Adjust gently.** Bend legs and ears into place without squeezing hard.
steps.expect: the dog shape is recognizable and not overpressurized.

recipes.verification: The finished balloon has a snout, two ears, four legs, a body, and a soft tail, and it stays twisted for at least 30 seconds.

recipes.title: make a bird feeder
recipes.name: make-a-bird-feeder
recipes.goal: Make a simple bird feeder from a bottle or pine cone, place it safely, and keep it clean for visiting birds.

steps.action: **Choose the base.** [BRANCH: bottle | pine cone] use a clean bottle for a refillable feeder, or a pine cone for a simple coated feeder.
steps.expect: the feeder body is dry and ready.

steps.action: **Add access.** For a bottle, have an adult cut small seed openings; for a pine cone, spread binder into the gaps.
steps.expect: birds can reach food without sharp edges.

steps.action: **Make a perch.** Push a pencil, dowel, or sturdy twig through the bottle below openings, or tie string to the pine cone top.
steps.expect: birds have a place to land or cling.

steps.action: **Fill with seed.** Pour seed into the bottle or roll the coated pine cone in seed.
steps.expect: food is held by the feeder.

steps.action: **Check for hazards.** Smooth sharp plastic, trim loose strings, and avoid sticky globs birds could step in.
steps.expect: the feeder has no obvious snags.

steps.action: **Hang it high.** Place it where birds can see it, near cover but away from cat jumping paths.
steps.expect: the feeder hangs steady and out of easy predator reach.

steps.action: **Watch from a distance.** Observe quietly for several days.
steps.expect: birds visit once they find the food.

steps.action: **Clean regularly.** Empty old seed, wash the feeder, and let it dry before refilling.
steps.expect: mold and droppings do not build up.

steps.action: **Remove if unsafe.** Take it down during mold, disease alerts, or repeated predator stalking.
steps.expect: feeding stops until conditions are safe.

recipes.verification: The feeder hangs securely, stays clean, contains bird-safe food, and is placed where cats cannot easily reach visiting birds.

recipes.title: make a cats cradle
recipes.name: make-a-cats-cradle
recipes.goal: A loop of string is arranged into the opening cat's cradle figure and passed between partners without dropping the pattern.

steps.action: **Set the loop.** Place the string around both hands, behind the thumbs and little fingers.
steps.expect: one strand crosses each palm.

steps.action: **Make the first palm pickup.** Use the right middle finger to pick up the left palm strand from below.
steps.expect: a diagonal strand runs to the right middle finger.

steps.action: **Make the second palm pickup.** Use the left middle finger to pick up the right palm strand from below.
steps.expect: a symmetrical woven X appears between the hands.

steps.action: **Open the cradle.** Spread fingers gently without pulling too tight.
steps.expect: the classic cat's cradle shape sits in the center.

steps.action: **Show the transfer points.** Partner identifies the two crossed X points near the middle.
steps.expect: both players agree which strands will be pinched.

steps.action: **Pinch and lift.** Partner pinches the X points from above, pulls them outward, then dips under the side strings.
steps.expect: string begins moving onto the partner's hands.

steps.action: **Release at the right time.** First player lets go only after the partner's fingers hold the new figure.
steps.expect: the pattern stays suspended.

steps.action: **Continue passes.** [BRANCH: practice the same transfer | learn the next named figure]
steps.expect: players can pass at least once without tangling.

recipes.verification: The opening cat's cradle shows a central woven X, and one partner transfer succeeds while the string pattern remains intact.

recipes.title: make a daisy chain
recipes.name: make-a-daisy-chain
recipes.goal: A closed loop of daisies linked stem-through-stem, sized as a crown, bracelet, or necklace, that holds together when worn.

steps.action: **Pick a working pile.** Pinch each stem off low, near the base, keeping the stem as long as possible; a crown takes roughly 15 to 25 daisies, a bracelet 8 to 10. Pick a third more than you think you need, because some stems will split.
steps.expect: a pile of long-stemmed daisies with firm, green, unkinked stems.

steps.action: **Slit the first stem.** Hold the stem between thumb and forefinger about halfway down, and press your thumbnail through it lengthwise to open a slit about 1 to 1.5 cm long. Keep the slit at least 2 cm above the stem's cut end, since a slit near the end tears out under any tension.
steps.expect: a clean eye-shaped slot through the stem, both edges intact.

steps.action: **Thread the next daisy.** Push the second daisy stem-end-first through the slit and pull it gently all the way through until its flower head rests against the slit. Pull along the stem's direction, not sideways.
steps.expect: two daisies locked head-to-stem, hanging as a short chain.

steps.action: **Repeat down the chain.** Slit the newly threaded daisy's stem and thread the next one, keeping slit lengths consistent so the flowers space evenly. Every few links, hold the chain up and check length against the wearer (around the head for a crown, wrist for a bracelet).
steps.expect: a growing chain with flowers evenly spaced and no torn links.

steps.action: **Close the loop.** When the chain reaches the target length, make the final slit longer, about 2 to 3 cm, in the last stem. Then thread the entire first flower, head and all, carefully through this big slit; the head acts as the knot. Ease the petals through with fingertips rather than yanking.
steps.expect: a closed ring; the first flower's head sits snug against the final slit and cannot slip back through.

steps.action: **Fit and wear.** Settle the crown or bracelet in place, adjusting spacing by sliding flowers gently along their slits.
steps.expect: the loop stays on during normal movement without any link tearing.

recipes.verification: The chain forms a closed loop with every flower held by a stem slit, the first flower's head anchors the final link, and the loop survives being picked up, worn, and taken off again without a link tearing.

recipes.title: make a flip book
recipes.name: make-a-flip-book
recipes.goal: A small stack of pages becomes a flip book animation that moves when thumbed from one corner.

steps.action: **Choose the flipping corner.** [BRANCH: right-handed flip | left-handed flip] put the drawing near the outer lower corner your thumb will release.
steps.expect: the action area sits where each page will be seen during the flip.

steps.action: **Stack pages squarely.** Align 20 to 40 pages and clip the binding edge.
steps.expect: the stack behaves like one little book.

steps.action: **Draw the first pose.** Make a simple shape near the corner, leaving room for movement.
steps.expect: page one shows the starting position clearly.

steps.action: **Change only a little per page.** On each next page, move the shape a few millimeters or alter one part.
steps.expect: the drawings differ gradually, not by teleportation.

steps.action: **Use onion-skin guessing.** Peek at the previous page edge or hold pages to light to place the next drawing.
steps.expect: the motion path stays smooth enough to follow.

steps.action: **Add timing.** Repeat a drawing for a pause, or make bigger jumps for speed.
steps.expect: the animation has slow and fast moments.

steps.action: **Test the thumb flip.** Hold the binding firmly and let the corner pages slip under your thumb. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* ink is hard to undo, so sketch in pencil until the timing test works.
steps.expect: the drawing appears to move.

steps.action: **Darken and finish.** Trace the best lines, number the backs if useful, and reclip the stack.
steps.expect: the final flip reads from start to finish.

recipes.verification: When flipped from the chosen corner, the stack shows one continuous recognizable motion from first page to last.

recipes.title: make a friendship bracelet pin
recipes.name: make-a-friendship-bracelet-pin
recipes.goal: Make a small friendship bracelet pin by threading beads onto a safety pin in a chosen color pattern, closing it securely, and gifting it safely.

steps.action: **Plan the pattern.** Lay beads on the tray in the order they will go onto the pin.
steps.expect: the color or letter sequence is visible before threading starts.

steps.action: **Open the safety pin.** Hold the clasp end steady and open the sharp point away from your face and fingers.
steps.expect: the pin is open without poking anyone.

steps.action: **Thread the beads.** Slide beads onto the open wire one at a time, following the planned order.
steps.expect: the beads sit on the pin wire without forcing.

steps.action: **Check spacing.** Leave enough bare wire near the point for the pin to close fully.
steps.expect: beads do not block the clasp.

steps.action: **Close the pin.** Push the point back into the clasp until it clicks or seats firmly.
steps.expect: the sharp point is covered.

steps.action: **Secure if needed.** [BRANCH: snug | loose] If the clasp feels loose, ask an adult to pinch it slightly with pliers; if snug, leave it alone.
steps.expect: the pin stays closed under a gentle tug.

steps.action: **Gift it.** Attach it to fabric only with permission, or place it in a small envelope with a note.
steps.expect: the recipient gets the bracelet pin without surprise pokes or loose beads.

recipes.verification: The bracelet pin is verified when the bead pattern is correct, the clasp fully covers the point, and a gentle shake does not release beads.

recipes.title: make a friendship bracelet
recipes.name: make-a-friendship-bracelet
recipes.goal: A finished candy-stripe friendship bracelet: even diagonal stripes, tight consistent knots, and a tie-off that fits the wearer's wrist without falling off.

steps.action: **Cut and anchor the strands.** Cut one strand per color, each about the length of your fingertip-to-shoulder (roughly 60-70 cm). Gather them, tie a single overhand knot 8-10 cm from one end, and anchor above the knot.
steps.expect: strands hang free below a firm anchor; the 8-10 cm tail above the knot is your future tie, do not trim it.

steps.action: **Order the colors and keep that order.** Arrange strands left to right in your stripe sequence (e.g. red, yellow, green, blue). The leftmost color is about to become the first stripe.
steps.expect: strands separated, not crossed, in a sequence you could re-derive if they tangle.

steps.action: **Learn the forward knot on the first pair.** Hold strand 2 taut with your right hand (the taut strand is the core, this is the secret of even bracelets). With strand 1, make a "4" over strand 2, pass the end through, pull up snug to the top. Then make the identical knot again on the same strand.
steps.expect: two half-hitches = one forward knot; a small bump in strand 1's color sits at the top, and strand 1 now hangs to the RIGHT of strand 2.

steps.action: **Carry the working strand across the row.** Same working strand (old strand 1) makes a forward knot over strand 3, then strand 4. Always double-knot; a single half-hitch flips the colors and is the classic beginner bug.
steps.expect: a full diagonal row of one color; the working strand has traveled to the far right and retires there.

steps.action: **Repeat rows with each new leftmost strand.** The new leftmost color knots across everything. Keep tension constant: taut core strand, knots pulled snug but not strangled, every knot slid up flush against the row above.
steps.expect: diagonal stripes cycling through your color order; edges straight, no gaps (loose) and no curling corkscrew (too tight, see F2).

steps.action: **Check length against the wrist.** Knot until the striped band wraps the wrist with a finger's width of slack. Band-only length is typically 14-15 cm for adults, 12-13 cm for kids.
steps.expect: band circles the wrist comfortably; ties are extra and not counted.

steps.action: **Tie off into a braid.** Tie one overhand knot flush against the last row, then braid the loose strands for 5-7 cm and finish with another overhand knot. Do the same to the starting tail if you left it loose.
steps.expect: a braid on each end that will not unravel; trim strand ends 1 cm past the final knots.

steps.action: **Attach to the wrist.** [BRANCH: permanent (square knot: right-over-left then left-over-right, trim ends; friendship-bracelet tradition is you wear it until it falls off) | removable (loop-and-knot closure: fold the starting tail into a loop when you begin, then pass the end braid through it and knot)] ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the permanent square knot plus trimming; confirm fit and the wearer's consent to the "until it falls off" deal before cutting.
steps.expect: bracelet on the wrist, snug over the wrist bone plus one finger of slack, staying put when the hand shakes.

recipes.verification: The band shows unbroken diagonal stripes in the planned color cycle with no color flips, lies flat without corkscrewing, fits the wrist with about one finger of slack, and both ends are braided and knotted so nothing unravels after a gentle tug test.

recipes.title: make a lava lamp
recipes.name: make-a-lava-lamp
recipes.goal: Make a temporary lava-lamp effect in a clear bottle using water, oil, food coloring, and a fizzing tablet reaction.

steps.action: **Set the container on a tray.** Place the clear bottle upright where spills can be wiped easily.
steps.expect: the work area is stable and protected.

steps.action: **Add water.** Fill the bottle about one quarter full with water.
steps.expect: a clear water layer sits at the bottom.

steps.action: **Add oil.** Pour vegetable oil until the bottle is mostly full, leaving air space at the top.
steps.expect: the oil floats above the water in a separate layer.

steps.action: **Add color.** Drop in several drops of food coloring and wait for them to sink into the water layer.
steps.expect: colored drops pass through oil and tint the water below.

steps.action: **Start the fizz.** Break a fizzing tablet into pieces and drop one piece into the bottle.
steps.expect: bubbles carry colored water blobs up through the oil.

steps.action: **Watch and repeat.** [BRANCH: gentle | active] Use one small tablet piece for slow blobs or another piece after fizz slows for more motion.
steps.expect: blobs rise, fall, and separate as bubbles form and pop.

steps.action: **Reuse or dispose.** Let fizz stop, cap loosely for short display, or pour contents into trash according to local guidance for oily waste.
steps.expect: the activity ends without pressure buildup or an oily sink mess.

recipes.verification: The lava lamp is verified when colored water blobs rise through the oil with fizzing bubbles and settle back down after bubbles pop.

recipes.title: make a leaf rubbing
recipes.name: make-a-leaf-rubbing
recipes.goal: Make a clear leaf rubbing by placing paper over a leaf vein-side up and rubbing with the side of a crayon.

steps.action: **Choose the leaf.** Pick a leaf with strong veins and no wet dirt, then brush off loose grit.
steps.expect: the leaf is clean enough not to smear the paper.

steps.action: **Place vein-side up.** Lay the underside of the leaf facing up on the flat surface.
steps.expect: the raised vein network can be felt with a fingertip.

steps.action: **Cover with paper.** Put paper over the leaf and hold the sheet still at the corners.
steps.expect: the leaf shape is hidden but does not slide underneath.

steps.action: **Rub with the crayon side.** Turn the crayon sideways and rub lightly across the paper in one direction.
steps.expect: the veins and outline begin appearing before the background fills in.

steps.action: **Build the color.** Add more pressure gradually, keeping strokes broad and even.
steps.expect: the full leaf shape appears without tearing the paper.

steps.action: **Layer colors.** [BRANCH: single-color | layered] Stop after one color for a clean print, or add a second light color from another direction.
steps.expect: the rubbing keeps the vein detail while gaining depth.

steps.action: **Lift and inspect.** Hold the paper flat, remove the leaf, and sign or label the rubbing if desired.
steps.expect: the final image shows the outline, stem, and main veins clearly.

recipes.verification: The rubbing is verified when the leaf outline and main vein pattern are visible on the paper without major smears or tears.

recipes.title: make a paper airplane
recipes.name: make-a-paper-airplane
recipes.goal: A classic dart paper airplane, folded with sharp creases and symmetric wings, that flies straight across a room instead of nose-diving at your feet.

steps.action: **Fold the sheet in half lengthwise, crease hard, and open it flat again.** This center crease is the spine and the symmetry reference for everything after.
steps.expect: a sharp valley line dividing the sheet into equal halves.

steps.action: **Fold the two top corners to the center line.** Each corner's edge lands exactly on the spine, making a point at the top. Crease with the fingernail.
steps.expect: a symmetric point; both diagonal edges kiss the center line with no overlap or gap.

steps.action: **Fold the angled edges to the center line again.** Take each new diagonal edge and fold it to the spine, sharpening the nose into a long point.
steps.expect: a narrow dart shape; the nose is a tight point and the symmetry still holds. Asymmetry here is the number-one cause of curving flights; refold rather than accept a 2 mm error.

steps.action: **Fold the plane in half along the original spine, folds inside.**
steps.expect: a slim triangle silhouette with the layered folds hidden inside the keel.

steps.action: **Fold the wings down, one per side.** From the nose, fold each side down so the wing's leading edge lies parallel to the keel's bottom, about 2 cm of keel remaining below. Match the second wing to the first by holding them together against the light.
steps.expect: two identical wings; viewed head-on the plane is a Y, wings level or in a slight upward V (dihedral), which is what makes it self-stabilize.

steps.action: **Trim and launch.** Grip the keel at the balance point (roughly a third back from the nose), throw straight ahead at a level or slightly upward angle with a smooth medium motion. Hard throws are for footballs; darts want speed the paper can hold.
steps.expect: a straight glide of several meters. Adjust from what you see: nose-dive → bend the wings' trailing edges up slightly; climbing-then-stalling → less up-bend or a touch more nose weight (a paperclip on the keel's front).

recipes.verification: The plane holds a straight-line glide across a room, both wings match against the light, the dihedral is visible head-on, and your last adjustment produced the change you predicted — which is the moment paper folding quietly became aeronautics.

recipes.title: make a paper boat
recipes.name: make-a-paper-boat
recipes.goal: A classic folded paper boat (the "newspaper hat" style with a raised sail) sits upright and floats on water for at least a minute or two before soaking through.

steps.action: **Fold the sheet in half top-to-bottom.** Short edges together, crease sharply with a fingernail. Keep the folded edge at the top for all following steps.
steps.expect: a half-size rectangle with the crisp fold along the top.

steps.action: **Mark the center line.** Fold in half left-to-right, crease lightly, unfold.
steps.expect: a visible vertical center crease.

steps.action: **Fold both top corners down to the center line.** The two corners of the folded (top) edge meet at the crease, forming a point at the top, like starting a paper airplane.
steps.expect: a triangle sitting on a rectangular strip of two loose flaps at the bottom.

steps.action: **Fold the bottom flaps up, one per side.** Fold the front strip up over the triangle's base; flip the model and fold the back strip up the same way. Fold the little protruding corners of each strip around the triangle's edges so nothing sticks out.
steps.expect: a clean paper hat shape (it literally fits on a head if made from newspaper).

steps.action: **Open the hat and flatten into a diamond.** Put thumbs inside the bottom opening, pull the front and back apart, and bring the left and right points together, re-flattening the model 90 degrees from before. Tuck one bottom flap corner over the other so they interlock.
steps.expect: a flat diamond (square standing on a corner).

steps.action: **Fold the bottom point of the diamond up to the top point; flip and repeat.** One loose bottom layer folds up on each side.
steps.expect: a smaller triangle again.

steps.action: **Open and flatten into a diamond a second time.** Same move as step 5: open the bottom, collapse the other way.
steps.expect: a smaller flat diamond with two loose top-corner layers.

steps.action: **Pull the boat open.** Grip the two loose top corners of the diamond (one per hand) and pull gently outward and apart. The model unfolds itself: hull opens, center sail rises. Ease it, don't yank; this is where tearing happens.
steps.expect: a boat with a flat-ish hull, two pointed ends, and an upright triangular sail.

steps.action: **Trim the hull and float it.** Pinch along the bottom to flatten the keel so it sits level, then set it gently onto calm water, lowering it flat rather than dropping it.
steps.expect: the boat floats upright, sail up, for at least a minute.

recipes.verification: The finished boat has the classic silhouette (two pointed ends, central sail), was produced without tears, and passed the float test: upright and dry-topped on calm water for at least 60 seconds.

recipes.title: make a paper fortune teller
recipes.name: make-a-paper-fortune-teller
recipes.goal: A square paper fortune teller is folded, labeled, filled with fortunes, and ready to play.

steps.action: **Make a square.** Fold a rectangular sheet diagonally, trim the extra strip, and open it.
steps.expect: paper has four equal sides.

steps.action: **Mark the center.** Fold diagonally both ways, then open flat.
steps.expect: crease lines cross at the center.

steps.action: **Fold corners inward.** Bring each corner point to the center.
steps.expect: a smaller square forms with four triangular flaps.

steps.action: **Flip and repeat.** Turn the square over and fold all four new corners to the center.
steps.expect: an even smaller square forms.

steps.action: **Fold for fingers.** Fold the square in half one way, open it, then fold in half the other way.
steps.expect: pockets puff open underneath.

steps.action: **Label outside flaps.** Write colors, symbols, or numbers on the four outside flaps.
steps.expect: each outside choice is readable.

steps.action: **Number and fill inside.** Number the eight inner triangles, lift them, and write one fortune under each.
steps.expect: every hidden flap has a short message.

steps.action: **Play a round.** Put thumbs and index fingers into the pockets and move the teller as choices are spelled or counted.
steps.expect: a final flap opens to reveal a fortune.

recipes.verification: The fortune teller opens in two directions on the fingers, has four outside choices, eight numbered inner choices, and eight hidden fortunes.

recipes.title: make a paper rocket
recipes.name: make-a-paper-rocket
recipes.goal: Make a paper rocket that launches from a straw or by blowing through a tube, then adjust it for distance.

steps.action: **Roll the body.** Wrap paper around a pencil to make a snug tube, then tape the seam.
steps.expect: the tube slides off the pencil without collapsing.

steps.action: **Seal the nose.** Pinch or fold one end closed and tape it airtight.
steps.expect: air cannot escape through the front.

steps.action: **Trim the tail.** Cut the open end straight so the straw can fit inside.
steps.expect: the rocket sits on the straw without snagging.

steps.action: **Add fins.** Tape three or four small paper triangles near the tail.
steps.expect: fins are evenly spaced and point backward.

steps.action: **Fit the launcher.** Slide the open end over a straw.
steps.expect: the rocket moves freely but does not wobble too much.

steps.action: **Launch safely.** Aim at open space and blow through the straw in one quick breath.
steps.expect: the rocket flies forward.

steps.action: **Measure distance.** Mark where the rocket lands.
steps.expect: each launch has a comparison point.

steps.action: **Adjust the design.** [BRANCH: nose heavy | tail wobbly] shorten tape at the nose, or straighten and resize fins.
steps.expect: flight becomes straighter or farther.

steps.action: **Repeat and compare.** Change only one feature at a time.
steps.expect: the best version is clear from the landing marks.

recipes.verification: The paper rocket leaves the straw, flies through open space, and improves after at least one measured adjustment.

recipes.title: make a photo book
recipes.name: make-a-photo-book
recipes.goal: Create a coherent photo book from selected images with a sequence, captions if needed, and a final proof ready to print or share.

steps.action: **Define the book idea.** Choose an event, trip, year, family story, portfolio, or visual theme.
steps.expect: every photo can be judged against one purpose.

steps.action: **Select a first edit.** Gather 40 to 80 candidate images and remove duplicates, blurred mistakes, and private images.
steps.expect: the working set is strong enough to sequence.

steps.action: **Choose the final set.** Pick fewer images than the maximum pages allow, favoring variety in distance, people, details, and mood.
steps.expect: the book has breathing room instead of crowded pages.

steps.action: **Build a sequence.** Arrange photos with a beginning, middle, and ending, using full-page images for important moments.
steps.expect: flipping pages feels like moving through a story.

steps.action: **Crop and align pages.** Check faces, horizons, margins, and gutter areas before finalizing each spread.
steps.expect: important details are not cut off or buried near the spine.

steps.action: **Add captions sparingly.** Use names, places, dates, or short context where memory may fade.
steps.expect: captions clarify without competing with the photos.

steps.action: **Proof every page.** Preview the whole book at page size and inspect spelling, image quality warnings, and page order.
steps.expect: obvious layout, crop, and typo problems are fixed before ordering.

steps.action: **Export or order.** Save a PDF proof or place the print order only after confirming cost, shipping, and privacy settings.
steps.expect: a final file or order confirmation exists.

recipes.verification: The finished photo book proof has a clear theme, intentional image sequence, checked crops and captions, and either an exported file or confirmed print order within budget.

recipes.title: make a popsicle stick catapult
recipes.name: make-a-popsicle-stick-catapult
recipes.goal: Build a small popsicle-stick catapult with rubber bands, a fulcrum stack, a throwing arm, and a bottle-cap cup for soft projectiles.

steps.action: **Stack the fulcrum.** Place six to eight sticks in a neat stack and wrap rubber bands tightly around both ends.
steps.expect: the stack acts like a firm block.

steps.action: **Make the arm pair.** Stack two sticks together and band one end so they open like a narrow mouth.
steps.expect: one end is hinged and the other end can separate.

steps.action: **Insert the fulcrum.** Slide the thick stack between the two arm sticks near the banded end.
steps.expect: the upper stick lifts into a springy throwing arm.

steps.action: **Band the crossing.** Wrap a rubber band in an X around the fulcrum and arm so the stack cannot slide out.
steps.expect: the frame stays together when the arm is pressed.

steps.action: **Attach the cup.** Tape or glue a bottle cap near the free end of the upper arm with the open side up.
steps.expect: the cap holds one soft projectile without wobbling.

steps.action: **Aim safely.** [BRANCH: target | distance-test] Point at a paper cup target or an empty floor zone, never at a person, animal, glass, screen, or light.
steps.expect: the launch path is clear before loading.

steps.action: **Launch lightly.** Press the arm down a short distance, release, and adjust the fulcrum position for more or less range.
steps.expect: the projectile travels toward the target without parts flying loose.

recipes.verification: The catapult is verified when it launches one soft projectile at a clear target while the frame, bands, and cup remain attached.

recipes.title: make a rubber band ball
recipes.name: make-a-rubber-band-ball
recipes.goal: You can build a round rubber band ball from a small core by wrapping bands in changing directions with even tension.

steps.action: **Make the core.** Fold a small piece of paper tightly or wad several rubber bands into a compact lump.
steps.expect: a firm center about marble size.

steps.action: **Anchor the first bands.** Wrap two or three bands around the core in different directions so they cross and hold the shape.
steps.expect: the core no longer unfolds.

steps.action: **Change direction every wrap.** Add each new band around a different axis: north-south, east-west, then diagonal.
steps.expect: the ball grows evenly instead of becoming a flat bundle.

steps.action: **Use steady tension.** Stretch bands enough to grip, but not so much that they are near snapping. [BRANCH: loose band | tight band] Twist loose bands once; discard bands that feel brittle or overstretched.
steps.expect: each band lies snugly without biting into one groove.

steps.action: **Correct the shape early.** If one side bulges, wrap the next bands around the smaller side to build it out.
steps.expect: the ball becomes rounder every few wraps.

steps.action: **Size up gradually.** Use small bands near the core and larger bands as the ball grows.
steps.expect: bands fit without excessive twisting.

steps.action: **Finish with clean wraps.** Add the last few bands evenly spaced so the surface looks tidy and holds together.
steps.expect: the ball can be tossed hand to hand without shedding bands.

recipes.verification: The rubber band ball is roughly round, holds together when bounced lightly in your hand, and has bands crossing in several directions.

recipes.title: make a snow fort
recipes.name: make-a-snow-fort
recipes.goal: Build a small snow fort for play with stable walls, clear exits, and no collapse-prone roof or tunnel.

steps.action: **Choose a safe site.** Pick flat ground away from traffic, roofs, trees with heavy snow, and hidden water.
steps.expect: the fort area has clear space on all sides.

steps.action: **Choose the build method.** [BRANCH: pack blocks | pile and hollow] Pack blocks with buckets or tubs, or pile snow and hollow only shallow wall openings.
steps.expect: the method fits the snow texture and available tools.

steps.action: **Mark the footprint.** Draw a circle, U shape, or low rectangle with at least one wide opening.
steps.expect: everyone can see the wall line and exit.

steps.action: **Build thick low walls.** Stack blocks or packed snow with walls at least 30 cm thick and no higher than chest height for the smallest player.
steps.expect: walls stand without leaning inward.

steps.action: **Pack each layer.** Press snow firmly into gaps and stagger block joints like bricks.
steps.expect: joints are filled and the wall does not wobble when tapped lightly.

steps.action: **Follow the safe-roof rule.** Keep the fort open to the sky unless an adult uses a rated structure outside this recipe.
steps.expect: no one is under a snow roof.

steps.action: **Avoid tunnels.** Do not dig crawl tunnels into piles, plow banks, or deep drifts because they can collapse without warning.
steps.expect: all play spaces are open or shallow enough to step out of.

steps.action: **Smooth sharp edges.** Round corners and clear loose chunks from the floor.
steps.expect: the inside has fewer trip points and no hard protrusions.

steps.action: **Check stability before play.** Push lightly on each wall section from outside and repair weak spots. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* collapse can trap or injure a child; stop play if any wall slumps or cracks.
steps.expect: walls remain upright during a gentle check.

recipes.verification: The fort has stable low walls, at least one open exit, no snow roof, and no crawl tunnel.

recipes.title: make a sock puppet
recipes.name: make-a-sock-puppet
recipes.goal: You can turn a clean sock into a puppet with a working mouth, eyes, hair, and a simple voice or personality.

steps.action: **Test the mouth fold.** Put your hand in the sock with fingers in the toe and thumb under them, then open and close your hand.
steps.expect: the toe bends like a mouth.

steps.action: **Mark the face.** With the sock on your hand, lightly mark where eyes and hair should sit above the mouth.
steps.expect: features land where the audience will see them.

steps.action: **Add the mouth shape.** Cut a felt oval or paper oval and glue it inside the folded mouth area. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* glue can stain or set fast, so confirm placement before pressing.
steps.expect: the mouth has a colored inside when it opens.

steps.action: **Glue on eyes.** Attach craft eyes, buttons, or felt circles above the fold, evenly spaced but not perfectly if you want character.
steps.expect: the puppet has a clear gaze.

steps.action: **Attach yarn hair.** Cut several yarn strands, tie or glue them together at the center, and attach them to the top of the head.
steps.expect: hair moves when the puppet talks.

steps.action: **Give it a voice.** [BRANCH: silly voice | serious narrator] Pick one voice and a favorite phrase, then move the mouth once per syllable.
steps.expect: speech looks connected to hand motion.

steps.action: **Rehearse a tiny scene.** Have the puppet introduce itself, ask a question, and react to an answer.
steps.expect: the puppet feels like a character, not just a decorated sock.

recipes.verification: The puppet opens and closes its mouth on your hand, has secure eyes and hair, and performs a three-line introduction.

recipes.title: make a sundial
recipes.name: make-a-sundial
recipes.goal: Make a simple sundial that uses a shadow to show local solar time and teaches why clock time can differ.

steps.action: **Choose the base.** Put the board or markable surface on level ground where shadows will not be blocked.
steps.expect: the surface stays still and the sun reaches it.

steps.action: **Set the gnomon angle.** Tilt the gnomon so it points toward the celestial pole at an angle equal to your latitude above the surface.
steps.expect: a 40 degree latitude uses a gnomon about 40 degrees above the base.

steps.action: **Aim it north or south.** In the northern hemisphere, point the raised end toward true north; in the southern hemisphere, point it toward true south.
steps.expect: the gnomon points along the local meridian, not just where a phone compass first guesses.

steps.action: **Secure the gnomon.** Tape, glue, or wedge it so the angle does not change.
steps.expect: the shadow moves, but the stick does not wobble.

steps.action: **Mark the first hour.** At a known clock time, mark the shadow tip and label the clock time.
steps.expect: one clear tick mark appears at the shadow tip.

steps.action: **Keep marking through the day.** Return each hour and mark the new shadow tip.
steps.expect: a curved or fan-shaped set of hour marks builds across the base.

steps.action: **Note true time differences.** Write down whether daylight saving time is active and how far you are from the center of your time zone.
steps.expect: you understand why noon by the clock may not match the shortest shadow.

steps.action: **Find solar noon.** The shortest shadow of the day is local solar noon.
steps.expect: the noon mark may be offset from 12:00 on the clock.

steps.action: **Use the dial later.** Place the dial in the same orientation and read the shadow against your marks.
steps.expect: the reading is close on sunny days when the base and gnomon are aligned.

recipes.verification: On a sunny later hour, the gnomon shadow falls near the matching marked hour when the dial is returned to its original orientation.

recipes.title: make a terrarium
recipes.name: make-a-terrarium
recipes.goal: A small terrarium is planted in a glass container with drainage, soil, suitable plants, and a watering plan that does not turn it into soup.

steps.action: **Choose open or sealed.** [BRANCH: open terrarium | sealed terrarium] use open for succulents and cacti, sealed for moisture-loving tropical plants.
steps.expect: the plant choice matches the container style.

steps.action: **Add a drainage layer.** Pour 2 to 4 cm of pebbles into the bottom.
steps.expect: water has a place to collect below the roots.

steps.action: **Sprinkle charcoal.** Add a thin layer of activated charcoal over the pebbles.
steps.expect: the bottom looks dusted, not buried.

steps.action: **Add soil.** Spoon in enough potting mix for the plant roots, usually 5 to 8 cm.
steps.expect: there is room for roots and still room above for leaves.

steps.action: **Plant small and gently.** Make holes, set plants in, and firm soil around roots without crushing stems.
steps.expect: each plant stands upright with its crown above the soil.

steps.action: **Clean the glass.** Brush soil from leaves and wipe the inside wall with a dry cloth or cotton swab.
steps.expect: the view looks like a tiny exhibit, not a jar after a landslide.

steps.action: **Water lightly.** Add water by spoon or spray bottle, aiming at soil, not leaves. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overwatering in a sealed jar can rot roots fast, so add less than feels satisfying.
steps.expect: soil darkens slightly while no puddle rises into the soil layer.

steps.action: **Place and observe.** Put it in bright indirect light and check condensation the next day.
steps.expect: plants remain upright and the glass is mostly clear.

recipes.verification: After 24 hours, the plants stand upright, the soil is lightly moist, and there is no standing water in the soil layer.

recipes.title: make a zine
recipes.name: make-a-zine
recipes.goal: Make a small folded zine with a clear theme, readable pages, and a reproducible master copy.

steps.action: **Fold the sheet into eighths.** Fold in half lengthwise, unfold, then fold into quarters across the short direction.
steps.expect: the paper has eight equal panels.

steps.action: **Make the center cut.** Fold the sheet in half across the short direction and cut only the middle crease between the two central panels.
steps.expect: a single slit appears in the center of the page.

steps.action: **Fold into booklet form.** Push the slit open into a diamond, then collapse the paper into a small booklet.
steps.expect: the sheet becomes an eight-page zine.

steps.action: **Number a dummy copy.** Write page numbers lightly on each panel, then unfold it flat.
steps.expect: the flat layout shows which panel becomes each page.

steps.action: **Plan one idea per page.** Assign cover, intro, several images or notes, and back page.
steps.expect: the zine has a beginning, middle, and ending.

steps.action: **Draw and letter the master.** Add text and images in the correct panel directions using dark readable marks.
steps.expect: the unfolded master can be copied or refolded.

steps.action: **Copy or refold the zine.** Duplicate the flat master if desired, then fold and cut each copy the same way.
steps.expect: a finished booklet opens in page order.

recipes.verification: The zine folds into a booklet with pages in order, readable text or images on every intended page, and a flat master that can be copied.

recipes.title: make invisible ink
recipes.name: make-invisible-ink
recipes.goal: A hidden message is written with simple invisible ink, dried, and revealed safely with adult-controlled heat or a non-heat alternative.

steps.action: **Mix the ink.** Combine lemon juice with a few drops of water. [BRANCH: lemon ink | baking-soda ink] use lemon for heat reveal, baking soda for grape-juice reveal.
steps.expect: a pale liquid sits in the bowl.

steps.action: **Write lightly.** Dip a swab and write on white paper without soaking it.
steps.expect: the message is damp and barely visible.

steps.action: **Let it dry fully.** Wait until the paper looks blank and feels dry.
steps.expect: the message disappears unless viewed at an angle.

steps.action: **Prepare the reveal area.** Move flammable clutter away and put the paper on a heat-safe surface.
steps.expect: only the paper and heat tool are in the work zone.

steps.action: **Reveal with gentle heat.** An adult holds the paper near a warm bulb or passes a warm iron over it with no steam. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overheated paper can scorch or burn, so stop at brown letters and never use an open flame.
steps.expect: the writing turns tan before the blank paper does.

steps.action: **Use the other ink if avoiding heat.** For baking-soda ink, brush grape juice over the dry page.
steps.expect: the hidden message changes color against the paper.

steps.action: **Read and preserve.** Let the page cool or dry, then hold it flat.
steps.expect: the message is legible without touching a hot surface.

steps.action: **Clean up.** Rinse bowls and swabs, and discard sticky paper scraps.
steps.expect: no lemon juice or grape juice remains on the table.

recipes.verification: The dried page first appears blank, then reveals a readable message after the chosen reveal method.

recipes.title: make oobleck
recipes.name: make-oobleck
recipes.goal: Make oobleck, a cornstarch and water mixture that feels solid when hit and liquid when moved slowly.

steps.action: **Measure the powder.** Put two parts cornstarch in the bowl.
steps.expect: a mound of dry white powder fills the bowl.

steps.action: **Add water slowly.** Add about one part water in small pours while stirring.
steps.expect: the mixture changes from powder to thick paste.

steps.action: **Adjust the texture.** [BRANCH: too dry | too runny] add drops of water if crumbly, or cornstarch if soupy.
steps.expect: the mixture flows slowly but resists quick pressure.

steps.action: **Test a fast hit.** Tap the surface quickly with a finger or spoon.
steps.expect: it feels firm for a moment.

steps.action: **Test a slow move.** Rest fingers on the surface and let them sink.
steps.expect: the mixture behaves like a thick liquid.

steps.action: **Squeeze and release.** Roll some oobleck into a ball, then open your hand.
steps.expect: it firms under pressure and then drips.

steps.action: **Name the rule.** Explain that tiny starch particles jam under sudden force and slide during slow motion.
steps.expect: the strange feel has a simple cause.

steps.action: **Contain play.** Keep the bowl over the tray and wipe dropped bits before they dry.
steps.expect: the mess stays local.

steps.action: **Dispose safely.** Scrape oobleck into trash or compost where allowed, then wash residue from tools.
steps.expect: no thick starch goes down the drain.

recipes.verification: The batch firms under quick force, flows under slow force, and is disposed of without putting thick oobleck down a drain.

recipes.title: make paper snowflakes
recipes.name: make-paper-snowflakes
recipes.goal: You can fold a square sheet into sixths, cut patterns that survive the folds, and unfold a six-sided paper snowflake.

steps.action: **Make a square.** Fold one corner of rectangular paper across to align with the opposite edge, then trim the extra strip. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cutting changes the sheet, so confirm the fold is aligned first.
steps.expect: one neat square.

steps.action: **Fold into a triangle.** Fold the square corner to corner and crease sharply.
steps.expect: a triangle with clean matched edges.

steps.action: **Fold the triangle in half.** Bring the two sharp corners together and crease, then reopen if you need a center guide.
steps.expect: a center line that helps divide the paper.

steps.action: **Fold to sixths.** Bring one side across about one-third, then overlap the other side to make a narrow cone shape with three stacked wedges.
steps.expect: the top forms a 60-degree wedge with mostly aligned edges.

steps.action: **Trim the uneven top.** Cut across the wide end to make a clean wedge tip.
steps.expect: a compact folded wedge ready for pattern cuts.

steps.action: **Cut shapes from the edges.** Snip triangles, curves, diamonds, and notches from both long sides. Do not cut the whole fold through from one side to the other.
steps.expect: holes appear while the wedge still holds together.

steps.action: **Open slowly.** Unfold one layer at a time, easing tight cuts with fingertips instead of pulling hard. [BRANCH: clean unfold | snag] If it snags, reverse and loosen the cut.
steps.expect: a six-sided snowflake appears without tearing.

steps.action: **Flatten the reveal.** Press under a book for a few minutes or smooth gently with clean hands.
steps.expect: the snowflake lies flat enough to display.

recipes.verification: The unfolded paper has six repeated arms, visible cutout shapes, and remains connected as one piece.

recipes.title: make shadow puppets
recipes.name: make-shadow-puppets
recipes.goal: Recognizable animal shadows appear crisp on a wall, you can hold and animate three or four classic shapes, and a short shadow story has been performed for an audience.

steps.action: **Set up the light.** Place the light 2-3 m from the wall, at roughly the height your hands will be, resting on a table or shelf so it cannot move. Kill the other lights.
steps.expect: an even bright patch on the wall; the darker the room, the higher the contrast.

steps.action: **Find the sharp zone.** Put your hand in the beam and slide it between light and wall. Close to the wall: small, sharp shadow. Close to the light: huge, blurry shadow.
steps.expect: you have located the distance (usually 30-60 cm from the wall) where the shadow is both large and crisp; this is your performance zone.

steps.action: **Learn the dog.** Palm facing sideways to the beam, fingers together and extended for the snout, thumb up for the ear, pinky dropped slightly to open the mouth.
steps.expect: a dog head profile on the wall; flapping the pinky makes it "bark".

steps.action: **Learn the bird.** Hook both thumbs together, palms facing the wall, fingers spread as wings; flap by bending the fingers, not the wrists.
steps.expect: a bird whose wings beat smoothly; wrist-flapping instead makes it lurch, which is the usual beginner error.

steps.action: **Learn the rabbit.** One fist knuckles-out for the head, index and middle finger up in a V for ears; the other hand cupped under it as the body. Wiggle the two ear fingers independently.
steps.expect: a rabbit with twitching ears; small finger motions read as large on the wall.

steps.action: **Add one hard shape.** [BRANCH: crocodile (two hands stacked palm-to-palm, hinging open as jaws) | wolf howl (dog shape tilted 45° upward with the mouth open)]
steps.expect: the shape reads instantly to someone who was not told what it is; if they have to guess, simplify the silhouette.

steps.action: **Compose a 2-minute story.** Three beats is enough: characters meet, a chase or problem, a resolution. Move puppets by walking your hands across the beam; grow a character by moving toward the light, shrink it by retreating to the wall.
steps.expect: a story arc where size changes and entrances/exits are deliberate, not accidental.

steps.action: **Perform.** Audience sits facing the wall; you crouch below or beside the beam so your head and body stay out of the light. Narrate in character voices.
steps.expect: the audience sees only puppets, never your silhouette blocking half the screen.

recipes.verification: A person who was not told the shapes can name the dog, bird, and rabbit from their shadows alone, the story ran start to finish with at least one size change, and the light source never got knocked over.

recipes.title: make slime
recipes.name: make-slime
recipes.goal: Make stretchy play slime from school glue and an activator, adjust the texture, and store it without contaminating food surfaces.

steps.action: **Cover the work surface.** Lay down parchment, a tray, or a washable mat.
steps.expect: spills land on a cleanable surface, not fabric or carpet.

steps.action: **Measure glue.** Pour 1/2 cup glue into the bowl.
steps.expect: glue sits in one puddle with no dried chunks.

steps.action: **Add color or mix-ins.** Stir in food coloring, glitter, or foam beads before activating.
steps.expect: color is even and mix-ins are suspended in the glue.

steps.action: **Add baking soda for lens-solution slime.** Stir in 1/2 teaspoon baking soda per 1/2 cup glue.
steps.expect: glue thickens slightly but still flows.

steps.action: **Add activator slowly.** [BRANCH: lens solution | borax solution] add 1 tablespoon lens solution, or 1 teaspoon borax solution at a time.
steps.expect: strings form and the mixture pulls from the bowl.

steps.action: **Stir until it clumps.** Scrape the sides and fold the mass through the wet spots.
steps.expect: one sticky lump forms around the spoon.

steps.action: **Knead with clean hands.** Pick up the lump and fold it for 2 to 5 minutes.
steps.expect: slime changes from wet and sticky to stretchy and smooth.

steps.action: **Fix stickiness.** Add activator a few drops at a time, then knead before adding more.
steps.expect: slime releases from fingers but still stretches.

steps.action: **Fix stiffness.** Add a pea-size dab of lotion or a few drops of warm water and knead.
steps.expect: slime softens without turning soupy.

steps.action: **Store immediately after play.** Put slime in an airtight container or zip bag.
steps.expect: the container closes fully and slime is not exposed to lint or crumbs.

steps.action: **Wash hands and tools.** Rinse bowls before residue dries, then wash with soap.
steps.expect: hands are clean and no slime remains in the sink drain.

recipes.verification: The slime stretches at least 15 cm without pouring like liquid, releases mostly from clean hands, and is sealed in a labeled container after use.

recipes.title: paint with watercolors
recipes.name: paint-with-watercolors
recipes.goal: Make a small watercolor painting using controlled washes, layered color, and preserved highlights.

steps.action: **Tape or steady the paper.** Secure the sheet to a board or table if it buckles easily.
steps.expect: the paper stays mostly flat while wet.

steps.action: **Sketch lightly.** Draw only the major shapes and mark any highlight areas to keep white.
steps.expect: pencil lines guide the painting without dominating it.

steps.action: **Mix a pale wash.** Add water to a color puddle until it is lighter than you think you need.
steps.expect: the first stroke is transparent, not opaque.

steps.action: **Paint the lightest layer.** Cover broad areas and leave highlights unpainted.
steps.expect: the subject has a light color base and visible white highlights.

steps.action: **Let the layer dry.** Wait until the shine leaves the paper before adding sharper details.
steps.expect: new strokes sit on top instead of spreading unpredictably.

steps.action: **Build shadows gradually.** Add darker mixtures in shadow areas with fewer strokes.
steps.expect: form appears without muddying the whole painting.

steps.action: **Add final accents.** Use a smaller brush or drier paint for edges, texture, and darkest details.
steps.expect: the image has focus points and still looks luminous.

recipes.verification: The finished painting has transparent color layers, at least one preserved or recovered highlight, and darker accents that define the subject.

recipes.title: pet a cat correctly
recipes.name: pet-a-cat-correctly
recipes.goal: A cat petted on its own terms: consent obtained, the approved zones serviced, the warning signs read, and the interaction ended before the famous sudden bite, leaving both parties wanting more.

steps.action: **Offer the greeting finger.** Crouch or sit at the cat's level, extend one relaxed finger or knuckle at nose height, half a meter away, and wait. This mimics cat-to-cat nose greeting and hands the decision over.
steps.expect: the cat approaches and sniffs, or does not. No approach is a complete answer; petting does not proceed by ambush.

steps.action: **Let the cat cast the first vote.** After the sniff: a cheek or body rub against your hand is a yes; walking away, a frozen stare, or retreating ears are a no.
steps.expect: an explicit yes before any petting begins.

steps.action: **Pet the approved zones only, with the fur, briefly.** Cheeks, under the chin, base of the ears, and the head's crown are the consensus zones; short strokes in the fur's direction. The belly, tail, paws, and (for many cats) the back near the tail are advanced-license territory that the default license does not include, regardless of how invitingly the belly is displayed — the belly roll is a trust signal, not a request.
steps.expect: leaning-in, purring, slow blinks, a tail held soft; all green.

steps.action: **Watch the license status continuously.** The revocation warnings arrive in order: tail starting to swish or thump, skin rippling along the back, ears rotating sideways/back, a sudden stillness, dilated pupils, a head swiveled toward your hand.
steps.expect: you catching the *first* sign, not the third; the bite everyone calls sudden was announced twice.

steps.action: **Pause at the first warning and let the cat re-vote.** Hand still or withdrawn a few centimeters; the cat resumes contact (license renewed) or disengages (license expired).
steps.expect: an exit with zero teeth involved; ending early is what makes you the favorite visitor.

steps.action: **Close on a high note.** A last chin scratch during clear enjoyment, then stop while it is good; optionally the slow-blink farewell (look at the cat, blink slowly; a returned slow blink is the species' handshake).
steps.expect: a cat that regards you as competent, which among cats is the whole social ladder.

recipes.verification: Consent preceded contact, only default-license zones were petted, the first warning sign paused the session, the interaction ended with the cat willing to return, and no skin was broken on either species.

recipes.title: pitch a tent
recipes.name: pitch-a-tent
recipes.goal: Pitch a tent on suitable ground so the body, poles, stakes, rain fly, and guy lines form a stable shelter for the expected weather.

steps.action: **Choose the site.** Pick flat, durable ground above runoff paths and away from dead limbs, ant nests, and sharp rocks.
steps.expect: the footprint area is level, legal, and safer than the surrounding options.

steps.action: **Orient the tent.** Point the narrow end or strongest side toward the wind and place the door where entry will stay dry and practical.
steps.expect: the layout works with wind, slope, and foot traffic.

steps.action: **Lay out the footprint and body.** Spread the footprint if used, then lay the tent body over it with corners aligned.
steps.expect: fabric lies flat without the footprint sticking out to catch rain.

steps.action: **Assemble the poles.** Let pole sections seat fully without snapping them together under tension.
steps.expect: poles are complete, straight, and fully joined.

steps.action: **Raise the tent.** [BRANCH: clips | sleeves] Insert poles through sleeves or attach clips in the tent maker's order, then lift the structure evenly.
steps.expect: the tent stands without twisted fabric or crossed poles.

steps.action: **Stake it taut.** Stake corners first, then adjust so the floor is smooth but not strained.
steps.expect: the tent holds its shape and the door zips without pulling hard.

steps.action: **Add fly and guy lines.** Attach the fly, tension it off the tent body, stake guy lines at useful angles, and do a wind check by pushing gently on the frame.
steps.expect: the fly sheds water, lines are visible, and the tent springs back under hand pressure.

recipes.verification: The tent is verified when it stands taut, zips normally, has a separated rain fly, and resists a gentle wind push without shifting stakes.

recipes.title: plan a scavenger hunt
recipes.name: plan-a-scavenger-hunt
recipes.goal: A scavenger hunt is planned and staged: clues hidden in a defined area, a difficulty ladder that keeps every player engaged, and a prize at the end that someone actually finds.

steps.action: **Define the boundary explicitly.** Walk the area and pick landmarks players can name ("the fence, the driveway, nothing upstairs"). Write the boundary on the first clue sheet.
steps.expect: a boundary you can state in one sentence, with no ambiguous zones (garages, neighbors' property, water) inside it.

steps.action: **Choose hunt structure.** [BRANCH: chain hunt (each clue points to the next, ends at the prize; best for one team) | checklist hunt (find N listed items in any order; best for competing teams, no shared clue to camp on)]
steps.expect: structure matches group: chain for cooperation, checklist for racing.

steps.action: **Write clues on a difficulty ladder.** First clue trivially easy (early success hooks players), middle clues moderate, and only the last one or two genuinely hard. For mixed ages, write each clue with a picture hint on the back so non-readers stay in.
steps.expect: 6-10 clues; you can solve each yourself in under 2 minutes; the first is solvable by the youngest player.

steps.action: **Number every clue on its back.** This is the non-obvious step that saves the hunt: when clue 4 goes missing, you know instantly which one to re-seed.
steps.expect: every clue carries its sequence number and the hunt is reconstructable from your master list.

steps.action: **Hide in reverse order, prize first.** Place the prize, then walk the chain backwards so each clue you hide points to a spot you have already confirmed. Waist height or below for young kids; never inside anything that latches shut.
steps.expect: every clue physically present, secure against wind, at the reachable height of the shortest player.

steps.action: **Do a full dry run yourself.** Follow the chain from clue 1 reading only what is written, not what you meant.
steps.expect: you reach the prize without using memory; any clue that made you pause gets rewritten now.

steps.action: **Brief the players and launch.** State the boundary, the "ask for a hint after 5 stuck minutes" rule, and (checklist hunts) the return time. Keep the master list in your pocket.
steps.expect: players moving toward clue 1; you positioned where you can see most of the area.

steps.action: **Shadow the hunt and drip hints.** Hint ladder: hot/cold first, then "look lower", then point at the zone. Never hand over the answer; the find must feel earned.
steps.expect: stuck time never exceeds ~5 minutes; energy stays up through the hard clues.

recipes.verification: The prize has been found by following the clues (not by accident), every clue on the master list is accounted for and collected, all players stayed inside the boundary, and nobody disengaged for more than a few minutes.
