recipes.title: plant a seed with a kid
recipes.name: plant-a-seed-with-a-kid
recipes.goal: A child has planted a seed in a pot with their own hands, the pot sits on a suitable windowsill with a care routine the child owns, and a sprout appears within the seed's normal germination window.

steps.action: **Set up a mess zone and let the kid do the touching.** Newspaper down, sleeves up. Your hands stay off the materials except to demonstrate; narrate instead of doing.
steps.expect: the kid is handling soil and seeds; you are talking, not planting.

steps.action: **Fill the pot with potting mix to 2 cm below the rim.** Kid scoops, you level. Tap the pot gently to settle; do not pack it hard.
steps.expect: loose, fluffy soil near the rim with room for watering.

steps.action: **Pre-moisten the soil.** Water a little at a time and let the kid stir with a finger until the mix feels like a wrung-out sponge, damp but not dripping. Dry potting mix repels water at first; this step prevents the seed washing out later.
steps.expect: uniformly dark, damp soil; no puddle.

steps.action: **Plant the seed at the right depth.** Rule of thumb the kid can learn: a seed goes as deep as two or three times its own size. Big bean: knuckle-deep hole, seed in, cover loosely. Tiny cress: sprinkle on the surface, dust of soil over. Plant 2 or 3 seeds per pot as insurance.
steps.expect: seeds covered at roughly the right depth; the kid can say the depth rule back to you.

steps.action: **Water gently and place on the windowsill.** Spray bottle or a slow dribble at the edge, not a pour on top of the seed. Saucer under the pot.
steps.expect: surface moist, seed still where it was planted, pot in bright light.

steps.action: **Make the waiting visible.** [BRANCH: plant one extra bean in a wet paper towel inside a clear jar or zip bag taped to the window (germination is visible in 2 to 3 days, which carries the kid through the invisible soil wait) | draw a calendar and cross off days, with the expected sprout window marked]
steps.expect: the kid has something to check daily that changes before the soil does.

steps.action: **Hand over a bounded care routine.** The kid's job: touch the soil every morning; if the top feels dry, water a little. Not more. Overwatering by an enthusiastic child is the number-one killer here.
steps.expect: the kid states the rule ("finger test first, then water") unprompted.

steps.action: **Greet the sprout and thin later.** When sprouts are up and 3 to 4 cm tall, keep the strongest one per pot and snip (not pull) the others at soil level, pulling disturbs the winner's roots. Let the kid choose the keeper.
steps.expect: one healthy seedling per pot, leaning toward the window.

steps.action: **Rotate the pot a quarter turn every couple of days.** Kid-friendly job that prevents a permanently bent stem.
steps.expect: seedling grows roughly straight over the following week.

recipes.verification: A live seedling stands in the pot on the windowsill within the seed packet's germination window (plus a few days); the child can state the finger-test watering rule and has performed it at least three times without prompting; the pot drains into its saucer, not the sill.

recipes.title: play 20 questions
recipes.name: play-20-questions
recipes.goal: Play 20 Questions with clear yes-or-no answers, honest clues, and a broad-to-narrow guessing strategy.

steps.action: **Pick the thing.** The answer keeper silently chooses a real or agreed imaginary person, place, object, or idea.
steps.expect: one fixed answer exists.

steps.action: **Set the category if desired.** [BRANCH: open game | category game] play with anything, or announce animal, vegetable, mineral, person, place, or object.
steps.expect: everyone knows the search space.

steps.action: **Ask broad first.** Start with questions that split many possibilities, such as living, human-made, bigger than a chair, or found indoors.
steps.expect: large groups of answers are removed.

steps.action: **Track the count.** Count every yes-or-no question, but do not count clarifying repeats caused by mishearing.
steps.expect: the group knows how many questions remain.

steps.action: **Narrow by traits.** Ask about size, use, location, material, time period, or category.
steps.expect: the answer space becomes small enough to guess.

steps.action: **Answer honestly.** The keeper gives the best truthful answer and says "sometimes" only when yes or no would mislead.
steps.expect: clues remain fair and consistent.

steps.action: **Make a candidate list.** After about ten questions, name two or three likely answers before spending a guess.
steps.expect: players compare possibilities instead of guessing wildly.

steps.action: **Use the final guess.** Ask "Is it..." when the evidence points to one answer.
steps.expect: the keeper confirms a win or says no.

steps.action: **Reveal and rotate.** If the group fails after 20 questions, reveal the thing and choose a new keeper.
steps.expect: the next round starts with a new answer.

recipes.verification: The round ends with either a correct guess within 20 counted questions or a revealed answer after the twentieth question.

recipes.title: play catch
recipes.name: play-catch
recipes.goal: Throw and catch a ball with a partner using a ready position, step-and-throw mechanics, and soft hands.

steps.action: **Choose the ball and glove setup.** [BRANCH: bare hands | glove] use a softer ball barehanded, or wear gloves for hard balls.
steps.expect: each player can close hands or glove around the ball.

steps.action: **Set the distance.** Start 3 to 5 m apart for beginners.
steps.expect: partners can talk normally and see each other's hands.

steps.action: **Take ready position.** Feet shoulder-width, knees soft, hands up near the chest.
steps.expect: the receiver can move left, right, forward, or back.

steps.action: **Grip the ball.** Hold it across the seams if present, with relaxed fingers and thumb underneath.
steps.expect: the ball is secure without a tight fist.

steps.action: **Point the front shoulder.** Turn the non-throwing shoulder toward the target.
steps.expect: the throwing hand moves behind the body comfortably.

steps.action: **Step and throw.** Step toward the partner with the opposite foot and bring the arm forward.
steps.expect: the ball leaves toward the partner's chest.

steps.action: **Follow through.** Let the throwing hand finish across the body and keep eyes on the receiver.
steps.expect: the thrower stays balanced after release.

steps.action: **Receive with soft hands.** Move the glove or hands to meet the ball, then give slightly as it arrives.
steps.expect: the ball settles instead of bouncing out.

steps.action: **Secure the catch.** Close the glove or second hand around the ball.
steps.expect: the ball is controlled before the next throw.

steps.action: **Progress gradually.** Add distance only after five comfortable catches in a row.
steps.expect: throws stay catchable at the new distance.

recipes.verification: Partners complete five consecutive catchable throws and catches at the chosen distance with controlled throws, ready hands, and no ball near the face.

recipes.title: play charades
recipes.name: play-charades
recipes.goal: A group has played several rounds of charades with fair teams, shared gesture conventions, a working timer, and a score both teams accept.

steps.action: **Split into two balanced teams.** Balance by mixing ages and the naturally theatrical with the reserved, not by friendship clusters.
steps.expect: two teams within one person of each other in size, neither stacked with all the extroverts.

steps.action: **Agree on categories and write slips.** Standard fair set: movies, TV shows, books, songs, famous people. Each player writes 3-5 slips for the OTHER team's bowl. Rule for fairness: if the writer doubts half the acting team would recognize the answer, it does not go in.
steps.expect: two bowls of folded slips; no inside jokes, no obscure picks meant to sabotage.

steps.action: **Teach the gesture conventions before round one.** These are the standard signs and skipping this briefing is the number one cause of chaotic games: category signs (movies: crank an old camera; TV: draw a rectangle; book: open palms; song: hand to mouth like singing; person: hands on hips), then hold up fingers for word count, then fingers again for which word, fingers on forearm for syllables, tug your earlobe for "sounds like", pinch fingers for "small word" (a, the, of), beckoning hands for "keep going, warmer", wave-off for "no, cold".
steps.expect: every player can produce the category signs and the "sounds like" ear tug on request.

steps.action: **State the two hard rules.** The actor may not speak, mouth words, or point at objects in the room; guessers may say anything and shout freely.
steps.expect: verbal agreement, especially from first-timers who will instinctively mouth words.

steps.action: **Run a turn.** Actor draws a slip (no swaps unless the group pre-agreed one free swap per game), timer starts when they signal the category. Actor plays only to their own team.
steps.expect: the turn opens with category sign then word count, before any acting; teams that skip the framing waste half the clock.

steps.action: **Score the turn.** [BRANCH: guessed before the buzzer → 1 point, slip discarded | timer expires → no point, and the slip is read aloud so everyone learns what it was]
steps.expect: score written down immediately; disputed "they said it at the buzzer" calls go to the timer holder, whose call is final.

steps.action: **Alternate teams and rotate actors.** Every player acts before anyone acts twice; nobody may opt out of acting entirely (shy players can take slips late in the game once the room is warm).
steps.expect: actor rotation visibly fair; the same ham is not up every other turn.

steps.action: **End at an agreed line.** Play to a point target (first to 10) or until the bowls empty, then total the score.
steps.expect: a final score both teams heard announced, and slips cleaned up.

recipes.verification: Every player acted at least once, all turns were timed with the same limit, the score sheet totals match the announced winner, and no slip disputes are still open.

recipes.title: play checkers
recipes.name: play-checkers
recipes.goal: Play a basic game of checkers with correct setup, diagonal movement, forced jumps, kinging, and winning conditions.

steps.action: **Orient the board.** Put a dark square in each player's left-hand corner.
steps.expect: pieces will move on dark squares only.

steps.action: **Set the men.** Place each player's twelve pieces on the dark squares of the three rows closest to them.
steps.expect: two empty rows remain in the middle.

steps.action: **Choose first player.** Let the player with dark pieces move first, or agree otherwise before starting.
steps.expect: turn order is clear.

steps.action: **Move diagonally forward.** Move one piece one dark square diagonally toward the opponent.
steps.expect: the piece lands on an empty dark square.

steps.action: **Jump when possible.** If an opposing piece is adjacent and the next dark square beyond it is empty, jump and remove the captured piece.
steps.expect: the jumped piece leaves the board.

steps.action: **Continue multiple jumps.** Keep jumping with the same piece if another jump is available from its new square.
steps.expect: one turn may capture several pieces.

steps.action: **Enforce forced jumps.** [BRANCH: jump exists | no jump] make a jump if one exists, otherwise make a normal move.
steps.expect: no player ignores a capture.

steps.action: **King a piece.** When a man reaches the far row, stack another checker on it.
steps.expect: the king can move and jump diagonally forward or backward.

steps.action: **Win the game.** Capture all opposing pieces or block all their legal moves.
steps.expect: the opponent has no playable turn.

recipes.verification: The final board shows one player with no pieces or no legal moves, and every capture followed the forced-jump rule.

recipes.title: play conkers
recipes.name: play-conkers
recipes.goal: Play conkers by drilling and stringing a horse chestnut, taking turns striking, and following rules that keep eyes and hands out of the swing path.

steps.action: **Choose sound conkers.** Pick firm horse chestnuts with no deep cracks, soft spots, or mold.
steps.expect: each conker feels hard and intact.

steps.action: **Drill the hole.** Wear eye protection, secure the conker on scrap wood, and drill straight through the center without holding it in your fingers.
steps.expect: a clean hole passes through without a hand near the bit.

steps.action: **Thread the string.** Push string through the hole and tie a large stopper knot below the conker.
steps.expect: the conker hangs securely from the string.

steps.action: **Set the stance.** One player dangles their conker at arm's length while the striker stands to the side with clear space.
steps.expect: eyes, hands, and faces are outside the swing line.

steps.action: **Strike in turns.** [BRANCH: striker | holder] The striker swings once at the hanging conker, then roles swap after a miss or agreed number of tries.
steps.expect: only one conker moves at a time and no one steps in.

steps.action: **Score breaks.** A player wins when the opponent's conker cracks, falls off the string, or can no longer be used.
steps.expect: the broken conker is removed from play.

steps.action: **Stop on unsafe swings.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an eye injury cannot be undone, so pause immediately if anyone removes eye protection or moves into range.
steps.expect: play resumes only after the area is safe again.

recipes.verification: The conkers game is verified when each round uses eye protection, a clear swing path, and an agreed win condition based on a broken or detached conker.

recipes.title: play fetch with a dog
recipes.name: play-fetch-with-a-dog
recipes.goal: The dog chases a thrown toy, brings it back, and releases it to your hand on cue, for a session that ends with the dog pleasantly tired rather than obsessive or lame.

steps.action: **Build toy value.** Wiggle the toy on the ground, let the dog grab it, play a few seconds of gentle tug, trade for a treat. A dog that does not care about the toy will not fetch it.
steps.expect: the dog orients to the toy the moment it appears.

steps.action: **Throw short and low.** Say your release word ("get it") and throw the toy 3 to 5 meters, low and away from the dog, never at it or straight up over its head (vertical leaps and hard stops are how fetch injures joints).
steps.expect: the dog chases and picks the toy up.

steps.action: **Trigger the return.** The moment the dog has the toy, crouch, open your arms, and move backward a few steps while calling its name brightly. Moving away pulls a dog toward you; walking at it starts a keep-away game.
steps.expect: the dog turns and comes at least most of the way back.

steps.action: **Cue the drop with a trade.** Say "drop it" once, then present the second identical toy (or a treat) at its nose. When the jaw opens, mark ("yes"), let it take the trade, and pick up the dropped toy. Never chase or pry the mouth.
steps.expect: the toy hits the ground within a couple seconds of the cue.

steps.action: **Restart instantly.** Throw the toy you now hold; the fast restart itself becomes the reward for the drop and the trade toy loses its value.
steps.expect: after several cycles, the dog starts dropping the toy at your feet unprompted to make the next throw happen.

steps.action: **Add structure as skill grows.** Ask for a sit before some throws; lengthen throws gradually; occasionally reward the return with a treat instead of a throw to keep the recall strong.
steps.expect: sit-throw-return-drop cycles running smoothly without chasing or shouting.

steps.action: **Stop before the dog does.** End after 10 to 20 throws, or at the first sign of heavy panting, wide flat tongue, lagging returns, or any limp. Fetch-obsessed dogs will run themselves into heatstroke; the human ends the game, always with a final treat and a calm minute of leash walking.
steps.expect: the dog is tired but recovers normal breathing within a few minutes.

recipes.verification: Across the last five throws of a session the dog returned to within arm's reach and released the toy on one "drop it" cue, the session ended on your initiative with the dog breathing normally within minutes, and the toy is put away until next time.

recipes.title: play frisbee
recipes.name: play-frisbee
recipes.goal: Throw and catch a flying disc with a partner using a flat backhand release and safe two-hand catches.

steps.action: **Face the target.** Stand sideways enough that the throwing shoulder points across your body.
steps.expect: the partner is visible and the throwing lane is clear.

steps.action: **Grip the disc for backhand.** Put the thumb on top, fingers curled under the rim, and index knuckle near the edge.
steps.expect: the disc feels secure but the wrist can snap.

steps.action: **Hold it level.** Keep the outer edge neither tipped up nor down.
steps.expect: the top of the disc looks like a flat plate.

steps.action: **Aim at chest height.** Pick a point on the partner's torso rather than the sky.
steps.expect: the throw has a clear target and safe height.

steps.action: **Step and pull across.** Step toward the target while drawing the disc from the far side of the body to the release point.
steps.expect: hips and shoulders turn smoothly, not with a wild arm swing.

steps.action: **Release flat with spin.** Snap the wrist and let the disc leave from a level hand.
steps.expect: the disc spins fast and starts on a straight line.

steps.action: **Follow through.** Let the throwing hand continue toward the target.
steps.expect: the arm finishes forward and the body stays balanced.

steps.action: **Prepare to catch.** The receiver bends knees, keeps eyes on the disc, and moves feet before reaching.
steps.expect: the disc arrives in front of the body, not beside the face.

steps.action: **Catch safely.** [BRANCH: pancake catch | two-hand rim catch] clap the disc between palms, or catch opposite rim edges with two hands.
steps.expect: the disc stops without hitting fingers hard.

steps.action: **Reset distance.** Move closer if throws wobble, farther if five throws arrive cleanly.
steps.expect: both players get repeatable catches.

recipes.verification: The pair completes five throws where the disc flies mostly flat, reaches catchable chest height, and is caught with two hands or a pancake catch.

recipes.title: play go fish
recipes.name: play-go-fish
recipes.goal: Play Go Fish by asking for ranks, collecting books of four, and ending with the most books.

steps.action: **Deal the hands.** Deal seven cards each for two or three players, or five cards each for four or more players.
steps.expect: every player has the agreed starting count.

steps.action: **Place the pond.** Put the remaining deck face down in the center.
steps.expect: the draw pile is reachable by all players.

steps.action: **Start the turn.** The player left of the dealer asks one other player for a rank they already hold.
steps.expect: the request is legal because the asker has at least one card of that rank.

steps.action: **Give matching cards.** If asked, hand over all cards of that rank.
steps.expect: the asker receives every matching card from that player.

steps.action: **Continue after a hit.** The asker takes another turn after receiving one or more cards.
steps.expect: successful asking keeps control.

steps.action: **Say go fish.** If the asked player has none, they say "go fish" and the asker draws one card.
steps.expect: a new card enters the asker's hand.

steps.action: **Play a drawn match.** If the drawn card is the requested rank, the asker shows it and goes again.
steps.expect: a lucky draw extends the turn.

steps.action: **Make books.** Place four of the same rank face up in front of you as soon as you collect them.
steps.expect: completed books leave your hand and count as points.

steps.action: **End the game.** [BRANCH: pond remains | pond empty] keep drawing while cards remain, or play out hands when the pond is empty.
steps.expect: the game ends when all books are made or no legal play remains.

recipes.verification: All completed books are face up, no cards remain in play, and the player with the most books is declared the winner.

recipes.title: play hangman
recipes.name: play-hangman
recipes.goal: Players run a fair word-guessing game where one player chooses a secret word and the other guesses letters before the drawing is completed.

steps.action: **Choose a fair word.** Pick a word or short phrase the guesser could reasonably know.
steps.expect: chooser can define and spell it.

steps.action: **Draw blanks.** Write one blank for each letter, leaving spaces or slashes between words.
steps.expect: guesser sees word length but not letters.

steps.action: **Draw the gallows.** Sketch the base and post, or choose another countdown drawing.
steps.expect: there is a clear wrong-guess track.

steps.action: **Guess one letter.** Guesser says a single unused letter.
steps.expect: both players know whether it has been guessed before.

steps.action: **Reveal or mark.** Fill every matching blank, or add one body part for a miss.
steps.expect: the board changes after each valid guess.

steps.action: **Track used letters.** Write incorrect and correct guessed letters off to the side.
steps.expect: repeats are easy to spot.

steps.action: **Use strategy.** Guess common vowels and consonants, then infer word patterns.
steps.expect: guesses become more targeted.

steps.action: **End the round.** [BRANCH: all blanks filled, guesser wins | drawing completed, chooser reveals word]
steps.expect: result is clear to both players.

recipes.verification: The final board either has every letter filled before the wrong-guess limit or shows the completed countdown with the secret word revealed.

recipes.title: play hopscotch
recipes.name: play-hopscotch
recipes.goal: Play a fair round of hopscotch by drawing a court, tossing a marker, hopping the pattern, and taking turns.

steps.action: **Draw the court.** Make numbered boxes from 1 to 10, mixing single boxes and side-by-side pairs.
steps.expect: the court has a start end, a turn-around end, and numbers that are easy to read.

steps.action: **Pick the marker.** Use something flat enough to stay put and soft enough not to bounce far.
steps.expect: the marker can land inside a square without rolling across lines.

steps.action: **Set the turn order.** Decide who goes first and whether touching a line counts as a miss.
steps.expect: every player knows the house rules before the first toss.

steps.action: **Toss to square 1.** Stand behind the start line and throw the marker underhand into the first square.
steps.expect: the marker rests inside square 1 and does not touch a boundary line.

steps.action: **Hop out, skipping the marker square.** Hop on one foot in single boxes and land with one foot in each paired box.
steps.expect: you pass square 1 without stepping on it or losing balance.

steps.action: **Turn at the top.** At the last box or pair, pivot carefully and prepare to come back.
steps.expect: you face the start line without stepping outside the court.

steps.action: **Pick up the marker on the return.** Stop in the square before the marker, bend, pick it up, then hop over that square.
steps.expect: marker is in hand and your foot never lands in its square.

steps.action: **Finish the pass.** Hop back over the start line and step out of the court.
steps.expect: the turn is complete with no line touch, missed square, or second foot in a single box.

steps.action: **Advance the target.** On the next successful turn, toss to the next number. [BRANCH: success | miss]
steps.expect: success moves your target up one number, while a miss passes play to the next person.

steps.action: **Win by clearing all squares.** Keep rotating turns until a player completes the highest number.
steps.expect: the winner has finished every numbered target in order.

recipes.verification: A completed turn has a legal toss, correct hop pattern, marker pickup, and return over the start line without a foul.

recipes.title: play i spy
recipes.name: play-i-spy
recipes.goal: Play a fair round of I Spy where players take turns giving clues about visible objects and guessing them.

steps.action: **Set the play area.** Choose a room, car view, park bench view, or waiting area that all players can see.
steps.expect: everyone knows what counts as visible.

steps.action: **Pick the first spy.** Choose the youngest player, rotate clockwise, or let the last winner start.
steps.expect: one person is responsible for the secret object.

steps.action: **Choose a fair object.** The spy silently picks something visible long enough for others to inspect.
steps.expect: the object is real and currently in the shared view.

steps.action: **Give the classic clue.** Say, "I spy with my little eye something..." followed by a color, shape, first letter, texture, or category.
steps.expect: the clue narrows the field without naming the object.

steps.action: **Tune clue difficulty by age.** [BRANCH: young child | older child | mixed ages] use color and size for younger players, letters or functions for older players, and multiple clues for mixed ages.
steps.expect: guessers have a reasonable chance.

steps.action: **Take guesses in turn.** Each player makes one guess per turn, with no grabbing or pointing into another player's face.
steps.expect: guesses move around the group fairly.

steps.action: **Add clues if stuck.** After three wrong rounds, give another true clue such as location, material, or use.
steps.expect: the answer becomes easier without changing.

steps.action: **Reveal and rotate.** When someone guesses correctly, show the object and make that player the next spy.
steps.expect: everyone agrees what the object was.

steps.action: **Use car-trip rules if moving.** Pick objects inside the car or things that stay visible long enough, such as "something blue in the car."
steps.expect: the game does not depend on objects already passed.

recipes.verification: A round succeeds when a guesser identifies the exact visible object and the next spy begins a new round.

recipes.title: play jacks
recipes.name: play-jacks
recipes.goal: Play a basic game of jacks by scattering the jacks, bouncing the ball once, and picking up sets from onesies through tens.

steps.action: **Set the play area.** Clear a flat space about an arm's reach wide and remove objects the ball could roll under.
steps.expect: the ball can bounce and be retrieved easily.

steps.action: **Scatter the jacks.** Hold all ten jacks a few inches above the surface and let them fall naturally.
steps.expect: the jacks spread out without leaving the play area.

steps.action: **Start onesies.** Toss the ball up, let it bounce once, pick up one jack, and catch the ball before it bounces again.
steps.expect: one jack is collected cleanly.

steps.action: **Continue the set.** Repeat until all ten jacks have been picked up one at a time.
steps.expect: the player completes onesies or loses the turn on a foul.

steps.action: **Move to higher numbers.** [BRANCH: twos-through-tens | beginner-repeat] Pick up two per bounce for twosies, then three, and so on, or repeat onesies for practice.
steps.expect: the target number for each turn is clear.

steps.action: **Call fouls fairly.** End the turn if the ball bounces twice, a wrong number of jacks is picked up, another jack is moved, or the ball is not caught.
steps.expect: play passes to the next player without argument.

steps.action: **Resume from the level missed.** On the next turn, restart the same number set rather than going back to onesies unless house rules say so.
steps.expect: progress through onesies to tens stays trackable.

recipes.verification: The game is verified when players can complete or fairly foul turns using the agreed pickup number from onesies toward tens.

recipes.title: play marbles
recipes.name: play-marbles
recipes.goal: Players draw a ring, shoot marbles knuckle-down, and take turns trying to knock target marbles out under agreed rules.

steps.action: **Draw the ring.** Make a circle 3 to 10 feet wide, scaled to player skill.
steps.expect: all players can see the boundary.

steps.action: **Set target marbles.** Place marbles in a cross, cluster, or center pile inside the ring.
steps.expect: targets are reachable but not touching the edge.

steps.action: **Choose rules.** [BRANCH: keepers, winners keep knocked-out marbles | friendlies, all marbles return after game]
steps.expect: no one is surprised by stakes.

steps.action: **Pick shooting order.** Flip a coin, lag toward a line, or let youngest go first.
steps.expect: turn order is agreed.

steps.action: **Shoot knuckle-down.** Rest a knuckle on the ground, tuck the shooter against a finger, and flick with the thumb.
steps.expect: the shooter leaves from inside or behind the agreed line.

steps.action: **Score a hit.** If a target marble leaves the ring, collect it or set it aside by the rules.
steps.expect: boundary result is visible.

steps.action: **Continue turns.** [BRANCH: shooter stays in ring, shoot from there next turn | shooter leaves ring, shoot from start line]
steps.expect: next position is clear.

steps.action: **End the game.** Stop when all target marbles are out or players reach the agreed round limit.
steps.expect: winner is the player with the most scored marbles.

recipes.verification: The ring is marked, turns were taken with knuckle-down shots, and the final score matches the marbles knocked out under the agreed rules.

recipes.title: play solitaire
recipes.name: play-solitaire
recipes.goal: Play Klondike solitaire by building tableau stacks, moving aces to foundations, and recognizing when the game is stuck.

steps.action: **Lay the tableau.** Deal seven columns from left to right, with one card in the first column through seven in the last.
steps.expect: the columns form a staircase of card counts.

steps.action: **Turn top cards face up.** Flip only the top card of each column.
steps.expect: seven visible cards are available for play.

steps.action: **Place the stock.** Put the remaining deck face down above the tableau, leaving space for a waste pile and four foundations.
steps.expect: the layout has all working areas.

steps.action: **Move aces up.** Send any exposed ace to an empty foundation spot.
steps.expect: each ace starts a suit pile.

steps.action: **Build down in color.** Move face-up cards onto the next higher rank of the opposite color.
steps.expect: a red 7 can sit on a black 8, and similar moves are legal.

steps.action: **Move stacks.** Move a face-up sequence together if it already alternates colors and descends by rank.
steps.expect: the whole legal run lands on a matching destination.

steps.action: **Fill empty columns.** Move only a king, or a stack headed by a king, into an empty tableau column.
steps.expect: empty spaces become useful without breaking the rules.

steps.action: **Turn the stock.** [BRANCH: draw one | draw three] reveal waste cards by the chosen rule and play the top available waste card.
steps.expect: new cards enter play without changing the tableau illegally.

steps.action: **Stop when stuck.** If no tableau, waste, or foundation move exists, turn through the stock until a move appears or the cycle repeats.
steps.expect: you either find progress or identify a lost position.

recipes.verification: The game is successful if all 52 cards end on the four suit foundations from ace through king.

recipes.title: play the license plate game
recipes.name: play-the-license-plate-game
recipes.goal: A group plays the license plate game on a trip with clear rules, fair scoring, and enough variants to keep the back seat from becoming a courtroom.

steps.action: **Pick the target.** [BRANCH: states game | alphabet game | numbers game] choose states for long trips, alphabet for shorter drives, numbers for heavy traffic.
steps.expect: everyone knows what counts.

steps.action: **Set the driver rule.** The driver may call plates only when safe, or may be the judge instead of a player.
steps.expect: no one asks the driver to stare at bumpers.

steps.action: **Define a valid spot.** Count only real license plates seen with eyes, not remembered sightings or plates in ads.
steps.expect: every point comes from the current trip.

steps.action: **Call it clearly.** Say the state, letter, or number out loud before another player does.
steps.expect: the group hears the claim.

steps.action: **Record contested finds.** Write down rare states or hard letters immediately.
steps.expect: the score does not depend on heroic memory.

steps.action: **Use fair scoring.** One point per new state, letter, or number, with ties allowed for simultaneous calls.
steps.expect: arguments end at the rule, not at volume.

steps.action: **Add variants when needed.** Try first-to-Z, all states, vanity plate phrases, or team play. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* unsafe distraction cannot be undone, so passengers handle spotting and recording while the driver drives.
steps.expect: the game stays lively without becoming chaotic.

steps.action: **Declare the finish.** End at the destination, rest stop, or completed list.
steps.expect: a winner or shared completed list is recognized.

recipes.verification: At the agreed endpoint, the group has a checklist or accepted score produced under the rules chosen at the start.

recipes.title: play thumb war
recipes.name: play-thumb-war
recipes.goal: You can play a fair thumb war with the standard grip, chant, pin, and agreed rules.

steps.action: **Make the grip.** Face your opponent, hook the four fingers of your right hands together, and leave thumbs upright.
steps.expect: both thumbs can move freely above the joined hands.

steps.action: **Set fair rules.** Agree that elbows stay still, finger hooks do not squeeze painfully, and a pin must last three counts.
steps.expect: both players know what counts before the round starts.

steps.action: **Say the chant.** Move thumbs side to side while saying, "One, two, three, four, I declare a thumb war."
steps.expect: both thumbs begin from neutral after the chant.

steps.action: **Probe for position.** Circle, feint, and lift your thumb to tempt the other thumb into reaching.
steps.expect: the contest is timing-based, not just pushing.

steps.action: **Go for the pin.** Press your thumb across the opponent's thumb when it extends too far. [BRANCH: clean pin | disputed pin] Count aloud for clean pins; reset disputed pins.
steps.expect: a clear hold starts the count.

steps.action: **Hold for three.** Keep steady pressure without twisting the wrist or squeezing fingers.
steps.expect: the opponent's thumb stays pinned through "one, two, three."

steps.action: **Reset politely.** Release immediately after a win or a stop call, shake out hands, and offer another round.
steps.expect: both players want to keep playing.

recipes.verification: A round begins with the chant, one player pins the other's thumb for a clear three-count, and both players agree the grip stayed fair.

recipes.title: press flowers
recipes.name: press-flowers
recipes.goal: Flowers flattened and dried to paper thinness with their color largely intact, ready to mount on cards, in frames, or in a journal. Active work is under an hour; the press itself takes two to four weeks.

steps.action: **Pick in the late morning of a dry day.** Wait until dew has evaporated; surface moisture is the main cause of browning and mold. Choose blooms just fully opened, not fading. Cut with a bit of stem.
steps.expect: petals dry to the touch, no browning edges, no insects hiding in the center.

steps.action: **Prepare each flower flat.** [BRANCH: flat-faced flower → press whole, face down | thick flower (rose, carnation) → split it in half through the stem with scissors, or press individual petals] Snip off bulky green backing parts that would tent the petals.
steps.expect: each specimen lies nearly flat on the table on its own.

steps.action: **Arrange between paper.** Fold a sheet of paper in half, lay flowers inside with no two touching, and shape petals with the tweezers exactly as you want them forever. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* petals dry in whatever position they are pressed; overlapped or folded petals cannot be unfolded later.
steps.expect: every petal splayed, nothing overlapping, layout final.

steps.action: **Load the book.** Place the paper folder deep inside the heavy book with at least a centimeter of pages on each side to buffer moisture, then close it and stack the extra weight on top. Label a sticky note with the date and page.
steps.expect: the loaded book sits flat under weight on a dry shelf; date noted.

steps.action: **Change the paper after 3 to 4 days.** Open carefully, lift each flower with tweezers (they are limp and tear-prone now), and transfer to fresh dry paper in the same book. This single swap prevents most mold and browning.
steps.expect: the old paper shows faint damp shadows; flowers still colorful, not slimy or spotted.

steps.action: **Press undisturbed for 2 to 4 weeks total.** Thin flowers finish in 2 weeks; split thick ones need 4. Resist peeking, since every opening risks shifting petals.
steps.expect: on opening, flowers are paper-thin, dry, and stiff, and lift off cleanly.

steps.action: **Mount.** Handle only with tweezers. Apply glue in pin-head dots to the flower's back (stem line and center, not the petal tips), place on the card or backing, cover with clean paper, and weight for an hour.
steps.expect: the flower is bonded flat with no glue showing at the edges.

recipes.verification: Each flower is dry, stiff, and translucent-thin, holds its color, shows no brown or fuzzy patches, and either lies loose ready for storage or is glued flat to its backing with no visible adhesive.

recipes.title: press leaves and flowers
recipes.name: press-leaves-and-flowers
recipes.goal: Press dry leaves and flowers flat between absorbent paper so they can be mounted for a craft, journal, or collection.

steps.action: **Pick dry specimens.** Choose leaves and flowers that are fresh, thin, and not muddy or wet.
steps.expect: the pieces feel dry to the touch and are not already wilting into mush.

steps.action: **Prepare the paper layers.** Place one sheet of absorbent paper inside a book or between two flat boards.
steps.expect: the pressing surface is clean and ready before arranging begins.

steps.action: **Arrange the shapes.** Lay each leaf or flower flat with space between pieces, spreading petals and turning the best side up.
steps.expect: no specimen overlaps another or folds under itself.

steps.action: **Cover and close.** Add a second paper sheet, close the book slowly, and keep the pages from sliding.
steps.expect: the specimens stay in position as pressure begins.

steps.action: **Add weight.** [BRANCH: book | board-stack] Use a heavy book alone for small pieces or boards plus weights for larger batches.
steps.expect: even pressure covers the full page.

steps.action: **Wait for drying.** Leave the press undisturbed for two to four weeks, checking only if paper feels damp and needs replacement.
steps.expect: moisture leaves slowly without mold or curled edges.

steps.action: **Mount the pressed pieces.** Lift with tweezers or fingertips, then attach with tiny dots of glue, tape corners, or photo mounts.
steps.expect: the finished leaf or flower lies flat on the chosen backing.

recipes.verification: The pressing is verified when the mounted specimen is fully dry, flat, intact, and attached without visible damp spots.

recipes.title: read sheet music basics
recipes.name: read-sheet-music-basics
recipes.goal: Read a simple treble-clef melody by identifying note names, basic rhythms, and measure boundaries.

steps.action: **Find the clef and staff.** Look for the treble clef and count the five lines from bottom to top.
steps.expect: the staff is oriented and the clef is known.

steps.action: **Name the line notes.** Use E, G, B, D, F from bottom line to top line.
steps.expect: notes sitting on lines can be named.

steps.action: **Name the space notes.** Use F, A, C, E from bottom space to top space.
steps.expect: notes sitting between lines can be named.

steps.action: **Mark difficult notes lightly.** Pencil names only above notes you cannot recognize quickly.
steps.expect: the page remains readable without every note being labeled.

steps.action: **Read rhythm shapes.** Identify whole, half, quarter, and eighth notes or rests in the piece.
steps.expect: each symbol has an approximate count value.

steps.action: **Tap the rhythm.** Clap or tap through one measure at a steady slow pulse.
steps.expect: the notes and rests fit inside the measure.

steps.action: **Play or sing slowly.** Move through the melody one measure at a time, saying note names if needed.
steps.expect: pitch order and rhythm begin to match the printed page.

recipes.verification: You can name the notes and clap the rhythm of at least four consecutive measures, then play or sing them slowly in the printed order.

recipes.title: record a podcast at home
recipes.name: record-a-podcast-at-home
recipes.goal: Record a clear short podcast segment at home with understandable speech, steady levels, and a usable audio file.

steps.action: **Pick the quietest room.** Choose a space with soft furnishings and turn off fans, alerts, and noisy appliances.
steps.expect: the room sounds dull and quiet when you pause.

steps.action: **Place the microphone close.** Position the mic 10 to 20 cm from your mouth and slightly off to the side.
steps.expect: speech sounds present without loud breath pops.

steps.action: **Set recording levels.** Speak at your real volume and adjust gain so peaks stay below clipping.
steps.expect: the meter moves strongly but does not hit red.

steps.action: **Record a test.** Capture 20 seconds of intro, silence, and normal speech.
steps.expect: playback is clear through headphones and background noise is acceptable.

steps.action: **Record the segment.** Follow the outline, leave short pauses after mistakes, and keep your mouth distance steady.
steps.expect: the take contains all planned points with visible pauses for edits.

steps.action: **Capture room tone.** Record 10 seconds of silence in the same position.
steps.expect: a clean noise sample is available for smoothing edits.

steps.action: **Save with a clear name.** Export or save the file with topic and date in the filename.
steps.expect: the recording can be found and played outside the recording app.

recipes.verification: The exported audio file plays from start to finish, speech is easy to understand through headphones, and no section clips or disappears.

recipes.title: ride a bike
recipes.name: ride-a-bike
recipes.goal: You can start, balance, pedal, steer, and stop a bicycle on flat ground without a helper holding the bike.

steps.action: **Set the bike for learning.** Lower the seat so your feet can dab the ground, check tire pressure, test both brakes, and remove the pedals if you can do so safely. [BRANCH: pedals come off | pedals stay on] Use a pedal wrench for removal, or keep them on and place your feet wide enough to avoid scraping.
steps.expect: the bike rolls freely, stops on command, and feels low enough to step off.

steps.action: **Practice brake stops before speed.** Walk the bike, squeeze the brake levers gently, then harder, feeling which lever controls which wheel. Avoid grabbing only the front brake.
steps.expect: you can stop the bike while walking without skidding or pitching forward.

steps.action: **Balance-glide with both feet.** Sit on the seat, push with both feet, lift them for one second, then put them down again. Look 10 to 20 m ahead, not at the front wheel.
steps.expect: short straight glides that end calmly with feet down.

steps.action: **Stretch the glide.** Push, lift both feet, and steer tiny corrections by leaning and turning the bars slightly. Repeat until you can glide for 5 to 10 m.
steps.expect: the bike tracks forward while your shoulders stay loose.

steps.action: **Add pedals when balance is real.** Reinstall pedals if removed, set one pedal high at about 2 o'clock, press it down to launch, then place the other foot on its pedal.
steps.expect: the bike moves from a stopped start without a running shove.

steps.action: **Pedal while looking ahead.** Keep light pressure on the bars, pedal smoothly, and aim for a distant point. Speed helps balance, but sprinting does not.
steps.expect: several pedal strokes in a line without staring down.

steps.action: **Turn wide and slow.** Make large circles in both directions, keeping your inside shoulder relaxed and your eyes toward the exit of the turn.
steps.expect: turns widen or tighten on purpose, not by panic.

steps.action: **Stop under control.** Coast, squeeze both brakes progressively, place one foot down as the bike slows, then step off.
steps.expect: a complete stop without jumping clear.

recipes.verification: On flat, car-free ground, you start from stopped, ride 20 m, make a wide turn, brake smoothly, and put one foot down without falling.

recipes.title: roll up a sleeping bag
recipes.name: roll-up-a-sleeping-bag
recipes.goal: Pack a sleeping bag neatly by zipping, flattening, pushing out air, and either rolling from the foot or using a stuff sack.

steps.action: **Empty and shake out.** Remove every item from the bag and shake loose dirt away from the zipper.
steps.expect: the bag is empty, dry enough to pack, and free of gritty debris.

steps.action: **Zip and align.** Zip the bag most or all of the way closed and line up the edges.
steps.expect: the bag forms one flat shape instead of a loose blanket.

steps.action: **Flatten the air.** Press from head toward foot with forearms or knees to move trapped air out.
steps.expect: the bag becomes thinner before rolling starts.

steps.action: **Roll from the foot.** Start at the foot end and roll tightly toward the head, pushing air forward as you go.
steps.expect: the roll stays narrow and firm instead of bulging.

steps.action: **Strap the roll.** Wrap built-in straps or separate straps around the roll and tighten evenly.
steps.expect: the roll holds its shape when lifted.

steps.action: **Use the stuff-sack method if preferred.** [BRANCH: roll | stuff-sack] For many backpacking bags, stuff the foot in first and feed fabric steadily rather than rolling.
steps.expect: the bag fills the sack without stressing one seam.

steps.action: **Store correctly.** Pack for travel now, then loosen or hang the bag at home if storage will last more than a short trip.
steps.expect: the bag is compact for transport and not left compressed long-term.

recipes.verification: The sleeping bag is verified when it is empty, dry enough for travel, secured in its straps or sack, and not under long-term compression.

recipes.title: shoot a short video on your phone
recipes.name: shoot-a-short-video-on-your-phone
recipes.goal: Shoot a short phone video with a clear subject, stable framing, usable sound, and enough coverage to edit.

steps.action: **Choose the video shape.** Decide horizontal for screens or vertical for social stories before recording.
steps.expect: all clips share the same orientation.

steps.action: **Clean the lens and frame.** Wipe the lens, then place the subject away from clutter and strong backlight.
steps.expect: the preview looks clear and the subject is easy to see.

steps.action: **Record a steady wide shot.** Hold the phone with two hands or brace it for 10 seconds.
steps.expect: the scene context is captured without wobble.

steps.action: **Record a medium shot.** Move closer and film the subject or action for another 10 seconds.
steps.expect: the main action is visible and fills more of the frame.

steps.action: **Record close details.** Film hands, tools, textures, or reaction shots.
steps.expect: the video has cutaway clips for editing.

steps.action: **Capture usable sound.** Move close enough for voices or record a few seconds of clean natural sound.
steps.expect: playback is understandable without maxing volume.

steps.action: **Review the clips.** Play the first and last seconds of each clip before leaving.
steps.expect: the files are saved, correctly oriented, and not accidentally blocked by a finger.

recipes.verification: The phone contains at least three usable clips in the same orientation: a wide shot, a medium shot, and a close detail shot with acceptable image and sound.

recipes.title: shoot in manual mode
recipes.name: shoot-in-manual-mode
recipes.goal: Take a correctly exposed photograph by setting aperture, shutter speed, and ISO yourself.

steps.action: **Switch to manual exposure.** Turn the mode dial or app control to M or Manual.
steps.expect: aperture, shutter speed, and ISO can be changed independently.

steps.action: **Set the ISO low.** Start at ISO 100 or 200 in bright light, or ISO 800 indoors.
steps.expect: the image preview or meter responds without adding obvious noise.

steps.action: **Choose the aperture for depth.** Use a low f-number for blurrier background or f/5.6 to f/8 for more depth.
steps.expect: the subject area matches the amount of sharpness you want.

steps.action: **Choose a safe shutter speed.** Set at least 1/125 second for hand-held still subjects, faster for motion.
steps.expect: hand shake and subject movement are unlikely to blur the frame.

steps.action: **Balance the meter.** Adjust shutter speed, aperture, or ISO until the exposure meter sits near zero.
steps.expect: the preview or test frame is neither very dark nor blown out.

steps.action: **Take a test frame.** Photograph the subject and inspect the histogram or highlight warning if available.
steps.expect: important tones fit inside the range without clipped highlights.

steps.action: **Make one creative adjustment.** Change one control on purpose, then compensate with another control to keep exposure similar.
steps.expect: the brightness stays controlled while depth, motion, or noise changes.

recipes.verification: The final image was taken in manual mode and has the intended brightness, sharp subject detail, and a deliberate aperture, shutter speed, and ISO combination.

recipes.title: shuffle cards
recipes.name: shuffle-cards
recipes.goal: Shuffle a standard deck so the cards are mixed, squared, and still easy to handle.

steps.action: **Square the deck.** Tap the short and long edges on the table until the cards form one block.
steps.expect: the deck sits flat with no corners sticking far out.

steps.action: **Choose a shuffle.** [BRANCH: riffle | overhand] use the riffle for stronger mixing, or the overhand for gentler handling.
steps.expect: you have one clear method for this pass.

steps.action: **Split for a riffle.** Hold half the deck in each hand, inner corners close together, thumbs on the inside edges.
steps.expect: two roughly equal packets meet at one corner.

steps.action: **Release the corners.** Bend only enough for the thumb edges to spring down and interlace.
steps.expect: cards fall in small alternating groups instead of two solid blocks.

steps.action: **Bridge lightly.** Push the interlaced cards inward, arch them just enough to relax together, then let them settle.
steps.expect: one joined deck forms without sharp creases.

steps.action: **Use an overhand pass.** Hold the deck in one hand and pull small packets from the top into the other hand.
steps.expect: several small groups transfer and change order.

steps.action: **Repeat the mix.** Do three to seven passes, alternating riffle and overhand if desired.
steps.expect: top and bottom cards change between passes.

steps.action: **Square and offer.** Tap all four edges, then place the deck where play can continue.
steps.expect: the deck is neat, flat, and ready to cut or deal.

recipes.verification: The deck is squared, no card is visibly damaged, and several cards from the original top or bottom are no longer together.

recipes.title: skip a stone
recipes.name: skip-a-stone
recipes.goal: A stone skipped across calm water for three or more bounces, via the three variables that actually matter: stone selection, spin, and a low flat launch angle.

steps.action: **Select the stone like it matters, because it is most of the result.** Flat, smooth, palm-sized, roughly round or triangular, about the weight of a large cookie; a slight thickness (not wafer-thin) carries momentum. Collect three or four candidates before throwing anything.
steps.expect: a small arsenal of flat stones; the perfect one gets saved for when your form warms up.

steps.action: **Grip for spin.** Index finger curled along the stone's edge, thumb on top, the flat faces parallel to the ground; the finger along the rim is the spin engine.
steps.expect: a grip where a wrist flick would clearly rotate the stone like a frisbee.

steps.action: **Set the stance low and sideways.** Feet sideways to the water like a discus thrower, knees bent, throwing shoulder dropped; the whole art is getting the release close to the water.
steps.expect: your throwing hand at knee height or lower at the release point.

steps.action: **Throw flat and fast with a hard wrist snap.** Sidearm swing, release when the stone points at the water 5 to 10 meters out, snapping the wrist so the stone leaves spinning hard. The launch angle wants to be shallow: stone nearly parallel to the surface, striking at roughly 20 degrees.
steps.expect: a spinning, flat, fast stone; the first contact throws a small skip, not a plunge.

steps.action: **Read the failure and adjust one variable.** Single plunge: angle too steep, get lower and flatter. Skips but dies fast: more wrist snap (spin is what stabilizes it against tipping). Veers and rolls into the water: the stone wobbled at release, grip flatter and snap cleaner.
steps.expect: each throw diagnosing itself; bounce counts climbing across the arsenal from step 1.

steps.action: **Count generously and pass the skill on.** House rules everywhere: the pitty-pat finale counts. Teaching a kid the grip in step 2 is the traditional payment for the shoreline you used.
steps.expect: three-plus bounces on your better throws, and the small ceremony of a personal record acknowledged aloud.

recipes.verification: Your better throws bounce three or more times, you can name which variable (stone, spin, angle) each failed throw missed, the arc stayed clear of every living thing, and at least one bystander asked how you did it.

recipes.title: skip rope
recipes.name: skip-rope
recipes.goal: A person sizes a jump rope and performs steady basic skips using wrist turns, small jumps, and consistent timing.

steps.action: **Check space.** Stand where the rope can swing overhead and behind you without striking anything.
steps.expect: at least an arm's length of clear space on every side.

steps.action: **Size the rope.** Step on the rope center and pull handles upward.
steps.expect: handles reach roughly armpit height for a beginner.

steps.action: **Adjust if possible.** Shorten or lengthen the rope before jumping.
steps.expect: the rope clears the head and brushes the floor lightly, not heavily.

steps.action: **Set posture.** Stand tall with elbows near ribs and handles slightly forward of hips.
steps.expect: shoulders are relaxed and wrists can rotate freely.

steps.action: **Practice wrist turns.** Swing the rope beside the body or behind-to-front without jumping.
steps.expect: the rope moves from the wrists, not big arm circles.

steps.action: **Find the floor tap.** Swing once and listen for the rope to tap in front of the toes.
steps.expect: the tap happens just before the jump moment.

steps.action: **Jump small.** Hop only 2 to 4 cm as the rope reaches the toes.
steps.expect: the rope passes under both feet with little knee bend.

steps.action: **Reset after misses.** If the rope catches, stop, place it behind heels, and restart calmly.
steps.expect: form returns instead of turning into high jumps.

steps.action: **Link repetitions.** Aim for sets of 5, then 10, then 30 smooth skips.
steps.expect: breathing and rope rhythm become predictable.

steps.action: **Cool down.** Stop before calves or shins ache sharply and walk for a minute.
steps.expect: heart rate settles and legs feel worked, not strained.

recipes.verification: The person completes at least 10 consecutive basic skips with small jumps, wrist-driven turns, and no contact with nearby objects.

recipes.title: solve a crossword
recipes.name: solve-a-crossword
recipes.goal: Solve a crossword by filling sure answers first, using crossing letters, spotting the theme, and recognizing wordplay.

steps.action: **Scan the easy clues.** Fill answers you know immediately, especially short common words and proper names.
steps.expect: several entries appear without guessing.

steps.action: **Mark uncertain fills.** Write light letters or small notes for maybes.
steps.expect: doubtful answers look different from confirmed ones.

steps.action: **Use crossings.** For each blank, check the across and down letters that intersect it.
steps.expect: a guessed word either strengthens or starts to fail.

steps.action: **Look for the theme.** Read long clues and repeated clue patterns.
steps.expect: a trick or shared idea explains several answers.

steps.action: **Watch wordplay tells.** Clues ending with question marks, odd grammar, or tiny words often signal puns or indirect meanings.
steps.expect: literal readings give way to playful answers.

steps.action: **Fill by pattern.** Use known letters, word length, and clue tense or part of speech.
steps.expect: fewer words fit the available spaces.

steps.action: **Work the stuck corner.** [BRANCH: many crossings | few crossings] solve from crossings if available, or move elsewhere to collect letters.
steps.expect: the hard area gains at least one anchor.

steps.action: **Walk away briefly.** Stop for a few minutes when the same wrong idea repeats.
steps.expect: returning makes alternate meanings easier to see.

steps.action: **Clean the grid.** Erase failed guesses and write final answers clearly.
steps.expect: every filled entry agrees with its crossings.

recipes.verification: Every square is filled, each across and down answer satisfies its clue, and no crossing letters contradict each other.

recipes.title: solve a rubiks cube beginner
recipes.name: solve-a-rubiks-cube-beginner
recipes.goal: Solve a standard 3x3 Rubik's Cube using a beginner layer-by-layer method, with accuracy prioritized over speed.

steps.action: **Learn the notation.** Hold one face toward you and read moves as F front, B back, R right, L left, U up, D down; an apostrophe means counterclockwise.
steps.expect: you can follow a sequence like R U R' U' without changing the whole cube orientation by mistake.

steps.action: **Pick white as the first layer.** Put the white center on the up face and use the centers as fixed color labels.
steps.expect: white center is on top, and the side centers tell you the target side colors.

steps.action: **Build the white cross.** Move four white edge pieces around the white center, matching each edge's side color to its side center.
steps.expect: a white plus sign on top, and each white edge lines up with the matching side center.

steps.action: **Insert the white corners.** Put each white corner below its target slot, then repeat R U R' U' until it drops into place.
steps.expect: the whole white face is solved, and the first side row matches the centers.

steps.action: **Solve the middle layer edges.** Find a top-layer edge with no yellow, line its front color with the center, then use the right or left insertion sequence. [BRANCH: edge goes right | edge goes left]
steps.expect: two bottom layers begin forming without breaking the solved white layer.

steps.action: **Make the yellow cross.** Use F R U R' U' F' until the yellow edges form a line, L shape, or cross; hold the pattern correctly before repeating.
steps.expect: a yellow cross appears on the top face.

steps.action: **Orient the yellow corners.** Use R U R' U R U2 R' while holding the cube as instructed by your chosen beginner guide.
steps.expect: all four top stickers are yellow, even if the top layer pieces are not yet in their final spots.

steps.action: **Position the yellow corners.** Cycle unsolved corners until each corner belongs between its three matching centers.
steps.expect: every corner sits in the correct location, though some edges may still need cycling.

steps.action: **Position the yellow edges.** Use the final edge-cycling algorithm, repeating only after restoring the same front face.
steps.expect: all six faces show one solid color.

steps.action: **Reset your expectations about speed.** Time the solve only after you can finish without notes; beginner solves often take several minutes.
steps.expect: the cube is solved and you know which stage felt slow.

recipes.verification: All six faces are solid colors, and each face color matches its center piece.

recipes.title: solve a sudoku
recipes.name: solve-a-sudoku
recipes.goal: You can solve an easy Sudoku grid using singles, pencil candidates, and box-line elimination without guessing.

steps.action: **Read the givens.** Scan the grid and notice rows, columns, or boxes that are already crowded with numbers.
steps.expect: several areas look close to finished.

steps.action: **Scan for obvious singles.** For each empty cell in a crowded unit, ask what digits are missing and whether only one can fit.
steps.expect: at least one cell has a forced value on easy puzzles.

steps.action: **Place only certain numbers.** Write a digit large only when row, column, and box all agree.
steps.expect: every placed digit can be defended by the rules.

steps.action: **Pencil candidates.** In unresolved cells, write small possible digits after eliminating numbers already present in the same row, column, and box.
steps.expect: each empty cell has a short candidate list.

steps.action: **Find hidden singles.** In each row, column, and box, look for a digit that appears as a candidate in only one place.
steps.expect: some placements become forced even when a cell has multiple candidates.

steps.action: **Use box-line elimination.** If all candidates for a digit inside one box sit on the same row or column, remove that digit from the rest of that row or column outside the box.
steps.expect: candidate lists shrink without guessing.

steps.action: **Loop the logic.** [BRANCH: new single appears | no progress] If a single appears, place it and rescan; if no progress, recheck candidates for a missed elimination.
steps.expect: each solved number unlocks more cells.

steps.action: **Finish cleanly.** Fill the last cells only when they are forced, then inspect every row, column, and box.
steps.expect: no digit repeats in any unit.

recipes.verification: All 81 cells are filled, and each row, column, and 3 by 3 box contains the digits 1 through 9 exactly once.

recipes.title: spin a basketball on your finger
recipes.name: spin-a-basketball-on-your-finger
recipes.goal: You can toss a basketball with backspin, catch its center on one fingernail, and keep it spinning with light slaps from the free hand.

steps.action: **Mark the spin axis.** Hold the ball with a seam line vertical and imagine a pole running through the top and bottom.
steps.expect: you know where the top center should land on your finger.

steps.action: **Learn the backspin toss.** Hold the ball at chest height with both hands, thumbs behind it, and toss upward while snapping both wrists toward you.
steps.expect: the ball rises with clear backward rotation.

steps.action: **Catch on the fingernail.** Put your index finger under the falling center, nail facing up, and let the ball settle on the nail or fingertip.
steps.expect: the ball spins in place for a moment before sliding.

steps.action: **Keep the finger quiet.** Move the whole hand under the ball instead of poking at it.
steps.expect: the finger stays near the center axis rather than chasing the edge.

steps.action: **Add the free-hand slap.** While the ball spins, brush the side lightly in the direction of spin with the other hand. [BRANCH: gentle slap | hard slap] Gentle adds speed; hard knocks the axis off.
steps.expect: spin lasts longer without the ball jumping sideways.

steps.action: **Reset before it falls.** When the wobble grows, catch the ball with both hands instead of letting it drop.
steps.expect: controlled resets and fewer bruised knuckles.

steps.action: **Build the hold time.** Practice in rounds of ten tosses, counting only spins that balance for at least three seconds.
steps.expect: the best attempts stretch from brief balance to several seconds.

recipes.verification: The basketball spins balanced on one finger for five seconds, and you add at least one free-hand slap without dropping it.

recipes.title: stargaze without equipment
recipes.name: stargaze-without-equipment
recipes.goal: You have spent an hour under a night sky with fully dark-adapted eyes, identified at least two or three constellations or landmarks (and the Milky Way if the site allows), and returned safely.

steps.action: **Pick the night and site in advance.** Aim for new moon, clear sky, and the darkest reachable location; a light-pollution map (web search "light pollution map") ranks candidate sites.
steps.expect: a chosen spot, a time at least 90 minutes after sunset, and a plan for getting back.

steps.action: **Arrive and settle before switching off lights.** Lay out the blanket or recline the chair while you can still see; note trip hazards and the way out.
steps.expect: a stable, dry spot with an open view of most of the sky.

steps.action: **Kill every white light and start the dark-adaptation clock.** Phone on red/night mode face-down or pocketed. Full adaptation takes 20 to 30 minutes and a single glance at a white screen resets it.
steps.expect: over 20 minutes, faint stars keep appearing; the sky visibly "fills in".

steps.action: **Anchor yourself with one bright landmark.** [BRANCH: northern hemisphere (find the Big Dipper, follow the two pointer stars of its bowl to Polaris, which fixes north) | southern hemisphere (find the Southern Cross and its two pointer stars; extend the cross's long axis about 4.5 lengths toward the south celestial pole)]
steps.expect: you can point to a cardinal direction using stars alone.

steps.action: **Hop from the anchor to neighbors.** From the Dipper: arc along its handle to Arcturus ("arc to Arcturus"). Near Orion (winter/summer depending on hemisphere): his belt of three stars points down-left to Sirius, the brightest star in the sky.
steps.expect: two or three named patterns you can find again on demand.

steps.action: **Use averted vision on faint targets.** Look slightly to the side of a dim object (the Milky Way band, a faint cluster); the eye's periphery is far more light-sensitive than its center.
steps.expect: faint objects pop into view when you look just off them and fade when you stare directly.

steps.action: **Confirm doubtful identifications with the app, sparingly.** Hold the phone (red mode, minimum brightness) up to the sky only when stuck; planets give themselves away by not twinkling.
steps.expect: the app's overlay matches what you see; adaptation loss is minimal.

steps.action: **Pack out by red light or phone-at-minimum.** Sweep the spot for dropped items before leaving.
steps.expect: nothing left behind; safe route home.

recipes.verification: You can, without the app, point to a cardinal direction using the stars and re-locate at least two constellations or named stars you identified; your eyes reached full adaptation (faint stars visible that were invisible on arrival); you are home with all your gear.

recipes.title: start a sketchbook habit
recipes.name: start-a-sketchbook-habit
recipes.goal: Begin a repeatable sketchbook habit with a simple prompt, low friction tools, and a finished first page.

steps.action: **Choose the smallest commitment.** Set a timer for 5 to 10 minutes rather than planning a long drawing session.
steps.expect: the session feels easy to start today.

steps.action: **Date the first page.** Write the date in a corner and leave the rest open for marks.
steps.expect: the page becomes a record, not a test.

steps.action: **Pick one nearby subject.** Choose a mug, shoe, plant, key, or your own hand.
steps.expect: the subject is available without setup.

steps.action: **Draw the big shapes first.** Block in the overall silhouette using light simple lines.
steps.expect: the object fits on the page before details begin.

steps.action: **Add three observed details.** Draw only a rim, shadow, fold, label, texture, or edge change you can actually see.
steps.expect: the sketch has specific evidence from the subject.

steps.action: **Write one note.** Add a sentence about what was hard, interesting, or worth trying next.
steps.expect: the page gives direction for the next session.

steps.action: **Set tomorrow's trigger.** Leave the sketchbook and tool where you will see them.
steps.expect: the next session has no search or setup barrier.

recipes.verification: The sketchbook contains a dated first page with a drawn subject, at least three observed details, and a visible setup cue for the next session.

recipes.title: start a vinyl collection
recipes.name: start-a-vinyl-collection
recipes.goal: Start a small vinyl record collection with playable records, basic care habits, and spending limits.

steps.action: **Set a collecting focus.** Choose a genre, artist, era, local scene, cover-art theme, or personal favorite list.
steps.expect: browsing has a clear filter.

steps.action: **Set a spending limit.** Decide the maximum price for one record and for the first month.
steps.expect: impulse purchases have a boundary.

steps.action: **Inspect condition.** Check vinyl under light for scratches, warps, grime, and sleeve damage.
steps.expect: the record looks playable for the price.

steps.action: **Confirm the pressing basics.** Read the artist, title, format speed, and track list before buying.
steps.expect: the record is the album or single you actually want.

steps.action: **Clean before playing.** Brush dust off the record and check the stylus area is clean.
steps.expect: playback starts with less crackle and lower wear.

steps.action: **Store records upright.** Place records vertically in sleeves, not stacked flat.
steps.expect: the collection stands without bending or heat exposure.

steps.action: **Log the first records.** Write down artist, title, condition, price, and where you found it.
steps.expect: the collection has a simple inventory from the start.

recipes.verification: You own or have selected at least one record that matches your focus, fits your budget, is stored upright, and has condition notes in an inventory.

recipes.title: swim freestyle basics
recipes.name: swim-freestyle-basics
recipes.goal: You can swim a short length of basic freestyle with a horizontal body, steady kick, reaching pull, body rotation, and controlled side breathing.

steps.action: **Start with pool safety.** Enter shallow water, identify the wall and ladder, and agree with your supervisor when to stop a drill.
steps.expect: you know exactly how to stand, grab the wall, or get help.

steps.action: **Set the body line.** Push gently from the wall with arms extended, face down, eyes toward the pool floor, and body long.
steps.expect: a brief glide with hips near the surface.

steps.action: **Add a small kick.** Kick from the hips with loose knees and relaxed ankles, making small bubbles rather than big splashes.
steps.expect: forward movement without legs dropping.

steps.action: **Learn the reach-and-pull.** One arm reaches forward, catches water with the forearm, pulls past the ribs, then exits near the hip. Switch arms slowly.
steps.expect: each pull moves water backward and your body forward.

steps.action: **Rotate the body.** Roll the ribs and hips slightly with each reach, as if each shoulder takes a turn pointing upward.
steps.expect: the recovering arm clears the water more easily.

steps.action: **Practice side breathing at the wall.** Hold the wall, face down, exhale bubbles, rotate one ear toward the shoulder, sip air, then return face down.
steps.expect: breath happens by rotation, not by lifting the head.

steps.action: **Swim with a breathing pattern.** [BRANCH: breathe every 2 strokes | breathe every 3 strokes] Use every 2 for oxygen comfort, or every 3 for bilateral practice.
steps.expect: the rhythm stays calm for 5 to 10 m.

steps.action: **Connect the short swim.** Push off, kick, alternate pulls, rotate, breathe to the side, and stand before form collapses.
steps.expect: a short freestyle segment that ends under control.

recipes.verification: In a supervised pool, you swim 10 m of freestyle, breathe to the side at least twice, and stop by standing or holding the wall.

recipes.title: take a good group photo
recipes.name: take-a-good-group-photo
recipes.goal: A group photo where everyone is visible, lit, and has their eyes open, captured in under two minutes of wrangling — because the photographer's real job is logistics, not artistry.

steps.action: **Pick the spot for light and background, and announce it with authority.** Open shade or soft light beats harsh noon sun (squints) and beats backlight (silhouettes); background two steps behind the group, free of bins, strangers, and poles that grow from heads. Groups follow confident pointing.
steps.expect: the group assembling where you said, light on their faces, clean background.

steps.action: **Arrange by rows in seconds, not minutes.** Taller behind, shorter and seated in front, nobody hidden: the caller's line is "if you can't see the camera, it can't see you." Tighten gaps ("everyone one step in") — groups always stand too far apart, and closeness reads as warmth in the print.
steps.expect: two loose rows, every face with a clear line to the lens, shoulders angled slightly inward.

steps.action: **Frame with margin and hold the camera straight.** Everyone fully in frame with headroom and elbow room (cropping later beats amputating now), horizon level, camera at the front row's face height — not a low angle, which flatters no one in a group.
steps.expect: the whole group plus margin in a level frame.

steps.action: **Run the countdown protocol and take a burst.** Loud and scripted: "Looking here — three, two, one!" and shoot a burst or three quick frames on and after "one." Blinks cluster on the count; the frame after the laugh that follows is often the best photo of the set.
steps.expect: several frames per pose; at least one with all eyes open (the burst is the blink insurance).

steps.action: **Check the review honestly before releasing the group.** Zoom the faces: eyes, focus, nobody mid-sentence. Retake immediately if needed — "one more, Maya blinked!" costs ten seconds now and is impossible tomorrow.
steps.expect: a verified keeper before the group dissolves.

steps.action: **Get the photographer into one.** Swap shooters, use the timer (camera propped or on a ledge, ten seconds, run), or hand the phone to a passerby with the frame pre-composed ("just press this"). The person who organized the photo belongs in the photo.
steps.expect: at least one frame containing everyone, including you.

steps.action: **Share while the group is still assembled.** The group chat drop or airdrop in the moment; the photo everyone waits three weeks for is the photo nobody gets.
steps.expect: the photo in everyone's possession before the goodbyes.

recipes.verification: Faces lit and visible, background clean, at least one all-eyes-open frame verified by zoom before the group dispersed, the photographer appears in one, and the file left your phone into the group's hands.

recipes.title: take a long exposure photo
recipes.name: take-a-long-exposure-photo
recipes.goal: Take a long-exposure photo that keeps static objects sharp while motion turns into blur, trails, or smooth texture.

steps.action: **Stabilize the camera.** Mount it on a tripod or place it on a firm surface.
steps.expect: the frame stays fixed when you release your hands.

steps.action: **Compose with static anchors.** Include buildings, rocks, rails, or trees along with the moving subject.
steps.expect: the photo will show contrast between sharp and blurred elements.

steps.action: **Set a slow shutter.** Start around 1 to 4 seconds for traffic or water, longer if the scene is dark.
steps.expect: moving subjects have time to streak or soften.

steps.action: **Lower sensitivity.** Use low ISO and a small aperture if available to avoid overexposure.
steps.expect: the preview or meter stays within a usable brightness range.

steps.action: **Use a timer or remote.** Trigger the shot without tapping during the exposure.
steps.expect: the camera starts after vibrations settle.

steps.action: **Review sharpness and blur.** Zoom into static objects and inspect the moving areas.
steps.expect: fixed objects are sharp while motion is visibly blurred.

steps.action: **Adjust and repeat.** Lengthen shutter for more blur or shorten it if the frame is too bright or chaotic.
steps.expect: the next frame moves closer to the intended effect.

recipes.verification: The final image contains at least one sharp static element and one intentionally blurred moving element, with exposure bright enough to read detail.

recipes.title: take a portrait photo
recipes.name: take-a-portrait-photo
recipes.goal: Create a flattering portrait with intentional light, clean background, sharp eyes, and a relaxed expression.

steps.action: **Choose soft light.** Place the subject beside a window or in open shade, facing slightly toward the brightest area.
steps.expect: the face is evenly lit without squinting or harsh nose shadows.

steps.action: **Clean the background.** Move clutter, bright objects, and poles away from behind the head.
steps.expect: the subject stands out as the clearest element in the frame.

steps.action: **Set the camera at eye level.** Hold the lens level with the subject's eyes and step back enough to avoid wide-angle distortion.
steps.expect: facial proportions look natural and the horizon does not tilt.

steps.action: **Focus on the near eye.** Tap the eye on a phone screen or use single-point autofocus on a camera.
steps.expect: the eye closest to the camera appears crisp.

steps.action: **Coach a small action.** Ask the subject to breathe out, turn the shoulders slightly, or look just beside the lens.
steps.expect: the pose looks relaxed instead of frozen.

steps.action: **Make three variations.** Take one close crop, one waist-up frame, and one environmental frame.
steps.expect: at least three usable compositions are available for review.

steps.action: **Review before leaving.** Zoom in on the eyes and check the edges of the frame.
steps.expect: the chosen image has sharp eyes, no unwanted background distractions, and comfortable expression.

recipes.verification: The final portrait has a consenting subject, sharp eyes, controlled light on the face, and no major background distraction touching the subject.

recipes.title: teach a dog to sit
recipes.name: teach-a-dog-to-sit
recipes.goal: The dog sits promptly on a single verbal cue or hand signal, without a treat visible, in everyday locations. Each training session is 3 to 5 minutes; most dogs get there in days of short sessions.

steps.action: **Charge the marker.** Say "yes" (or click) and immediately give a treat; repeat 5 to 10 times doing nothing else.
