steps.action: **Choose the shape.** [BRANCH: rounded | squoval | square] pick rounded for short nails, squoval for most everyday nails, or square only if corners do not catch.
steps.expect: a clear target shape before filing.

steps.action: **File in one direction.** Start at one side and stroke toward the center, then repeat from the other side toward the center. Do not saw back and forth.
steps.expect: length comes down gradually without white peeling layers.

steps.action: **Keep the file under the free edge.** Angle it slightly under the nail tip, not flat across the nail surface.
steps.expect: the edge shortens while the top of the nail stays intact.

steps.action: **Match the nails by sight.** Compare both hands with fingers relaxed and adjust only the longer or sharper edges.
steps.expect: nails look even enough without chasing perfect symmetry.

steps.action: **Smooth the edge.** Use the fine side of the file or a buffer block on the free edge only.
steps.expect: no scratchy points when you lightly brush the nail over fabric.

steps.action: **Stop before thinning.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* heavy filing across the nail plate removes protective layers until they grow out. Avoid filing the top surface unless smoothing one tiny snag.
steps.expect: the nail plate still feels firm, not bendy or hot.

steps.action: **Moisturize the nail folds.** Apply hand cream or cuticle oil around the nail and under the free edge.
steps.expect: skin around the nail feels comfortable, not tight.

recipes.verification: Each nail has a chosen shape, a smooth free edge that does not snag fabric, and no visible thinning or soreness from filing.

recipes.title: fix your sleep schedule
recipes.name: fix-your-sleep-schedule
recipes.goal: Sleep and wake times land within 30 minutes of a chosen target on most nights, achieved by anchoring a fixed wake time and shifting gradually, so mornings stop requiring heroics.

steps.action: **Fix the wake time first and hold it seven days a week.** The wake anchor drives the whole system; bedtime follows it. Weekend sleep-ins of 2+ hours are self-inflicted jet lag and undo the week's progress.
steps.expect: one wake time written down, same on Saturday as on Tuesday.

steps.action: **Shift toward the target gradually.** [BRANCH: current schedule is within an hour of target → jump straight to the target wake time | it is off by more → move the alarm 15-30 minutes earlier every 1-2 days until it lands] Do not attempt a 3-hour jump in one night; you will lie awake, conclude it failed, and quit.
steps.expect: each morning's alarm is only slightly earlier than yesterday's; each is achievable.

steps.action: **Get bright light within an hour of waking.** Ten to twenty minutes of outdoor daylight (even overcast beats indoor bulbs by an order of magnitude), or the bright lamp during breakfast. Morning light is the strongest lever that pulls the body clock earlier.
steps.expect: light exposure logged before the first hour ends; grogginess lifts faster than it did without it.

steps.action: **Put the alarm across the room and stand up at the first ring.** Getting vertical is the commitment point; snoozing trades fragmented, useless sleep for a groggier start.
steps.expect: feet on floor within a minute of the alarm; snooze not touched.

steps.action: **Protect the day: caffeine cutoff and no rescue naps after mid-afternoon.** Last caffeine 8+ hours before target bedtime; if a nap is unavoidable, keep it to 20 minutes and before 3 p.m. (see `daily/self-care/take-a-power-nap`).
steps.expect: normal sleep pressure building by evening instead of being drained by a 6 p.m. couch nap.

steps.action: **Dim the last two hours and set a screens-down time.** Lower the lights, warm-shift or shelve bright screens, and pick a wind-down routine (shower, reading, stretching) that starts at the same time nightly. Evening bright light pushes the clock later and cancels the morning's work.
steps.expect: the home is dim and the routine underway two hours before target bedtime.

steps.action: **Go to bed sleepy, not merely on schedule.** Get in bed at the target only if drowsy; if 20 minutes pass without sleep, get up, sit in dim light with something boring on paper, and return when heavy-eyed. Lying awake trains the bed as a place of frustration.
steps.expect: time in bed awake stays short; the bed stays associated with sleep.

steps.action: **Hold the anchor for two weeks before judging.** The wake time stays fixed through the rough first days; daytime sleepiness in days 2-4 is the adjustment working, not failing.
steps.expect: by days 7-10, waking shortly before the alarm and natural evening sleepiness near the target bedtime.

recipes.verification: Over the trailing week: wake time within 30 minutes of target on at least 6 of 7 days including the weekend, falling asleep within about 20 minutes of lights-out on most nights, and no naps after 3 p.m. Daytime alertness without heroic caffeine confirms the schedule has actually taken.

recipes.title: floss your teeth
recipes.name: floss-your-teeth
recipes.goal: The spaces between all teeth — where the brush doesn't reach — are cleaned once daily, without sawing your gums.

steps.action: **Dispense a working length.** String: ~45 cm, wound around each middle finger leaving ~5 cm taut between thumbs/indexes. Pick/interdental brush: inspect it's clean and intact.
steps.expect: a controllable taut segment or a sound tool.

steps.action: **Seesaw gently through each contact point.** Slide the floss between two teeth with a light back-and-forth *glide* — never snap it down (snapping cuts the gum).
steps.expect: floss passes the tight contact and reaches the gumline without a sting.

steps.action: **Hug each tooth in a C-shape and wipe.** Curve the floss against one tooth's side, slide gently *under* the gumline's edge, wipe up-and-down 2–3 times; then re-curve against the neighboring tooth and repeat before moving on.
steps.expect: each gap gets both of its walls wiped, not just a straight-down poke.

steps.action: **Advance to fresh floss as you go.** Unwind a clean section every few teeth (picks: rinse between areas).
steps.expect: you're not relocating one gap's plaque into the next.

steps.action: **Cover every gap systematically, including behind the last molars.** A fixed route (upper right → upper left → lower left → lower right) prevents skipped zones.
steps.expect: all gaps done in one pass, backmost surfaces included.

steps.action: **Rinse mouth, discard the floss, wash hands.**
steps.expect: debris out; floss in the bin (not the toilet — it clogs and it's plastic).

recipes.verification: Every interdental gap was wiped on both walls in one systematic pass, no gum was snapped or sawed, and — the real metric — it happened again tomorrow.

recipes.title: foam roll sore muscles
recipes.name: foam-roll-sore-muscles
recipes.goal: Use a foam roller to reduce muscle tightness temporarily without irritating joints, nerves, or injuries.

steps.action: **Choose one muscle area.** Pick calves, quads, glutes, hamstrings, or upper back, avoiding joints and the low back spine.
steps.expect: the target area is muscle, not bone or a joint line.

steps.action: **Apply light pressure first.** Support body weight with hands or the opposite leg so pressure is tolerable.
steps.expect: sensation feels like firm pressure, not sharp pain.

steps.action: **Roll slowly.** Move 1 to 2 inches per second over the muscle for 30 to 60 seconds.
steps.expect: tenderness decreases slightly or stays tolerable.

steps.action: **Pause on tender spots.** Hold gentle pressure on a sore spot for 10 to 20 seconds while breathing normally.
steps.expect: the spot softens or becomes less reactive.

steps.action: **Move after rolling.** Walk, squat, or stretch lightly through the new range.
steps.expect: movement feels a little easier than before rolling.

steps.action: **Limit total dose.** Spend no more than 1 to 2 minutes per muscle area.
steps.expect: skin is not bruised and soreness is not worse afterward.

recipes.verification: After rolling, the target muscle moves at least as well as before, pain is not sharper, and no bruising, numbness, or swelling has appeared.

recipes.title: get ready for bed
recipes.name: get-ready-for-bed
recipes.goal: You are in bed at your intended time with tomorrow prepared, the home secured, and conditions set for falling asleep.

steps.action: **Start winding down 30–60 minutes before the target.** Finish active tasks; dim the lights.
steps.expect: nothing "quick" is still being started inside the wind-down window.

steps.action: **Prepare tomorrow's friction points.** Lay out clothes, pack the bag, note the top task for tomorrow; set the alarm and *verify AM/PM and volume*.
steps.expect: alarm confirmed set for the right time; morning needs staged.

steps.action: **Secure the home.** Lock doors, check the stove is off, blow out candles, water/let out pets per routine.
steps.expect: a consistent short checklist mentally ticked — same order every night makes omissions feel wrong.

steps.action: **Do the bathroom routine.** Brush teeth (`daily/brush-your-teeth`), wash face, medications if prescribed.
steps.expect: routine complete; water off.

steps.action: **Set the bedroom conditions.** Cool (≈17–19 °C), dark (curtains/eye mask), quiet (or steady white noise); phone charging *away from the pillow*, on do-not-disturb.
steps.expect: room dark, cool, quiet; phone out of arm's reach.

steps.action: **Get into bed at the target time and do something calm and screen-free.** Read a few pages, breathe slowly; lights fully out when drowsy.
steps.expect: lights out within ~15–20 minutes of getting in.

recipes.verification: Alarm verified, home secured, tomorrow staged, room dark/cool/quiet, phone out of reach, and lights out within the intended window.

recipes.title: get something out of your eye
recipes.name: get-something-out-of-your-eye
recipes.goal: A loose speck is flushed from the eye without rubbing, scraping, or worsening an injury.

steps.action: **Stop rubbing.** Keep fingers away from the eye even if it itches or waters.
steps.expect: the surface is not scratched further.

steps.action: **Wash your hands.** Use soap and water before touching eyelids or contacts.
steps.expect: hands are clean.

steps.action: **Blink several times.** Let tears move the speck toward the corner of the eye.
steps.expect: watering may loosen the particle.

steps.action: **Remove contacts if present.** Take out lenses only if they come out easily.
steps.expect: flushing can reach the eye surface.

steps.action: **Flush the eye.** Pour clean water or saline from the inner corner outward, or use an eyewash stream.
steps.expect: fluid runs across the eye and away from the other eye.

steps.action: **Check the lower lid.** Gently pull the lower lid down and look for a loose speck.
steps.expect: any visible loose particle can be rinsed away.

steps.action: **Try upper-over-lower lid.** Pull the upper lid gently over the lower lid and blink.
steps.expect: lashes may sweep a loose speck out.

steps.action: **Flush again.** Repeat gentle rinsing for several minutes if irritation continues.
steps.expect: discomfort improves.

steps.action: **Stop if embedded.** Do not touch an object stuck in the eye or under the lid.
steps.expect: embedded material is left for medical care.

steps.action: **Rest the eye.** Avoid contacts and eye makeup until irritation is gone.
steps.expect: the eye is less irritated.

recipes.verification: The eye feels clear after flushing, vision is normal, and no embedded object, chemical exposure, or severe pain remains.

recipes.title: give yourself a manicure
recipes.name: give-yourself-a-manicure
recipes.goal: Shape, clean, and polish fingernails at home with a smooth finish and minimal irritation.

steps.action: **Wash and dry hands.** Clean under nails gently and dry completely.
steps.expect: nails are clean and not slippery.

steps.action: **Trim if needed.** Clip only obvious extra length before filing.
steps.expect: nails are close to the desired length.

steps.action: **Shape with a file.** File from the outer edge toward the center in one direction rather than sawing hard.
steps.expect: each nail has an even shape with no sharp corners.

steps.action: **Soak briefly.** Soak fingertips in warm water for 3 to 5 minutes.
steps.expect: cuticles feel softer but skin is not wrinkled or sore.

steps.action: **Push cuticles gently.** Use a cuticle pusher to nudge softened cuticle back; do not cut living skin.
steps.expect: nail plates look tidy without bleeding or pain.

steps.action: **Clean the nail plate.** Wipe nails with remover or alcohol to remove oil, then let them dry.
steps.expect: the nail surface is dry and ready for polish.

steps.action: **Apply base coat.** Paint a thin layer and cap the free edge lightly.
steps.expect: each nail has an even clear base.

steps.action: **Apply color in thin coats.** [BRANCH: sheer | opaque] use two light coats for most polish, adding a third only if needed.
steps.expect: color looks even without thick ridges.

steps.action: **Apply top coat.** Seal the color and free edge with a thin top coat.
steps.expect: nails look glossy or evenly matte, depending on the product.

steps.action: **Let polish dry.** Keep hands still for at least 10 to 20 minutes and avoid hot water for about an hour.
steps.expect: light touch does not dent the surface.

recipes.verification: All nails are shaped smoothly, cuticles are uncut and comfortable, and polish is dry enough that a light touch leaves no mark.

recipes.title: go for a run
recipes.name: go-for-a-run
recipes.goal: A run completed at the right effort for its purpose, over a sensible route, with the traffic, weather, and body signals all handled, and recovery started when it ends.

steps.action: **Warm up.** Three minutes of brisk walking plus leg swings (`daily/self-care/warm-up-before-exercise`), then start the run itself slow.
steps.expect: first kilometer noticeably slower than the run's average; that is correct, not weak.

steps.action: **Settle into the day's effort using the talk test.** Easy runs: full sentences possible. Steady: phrases. Hard workout intervals: words. If the plan says easy and you cannot chat, slow down regardless of pace numbers.
steps.expect: breathing matched to the run's stated purpose.

steps.action: **Run the route with traffic logic.** Sidewalks and paths where they exist; facing oncoming traffic where they do not; `embodied/mobility/cross-a-street` at every crossing with headphones low or one ear out; visible colors or lights at dusk and dark.
steps.expect: every junction treated as a junction, not as pace interruption.

steps.action: **Check form when it gets hard.** Shoulders down, gaze ahead, quick light steps rather than reaching strides. Form decays with fatigue and shortening the stride restores it cheaply.
steps.expect: periodic thirty-second form scans, especially in the final third.

steps.action: **Distinguish discomfort from pain.** Effort, burning legs, and general tiredness are the sport. Sharp, localized, one-sided, or gait-changing pain is a stop signal: walk, cut the route short, and let it be assessed by rest and, if persistent, a professional.
steps.expect: honest triage in the moment; no limping through kilometers to satisfy a number.

steps.action: **Finish with a ramp down, not a dead stop.** Last minutes easier, then a few minutes of walking; gentle stretching after is where the static holds belong.
steps.expect: breathing recovered during the walk; legs looser after the stretch.

steps.action: **Start recovery immediately.** Water, food within the hour for longer runs, sweaty kit into the wash cycle (`daily/home/do-the-laundry`), and the run logged if you track.
steps.expect: rehydrated, fed, and the kit not fermenting in a bag (`daily/self-care/pack-a-gym-bag` F2).

recipes.verification: The run matched its stated purpose on the talk test, junctions were crossed properly, no sharp pain was run through, it ended with a walk and stretch, and recovery (water, food, laundry, log) happened within the hour.

recipes.title: ice an injury
recipes.name: ice-an-injury
recipes.goal: A minor acute sprain, strain, or bruise is cooled safely with rest, compression, and elevation while signs needing medical care are recognized.

steps.action: **Stop the activity.** Move out of the situation that caused the injury.
steps.expect: the injured part is no longer being loaded or struck.

steps.action: **Screen for serious injury.** Check for deformity, inability to bear weight, numbness, severe swelling, open wound, or head, neck, chest, belly, or spine injury.
steps.expect: either minor-injury care is reasonable or urgent care is needed.

steps.action: **Rest the area.** Keep the injured part still and supported.
steps.expect: pain decreases when movement stops.

steps.action: **Wrap ice in a barrier.** Place ice or a cold pack inside a towel.
steps.expect: cold reaches the skin without direct ice contact.

steps.action: **Ice for 15-20 minutes.** Apply cold over the sore area, checking skin every few minutes.
steps.expect: area feels cold and numb but not burning, white, or painful from cold.

steps.action: **Compress if suitable.** Wrap an elastic bandage snugly from farther out toward the body, avoiding tightness.
steps.expect: swelling support improves without tingling or color change.

steps.action: **Elevate above heart level.** Prop the injured area on pillows when possible.
steps.expect: swelling pressure feels reduced.

steps.action: **Pause between icing rounds.** Wait at least 40-60 minutes before icing again.
steps.expect: skin returns to normal temperature and color.

steps.action: **Reassess function.** After the first rounds, check pain, swelling, movement, and weight bearing.
steps.expect: mild injuries improve or remain stable.

steps.action: **Seek care when the pattern is not minor.** Call a clinician or emergency services for severe symptoms or worsening function.
steps.expect: serious injuries are not delayed by home icing.

recipes.verification: The injured area has been rested, iced through a cloth for no more than 20 minutes at a time, optionally compressed without circulation changes, elevated, and screened for urgent warning signs.

recipes.title: improve your desk posture
recipes.name: improve-your-desk-posture
recipes.goal: Your desk setup supports a neutral posture, reduces avoidable strain, and builds in movement every 30 minutes.

steps.action: **Set foot support.** Put both feet flat on the floor, or use a stable footrest if they do not reach.
steps.expect: thighs feel supported and feet are not dangling.

steps.action: **Set chair height.** Adjust so elbows rest near 90 degrees when hands reach the keyboard.
steps.expect: shoulders can drop instead of shrugging.

steps.action: **Support the lower back.** Sit back in the chair and add a small cushion or rolled towel if the low back collapses.
steps.expect: the spine feels supported without forcing a stiff arch.

steps.action: **Raise the monitor.** Place the top of the screen around eye level and about an arm's length away.
steps.expect: eyes look forward with the neck mostly neutral.

steps.action: **Center the screen and keyboard.** Put the main screen and keyboard directly in front of your body.
steps.expect: torso does not twist for normal typing.

steps.action: **Keep wrists neutral.** Float wrists level with forearms, keep the mouse close, and avoid bending wrists up, down, or sideways.
steps.expect: hands reach controls without strain.

steps.action: **Relax shoulders and jaw.** Drop shoulders, unclench the jaw, and let elbows stay near the body.
steps.expect: upper body feels less braced.

steps.action: **Move every 30 minutes.** Stand, walk, stretch calves, open the chest, or change position for 1 to 2 minutes.
steps.expect: posture resets before stiffness builds.

steps.action: **Recheck during real work.** After 20 minutes of typing, notice which body part tightened first and adjust that part.
steps.expect: the setup matches your actual habits, not just a staged pose.

recipes.verification: Feet are supported, screen is near eye level, wrists stay neutral, shoulders are relaxed, and a movement break happens at least every 30 minutes.

recipes.title: improve your posture daily
recipes.name: improve-your-posture-daily
recipes.goal: Improve daily posture by building awareness, strength, mobility, and movement breaks instead of forcing a rigid pose.

steps.action: **Check your baseline.** Stand normally and notice head, ribs, pelvis, shoulders, and weight distribution.
steps.expect: you see the posture you actually use, not a forced correction.

steps.action: **Stack gently.** Bring ears over shoulders, ribs over pelvis, and weight balanced over mid-foot.
steps.expect: posture feels taller but not stiff.

steps.action: **Open the front.** Do 5 slow chest-opening breaths with shoulders relaxed.
steps.expect: chest and upper back feel less compressed.

steps.action: **Strengthen the back line.** Do 8 to 12 rows with a band or squeeze shoulder blades gently without shrugging.
steps.expect: upper back muscles engage.

steps.action: **Train hips and core.** Do 8 slow hip hinges or glute bridges and a short plank variation.
steps.expect: posture support comes from hips and trunk, not neck tension.

steps.action: **Set movement cues.** Change position, stand, or walk for 1 minute every 30 to 60 minutes.
steps.expect: stiffness is interrupted before it becomes pain.

steps.action: **Review one daily trigger.** Pick one situation, such as phone use or dishwashing, and apply the gentle stack there.
steps.expect: posture practice enters real life.

recipes.verification: For seven days, you complete a 10-minute posture routine, take movement breaks, and can demonstrate a relaxed stacked posture during one daily activity without pain increase.

recipes.title: keep a journal
recipes.name: keep-a-journal
recipes.goal: A journal entry gets written most days with minimal friction, sustained for weeks rather than abandoned after an ambitious first week, and missed days cost nothing.

steps.action: **Lower the bar before you start.** Define the minimum entry as one true sentence, dated. "Tired. Long day, shipped the report." is a complete entry. Ambitious daily-page quotas are the number one reason journals die in week two.
steps.expect: a written-down personal rule: one sentence counts.

steps.action: **Stage the journal at the anchor location.** Notebook on the pillow or next to the coffee machine; app icon on the phone's first screen. The journal must be closer to hand than the distraction that replaces it.
steps.expect: starting an entry requires zero searching.

steps.action: **Write at the same time every day.** Attach it to the anchor: pour coffee, open journal; or get into bed, write, then lights out. Consistency of the trigger matters far more than the length of the entry.
steps.expect: within a week the anchor itself reminds you; no alarm needed.

steps.action: **Start each entry with the date, then the first true thing.** The date makes the notebook a record; the first sentence is whatever is actually on your mind, however mundane.
steps.expect: the blank-page pause lasts seconds, not minutes.

steps.action: **When stuck, use a rotating prompt.** [BRANCH: nothing comes → pick one: what drained me today, what surprised me, what am I avoiding, what would I tell a friend in my situation | words are flowing → skip the prompt] Keep three or four favorite prompts written inside the front cover.
steps.expect: even a flat day yields a few sentences.

steps.action: **Stop while it is still easy.** End at the natural pause, even after two sentences. Ending mid-thought at "still easy" makes tomorrow's entry inviting; writing to exhaustion makes it a chore.
steps.expect: closing the journal feels slightly early, not relieved.

steps.action: **When you miss days, resume without backfilling.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* days not written stay unwritten; that is fine. Write today's date after the gap and continue. Reconstructing missed days from memory produces homework, guilt, and quitting.
steps.expect: a visible date gap in the notebook and a normal entry after it, with no apology paragraph.

recipes.verification: Over the trailing two weeks: entries exist for most days (10 of 14 is strong), every entry is dated, at least one gap was resumed with no backfilled entries, and the median entry took under ten minutes.

recipes.title: limit doomscrolling
recipes.name: limit-doomscrolling
recipes.goal: Reduce compulsive scrolling by noticing the trigger, adding friction, replacing the behavior, and protecting bedtime.

steps.action: **Name the trigger.** Notice whether scrolling starts from boredom, anxiety, avoidance, loneliness, or bedtime autopilot.
steps.expect: one common trigger is written down.

steps.action: **Choose a target window.** Pick the riskiest time, such as waking, lunch, after work, or bed.
steps.expect: the plan focuses on one repeatable moment.

steps.action: **Add friction to the feed.** [BRANCH: app | browser] Remove the app, log out, move it off the home screen, or block the site during the target window.
steps.expect: opening the feed now requires an extra deliberate step.

steps.action: **Turn off nonessential notifications.** Keep calls, direct messages, and safety alerts if needed; mute algorithmic pulls.
steps.expect: fewer prompts invite you back.

steps.action: **Set a hard time limit.** Use a built-in app limit, timer, or rule like "10 minutes after dinner."
steps.expect: scrolling has a visible stop point.

steps.action: **Install a replacement.** Put a book, walk shoes, puzzle, music, journal, or message-a-friend option where the phone used to be.
steps.expect: the trigger has somewhere else to go.

steps.action: **Protect bedtime with a no-feed rule.** Keep the phone out of bed or use grayscale and charging outside reach. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not use scrolling while driving, walking in traffic, or supervising a child near hazards.
steps.expect: the bed is no longer paired with feeds.

steps.action: **Review after three days.** Keep the friction that worked and tighten only the window that failed.
steps.expect: the system improves without a dramatic reset.

recipes.verification: During the target window, friction interrupted automatic opening, a replacement was used at least once, and bedtime scrolling did not happen in bed.

recipes.title: manage a hangover
recipes.name: manage-a-hangover
recipes.goal: Hangover symptoms are managed with hydration, food, rest, and monitoring while avoiding ineffective or risky fixes.

steps.action: **Check for emergency signs.** Look for confusion, slow breathing, repeated vomiting, blue or pale skin, seizure, or inability to wake
steps.expect: you know whether this is a hangover or an emergency.

steps.action: **Stop drinking alcohol.** Do not use more alcohol as treatment
steps.expect: no additional alcohol is being consumed.

steps.action: **Sip fluids.** Drink water or electrolytes slowly, especially if nauseated
steps.expect: fluids stay down and thirst eases gradually.

steps.action: **Eat something gentle.** Try toast, rice, bananas, soup, eggs, or another tolerable food [BRANCH: hungry | nauseated]
steps.expect: blood sugar feels steadier without worsening nausea.

steps.action: **Rest in a safe position.** Sleep or lie down where someone can check on you if symptoms are significant
steps.expect: you are not driving, cooking, or doing risky tasks.

steps.action: **Use pain relief carefully.** Follow medicine labels and avoid acetaminophen after heavy drinking unless a clinician says it is safe
steps.expect: any medicine choice respects liver, stomach, and kidney risks.

steps.action: **Avoid false cures.** Skip cold showers, excessive caffeine, sauna sweating, and intense exercise as fixes
steps.expect: symptoms are managed without added dehydration or injury risk.

steps.action: **Prevent the next one.** Plan food, pacing, water, and a ride before future drinking
steps.expect: a practical prevention step is identified.

recipes.verification: You can keep fluids down, symptoms are improving, and no emergency signs such as confusion, slow breathing, repeated vomiting, or chest pain are present.

recipes.title: manage a panic attack
recipes.name: manage-a-panic-attack
recipes.goal: A panic attack is managed with grounding, slower breathing, and aftercare while urgent medical or safety concerns are not ignored.

steps.action: **Name what is happening.** Say to yourself, this may be panic and it can pass.
steps.expect: the experience has a label instead of feeling mysterious.

steps.action: **Sit or steady yourself.** Place both feet on the floor or lean against a stable surface.
steps.expect: falling risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Use five senses.** Name 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, and 1 you taste.
steps.expect: attention shifts toward the present room.

steps.action: **Slow the exhale.** Breathe in gently and make the exhale longer than the inhale.
steps.expect: breathing feels less rushed after several cycles.

steps.action: **Release muscle tension.** Drop shoulders, unclench jaw, and soften hands.
steps.expect: the body is not bracing as hard.

steps.action: **Reduce stimulation.** Step away from noise, bright screens, crowds, or conflict if safe.
steps.expect: fewer inputs compete for attention.

steps.action: **Use a support script.** Text or call a trusted person and say you are having panic and need calm company.
steps.expect: support is specific and practical.

steps.action: **Let the wave pass.** Remind yourself that panic peaks and settles even when it feels intense.
steps.expect: the goal becomes riding it out, not fighting every sensation.

steps.action: **Do gentle aftercare.** Drink water, eat something light if needed, and avoid judging yourself.
steps.expect: recovery continues after symptoms drop.

steps.action: **Plan follow-up.** If attacks are new, frequent, or disruptive, contact a clinician or therapist.
steps.expect: ongoing panic is not managed alone.

recipes.verification: Breathing and attention are steadier, immediate safety is maintained, and medical or self-harm warning signs have been addressed.

recipes.title: manage seasonal allergies
recipes.name: manage-seasonal-allergies
recipes.goal: Reduce seasonal allergy symptoms by limiting pollen exposure and using appropriate over-the-counter care when suitable.

steps.action: **Check pollen timing.** Look up local pollen level or note whether symptoms spike after outdoor exposure.
steps.expect: you know the highest-risk part of the day or week.

steps.action: **Reduce indoor pollen.** Keep windows closed during high pollen, use ventilation or filtration if available, and wipe visible dust.
steps.expect: sleeping and work areas have less outdoor air and dust.

steps.action: **Decontaminate after outdoor time.** Change clothes, wash hands and face, and shower before bed after high exposure.
steps.expect: pollen is not carried onto bedding.

steps.action: **Rinse the nose safely.** Use sterile, distilled, or previously boiled and cooled water for saline rinses if you choose rinsing.
steps.expect: nasal passages feel clearer without unsafe tap-water exposure.

steps.action: **Use medicines responsibly.** Follow the label for antihistamines, nasal steroid sprays, or eye drops, checking interactions and drowsiness warnings.
steps.expect: doses match the package and side effects are understood.

steps.action: **Track response for one week.** Note symptoms, exposure, and any medicine used.
steps.expect: triggers and effective measures are clearer.

recipes.verification: After one week, symptoms are milder or better timed, bedding exposure is controlled, any medicine is used according to label, and red-flag symptoms are absent.

recipes.title: meditate for ten minutes
recipes.name: meditate-for-ten-minutes
recipes.goal: Ten minutes of seated breath-focused meditation are completed: a settled posture held, attention repeatedly returned to the breath, the session ended by a timer rather than restlessness.

steps.action: **Set the timer and remove interruptions.** Ten minutes, gentle chime, Do Not Disturb on.
steps.expect: countdown running; no notifications will fire.

steps.action: **Take the posture.** Sit with hips slightly above knees (sit on the front edge of a chair or a folded blanket), spine tall but not rigid, shoulders dropped, hands resting on thighs. Imagine a string lifting the crown of your head.
steps.expect: upright and stable, able to breathe fully, no strain in the low back.

steps.action: **Settle the eyes and take three anchoring breaths.** Close the eyes, or soften the gaze downward. Breathe in slowly through the nose, out slowly, three times, letting the body settle a little more on each exhale.
steps.expect: a small drop in shoulder and jaw tension.

steps.action: **Choose one breath anchor and stay with it.** Pick a single point where you feel the breath most clearly: the nostrils, the chest, or the belly rising and falling. Let the breath be natural, not controlled; just feel it at that one place.
steps.expect: attention resting on the sensation of one breath, then the next.

steps.action: **Notice when the mind wanders, and return.** It will wander into thoughts, plans, sounds, within seconds. Noticing that you have wandered is not failure; it is the whole exercise. The moment of noticing is one repetition, like a rep in the gym.
steps.expect: you catch yourself mid-thought and gently move attention back to the anchor, without commentary or self-criticism.

steps.action: **Repeat the return for the full ten minutes.** Wander, notice, return, hundreds of times if needed. Do not count how many times, do not grade the session by how "calm" it felt. Label a persistent pull ("thinking", "hearing") softly and come back.
steps.expect: a repeating cycle of drifting and returning; each return is the work being done.

steps.action: **End at the chime, not before.** When the timer sounds, keep the eyes closed for a few breaths, notice how the body and mind feel now versus at the start, then open the eyes and stretch gently before standing.
steps.expect: session closed deliberately; a brief pause before re-entering activity.

recipes.verification: The timer ran the full ten minutes and ended the session; you maintained an upright seated posture; you noticed wandering and returned to the breath anchor repeatedly (many times is normal and good); you did not end early out of restlessness or grade the session by how calm it felt.

recipes.title: pack a gym bag
recipes.name: pack-a-gym-bag
recipes.goal: A gym bag packed the night before that contains everything the workout and the after-shower need, so a missing sock never becomes the reason today's session died.

steps.action: **Pack the workout layer.** Shoes (the item most often forgotten because they live by the door), shorts/leggings, shirt, sports socks, and sport-specific kit (gloves, goggles and cap for the pool, towel for the mat class).
steps.expect: the full outfit physically in the bag, not "the shoes I'll grab on the way".

steps.action: **Pack the shower layer.** Flip-flops for shared showers, towel, and travel-size toiletries that live in the bag permanently (shower gel, shampoo, deodorant). Permanent residents beat nightly decanting.
steps.expect: a small toiletry pouch that never leaves the bag.

steps.action: **Pack the after layer.** Full change: underwear, socks, shirt, and whatever the day after the gym requires (work clothes if commuting through the session). Underwear is the most-forgotten after-item; check it explicitly.
steps.expect: tomorrow-you can dress completely from the bag.

steps.action: **Add the small enablers.** Water bottle (filled in the morning, packed empty tonight), lock for the locker, headphones, membership card or the phone that carries it, hair ties, plasters.
steps.expect: the pocket inventory done; the lock is the one that strands people.

steps.action: **Separate wet from dry in advance.** The empty wet-bag goes in now so the post-shower swimsuit or sweaty kit has a destination other than your clean clothes.
steps.expect: a dedicated wet compartment ready.

steps.action: **Stage the bag at the door.** Same principle as `daily/food/pack-a-lunch`: night-you plans around morning-you's memory.
steps.expect: the bag physically between you and leaving.

recipes.verification: The bag contains the three layers (workout, shower, after) plus lock and bottle, wet and dry have separate homes, it sits at the door, and the morning requires zero decisions beyond picking it up.

recipes.title: practice deep breathing
recipes.name: practice-deep-breathing
recipes.goal: Your heart rate and sense of urgency drop measurably within a few minutes, using a breathing pattern matched to the situation: a physiological sigh for acute spikes, box breathing for sustained calm.

steps.action: **Name the situation.** [BRANCH: acute spike (about to speak, just got bad news, flash of anger) → physiological sigh, steps 2-3 | sustained stress (racing mind, can't settle, pre-sleep) → box breathing, steps 4-6]
steps.expect: you have picked one pattern; do not improvise a hybrid.

steps.action: **Physiological sigh: double inhale through the nose.** One normal inhale, then a second short sniff stacked on top to fully inflate the lungs.
steps.expect: a slight stretch at the top of the chest; the second sniff is small, not a full breath.

steps.action: **Long slow exhale through the mouth.** Exhale until the lungs feel empty, longer than both inhales combined. Repeat 1-3 times total, then stop.
steps.expect: a noticeable drop in tension by the second repetition; more than 3 repetitions adds nothing.

steps.action: **Box breathing: settle the count.** Inhale through the nose for a 4 count, hold 4, exhale 4, hold empty 4. Count in your head, not aloud.
steps.expect: the first box feels awkward; that is normal.

steps.action: **Run boxes for 2-5 minutes.** Keep the exhale unhurried; if 4 feels strained, drop to a 3 count rather than gasping through 4.
steps.expect: by minute two, shoulders drop and the counting itself crowds out the racing thoughts.

steps.action: **Exit gently.** Let breathing return to automatic; do not evaluate whether it "worked" mid-pattern.
steps.expect: breathing continues slow on its own for a while after you stop counting.

recipes.verification: After the chosen pattern: exhales are audibly slower than before you started, shoulders are lower, and you can hold attention on one thing for ten seconds without it bouncing. If you wear a heart rate monitor, expect a drop of roughly 5-15 bpm from the stressed reading.

recipes.title: prepare for a heat wave
recipes.name: prepare-for-a-heat-wave
recipes.goal: You, your home, and the vulnerable people around you get through a multi-day heat wave without heat illness: the home stays as cool as physics allows, hydration stays ahead of losses, and warning signs are caught early.

steps.action: **Stock up before the peak.** Water, electrolyte options (oral rehydration salts or sports drinks), food that needs no cooking, and any prescription refills.
steps.expect: no errands required during the hottest days.

steps.action: **Start hydrating the day before.** Drink regularly without waiting for thirst; thirst lags dehydration, and older adults barely feel it at all. Cut back alcohol; it works against you.
steps.expect: pale-yellow urine going into day one of the heat.

steps.action: **Run the night-flush cycle.** Each night when outside air drops below inside temperature, open windows on opposite sides of the home for cross-flow; a fan blowing hot air out one window accelerates it.
steps.expect: indoor temperature drops several degrees by morning.

steps.action: **Seal the home at dawn.** Close all windows and cover them, outside shading (shutters, awnings) beating inside curtains, before outdoor temperature crosses indoor. Keep everything shut through the day.
steps.expect: the home stays cooler than outside well into the afternoon; opening a window "for air" at 2 pm imports heat.

steps.action: **Designate and defend one cool room.** Usually the lowest floor or the north-facing room. Close its door, and everyone sleeps or rests there during the peak if the rest of the home overheats.
steps.expect: one room measurably cooler than the others.

steps.action: **Use fans correctly.** A fan on your skin cools by evaporation and works better with a spritz of water or a damp shirt. [BRANCH: indoor temperature under about 35 °C / 95 °F → fan on people helps | above that → fans on dry skin can add heat; switch to damp cloths, cool showers, forearms in cool water]
steps.expect: skin feels cooler, not blasted with hot air.

steps.action: **Shift activity to the edges of the day.** Exercise, errands, and cooking (which heats the home) before 10 am or after sunset.
steps.expect: no strenuous outdoor effort between late morning and early evening.

steps.action: **Check on high-risk neighbors daily, in person or by call.** Ask specifically: are you drinking, is your home cooler than outside, are you dizzy or confused. Twice daily during the peak.
steps.expect: a direct answer each day; no answer for a day triggers a visit.

steps.action: **Watch each other for heat illness.** Heavy sweating, cramps, nausea, headache: heat exhaustion. Confusion, hot dry or clammy skin, fainting: possible heat stroke.
steps.expect: everyone in the household can name the difference (see F3, F4).

recipes.verification: Through the final day of the warning: indoor peak temperature stayed below the outdoor peak, everyone's urine stayed pale and nobody progressed past mild heat symptoms, every high-risk contact was reached daily, and no person or animal was ever in a parked car or sealed hot room.

recipes.title: prevent and treat chafing
recipes.name: prevent-and-treat-chafing
recipes.goal: Skin rubbing is prevented during movement, and mild raw chafed skin is cleaned, soothed, and protected while it heals.

steps.action: **Identify friction and moisture.** Check where skin rubs skin, fabric, straps, or seams.
steps.expect: the trigger area is clear.

steps.action: **Choose smoother clothing.** Wear moisture-wicking, well-fitting fabric and avoid rough seams over the spot.
steps.expect: the skin moves with less rubbing.

steps.action: **Apply a barrier before activity.** Coat the high-friction area with balm, petroleum jelly, zinc oxide, or an anti-chafe product.
steps.expect: the skin feels slick or protected.

steps.action: **Keep sweat under control.** Change wet clothing when possible and dry folds gently.
steps.expect: the area is less damp.

steps.action: **Clean raw skin.** For existing chafing, wash with mild soap and water, then pat dry.
steps.expect: sweat and grit are removed without scrubbing.

steps.action: **Soothe and cover.** Apply a bland barrier and use soft breathable fabric or a nonstick dressing if needed.
steps.expect: the area stings less when clothing touches it.

steps.action: **Reduce rubbing until healed.** Modify the activity, route, pace, or clothing for a day or two.
steps.expect: the skin is not repeatedly reopened.

recipes.verification: The rubbing source is reduced, the skin is clean and protected, and pain decreases during normal movement instead of increasing.

recipes.title: put in contact lenses
recipes.name: put-in-contact-lenses
recipes.goal: Contact lenses are inserted correctly, worn within their schedule, and removed and stored (or discarded) hygienically, keeping the habit that protects your eyes intact.

steps.action: **Start with the same eye every time.** A fixed order prevents mixing left and right lenses.
steps.expect: a habit-locked sequence, right eye first for most people.

steps.action: **Take the lens out and inspect it.** On a dry fingertip, check it is clean, undamaged, and right-side out: correct orientation looks like a bowl with straight walls; inside-out flares like a saucer at the rim.
steps.expect: an intact bowl-shaped lens. Torn or nicked lenses are discarded, never worn.

steps.action: **Hold the lids and place the lens.** Pull the lower lid down with the middle finger of the lens hand, hold the upper lashes with the other hand, look slightly up or straight at the mirror, and place the lens gently on the eye.
steps.expect: the lens settles with a blink or two; vision clears in that eye.

steps.action: **Repeat for the other eye, then assess.**
steps.expect: clear, comfortable vision in both eyes. Persistent grit, burning, or blur means take it out and restart at step 2; a lens that hurts is telling you something (debris, inside-out, or a tear).

steps.action: **Respect the wearing schedule during the day.** Dailies come out and go in the trash; monthlies/two-weeklies track their opening date. Do not sleep, shower, or swim in lenses unless your prescriber explicitly approved a specific product for it.
steps.expect: removal happens before sleep, every night.

steps.action: **Remove with clean hands.** Look up, slide the lens down onto the white with a fingertip, pinch gently with pad-of-finger and thumb.
steps.expect: lens out without fingernail contact with the eye.

steps.action: **Clean and store reusables; discard dailies.** Rub each lens in fresh solution for a few seconds, rinse with solution, and store in fresh solution. Empty and air-dry the case daily, upside down on a tissue; replace the case monthly to quarterly.
steps.expect: lenses in fresh solution (never topped-up old solution), case drying open.

recipes.verification: Lenses went in clean-handed in the fixed order, vision is clear and comfortable, they came out before sleep, reusables sit in fresh solution in a drying-cycle case, and any red-or-painful eye ended the wearing immediately rather than being pushed through.

recipes.title: put in earplugs correctly
recipes.name: put-in-earplugs-correctly
recipes.goal: Foam or reusable earplugs are inserted cleanly and deeply enough to reduce sound while staying comfortable.

steps.action: **Inspect the earplugs.** Check that foam is clean and rebounds, or reusable plugs are intact.
steps.expect: plugs are clean and undamaged.

steps.action: **Wash and dry hands.** Clean hands before touching the part that enters the ear.
steps.expect: fingers are dry and free of lotion.

steps.action: **Compress foam if used.** Roll a foam plug into a narrow crease-free cylinder.
steps.expect: the plug is thin enough to enter the canal.

steps.action: **Open the ear canal.** Reach over your head and gently pull the top of the ear up and back.
steps.expect: the ear canal straightens.

steps.action: **Insert and hold.** Place the plug into the canal and hold it while foam expands, or seat reusable flanges with gentle pressure.
steps.expect: the plug seals without pain.

steps.action: **Check fit.** Cup hands over ears and release them while listening to steady room noise.
steps.expect: sound changes little because the plugs are already sealing.

steps.action: **Remove gently.** Twist slowly to break the seal before pulling out.
steps.expect: the plug comes out without a painful suction feeling.

recipes.verification: Each plug sits mostly inside the ear canal, feels comfortable, and noticeably reduces steady sound without pain.

recipes.title: quit vaping
recipes.name: quit-vaping
recipes.goal: Stop vaping nicotine with a clear quit plan, withdrawal supports, and relapse recovery steps.

steps.action: **Set the quit date.** Pick a specific date and remove the idea of waiting for a perfect week.
steps.expect: one date is written down.

steps.action: **Map triggers.** List times, places, emotions, and people linked to vaping.
steps.expect: the top three triggers are visible.

steps.action: **Choose support.** Decide whether to use counseling, a quitline, a clinician, nicotine replacement, or a pharmacist-guided plan.
steps.expect: at least one support is ready before the quit date.

steps.action: **Remove supplies.** Dispose of devices, pods, chargers, and backups on quit day.
steps.expect: vaping requires leaving to obtain supplies, not reaching into a drawer.

steps.action: **Prepare craving actions.** Use delay, deep breathing, water, walking, gum, or texting support for 5 to 10 minutes.
steps.expect: each craving has a replacement behavior.

steps.action: **Handle withdrawal as temporary.** Expect irritability, cravings, sleep changes, or concentration problems during the first days.
steps.expect: symptoms are treated as withdrawal, not proof you need to vape.

steps.action: **Review daily.** Each evening, note cravings survived, triggers, and tomorrow's highest-risk moment.
steps.expect: the next day has one concrete prevention move.

recipes.verification: You reach seven consecutive vape-free days, have no devices or pods accessible, and can name your top triggers plus the support used when cravings peaked.

recipes.title: recover from a cold
recipes.name: recover-from-a-cold
recipes.goal: You get through a common cold with the least misery and lost time, avoid infecting others, and recognize early if what you have is not actually a cold.

steps.action: **Confirm it looks like a cold, not something else.** Sudden onset with high fever, body aches, and exhaustion points to flu; loss of smell or known exposure suggests testing for COVID if tests are available.
steps.expect: gradual onset and throat-first symptoms; anything else, see Decision points.

steps.action: **Cancel what can be canceled for the first 48-72 hours.** The early phase is when rest changes the trajectory and when you are most contagious.
steps.expect: calendar cleared of gyms, gatherings, and visits to elderly or infant relatives.

steps.action: **Drink fluids on a schedule, not by thirst.** Water, broth, warm tea; a practical target is pale-yellow urine. Warm liquids also loosen congestion.
steps.expect: urinating regularly, urine pale; throat feels less raw after warm drinks.

steps.action: **Treat the symptoms that block sleep, and only those.** Sore throat or headache: paracetamol/acetaminophen or ibuprofen at label doses. Blocked nose: saline rinse or spray first; a decongestant only if saline is not enough. Night cough in adults: a spoonful of honey is as good as most syrups.
steps.expect: enough relief to sleep; you are not stacking multi-symptom products (see F2).

steps.action: **Sleep more than usual, with the head slightly elevated.** An extra pillow reduces postnasal drip coughing.
steps.expect: fewer night wakings from cough; mornings are the worst point and that is normal.

steps.action: **Protect other people.** Hand washing, sneezing into the elbow, a mask if you must share indoor space, own towel and cup at home.
steps.expect: housemates not sick a week later.

steps.action: **Return to activity gradually after day 3-5.** The rule of thumb: symptoms above the neck only (sniffles, mild sore throat) permit light activity; anything with fever, chest involvement, or body aches means keep resting.
steps.expect: light activity does not worsen next-day symptoms.

steps.action: **Ride out the tail.** A dry cough and fatigue commonly linger 1-2 weeks after everything else clears.
steps.expect: slow steady improvement; the pattern to fear is improvement followed by a new decline (see F4).

recipes.verification: By day 10: no fever, congestion largely cleared, energy near baseline, and any residual cough clearly diminishing week over week. Nobody in your household caught it after your day-2 precautions began, and no red-flag symptom from the Decision points ever appeared unaddressed.

recipes.title: recover from a hard workout
recipes.name: recover-from-a-hard-workout
recipes.goal: Recover from a hard workout by restoring fluids, food, mobility, and sleep while watching for injury signs.

steps.action: **Cool down gradually.** Walk, pedal easy, or move lightly for 5 to 10 minutes.
steps.expect: heart rate and breathing come down steadily.

steps.action: **Rehydrate.** Drink water and include electrolytes if the session was long, hot, or very sweaty.
steps.expect: thirst decreases and urine trends pale over time.

steps.action: **Eat a recovery meal.** Include protein and carbohydrate within a few hours.
steps.expect: hunger is addressed and energy starts returning.

steps.action: **Use gentle mobility.** Stretch lightly or move sore areas through comfortable range.
steps.expect: stiffness decreases without provoking sharp pain.

steps.action: **Plan the next day easy.** Choose rest, walking, light cycling, or technique work instead of another max effort.
steps.expect: recovery has a protected slot.

steps.action: **Sleep deliberately.** Set up a normal bedtime and reduce late caffeine or alcohol.
steps.expect: the highest-value recovery block is protected.

steps.action: **Check symptoms the next morning.** Compare soreness, swelling, range of motion, and energy.
steps.expect: normal soreness is diffuse and improving, not sharp or worsening.

recipes.verification: Within 24 to 48 hours, hydration, food, sleep, and easy movement occurred, soreness is stable or improving, and no red-flag injury or illness signs are present.

recipes.title: reduce caffeine without headaches
recipes.name: reduce-caffeine-without-headaches
recipes.goal: Lower caffeine intake gradually while minimizing withdrawal headaches and sleep disruption.

steps.action: **Measure the baseline.** Write down all caffeine sources for two normal days.
steps.expect: average daily servings are visible.

steps.action: **Set a reduction target.** Reduce total caffeine by about 10 to 25 percent for the first step.
steps.expect: the first cut is small enough to be sustainable.

steps.action: **Cut the latest dose first.** Move or remove caffeine taken within 8 hours of bedtime.
steps.expect: evening sleep pressure is less disrupted.

steps.action: **Blend down gradually.** Mix regular with decaf, choose smaller servings, or swap one drink for tea.
steps.expect: caffeine drops without an abrupt cliff.

steps.action: **Hydrate and eat normally.** Pair the reduction with water and regular meals.
steps.expect: headache triggers from dehydration or skipped food are reduced.

steps.action: **Hold each level several days.** Stay at the new amount until headaches and irritability settle.
steps.expect: symptoms remain mild or fade before the next cut.

steps.action: **Track sleep and headaches.** Note caffeine amount, cutoff time, headache, and bedtime for one week.
steps.expect: patterns show whether the taper speed is working.

recipes.verification: After one to three weeks, daily caffeine is at or below the target, the last dose is at least 8 hours before bedtime, and headaches are absent or mild for three consecutive days.

recipes.title: reduce eye strain from screens
recipes.name: reduce-eye-strain-from-screens
recipes.goal: Reduce screen-related eye fatigue by adjusting distance, lighting, breaks, and dryness triggers.

steps.action: **Set screen distance.** Place the screen about an arm's length away with the top near or slightly below eye level.
steps.expect: eyes look slightly downward without neck strain.

steps.action: **Match brightness to the room.** Adjust screen brightness so it is not a glowing rectangle or too dim to read.
steps.expect: text is clear without squinting.

steps.action: **Increase readable size.** Raise zoom or font size until normal text is easy at the chosen distance.
steps.expect: you can read without leaning forward.

steps.action: **Control glare.** Turn the screen away from windows or bright lamps and use indirect lighting.
steps.expect: reflections no longer cover the working area.

steps.action: **Use break cycles.** Every 20 minutes, look at something far away for about 20 seconds.
steps.expect: eye focusing relaxes before fatigue builds.

steps.action: **Blink and handle dryness.** Blink fully during breaks and consider preservative-free artificial tears if dryness is common.
steps.expect: burning or gritty sensation decreases.

steps.action: **Recheck after one work block.** After 45 to 60 minutes, note strain, posture, and readability.
steps.expect: symptoms are milder than before the setup change.

recipes.verification: After a normal screen session, text remains readable at arm's length, glare is controlled, breaks occurred at least twice per hour, and eye discomfort is reduced or absent.

recipes.title: relieve a blocked nose
recipes.name: relieve-a-blocked-nose
recipes.goal: A blocked nose feels easier to breathe through using safe home measures and appropriate escalation when symptoms suggest more than congestion.

steps.action: **Drink fluids.** Sip water or warm drinks through the day.
steps.expect: mucus feels less thick over time.

steps.action: **Use saline.** Spray saline or use a clean saline rinse device as directed.
steps.expect: the nose feels moister and easier to clear.

steps.action: **Blow gently.** Clear one nostril at a time without force.
steps.expect: pressure does not spike in the ears or sinuses.

steps.action: **Try steam or humidity.** Use a warm shower or humidifier, avoiding scalding steam.
steps.expect: nasal passages feel temporarily looser.

steps.action: **Sleep propped up.** Raise the head with pillows or a wedge.
steps.expect: drainage feels less blocked when lying down.

steps.action: **Avoid smoke and strong scents.** Move away from irritants.
steps.expect: burning or sneezing decreases.

steps.action: **Consider medicine limits.** Use nasal decongestant sprays only for the label's short limit, often no more than 3 days.
steps.expect: rebound congestion is avoided.

steps.action: **Check oral decongestant warnings.** Avoid or ask a clinician first with high blood pressure, heart disease, pregnancy, or certain medicines.
steps.expect: unsafe interactions are avoided.

steps.action: **Watch for allergy pattern.** Notice itchy eyes, sneezing, or clear drainage after triggers.
steps.expect: allergy care can be considered.

steps.action: **Reassess daily.** Track fever, facial pain, duration, and breathing.
steps.expect: worsening symptoms are not missed.

recipes.verification: Breathing through the nose is easier, symptoms are not worsening, and no urgent warning sign is present.

recipes.title: relieve a leg cramp
recipes.name: relieve-a-leg-cramp
recipes.goal: A sudden leg cramp relaxes, the muscle is gently reloaded, and you know when leg pain is not just a cramp.

steps.action: **Stop the trigger.** Pause exercise or sit up in bed so you can control the leg.
steps.expect: the muscle is still tight but you are balanced.

steps.action: **Stretch the cramped muscle.** For a calf cramp, straighten the knee and pull toes toward the shin; for a hamstring, straighten the knee; for a quad, bend the knee gently.
steps.expect: the cramp begins to ease within 30 to 60 seconds.

steps.action: **Load it lightly.** Put weight through the leg if safe, or press the foot against the floor or your hand.
steps.expect: the muscle receives a steady signal to release.

steps.action: **Walk slowly.** Take small steps once the worst spasm lets go.
steps.expect: the muscle feels sore but no longer locked.

steps.action: **Massage gently.** Rub along the tight band without digging hard into a tender spot.
steps.expect: remaining tightness softens.

steps.action: **Hydrate.** Drink water, and consider an electrolyte drink after heavy sweating, vomiting, diarrhea, or long exercise.
steps.expect: thirst eases and you are not lightheaded.

steps.action: **Apply heat after the spasm.** Use a warm towel or heating pad for 10 to 15 minutes if soreness remains.
steps.expect: the muscle feels looser and less guarded.

steps.action: **Prevent nighttime repeats.** Stretch calves before bed, keep blankets loose around feet, and review hard workouts, dehydration, alcohol, and new medicines as triggers.
steps.expect: fewer cramps over the next nights.

recipes.verification: The leg can move through normal range, you can walk without the muscle locking, and no clot, injury, or nerve warning signs are present.

recipes.title: relieve a tension headache
recipes.name: relieve-a-tension-headache
recipes.goal: A likely tension headache is reduced by hydration, eye rest, muscle relaxation, and careful medicine choices, while dangerous headache patterns are recognized.

steps.action: **Screen for red flags.** Check for sudden worst headache, head injury, fever with stiff neck, weakness, confusion, vision loss, pregnancy with severe headache, or new headache after age 50.
steps.expect: no urgent warning sign before self-care continues.

steps.action: **Drink water slowly.** Have a full glass of water, especially after heat, exercise, alcohol, or skipped meals.
steps.expect: thirst decreases and your mouth feels less dry.

steps.action: **Rest your eyes.** Look away from screens for 10 minutes, dim harsh light, and relax the jaw.
steps.expect: forehead and eye pressure stop building.

steps.action: **Release the neck and shoulders.** Drop shoulders, tuck chin gently, turn head left and right, then hold a light side stretch for 15 seconds per side.
steps.expect: neck motion feels smoother, with no sharp pain.

steps.action: **Use heat or pressure.** Place a warm cloth on the neck or massage the temples and jaw with light circular pressure.
steps.expect: tight muscles soften and the pain becomes less pointed.

steps.action: **Time caffeine carefully.** [BRANCH: regular caffeine user | caffeine-sensitive or late day] take a small normal dose early, or skip it to avoid jitters and poor sleep.
steps.expect: alertness improves without a rebound or sleep penalty.

steps.action: **Consider a pain reliever only within limits.** Use acetaminophen, ibuprofen, or another familiar medicine only as labeled, avoiding duplicates and medical conflicts. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* overdosing pain medicine can cause serious harm, so confirm dose, timing, and ingredients before taking it.
steps.expect: medicine use is recorded and stays within the package limit.

steps.action: **Recheck after 30 to 60 minutes.** If the headache worsens, becomes unusual, or repeats frequently, contact a clinician.
steps.expect: pain trends down, or you switch from home care to medical advice.

recipes.verification: Within 1 hour, headache intensity is clearly lower, no red flags are present, and any medicine taken is within labeled dose and timing limits.

recipes.title: relieve constipation
recipes.name: relieve-constipation
recipes.goal: Mild constipation is relieved with fluids, fiber, movement, toilet positioning, and gentle medicine when appropriate.

steps.action: **Drink fluids.** Sip water or warm fluids through the day unless a clinician has restricted fluids.
steps.expect: urine is not dark and hard stools may soften.

steps.action: **Add fiber gradually.** [BRANCH: low fiber diet | already high fiber] add fruits, vegetables, beans, oats, or psyllium slowly; avoid sudden large increases if bloated.
steps.expect: stool bulk improves without major gas or cramping.

steps.action: **Move your body.** Walk or do gentle activity if safe.
steps.expect: bowel movement signals may increase. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not ignore severe abdominal pain, vomiting, or inability to pass gas while taking laxatives.

steps.action: **Use toilet posture.** Sit with knees higher than hips using a small footstool, lean forward, and relax the belly.
steps.expect: pushing requires less strain.

steps.action: **Respond to urges.** Use the bathroom when the urge appears and allow unhurried time.
steps.expect: stool is not held until harder.

steps.action: **Avoid straining.** Breathe out gently instead of bearing down hard.
steps.expect: hemorrhoid and fainting risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Try a gentle laxative if needed.** Use an over-the-counter osmotic laxative, stool softener, or fiber supplement as labeled.
steps.expect: relief occurs within the label timeframe.

steps.action: **Review constipating medicines.** Note opioids, iron, calcium, antacids, antihistamines, and some antidepressants.
steps.expect: a clinician or pharmacist can advise safer adjustments.

steps.action: **Escalate if not improving.** Contact a clinician if constipation lasts more than several days despite care or keeps recurring.
steps.expect: obstruction, medication effects, and other causes are considered.

recipes.verification: A bowel movement occurs without severe straining, or medical care is arranged because red-flag symptoms or persistent constipation are present.

recipes.title: relieve dry eyes from screens
recipes.name: relieve-dry-eyes-from-screens
recipes.goal: Screen-related dry eye discomfort is reduced by blinking, resting focus, improving airflow, and using lubricating drops when appropriate.

steps.action: **Pause and assess symptoms.** Look away from the screen and note pain, redness, vision change, or discharge.
steps.expect: symptoms fit mild dryness rather than urgent eye trouble.

steps.action: **Blink deliberately.** Close eyes fully for 2 seconds, squeeze gently for 2 seconds, then open; repeat 5 times.
steps.expect: the eye surface feels more coated.

steps.action: **Use distance breaks.** Every 20 minutes, look at something far away for about 20 seconds.
steps.expect: focusing muscles relax and blinking increases.

steps.action: **Lower the screen slightly.** Position the screen so your gaze is slightly downward.
steps.expect: eyelids cover more of the eye surface.

steps.action: **Reduce drying airflow.** Move fans, vents, or heaters away from your face.
steps.expect: eyes feel less exposed to moving air.

steps.action: **Use artificial tears if needed.** Put in preservative-free lubricating drops according to the label.
steps.expect: grittiness eases without stinging beyond a few seconds.

steps.action: **Clean contact lenses if worn.** Follow lens care instructions or switch to glasses for the session.
steps.expect: lens-related dryness decreases.

recipes.verification: After a 10-minute screen break routine, eyes feel less gritty, blinking is comfortable, and no urgent symptoms such as severe pain or vision loss are present.

recipes.title: remove a bee stinger
recipes.name: remove-a-bee-stinger
recipes.goal: A bee stinger is removed quickly, the sting is cleaned and cooled, and allergic reaction signs are monitored.

steps.action: **Check for allergy symptoms.** Look for breathing trouble, throat tightness, widespread hives, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting.
steps.expect: anaphylaxis signs are ruled in or out immediately.

steps.action: **Use epinephrine if prescribed.** [BRANCH: severe allergy signs | local sting only] use the auto-injector and call emergency services for severe signs; continue local care only if symptoms are local.
steps.expect: emergency treatment starts when needed. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not wait to see if anaphylaxis improves on its own.

steps.action: **Scrape the stinger out fast.** Use a credit card edge, fingernail, or other flat edge to scrape across the skin.
steps.expect: the stinger is removed quickly.

steps.action: **Avoid pinching the venom sac.** Do not squeeze with tweezers if a sac is visible.
steps.expect: less venom may be pushed into the skin.

steps.action: **Wash the area.** Clean with soap and water.
steps.expect: surface germs and venom residue are reduced.

steps.action: **Apply cold.** Wrap a cold pack in cloth and apply for 10 to 15 minutes at a time.
steps.expect: pain and swelling decrease.

steps.action: **Elevate if possible.** Raise the stung limb above heart level.
steps.expect: swelling is limited.

steps.action: **Use symptom relief if safe.** Consider an oral antihistamine for itching or acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain as labeled.
steps.expect: discomfort is controlled without exceeding label doses.

steps.action: **Monitor for delayed problems.** Watch for spreading redness, warmth, pus, fever, or swelling that worsens after 24 to 48 hours.
steps.expect: infection or delayed reaction triggers medical care.

recipes.verification: The stinger is out, the area is washed and cooled, and emergency allergy symptoms are absent or emergency services have been called.

recipes.title: remove a hangnail
recipes.name: remove-a-hangnail
recipes.goal: A torn strip of skin beside the nail is softened, clipped cleanly, protected, and watched for infection.

steps.action: **Wash your hands and tool.** Clean your hands, then wipe the clipper or nipper with alcohol if available.
steps.expect: clean skin and a clean cutting edge.

steps.action: **Soften the skin.** Soak the finger in warm water for 5 minutes, then pat it damp, not dry.
steps.expect: the hangnail lies flatter and feels less stiff.

steps.action: **Identify only the loose flap.** Find where the torn skin lifts away from living skin. Do not cut normal cuticle.
steps.expect: a visible loose strip with a clear base.

steps.action: **Clip at the base.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* clip only the dead loose flap at its base; never tear or pull it.
steps.expect: the snag is gone without a new split.

steps.action: **Rinse if it bled.** If a pinpoint bleed appears, rinse with water and hold clean pressure for a minute.
steps.expect: bleeding stops quickly.

steps.action: **Seal in moisture.** Apply thick hand cream, cuticle oil, or petroleum jelly around the nail fold.
steps.expect: the skin feels coated and less tight.

steps.action: **Cover if it rubs.** Use a small bandage if clothing, gloves, or work will catch the area.
steps.expect: the spot is protected from snagging.

steps.action: **Watch for infection.** Check daily for increasing redness, warmth, swelling, pus, red streaks, or worsening pain.
steps.expect: tenderness fades over 24 to 48 hours.

recipes.verification: The loose hangnail is clipped flush without tearing, the area is moisturized or covered, and there are no infection signs on daily checks.

recipes.title: remove a splinter
recipes.name: remove-a-splinter
recipes.goal: A small superficial splinter is removed cleanly in the direction it entered, with the skin cleaned and monitored afterward.

steps.action: **Wash hands and skin.** Clean your hands and the splinter area with soap and water.
steps.expect: dirt and surface oils are removed.

steps.action: **Inspect under bright light.** Identify the entry angle and whether an end is exposed.
steps.expect: you know which direction the splinter entered.

steps.action: **Clean the tool.** Wipe tweezers, and needle if used, with alcohol.
steps.expect: tool tips are clean and dry.

steps.action: **Grip an exposed end.** If the end is visible, grasp it close to the skin with tweezers.
steps.expect: the splinter does not crush or break.

steps.action: **Pull with the grain.** Draw the splinter out along the same angle it entered.
steps.expect: it slides out with minimal new tearing.

steps.action: **Expose a buried tip if needed.** If the tip is just under skin, lift only the top skin layer with a sterile needle.
steps.expect: enough tip is visible for tweezers.

steps.action: **Stop if it is deep.** Do not dig for a splinter that is invisible, under a nail, or near an eye.
steps.expect: the area is left intact for medical removal.

steps.action: **Wash again.** Rinse the site with soap and water after removal.
steps.expect: no visible debris remains.

steps.action: **Cover if irritated.** Apply a small bandage if the spot bleeds or will rub on clothing.
steps.expect: the wound is protected but not tight.

steps.action: **Monitor.** Check over the next day for redness, swelling, pus, fever, or increasing pain.
steps.expect: symptoms improve rather than spread.

recipes.verification: The splinter is fully removed or safely referred for care, the skin is clean, and there are no spreading infection signs.

recipes.title: reset your circadian rhythm
recipes.name: reset-your-circadian-rhythm
recipes.goal: Shift the body clock toward a stable sleep-wake schedule using consistent wake time, light timing, meals, and evening dimming.

steps.action: **Set the wake anchor.** Choose one wake time and keep it within 30 minutes daily.
steps.expect: mornings have a fixed reference point.

steps.action: **Get morning light.** Seek outdoor light for 10 to 30 minutes within an hour of waking.
steps.expect: alertness rises earlier in the day.

steps.action: **Move meals earlier.** Eat breakfast or a first meal after waking and avoid heavy meals close to bedtime.
steps.expect: digestion cues align with the new day.

steps.action: **Use daytime activity.** Add walking or exercise earlier in the day when possible.
steps.expect: sleep pressure builds naturally by evening.

steps.action: **Cut late caffeine.** Stop caffeine at least 8 hours before target bedtime.
steps.expect: stimulant effects are less likely at lights-out.

steps.action: **Dim the evening.** Lower bright lights and reduce stimulating screens for the last 1 to 2 hours.
steps.expect: the environment signals night.

steps.action: **Shift gradually.** Move wake time by 15 to 30 minutes every few days if the gap is large.
steps.expect: the change is tolerable enough to maintain.

steps.action: **Hold for two weeks.** Keep the same anchor through weekends and one bad night.
steps.expect: sleepiness begins arriving near the target bedtime.

recipes.verification: For seven consecutive days, wake time stays within 30 minutes of target, morning light happens within an hour, caffeine cutoff is met, and sleepiness appears closer to the planned bedtime.

recipes.title: set up an ergonomic desk
recipes.name: set-up-an-ergonomic-desk
recipes.goal: Arrange a desk so common work happens with supported feet, neutral wrists, relaxed shoulders, and regular movement.

steps.action: **Set the chair height.** Raise or lower the chair so elbows are near 90 degrees at the keyboard.
steps.expect: shoulders can drop while typing.

steps.action: **Support the feet.** Put feet flat on the floor or on a stable footrest.
steps.expect: thighs are supported and feet do not dangle.

steps.action: **Support the low back.** Sit back and add a small cushion or rolled towel if needed.
steps.expect: the back feels supported without rigid bracing.

steps.action: **Place the screen.** Put the main screen directly ahead, about arm's length away, with the top near eye level.
steps.expect: neck stays mostly neutral.

steps.action: **Place keyboard and mouse.** Keep both close enough that elbows stay near the body and wrists remain straight.
steps.expect: reaching and wrist bending are minimal.

steps.action: **Clear pressure points.** Move hard desk edges away from wrists and forearms.
steps.expect: no edge presses into soft tissue while working.

steps.action: **Add movement reminders.** Set a cue to stand, walk, or change position every 30 minutes.
steps.expect: posture resets before stiffness builds.

recipes.verification: Feet are supported, screen is centered near eye level, wrists are neutral, shoulders are relaxed, and at least one movement break occurs every 30 minutes.

recipes.title: shave your face
recipes.name: shave-your-face
recipes.goal: A clean, comfortable shave with no cuts, minimal irritation, and the sink left as you found it.

steps.action: **Soften the stubble first.** Shave after a shower, or hold a warm wet cloth against the face for a minute. Softened hair cuts with far less force.
steps.expect: skin warm and damp, stubble noticeably softer to the touch.

steps.action: **Apply lather to every area you will shave.** Work cream or gel into the stubble against the grain so it stands up.
steps.expect: even coverage with no dry patches.

steps.action: **Shave with the grain first, in short light strokes.** Let the razor's weight do the work; pressing harder removes skin, not more hair. Rinse the blade every few strokes.
steps.expect: smooth passes, cream cleared in strips, no pulling sensation. Pulling means a dull blade; stop and swap it.

steps.action: **Stretch the skin at tricky spots.** Jawline, chin, and upper lip: pull the skin flat with the free hand and slow down.
steps.expect: flat surfaces under the blade; these are the zones where cuts happen.

steps.action: **Re-lather and go across or against the grain only if you want a closer finish.** Against-grain is where irritation and ingrown hairs start; skip it if your skin protests.
steps.expect: closer result at slightly higher irritation cost, chosen deliberately.

steps.action: **Rinse with cool water and pat dry.** Cool water calms the skin; rubbing with a towel undoes that.
steps.expect: clean face, no remaining lather, minor redness at most.

steps.action: **Apply aftershave balm and clean the sink.** Rinse stubble off the basin, rinse and shake the razor dry, store it blade-up to dry.
steps.expect: moisturized skin, clean sink, a razor that will not rust between uses.

recipes.verification: The shaved areas are smooth in the direction you shaved, there are no active cuts, irritation is minor and fading, the razor is rinsed and stored dry, and the sink holds no stubble ring.

recipes.title: sleep cooler in summer
recipes.name: sleep-cooler-in-summer
recipes.goal: Make a hot bedroom safer and more sleep-friendly using ventilation, bedding, hydration, and heat-risk checks.

steps.action: **Block daytime heat.** Close curtains or blinds on sun-facing windows during the hottest hours.
steps.expect: the room gains less heat before bedtime.

steps.action: **Vent when outside air cools.** Open windows or use fans only when outdoor air is cooler or airflow helps evaporation.
steps.expect: air movement improves without pulling in hotter air.

steps.action: **Lighten the bed.** Use breathable sheets, lighter sleepwear, and fewer blankets.
steps.expect: heat can escape from the body.

steps.action: **Pre-cool the body.** Take a lukewarm shower or use a cool cloth before bed.
steps.expect: skin feels cooler without shivering.

steps.action: **Hydrate sensibly.** Drink water earlier in the evening and keep water nearby.
steps.expect: thirst is reduced without excessive overnight bathroom trips.

steps.action: **Move if needed.** Sleep in the coolest safe room, lower floor, or temporary cooling center if home remains dangerously hot.
steps.expect: the sleep location is cooler than the original room.

steps.action: **Watch for heat illness.** Check for dizziness, confusion, nausea, rapid pulse, fainting, or inability to cool down.
steps.expect: red flags trigger immediate cooling and medical help.

recipes.verification: Before sleep, bedding is lighter, airflow or cooling is set, water is available, the room is the coolest safe option, and no heat-illness red flags are present.

recipes.title: soothe a sore throat
recipes.name: soothe-a-sore-throat
recipes.goal: Throat pain is reduced enough to swallow, rest, and speak lightly while you watch for signs that need medical care.

steps.action: **Check for urgent symptoms first.** Look for trouble breathing, drooling, inability to swallow, severe one-sided swelling, stiff neck, rash, or confusion.
steps.expect: you either proceed with home care or seek urgent care immediately.

steps.action: **Make a salt-water gargle.** Stir about 1/2 teaspoon salt into a cup of warm water until dissolved.
steps.expect: the water tastes salty but not painfully strong.

steps.action: **Gargle without swallowing.** Tilt the head back, gargle 10 to 15 seconds, spit, and repeat until the cup is gone.
steps.expect: mucus loosens and the raw feeling dulls for a while.

steps.action: **Sip warm fluids.** Drink warm water, tea, broth, or honey-lemon water if honey is safe for you.
steps.expect: swallowing feels smoother and the throat stays moist.
