steps.action: **Use a lozenge or hard candy.** Let it dissolve slowly rather than chewing it.
steps.expect: saliva production increases and the scratchy feeling eases.

steps.action: **Add humidity.** [BRANCH: humidifier | steam] run a clean humidifier, or sit near a warm shower steam source without burning yourself.
steps.expect: dry air irritation decreases within 10 to 20 minutes.

steps.action: **Rest the voice.** Speak quietly only when needed and avoid whispering, which can strain the throat.
steps.expect: talking causes less scraping pain.

steps.action: **Track red flags.** See a doctor for fever above 101.5 F or 38.6 C, symptoms longer than 3 to 5 days, pus on tonsils, dehydration, repeated strep exposure, or pain that keeps worsening.
steps.expect: home care stays limited to mild, improving symptoms.

recipes.verification: Within 30 minutes, you can swallow small sips of fluid with less pain and no urgent red-flag symptom is present.

recipes.title: soothe itchy skin
recipes.name: soothe-itchy-skin
recipes.goal: Itchy skin is cooled, moisturized, protected from scratching, and escalated if it suggests allergy or infection.

steps.action: **Stop scratching.** Press or tap around the area instead of digging nails into skin.
steps.expect: the skin is not broken further.

steps.action: **Cool the area.** Apply a cool damp cloth for 10 to 15 minutes.
steps.expect: itching feels less intense.

steps.action: **Wash gently.** Rinse away sweat, plants, soap residue, or irritants with mild soap and water.
steps.expect: obvious irritants are removed.

steps.action: **Pat dry.** Use a towel gently without rubbing.
steps.expect: the skin is dry but not abraded.

steps.action: **Moisturize.** Apply fragrance-free moisturizer while skin is slightly damp.
steps.expect: dryness and tightness ease.

steps.action: **Use anti-itch medicine carefully.** Consider an oral antihistamine or topical product only as labeled.
steps.expect: medicine is used safely if chosen.

steps.action: **Cover if needed.** Use loose clothing or a clean bandage to reduce scratching.
steps.expect: nails cannot easily damage the skin.

steps.action: **Avoid triggers.** Pause fragranced products, hot showers, wool, and harsh detergents.
steps.expect: irritation is not reinforced.

steps.action: **Watch the pattern.** Note whether the itch spreads, forms hives, blisters, pus, or red streaks.
steps.expect: concerning changes are recognized.

steps.action: **Seek care if worsening.** Contact a clinician for spreading, infected, or persistent rash.
steps.expect: serious causes are evaluated.

recipes.verification: Itching is reduced, skin remains unbroken, and there are no severe allergy, infection, or spreading-rash signs.

recipes.title: start a couch to 5k
recipes.name: start-a-couch-to-5k
recipes.goal: Build from little or no running to finishing a comfortable 5 km using gradual run-walk sessions.

steps.action: **Pick three weekly run days.** Put them on the calendar with rest or easy walking days between them.
steps.expect: three specific sessions are scheduled before the week starts.

steps.action: **Start each session with walking.** Walk briskly for 5 minutes before any jogging.
steps.expect: breathing is warmer and joints feel less stiff.

steps.action: **Use short run-walk intervals.** Begin with 60 seconds easy jogging followed by 90 seconds walking, repeated for 20 minutes.
steps.expect: you finish feeling worked but able to speak in short sentences.

steps.action: **Progress only one notch per week.** Add a little jogging time or reduce walking time, keeping total session time near 25 to 35 minutes.
steps.expect: the next week feels challenging but not like a test.

steps.action: **Keep the pace easy.** Jog slowly enough that you could hold a conversation, even if that feels almost like walking.
steps.expect: breathing stays controlled and form does not collapse.

steps.action: **Stop for sharp pain.** If pain is sharp, one-sided, or changes your stride, stop running and walk home.
steps.expect: discomfort is not forced into a limp.

steps.action: **Finish with a cooldown.** Walk 5 minutes, drink water, and note distance or time completed.
steps.expect: breathing settles and the session is logged.

steps.action: **Attempt 5 km when continuous running feels manageable.** Choose a flat route and treat the first 5 km as completion, not racing.
steps.expect: the distance is completed without sprinting or limping.

recipes.verification: You complete 5 km at an easy effort without sharp pain, with a warmup, cooldown, and at least eight weeks of mostly consistent gradual sessions recorded.

recipes.title: start a gratitude practice
recipes.name: start-a-gratitude-practice
recipes.goal: Create a short daily gratitude practice that notices specific good moments without denying real problems.

steps.action: **Choose the anchor.** Tie the practice to one existing daily moment.
steps.expect: you know exactly when the entry will happen.

steps.action: **Write three specific items.** Name concrete things, people, comforts, or moments from the last 24 hours.
steps.expect: each line points to an actual event or detail.

steps.action: **Add why one item mattered.** Pick one line and write a short reason it affected you.
steps.expect: the entry feels connected rather than generic.

steps.action: **Keep the tone honest.** Allow hard days to include small gratitudes like clean water, a text reply, or five quiet minutes.
steps.expect: the practice does not require pretending everything is fine.

steps.action: **Review weekly.** Once a week, reread entries and mark any repeated themes.
steps.expect: patterns in support, values, or routines become visible.

recipes.verification: At least five entries exist after one week, each includes a specific gratitude, and one weekly review identifies at least one repeated theme.

recipes.title: start meditating daily
recipes.name: start-meditating-daily
recipes.goal: Start a daily meditation habit using short sessions that train attention without requiring a blank mind.

steps.action: **Choose a daily anchor.** Attach meditation to waking, lunch, or bedtime.
steps.expect: the session has a predictable trigger.

steps.action: **Set a short timer.** Begin with 5 minutes for the first week.
steps.expect: the duration feels small enough to repeat daily.

steps.action: **Take a stable posture.** Sit or stand upright with shoulders relaxed and hands supported.
steps.expect: breathing is easy and the body does not strain.

steps.action: **Pick one anchor.** Feel the breath at the nose, chest, belly, or feet on the floor.
steps.expect: attention has one simple place to return.

steps.action: **Notice and return.** When thoughts, sounds, or feelings pull attention away, label them lightly and return to the anchor.
steps.expect: wandering happens many times and each return counts as practice.

steps.action: **End deliberately.** At the timer, take one breath, notice the room, and stand slowly.
steps.expect: the session closes by choice, not by frustration.

steps.action: **Mark completion.** Check off the day or write one word about the session.
steps.expect: the habit streak is visible without judging performance.

recipes.verification: You complete at least five sessions in seven days, each ended by a timer, and you can describe returning attention to the chosen anchor at least once per session.

recipes.title: stop a shaving cut from bleeding
recipes.name: stop-a-shaving-cut-from-bleeding
recipes.goal: A small shaving nick stops bleeding, stays clean, and is protected from irritation.

steps.action: **Rinse the cut.** Use cool clean water to remove shaving cream and loose blood.
steps.expect: the cut surface is visible.

steps.action: **Apply direct pressure.** Press clean tissue or gauze on the cut without peeking for several minutes.
steps.expect: bleeding slows.

steps.action: **Use cold water.** Splash or hold cool water on the area after pressure.
steps.expect: oozing decreases.

steps.action: **Apply styptic if available.** Wet the styptic pencil and touch only the nick briefly.
steps.expect: stinging is brief and bleeding reduces.

steps.action: **Blot gently.** Pat around the area without wiping across the cut.
steps.expect: the clot stays in place.

steps.action: **Add a tiny balm layer.** Dab a small amount of fragrance-free balm or petroleum jelly over the nick.
steps.expect: the area is protected without smearing.

steps.action: **Avoid aftershave on it.** Keep alcohol-based products off the open cut.
steps.expect: irritation and burning are avoided.

steps.action: **Pause shaving nearby.** Do not run the razor over the cut again.
steps.expect: the nick does not reopen.

steps.action: **Check after 10 minutes.** Look for continued bleeding, swelling, or a flap of skin.
steps.expect: the cut is sealed or needs more attention.

steps.action: **Clean the razor.** Rinse and dry the razor before storing it.
steps.expect: future irritation risk is reduced.

recipes.verification: The shaving nick is no longer actively bleeding and is lightly protected without signs of a deeper wound.

recipes.title: stop hiccups
recipes.name: stop-hiccups
recipes.goal: Hiccups stop or become mild enough to ignore, using safe breathing and swallowing tricks that interrupt the diaphragm spasm reflex.

steps.action: **Sit upright and relax your belly.** Put both feet on the floor and let the shoulders drop.
steps.expect: breathing feels less rushed and the hiccup rhythm is easy to notice.

steps.action: **Try one controlled breath hold.** Inhale normally, hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then exhale slowly through the nose or pursed lips.
steps.expect: the next few breaths come slower, and the hiccup pattern may pause.

steps.action: **Repeat once, not endlessly.** If the first hold helped but did not stop it, do one more gentle hold after three normal breaths.
steps.expect: either the hiccups stop or you know this trick is not enough.

steps.action: **Use the small-sip water trick.** Take 8 to 10 tiny sips in a row without talking between them.
steps.expect: repeated swallowing gives the throat and vagus nerve a steady competing signal.

steps.action: **Switch posture if needed.** [BRANCH: can bend safely | cannot bend safely] bend forward slightly and sip from the far side of the glass, or stay upright and sip through a straw.
steps.expect: swallowing feels deliberate, and the diaphragm has a chance to reset.

steps.action: **Add a diaphragm reset.** Breathe in so the belly expands, hold 3 seconds, then exhale twice as long as the inhale.
steps.expect: the abdomen softens and the chest stops jumping as sharply.

steps.action: **Wait two quiet minutes.** Do not talk, laugh hard, smoke, drink alcohol, or gulp carbonated drinks during the pause.
steps.expect: any remaining hiccups are spaced farther apart.

steps.action: **Escalate if hiccups persist.** If hiccups last more than 48 hours, keep returning, or come with severe pain, weakness, confusion, vomiting, or trouble breathing, contact a doctor.
steps.expect: persistent or concerning hiccups are treated as a medical symptom, not a willpower problem.

recipes.verification: No hiccup occurs for 5 continuous minutes while you breathe normally, talk softly, and swallow without discomfort.

recipes.title: strengthen a weak ankle
recipes.name: strengthen-a-weak-ankle
recipes.goal: Build ankle strength and balance gradually after mild weakness or old sprains while avoiding signs that need clinical care.

steps.action: **Check baseline safely.** Stand near support and compare ankle pain, swelling, and balance side to side.
steps.expect: you know the starting difference without provoking pain.

steps.action: **Restore range of motion.** Trace the alphabet with the foot or make slow ankle circles.
steps.expect: movement is smooth and pain stays mild.

steps.action: **Strengthen four directions.** Use a band or gentle hand resistance for up, down, inward, and outward ankle motions.
steps.expect: muscles work around the ankle without sharp pain.

steps.action: **Add calf raises.** Rise onto both toes slowly, then lower with control.
steps.expect: calf and ankle load feels symmetrical or only mildly harder on one side.

steps.action: **Train balance.** Stand on one foot near support for 20 to 30 seconds.
steps.expect: wobbling decreases across attempts.

steps.action: **Progress carefully.** Add single-leg calf raises, uneven surfaces, or light hops only when pain-free basics are easy.
steps.expect: challenge increases without swelling afterward.

steps.action: **Recheck next day.** Note pain, swelling, and walking quality.
steps.expect: the ankle is no worse the day after training.

recipes.verification: For two weeks, exercises are completed at least four days per week, walking is not worsened the next day, and single-leg balance time improves or becomes more controlled.

recipes.title: stretch at your desk
recipes.name: stretch-at-your-desk
recipes.goal: Once per work hour, a short neck-shoulders-hips sequence is completed at the desk, leaving muscles noticeably looser and posture reset, with no strain from overstretching.

steps.action: **Set the hourly trigger once, at the start of the day.** A repeating alarm labeled "stretch" beats intending to remember; snoozing is allowed, skipping twice in a row is the failure signal.
steps.expect: a recurring reminder exists for every working hour.

steps.action: **When it fires, stand up and step away from the chair.** Standing is half the benefit; the sequence done seated is the fallback, not the default.
steps.expect: standing, weight even on both feet, screen out of reach.

steps.action: **Neck: slow half-circles and side holds.** Drop chin to chest, roll the ear toward one shoulder, hold 15 seconds, roll to the other side, hold 15 seconds. Move only through the front half circle; never roll the head backward in a full circle.
steps.expect: a mild pull along the side of the neck, no pinching or tingling.

steps.action: **Shoulders: rolls, then a chest opener.** Five slow shoulder rolls backward, then clasp hands behind the back, straighten the arms, and lift the knuckles an inch while squeezing the shoulder blades. Hold 20 seconds, breathing normally.
steps.expect: the front of the shoulders and chest feel a gentle stretch; shoulders sit lower than before.

steps.action: **Hips: standing hip-flexor lunge or seated figure-4.** [BRANCH: space and privacy allow → half-kneel or split-stance lunge, back leg's hip pressed gently forward, 20 seconds per side | open-plan office → seated, ankle over opposite knee, hinge forward from the hips, 20 seconds per side]
steps.expect: stretch felt in the front of the hip (lunge) or outer hip and glute (figure-4).

steps.action: **Hold everything static; never bounce.** Each position is a steady hold at mild tension, roughly 3 of 10 discomfort. Bouncing (ballistic stretching) triggers the muscle's protective contraction and is how desk stretchers strain themselves.
steps.expect: tension eases slightly during each hold instead of building.

steps.action: **Reset posture and sit back down.** Roll shoulders back once, sit with hips against the chair back, screen at eye height.
steps.expect: sitting feels noticeably different for the first minute; timer still armed for the next hour.

recipes.verification: At the end of the workday: the hourly reminder fired and was answered (full or fallback version) at least 5 of 8 hours, each stretch was a static hold with no bouncing, and there is no new pain in neck, shoulders, or hips.

recipes.title: take a power nap
recipes.name: take-a-power-nap
recipes.goal: A nap of 20 minutes or less is taken in the early afternoon and ends on time, restoring alertness for the rest of the day without grogginess and without damaging that night's sleep.

steps.action: **Confirm the window.** Nap in the early afternoon dip, roughly 1-3 p.m. for a standard schedule. Later naps drain the sleep pressure the night needs. [BRANCH: after 3 p.m. and dragging → skip the nap; use daylight, a walk, and an earlier bedtime instead | within the window → proceed]
steps.expect: current time is inside the window before any lying down happens.

steps.action: **Optionally take the coffee-nap.** Drink a cup of coffee quickly, right before lying down. Caffeine takes about 20 minutes to hit the bloodstream, so it kicks in exactly at wake-up and stacks with the nap's benefit. Skip this if bedtime is under 8 hours away or caffeine sits badly with you.
steps.expect: coffee finished within a couple of minutes, immediately followed by lying down.

steps.action: **Set the alarm for about 25 minutes.** That budgets around 5 minutes to fall asleep and caps actual sleep near 20. The cap is the whole trick: past 25-30 minutes of sleep you descend into deep slow-wave sleep, and waking from that produces sleep inertia (half an hour or more of heavy grogginess, worse than no nap).
steps.expect: alarm set, volume confirmed, phone face-down and silenced otherwise.

steps.action: **Kill light and noise cheaply.** Dim the room or use an eye mask or a hood; earplugs or steady background noise if the environment is loud. Loosen tight clothing, shoes off if possible.
steps.expect: eyes closed in near-dark, no notification pings possible.

steps.action: **Lie back and let it happen without performance pressure.** Slow breathing, let thoughts wander. Even drowsy rest without full sleep restores measurable alertness, so "I never actually fell asleep" is still a win.
steps.expect: muscles unclench within a few minutes; drifting, or at worst calm rest.

steps.action: **Get up at the alarm, immediately and fully.** Sit up, stand, light on or curtains open, a few shoulder rolls and a glass of water. Do not negotiate for five more minutes; the second doze is the one that overshoots into deep sleep.
steps.expect: upright and in bright light within a minute of the alarm.

steps.action: **Re-engage with something easy for the first minutes.** Light tasks first; full sharpness arrives within 5-15 minutes (near-instantly if the coffee-nap was used).
steps.expect: alertness noticeably better than pre-nap by the 15-minute mark.

recipes.verification: Asleep or resting within roughly 10 minutes, up at the first alarm with total lie-down time under 30 minutes, subjective alertness clearly improved within 15 minutes of rising, and that night's sleep onset was normal.

recipes.title: take a proper break
recipes.name: take-a-proper-break
recipes.goal: Take a break that actually restores attention by leaving the work surface, moving the body, hydrating, and mentally detaching.

steps.action: **Stop at a real boundary.** Finish the current sentence, line, dish, or message, then pause.
steps.expect: the work is left in a stable state.

steps.action: **Write the re-entry cue.** Note the next action you will take when you return.
steps.expect: you do not need to hold the task in memory.

steps.action: **Set the break length.** [BRANCH: short reset | longer recovery] Use 5 minutes after a short sprint, or 15-30 minutes after a long block.
steps.expect: the break has an end, not a vague escape.

steps.action: **Leave the screen.** Stand up and move away from the desk or device.
steps.expect: your eyes and hands are no longer locked to the same work posture.

steps.action: **Move lightly.** Walk, stretch, shake out hands, or look out a window at distance.
steps.expect: breathing deepens and physical stiffness drops.

steps.action: **Hydrate or snack deliberately.** Drink water; eat if hunger is the issue. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not use the break for purchases, replies, or decisions you would not make while rested.
steps.expect: the body need is addressed without opening a new rabbit hole.

steps.action: **Detach for the remaining time.** No work talk, work tabs, or problem-solving rehearsal.
steps.expect: attention is not secretly still at the desk.

steps.action: **Return on the timer and use the cue.** Sit down, read the re-entry note, and start with the next action.
steps.expect: the transition back is clean.

recipes.verification: You left the work surface, moved, hydrated or handled a body need, avoided work content, and returned at the planned time with a written next action.

recipes.title: take a shower
recipes.name: take-a-shower
recipes.goal: You are clean, dried, and dressed after a shower, without scalds, slips, or a flooded bathroom.

steps.action: **Stage everything before undressing.** Towel on the hook by the shower, clothes in the dry zone, toiletries inside the stall.
steps.expect: nothing will require a dripping walk across the bathroom.

steps.action: **Start the water and set the temperature *before* getting in.** Run the mixer toward warm, test with a hand/wrist in the spray, adjust to comfortably warm — not reddening-hot.
steps.expect: stable comfortable temperature at the hand test; curtain/door positioned to keep spray inside.

steps.action: **Enter carefully and wet down fully.** One hand on a wall/grab point while stepping in.
steps.expect: hair and body fully wet.

steps.action: **Shampoo the hair.** A coin-sized amount worked into the scalp, then rinsed completely.
steps.expect: no slippery residue at the scalp when rinsed.

steps.action: **Wash the body top-down with soap.** Face, neck, torso, arms, groin, legs, feet — top-down so rinse water carries soap past already-clean skin. Mind the extra-slip while feet are soapy.
steps.expect: all skin lathered and rinsed; no soap film left.

steps.action: **Shut off the water and squeegee excess off your body with your hands.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* none — but this is the slip-critical moment: wring hair inside the stall, then reach for the towel *before* stepping out.
steps.expect: towel in hand while still standing on the wet-safe surface.

steps.action: **Step out onto the mat and dry fully, feet last and thoroughly.**
steps.expect: dry body, dry feet before walking on tile; floor around the mat essentially dry.

steps.action: **Leave the wet zone tidy.** Hang the towel spread out, curtain spread to dry, ventilate (fan or window).
steps.expect: moisture venting; no puddles.

recipes.verification: You are clean, fully dry (feet included), dressed, the bathroom floor is dry, the towel and curtain are spread to dry, and ventilation is running.

recipes.title: tie shoelaces
recipes.name: tie-shoelaces
recipes.goal: Both shoes are tied with a snug, flat bow that stays tied through a day of walking.

steps.action: **Snug the lacing from the toe upward.** Pull each crossing pair gently up the shoe so the shoe hugs the foot, finishing with both lace ends equal.
steps.expect: shoe feels evenly snug; two equal free ends.

steps.action: **Make the starting knot.** Cross the ends, wrap one under the crossing point, pull both tight against the shoe.
steps.expect: a flat base knot lying against the tongue.

steps.action: **Form a loop ("bunny ear") with one end.** Pinch it at its base.
steps.expect: one stable loop, a few centimeters tall.

steps.action: **Wrap the other end around the loop's base, and push a fold of it through the gap behind the wrap.**
steps.expect: a second loop emerging through the gap.

steps.action: **Grab both loops and pull apart firmly.**
steps.expect: a symmetric bow with two loops and two free ends, seated tight against the base knot.

steps.action: **Check the bow's orientation.** A correctly tied (square) bow sits *horizontal* across the shoe. A vertical, twisting bow is a granny knot — it will untie itself; see F1.
steps.expect: horizontal bow.

steps.action: **Repeat for the other shoe.**
steps.expect: both shoes tied, bows horizontal, ends clear of the ground.

recipes.verification: Both bows lie horizontal and tight, nothing touches the ground, and the shoes stay tied through normal walking without re-tying.

recipes.title: treat a blister
recipes.name: treat-a-blister
recipes.goal: A friction blister is protected, pain is reduced, and infection risk is minimized while the skin heals.

steps.action: **Wash hands and the area.** Clean with soap and water, then dry gently.
steps.expect: skin is clean and grit is removed.

steps.action: **Identify blister type.** [BRANCH: intact and tolerable | intact but painful or likely to burst | already torn]
steps.expect: the covering skin condition is clear.

steps.action: **Leave intact blisters closed when possible.** Do not pop a blister that is small, clean, and not limiting movement.
steps.expect: fluid cushion remains under unbroken skin.

steps.action: **Pad around pressure.** Use a donut of moleskin or a blister bandage so shoe pressure lands around the blister.
steps.expect: walking pressure decreases immediately.

steps.action: **Drain only if necessary.** If large, painful, or certain to tear, sterilize a needle, puncture near the edge, and leave roof skin in place.
steps.expect: fluid drains while the protective top skin remains attached.

steps.action: **Cover the blister.** Apply a hydrocolloid blister bandage or sterile gauze with light tape.
steps.expect: dressing stays put without squeezing the blister.

steps.action: **Reduce friction source.** Change socks, loosen laces, add padding, or stop the activity.
steps.expect: the same spot is no longer being rubbed.

steps.action: **Change dressing as needed.** Replace loose, wet, or dirty coverings with clean ones.
steps.expect: wound stays covered and dry enough to heal.

steps.action: **Watch for infection.** Check daily for spreading redness, warmth, pus, red streaks, fever, or worsening pain.
steps.expect: either normal healing or a clear reason to seek care.

steps.action: **Let dead skin release naturally.** Trim only loose, clean dead skin after healing begins.
steps.expect: tender new skin remains protected.

recipes.verification: The blister is clean, covered or padded, protected from further rubbing, and shows no spreading redness, pus, fever, or worsening pain.

recipes.title: treat a bug bite
recipes.name: treat-a-bug-bite
recipes.goal: Calm a minor bug bite, reduce itching and swelling, and recognize signs that need medical help.

steps.action: **Move away from insects.** Leave the area or cover exposed skin before treating the bite.
steps.expect: no new bites are happening.

steps.action: **Check for a stinger or tick.** [BRANCH: visible stinger | attached tick | simple bite] scrape a stinger away, remove a tick with fine tweezers, or continue for a simple bite.
steps.expect: no insect parts remain on the skin surface.

steps.action: **Wash the bite.** Clean with soap and running water, then pat dry.
steps.expect: dirt, saliva, and surface irritants are removed.

steps.action: **Apply a cold compress.** Wrap ice or a cold pack in cloth and hold it on for 10 minutes.
steps.expect: swelling and heat start to decrease.

steps.action: **Use anti-itch treatment.** Apply hydrocortisone cream, calamine, or an oral antihistamine according to the label.
steps.expect: itching becomes less intense within the product's expected time.

steps.action: **Avoid scratching.** Trim nails, cover the bite with a bandage, or tap around it instead of scratching.
steps.expect: the skin stays unbroken.

steps.action: **Repeat comfort care.** Reapply cold compresses and labeled anti-itch treatment as needed.
steps.expect: symptoms remain manageable and localized.

steps.action: **Watch for allergic red flags.** Look for trouble breathing, lip or tongue swelling, dizziness, vomiting, or hives away from the bite. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* severe allergic reactions can progress quickly; call emergency services immediately if these appear.
steps.expect: either no red flags are present or urgent help is contacted.

steps.action: **Watch for infection.** Check over the next 24 to 48 hours for spreading redness, warmth, pus, fever, or worsening pain.
steps.expect: the bite improves or stays stable rather than spreading.

steps.action: **Seek care when needed.** Contact a clinician for infection signs, a bite near the eye, a tick bite concern, or symptoms lasting more than a few days.
steps.expect: concerning cases are assessed instead of ignored.

recipes.verification: The bite is clean, itch is controlled without scratching, and no allergic-reaction or infection red flags are present.

recipes.title: treat a canker sore
recipes.name: treat-a-canker-sore
recipes.goal: A canker sore is kept clean, less irritated, and monitored until it heals or needs dental or medical care.

steps.action: **Identify the sore.** Look for a small round or oval painful ulcer inside the mouth.
steps.expect: it matches a typical canker sore location.

steps.action: **Rinse with salt water.** Mix salt in warm water and swish gently, then spit.
steps.expect: the area feels cleaner, even if it stings briefly.

steps.action: **Brush gently.** Use a soft toothbrush and avoid scraping the sore.
steps.expect: teeth are clean without reopening the ulcer.

steps.action: **Avoid irritants.** Skip spicy, acidic, crunchy, or very hot foods while it hurts.
steps.expect: meals cause less burning.

steps.action: **Use topical relief.** Apply an oral pain gel or protective paste as labeled.
steps.expect: pain is reduced or the sore is shielded.

steps.action: **Keep hydrated.** Sip cool water if eating is uncomfortable.
steps.expect: dry mouth does not worsen irritation.

steps.action: **Do not pick it.** Keep fingers and sharp foods away from the ulcer.
steps.expect: the sore is not enlarged.

steps.action: **Track healing time.** Note the first day you noticed it.
steps.expect: you can tell if it persists beyond the usual 1 to 2 weeks.

steps.action: **Check for triggers.** Notice recent mouth injury, stress, dental appliance rubbing, or new toothpaste.
steps.expect: avoidable irritation is identified.

steps.action: **Escalate if persistent.** Contact a dentist or clinician if it does not improve as expected.
steps.expect: lingering ulcers are assessed.

recipes.verification: The sore is protected from irritants, pain is manageable, and it is improving within the expected healing window.

recipes.title: treat a cold sore
recipes.name: treat-a-cold-sore
recipes.goal: A cold sore is treated early, kept clean, and managed so it heals while reducing spread to other people and other body sites.

steps.action: **Start at the tingle.** Apply over-the-counter antiviral cream as directed, or start prescribed antiviral tablets if you already have them for outbreaks.
steps.expect: treatment begins before or soon after blisters appear.

steps.action: **Wash before and after touching it.** Use soap and water any time you apply medicine or balm.
steps.expect: lower risk of spreading virus to eyes, fingers, or other people.

steps.action: **Keep it moist.** Apply petroleum jelly or bland balm to reduce cracking.
steps.expect: the sore feels less tight and is less likely to split.

steps.action: **Do not pick.** Let blisters and crusts stay in place. Picking delays healing and spreads virus.
steps.expect: crust remains intact until it loosens naturally.

steps.action: **Avoid sharing mouth-contact items.** Do not share cups, utensils, lip balm, towels, razors, or kissing while the sore is active.
steps.expect: less chance of passing it on.

steps.action: **Avoid oral contact.** Skip oral sex during tingling, blisters, or crusting because HSV can spread to genitals.
steps.expect: no direct contact with active lesions.

steps.action: **Use sun and wind protection.** Apply SPF lip balm when outdoors and protect cracked skin from wind.
steps.expect: less irritation and fewer trigger exposures.

steps.action: **Track healing.** Most cold sores crust and heal in about 7 to 10 days, sometimes up to 2 weeks.
steps.expect: pain and crusting steadily decrease.

recipes.verification: The sore is treated early if possible, kept moist and unpicked, contact-spread precautions are in place, and healing improves within 7 to 14 days.

recipes.title: treat a corn or callus
recipes.name: treat-a-corn-or-callus
recipes.goal: A corn or callus is softened, cushioned, and prevented from recurring by reducing pressure or friction.

steps.action: **Inspect the skin.** Check for open skin, redness, drainage, bleeding, or severe tenderness.
steps.expect: only intact thickened skin is treated at home.

steps.action: **Soak the area.** Soak the foot or hand in warm water for 10 to 15 minutes.
steps.expect: thick skin feels softer.

steps.action: **File gently.** [BRANCH: foot callus | hand callus] rub lightly with a pumice stone or file, removing only softened surface skin.
steps.expect: the area is smoother without pain or bleeding. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not cut corns or calluses with a blade, razor, or sharp tool.

steps.action: **Moisturize.** Apply a plain moisturizer to intact skin after drying.
steps.expect: skin feels less dry and cracked.

steps.action: **Cushion pressure.** Use a non-medicated pad, moleskin, or gel cushion around the corn or callus.
steps.expect: walking or gripping causes less rubbing.

steps.action: **Address footwear or tools.** Switch to wider shoes, thicker socks, gloves, or adjusted handles that remove the pressure point.
steps.expect: the same spot is not repeatedly compressed.

steps.action: **Repeat gradually.** Soak, file lightly, and moisturize a few times per week.
steps.expect: thick skin reduces slowly without injury.

steps.action: **Monitor for injury.** Stop if pain, bleeding, redness, or drainage appears.
steps.expect: complications trigger medical care.

steps.action: **Get help if persistent.** See a clinician or podiatrist if pain continues or the cause cannot be corrected.
steps.expect: structural or footwear issues are assessed.

recipes.verification: Only intact thickened skin was gently filed, the area is cushioned, and the pressure source has been reduced.

recipes.title: treat a minor cut
recipes.name: treat-a-minor-cut
recipes.goal: A minor cut or scrape is cleaned, protected, and healing, and you know the specific signs that mean it needs professional care instead.

steps.action: **Wash your hands before touching the wound.** (`daily/self-care/wash-hands`.)
steps.expect: clean hands; gloves if treating someone else and they are available.

steps.action: **Stop the bleeding with direct pressure.** Press a clean cloth or gauze firmly on the cut for several minutes without peeking. Lifting the cloth to check restarts the clock.
steps.expect: bleeding stopped or reduced to a slow ooze after 5 minutes of uninterrupted pressure. Still soaking through after 10 minutes of firm pressure is a seek-care sign.

steps.action: **Rinse the wound under cool running water.** Let the stream flush it for a minute or two; wash the skin *around* it with mild soap. Soap, alcohol, and hydrogen peroxide inside the wound itself damage tissue and slow healing; water does the cleaning.
steps.expect: visible dirt and debris flushed out; the wound looks clean.

steps.action: **Remove small debris the water missed.** Tweezers cleaned with alcohol, working gently at the surface only. Anything that resists a gentle pull stays for a professional.
steps.expect: no visible grit; no digging.

steps.action: **Dress it.** A thin layer of antibiotic ointment or petroleum jelly (keeps the wound moist, which heals faster than drying out), then a bandage sized so the pad covers the wound and the adhesive grips dry skin.
steps.expect: wound covered, pad not stuck to the cut itself.

steps.action: **Change the dressing daily and keep it dry.** Re-dress after showers, or sooner if wet or dirty. Each change is a ten-second inspection.
steps.expect: day by day, the wound looks calmer: less red, drier edges, then a scab or closed line.

steps.action: **Watch for infection over the next days.** Increasing redness spreading outward, swelling, warmth, throbbing pain, pus, or fever mean the recipe is over and a clinician is next.
steps.expect: none of those; steady quiet healing.

recipes.verification: Bleeding stopped with pressure, the wound was flushed clean with water only, it is dressed moist and covered, dressings are changed daily, and the infection watch-list is being checked and staying negative.

recipes.title: treat a paper cut
recipes.name: treat-a-paper-cut
recipes.goal: A paper cut is cleaned, bleeding is stopped, stinging is reduced, and the cut is protected from reopening.

steps.action: **Wash your hands.** Clean your hands with soap and water before touching the cut.
steps.expect: dirt and germs from your hands are reduced.

steps.action: **Rinse the cut.** Hold the cut under clean running water for a short rinse.
steps.expect: paper dust or surface debris is gone.

steps.action: **Stop the bleeding.** [BRANCH: light bleeding | persistent bleeding] press clean gauze or cloth firmly for several minutes; seek care if bleeding continues after 10 minutes.
steps.expect: bleeding stops or becomes a tiny ooze. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not seal a dirty or deep cut closed with glue or tape before proper cleaning and assessment.

steps.action: **Wash around it.** Use mild soap on the surrounding skin, not deep in the cut.
steps.expect: the area is clean without extra stinging from harsh chemicals.

steps.action: **Reduce sting.** Hold a cool damp cloth on the cut for a minute if it burns.
steps.expect: stinging settles.

steps.action: **Apply a thin barrier.** Use a tiny amount of petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment if you can use it safely.
steps.expect: the cut stays moist and less likely to crack open.

steps.action: **Cover with a thin bandage.** Place a small bandage so the pad covers the cut and the adhesive sits on dry skin.
steps.expect: the cut is protected without bulky pressure.

steps.action: **Protect the movement point.** If on a fingertip or knuckle, place the bandage so bending does not pull the cut apart.
steps.expect: normal motion does not reopen it.

steps.action: **Change when wet or dirty.** Replace the bandage and inspect for redness, swelling, pus, warmth, or worsening pain.
steps.expect: infection signs are noticed early.

recipes.verification: Bleeding has stopped, the cut is clean and covered, and there are no signs that require medical care.

recipes.title: treat a stye
recipes.name: treat-a-stye
recipes.goal: A likely stye is cared for with warm compresses and hygiene while monitoring for signs that need medical care.

steps.action: **Check for urgent signs.** Look for vision changes, severe pain, fever, spreading redness, or swelling closing the eye.
steps.expect: none of those urgent signs are present.

steps.action: **Wash hands.** Clean hands with soap and water before touching near the eye.
steps.expect: hands are clean and dry.

steps.action: **Warm a compress.** Wet a clean cloth with warm, not hot, water and wring it out.
steps.expect: cloth feels comfortably warm on the inner wrist.

steps.action: **Apply the compress.** Hold it on the closed eyelid for 10-15 minutes, rewarming as needed.
steps.expect: the lid feels warmed and softened without burning.

steps.action: **Clean the lid gently.** Wipe crust from the lash line with clean water or diluted mild cleanser.
steps.expect: crust loosens without rubbing the eye.

steps.action: **Avoid squeezing.** Leave the bump alone between compresses. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* squeezing can worsen infection or injure the eyelid; do not try to pop it.
steps.expect: the stye drains only on its own, if at all.

steps.action: **Pause eye makeup and contacts.** Use glasses and skip eye cosmetics until healed.
steps.expect: fewer irritants contact the eyelid.

steps.action: **Repeat daily.** Use warm compresses 3-4 times per day until improving.
steps.expect: tenderness and swelling trend down over several days.

recipes.verification: The eyelid is being warmed with clean compresses, the bump is not squeezed, and pain, swelling, and redness are stable or improving without vision changes.

recipes.title: treat a sunburn
recipes.name: treat-a-sunburn
recipes.goal: A mild to moderate sunburn is cooled, moisturized, protected, and monitored for signs that require medical care.

steps.action: **Get out of UV exposure.** Move indoors or into full shade and cover burned skin
steps.expect: the burn is no longer exposed to direct sun.

steps.action: **Cool with water, not ice.** Use a cool shower, bath, or damp cloth for 10 to 15 minutes
steps.expect: skin feels less hot without numbness or sharp cold pain.

steps.action: **Pat dry gently.** Leave the skin slightly damp instead of rubbing
steps.expect: the towel does not scrape or sting the burn.

steps.action: **Moisturize while damp.** Apply fragrance-free moisturizer or aloe gel in a thin layer
steps.expect: skin feels less tight and no greasy heat-trapping layer forms.

steps.action: **Hydrate.** Drink water or an electrolyte drink, especially after sweating
steps.expect: urine becomes pale and thirst eases over time.

steps.action: **Leave blisters intact.** Do not pop blisters; ⚠️ *Irreversible:* opened blisters increase infection risk and slow healing
steps.expect: blister roofs remain clean and unbroken.

steps.action: **Reduce friction.** Wear loose, soft clothing and avoid exfoliants, retinoids, and harsh soaps
steps.expect: clothing does not scrape the burned area.

steps.action: **Monitor severity.** Watch pain, swelling, fever, chills, dizziness, confusion, or widespread blistering [BRANCH: mild | serious]
steps.expect: you know whether home care is enough.

recipes.verification: The burned skin is cool, moisturized, protected from sun and friction, and no serious symptoms or infection signs are present.

recipes.title: treat an ingrown toenail
recipes.name: treat-an-ingrown-toenail
recipes.goal: A mildly ingrown toenail is cleaned, pressure is reduced, and the nail edge is encouraged to grow out without digging into the skin.

steps.action: **Wash your hands and foot.** Clean the toe with soap and water before touching the nail fold.
steps.expect: the skin is clean and debris is gone.

steps.action: **Soak the toe.** Soak in warm water for 10 to 15 minutes, then pat dry.
steps.expect: the skin and nail edge feel softer.

steps.action: **Reduce pressure.** Put on open-toe sandals or wide shoes, and avoid tight socks.
steps.expect: the sore side is not pressed by footwear.

steps.action: **Lift only the visible edge.** If the corner is visible, slide a tiny piece of clean cotton or waxed dental floss under the edge.
steps.expect: the nail edge sits just above the skin without sharp pain.

steps.action: **Avoid digging or cutting the side.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not cut a wedge, dig with scissors, or tear skin because this can worsen infection and shape.
steps.expect: the nail corner remains intact.

steps.action: **Repeat gently.** Soak once or twice daily and replace the cotton with a clean tiny piece after each soak.
steps.expect: pressure gradually decreases over several days.

steps.action: **Protect the toe.** Keep it clean and dry between soaks, and avoid running or impact until pain improves.
steps.expect: the toe is less sore during normal walking.

recipes.verification: The toe is clean, the nail corner is not being cut into, footwear does not press on it, and pain is improving rather than worsening over 48 hours.

recipes.title: treat athletes foot
recipes.name: treat-athletes-foot
recipes.goal: Athlete's foot is treated with dryness, antifungal medicine, and habits that reduce spread and recurrence.

steps.action: **Wash and dry feet.** Clean feet daily and dry carefully between toes.
steps.expect: skin is clean and moisture is removed.

steps.action: **Apply antifungal treatment.** [BRANCH: cream | spray or powder] apply an over-the-counter antifungal as labeled to affected skin and nearby area.
steps.expect: medicine covers the rash without heavy buildup.

steps.action: **Continue long enough.** Use treatment for the full label course, often 1 to 4 weeks, and a bit after symptoms clear if the label says so.
steps.expect: fungus is less likely to return. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not cut away deep cracked skin or open blisters at home.

steps.action: **Change socks daily.** Use clean dry socks and change sooner after sweating.
steps.expect: feet stay drier through the day.

steps.action: **Rotate shoes.** Let shoes dry fully between wears and choose breathable footwear.
steps.expect: damp shoe interiors are reduced.

steps.action: **Treat shoes if needed.** Use antifungal powder or spray in shoes as labeled.
steps.expect: reinfection from footwear is less likely.

steps.action: **Protect shared spaces.** Wear sandals in locker rooms, pools, and shared showers.
steps.expect: spread to and from surfaces is reduced.

steps.action: **Avoid sharing towels.** Launder towels and socks after use.
steps.expect: fungus is not passed to others.

steps.action: **Reassess after treatment.** Check whether itching, scaling, and cracking are clearly improving.
steps.expect: lack of improvement triggers medical advice.

recipes.verification: Feet are dry, antifungal treatment is being used as labeled, towels are not shared, and rash is improving without infection signs.

recipes.title: treat dandruff
recipes.name: treat-dandruff
recipes.goal: Scalp flaking and itch are reduced using appropriate shampoo contact time, rotation, and scalp care while recognizing when it may be a medical condition.

steps.action: **Choose one active ingredient.** Start with a dandruff shampoo that matches your scalp tolerance and label instructions.
steps.expect: you know which active ingredient you are testing.

steps.action: **Wet hair and scalp fully.** Use warm water and part the hair enough to reach the scalp.
steps.expect: the scalp is wet, not just the hair surface.

steps.action: **Massage into the scalp.** Apply shampoo to the scalp with fingertips, not nails.
steps.expect: the lather touches the flaky or itchy areas.

steps.action: **Leave it on.** Keep the medicated shampoo on for the label time, often 3 to 5 minutes.
steps.expect: the shampoo has contact time before rinsing.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly.** Rinse until the water runs clear and the scalp no longer feels slippery.
steps.expect: no medicated residue remains in the hair.

steps.action: **Repeat on schedule.** Use 2 to 3 times weekly at first, then reduce as flaking improves.
steps.expect: flakes and itch trend down over several weeks.

steps.action: **Rotate if needed.** [BRANCH: improving | not improving] keep the same shampoo if improving, or alternate active ingredients after a few weeks if not.
steps.expect: the routine is adjusted without over-washing.

recipes.verification: After 2 to 4 weeks, scalp itch and visible flakes are clearly less frequent without redness, pain, or worsening hair loss.

recipes.title: treat dry skin
recipes.name: treat-dry-skin
recipes.goal: Dry skin is cleaned gently, moisturized while damp, protected from irritants, and screened for signs that it is a medical skin condition.

steps.action: **Use lukewarm water.** Shower or wash with lukewarm water, not hot water, and keep bathing brief.
steps.expect: skin feels clean without a tight, squeaky feeling.

steps.action: **Use mild cleanser sparingly.** Clean sweaty or dirty areas, but avoid scrubbing dry patches with harsh soap.
steps.expect: skin is clean with less stinging.

steps.action: **Pat dry.** Leave the skin slightly damp instead of rubbing it completely dry.
steps.expect: no dripping water, but the surface still feels moist.

steps.action: **Moisturize damp skin.** Apply moisturizer within 3 minutes of washing. Choose ointment for very dry skin, cream for daily use, or lotion for mild dryness.
steps.expect: skin feels coated and comfortable.

steps.action: **Choose helpful ingredients.** Look for petrolatum, dimethicone, glycerin, ceramides, hyaluronic acid, urea, or lactic acid if tolerated.
steps.expect: a product that reduces tightness without burning.

steps.action: **Avoid common irritants.** Skip fragrance, strong exfoliants, alcohol-heavy products, and scratchy fabrics on the area.
steps.expect: fewer stinging or itching flares.

steps.action: **Protect hands and exposed skin.** Wear gloves for cleaning or wet work, and use moisturizer after handwashing.
steps.expect: fewer cracks from repeated water exposure.

steps.action: **Recheck after a week.** Track itching, cracks, redness, and whether the routine helps.
steps.expect: visible flaking and tightness improve over several days.

recipes.verification: After several days, the skin is less tight and flaky, moisturizer is applied after washing, and no infection or persistent rash warning signs are present.

recipes.title: treat heartburn
recipes.name: treat-heartburn
recipes.goal: Mild heartburn is relieved with posture, trigger control, and appropriate over-the-counter medicine while dangerous chest symptoms are recognized.

steps.action: **Sit upright.** Stay seated or stand and loosen tight waist clothing.
steps.expect: reflux pressure may ease within minutes.

steps.action: **Avoid lying down.** Wait at least 2 to 3 hours after eating before lying flat.
steps.expect: stomach contents are less likely to reflux.

steps.action: **Take an antacid if appropriate.** [BRANCH: occasional symptoms | frequent symptoms] use an antacid as labeled for occasional symptoms; contact a clinician for frequent or persistent symptoms.
steps.expect: burning improves within the expected label timeframe. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not assume new chest pain is heartburn when emergency heart symptoms are present.

steps.action: **Sip water.** Drink small sips of water if tolerated.
steps.expect: throat irritation feels less intense.

steps.action: **Avoid triggers today.** Skip large meals, alcohol, peppermint, chocolate, caffeine, acidic foods, spicy foods, and high-fat meals if they trigger symptoms.
steps.expect: symptoms are less likely to flare again.

steps.action: **Raise the head for sleep.** If nighttime symptoms recur, elevate the head of the bed or use a wedge.
steps.expect: nighttime reflux is reduced without bending only at the waist.

steps.action: **Review medicine timing.** Separate antacids from other medicines when the labels or pharmacist advise spacing.
steps.expect: interactions are avoided.

steps.action: **Track recurrence.** Note food, timing, position, medicine used, and response.
steps.expect: patterns become clear for prevention or clinician review.

steps.action: **Escalate persistent symptoms.** Call a clinician if symptoms last despite labeled medicine, occur often, or are new after age 40 to 50.
steps.expect: serious causes are considered.

recipes.verification: Burning improves with upright posture and labeled treatment, and no emergency chest-pain or gastrointestinal red flags are present.

recipes.title: treat poison ivy
recipes.name: treat-poison-ivy
recipes.goal: Poison ivy, oak, or sumac exposure is washed off early, itching is controlled, and serious reactions are escalated.

steps.action: **Wash skin quickly.** Within the first hour if possible, wash exposed skin with soap and cool running water.
steps.expect: plant oil is removed before more binds to skin.

steps.action: **Clean under nails.** Scrub gently under fingernails with soap and water.
steps.expect: oil is less likely to spread by scratching.

steps.action: **Remove contaminated clothing.** [BRANCH: washable items | gear or shoes] wash clothing in detergent; wipe shoes, tools, and pet fur with appropriate protection.
steps.expect: oil is not reintroduced to skin. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not burn contaminated plants or brush because smoke exposure can injure the airway.

steps.action: **Use cool compresses.** Apply cool wet cloths for 15 to 30 minutes several times daily.
steps.expect: itching and heat decrease.

steps.action: **Apply itch relief.** Use calamine lotion or hydrocortisone cream as labeled on intact skin.
steps.expect: itching becomes more manageable.

steps.action: **Consider antihistamine.** Use an oral antihistamine as labeled if itching disrupts sleep and it is safe with your conditions and medicines.
steps.expect: scratching is reduced, especially at night.

steps.action: **Avoid scratching.** Keep nails short and cover weepy areas with clean loose gauze.
steps.expect: skin breaks and infection risk are reduced.

steps.action: **Monitor spread and severity.** Check daily for face or eye involvement, severe swelling, pus, fever, or rapidly expanding rash.
steps.expect: serious symptoms trigger medical care.

steps.action: **Call if not improving.** Contact a clinician if rash is severe, widespread, or not improving after about a week.
steps.expect: stronger treatment is considered when needed.

recipes.verification: Exposed skin and contaminated items have been washed, itching is controlled, and no emergency or see-a-doctor thresholds are present.

recipes.title: trim a beard
recipes.name: trim-a-beard
recipes.goal: A beard is trimmed dry to an even length with a clean neckline, controlled cheek line, and tidy details around the mouth.

steps.action: **Comb with the grain.** Comb the beard downward and outward so hairs sit naturally
steps.expect: long stray hairs and dense areas are easy to see.

steps.action: **Start with a longer guard.** Choose a guard longer than your target length for the first pass
steps.expect: the trimmer removes only the longest uneven tips.

steps.action: **Trim dry in sections.** Move with the grain over cheeks, jaw, and chin, using steady overlapping passes
steps.expect: bulk reduces evenly without sudden bare patches.

steps.action: **Step down slowly.** Shorten the guard only if the beard still looks too full [BRANCH: short beard | medium beard | long beard]
steps.expect: length changes happen gradually.

steps.action: **Set the neckline.** Place the line about one to two finger widths above the Adam's apple, curving toward each ear
steps.expect: the beard ends under the jaw rather than high on the face.

steps.action: **Clean below the neckline.** Trim or shave below the line with light pressure
steps.expect: the neck looks clean and the beard still covers the underside of the jaw.

steps.action: **Refine cheek lines.** Remove only obvious outliers unless you want a sharp carved line
steps.expect: cheeks look intentional without cutting into the beard body.

steps.action: **Detail the mustache.** Comb down and snip hairs crossing the lip, then trim corners carefully
steps.expect: mouth edges are clear and the mustache remains even.

steps.action: **Check symmetry.** Look straight, turn both sides, and touch up with comb-and-scissor for single long hairs
steps.expect: both sides balance without looking over-trimmed.

recipes.verification: In bright light, the beard has an even overall length, a clean neckline under the jaw, and no hairs crossing the lip.

recipes.title: trim toenails safely
recipes.name: trim-toenails-safely
recipes.goal: All toenails are trimmed straight across, left long enough to protect the toe tip, and smoothed without cutting skin or encouraging ingrown edges.

steps.action: **Soften the nails.** Wash your feet or trim after a shower, then dry between the toes.
steps.expect: nails feel slightly more flexible and the skin is clean.

steps.action: **Inspect each toe.** Look for redness, swelling, drainage, dark discoloration, numbness, or nails too thick for the clipper.
steps.expect: you know which nails are safe to trim and which should be left for a clinician or podiatrist.

steps.action: **Position the clipper straight across.** Hold the blade nearly perpendicular to the nail, not wrapped around the corners.
steps.expect: the planned cut line is flat across the nail tip.

steps.action: **Take small straight cuts.** Clip from one side toward the other while leaving a small white edge beyond the skin.
steps.expect: the nail is shorter but not cut into the corner or pink tissue.

steps.action: **Leave corners visible.** Do not round down the sides or chase the nail into the groove.
steps.expect: both corners still reach past the skin fold.

steps.action: **Smooth sharp points.** File only the front edge and any rough snag, keeping the shape straight across.
steps.expect: socks slide over the nail without catching.

steps.action: **Clean up.** Discard clippings, wash or wipe the clippers, and put on roomy socks or shoes.
steps.expect: the area is clean and no toe feels pinched.

recipes.verification: Each toenail has a straight front edge with visible corners, no bleeding, no skin cut, and no shoe pressure pain when you stand.

recipes.title: trim your fingernails
recipes.name: trim-your-fingernails
recipes.goal: All ten fingernails are trimmed to a comfortable, even length with smooth edges, and the clippings are contained and discarded.

steps.action: **Soften if needed.** Trim after a shower/handwash when nails are slightly soft — dry brittle nails crack and shatter clippings.
steps.expect: nails flex slightly under thumb pressure.

steps.action: **Set up over a catch surface.** Clip over a bin or a spread tissue.
steps.expect: clippings will land somewhere collectable, not across the sofa.

steps.action: **Clip each nail in 2–3 small cuts following the fingertip's curve.** Not one big cut across. Leave a thin white margin (~1 mm) — cutting to the quick hurts and invites infection.
steps.expect: nail edge follows a gentle curve, white margin visible, no pink exposed.

steps.action: **Work through all ten in a fixed order.** Dominant hand clips the other first (the awkward hand then does its work while you're warmed up).
steps.expect: all ten trimmed to visually consistent length.

steps.action: **File the edges smooth.** One-direction strokes (not sawing) along each edge until nothing snags when brushed against fabric.
steps.expect: no catch on a fabric drag test.

steps.action: **Collect and discard clippings; wash hands.** Fold the tissue, wipe the surface.
steps.expect: no clippings left on floor or table; hands washed.

recipes.verification: All ten nails show an even curve with a thin white margin, nothing snags on fabric, and the workspace and floor hold zero clippings.

recipes.title: unclog your ears
recipes.name: unclog-your-ears
recipes.goal: Ear pressure or mild blockage is relieved safely, or warning signs are recognized and medical care is chosen instead.

steps.action: **Screen for warning signs.** Check for pain, discharge, fever, dizziness, sudden hearing loss, or injury.
steps.expect: either no red flags or a clear reason to stop.

steps.action: **Swallow and yawn.** Sip water, chew gum, or yawn several times.
steps.expect: small clicks or pressure shifts may occur.

steps.action: **Try a gentle Valsalva.** Pinch nose, close mouth, and blow softly for 1 to 2 seconds.
steps.expect: ears may pop without pain.

steps.action: **Use warmth.** Hold a warm compress against the ear or take a warm shower.
steps.expect: muscles relax and fullness may ease.

steps.action: **Stay upright.** Sit or stand, especially if congestion is involved.
steps.expect: drainage feels easier than lying flat.

steps.action: **Repeat gently.** [BRANCH: pressure after flight | pressure from cold congestion] repeat swallowing or steam, not forceful blowing.
steps.expect: gradual improvement without sharp pain.

steps.action: **Avoid inserting objects.** Do not use cotton swabs, hairpins, or candles in the ear canal.
steps.expect: the ear canal is not irritated or scratched.

steps.action: **Escalate if needed.** Contact a clinician if symptoms persist, worsen, or include warning signs.
steps.expect: unsafe cases are handled medically.

recipes.verification: Pressure or muffled hearing improves without pain, discharge, dizziness, or any object inserted into the ear canal.

recipes.title: use a neti pot
recipes.name: use-a-neti-pot
recipes.goal: Nasal passages are rinsed with sterile saline using a neti pot or squeeze bottle without introducing unsafe water or forcing fluid.

steps.action: **Use safe water only.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* unsafe water can cause rare but severe infection, so use distilled, sterile, or previously boiled and cooled water
steps.expect: rinse water source is confirmed safe before mixing.

steps.action: **Mix saline.** Add the saline packet or measured salt to lukewarm safe water and dissolve fully
steps.expect: the solution is clear and feels close to body temperature.

steps.action: **Wash hands and device.** Clean hands and use a clean pot or bottle
steps.expect: no old residue or visible debris remains.

steps.action: **Lean over the sink.** Tilt your head forward and slightly to one side, keeping the forehead and chin roughly level
steps.expect: the upper nostril is positioned above the lower nostril.

steps.action: **Pour gently.** Place the spout at the upper nostril and let saline flow without squeezing hard [BRANCH: neti pot | squeeze bottle]
steps.expect: saline exits the lower nostril or mouth without sharp pain.

steps.action: **Breathe through your mouth.** Keep the mouth open and do not inhale through the nose during the rinse
steps.expect: breathing remains easy while fluid flows.

steps.action: **Switch sides.** Use the remaining solution on the other nostril with the opposite head tilt
steps.expect: both sides feel rinsed.

steps.action: **Drain without force.** Lean forward, gently blow through one nostril at a time, and avoid hard pressure
steps.expect: excess saline drains out over several minutes.

steps.action: **Clean and dry the device.** Wash the pot or bottle and air-dry completely
steps.expect: the device is clean, open, and dry for next use.

recipes.verification: Both nostrils have been rinsed with sterile saline, excess fluid has drained, and there is no sharp pain, ear pressure, or bleeding.

recipes.title: use a tongue scraper
recipes.name: use-a-tongue-scraper
recipes.goal: The tongue surface is gently cleaned from back to front to reduce coating and help freshen breath without irritating tissue.

steps.action: **Wash the scraper.** Rinse it under running water before use.
steps.expect: the scraper surface is visibly clean.

steps.action: **Stick out your tongue.** Relax your jaw and hold the scraper with both hands if it is U-shaped.
steps.expect: you can see the coated part of the tongue.

steps.action: **Start as far back as comfortable.** Place the scraper near the back of the tongue without forcing a gag.
steps.expect: you feel pressure but not choking or pain.

steps.action: **Scrape back to front.** Pull the scraper forward in one smooth pass with gentle pressure.
steps.expect: coating collects on the scraper edge.

steps.action: **Rinse between passes.** Rinse the scraper after each pass before touching the tongue again.
steps.expect: removed coating is washed away instead of spread around.

steps.action: **Repeat a few times.** Make 3 to 5 gentle passes, moving across the tongue surface.
steps.expect: the tongue looks less coated and feels cleaner.

steps.action: **Rinse and store.** Rinse your mouth and wash the scraper before drying or storing it.
steps.expect: the tool is clean and ready for the next use.

recipes.verification: After scraping, the tongue has less visible coating, the scraper is rinsed clean, and there is no pain, bleeding, or raw feeling.

recipes.title: wake up without hitting snooze
recipes.name: wake-up-without-hitting-snooze
recipes.goal: Get out of bed at the first alarm without negotiating with the snooze button.

steps.action: **Choose one wake time.** Use the same time most days, including weekends within about an hour.
steps.expect: the alarm time is set once, not debated nightly.

steps.action: **Put the phone or alarm across the room.** Place it far enough that turning it off requires standing.
steps.expect: you must leave the bed to stop the sound.

steps.action: **Prepare the first move before bed.** Put slippers, glasses, robe, or water where your feet land.
steps.expect: the first action has no search step.

steps.action: **Let light reach you fast.** [BRANCH: window available | dark morning] Open curtains before bed if private, or use a lamp on a timer.
steps.expect: light appears within the first minute of waking.

steps.action: **Use the one-move-out-of-bed rule.** When the alarm rings, sit up, put both feet on the floor, and stand before thinking about how you feel.
steps.expect: your body is vertical before the argument starts.

steps.action: **Turn off the alarm while standing.** Do not carry it back to bed. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* avoid placing the alarm somewhere hazardous, such as near stairs, hot appliances, or a wet bathroom floor.
steps.expect: alarm is off and you are still upright.

steps.action: **Go directly to the first destination.** Bathroom, window, sink, or water first; messages come later.
steps.expect: one non-bed action is complete within two minutes.

steps.action: **Keep the wake time after a bad night.** Make bedtime earlier later, but do not pay the debt by snoozing.
steps.expect: the anchor survives one rough morning.

recipes.verification: The alarm was stopped once, you stood up before checking messages, and you completed the first morning destination without using snooze.

recipes.title: warm up before exercise
recipes.name: warm-up-before-exercise
recipes.goal: Five to ten minutes that take your body from resting to ready for the session ahead, raising temperature and rehearsing the movements, so the workout starts at minute one instead of minute fifteen.

steps.action: **Raise the pulse gently for 3 to 5 minutes.** Brisk walk, easy jog, cycling, rowing, or jumping jacks at conversational effort. The goal is warmth and light sweat onset, not fatigue.
steps.expect: breathing elevated but easy, body noticeably warmer.

steps.action: **Move the joints through their ranges, dynamically.** Leg swings, arm circles, hip circles, torso rotations, ankle rolls: 8 to 10 controlled reps each, flowing rather than held. Static stretching (long holds) belongs after the session, not here.
steps.expect: joints moving freely through full range with no pinching.

steps.action: **Rehearse the session's actual movements at low intensity.** Runners: drills and a few strides building speed. Lifters: the first exercise with an empty bar or light dumbbells for 1 to 2 sets. Sports: the sport's motions at half speed (easy rallies, light dribbling).
steps.expect: the exact patterns of the day grooved with light loads or speeds.

steps.action: **Ramp, do not jump.** Bridge the last gap gradually: the lifter adds weight in steps toward the working sets; the runner's first kilometer is the slowest; the class's first round is deliberately easy.
steps.expect: working intensity reached through 2 or 3 rising steps.

steps.action: **Do a readiness check before the real work.** Anything painful (sharp, joint-specific, one-sided) during the warm-up gets respected: modify the session around it rather than through it. General stiffness that faded is normal; pain that sharpened is information.
steps.expect: a green light, or a consciously modified plan.

recipes.verification: By the end you are warm, lightly sweating, joints moving freely, the day's specific movements have been rehearsed and ramped, and any pain signal was caught and acted on before working intensity, with the whole thing inside ten minutes.

recipes.title: warm up cold hands
recipes.name: warm-up-cold-hands
recipes.goal: Warm cold hands safely by restoring body warmth, improving circulation, and avoiding burns on numb skin.

steps.action: **Leave the cold source.** Move indoors, into a vehicle, or behind a windbreak.
steps.expect: hands are no longer exposed to wind or wet cold.

steps.action: **Warm the core first.** Put on a hat, jacket, dry socks, or blanket and drink a warm nonalcoholic beverage if available.
steps.expect: the body feels less chilled overall.

steps.action: **Remove wet items.** Take off wet gloves, rings, or tight cuffs that restrict circulation.
steps.expect: fingers have room and are not compressed.

steps.action: **Use gentle movement.** Open and close fists, swing arms lightly, or place hands under armpits.
steps.expect: fingers begin to tingle or regain normal color.

steps.action: **Use lukewarm water if needed.** [BRANCH: mild cold | numb hands] For numb hands, use lukewarm water only, not hot water or direct heat.
steps.expect: warming feels gradual rather than painful.

steps.action: **Add layers.** Put on dry gloves or mittens after hands are warming, and add a windproof outer layer outdoors.
steps.expect: warmth is retained for several minutes.

steps.action: **Avoid direct heat burns.** Do not press numb hands against heaters, fires, heating pads, or hot water bottles. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* numb skin can burn before pain is felt; test warmth with an elbow or another person first.
steps.expect: no red, blistered, or overheated skin appears.

steps.action: **Watch for Raynaud patterns.** Notice fingers turning white or blue, then red, especially after cold or stress.
steps.expect: repeated color-change episodes are recognized.

steps.action: **Seek medical advice when needed.** Contact a clinician for frequent Raynaud-like attacks, severe pain, blisters, or numbness that does not improve.
steps.expect: concerning symptoms are not treated as routine cold hands.

recipes.verification: Hands feel warm or improving, finger color is normalizing, and no direct-heat burn or worsening numbness is present.

recipes.title: wash hands
recipes.name: wash-hands
recipes.goal: Your hands are hygienically clean and dry, appropriate for eating, food handling, or after contamination.

steps.action: **Turn on the water and wet both hands fully.** Comfortable temperature — hot water is not required for hygiene.
steps.expect: both hands wet to the wrists.

steps.action: **Apply soap.** One pump of liquid soap or rub the bar between palms.
steps.expect: enough soap to cover both hands.

steps.action: **Lather and scrub for at least 20 seconds.** Cover all surfaces in sequence: palms together, backs of hands, between fingers interlaced, backs of fingers, both thumbs (grip and rotate), fingertips scrubbed against palms.
steps.expect: full lather on every surface; ~20 s elapsed (about the time of singing "Happy Birthday" twice).

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly under running water.** Fingers pointing down.
steps.expect: no visible soap remains; water runs clear off the fingertips.

steps.action: **Turn off the tap.** In public restrooms, use the paper towel or your elbow on lever taps to avoid re-contaminating.
steps.expect: tap closed without bare-palm contact where avoidable.

steps.action: **Dry completely.** Pat with a clean/paper towel or use the air dryer until fully dry — damp hands transfer microbes far more readily.
steps.expect: hands feel dry, including between fingers.

recipes.verification: All hand surfaces were lathered for ~20 seconds, rinsed clear, and hands are completely dry, without re-touching the dirty tap.

recipes.title: wash your face
recipes.name: wash-your-face
recipes.goal: Your face is cleansed morning and evening without being stripped or scrubbed raw, which is the difference between skincare and skin damage.

steps.action: **Wash your hands first.** Cleansing with dirty hands moves grime around.
steps.expect: clean hands (`daily/self-care/wash-hands`).

steps.action: **Wet the face with lukewarm water.** Hot water strips and reddens; cold does not loosen oil.
steps.expect: comfortably warm water, face fully wet.

steps.action: **Work a small amount of cleanser in gentle circles for 30 to 60 seconds.** Fingertips, light pressure, covering forehead, nose, cheeks, chin, jawline, and down onto the neck. The time matters more than the force.
steps.expect: light lather or slip everywhere; no scrubbing sensation.

steps.action: **Mind the edges.** Hairline, eyebrows, the creases beside the nose, and under the jaw collect cleanser and grime alike.
steps.expect: the zones people miss get their two seconds each.

steps.action: **Rinse thoroughly with the same lukewarm water.** Residue left along the hairline and jaw is a common breakout cause.
steps.expect: no slick or filmy patches when you run a finger across.

steps.action: **Pat dry with the clean towel.** Pat, not drag.
steps.expect: dry face, no towel-burn redness.

steps.action: **Follow with moisturizer while the skin is still slightly damp.** Damp skin locks the moisture in; morning versions ideally carry SPF (`daily/self-care/apply-sunscreen` for real sun days).
steps.expect: skin comfortable, not tight, two minutes later.

recipes.verification: The face was cleansed for the full 30 to 60 seconds at lukewarm temperature, rinsed with no residue at the edges, patted dry with a clean towel, and moisturized while damp, and the skin feels comfortable rather than tight an hour later.

recipes.title: accept a compliment
recipes.name: accept-a-compliment
recipes.goal: A compliment is received with a plain thank-you and warmth, leaving the giver glad they said it, instead of being argued with, deflected, or awkwardly boomeranged.

steps.action: **Let it land.** Half a second of pause, eye contact if in person. Resist the reflex to start talking before they finish.
steps.expect: the compliment was fully spoken; you did not talk over its ending.

steps.action: **Say "thank you," full stop.** The complete move is two words plus a smile. Not "thanks, but," not "oh, this old thing," not "it was nothing." The period is the technique.
steps.expect: you have stopped speaking and the silence feels longer to you than to them (it always does).

steps.action: **Do not deflect, discount, or rebut.** Deflection ("it was all luck," "the team did everything," "I got it on sale") reads as arguing with their judgment: they said something kind and you told them they were wrong.
steps.expect: nothing you said contradicted the compliment.

steps.action: **Optionally add one sentence of warmth or truth.** [BRANCH: earned achievement → own it briefly ("thanks, I worked hard on that") | genuinely shared credit → share specifically ("thank you, and Maya built the hard half") | small thing → warmth only ("thanks, that's kind of you")] One sentence, then done.
steps.expect: the addition is a single sentence and none of it shrinks the thank-you.

steps.action: **Return warmth, not a rebuttal and not an instant counter-compliment.** A reflexive "no YOU look great" reads as a formality, not a gift. If you genuinely have a compliment for them, bank it and deliver it later or on a different topic, where it stands on its own.
steps.expect: the exchange ends warm; no compliment was traded back within the same breath.

steps.action: **Move the conversation forward.** A natural pivot ("thanks! How was your weekend?") releases any lingering awkwardness for both of you.
steps.expect: conversation continues normally; nobody is stranded in the moment.

recipes.verification: You said "thank you" without any qualifier that shrank it, said at most one added sentence, gave no instant counter-compliment, and the conversation moved on with the giver visibly at ease. If you can recall your exact words and none argue with the compliment, it succeeded.

recipes.title: answer a phone call
recipes.name: answer-a-phone-call
recipes.goal: An incoming phone call is handled appropriately: answered and concluded politely with any needed information exchanged — or correctly declined — without falling for a scam call.

steps.action: **Glance at the caller ID before answering.** [BRANCH: known contact → answer warmly | unknown number → answer neutrally, guard up | obvious spam pattern → let it ring to voicemail]
steps.expect: you know which stance you're taking before speaking.

steps.action: **Answer and identify the exchange.** Known: "Hi <name>." Unknown: "Hello?" and let *them* state who they are and why they're calling — you are not obliged to confirm your name to an unknown caller.
steps.expect: the caller states an identity and a purpose.

steps.action: **Establish the purpose.** If it's unclear after their opener, ask: "What is this regarding?"
steps.expect: a concrete purpose you can act on: information, a request, a scheduling matter.

steps.action: **Handle the substance.** Answer, take notes for anything with numbers/dates/names, and read critical details back ("So that's Tuesday the 4th at 3 pm?").
steps.expect: both sides confirm the key facts; notes captured.

steps.action: **Refuse sensitive disclosures to inbound callers.** Banks, tax offices, and couriers do not ask for full passwords, PINs, or one-time codes on calls *they* placed. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a read-out 2FA code hands over the account — never read codes to any inbound caller; hang up and call the institution's official number yourself.
steps.expect: any such request is declined; legitimate callers accept the call-back offer, scammers pressure you.

steps.action: **Close the call.** Summarize any agreed action ("I'll send that today"), exchange goodbyes, and let the closing be mutual rather than hanging up mid-sentence.
steps.expect: both parties said a closing; call ended.

steps.action: **Act on the outcome immediately.** Calendar the appointment, write the task, or save the number with a name.
steps.expect: nothing from the call exists only in memory.

recipes.verification: The call ended with a mutual close; you can state who called, why, and what was agreed; agreed actions are captured outside your head; and no code, PIN, or password was disclosed to an inbound caller.

recipes.title: apologize well
recipes.name: apologize-well
recipes.goal: A real apology delivered for something you actually did: one that names the harm, skips the self-defense, repairs what it can, and leaves the other person freer rather than obligated.

steps.action: **Name what you did, concretely.** "I'm sorry I made that joke about your work in front of the team." Naming it proves you know what happened; vagueness ("sorry about yesterday") makes them do the work of prosecuting it.
steps.expect: the specific act stated in your words, without euphemism.

steps.action: **Acknowledge the impact on them.** "That undermined you in a meeting where you needed the room's confidence." Impact, not intent: what it did to them is the subject.
steps.expect: their experience reflected accurately enough that they feel seen rather than managed.

steps.action: **Do not attach the defense.** No "but", no "I was stressed", no "you know I didn't mean it", and never "I'm sorry you feel that way" (which apologizes for their feelings instead of your act). Explanations can come later if they ask; welded to the apology they read as retraction.
steps.expect: a full stop where the excuse wanted to go.

steps.action: **Offer repair where repair exists.** Correct the record with the people who heard it, fix or replace what broke (`daily/social/borrow-and-return-an-item`'s broke-it protocol is this step in miniature), redo the work, cover the cost. Ask if unsure: "What would help?"
steps.expect: a concrete offer, or a sincere question, not just sentiment.

steps.action: **State the change, modestly.** "I'll keep that stuff out of group settings." One credible behavioral sentence beats grand reform speeches; the future is where apologies are actually judged.
steps.expect: a specific, keepable commitment.

steps.action: **Let them respond without steering.** They may accept, need time, or still be angry; all are legitimate. Do not extract absolution ("so are we good?") on the spot; the apology is a gift with no receipt required.
steps.expect: their response received as given; pressure absent.
