steps.expect: the child has control without delaying bedtime.

steps.action: **Hold the final boundary.** Return calmly after extra requests and repeat the same short phrase.
steps.expect: bedtime does not restart repeatedly.

steps.action: **Review after several nights.** Adjust timing if the child is not sleepy, is overtired, or wakes hard in the morning.
steps.expect: the routine fits the child's actual sleep pattern.

recipes.verification: The child completes the same bedtime sequence most nights and is in the sleep space at the target time with predictable caregiver responses.

recipes.title: set a boundary
recipes.name: set-a-boundary
recipes.goal: State a limit clearly and kindly, then hold it without over-explaining or turning it into a debate.

steps.action: **Name the limit to yourself first.** Write the exact behavior and what you will or will not do.
steps.expect: the boundary is concrete.

steps.action: **Choose the right channel.** [BRANCH: low-stakes | emotionally loaded] Use text for simple logistics, in person or call for important relationships.
steps.expect: the channel fits the weight.

steps.action: **Lead with the boundary.** Say "I cannot lend money" or "I need you to call before visiting."
steps.expect: the limit is visible in the first sentence.

steps.action: **Be direct and kind.** Use calm language without insults, diagnoses, or courtroom evidence.
steps.expect: the person hears a boundary, not an attack.

steps.action: **Give one short reason if useful.** Stop before defending your entire life.
steps.expect: the explanation supports the limit without replacing it.

steps.action: **Name the consequence.** Say what you will do if the boundary is ignored, such as leave, end the call, or stop responding. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not threaten consequences you cannot or will not carry out.
steps.expect: the next step is predictable.

steps.action: **Repeat once if challenged.** Use the same sentence with fewer words.
steps.expect: the discussion does not expand under pressure.

steps.action: **Follow through calmly.** If the line is crossed, do the stated action.
steps.expect: the boundary becomes real.

recipes.verification: The other person has heard the specific limit, the requested behavior, and the consequence, and you acted consistently if the limit was tested.

recipes.title: set up a chore chart
recipes.name: set-up-a-chore-chart
recipes.goal: Create a chore chart that gives children clear, age-appropriate household responsibilities without turning chores into constant conflict.

steps.action: **List needed tasks.** Choose routine chores such as dishes, laundry sorting, pet water, trash, or toy cleanup.
steps.expect: the chart starts from real household needs.

steps.action: **Match by age and ability.** Assign tasks the child can learn safely with reasonable effort.
steps.expect: chores are challenging but possible.

steps.action: **Define done.** Show what finished looks like for each chore.
steps.expect: the child can tell when a task is complete.

steps.action: **Set timing.** Put chores on specific days or daily windows.
steps.expect: the child knows when to act.

steps.action: **Choose feedback.** Use checkmarks, rotation, allowance link, or family contribution language consistently.
steps.expect: progress is visible and predictable.

steps.action: **Review weekly.** Adjust chores that are too hard, too easy, unsafe, or unfairly distributed.
steps.expect: the system improves without daily renegotiation.

recipes.verification: The chart shows each child's chores, timing, and completion method, and each child can explain one assigned task.

recipes.title: set up a playdate
recipes.name: set-up-a-playdate
recipes.goal: Arrange a playdate with clear logistics, compatible expectations, allergy awareness, supervision, and a clean pickup plan.

steps.action: **Choose a good match.** Consider age, interests, energy level, and whether the children usually play well together.
steps.expect: the invitation is likely to fit both children.

steps.action: **Suggest a short window.** Offer a specific day, start time, end time, and location, especially for a first playdate.
steps.expect: the other caregiver can answer without doing all the planning.

steps.action: **Confirm the supervising adult.** State who will be present and ask who is allowed to pick up the child.
steps.expect: both sides know which adult is responsible.

steps.action: **Ask about allergies and needs.** Ask about food allergies, pets, medications, bathroom help, fears, and any rules around screens or swimming.
steps.expect: safety issues are known before the child arrives.

steps.action: **Agree on food and activities.** [BRANCH: snack provided | no snack] keep snacks simple and avoid risky foods when allergies are uncertain.
steps.expect: nobody is surprised by food, screens, pets, pools, or outings.

steps.action: **Prepare the space.** Put away fragile items, hazards, private documents, weapons, medications, and toys that the host child cannot share.
steps.expect: the play area supports supervision and fewer conflicts.

steps.action: **Start with structure.** Offer one or two activity options, then let the children play while an adult stays within appropriate range.
steps.expect: the children settle into play without needing constant adult direction.

steps.action: **Handle conflict early.** Step in for hitting, exclusion, unsafe climbing, or repeated distress, and redirect before it becomes the whole visit.
steps.expect: small problems are corrected without ending the playdate immediately.

steps.action: **Do the pickup clearly.** Have shoes, belongings, and any artwork or toys ready, share a brief report, and end on time.
steps.expect: the child leaves with the approved adult and no missing essentials.

recipes.verification: The playdate has a confirmed time, place, supervising adult, allergy or medical notes, activity expectations, and pickup plan.

recipes.title: sleep train a baby
recipes.name: sleep-train-a-baby
recipes.goal: Help a baby learn a predictable sleep pattern while keeping feeding, safety, and attachment needs protected.

steps.action: **Confirm readiness.** Check growth, feeding, reflux, medication, and developmental concerns with the pediatrician before reducing night help.
steps.expect: you know whether sleep training is appropriate now.

steps.action: **Set a repeatable bedtime.** Use feeding, diaper, sleepwear, dim light, short song, and crib in the same order each night.
steps.expect: the baby gets consistent cues that sleep is next.

steps.action: **Place the baby down drowsy.** Put the baby in the sleep space calm but awake enough to notice the crib.
steps.expect: the baby has a chance to practice falling asleep there.

steps.action: **Respond on a schedule.** [BRANCH: gradual checks | caregiver presence] use brief checks or quiet presence without restarting full play or feeding unless needed.
steps.expect: comfort is offered without making waking more stimulating.

steps.action: **Track patterns.** Record bedtime, wakeups, feeds, naps, illness, and soothing response for one week.
steps.expect: changes are based on patterns rather than one hard night.

steps.action: **Protect daytime needs.** Keep age-appropriate naps, feeds, daylight, and connection during the day.
steps.expect: the baby is not overtired, hungry, or undercomforted by bedtime.

recipes.verification: The baby sleeps in a safe sleep space, bedtime follows the same routine most nights, and wake responses match the chosen plan without ignoring medical or feeding needs.

recipes.title: soothe a crying baby
recipes.name: soothe-a-crying-baby
recipes.goal: Respond to a crying baby with a calm checklist, safe soothing techniques, and clear escalation when crying may signal illness or danger.

steps.action: **Check your own state.** Take one slow breath, loosen your shoulders, and put the baby down safely for a minute if you feel close to losing control. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never shake a baby, because shaking can cause brain injury or death.
steps.expect: you can handle the next step without rough motion.

steps.action: **Run the basic checklist.** Check hunger, diaper, tiredness, wind or gas, temperature, tight clothing, hair wrapped around toes or fingers, and signs of illness.
steps.expect: any obvious need is found or ruled out.

steps.action: **Feed or burp if indicated.** Offer the normal feed if hungry, or hold upright and burp after feeding.
steps.expect: sucking, swallowing, burping, or relaxed pauses give you information.

steps.action: **Change and adjust comfort.** Replace a wet or soiled diaper, adjust layers, and move away from bright light or loud noise.
steps.expect: the baby's body is clean, comfortable, and not overheated.

steps.action: **Use the 5 S's safely.** [BRANCH: swaddle if age-appropriate | skip swaddle] use swaddling only before rolling, side or stomach position only while held and awake, shushing, swinging with gentle motion, and sucking with a pacifier if accepted.
steps.expect: the baby has rhythmic input without unsafe sleep positioning.

steps.action: **Hold with steady support.** Support the head and neck, keep movements small, and try walking, rocking, or a carrier if used correctly.
steps.expect: crying may soften, pause, or change pattern.

steps.action: **Try a reset.** Move to a dim room, step outside briefly if weather is safe, or give a warm bath if the baby enjoys baths and can be held securely.
steps.expect: a new environment interrupts the crying cycle without overstimulation.

steps.action: **Take a safe break if needed.** Place the baby on their back in an empty crib or bassinet, leave the room for a few minutes, and call another trusted adult.
steps.expect: the baby remains safe while you regain control.

steps.action: **Escalate when it does not fit normal crying.** Call a pediatrician, nurse line, or emergency service for fever in a young infant, trouble breathing, blue color, limpness, seizure, injury, repeated vomiting, dehydration signs, a bulging soft spot, a new weak cry, or crying that is extreme and cannot be settled.
steps.expect: medical help is involved when crying may be a symptom.

recipes.verification: The baby's immediate needs have been checked, soothing was attempted safely, and either the baby is settling or medical or caregiver support has been contacted.

recipes.title: split a bill
recipes.name: split-a-bill
recipes.goal: A shared bill (meal, taxi, group purchase) is divided and settled such that the venue is paid once, everyone's share is fair *enough*, and no friendship absorbs hidden cost.

steps.action: **Set the split *method* before or when the bill lands — not after negotiation-fatigue.** [BRANCH: even split (default for similar orders) | pay-for-what-you-had (fair when orders diverged: someone had wine + steak, someone had soup) | one payer, reimbursed later] Someone just naming a method usually settles it: "Even split OK with everyone?"
steps.expect: an agreed method, chosen in seconds, not litigated.

steps.action: **Determine the total including service.** Bill + tip per local custom (`daily/order-at-a-restaurant` variations) — the tip is part of the split, not the payer's private burden.
steps.expect: one number everyone is dividing.

steps.action: **Execute the mechanics.** Even: total ÷ N, rounded *up* to a clean unit. Itemized: each claims their lines, shared plates ÷ their sharers, then proportional tip. Ask whether the venue splits cards ("Can we do two/three cards?") — many do, some don't.
steps.expect: each person's number known; venue's card-splitting policy known.

steps.action: **Pay the venue once, cleanly.** [BRANCH: venue splits cards → each pays their number | one card pays all → others transfer to the payer *now, at the table*, by app] "Now at the table" is the load-bearing phrase — in-the-moment transfers actually happen; "I'll get you back" decays.
steps.expect: venue fully paid; transfers visibly initiated on phones before coats go on.

steps.action: **The payer states the received total matches.** "Got it from everyone — we're square."
steps.expect: public closure; no one privately unsure whether they paid.

recipes.verification: The venue was paid exactly once in full including service; every participant can name what they paid; the payer (if any) has received all transfers — confirmed aloud; and the method for this group next time got easier, not touchier.

recipes.title: split chores with a roommate
recipes.name: split-chores-with-a-roommate
recipes.goal: Create a chore system with a roommate that covers visible mess and invisible work, so the home runs without one person becoming the unpaid manager.

steps.action: **Name the problem without accusation.** Start with the home, not character: "I want us to make chores clearer so neither of us has to keep score in our heads."
steps.expect: the conversation opens as a shared logistics problem.

steps.action: **List visible and invisible work.** Include dishes, trash, bathroom, floors, mail, supplies, rent reminders, repair calls, guests, pet care, and noticing when things are low.
steps.expect: the list shows both scrubbing and mental tracking.

steps.action: **Set minimum standards.** Define what "done" means for each task: trash bag replaced, sink wiped, bathroom mirror cleaned, supplies added to the list.
steps.expect: fewer arguments about whether a chore counts.

steps.action: **Choose rotate or divide.** [BRANCH: rotate | divide] rotate disliked tasks weekly for fairness; divide stable tasks if schedules and preferences make ownership easier.
steps.expect: every recurring task has one owner at a time.

steps.action: **Build the shared tracker.** Put tasks, owners, due days, and supply needs somewhere both people can see without asking.
steps.expect: the system remembers, not one roommate.

steps.action: **Add exceptions before they happen.** Decide what happens during travel, exams, overtime, illness, or hosting guests.
steps.expect: temporary overload has a swap rule instead of resentment.

steps.action: **Schedule a check-in.** Pick a 15-minute check-in after two weeks, then monthly if useful. Keep it about the system: what is unclear, too frequent, or unfair.
steps.expect: there is a named time to adjust, not a fight at midnight.

steps.action: **Use repair language when it slips.** Say "The bathroom was due yesterday. Can you do it tonight or trade for trash?" not "You never clean." ⚠️ *Irreversible:* angry texts and public shaming change the roommate relationship, so pause before sending them.
steps.expect: problems turn into actions, not character trials.

recipes.verification: Every recurring shared chore has an owner, a due rhythm, a definition of done, and a check-in date visible to all roommates.

recipes.title: support a kid through exams
recipes.name: support-a-kid-through-exams
recipes.goal: Help a child prepare for exams with structure, rest, emotional support, and honest study habits.

steps.action: **Map the exams.** Write each exam date, topic, and weight on a visible calendar.
steps.expect: the child sees what is coming.

steps.action: **Break study blocks down.** Choose short sessions for one subject, skill, or chapter at a time.
steps.expect: studying has a doable next action.

steps.action: **Use active practice.** Have the child retrieve facts, solve problems, explain concepts, or take practice questions.
steps.expect: the child tests memory instead of only rereading.

steps.action: **Protect sleep and food.** Set bedtime, meals, water, and movement breaks during exam week.
steps.expect: the child's body is supported for learning.

steps.action: **Plan test-day logistics.** Pack supplies, charge devices, check room or transport, and set alarms.
steps.expect: preventable stress is reduced.

steps.action: **Debrief without shame.** After each exam, note what helped and what to change next time.
steps.expect: the child learns from the process without panic.

recipes.verification: The child has a dated study plan, completed at least one active practice block per exam, and has test-day materials ready.

recipes.title: talk to a teen about social media
recipes.name: talk-to-a-teen-about-social-media
recipes.goal: Have a respectful conversation with a teen about social media safety, privacy, mental health, and boundaries.

steps.action: **Start with curiosity.** Ask what apps they use, what they like, and what feels stressful.
steps.expect: the teen is more likely to talk honestly.

steps.action: **Name real risks.** Discuss privacy, screenshots, scams, sexual pressure, harassment, comparison, and sleep disruption.
steps.expect: the conversation covers concrete hazards.

steps.action: **Agree on boundaries.** Set rules for private accounts, location sharing, sleep hours, unknown contacts, and reportable situations.
steps.expect: expectations are specific.

steps.action: **Check settings together.** Review privacy, comments, direct messages, location, blocking, and reporting tools.
steps.expect: the teen knows how to reduce exposure.

steps.action: **Plan help-seeking.** Identify when they should come to an adult, save evidence, block, report, or call for urgent help.
steps.expect: the teen has a response plan.

steps.action: **Schedule follow-up.** Revisit the topic after a week or after a new app, conflict, or rule problem.
steps.expect: social media remains an ongoing conversation.

recipes.verification: The teen can name the agreed boundaries, show key privacy settings, and identify when and how to seek adult help.

recipes.title: talk to kids about money
recipes.name: talk-to-kids-about-money
recipes.goal: Teach children basic money concepts through honest, age-appropriate conversations and small real choices.

steps.action: **Pick one concept.** Choose needs versus wants, saving, spending, giving, earning, or waiting.
steps.expect: the conversation has a clear focus.

steps.action: **Use a real example.** Show a grocery choice, toy budget, coin jar, or simple allowance plan.
steps.expect: money is connected to something visible.

steps.action: **Explain tradeoffs calmly.** Say what the money can do and what choosing it means giving up.
steps.expect: the child hears limits without fear.

steps.action: **Let the child decide small.** Offer a safe choice within a fixed amount.
steps.expect: the child practices agency and consequence.

steps.action: **Reflect afterward.** Ask what felt worth it, what they might save for, or what they learned.
steps.expect: the child links choice to outcome.

steps.action: **Repeat regularly.** Use brief everyday moments rather than one large lecture.
steps.expect: money skills build over time.

recipes.verification: The child can explain the chosen money concept and has made or observed one small tradeoff within a clear boundary.

recipes.title: teach a child to share
recipes.name: teach-a-child-to-share
recipes.goal: Teach sharing as a practiced social skill using turn-taking, preparation, and clear limits instead of forced surrender.

steps.action: **Prepare the environment.** Put away fragile favorites, duplicate high-demand toys when possible, and choose a few shareable items.
steps.expect: the hardest conflicts are reduced before children start.

steps.action: **Name the rule simply.** Say, "You can take turns. When the timer rings, it is the next person's turn."
steps.expect: children hear the rule before conflict begins.

steps.action: **Use visible turns.** Give the first child a short turn with a timer, song, or count that matches the age.
steps.expect: everyone can see when a turn starts and ends.

steps.action: **Coach the handoff.** Help the child give the toy to the next child and say, "Your turn is done; you can have another turn soon."
steps.expect: the toy changes hands without grabbing.

steps.action: **Protect active play.** [BRANCH: child is still using toy | toy is abandoned] let a child finish a short active turn, or invite another child when the toy is free.
steps.expect: sharing does not feel like immediate confiscation.

steps.action: **Praise the specific behavior.** Notice waiting, offering, trading, and returning, not just being "nice."
steps.expect: children know which action to repeat.

steps.action: **Repair grabs or tears.** Block grabbing, return the toy to the turn holder, and restart with a shorter timer.
steps.expect: the rule remains predictable after conflict.

recipes.verification: The child completes at least one supported turn-taking exchange, waits with help, and sees that toys return after a turn.

recipes.title: teach a kid to ride a bike
recipes.name: teach-a-kid-to-ride-a-bike
recipes.goal: Teach a child to balance, steer, brake, and ride a bicycle with confidence and safe habits.

steps.action: **Fit the gear.** Adjust the helmet level, tighten straps, and set the seat so feet can touch the ground for balance practice.
steps.expect: the child can sit and stop without tipping immediately.

steps.action: **Practice braking.** Have the child walk the bike and squeeze or backpedal the brake repeatedly.
steps.expect: the child can stop on command.

steps.action: **Glide first.** Remove pedals if practical or have the child push off and coast with feet lifted briefly.
steps.expect: the child feels balance before pedaling.

steps.action: **Add pedaling.** Start with one pedal high, push off, and pedal while looking forward.
steps.expect: the bike rolls several yards under the child's power.

steps.action: **Practice turns and stops.** Set wide markers and have the child ride, turn, brake, and put a foot down.
steps.expect: steering and stopping become deliberate.

steps.action: **End before exhaustion.** Stop after a good attempt or when frustration rises.
steps.expect: the child wants to try again later.

recipes.verification: The child can start, ride straight for several yards, make a wide turn, brake, and stop with the helmet still fitted correctly.

recipes.title: teach a kid to swim
recipes.name: teach-a-kid-to-swim
recipes.goal: Build a child's basic water comfort and swimming skills while treating water as a serious safety environment.

steps.action: **Set water rules.** Explain walk near water, ask before entering, stay where the adult can reach, and stop on cue.
steps.expect: the child can repeat the rules.

steps.action: **Enter gradually.** Start on steps or shallow water and let the child adjust to temperature and depth.
steps.expect: the child remains calm enough to listen.

steps.action: **Practice breath control.** Blow bubbles, hum into water, and wet the face without forcing submersion.
steps.expect: the child learns to manage water near the face.

steps.action: **Practice floating with support.** Hold the child's back or hands while they relax into front and back floats.
steps.expect: the child feels buoyancy with adult support.

steps.action: **Add kicks and reaches.** Move short distances between adult and wall with close spotting.
steps.expect: the child coordinates movement without panic.

steps.action: **End with safe exit practice.** Have the child reach the wall, climb out, and wait before reentering.
steps.expect: exiting becomes part of the skill, not an afterthought.

recipes.verification: The child follows water rules, exits safely, and practices one supported float or short assisted swim without distress.

recipes.title: teach a kid to tie shoes
recipes.name: teach-a-kid-to-tie-shoes
recipes.goal: Teach a child the bunny-ears shoe-tying method through slow practice, visible steps, and enough repetition for muscle memory to start forming.

steps.action: **Practice off-foot.** Put the shoe on a table or the child's lap with the toe pointing away from the child.
steps.expect: the child can see and reach both laces.

steps.action: **Name the two laces.** If helpful, call them left and right or use two colors so each lace has an identity.
steps.expect: the child can point to the lace you name.

steps.action: **Make the starting knot.** Cross one lace over the other, tuck it through the hole, and pull both ends snug.
steps.expect: a simple base knot sits flat on the shoe.

steps.action: **Make two bunny ears.** Fold each lace into a loop, keeping the loose ends short enough that the loops do not collapse.
steps.expect: the child is pinching one loop in each hand.

steps.action: **Cross the ears.** Cross one loop over the other, the same way the first knot crossed.
steps.expect: the loops make an X above the shoe.

steps.action: **Tuck one ear through.** Push one loop through the opening under the X and grab it from the other side.
steps.expect: both loops are visible again, one from each side.

steps.action: **Pull the ears, not the ends.** Pull both loops outward until the knot tightens, then adjust loops and tails to similar lengths.
steps.expect: the shoe has a bow that stays tied when gently tugged.

steps.action: **Repeat slowly.** [BRANCH: child leads | adult demonstrates] let the child narrate each step, and only demonstrate again when they cannot find the next motion.
steps.expect: the child completes more of the sequence each round.

steps.action: **Move to on-foot practice.** Put the shoe on the child's foot after off-foot success and repeat with the toe pointing away.
steps.expect: the child can tie in the position they will use day to day.

recipes.verification: The child can tie one shoe into a snug bow using bunny ears with only verbal prompts or no help.

recipes.title: teach a teen to drive
recipes.name: teach-a-teen-to-drive
recipes.goal: Teach a teen driving skills through legal, supervised, gradual practice with safety as the first measure of progress.

steps.action: **Review legal limits.** Confirm permit rules, required supervisor, passenger limits, hours, and practice log needs.
steps.expect: the session is lawful before the car moves.

steps.action: **Set the vehicle.** Adjust seat, mirrors, belt, phone storage, and controls while parked.
steps.expect: the teen can see, reach pedals, and avoid phone distraction.

steps.action: **Start in an empty lot.** Practice starting, stopping, turning, parking, and scanning at very low speed.
steps.expect: basic control improves away from traffic.

steps.action: **Add quiet streets.** Move to simple roads only after smooth braking and lane position are reliable.
steps.expect: the teen handles low-risk traffic calmly.

steps.action: **Debrief immediately.** Discuss one strength and one specific next skill after each drive.
steps.expect: feedback is clear and limited.

steps.action: **Increase complexity slowly.** Add rain, night, highways, or busy traffic only when earlier skills are consistent and legal.
steps.expect: difficulty rises by plan, not pressure.

recipes.verification: The teen practiced within legal limits, completed the planned skill safely, and logged or discussed one concrete next driving goal.

recipes.title: tip appropriately
recipes.name: tip-appropriately
recipes.goal: Choose a reasonable tip for a service situation while accounting for country norms, service type, payment method, and when tipping is not expected.

steps.action: **Identify the country norm.** Before applying a percentage, ask whether tipping is standard, optional, or unusual in that country.
steps.expect: you avoid importing the wrong custom.

steps.action: **Check for included service.** Look for "service charge," "gratuity," "cover," or local equivalents on the bill.
steps.expect: you know whether a tip has already been added.

steps.action: **Match the service type.** Use table service, bar, delivery, taxi, hotel, salon, or counter service as the category.
steps.expect: the tip decision fits the work performed.

steps.action: **Estimate the local range.** In the United States, table service is commonly around 15 to 20 percent before tax, with more for exceptional service.
steps.expect: you have a starting number rather than guessing under pressure.

steps.action: **Adjust for service quality and constraints.** Reduce for serious service failures, not for kitchen delays the server did not control.
steps.expect: the amount reflects the service fairly.

steps.action: **Choose cash or card.** [BRANCH: cash | card] leave cash when you want the worker to receive it directly, or add it on card when that is the available method.
steps.expect: the tip is visible and not accidentally skipped.

steps.action: **Handle counter prompts.** For quick counter service, choose a small amount, custom amount, or no tip based on local norm and effort.
steps.expect: the screen prompt does not force a decision you do not mean.

steps.action: **Do the math.** Move the decimal for 10 percent, double it for 20 percent, and round to a simple amount.
steps.expect: the final total is legible and affordable.

steps.action: **Close the transaction.** Write the tip and total clearly, or hand cash directly with thanks.
steps.expect: the worker and payment system can read your intent.

recipes.verification: The final paid amount reflects local custom, service type, any included charge, and your intentional choice.

recipes.title: wait in line
recipes.name: wait-in-line
recipes.goal: You join, hold, and complete a queue correctly — reaching the service point in fair order without conflict.

steps.action: **Identify the queue system before joining.** [BRANCH: physical line → find its *end* | numbered-ticket machine → take a ticket | app/virtual queue → register] Ask when ambiguous: "Are you in line?" / "Is this the line for X?"
steps.expect: you know which mechanism governs and where its tail is.

steps.action: **Join at the end.** Stand behind the last person at a culturally sane gap (~arm's length in most places); with a ticket, sit anywhere and watch the counter display.
steps.expect: your position established; late arrivals form up behind you.

steps.action: **Hold your place.** Advance as the line does; keep the gap from yawning open (a big gap invites honest confusion and less-honest insertion). Phone use is fine — inattention that stalls the line is not.
steps.expect: steady position; no one legitimately confused about the order.

steps.action: **Handle interlopers proportionately.** Someone joins ahead: assume confusion first — "Excuse me, the line ends back there." Most comply instantly. Non-compliance: one calm repetition, then let staff handle it; a queue spot is never worth escalation.
steps.expect: order restored or delegated, tone level throughout.

steps.action: **Prepare during the final approach.** Documents/payment/order decision out and ready one or two turns before yours.
steps.expect: when called, you step up and transact without a pocket-dig delay.

steps.action: **Complete your business efficiently and clear the service point.** Post-transaction packing/sorting happens a step aside, not at the counter.
steps.expect: the next person is being served while you finish organizing off to the side.

recipes.verification: You were served in arrival order, no conflict trailed your interactions, and the queue behind you inherited a clean, unambiguous structure.

recipes.title: welcome a new colleague
recipes.name: welcome-a-new-colleague
recipes.goal: A new colleague ends their first week knowing the practical basics, having eaten lunch with people instead of alone, and knowing exactly who to ping with dumb questions.

steps.action: **Prepare the day before.** Learn how to pronounce their name, skim their role, and note the two or three practical things nobody documents (where the good coffee is, which printer works, which meetings are skippable).
steps.expect: you can greet them by name without reading it off a screen.

steps.action: **Greet them within their first hour.** Walk over (or send a chat message for remote starts), introduce yourself with name and what you do in one sentence, and say you're a go-to for questions.
steps.expect: they know one concrete person, you, by name.

steps.action: **Give the two-minute practical tour.** Bathrooms, kitchen, exits, where their team sits, and the unwritten norms (headphones etiquette, meeting-room booking). Skip org-chart lore; it does not stick on day one.
steps.expect: they can find coffee and a bathroom unassisted.

steps.action: **Invite them to lunch on day one, as a group.** Say the time and place, and recruit one or two teammates so it is not a one-on-one interview. [BRANCH: they accept → go | they decline or brought food → offer a coffee walk that afternoon instead]
steps.expect: the new person does not eat alone on day one.

steps.action: **Hand over the tribal knowledge.** Send links to the team chat channels, the docs people actually use, and a one-line "who to ask for what" list.
steps.expect: they acknowledge receipt; the list is short enough to actually read.

steps.action: **Make the question channel explicit.** Say the exact words: "Ping me anytime, especially with questions that feel too dumb to ask in the channel."
steps.expect: they ping you at least once in the first days. Silence for a full week is a signal, not a success (see F2).

steps.action: **Check in at the one-week mark.** A short, private conversation: what's confusing, what's blocking, who have they not met yet that they should. Fix one concrete blocker on the spot if you can.
steps.expect: at least one specific confusion surfaced and addressed, not just "everything's fine."

recipes.verification: By end of week one: the new colleague has eaten lunch or coffee with teammates at least once, has asked you (or the buddy) at least one logistical question, and can name who to ask for equipment, code access, and HR matters. If any of the three is false, the welcome is not done.

recipes.title: welcome a newcomer to a group
recipes.name: welcome-a-newcomer-to-a-group
recipes.goal: A newcomer enters a group with names, context, and at least one easy way to participate.

steps.action: **Greet them promptly.** Use their name, say yours, and make the first minute simple: "I'm glad you made it."
steps.expect: they are no longer standing unnoticed.

steps.action: **Orient them to the space.** Point out where coats, bathrooms, food, seats, chat links, or materials are.
steps.expect: they can meet basic needs without asking publicly.

steps.action: **Introduce them around.** Start with two or three friendly people and include a useful hook, not a biography.
steps.expect: names come with reasons to talk.

steps.action: **Give the unwritten rules.** Explain norms kindly, such as how turns work, whether people bring snacks, or where beginners usually start.
steps.expect: hidden expectations become visible.

steps.action: **Include them in the next activity.** [BRANCH: structured group | casual group] In a structured group, give them a role or partner; in a casual group, invite them into a conversation with an easy topic.
steps.expect: they are participating, not only watching.

steps.action: **Check consent around attention.** Ask before making them introduce themselves to everyone or answer personal questions. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a forced spotlight can make a first visit feel unsafe, so do not surprise them with public attention.
steps.expect: attention level matches their comfort.

steps.action: **Keep an eye on the edges.** Notice if they drift alone, cannot follow jargon, or miss a transition.
steps.expect: you can re-include them before awkwardness hardens.

steps.action: **Check back before they leave.** Ask how it went, answer questions, and tell them the next meeting or channel if they want it.
steps.expect: they know how to return.

recipes.verification: The newcomer knows at least three names, understands the basic norms, joins one activity or conversation, and knows how to come back.

recipes.title: write a best man or maid of honor speech
recipes.name: write-a-best-man-or-maid-of-honor-speech
recipes.goal: A short wedding speech that honors the couple, gives the room one or two clean stories, and ends in a toast before attention thins.

steps.action: **Set a firm length.** Aim for three to five minutes, roughly 450 to 700 spoken words, and write the limit at the top of your draft.
steps.expect: a draft target that prevents rambling before you start.

steps.action: **Open with your relationship.** Say who you are, thank the hosts briefly if appropriate, and name the honor of standing beside the bride, groom, or couple.
steps.expect: guests who do not know you understand why you are speaking.

steps.action: **Choose one or two stories.** Pick stories that show kindness, steadiness, humor, courage, or how the couple works together. [BRANCH: one story | two stories] Use one strong story if it says enough; use two only if the second adds a new quality.
steps.expect: the stories point toward the marriage, not your own greatest hits.

steps.action: **Keep every story clean.** Cut exes, drunken disasters, private family pain, money trouble, and inside jokes that only one table understands. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once said into a microphone, the line becomes part of the wedding memory, so remove anything the couple would have to forgive.
steps.expect: nothing in the speech makes either partner brace.

steps.action: **Add the partner warmly.** If you know the spouse well, include a specific example; if you do not, say what you have seen them bring out in your friend.
steps.expect: both halves of the couple feel included.

steps.action: **Write the toast last.** Close with a single sentence wish, ask everyone to raise a glass, and name the couple clearly.
steps.expect: a clean ending the room can repeat.

steps.action: **Rehearse aloud with a timer.** Practice standing, mark breath points, and trim every sentence that feels hard to say naturally.
steps.expect: the speech fits the time limit and sounds like you, only steadier.

steps.action: **Bring a readable copy.** Print large text or use note cards, number the pages, and keep a backup on your phone.
steps.expect: you can recover if nerves, lighting, or a dropped page interfere.

steps.action: **Deliver and stop.** Speak slower than conversation, look at the couple for the toast, then sit down after the glass raise.
steps.expect: applause or warmth arrives at the end, not a drift into another anecdote.

recipes.verification: The final speech is under five minutes, includes one or two respectful stories, mentions both partners, and ends with a clear toast naming the couple.

recipes.title: write a condolence note
recipes.name: write-a-condolence-note
recipes.goal: A short, sincere note reaches a grieving person and does its one job: they feel their loss was seen and they are not alone. It does not try to fix, explain, or brighten anything.

steps.action: **Write now, or whenever you can. Late is fine.** The only true deadline is never. Notes arriving weeks or months later often land hardest, because the first-wave support has receded by then.
steps.expect: you have stopped waiting for the perfect moment; pen is on paper.

steps.action: **Open by naming the loss and the person.** "I was so sorry to hear about your father, Daniel." Use the deceased's name; the bereaved does not get to hear it enough, and vagueness ("your loss") reads as distance.
steps.expect: first sentence contains both the relationship and, where you know it, the name.

steps.action: **Give one specific memory or true observation.** The heart of the note, one to three sentences: "I still think about him teaching half the neighborhood to fix bikes" or, if you never met the deceased, something true about the bereaved: "the way you talked about her every Monday told me what she meant to you."
steps.expect: a sentence that could not have been written about anyone else's loss.

steps.action: **Say the plain hard thing without repair.** "There's nothing I can say that makes this better. I'm so sorry." Do not add a lesson, a comparison to your own losses, or a bright side.
steps.expect: no sentence in the note starts with "at least," and nothing explains, ranks, or silver-lines the death.

steps.action: **Make any offer of help specific, or leave it out.** "Let me know if you need anything" transfers work to the griever and yields nothing. Instead: "I'll text next week about dropping off dinner" or "I can take the school run any morning." Only write what you will actually do.
steps.expect: either a concrete, initiated-by-you offer, or no offer at all.

steps.action: **Close warmly and briefly, then stop.** "With love," "Thinking of you and your family." Sign and send to the best address you have; a mutual friend can supply one. Total length: 4-8 sentences is right.
steps.expect: the finished note fits on one card face, maybe two; brevity here is a kindness, not a failure of effort.

steps.action: **Follow up past the early wave.** Grief outlasts the casseroles. A short check-in a month or two later, and a line on the first anniversary or the deceased's birthday if you know it, is worth more than the note itself.
steps.expect: a reminder set for the later check-in; no reply to any of it is expected or owed (see F4).

recipes.verification: The finished note names the loss (and the deceased where known), contains at least one sentence specific to this person, contains zero silver-lining or explanatory phrases, makes either a concrete offer or none, runs 4-8 sentences, and has actually been sent, however late. A later check-in is scheduled.

recipes.title: write a heartfelt message
recipes.name: write-a-heartfelt-message
recipes.goal: Write and send a sincere message that tells someone specifically why they matter.

steps.action: **Choose the purpose.** [BRANCH: gratitude | care | congratulations | apology-adjacent] Decide what the message should make clearer.
steps.expect: the message has one emotional job.

steps.action: **Name the person directly.** Start with their name or a natural greeting.
steps.expect: the opening feels meant for them.

steps.action: **Use one specific memory or trait.** Mention what they did, how they show up, or a moment you remember.
steps.expect: the message cannot be sent unchanged to anyone else.

steps.action: **Say why it mattered.** Connect the detail to its impact on you or others.
steps.expect: the feeling has evidence.

steps.action: **Keep the tone genuine.** Use your own words, not grand language you would never say aloud.
steps.expect: the sentence sounds like you.

steps.action: **Cut performance.** Remove phrases written to impress an audience or force a reaction. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once sent, private feelings can be forwarded or screenshotted, so do not include secrets or pressure.
steps.expect: the message serves the recipient, not your image.

steps.action: **End simply.** Close with appreciation, care, pride, or a concrete next step if appropriate.
steps.expect: the ending does not demand a perfect reply.

steps.action: **Send it.** Do one final check for name, channel, and tone, then send.
steps.expect: the message leaves drafts and reaches them.

recipes.verification: The sent message names a specific detail, says why it matters, uses your natural voice, and does not require the recipient to manage your feelings.

recipes.title: write wedding vows
recipes.name: write-wedding-vows
recipes.goal: Write vows that sound like you, honor your partner specifically, and give the ceremony a clear promise instead of a speech that wanders.

steps.action: **Set the container together.** Agree on approximate length, tone, and whether you will share drafts or keep them private. [BRANCH: matching tone | surprise tone] choose matching if one partner fears imbalance; choose surprise only if both are comfortable.
steps.expect: both people know whether the vows are 1 minute, 3 minutes, formal, funny, spiritual, or plainspoken.

steps.action: **Use a promise structure.** Draft in four parts: what I see in you, one story that shows it, what our life has taught me, and three promises I can actually keep.
steps.expect: the draft has a spine and does not become a biography.

steps.action: **Choose specific stories.** Pick one or two moments with concrete details: the bus stop in the rain, the hospital chair, the terrible first apartment, the way they label leftovers.
steps.expect: a stranger could understand why this person is loved, and your partner could recognize themselves instantly.

steps.action: **Make promises behavioral.** Replace "I promise to love you forever" alone with actions: listen before defending, make coffee on early flights, protect our jokes, ask for repair after hard days.
steps.expect: the vows include promises that would change a normal Tuesday.

steps.action: **Cut private material.** Remove sexual details, family secrets, financial history, medical specifics, exes, and jokes that make your partner the punchline. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once spoken in a ceremony or recorded, private details cannot be fully taken back.
steps.expect: every line could be heard by the room without your partner flinching.

steps.action: **Practice aloud with a timer.** Read slowly, standing up, at least three times. Mark breaths and hard words.
steps.expect: the vows fit the agreed length and your mouth can say every sentence naturally.

steps.action: **Prepare the backup card.** Print or handwrite the final version in large type on a card, not a phone if avoidable. Give a spare copy to the officiant or best person.
steps.expect: you can read through tears, wind, dead batteries, or shaking hands.

steps.action: **Deliver to your partner, not the audience.** Hold the card low, look up at the starts and endings of sentences, and slow down when emotion rises.
steps.expect: your partner receives the vows as a promise, while guests simply witness it.

recipes.verification: The final vows fit the agreed length, include at least one specific story, contain concrete promises, and exist on a readable backup card.

recipes.title: add a comment to a document
recipes.name: add-a-comment-to-a-document
recipes.goal: A comment is attached to specific text or a location in a document without changing the main text.

steps.action: **Select the target text.** Highlight the word, sentence, or paragraph the comment should discuss.
steps.expect: the target text is highlighted.

steps.action: **Insert a comment.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose Review > New Comment; in Google Docs, choose Insert > Comment or press `Ctrl+Alt+M` on Windows/ChromeOS or `Command+Option+M` on Mac.
steps.expect: a comment box opens beside the document or near the text.

steps.action: **Type the comment.** Write a clear note, question, or requested change.
steps.expect: the comment text appears in the comment box.

steps.action: **Post the comment.** Click Post, Comment, or press the editor's submit shortcut.
steps.expect: the comment is saved and linked to the selected text.

steps.action: **Check the anchor.** Click the highlighted text or comment marker.
steps.expect: the comment and its related text are connected.

recipes.verification: The comment is visible in the document margin or comment panel and is anchored to the intended text or location.

recipes.title: add a dropdown list to a cell
recipes.name: add-a-dropdown-list-to-a-cell
recipes.goal: Add a dropdown list to one or more spreadsheet cells so users choose from allowed values.

steps.action: **Select the input cells.** Highlight the cells that should have the dropdown.
steps.expect: the target input cells are selected.

steps.action: **Open data validation.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Data > Data Validation`; Google Sheets: choose `Data > Data validation`.
steps.expect: validation settings appear.

steps.action: **Choose list criteria.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Allow: List`; Google Sheets: choose `Dropdown` or `Dropdown from a range`.
steps.expect: list settings are active.

steps.action: **Enter allowed values.** Type values separated by commas, such as `Open,In progress,Done`, or select a source range.
steps.expect: the allowed values are listed in the validation settings.

steps.action: **Save the validation.** Click `OK` in Excel or `Done` in Google Sheets.
steps.expect: a dropdown arrow or chip appears when a target cell is selected.

steps.action: **Test the dropdown.** Click a target cell and choose one allowed value.
steps.expect: the cell fills with the selected value.

recipes.verification: Each target cell offers only the intended dropdown choices, and selecting a choice writes that value into the cell.

recipes.title: add a footnote
recipes.name: add-a-footnote
recipes.goal: A footnote marker is inserted in the text and a matching note appears at the bottom of the page.

steps.action: **Place the cursor.** Click immediately after the word, sentence, or punctuation that needs a footnote.
steps.expect: the insertion cursor appears at the citation point.

steps.action: **Insert the footnote.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose References > Insert Footnote; in Google Docs, choose Insert > Footnote.
steps.expect: a superscript footnote number appears in the text and the cursor moves to the footnote area.

steps.action: **Type the note.** Enter the source, explanation, or citation text.
steps.expect: the footnote text appears at the bottom of the page.

steps.action: **Return to the main text.** Click back after the footnote marker or continue after the cited sentence.
steps.expect: the cursor is back in the document body.

steps.action: **Check numbering.** Add or inspect nearby footnotes if present.
steps.expect: footnote numbers are sequential and automatically updated.

recipes.verification: The document shows a superscript marker at the intended location and matching footnote text at the bottom of the page.

recipes.title: add page numbers
recipes.name: add-page-numbers
recipes.goal: Page numbers appear in the document header or footer in the chosen position.

steps.action: **Open page number options.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose Insert > Page Number; in Google Docs, choose Insert > Page numbers.
steps.expect: page number placement options appear.

steps.action: **Choose a position.** Select top or bottom of page and the alignment you need.
steps.expect: page numbers appear on document pages.

steps.action: **Check the first page setting.** Enable or disable different first page if the title page should not show a number.
steps.expect: the first page follows the intended numbering rule.

steps.action: **Review several pages.** Scroll through the beginning, middle, and end of the document.
steps.expect: numbering increments in order.

steps.action: **Close header or footer editing.** Click back in the document body or choose Close Header and Footer.
steps.expect: the document returns to normal editing mode.

recipes.verification: Each required page shows the correct page number in sequence and in the intended header or footer position.

recipes.title: adjust screen resolution
recipes.name: adjust-screen-resolution
recipes.goal: Change the screen resolution so display content is clearer, larger, or better matched to the monitor.

steps.action: **Open display settings.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: open Settings > System > Display; Mac: open System Settings > Displays.
steps.expect: display controls are visible.

steps.action: **Select the display.** If multiple screens appear, choose the one you want to adjust.
steps.expect: the selected display is highlighted or named.

steps.action: **Choose resolution or scaling.** Pick `Recommended`, `Default`, or another listed resolution or scaled option.
steps.expect: the screen preview or resolution value changes.

steps.action: **Confirm the change.** Accept the confirmation prompt if the display looks usable.
steps.expect: the new setting remains active.

steps.action: **Check readability.** Look at text, icons, and windows on the adjusted screen.
steps.expect: content is sharp and sized appropriately.

recipes.verification: The intended display shows the selected resolution or scaling, and text appears readable without blur.

recipes.title: apply a heading style
recipes.name: apply-a-heading-style
recipes.goal: Selected text is formatted with a real heading style so the document structure is recognized by the editor.

steps.action: **Select the heading text.** Highlight the line that should become a heading.
steps.expect: only the intended heading text is selected.

steps.action: **Open the style menu.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, use Home > Styles; in Google Docs, use the style menu that usually says Normal text.
steps.expect: heading style options are visible.

steps.action: **Choose the correct level.** Select Heading 1 for major sections, Heading 2 for subsections, or a lower level for nested sections.
steps.expect: the selected text changes to the heading style.

steps.action: **Check document navigation.** Open Navigation Pane in Word or Document outline in Google Docs if needed.
steps.expect: the heading appears in the document outline at the correct level.

recipes.verification: The selected line uses the intended built-in heading style and appears correctly in the document outline if the outline is available.

recipes.title: attach a file to an email
recipes.name: attach-a-file-to-an-email
recipes.goal: Attach a file to an email so the recipient can download or view it.

steps.action: **Open the draft.** Start a new email or open an existing draft.
steps.expect: the compose window is active.

steps.action: **Choose attach.** Click or tap the paperclip, `Attach`, or `Insert file` control.
steps.expect: a file picker or attachment menu opens.

steps.action: **Select the file.** Browse to the file, select it, and choose `Open`, `Attach`, or `Insert`.
steps.expect: the file name appears in the message as an attachment or upload.

steps.action: **Wait for upload.** Do not send until any progress bar finishes.
steps.expect: the attachment shows complete, with no spinning indicator.

steps.action: **Check size and access.** If the app converts it to a cloud link, confirm the link permissions allow only the intended recipient when possible.
steps.expect: the recipient can access the file without exposing it broadly.

steps.action: **Send the email.** Add the recipient, subject, and body, then click or tap `Send`.
steps.expect: the message appears in Sent with the attachment or file link.

recipes.verification: The sent email contains the correct file name, size or link, and access setting for the intended recipient.

recipes.title: autofill a series
recipes.name: autofill-a-series
recipes.goal: Fill a spreadsheet range with a continuing number, date, or text series.

steps.action: **Enter the starting values.** Type the first two values of the series in adjacent cells, such as `1` and `2`.
steps.expect: the pattern cells contain the seed values.

steps.action: **Select the seed cells.** Highlight both starting cells.
steps.expect: a border surrounds the selected pattern.

steps.action: **Drag the fill handle.** Drag the small square at the selection corner across or down the target range.
steps.expect: a preview or outline extends over the cells to fill.

steps.action: **Release to fill.** Let go at the last target cell.
steps.expect: the cells fill with the continued series.

steps.action: **Check the pattern.** Review the last few filled values.
steps.expect: the sequence follows the intended increment or calendar pattern.

recipes.verification: The filled range contains a continuous series that matches the seed pattern through the final cell.

recipes.title: back up a computer with time machine or file history
recipes.name: back-up-a-computer-with-time-machine-or-file-history
recipes.goal: Create an automatic computer backup using Time Machine on Mac or File History on Windows, then verify that files can be restored.

steps.action: **Connect the backup drive.** Plug in the external drive and wait for the operating system to recognize it.
steps.expect: the drive appears in Finder, File Explorer, or system backup settings.

steps.action: **Start the backup setup.** [BRANCH: Mac | Windows] open System Settings > General > Time Machine on Mac, or Settings > System > Storage > Advanced storage settings > Backup options/File History on Windows.
steps.expect: the OS shows backup destination options.

steps.action: **Select the backup drive.** Choose the external drive as the backup destination. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* formatting or erasing the drive deletes its existing contents, so confirm it contains nothing you need first.
steps.expect: the drive is assigned to Time Machine or File History.

steps.action: **Enable encryption if offered.** Turn on encrypted backups and store the password in a password manager.
steps.expect: the backup settings show encryption enabled or the password is stored before the first backup proceeds.

steps.action: **Choose included folders.** Confirm Documents, Desktop, Pictures, and other important user folders are included, and exclude only files you can replace.
steps.expect: the backup scope covers critical data.

steps.action: **Run the first backup.** Start the backup and keep the computer awake and connected to power until it finishes.
steps.expect: backup progress completes without errors.

steps.action: **Restore a test file.** Use Time Machine or File History to restore a copy of a harmless file to a temporary folder.
steps.expect: the restored file opens correctly.

steps.action: **Set a backup routine.** Leave automatic backups enabled and connect the drive on a predictable schedule if it is not always attached.
steps.expect: settings show the latest backup time and future backups are automatic or scheduled.

recipes.verification: Backup settings show a successful backup from today, encryption is enabled when sensitive data is present, and a test restore opens correctly from the backup.

recipes.title: back up your files
recipes.name: back-up-your-files
recipes.goal: Your important files exist in at least two places besides the original device — one of them off-site — and you have proven you can restore from them.

steps.action: **Inventory what to protect.** List the folders that would hurt to lose; check their total size. Exclude what's re-downloadable (installers, media libraries with accounts).
steps.expect: a short folder list and a size number that fits your destinations.

steps.action: **Adopt the 3-2-1 shape.** 3 copies (original + 2 backups), 2 different media, 1 off-site. [BRANCH: cloud-first (sync tool + external drive) | drive-first (two drives, one stored elsewhere)]
steps.expect: you can say where each of the three copies will live.

steps.action: **Set up the cloud/off-site copy.** Install the sync client (or enable the OS's built-in backup) and point it at the inventory folders.
steps.expect: initial upload running; the client shows progress and finishes with all folders marked synced.

steps.action: **Set up the local copy.** Connect the external drive; use the OS backup tool (Time Machine / File History / rsync script) targeting the same inventory, scheduled automatically — manual copying is a backup plan that stops happening within a month.
steps.expect: first full backup completes; the schedule shows a next run time.

steps.action: **Encrypt what leaves your control.** Turn on the drive's/OS's encryption for the external disk; confirm the cloud provider encrypts at rest (or use an encrypting client for sensitive folders). ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an encrypted backup with a lost password is destroyed data — store the backup password in your password manager *now*.
steps.expect: both destinations encrypted; password stored.

steps.action: **Run a restore test — this is the step everyone skips.** Pick 3 random files, restore them from *each* destination to a temp folder, open them.
steps.expect: all restored files open correctly; you know the restore procedure cold.

steps.action: **Schedule the off-site rotation and a periodic check.** Drive-first setups: swap the off-site drive on a recurring reminder (monthly). All setups: calendar a quarterly 5-minute check that both backups are current.
steps.expect: reminders exist; latest-backup timestamps are recent at each check.

recipes.verification: Three current copies exist (original, local drive, off-site/cloud), a random-file restore succeeded from both backup legs within recent memory, the backup password is in the password manager, and automatic schedules show recent successful runs.

recipes.title: back up your messaging app
recipes.name: back-up-your-messaging-app
recipes.goal: Your messaging app has a current cloud backup, the backup frequency is deliberate, media handling is understood, and you know how restore would work.

steps.action: **Open the app's backup settings.** Look under Settings > Chats, Account, Storage, or Backup depending on the app.
steps.expect: you see backup status or a backup option.

steps.action: **Choose the cloud destination.** Confirm the backup account, such as iCloud, Google Drive, or the app's own cloud.
steps.expect: the destination account is correct.

steps.action: **Set backup frequency.** [BRANCH: daily | weekly | manual] choose daily for active important chats, weekly for casual use, or manual if storage is tight.
steps.expect: the schedule matches the importance of the messages.

steps.action: **Decide whether media is included.** Check whether photos, videos, voice notes, and documents are included or excluded.
steps.expect: you know what will restore later.

steps.action: **Enable encryption if offered.** Save the password or recovery key somewhere secure before turning on encrypted backup.
steps.expect: the app confirms encrypted backup or shows the key setup complete.

steps.action: **Run a backup now.** Start a manual backup while on Wi-Fi and keep the app open if it asks.
steps.expect: progress completes and shows today's date.

steps.action: **Verify cloud storage.** Check that the cloud account has enough remaining storage for future backups.
steps.expect: no storage warning appears.

steps.action: **Review restore requirements.** Note that restore usually requires the same phone number, account, and encryption password if enabled.
steps.expect: you know what credentials are needed before replacing a phone.

recipes.verification: The app's backup screen shows a successful backup dated today, with the expected cloud account, frequency, and media setting.

recipes.title: back up your phone
recipes.name: back-up-your-phone
recipes.goal: Create a current phone backup and verify that the important data would be recoverable after loss, damage, or replacement.

steps.action: **Choose backup location.** [BRANCH: cloud | computer] use cloud for automatic recovery, or a computer for local control and large backups.
steps.expect: you know where the backup will be stored.

steps.action: **Check what is included.** Review whether photos, messages, contacts, app data, device settings, and health data are included.
steps.expect: critical categories are either included or handled separately.

steps.action: **Free storage if needed.** Compare available cloud or computer storage with the estimated backup size.
steps.expect: there is enough space to finish the backup.

steps.action: **Connect power and Wi-Fi.** Plug in the phone and connect to a trusted Wi-Fi network unless using a computer cable.
steps.expect: the backup will not fail from battery or cellular limits.

steps.action: **Start the backup.** Use the phone's backup settings or the computer's device-management app.
steps.expect: progress starts or the phone reports a backup is queued.

steps.action: **Keep the phone available.** Leave it locked or idle until the backup completes.
steps.expect: the backup finishes without interruption.

steps.action: **Verify timestamp and size.** Open backup settings and confirm the latest backup date, time, and device name.
steps.expect: the newest backup is from today and belongs to this phone.

steps.action: **Check separate apps.** Confirm chat apps, authenticator apps, banking apps, and photo services have their own backup or transfer plan if needed.
steps.expect: app-specific data is not assumed without evidence.

steps.action: **Set cadence.** Turn on automatic backup or schedule a manual backup before travel, repairs, and phone upgrades.
steps.expect: the next backup will happen without relying on memory.

recipes.verification: Backup settings show a completed backup from today for this phone, and your most important data categories are listed as included or separately backed up.

recipes.title: block a phone number
recipes.name: block-a-phone-number
recipes.goal: Calls and messages from a specific phone number are blocked on your phone, and obvious spam can also be reported through the platform or carrier.

steps.action: **Open the number source.** [BRANCH: call log | messages | contacts] start from Recents, the conversation thread, voicemail, or the contact card.
steps.expect: the exact number or contact is visible.

steps.action: **Confirm the number is the one to block.** Check area code, name, and recent time so you do not block a legitimate contact by mistake.
steps.expect: the unwanted caller is identified.

steps.action: **Open the info or details screen.** On iPhone, tap the info button or contact card; on Android, tap the number, details, or three-dot menu depending on the phone app.
steps.expect: blocking or spam options appear.

steps.action: **Block the number.** Choose Block Caller, Block/report spam, or Block number, then confirm.
steps.expect: the phone shows the number as blocked.

steps.action: **Report spam when appropriate.** If the call or text was scam, robocall, phishing, or harassment, use Report Junk, Report Spam, or the carrier spam option when shown.
steps.expect: the report is submitted without needing to reply to the sender.

steps.action: **Check message handling.** Know that blocked callers may still leave voicemail in a blocked folder, and texts may be hidden rather than visibly rejected.
steps.expect: you know where blocked items would appear if needed.

steps.action: **Repeat across linked devices if needed.** Tablets, computers, messaging apps, and carrier services may have separate block lists.
steps.expect: the block applies where you actually receive calls or messages.

recipes.verification: The phone's blocked list includes the exact number, and new calls or messages from that number no longer appear in the normal inbox or call flow.

recipes.title: book an appointment online
recipes.name: book-an-appointment-online
recipes.goal: An appointment is booked through the correct online portal, confirmed with date, time, location or link, and saved to a calendar with rescheduling details.

steps.action: **Find the real booking portal.** Start from the provider's official website, app, or account, not from sponsored search results.
steps.expect: the portal branding and domain match the provider.

steps.action: **Choose the correct service type.** Select the reason, duration, location, provider, or appointment category that matches the need.
steps.expect: available slots are for the right service, not a similar shorter visit.

steps.action: **Filter by practical constraints.** Check location, time zone, in-person versus virtual, language, provider, and preparation requirements.
steps.expect: the slot list only includes appointments you can actually attend.

steps.action: **Pick a slot and review details.** Select the date/time, then read the confirmation page before finalizing.
steps.expect: the page shows service, provider, location or video link rules, and time zone.

steps.action: **Enter contact and required details.** Provide phone, email, account number, insurance, reason for visit, or notes as requested.
steps.expect: required fields validate and the portal can send reminders.

steps.action: **Confirm the booking.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some appointments charge missed-visit fees or deposits, so confirm cancellation policy before final booking.
steps.expect: the portal shows booked, confirmed, or request received.

steps.action: **Save the confirmation number.** Screenshot or download the confirmation page and keep any email or text.
steps.expect: you have the date, time, provider, address/link, and confirmation number.

steps.action: **Put it on your calendar.** Add travel time, preparation tasks, documents to bring, and the reschedule/cancel deadline.
steps.expect: calendar entry has reminders and all logistics.

steps.action: **Locate the reschedule path.** Before leaving the portal, identify Manage appointment, Cancel, or Reschedule.
steps.expect: you know how to change the booking without starting from scratch.

recipes.verification: The appointment appears in the portal or confirmation message with date, time, location/link, service type, and confirmation number, and the same details are on your calendar.

recipes.title: bookmark a page
recipes.name: bookmark-a-page
recipes.goal: Save the current web page as a browser bookmark so it can be opened later.

steps.action: **Confirm the page.** Check the title and address bar.
steps.expect: the page shown is the one you want to save.

steps.action: **Open bookmark controls.** Press `Ctrl+D` on Windows/Linux or `Command+D` on Mac, or click the star in the address bar.
steps.expect: a bookmark dialog or popover opens.

steps.action: **Choose a name and folder.** Edit the bookmark name if needed and select a folder such as Bookmarks Bar or Favorites.
steps.expect: the dialog shows the intended name and folder.

steps.action: **Save the bookmark.** Click `Done`, `Save`, or the equivalent button.
steps.expect: the star or bookmark icon shows the page is saved.

recipes.verification: The page appears in the selected bookmark folder and opens when clicked.

recipes.title: calculate an average
recipes.name: calculate-an-average
recipes.goal: Calculate the arithmetic average of a spreadsheet range.

steps.action: **Select the result cell.** Click the empty cell where the average should appear.
steps.expect: the result cell is active.

steps.action: **Enter the average formula.** Type `=AVERAGE(C2:C20)`, replacing `C2:C20` with the actual range.
steps.expect: the formula appears with the range highlighted.

steps.action: **Confirm the formula.** Press `Enter` or `Return`.
steps.expect: the average appears in the result cell.

steps.action: **Check the range.** Click the result cell and inspect the formula bar.
steps.expect: the formula includes only the intended numeric cells.

recipes.verification: The result cell contains an `AVERAGE`, `AVERAGEIF`, or weighted-average formula, and its range matches the intended values.

recipes.title: cancel a free trial before it charges
recipes.name: cancel-a-free-trial-before-it-charges
recipes.goal: A free trial is canceled before the first paid charge, with confirmation saved and the next statement monitored.

steps.action: **Find the billing date immediately.** Check signup email, account billing page, app store subscription page, or card authorization.
steps.expect: you know the exact date and time the trial converts to paid.

steps.action: **Set a calendar reminder before the deadline.** Put one reminder 3 to 7 days before the charge and another on the last safe day.
steps.expect: the reminder includes service name, account email, and cancel path.

steps.action: **Locate where the subscription is managed.** [BRANCH: service website | Apple App Store | Google Play | payment provider] Follow the place where billing was initiated.
steps.expect: the active trial appears with price and renewal date.

steps.action: **Start cancellation from the billing page.** Use Account, Billing, Subscription, Membership, or Manage plan menus, ignoring upgrade prompts.
steps.expect: you reach a page offering cancel, end trial, or turn off renewal.

steps.action: **Read retention screens carefully.** Decline pause, discount, and downgrade offers unless you intentionally want them.
steps.expect: the next button still leads toward cancellation, not a cheaper active plan.

steps.action: **Confirm cancellation.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* canceling may remove trial access immediately, so download needed data first if the service warns access will end now.
steps.expect: status changes to canceled, expires on, or auto-renew off.

steps.action: **Capture proof.** Screenshot the final confirmation and save the cancellation email.
steps.expect: proof shows service name, account, cancellation date, and trial end date.

steps.action: **Watch the next statement.** Check the card, bank, PayPal, Apple, or Google transaction list after the scheduled billing date passes.
steps.expect: no new paid charge appears, or any charge is identified quickly for refund/dispute.

recipes.verification: The subscription status says canceled or auto-renew off, proof is saved, and the first expected billing date passes without an unrecognized paid charge.

recipes.title: cast your screen to a tv
recipes.name: cast-your-screen-to-a-tv
recipes.goal: Your phone, tablet, or computer displays content on a TV or streaming device, and you can stop casting when finished.

steps.action: **Put both devices on the same Wi-Fi.** Check the TV or streaming device network and the phone or computer network. Guest networks may block discovery.
steps.expect: both devices use the same normal home or room Wi-Fi.

steps.action: **Open the content or screen-mirroring control.** [BRANCH: cast icon in an app | AirPlay | system screen mirror] use the app's Cast icon for YouTube or streaming apps, AirPlay for Apple devices, or system mirroring for the whole screen.
steps.expect: a device list appears.

steps.action: **Choose the correct TV.** Select the room name or streaming device, then enter any code shown on the TV if prompted.
steps.expect: the TV changes to the cast session or mirrored screen.

steps.action: **Confirm audio output.** Play a short clip and check whether sound comes from the TV, receiver, or phone.
steps.expect: audio comes from the expected speakers.

steps.action: **Adjust orientation and privacy.** For full-screen mirroring, close private apps and notifications; rotate the phone if landscape content matters.
steps.expect: the TV shows only content you intend others to see.

steps.action: **Expect some latency.** Use casting for video, slides, photos, and casual browsing. Avoid it for precise gaming or fast cursor work unless latency is acceptable.
steps.expect: video may lag slightly behind the device.

steps.action: **Stop casting deliberately.** Tap the Cast icon, AirPlay control, or Screen Mirroring control, then choose Stop, Disconnect, or the device name again.
steps.expect: the TV returns to its previous app or home screen.

recipes.verification: The selected TV shows the intended content, audio plays from the expected output, and the device can disconnect the session on command.

recipes.title: cc and bcc an email
recipes.name: cc-and-bcc-an-email
recipes.goal: Send an email with visible copy recipients in `Cc` and private copy recipients in `Bcc`.

steps.action: **Start the message.** Open a new message or reply draft.
steps.expect: the compose window is open.

steps.action: **Add primary recipients.** Put the people expected to act on the message in `To`.
steps.expect: each primary recipient appears in the `To` field.

steps.action: **Show copy fields.** Click or tap `Cc`, `Bcc`, or `Cc/Bcc` if those fields are hidden.
steps.expect: separate `Cc` and `Bcc` fields are visible.

steps.action: **Add visible copy recipients.** Put people who should be kept informed in `Cc`.
steps.expect: the copied recipients are visible in the `Cc` field.

steps.action: **Add private copy recipients.** Put recipients whose addresses should not be shown to others in `Bcc`.
steps.expect: the private recipients appear only in the `Bcc` field.

steps.action: **Review recipient etiquette.** Confirm everyone in `To` and `Cc` can appropriately see each other's addresses, and use `Bcc` for large groups or privacy-sensitive lists.
steps.expect: no private address is exposed in `To` or `Cc`.

steps.action: **Send the email.** Click or tap `Send` after checking subject and body.
steps.expect: the message leaves the outbox or appears in Sent.

recipes.verification: The sent message shows intended people in `To` and `Cc`, and `Bcc` recipients are not visible to other recipients.

recipes.title: change line spacing
recipes.name: change-line-spacing
recipes.goal: Selected text or the whole document uses the intended line spacing.

steps.action: **Select the text to change.** Highlight a paragraph range, or press `Ctrl+A` or `Command+A` to select the whole document.
steps.expect: the intended text is selected.

steps.action: **Open line spacing controls.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose Home > Line and Paragraph Spacing; in Google Docs, choose Format > Line & paragraph spacing.
steps.expect: spacing choices appear.

steps.action: **Choose the spacing.** Select Single, 1.15, 1.5, Double, or a custom spacing option.
steps.expect: the selected text changes vertical spacing.

steps.action: **Check paragraph spacing.** Adjust before or after paragraph spacing if extra gaps remain.
steps.expect: paragraphs have the intended amount of space between them.

steps.action: **Review page flow.** Scroll through the changed section or document.
steps.expect: text is readable and page breaks still fall acceptably.

recipes.verification: The selected text displays with the intended line spacing, and paragraph gaps match the document requirement.

recipes.title: change the system volume
recipes.name: change-the-system-volume
recipes.goal: Raise, lower, or mute the device's main sound volume.

steps.action: **Find volume controls.** Use keyboard volume keys, side buttons, menu bar, taskbar, Control Center, or quick settings.
steps.expect: a volume slider or on-screen volume indicator appears.

steps.action: **Adjust the level.** Move the slider or press volume up/down to the desired level.
steps.expect: the volume number or bar changes.

steps.action: **Mute if needed.** Click or tap the speaker icon or mute button.
steps.expect: the icon shows muted and sound stops.

steps.action: **Check the output device.** If sound is wrong or absent, open sound output settings and choose the intended device.
steps.expect: the selected speaker or headphones are listed as active.

steps.action: **Test audio.** Play a short sound, video, or system test tone.
steps.expect: sound plays at the intended loudness or remains muted.

recipes.verification: The system volume indicator shows the intended level or mute state, and test audio behaves accordingly.

recipes.title: change your desktop wallpaper
recipes.name: change-your-desktop-wallpaper
recipes.goal: Set a new desktop wallpaper image.

steps.action: **Open wallpaper settings.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: right-click the desktop and choose `Personalize`; Mac: choose `Apple menu > System Settings > Wallpaper`.
steps.expect: wallpaper or background settings are visible.

steps.action: **Choose an image source.** Select a built-in image, solid color, photo folder, or `Browse photos`/`Add Photo`.
steps.expect: image choices or a file picker appears.

steps.action: **Select the wallpaper.** Click the image you want to use.
steps.expect: the desktop preview updates.

steps.action: **Set fit or display options.** Choose Fill, Fit, Stretch, Tile, Center, or the closest available option.
steps.expect: the image is framed acceptably on the screen.

steps.action: **Close settings.** Exit the settings window after the wallpaper appears correctly.
steps.expect: the desktop shows the new wallpaper.

recipes.verification: The desktop background displays the selected image after settings are closed.

recipes.title: change your wifi password
recipes.name: change-your-wifi-password
