recipes.goal: Your router broadcasts the same Wi-Fi network with a new strong password, and trusted devices are reconnected.

steps.action: **Connect locally.** Join the current Wi-Fi or plug a computer into the router with Ethernet.
steps.expect: the device can reach the router or internet.

steps.action: **Find the router admin address.** Check the router label, app, gateway address, or common addresses such as `192.168.1.1` or `192.168.0.1`.
steps.expect: a router login page or app dashboard opens.

steps.action: **Log in as admin.** Use the router admin password, not the Wi-Fi password unless the label says they are the same.
steps.expect: wireless or network settings are available.

steps.action: **Open wireless settings.** Find Wi-Fi, Wireless, SSID, or WLAN settings for the main network.
steps.expect: the current network name and password field are visible.

steps.action: **Set a strong Wi-Fi password.** Use WPA2-Personal or WPA3-Personal if available and a unique password of at least 14 characters.
steps.expect: the new password is accepted by the router UI.

steps.action: **Save changes.** Apply or save, then wait for the Wi-Fi radios to restart.
steps.expect: connected Wi-Fi devices drop offline briefly.

steps.action: **Reconnect your main device.** [BRANCH: same SSID | new SSID] Same SSID: forget the old saved password if prompted. New SSID: select the new network name.
steps.expect: the device reconnects with internet access.

steps.action: **Reconnect household devices.** Update phones, laptops, TVs, printers, cameras, smart plugs, and guest devices as needed.
steps.expect: each trusted device returns online.

steps.action: **Store the password securely.** Save it in a password manager or a private household record.
steps.expect: authorized people can retrieve it later without reading the router label aloud.

recipes.verification: A device connects to the Wi-Fi using the new password, reaches the internet, and the old password no longer works.

recipes.title: check a links real destination
recipes.name: check-a-links-real-destination
recipes.goal: Check where a link really goes before opening it or entering information.

steps.action: **Hover without clicking.** Move the pointer over the link and keep the mouse button untouched.
steps.expect: the browser or app shows a destination preview.

steps.action: **Read the domain.** Look for the main domain immediately before the first single slash after `https://`.
steps.expect: the domain matches the organization you expect.

steps.action: **Check for lookalikes.** Compare spelling, extra words, hyphens, and unusual endings such as `.zip` or unfamiliar country codes.
steps.expect: the domain does not rely on a confusing imitation.

steps.action: **Copy if you need a closer look.** Right-click and choose `Copy Link Address`, then paste into a plain text note.
steps.expect: the full URL is visible as text.

steps.action: **Open only if it matches.** Use a new tab or type the known official site manually if uncertain.
steps.expect: you either reach the expected site or avoid opening the suspicious link.

recipes.verification: The link's real destination domain is identified, and it matches the expected organization before any sensitive action.

recipes.title: check free disk space
recipes.name: check-free-disk-space
recipes.goal: Check how much storage space remains on your computer or a connected drive.

steps.action: **Open storage location.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: open File Explorer and choose `This PC`; Mac: choose `Apple menu > System Settings > General > Storage` or select a disk in Finder.
steps.expect: available disks or storage categories are visible.

steps.action: **Read free space.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: look under the drive name or right-click the drive and choose `Properties`; Mac: read available storage in Settings or press `Command+I` on a selected disk.
steps.expect: used and free space values are shown.

steps.action: **Check the correct drive.** Confirm you are reading the internal disk, external drive, or cloud-synced local storage you care about.
steps.expect: the disk name matches the target.

steps.action: **Note whether action is needed.** Compare free space with the task requirement, such as an update, download, or copy.
steps.expect: you know whether there is enough space.

recipes.verification: The intended disk shows a specific free-space amount, such as `42 GB available`, that can be compared with the needed amount.

recipes.title: check if your data was in a breach
recipes.name: check-if-your-data-was-in-a-breach
recipes.goal: You determine whether an email address or phone number appears in known data breaches, then take password and two-factor actions for affected accounts.

steps.action: **Use a reputable breach-check service.** Open a known service such as Have I Been Pwned or a password manager's built-in breach monitor by typing the address directly.
steps.expect: the site explains what it checks and does not ask for your password.

steps.action: **Check one identifier at a time.** Enter an email address or phone number, then submit.
steps.expect: the result lists no breaches or names specific breach incidents.

steps.action: **Record affected services.** Note breached sites, data types exposed, and breach dates.
steps.expect: you have a short action list by account.

steps.action: **Prioritize passwords reused anywhere.** Search your password manager for the affected email and reused or weak passwords.
steps.expect: reused passwords are identified before lower-risk cleanup.

steps.action: **Change exposed or reused passwords.** Log in through each service's official site and set a unique password generated by the password manager.
steps.expect: the password manager stores a new unique password for each affected account.

steps.action: **Turn on two-factor authentication.** Prefer authenticator app, passkey, or security key over SMS when available.
steps.expect: the account shows 2FA enabled and recovery codes saved privately.

steps.action: **Review account activity.** Check recent logins, devices, recovery email, phone number, forwarding rules, and payment details on affected accounts.
steps.expect: no unknown sessions or settings remain.

steps.action: **Monitor for follow-up scams.** Treat breach-themed calls, texts, and emails as suspicious, especially if they cite old personal details.
steps.expect: you verify through official channels before acting.

recipes.verification: Every affected account with reused, weak, or exposed credentials now has a unique password and 2FA enabled where supported, and account activity shows no unknown active sessions.

recipes.title: childproof a tablet for a kid
recipes.name: childproof-a-tablet-for-a-kid
recipes.goal: Configure a tablet so a child can use age-appropriate apps and content while purchases, adult content, location sharing, and settings changes are restricted.

steps.action: **Update the tablet.** Install system updates and app updates before setting restrictions.
steps.expect: parental-control options are current.

steps.action: **Create or select a child profile.** [BRANCH: iPad | Android tablet | Amazon Fire] use Family Sharing child account, Google Family Link, or Amazon Kids profile.
steps.expect: the child uses a managed profile or child account.

steps.action: **Set a parent passcode.** Choose a Screen Time, Family Link, or parental-control PIN that the child does not know.
steps.expect: restrictions cannot be changed from the child profile.

steps.action: **Restrict purchases and installs.** Require approval or block app installs, in-app purchases, and paid downloads.
steps.expect: store purchases require parent approval.

steps.action: **Set content limits.** Choose age ratings for apps, movies, websites, games, books, and search filtering.
steps.expect: adult or above-age content is blocked in the child profile.

steps.action: **Configure screen time.** Add downtime, daily limits, bedtime, or school-hour rules.
steps.expect: the tablet shows when use is allowed and limited.

steps.action: **Review privacy permissions.** Disable unnecessary camera, microphone, contacts, Bluetooth, and location access for child apps.
steps.expect: apps have only needed permissions.

steps.action: **Test as the child.** Switch to the child profile and try installing an app, opening a blocked site, and using an allowed app.
steps.expect: blocked actions fail and allowed apps work.

recipes.verification: From the child profile, age-appropriate apps work, blocked websites and purchases are stopped, screen-time rules display correctly, and parent controls require the parent passcode.

recipes.title: choose a security question answer
recipes.name: choose-a-security-question-answer
recipes.goal: Create security question answers that work like extra passwords instead of easy-to-guess personal facts.

steps.action: **Read the available questions.** List the questions the site allows, such as pet, school, street, city, or mother's maiden name.
steps.expect: you know which questions are mandatory and optional.

steps.action: **Assume honest answers are unsafe.** Treat public records, social media, old yearbooks, family knowledge, and data brokers as attacker sources.
steps.expect: you reject answers based on real biographical facts.

steps.action: **Generate answer strings.** Use random words, a password-manager generator, or memorable nonsense unrelated to the question.
steps.expect: each answer is unique and not guessable from your life.

steps.action: **Store the exact answers.** Save question and answer pairs in your password manager under the account entry.
steps.expect: capitalization, spaces, and punctuation are recorded exactly.

steps.action: **Enter the answers.** Paste or type each stored answer into the site's form.
steps.expect: the form accepts the answers and shows no mismatch warning.

steps.action: **Check recovery options.** Add or verify a current email, phone, authenticator, or recovery code if the site offers stronger recovery.
steps.expect: security questions are not your only recovery method.

steps.action: **Save changes.** Submit the security settings. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* losing unstored fake answers can lock you out, so confirm they are stored before saving.
steps.expect: the site confirms security questions were updated.

steps.action: **Test retrieval privately.** Open the password manager entry and confirm you can find the exact answers.
steps.expect: you can recover the answers without relying on memory.

steps.action: **Review old accounts.** Update any high-value account still using honest answers.
steps.expect: banking, email, benefits, and cloud accounts no longer rely on public facts.

recipes.verification: Each security question answer is unique, not a true personal fact, and stored exactly in a password manager or secure record.

recipes.title: clean up your digital footprint
recipes.name: clean-up-your-digital-footprint
recipes.goal: Reduce unnecessary public and semi-public information about you across accounts, search results, old posts, and data-sharing settings.

steps.action: **Inventory accounts.** Search your password manager, email, app stores, and browser history for old accounts and profiles.
steps.expect: you have a list of places to review.

steps.action: **Search yourself.** Search your name, usernames, phone numbers, emails, and image results in a private window.
steps.expect: public exposures are listed.

steps.action: **Triage by risk.** Prioritize home address, phone, family links, workplace, old resumes, public photos, and accounts with reused passwords.
steps.expect: the highest-risk items are first.

steps.action: **Update privacy settings.** Limit profile visibility, search indexing, contact discovery, ad personalization, and public friend lists.
steps.expect: active accounts expose less information.

steps.action: **Remove or edit old content.** Delete, unpublish, anonymize, or request removal for posts and profiles that no longer need to be public. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* permanent deletion may remove photos, messages, or purchase records; export needed data first.
steps.expect: unnecessary content is removed or queued for removal.

steps.action: **Close unused accounts.** [BRANCH: delete | deactivate | keep] delete low-value accounts, deactivate uncertain ones, and keep accounts needed for receipts or recovery.
steps.expect: account status matches future need.

steps.action: **Secure what remains.** Change reused passwords, enable multi-factor authentication, and remove stale connected apps.
steps.expect: remaining accounts are harder to abuse.

steps.action: **Track follow-up.** Record removal requests, deletion windows, and accounts that need rechecking.
steps.expect: pending cleanup is not forgotten.

recipes.verification: Your inventory shows reviewed accounts, high-risk public exposures are removed or restricted, remaining accounts have unique passwords and MFA where available, and pending removals have follow-up dates.

recipes.title: clean up your inbox
recipes.name: clean-up-your-inbox
recipes.goal: Your inbox contains only messages that still need attention, while older mail is archived, filtered, or unsubscribed from without losing important records.

steps.action: **Sort by newest first.** Open the inbox and keep the default recent view so you see current obligations first.
steps.expect: the top of the inbox reflects recent mail.

steps.action: **Do a quick sweep.** Select obvious newsletters, receipts, alerts, and completed threads from the last few pages.
steps.expect: a batch of low-value messages is selected.

steps.action: **Archive instead of deleting.** Move selected messages to Archive or All Mail unless they are spam or truly unwanted.
steps.expect: the inbox count drops while search can still find the messages.

steps.action: **Unsubscribe from repeat noise.** Open recurring senders you no longer read and use the unsubscribe link or built-in unsubscribe button.
steps.expect: the sender confirms removal or says it may take a few days.

steps.action: **Create simple folders or labels.** [BRANCH: folders | labels] make only broad containers such as Receipts, Travel, Work, School, or Action.
steps.expect: the list is short enough to remember.

steps.action: **Add filters for predictable mail.** Route receipts, statements, newsletters, or alerts to labels and optionally skip the inbox.
steps.expect: future matching messages file themselves.

steps.action: **Process action mail.** For each remaining message, reply, turn it into a task, schedule time, or leave it in the inbox only if it truly needs action.
steps.expect: the inbox is mostly actionable.

steps.action: **Set an inbox-zero-ish rule.** Pick a sustainable target, such as under 20 messages or no unread messages, instead of chasing perfection.
steps.expect: you have a clear stopping point for routine cleanup.

recipes.verification: The inbox shows only current action items or your chosen small threshold, and at least one recurring noise source is unsubscribed or filtered.

recipes.title: clear an app cache
recipes.name: clear-an-app-cache
recipes.goal: You clear temporary app cache to fix slowness or storage pressure without confusing it with clearing app data, which can remove sign-in and local settings.

steps.action: **Identify the symptom.** Confirm whether the problem is storage use, slow loading, stale images, or app glitches.
steps.expect: there is a specific reason to clear cache.

steps.action: **Open app storage settings.** Go to Settings > Apps, choose the app, then open Storage or Storage and cache.
steps.expect: cache and data sizes are visible if the platform exposes them.

steps.action: **Read the labels carefully.** Cache is temporary files; data is account state, downloads, settings, and local app content.
steps.expect: you can tell which button clears cache only.

steps.action: **Clear cache only.** Tap Clear cache if available.
steps.expect: cache size drops, while the app remains installed and signed in.

steps.action: **Reopen the app.** Launch the app and repeat the action that was slow or broken.
steps.expect: the app rebuilds temporary files and may load slightly slower the first time.

steps.action: **Avoid clearing data unless needed.** [BRANCH: cache fixed it | cache did not fix it] stop if the app works, or consider Clear data only after confirming credentials and local downloads.
steps.expect: you do not erase account state by accident.

steps.action: **Use in-app cache tools if present.** For browsers, maps, music, and social apps, check their own storage or offline-download settings.
steps.expect: large cached or offline items can be managed more precisely.

steps.action: **Repeat only when useful.** Do not clear cache daily; use it when storage is tight or stale temporary files cause problems.
steps.expect: cache returns over time as the app runs normally.

recipes.verification: The app's cache size is reduced, the app opens, and your account data remains intact unless you deliberately chose Clear data.

recipes.title: clear one sites data
recipes.name: clear-one-sites-data
recipes.goal: Clear cookies and stored data for one website without clearing data for every site.

steps.action: **Open site data controls.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] open privacy, security, cookies, or website data settings.
steps.expect: the browser offers a way to view stored site data.

steps.action: **Search for the site.** Enter the site's domain, such as `example.com`, in the site data search field.
steps.expect: matching stored data entries appear.

steps.action: **Select only that site.** Choose the matching domain or site entry.
steps.expect: no unrelated sites are selected.

steps.action: **Remove the site data.** Click `Remove`, `Delete`, `Clear`, or the trash icon for that site.
steps.expect: the entry disappears or shows pending removal.

steps.action: **Reload the site.** Open the site again and sign in if needed.
steps.expect: the site behaves like a fresh visit for that browser profile.

recipes.verification: The browser no longer lists stored data for the selected site, and revisiting the site starts a fresh session or asks for sign-in.

recipes.title: clear your browser cache
recipes.name: clear-your-browser-cache
recipes.goal: Clear cached website files when they are causing stale pages or display problems, while keeping passwords and useful sign-in data when possible.

steps.action: **Decide whether cache is the right target.** Use cache clearing for broken layouts, old images, failed updates, or site files that will not refresh.
steps.expect: there is a specific site problem, not just a vague wish to clean everything.

steps.action: **Try a hard refresh first.** Press the browser's hard-refresh shortcut or reload while bypassing cache.
steps.expect: the page either fixes itself or still shows the same problem.

steps.action: **Open browsing data settings.** [BRANCH: Chrome or Edge | Firefox | Safari] use the browser menu to find privacy, history, or clear browsing data.
steps.expect: a dialog lists data types and time range.

steps.action: **Choose the smallest useful time range.** Pick last hour, last day, or all time based on when the problem started.
steps.expect: the range covers the broken cached files without clearing more than needed.

steps.action: **Select cached files only if possible.** Leave passwords checked off, and leave cookies unchecked unless the site specifically has login or session trouble.
steps.expect: cached images and files are selected, passwords are not.

steps.action: **Understand logout effects.** If you clear cookies or site data, expect websites to log you out and forget carts or preferences.
steps.expect: you know whether sign-ins will be affected before clicking.

steps.action: **Clear the data.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* clearing cookies or site data removes local sessions, so confirm saved passwords and recovery access first.
steps.expect: the browser reports the selected data was cleared.

steps.action: **Reload the problem site.** Open the site again and sign in only if needed.
steps.expect: the site downloads fresh files and either works or fails consistently.

steps.action: **Escalate only if needed.** If the issue remains, test a private window, another browser, or another network.
steps.expect: you know whether the problem is cache, browser profile, or the website itself.

recipes.verification: The affected site reloads fresh content, and saved passwords remain available in the browser or password manager.

recipes.title: compress a pdf
recipes.name: compress-a-pdf
recipes.goal: You reduce a PDF file to a practical size while keeping the text, images, forms, and page order readable enough for the recipient or upload site.

steps.action: **Make a working copy.** Duplicate the PDF and rename it with `compressed` or the target size.
steps.expect: the original file remains untouched and the copy is ready to edit.

steps.action: **Check what is making it large.** Open the PDF and scan for full-page photos, scans, high-resolution images, or embedded graphics. Images usually create most of the file size.
steps.expect: you know whether compression can help a lot or only a little.

steps.action: **Try the built-in export first.** [BRANCH: macOS Preview | Windows print/export | Adobe Acrobat or office app] choose the lowest-friction built-in option such as Export, Save As Reduced Size, or Print to PDF with lower quality.
steps.expect: a second PDF is created with a smaller file size.

steps.action: **Use a trusted tool if built-in export is not enough.** Prefer Adobe Acrobat, your scanner software, or an offline PDF utility from a known vendor. Use online compressors only for non-sensitive files.
steps.expect: the tool offers quality or size settings before saving.

steps.action: **Set the target deliberately.** Choose screen or email quality for casual reading, and higher quality for documents with fine print, signatures, diagrams, or photos that matter.
steps.expect: the output size moves toward the limit without obvious damage.

steps.action: **Open the compressed file and inspect pages.** Zoom into small text, signatures, barcodes, QR codes, tables, and image-heavy pages.
steps.expect: the content is still legible at normal viewing and printing size.

steps.action: **Check forms, links, and page count.** If the PDF had fillable fields, bookmarks, links, or attachments, verify they survived.
steps.expect: page count and important interactive parts match the original.

steps.action: **Keep the best version.** If the file is still too large, run another pass at lower image quality; if it looks bad, go back to the previous copy and use gentler settings.
steps.expect: one compressed PDF meets the upload or sharing requirement.

recipes.verification: The compressed PDF is below the required size, opens without errors, has the same required pages, and remains readable when zoomed into the smallest important text.

recipes.title: connect a second monitor
recipes.name: connect-a-second-monitor
recipes.goal: Connect and configure a second monitor for extending or mirroring your screen.

steps.action: **Connect power.** Plug the monitor into power and turn it on.
steps.expect: the monitor power light turns on.

steps.action: **Connect video.** Plug HDMI, DisplayPort, USB-C, Thunderbolt, VGA, or an adapter into the monitor and computer.
steps.expect: the monitor detects a signal or the computer shows a display change.

steps.action: **Select monitor input.** Use the monitor buttons to choose the input matching the cable.
steps.expect: the monitor shows the computer image or a waiting-for-signal message on the right input.

steps.action: **Open display settings.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: Settings > System > Display; Mac: System Settings > Displays.
steps.expect: two displays are shown.

steps.action: **Choose layout.** Select extend, mirror, duplicate, or use as main display.
steps.expect: windows move according to the chosen layout.

steps.action: **Arrange displays.** Drag display thumbnails to match their physical positions.
steps.expect: the pointer crosses between screens in the expected direction.

steps.action: **Set resolution or scaling.** Choose recommended settings for each display.
steps.expect: both screens look sharp and readable.

recipes.verification: Both displays are visible in display settings, and the pointer or mirrored image behaves according to the selected layout.

recipes.title: connect to wifi
recipes.name: connect-to-wifi
recipes.goal: Your device is connected to the intended Wi-Fi network — home, work, or public — with working internet and sane security posture for the network's trust level.

steps.action: **Open Wi-Fi settings and identify the *exact* network name.** Venues post theirs; homes have it on the router sticker. Twin-named networks ("CafeFreeWiFi" vs "Cafe_Free_WiFi") are how evil-twin attacks work — the posted name, character for character, is the one.
steps.expect: the intended SSID visible in the list with plausible signal strength.

steps.action: **Select it and authenticate.** [BRANCH: password network → enter the key exactly (case matters) | open venue network → connect, then expect a captive portal | enterprise (work/university) → username + password, accept the org's certificate only if it matches expectations]
steps.expect: status moves to "connected"; wrong-password errors mean the key, not the world, is at fault.

steps.action: **Clear the captive portal if one appears.** Open a browser if it doesn't auto-pop (try any http site); accept terms / enter the room number or voucher. Give marketing fields the minimum.
steps.expect: the portal releases you; general sites load.

steps.action: **Verify actual internet.** Load a known site or run the OS's connectivity check. Connected-but-no-internet → F2.
steps.expect: pages load at usable speed.

steps.action: **Set the trust posture to match the network.** Public/venue: mark it "public" when the OS asks (disables file sharing), avoid logging into sensitive accounts without HTTPS (the padlock), and prefer your phone's hotspot for banking-class tasks. Home: fine.
steps.expect: sharing off on public networks; sensitive tasks deferred or tunneled.

steps.action: **Manage the remembering.** Home/work: let it auto-join. One-time public networks: forget them after use — auto-rejoining "Airport_Free" forever is a tracking and evil-twin surface.
steps.expect: the saved-networks list holds only networks you actually trust.

recipes.verification: The device shows the intended SSID connected, real pages load, sharing is off if the network is public, and the saved list contains no one-time networks set to auto-join.

recipes.title: convert a file format
recipes.name: convert-a-file-format
recipes.goal: A file is converted to the needed format while preserving the content quality required for its next use.

steps.action: **Open the original in its native app.** Use the program that created the file when possible, such as Word for DOCX or Photos for HEIC.
steps.expect: the file displays correctly before conversion.

steps.action: **Look for export or save-as.** Choose File > Export, Save As, Download, or Share, depending on the app.
steps.expect: the app shows a list of output formats.

steps.action: **Pick the target format.** [BRANCH: document | image | audio/video] Documents often become PDF; images become JPG, PNG, or TIFF; media becomes MP4, MP3, or WAV.
steps.expect: the chosen extension matches the requirement.

steps.action: **Choose quality settings.** For documents, embed fonts if offered; for images and video, balance quality against file size.
steps.expect: the estimated size and quality settings are visible before saving.

steps.action: **Save as a new file.** Keep the original untouched and put the converted file beside it with a clear name.
steps.expect: both original and converted files exist.

steps.action: **Use a converter only when needed.** If the app cannot export the format, use a trusted offline converter or reputable service, avoiding sensitive files online.
steps.expect: the converter produces a downloadable file in the target format.

steps.action: **Open the converted file.** Use the recipient's likely app or a common viewer to check layout, fonts, images, sound, or playback.
steps.expect: the converted file opens without errors and looks or plays as intended.

steps.action: **Send or upload the converted copy.** Upload the new file, not the original, and keep both until the recipient confirms it works.
steps.expect: the destination accepts the file type and size.

recipes.verification: The converted file opens in a common viewer, contains the expected content, and is accepted by the target service or recipient.

recipes.title: convert an image format
recipes.name: convert-an-image-format
recipes.goal: Save an image in a different file format such as JPG, PNG, HEIC, GIF, or WebP.

steps.action: **Open the image.** Open the file in an editor, photo app, preview app, or trusted converter.
steps.expect: the image is visible.

steps.action: **Choose export or save as.** Select `Export`, `Save as`, `Download as`, or format options.
steps.expect: a format dropdown or file-type menu appears.

steps.action: **Select the new format.** Choose the required format, such as JPG for photos or PNG for transparency.
steps.expect: the selected extension or format is shown.

steps.action: **Set quality if offered.** Choose a quality level that balances file size and clarity.
steps.expect: the estimated file size or quality setting is visible.

steps.action: **Save the converted file.** Use a new name or location to avoid confusing it with the original.
steps.expect: a new file with the target extension is created.

steps.action: **Open the result.** View the converted file in the target app or a file viewer.
steps.expect: the image displays correctly.

recipes.verification: The converted file has the desired extension and opens correctly in the target app or upload form.

recipes.title: copy a file
recipes.name: copy-a-file
recipes.goal: Create a second copy of a file in another location while keeping the original.

steps.action: **Select the source file.** Click the file once in File Explorer, Finder, or the desktop.
steps.expect: the file is highlighted.

steps.action: **Copy it.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Ctrl+C` or right-click and choose `Copy`; Mac: press `Command+C` or choose `Edit > Copy`.
steps.expect: the file is stored on the clipboard.

steps.action: **Open the destination folder.** Navigate to where the copy should go.
steps.expect: the destination folder is visible.

steps.action: **Paste the copy.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Ctrl+V`; Mac: press `Command+V`.
steps.expect: a copy of the file appears in the destination.

steps.action: **Resolve name conflicts.** If prompted, choose `Keep both`, `Replace`, or rename the copy intentionally.
steps.expect: the destination contains the intended version.

recipes.verification: The original file remains in its source location, and a readable copy exists in the destination.

recipes.title: copy a link address
recipes.name: copy-a-link-address
recipes.goal: Copy a link's destination URL without opening it.

steps.action: **Point at the link.** Move the pointer over the link text, button, or image.
steps.expect: the cursor changes or the browser shows a destination preview.

steps.action: **Open the link menu.** Right-click the link, or `Control`-click it on Mac.
steps.expect: a context menu with link actions appears.

steps.action: **Copy the address.** Choose `Copy Link Address`, `Copy Link`, or `Copy Link Location`.
steps.expect: the URL is placed on the clipboard.

steps.action: **Paste where needed.** Click the destination field or document and press `Ctrl+V` or `Command+V`.
steps.expect: the copied URL appears as text.

recipes.verification: Pasting from the clipboard produces the link destination URL you intended to copy.

recipes.title: copy and paste text
recipes.name: copy-and-paste-text
recipes.goal: Selected text is duplicated into a new location without removing it from the original location.

steps.action: **Select the text.** Drag across the text, or click at the start, hold `Shift`, and click at the end.
steps.expect: the selected text is highlighted.

steps.action: **Copy the selection.** Press `Ctrl+C` on Windows/Linux or `Command+C` on Mac, or choose Edit > Copy.
steps.expect: the original text remains in place.

steps.action: **Place the cursor.** Click where the copied text should appear.
steps.expect: the insertion cursor blinks at the target location.

steps.action: **Paste the text.** Press `Ctrl+V` on Windows/Linux or `Command+V` on Mac, or choose Edit > Paste.
steps.expect: the copied text appears at the cursor.

steps.action: **Check spacing.** Add or remove spaces or line breaks around the pasted text if needed.
steps.expect: the pasted text reads naturally in its new location.

recipes.verification: The original text is still present, and the same text appears in the intended new location.

recipes.title: copy text from an image
recipes.name: copy-text-from-an-image
recipes.goal: Extract readable text from a photo, screenshot, or image and copy it for reuse.

steps.action: **Open the image.** View the photo or screenshot in an app that supports text recognition.
steps.expect: the text in the image is visible.

steps.action: **Activate text recognition.** Choose `Live Text`, `Copy text`, `Lens`, OCR, or select directly over the text.
steps.expect: recognized words become selectable or highlighted.

steps.action: **Select the text.** Drag selection handles or choose `Select all` for the recognized text.
steps.expect: the intended text is highlighted.

steps.action: **Copy the text.** Click or tap `Copy`.
steps.expect: the text is placed on the clipboard.

steps.action: **Paste into a text field.** Paste into Notes, a document, email, or form.
steps.expect: editable text appears.

steps.action: **Proofread carefully.** Compare the pasted text with the original image.
steps.expect: numbers, names, dates, and punctuation are correct.

recipes.verification: The pasted text matches the image text closely enough for the intended use, with critical fields manually checked.

recipes.title: count words in a document
recipes.name: count-words-in-a-document
recipes.goal: The current word count for a document or selected text is found.

steps.action: **Select text only if needed.** Highlight the passage to count, or leave nothing selected for the whole document.
steps.expect: either the intended passage is highlighted or the document is unselected.

steps.action: **Open word count.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose Review > Word Count or check the status bar; in Google Docs, choose Tools > Word count or press `Ctrl+Shift+C` on Windows/ChromeOS or `Command+Shift+C` on Mac.
steps.expect: a word count panel or status value appears.

steps.action: **Read the count.** Note the words value and whether it applies to the selection or entire document.
steps.expect: the count matches the intended scope.

steps.action: **Close or pin the count.** Close the dialog, or enable display while typing if available.
steps.expect: the document is ready for continued editing.

recipes.verification: The displayed word count corresponds to the intended document scope and any stated counting rule.

recipes.title: create a desktop shortcut
recipes.name: create-a-desktop-shortcut
recipes.goal: Create a desktop shortcut or alias that opens a file, folder, app, or website without moving the original item.

steps.action: **Locate the target.** Find the app, file, folder, or website address you want the shortcut to open.
steps.expect: the target is visible or its URL is copied.

steps.action: **Create the shortcut.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: right-click the target and choose `Show more options > Send to > Desktop (create shortcut)` or right-click Desktop and choose `New > Shortcut`; Mac: select the item and choose `File > Make Alias` or press `Option+Command` while dragging to the desktop.
steps.expect: a shortcut or alias appears.

steps.action: **Name it clearly.** Rename the shortcut if the default name is unclear.
steps.expect: the desktop label identifies the target.

steps.action: **Test it.** Double-click the shortcut or alias.
steps.expect: the intended item opens.

recipes.verification: The desktop shortcut or alias opens the intended target while the original item remains in its original location.

recipes.title: create a folder
recipes.name: create-a-folder
recipes.goal: Create a new empty folder in a chosen location.

steps.action: **Open the destination.** Go to the desktop or open the parent folder in File Explorer or Finder.
steps.expect: the location where the folder will live is visible.

steps.action: **Create the folder.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Ctrl+Shift+N` or choose `New > Folder`; Mac: press `Shift+Command+N` or choose `File > New Folder`.
steps.expect: a new folder appears with its name selected.

steps.action: **Name the folder.** Type the folder name and press `Enter` on Windows or `Return` on Mac.
steps.expect: the folder shows the chosen name.

steps.action: **Open it if needed.** Double-click the folder to confirm it is empty or ready for files.
steps.expect: the folder opens with no unexpected contents.

recipes.verification: The new folder exists at the intended location, has the intended name, and can be opened.

recipes.title: create a shared photo album
recipes.name: create-a-shared-photo-album
recipes.goal: Create a shared photo album with the right people, permissions, and privacy settings, then confirm others can view or contribute as intended.

steps.action: **Choose the photo service.** [BRANCH: iPhone family | Android or mixed group | private link] use iCloud Shared Albums, Google Photos shared albums, or a private album link.
steps.expect: one service matches the devices in the group.

steps.action: **Create the album.** Open Photos or Google Photos, create a new shared album, and give it a specific name.
steps.expect: an empty shared album appears in the app.

steps.action: **Add initial photos.** Select only photos meant for this audience and avoid accidental screenshots or private images.
steps.expect: the album contains the intended starter set.

steps.action: **Invite people directly.** Add recipients by verified Apple ID, Google account, phone number, or email rather than posting a public link.
steps.expect: the invite list contains only intended people.

steps.action: **Set contribution permissions.** Decide whether invitees can add photos, comment, like, download, or invite others.
steps.expect: permissions match the album's purpose.

steps.action: **Check link sharing.** Turn off public link sharing unless the album is meant to be broadly accessible.
steps.expect: access requires the chosen invitations or a deliberate private link.

steps.action: **Verify from another account.** Ask one recipient to open the album and, if allowed, add a test photo or comment.
steps.expect: recipient access works exactly as intended.

recipes.verification: The shared album opens for an intended recipient, permissions allow only the intended actions, link sharing is off or deliberate, and the album contains only approved photos.

recipes.title: create a strong password
recipes.name: create-a-strong-password
recipes.goal: Create a password that is long, unique to one account, and practical to store without reuse.

steps.action: **Confirm the account page.** Check the URL and start from a bookmark or official app if possible.
steps.expect: the password is being entered on the real service.

steps.action: **Choose a storage handoff.** [BRANCH: password manager | browser password manager | written temporary note] decide where the password will live before generating it.
steps.expect: there is a place to save the password immediately.

steps.action: **Favor length over complexity tricks.** Use a random manager password or a passphrase of at least four unrelated words if you must type it manually.
steps.expect: the password is long enough to resist guessing without being impossible to enter.

steps.action: **Make it unique.** Do not reuse a password pattern from email, banking, work, school, or shopping accounts.
steps.expect: this exact password belongs to one account only.

steps.action: **Avoid personal clues.** Do not use birthdays, pet names, teams, addresses, lyrics, quotes, or keyboard paths.
steps.expect: someone who knows you could not guess the password.

steps.action: **Save before submitting if allowed.** Store the password in the manager entry with the correct site name and username.
steps.expect: the manager can fill or reveal it before you lose the form.

steps.action: **Submit and update the saved entry.** If the site forces symbols or length changes, update the manager entry to the exact accepted password.
steps.expect: the account accepts the password and the saved copy matches.

steps.action: **Add account recovery protection.** Turn on multi-factor authentication where available and update recovery email or phone.
steps.expect: a stolen password alone is not enough to sign in.

steps.action: **Remove temporary copies.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* deleting the only copy can lock you out, so verify the saved entry first.
steps.expect: sticky notes, screenshots, and clipboard copies are gone after the manager entry works.

recipes.verification: You can sign out and sign back in using the saved password, and that password is not used on any other account.

recipes.title: create a zip archive
recipes.name: create-a-zip-archive
recipes.goal: Compress one or more files or folders into a `.zip` archive for sharing or storage.

steps.action: **Select the items.** Click one item, or use `Ctrl+click` on Windows or `Command+click` on Mac to select multiple items.
steps.expect: every item to include is highlighted.

steps.action: **Create the archive.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: right-click and choose `Compress to ZIP file` or `Send to > Compressed (zipped) folder`; Mac: right-click or Control-click and choose `Compress`.
steps.expect: a new `.zip` file appears in the same folder.

steps.action: **Rename the archive.** Give the zip file a clear name and keep the `.zip` extension.
steps.expect: the archive has a useful filename.

steps.action: **Open to inspect contents.** Double-click the zip or preview its contents without extracting if the system supports it.
steps.expect: the expected files are inside.

recipes.verification: The `.zip` archive exists, opens successfully, and contains exactly the selected files or folders.

recipes.title: create an email folder
recipes.name: create-an-email-folder
recipes.goal: Create an email folder or label to organize related messages.

steps.action: **Open folder controls.** Find the folder, label, or mailbox list in your mail app.
steps.expect: existing folders or labels are visible.

steps.action: **Choose create.** Click or tap `New folder`, `Create label`, `Add mailbox`, or the plus button.
steps.expect: a naming dialog or text field appears.

steps.action: **Name the folder.** Enter a short, clear name.
steps.expect: the typed name appears without spelling errors.

steps.action: **Choose its location.** If asked, place it under the account or parent folder where you want it.
steps.expect: the location preview or parent folder is correct.

steps.action: **Save the folder.** Click or tap `Create`, `Save`, or `Done`.
steps.expect: the new folder or label appears in the folder list.

steps.action: **Move a test email if needed.** Drag or move one relevant message into the folder.
steps.expect: the message appears when the folder is opened.

recipes.verification: The new folder or label is visible in the mail app, and a moved test message appears inside it.

recipes.title: crop an image
recipes.name: crop-an-image
recipes.goal: Remove unwanted edges from an image while keeping the important subject.

steps.action: **Open the image.** Open the file in Photos, Preview, Paint, Gallery, or another image editor.
steps.expect: the image is visible.

steps.action: **Enter crop mode.** Choose `Edit`, `Crop`, or the crop icon.
steps.expect: crop handles or a crop frame appear.

steps.action: **Adjust the crop frame.** Drag the corners or edges around the area to keep.
steps.expect: unwanted edges fall outside the crop frame.

steps.action: **Use aspect ratio if needed.** Select a preset such as square, 4:3, 16:9, or original ratio when required.
steps.expect: the crop frame keeps that shape while resizing.

steps.action: **Apply the crop.** Click or tap `Apply`, `Done`, or the checkmark.
steps.expect: the image preview shows only the selected area.

steps.action: **Save the result.** Choose `Save a copy` or `Export` if you need to preserve the original.
steps.expect: the cropped image is saved.

recipes.verification: The saved image contains the intended subject and excludes the unwanted edges.

recipes.title: cut and paste text
recipes.name: cut-and-paste-text
recipes.goal: Selected text is moved from one location to another in the same document or text editor.

steps.action: **Select the text to move.** Drag across the text or use `Shift` with arrow keys.
steps.expect: only the text you want to move is highlighted.

steps.action: **Cut the selection.** Press `Ctrl+X` on Windows/Linux or `Command+X` on Mac, or choose Edit > Cut.
steps.expect: the selected text disappears from its original location.

steps.action: **Click the new location.** Place the cursor where the text should go.
steps.expect: the insertion cursor blinks at the target spot.

steps.action: **Paste the text.** Press `Ctrl+V` on Windows/Linux or `Command+V` on Mac, or choose Edit > Paste.
steps.expect: the moved text appears at the new location.

steps.action: **Repair surrounding punctuation.** Check spaces, commas, periods, and paragraph breaks around both locations.
steps.expect: the sentence or paragraph reads correctly after the move.

recipes.verification: The selected text no longer appears in its original location and appears once at the intended new location.

recipes.title: delete a file safely
recipes.name: delete-a-file-safely
recipes.goal: Send an unwanted file to Trash or Recycle Bin without permanently deleting the wrong item.

steps.action: **Select the file.** Click the file once and confirm its name, icon, and location.
steps.expect: only the intended file is highlighted.

steps.action: **Delete to recoverable storage.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Delete` or right-click and choose `Delete`; Mac: press `Command+Delete` or choose `File > Move to Trash`.
steps.expect: the file disappears from the folder.

steps.action: **Use confirmation carefully.** If a prompt appears, read the filename before choosing `Yes`, `Move to Trash`, or `Delete`.
steps.expect: the prompt closes and the file is moved to Trash or Recycle Bin.

steps.action: **Leave the bin intact briefly.** Do not empty Trash or Recycle Bin until you are sure the file is not needed.
steps.expect: the file can still be restored if necessary.

recipes.verification: The file no longer appears in its original folder and is recoverable from Trash or Recycle Bin unless the system explicitly warned otherwise.

recipes.title: delete your search and location history
recipes.name: delete-your-search-and-location-history
recipes.goal: Delete or reduce stored search and location history for an account and its devices while understanding what records may remain elsewhere.

steps.action: **Open the account activity page.** Go through the provider's official privacy, data, or activity controls while signed in.
steps.expect: you see categories such as web activity, search history, location history, or timeline.

steps.action: **Review what is being stored.** Check whether search, voice, app, map, and location activity are enabled.
steps.expect: each activity type shows on, off, paused, or auto-delete status.

steps.action: **Export first if needed.** If the history is needed for records, use the provider's download or export tool before deletion.
steps.expect: any wanted archive is saved before removal.

steps.action: **Delete the chosen activity.** [BRANCH: all time | date range | single item] choose the smallest deletion that matches your goal. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* deleted account activity may not be recoverable, so confirm the account and time range before deleting.
steps.expect: the page confirms deletion or removal.

steps.action: **Set auto-delete.** Choose a retention period such as 3, 18, or 36 months if the provider offers it.
steps.expect: future activity has an automatic deletion schedule.

steps.action: **Pause unwanted collection.** Turn off or pause search, web, app, or location history categories you do not want saved.
steps.expect: the account shows those categories as off or paused.

steps.action: **Clean per-device history.** On each phone or browser, clear local browser history, map searches, recent destinations, and app cache where appropriate.
steps.expect: the device no longer shows the deleted local searches or places.

steps.action: **Check signed-in devices.** Remove old devices and confirm sync settings so history does not reappear from another device.
steps.expect: only current devices remain connected.

steps.action: **Understand what remains.** Note that websites, employers, schools, mobile carriers, and internet providers may keep separate logs.
steps.expect: you know the deletion affects account and device history, not every external record.

recipes.verification: The account activity page shows the chosen search or location items deleted, future collection paused or auto-delete enabled as intended, and each checked device no longer displays the local history.

recipes.title: detect ai generated images
recipes.name: detect-ai-generated-images
recipes.goal: Assess whether an image may be AI-generated or manipulated by combining visual inspection, provenance checks, and source verification.

steps.action: **Save the context.** Record where you found the image, the account, caption, date, and any claims attached to it.
steps.expect: the image is tied to its original claim.

steps.action: **Inspect visible details.** Zoom in on hands, teeth, text, reflections, shadows, edges, repeated patterns, and background objects.
steps.expect: possible generation or editing artifacts are noted.

steps.action: **Check provenance.** Look for metadata, content credentials, watermarking, creator statements, or platform labels. [BRANCH: provenance present | provenance absent] verify present claims; treat absence as inconclusive.
steps.expect: you know whether origin evidence exists.

steps.action: **Reverse-search the image.** Use image search or search distinctive caption terms to find earlier versions and related posts.
steps.expect: you identify the earliest credible source you can find.

steps.action: **Compare against real-world facts.** Check whether the place, event, product, uniform, weather, or public figure appearance matches known records.
steps.expect: the image claim is supported, contradicted, or unresolved.

steps.action: **Use detectors cautiously.** If using an AI-image detector, run more than one and record the result as a weak signal, not proof.
steps.expect: detector output is not treated as a final verdict.

recipes.verification: Your conclusion includes visual evidence, source/provenance evidence, and an uncertainty label; if those are missing, the image is marked unverified rather than authentic or fake.

recipes.title: dictate a text message
recipes.name: dictate-a-text-message
recipes.goal: You can speak a text message, include punctuation, review the transcription, and send it only after confirming it says what you mean.

steps.action: **Enable dictation.** In keyboard settings, turn on dictation, voice typing, or speech input for your language.
steps.expect: a microphone button appears on the keyboard.

steps.action: **Open the conversation.** Choose the intended recipient before starting voice input.
steps.expect: the message field is active in the correct chat.

steps.action: **Start dictation.** Tap the microphone on the keyboard or in the message field.
steps.expect: the phone shows a listening indicator.

steps.action: **Speak in short phrases.** Say the message naturally, then say punctuation such as "comma," "period," or "question mark."
steps.expect: words and punctuation appear in the draft.

steps.action: **Pause to stop.** Stop speaking or tap the microphone again when the draft is complete.
steps.expect: the keyboard returns to normal editing mode.

steps.action: **Review before sending.** Read the full message, especially names, numbers, dates, and any sensitive wording.
steps.expect: mistakes are visible while the message is still unsent.

steps.action: **Fix errors manually.** [BRANCH: small typo | badly wrong] edit small errors by keyboard, or delete and redictate if the meaning changed.
steps.expect: the draft matches your intended message.

steps.action: **Send deliberately.** Tap Send only after the recipient and message are both correct.
steps.expect: the message appears in the conversation as sent.

recipes.verification: A dictated draft includes the intended words and punctuation, is reviewed before sending, and appears in the correct conversation after you tap Send.

recipes.title: digitize old photos
recipes.name: digitize-old-photos
recipes.goal: Create clear digital copies of printed photos, name and organize them, and back them up so the originals can be handled less often.

steps.action: **Sort photos into batches.** Group by album, year, event, person, or envelope before scanning.
steps.expect: each batch has a simple label you can use for filenames.

steps.action: **Clean the scanning surface.** Wipe scanner glass or phone camera lens with a microfiber cloth and remove dust from photos gently.
steps.expect: the glass or lens is clear and photos are flat.

steps.action: **Choose scan settings.** Use 300 dpi for normal sharing, 600 dpi for archiving small prints, and JPEG or TIFF depending on quality needs.
steps.expect: the first test scan is sharp at full-screen size.

steps.action: **Scan a small test batch.** Capture 3-5 photos and check crop, glare, color, and orientation before continuing.
steps.expect: the files look straight, evenly lit, and complete.

steps.action: **Scan the full batch.** Work in labeled batches and keep originals in order until each batch is verified.
steps.expect: every physical photo has a matching digital file.

steps.action: **Rename and organize files.** Use folder names like `1978-family-trip` and filenames with dates or sequence numbers when exact dates are unknown.
steps.expect: files sort in a useful order without relying on memory.

steps.action: **Back up the scans.** Copy the finished folders to cloud storage or an external drive in addition to the computer.
steps.expect: the same folders exist in at least two locations.

steps.action: **Return originals safely.** Put photos back into archival sleeves or their original album after digital copies are verified.
steps.expect: originals are protected and the digital files are easy to find.

recipes.verification: Each batch has matching digital files, sample images open clearly at full size, filenames or folders identify the batch, and at least one backup copy exists.

recipes.title: disable a browser extension
recipes.name: disable-a-browser-extension
recipes.goal: Turn off a browser extension temporarily without uninstalling it.

steps.action: **Open extension settings.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] open the browser menu and choose `Extensions`, `Add-ons and themes`, or `Settings` > `Extensions`.
steps.expect: a list of installed extensions appears.

steps.action: **Find the extension.** Use the extension name, icon, or search field if available.
steps.expect: the target extension is visible in the list.

steps.action: **Turn it off.** Toggle the extension off or clear its enable checkbox.
steps.expect: the extension shows disabled, off, or unchecked.

steps.action: **Reload the affected page.** Return to the web page and refresh it with `Ctrl+R` or `Command+R`.
steps.expect: the page runs without that extension active.

steps.action: **Re-enable if needed.** Return to the extensions list and toggle it back on when finished.
steps.expect: the extension becomes active again.

recipes.verification: The extension list shows the target extension disabled, and the affected page reloads with that extension inactive.

recipes.title: download a file from a link
recipes.name: download-a-file-from-a-link
recipes.goal: Download a file from a link and confirm it saved to the expected location.

steps.action: **Inspect the link.** Hover over the link or long-press if on a touch device.
steps.expect: the destination or file name appears.

steps.action: **Start the download.** Click the link, or right-click and choose `Save Link As`.
steps.expect: the browser starts a download or opens a save dialog.

steps.action: **Choose a folder if asked.** Select Downloads or another known folder and keep or edit the filename.
steps.expect: the save location and filename are visible before saving.

steps.action: **Wait for completion.** Watch the browser downloads button or shelf.
steps.expect: the download shows complete with no warning.

steps.action: **Open the containing folder.** Use `Show in folder`, `Show in Finder`, or the downloads list.
steps.expect: the file appears in the expected folder.

recipes.verification: The expected file exists in the chosen folder and the browser download list shows it completed successfully.

recipes.title: download your invoices and receipts
recipes.name: download-your-invoices-and-receipts
recipes.goal: Invoices and receipts are downloaded from accounts or email, named consistently, and stored where they can be found for returns, reimbursements, accounting, or taxes.

steps.action: **Identify where records live.** Check Account, Orders, Billing, Payments, Invoices, Receipts, Trips, or Statements.
steps.expect: you find a list of transactions or documents.

steps.action: **Set the date range and filters.** Filter by year, month, vendor, payment method, or status.
steps.expect: the list matches the period you need.

steps.action: **Open one record and inspect it.** Confirm it contains vendor name, date, amount, taxes, payment method, and invoice or receipt number.
steps.expect: the document is suitable for your purpose.

steps.action: **Use bulk export when available.** [BRANCH: bulk export | one-by-one download] Export CSV/PDF bundles for many records; download individual PDFs when bulk export is absent.
steps.expect: files appear in Downloads or the chosen folder.

steps.action: **Name files consistently.** Use a sortable pattern such as `2026-07-merchant-amount-purpose.pdf`.
steps.expect: filenames reveal date, source, and reason without opening each file.

steps.action: **Store in the right folder.** Move files into Tax, Reimbursements, Warranty, Project, or Household folders, not loose Downloads.
steps.expect: the folder contains the complete batch.

steps.action: **Check for missing receipts.** Compare the downloaded files against card, bank, app, or email transaction lists.
steps.expect: every needed expense has either a receipt or a note explaining the gap.

steps.action: **Back up the folder.** Ensure the folder syncs to your backup system or external drive.
steps.expect: the records are not only on one computer.

recipes.verification: The target folder contains named invoice or receipt files covering the needed date range, and a spot check confirms amounts match payment records.

recipes.title: duplicate a file
recipes.name: duplicate-a-file
recipes.goal: Make a copy of a file in the same folder so you can edit or rename it separately.

steps.action: **Select the file.** Click the file once.
steps.expect: the file is highlighted.

steps.action: **Duplicate it.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Ctrl+C` then `Ctrl+V`; Mac: press `Command+D` or choose `File > Duplicate`.
steps.expect: a second file appears in the same folder.

steps.action: **Rename the duplicate if needed.** Give the copy a clear name that distinguishes it from the original.
steps.expect: the duplicate has a unique filename.

steps.action: **Open the duplicate if needed.** Double-click the copy, not the original.
steps.expect: the duplicate opens and can be edited independently.

recipes.verification: The folder contains the original file and a separate duplicate with its own filename.

recipes.title: e sign a document
recipes.name: e-sign-a-document
recipes.goal: A document is electronically signed through a legitimate service, with all required signature blocks completed and a signed copy saved.

steps.action: **Verify the signing request.** Confirm the sender, subject, and service match what you expected, such as DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign, Dropbox Sign, or an organization's own portal.
steps.expect: the request appears in the official service or known account, not only in an email link.

steps.action: **Open from the official route.** Use the signing service's app, website, or the organization's portal when possible.
steps.expect: the browser address belongs to the signing provider or organization.

steps.action: **Read the full document first.** Use page thumbnails and search to inspect names, dates, amounts, obligations, renewal terms, and attachments.
steps.expect: you understand what the signature will authorize.

steps.action: **Check signer identity and role.** Make sure the document names you correctly and that you are signing as yourself, guardian, employee, officer, or authorized representative as intended.
steps.expect: the signer label and capacity match your authority.

steps.action: **Complete required fields in order.** Click each signature, initial, date, checkbox, and text field the service highlights.
steps.expect: every required block shows completed status and the next required field advances.

steps.action: **Pause at final review.** Look for missed initials, altered dates, blank pages, addenda, or payment authorizations.
steps.expect: the service reports no missing required fields and the document still matches what you agreed to sign.

steps.action: **Finish signing.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an e-signature can be legally binding like ink, so do not finish if terms, identity, or authority are wrong.
steps.expect: the service shows completed, signed, or sent to all parties.

steps.action: **Download the signed copy and certificate.** Save the signed PDF, and if offered, the audit trail or certificate of completion.
steps.expect: your folder contains the signed document with date and parties in the filename.

steps.action: **Confirm distribution.** Check that the completed document was sent to the requester or appears in the portal.
steps.expect: email or portal status confirms delivery.

recipes.verification: The signing service or portal shows completed status, and you possess a readable signed PDF plus any audit certificate or completion email.

recipes.title: eject a usb drive safely
recipes.name: eject-a-usb-drive-safely
recipes.goal: Safely disconnect a USB drive after the computer has finished reading from or writing to it.

steps.action: **Close drive files.** Close documents, media, installers, and folder windows that are using the USB drive.
steps.expect: no open app is actively using files from the drive.

steps.action: **Choose eject.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: click the system tray USB icon and choose `Eject`, or right-click the drive in File Explorer and choose `Eject`; Mac: click the eject button next to the drive in Finder or drag the drive icon to Trash/Eject.
steps.expect: the system starts unmounting the drive.

steps.action: **Wait for confirmation.** Watch for `Safe to Remove Hardware` on Windows or for the drive icon to disappear on Mac.
steps.expect: the operating system indicates the drive is no longer mounted.

steps.action: **Unplug the drive.** Pull the USB connector straight out without bending it.
steps.expect: the drive is physically disconnected.

recipes.verification: The drive icon disappears or the system says it is safe to remove, and the drive can be unplugged without warnings.

recipes.title: empty the recycle bin
recipes.name: empty-the-recycle-bin
recipes.goal: Permanently remove files already placed in Trash or Recycle Bin to free space.

steps.action: **Open the bin.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: double-click `Recycle Bin`; Mac: click `Trash` in the Dock.
steps.expect: deleted items are listed.

steps.action: **Review the contents.** Scan filenames, dates, and folders for anything you may need.
steps.expect: only unwanted files remain in the bin.

steps.action: **Restore mistakes first.** Right-click any needed item and choose `Restore` on Windows or `Put Back` on Mac.
steps.expect: needed items leave the bin before emptying.

steps.action: **Empty the bin.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: choose `Empty Recycle Bin`; Mac: choose `Finder > Empty Trash` or click `Empty`. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm that everything remaining can be permanently removed.
steps.expect: a permanent deletion confirmation appears.

steps.action: **Confirm deletion.** Choose `Yes`, `Empty Recycle Bin`, or `Empty Trash`.
steps.expect: the bin becomes empty.

recipes.verification: Trash or Recycle Bin opens empty, and available disk space has increased if large files were removed.

recipes.title: enter a formula in a spreadsheet
recipes.name: enter-a-formula-in-a-spreadsheet
recipes.goal: Enter a working formula in a spreadsheet cell and see the calculated result.

steps.action: **Select the result cell.** Click the empty cell where the answer should appear.
steps.expect: the cell border shows it is active.

steps.action: **Start the formula.** Type `=` followed by the formula, such as `=B2*C2` or `=SUM(B2:B10)`.
steps.expect: the formula text appears in the cell or formula bar.

steps.action: **Confirm the formula.** Press `Enter` or `Return`.
steps.expect: the cell shows the calculated result instead of the formula text.

steps.action: **Review the references.** Click the result cell and inspect the formula bar.
steps.expect: the formula bar still shows the formula beginning with `=`.

recipes.verification: The selected cell displays a calculated value, and the formula bar shows a formula beginning with `=` that references the intended cells.

recipes.title: export a document to pdf
recipes.name: export-a-document-to-pdf
recipes.goal: A document is saved as a PDF that preserves layout for sharing, uploading, or printing.

steps.action: **Review the document first.** Check title, page breaks, images, and final edits.
steps.expect: the document is ready to export.

steps.action: **Open export or download.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose File > Save As or File > Export > Create PDF/XPS; in Google Docs, choose File > Download > PDF Document.
steps.expect: PDF is available as an output format.

steps.action: **Choose the save location.** Select a folder and enter a clear file name ending in `.pdf`.
steps.expect: the save dialog shows the intended PDF name and location.

steps.action: **Save or download the PDF.** Click Save, Export, Publish, or Download.
steps.expect: a PDF file is created.

steps.action: **Open the PDF.** View the exported file in a PDF viewer.
steps.expect: the PDF opens without errors.

steps.action: **Inspect layout.** Check page count, headings, images, links, and any special characters.
steps.expect: the PDF matches the source document closely enough for its purpose.

recipes.verification: The PDF exists at the chosen location, opens successfully, and shows the expected content and page count.

recipes.title: export your data
recipes.name: export-your-data
recipes.goal: You hold a complete, openable copy of your data from an online service (email, photos, documents, social account), extracted in a portable format, verified as readable, and stored somewhere durable.

steps.action: **Find the account's export tool.** Look under Settings for "Export", "Download your data", "Takeout", or "Data & privacy". Most large platforms have a dedicated page.
steps.expect: a page listing which data categories you can include.

steps.action: **Select scope and format deliberately.** Include what you actually want; deselect noise. Prefer open formats when offered (MBOX for mail, JSON or CSV for records, original-resolution for photos).
steps.expect: a summary showing selected categories and a chosen file type.

steps.action: **Choose delivery and size chunking.** [BRANCH: download link by email | deliver to a linked cloud drive] Set a per-file split (2 GB is a safe default) so a single corrupt part does not sink the whole archive.
steps.expect: a confirmation that the export job has started.

steps.action: **Wait for the job to finish.** Exports are queued and can take minutes to days depending on volume.
steps.expect: an email or on-page notice that the archive is ready, usually with a link that expires (often 7 days).

steps.action: **Download every part before the link expires.** Verify each file's size matches what the page claims; a truncated download is the most common silent failure.
steps.expect: all parts on disk, sizes matching, no browser "failed" entries.

steps.action: **Verify the archive opens.** Unzip it and open a sample from each category: a few emails, some photos at full resolution, one document. Do not trust an unopened zip.
steps.expect: sample files open correctly and look complete.

steps.action: **Store it safely and record what it is.** Move the verified archive to your backup destination; encrypt it if it contains personal data. Name the folder with the service and date.
steps.expect: archive filed, dated, and included in your backup rotation.

recipes.verification: A dated archive of the selected data sits in your backup location, every part downloaded at full size, and you have personally opened a sample from each category and confirmed it is readable outside the original service.

recipes.title: fact check with ai
recipes.name: fact-check-with-ai
recipes.goal: Use AI to organize a fact-check while independently confirming important claims with reliable sources.

steps.action: **Extract checkable claims.** Ask the AI to list specific factual claims, dates, numbers, quotes, and named entities separately from opinions.
steps.expect: you have a numbered claim list.

steps.action: **Rank claim risk.** Mark claims that affect health, safety, law, finances, reputation, or public affairs as high priority.
steps.expect: the riskiest claims are checked first.

steps.action: **Request source leads.** Ask for likely primary sources, official records, papers, or reputable reporting, and require the AI to say when it is uncertain.
steps.expect: you have search targets, not a final verdict.

steps.action: **Verify outside the model.** Open the cited or suggested sources yourself and compare the exact claim against the source text. [BRANCH: primary source found | only commentary found] use primary sources when available; otherwise note the lower confidence.
steps.expect: each important claim has evidence, contradiction, or unknown status.

steps.action: **Check dates and context.** Confirm publication dates, event dates, geographic scope, and whether a quote or statistic is being reused out of context.
steps.expect: stale or misframed claims are identified.

steps.action: **Record a verdict.** Label each claim true, false, misleading, unsupported, or needs expert review, with a short reason.
steps.expect: the fact-check is auditable.

recipes.verification: Every high-priority claim has a recorded verdict and at least one independently opened source or an explicit unsupported status.

recipes.title: factory reset a device safely
recipes.name: factory-reset-a-device-safely
recipes.goal: A device is wiped back to factory state with your data verifiably gone, your accounts deregistered so it is not locked to you (or to a previous owner), ready to sell, recycle, or hand on without leaking your information.

steps.action: **Back up first and verify the backup opens.** Confirm your files, photos, and app data are safely copied and you have opened a sample. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the reset erases local data with no undo; do not proceed on an unverified backup.
steps.expect: a verified backup exists off the device.

steps.action: **Deregister and sign out of accounts.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* leaving activation lock on (Find My / Google account / Samsung account) can render the wiped device unusable to the next owner. Turn off Find My, then sign out of the platform account and any DRM/store accounts.
steps.expect: the device no longer shows a linked owner account or activation lock.

steps.action: **Remove tied hardware and licenses.** Unpair watches and accessories, deauthorize the machine from media/software licenses that count device slots, and note anything using device-bound authentication.
steps.expect: paired devices dropped; license count freed.

steps.action: **Remove physical media and SIM.** Take out the SIM and any memory card so they do not leave with the device.
steps.expect: SIM and cards in your hand, slots empty.

steps.action: **Confirm encryption is on, then reset.** Modern phones and laptops encrypt storage by default, which is what makes a reset actually unrecoverable. Verify encryption is enabled, then run the factory reset / erase-all-content from settings.
steps.expect: a warning listing what will be erased, then the device reboots into a wipe.

steps.action: **Let the wipe finish untouched.** Do not interrupt power or force-restart during the erase.
steps.expect: the device boots to the initial "welcome / set up" screen, as if new.

steps.action: **Verify the clean state.** Walk to (or just short of) the setup screen and confirm no account is pre-filled, no data or apps remain, and no activation lock prompts for a previous owner's credentials.
steps.expect: a genuinely empty device with no trace of your accounts.

recipes.verification: The device boots to a factory setup screen with no accounts pre-filled, no activation or previous-owner lock, no residual data or apps, SIM and cards removed, and every account that was tied to it has been signed out and deregistered. Your verified backup holds everything you needed to keep.

recipes.title: fill out an online form
recipes.name: fill-out-an-online-form
recipes.goal: An online form is completed accurately, saved or submitted once, and confirmed with a receipt, reference number, or on-screen success message.

steps.action: **Confirm the form source.** Open the form from the organization's official website, app, or message center, not from an ad or unsolicited link.
steps.expect: the address bar shows the expected domain and a lock icon.

steps.action: **Scan the whole form before typing.** Note required fields, file uploads, payment sections, and whether the form has multiple pages.
steps.expect: you know what information is missing before you start entering data.

steps.action: **Enter required fields in the requested format.** Match examples exactly for dates, phone numbers, postal codes, currency, and ID numbers.
steps.expect: required fields no longer show red outlines or "invalid format" messages.

steps.action: **Use save-as-you-go when available.** Click Save, Save draft, or Continue after each page, especially before uploads or long text fields.
steps.expect: the page shows a saved timestamp, draft ID, or the next page loads without losing prior entries.

steps.action: **Upload or attach only the requested files.** Choose the correct field for each document and wait until each upload finishes before moving on.
steps.expect: each attachment shows its filename, size, and a completed status.

steps.action: **Review the summary page line by line.** Compare names, dates, amounts, addresses, uploaded filenames, and contact details against your source documents.
steps.expect: every item matches your records, or the edit link takes you back to fix it.

steps.action: **Submit only when the summary is correct.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some submissions create legal declarations, applications, orders, or payments, so confirm accuracy before pressing Submit.
steps.expect: the site stops editing mode and shows a confirmation screen.

steps.action: **Save proof of submission.** Download the receipt, print to PDF, or screenshot the confirmation with date, time, and reference number visible.
steps.expect: you have a local copy named for the organization and date.

recipes.verification: The form has a confirmation page, receipt, email, or account message showing the submitted date, reference number, and the final data or attached filenames.

recipes.title: filter a spreadsheet
recipes.name: filter-a-spreadsheet
recipes.goal: Show only spreadsheet rows that match a chosen condition without deleting the other rows.

steps.action: **Select the table.** Click inside the data range.
steps.expect: a cell in the table is active.

steps.action: **Turn on filters.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Data > Filter`; Google Sheets: choose `Data > Create a filter`.
steps.expect: filter arrows or funnel icons appear in the header row.

steps.action: **Open the target column filter.** Click the filter icon in the column header.
steps.expect: a menu with sort and filter options opens.

steps.action: **Choose the condition.** Select values to show, or use a condition such as `Text contains` or `Greater than`.
steps.expect: the menu shows the intended filter rule.

steps.action: **Apply the filter.** Click `OK` or confirm the menu.
steps.expect: nonmatching rows are hidden and row numbers may skip.

recipes.verification: Filter icons are visible, at least one row remains visible, hidden rows are not deleted, and every visible row matches the selected condition.

recipes.title: find a lost phone
recipes.name: find-a-lost-phone
recipes.goal: Locate, secure, or wipe a missing phone while reducing the chance of account or SIM misuse.

steps.action: **Act fast.** Start before the battery dies or the phone is powered off.
steps.expect: location tools still have the best chance to contact the phone.

steps.action: **Open the official find-my-device site.** [BRANCH: iPhone | Android] use iCloud Find Devices for iPhone or Google Find My Device for Android.
steps.expect: your account shows a device list.

steps.action: **Select the missing phone.** Choose the exact model or device name, not an old phone or tablet.
steps.expect: the map, battery, and last-seen time belong to the missing phone.

steps.action: **Ring it if the location is safe and nearby.** Use Play Sound or Ring when it may be in a room, car, bag, or couch.
steps.expect: the phone rings even if it was on silent, if online and powered.

steps.action: **Lock it if it is not immediately in reach.** Use Lost Mode, Secure Device, or Lock with a contact message that does not reveal your home address.
steps.expect: the screen requires the passcode and can show a safe callback number.

steps.action: **Use the map without confronting thieves.** If the phone appears at an unfamiliar address, record the location and time.
steps.expect: you have evidence without putting yourself in danger.

steps.action: **Report theft when appropriate.** Contact local police or venue security with serial number, IMEI, last location, and screenshots.
steps.expect: the report has identifiers that distinguish your phone.
