steps.action: **Suspend the SIM or eSIM.** Call the carrier or use its account portal to block calls, texts, and number-porting misuse.
steps.expect: the line cannot be used for new charges or SMS codes.

steps.action: **Erase only when recovery is unlikely or data risk is high.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* remote erase deletes local data and may limit future tracking; confirm backups and selected device first.
steps.expect: the account reports erase pending or completed.

steps.action: **Change critical passwords.** Prioritize email, banking, password manager, and account recovery methods if the phone was unlocked or stolen.
steps.expect: sessions and recovery access are safer.

recipes.verification: The missing phone is either found in hand, locked with tracking evidence saved, or erased after the SIM and critical accounts are secured.

recipes.title: find and replace text
recipes.name: find-and-replace-text
recipes.goal: One word, phrase, or pattern is located and replaced with the intended text in a document.

steps.action: **Open find and replace.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, press `Ctrl+H` or `Command+Shift+H`; in Google Docs, choose Edit > Find and replace or press `Ctrl+H` on Windows/ChromeOS.
steps.expect: find and replace fields are visible.

steps.action: **Enter the text to find.** Type the current word or phrase exactly as it appears.
steps.expect: matching instances are highlighted or counted.

steps.action: **Enter the replacement.** Type the new word or phrase in the replace field.
steps.expect: both find and replacement values are visible for review.

steps.action: **Review one match.** Use Find Next, Previous, or the match arrows before replacing all.
steps.expect: the first intended occurrence is selected.

steps.action: **Replace deliberately.** Click Replace for one occurrence or Replace All only when every match should change.
steps.expect: the selected match or all matches update.

steps.action: **Scan the changed areas.** Search for the old text again and read nearby sentences.
steps.expect: intended replacements are present and unintended wording is absent.

recipes.verification: The old text is absent where it should be changed, and each replacement reads correctly in context.

recipes.title: find text on a page
recipes.name: find-text-on-a-page
recipes.goal: Find a word or phrase on the currently open web page.

steps.action: **Open page find.** Press `Ctrl+F` on Windows/Linux or `Command+F` on Mac.
steps.expect: a small Find box appears in the browser.

steps.action: **Type the target text.** Enter the word or phrase exactly enough to identify it.
steps.expect: matching text is highlighted on the page and the match count updates.

steps.action: **Move between matches.** Press `Enter` for the next match or `Shift+Enter` for the previous match.
steps.expect: the highlight moves to another occurrence.

steps.action: **Close find.** Press `Esc` or click the close button on the Find box.
steps.expect: the Find box closes and the page remains at the selected match.

recipes.verification: The browser highlights at least one matching occurrence, or the Find box shows zero matches for the exact search text.

recipes.title: find your wifi password
recipes.name: find-your-wifi-password
recipes.goal: You find the password for a Wi-Fi network you are authorized to use, either from the router, a saved device, or the router admin page.

steps.action: **Check the router label.** Look for Wi-Fi Password, Network Key, WPA Key, or Wireless Key, separate from Admin Password.
steps.expect: a printed default network name and password are visible.

steps.action: **Confirm the network name.** Match the SSID on the label to the Wi-Fi network you want.
steps.expect: the name matches exactly or you know the password was changed.

steps.action: **Reveal a saved password on Windows.** Open known network properties or Control Panel wireless status, then show security key after approving admin prompts.
steps.expect: Windows displays the saved Wi-Fi password.

steps.action: **Reveal a saved password on macOS.** Use System Settings Wi-Fi details or Keychain Access, authenticate, and show the saved password.
steps.expect: macOS displays the saved network password.

steps.action: **Reveal or share on mobile.** [BRANCH: iPhone/iPad | Android] iPhone can show saved passwords in Wi-Fi details or share to nearby Apple devices. Android often shows a QR code or text password after authentication.
steps.expect: the phone shows or shares the credential.

steps.action: **Check the router admin page.** Log in to the router app or web page and open wireless settings.
steps.expect: the current Wi-Fi password or a masked field with reveal option appears.

steps.action: **Record it securely.** Save the password in a password manager or private household note, not a public message thread.
steps.expect: you can retrieve it later without exposing it broadly.

steps.action: **Connect the new device.** Enter the password exactly, watching capitalization and similar characters.
steps.expect: the new device joins the intended network.

recipes.verification: The target device joins the intended Wi-Fi network using the found password and loads a normal website.

recipes.title: fix a printer paper jam
recipes.name: fix-a-printer-paper-jam
recipes.goal: The jammed paper is removed without tearing rollers or sensors, and the printer is reset to print normally.

steps.action: **Stop the print job.** Cancel the job from the computer or phone before touching the printer.
steps.expect: the queue stops sending new pages.

steps.action: **Power off and unplug.** Turn the printer off, then unplug power so rollers cannot start while your hands are inside.
steps.expect: the display and status lights go dark.

steps.action: **Open the designed access points.** Open the paper tray, rear door, duplexer, cartridge door, or automatic document feeder cover, using latches rather than prying panels.
steps.expect: the paper path is visible from at least one side.

steps.action: **Pull paper with the paper path.** Grip the largest visible part of the sheet with both hands and pull slowly in the direction paper normally travels, not backward against the rollers.
steps.expect: the sheet slides out in one piece or exposes the next safe grip point.

steps.action: **Remove loose scraps.** Use a flashlight to check corners, rollers, the rear door, and the output slot for torn pieces.
steps.expect: no scraps, labels, staples, or curled corners remain.

steps.action: **Check the carriage path.** [BRANCH: inkjet | laser] Inkjet: slide the printhead carriage gently only if the manual allows it. Laser: leave hot fuser areas alone until cool.
steps.expect: no paper blocks the moving path.

steps.action: **Reload paper flat.** Remove wrinkled sheets, square the stack, set guides snugly, and keep below the fill line.
steps.expect: the tray feeds one clean stack without bowed paper.

steps.action: **Close and reset.** Close all covers, plug in, power on, and follow any on-screen clear-jam prompt.
steps.expect: the jam message clears or changes to a specific cover or tray warning.

steps.action: **Print one test page.** Send a simple one-page print before resuming the full job.
steps.expect: one page feeds and exits without skewing or stopping.

recipes.verification: The printer completes a one-page test print with no jam, skew, grinding noise, or leftover jam message.

recipes.title: flag an important email
recipes.name: flag-an-important-email
recipes.goal: Mark an email as important so it is easier to find or follow up later.

steps.action: **Open or select the email.** Click, tap, or checkbox the message you want to mark.
steps.expect: the message is highlighted or open.

steps.action: **Find the marker control.** Look for a flag, star, pin, importance marker, or more-options menu.
steps.expect: the marking control is visible.

steps.action: **Apply the marker.** Click or tap the flag, star, or equivalent action.
steps.expect: the message shows the selected marker.

steps.action: **Confirm follow-up visibility.** Open the flagged, starred, important, or pinned view if your app has one.
steps.expect: the marked email appears in that view.

recipes.verification: The email displays a flag, star, pin, or importance marker and appears in the corresponding filtered view.

recipes.title: force quit a frozen app
recipes.name: force-quit-a-frozen-app
recipes.goal: A frozen app is closed without restarting the whole device unless the system itself is unresponsive.

steps.action: **Wait briefly.** Give the app 30 to 60 seconds if it froze during saving, printing, syncing, or exporting.
steps.expect: either it recovers or stays clearly frozen.

steps.action: **Try the normal quit path.** Use the app menu, close button, or back gesture once.
steps.expect: the app closes or remains stuck without responding.

steps.action: **Open the force-quit tool.** [BRANCH: Windows | macOS | iPhone/iPad | Android] Windows: Ctrl+Shift+Esc. macOS: Option+Command+Esc. iPhone/iPad: open the app switcher. Android: open Recents or App info.
steps.expect: a list of running apps appears.

steps.action: **Select the frozen app.** Choose only the app that is not responding, not system services or unrelated background tasks.
steps.expect: the target app is highlighted or shown in app details.

steps.action: **Force close it.** Use End task, Force Quit, swipe up, or Force stop. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* unsaved changes in that app can be lost, so confirm no visible save is still progressing.
steps.expect: the app disappears or its process ends.

steps.action: **Relaunch the app.** Open it again from the launcher, taskbar, dock, or home screen.
steps.expect: the app starts fresh, sometimes with a recovery prompt.

steps.action: **Recover available work.** Accept document recovery, reopen recent files, or check autosave/cloud history.
steps.expect: the newest available saved version is visible.

steps.action: **Escalate only if the device is frozen.** If keyboard, pointer, touch, and system controls do not respond, restart the device using the normal power menu or hardware restart recipe.
steps.expect: the device, not just the app, restarts.

recipes.verification: The frozen app is closed, relaunches to a usable state, and the device responds normally without repeated hangs.

recipes.title: format cells as currency
recipes.name: format-cells-as-currency
recipes.goal: Display selected spreadsheet numbers as currency.

steps.action: **Select the amount cells.** Drag across the cells that should show currency.
steps.expect: all intended amount cells are highlighted.

steps.action: **Apply currency format.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Home > Number Format > Currency`; Google Sheets: choose `Format > Number > Currency`.
steps.expect: the selected numbers display with a currency symbol and decimal places.

steps.action: **Adjust the symbol if needed.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Home > Number Format > More Number Formats`; Google Sheets: choose `Format > Number > Custom currency`.
steps.expect: the selected cells use the intended currency symbol.

steps.action: **Check one formula cell.** Click a formatted cell and inspect the formula bar.
steps.expect: the underlying value remains numeric, without a typed currency symbol in the formula bar.

recipes.verification: The selected cells display the intended currency symbol, and calculations still treat the values as numbers.

recipes.title: free up cloud storage
recipes.name: free-up-cloud-storage
recipes.goal: Your cloud storage has usable free space again because the largest files, backups, photos, and trash were reviewed instead of blindly upgraded.

steps.action: **Open storage management.** Go to the provider's storage page for iCloud, Google, Microsoft, Dropbox, or your service.
steps.expect: a usage breakdown appears.

steps.action: **Find the largest categories.** Sort by size or review storage by photos, drive files, mail, backups, and shared items.
steps.expect: one or two categories explain most usage.

steps.action: **Review large files first.** Download, move, or delete videos, archives, duplicate exports, and installers you no longer need.
steps.expect: selected large items are removed or moved.

steps.action: **Check photos and videos.** Delete obvious duplicates and long videos, or move originals to another backed-up location.
steps.expect: photo storage estimate drops or queued deletes appear.

steps.action: **Review device backups.** Remove backups for old phones, tablets, or computers you no longer own.
steps.expect: backup storage no longer includes obsolete devices.

steps.action: **Empty trash and recently deleted.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the selected trash items are disposable before permanently deleting them.
steps.expect: storage is actually released after trash clears.

steps.action: **Account for shared albums.** [BRANCH: owner | viewer] if you own shared items they may count against you; if you only view them they may not.
steps.expect: you know which shared content affects your quota.

steps.action: **Decide prune or upgrade.** If needed files still exceed the plan, compare the monthly cost of upgrading with the time cost of ongoing pruning.
steps.expect: you choose a sustainable storage plan.

recipes.verification: The storage dashboard shows enough free space for expected uploads and backups, with trash or recently deleted emptied only for confirmed disposable items.

recipes.title: free up storage space
recipes.name: free-up-storage-space
recipes.goal: A phone or computer that is "storage full" has meaningful free space again, reclaimed by finding the actual large consumers and removing or offloading them, without deleting anything you cannot get back.

steps.action: **Open the storage breakdown and read it before deleting anything.** The settings screen ranks what is using space: apps, photos, messages, system, "other".
steps.expect: a sorted list showing the top few consumers, not a single "full" number.

steps.action: **Identify the real hogs.** Usually it is photos/videos, one or two large apps (games, streaming with downloads), and message attachments. Sort by size and target the top of the list; ignore the long tail of tiny apps.
steps.expect: two or three items that together account for most of the used space.

steps.action: **Offload photos and videos (the usual winner).** Turn on cloud photo sync (iCloud Photos "Optimize Storage" / Google Photos backup), confirm it has finished uploading, then let it store full-resolution copies in the cloud and keep smaller ones on device.
steps.expect: the cloud shows your library backed up, and the on-device photo storage figure drops.

steps.action: **Clear app caches, not app data.** Offload or clear the cache of the biggest apps. iPhone: "Offload App" keeps your documents and data while removing the app binary. Android: Storage > Clear cache (not Clear data).
steps.expect: space freed while your logins, saved games, and files remain intact.

steps.action: **Remove downloaded media you can re-download.** Offline movies, podcasts, streamed music, and map areas re-download anytime. Delete these first; they are the safest wins.
steps.expect: large media entries shrink; the content is still available to stream later.

steps.action: **Clear message attachments.** Old photos and videos in chat threads pile up. Review large attachments (iPhone: iPhone Storage > Messages > Review Large Attachments) and delete the bulky ones.
steps.expect: the Messages storage figure drops noticeably.

steps.action: **Empty the trash / recently-deleted.** Deleting photos or files often just moves them to a "Recently Deleted" bin that still counts. Empty it to actually reclaim the space.
steps.expect: the freed space finally appears in the available figure.

steps.action: **Re-check the free space.** Return to the storage screen.
steps.expect: available space has risen by a clear amount and the device is no longer at the full threshold.

recipes.verification: The storage screen shows a clear increase in available space, the top consumers were addressed deliberately, and nothing irreplaceable was deleted: photos are confirmed in a backup, and only re-downloadable or cache data was removed.

recipes.title: freeze a header row
recipes.name: freeze-a-header-row
recipes.goal: Keep the header row visible while scrolling through a spreadsheet.

steps.action: **Identify the header row.** Scroll to the top of the sheet and confirm which row contains labels.
steps.expect: the header row is visible.

steps.action: **Freeze the header.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `View > Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row`; Google Sheets: choose `View > Freeze > 1 row`.
steps.expect: a freeze line appears below the header row.

steps.action: **Test the scroll.** Scroll down several rows.
steps.expect: the header row stays visible at the top of the grid.

recipes.verification: After scrolling down, the intended header row remains visible above the moving data rows.

recipes.title: insert a hyperlink
recipes.name: insert-a-hyperlink
recipes.goal: Selected text becomes a clickable hyperlink to the intended web page, email address, or document location.

steps.action: **Select the link text.** Highlight the word or phrase readers should click.
steps.expect: the intended display text is highlighted.

steps.action: **Open the link dialog.** Press `Ctrl+K` on Windows/Linux or `Command+K` on Mac, or choose Insert > Link.
steps.expect: a link box or dialog appears.

steps.action: **Enter the destination.** Paste the full URL, email address, or document target into the link field.
steps.expect: the destination appears in the link field.

steps.action: **Apply the link.** Click Apply, OK, or press `Enter`.
steps.expect: the selected text changes to link styling, usually blue and underlined.

steps.action: **Test the link.** Hold `Ctrl` or `Command` if required and click the linked text.
steps.expect: the intended page, email draft, or target opens.

recipes.verification: The selected text is clickable and opens the intended destination when tested.

recipes.title: insert a page break
recipes.name: insert-a-page-break
recipes.goal: Text after the cursor starts on a new page using a real page break.

steps.action: **Place the cursor.** Click immediately before the content that should start on the next page.
steps.expect: the insertion cursor appears at the break point.

steps.action: **Insert the page break.** Press `Ctrl+Enter` on Windows/Linux or `Command+Enter` on Mac, or choose Insert > Break > Page Break.
steps.expect: the following content moves to the top of the next page.

steps.action: **Show breaks if needed.** Turn on paragraph marks or non-printing characters if the break is hard to see.
steps.expect: a page break marker is visible in the document.

steps.action: **Review nearby pages.** Check the end of the previous page and the start of the next page.
steps.expect: no extra blank paragraphs or unwanted spacing appear.

recipes.verification: The intended content starts at the top of the next page because of a page break, not repeated blank lines.

recipes.title: insert a table in a document
recipes.name: insert-a-table-in-a-document
recipes.goal: A table with the needed number of rows and columns is inserted into a document.

steps.action: **Place the cursor.** Click where the table should appear in the document.
steps.expect: the insertion cursor blinks at the table location.

steps.action: **Open the table menu.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose Insert > Table; in Google Docs, choose Insert > Table.
steps.expect: a grid or table size menu appears.

steps.action: **Choose the table size.** Drag or select the number of columns and rows needed.
steps.expect: a blank table appears in the document.

steps.action: **Enter headers.** Type column labels in the first row if the table has categories.
steps.expect: the top row identifies what each column contains.

steps.action: **Fill cells.** Click or press `Tab` to move through cells and enter content.
steps.expect: each cell contains the intended text or data.

steps.action: **Adjust fit.** Drag column borders or use table layout controls so text is readable.
steps.expect: columns and rows fit the content without awkward clipping.

recipes.verification: The table appears at the intended location with the needed rows, columns, headers, and readable cell content.

recipes.title: insert an image into a document
recipes.name: insert-an-image-into-a-document
recipes.goal: An image is placed into a document at the intended location with readable size and layout.

steps.action: **Place the cursor.** Click where the image should appear.
steps.expect: the insertion cursor marks the image location.

steps.action: **Open image insertion.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose Insert > Pictures; in Google Docs, choose Insert > Image.
steps.expect: source options for the image appear.

steps.action: **Choose the image.** Select the file, upload source, or cloud image and confirm insertion.
steps.expect: the image appears in the document.

steps.action: **Resize proportionally.** Drag a corner handle, not a side handle, to fit the image.
steps.expect: the image changes size without looking stretched.

steps.action: **Set wrapping if needed.** Choose inline, square, tight, or break text depending on the layout.
steps.expect: surrounding text flows the way you intend.

steps.action: **Add alt text if the document will be shared.** Use the image options or context menu to describe the image briefly.
steps.expect: the image has a short text description for accessibility.

recipes.verification: The image appears at the intended location, is not distorted, and does not obscure nearby text.

recipes.title: install an application
recipes.name: install-an-application
recipes.goal: A named application is installed from a trustworthy source and launches successfully on your device.

steps.action: **Identify the official source.** [BRANCH: OS app store | vendor website | package manager] Prefer the platform store or package manager; for direct downloads, navigate to the vendor's site yourself rather than clicking ads or search-ad results.
steps.expect: publisher name on the store page / site domain matches the real vendor.

steps.action: **Check compatibility and cost.** OS version, architecture, disk space, license (free / trial / subscription).
steps.expect: your device meets stated requirements; the price is what you expect.

steps.action: **Download or begin install.** Store: click Install/Get. Website: download the installer for your OS. Package manager: run the install command.
steps.expect: download completes from the expected domain; file size roughly matches the site's stated size.

steps.action: **Run the installer.** Approve the OS's confirmation prompt only if the publisher shown matches step 1. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* granting an installer admin rights executes arbitrary code — abort if the publisher name is unexpected or unsigned.
steps.expect: an install wizard or progress bar; decline any bundled "offers"/toolbars.

steps.action: **Complete setup choices.** Default install location is usually right; uncheck auto-start unless wanted.
steps.expect: "installation complete."

steps.action: **Launch the application.**
steps.expect: the app opens to its first-run screen without errors.

steps.action: **Clean up.** Delete the downloaded installer file.
steps.expect: installer removed; app still launches from the applications menu.

recipes.verification: The application launches from the system's normal launcher (not the installer), shows the expected version in its About screen, and the installer artifact is deleted.

recipes.title: join an online meeting
recipes.name: join-an-online-meeting
recipes.goal: Join an online meeting with working audio and video, use basic etiquette, and recover quickly from common connection problems.

steps.action: **Open the invitation early.** Click the meeting link or copy the meeting ID from the calendar invite 5 to 10 minutes before start.
steps.expect: a browser page or meeting app opens.

steps.action: **Choose app or browser.** [BRANCH: installed app | browser join] Use the app for best features or browser if installation is blocked.
steps.expect: the meeting lobby or preview screen appears.

steps.action: **Enter your display name.** Use the name attendees will recognize.
steps.expect: the preview shows the correct participant name.

steps.action: **Test audio output.** Play the test sound or check device speaker selection.
steps.expect: you hear the test sound clearly.

steps.action: **Test microphone and camera.** Speak and watch the level meter, then preview the camera if needed.
steps.expect: the meter moves and video shows the intended view.

steps.action: **Join muted unless speaking immediately.** Turn microphone off before entering if you are not the presenter.
steps.expect: the meeting controls show the microphone muted.

steps.action: **Use meeting etiquette.** Keep background noise low, unmute only to talk, and use chat or raise-hand controls when appropriate.
steps.expect: others can hear you only when intended.

steps.action: **Share screen only when ready.** Close private windows, choose the specific window or tab, then start sharing.
steps.expect: the meeting shows a screen-share indicator and the intended content only.

steps.action: **Leave correctly.** Click Leave or End, then close any browser tab if needed.
steps.expect: your name no longer appears in the meeting.

recipes.verification: You are listed in the meeting, can hear others, can be heard when unmuted, and can leave without the meeting app staying active.

recipes.title: make a bulleted list
recipes.name: make-a-bulleted-list
recipes.goal: Separate lines of text are formatted as a bulleted list.

steps.action: **Select existing items or place the cursor.** Highlight the lines to convert, or click where a new list should start.
steps.expect: the target lines are selected or the cursor is ready.

steps.action: **Turn on bullets.** Click the Bullets button or choose Format > Bullets and numbering > Bulleted list.
steps.expect: each selected line starts with a bullet, or a new bullet appears.

steps.action: **Type list items.** Type an item and press `Enter` for the next bullet.
steps.expect: a new bullet appears on the next line.

steps.action: **End the list.** Press `Enter` on a blank bullet line, or turn the Bullets button off.
steps.expect: the cursor returns to normal paragraph text.

steps.action: **Adjust item levels if needed.** Press `Tab` to indent an item or `Shift+Tab` to move it back.
steps.expect: the bullet level changes without losing the item text.

recipes.verification: Each intended item appears as its own bullet, and normal text resumes after the list.

recipes.title: make a simple chart
recipes.name: make-a-simple-chart
recipes.goal: Create a basic chart from labeled spreadsheet data.

steps.action: **Select the chart data.** Drag across the labels and numbers, including headers if present.
steps.expect: the intended data range is highlighted.

steps.action: **Insert a chart.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Insert > Recommended Charts` or a chart type; Google Sheets: choose `Insert > Chart`.
steps.expect: a chart appears on or near the sheet.

steps.action: **Choose the chart type.** Pick a column, bar, line, or pie chart that matches the data.
steps.expect: the chart updates to the selected type.

steps.action: **Set the title.** Click the chart title or use chart settings to enter a clear title.
steps.expect: the chart title describes what the numbers show.

steps.action: **Check the axes or legend.** Confirm labels and values are assigned correctly.
steps.expect: category labels and numeric scale or legend match the selected data.

recipes.verification: The chart is visible, uses the intended data range, has a descriptive title, and displays the selected labels and numeric values correctly.

recipes.title: make text bold or italic
recipes.name: make-text-bold-or-italic
recipes.goal: Selected text is formatted as bold, italic, or both.

steps.action: **Select the text.** Highlight the word, sentence, or paragraph to format.
steps.expect: the intended text is highlighted.

steps.action: **Apply bold if needed.** Press `Ctrl+B` on Windows/Linux or `Command+B` on Mac, or click the Bold `B` button.
steps.expect: the selected text appears heavier.

steps.action: **Apply italic if needed.** Press `Ctrl+I` on Windows/Linux or `Command+I` on Mac, or click the Italic `I` button.
steps.expect: the selected text appears slanted.

steps.action: **Click away or move the cursor.** Place the cursor where you want to keep typing.
steps.expect: the formatted text remains bold, italic, or both.

recipes.verification: Only the intended text displays with bold, italic, or both, and surrounding text keeps its prior style.

recipes.title: manage notifications
recipes.name: manage-notifications
recipes.goal: Your phone interrupts you only for things that actually deserve an interruption. Every app's notifications are triaged into keep, silence, or off; a priority/focus mode protects your attention when needed; and the badge count reflects real, unread items rather than noise.

steps.action: **Open the per-app notification list.** Both platforms list every app that can notify you, often with how many you got recently.
steps.expect: a long list, most of which you never consciously chose to enable.

steps.action: **Triage each app into three buckets.** For every app decide: interrupt me (messages from people, calls, calendar, security alerts), silent/no-buzz (news, social, shopping: allowed but quiet), or off entirely (games, promos, "we miss you" apps).
steps.expect: each app assigned; the interrupt bucket is short, a handful at most.

steps.action: **Turn off the noise.** For the "off" bucket, disable Allow Notifications. For the "silent" bucket, keep them delivered to the notification list but turn off sound, vibration, and lock-screen banners.
steps.expect: those apps stop making sound or popping up, while still logging quietly if you left them silent.

steps.action: **Shape the important ones.** For the interrupt bucket, enable sound and banners, and on iPhone consider marking key ones Time Sensitive so they cut through Focus modes.
steps.expect: only your short interrupt list can make noise or vibrate.

steps.action: **Kill badge dots that are not real.** Turn off the red badge for apps whose count is meaningless (social apps inflating a "3" to pull you in). Keep badges only where the number means genuine unread items (messages, email, tasks).
steps.expect: the badges left on your home screen correspond to things you would actually want to clear.

steps.action: **Set up a priority / focus mode.** iPhone: Focus (Do Not Disturb, Work, Sleep) with an allow-list of people and apps. Android: Do Not Disturb with priority exceptions and a schedule. Allow only favorite contacts and repeat callers to break through.
steps.expect: a mode that, when on, silences everything except your named exceptions, and a schedule (e.g. sleep hours) that turns it on automatically.

steps.action: **Configure repeat-caller and emergency bypass.** So a genuine emergency (someone calling twice) still reaches you even in Do Not Disturb.
steps.expect: the "allow repeated calls" / emergency bypass option is on.

steps.action: **Live with it for a few days, then adjust.** Any app that buzzed you and made you think "why did I get this" gets demoted; anything you missed gets promoted.
steps.expect: after tuning, notifications feel like signal, and reaching for the phone is a choice, not a reflex.

recipes.verification: Only a short, deliberate set of apps can make sound or vibrate; the rest are silent or off; badges remain only where the count is real; and a scheduled focus/priority mode silences everything except named exceptions while still letting a repeated emergency call through.

recipes.title: mark an email as spam
recipes.name: mark-an-email-as-spam
recipes.goal: Move an unwanted or suspicious email to spam or junk and help future filtering.

steps.action: **Select the email.** Click, tap, or checkbox the message without opening attachments or links.
steps.expect: the email is selected.

steps.action: **Choose spam or junk.** Click or tap `Report spam`, `Junk`, `Block`, or the stop-sign icon.
steps.expect: a confirmation or immediate move begins.

steps.action: **Confirm reporting.** If asked, choose whether to report spam, phishing, or just move to junk.
steps.expect: the message leaves the inbox.

steps.action: **Avoid interacting with content.** Do not reply, unsubscribe, open links, or download attachments from suspicious messages.
steps.expect: no external content or attachment is opened.

steps.action: **Check the spam folder.** Open Spam or Junk if you need to confirm where it went.
steps.expect: the email appears there or is hidden from the inbox.

recipes.verification: The email no longer appears in the inbox and is listed in Spam, Junk, or the provider's reported-spam state.

recipes.title: merge cells
recipes.name: merge-cells
recipes.goal: Merge adjacent spreadsheet cells into one larger cell for a title or label.

steps.action: **Select adjacent cells.** Drag across the cells that should become one cell.
steps.expect: the intended cells are highlighted.

steps.action: **Confirm only one value matters.** Check whether more than the upper-left cell contains data.
steps.expect: no important data will be discarded by the merge.

steps.action: **Merge the cells.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Home > Merge & Center` or its dropdown; Google Sheets: choose `Format > Merge cells > Merge all`.
steps.expect: the selected cells become one larger cell.

steps.action: **Adjust alignment.** Set horizontal and vertical alignment as needed.
steps.expect: the merged cell content appears in the intended position.

recipes.verification: The selected adjacent cells display as one cell, and the visible content is the intended title or label.

recipes.title: merge pdf files
recipes.name: merge-pdf-files
recipes.goal: You combine multiple PDF files into one correctly ordered PDF with the intended page range, pagination, and readable content.

steps.action: **Create a staging folder.** Copy the PDFs into one folder and rename them with leading numbers such as `01-application.pdf`, `02-id.pdf`, and `03-receipt.pdf`.
steps.expect: the file list sorts in the same order as the final packet.

steps.action: **Open the merge tool.** [BRANCH: macOS Preview | Adobe Acrobat | browser or office PDF tool] use a built-in or trusted tool that shows page thumbnails before saving.
steps.expect: thumbnails or a file-order list is visible.

steps.action: **Add files in final order.** Drag files or use Add Files, then confirm the sequence before merging. Order matters because many portals review the first pages first.
steps.expect: the first thumbnail is the intended first page.

steps.action: **Set page ranges if needed.** Include only the pages required from each source, such as pages 2-4 of a statement or only the signature page.
steps.expect: unwanted cover sheets, blank pages, or duplicates are excluded.

steps.action: **Merge into a new file.** Save as a new PDF name that describes the packet and date. Do not overwrite source PDFs.
steps.expect: one combined PDF appears in the staging folder.

steps.action: **Review pagination from start to finish.** Open the merged file, use thumbnails, and check that each section begins where expected.
steps.expect: page count and section order match your plan.

steps.action: **Inspect rotated and scanned pages.** Rotate sideways pages, remove accidental blanks, and confirm scans are not upside down.
steps.expect: every page can be read without turning the screen.

steps.action: **Check size and upload rules.** If the merged file is too large, compress a copy rather than redoing the merge blindly.
steps.expect: the final PDF satisfies the recipient's file-size and format rules.

recipes.verification: The merged PDF opens, its pages appear in the intended order, the page count matches the selected ranges, and the first and last required pages are correct.

recipes.title: move a file
recipes.name: move-a-file
recipes.goal: Move a file from one location to another so it exists only in the destination.

steps.action: **Locate the file.** Open the folder containing the file in File Explorer or Finder.
steps.expect: the file is visible.

steps.action: **Select the file.** Click the file once.
steps.expect: the file is highlighted.

steps.action: **Cut the file.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Ctrl+X` or right-click and choose `Cut`; Mac: press `Command+C` first because Finder moves during paste.
steps.expect: Windows dims the file, or Mac keeps it selected for moving later.

steps.action: **Open the destination.** Navigate to the folder where the file should go.
steps.expect: the destination folder contents are visible.

steps.action: **Paste as a move.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Ctrl+V`; Mac: press `Option+Command+V` or choose `Edit > Move Item Here`.
steps.expect: the file appears in the destination.

steps.action: **Check the original location.** Return to the source folder if needed.
steps.expect: the file is no longer in the original folder.

recipes.verification: The file appears in the destination folder and no longer appears in the original folder.

recipes.title: mute a browser tab
recipes.name: mute-a-browser-tab
recipes.goal: Silence sound from one browser tab without muting the whole computer.

steps.action: **Find the noisy tab.** Look for a speaker icon or audio indicator on the tab.
steps.expect: the tab producing sound is identifiable.

steps.action: **Open the tab menu.** Right-click the tab, or `Control`-click it on Mac.
steps.expect: a context menu appears for that tab.

steps.action: **Mute the tab or site.** Choose `Mute Tab`, `Mute Site`, or `Mute Tab Audio`.
steps.expect: the speaker icon changes to a muted indicator and audio stops.

steps.action: **Unmute when needed.** Reopen the tab menu and choose the unmute option.
steps.expect: audio from that tab or site can play again.

recipes.verification: The tab or site shows a muted indicator and no sound plays from it while other computer audio can still play.

recipes.title: name a cell range
recipes.name: name-a-cell-range
recipes.goal: Give a spreadsheet cell range a reusable name for formulas.

steps.action: **Select the range.** Drag across the cells that should be named.
steps.expect: the intended range is highlighted.

steps.action: **Open named range tools.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: click the Name Box left of the formula bar or choose `Formulas > Define Name`; Google Sheets: choose `Data > Named ranges`.
steps.expect: a field or panel for naming the range appears.

steps.action: **Enter the range name.** Type a valid name such as `Sales_Q1` and confirm.
steps.expect: the name appears in the Name Box or named ranges panel.

steps.action: **Use the name in a formula.** Enter a formula such as `=SUM(Sales_Q1)`.
steps.expect: the formula returns a result using the named range.

recipes.verification: The named range appears in the workbook's named range list, and `=SUM(range_name)` or another formula using it returns the expected value.

recipes.title: open a link in a new tab
recipes.name: open-a-link-in-a-new-tab
recipes.goal: Open a link in a separate tab while keeping the current page available.

steps.action: **Point at the link.** Move the pointer over the link and pause.
steps.expect: the browser status area shows the link destination or the cursor changes.

steps.action: **Open the context menu.** Right-click the link, or press `Control` and click on Mac.
steps.expect: a menu appears with link actions.

steps.action: **Choose new tab.** Select `Open Link in New Tab`.
steps.expect: a new tab appears for the link while the original page stays open.

steps.action: **Switch when ready.** Click the new tab, or press `Ctrl+Tab` on Windows/Linux or `Control+Tab` on Mac.
steps.expect: the linked page is visible in the new tab.

recipes.verification: The original page remains in one tab, and the linked destination is open in another tab.

recipes.title: open a private window
recipes.name: open-a-private-window
recipes.goal: Open a private browsing window for a session that should not be saved in local browser history.

steps.action: **Open a private window.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] press `Ctrl+Shift+N` in Chrome, `Ctrl+Shift+P` in Firefox, or `Command+Shift+N` on Mac browsers that support it.
steps.expect: a new private or incognito window opens.

steps.action: **Confirm private mode.** Look for `Incognito`, `Private Browsing`, a mask icon, or a dark private-mode start page.
steps.expect: the window clearly indicates private browsing.

steps.action: **Browse in that window only.** Type the address or search query into the private window.
steps.expect: pages open inside the private window, not in the normal window.

steps.action: **Close the window when done.** Close all private tabs and the private window.
steps.expect: local history, cookies, and site data from that private session are discarded.

recipes.verification: The browser window shows a private or incognito indicator, and closing it removes that session's local cookies and history.

recipes.title: open the task manager
recipes.name: open-the-task-manager
recipes.goal: Open the system tool that shows running apps and resource usage.

steps.action: **Use the quick shortcut.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Ctrl+Shift+Esc`; Mac: press `Command+Space`, type `Activity Monitor`, and press `Return`.
steps.expect: Task Manager or Activity Monitor opens.

steps.action: **Use the menu path if needed.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: right-click the taskbar and choose `Task Manager`, or press `Ctrl+Alt+Delete` and choose `Task Manager`; Mac: open `Applications > Utilities > Activity Monitor`.
steps.expect: the system monitor window is visible.

steps.action: **Choose the relevant tab or column.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: use `Processes` or `Performance`; Mac: use CPU, Memory, Energy, Disk, or Network tabs.
steps.expect: running apps and resource values are shown.

recipes.verification: Task Manager on Windows or Activity Monitor on Mac is open and lists running processes or resource usage.

recipes.title: opt out of data brokers
recipes.name: opt-out-of-data-brokers
recipes.goal: Reduce personal information exposed by data brokers by finding listings, submitting opt-out requests, and tracking removals.

steps.action: **Prepare identity variants.** List common names, previous names, cities, phone numbers, emails, and addresses that brokers may use.
steps.expect: search terms cover likely records.

steps.action: **Search major broker sites.** Look for your listings using exact and variant details.
steps.expect: you identify records to remove.

steps.action: **Submit opt-out requests.** Use each broker's removal or suppression form and provide only the minimum information required to match the record.
steps.expect: each request is submitted or queued for verification.

steps.action: **Complete verification.** Open confirmation emails or forms and confirm the removal request. [BRANCH: email verification | identity verification] use email when available; avoid sending ID unless the broker is legitimate and the risk is acceptable.
steps.expect: the broker confirms receipt.

steps.action: **Track deadlines.** Record broker name, URL, date submitted, confirmation code, and promised removal time.
steps.expect: pending removals can be followed up.

steps.action: **Recheck listings.** After the stated window, search again and resubmit if the listing remains.
steps.expect: removed records no longer appear or are suppressed.

recipes.verification: Your tracking sheet shows submitted and confirmed requests, and follow-up searches no longer show the targeted broker listings or show them as suppressed.

recipes.title: organize files into folders
recipes.name: organize-files-into-folders
recipes.goal: Your files are grouped into a simple folder structure with consistent names, useful dates, and no giant "misc" pile that becomes impossible to search.

steps.action: **Pick the root location.** Choose one main place, such as Documents, a cloud drive, or an external drive, for the files you are organizing.
steps.expect: you know where the top-level folders will live.

steps.action: **Create a top-level scheme.** Make broad folders such as Admin, Work, School, Home, Finance, Photos, and Archive.
steps.expect: every common file type has an obvious first destination.

steps.action: **Use consistent names.** Rename folders with plain words and avoid duplicates like Work, work stuff, and Job files.
steps.expect: similar files point to the same folder.

steps.action: **Add dates where they help.** Use `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM` at the start of records, exports, scans, and project snapshots.
steps.expect: dated files sort correctly by name.

steps.action: **Limit nesting.** [BRANCH: broad folder | project folder] use two or three levels for ongoing work, and create deeper folders only for large projects.
steps.expect: you can reach common files in a few clicks.

steps.action: **Sort the loose files.** Move desktop, downloads, and old cloud-drive clutter into the chosen folders.
steps.expect: loose-file areas shrink substantially.

steps.action: **Replace misc with a decision.** If tempted to make Misc, choose Archive, To Sort, or a specific category with a review date.
steps.expect: there is no permanent catch-all folder.

steps.action: **Search-test the system.** Look for one tax file, one photo, and one active document using folder browsing and search.
steps.expect: each file is findable without guessing several places.

recipes.verification: A new file can be named, dated if useful, and placed in one clear folder without creating or using a permanent Misc folder.

recipes.title: pair a bluetooth device
recipes.name: pair-a-bluetooth-device
recipes.goal: Pair a Bluetooth accessory such as headphones, keyboard, mouse, speaker, or controller with your device.

steps.action: **Turn on Bluetooth.** Open Bluetooth settings and enable Bluetooth.
steps.expect: the device shows Bluetooth as on.

steps.action: **Put the accessory in pairing mode.** Hold the pairing button or follow the accessory's pairing instructions.
steps.expect: a light flashes or the accessory announces pairing mode.

steps.action: **Find the accessory.** In Bluetooth settings, wait for the accessory name to appear under available devices.
steps.expect: the accessory is listed.

steps.action: **Select the accessory.** Click or tap the accessory name and choose `Pair`, `Connect`, or equivalent.
steps.expect: the device starts pairing or asks for a code.

steps.action: **Confirm any code.** If a code appears, verify it matches on both devices or enter it as instructed.
steps.expect: pairing completes and the accessory shows connected.

steps.action: **Test the accessory.** Play audio, type, move the pointer, or press controls depending on the device.
steps.expect: the accessory works with the paired device.

recipes.verification: Bluetooth settings show the accessory as connected, and the accessory performs its expected function.

recipes.title: pair bluetooth headphones
recipes.name: pair-bluetooth-headphones
recipes.goal: Your Bluetooth headphones are paired with the intended phone, computer, tablet, or TV and play audio reliably from that device.

steps.action: **Charge and reset the obvious state.** Put the headphones near the device, charge them if uncertain, and turn them off and back on.
steps.expect: the headphones power on and announce or show battery.

steps.action: **Enter pairing mode.** Hold the Bluetooth, power, or case button until the light flashes or the voice prompt says pairing. For earbuds, the case button often matters.
steps.expect: the headphones are discoverable, usually with a blinking blue or white light.

steps.action: **Open Bluetooth settings on the device.** [BRANCH: phone | computer | TV] go to Bluetooth or connected devices and start scanning if needed.
steps.expect: the headphones appear by model name or brand.

steps.action: **Select the headphones.** Tap or click the correct name and approve pairing prompts. Ignore duplicate low-energy entries unless the manual says otherwise.
steps.expect: the device reports connected for audio.

steps.action: **Play a test sound.** Start music, a video, or the system test sound and raise volume on both the device and headphones.
steps.expect: sound comes through the headphones.

steps.action: **Handle multi-device switching.** If the headphones connect to an old phone or laptop instead, pause Bluetooth there or disconnect them from that device.
steps.expect: the intended device becomes the active audio source.

steps.action: **Check call microphone if needed.** Make a test recording or call, then choose the headphone mic in app settings if available.
steps.expect: both playback and microphone work for the intended app.

steps.action: **Use forget-and-repair if unstable.** Remove the headphones from Bluetooth settings on the device, reset pairing mode, and pair again.
steps.expect: the device creates a fresh trusted pairing.

recipes.verification: The intended device lists the headphones as connected for audio, test playback is audible through them, and any needed microphone test succeeds.

recipes.title: password protect a pdf
recipes.name: password-protect-a-pdf
recipes.goal: A PDF requires a password to open, and the password is shared separately from the file.

steps.action: **Make a copy of the PDF.** Keep the original unprotected until you confirm the protected version opens.
steps.expect: two files exist, original and protected working copy.

steps.action: **Open security settings.** Use Protect, Encrypt, Set Password, Export as PDF with password, or equivalent in your PDF tool.
steps.expect: the app offers an open password or document-open password.

steps.action: **Set an open password.** Choose the option that requires a password to view the PDF, not only a permissions password for editing or printing.
steps.expect: the settings say the document requires a password to open.

steps.action: **Use a strong password.** Use a password manager to generate a long unique password, or a memorable passphrase with several random words.
steps.expect: the password is not reused from an account.

steps.action: **Save the protected PDF.** Save with a clear filename such as `statement-protected.pdf`.
steps.expect: the file writes successfully and remains a PDF.

steps.action: **Test from closed state.** Close the PDF fully, reopen it, and enter the password.
steps.expect: the viewer blocks access until the correct password is entered.

steps.action: **Share file and password separately.** [BRANCH: email | secure portal] Send the PDF in one place and the password by another method.
steps.expect: no single intercepted message contains both file and password.

steps.action: **Document removal steps.** If you need to remove protection later, open with the password, return to security settings, clear the open password, and save a new copy.
steps.expect: the unprotected copy opens without a prompt.

recipes.verification: Closing and reopening the protected PDF prompts for the open password, and the correct password reveals the expected pages.

recipes.title: paste values only
recipes.name: paste-values-only
recipes.goal: Paste spreadsheet results as fixed values without formulas or formatting.

steps.action: **Copy the source range.** Select the cells and press `Ctrl+C` or `Command+C`.
steps.expect: the source range has a moving border or copy highlight.

steps.action: **Select the destination.** Click the top-left cell where the values should go.
steps.expect: the destination cell is active.

steps.action: **Paste values only.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Home > Paste > Paste Values` or press `Ctrl+Alt+V`, then `V`, then `Enter`; Google Sheets: choose `Edit > Paste special > Values only` or press `Ctrl+Shift+V` on Windows/Linux or `Command+Shift+V` on Mac.
steps.expect: displayed values appear in the destination cells.

steps.action: **Inspect a pasted cell.** Click a destination cell and look at the formula bar.
steps.expect: the formula bar shows a fixed value, not a formula beginning with `=`.

recipes.verification: The destination cells show the copied results, and their formula bars contain fixed values rather than formulas.

recipes.title: pin a browser tab
recipes.name: pin-a-browser-tab
recipes.goal: Pin an important browser tab so it stays compact and harder to close accidentally.

steps.action: **Select the tab.** Click the tab you want to pin.
steps.expect: the page is active and the tab is highlighted.

steps.action: **Open the tab menu.** Right-click the tab, or `Control`-click it on Mac.
steps.expect: a tab context menu appears.

steps.action: **Pin the tab.** Choose `Pin`, `Pin Tab`, or `Pin Tab to Start`.
steps.expect: the tab shrinks and moves to the left side of the tab bar.

steps.action: **Test the pinned position.** Open another tab or switch tabs.
steps.expect: the pinned tab remains at the left and shows a small site icon.

recipes.verification: The chosen tab is pinned at the left side of the tab bar and remains open while other tabs are opened or closed.

recipes.title: pin a site as an app
recipes.name: pin-a-site-as-an-app
recipes.goal: Install or pin a website so it opens like an app from the desktop, dock, taskbar, or launcher.

steps.action: **Open the site.** Navigate to the website you want to pin.
steps.expect: the site loads and shows the account or page you want.

steps.action: **Open app or shortcut controls.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] open the browser menu and look for `Install`, `Save and Share`, `Add to Dock`, or shortcut options.
steps.expect: the browser offers an install, app, or shortcut action if supported.

steps.action: **Create the app shortcut.** Choose `Install`, `Create shortcut`, or `Add to Dock`, then confirm the name.
steps.expect: the site is added as an app or shortcut.

steps.action: **Launch it once.** Open the new app from the desktop, dock, taskbar, Start menu, or launcher.
steps.expect: the site opens in its own window or browser shortcut.

steps.action: **Pin it if needed.** Right-click the launched app icon and choose pin, keep in dock, or add to taskbar.
steps.expect: the app remains available from the chosen launcher.

recipes.verification: The site appears in the operating system launcher, dock, taskbar, or desktop and opens successfully from that pinned entry.

recipes.title: pin an app to the taskbar
recipes.name: pin-an-app-to-the-taskbar
recipes.goal: Pin a frequently used app to the Windows taskbar or Mac Dock for quick access.

steps.action: **Find the app.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Win` and type the app name; Mac: open Launchpad or Finder `Applications`.
steps.expect: the app appears in search or the app list.

steps.action: **Open or select pin controls.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: right-click the app and choose `Pin to taskbar`; Mac: open the app, then right-click or Control-click its Dock icon.
steps.expect: a menu with pin or Dock options appears.

steps.action: **Pin the app.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: click `Pin to taskbar`; Mac: choose `Options > Keep in Dock`.
steps.expect: the app icon stays in the taskbar or Dock.

steps.action: **Test the pinned icon.** Close or minimize the app, then click the pinned icon.
steps.expect: the app opens or comes forward.

recipes.verification: The app icon remains visible on the taskbar or Dock after the app is closed and launches the intended app when clicked.

recipes.title: preview a file without opening it
recipes.name: preview-a-file-without-opening-it
recipes.goal: View a file's contents quickly without fully opening it in its default app.

steps.action: **Select the file.** Click the file once in File Explorer or Finder.
steps.expect: the file is highlighted but not opened.

steps.action: **Open preview.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Alt+P` in File Explorer to show the Preview pane; Mac: press `Space` to open Quick Look.
steps.expect: a preview pane or floating preview appears.

steps.action: **Review the content.** Scroll, zoom, or page through if the preview supports it.
steps.expect: enough content is visible to identify the file.

steps.action: **Close preview.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Alt+P` again or select another file; Mac: press `Space` again or `Esc`.
steps.expect: the preview closes or updates.

recipes.verification: A preview displays the selected file's recognizable contents without launching the full default editing app.

recipes.title: protect a sheet
recipes.name: protect-a-sheet
recipes.goal: Protect a spreadsheet sheet so accidental edits are blocked or warned against.

steps.action: **Select the sheet to protect.** Click the sheet tab containing the data or formulas to guard.
steps.expect: the intended sheet is active.

steps.action: **Open protection settings.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Review > Protect Sheet`; Google Sheets: choose `Data > Protect sheets and ranges`.
steps.expect: protection options appear.

steps.action: **Set allowed edits.** Choose whether users can select cells, sort, filter, or edit specific ranges.
steps.expect: the settings match the intended editing limits.

steps.action: **Apply protection.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: enter an optional password and click `OK`; Google Sheets: click `Set permissions` and choose warning-only or restricted editors.
steps.expect: the sheet shows protection is active.

steps.action: **Test a blocked edit.** Try editing a protected cell, then cancel the change.
steps.expect: Excel blocks the edit or Google Sheets shows a warning or permission message.

recipes.verification: A protected cell cannot be edited without permission or confirmation, while any intended editable cells remain editable.

recipes.title: protect an elderly relative from scams
recipes.name: protect-an-elderly-relative-from-scams
recipes.goal: An elderly relative has practical scam protections, a calm family response plan, and a no-shame route for reporting suspicious calls, texts, emails, or payments.

steps.action: **Start with a calm conversation.** Frame the topic as criminals getting better, not the relative being careless.
steps.expect: the relative is willing to talk without feeling accused.

steps.action: **Name the common scams.** Cover grandchild emergency, romance, tech support, bank fraud, government threat, lottery/prize, delivery, investment, and gift-card scams.
steps.expect: the relative recognizes at least a few scripts.

steps.action: **Create a verification rule.** Agree that urgent money or secrecy requests require calling a known family number or official number first.
steps.expect: the rule is simple enough to remember under stress.

steps.action: **Harden phone and messages.** Enable spam filtering, block unknown repeat callers, silence unknown callers if acceptable, and pin trusted contacts.
steps.expect: fewer suspicious calls and easier access to real contacts.

steps.action: **Protect financial accounts.** Turn on transaction alerts, set lower transfer limits where practical, and discuss trusted-contact or view-only monitoring options.
steps.expect: unusual transactions generate alerts before losses grow.

steps.action: **Secure key accounts.** Use unique passwords, a password manager if acceptable, and 2FA for email, bank, and phone carrier accounts.
steps.expect: account takeover becomes harder.

steps.action: **Limit exposed payment paths.** Discuss avoiding gift cards for emergencies, not storing cards on unfamiliar sites, and using a credit card rather than debit for online purchases when possible.
steps.expect: risky payment methods are less available in panic moments.

steps.action: **Make an after-a-hit plan.** Write down who to call first: bank/card, trusted family contact, local police/nonemergency if needed, and account providers.
steps.expect: the relative has a visible action list.

steps.action: **Schedule gentle check-ins.** Review recent calls, texts, charges, and mail periodically with permission.
steps.expect: problems surface early without interrogation.

recipes.verification: The relative can state the verification rule, has spam and transaction alerts enabled where acceptable, and has a written after-a-hit contact plan.

recipes.title: recover a deleted file
recipes.name: recover-a-deleted-file
recipes.goal: A deleted file is restored from trash, recently deleted, cloud history, backup, or recovery tools with the best chance of preserving the original content.

steps.action: **Stop writing to the drive.** If the file was on a hard drive, SSD, memory card, or USB drive, stop saving, installing, downloading, or editing there.
steps.expect: no new files are intentionally written to the affected storage.

steps.action: **Check Trash or Recycle Bin.** Search by name, date deleted, or original location, then restore if found.
steps.expect: the file returns to its original folder or a chosen folder.

steps.action: **Check app-level recently deleted.** [BRANCH: photos | notes | cloud docs] Look inside the app's Recently Deleted, Trash, Deleted Items, or Archive area.
steps.expect: the file or item appears with a restore option.

steps.action: **Check cloud storage.** Search Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive, or SharePoint trash and account activity.
steps.expect: a restorable deleted copy or previous version is listed.

steps.action: **Use version history.** For cloud documents, right-click or open File > Version history and restore or copy the needed version.
steps.expect: older versions show timestamps and editors.

steps.action: **Check backups.** Use File History, Time Machine, Windows Backup, phone backup, NAS snapshots, or organization backup portals.
steps.expect: a dated backup contains the file.

steps.action: **Use recovery tools carefully.** Install recovery software on a different drive, scan the affected drive read-only, and recover to a different destination.
steps.expect: candidate files are found without overwriting the original space.

steps.action: **Verify and rename.** Open the recovered file, compare size and date, and save a clean copy with a clear name.
steps.expect: the recovered file opens with expected content.

recipes.verification: The recovered file opens successfully and contains the expected recent content, not just the correct filename.

recipes.title: recover a hacked account
recipes.name: recover-a-hacked-account
recipes.goal: Regain control of a compromised online account and reduce the chance that the attacker can re-enter.

steps.action: **Move to a clean device and network.** Use a trusted phone or computer, update the browser, and avoid links from suspicious emails.
steps.expect: you are on the service's official site or app.

steps.action: **Change the password first.** Use the account security page or recovery flow to set a new unique password from a password manager.
steps.expect: the service confirms the password changed.

steps.action: **Revoke active sessions.** Sign out of all devices, apps, browsers, and remembered logins.
steps.expect: the account lists only your current clean session afterward.

steps.action: **Check recovery settings.** Remove unknown emails, phone numbers, security questions, forwarding rules, and backup addresses.
steps.expect: every recovery option belongs to you.

steps.action: **Turn on two-factor authentication.** [BRANCH: authenticator app | security key | SMS] choose the strongest method available and save backup codes somewhere private.
steps.expect: future sign-ins require the second factor.

steps.action: **Review connected apps and permissions.** Remove unknown third-party apps, tokens, mail clients, and browser extensions.
steps.expect: only services you recognize still have access.

steps.action: **Inspect recent account activity.** Look for password changes, purchases, messages, posts, bank changes, or forwarding rules made during the compromise.
steps.expect: suspicious actions are identified for cleanup or reporting.

steps.action: **Notify affected contacts.** Tell people who may have received scams from your account not to click links or send money.
steps.expect: key contacts know the compromise is contained.

steps.action: **Secure related accounts.** Change passwords anywhere the old password was reused, starting with email, banking, and phone carrier accounts.
steps.expect: reused credentials no longer unlock other accounts.

recipes.verification: The password is unique, unknown sessions and recovery methods are gone, 2FA is enabled, and recent activity shows no new unauthorized actions after the cleanup.

recipes.title: recover an unsaved document
recipes.name: recover-an-unsaved-document
recipes.goal: Recover the newest usable version of a document that was closed, crashed, or never saved, then save it in a durable location.

steps.action: **Do not create more confusion.** Stop editing similarly named files and keep the app open if a recovery pane is visible.
steps.expect: the current recovery state is preserved.

steps.action: **Check the app recovery pane.** Reopen the app and look for Document Recovery, Recovered files, Recent, or Restore previous session.
steps.expect: the app lists one or more recovered drafts or recent files.

steps.action: **Search recent files.** Use the app's File > Open Recent or Home > Recent list and sort by modified date.
steps.expect: likely versions appear near the top of the recent list.

steps.action: **Check autosave cloud history.** [BRANCH: Microsoft 365 | Google Docs | Apple iWork] open OneDrive/SharePoint version history, Google Drive version history, or iCloud Drive Browse Versions if available.
steps.expect: older versions or autosaved drafts are available to inspect.

steps.action: **Search temporary recovery folders.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] search File Explorer for `*.asd`, `*.wbk`, or the document name, or search Finder Recents and app containers for the title.
steps.expect: candidate temporary files appear with plausible timestamps.

steps.action: **Open candidates read-only when possible.** Open each candidate and compare the timestamp and contents before saving over anything.
steps.expect: the best recovered version is identified.

steps.action: **Save the recovered copy immediately.** Use Save As to put the file in Documents, Desktop, OneDrive, Google Drive, or iCloud Drive with a clear name.
steps.expect: the document has a normal filename and appears in a known folder.

steps.action: **Enable autosave for next time.** Turn on AutoSave or automatic backup in the app and confirm the save location syncs.
steps.expect: future edits show saved or synced status.

recipes.verification: The recovered document opens in the correct app, contains the needed content, has been saved with a normal filename in a known folder, and that folder shows saved or synced status.

recipes.title: redact a pdf
recipes.name: redact-a-pdf
recipes.goal: A PDF copy is permanently redacted so hidden text, metadata, and sensitive marks cannot be recovered by selection, search, or layer inspection.

steps.action: **Make a working copy.** Duplicate the PDF and add `redacted` to the filename before editing.
steps.expect: the original and working copy are both present.

steps.action: **Open the real redaction tool.** Choose Redact, Mark for Redaction, or Sanitize, not drawing, highlight, comment, or rectangle tools.
steps.expect: the app shows redaction marks as pending edits.

steps.action: **Mark sensitive content.** Select names, account numbers, addresses, barcodes, signatures, headers, footers, and repeated instances found by search.
steps.expect: every sensitive item is covered by a pending redaction mark.

steps.action: **Apply redactions permanently.** Confirm the tool's Apply or Redact command. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* this removes content from the working copy, so confirm you are not editing the only original.
steps.expect: pending marks become permanent solid areas.

steps.action: **Sanitize hidden data.** Remove metadata, comments, attachments, form data, hidden text, and previous revisions if the tool offers it.
steps.expect: the sanitizer reports completion or lists removed data types.

steps.action: **Flatten or save as final.** Save the redacted PDF as a new final file, using PDF/A or print-to-PDF only if your workflow requires flattening.
steps.expect: the final PDF opens as a normal document without editable redaction annotations.

steps.action: **Verify by searching and copying.** Search for redacted words and try selecting across blacked-out areas, then paste into a plain-text editor.
steps.expect: redacted text cannot be found or pasted.

steps.action: **Review visually.** Zoom through every page, including margins and thumbnails, to catch missed small text or page images.
steps.expect: only intended visible content remains.

recipes.verification: Searching and copy-pasting cannot recover any redacted text, and document properties show no sensitive metadata or attachments.

recipes.title: reference another cell
recipes.name: reference-another-cell
recipes.goal: Use the value from another cell in a spreadsheet formula.

steps.action: **Select the destination cell.** Click the cell where the referenced value or calculation should appear.
steps.expect: the destination cell is active.

steps.action: **Start a reference formula.** Type `=` and click the source cell, or type its address such as `=A2`.
steps.expect: the formula shows the source cell reference.

steps.action: **Add calculation if needed.** Extend the formula, such as `=A2*1.08` or `=A2+B2`.
steps.expect: the complete formula appears in the cell or formula bar.

steps.action: **Confirm the formula.** Press `Enter` or `Return`.
steps.expect: the destination cell displays the referenced value or calculated result.

recipes.verification: Changing the source cell changes the destination result, and the formula bar shows the intended cell reference.

recipes.title: remove a background from an image
recipes.name: remove-a-background-from-an-image
recipes.goal: Create a clean cutout image with the background removed and export it in a format that preserves transparency.

steps.action: **Choose the safest editor.** [BRANCH: local editor | web service] use local editing for private images; use a web remover only for non-sensitive images.
steps.expect: the tool matches the image sensitivity.

steps.action: **Open the highest-quality image.** Use the original file instead of a screenshot or compressed chat copy.
steps.expect: edges and details are sharp enough to edit.

steps.action: **Remove the background.** Run the background remover or select the subject manually.
steps.expect: the subject appears on a transparent or plain preview.

steps.action: **Refine edges.** Check hair, fingers, transparent objects, shadows, and holes inside the subject.
steps.expect: visible edge mistakes are fixed or acceptable.

steps.action: **Export with transparency.** Save as PNG or another format that supports alpha; avoid JPEG for transparent cutouts.
steps.expect: the file reopens with a transparent background.

steps.action: **Test on the destination background.** Place the cutout on light, dark, and intended backgrounds.
steps.expect: halos or missing areas are visible before final use.

recipes.verification: The exported image opens with transparency, the subject edges look acceptable on the intended background, and no unwanted private detail remains visible.

recipes.title: remove duplicate rows
recipes.name: remove-duplicate-rows
recipes.goal: Remove duplicate rows from a spreadsheet range based on selected columns.

steps.action: **Make a reversible copy.** Duplicate the sheet or copy the table to a new sheet.
steps.expect: an unchanged backup exists in the workbook.

steps.action: **Select the data range.** Highlight the table including headers if present.
steps.expect: all rows to check are selected.

steps.action: **Open duplicate removal.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Data > Remove Duplicates`; Google Sheets: choose `Data > Data cleanup > Remove duplicates`.
steps.expect: a duplicate removal dialog opens.

steps.action: **Choose comparison columns.** Check the columns that must match for a row to count as duplicate.
steps.expect: only the intended key columns are selected.

steps.action: **Remove duplicates.** Confirm the dialog.
steps.expect: the app reports how many duplicate rows were removed and how many unique rows remain.

recipes.verification: The cleaned range has no repeated rows according to the selected comparison columns, and the backup sheet still contains the original data.

recipes.title: remove malware from a computer
recipes.name: remove-malware-from-a-computer
recipes.goal: Contain suspected malware, remove it with trusted tools, protect accounts, and decide whether a full reinstall is safer than cleanup.

steps.action: **Disconnect from networks.** Turn off Wi-Fi, unplug Ethernet, and disconnect unknown USB devices.
steps.expect: the computer is offline and cannot keep communicating with remote services.

steps.action: **Record symptoms.** Note pop-ups, ransom notes, unknown apps, browser redirects, antivirus alerts, and the time they started.
steps.expect: you have a short incident note for recovery decisions.

steps.action: **Use built-in protection first.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] run Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options > Full scan, or update macOS and check Login Items and Profiles for unknown entries.
steps.expect: the built-in tool reports clean, quarantined, or detected threats.

steps.action: **Run an offline or second-opinion scan.** On Windows use Microsoft Defender Offline scan; on Mac or Windows use a reputable security vendor's scanner from the official site.
steps.expect: the scan completes and lists any removed or quarantined items.

steps.action: **Remove suspicious persistence.** Uninstall unknown apps, delete unknown browser extensions, and remove unfamiliar login items or profiles.
steps.expect: suspicious entries no longer appear after restart.

steps.action: **Change important passwords from a trusted device.** Start with email, password manager, banking, cloud storage, and work accounts.
steps.expect: critical accounts have new passwords and multi-factor authentication enabled.

steps.action: **Decide whether to reinstall.** If ransomware, credential theft, remote-control tools, or repeated detections occurred, back up only personal files and reinstall the OS. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* reinstalling or wiping can destroy local data, so confirm backups before erasing.
steps.expect: you either have a clean scan or a reinstall plan with verified backups.

steps.action: **Reconnect and monitor.** Reconnect to the internet only after cleanup, then watch for returning symptoms for several days.
steps.expect: no new alerts, redirects, unknown apps, or account-login warnings appear.

recipes.verification: Trusted scans complete without active threats, suspicious apps/extensions/login items are gone after restart, important account passwords were changed from a trusted device, and symptoms do not return after reconnecting.

recipes.title: rename a file
recipes.name: rename-a-file
recipes.goal: Give an existing file a new name without changing its contents or location.

steps.action: **Select the file.** Click the file once in File Explorer, Finder, or the desktop.
steps.expect: the file is highlighted.

steps.action: **Start renaming.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `F2` or right-click and choose `Rename`; Mac: press `Return` or choose `File > Rename`.
steps.expect: the filename text becomes editable.

steps.action: **Type the new name.** Replace only the name part and leave extensions such as `.pdf`, `.jpg`, or `.docx` unchanged unless needed.
steps.expect: the typed name appears in the edit box.

steps.action: **Save the name.** Press `Enter` on Windows or `Return` on Mac.
steps.expect: the file remains in place with the new name.

recipes.verification: The file appears in the same folder with the exact new filename and opens normally.

recipes.title: rename many files at once
recipes.name: rename-many-files-at-once
recipes.goal: Rename a group of selected files with a shared base name or batch rename tool.

steps.action: **Open the folder.** Navigate to the files in File Explorer or Finder.
steps.expect: all target files are visible.

steps.action: **Select the files.** Use `Ctrl+click` on Windows or `Command+click` on Mac for individual files, or `Shift+click` for a range.
steps.expect: only the files to rename are highlighted.

steps.action: **Start batch rename.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `F2`, type a base name, and press `Enter`; Mac: right-click the selection and choose `Rename`.
steps.expect: a batch rename action begins.

steps.action: **Choose the naming pattern.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: use one base name and let Windows add numbers; Mac: choose `Format`, `Replace Text`, or `Add Text`, then set the exact pattern.
steps.expect: the preview or selected files show the intended naming style.

steps.action: **Apply the rename.** Confirm the rename action.
steps.expect: all selected files now share the new pattern.

recipes.verification: Every intended file has the new naming pattern, no unintended file was renamed, and files still open normally.

recipes.title: reopen a closed tab
recipes.name: reopen-a-closed-tab
recipes.goal: Restore a browser tab that was closed by mistake.

steps.action: **Use the reopen shortcut.** Press `Ctrl+Shift+T` on Windows/Linux or `Command+Shift+T` on Mac.
steps.expect: the most recently closed tab reopens.

steps.action: **Repeat if needed.** Press the shortcut again for earlier closed tabs.
steps.expect: tabs reopen in reverse order of closing.

steps.action: **Check the restored page.** Look at the address bar and page content.
steps.expect: the page matches the tab you intended to restore.

recipes.verification: The page from the accidentally closed tab is open again in a browser tab.

recipes.title: reply all to an email
recipes.name: reply-all-to-an-email
recipes.goal: Reply to an email thread so everyone already included receives your response.

steps.action: **Review the recipient list.** Expand details if needed and read all `To` and `Cc` recipients.
steps.expect: you know who will receive a reply-all response.

steps.action: **Decide whether everyone needs it.** Use reply all only when the whole group needs your response or context.
steps.expect: no unnecessary or private recipient remains included.

steps.action: **Choose reply all.** Click or tap `Reply all`, usually shown as a double-arrow or menu option.
steps.expect: a reply draft opens with the original recipients included.

steps.action: **Write the response.** Keep the message relevant to the whole thread.
steps.expect: the draft contains only information appropriate for all listed recipients.

steps.action: **Recheck recipients before sending.** Remove anyone who should not receive the response, and do not add hidden recipients to create side conversations.
steps.expect: the visible recipient list is intentional.
