steps.action: **Send the reply.** Click or tap `Send`.
steps.expect: the reply appears in the thread and Sent folder.

recipes.verification: The sent reply appears in the original thread and was delivered to the intended original participants, with no unintended private content.

recipes.title: report a scam
recipes.name: report-a-scam
recipes.goal: A scam is reported to the right platform, financial institution, and authority while evidence is preserved and affected accounts are secured.

steps.action: **Stop interaction.** Do not reply, click more links, send more money, or provide more codes.
steps.expect: the scammer no longer receives new information from you.

steps.action: **Preserve evidence.** Save screenshots, emails with headers if possible, phone numbers, usernames, URLs, receipts, tracking numbers, and timestamps.
steps.expect: evidence is stored before deletion or blocking.

steps.action: **Secure affected accounts.** Change passwords, revoke suspicious sessions, turn on two-factor authentication, and check recovery details.
steps.expect: account access is under your control.

steps.action: **Contact the money handler.** If payment or banking was involved, call the bank, card issuer, payment app, or crypto exchange through official support.
steps.expect: fraud report, dispute, freeze, or case number is opened.

steps.action: **Report to the platform.** Use the marketplace, social network, email provider, phone carrier, job site, or app's report flow.
steps.expect: the account, listing, message, or transaction is flagged.

steps.action: **Report to authorities.** File with the consumer protection, cybercrime, police, or identity-theft authority relevant to your location.
steps.expect: a report number or confirmation is saved.

steps.action: **Warn affected people.** Tell contacts, family, coworkers, or group admins if the scam used your name or could target them next.
steps.expect: likely secondary targets know not to trust the scam.

steps.action: **Monitor follow-up.** Watch accounts, credit, mail, and messages for repeated attempts or retaliation.
steps.expect: new suspicious activity is caught quickly.

recipes.verification: Evidence is saved, affected accounts are secured, and each relevant platform, financial provider, or authority has issued a report confirmation or case number.

recipes.title: reset a forgotten pin
recipes.name: reset-a-forgotten-pin
recipes.goal: A forgotten PIN is reset through the service's official recovery flow, identity is verified, and the new PIN is memorable without being easy to guess.

steps.action: **Identify the issuer.** Determine whether the PIN belongs to a phone, bank card, device, app, benefits account, or workplace system.
steps.expect: one specific service owns the reset.

steps.action: **Open the official reset path.** Use the official app, typed website address, device settings, or phone number printed on your card or statement.
steps.expect: the page or agent clearly names the service.

steps.action: **Choose forgot PIN.** Select the recovery option for a forgotten PIN rather than trying random guesses.
steps.expect: the service asks for identity verification.

steps.action: **Verify identity.** Provide only the requested proof through the official flow.
steps.expect: verification succeeds or the service gives a documented next step.

steps.action: **Create the new PIN.** Pick numbers you can remember but others cannot guess, avoiding birthdays, addresses, repeated digits, or 1234.
steps.expect: the service accepts the PIN rules.

steps.action: **Confirm the new PIN.** Re-enter the same PIN carefully in the confirmation field or keypad.
steps.expect: the reset completes and a success message appears.

steps.action: **Update where used.** Change saved notes, password manager entries, or household instructions that refer to the old PIN.
steps.expect: only the new, correct reference remains.

steps.action: **Test once.** Sign in, unlock, or authorize a small non-destructive action if the service allows it.
steps.expect: the new PIN works without repeated failures.

recipes.verification: The official service confirms the reset, and the new PIN unlocks or authorizes the intended account exactly once.

recipes.title: resize an image
recipes.name: resize-an-image
recipes.goal: Change an image's pixel dimensions or file size for sharing, uploading, or storage.

steps.action: **Open the resize tool.** Open the image in an editor that has resize, image size, or export-size controls.
steps.expect: the image is loaded in the editor.

steps.action: **Choose resize settings.** Select pixels, percentage, or a preset size.
steps.expect: width and height fields or size presets are visible.

steps.action: **Keep proportions linked.** Leave aspect ratio, lock, or constrain proportions enabled unless you intentionally want distortion.
steps.expect: changing one dimension updates the other.

steps.action: **Enter the target size.** Type the required width, height, percentage, or export quality.
steps.expect: the preview or file-size estimate updates.

steps.action: **Save a copy.** Export or save under a new name if you need the original size later.
steps.expect: a resized image file is created.

steps.action: **Check the result.** Open file details or properties to confirm dimensions and size.
steps.expect: the numbers match the target or upload requirement.

recipes.verification: The saved image has the required pixel dimensions or file size and opens without distortion.

recipes.title: restart a frozen phone
recipes.name: restart-a-frozen-phone
recipes.goal: A frozen phone is restarted with a soft reset, preserving data and avoiding a factory reset.

steps.action: **Confirm it is frozen.** Try the power button, volume buttons, touch screen, and charging cable for a minute.
steps.expect: the phone either responds or remains stuck on the same screen.

steps.action: **Avoid erase options.** Do not choose reset all content, factory reset, recovery erase, or wipe data. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* factory reset deletes local data unless a backup exists.
steps.expect: no erase confirmation screen is accepted.

steps.action: **Use the iPhone button combo.** [BRANCH: iPhone with Face ID or iPhone 8 or later | older iPhone] Newer: press Volume Up, press Volume Down, then hold Side until the Apple logo appears. Older: hold the documented Home plus Side or Top combo.
steps.expect: the Apple logo appears.

steps.action: **Use the Android button combo.** Hold Power for 20 to 30 seconds, or hold Power plus Volume Down for 10 to 20 seconds on models that require it.
steps.expect: the screen goes black or the maker logo appears.

steps.action: **Wait through reboot.** Leave the phone alone for several minutes, especially after an update or low-battery crash.
steps.expect: the lock screen or startup screen appears.

steps.action: **Unlock and check basics.** Enter the passcode after restart, then check touch, cellular, Wi-Fi, and battery level.
steps.expect: the phone responds normally.

steps.action: **Charge and cool if needed.** If the phone froze while hot or nearly empty, charge it on a hard surface and remove the case temporarily.
steps.expect: battery and temperature stabilize.

steps.action: **Update or uninstall the trigger app.** If the same app caused the freeze, update it or remove it after data is backed up.
steps.expect: the freeze does not recur immediately.

recipes.verification: The phone reaches the lock screen, accepts the passcode, and responds to touch and buttons for several minutes.

recipes.title: revoke third party app access
recipes.name: revoke-third-party-app-access
recipes.goal: Unknown, unused, or risky third-party app access is removed from important accounts, including OAuth grants, integrations, and connected devices.

steps.action: **Start with high-value accounts.** Review email, cloud storage, social, finance, password manager, and work accounts first.
steps.expect: you are in the account security or privacy settings.

steps.action: **Find connected app settings.** Look for Security, Privacy, Apps with access, Third-party access, Integrations, Authorized apps, or Devices.
steps.expect: a list of apps, services, grants, or sessions appears.

steps.action: **Open details for each item.** Check app name, publisher, permissions, last used date, and connected account.
steps.expect: you can tell what data each app can read or change.

steps.action: **Classify each grant.** [BRANCH: known and still needed | unknown | unused | over-permissioned] Keep only grants that have a current purpose.
steps.expect: each item has a keep or revoke decision.

steps.action: **Revoke unknown or unused access.** Click Remove, Revoke, Disconnect, or Delete access for items you do not recognize or no longer need.
steps.expect: the app disappears from the list or shows access revoked.

steps.action: **Review OAuth scope warnings.** Pay special attention to grants that can read email, files, contacts, calendars, financial data, or act on your behalf.
steps.expect: broad grants are either justified or removed.

steps.action: **Check active sessions and devices too.** Sign out old browsers, phones, TVs, and locations you do not use.
steps.expect: only current devices remain signed in.

steps.action: **Repeat on linked accounts.** If an app connected Google to Dropbox, Slack, or Microsoft, review both sides when practical.
steps.expect: the same unused integration is not still alive elsewhere.

steps.action: **Set a periodic re-check.** Add a quarterly or semiannual reminder for important accounts.
steps.expect: access review will happen again without relying on memory.

recipes.verification: The connected-app list contains only recognized, currently used apps, and high-risk grants for email, files, contacts, calendars, or financial data are either removed or explicitly justified.

recipes.title: rotate an image
recipes.name: rotate-an-image
recipes.goal: Turn an image to the correct orientation.

steps.action: **Open the image.** Open the file in Photos, Preview, Paint, Gallery, or another image viewer.
steps.expect: the image appears on screen.

steps.action: **Find rotate.** Look for a curved arrow, `Rotate`, or edit menu.
steps.expect: a rotation control is visible.

steps.action: **Rotate the image.** Click or tap rotate left or rotate right until the image is upright.
steps.expect: the preview changes orientation.

steps.action: **Save the image.** Choose `Save`, `Done`, or `Save a copy` depending on whether you want to replace the file.
steps.expect: the image stays in the corrected orientation after closing and reopening.

recipes.verification: The image opens upright in the target app or viewer after saving.

recipes.title: run a spellcheck
recipes.name: run-a-spellcheck
recipes.goal: Spelling and basic writing errors are reviewed and corrected in a document.

steps.action: **Set the document language if needed.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, use Review > Language > Set Proofing Language; in Google Docs, use File > Language.
steps.expect: the proofing language matches the document.

steps.action: **Start spelling and grammar check.** In Word, choose Review > Editor or Spelling & Grammar; in Google Docs, choose Tools > Spelling and grammar > Spelling and grammar check.
steps.expect: the first suggestion appears.

steps.action: **Review each suggestion.** Read the sentence before accepting, ignoring, or changing a suggestion.
steps.expect: each flagged item is handled deliberately.

steps.action: **Add valid terms if appropriate.** Add names, technical terms, or brand words to the dictionary only when they are correctly spelled.
steps.expect: valid repeated terms stop being flagged.

steps.action: **Finish the checker.** Continue until the tool reports no remaining issues or returns to the start.
steps.expect: the spellcheck session ends without unresolved obvious spelling flags.

steps.action: **Read key passages manually.** Scan headings, names, numbers, and short sentences.
steps.expect: errors that spellcheck may miss are caught.

recipes.verification: The spellcheck tool reports no unresolved spelling issues, and a manual scan of important names and headings shows no obvious errors.

recipes.title: save a webpage as pdf
recipes.name: save-a-webpage-as-pdf
recipes.goal: Save the current web page as a PDF file for offline reading or record keeping.

steps.action: **Open print.** Press `Ctrl+P` on Windows/Linux or `Command+P` on Mac.
steps.expect: the browser print dialog opens.

steps.action: **Choose PDF output.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] select `Save to PDF`, `Microsoft Print to PDF`, or `PDF` > `Save as PDF` depending on the browser and operating system.
steps.expect: the destination indicates a PDF file will be created.

steps.action: **Set page options.** Choose pages, layout, scale, headers, footers, and background graphics as needed.
steps.expect: the preview shows the content you want in the PDF.

steps.action: **Save the file.** Click `Save` or `Print`, choose a folder, and enter a clear filename.
steps.expect: a PDF file is created in the selected location.

steps.action: **Open the PDF.** Open the saved file from the download bar or file manager.
steps.expect: the PDF opens and displays the saved page content.

recipes.verification: The saved PDF opens locally and contains the intended page content, not a blank page, print dialog, or login screen.

recipes.title: scan a document to email
recipes.name: scan-a-document-to-email
recipes.goal: A paper document is scanned into a readable PDF and sent to the intended email recipient.

steps.action: **Prepare the pages.** Remove staples, smooth folds, align page order, and decide whether the pages are one-sided or two-sided.
steps.expect: pages feed or lie flat without clips or curled corners.

steps.action: **Choose glass or feeder.** [BRANCH: scanner glass | automatic feeder] Use glass for fragile, small, or bound pages; use the feeder for clean loose pages.
steps.expect: the first page is positioned against the corner mark or loaded face-up or face-down as labeled.

steps.action: **Select PDF output.** In the scanner app, printer screen, or computer scan utility, choose PDF for documents and JPEG only for photos.
steps.expect: the preview or settings panel shows PDF as the file type.

steps.action: **Set readable quality.** Use 200 to 300 dpi for normal text, grayscale for forms, and color only when color marks matter.
steps.expect: the estimated file size stays reasonable for email.

steps.action: **Scan the pages.** Start the scan and add pages when prompted, keeping the same orientation.
steps.expect: each page appears in preview without cut-off edges.

steps.action: **Check and save.** Rotate pages, delete blanks, name the file clearly, and save it somewhere you can find.
steps.expect: one PDF opens locally with all pages in order.

steps.action: **Send by email.** [BRANCH: scan-to-email | save-then-attach] Use scan-to-email only if the printer is already configured; otherwise attach the saved PDF from your mail app.
steps.expect: the email draft contains the PDF attachment.

steps.action: **Confirm recipient and send.** Check the address, subject, and attachment before sending.
steps.expect: the sent-mail folder shows the message with the PDF attached.

recipes.verification: The sent email contains a PDF that opens, has every intended page in order, and is readable at normal zoom.

recipes.title: scan a document with your phone
recipes.name: scan-a-document-with-your-phone
recipes.goal: A paper document is captured as a clean, cropped, readable multi-page PDF using the phone's built-in scanner, saved with a name you can find again, not a crooked photo in the camera roll.

steps.action: **Open the native scanner, not the plain camera.** iPhone: Notes > new note > camera icon > Scan Documents, or Files > three-dot menu > Scan. Android: Google Drive > + > Scan.
steps.expect: a viewfinder that highlights the page edges automatically rather than a normal photo screen.

steps.action: **Set up the shot for clean edge detection.** Lay the page flat, fill most of the frame, and keep the phone parallel to the page (shoot straight down, not at an angle). Even light, no hard shadow from your own hand.
steps.expect: a colored overlay snaps to all four corners of the page.

steps.action: **Capture, letting auto-detect fire.** Most scanners shoot automatically when the page is steady and squared; otherwise tap the shutter.
steps.expect: the page captures and the app shows a cropped, de-skewed preview, not the whole tabletop.

steps.action: **Fix the crop if the corners are wrong.** Drag the corner handles to the actual page edges. This is the step people skip, and it is what separates a scan from a photo.
steps.expect: the crop outline sits exactly on the paper edges with no table showing and no text cut off.

steps.action: **Add more pages for a multi-page document.** Keep shooting; each page appends. Scan them in reading order.
steps.expect: a running page count that matches the number of physical pages you have fed.

steps.action: **Choose the right filter.** Black-and-white/document filter for text (smaller, sharper, more legible); color only when color matters (photos, highlighted forms, ID cards).
steps.expect: text looks crisp and high-contrast; the file is not a heavy full-color photo of text.

steps.action: **Save as PDF and name it meaningfully.** Finish/Save, keep the format as PDF for a multi-page document. Rename from the default "Scan 2026-07-20" to something findable like `tax-2025-receipt-electric.pdf`.
steps.expect: a single PDF with all pages in order, under a searchable name, in a folder you will look in.

steps.action: **Verify before you rely on it.** Open the PDF and read the smallest text on the most important page.
steps.expect: every page present, right-side up, in order, and fully legible.

recipes.verification: Opening the saved PDF shows every page cropped to the paper edges, upright, in order, and legible down to the smallest important text, under a filename you can find by searching.

recipes.title: scan a qr code safely
recipes.name: scan-a-qr-code-safely
recipes.goal: Open a QR code only after checking where it leads and avoiding credential theft, payment scams, or malicious downloads.

steps.action: **Inspect the physical code.** Look for stickers placed over a real code, torn edges, mismatched branding, or a code added to a public surface.
steps.expect: the code appears original or you decide not to scan it.

steps.action: **Use the built-in camera first.** Open the camera or trusted QR scanner, not a random scanner app from an ad.
steps.expect: the phone previews a URL before opening it.

steps.action: **Read the preview URL.** Check the domain, spelling, country code, and whether it uses HTTPS.
steps.expect: the link visibly matches the organization or service you expected.

steps.action: **Avoid automatic sign-in.** If the link opens a login page from a random poster, parking meter, restaurant table, or flyer, stop.
steps.expect: you do not enter passwords or one-time codes from an unverified QR link.

steps.action: **Cross-check important actions.** For payments, fines, delivery issues, tickets, or account warnings, type the known official website yourself or use the official app.
steps.expect: the same action appears after independent navigation.

steps.action: **Open low-risk links only.** Menus, event pages, and public documents are usually safer if the domain checks out.
steps.expect: the page content matches the physical context.

steps.action: **Reject unexpected downloads.** Do not install apps, profiles, certificates, or files prompted by a scanned code.
steps.expect: no new app, configuration profile, or permission is granted.

steps.action: **Close suspicious pages.** If the page redirects repeatedly, asks for payment immediately, or claims urgency, close the browser tab.
steps.expect: the suspicious page is no longer active.

steps.action: **Report tampered codes.** Tell staff, the business, parking authority, or venue if a stickered or fake code is present.
steps.expect: the owner can remove or verify the code.

recipes.verification: The opened page domain matches the intended organization, and you did not enter credentials, payment details, or install anything from an unverified QR link.

recipes.title: schedule an email to send later
recipes.name: schedule-an-email-to-send-later
recipes.goal: An email is composed, scheduled for the intended future time, verified in the queued folder, and still cancelable before it sends.

steps.action: **Compose the email normally.** Add recipients, subject, body, signature, and attachments before scheduling.
steps.expect: the draft is complete and ready to send.

steps.action: **Proofread before scheduling.** Check names, dates, links, attachments, and whether reply-all is appropriate.
steps.expect: no obvious correction remains.

steps.action: **Open schedule send.** [BRANCH: Gmail | Outlook | Apple Mail or other] Use the arrow beside Send, Schedule send, Delay delivery, or Send Later option.
steps.expect: a date and time picker appears.

steps.action: **Choose the send time.** Pick the intended date, local time, and time zone if the app shows one.
steps.expect: the scheduled time displays clearly before confirmation.

steps.action: **Confirm scheduling.** Click or tap Schedule, Send later, or OK.
steps.expect: the message leaves Drafts and moves to Scheduled, Outbox, or Send Later.

steps.action: **Verify the queued message.** Open the scheduled folder and confirm recipient, subject, attachments, and send time.
steps.expect: the message is queued for the intended time.

steps.action: **Edit or cancel if needed.** Open the scheduled message before send time, cancel scheduled send, edit the draft, then reschedule.
steps.expect: the old queued version is gone or replaced.

steps.action: **Keep the account available.** Leave internet and account access normal; some desktop clients send only when the app or device is online.
steps.expect: the service or app can send at the scheduled time.

recipes.verification: The scheduled folder shows the email queued for the intended date, time, recipients, and attachments.

recipes.title: schedule social media posts
recipes.name: schedule-social-media-posts
recipes.goal: Schedule social media posts for future publication with correct timing, assets, approvals, and account permissions.

steps.action: **Select the scheduler.** [BRANCH: platform-native | third-party tool] use native scheduling for fewer permissions or a trusted tool for cross-platform calendars.
steps.expect: the scheduler can publish to the target account.

steps.action: **Draft the post.** Write platform-specific copy, attach media, add alt text, and check links.
steps.expect: the preview matches the intended post.

steps.action: **Confirm audience and account.** Verify profile, page, channel, visibility, and cross-posting settings before scheduling.
steps.expect: the post is assigned to the correct destination.

steps.action: **Set date and timezone.** Choose the publish time and confirm the scheduler's timezone, especially for campaigns or travel.
steps.expect: the scheduled time matches the audience time.

steps.action: **Review approvals and compliance.** Check brand, sponsorship disclosure, regulated claims, and crisis-sensitive timing.
steps.expect: required approvals are complete.

steps.action: **Schedule the post.** Save or schedule the post. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once the scheduled time arrives, the post may publish publicly before you notice an error.
steps.expect: the post appears in the scheduled queue.

steps.action: **Verify after publishing.** Check the live post soon after release for formatting, media, tags, and link behavior.
steps.expect: the live post matches the approved version.

recipes.verification: The scheduled queue shows the correct account, content, assets, visibility, date, timezone, and approval status, and the live post is checked after publication.

recipes.title: screen record your phone
recipes.name: screen-record-your-phone
recipes.goal: You record a short phone screen video with the right audio setting, stop it cleanly, trim it, and confirm it is safe to share.

steps.action: **Add the screen-recording control if missing.** On iPhone, add Screen Recording in Control Center settings; on Android, edit Quick Settings and add Screen Record if it is not already visible.
steps.expect: the recording tile or button is available from quick controls.

steps.action: **Prepare the screen.** Close private apps, clear notifications, and open the app or page you need to show.
steps.expect: only intended content is visible.

steps.action: **Choose the audio setting.** [BRANCH: no audio | device audio | microphone] use no audio for visual bugs, device audio for playback issues, or microphone when explaining steps aloud.
steps.expect: the recorder shows the selected audio mode before starting.

steps.action: **Start recording.** Tap the screen-recording control, confirm any privacy prompt, and wait for the countdown.
steps.expect: a red status indicator, timer, or recording icon appears.

steps.action: **Perform the action slowly.** Reproduce the issue or demonstrate the task with pauses between taps so the viewer can follow.
steps.expect: the important sequence is captured once without rushing.

steps.action: **Stop the recording.** Tap the red status bar, notification, or quick setting, then confirm Stop if asked.
steps.expect: the phone saves the video to Photos, Gallery, or Movies.

steps.action: **Trim the start and end.** Open the video editor and remove countdown time, accidental swipes, and idle ending.
steps.expect: the saved clip starts near the useful action and ends after the result.

steps.action: **Check size and privacy before sending.** Watch the clip, listen if audio was recorded, and compress or shorten if the file is too large.
steps.expect: the clip is understandable, shareable, and does not expose avoidable private details.

recipes.verification: The saved video plays from start to finish, shows the intended phone actions, uses the intended audio mode, and is short enough to share.

recipes.title: search within a website
recipes.name: search-within-a-website
recipes.goal: Find pages on one specific website without browsing the whole site manually.

steps.action: **Try the site's search box.** Open the site and look for `Search`, a magnifying glass icon, or a search field.
steps.expect: a field accepts your query.

steps.action: **Run a focused query.** Type the topic or phrase and submit with `Enter` or the search button.
steps.expect: the site shows results from that website.

steps.action: **Use a search engine if needed.** In a search engine, type `site:example.com search terms` using the real domain.
steps.expect: results are limited to that domain.

steps.action: **Open likely results carefully.** Use titles, snippets, and URLs to choose a relevant result.
steps.expect: the opened page is on the intended website.

steps.action: **Refine the search.** Add exact phrases in quotation marks or extra keywords if results are too broad.
steps.expect: the result list becomes more specific.

recipes.verification: At least one search result opens on the intended domain and contains information matching the query.

recipes.title: search your computer for a file
recipes.name: search-your-computer-for-a-file
recipes.goal: Find a file on your computer by searching for its name, type, or recent location.

steps.action: **Open system search.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Win` and type, or open File Explorer and use the search box; Mac: press `Command+Space` for Spotlight or open Finder search.
steps.expect: a search field is active.

steps.action: **Enter a useful query.** Type the exact name, part of the name, or an extension such as `.pdf`, `.jpg`, or `.xlsx`.
steps.expect: results begin to appear.

steps.action: **Narrow by location if needed.** Search inside Documents, Downloads, Desktop, or the likely project folder.
steps.expect: fewer and more relevant results appear.

steps.action: **Check details before opening.** Look at the file path, date modified, size, and icon.
steps.expect: one result looks like the intended file.

steps.action: **Open or reveal the file.** Double-click to open it, or use right-click `Open file location` on Windows or `Show in Finder` on Mac.
steps.expect: the file or its containing folder opens.

recipes.verification: The intended file is visible in its containing folder or opens with the expected contents.

recipes.title: search your email
recipes.name: search-your-email
recipes.goal: Find a specific email or set of emails using your mail app's search tools.

steps.action: **Open search.** Click or tap the mail app's search box or magnifying glass.
steps.expect: the cursor is in the email search field.

steps.action: **Enter a narrow clue.** Type a sender name, email address, subject word, or exact phrase.
steps.expect: matching messages appear or the app offers search suggestions.

steps.action: **Apply filters.** Add date, folder, attachment, unread, sender, or recipient filters if too many results appear.
steps.expect: the result list gets shorter and more relevant.

steps.action: **Open likely matches.** Select a result and check sender, date, subject, and body.
steps.expect: you can tell whether it is the email you need.

steps.action: **Save or act on the result.** Star, flag, move, download, or reply once you find the right email.
steps.expect: the needed follow-up action is complete.

recipes.verification: The target email is open or selected, and its sender, date, subject, or contents match the clue you were searching for.

recipes.title: secure your home wifi
recipes.name: secure-your-home-wifi
recipes.goal: Home Wi-Fi is protected with a strong router admin password, modern encryption, a strong network passphrase, guest isolation, and firmware updates.

steps.action: **Find the router admin route.** Use the router maker's app or type the gateway address from your network settings.
steps.expect: you reach the router login screen, not a search-result support page.

steps.action: **Log in and change the admin password.** Replace default or reused admin credentials with a unique password stored in your password manager.
steps.expect: the router accepts the new admin password and requires it for future changes.

steps.action: **Update router firmware.** Check for Firmware, Software update, or Router update and install available updates.
steps.expect: the router restarts and reports current firmware.

steps.action: **Set Wi-Fi encryption to WPA3 or WPA2.** [BRANCH: WPA3 available | WPA2 only] Use WPA3-Personal if all devices support it, or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode when needed.
steps.expect: security mode is not WEP, WPA, or open.

steps.action: **Set a strong Wi-Fi passphrase.** Use a long phrase or generated password that is not reused elsewhere.
steps.expect: the network saves the new passphrase and reconnects your device after entry.

steps.action: **Disable risky convenience features.** Turn off WPS PIN, remote admin from internet, and default open setup networks unless specifically needed.
steps.expect: outside devices cannot administer the router or join by PIN.

steps.action: **Create a guest network.** Enable guest Wi-Fi with a separate passphrase and client isolation if available.
steps.expect: guests can reach the internet but not your private devices.

steps.action: **Check connected devices.** Review the device list and rename known devices for easier future checks.
steps.expect: unknown devices are removed or blocked after you change the Wi-Fi passphrase.

steps.action: **Save recovery details.** Store admin login, Wi-Fi passphrase, router model, and ISP support details privately.
steps.expect: you can recover settings without using factory defaults.

recipes.verification: The router shows a unique admin password, WPA3 or WPA2 encryption, WPS/remote admin disabled unless intentionally needed, current firmware, and a separate guest network.

recipes.title: select all text
recipes.name: select-all-text
recipes.goal: All editable text or content in the active document, field, or page area is selected.

steps.action: **Click inside the target area.** Place the cursor in the document body or text field you want to affect.
steps.expect: the insertion cursor appears in that area.

steps.action: **Use Select All.** Press `Ctrl+A` on Windows/Linux or `Command+A` on Mac, or choose Edit > Select All.
steps.expect: the text or content in the active area is highlighted.

steps.action: **Confirm the selection scope.** Look for whether only one field, the whole document, or the whole page is selected.
steps.expect: the highlighted area matches what you intend to change.

steps.action: **Take the next action.** Copy, cut, delete, format, or replace the selected content.
steps.expect: the next action applies to the highlighted content.

recipes.verification: Every intended piece of text is highlighted, and no unrelated area is included.

recipes.title: set a default app
recipes.name: set-a-default-app
recipes.goal: Choose which app opens a file type or common task by default.

steps.action: **Open default app settings.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: open `Settings > Apps > Default apps`; Mac: select a sample file in Finder and press `Command+I`.
steps.expect: default app controls are visible.

steps.action: **Choose the target type.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: search for the app, file extension, or link type; Mac: expand `Open with` in the file Info window.
steps.expect: the current default is shown.

steps.action: **Select the preferred app.** Choose the app from the list, or browse to it if needed.
steps.expect: the preferred app appears as the selected default.

steps.action: **Apply broadly if needed.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: confirm each file type or protocol prompt; Mac: click `Change All` to apply to all files of that type.
steps.expect: the system accepts the new default.

steps.action: **Test with a file or link.** Double-click the target file type or open the target link.
steps.expect: it opens in the chosen app.

recipes.verification: A test file, link, or protocol opens automatically in the selected app without asking.

recipes.title: set a recurring reminder
recipes.name: set-a-recurring-reminder
recipes.goal: A reminder repeats on the right schedule or trigger, alerts you in the right place, and gets reviewed often enough that ignored reminders do not pile up.

steps.action: **Choose the right app.** Use reminders or tasks for actions, calendar for appointments, and medication or finance apps for regulated routines when appropriate.
steps.expect: the reminder lives where you will actually act on it.

steps.action: **Create the reminder.** Enter a short verb-first title such as "Take trash out" or "Pay rent."
steps.expect: the reminder is easy to understand at a glance.

steps.action: **Set the first due time.** Choose the first date and time when the action should happen.
steps.expect: the initial alert is scheduled.

steps.action: **Add the repeat rule.** [BRANCH: daily | weekly | monthly | custom] choose the recurrence that matches the real-world routine.
steps.expect: future occurrences appear or the rule is shown.

steps.action: **Use a location trigger if better.** For errands, add a location such as arriving at home, work, or a store instead of a fixed time.
steps.expect: the app shows the location condition.

steps.action: **Set notification behavior.** Allow alerts, sound, lock-screen visibility, or priority only if the reminder should interrupt you.
steps.expect: the reminder can notify you at the intended moment.

steps.action: **Practice snooze discipline.** If you snooze, choose a real next action time rather than repeatedly pushing it by a few minutes.
steps.expect: snoozed reminders remain intentional.

steps.action: **Schedule a review.** Weekly or monthly, delete stale reminders, adjust repeat rules, and promote missed reminders to a better app or time.
steps.expect: the list stays trusted and current.

recipes.verification: The reminder shows the correct next occurrence, repeat rule, trigger type, and notification setting, and it appears in your review list.

recipes.title: set a system timer
recipes.name: set-a-system-timer
recipes.goal: Set a countdown timer on your device so it alerts you after a chosen duration.

steps.action: **Open the timer tool.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac | mobile-app] open Clock, Alarms & Clock, Siri, Google Assistant, or another system timer.
steps.expect: timer controls are visible.

steps.action: **Enter the duration.** Set hours, minutes, and seconds as needed.
steps.expect: the timer shows the intended countdown length.

steps.action: **Name the timer if available.** Add a label such as laundry, break, or oven.
steps.expect: the label appears with the timer.

steps.action: **Start the timer.** Click or tap `Start`.
steps.expect: the countdown begins decreasing.

steps.action: **Confirm alert settings.** Check that volume, focus mode, or notification settings will allow the timer alert.
steps.expect: the device can play or show the timer alert.

recipes.verification: The countdown is running with the intended duration and will alert through visible notification, sound, or vibration.

recipes.title: set parental controls on a game console
recipes.name: set-parental-controls-on-a-game-console
recipes.goal: A game console uses a family account setup with age limits, spending controls, screen time rules, and chat settings that match the child's needs.

steps.action: **Update the console.** Install pending system updates before changing account controls.
steps.expect: parental-control menus match current platform options.

steps.action: **Create or open the family group.** Sign in as the adult organizer and add the child's account to the family.
steps.expect: the child appears under family members.

steps.action: **Set age limits.** Choose content ratings for games, apps, videos, and web access based on age and maturity.
steps.expect: games above the rating require approval or are blocked.

steps.action: **Require purchase approval.** Turn on spending limits, wallet restrictions, or adult approval for purchases.
steps.expect: the child cannot buy games or add-ons without permission.

steps.action: **Set screen time.** [BRANCH: schedule | daily limit] choose allowed hours, total time per day, or both.
steps.expect: the console shows when play is allowed.

steps.action: **Adjust chat and multiplayer.** Limit voice chat, text chat, friend requests, user-generated content, and cross-play as needed.
steps.expect: communication settings match the household rule.

steps.action: **Protect the adult account.** Set a console passcode or require the adult password before changing controls.
steps.expect: the child cannot disable restrictions from the console.

steps.action: **Test with the child account.** Try launching a blocked game, making a purchase, and opening chat.
steps.expect: restrictions trigger exactly where expected.

recipes.verification: When signed in as the child, over-age content, unapproved purchases, out-of-hours play, and restricted chat are blocked or require adult approval.

recipes.title: set screen time limits
recipes.name: set-screen-time-limits
recipes.goal: Set realistic device limits that reduce unwanted screen time without breaking essential access.

steps.action: **Open the built-in screen-time tool.** [BRANCH: iOS | Android | desktop] use Screen Time, Digital Wellbeing, Family Link, or the operating system's focus controls.
steps.expect: the device shows usage, app timers, downtime, or focus settings.

steps.action: **Review actual usage first.** Look at the last 7 days, not just today.
steps.expect: the biggest apps and peak time windows are visible.

steps.action: **Choose app limits for specific drains.** Set timers on social, video, games, or shopping apps rather than every app.
steps.expect: only selected apps will lock or warn after the limit.

steps.action: **Choose downtime for daily boundaries.** Set a sleep, work, school, or family window when most apps are blocked.
steps.expect: the schedule has start and end times.

steps.action: **Keep essentials allowed.** Add phone, maps, messages, calendar, banking, transit, medical, or work apps as needed.
steps.expect: important tasks still work during limits.

steps.action: **Use honest defaults.** Start with a limit you can actually follow, such as 30 minutes less than current use.
steps.expect: the limit is challenging but not instantly ignored.

steps.action: **Handle kids differently from self-limits.** [BRANCH: child | self] for kids, set a parent passcode and content rules. for self, avoid making the override too easy.
steps.expect: the person subject to the limit cannot casually remove it.

steps.action: **Plan for the override trap.** Decide when "one more minute" or "ignore today" is allowed before the prompt appears.
steps.expect: overrides have a rule, not a mood.

steps.action: **Turn on notifications or reports.** Enable weekly summaries or parent reports if useful.
steps.expect: usage feedback arrives without manually checking every day.

steps.action: **Review after one week.** Tighten, loosen, or move limits based on actual misses.
steps.expect: the rule matches behavior better than the first guess.

recipes.verification: During the chosen limit window, a restricted app shows a timer, warning, or block while essential apps remain usable.

recipes.title: set up a baby monitor
recipes.name: set-up-a-baby-monitor
recipes.goal: Set up a baby monitor with safe physical placement, reliable audio/video, appropriate alerts, and restricted account access.

steps.action: **Choose a safe location.** Place or mount the camera at least 3 feet from the crib and out of reach of the child and cords.
steps.expect: no cord, mount, or device can fall into or be pulled into the crib.

steps.action: **Power and pair the monitor.** Follow the vendor pairing steps for the parent unit or phone app.
steps.expect: live audio or video appears on the parent unit or app.

steps.action: **Secure Wi-Fi models.** Connect to the home Wi-Fi, update firmware, and set a strong unique account password.
steps.expect: the app shows current firmware and account access is protected.

steps.action: **Adjust view and audio.** Aim the camera at the sleep area without showing more of the room than needed.
steps.expect: the baby is visible or audible from normal sleep positions.

steps.action: **Set alert sensitivity.** Configure sound, motion, cry, temperature, or breathing alerts according to the model and test each one.
steps.expect: alerts trigger when tested and are not constantly firing.

steps.action: **Limit sharing.** Add only caregivers who need access and remove default or temporary users.
steps.expect: the user list contains only approved caregivers.

steps.action: **Test range and night use.** Walk to normal listening locations and check night vision, volume, and battery.
steps.expect: monitoring works from the places caregivers will actually be.

recipes.verification: The monitor shows reliable audio/video from normal caregiver locations, alerts work at a tolerable sensitivity, cords are out of reach, and only approved caregivers have access.

recipes.title: set up a custom gpt
recipes.name: set-up-a-custom-gpt
recipes.goal: Create a custom chatbot configuration for a specific task with clear instructions, safe knowledge handling, and a test set that catches obvious failures.

steps.action: **Define the job.** Write the assistant's purpose, audience, allowed tasks, refused tasks, and escalation rules.
steps.expect: the scope is narrow enough to test.

steps.action: **Configure instructions.** Enter behavior rules, preferred format, tone, uncertainty handling, and privacy limits.
steps.expect: the assistant has explicit operating rules.

steps.action: **Add knowledge carefully.** [BRANCH: no files | approved files] skip uploads if not needed; upload only documents you have rights to use and that are allowed for the platform.
steps.expect: knowledge sources are intentional and permitted.

steps.action: **Set tool access.** Enable browsing, code, actions, connectors, or image tools only when the task requires them.
steps.expect: the assistant has no unnecessary capabilities.

steps.action: **Test with normal and adversarial prompts.** Try expected questions, unclear requests, prompt-injection attempts, and requests outside scope.
steps.expect: useful answers stay in scope and risky requests are handled safely.

steps.action: **Publish with the right visibility.** Choose private, workspace, link-only, or public visibility according to data and audience.
steps.expect: only intended users can access it.

steps.action: **Monitor and revise.** Review feedback, failures, and outdated instructions on a recurring schedule.
steps.expect: there is a maintenance path after launch.

recipes.verification: The custom GPT answers the test prompts correctly, refuses or redirects out-of-scope prompts, uses only approved knowledge and tools, and is visible only to the intended audience.

recipes.title: set up a guest wifi network
recipes.name: set-up-a-guest-wifi-network
recipes.goal: A separate guest Wi-Fi network is enabled so visitors can use the internet without reaching private computers, phones, storage devices, or smart-home controls.

steps.action: **Open router settings.** Use the router maker's app or admin address while connected to your home network.
steps.expect: you can see Wi-Fi or network settings.

steps.action: **Find guest network controls.** Look for Guest Wi-Fi, Guest access, Visitor network, IoT network, or Additional SSID.
steps.expect: a separate network can be enabled.

steps.action: **Enable the guest network.** Turn on the guest SSID for 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, or both as the router permits.
steps.expect: a new network name appears in the router settings.

steps.action: **Name it clearly.** Use a name that guests can recognize but that does not reveal sensitive details like apartment number or full name.
steps.expect: the guest network is easy to distinguish from the private network.

steps.action: **Set a separate password.** Use a strong passphrase that is different from the private Wi-Fi password.
steps.expect: guests can be given access without exposing the main network password.

steps.action: **Turn on isolation.** Enable settings like guest isolation, block local network access, internet only, or prevent access to LAN.
steps.expect: guests can reach the internet but not private devices.

steps.action: **Separate smart devices if useful.** [BRANCH: guest-only visitors | IoT segregation] Put untrusted smart plugs, cameras, or toys on an IoT/guest network if they do not need local access.
steps.expect: risky devices are separated from laptops and phones.

steps.action: **Test from a phone.** Join the guest network and browse the web, then try to reach a printer, file share, router admin page, or smart hub.
steps.expect: internet works and private resources are blocked.

steps.action: **Share access safely.** Give guests the guest password or QR code, and rotate it when it spreads too widely.
steps.expect: visitors connect without touching the private network.

recipes.verification: A test device on guest Wi-Fi can access the internet but cannot access router administration, local file shares, printers, or private smart-home controls unless explicitly allowed.

recipes.title: set up a hardware security key
recipes.name: set-up-a-hardware-security-key
recipes.goal: Add a hardware security key to important accounts for phishing-resistant sign-in while preserving recovery access.

steps.action: **Choose priority accounts.** Start with email, password manager, financial, work, developer, and cloud accounts.
steps.expect: the first account to secure is identified.

steps.action: **Check compatibility.** Confirm whether the account supports passkeys, FIDO2, WebAuthn, U2F, USB, NFC, or Lightning for your devices.
steps.expect: your key can work with the account and devices.

steps.action: **Register the first key.** Open security settings, add a security key or passkey, touch the key when prompted, and name it clearly.
steps.expect: the account lists the key as registered.

steps.action: **Register a backup key.** Add a second key and store it separately from the first.
steps.expect: loss of one key will not lock you out.

steps.action: **Save recovery codes.** Download or copy backup codes to a password manager or offline secure place. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* removing other sign-in methods before recovery is tested can lock you out.
steps.expect: recovery material is stored before tightening settings.

steps.action: **Test sign-in.** Sign out or use a private browser window and sign in with the key and recovery path.
steps.expect: both normal and backup access work.

steps.action: **Tighten authentication.** Disable weaker methods only if the account supports safe recovery and you accept the lockout risk.
steps.expect: account security is stronger without single-point lockout.

recipes.verification: The account lists at least one working hardware key, a backup key or recovery path is stored and tested, and sign-in succeeds using the key.

recipes.title: set up a home media server
recipes.name: set-up-a-home-media-server
recipes.goal: Set up a home media server that indexes your owned media, streams on your local network, backs up the library, and avoids unnecessary public exposure.

steps.action: **Choose the server device.** Pick a NAS, desktop, mini PC, or always-on laptop with enough storage, network connection, and power reliability.
steps.expect: one device is assigned as the server.

steps.action: **Organize media folders.** Create clear folders such as Movies, TV Shows, Music, and Home Videos on the media drive.
steps.expect: the library has predictable folder paths.

steps.action: **Install media server software.** Install Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, or the NAS vendor media app from its official source.
steps.expect: the server dashboard opens locally.

steps.action: **Add libraries.** Point the server to the media folders and choose the matching content type for each library.
steps.expect: the dashboard starts scanning and shows titles or files.

steps.action: **Create user access.** Set an admin password, create household user profiles, and avoid sharing the admin account.
steps.expect: users can browse media without admin rights.

steps.action: **Test local playback.** Open the server app on a TV, phone, browser, or streaming box on the same network and play sample files.
steps.expect: video and audio play smoothly on local Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

steps.action: **Configure remote access deliberately.** Leave remote access off unless you need it; if enabled, use strong passwords, updates, and the vendor's secure method.
steps.expect: public exposure is either disabled or intentionally configured.

steps.action: **Back up the library and settings.** Back up irreplaceable media and the server configuration to another drive or cloud storage.
steps.expect: a restore copy exists outside the media server device.

recipes.verification: The server dashboard shows indexed libraries, at least one client can play sample media locally, household users have non-admin access, and media plus settings are backed up.

recipes.title: set up a home printer
recipes.name: set-up-a-home-printer
recipes.goal: Your home printer is unpacked, connected to one device, loaded with ink or toner and paper, and able to print a clean test page.

steps.action: **Unpack and remove shipping material.** Take out tape, foam blocks, orange clips, and cardboard from trays, lids, cartridge bays, and the scanner area.
steps.expect: covers and trays move freely with no packing tabs visible.

steps.action: **Place and power the printer.** Set it on a level surface near an outlet and, for Wi-Fi setup, within strong router range. Plug it directly into wall power for setup.
steps.expect: the printer starts and shows a language or setup screen.

steps.action: **Install ink or toner.** Open the cartridge door, remove seals from cartridges, and seat each color in its labeled slot until it clicks or locks.
steps.expect: the printer recognizes the cartridges and stops asking for installation.

steps.action: **Load paper correctly.** Fan plain paper, square the stack, put it print-side down or up as marked on the tray, and slide guides until they touch without bending the paper.
steps.expect: the tray closes and the paper-size prompt matches the loaded paper.

steps.action: **Choose the first connection path.** [BRANCH: USB | Wi-Fi] USB: connect the cable only when the installer asks. Wi-Fi: use the printer screen, WPS, or maker app to join the 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz network the printer supports.
steps.expect: the printer reports connected or the installer finds it.

steps.action: **Install the current driver or app.** Get it from the printer maker's site or app store, not a random driver mirror, then add the printer when prompted.
steps.expect: the printer appears in the system printer list with an online status.

steps.action: **Run alignment or calibration.** Print the alignment page, scan it if the model asks, or confirm the pattern on screen.
steps.expect: the printer stores alignment settings and returns to ready.

steps.action: **Print a test page.** Use the OS test page or a simple one-page document before trying labels, photos, or duplex printing.
steps.expect: one complete page prints with readable text and no missing colors.

recipes.verification: The printer is listed as online on the device and prints a complete one-page test with the expected text or alignment pattern.

recipes.title: set up a legacy contact for your accounts
recipes.name: set-up-a-legacy-contact-for-your-accounts
recipes.goal: Designate trusted legacy contacts or account recovery instructions so family can handle important digital accounts if you die or become incapacitated.

steps.action: **Choose priority accounts.** Start with Apple, Google, Meta/Facebook, Microsoft, password manager, cloud storage, email, financial, and domain registrar accounts.
steps.expect: you have a prioritized account list.

steps.action: **Confirm the contact's identity.** Verify the legacy contact's current email, phone number, and legal name.
steps.expect: you will not send access instructions to an outdated contact.

steps.action: **Add platform legacy contacts.** [BRANCH: Apple | Google | Facebook] use Apple Account > Sign-In and Security > Legacy Contact, Google Inactive Account Manager, or Facebook Memorialization Settings.
steps.expect: the platform shows the selected contact or inactive-account plan.

steps.action: **Save access keys or instructions.** Store any generated access key, recovery code, or written instruction in your password manager or estate documents.
steps.expect: the contact can find the instructions without seeing your passwords today.

steps.action: **Document accounts without legacy tools.** For services without legacy contacts, record the service name, account email, billing impact, and support process.
steps.expect: your executor can identify what exists and whom to contact.

steps.action: **Avoid sharing live passwords casually.** Use emergency access features or sealed instructions instead of texting passwords.
steps.expect: everyday account security is preserved.

steps.action: **Review annually.** Check contacts after relationship changes, moves, new phone numbers, or account changes.
steps.expect: legacy contacts and instructions remain current.

recipes.verification: Each priority account either shows a configured legacy contact/inactive-account plan or appears in a secure instruction list, and the trusted contact knows where the instructions are.

recipes.title: set up a mesh wifi system
recipes.name: set-up-a-mesh-wifi-system
recipes.goal: Replace or extend home Wi-Fi with a mesh system that has a working main router, well-placed nodes, secure network settings, and tested coverage.

steps.action: **Document current network details.** Note modem/gateway model, current Wi-Fi name, password, and any special ISP settings.
steps.expect: you can restore or reuse the old settings if setup fails.

steps.action: **Place the main mesh unit.** Connect it by Ethernet to the modem or gateway and plug it into power.
steps.expect: the main unit powers on and the app can find it.

steps.action: **Set up the network in the app.** Follow the vendor app to create the Wi-Fi name, password, admin account, and automatic updates.
steps.expect: the app reports the main unit online.

steps.action: **Add satellite nodes one at a time.** Place nodes halfway between the main unit and weak areas, not at the far dead zone.
steps.expect: each node joins with a good or excellent connection rating.

steps.action: **Disable duplicate Wi-Fi if needed.** If the old gateway still broadcasts Wi-Fi, turn off its Wi-Fi or put it in bridge mode when appropriate.
steps.expect: devices see one intended network name, not confusing duplicates.

steps.action: **Reconnect important devices.** Join phones, laptops, printers, smart-home hubs, and work devices to the new network.
steps.expect: critical devices show internet access.

steps.action: **Test coverage.** Walk through bedrooms, office, kitchen, and outdoor areas where you need signal and run a speed or video-call test.
steps.expect: each target area has stable connection and acceptable speed.

steps.action: **Secure guest and admin settings.** Enable WPA2/WPA3, create a guest network if needed, and protect the mesh admin account with a strong password and multi-factor authentication if offered.
steps.expect: guests and smart devices do not require sharing the admin password.

recipes.verification: The mesh app shows all nodes online with healthy connection, old duplicate Wi-Fi is disabled or intentionally named, and speed tests or video calls work in the target rooms.

recipes.title: set up a new phone
recipes.name: set-up-a-new-phone
recipes.goal: A new phone ends up holding your accounts, apps, messages, and photos as they were on the old phone, and the old phone is safely wiped only after the new one is confirmed complete.

steps.action: **Back up the old phone first, on purpose.** iPhone: Settings > your name > iCloud > iCloud Backup > Back Up Now, or an encrypted Finder/iTunes backup to a computer. Android: Settings > System > Backup > Back up now (Google One).
steps.expect: a "last backup: just now" timestamp, not one from days ago.

steps.action: **Note what backups miss.** Two-factor authenticator codes, some app logins (banking, WhatsApp), and eSIM often do NOT ride along in a generic backup. List these to handle by hand.
steps.expect: a short written list of apps you will re-authenticate manually.

steps.action: **Handle authenticator apps before wiping anything.** Use the app's built-in transfer (Google Authenticator export, Authy multi-device) or move each 2FA to the new phone while the old one still works.
steps.expect: the new phone generates valid codes for at least one critical account before you go further.

steps.action: **Start the new phone and use the direct transfer flow.** iPhone: Quick Start, hold the phones near each other. Android: "Copy apps & data" with the cable or wireless option. Choose restore-from-backup or device-to-device.
steps.expect: a transfer progress bar with an item count and a time estimate.

steps.action: **Wait for the transfer to finish fully.** Keep both phones close, awake, and on power. Do not "skip" to use the phone early; apps re-download in the background for a while after.
steps.expect: progress reaches 100% and the new phone boots to a home screen resembling the old layout.

steps.action: **Restore and verify each critical app by hand.** Open banking, messaging, email, and photos one at a time. Re-login where prompted, re-approve 2FA. Confirm messages and photos actually appear.
steps.expect: each critical app opens signed in with your real data visible, not an empty first-run screen.

steps.action: **Move your phone number / eSIM.** Physical SIM: swap the tray. eSIM: use the carrier's eSIM transfer in Settings or the carrier app. Make a test call and send a test text.
steps.expect: the new phone shows signal and your number; a test call and text both go through.

steps.action: **Confirm the new phone is complete before touching the old one.** Photos, contacts, messages, 2FA, apps, phone number all verified present.
steps.expect: a deliberate "yes, everything is here" check across all of the above.

steps.action: **Wipe the old phone.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* this erases the old phone permanently. Only after step 8 passes. Sign out of your account first (iPhone: turn off Find My / sign out of iCloud; Android: remove Google account) to release the activation lock, then Settings > Erase All Content and Settings.
steps.expect: the old phone reboots to the "Hello / welcome" first-time setup screen, holding none of your data.

recipes.verification: The new phone shows your contacts, messages, photos, signed-in apps, working 2FA, and your phone number with a successful test call and text; the old phone has been erased to its first-time setup screen only after all of that was confirmed.

recipes.title: set up a robot vacuum
recipes.name: set-up-a-robot-vacuum
recipes.goal: A robot vacuum is charged, connected to its app, mapped, restricted from problem areas, and scheduled with basic maintenance understood.

steps.action: **Place the dock.** Put it against a wall on hard floor with open space around it, near power and Wi-Fi.
steps.expect: the dock sits flat and the charging light works.

steps.action: **Charge the vacuum.** Seat the robot on the dock until the app or indicator shows enough charge for setup.
steps.expect: the robot reports charging.

steps.action: **Install and pair the app.** Use the official app, add the model, and follow Wi-Fi pairing prompts.
steps.expect: the robot appears online in the app.

steps.action: **Prepare the home for mapping.** Open interior doors, lift cords, secure rug tassels, and block areas that could trap the robot.
steps.expect: the floor is passable for a first mapping run.

steps.action: **Run mapping.** [BRANCH: mapping-only run | clean-and-map run] Use mapping-only if offered; otherwise start a full clean and let it finish.
steps.expect: the app shows a map or room outline.

steps.action: **Name rooms and set zones.** Label rooms, split or merge boundaries, and add no-go zones for cords, pet bowls, stairs, thick rugs, or delicate areas.
steps.expect: the map shows named rooms and restricted areas.

steps.action: **Test a targeted clean.** Send the vacuum to one room or zone and watch the start of the run.
steps.expect: it leaves the dock, cleans the chosen area, and returns or asks for help.

steps.action: **Set a schedule.** Pick times when floors are clear and people are not sleeping, and avoid times pets may be loose with messes.
steps.expect: the schedule shows correct days, time, suction or mop mode.

steps.action: **Empty and maintain.** Empty the bin, clean brushes, remove hair, wash or replace filters as allowed, and fill mop tanks only with approved liquid.
steps.expect: the robot reports ready with no maintenance alert.

recipes.verification: The robot completes a targeted cleaning run, returns to the dock, and the app shows a saved map with no-go zones and a schedule.

recipes.title: set up a shared family calendar
recipes.name: set-up-a-shared-family-calendar
recipes.goal: Your household has one shared calendar for family events, with members added, colors and notifications set, and editing rights controlled.

steps.action: **Create a separate calendar.** Make a new calendar named Family, Household, or another shared name instead of sharing your personal calendar.
steps.expect: a new empty calendar appears in your calendar list.

steps.action: **Set the calendar description.** Add a short note such as "shared appointments, school dates, travel, and household reminders."
steps.expect: members can recognize the calendar's purpose.

steps.action: **Add family members.** Invite each person by email or account address.
steps.expect: every member appears as pending or accepted.

steps.action: **Choose who can edit.** [BRANCH: adults edit | everyone edits] give edit rights to people who schedule events and view rights to people who only need awareness.
steps.expect: permissions differ by member if needed.

steps.action: **Color-code the calendar.** Pick a distinct color for the shared calendar, and optionally use event titles or emojis avoided here for each person.
steps.expect: family events stand out from personal events.

steps.action: **Set default notifications.** Add reminders such as one day before and one hour before for events where advance notice matters.
steps.expect: new family events include useful alerts.

steps.action: **Add key recurring events.** Enter school schedules, practices, trash pickup, medication reminders, custody exchanges, or bill dates as appropriate.
steps.expect: repeated family obligations appear on future dates.

steps.action: **Test on each device.** Ask members to accept, show the calendar, and create or view a harmless test event.
steps.expect: everyone sees the same shared calendar on phone and web.

recipes.verification: Each intended member can see the shared family calendar, and only the intended people can create or edit events on it.

recipes.title: set up a smart doorbell
recipes.name: set-up-a-smart-doorbell
recipes.goal: Install a smart doorbell, connect it to Wi-Fi and the vendor app, confirm chime and video behavior, and configure privacy-aware alerts.

steps.action: **Check compatibility and placement.** Confirm wired voltage, battery requirements, Wi-Fi signal, field of view, and local mounting rules.
steps.expect: the doorbell can see the approach and connect reliably.

steps.action: **Turn off power for wired installs.** For wired doorbells, switch off the breaker and verify the old chime no longer rings.
steps.expect: the doorbell circuit is not powered.

steps.action: **Mount the bracket.** Use the included level, anchors, wedge, or angle mount as needed near the existing button or chosen battery location.
steps.expect: the bracket is secure and aligned.

steps.action: **Connect power or battery.** Attach low-voltage wires to a wired unit or insert the charged battery for a battery unit.
steps.expect: the doorbell powers on or enters setup mode.

steps.action: **Add the device in the app.** Scan the QR code, choose the home, and connect to the intended 2.4 GHz or compatible Wi-Fi network.
steps.expect: the app shows the doorbell online with live video.

steps.action: **Test ringing and audio.** Press the doorbell, answer from the phone, and test the indoor chime if used.
steps.expect: notifications, two-way audio, and chime behavior match your choice.

steps.action: **Set motion zones and privacy zones.** Exclude sidewalks, neighbors' windows, and busy roads where the app supports zones.
steps.expect: alerts focus on your property approach.

steps.action: **Review sharing and storage.** Add household members only if needed and choose whether cloud recording, local storage, or no recording is appropriate.
steps.expect: access and recording settings match household consent.

recipes.verification: The app shows the doorbell online, live video and two-way audio work, a press triggers the intended notification or chime, and privacy/motion zones are set.

recipes.title: set up a smart plug
recipes.name: set-up-a-smart-plug
recipes.goal: A smart plug is paired to its app, named clearly, connected to Wi-Fi, and running any schedule or away routine you choose.

steps.action: **Check the load rating.** Read the plug's amperage and wattage limits before plugging in lamps, fans, heaters, or appliances.
steps.expect: the planned device is below the rating.

steps.action: **Install the maker app.** Download the official app named on the box or manual and sign in if required.
steps.expect: the app opens to an add-device flow.

steps.action: **Plug in near the router.** Put the smart plug in a wall outlet for setup, avoiding power strips for the first pairing attempt.
steps.expect: the indicator light turns on or blinks.

steps.action: **Put the plug in pairing mode.** Hold the button until the light blinks in the pattern the app requests.
steps.expect: the app can start scanning or asks for Wi-Fi details.

steps.action: **Connect to the right Wi-Fi band.** [BRANCH: 2.4 GHz only | dual-band supported] Use 2.4 GHz for most smart plugs, or the listed band if the plug supports both.
steps.expect: the app reports successful Wi-Fi connection.

steps.action: **Name the plug by purpose.** Use names such as `Living Room Lamp`, not `Plug 1`, especially if using voice assistants.
steps.expect: the app shows the clear name in the device list.

steps.action: **Test manual control.** Turn the plug off and on from the app while watching the connected device.
steps.expect: the device power changes within a few seconds.

steps.action: **Create a schedule or away routine.** Set on/off times, sunrise/sunset options, or randomized away mode only for suitable devices.
steps.expect: the schedule appears enabled with the correct days and time zone.

steps.action: **Move to final outlet.** Place the plug where it will be used and test control again.
steps.expect: the app still shows online and controls the device.

recipes.verification: The smart plug appears online, switches the connected device from the app, and shows the intended schedule or away routine enabled.

recipes.title: set up a smart speaker routine
recipes.name: set-up-a-smart-speaker-routine
recipes.goal: Create a smart speaker routine that performs the intended actions reliably without exposing private commands or controlling sensitive devices unexpectedly.

steps.action: **Choose a simple routine goal.** Pick a morning, bedtime, leaving home, arrival, or reminder routine with a clear trigger.
steps.expect: the routine has one primary purpose.

steps.action: **Open routine automation settings.** [BRANCH: Alexa | Google Home | Apple Home] open Alexa > More > Routines, Google Home > Automations, or Home > Automation/Shortcuts.
steps.expect: the app shows routine or automation creation controls.

steps.action: **Set the trigger.** Choose voice phrase, time, sunrise/sunset, alarm dismissal, device state, or location if supported.
steps.expect: the trigger is visible and specific.

steps.action: **Add actions in order.** Add lights, speaker volume, weather, calendar, music, announcements, plugs, or thermostat changes one at a time.
steps.expect: the action list matches the intended sequence.

steps.action: **Avoid risky actions.** Do not include door unlocking, oven controls, or security disarming unless the platform requires explicit confirmation and the household agrees.
steps.expect: sensitive devices are absent or protected by confirmation.

steps.action: **Choose target speaker or room.** Set where audio plays and which devices respond.
steps.expect: the routine will not announce private information in the wrong room.

steps.action: **Test and adjust.** Run the routine manually, then trigger it normally once.
steps.expect: each action runs in order with acceptable volume and timing.

recipes.verification: The routine appears in the smart-home app, runs from its normal trigger, performs each action in order, and avoids unintended sensitive device or private-information behavior.

recipes.title: set up a smart thermostat
recipes.name: set-up-a-smart-thermostat
recipes.goal: Install and configure a smart thermostat so heating and cooling work correctly, schedules are sensible, and account/location settings are private.

steps.action: **Confirm compatibility.** Use the vendor compatibility checker and photograph the old thermostat wiring before removing anything.
steps.expect: wire labels and compatibility result are saved.

steps.action: **Turn off HVAC power.** Switch off the HVAC breaker or furnace switch and confirm the old thermostat display turns off.
steps.expect: the thermostat has no power.

steps.action: **Label and move wires.** Label each wire by terminal, remove the old base, and connect wires to the matching terminals on the new base.
steps.expect: each wire is secure in a labeled terminal.

steps.action: **Attach the thermostat and restore power.** Mount the display, turn the breaker back on, and wait for startup.
steps.expect: the thermostat powers on and begins setup.

steps.action: **Configure equipment type.** In the app or thermostat, select heat pump, conventional, boiler, furnace, stages, fuel type, and accessories accurately.
steps.expect: the thermostat accepts the equipment configuration.

steps.action: **Connect Wi-Fi and account.** Join the home Wi-Fi network and sign in with the vendor account.
steps.expect: the app shows the thermostat online.

steps.action: **Test heat, cool, and fan.** Run each mode briefly and listen for the correct equipment.
steps.expect: warm air, cool air, and fan behavior match the selected test.

steps.action: **Set schedule and privacy options.** Configure comfort temperatures, away behavior, geofencing only if wanted, and household access.
steps.expect: schedules and permissions match the household's routine.

recipes.verification: The thermostat appears online in the app, heat/cool/fan tests operate the correct equipment, the schedule is active, and household access and location settings are intentional.

recipes.title: set up a video call
recipes.name: set-up-a-video-call
recipes.goal: You host or join a video call on a platform everyone can reach, with working audio and video confirmed before the scheduled time, and (if hosting) the controls you need to keep the meeting orderly.

steps.action: **Choose the platform for the participants, not the features.** Favor one your guests already have or can join from a browser with no install.
steps.expect: a platform where every participant has a clear path to join.

steps.action: **Create the meeting.** Schedule it (date, time, time zone) or start an instant one; enable a waiting room or passcode for anything non-public.
steps.expect: a meeting exists with a join link and, if set, a passcode.

steps.action: **Share the link the right way.** Send the link plus the time zone and passcode through a channel everyone reads. Do not post a passcode-free link anywhere public.
steps.expect: participants confirm they received a link they can open.

steps.action: **Test audio and video before the call.** Open the app's device settings, pick the correct microphone, speaker, and camera, and use the "test mic/speaker" tool. Headphones prevent the echo that plagues open-speaker calls.
steps.expect: the mic meter moves when you speak; you hear the test tone; your camera preview shows you well-lit and framed.

steps.action: **Set your entry state.** Decide whether you join muted and camera-off; on a large call, muted-on-entry is polite.
steps.expect: you enter in the state you intended, not blasting background noise.

steps.action: **As host, learn the three controls that matter.** Mute-all, admit-from-waiting-room, and remove-participant. Know where they are before you need them.
steps.expect: you can locate mute-all and the participant list within seconds.

steps.action: **Start, admit, and confirm the room can hear each other.** Let people in, ask for a quick audio check, and share your screen only when ready.
steps.expect: participants confirm two-way audio and video; the call is under way.

recipes.verification: The meeting link reached every participant, your microphone, speaker, and camera were confirmed working before the start, the call connected with two-way audio and video, and (as host) you can mute all, admit from the waiting room, and remove a participant.

recipes.title: set up a vpn
recipes.name: set-up-a-vpn
recipes.goal: Your device routes internet traffic through a reputable VPN service, and you have verified that the visible IP address and basic leak checks match the VPN location.

steps.action: **Choose the provider before installing anything.** Prefer a known paid provider with transparent ownership, audited apps, no traffic logging claims, and support for your devices. Avoid random app-store VPNs with vague company names.
steps.expect: one provider selected from its official website or verified app-store listing.

steps.action: **Create the account and download the official app.** Use the provider's website link to reach the desktop installer or the app-store listing. Do not install browser ads, coupon bundles, or lookalike apps.
steps.expect: the official VPN app is installed and opens to a sign-in screen.

steps.action: **Sign in and allow the VPN profile.** On iOS, Android, macOS, or Windows, approve the system prompt that lets the app create a VPN configuration.
steps.expect: the OS shows the provider as an available VPN configuration.

steps.action: **Connect to a nearby server first.** [BRANCH: privacy on public Wi-Fi | region-specific access] choose nearby for speed, or choose the required country only when you actually need that location.
steps.expect: the app reports connected and the OS shows the VPN indicator.

steps.action: **Verify the visible IP address.** Open a reputable IP-check page in a browser and compare it with the VPN app's connected country or city.
steps.expect: the page shows the VPN server's public IP, not your home or mobile carrier IP.

steps.action: **Run a leak check.** Use the provider's DNS leak test or another known leak-test page, then check DNS and WebRTC results.
steps.expect: DNS servers belong to the VPN provider or its chosen resolver, and no home ISP address appears.

steps.action: **Set the everyday behavior.** Enable auto-connect on untrusted Wi-Fi, keep kill switch on if the app offers it, and leave trusted home networks optional if speed matters.
steps.expect: the app reconnects automatically in the situations you selected.

steps.action: **Use it where it helps.** Turn the VPN on for hotel, airport, cafe, school guest Wi-Fi, and any network where you do not trust local operators. Leave it off when it breaks banking, streaming, work apps, or local printers.
steps.expect: you know when the VPN should be on and how to disconnect it.

recipes.verification: The VPN app and OS both show connected, an IP-check page shows the VPN location, a DNS leak test does not reveal the home ISP, and normal browsing still works.

recipes.title: set up an authenticator app
recipes.name: set-up-an-authenticator-app
recipes.goal: Add an authenticator app to an account so sign-ins require both the password and a time-based code.

steps.action: **Install a trusted authenticator.** Use a well-known authenticator app from the official app store or your organization's required app.
steps.expect: the app opens without asking for your account password.

steps.action: **Open account security settings.** Find two-factor authentication, multi-factor authentication, or two-step verification.
steps.expect: the account offers an authenticator app option.

steps.action: **Start authenticator setup.** Choose app-based codes instead of SMS when available.
steps.expect: the site shows a QR code or setup key.

steps.action: **Scan the QR code.** In the authenticator app, add an account and scan the displayed QR code.
steps.expect: a new entry appears with a six-digit or eight-digit changing code.
