steps.action: **Save backup codes first.** Download, print, or write the one-time backup codes before finishing setup.
steps.expect: backup codes are stored somewhere separate from the phone.

steps.action: **Enter the current code.** Type the code from the app into the website before it expires.
steps.expect: the site accepts the code and confirms authenticator setup.

steps.action: **Make a device-loss plan.** Add a second trusted method, backup phone, security key, or recovery email if the account supports it.
steps.expect: losing the phone will not permanently lock the account.

steps.action: **Test in a fresh sign-in.** Sign out or use a private window, then sign in with password plus authenticator code.
steps.expect: the account asks for and accepts the app code.

steps.action: **Remove weaker methods if appropriate.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* removing SMS or email recovery can lock you out if the app is lost, so confirm backup codes and a second method first.
steps.expect: the account security page shows the intended methods only.

recipes.verification: A fresh sign-in succeeds only after entering a current authenticator code, and backup codes are stored off the phone.

recipes.title: set up an email signature
recipes.name: set-up-an-email-signature
recipes.goal: Outgoing email ends with a short, readable signature that gives people the right name, role, and contact details without cluttering replies.

steps.action: **Draft the core signature.** Write two to four lines: name, role or team, organization if needed, and one contact method.
steps.expect: the signature is readable without scrolling.

steps.action: **Keep links as text.** Use normal linked text for website, scheduling page, or profile links instead of image-only badges.
steps.expect: the signature still makes sense if images are blocked.

steps.action: **Avoid heavy formatting.** Use plain fonts, one optional divider, and no large logo unless your workplace requires it.
steps.expect: the signature looks clean in a narrow message pane.

steps.action: **Open signature settings.** In your email app, find Settings > Signature or Settings > See all settings > Signature.
steps.expect: you see an editor for new messages and sometimes replies.

steps.action: **Paste the main signature.** Add the short version for new messages and save it as the default for the account.
steps.expect: a new compose window inserts the signature automatically.

steps.action: **Create a reply variant.** [BRANCH: full signature | reply signature] use the full version for new threads and a one-line version for replies, such as name plus phone.
steps.expect: replies stay compact.

steps.action: **Set a mobile version.** In the phone email app, replace "Sent from my phone" with a short signature or turn the mobile signature off.
steps.expect: mobile messages no longer add a generic footer.

steps.action: **Send a test.** Email yourself from web and mobile, then view the result on a phone and a computer.
steps.expect: line breaks, links, and contact details display correctly.

recipes.verification: A new email and a reply from each device show the intended signature, with correct contact details and working text links.

recipes.title: set up autopay
recipes.name: set-up-autopay
recipes.goal: Autopay is enabled for a bill with the right payment source, amount rule, due-date buffer, and monitoring so payments happen without overdrafts or missed bills.

steps.action: **Open the biller's billing page directly.** Use a bookmark, typed address, or the biller's app.
steps.expect: the account shows your current balance and due date.

steps.action: **Choose the payment source deliberately.** Prefer a source with predictable funds and no processing fee; avoid debit if overdraft risk is high.
steps.expect: you know the source, fees, and whether the biller stores it.

steps.action: **Pick the amount rule.** [BRANCH: full balance | statement balance | minimum due | fixed amount] Choose the smallest rule that still meets your goal without creating debt or late fees.
steps.expect: the autopay setup page shows the chosen rule in plain language.

steps.action: **Set a safe payment date.** Schedule payment several days before the due date while leaving enough paycheck or account buffer to avoid overdraft.
steps.expect: the payment date, due date, and funding date make sense together.

steps.action: **Enter and verify payment details.** Type routing/account or card numbers carefully, then compare the last four digits and billing address.
steps.expect: the saved payment method shows the expected institution and last four digits.

steps.action: **Confirm autopay enrollment.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an authorized autopay can pull money automatically, so confirm amount rule, account, and date before enabling.
steps.expect: status changes to autopay on, enrolled, or automatic payments enabled.

steps.action: **Save the confirmation.** Screenshot or download the autopay page showing amount rule, payment source, and first scheduled date.
steps.expect: proof exists outside the biller site.

steps.action: **Verify the first run.** Check both the biller and payment account after the first scheduled payment.
steps.expect: the biller marks paid and the payment account shows one matching debit or charge.

steps.action: **Monitor monthly.** Keep statement alerts on even after autopay works.
steps.expect: you receive bill amount and payment posted notifications.

recipes.verification: Autopay status is active, first scheduled payment posts once to the biller and payment source, and alerts remain enabled for future bills.

recipes.title: set up do not disturb and focus modes
recipes.name: set-up-do-not-disturb-and-focus-modes
recipes.goal: Configure Do Not Disturb or Focus modes so interruptions are reduced while urgent people and apps can still reach you.

steps.action: **Choose focus scenarios.** List the modes you need, such as Sleep, Work, Driving, Personal, Study, or Meeting.
steps.expect: each mode has a clear purpose.

steps.action: **Open focus settings.** [BRANCH: iPhone | Android | Windows | Mac] use Settings > Focus, Settings > Notifications > Do Not Disturb, Settings > System > Focus, or System Settings > Focus.
steps.expect: the device shows available focus or DND controls.

steps.action: **Allow important people.** Add close family, caregivers, school, work emergency contacts, or repeat callers where appropriate.
steps.expect: urgent contacts are listed as allowed interruptions.

steps.action: **Allow critical apps.** Permit alarms, calendar, medical, security, delivery, or work apps that must break through.
steps.expect: only necessary apps are in the allowed list.

steps.action: **Set schedules or triggers.** Add time, location, calendar, bedtime, driving, or app-based triggers.
steps.expect: the mode turns on automatically under the intended condition.

steps.action: **Customize screens and badges.** Hide notification badges, dim lock screen, or choose a work/home screen if supported.
steps.expect: distracting notifications are visually reduced.

steps.action: **Test an allowed and blocked alert.** Ask a trusted contact to message or call, and send a test notification from a nonallowed app.
steps.expect: allowed alerts arrive and blocked alerts stay silent.

steps.action: **Review status sharing.** Decide whether apps may tell others that notifications are silenced.
steps.expect: focus status sharing matches your privacy preference.

recipes.verification: The chosen focus mode activates by its schedule or trigger, allowed contacts/apps can interrupt, nonallowed notifications are silent, and status sharing is intentional.

recipes.title: set up dual monitors
recipes.name: set-up-dual-monitors
recipes.goal: Connect and configure two monitors so the desktop extends across both screens with the correct order, resolution, scale, and main display.

steps.action: **Connect power and video.** Plug each monitor into power and connect each video cable firmly to the computer or dock.
steps.expect: both monitors show a logo, desktop, or no-signal message.

steps.action: **Select monitor inputs.** Use each monitor's physical input/source button to choose HDMI, DisplayPort, USB-C, or the port you used.
steps.expect: at least one monitor shows the computer desktop.

steps.action: **Open display settings.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] on Windows open Settings > System > Display; on Mac open System Settings > Displays.
steps.expect: the settings page shows two display rectangles or two monitor names.

steps.action: **Detect missing displays.** Click Detect on Windows or hold Option and click Detect Displays on Mac if a screen is absent.
steps.expect: both connected monitors appear in display settings.

steps.action: **Choose extended desktop.** Set the mode to Extend these displays on Windows or arrange displays without mirroring on Mac.
steps.expect: moving the pointer past one screen edge enters the other display.

steps.action: **Arrange screen order.** Drag the display rectangles to match the physical left-right and height position.
steps.expect: the pointer crosses between monitors at the correct edge.

steps.action: **Set resolution and scale.** Choose the recommended resolution and a readable scale for each monitor.
steps.expect: text is sharp and UI elements are a comfortable size on both screens.

steps.action: **Set the main display.** Choose the monitor that should hold the taskbar, Dock, menu bar, or new windows.
steps.expect: primary controls appear on the preferred screen.

recipes.verification: Both monitors are visible in display settings, the desktop extends across them, the pointer crosses in the expected direction, and the main display is the one you chose.

recipes.title: set up email aliases
recipes.name: set-up-email-aliases
recipes.goal: Create email aliases so you can separate identities, filter mail, and disable exposed addresses without replacing your main inbox.

steps.action: **Choose alias strategy.** [BRANCH: provider alias | custom domain | relay service] use provider aliases for simplicity, a custom domain for control, or a relay for disposable forwarding.
steps.expect: the alias source matches your needs.

steps.action: **Create the alias.** Add the alias in the provider settings or relay dashboard and point it to your real inbox.
steps.expect: the alias appears as active.

steps.action: **Send a test message.** Email the alias from another account and confirm it arrives in the main inbox.
steps.expect: forwarding works.

steps.action: **Set filters and labels.** Route mail from the alias to a folder or label and mark the service it belongs to.
steps.expect: alias mail is easy to identify.

steps.action: **Configure sending if needed.** Add send-as settings, verification, SPF, DKIM, or DMARC only when you must reply from the alias.
steps.expect: outgoing mail does not reveal the wrong address.

steps.action: **Record the mapping.** Save which alias belongs to which site in a password manager or account note.
steps.expect: you can disable a leaked alias later.

recipes.verification: A test email to the alias reaches the correct inbox, is labeled or filtered, and any reply path uses the intended sender address.

recipes.title: set up email filters
recipes.name: set-up-email-filters
recipes.goal: Create email rules that label, archive, or route predictable messages so the inbox stays useful without hiding important mail.

steps.action: **Pick one message type.** Start with a newsletter, receipt, alert, or recurring sender instead of building many rules at once.
steps.expect: one sample email is open or selected.

steps.action: **Choose the filter criteria.** Use sender for reliable sources, subject words for recurring notices, and recipient address for aliases.
steps.expect: the preview finds the intended messages and few unrelated ones.

steps.action: **Decide the action.** [BRANCH: label only | label and archive | forward | delete] use label only for important mail, label and archive for low-urgency mail, and delete only for obvious junk.
steps.expect: the rule action matches how quickly you need to see the messages.

steps.action: **Create a clear label or folder.** Use names like Newsletters, Receipts, Travel, or School instead of vague names like Misc.
steps.expect: the destination is easy to scan later.

steps.action: **Apply the rule to matching old mail if useful.** Select the option to filter existing conversations only after checking the preview.
steps.expect: old matching messages move or gain labels as expected.

steps.action: **Keep subscriptions separate from filters.** For unwanted legitimate marketing, use unsubscribe first; filter only if unsubscribe fails or you still need records.
steps.expect: future unwanted mail should decrease rather than just disappear.

steps.action: **Create a newsletter folder.** Send non-urgent reading to a newsletter label or folder and archive it from the inbox.
steps.expect: newsletters remain searchable without crowding daily mail.

steps.action: **Test with a recent message.** Search the sender or subject and confirm the label, archive state, and inbox visibility.
steps.expect: the rule affects the intended messages only.

recipes.verification: A test search shows matching messages have the intended label or folder, inbox state is correct, and unrelated messages are unaffected.

recipes.title: set up email on a new device
recipes.name: set-up-email-on-a-new-device
recipes.goal: Add an existing email account to a new phone, tablet, or computer and confirm it can send, receive, and sync correctly.

steps.action: **Choose the mail app.** Use the provider's official app, the device mail app, or the approved work app.
steps.expect: the app opens an "add account" or "sign in" flow.

steps.action: **Select the provider.** Pick Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, iCloud, Exchange, or "Other" only if your provider is not listed.
steps.expect: the app asks for your email address.

steps.action: **Sign in through the provider page.** Enter the email address and password only on the provider's real login screen.
steps.expect: the provider asks for a password, passkey, or 2FA approval.

steps.action: **Complete 2FA.** Approve the prompt, enter the code, or use a security key.
steps.expect: the app advances to permissions or sync settings.

steps.action: **Use an app password if required.** [BRANCH: modern sign-in | app password] For older mail apps, generate an app-specific password in account security settings.
steps.expect: the app accepts the generated password without exposing your main password.

steps.action: **Choose sync settings.** Select mail, contacts, calendars, notes, sync range, and notification preferences.
steps.expect: the inbox begins loading recent messages.

steps.action: **Verify incoming mail.** Send a test message to the account from another address or refresh the inbox.
steps.expect: the test message appears on the new device.

steps.action: **Verify outgoing mail.** Send a short test message from the new device to another account.
steps.expect: the message appears in Sent and arrives at the destination.

steps.action: **Secure the device.** Enable screen lock and remote wipe options if the device stores work or personal mail.
steps.expect: mail is protected if the device is lost.

recipes.verification: The new device receives a fresh test email, sends a test email that arrives elsewhere, and shows the account under the intended mail app settings.

recipes.title: set up location based reminders
recipes.name: set-up-location-based-reminders
recipes.goal: Create a reminder that alerts when you arrive at or leave a specific place, with location permissions limited to the reminder app.

steps.action: **Choose the reminder app.** [BRANCH: iPhone | Android] use Apple Reminders on iPhone or Google Keep, Google Assistant, Tasks where supported, or another trusted reminder app on Android.
steps.expect: the chosen app can create location-based alerts.

steps.action: **Check app location permission.** [BRANCH: iOS | Android] use Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services or Settings > Location > App location permissions.
steps.expect: the reminder app has location access while needed.

steps.action: **Create the reminder text.** Write a specific action such as "Buy printer paper" or "Return library book."
steps.expect: the reminder clearly says what to do.

steps.action: **Add the location trigger.** Choose Arriving, Leaving, Getting in car, or Getting out of car if available, then enter the address or saved place.
steps.expect: the app shows a map pin or named place.

steps.action: **Adjust the radius if available.** Make the trigger area large enough for the parking lot or building entrance but not the whole neighborhood.
steps.expect: the reminder has a reasonable geofence.

steps.action: **Save and sync.** Save the reminder and confirm it appears on the correct list or account.
steps.expect: the reminder remains visible after closing and reopening the app.

steps.action: **Test with a nearby place if practical.** Create a temporary test reminder for a nearby location and delete it after it fires.
steps.expect: location alerts work on the device.

recipes.verification: The reminder shows the correct text, place, arrival or departure trigger, and account/list, and a test or future visit produces the expected alert.

recipes.title: set up parental controls
recipes.name: set-up-parental-controls
recipes.goal: A child's device and accounts have age-appropriate limits configured through the platform's own family tools, and the child understands the rules well enough that the controls back up a conversation rather than replace it.

steps.action: **Create or link the child's account under a family group.** Use the OS/platform family tool (Family Sharing, Family Link, Microsoft Family, console family) with the child's true age.
steps.expect: the child account appears as a supervised member under your account.

steps.action: **Have the conversation first.** Tell the child what you are turning on and why, and agree on the rules together. Controls a child does not understand become a game to defeat.
steps.expect: the child can restate the main rule in their own words.

steps.action: **Set content age ratings.** Cap app store, video, and browser content to an age band you have discussed, not the strictest possible setting.
steps.expect: a test search for above-band content is blocked or filtered.

steps.action: **Set screen-time and downtime limits.** Configure a daily time budget and a bedtime "downtime" window; allow the apps a child genuinely needs (calls to family, homework) during downtime.
steps.expect: the device shows the schedule and warns as the limit approaches.

steps.action: **Configure purchase and install approval.** Require your approval for new installs and any purchase. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* in-app purchases can spend real money instantly; turn on "ask to buy" and remove any stored card the child can reach before handing the device over.
steps.expect: a test install request lands on your device for approval.

steps.action: **Tune privacy and communication.** Limit who can contact the child, turn off precise location sharing to strangers, and switch profiles to private where the app allows.
steps.expect: the child's profile is not publicly searchable; contact is restricted to approved people.

steps.action: **Record recovery details and schedule a review.** Save the family account password in your password manager, and put a calendar note to revisit the settings as the child gets older.
steps.expect: credentials stored; a review date set.

recipes.verification: The child's account is supervised under your family group with an age-appropriate content level, a screen-time schedule that actually triggers, purchase approval routed to you, restricted contact and location, and a child who can explain the top rule. The family password is stored and a review is scheduled.

recipes.title: set up voicemail
recipes.name: set-up-voicemail
recipes.goal: Your voicemail answers missed calls with a clear greeting, has a private PIN, notifies you when a message arrives, and has enough space for new messages.

steps.action: **Open voicemail setup.** In the Phone app, open Voicemail or press and hold `1` to call the voicemail system.
steps.expect: voicemail opens or a recorded setup menu answers.

steps.action: **Create or confirm the PIN.** Choose a PIN that is not your birthday, phone number, or a repeated digit pattern.
steps.expect: the system accepts the PIN and asks for the next setup item.

steps.action: **Record a short greeting.** Say your name and that callers should leave a message; avoid explaining why you missed the call.
steps.expect: playback sounds clear and includes the right name.

steps.action: **Save the greeting.** [BRANCH: custom greeting | default greeting] keep the custom greeting if it sounds professional, or use the default greeting if you need privacy.
steps.expect: the voicemail menu marks the chosen greeting as active.

steps.action: **Turn on message notifications.** In Phone or carrier voicemail settings, allow voicemail alerts, badges, and transcription if you want it.
steps.expect: missed voicemail messages can show a notification.

steps.action: **Check existing messages.** Play old messages, write down anything needed, then archive or delete messages you no longer need.
steps.expect: the inbox list is short and current.

steps.action: **Fix a full mailbox.** Delete old saved messages, then open the deleted or trash folder and clear it if your carrier has one.
steps.expect: the mailbox storage warning disappears or the message count drops.

steps.action: **Test from another phone.** Call your number, let it go to voicemail, leave a short test, then retrieve it.
steps.expect: the greeting plays, the test message arrives, and you can play it back.

recipes.verification: A test caller hears the active greeting, can leave a message, and your phone shows or lists that message while the mailbox has room for more.

recipes.title: set your homepage
recipes.name: set-your-homepage
recipes.goal: Set the page your browser opens when you click the Home button or start the browser.

steps.action: **Copy or type the homepage address.** Use the exact `https://` address for the page you want.
steps.expect: the address is ready to paste into settings.

steps.action: **Open browser settings.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] open the browser menu and choose `Settings` or `Preferences`.
steps.expect: the browser settings page or window opens.

steps.action: **Find startup or homepage settings.** Search settings for `home`, `startup`, or `new windows`.
steps.expect: controls for the Home button, new windows, or startup pages appear.

steps.action: **Enter the address.** Choose custom page or homepage and paste the desired address.
steps.expect: the setting shows the exact homepage URL.

steps.action: **Test the setting.** Click the Home button or restart the browser if you changed startup pages.
steps.expect: the chosen page opens.

recipes.verification: Clicking the browser Home button or starting the browser opens the chosen homepage URL.

recipes.title: share a calendar
recipes.name: share-a-calendar
recipes.goal: Another person can see or use the correct calendar with the permission level you intend, and you know how to revoke access later.

steps.action: **Choose the exact calendar.** In calendar settings, select the calendar you want to share, not the whole account.
steps.expect: settings show one named calendar.

steps.action: **Review current events.** Check whether private appointments, addresses, notes, or meeting links are visible on that calendar.
steps.expect: you know what the recipient might see.

steps.action: **Pick the sharing method.** [BRANCH: invite by email | share link] use an email invite for named access or a subscription link for read-only viewing when supported.
steps.expect: the sharing panel shows an invite field or link option.

steps.action: **Set permission level.** Choose free/busy only, view details, make changes, or manage sharing based on the recipient's role.
steps.expect: the selected permission appears beside the recipient or link.

steps.action: **Send the invite or link.** Share it through the calendar app or copy the subscription link into a message.
steps.expect: the recipient receives access instructions.

steps.action: **Have them subscribe or accept.** Ask the recipient to accept the invite or add the subscription link in their calendar app.
steps.expect: the calendar appears in their calendar list.

steps.action: **Test visibility.** Create or identify a harmless test event and ask what they can see or edit.
steps.expect: their access matches the permission level.

steps.action: **Record how to revoke.** Return to sharing settings and note where Remove, Stop sharing, or permission changes live.
steps.expect: you can remove access later without searching.

recipes.verification: The recipient can see the selected calendar at the intended permission level, and you can identify the control that revokes their access.

recipes.title: share a large file
recipes.name: share-a-large-file
recipes.goal: Send a large file by cloud link or transfer service while controlling who can access it and for how long.

steps.action: **Check file size and type.** Right-click or inspect file details, then note the extension and size.
steps.expect: you know whether ordinary email attachment limits will fail.

steps.action: **Choose sharing method.** [BRANCH: cloud link | transfer service] Use cloud storage for ongoing collaboration and a transfer service for one-time delivery.
steps.expect: you have selected a service that supports the file size.

steps.action: **Rename clearly.** Use a filename that identifies project, version, and date without sensitive secrets.
steps.expect: the recipient can recognize the file before opening it.

steps.action: **Upload the file.** Place it in the chosen folder or transfer page and wait for upload completion.
steps.expect: the service shows upload complete or the file appears in storage.

steps.action: **Set permissions.** Choose specific people when possible, otherwise set a restricted link with view or download rights only.
steps.expect: the access setting matches the intended recipients.

steps.action: **Set expiry if available.** Add an expiration date for temporary links, especially for personal, financial, legal, or work files.
steps.expect: the link will stop working after the chosen date.

steps.action: **Send the link.** Include file name, size, deadline, and any password in a separate channel if needed.
steps.expect: the recipient receives the link and context.

steps.action: **Confirm access.** Ask the recipient to open or download the file before the deadline.
steps.expect: the recipient confirms successful access.

steps.action: **Clean up access.** Remove the link, revoke broad sharing, or delete the transfer after confirmation.
steps.expect: the file is no longer exposed beyond the intended purpose.

recipes.verification: The intended recipient can access the correct file, and the sharing settings show only the intended audience, permission level, and expiry.

recipes.title: share your location with family safely
recipes.name: share-your-location-with-family-safely
recipes.goal: Share live or periodic location with trusted family members while limiting duration, audience, and notification exposure.

steps.action: **Choose the sharing app.** [BRANCH: iPhone family | Android or mixed family | short trip] use Find My for iPhone groups, Google Maps Location Sharing for mixed devices, or Messages/WhatsApp for temporary sharing.
steps.expect: everyone knows which app will show the location.

steps.action: **Review location permissions.** [BRANCH: iOS | Android] open Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services or Settings > Location > App location permissions and allow only the chosen app.
steps.expect: the chosen app has location access and unrelated apps do not gain new access.

steps.action: **Select recipients carefully.** Add only the family members who need access and verify names, phone numbers, or email addresses.
steps.expect: the recipient list contains no old contacts or group chats.

steps.action: **Set a duration.** Choose one hour, until end of day, indefinitely only for trusted caregivers, or a custom trip duration.
steps.expect: the app shows when sharing will stop or that it is indefinite.

steps.action: **Start sharing.** Confirm the sharing prompt and wait for the recipient to see your location.
steps.expect: the recipient's phone shows your approximate current location.

steps.action: **Tune notifications.** Enable useful arrival/departure notifications only for places everyone agrees to, such as home, school, or work.
steps.expect: notifications are limited to agreed places and people.

steps.action: **Review active sharing.** Open the app's sharing list and remove anyone who no longer needs access.
steps.expect: only intended family members remain.

recipes.verification: The intended family member can see your current location in the chosen app, the sharing duration is visible, and the active sharing list contains only approved recipients.

recipes.title: show hidden files
recipes.name: show-hidden-files
recipes.goal: Temporarily display hidden files and folders so you can inspect or select them.

steps.action: **Open the target folder.** Navigate to the folder where hidden files may be located.
steps.expect: normal files and folders are visible.

steps.action: **Turn on hidden items.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: in File Explorer choose `View > Show > Hidden items`; Mac: press `Shift+Command+.` in Finder.
steps.expect: dimmed or dot-prefixed hidden files appear if present.

steps.action: **Inspect the needed item.** Select or view the hidden file without editing unrelated files.
steps.expect: the target hidden item is visible and identifiable.

steps.action: **Turn hidden items off when finished.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: uncheck `View > Show > Hidden items`; Mac: press `Shift+Command+.` again.
steps.expect: hidden files disappear from normal view.

recipes.verification: Hidden items become visible while the setting is on and are hidden again after the setting is turned off.

recipes.title: sort a spreadsheet by a column
recipes.name: sort-a-spreadsheet-by-a-column
recipes.goal: Sort rows in a spreadsheet by the values in one column while keeping each row's data together.

steps.action: **Select the data range.** Click any cell in the data table or drag across the full range.
steps.expect: the table or intended range is active.

steps.action: **Open sort.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Data > Sort`; Google Sheets: choose `Data > Sort range > Advanced range sorting options`.
steps.expect: a sort dialog opens.

steps.action: **Set header handling.** Check `My data has headers` in Excel or `Data has header row` in Google Sheets if the first row is labels.
steps.expect: column names, not row values, appear as sort choices.

steps.action: **Choose the sort column and order.** Select the column, then choose ascending `A to Z` or descending `Z to A`.
steps.expect: the dialog shows the intended column and direction.

steps.action: **Apply the sort.** Click `OK` in Excel or `Sort` in Google Sheets.
steps.expect: rows reorder and values in the sort column follow the chosen order.

recipes.verification: The full rows remain intact, the selected column is in ascending or descending order, and the header row remains at the top if one exists.

recipes.title: sort files in a folder
recipes.name: sort-files-in-a-folder
recipes.goal: Change how files are ordered in a folder so you can find or compare items more easily.

steps.action: **Open view controls.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: use File Explorer's `Sort` menu or column headers; Mac: use Finder's `View > Sort By` or `View > Show View Options`.
steps.expect: sorting choices are available.

steps.action: **Choose a sort field.** Select `Name`, `Date modified`, `Kind` or `Type`, or `Size`.
steps.expect: files reorder by that field.

steps.action: **Set direction if needed.** Click the column header again or choose ascending or descending order.
steps.expect: newest-to-oldest, oldest-to-newest, A-to-Z, or Z-to-A order matches your choice.

steps.action: **Group only if useful.** Turn grouping on for categories like type or date, or turn it off for a simple list.
steps.expect: the folder layout becomes easier to scan.

recipes.verification: The visible file list is ordered by the selected field and direction in the active folder.

recipes.title: speed up a slow computer
recipes.name: speed-up-a-slow-computer
recipes.goal: Improve everyday computer responsiveness by identifying the main bottleneck, reducing startup load, freeing storage, and applying safe updates.

steps.action: **Restart once.** Save work, restart the computer, and wait five minutes after signing in.
steps.expect: temporary update or memory issues are cleared before diagnosis.

steps.action: **Check storage space.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] open Settings > System > Storage on Windows or System Settings > General > Storage on Mac.
steps.expect: the system shows available space and large categories.

steps.action: **Free obvious storage.** Empty Trash or Recycle Bin, remove downloaded installers, and uninstall apps you recognize and no longer use.
steps.expect: at least 10-20% of the drive is free or the largest clutter category is reduced.

steps.action: **Find heavy processes.** Open Task Manager on Windows or Activity Monitor on Mac and sort by CPU and Memory.
steps.expect: you can identify whether one app is consuming unusual resources.

steps.action: **Disable unneeded startup apps.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] use Task Manager > Startup apps on Windows or System Settings > General > Login Items on Mac.
steps.expect: nonessential apps are disabled from launching at sign-in.

steps.action: **Apply system and browser updates.** Run Windows Update or Software Update, then update browsers and core apps.
steps.expect: updates complete or show a clear pending restart.

steps.action: **Scan for unwanted software.** Run Windows Security or a reputable antivirus scan, and remove suspicious browser extensions you did not install intentionally.
steps.expect: the scan completes and unknown extensions are gone.

steps.action: **Measure again.** Restart and repeat the slow action that triggered the work.
steps.expect: startup, app launch, or browsing feels faster or the remaining bottleneck is clear.

recipes.verification: After a restart, the drive has adequate free space, unnecessary startup apps remain disabled, no obvious process is constantly maxing CPU or memory, and the original slow task completes faster or has a named bottleneck.

recipes.title: split text into columns
recipes.name: split-text-into-columns
recipes.goal: Split text from one spreadsheet column into separate columns using a delimiter.

steps.action: **Back up nearby data.** Confirm the columns to the right are empty or insert new blank columns.
steps.expect: split output will not overwrite important data.

steps.action: **Select the text column.** Click the column letter or select the cells to split.
steps.expect: the combined text cells are highlighted.

steps.action: **Open split tools.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Data > Text to Columns`; Google Sheets: choose `Data > Split text to columns`.
steps.expect: split options appear.

steps.action: **Choose the delimiter.** Select comma, space, tab, semicolon, or custom delimiter.
steps.expect: the preview shows text separated into the expected columns.

steps.action: **Apply the split.** Finish the wizard in Excel or accept the delimiter in Google Sheets.
steps.expect: each part appears in its own column.

recipes.verification: The original combined text is separated into adjacent columns, and no intended data to the right was overwritten.

recipes.title: spot a deepfake
recipes.name: spot-a-deepfake
recipes.goal: Evaluate whether audio or video may be a deepfake by checking provenance, content, technical clues, and corroborating sources.

steps.action: **Capture the claim.** Record what the media is alleged to show, who shared it, when, and where.
steps.expect: the verification target is specific.

steps.action: **Check the source trail.** Look for the earliest upload, original account, platform labels, content credentials, or creator disclosure.
steps.expect: provenance is known or marked missing.

steps.action: **Inspect technical signs.** Watch for lip-sync mismatch, unnatural blinking, inconsistent lighting, warped jewelry, audio glitches, or odd pauses.
steps.expect: suspicious artifacts are documented.

steps.action: **Compare with known records.** Search for the same event, speech, outfit, room, weather, and public schedule from trusted sources. [BRANCH: public figure | private person] use public records for public figures; avoid spreading private-person media.
steps.expect: context supports, contradicts, or fails to verify the media.

steps.action: **Check for corroboration.** Look for independent witnesses, full-length footage, transcripts, or reputable reporting.
steps.expect: the clip is not evaluated in isolation.

steps.action: **State confidence carefully.** Label the media verified, likely authentic, likely manipulated, or unverified, and explain why.
steps.expect: the conclusion does not overclaim.

recipes.verification: The final assessment cites the original or earliest source found, at least one corroborating or contradicting source, and a confidence label with reasons.

recipes.title: spot a fake website
recipes.name: spot-a-fake-website
recipes.goal: Decide whether a website is likely legitimate before entering passwords, personal data, or payment details.

steps.action: **Pause before interacting.** Do not type passwords, card numbers, or codes until the site passes basic checks.
steps.expect: no sensitive data has been submitted yet.

steps.action: **Check the URL exactly.** Read the domain from right to left before the first single slash, watching for misspellings, extra words, and strange endings.
steps.expect: the domain matches the real organization exactly or raises a concern.

steps.action: **Treat the padlock as limited.** Confirm HTTPS is present, but remember it only means the connection is encrypted.
steps.expect: you do not treat the padlock as proof the business is real.

steps.action: **Reach the site independently.** Open a new tab and search for the organization or use a saved bookmark instead of the link that brought you there.
steps.expect: the independent route lands on the same domain or a different official one.

steps.action: **Inspect contact and policy pages.** Look for a real address, support channel, return policy, privacy policy, and consistent company name.
steps.expect: business details are specific and consistent.

steps.action: **Look for payment red flags.** Watch for wire transfer, crypto, gift cards, payment through friends-and-family, or pressure to bypass normal checkout.
steps.expect: payment options look standard for the transaction.

steps.action: **Check outside reviews.** Search the domain plus "reviews", "scam", or "complaints" and read recent independent results.
steps.expect: there is a track record beyond the site's own testimonials.

steps.action: **Test the offer against reality.** Compare prices, availability, and urgency claims with known retailers or official sites.
steps.expect: extreme discounts or impossible stock are treated as warnings.

steps.action: **Decide before submitting.** [BRANCH: looks legitimate | uncertain or suspicious] proceed with a low-risk payment method, or close the site and use an official channel.
steps.expect: sensitive data is entered only on a site you can justify trusting.

recipes.verification: Before entering sensitive data, the exact domain, independent access route, business details, reviews, and payment method all match a legitimate organization.

recipes.title: spot a phishing email
recipes.name: spot-a-phishing-email
recipes.goal: A suspicious email correctly classified as phishing or legitimate using a repeatable check sequence — and the phishing one neutralized without a single click, because the click *is* the attack.

steps.action: **Read the pressure, not just the content.** Phishing's signature is manufactured urgency plus a demanded action: account suspended, package held, invoice overdue, boss needs gift cards, "unusual sign-in." Legitimate institutions rarely demand same-hour action by email link.
steps.expect: a pressure-score; high pressure raises the bar for every following check.

steps.action: **Inspect the true sender address, not the display name.** Expand the sender details: display "PayPal" wrapping `paypal-security@accounts-verify.net` is the tell. Lookalike domains (rn for m, extra words, wrong TLD) are the industry standard.
steps.expect: either the institution's exact known domain, or your answer.

steps.action: **Hover, never click, the links.** Hold/long-press or hover to preview each URL: the visible text and the destination diverge in phishing, and the destination's *registered domain* (the part before the first single slash, read right-to-left) is the truth. `paypal.com.secure-login.info` belongs to `secure-login.info`.
steps.expect: every link's real destination read; one mismatch convicts the whole email.

steps.action: **Audit the remaining tells.** Generic greeting ("Dear Customer") where the real institution knows your name; attachment types that execute (.html, .zip, .docm — unexpected attachments are hostile until proven otherwise); reply-to differing from sender; and, decreasingly, language errors (modern phishing is fluently written — absence of typos proves nothing now).
steps.expect: an accumulating verdict, weighted toward the sender and link evidence.

steps.action: **Verify through your own channel when stakes exist.** Anything touching money, logins, or your employer: open the institution's site or app by *typing the address* or using your bookmark (`accounts/log-in` step 1's law), or call the number from your card/statement. The real account's own message center confirms or denies in seconds.
steps.expect: ground truth obtained without the email's participation.

steps.action: **Sentence and execute.** Phishing: report via the mail client's report-phishing button (it trains everyone's filters), then delete; work email forwards to IT/security first — they genuinely want it. Legitimate after all: proceed via your own channel anyway, having lost nothing.
steps.expect: the email dispatched appropriately; zero of its links clicked either way.

recipes.verification: The verdict was reached from sender, links, and out-of-band verification — not from the email's own claims; nothing was clicked pre-verdict; the phish was reported, not just deleted; and any already-clicked exposure triggered the password/2FA/card protocol within minutes, not days.

recipes.title: spot a phone scam
recipes.name: spot-a-phone-scam
recipes.goal: A suspicious phone call is handled without giving money, codes, account access, or private information, and legitimate issues are verified by calling back through official numbers.

steps.action: **Pause the conversation.** Do not answer security questions, confirm personal details, or follow instructions while surprised.
steps.expect: the caller has not received useful information.

steps.action: **Listen for pressure and secrecy.** Scam callers push fear, time limits, "do not tell anyone", arrest threats, account closure, or family emergency stories.
steps.expect: pressure makes the call untrusted.

steps.action: **Listen for payment tells.** Gift cards, crypto, wire transfer, payment apps, remote access software, and one-time codes are red flags.
steps.expect: any such demand is treated as scam evidence.

steps.action: **Refuse remote control or code sharing.** Do not install apps, read verification codes, or approve login prompts for a caller.
steps.expect: no account or device access has been granted.

steps.action: **End the call politely or silently.** Say you will call back through the official number, then hang up.
steps.expect: the caller cannot keep escalating pressure.

steps.action: **Find the official number yourself.** Use the number on your card, statement, official website, app, or prior verified contact.
steps.expect: the number is independent of the incoming call or voicemail.

steps.action: **Call back and verify.** Ask whether the claimed issue exists.
steps.expect: the real organization confirms, denies, or documents next steps.

steps.action: **Report and block scam calls.** Use phone blocking, carrier spam tools, and appropriate fraud reporting channels.
steps.expect: the number is blocked and the call is recorded for reference.

recipes.verification: No money, codes, remote access, or private information were given to the incoming caller, and any claimed issue was checked through an official callback number.

recipes.title: spot a scam text message
recipes.name: spot-a-scam-text-message
recipes.goal: A suspicious text message is identified as scam or legitimate without clicking its link, and scam messages are reported and blocked.

steps.action: **Stop before tapping anything.** Treat links, attachments, and phone numbers in the message as untrusted.
steps.expect: no link has opened and no reply has been sent.

steps.action: **Read the pressure pattern.** Look for urgency, threats, prizes, failed delivery, unpaid toll, bank lock, tax refund, or "reply YES" prompts.
steps.expect: pressure or reward language raises suspicion.

steps.action: **Inspect the sender and link preview.** Long-press only if your phone previews safely; otherwise do not interact.
steps.expect: the sender is a short code, unknown number, or spoofable name, and any link domain can be judged.

steps.action: **Compare against your real account.** Open the company's official app or type its website yourself.
steps.expect: the real account either confirms the issue or shows nothing is pending.

steps.action: **Verify through an official channel.** Call the number on your card, statement, delivery account, or government website, not the text.
steps.expect: confirmation comes from a source independent of the message.

steps.action: **Do not reply to scam texts.** Replying can confirm your number is active.
steps.expect: the conversation remains unanswered.

steps.action: **Report and block.** Use the phone's Report Junk/Spam option or forward SMS scams to the carrier reporting number where available, then block the sender.
steps.expect: the thread is marked reported or the sender is blocked.

steps.action: **Act if you already clicked or entered data.** Change affected passwords, enable 2FA, contact the bank/card issuer, and watch accounts.
steps.expect: exposed accounts are secured through official apps or websites.

recipes.verification: No scam link was used for login or payment, the issue was checked through an official channel, and scam messages were reported and blocked.

recipes.title: stop a page from loading
recipes.name: stop-a-page-from-loading
recipes.goal: Stop a web page from continuing to load when it is slow, wrong, or unwanted.

steps.action: **Use the stop control.** Click the `X` stop button in the address bar or toolbar while the page is loading.
steps.expect: the loading spinner stops or changes back to a reload icon.

steps.action: **Use the keyboard if needed.** Press `Esc` while the page is loading.
steps.expect: the browser stops requesting more page content.

steps.action: **Check what loaded.** Look at the visible page and address bar.
steps.expect: the tab stays on the partially loaded or previous page without continuing to load.

steps.action: **Decide next action.** Close the tab, edit the address, or press Reload if you stopped it accidentally.
steps.expect: the browser follows the action you choose.

recipes.verification: The loading indicator stops, the browser no longer shows active page loading, and no unwanted download is continuing.

recipes.title: sum a column
recipes.name: sum-a-column
recipes.goal: Calculate the total of numbers in one spreadsheet column.

steps.action: **Click the total cell.** Select the empty cell below or beside the numbers.
steps.expect: the intended total cell is active.

steps.action: **Enter the sum formula.** Type `=SUM(B2:B20)`, replacing `B2:B20` with the actual number range.
steps.expect: the formula appears with the selected range highlighted.

steps.action: **Confirm the total.** Press `Enter` or `Return`.
steps.expect: the total appears in the cell.

steps.action: **Check the included cells.** Click the total cell and inspect the range in the formula bar.
steps.expect: the range covers all intended numbers and excludes labels or unrelated rows.

recipes.verification: The total cell contains a `SUM` or `SUBTOTAL` formula whose range matches the intended column cells, and the displayed result changes when one included number changes.

recipes.title: summarize a document with ai
recipes.name: summarize-a-document-with-ai
recipes.goal: Generate a useful document summary with AI while protecting sensitive content and checking that the summary reflects the source.

steps.action: **Classify the document.** Decide whether it contains confidential, regulated, personal, privileged, or copyrighted material.
steps.expect: you know whether the chosen AI tool is appropriate.

steps.action: **Prepare the input.** Remove unnecessary pages, redact sensitive identifiers, and keep section headings or page numbers if possible.
steps.expect: the uploaded text contains only what the task needs.

steps.action: **Set summary requirements.** Ask for audience, length, format, key points, decisions, open questions, and page or section references.
steps.expect: the model has a concrete target.

steps.action: **Generate the summary.** Upload or paste the document and request that uncertain or missing points be labeled clearly. [BRANCH: full document | excerpt] use excerpts for sensitive or very long material.
steps.expect: you receive a structured summary.

steps.action: **Cross-check claims.** Compare names, numbers, deadlines, obligations, and conclusions against the original.
steps.expect: important facts are confirmed or corrected.

steps.action: **Store or delete output.** Save the checked summary in the right location and delete uploads or chats if policy requires it.
steps.expect: document handling follows your retention needs.

recipes.verification: The final summary includes the required format, covers each important section, and every critical name, number, deadline, or obligation matches the original document.

recipes.title: take a screenshot of part of the screen
recipes.name: take-a-screenshot-of-part-of-the-screen
recipes.goal: Capture a selected area of the screen as an image.

steps.action: **Prepare the screen.** Arrange windows and hide private tabs, notifications, and account details.
steps.expect: only the intended content is visible near the capture area.

steps.action: **Start area capture.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac] Windows: press `Windows+Shift+S`; Mac: press `Command+Shift+4`.
steps.expect: the cursor changes to a crosshair or snipping tool.

steps.action: **Select the region.** Drag around the exact area to capture, then release.
steps.expect: the selected area flashes, copies, or opens as a screenshot preview.

steps.action: **Save or paste the screenshot.** Click the notification to save, or paste into the destination with `Ctrl+V` or `Command+V`.
steps.expect: the screenshot appears in the file location or target app.

steps.action: **Inspect the image.** Open or zoom the screenshot before sharing.
steps.expect: no unintended private information is visible.

recipes.verification: The saved or pasted screenshot contains only the intended screen region and is readable.

recipes.title: take a screenshot
recipes.name: take-a-screenshot
recipes.goal: You capture the correct part of the screen, find the saved image, and optionally annotate it without exposing unnecessary private information.

steps.action: **Choose the capture area.** [BRANCH: full screen | window | region] use full screen for context, window for one app, or region when only a small detail matters.
steps.expect: you know what will be included and what should be excluded.

steps.action: **Use the platform shortcut.** Windows: `Win+Shift+S` for Snipping Tool or `PrtScn`; macOS: `Shift+Command+5` or `Shift+Command+4`; Chromebook: `Ctrl+Show windows`; iPhone: side button plus volume up; Android: power plus volume down on most phones.
steps.expect: a capture overlay, flash, or thumbnail appears.

steps.action: **Select the region or window if prompted.** Drag around the exact area, or click the target window. Include enough surrounding context for the recipient to understand it.
steps.expect: the selected area is captured.

steps.action: **Find where it saved.** Windows Snipping Tool often copies to clipboard and may save under Pictures or Screenshots; macOS saves to Desktop unless changed; phones save to Photos or Gallery; Chromebooks save to Downloads.
steps.expect: the screenshot is visible in the expected location or clipboard.

steps.action: **Annotate only what helps.** Use Markup, Snipping Tool, Preview, Photos, or a trusted editor to draw arrows, boxes, or blur sensitive details.
steps.expect: the important area is obvious and private details are hidden if needed.

steps.action: **Check image clarity.** Open the screenshot before sending and zoom in on the important text.
steps.expect: text and controls are readable at normal viewing size.

steps.action: **Share the right file.** Attach the image file, paste from clipboard, or drag it into the message or support form.
steps.expect: the recipient or form shows the screenshot preview.

recipes.verification: The screenshot file or clipboard image shows exactly the intended content, is readable, and contains no avoidable private information.

recipes.title: toggle dark mode
recipes.name: toggle-dark-mode
recipes.goal: Switch the device or app between light mode and dark mode.

steps.action: **Open appearance settings.** [BRANCH: Windows | Mac | mobile-app] Windows: Settings > Personalization > Colors; Mac: System Settings > Appearance; mobile: open Display or Appearance settings.
steps.expect: light and dark appearance options are visible.

steps.action: **Choose the mode.** Select `Dark`, `Light`, or automatic scheduling.
steps.expect: menus and windows change appearance.

steps.action: **Check app-specific settings.** If one app does not follow the system, open that app's theme or appearance setting.
steps.expect: the app uses the intended theme.

steps.action: **Confirm readability.** Look at text, icons, and buttons in a common app.
steps.expect: contrast is comfortable and content remains readable.

recipes.verification: The operating system or target app visibly uses the selected light, dark, or automatic appearance setting.

recipes.title: block a merchant from recharging
recipes.name: block-a-merchant-from-recharging
recipes.goal: You stop a merchant from charging you again by canceling authorization at the merchant and, when needed, blocking future charges with the payment provider.

steps.action: **Identify the recurring authority.** Match past charges to a subscription, billing agreement, trial, account wallet, or merchant authorization.
steps.expect: you know who is initiating the recharge and through which payment method.

steps.action: **Cancel at the merchant first when possible.** Use account settings or support to cancel the plan, trial, or authorization and save confirmation.
steps.expect: the merchant status shows canceled, closed, or no future renewal.

steps.action: **Remove stored payment credentials.** Delete the saved card, revoke wallet authorization, or remove the billing agreement if the platform allows it.
steps.expect: the merchant no longer lists an active payment method or agreement.

steps.action: **Open issuer or payment-provider controls.** In the bank, card, or wallet app, look for merchant controls, stop payment, subscription controls, virtual card lock, or charge block.
steps.expect: the provider shows options to block, lock, replace, or dispute future merchant charges.

steps.action: **Choose the least disruptive block that works.** [BRANCH: virtual card, lock or delete that merchant card | card network merchant block available, block the descriptor | bank ACH debit, request stop payment | no merchant block, replace card if risk justifies it]
steps.expect: future charges from the merchant are blocked or the vulnerable credential is no longer usable.

steps.action: **Confirm consequences.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before blocking or replacing a card, confirm it will not break essential bills, payroll, refunds, or legitimate subscriptions.
steps.expect: the block or replacement affects only the intended merchant as much as possible.

steps.action: **Monitor the next billing cycle.** Set an alert for the merchant name and amount, then check statements after the expected recharge date.
steps.expect: no new posted charge appears, or an attempted charge is declined.

recipes.verification: The merchant account shows canceled or no active authorization, the payment provider shows a block, lock, stop payment, or replaced credential for the merchant, and no new posted charge appears after the next expected billing date.

recipes.title: cancel a recurring charge in settings
recipes.name: cancel-a-recurring-charge-in-settings
recipes.goal: You cancel a recurring charge from the service's own account settings and keep proof that future billing should stop.

steps.action: **Confirm the recurring charge source.** Match the card or bank transaction descriptor to the service account, app store, or billing provider.
steps.expect: you know which account and platform controls the subscription.

steps.action: **Open billing or subscription settings.** Sign in through the official website and navigate to Account, Billing, Subscriptions, Membership, or Manage plan.
steps.expect: the active plan, price, billing interval, renewal date, and payment method are visible.

steps.action: **Check cancellation consequences.** Read whether cancellation ends service immediately or at the end of the paid period.
steps.expect: you understand what access, credits, storage, or data may be lost and when.

steps.action: **Start the cancellation flow.** Choose Cancel, End subscription, Manage renewal, or similar.
steps.expect: the service shows a confirmation path, retention offer, or reason survey.

steps.action: **Decline retention offers that do not meet your goal.** [BRANCH: acceptable discount, switch only if the new price and end date are explicit | no acceptable offer, continue cancellation]
steps.expect: the next screen either confirms a new lower plan or continues toward cancellation.

steps.action: **Confirm the final cancellation.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before confirming, verify the account, plan, renewal date, and any data-loss warning.
steps.expect: the site displays "canceled," "expires on," or "will not renew" with a confirmation number or email notice.

steps.action: **Save proof.** Download, print to PDF, or screenshot the confirmation page and save the confirmation email.
steps.expect: you have a dated record showing the plan will not renew.

steps.action: **Remove or monitor the payment method if appropriate.** If the service allows it after cancellation, delete the saved card; otherwise set a card alert for the old price.
steps.expect: either the card is removed or you have a monitoring rule for unexpected future charges.

recipes.verification: The subscription status shows canceled or non-renewing, the next billing date is removed or marked as an access-expiration date, and a dated confirmation page or email is saved.

recipes.title: compare prices with a browser tool
recipes.name: compare-prices-with-a-browser-tool
recipes.goal: You use a browser price-comparison or coupon tool to verify the best available price without handing over unnecessary data or being steered into a worse checkout.

steps.action: **Choose a reputable tool.** Use a known price tracker, coupon tool, or shopping comparison site with clear ownership, reviews, and privacy policy.
steps.expect: the tool's publisher and data practices are identifiable.

steps.action: **Review permissions before enabling.** Check whether the extension can read all sites, shopping sites only, or checkout pages.
steps.expect: you understand what browsing and purchase data the tool may access.

steps.action: **Search by exact product identifiers.** Use model number, UPC, ISBN, SKU, size, color, and condition rather than broad product names.
steps.expect: comparison results match the item you intend to buy.

steps.action: **Compare all-in totals.** Include item price, shipping, taxes, fees, membership requirements, coupons, delivery speed, return cost, and seller reputation.
steps.expect: each candidate has a comparable final cost.

steps.action: **Check price history and coupon reliability.** Review recent price drops, normal range, and whether coupons actually apply to your cart.
steps.expect: you know whether the current price is good or just advertised as a deal.

steps.action: **Verify merchant legitimacy.** For the cheapest seller, check reviews, return policy, and payment protections before leaving a trusted merchant.
steps.expect: the lower price does not rely on an unsafe seller or irreversible payment.

steps.action: **Use the tool at checkout only if needed.** Apply coupon codes or cashback deliberately. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before paying, confirm the final merchant, total, coupon, shipping, return policy, and that no unwanted membership was added.
steps.expect: checkout shows the best acceptable all-in price.

steps.action: **Disable or limit the tool after purchase.** Turn off site access or uninstall if you do not want ongoing browsing collection.
steps.expect: the extension no longer has broad access beyond your intended use.

recipes.verification: Before payment, at least two legitimate purchase options have been compared on all-in total for the exact item, the chosen checkout is at or below your maximum price, and any browser tool permissions are limited or disabled afterward.

recipes.title: complete a multi step checkout
recipes.name: complete-a-multi-step-checkout
recipes.goal: You complete an online checkout accurately, avoid unwanted add-ons, and receive a valid order confirmation.

steps.action: **Review the cart contents.** Confirm item names, variants, sizes, quantities, dates, subscriptions, and delivery method.
steps.expect: cart contains only intended purchases.

steps.action: **Check seller and return terms.** Verify merchant identity, delivery estimate, return window, warranty, cancellation policy, and support channel.
steps.expect: the purchase source and remedy path are acceptable.

steps.action: **Enter shipping or service details.** Use the correct recipient, address, phone, email, and delivery instructions.
steps.expect: address validation succeeds or the exact intended address is selected.

steps.action: **Apply discounts and credits.** Enter promo codes, gift cards, store credits, or loyalty rewards and verify the reduction.
steps.expect: checkout total decreases by the expected amount.

steps.action: **Choose payment deliberately.** Select card, wallet, virtual card, or financing based on protection, fees, and budget.
steps.expect: payment method is accepted and no unwanted financing is selected.

steps.action: **Remove unwanted extras.** Decline preselected insurance, tips, subscriptions, donations, expedited shipping, or bundles unless intentional.
steps.expect: final review shows only chosen add-ons.

steps.action: **Perform the final review.** Compare total price against your cap, shipping date, billing address, and refund policy. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* clicking place order authorizes payment and may start fulfillment immediately.
steps.expect: final checkout page is correct and within budget.

steps.action: **Place the order once.** Submit payment and wait for completion without refreshing.
steps.expect: order confirmation page with order number.

steps.action: **Save and verify confirmation.** Check email or account order history for status, total, merchant, and delivery details.
steps.expect: a saved confirmation matching the intended purchase.

recipes.verification: The merchant account or email shows one order confirmation number with the intended items, delivery details, and final total at or below the price cap.

recipes.title: create a shopping account safely
recipes.name: create-a-shopping-account-safely
recipes.goal: You create a shopping account with enough security and privacy controls to buy safely without oversharing.

steps.action: **Verify the merchant site.** Navigate directly or from a trusted search result and confirm the domain and HTTPS.
steps.expect: account creation happens on the legitimate site.

steps.action: **Use a unique email strategy.** Choose your primary email, an alias, or a masked email depending on trust and receipt needs.
steps.expect: the account can receive confirmations without exposing unnecessary identity.

steps.action: **Create a strong unique password.** Generate and save a password in a password manager.
steps.expect: password manager stores the new login.

steps.action: **Limit required profile data.** Enter only required name, contact, and address details; skip optional birthday, gender, or preferences unless useful.
steps.expect: account profile contains minimal necessary information.

steps.action: **Enable security controls.** Turn on two-factor authentication or passkeys if available, and verify the recovery email or phone.
steps.expect: login requires the added security factor or passkey.

steps.action: **Set communication preferences.** Opt out of marketing texts, emails, and data sharing where available.
steps.expect: preferences show only transactional messages or desired subscriptions.

steps.action: **Review saved data choices.** Decide whether to save shipping address or payment method based on purchase frequency and account trust. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some profile data may be copied into merchant records after orders, so avoid optional oversharing.
steps.expect: only intentional data is saved.

steps.action: **Confirm account creation.** Click the verification email or code and log in once successfully.
steps.expect: account dashboard opens under the new credentials.

recipes.verification: You can log in to the verified merchant account with a unique saved credential, security controls are enabled where available, and only necessary personal data is stored.

recipes.title: delete a saved card from a site
recipes.name: delete-a-saved-card-from-a-site
recipes.goal: You remove a stored payment card from a site so it cannot be used for future checkouts or automatic charges through that account.

steps.action: **Open payment settings from the official site.** Navigate to Account, Wallet, Payment methods, Billing, or Membership settings.
steps.expect: saved cards are listed with brand, last four digits, and expiration date.

steps.action: **Identify the exact card.** Compare brand, last four digits, expiration date, and billing address to the card you intend to remove.
steps.expect: only the target card is selected for removal.

steps.action: **Check dependencies.** Look for subscriptions, active orders, preorders, rentals, or account balances tied to the card.
steps.expect: you know whether deleting the card will interrupt an active obligation.

steps.action: **Add a replacement if required.** [BRANCH: site requires a default card, add and verify a safer replacement first | no default required, continue deletion]
steps.expect: the target card is no longer the only eligible payment method if a default is required.

steps.action: **Delete the card.** Click Remove, Delete, or Trash for the target card. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the last four digits before removing; future payments may fail if this was the only valid method.
steps.expect: a confirmation prompt appears or the card disappears from the wallet.

steps.action: **Confirm removal.** Complete any password, multi-factor, or modal confirmation.
steps.expect: the card is absent from the saved payment list or marked removed.

steps.action: **Check recurring billing separately.** Open subscriptions or orders to ensure they did not retain the deleted card in a separate billing profile.
steps.expect: no active recurring charge still points to the removed card.

recipes.verification: The target card's brand, last four digits, and expiration no longer appear in the site's saved payment methods, and no active subscription or order lists that card as its billing method.

recipes.title: dispute a charge in an app
recipes.name: dispute-a-charge-in-an-app
recipes.goal: You dispute an incorrect, unauthorized, duplicate, or undelivered charge through the bank, card, or payment app and keep enough evidence to track the case.

steps.action: **Identify the exact transaction.** Open the posted transaction and confirm merchant descriptor, date, amount, card, and status.
steps.expect: you can distinguish the disputed charge from authorizations, tips, or legitimate duplicates.

steps.action: **Try the merchant path when appropriate.** For non-fraud issues, contact the merchant first and save the response or lack of response.
steps.expect: you have merchant evidence or a reason to escalate directly.

steps.action: **Open the dispute flow.** In the financial app, choose Report a problem, Dispute charge, Get help, or similar.
steps.expect: the app asks for the dispute reason and transaction details.

steps.action: **Choose the accurate reason.** [BRANCH: unauthorized, select fraud/unauthorized and be ready to replace the card | duplicate, select duplicate charge | canceled service, select charged after cancellation | goods not received, select non-receipt]
steps.expect: the selected category matches your evidence.

steps.action: **Upload concise evidence.** Attach receipts, cancellation confirmations, tracking screenshots, merchant chat logs, or saved receipts.
steps.expect: the case file contains documents that directly support the claim.

steps.action: **Submit the dispute.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the claim is truthful and the amount is correct before submitting because the bank may contact the merchant and restrict the card.
steps.expect: the app issues a case number, provisional credit notice, or investigation timeline.

steps.action: **Save the case record.** Screenshot or export the case number, submitted reason, amount, and expected response date.
steps.expect: you have a dated record independent of the app screen.

steps.action: **Monitor and respond.** Check messages from the issuer and answer requests for more evidence before deadlines.
steps.expect: the dispute remains open, credited, won, denied, or awaiting your response with clear status.

recipes.verification: The app shows a submitted dispute for the correct posted transaction amount, with a case number or investigation status saved, and any required evidence has been uploaded before the stated deadline.

recipes.title: export your order history
recipes.name: export-your-order-history
recipes.goal: You export a usable order history from a merchant or marketplace account so purchases can be audited, summarized, returned, reimbursed, or archived.

steps.action: **Define the export scope.** Choose the date range, order statuses, and categories you need before opening the account tools.
steps.expect: a clear scope such as "all completed orders from 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31."

steps.action: **Open order history or privacy tools.** Sign in directly through the merchant's site and look for Orders, Purchase history, Account data, Privacy, or Download data.
steps.expect: a page lists past orders or offers a data export request.

steps.action: **Choose the most structured format available.** Prefer CSV or JSON for analysis; use PDF only if no structured export exists.
steps.expect: the site shows an export, download, or request option with the chosen format.

steps.action: **Filter to the intended range.** Apply date, order status, marketplace, or account filters.
steps.expect: the on-screen count or preview matches the expected period and excludes unrelated orders.

steps.action: **Request or download the export.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* if the request emails a data archive or exposes sensitive history, confirm the destination email and account are yours before submitting.
steps.expect: the file downloads immediately or the site confirms an export request with a processing window.

steps.action: **Verify the file opens correctly.** Open the export in a spreadsheet, text editor, or PDF viewer without changing its contents.
steps.expect: rows or pages show order dates, order IDs, item descriptions, totals, taxes, shipping, and statuses.

steps.action: **Store the raw export and a working copy.** Keep the original unchanged and make a separate copy for sorting, formulas, or redaction.
steps.expect: both files are saved in secure storage with names that include merchant and date range.

steps.action: **Reconcile a sample against the site.** Pick three orders from different months and compare the export fields to the live order pages.
steps.expect: sampled order IDs, dates, totals, and statuses match the account.

recipes.verification: A readable export covering the intended date range is stored securely, includes order IDs, dates, statuses, and totals, and at least three sampled orders match the merchant's live order details.

recipes.title: fill and submit a web form correctly
recipes.name: fill-and-submit-a-web-form-correctly
recipes.goal: You complete a web form accurately, submit it once, and save proof that the site accepted it.

steps.action: **Verify the site and purpose.** Confirm the domain, HTTPS lock, organization name, and reason the form needs your information.
steps.expect: you are on the legitimate form page.

steps.action: **Read all instructions first.** Note required fields, file formats, character limits, deadlines, and whether submission is final.
steps.expect: a clear list of what must be entered or uploaded.

steps.action: **Prepare source information.** Gather documents and copy exact values from reliable records rather than memory.
steps.expect: inputs are ready and consistent.

steps.action: **Fill required fields carefully.** Enter names, dates, addresses, account numbers, and contact details in the requested format.
steps.expect: required-field indicators clear without validation errors.

steps.action: **Upload files correctly.** Attach only requested files, within size and format limits, with readable names.
steps.expect: each upload shows completed status or filename.

steps.action: **Review before submitting.** Check spelling, dates, amounts, consent boxes, and legal declarations. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some forms create legal or financial records when submitted, so confirm accuracy first.
steps.expect: the review page or visible fields match your source records.

steps.action: **Submit once and wait.** Click the final submit button one time and let the confirmation load.
steps.expect: a success page, reference number, or confirmation email.

steps.action: **Save proof.** Download the receipt, screenshot confirmation, and save any submitted copy.
steps.expect: you can prove what was submitted and when.

recipes.verification: The form shows a success confirmation or reference number, and a saved receipt or email contains the submitted timestamp and enough detail to identify the transaction.

recipes.title: read a checkout total before paying
recipes.name: read-a-checkout-total-before-paying
recipes.goal: You review the final checkout total and terms before paying so you do not approve hidden fees, wrong quantities, subscriptions, or unwanted add-ons.

steps.action: **Pause on the final review screen.** Do not rely on the cart subtotal or advertised price.
steps.expect: the page shows the final order summary or a button that will place the order.

steps.action: **Read every price line.** Check item subtotal, quantity, discounts, shipping, service fees, taxes, tips, deposits, currency, and total due today.
steps.expect: the final total and any future amount are known.

steps.action: **Look for recurring terms.** Search the page for subscription, auto-renew, trial, monthly, membership, installment, deposit, or due later.
steps.expect: you know whether this is one-time payment or recurring billing.

steps.action: **Check fulfillment details.** Verify delivery address, pickup location, dates, cancellation window, return policy, and seller.
steps.expect: the purchase will go to the correct place under acceptable terms.

steps.action: **Remove unwanted add-ons.** [BRANCH: warranty, donation, insurance, expedited shipping, tip, membership, or bundle added unintentionally, remove it | desired add-on, keep it after confirming price]
steps.expect: only intentional items and services remain.

steps.action: **Compare against your cap.** If the total exceeds your maximum, adjust shipping, remove items, find a discount, or abandon the cart.
steps.expect: the final total is at or below your cap or you decide not to buy.

steps.action: **Confirm once and pay.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before clicking the final button, confirm total, currency, seller, quantity, delivery, and recurring terms.
steps.expect: the site returns an order confirmation or payment receipt at the reviewed total.

steps.action: **Save the confirmation.** Store the receipt or screenshot showing the total and order number.
steps.expect: you have proof of what you approved.

recipes.verification: Payment is submitted only after the final total, currency, quantity, seller, delivery terms, and recurring status are reviewed and within the chosen cap, and the saved confirmation matches that approved total.

recipes.title: request your data from a store
recipes.name: request-your-data-from-a-store
recipes.goal: You request a copy of the personal data a store holds about you and save the response securely for review or portability.

steps.action: **Find the official privacy request path.** Use the store's Privacy, Account data, Download my data, or Data subject request page.
steps.expect: you are on a store-owned page that describes data access requests.

steps.action: **Choose the access/export request type.** Select request a copy, access my data, or data portability rather than deletion or opt-out.
steps.expect: the form clearly asks the store to provide your data, not erase it.

steps.action: **Enter only required identity details.** Provide account email, name, region, and order number only if required to locate the account.
steps.expect: the form accepts the minimum information needed to process the request.

steps.action: **Select scope and format.** [BRANCH: broad audit, request all account data | specific transaction review, request order, payment, and communication data for the relevant period]
steps.expect: the request scope is visible before submission.

steps.action: **Submit the request.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the email address is yours because the response may contain sensitive account history.
steps.expect: the site or email confirms the request ID and expected response timeframe.
