steps.action: **Complete verification promptly.** Respond to confirmation emails or identity checks from the official store domain.
steps.expect: the request status changes to verified, processing, or accepted.

steps.action: **Download the archive when available.** Use the official link before it expires and avoid public Wi-Fi for the download.
steps.expect: a ZIP, JSON, CSV, PDF, or HTML archive downloads successfully.

steps.action: **Store and inspect safely.** Save the original archive privately, scan filenames for categories, and open a copy for review.
steps.expect: you can locate order history, account profile, addresses, and other requested data without altering the original.

recipes.verification: The store has confirmed a data-access request, the requested archive has been downloaded before link expiration, and the original file is stored securely with the request ID and date.

recipes.title: resolve a failed payment
recipes.name: resolve-a-failed-payment
recipes.goal: You identify why a payment failed, fix the correct cause, and complete the transaction only once at the intended price.

steps.action: **Read the exact failure message.** Note whether the payment was declined, timed out, authentication failed, address mismatch occurred, or the merchant could not process it.
steps.expect: you have a specific error category rather than a vague "it failed."

steps.action: **Check whether money moved.** Open the card, bank, or wallet account and look for pending authorizations.
steps.expect: you know whether there is no charge, a pending hold, or a posted payment.

steps.action: **Verify checkout details.** Confirm card number, expiration, CVV, billing address, ZIP/postal code, name, currency, and total.
steps.expect: all payment fields match the issuer records.

steps.action: **Fix the most likely cause.** [BRANCH: expired card, update card | insufficient funds, choose another method | fraud block, approve in issuer app | address mismatch, correct billing address | processor timeout, wait and retry once]
steps.expect: the error source is addressed before another attempt.

steps.action: **Retry deliberately.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before clicking Pay again, confirm the cart, total, shipping, and quantity have not changed and no duplicate order exists.
steps.expect: the retry produces either an order confirmation or a new, documented error.

steps.action: **Save the result.** If successful, save the order number; if failed, save the error and timestamp.
steps.expect: there is a record showing whether payment completed.

steps.action: **Clear duplicate holds if needed.** If multiple pending authorizations appear without orders, contact the merchant and issuer with timestamps.
steps.expect: you know which holds will expire automatically or need release.

recipes.verification: Exactly one successful order, bill payment, or subscription payment exists at the intended total, or the payment remains unresolved with no posted charge and a documented support case or next action.

recipes.title: save a payment method securely
recipes.name: save-a-payment-method-securely
recipes.goal: You save a payment method only where it is useful, protected, and easy to remove or monitor.

steps.action: **Decide whether saving is necessary.** Use guest or one-time payment when repeat purchases are unlikely or the merchant is low trust.
steps.expect: a clear reason to save or not save the method.

steps.action: **Verify account security first.** Confirm unique password, two-factor authentication or passkey, recovery options, and recent login activity.
steps.expect: the account is secured before payment data is stored.

steps.action: **Choose the safest payment type.** Prefer tokenized wallet, virtual card, or credit card over debit or bank debit where protections are weaker.
steps.expect: selected method limits direct bank exposure where possible.

steps.action: **Enter payment details on the official page.** Check domain, HTTPS, billing address, and card network prompts.
steps.expect: payment method validates without browser warnings.

steps.action: **Set controls and alerts.** Enable transaction notifications, spending limits, merchant lock, or virtual card limit if available.
steps.expect: future charges will be visible quickly and constrained where possible.

steps.action: **Confirm storage scope.** Check whether the method is saved for one merchant, a marketplace wallet, subscriptions, family sharing, or all future purchases. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* saving a method can authorize future one-click or recurring charges until removed.
steps.expect: storage scope matches your intent.

steps.action: **Label and test removal path.** Note where the method appears and how to delete it.
steps.expect: you can find the saved method in account payment settings.

steps.action: **Review after the first charge.** Match the authorization or test charge to the merchant and amount.
steps.expect: no unexpected charge appears.

recipes.verification: The payment method appears only in the intended account or wallet, account security is enabled, alerts are active, and the first charge or authorization matches expectations.

recipes.title: save a receipt for records
recipes.name: save-a-receipt-for-records
recipes.goal: You save a durable copy of a purchase receipt so you can prove the transaction later for returns, warranties, reimbursement, taxes, or disputes.

steps.action: **Open the official receipt source.** Sign in to the merchant account or open the original confirmation email; avoid using forwarded screenshots as the primary record.
steps.expect: the receipt page or email shows the merchant name, order number, date, items, taxes, fees, payment method, and total.

steps.action: **Check the receipt details before saving.** Compare the receipt total and date against your card or bank activity.
steps.expect: the merchant, date, and amount match the payment record or the difference is explained by pending authorization timing.

steps.action: **Save a complete PDF copy.** Use the browser print dialog or merchant download button, select `Save as PDF`, and include all pages.
steps.expect: a PDF file opens locally and contains the full order details, not only the visible first screen.

steps.action: **Name the file consistently.** Use a sortable name such as `2026-08-25-merchant-order1234-89.20.pdf`.
steps.expect: the filename identifies the date, merchant, order number, and total without opening the file.

steps.action: **Store it in the right records folder.** Move the PDF to the folder used for receipts, reimbursements, taxes, or warranties.
steps.expect: the file appears in the intended folder and is included in that folder's backup or sync system.

steps.action: **Capture supporting proof if needed.** [BRANCH: physical item, photograph serial numbers, packing slip, and warranty card | service purchase, save the terms, plan name, or service dates shown on the receipt]
steps.expect: supporting files are stored beside the receipt or linked in the same record.

steps.action: **Protect sensitive details.** If you must share the receipt, redact full address, phone number, full card digits, and unrelated items first.
steps.expect: the retained original stays private and any shared copy exposes only what the recipient needs.

recipes.verification: A readable PDF or equivalent complete receipt file is stored in the chosen records location, its filename includes date, merchant, order number, and total, and the saved contents match the transaction record.

recipes.title: set a spending alert on a card
recipes.name: set-a-spending-alert-on-a-card
recipes.goal: You set a card alert that notifies you when a transaction crosses a chosen amount or when any charge posts from the card.

steps.action: **Open the card issuer's official app or website.** Sign in and select the exact card account.
steps.expect: the account screen shows the card name, last four digits, balance, and recent transactions.

steps.action: **Navigate to alert settings.** Open Alerts, Notifications, Card controls, Security, or Spending controls.
steps.expect: transaction alert options are visible.

steps.action: **Choose the alert type.** [BRANCH: fraud monitoring, choose every card-not-present or every transaction alert | budget monitoring, choose amount threshold | merchant monitoring, choose recurring or merchant-specific alert if available]
steps.expect: the selected alert rule matches the risk you want to catch.

steps.action: **Set the threshold and delivery channel.** Enter an amount low enough to catch unwanted charges and choose push, SMS, or email.
steps.expect: the app shows the chosen amount and notification destination.

steps.action: **Save the alert.** Confirm the rule and any device permission prompts.
steps.expect: the alert appears as active in the issuer's settings.

steps.action: **Test notification reachability.** Use the issuer's test alert feature if available, or confirm notifications are enabled at the phone and email level.
steps.expect: a test notification arrives or the app shows notification permissions are enabled.

steps.action: **Document the monitoring rule.** Note which card, threshold, and channel you set, especially if monitoring a disputed or canceled merchant.
steps.expect: you can later prove the alert was configured and know what event should trigger it.

recipes.verification: The issuer shows an active alert on the correct card with the intended threshold or transaction type, the delivery channel is confirmed, and a test or permission check shows notifications can reach you.

recipes.title: set up a virtual payment card
recipes.name: set-up-a-virtual-payment-card
recipes.goal: You create a virtual card with limits that match a specific merchant, subscription, or purchase risk.

steps.action: **Choose the virtual-card provider.** Use a trusted issuer or wallet and confirm fees, funding source, dispute rights, and merchant acceptance.
steps.expect: a provider that supports the purchase type.

steps.action: **Secure the provider account.** Enable strong authentication and check recovery settings before creating card numbers.
steps.expect: account access is protected.

steps.action: **Create a card for one purpose.** Name it after the merchant or subscription so future charges are recognizable.
steps.expect: a distinct virtual card record exists.

steps.action: **Set spending controls.** Configure merchant lock, single-use setting, per-transaction cap, monthly cap, or expiration date based on the purchase.
steps.expect: limits match the expected charge plus a small buffer.

steps.action: **Copy details only into the intended checkout.** Enter card number, expiration, CVV, and billing address on the official merchant page.
steps.expect: merchant accepts the virtual card or gives a clear rejection.

steps.action: **Save the card only if needed.** For subscriptions, save it and calendar renewal; for one-time purchases, keep it single-use or pause after authorization. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once shared with a merchant, the number may be attempted for future charges until locked or deleted.
steps.expect: card status reflects the intended future use.

steps.action: **Verify the authorization.** Check provider activity for merchant name, amount, and status.
steps.expect: only the expected authorization appears.

steps.action: **Adjust after fulfillment.** Lock, lower limit, or delete the card once shipment, service access, or trial cancellation is complete.
steps.expect: future unwanted charges are blocked or capped.

recipes.verification: The virtual card exists with the intended merchant label, spending controls, and activity showing only the expected authorization or charge.

recipes.title: track a refund status
recipes.name: track-a-refund-status
recipes.goal: You determine whether a refund has been approved, issued, pending, or missing, and you record the next action needed to receive the money.

steps.action: **Start with the merchant or platform status.** Open the order, return, cancellation, or refund page from the official account.
steps.expect: the status shows requested, received, approved, issued, denied, or closed.

steps.action: **Match the refund to the original payment.** Confirm refund amount, taxes, shipping, restocking fees, gift cards, and original payment method.
steps.expect: the expected net refund amount is clear.

steps.action: **Check return delivery if goods were shipped back.** Use tracking to confirm the return arrived and was accepted.
steps.expect: the carrier shows delivered or the platform shows item received.

steps.action: **Check the payment account.** Open card, bank, wallet, or gift-card activity for the refund date range.
steps.expect: the refund is posted, pending, or absent from the original payment method.

steps.action: **Record the stated timeline.** Note the merchant's expected processing time and the issuer's posting time.
steps.expect: you know the date when the refund becomes overdue.

steps.action: **Escalate if overdue.** Contact merchant support with order number, tracking, refund approval, and payment method last four.
steps.expect: support provides a case number, corrected refund, or explanation.

steps.action: **Use issuer dispute only after merchant path fails.** [BRANCH: refund approved but never posted, ask the issuer about missing credit | refund denied incorrectly, consider a dispute with evidence]
steps.expect: the next escalation path is documented without duplicating requests.

recipes.verification: The refund status is documented as posted, pending with a known due date, denied with a reason, or escalated with a case number; the expected amount and payment destination are recorded.

recipes.title: turn off auto renew
recipes.name: turn-off-auto-renew
recipes.goal: You turn off automatic renewal while keeping the current paid term active until its expiration date.

steps.action: **Open the active plan settings.** Sign in and navigate to billing, subscription, membership, domain, or renewal settings.
steps.expect: the current plan, renewal date, and auto-renew status are visible.

steps.action: **Separate auto-renew from cancellation.** Read the labels carefully so you choose "turn off auto-renew" or "disable renewal," not "cancel now" unless that is intended.
steps.expect: the page indicates the current term remains active after renewal is disabled.

steps.action: **Check what will happen at expiration.** Review whether service stops, enters a grace period, downgrades, or deletes data.
steps.expect: you know the exact expiration date and consequence.

steps.action: **Disable auto-renew.** Toggle auto-renew off or choose Do not renew. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* for domains, insurance, or scarce plans, confirm you are willing to lose the asset or coverage after expiration.
steps.expect: the toggle changes to off or the renewal action moves to manual.

steps.action: **Complete any confirmation prompt.** Confirm through password, multi-factor, survey, or final modal if required.
steps.expect: the account status says auto-renew is off, expires on a date, or renewal canceled.

steps.action: **Save evidence.** Save the confirmation page or email showing the disabled renewal and expiration date.
steps.expect: proof is stored with the account name and date.

steps.action: **Add a manual review reminder.** Put the expiration date and a decision deadline on your calendar.
steps.expect: you have a reminder before service, coverage, or ownership ends.

recipes.verification: The account shows auto-renew disabled for the correct product, the current term's expiration date is visible, and a confirmation record has been saved.

recipes.title: update an expired card on file
recipes.name: update-an-expired-card-on-file
recipes.goal: You replace an expired saved card with a valid payment method so future orders or renewals do not fail.

steps.action: **Open billing or wallet settings.** Sign in through the official site and navigate to Payment methods, Billing, Wallet, or Subscription payment.
steps.expect: saved payment methods and expiration dates are visible.

steps.action: **Identify the expired card.** Match brand, last four digits, and expired month/year.
steps.expect: the card needing replacement is clear.

steps.action: **Add the replacement payment method.** Enter the new card details or choose a saved wallet token.
steps.expect: the site accepts the new method or asks for verification.

steps.action: **Complete verification.** Approve issuer authentication, billing address check, or small authorization if required.
steps.expect: the new card appears as active or verified.

steps.action: **Set the correct default.** Choose the new card for subscriptions, upcoming orders, or account default billing.
steps.expect: active services show the new last four digits as their payment method.

steps.action: **Remove the expired card if safe.** [BRANCH: no active dependency, remove it | historical receipts or issuer updater still needed, leave it but not as default]
steps.expect: the expired card cannot be used for future charges or is clearly not default.

steps.action: **Retry any failed payment.** If the update was prompted by a failed renewal, use the merchant's retry or pay-now button once. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm amount, plan, and billing period before paying.
steps.expect: the overdue balance clears or the next renewal date updates.

recipes.verification: The account shows a valid active payment method as default for the intended orders or subscriptions, the expired card is removed or non-default, and any failed payment has either cleared once or has a documented next step.

recipes.title: verify a merchant is legitimate
recipes.name: verify-a-merchant-is-legitimate
recipes.goal: You decide whether an online merchant is safe enough to buy from before entering payment or identity information.

steps.action: **Inspect the domain carefully.** Check spelling, top-level domain, age cues, and whether the link came from an ad, email, or social post.
steps.expect: the domain either matches the known brand exactly or is identified as a separate seller.

steps.action: **Check secure connection and checkout ownership.** Confirm the browser shows HTTPS and payment forms are on the merchant, platform, or known processor domain.
steps.expect: no password or card fields appear on a suspicious or misspelled host.

steps.action: **Verify business identity.** Look for a real legal name, physical address, customer-service channel, return policy, privacy policy, and terms.
steps.expect: the merchant provides enough accountable contact information to pursue support or claims.

steps.action: **Compare external reputation.** Search independent reviews, complaint databases, marketplace feedback, and recent scam reports using the merchant name plus domain.
steps.expect: reputation signals are consistent with a real business or reveal unresolved fraud patterns.

steps.action: **Evaluate price and urgency.** Compare the offer against normal market prices and note countdown timers, fake scarcity, or unrealistic discounts.
steps.expect: the deal is plausible or flagged as too risky.

steps.action: **Check payment protections.** Prefer credit card, trusted wallet, or marketplace checkout; avoid wire, crypto, gift card, friends-and-family transfer, or off-platform payment.
steps.expect: the payment path includes chargeback or buyer-protection options.

steps.action: **Decide before sharing sensitive data.** [BRANCH: legitimacy confirmed, proceed with a protected payment method | unresolved red flags, abandon or buy from a reputable seller] ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not enter payment or identity data until red flags are resolved.
steps.expect: you have a buy or walk-away decision supported by evidence.

recipes.verification: Before checkout, the merchant has a verified domain or accountable seller profile, plausible pricing, clear return and contact information, no unresolved scam red flags, and a protected payment method is available; otherwise the purchase is abandoned.

recipes.title: verify a purchase confirmation
recipes.name: verify-a-purchase-confirmation
recipes.goal: You confirm that a purchase actually went through once, for the correct item, amount, merchant, and delivery or access details.

steps.action: **Start with the merchant confirmation page.** Record order number, timestamp, total, items, delivery address, and estimated delivery or access date.
steps.expect: a visible order reference or clear pending message.

steps.action: **Check confirmation email.** Verify sender domain, order number, item details, total, and links without clicking suspicious buttons.
steps.expect: email matches the checkout result.

steps.action: **Check merchant order history.** Log in directly to the merchant site or app and open the order.
steps.expect: the order appears with the same status and details.

steps.action: **Check payment activity.** Compare authorization or charge amount, merchant descriptor, and currency against the expected total.
steps.expect: one matching authorization or charge, not duplicates.

steps.action: **Verify fulfillment details.** Confirm shipping address, pickup location, digital delivery email, traveler name, or license key recipient.
steps.expect: delivery/access information is correct.

steps.action: **Save proof.** Store the receipt, invoice, order page PDF, or screenshot in a place you can find later.
steps.expect: proof includes order number, merchant, amount, and date.

steps.action: **Act quickly on mismatches.** If item, address, date, or amount is wrong, use cancel/change support immediately. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some orders ship or digital goods activate quickly, reducing refund options.
steps.expect: correction, cancellation, or support case number if needed.

steps.action: **Monitor final settlement.** Recheck when the charge posts or shipment occurs.
steps.expect: posted amount and fulfillment status still match the order.

recipes.verification: Merchant order history, confirmation email, and payment activity all show one matching purchase with the correct order number, item/service, amount, and fulfillment details.

recipes.title: transcribe audio to text
recipes.name: transcribe-audio-to-text
recipes.goal: Turn an audio recording into readable text and verify the parts where accuracy matters.

steps.action: **Confirm consent and sensitivity.** Check whether the recording includes private conversations, protected information, or people who did not consent.
steps.expect: you know whether transcription is allowed.

steps.action: **Choose a transcription method.** [BRANCH: local app | cloud service] use local tools for sensitive audio; use cloud tools when allowed and convenient.
steps.expect: the service matches the privacy level.

steps.action: **Prepare the audio.** Use the clearest file available, trim unrelated sections, and note speaker names if known.
steps.expect: the input is easier to transcribe accurately.

steps.action: **Run transcription.** Upload or import the file and enable speaker labels, timestamps, or language settings when useful.
steps.expect: a draft transcript is produced.

steps.action: **Review difficult sections.** Replay unclear, technical, accented, noisy, or high-stakes sections while editing the text.
steps.expect: important phrases are corrected.

steps.action: **Export and label.** Save the transcript with date, source, language, and whether it is edited or machine-generated.
steps.expect: future readers know the transcript status.

recipes.verification: The transcript opens in the chosen format, important sections have been checked against the audio, and unclear passages are marked rather than silently guessed.

recipes.title: transfer a messaging app to a new phone
recipes.name: transfer-a-messaging-app-to-a-new-phone
recipes.goal: Your messaging app moves to a new phone with account verification, restored chats, and checked media, while the old phone is preserved until the transfer is confirmed.

steps.action: **Back up on the old phone first.** Open the app's backup settings and run a fresh backup before installing or verifying on the new phone.
steps.expect: the backup screen shows a successful backup dated today.

steps.action: **Keep the old phone unchanged.** Do not delete the app, erase the phone, or trade it in yet.
steps.expect: the old chat history remains readable.

steps.action: **Install the app on the new phone.** Download the same messaging app from the official app store.
steps.expect: the app opens to sign-in or phone verification.

steps.action: **Verify the number or account.** Enter the phone number or account and complete SMS, call, passkey, or email verification.
steps.expect: the app recognizes the account.

steps.action: **Choose restore or transfer.** [BRANCH: cloud restore | direct phone transfer] select the method your app offers and sign in to the matching cloud account if needed.
steps.expect: the app finds the backup or begins device transfer.

steps.action: **Wait for chat restore.** Keep both phones charged and near Wi-Fi until messages finish restoring.
steps.expect: recent conversations appear on the new phone.

steps.action: **Check media separately.** Open several older chats and confirm photos, videos, voice notes, and documents are present or downloading.
steps.expect: important media either appears or shows a clear download state.

steps.action: **Confirm before wiping old phone.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* erase or trade in the old phone only after chats, contacts, groups, and media have been checked on the new phone.
steps.expect: the old phone is no longer needed for recovery.

recipes.verification: The new phone can send and receive messages in the account, recent chats are present, and sampled older media opens before the old phone is erased.

recipes.title: transfer a phone number to a new carrier
recipes.name: transfer-a-phone-number-to-a-new-carrier
recipes.goal: Your existing phone number is ported to a new carrier while the old account remains active until the transfer completes.

steps.action: **Do not cancel the old line.** Keep the old carrier account active until the port finishes. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* canceling first can lose the number; confirm the new carrier has completed the port before closing anything.
steps.expect: the old line still works or is still listed as active.

steps.action: **Collect port details.** Get the old carrier account number, transfer PIN or port PIN, billing ZIP or postal code, and account holder name.
steps.expect: the details are current and copied exactly.

steps.action: **Start with the new carrier.** Open the new carrier's official activation, checkout, store, or support flow.
steps.expect: the new carrier asks whether to keep an existing number.

steps.action: **Enter transfer information.** Provide the phone number and matching old-carrier details.
steps.expect: the new carrier accepts the request or names the mismatch.

steps.action: **Install SIM or eSIM.** Follow the new carrier instructions for physical SIM, eSIM, or device activation.
steps.expect: the phone shows the new carrier or activation pending.

steps.action: **Wait for port completion.** Keep both carriers' messages available and do not repeat the request unless instructed.
steps.expect: calls, texts, and data shift to the new carrier.

steps.action: **Verify the number.** Call and text another phone, then receive a call and text back.
steps.expect: the transferred number sends and receives normally.

steps.action: **Confirm old account closure.** Check the old carrier after the port; the transferred line should close automatically or show final billing.
steps.expect: the old number is no longer active as a billable old-carrier line.

recipes.verification: The same phone number works for outbound and inbound calls and texts on the new carrier, and the old carrier no longer bills that active line.

recipes.title: transfer data to a new computer
recipes.name: transfer-data-to-a-new-computer
recipes.goal: Move your documents, photos, browser data, and application settings to a new computer, then verify the old computer still has an untouched copy until the transfer is proven complete.

steps.action: **Update both computers.** Install pending system updates and restart before starting the transfer.
steps.expect: both computers are on the desktop with no restart pending.

steps.action: **Inventory important data.** Check Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, Videos, browser profiles, email archives, password manager, project folders, and license keys.
steps.expect: you have a short list of data and apps that must appear on the new computer.

steps.action: **Choose a transfer method.** [BRANCH: Windows PC to Windows PC | Mac to Mac | mixed systems] use OneDrive or an external drive on Windows, Migration Assistant on Mac, or an external drive/cloud storage for mixed systems.
steps.expect: one method is selected and has enough storage or network access.

steps.action: **Back up the old computer first.** Create a current backup with File History, Time Machine, or a full external-drive copy before migration.
steps.expect: the backup tool reports a successful backup from today.

steps.action: **Run the transfer.** Start the selected tool, keep both devices awake and powered, and transfer user files before wiping or selling anything.
steps.expect: the new computer shows copied folders or the migration tool reports complete.

steps.action: **Install missing apps.** Download apps only from official stores or vendor websites, then sign in and restore settings where available.
steps.expect: required apps launch and show your account or expected local data.

steps.action: **Verify critical files.** Open samples from documents, photos, spreadsheets, browser bookmarks, email, and any work folders.
steps.expect: files open correctly and recent items are present.

steps.action: **Keep the old computer unchanged.** Do not erase, trade in, or recycle the old computer until you have used the new one for at least a week.
steps.expect: the old computer remains available as a fallback.

recipes.verification: The new computer contains the inventoried folders, critical files open successfully, required apps launch, browser bookmarks are present, and the old computer plus backup remain available.

recipes.title: transfer photos off your phone
recipes.name: transfer-photos-off-your-phone
recipes.goal: Your phone's photos and videos exist as full-resolution files in a second location (computer or cloud), organized so you can find them, and verified complete before any copy is deleted from the phone.

steps.action: **Check how much you are moving.** Read the phone's storage screen for total photo and video size, and confirm the destination has more free space than that.
steps.expect: a size figure and a destination with headroom.

steps.action: **Pick the transfer path.** [BRANCH: cable to a computer (fastest, full quality, no account) | cloud sync (automatic, off-device, needs quota)] Cable for a one-time bulk offload; cloud for ongoing backup.
steps.expect: a clear choice and, for cable, the phone connected and unlocked.

steps.action: **Cable path: set the phone to file transfer.** On the connection prompt choose "Transfer files" / "Photos", not "Charging only".
steps.expect: the phone's storage appears as a drive or device in the computer's file browser.

steps.action: **Copy, do not move.** Drag the camera folder (DCIM and any others) to a dated folder on the destination. Copying leaves the originals in place until you have verified.
steps.expect: a progress bar; the copy finishes with a file count matching the phone.

steps.action: **Verify the copy before trusting it.** Compare the file count, then open a dozen photos and one video from the destination at full size, including a recent and an old one.
steps.expect: files open, look sharp, and the count lines up. A folder of zero-byte files is a known cable failure.

steps.action: **Give the copy structure.** Sort into folders by year, event, or however you will actually search later; a single dump of 10,000 files is technically a backup and practically unusable.
steps.expect: a browsable folder tree.

steps.action: **Only now, delete from the phone if you need the space.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* deletion removes your originals; delete only after step 5 passed. Most phones keep deleted items in a "Recently Deleted" album for ~30 days as a last safety net.
steps.expect: phone storage freed; the second copy untouched.

recipes.verification: Every photo and video sits in a second location at full resolution, the file count matches the phone, you have opened a sample and confirmed it is readable, the copy is organized into a browsable structure, and nothing was deleted from the phone until that verification passed.

recipes.title: translate a webpage
recipes.name: translate-a-webpage
recipes.goal: Translate a webpage enough to understand and act on it while checking important details against the original language when needed.

steps.action: **Open the original page.** Use the direct URL instead of a screenshot when possible.
steps.expect: the original page loads.

steps.action: **Translate with the browser or service.** [BRANCH: built-in browser translation | external translator] use built-in translation for convenience; paste text or URL into a trusted translator if needed.
steps.expect: the page text appears in your target language.

steps.action: **Check layout-sensitive items.** Compare buttons, forms, prices, dates, units, addresses, and warnings against the original page.
steps.expect: critical interface details are not misplaced or mistranslated.

steps.action: **Verify specialized terms.** Look up legal, medical, technical, cultural, or idiomatic phrases separately.
steps.expect: high-stakes terms are not accepted blindly.

steps.action: **Avoid submitting secrets through translation.** Do not paste passwords, private messages, confidential contracts, or personal records into third-party translation boxes.
steps.expect: sensitive input stays out of unapproved services.

steps.action: **Act only after confirmation.** Before buying, signing, traveling, or changing settings, confirm the key sentence or form field.
steps.expect: the action is based on checked meaning.

recipes.verification: You can identify the page's purpose, key warnings, required fields, and intended action in the target language, and any high-stakes term has been independently checked.

recipes.title: trim a video clip
recipes.name: trim-a-video-clip
recipes.goal: Shorten a video by setting a new start and end point.

steps.action: **Open the video editor.** Open the clip in Photos, Gallery, QuickTime, Clipchamp, iMovie, or another editor.
steps.expect: the video timeline is visible.

steps.action: **Choose trim.** Select `Edit`, `Trim`, scissors, or timeline handles.
steps.expect: trim handles or a highlighted timeline range appear.

steps.action: **Set the start point.** Drag the left handle or playhead to the first frame you want to keep.
steps.expect: playback starts at the intended moment.

steps.action: **Set the end point.** Drag the right handle to the last frame you want to keep.
steps.expect: playback ends at the intended moment.

steps.action: **Preview the clip.** Play the trimmed range from start to finish.
steps.expect: only the desired section plays.

steps.action: **Save a copy.** Choose `Save as copy`, `Export`, or equivalent when available.
steps.expect: a new trimmed video file is created.

recipes.verification: The saved video starts and ends at the intended moments and plays without including the removed sections.

recipes.title: troubleshoot slow internet
recipes.name: troubleshoot-slow-internet
recipes.goal: Identify whether slow internet comes from the device, Wi-Fi, router, modem, ISP, or a specific service, then apply the right fix.

steps.action: **Define the symptom.** Note whether everything is slow, one app is slow, Wi-Fi drops, or uploads are the problem.
steps.expect: the problem is described clearly enough to test.

steps.action: **Run a baseline speed test.** Test near the router on Wi-Fi and record download, upload, latency, and time of day.
steps.expect: you have numbers to compare against the plan.

steps.action: **Test another device.** Run the same test on a second phone or computer.
steps.expect: you know whether the issue follows one device or the network.

steps.action: **Restart network equipment.** Unplug modem and router or mesh for 30 seconds, plug modem first, then router, and wait until lights stabilize.
steps.expect: internet returns and equipment shows normal status.

steps.action: **Compare wired or close-range performance.** Use Ethernet if possible, or stand beside the router and retest.
steps.expect: you know whether Wi-Fi distance is the bottleneck.

steps.action: **Check router or mesh status.** Open the router app/admin page and look for offline nodes, firmware updates, connected-device load, or ISP outage notices.
steps.expect: obvious network health warnings are resolved or noted.

steps.action: **Reduce local congestion.** Pause large downloads, cloud backups, game updates, and video streams, then retest.
steps.expect: speeds or latency improve if local traffic was the cause.

steps.action: **Contact the ISP with evidence.** If wired or near-router speed remains far below plan after restart, report timestamps and test results.
steps.expect: the ISP can check line signal, outage, provisioning, or modem issues.

recipes.verification: A current test identifies the bottleneck, and after the fix the affected device or location reaches an acceptable speed and latency for browsing, calls, or streaming.

recipes.title: turn off ad personalization
recipes.name: turn-off-ad-personalization
recipes.goal: Reduce personalized advertising by turning off ad personalization in major accounts, browsers, devices, and apps.

steps.action: **List ad surfaces.** Note major accounts, phone OS, browser, social apps, streaming apps, and shopping apps you use.
steps.expect: you have a short checklist.

steps.action: **Open privacy or ad settings.** Find each account's ads, privacy, personalization, or data controls page.
steps.expect: a personalization toggle or category list is visible.

steps.action: **Turn off personalization.** Disable personalized ads, interest-based ads, activity-based targeting, or partner data use where available.
steps.expect: the setting shows off or limited.

steps.action: **Reset ad identifiers.** [BRANCH: mobile | browser] reset or delete the device ad ID on phones; clear advertising cookies or site data in browsers if appropriate.
steps.expect: old targeting identifiers are reduced.

steps.action: **Limit app tracking.** Deny cross-app tracking and review app permissions for location, contacts, microphone, and photos.
steps.expect: fewer apps can feed ad profiles.

steps.action: **Repeat periodically.** Recheck after installing new apps, changing devices, or joining new services.
steps.expect: settings stay aligned over time.

recipes.verification: Major accounts and devices show personalized ads disabled or limited, mobile ad tracking is restricted, and browser tracking controls are set as intended.

recipes.title: turn on automatic backups
recipes.name: turn-on-automatic-backups
recipes.goal: Automatic backups are enabled for important files or a device, and a restore test proves the backup can actually recover data.

steps.action: **Choose cloud, local, or both.** [BRANCH: cloud backup | local drive backup | both] Use cloud for off-site protection and local drive for fast restore.
steps.expect: you know where backup copies will live.

steps.action: **Open the backup settings.** Use OS settings, phone backup settings, cloud client, or backup software from a trusted provider.
steps.expect: a backup status page shows destinations and included data.

steps.action: **Select what to include.** Add Documents, Desktop, Photos, key project folders, phone photos, messages, and app data that would hurt to lose.
steps.expect: included folders match your real priorities.

steps.action: **Exclude disposable or risky items.** Skip caches, downloads, temporary files, and huge re-downloadable media unless you truly need them.
steps.expect: backup size fits the destination.

steps.action: **Turn on automatic schedule or continuous sync.** Choose hourly, daily, when connected to power, or continuous depending on the tool.
steps.expect: settings show automatic backup enabled and a next run or active sync.

steps.action: **Secure the backup.** Enable encryption for drives and use strong account protection for cloud backups.
steps.expect: the backup destination requires your account or password to access.

steps.action: **Run the first backup now.** Keep the device awake, powered, and online until the initial run finishes.
steps.expect: status changes from running to completed, synced, or backed up.

steps.action: **Perform a restore test.** Restore one small file to a temporary folder and open it.
steps.expect: the restored file opens and matches the original.

steps.action: **Set a recurring check.** Add a monthly or quarterly reminder to verify last backup time and storage space.
steps.expect: backup health will be checked before a crisis.

recipes.verification: Backup status shows a recent successful automatic run, the selected important data is included, and at least one file has been restored and opened successfully.

recipes.title: turn on track changes
recipes.name: turn-on-track-changes
recipes.goal: Future edits are recorded as tracked changes so reviewers can see what changed.

steps.action: **Find the tracking control.** [BRANCH: Word | Google Docs] In Word, choose Review > Track Changes; in Google Docs, use the mode menu near Share and choose Suggesting.
steps.expect: tracking or suggesting mode is visibly enabled.

steps.action: **Make a small test edit.** Add or delete a word in a harmless spot.
steps.expect: the edit appears as markup, a suggestion, or a colored change.

steps.action: **Undo the test edit if needed.** Press `Ctrl+Z` or `Command+Z` after confirming tracking works.
steps.expect: the test change disappears.

steps.action: **Continue editing normally.** Type, delete, and format as needed while tracking stays on.
steps.expect: new edits appear as tracked changes or suggestions.

recipes.verification: A new edit appears as a tracked change, suggestion, or visible markup rather than silently changing the document.

recipes.title: undo and redo an action
recipes.name: undo-and-redo-an-action
recipes.goal: The most recent edit is reversed, and optionally restored, in a document or text editor.

steps.action: **Undo the last action.** Press `Ctrl+Z` on Windows/Linux or `Command+Z` on Mac, or choose Edit > Undo.
steps.expect: the most recent change reverses.

steps.action: **Repeat only if needed.** Press the same undo shortcut again for earlier actions.
steps.expect: each press steps back one edit.

steps.action: **Redo if you went too far.** Press `Ctrl+Y` or `Ctrl+Shift+Z` on Windows/Linux, or `Command+Shift+Z` on Mac, or choose Edit > Redo.
steps.expect: the undone change returns.

steps.action: **Stop at the correct state.** Read the affected sentence, paragraph, or object before continuing.
steps.expect: the document shows the intended version.

recipes.verification: The unwanted action is no longer visible, or the redone action is visible again if redo was used.

recipes.title: unsubscribe from a mailing list
recipes.name: unsubscribe-from-a-mailing-list
recipes.goal: A specific sender's recurring emails stop arriving in your inbox.

steps.action: **Classify the sender.** Legitimate list you subscribed to (retailer, newsletter) vs. unknown spam. [BRANCH: legitimate → continue | unknown spam → skip to step 5]
steps.expect: you can name how the sender got your address, or you can't (→ spam path).

steps.action: **Open the most recent email and find the unsubscribe control.** Check the mail client's built-in "Unsubscribe" button near the sender name first; otherwise the link in the footer.
steps.expect: an unsubscribe link or one-click button exists.

steps.action: **Execute the unsubscribe.** Click; if a preference page opens, choose "unsubscribe from all". Do not enter your password — unsubscribing never requires login credentials.
steps.expect: a confirmation page: "you have been unsubscribed."

steps.action: **Allow the processing window.** Senders may legally take several days to stop.
steps.expect: no new mail from this sender after ~10 days.

steps.action: **For unknown spam: mark as spam instead.** Use the client's Spam/Junk button — clicking links in true spam confirms your address is live.
steps.expect: future messages route to the spam folder automatically.

steps.action: **Escalate persistent senders.** If mail continues past the window, create a filter: from-address → delete/archive.
steps.expect: the sender no longer reaches the inbox regardless of their behavior.

recipes.verification: No message from the sender has reached the inbox for 10 consecutive days (spam-folder arrivals count as success).

recipes.title: update software safely
recipes.name: update-software-safely
recipes.goal: Your OS and applications are updated — closing the security holes updates exist for — at a moment you chose, through legitimate channels, with a fallback if an update misbehaves.

steps.action: **Verify the update's channel before anything else.** Legitimate: the OS's own settings/updater, the platform app store, the app's built-in updater. Illegitimate: a *website popup* saying your player/browser is outdated — that's a malware genre, close it.
steps.expect: the update lives inside a channel you deliberately opened.

steps.action: **Read what it is.** Security patches: apply promptly, always. Feature/major-version upgrades (the .0 releases): fine to wait days-to-weeks while early adopters find the bugs — your call, made consciously.
steps.expect: you know whether this is "patch now" or "major, scheduled for the weekend".

steps.action: **Prepare the ground for OS updates.** Backup current (step 0 of every OS update), work saved and apps closed, charger in, and don't start it 20 minutes before a meeting. App updates need none of this ceremony.
steps.expect: nothing running that losing would hurt; power secured.

steps.action: **Run the update and leave it alone.** Let it download, install, reboot as many times as it wants. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* interrupting an OS/firmware update mid-write (forcing power-off at the "do not turn off" screen) can brick devices — the one absolute rule is *wait it out*, even when the progress bar seems dead (they routinely stall-then-jump).
steps.expect: the do-not-power-off phases pass; the system returns to a login screen.

steps.action: **Verify the version and the vitals.** Settings shows the new version; then a 2-minute smoke test of what you depend on: the apps you use daily open, peripherals (printer, audio) work, files present.
steps.expect: new version confirmed; daily-driver functionality intact.

steps.action: **Sweep the stragglers.** App store "update all" for the long tail; browsers self-update on restart (so restart the browser you never close); firmware-bearing devices (router, watch) on their own cadence.
steps.expect: no red badges left; the machine's software surface is current.

recipes.verification: Version numbers show current across OS and daily apps, the smoke test passed, auto-update posture is set deliberately, any pinned exception is documented with a revisit date, and the backup that preceded the OS update is intact for the rollback window.

recipes.title: update your address across accounts
recipes.name: update-your-address-across-accounts
recipes.goal: Your mailing and service address is updated across important accounts in a planned order, with each change confirmed and tracked.

steps.action: **Make the master list.** List banks, credit cards, payroll, tax or government agencies, insurance, healthcare, utilities, subscriptions, deliveries, schools, and employers.
steps.expect: every account that sends mail or verifies address is visible in one list.

steps.action: **Mark priorities.** Put bank, government, insurance, healthcare, payroll, and utilities at the top.
steps.expect: identity, money, and essential service accounts are first.

steps.action: **Start mail forwarding.** File forwarding with the postal service or local equivalent for the move date.
steps.expect: confirmation or receipt shows forwarding is scheduled.

steps.action: **Update financial accounts.** Sign in through official sites or apps and change mailing, residential, and billing addresses as needed.
steps.expect: each account shows the new address or a pending confirmation.

steps.action: **Update government and healthcare.** Use official portals or phone numbers for ID, tax, benefits, voter, insurer, doctor, and pharmacy records.
steps.expect: each record has a confirmation page, letter, or case number.

steps.action: **Update deliveries and subscriptions.** Change retailers, meal delivery, memberships, and recurring shipments before the next order date.
steps.expect: saved shipping addresses and active orders point to the new address.

steps.action: **Confirm each change.** Record the date, account, confirmation number, and whether proof is still needed.
steps.expect: the master list shows done, pending, or blocked for every entry.

steps.action: **Watch old-address mail.** For the first month, check forwarded mail for missed accounts.
steps.expect: any missed sender is added back to the list.

recipes.verification: The master list has every account marked done or intentionally pending, with confirmation details for each completed address change.

recipes.title: update your apps
recipes.name: update-your-apps
recipes.goal: Your apps are updated deliberately, with automatic updates configured, important security fixes installed, and storage or rollback issues understood.

steps.action: **Open the update list.** Go to the App Store, Play Store, Microsoft Store, or app updater and view available updates.
steps.expect: pending updates and recently updated apps are visible.

steps.action: **Scan for important updates.** Prioritize browsers, messaging, banking, password managers, security tools, and work apps.
steps.expect: high-impact apps are identified.

steps.action: **Free space if blocked.** If updates fail for storage, delete downloads, clear trash, or remove unused apps before retrying.
steps.expect: the device has enough free space to install updates.

steps.action: **Update critical apps first.** Install security-sensitive app updates before games or rarely used apps.
steps.expect: the most important updates finish successfully.

steps.action: **Choose auto-update behavior.** [BRANCH: auto on | auto off] turn on auto-updates for convenience, or keep manual updates for apps where changes disrupt work.
steps.expect: the setting matches your tolerance for surprise changes.

steps.action: **Check Wi-Fi and data rules.** Set updates to use Wi-Fi only if mobile data is limited.
steps.expect: large updates will not unexpectedly use cellular data.

steps.action: **Open key apps after updating.** Launch important apps and confirm sign-in, permissions, and main screens still work.
steps.expect: no urgent app is broken by the update.

steps.action: **Note rollback limits.** Understand that app stores usually do not provide an easy official rollback to older versions.
steps.expect: you treat major updates to critical tools with care.

recipes.verification: The app store shows no pending critical updates, auto-update settings are intentional, and key apps open normally after updating.

recipes.title: upload a document to a portal
recipes.name: upload-a-document-to-a-portal
recipes.goal: A required document is uploaded to the correct portal field in the accepted format, readable quality, and confirmed as received.

steps.action: **Open the portal from a trusted route.** Type the site address, use a bookmark, or start from the organization's official page.
steps.expect: the portal domain and login branding match the organization.

steps.action: **Read the upload requirements first.** Check allowed file types, maximum size, page count, naming rules, and whether color is required.
steps.expect: you can state the exact limits before selecting a file.

steps.action: **Inspect the document locally.** Open it and zoom to the smallest text, stamps, signatures, and corners.
steps.expect: every page is upright, complete, readable, and not cropped.

steps.action: **Prepare the file to fit the limits.** Rename it clearly, combine pages into one PDF if requested, or compress only enough to meet the size cap.
steps.expect: the file extension and size match the portal's requirements.

steps.action: **Choose the correct upload field.** Match the portal label to the document type, such as proof of address, transcript, ID front, or pay stub.
steps.expect: the selected field name matches the document content.

steps.action: **Upload and wait for completion.** Select the file once, then wait through scanning, processing, or progress bars without closing the tab.
steps.expect: the portal shows the filename with uploaded, complete, or ready status.

steps.action: **Preview the uploaded copy if possible.** Open the portal preview or download-back link.
steps.expect: the portal copy is the same document, not a blank page or wrong file.

steps.action: **Submit or save the upload.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some portals lock the upload after final submission, so verify field and file before clicking Submit.
steps.expect: the item changes from draft/uploaded to submitted/received.

steps.action: **Save confirmation.** Download a receipt or screenshot the status page with filename, date, and reference number visible.
steps.expect: proof exists outside the portal.

recipes.verification: The portal status for the required document shows submitted, received, accepted, or equivalent, with the expected filename and date visible.

recipes.title: upscale an old photo
recipes.name: upscale-an-old-photo
recipes.goal: Improve the usable resolution of an old photo while preserving the original file and avoiding misleading edits.

steps.action: **Preserve the original.** Make a copy before editing and keep the untouched file in a safe folder.
steps.expect: the original can be restored at any time.

steps.action: **Choose a tool.** [BRANCH: local editor | AI web service] prefer local tools for family, identity, or sensitive images; use web services only when acceptable.
steps.expect: privacy risk is understood.

steps.action: **Set conservative enhancement.** Choose moderate upscaling and avoid aggressive face reconstruction unless the goal is clearly cosmetic.
steps.expect: the image improves without changing identity-defining features.

steps.action: **Run the upscale.** Process the copy and save the output with a new filename that marks it as enhanced.
steps.expect: both original and enhanced files exist.

steps.action: **Compare closely.** Check eyes, teeth, hands, clothing patterns, text, and background details for invented artifacts.
steps.expect: artificial changes are accepted, reduced, or rejected.

steps.action: **Export for use.** Save a high-quality version for printing or sharing and keep notes about the tool used.
steps.expect: recipients can distinguish restoration from original evidence.

recipes.verification: The enhanced file is larger or clearer, the untouched original still exists, and any invented or uncertain details are either absent or clearly disclosed.

recipes.title: use a chatbot safely
recipes.name: use-a-chatbot-safely
recipes.goal: Use a chatbot for drafting, brainstorming, learning, and routine assistance while controlling privacy, hallucination, and overreliance risks.

steps.action: **Check the data setting.** Review whether chats are saved, used for training, or shared with an organization administrator.
steps.expect: you know the privacy boundary before typing.

steps.action: **Remove sensitive data.** Replace names, account numbers, credentials, client details, and private health or legal facts with placeholders unless the tool is approved for them.
steps.expect: the prompt does not expose unnecessary personal data.

steps.action: **Use it for bounded tasks.** Ask for drafts, checklists, explanations, transformations, or options instead of asking it to make final high-stakes decisions.
steps.expect: the answer is a starting point you can review.

steps.action: **Demand uncertainty.** Ask the chatbot to flag assumptions, missing information, and claims that require current sources.
steps.expect: unsupported points are visible.

steps.action: **Verify important output.** [BRANCH: low-stakes | high-stakes] proofread low-stakes output yourself; verify high-stakes claims with authoritative sources or professionals.
steps.expect: no important claim is accepted solely because the chatbot said it.

steps.action: **Clean up when needed.** Delete sensitive chats if available and avoid saving private outputs in shared workspaces.
steps.expect: retained chat history matches your privacy needs.

recipes.verification: The chatbot account settings, prompt content, and review process match the sensitivity of the task, and any important factual claim has been checked outside the chat.

recipes.title: use a disposable email
recipes.name: use-a-disposable-email
recipes.goal: Use a disposable or relay email address for low-trust signups without losing access to accounts you may need later.

steps.action: **Classify the signup.** Decide whether the site is throwaway, low-trust, or important for purchases, identity, work, or recovery.
steps.expect: you know whether disposable email is appropriate.

steps.action: **Choose address type.** [BRANCH: temporary inbox | forwarding relay] use temporary inboxes only for throwaway access; use relay aliases when future recovery matters.
steps.expect: the address lifespan matches the account.

steps.action: **Create the address.** Generate or copy the disposable address and use it only for that specific site.
steps.expect: the site receives a unique address.

steps.action: **Complete verification.** Open the disposable inbox or relay mailbox and use the confirmation code or link.
steps.expect: the account verifies successfully.

steps.action: **Save recovery details when needed.** For relay aliases, store the alias and site name in your password manager.
steps.expect: you can identify and manage the alias later.

steps.action: **Disable or discard.** When the signup is no longer needed, disable the relay alias or abandon the temporary inbox.
steps.expect: future spam to that address stops or becomes irrelevant.

recipes.verification: The signup is verified, the address type matches the account importance, and any reusable alias is recorded in your password manager.

recipes.title: use a pivot table
recipes.name: use-a-pivot-table
recipes.goal: Create a simple pivot table that summarizes spreadsheet rows by category.

steps.action: **Select the source data.** Click inside the data table or highlight the full range.
steps.expect: the intended source data is active.

steps.action: **Insert the pivot table.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Insert > PivotTable`; Google Sheets: choose `Insert > Pivot table`.
steps.expect: a pivot table setup dialog appears.

steps.action: **Choose the destination.** Place the pivot table on a new worksheet or new sheet.
steps.expect: an empty pivot table area opens with a field list or editor.

steps.action: **Add a row field.** Drag or add the category column to Rows, such as `Region` or `Product`.
steps.expect: category names appear down the pivot table.

steps.action: **Add a value field.** Drag or add a numeric column to Values, such as `Sales`.
steps.expect: summarized numbers appear beside the categories.

steps.action: **Set the summary function.** Choose `SUM`, `COUNT`, or `AVERAGE` as needed.
steps.expect: the value heading shows the selected summary type.

recipes.verification: The pivot table lists categories from the chosen row field and shows the selected summary calculation for the intended numeric field.

recipes.title: use a voice assistant
recipes.name: use-a-voice-assistant
recipes.goal: Your voice assistant responds to the right wake word, handles common commands, and has history and privacy settings you understand.

steps.action: **Choose the assistant entry point.** Open the assistant app or device settings for Siri, Google Assistant, Alexa, or another installed assistant.
steps.expect: assistant setup or settings are visible.

steps.action: **Enable the wake word.** Turn on the wake phrase only on devices where hands-free use is helpful.
steps.expect: the device listens for the selected wake word.

steps.action: **Train voice recognition if offered.** Read the sample phrases so the assistant can distinguish your voice.
steps.expect: setup confirms your voice model or personal results.

steps.action: **Test common commands.** Ask for the weather, a timer, a reminder, and a calendar check.
steps.expect: each command returns an answer or asks for a missing permission.

steps.action: **Connect useful permissions.** [BRANCH: reminders | calls | smart home] allow only the services you actually plan to use.
steps.expect: the assistant can complete those specific tasks.

steps.action: **Set communication rules.** If using calls or messages, confirm the assistant asks before sending or calling when possible.
steps.expect: outgoing actions require clear confirmation.

steps.action: **Review history settings.** Open assistant privacy or activity history and choose whether voice recordings or transcripts are saved.
steps.expect: you know where to view and delete past activity.

steps.action: **Place devices carefully.** Keep always-listening speakers out of bathrooms, guest rooms, and sensitive work areas.
steps.expect: the assistant is available without sitting in the most private spaces.

recipes.verification: The assistant responds from the intended device, completes a timer and reminder correctly, and its history settings match your privacy choice.

recipes.title: use cloud storage
recipes.name: use-cloud-storage
recipes.goal: You have a cloud storage account set up with a folder structure you can navigate, a clear understanding of whether it is syncing or backing up, and sharing permissions set so the right people have exactly the access you intend.

steps.action: **Decide sync versus backup, because they are not the same.** Sync mirrors a folder across devices and the cloud; delete a file on one device and it vanishes everywhere. Backup keeps a separate protected copy. Cloud sync alone is not a backup.
steps.expect: you can state which of the two this account is doing for you.

steps.action: **Design a shallow, named folder structure.** A few top-level folders by area (Documents, Photos, Projects, Shared) beat a deep maze. Name for how you will search later.
steps.expect: a top level you can scan in one screen.

steps.action: **Choose what syncs to each device.** Use selective sync so a small laptop is not forced to hold your entire library; keep large archives cloud-only.
steps.expect: each device shows only the folders you chose, with free space intact.

steps.action: **Understand "online-only" versus "available offline."** Files marked online-only download on open and need a connection; mark anything you need on a plane as available offline first.
steps.expect: a test online-only file downloads on open, and an offline-marked file opens with the network off.

steps.action: **Set sharing permissions per item, most restrictive that still works.** Share a specific folder or file, choose view versus edit, and prefer named people over "anyone with the link."
steps.expect: the share dialog shows exactly who has access and at what level.

steps.action: **Check link scope before sending.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a public "anyone with the link" share can be forwarded and indexed beyond your control; treat it as posting publicly and set an expiry or restrict to named accounts for anything private.
steps.expect: the link's audience matches your intent; sensitive items are not world-readable.

steps.action: **Confirm sync health and review shares periodically.** Watch the app's sync status reach "up to date," and revisit the shared-items list to revoke access people no longer need.
steps.expect: sync status green; the shared list contains only current, intended recipients.

recipes.verification: The account has a shallow named folder structure, you can state whether each device is syncing or holding a backup, selective and offline settings behave as tested, every share shows exactly the intended people and access level with no unintended public links, and the app reports sync as up to date.

recipes.title: use conditional formatting
recipes.name: use-conditional-formatting
recipes.goal: Highlight spreadsheet cells automatically when they match a rule.

steps.action: **Select the cells to format.** Drag across the range where the rule should apply.
steps.expect: the target range is highlighted.

steps.action: **Open conditional formatting.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules`; Google Sheets: choose `Format > Conditional formatting`.
steps.expect: conditional formatting options appear.

steps.action: **Choose the rule.** Select a condition such as `Greater Than` and enter `100`, or use a custom formula such as `=$B2="Late"`.
steps.expect: the rule shows the intended condition.

steps.action: **Choose the style.** Pick a fill color or text style that will mark matching cells.
steps.expect: a preview or sample shows the selected style.

steps.action: **Apply the rule.** Click `OK` in Excel or `Done` in Google Sheets.
steps.expect: cells matching the rule are highlighted.

recipes.verification: At least one cell that meets the condition is highlighted, a cell that does not meet it is unhighlighted, and the rule's applied range matches the selected cells.

recipes.title: use incognito mode correctly
recipes.name: use-incognito-mode-correctly
recipes.goal: Use a private browsing window for local privacy without mistaking it for anonymity from websites, networks, employers, or internet providers.

steps.action: **Open a private window.** Use the browser menu or keyboard shortcut for incognito, private, or InPrivate mode.
steps.expect: the browser shows a separate private-mode window or badge.

steps.action: **Confirm what it protects locally.** Treat it as a window that will not save browsing history, cookies, form entries, or site sessions after it closes.
steps.expect: you know the protection is mainly on this device.

steps.action: **Confirm what it does not hide.** Remember that websites, downloads, bookmarks, employers, schools, internet providers, and network admins may still see activity.
steps.expect: you do not treat the session as anonymous.

steps.action: **Use it for the right task.** [BRANCH: shared computer | separate login | price or search test] use it to avoid staying signed in, test a second account, or reduce local tracking from existing cookies.
steps.expect: the task benefits from a clean local session.

steps.action: **Avoid sensitive downloads on shared machines.** If you download a file, delete it afterward and empty trash if appropriate.
steps.expect: no private file remains in the downloads folder.

steps.action: **Sign out before closing.** Log out of accounts used in the private window, especially email, banking, work, and social media.
steps.expect: the page confirms sign-out or returns to a public login screen.

steps.action: **Close every private window.** Close all private windows, not just one tab, to clear that session's cookies.
steps.expect: reopening private mode starts without the previous login.

steps.action: **Use stronger tools when needed.** For real anonymity or location masking, evaluate a reputable VPN, Tor Browser, or policy-approved work tool.
steps.expect: private mode is not the only privacy control for high-risk tasks.

recipes.verification: After all private windows are closed and reopened, the site no longer shows the prior session, while any downloaded or bookmarked files are handled intentionally.

recipes.title: use reader mode
recipes.name: use-reader-mode
recipes.goal: View an article-style page in a cleaner reading layout.

steps.action: **Look for reader controls.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] check the address bar, toolbar, or side panel for a reader, page, or document icon.
steps.expect: a reader option appears if the page is eligible.

steps.action: **Open reader mode.** Click the reader icon or choose the reader option from the browser menu.
steps.expect: the page changes to a simplified text layout.

steps.action: **Adjust reading settings.** Change text size, font, color theme, or width if controls are available.
steps.expect: the article remains readable and fits the window.

steps.action: **Leave reader mode.** Click the reader icon again, close the side panel, or use the Back button if needed.
steps.expect: the original web page view returns.

recipes.verification: The page displays in a simplified reader layout with the main article text visible and adjustable.

recipes.title: use voice typing well
recipes.name: use-voice-typing-well
recipes.goal: Use voice typing to produce accurate text faster while protecting privacy and correcting speech-recognition errors.

steps.action: **Check microphone and language.** Select the correct input language, keyboard, and microphone source.
steps.expect: the dictation control responds when you speak.

steps.action: **Choose a private setting.** Move away from people if the text includes names, work content, passwords, health details, or financial information.
steps.expect: sensitive speech cannot be easily overheard.

steps.action: **Dictate in short chunks.** Speak one or two sentences at a time and say punctuation where the system expects it.
steps.expect: text appears with fewer long-range errors.

steps.action: **Use commands deliberately.** [BRANCH: plain dictation | editing commands] dictate words normally; use supported commands such as new paragraph or delete only when you know they work.
steps.expect: commands change formatting instead of appearing as text.

steps.action: **Proofread before sending.** Check names, numbers, negations, dates, medications, addresses, and tone.
steps.expect: recognition mistakes are corrected.

steps.action: **Turn off dictation.** Stop listening mode when finished and check that the microphone indicator is off.
steps.expect: the device is no longer capturing speech for the text field.

recipes.verification: The final text matches what you intended, critical details are manually checked, and dictation is stopped after use.

recipes.title: view a pages source
recipes.name: view-a-pages-source
recipes.goal: Open the HTML source for the current web page.

steps.action: **Open page source.** [BRANCH: Chrome | Firefox | Safari] press `Ctrl+U` on Windows/Linux or `Command+Option+U` in Safari on Mac.
steps.expect: a new tab or window opens with page source.

steps.action: **Search within source if needed.** Press `Ctrl+F` or `Command+F` and type a tag, word, or URL.
steps.expect: matching source text is highlighted.

steps.action: **Return to the page.** Switch back to the original tab when finished.
steps.expect: the normal web page remains unchanged.

recipes.verification: A source view opens showing HTML or source text for the page URL, and the original page is still available.

recipes.title: watermark your images
recipes.name: watermark-your-images
recipes.goal: Add a visible or metadata watermark to images so viewers can identify ownership, origin, or permitted use.

steps.action: **Choose watermark type.** [BRANCH: visible | metadata | both] use visible marks for deterrence and metadata for attribution that does not alter the image.
steps.expect: the watermark goal is clear.

steps.action: **Create a working copy.** Duplicate the original image before editing.
steps.expect: the unwatermarked original remains available.

steps.action: **Place the watermark.** Add your name, logo, copyright notice, or content label in a consistent corner or repeated pattern.
steps.expect: the mark is readable but does not hide essential content.

steps.action: **Set opacity and size.** Adjust contrast so the watermark survives casual cropping or reposting without ruining the image.
steps.expect: the image remains usable.

steps.action: **Add metadata if needed.** Enter creator, copyright, license, contact, and usage terms in the editor's metadata fields.
steps.expect: attribution travels with files that preserve metadata.

steps.action: **Export and test.** Save a distribution copy and upload or message it to yourself to see whether the platform strips metadata or compresses the watermark.
steps.expect: the intended mark remains visible or metadata loss is known.

recipes.verification: The exported copy contains the intended visible watermark or metadata, and the original image remains unchanged in a separate file.

recipes.title: wrap text in a cell
recipes.name: wrap-text-in-a-cell
recipes.goal: Make long text display on multiple lines inside spreadsheet cells.

steps.action: **Select the text cells.** Highlight the cell or range with long text.
steps.expect: the intended cells are selected.

steps.action: **Turn on text wrapping.** [BRANCH: Excel | Google Sheets] Excel: choose `Home > Wrap Text`; Google Sheets: choose `Format > Wrapping > Wrap`.
steps.expect: long text breaks onto multiple lines inside each cell.

steps.action: **Adjust row height if needed.** Double-click the row boundary or use auto-fit.
steps.expect: all wrapped lines are visible.

recipes.verification: The selected long text is visible on multiple lines within each cell, without spilling over adjacent cells.

recipes.title: write a good ai prompt
recipes.name: write-a-good-ai-prompt
recipes.goal: Write a prompt that gives an AI system enough context, constraints, and success criteria to produce a useful first draft without exposing unnecessary private information.

steps.action: **State the task plainly.** Begin with one sentence that names the deliverable, audience, and purpose.
steps.expect: the prompt has a clear verb such as draft, compare, summarize, plan, or rewrite.

steps.action: **Add relevant context.** Include only facts the model needs, replacing private names, account numbers, medical details, and secrets with labels like `[client]` or `[account]`.
steps.expect: the prompt is useful without revealing avoidable personal data.

steps.action: **Define constraints.** Specify format, length, tone, sources allowed, assumptions to avoid, and anything the answer must not do. [BRANCH: creative | factual] creative prompts can allow options; factual prompts should require uncertainty labels and source checks.
steps.expect: the model has boundaries to follow.

steps.action: **Give examples when helpful.** Add one short example of a good output or a bad output to avoid.
steps.expect: the requested style or structure is easier to infer.

steps.action: **Ask for questions or caveats.** Tell the model to ask clarifying questions if blocked and to flag low-confidence claims instead of inventing details.
steps.expect: the prompt discourages hallucinated certainty.

steps.action: **Test and revise.** Run the prompt once, compare the result with your goal, then tighten vague wording.
steps.expect: the next version fixes the biggest mismatch you observed.

recipes.verification: The prompt names the deliverable, audience, context, constraints, output format, and uncertainty behavior, and a test response satisfies those requirements without using private details unnecessarily.

recipes.title: zip and unzip files
recipes.name: zip-and-unzip-files
recipes.goal: Files are compressed into a ZIP archive or extracted from one into a normal folder you can use.

steps.action: **Collect the source files.** Put the files in one folder and remove temporary items you do not want to share.
steps.expect: the folder contains only the intended files.

steps.action: **Compress the folder.** [BRANCH: Windows | macOS | mobile] Windows: right-click > Compress to ZIP file. macOS: right-click > Compress. Mobile: use Files or a trusted file manager.
steps.expect: a `.zip` file appears beside the folder.

steps.action: **Rename the archive clearly.** Use a short name without odd punctuation if it will be emailed or uploaded.
steps.expect: the ZIP name describes the contents and ends in `.zip`.

steps.action: **Add a password only if needed.** Use 7-Zip, Keka, WinZip, or similar when the built-in tool lacks encryption.
steps.expect: opening the ZIP prompts for the password on another device.

steps.action: **Share the ZIP.** Attach or upload the archive, and send any password in a separate channel.
steps.expect: the destination receives one archive instead of many loose files.

steps.action: **Extract a ZIP before editing.** Double-click or right-click Extract All, then choose a destination folder.
steps.expect: a normal folder appears with the files inside.

steps.action: **Avoid the already-extracted trap.** If you see both `Project.zip` and a `Project` folder, edit files in the folder, not inside the ZIP preview window.
steps.expect: saved edits remain visible after closing and reopening the file.

steps.action: **Delete extras only after checking.** Remove duplicate archives or extracted folders once you know which copy is current.
steps.expect: storage is cleaned without losing the working copy.

recipes.verification: The ZIP opens on another device or the extracted folder contains every expected file and can be edited normally.

recipes.title: zoom a web page
recipes.name: zoom-a-web-page
recipes.goal: Make a web page larger or smaller without changing the whole computer display.

steps.action: **Zoom in.** Press `Ctrl++` on Windows/Linux or `Command++` on Mac.
steps.expect: page text and content become larger.

steps.action: **Zoom out if needed.** Press `Ctrl+-` on Windows/Linux or `Command+-` on Mac.
steps.expect: page content becomes smaller.

steps.action: **Return to normal size.** Press `Ctrl+0` on Windows/Linux or `Command+0` on Mac.
steps.expect: the page returns to 100 percent zoom.

steps.action: **Check layout.** Scroll and inspect buttons, menus, and text.
steps.expect: important controls remain visible and usable.

recipes.verification: The page is readable at the chosen zoom level, and the browser zoom indicator shows the expected percentage.

recipes.title: answer the door for a resident
recipes.name: answer-the-door-for-a-resident
recipes.goal: Respond to a door knock or bell for a resident while preserving their consent, privacy, and physical security.

steps.action: **Check with the resident.** Ask whether they expect anyone and whether they want the door answered.
steps.expect: the resident gives permission or says not to answer.

steps.action: **Approach without opening.** Keep the door locked while moving to a peephole, window, camera, or intercom.
steps.expect: visitor identity can be assessed without entry.

steps.action: **Identify the visitor.** Ask who they are and why they are there.
steps.expect: the visitor states a name, role, or delivery purpose.

steps.action: **Confirm with the resident.** Relay identity quietly and ask whether to admit, decline, or take a message.
steps.expect: resident instruction is clear.
