steps.action: **Open only as instructed.** [BRANCH: admit | decline | package] unlock and open for approved entry, speak through the door for decline, or receive package without granting entry.
steps.expect: the visitor gets the intended response.

steps.action: **Maintain doorway control.** Stand clear of the swing path and avoid blocking the resident's mobility route.
steps.expect: the door can be closed quickly if needed.

steps.action: **Close and relock.** Shut the door after the interaction and re-engage locks.
steps.expect: the entry returns to secure status.

steps.action: **Report the outcome.** Tell the resident who came and what was done.
steps.expect: the resident knows the final status.

recipes.verification: The door interaction matches the resident's instruction, the door is closed and locked afterward, and no unauthorized person has entered.

recipes.title: assist someone into a coat
recipes.name: assist-someone-into-a-coat
recipes.goal: Help a person put on a coat without forcing joints, disturbing devices, or compromising comfort.

steps.action: **Ask preference and limits.** Confirm which arm should go first and whether any side hurts.
steps.expect: the person gives a preference or agrees to proceed.

steps.action: **Open the coat fully.** Unzip or unbutton it and find the inside of each sleeve.
steps.expect: sleeves are clear and not twisted.

steps.action: **Support the first sleeve.** Hold the cuff open near the person's hand without pulling the arm.
steps.expect: the person can place their hand into the sleeve.

steps.action: **Guide fabric over the arm.** Slide the sleeve up while the person moves as able.
steps.expect: fabric passes the elbow without snagging.

steps.action: **Bring the coat behind the shoulders.** Keep the collar low and avoid brushing face, glasses, or tubing.
steps.expect: the back panel rests behind the person.

steps.action: **Guide the second sleeve.** Offer the sleeve opening and let the person insert the second hand.
steps.expect: both arms are inside sleeves.

steps.action: **Settle the coat.** Smooth shoulders, cuffs, and back hem while asking about comfort.
steps.expect: the coat sits evenly and does not pull.

steps.action: **Fasten only if requested.** Zip, button, or snap from bottom to top while avoiding skin and devices.
steps.expect: closure is secure or intentionally left open.

recipes.verification: The coat is on with both arms placed comfortably, no device or skin is pinched, and the person confirms the fit is acceptable.

recipes.title: bring a blanket to someone
recipes.name: bring-a-blanket-to-someone
recipes.goal: Bring and place a blanket for someone so they are warmer without restricting movement, breathing, or medical equipment.

steps.action: **Confirm preference.** Ask whether they want the blanket and where they want it placed.
steps.expect: the person gives consent and placement preference.

steps.action: **Select a clean blanket.** Choose one appropriate for warmth and size.
steps.expect: blanket is dry, odor-free, and not visibly soiled.

steps.action: **Carry it clear of the floor.** Hold folded fabric away from spills, wheels, and footwear.
steps.expect: the blanket remains clean during transport.

steps.action: **Unfold near the person.** Keep fabric away from face, food, and devices.
steps.expect: edges are controlled and visible.

steps.action: **Drape as requested.** Place it over lap, shoulders, or bed area without covering face or controls.
steps.expect: the person is covered where requested.

steps.action: **Free devices and hands.** Keep call button, oxygen tube, IV line, walker, and wheelchair controls accessible.
steps.expect: no equipment is trapped under fabric.

steps.action: **Check comfort.** Ask if the blanket is too heavy, too warm, or needs adjustment.
steps.expect: the person confirms comfort or requests a change.

recipes.verification: The blanket is cleanly placed where requested, the person's face, hands, call controls, and medical devices remain accessible, and the person confirms comfort.

recipes.title: buckle a child into a car seat
recipes.name: buckle-a-child-into-a-car-seat
recipes.goal: The child is seated in the car seat with harness straps over the shoulders, buckle and chest clip fastened, chest clip at armpit level, and harness snug enough to pass the pinch test.

steps.action: **Prepare the harness.** Loosen straps, open the buckle and chest clip, and move straps to the sides without twisting.
steps.expect: seating area is clear and both shoulder straps are visible.

steps.action: **Seat the child fully back.** Place the child with hips and back against the car-seat shell, centered between side bolsters.
steps.expect: child's bottom is deep in the seat and spine follows the seat back.

steps.action: **Route straps over shoulders.** Bring each harness strap over the matching shoulder and down the torso without crossing.
steps.expect: straps lie flat from shoulder slot to buckle tongue.

steps.action: **Check shoulder slot height.** [BRANCH: rear-facing | forward-facing] for rear-facing, straps come from at or below shoulders; for forward-facing, at or above shoulders.
steps.expect: harness exits at the correct height for seat direction.

steps.action: **Buckle the crotch buckle.** Insert each buckle tongue into the buckle until each side clicks, then tug both tongues upward.
steps.expect: both tongues stay locked.

steps.action: **Fasten the chest clip.** Bring clip halves together at the child's chest and press until they click.
steps.expect: clip is closed and centered on the sternum.

steps.action: **Tighten the harness.** Pull the adjuster strap steadily while feeding slack from hip and belly areas upward toward the shoulders.
steps.expect: harness lies flat and slack disappears from the torso.

steps.action: **Set clip height and pinch test.** Slide the chest clip to armpit level, then pinch the webbing vertically at the collarbone.
steps.expect: no webbing fold can be pinched between fingers.

recipes.verification: The child is centered, buckle and chest clip are latched, chest clip is at armpit level, harness straps are flat, and the collarbone pinch test cannot lift a fold of webbing.

recipes.title: fetch an item for a person
recipes.name: fetch-an-item-for-a-person
recipes.goal: A person's request — "bring me my glasses / the remote / my blue pills" — ends with the *correct* item in their confirmed possession, with ambiguity resolved by asking rather than guessing.

steps.action: **Parse the request into item + distinguishing features + likely location.** "My glasses" → whose, which pair (reading vs. distance), where last seen. Missing features that matter → ask *now*, one compact question: "The reading glasses or the black ones?"
steps.expect: a search target specific enough that a wrong-item pickup would be surprising.

steps.action: **Search likely locations in probability order.** The item's home spot → where the person last was → adjacent surfaces. Search visually before disturbing things; lift-and-look under papers/cushions with restoration (`embodied/household/tidy-a-room` principles: nothing hidden, nothing rearranged).
steps.expect: candidate found within 2–3 locations, rooms left as found.

steps.action: **Verify the candidate against the distinguishing features.** Right color/type/label? **Medication special case:** the label must match the person's name and the named medicine exactly — ⚠️ *Irreversible:* delivering the wrong person's medication or the wrong drug is the category's serious harm; when any doubt exists, bring the *labeled container* to the person rather than loose items, and say what you observed: "This says 5 mg — is that the one?"
steps.expect: a candidate that matches every stated feature, or an explicit doubt being surfaced.

steps.action: **If not found after the likely locations: report and re-scope, don't spiral.** Return (or call out) with what you checked: "Not on the nightstand or the sofa — where else should I look?" The requester's memory usually solves it in one exchange.
steps.expect: a new location hint or a redefined target; the search stays collaborative.

steps.action: **Carry it back per its fragility.** Glasses by the frame (never lenses), liquids upright, the phone not stacked under the book (`embodied/mobility/carry-and-deliver-an-item`).
steps.expect: item intact and clean on arrival.

steps.action: **Hand over into confirmed possession.** Into a ready hand ("got it?"), or placed at their stated spot within easy reach — for limited-mobility requesters, *within actual reach* matters more than proximity: on the tray table, not the far counter.
steps.expect: the person confirms it's the right item, in hand or in reach.

recipes.verification: The person has the correct item confirmed (name-matched, for anything medical), within actual reach; searched rooms are as they were; any ambiguity, damage, or safety flag traveled *to the person* rather than being absorbed silently.

recipes.title: give a medication reminder
recipes.name: give-a-medication-reminder
recipes.goal: At the scheduled time, the person is reminded to take a specific medication, the reminder is matched to the correct labeled dose, the outcome (taken, refused, deferred) is confirmed, and the event is logged for caregivers.

steps.action: **Trigger on the scheduled time, not on convenience.** Prompt within the schedule's window, not early to batch tasks nor late because you were busy.
steps.expect: current time falls inside the prescribed window for this specific dose.

steps.action: **Match the label to the schedule before speaking.** Read the container label and confirm drug name and dose match the schedule entry exactly. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a wrong drug or dose taken cannot be undone. If the label does not match the schedule, do not prompt for it; flag the caregiver.
steps.expect: label name and dose are an exact match to the schedule line.

steps.action: **Give a clear, specific reminder.** Name the medication and the time, not just "take your pills." Keep it calm and unhurried.
steps.expect: the person acknowledges and understands which medication is due.

steps.action: **Present the aid, not the decision.** Point to or bring the correctly labeled container and a glass of water. Let the person handle and take the dose themselves.
steps.expect: the person has the right container and water in reach.

steps.action: **Confirm the outcome.** Watch or ask to confirm what actually happened. [BRANCH: taken → record time and dose | deferred ("in a minute") → set a short re-prompt and log the deferral | refused → go to refusal handling]
steps.expect: an unambiguous outcome, not an assumption that presenting equals taking.

steps.action: **Handle refusal without pressure.** Do not argue, coax repeatedly, or physically insist. Ask once if they want to wait a few minutes, then record the refusal and notify the caregiver per the plan.
steps.expect: refusal recorded and escalated; the person is not badgered.

steps.action: **Log the event immediately.** Write the drug, dose, scheduled time, actual time, and outcome (taken / deferred / refused) while it is fresh.
steps.expect: a complete, timestamped entry a caregiver can read later.

recipes.verification: The care log shows a timestamped entry for the scheduled dose with a confirmed outcome, the medication presented matched the schedule's drug and dose, and any refusal or miss was escalated to the caregiver rather than resolved by the robot.

recipes.title: guide someone by the arm
recipes.name: guide-someone-by-the-arm
recipes.goal: A person is guided through a space by consented arm contact, matched pace, and clear warning of obstacles or changes in terrain.

steps.action: **Ask for consent.** Ask whether the person wants arm guidance and which side they prefer.
steps.expect: person gives clear consent and side preference.

steps.action: **Describe the route briefly.** Name the destination and any immediate obstacle such as a doorway, ramp, or step.
steps.expect: person knows the first movement segment.

steps.action: **Offer the arm.** Place the actor's forearm or elbow near the person's hand without grabbing them.
steps.expect: person can choose where to hold.

steps.action: **Wait for their hold.** Pause until they take the arm, sleeve, or elbow at their preferred grip pressure.
steps.expect: contact is initiated by the person.

steps.action: **Start slowly.** Move at their pace with half steps until rhythm is matched.
steps.expect: both bodies move together without pulling.

steps.action: **Maintain side-by-side alignment.** Keep the guiding arm relaxed and slightly ahead only enough to signal direction.
steps.expect: person follows without shoulder twist or forced reach.

steps.action: **Warn before obstacles.** Announce turns, narrow spaces, floor changes, ramps, steps, doors, and people before reaching them.
steps.expect: person has time to adjust gait.

steps.action: **Pause on uncertainty.** [BRANCH: obstacle clear | obstacle uncertain] continue if clear; stop and re-scan if crowded, narrow, or unclear.
steps.expect: movement resumes only when path is safe.

steps.action: **End the guide deliberately.** Stop at the destination, state arrival, and wait for them to release or transfer support.
steps.expect: person is stable before contact ends.

recipes.verification: The person reaches the destination or next stable waypoint, remains balanced, and releases or continues the guide by explicit consent.

recipes.title: hand a tool to a person safely
recipes.name: hand-a-tool-to-a-person-safely
recipes.goal: A tool is transferred to a person handle-first, with release only after the person has control.

steps.action: **Identify the safe grip area.** Locate the handle or non-working end of the tool.
steps.expect: sharp, hot, or active parts are oriented away from the person.

steps.action: **Grip the working end safely if needed.** Hold the tool so the handle points toward the person and hazards point down or away.
steps.expect: the handle is unobstructed for the receiver.

steps.action: **Announce the handoff.** Pause near the person and present the tool at chest or hand height.
steps.expect: the person looks at the tool or extends a hand.

steps.action: **Move slowly into reach.** Advance the handle until it is within the person's open grasp without touching their body.
steps.expect: the person can close fingers around the handle.

steps.action: **Wait for secure grasp.** Maintain your grip until the person has wrapped fingers around the handle.
steps.expect: the tool is supported by both parties.

steps.action: **Confirm transfer.** Reduce grip force slightly while observing whether the tool remains steady in the person's hand.
steps.expect: the person supports the tool without dropping or twisting.

steps.action: **Release and withdraw.** Let go fully and move your hand away from the tool path.
steps.expect: the person holds the tool alone and hazardous ends remain clear.

recipes.verification: The person has sole stable control of the tool by its handle, and no sharp, hot, or active part is directed toward either person.

recipes.title: hand an object to a person
recipes.name: hand-an-object-to-a-person
recipes.goal: An object is transferred to a person only after they are ready, gripping it, and receiving the safe end or intended handle.

steps.action: **Confirm intent.** Ask or verify that the person wants the object now.
steps.expect: person gives verbal, gestural, or contextual consent.

steps.action: **Approach slowly.** Stop outside their personal space and within arm reach.
steps.expect: person can see the actor and object.

steps.action: **Orient the safe end.** Turn handles, blunt ends, labels, or grip surfaces toward the person.
steps.expect: hazardous, hot, sharp, or messy surfaces face away from them.

steps.action: **Announce the handoff.** State the object name and where it will be offered if speech is appropriate.
steps.expect: person attends to the object.

steps.action: **Offer at reachable height.** Extend the object midway between actor and person, close to their dominant hand if known.
steps.expect: person can reach without leaning dangerously.

steps.action: **Hold steady.** Keep the object still and supported while they place fingers or hand on it.
steps.expect: their grip contacts a stable part of the object.

steps.action: **Wait for grip confirmation.** [BRANCH: verbal confirm | physical confirm] accept "got it" or detect firm opposing grip and load support.
steps.expect: person is bearing the object's weight or controlling it.

steps.action: **Release gradually.** Open the actor's grip slowly while watching for slip.
steps.expect: object remains in the person's control.

steps.action: **Withdraw and pause.** Move hands back without brushing their body or assistive devices.
steps.expect: person holds the object comfortably.

recipes.verification: The person has consented, holds the object independently by a safe surface, and the actor has fully released without drop or contact.

recipes.title: help someone drink from a cup
recipes.name: help-someone-drink-from-a-cup
recipes.goal: Help a person take a drink from a cup while minimizing choking, spills, burns, and loss of control.

steps.action: **Confirm consent and drink type.** Ask if they want a sip and verify the cup contents.
steps.expect: the person agrees and the drink is appropriate.

steps.action: **Check posture.** Ensure head and torso are upright, not lying back.
steps.expect: the person's mouth and throat are positioned for swallowing.

steps.action: **Check temperature.** Test or confirm that the drink is not too hot.
steps.expect: temperature is safe for the person's mouth.

steps.action: **Offer the cup or straw.** Bring it into view and within comfortable reach.
steps.expect: the person can see or feel the cup before contact.

steps.action: **Support without forcing.** Hold the cup steady while the person controls lip contact or straw use.
steps.expect: lips seal or straw is positioned without pushing.

steps.action: **Tilt slowly for a small sip.** Raise the cup only enough for a controlled amount.
steps.expect: liquid reaches the mouth without flooding.

steps.action: **Pause for swallow.** Lower the cup and wait for the person to swallow and breathe normally.
steps.expect: no coughing, wet voice, or distress appears.

steps.action: **Repeat only if safe.** [BRANCH: wants more | stop] continue small sips if requested, otherwise set cup down.
steps.expect: drinking ends by consent or after safe sips.

steps.action: **Wipe and settle.** Offer a napkin and place the cup in a stable reachable place if allowed.
steps.expect: face, clothing, and cup area are clean and comfortable.

recipes.verification: The person has taken only consented, controlled sips, remains upright, shows normal breathing and voice, and the cup is set down securely.

recipes.title: help someone find misplaced glasses
recipes.name: help-someone-find-misplaced-glasses
recipes.goal: Help someone locate misplaced glasses and return them without damaging the glasses or disturbing private belongings unnecessarily.

steps.action: **Ask for last known use.** Ask where the glasses were last worn, removed, or cleaned.
steps.expect: one or more likely search areas are identified.

steps.action: **Check the person first.** Look at head, neckline, lap, pockets, bedcovers, and nearby chair arms.
steps.expect: glasses are found there or ruled out.

steps.action: **Search visible surfaces.** Inspect tables, counters, nightstands, bathroom sinks, and cases without moving private items yet.
steps.expect: obvious locations are checked.

steps.action: **Lift soft items carefully.** Raise blankets, towels, papers, or clothing one layer at a time.
steps.expect: hidden glasses are not crushed or flung.

steps.action: **Ask before private search.** Request permission before opening drawers, bags, cabinets, or mail piles.
steps.expect: consent is given or the area is skipped.

steps.action: **Check unsafe spots.** Look under chairs, near floor edges, and beside beds before anyone steps or sits.
steps.expect: glasses are recovered or protected from damage.

steps.action: **Return the glasses safely.** Hand them over by the frame or place them in the person's hand or case as preferred.
steps.expect: the person has control of the glasses.

steps.action: **Store or mark the location.** If requested, place the case in a consistent reachable spot.
steps.expect: the person knows where the glasses are now.

recipes.verification: The glasses are found and returned intact to the person or placed in a known case/location, with private areas searched only by permission.

recipes.title: help someone into a wheelchair
recipes.name: help-someone-into-a-wheelchair
recipes.goal: Assist a person into a wheelchair only with consent, proper setup, and enough ability or trained help for a safe transfer.

steps.action: **Confirm readiness.** Ask about pain, dizziness, weakness, and preferred transfer method.
steps.expect: the person consents or the task pauses.

steps.action: **Position the wheelchair.** Place it close to the stronger side if known, angled slightly toward the person.
steps.expect: the transfer path is short and clear.

steps.action: **Lock both brakes.** Engage brakes and test that the chair does not roll.
steps.expect: the wheelchair stays still when pushed lightly.

steps.action: **Move footrests aside.** Swing away or remove footrests before the person stands or pivots.
steps.expect: no metal parts block feet.

steps.action: **Prepare support.** Apply a gait belt if trained and place walker or helper stance as prescribed.
steps.expect: support is ready before movement starts.

steps.action: **Cue the stand or slide.** [BRANCH: stand-pivot | slide-board] guide the agreed method without pulling arms or lifting dead weight.
steps.expect: the person begins moving with control.

steps.action: **Guide hips to the chair.** Keep close support while they turn or slide until hips contact the wheelchair seat.
steps.expect: the person is centered over the seat, not the wheel or armrest.

steps.action: **Lower and settle.** Help them sit fully back, then place feet on footrests if appropriate. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an uncontrolled fall can injure the person; stop and call for trained help if weight bearing or balance is uncertain.
steps.expect: the person is seated upright with feet supported.

steps.action: **Confirm comfort and safety.** Check brakes, posture, clothing, tubing, and lap belt if used.
steps.expect: nothing is pinched, dragged, or unstable.

recipes.verification: The person is seated fully in the wheelchair, brakes are locked, feet and medical devices are clear of moving parts, and the person confirms they are comfortable or stable.

recipes.title: help someone put on shoes
recipes.name: help-someone-put-on-shoes
recipes.goal: Help a person put on shoes with feet protected, fasteners secure, and no painful forcing.

steps.action: **Ask about comfort and order.** Confirm which foot to start with and whether any foot is painful.
steps.expect: the person consents and identifies limits.

steps.action: **Prepare the shoe.** Loosen laces, straps, or tongue and remove objects inside.
steps.expect: the opening is wide and clear.

steps.action: **Support the foot.** Lift only as much as needed, keeping the ankle aligned.
steps.expect: the foot is stable without pulling the leg.

steps.action: **Slide the shoe on.** Guide toes into the toe box and ease the heel in without crumpling the back.
steps.expect: toes and heel are fully inside.

steps.action: **Check fit before fastening.** Ask if toes are cramped or seams pinch.
steps.expect: the person reports acceptable comfort or asks for adjustment.

steps.action: **Fasten securely.** Tie laces, close straps, or zip so the shoe stays on without cutting circulation.
steps.expect: fasteners are snug and flat.

steps.action: **Repeat for the other foot.** Use the same consent and comfort checks.
steps.expect: both shoes are on the correct feet.

steps.action: **Confirm standing safety.** Check soles, laces, and foot placement before the person stands.
steps.expect: no loose lace or unstable heel remains.

recipes.verification: Both shoes are on the correct feet, fastened securely, comfortable by the person's report, and free of loose parts that could cause tripping.

recipes.title: help someone stand up
recipes.name: help-someone-stand-up
recipes.goal: Help a person move from sitting to standing only if they can participate and bear weight, then confirm they are steady before walking.

steps.action: **Ask how they feel.** Check pain, dizziness, weakness, and whether they can put weight on their legs.
steps.expect: the person answers clearly or signals stop.

steps.action: **Decide if help is safe.** Do not lift dead weight or pull someone who cannot bear weight.
steps.expect: either they can assist, or the task pauses for more help.

steps.action: **Set the environment.** Lock wheelchair brakes, move rugs, and place walker or cane in front if used.
steps.expect: feet and assistive device have clear space.

steps.action: **Position their feet.** Cue feet flat, hip-width, and slightly behind the knees.
steps.expect: shins angle forward enough for standing.

steps.action: **Move them to the seat edge.** Ask them to scoot forward using chair arms or the seat.
steps.expect: hips are near the front edge, not deep in the chair.

steps.action: **Apply a gait belt if trained.** Place it snugly over clothing at the waist, avoiding tubes or tender areas.
steps.expect: two fingers fit under the belt and it does not ride up.

steps.action: **Set your stance.** Stand close, feet staggered, knees bent, back neutral.
steps.expect: your body can guide without twisting.

steps.action: **Cue the motion.** Count "one, two, three, stand" and ask them to push from the chair, not pull your neck.
steps.expect: they lean forward and begin pushing with legs and arms.

steps.action: **Brace and guide.** Hold the gait belt or support at the trunk while they stand.
steps.expect: you guide balance but their legs supply the lift.

steps.action: **Pause upright.** Keep support until they report no dizziness and knees are not buckling.
steps.expect: posture is steady for several breaths.

steps.action: **Check gait readiness.** Ask them to shift weight, march once, or place hands on walker.
steps.expect: they can bear weight before taking a step.

steps.action: **Stop if unsafe.** [BRANCH: steady | not weight-bearing] continue only if steady; if not, sit them back down and call for help.
steps.expect: no forced walking occurs.

recipes.verification: The person stands with their own weight through both legs, remains steady for several breaths, and either walks with the proper aid or sits back down safely.

recipes.title: help with a video call to family
recipes.name: help-with-a-video-call-to-family
recipes.goal: An older or less-technical family member is connected to a video call with relatives, sees and hears them clearly, is framed well and comfortable, and the helper steps back so the call belongs to the person, not the person handling the device.

steps.action: **Stage the device before the scheduled time.** Charge above 50%, open the app, confirm the contact is correct.
steps.expect: app open on the contact, battery healthy, no login prompt waiting to ambush the call.

steps.action: **Fix the lighting first.** Light should fall on the person's face, not behind them. Move a lamp to the front or turn the chair away from a bright window.
steps.expect: the face is clearly lit in the self-preview, not a dark silhouette against a glowing background.

steps.action: **Set framing with a stand, not a hand.** Prop the device so the camera sits near eye level and the person's head and shoulders fill the frame with a little headroom.
steps.expect: in the self-view the person is centered, looking slightly up or level, both eyes visible.

steps.action: **Set volume and confirm audio before dialing.** Raise media volume to about 70%, unmute the mic, and if the person is hard of hearing enable captions in the app settings.
steps.expect: volume near max-but-not-distorting; captions toggle on if needed; mic shows unmuted.

steps.action: **Place the call and confirm two-way.** Tap call, wait for the far end. When they answer, ask the person to say hello and watch for a reply. [BRANCH: they hear and see each other → hand off | one side is silent or frozen → F1/F2].
steps.expect: both parties visibly react to each other within a few seconds.

steps.action: **Hand the call to the person and step out of frame.** Confirm they know one control: how to end the call (point to the red button once).
steps.expect: the person is talking to family, not to you; you are out of the shot.

steps.action: **Stay reachable but silent.** Remain within earshot for a freeze or a dropped call, without hovering in frame or narrating.
steps.expect: the conversation runs on its own; you intervene only if something breaks.

steps.action: **Exit gracefully at the end.** When they finish, help tap end if asked, put the device back on its charger, and leave it ready for next time.
steps.expect: call ended cleanly, device charging, app still signed in for the next call.

recipes.verification: The family member sees and hears their relatives, is well framed and comfortable, the helper is out of frame, and at the end the call is ended cleanly with the device back on its charger and still signed in.

recipes.title: keep a daily care log
recipes.name: keep-a-daily-care-log
recipes.goal: A running log of a person's day (meals, fluids, medications, activity, mood, and notable events) is kept in objective, timestamped language, with defined thresholds flagged for the caregiver and a clean handoff at shift change.

steps.action: **Record on the event, not from memory.** Enter each item as it happens with a timestamp, rather than reconstructing the day at the end.
steps.expect: entries carry the actual clock time they occurred.

steps.action: **Log the core categories.** Capture meals and how much was eaten, fluids, medications (taken/refused/missed), toileting if in the plan, activity and mobility, sleep, and mood or behavior changes.
steps.expect: each category has entries or an explicit "none observed" for the period.

steps.action: **Write objectively, describe don't diagnose.** Record what you observed: "ate about half the lunch, left the vegetables," not "poor appetite"; "walked to the kitchen with the walker, steady," not "doing well."
steps.expect: entries a different caregiver could verify from the same observation.

steps.action: **Note deviations from baseline.** When something differs from this person's normal (ate much less, more confused, did not get up), record the observation and the baseline it differs from.
steps.expect: the deviation is explicit, not buried in routine notes.

steps.action: **Flag at the plan's thresholds.** [BRANCH: within normal range → log only | crosses a threshold (skipped meal, low fluids, a fall, refused medication, new confusion) → log and raise a caregiver alert]
steps.expect: every threshold crossing produces both a log entry and an alert, not just a note.

steps.action: **Keep opinions and identity separate.** Record behavior and facts, not judgments about the person; do not speculate about causes you cannot observe.
steps.expect: no diagnostic or evaluative language in the factual log.

steps.action: **Hand off at shift change.** Summarize the period for the incoming caregiver: what happened, any open flags, anything to watch. Confirm the summary is received.
steps.expect: the next caregiver acknowledges the flags and open items; nothing time-sensitive is lost in the gap.

recipes.verification: The log for the period contains timestamped, objective entries across the core categories, every care-plan threshold crossing has a matching caregiver alert, and the shift-change handoff was acknowledged with all open flags carried forward.

recipes.title: respond to a fall
recipes.name: respond-to-a-fall
recipes.goal: After a person falls, they are assessed before any movement, emergency help is called when thresholds are met, they are kept calm and comfortable, and the event is documented, without the robot lifting them prematurely.

steps.action: **Stop and do not lift immediately.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* moving someone with a fracture, spinal injury, or head trauma can cause permanent harm. Do not haul them up because it seems helpful.
steps.expect: the person stays where they landed until assessed.

steps.action: **Check responsiveness and breathing.** Speak to them, ask if they can hear you, look for breathing and any obvious severe bleeding or deformity.
steps.expect: a clear read on whether they are conscious and breathing normally.

steps.action: **Call emergency services at the hard thresholds.** [BRANCH: unconscious, not breathing normally, seizing, severe bleeding, a visibly deformed or painful hip/leg, hit their head, on blood thinners, or cannot get up → call emergency services now, then the caregiver | alert and uninjured and says they are fine → go to the assisted-recovery branch]
steps.expect: for any threshold hit, emergency services are contacted before any attempt to move them.

steps.action: **Keep them still and talk to them.** Ask them not to rush to get up. Tell them help is coming if you called. Keep your presence calm and steady.
steps.expect: the person stays calm and does not scramble to stand on a possibly injured limb.

steps.action: **Ask what hurts before any recovery.** Have them slowly check whether they can move fingers, arms, and legs and where the pain is, without forcing anything.
steps.expect: a clear picture of pain and mobility that confirms whether self-recovery is safe.

steps.action: **Assist recovery only if clearly uninjured.** If they are alert, pain-free, and want to get up, let them do the work in stages (roll to side, to hands and knees, up to a sturdy chair) while you steady the chair and spot them. Do not pull them up by the arms.
steps.expect: the person rises under their own power in stages; the robot stabilizes furniture, never bears their weight up.

steps.action: **Comfort and monitor after.** Provide a blanket for shock or cold, stay with them, and watch for delayed symptoms (dizziness, confusion, worsening pain).
steps.expect: the person is warm, seated or resting, and observed for a change.

steps.action: **Document the fall.** Log the time, what was seen, injuries reported, whether emergency services or the caregiver were called, and the outcome.
steps.expect: a complete timestamped entry and the caregiver notified regardless of severity.

recipes.verification: The person was assessed before any movement, emergency services were called whenever a threshold was met, no premature lift occurred, the person is comfortable and monitored, and a timestamped log entry with caregiver notification exists.

recipes.title: serve a meal at a table
recipes.name: serve-a-meal-at-a-table
recipes.goal: Serve a meal at a table so the person can eat safely, comfortably, and with the correct food and utensils.

steps.action: **Confirm meal identity.** Check the person's name, diet instructions, allergies, and meal contents.
steps.expect: the meal is safe for this person.

steps.action: **Clear the place setting.** Remove clutter and wipe spills from the eating area.
steps.expect: plate, cup, and utensils have stable spaces.

steps.action: **Place the main plate.** Set it centered in front of the person or where they prefer.
steps.expect: the plate is stable and reachable.

steps.action: **Orient utensils and napkin.** Put utensils on the usable side and napkin within reach.
steps.expect: the person can pick them up without stretching.

steps.action: **Place drink safely.** Put the cup away from the plate edge and confirm temperature if hot.
steps.expect: the cup is upright and reachable without tipping.

steps.action: **Announce hot, sharp, or spill risks.** Point out hot bowls, knives, or lidded containers.
steps.expect: the person knows which items need caution.

steps.action: **Ask before cutting or opening items.** Offer assistance with packets, lids, or cutting food.
steps.expect: assistance is consented to or declined.

steps.action: **Confirm readiness.** Check posture, call bell or phone access if relevant, and comfort before leaving.
steps.expect: the person can begin eating safely.

recipes.verification: The correct meal is placed within reach on a clean table, hazards are identified, adaptive needs are met, and the person is upright and ready to eat.

recipes.title: set up a bedside station
recipes.name: set-up-a-bedside-station
recipes.goal: The essentials a person needs from bed (water, medication, light, a way to call for help, their glasses and phone) are arranged on a bedside surface so every one of them is reachable without standing up, with medications visible and clearly organized.

steps.action: **Clear and stabilize the surface.** Remove clutter, wipe it, confirm the nightstand does not rock.
steps.expect: a clean, steady surface at about the height of the mattress top.

steps.action: **Place water within easy reach, spill-safe.** A lidded cup or a bottle with a straw beats an open glass that gets knocked over in the dark. Set it on the side the person's dominant hand reaches.
steps.expect: the person can grasp and drink without leaning off the bed; a spill would not soak bedding or electronics.

steps.action: **Stage medication visibly and unambiguously.** Use a labeled day/time pill organizer, not loose bottles, so "did I take it" is answerable by looking. Keep it in a consistent spot and orientation. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an accidental double dose is real harm. Stage only the doses due, per the person's schedule, and keep the rest out of the station if confusion or a double-dose risk exists.
steps.expect: the correct compartment is visible and distinguishable; nothing about which pills, when, is left to memory.

steps.action: **Position light for one-touch on/off.** A lamp or a touch light the person can turn on before sitting up, reachable without fumbling. Route the cord so it cannot pull the lamp down.
steps.expect: light comes on with a single reachable touch; the cord is tucked, not draped across the reach path.

steps.action: **Set the call device where it is always found.** Phone on its charger, or a dedicated call button or bell, in a fixed spot the person can locate in the dark by feel.
steps.expect: the person taps or presses it from lying down; it is charged and (if a phone) volume-up and unlocked-to-dial or on emergency-accessible.

steps.action: **Add the small dignity items.** Glasses (folded, lenses up), tissues, the TV remote, anything the person reaches for reflexively.
steps.expect: each item in a consistent, felt-for spot within the reach zone.

steps.action: **Run the reach test from the bed.** Have the person lie as they normally do and touch each item in turn: water, meds, light, call device, glasses. Anything they strain for gets moved closer.
steps.expect: every essential is reached without the person lifting their torso off the bed or overbalancing.

recipes.verification: From their normal lying position the person can reach water, the correct staged medication, a one-touch light, and a charged call device, plus glasses and personal items, without standing or overbalancing; medications are visible and organized rather than loose; no cord crosses the reach path.

recipes.title: steady someone who is walking
recipes.name: steady-someone-who-is-walking
recipes.goal: A walking person receives consensual, side-by-side steadying support while maintaining their own balance and direction.

steps.action: **Ask before touching.** Say what support you can offer and wait for consent.
steps.expect: the person agrees, declines, or requests a specific kind of help.

steps.action: **Move to the support side.** Stand slightly behind and to the side the person chooses, leaving their feet and aid clear.
steps.expect: you can see their footing without blocking the path.

steps.action: **Offer an arm or forearm.** Present your forearm for them to hold instead of grabbing their hand or shoulder.
steps.expect: the person controls the contact and grip pressure.

steps.action: **Start at their pace.** Take small steps that match their cadence and stride length.
steps.expect: neither person is pulling the other forward.

steps.action: **Watch the walking surface.** Scan for rugs, cords, wet spots, thresholds, and uneven flooring.
steps.expect: hazards are seen before the person reaches them.

steps.action: **Pause for instability.** [BRANCH: steady | unsteady] continue if gait is stable, or stop and guide toward a chair or rail if it is not.
steps.expect: support changes before balance is lost.

steps.action: **Turn slowly.** For corners or direction changes, cue the turn and move in a wide arc.
steps.expect: feet turn without crossing or tangling.

steps.action: **Release only when stable.** Stop at the destination and confirm they are seated or standing securely before letting go.
steps.expect: the person is supported by the chair, rail, walker, or their own stance.

recipes.verification: The person reaches the destination without a fall, with consent maintained and stable support present until seated or balanced.

recipes.title: align and close a drawer
recipes.name: align-and-close-a-drawer
recipes.goal: The drawer is aligned on its runners and closed flush with the cabinet or desk front.

steps.action: **Inspect the gap.** Look along both drawer sides and the top edge.
steps.expect: any skew or obstruction is visible.

steps.action: **Grip the handle centered.** Place hand at the middle of the handle or front face to avoid twisting.
steps.expect: pull or push force will be centered.

steps.action: **Square the drawer.** If one side is ahead, pull back slightly and guide the front until both side gaps match.
steps.expect: the drawer front is parallel to the cabinet face.

steps.action: **Push straight inward.** Apply steady centered pressure along the drawer travel direction.
steps.expect: the drawer slides inward without scraping.

steps.action: **Slow near closure.** Reduce force in the final few centimeters to avoid slamming.
steps.expect: the drawer face approaches the cabinet evenly.

steps.action: **Seat flush.** Push gently until the latch or stop engages.
steps.expect: the drawer front is flush or evenly recessed with adjacent surfaces.

steps.action: **Release and observe.** Remove hand and watch for rebound.
steps.expect: the drawer stays closed and aligned.

recipes.verification: The drawer front is flush and parallel to the cabinet, stays closed after release, and no contents protrude.

recipes.title: button a shirt
recipes.name: button-a-shirt
recipes.goal: The shirt front is closed with each button seated through its matching buttonhole, the plackets aligned, and the collar button handled last if used.

steps.action: **Find the bottom pair.** Trace both plackets to the lowest button and its same-height hole.
steps.expect: button and hole edges meet without diagonal pull.

steps.action: **Align the plackets.** Hold the button side flat behind the hole side so hems and seam lines match.
steps.expect: both front edges stack evenly.

steps.action: **Pinch the button.** Grip the button rim between thumb and index finger, not the thread shank.
steps.expect: button tilts while remaining attached and centered.

steps.action: **Open the hole.** With the other thumb and index finger, spread the buttonhole lips into a narrow oval.
steps.expect: the slot exposes enough space for the button edge.

steps.action: **Angle the button through.** Lead one edge of the button through the hole, then roll the rest of the button after it.
steps.expect: part of the button appears on the outside face.

steps.action: **Pull the fabric over.** Draw the hole-side placket around the button while pushing the button forward gently.
steps.expect: button pops fully through and lies flat.

steps.action: **Continue bottom-up.** Repeat each matched pair upward, checking alignment after every button. [BRANCH: skipped hole | correct pair]
steps.expect: no puckers or crossed plackets appear.

steps.action: **Button the collar last.** If desired, use lighter force at the neck and stop if it constricts.
steps.expect: collar closes without pressure on the throat.

recipes.verification: All chosen buttons pass through their matching holes, both plackets hang evenly from hem to collar, and no button is under visible strain.

recipes.title: change bed sheets
recipes.name: change-bed-sheets
recipes.goal: Remove used bed linens and make the bed with clean fitted sheet, top layer, and pillowcases so the sleeping surface is smooth and ready.

steps.action: **Clear the bed area.** Move phones, books, glasses, and breakables from the bed and nearby edges.
steps.expect: bedding can move without knocking items down.

steps.action: **Strip pillowcases.** Pull each pillowcase off by turning it inside out around the pillow.
steps.expect: pillows are bare and used cases are in the laundry basket.

steps.action: **Remove top layers.** Fold back blanket, duvet, or flat sheet and place washable used linens in the basket.
steps.expect: only the fitted sheet remains on the mattress.

steps.action: **Remove the fitted sheet.** Lift one corner at a time and release the elastic from under the mattress.
steps.expect: the mattress surface is bare.

steps.action: **Check the mattress pad.** Smooth it or replace it if wet or dirty.
steps.expect: the pad lies flat with corners secured.

steps.action: **Orient the clean fitted sheet.** Find the long side and corner seams before stretching it onto the bed.
steps.expect: seams line up with mattress corners.

steps.action: **Secure fitted corners.** Hook the far corners first, then near corners, lifting the mattress just enough to tuck elastic under.
steps.expect: elastic wraps under all four corners.

steps.action: **Smooth the fitted sheet.** Pull wrinkles toward the edges and tuck any loose sides.
steps.expect: the sleeping surface is flat and taut.

steps.action: **Add flat sheet or duvet.** [BRANCH: flat sheet | duvet] align the top edge evenly, or shake the duvet into place.
steps.expect: both sides hang about the same length.

steps.action: **Tuck or fold the foot.** For a flat sheet, tuck the foot end under the mattress.
steps.expect: the sheet stays anchored when lightly pulled.

steps.action: **Dress pillows.** Insert pillows into clean cases, corners first, then shake and flatten.
steps.expect: pillow corners fill the case corners.

steps.action: **Finish the top.** Place pillows at the head and smooth the top layer.
steps.expect: the bed looks even and ready to use.

recipes.verification: The mattress is covered by a clean fitted sheet with all four corners secured, top bedding is even, and every pillow has a clean pillowcase.

recipes.title: clean a litter box
recipes.name: clean-a-litter-box
recipes.goal: The litter box is free of clumps and solids, litter sits at the correct depth, and waste is bagged and binned. On the weekly cycle, the box itself is washed and refilled with fresh litter.

steps.action: **Stage the bag before touching anything.** Open the waste bag and set it beside the box, or cuff it over one hand like a glove.
steps.expect: bag open and reachable one-handed; the other hand stays clean for the scoop.

steps.action: **Scoop solids first.** Lift each stool with the scoop, tilt to let clean litter sift back through the slots, drop the solid into the bag.
steps.expect: only waste in the bag; litter rain falls back into the box, not the floor.

steps.action: **Probe for urine clumps.** Drag the scoop along the box floor and into the corners; clumps stick to the base and corners where cats aim. Lift gently: a rushed lift shatters the clump into crumbs you cannot recover.
steps.expect: intact clumps in the bag; the scoop passes corner to corner without resistance.

steps.action: **Check litter depth.** Level the remaining litter and eyeball the depth against roughly 5 to 7 cm (2 to 3 inches). Too shallow and urine hits the box floor and welds to it; too deep and some cats refuse the box.
steps.expect: even bed at target depth after any top-up from the litter supply.

steps.action: **Tie off and bin the bag.** Knot the bag and put it in a closed bin. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never flush clumping litter, even one clump; it expands and sets in pipes like mortar.
steps.expect: bag knotted, bin lid closed, no odor escaping.

steps.action: **Wipe the surround.** Sweep or wipe scatter from the floor and the box rim.
steps.expect: no granules within a step of the box; the rim is dry.

steps.action: **Weekly cycle: full change.** [BRANCH: daily visit → done at step 6 | weekly visit → continue] Dump all litter into a bag, wash the box with mild dish soap and warm water, dry it fully, refill to target depth. Skip ammonia and strong citrus cleaners: the smell drives cats away from the box.
steps.expect: box visibly clean, fully dry before refill, fresh litter at 5 to 7 cm.

steps.action: **Wash hands.** Soap, 20 seconds, even if a scoop and bag did all the touching.
steps.expect: hands washed before handling food or face.

recipes.verification: Scoop passes the full box floor with no resistance and brings up nothing; litter is level at 5 to 7 cm; waste bag is knotted inside a closed bin; floor around the box is granule-free; hands washed. On a weekly visit, additionally: the box was washed and fully dried before refill.

recipes.title: close curtains and blinds
recipes.name: close-curtains-and-blinds
recipes.goal: Close curtains or blinds evenly for privacy, light control, or sleep, without tangling cords or stressing the window hardware.

steps.action: **Identify the control.** [BRANCH: curtain | cord blind | wand blind | motorized blind] locate the fabric edge, cord, wand, chain, switch, or remote.
steps.expect: the correct control is in hand before pulling.

steps.action: **Release tiebacks.** Undo hooks, magnets, or fabric ties holding curtains open.
steps.expect: fabric hangs freely.

steps.action: **Close curtains by sliding.** Hold the leading edge or pull wand and move fabric along the rod or track.
steps.expect: panels meet or overlap at the center.

steps.action: **Lower blinds if raised.** Pull the cord toward the center to unlock, guide it slowly, then move it back to lock.
steps.expect: the bottom rail descends evenly and stops at the sill.

steps.action: **Tilt blind slats.** Rotate the wand or pull the tilt cords until slats overlap closed.
steps.expect: outside view is blocked while slats remain aligned.

steps.action: **Use motor controls gently.** Press close or down once and wait for movement to finish.
steps.expect: the blind travels without repeated button presses.

steps.action: **Even the bottom edge.** Adjust one side only if the rail or curtain hem is noticeably crooked.
steps.expect: the lower edge is level enough that it does not snag.

steps.action: **Check privacy from inside.** Step back and look for gaps at the center, sides, and sill.
steps.expect: no direct line of sight remains through the covering.

steps.action: **Secure cords safely.** Wind loose cords on a cleat or place them high out of reach.
steps.expect: no loop hangs where a child or pet could reach it.

recipes.verification: The curtains or blinds cover the window evenly, block direct view through the window, and all cords are secured away from children and pets.

recipes.title: coil a hose or cable
recipes.name: coil-a-hose-or-cable
recipes.goal: The hose or cable is coiled in even over-under loops, secured without kinks, and stored on a hook or shelf without stressing connectors.

steps.action: **Straighten the length.** Walk the hose or cable out enough to remove crossings and sharp bends.
steps.expect: the line lies mostly straight with no trapped loops.

steps.action: **Hold the starting end.** Grip one end in the non-dominant hand with the connector hanging below the hand, not bearing weight.
steps.expect: first connector is controlled and protected.

steps.action: **Make the first over loop.** Draw a loop toward your hand in the natural curl direction and place it into the holding hand.
steps.expect: loop is round and about the planned coil diameter.

steps.action: **Make the under loop.** For the next loop, rotate the incoming line half a turn opposite the natural curl before placing it in the hand.
steps.expect: the loop lies flat without twisting the previous loop.

steps.action: **Alternate over and under.** Continue one over loop, one under loop, keeping loop diameters consistent.
steps.expect: coil hangs straight from the hand and does not spiral.

steps.action: **Remove small kinks early.** If a twist appears, lower the coil and let the free length rotate until tension releases.
steps.expect: line relaxes and the next loop forms without a hard bend.

steps.action: **Secure the coil.** Wrap a strap, hook-and-loop tie, or soft cord around the middle with enough tension to hold shape but not flatten the line.
steps.expect: loops stay together when lifted.

steps.action: **Hang or store.** Lift from the coil body, not the connector, and place it on a wide hook or shelf.
steps.expect: coil rests evenly with connectors visible and unstressed.

recipes.verification: The stored coil has even loops, no sharp kinks, and connectors or hose ends are visible without bearing the coil's weight.

recipes.title: collect and sort mail
recipes.name: collect-and-sort-mail
recipes.goal: All mail is retrieved from the box, sorted by recipient and class, junk is safely diverted, and each remaining piece sits in its recipient's known spot with nothing left in transit.

steps.action: **Retrieve everything from the box.** Open the box, take all contents including flyers wedged at the back, and check for a package slip or an overflow parcel below or beside the box. Close and (if locking) relock the door.
steps.expect: box visibly empty, door shut, key back in pocket before walking away.

steps.action: **Carry it all inside in one stack.** Sort at a table, not standing at the box: wind and one-handed sorting at the box is how checks end up in the hedge.
steps.expect: full stack on a flat surface indoors.

steps.action: **First pass: sort by recipient.** Deal the stack into one pile per person in the household, plus a pile for former residents or wrong addresses. Check the name line, not just the surname, in shared households.
steps.expect: every piece in exactly one pile; the misdelivered pile set apart.

steps.action: **Second pass: sort each recipient's pile by class.** [BRANCH: action mail (bills, official notices, anything with a deadline) | personal correspondence | periodicals and catalogs | junk] The envelope tells you: window envelopes and government or bank return addresses are action mail; bulk-rate markings and "resident" addressing are junk.
steps.expect: each pile split into at most four sub-stacks.

steps.action: **Divert the junk stream immediately.** Plain unaddressed flyers go straight to recycling. Anything showing a name plus address, and especially prefilled credit or loan offers, goes to the shredder pile, never whole into the bin. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* shredding: confirm a piece is truly junk before it enters the shred pile; real notices in bulk envelopes exist, so open anything ambiguous first.
steps.expect: junk gone from the sorted piles; shred pile contains only confirmed junk with personal data.

steps.action: **Handle the misdelivered pile.** Neighbor's mail: hand-deliver or leave in their box. Former residents: mark "not at this address, return to sender" and put it back in outgoing mail; do not open it (opening others' mail is illegal in most locales) and do not bin it.
steps.expect: misdelivered pile empty by end of task or staged in outgoing mail.

steps.action: **Deliver each pile to its recipient's spot.** Action mail on top of each stack, deadline side up. Tell present recipients about anything that looks urgent.
steps.expect: every landing spot holds only its owner's mail; your own action mail is in your workflow, not back in the tray.

steps.action: **Run the shredder.** Shred the confirmed-junk pile now; a "shred later" pile becomes a data-breach drawer.
steps.expect: shred pile empty, shreds in the bin.

recipes.verification: The mailbox is empty and locked, every retrieved piece is either in its recipient's spot, in outgoing mail marked return-to-sender, recycled, or shredded, and no stack remains on the sorting table. Anyone in the household can find their mail without asking.

recipes.title: empty a robot vacuum bin
recipes.name: empty-a-robot-vacuum-bin
recipes.goal: Remove collected debris from a robot vacuum dust bin, reseat the bin and filter, and leave the robot ready to run.

steps.action: **Stop and steady the robot.** Confirm it is not running, then hold the body or dock area steady.
steps.expect: wheels and brushes are not moving.

steps.action: **Release the dust bin.** Press the bin latch and pull the bin straight out along its rails.
steps.expect: the bin separates without forcing or twisting.

steps.action: **Hold over the trash can.** Keep the bin opening fully inside the trash perimeter.
steps.expect: any falling dust will land in the trash.

steps.action: **Open and empty the bin.** Release the bin door and tap the side lightly until debris falls out.
steps.expect: the main chamber is visibly empty.

steps.action: **Check the filter.** Lift or tap the filter only as the manufacturer allows, keeping dust over the trash.
steps.expect: filter is seated, dry, and not packed with loose dust.

steps.action: **Reinsert the bin.** Close the bin door and slide the bin back until it clicks or sits flush.
steps.expect: the robot body has no protruding bin edge or open latch.

recipes.verification: The robot vacuum dust bin is empty, closed, fully seated in the robot, and the robot shows no bin or filter error.

recipes.title: feed a pet
recipes.name: feed-a-pet
recipes.goal: The pet receives a measured portion of the correct food at its scheduled time, with fresh water in a clean bowl beside it.

steps.action: **Confirm it is a scheduled mealtime.** Pets solicit food at any hour; the schedule is the source of truth, not the begging.
steps.expect: current time matches a feeding slot and this meal was not already given by someone else in the household.

steps.action: **Check and refresh the water first.** Dump old water, rinse the bowl, refill with fresh. Do this every visit, not only when the bowl is empty: the slick film on the bowl wall is bacterial growth, not water residue.
steps.expect: water bowl full of clean water, no film on the wall, bowl stable on the floor.

steps.action: **Inspect the food bowl.** [BRANCH: bowl clean and dry → proceed | residue, crust, or grease film → wash with dish soap and hot water, dry, then proceed]
steps.expect: a bowl you would eat from yourself; chin acne in cats and dogs traces to dirty plastic bowls more often than to diet.

steps.action: **Measure the portion.** Level the measuring cup at the exact per-meal amount; do not round up "because they seem hungry". For wet food, portion by can fraction or by weight per the label.
steps.expect: the measured amount matches the per-meal ration; no heaping.

steps.action: **Deliver the bowl.** Place it at the usual feeding spot, away from the litter box for cats. Multi-pet homes: separate feeding stations out of sight of each other, or the fast eater takes both.
steps.expect: each animal at its own bowl; no bowl swapping.

steps.action: **Observe the start of eating.** Watch the first minute. Appetite is the cheapest health signal a keeper has: refusal of a normally loved food is worth noting the same day.
steps.expect: the pet eats with normal enthusiasm.

steps.action: **Close and store the food.** Reseal the container fully; return wet food remainders to the refrigerator, covered, and use within the label window.
steps.expect: container sealed, no food accessible for self-service raids.

steps.action: **Clear uneaten wet food after 30 to 60 minutes.** Kibble may stand until the next meal if the animal grazes; wet food may not.
steps.expect: no spoiling wet food left at the station; bowl washed or soaking.

recipes.verification: The correct animal ate a measured portion at the scheduled time; the water bowl holds fresh clean water; the food container is sealed and stored; no wet food is standing past its window; the feeding area is free of scattered food.

recipes.title: fold a blanket
recipes.name: fold-a-blanket
recipes.goal: A blanket is folded into a flat, compact shape with aligned edges and stacked where it will stay stable.

steps.action: **Shake out the blanket.** Lift one edge and give a small shake to release twists and hidden objects.
steps.expect: the blanket hangs freely with no hard objects inside.

steps.action: **Spread it flat.** Lay the blanket on the work surface with the long edges visible.
steps.expect: the fabric is open enough to identify all corners.

steps.action: **Match the first corners.** Bring two adjacent corners together along the long edge.
steps.expect: one long edge is doubled and roughly aligned.

steps.action: **Halve the blanket.** Bring the opposite corners to the matched corners, making a rectangle.
steps.expect: all four corners are grouped and edges are close.

steps.action: **Smooth the surface.** Sweep hands from the folded edge outward to push out air and wrinkles.
steps.expect: the rectangle lies flatter and does not bulge.

steps.action: **Fold into thirds.** Fold one short side toward the center, then fold the other side over it.
steps.expect: the width is compact and the edges form a neat stack.

steps.action: **Fold once more if needed.** [BRANCH: shelf is narrow | blanket is already shelf-sized] fold in half for narrow storage or leave it as is.
steps.expect: the folded blanket matches the storage space.

steps.action: **Place it stable.** Set the folded blanket flat with the heaviest fold at the bottom.
steps.expect: the stack stays level and does not slide.

recipes.verification: The blanket is dry, folded flat with corners aligned, and rests in storage without sliding or tipping.

recipes.title: fold a map or large paper
recipes.name: fold-a-map-or-large-paper
recipes.goal: The map or large paper is folded along existing creases, accordioned into panels, folded in half if designed that way, and stored without new forced creases.

steps.action: **Lay the paper flat.** Spread it on the surface and smooth gently from center to edges with open palms.
steps.expect: existing crease pattern is visible.

steps.action: **Find the original folds.** Look for alternating mountain and valley creases, worn edges, or printed panel boundaries.
steps.expect: a fold sequence can be followed without guessing.

steps.action: **Align the first crease.** Lift one edge and let the paper bend where it already wants to bend.
steps.expect: the old crease rises cleanly without a new diagonal line.

steps.action: **Accordion the panels.** Fold one panel forward, the next panel backward, continuing the existing zigzag pattern.
steps.expect: panel edges stack evenly.

steps.action: **Square each fold.** Before pressing, align corners and printed borders, then run fingertips along the crease with light pressure.
steps.expect: folded stack stays rectangular.

steps.action: **Fold the stack in half if designed.** [BRANCH: center cross-crease present → fold in half | no cross-crease → stop at accordion stack] follow only the existing cross-crease.
steps.expect: final packet matches the old worn outline.

steps.action: **Avoid forcing resistance.** If paper buckles away from a fold, open it and search for the missed earlier crease.
steps.expect: resistance disappears when the correct sequence is restored.

steps.action: **Store flat or sleeved.** Slide the folded packet into its sleeve, drawer, or book without bending corners.
steps.expect: packet remains flat and corners are protected.

recipes.verification: The paper is folded into its original panel stack with aligned edges and no new forced crease crossing the printed surface.

recipes.title: fold a towel
recipes.name: fold-a-towel
recipes.goal: A clean towel is folded into a neat rectangle that stacks evenly on a shelf or displays with the smooth edge facing out.

steps.action: **Shake the towel open.** Hold two corners and give one controlled shake away from faces and objects.
steps.expect: the towel hangs flat enough to see its long and short edges.

steps.action: **Lay it face down.** Put the towel on the surface with the display side down if one side looks better.
steps.expect: the better side will end up outside after folding.

steps.action: **Smooth the fabric.** Run both hands from the center outward to remove twists and bunched corners.
steps.expect: edges lie straight and corners are visible.

steps.action: **Fold one long side to the center.** Bring the left long edge inward about one-third of the towel width.
steps.expect: the fold line is straight from top to bottom.

steps.action: **Fold the other long side over it.** Bring the right long edge across to make a long narrow rectangle.
steps.expect: the towel is in thirds with aligned edges.

steps.action: **Fold the towel in half crosswise.** Bring the short ends together without stretching the fabric.
steps.expect: the towel becomes a shorter rectangle with corners matched.

steps.action: **Make the display fold.** [BRANCH: shelf stack | visible display] fold in half again for compact storage, or fold one end under so the smooth folded edge faces outward.
steps.expect: the front edge is smooth and no raw corners face out.

steps.action: **Stack without crushing.** Place the towel on the pile with folded edges aligned.
steps.expect: the stack stays level and does not lean.

recipes.verification: The folded towel is dry, rectangular, smooth on the visible side, and stackable without leaning or unfolding.

recipes.title: fold a tshirt
recipes.name: fold-a-tshirt
recipes.goal: A clean, dry t-shirt is folded into a flat, compact rectangle that stacks stably in a drawer or on a shelf.

steps.action: **Spread the shirt face-down on the surface.** Chest down, back up, collar away from you. Grasp the hem and give one straightening shake before laying down.
steps.expect: shirt lies flat, sleeves out to the sides, no major folds trapped under it.

steps.action: **Smooth the fabric.** Two flat-hand (or flat-gripper) sweeps outward from the spine to the edges.
steps.expect: no wrinkles or bunched fabric; seams lie straight.

steps.action: **Fold the first side in.** Grasp the shirt's left shoulder and left hem corner; fold the left third over the back, sleeve included, so the fold line runs shoulder-to-hem.
steps.expect: left edge now runs parallel to the shirt's centerline, about a third of the way across.

steps.action: **Fold the left sleeve back.** Fold the protruding sleeve back toward the left edge so it lies within the folded panel.
steps.expect: no sleeve fabric sticks out past the folded edge.

steps.action: **Repeat steps 3–4 on the right side.**
steps.expect: a long rectangle roughly one-third the original width; both sleeves contained; edges parallel.

steps.action: **Fold the rectangle in half (or thirds) hem-to-collar.** Grasp the hem edge, fold up to just below the collar; for deep shelves fold once (half), for drawers fold twice (thirds).
steps.expect: a compact rectangle, collar visible on top face when flipped.

steps.action: **Flip it face-up and place it on the stack.**
steps.expect: the shirt front/graphic faces up, rectangle sits flat without springing open.

recipes.verification: The folded shirt is a flat rectangle with no protruding sleeves, front face up, roughly consistent with the others in the stack, and the stack (or file row) remains stable after placement.

recipes.title: gather items into a basket
recipes.name: gather-items-into-a-basket
recipes.goal: Multiple household items are collected into a basket, placed rather than tossed, balanced for carrying, and moved without spills.

steps.action: **Inspect the basket.** Check handles, bottom, and interior for damage or contaminants.
steps.expect: basket can hold the planned load.

steps.action: **Plan pickup order.** Scan the room and choose nearby items first, with heavy or flat items before fragile ones.
steps.expect: a route and placement order are known.

steps.action: **Place the basket near the first item.** Set it on the floor, table, or hip-height surface within reach.
steps.expect: basket is stable and open side faces up.

steps.action: **Pick up the first item.** Grip the item securely using its handle, sides, or underside.
steps.expect: item is controlled without dragging or scraping.

steps.action: **Place, not toss.** Lower the item into the basket until it contacts the bottom or another stable item.
steps.expect: item remains where placed and basket does not tip.

steps.action: **Repeat with balance checks.** Add items around the center, distributing weight left and right.
steps.expect: basket remains level after each placement.

steps.action: **Protect fragile items.** Put fragile or soft items on top or in a separated area. [BRANCH: fragile present | no fragile] cushion and isolate fragile items; continue normal loading otherwise.
steps.expect: fragile items are not under heavy load.

steps.action: **Stop before overfilling.** Leave handle access and line of sight to the basket rim.
steps.expect: no item rises above the rim in a way that can fall during carry.

steps.action: **Lift and carry the basket.** Use both handles or support the bottom, then move slowly with the load close.
steps.expect: basket stays level and items do not shift out.

recipes.verification: All intended safe items are inside the basket, the load is balanced, handles or bottom are supported, and no item falls during a short carry test.

recipes.title: hammer a nail
recipes.name: hammer-a-nail
recipes.goal: The nail is driven straight into the target surface until the head sits flush or at the intended proud height.

steps.action: **Mark the target.** Place a small mark where the nail point should enter.
steps.expect: mark is visible and reachable by the hammer face.

steps.action: **Grip the nail safely.** Hold the nail near its head with fingertips pinched lightly at the sides.
steps.expect: point touches the mark and fingers stay above the target.

steps.action: **Start with light taps.** Tap from the wrist until the point bites into the material.
steps.expect: nail stands without full hand support.

steps.action: **Release fingers.** Move the holding hand away from the strike zone. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* missed blows can injure fingers or mar the surface, so confirm the nail stands alone first.
steps.expect: only the hammer hand remains near the nail.

steps.action: **Swing from the elbow.** Hold the hammer near the handle end and strike the nail head squarely.
steps.expect: nail advances with each hit and does not bend.

steps.action: **Correct early lean.** [BRANCH: nail straight | nail leaning] tap the high side gently before it is deep.
steps.expect: shaft returns near perpendicular.

steps.action: **Sink to final height.** Use controlled lighter blows as the head nears the surface.
steps.expect: nail head reaches flush without denting around it.

steps.action: **Stop and inspect.** Set the hammer down away from edges and check the fastened item.
steps.expect: nail holds firm under a light tug.

recipes.verification: The nail is straight, seated at the intended depth, and the workpiece or hanging point resists a light load without shifting.

recipes.title: hang a shirt on a hanger
recipes.name: hang-a-shirt-on-a-hanger
recipes.goal: The shirt is supported by the hanger at both shoulders, the top button or placket stabilizes the collar, and the hanger is hooked securely on the rail.

steps.action: **Hold the shirt by the collar.** Lift the shirt so the front faces you and the shoulder seams hang naturally.
steps.expect: collar opening and both shoulders are visible.

steps.action: **Button the top.** Fasten the top button or the highest practical button to keep the shirt from sliding off.
steps.expect: collar forms a closed loop or narrow opening.

steps.action: **Orient the hanger.** Hold the hanger hook upward with the left and right arms matching the shirt shoulders.
steps.expect: hanger curve faces the same direction as the shirt chest.

steps.action: **Insert through the collar or hem.** [BRANCH: collar opening wide enough → slide one hanger arm through collar | delicate collar → insert through bottom hem] guide one arm at a time.
steps.expect: hanger arms are inside the shirt body without stretching fabric.

steps.action: **Seat the first shoulder.** Push one hanger tip into the matching shoulder seam using gentle outward pressure.
steps.expect: fabric drapes over the hanger tip without a pointy bulge.

steps.action: **Seat the second shoulder.** Lift the opposite shoulder fabric and guide the second hanger tip into place.
steps.expect: both shoulder seams rest near the hanger ends.

steps.action: **Square the shirt.** Tug lightly at both side seams and smooth the front placket downward.
steps.expect: shirt hangs symmetrical with no twisted sleeve.

steps.action: **Hook the rail.** Lift by the hanger hook, place it over the closet rail, and release only after the hook is fully seated.
steps.expect: hanger remains on the rail and shirt hangs clear of the floor.

recipes.verification: The shirt hangs from the rail with both shoulder seams supported evenly, the top secured, and no sleeve or placket twist visible.

recipes.title: hang an item on a hook
recipes.name: hang-an-item-on-a-hook
recipes.goal: An item with a loop, collar, handle, or hanging point is placed on a hook and remains supported after release.

steps.action: **Approach the hook.** Move until the hook is centered in the work area and below or near comfortable reach height.
steps.expect: hook tip and load direction are visible.

steps.action: **Identify the hanging point.** Find the item's loop, collar, strap, or hole that should bear weight.
steps.expect: hanging point is graspable and not tangled.

steps.action: **Grip below the hanging point.** Hold the item so the loop or collar can move freely over the hook.
steps.expect: item is controlled and the hanging point is exposed.

steps.action: **Lift to hook height.** Raise the hanging point slightly above the hook tip.
steps.expect: loop or collar clears the hook tip.

steps.action: **Align with the hook opening.** Move the hanging point toward the hook from the open side.
steps.expect: hook tip enters the loop, collar, or handle.

steps.action: **Lower onto the hook.** Let the item's weight transfer down onto the deepest part of the hook.
steps.expect: item settles against the hook curve or backstop.

steps.action: **Release gradually.** Open the grip while keeping a guard hand nearby.
steps.expect: item remains hanging without sliding off.

steps.action: **Confirm the hold.** Watch for sway, tilt, or hook flex for two seconds.
steps.expect: item is still and supported.

steps.action: **Clear the area.** Withdraw the hand downward and away from the hook tip.
steps.expect: item and nearby objects remain undisturbed.

recipes.verification: The item hangs from the intended point, the hook supports the load without movement, and the item remains in place after release.

recipes.title: hang clothes on a drying line
recipes.name: hang-clothes-on-a-drying-line
recipes.goal: Wet clothes are hung on a drying line with enough spacing and support to dry without falling.

steps.action: **Inspect the line.** Tug downward lightly at the midpoint and check for dirt or slack.
steps.expect: the line holds tension and stays attached.

steps.action: **Pick up one garment.** Grasp the garment at two corners or shoulder points and lift it clear of the pile.
steps.expect: the garment hangs unfolded from the grip.

steps.action: **Shake out folds.** Give one or two short downward shakes while keeping the garment away from the floor.
steps.expect: major wrinkles open and edges are visible.

steps.action: **Drape over the line.** Place the garment midpoint or top edge across the line with balanced weight on both sides.
steps.expect: the garment remains on the line when lightly released.

steps.action: **Clip the garment.** Pinch a clothespin open, capture fabric and line together, and release at a reinforced edge.
steps.expect: the pin clamps fabric to the line without tearing.

steps.action: **Space the next garment.** Leave a hand-width gap before hanging the next item.
steps.expect: adjacent garments do not overlap.

steps.action: **Check the full row.** Look along the line and adjust sagging or bunched items.
steps.expect: all clothes are supported, separated, and clear of the floor.

recipes.verification: Each garment remains attached after a light tug, has airflow space around it, and hangs clear of the floor.

recipes.title: hang laundry to dry
recipes.name: hang-laundry-to-dry
recipes.goal: A washed load is hung to dry with air space and shape preserved, so it dries fast, wrinkles less, and smells like laundry rather than a damp cellar.

steps.action: **Shake each piece out hard before hanging.** Two sharp snaps per item unrolls the spin-cycle knots, releases wrinkles, and halves ironing later (`daily/home/iron-a-shirt` gratitude included).
steps.expect: items going up as flat panels, not twisted ropes.

steps.action: **Hang heavy and slow-drying items on the outside or windward positions.** Towels, jeans, hoodies get the airiest spots with maximum spacing; quick-dry synthetics fill the inner rungs.
steps.expect: the load arranged by drying difficulty, thickest pieces catching the most air.

steps.action: **Preserve garment shape as you hang.** Shirts on hangers (buttoned once at the collar) or by the hem, not the shoulders (pin-shoulders make peaks); trousers by the waistband or cuffs, straightened along the crease; knits *never* hang — they stretch; they lie flat on the rack's top or a towel.
steps.expect: nothing hanging by a point that will dent or stretch it.

steps.action: **Give everything a finger of air space.** Overlapping fabric dries at the speed of its slowest layer; a crammed rack is a mildew experiment. Two rack loads beat one compressed one.
steps.expect: visible gaps between all items; airflow paths through the rack.

steps.action: **Open the details.** Unfold cuffs and collars, open pockets outward, unroll waistbands, hang socks in pairs by the toes. The folded-over hem is where damp hides at the six-hour check.
steps.expect: every double-layer spot spread open.

steps.action: **Position for air and check back.** Rack near the open window or fan (not touching a cold exterior wall), line-loads pinned firmly at two points per item. Rotate or flip thick items at the half-dry point.
steps.expect: full dryness in hours (breezy outdoors) to a day (indoors); waistbands and seams pass the `daily/errands/use-a-laundromat` step 6 touch test before anything folds away.

recipes.verification: Every item hangs shaken-flat with air space, by a shape-safe point, details opened, thickest pieces in the best air; the room has moving air; and at collection every seam and waistband passes the touch test before folding (`embodied/household/fold-a-tshirt` receives them warm-dry, ideally).

recipes.title: insert a usb plug
recipes.name: insert-a-usb-plug
