recipes.goal: The USB plug is fully seated in the matching port without forcing or damaging the connector.

steps.action: **Stabilize the device.** Hold or brace the device so the port does not move during insertion.
steps.expect: the port opening remains stationary.

steps.action: **Grip the plug shell.** Hold the rigid connector body, not the flexible cable.
steps.expect: the plug tip is visible and controlled.

steps.action: **Inspect orientation.** Compare the plug shape to the port shape and rotate until keyed edges match.
steps.expect: the plug face matches the port opening.

steps.action: **Align straight to the port.** Bring the plug tip to the port centerline without side angle.
steps.expect: the plug touches the port opening evenly.

steps.action: **Insert with light pressure.** Push along the port axis using steady low force.
steps.expect: the plug slides inward without scraping or bending.

steps.action: **Seat fully.** Stop when resistance increases at the end of travel.
steps.expect: little or no metal connector remains visible and the plug feels secure.

steps.action: **Release and check cable slack.** Let go of the connector and route the cable without pulling sideways.
steps.expect: the connector stays seated and the cable has a gentle bend.

recipes.verification: The connector is fully seated, remains in place after release, and the device detects the connection if powered.

recipes.title: light a candle safely
recipes.name: light-a-candle-safely
recipes.goal: A candle is lit in a stable, clear location and later extinguished without fire, wax, or burn hazards.

steps.action: **Choose the location.** Set the candle on a stable surface away from curtains, paper, bedding, shelves, and edges.
steps.expect: there is at least 30 cm of clear space around and above the flame path.

steps.action: **Check the holder and wax.** Confirm the candle stands upright and the holder will catch melted wax.
steps.expect: nothing wobbles, leans, or exposes bare flame to a fragile surface.

steps.action: **Clear nearby movement.** Move sleeves, hair, pets, and children away before ignition.
steps.expect: no person or object crosses over the wick.

steps.action: **Light the wick.** [BRANCH: lighter | match] hold flame to the wick base until it catches, then pull the flame source away.
steps.expect: the wick has a small steady flame.

steps.action: **Adjust only from the holder.** If the candle needs repositioning, lift the holder, not the hot wax or flame area. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an unattended flame can start a fire, so never leave the room while it is burning.
steps.expect: the candle remains upright and watched.

steps.action: **Watch the first minute.** Look for high flame, smoking, tunneling, or nearby draft flicker.
steps.expect: the flame stays steady and contained.

steps.action: **Burn within limits.** Follow label timing and stop before the candle burns near the bottom of the jar or holder.
steps.expect: wax pool remains controlled and the holder is not overheating.

steps.action: **Extinguish deliberately.** Use a snuffer, wick dipper, or gentle breath from the side, then wait until smoke clears before moving it.
steps.expect: no glowing ember remains and the holder cools in place.

recipes.verification: While lit, the candle has a steady flame in a stable holder with clear surroundings; when finished, the wick is fully out and no ember glows.

recipes.title: load a washing machine
recipes.name: load-a-washing-machine
recipes.goal: A sorted load of laundry is in the washing machine drum, dosed, and running on the right cycle, with the pre-load checks done that prevent the classic disasters.

steps.action: **Check the drum before loading.** Open the door fully and look inside: forgotten laundry from the last run, a stray sock, or a resident item (the previous user's bra wire).
steps.expect: an empty drum. Wet forgotten laundry gets its own decision: re-run it or line it out, but never bury it under a new load.

steps.action: **Run the pocket-and-fastener pass one item at a time as you load.** Even if sorting "already did it": a tissue or pen at this second gate costs seconds; missed, it costs the whole load (`daily/home/do-the-laundry` F2). Bras into a mesh bag (wires kill drums), hooks and velcro closed, prints turned inside out.
steps.expect: every item pocket-flat, fasteners closed, protectors bagged.

steps.action: **Load loosely to the three-quarter line.** Items dropped in one at a time, not a compressed brick; a hand should fit upright between the load's top and the drum. Overloading is the most common cause of both bad cleaning and drum-bearing wear.
steps.expect: drum at most three-quarters full, contents loose.

steps.action: **Balance heavy items.** A single duvet, towel-heavy loads, or one soaked hoodie among lights will thump the spin; distribute heavy pieces evenly or pair them with similar weights.
steps.expect: no single heavy item alone in an otherwise light load.

steps.action: **Dose detergent into the correct compartment.** Main-wash compartment per the cap's line for the load size and soil level (`do-the-laundry` step 4's under-dosing wisdom); softener only to its max mark; pods go into the drum *under* the clothes, never the drawer.
steps.expect: right product, right compartment, at or below the line.

steps.action: **Select cycle and temperature from the most delicate item in the load.** The care-label read from sorting governs: 30 to 40 °C normal cycle for everyday mixed cottons, delicate cycle and low spin for the fragile pile.
steps.expect: dial and options matching the load's weakest member.

steps.action: **Close the door until it clicks, start, and confirm it took.** Watch for the door lock light and water intake sound in the first minute. Note the end time (`do-the-laundry` step 6: wet clothes wait for no one).
steps.expect: locked door, water sound, cycle time displayed, an alarm set for the end.

recipes.verification: The drum held only checked, protected items at three-quarters loose; detergent sat in the correct compartment; the cycle matches the weakest fabric; the door locked and water flowed; and the finish alarm is set.

recipes.title: make a bed neatly
recipes.name: make-a-bed-neatly
recipes.goal: The bed is made with wrinkle-free tensioned sheets in the correct layer order, the duvet squared to the mattress, and pillows placed. Written so a bimanual robot can execute it as a sequence of graspable, verifiable states.

steps.action: **Strip check.** [BRANCH: bed already bare → skip to step 2 | linens on it → remove and clear] Confirm the mattress top is empty and the fitted sheet, if present, is being changed or reused per plan.
steps.expect: bare mattress top, all four corners visible, no bunched fabric underneath.

steps.action: **Orient the fitted sheet.** Identify the deeper pockets, which are the short ends on most sheets, and align them to the head and foot. Reading the sheet wrong here forces a full restart, so verify before the first corner.
steps.expect: short-end pockets aligned to short mattress ends, sheet label at a bottom corner.

steps.action: **Seat two diagonal corners first.** Pull the sheet fully over one top corner, then the diagonally opposite bottom corner. Diagonals distribute tension so the sheet cannot walk off a corner as you work the next.
steps.expect: two opposite corners fully seated, elastic gripping under the mattress edge.

steps.action: **Seat the remaining two corners and tension.** Fit the last two corners, then run both hands from center to edges to pull the top surface flat.
steps.expect: no wrinkles or slack on the sleeping surface; a flat hand sweep meets no ridges; corners stay put under a tug.

steps.action: **Lay the flat sheet.** Spread it wrong-side-up (so the finished hem shows when folded down), top hem level with the mattress head, even overhang on both long sides.
steps.expect: equal side overhang within a hand's width; top hem square to the head edge.

steps.action: **Add the duvet, squared.** Lay the duvet over the flat sheet, its top edge one hand-width below the mattress head so the flat sheet can fold back over it. Square the duvet: equal overhang left and right, foot edge parallel to the mattress foot.
steps.expect: duvet centered, side overhangs equal, foot edge parallel not skewed.

steps.action: **Fold the flat sheet back over the duvet's top edge.** Turn the top sheet down over the duvet in a crisp band.
steps.expect: an even fold line running straight across the bed, hem side showing.

steps.action: **Optional hospital corners on the foot (flat-sheet beds).** Tuck the foot overhang under, lift the side drape to a 45-degree fold, tuck the underneath, drop the top flap.
steps.expect: a clean angled corner at each foot corner; drape hangs flat.

steps.action: **Place pillows.** Insert into cases (grasp the pillow by a short end, gather the case, pull it over), then set them squared at the head, standing or flat per style.
steps.expect: pillows fully in cases with corners filled, top edges aligned, centered on the bed width.

steps.action: **Final smooth.** One pass with a flat hand over the whole visible surface.
steps.expect: no wrinkles across the duvet top; overhangs even on both sides; the bed looks symmetric from the foot.

recipes.verification: Flat-hand sweep across the sleeping and duvet surfaces meets no ridges; both long-side overhangs are equal within a hand's width; the duvet foot edge is parallel to the mattress foot; pillows are cased with filled corners and aligned at the head; viewed from the foot, the bed is left-right symmetric.

recipes.title: open a cabinet
recipes.name: open-a-cabinet
recipes.goal: A cabinet door is opened far enough for access while maintaining clearance for the door swing and nearby items.

steps.action: **Identify the hinge side.** Look for visible hinges or infer from the handle side.
steps.expect: predicted swing arc and pull direction are known.

steps.action: **Stand outside the swing arc.** Position the body or chassis slightly to the handle side.
steps.expect: the door can open without striking the actor.

steps.action: **Check adjacent clearance.** Inspect nearby walls, handles, appliances, and fragile objects in the arc.
steps.expect: no object blocks the first 90 degrees of motion.

steps.action: **Grasp the handle or edge.** Use a full grip on the handle, knob, or safe outer edge.
steps.expect: grip is secure without fingers near the hinge gap.

steps.action: **Release the latch.** Pull or press as the mechanism requires, using low force first. [BRANCH: pull door | push-latch door] pull a handle door; press and release a push-latch door.
steps.expect: door separates from the frame.

steps.action: **Swing the door open.** Move the door through its hinge arc slowly, keeping wrist aligned with the handle path.
steps.expect: door opens without scraping or rebound.

steps.action: **Stop at useful clearance.** Hold at 70 to 110 degrees unless the hinge or wall stop limits travel sooner.
steps.expect: cabinet interior is accessible and the door is not forced.

steps.action: **Hold or park the door.** Keep a hand on springy or self-closing doors; release only if the door remains still.
steps.expect: door stays open at the selected angle.

steps.action: **Re-scan the opening.** Check shelves and loose contents before reaching inside.
steps.expect: no item is falling or leaning out.

recipes.verification: The cabinet door is open to a stable access angle, the swing arc is clear, and no contents are falling from the cabinet.

recipes.title: open a drawer
recipes.name: open-a-drawer
recipes.goal: A drawer is opened in a straight, controlled motion to expose its contents without pulling it free or spilling items.

steps.action: **Face the drawer.** Align the body or chassis with the drawer's travel direction.
steps.expect: pull direction is straight out from the cabinet face.

steps.action: **Check surrounding clearance.** Confirm knees, feet, wheels, and nearby items are outside the drawer path.
steps.expect: drawer can open without collision.

steps.action: **Grasp the handle.** Wrap fingers around the handle or place a firm pinch on the pull recess.
steps.expect: grip holds when lightly tensioned.

steps.action: **Start the pull straight.** Pull outward along the drawer rails without lifting or twisting.
steps.expect: drawer begins sliding evenly.

steps.action: **Control the speed.** Continue pulling slowly, moving the body back if needed to keep elbow and wrist aligned.
steps.expect: contents remain seated and do not surge forward.

steps.action: **Stop before full extension.** Ease force when resistance increases or the drawer reaches useful access.
steps.expect: drawer is open and still supported by its rails.

steps.action: **Let contents settle.** Hold the handle still for one beat.
steps.expect: loose items stop shifting.

steps.action: **Release or maintain hold.** [BRANCH: drawer self-stable | drawer rolls] release if stable; keep a light hold if it drifts.
steps.expect: drawer stays at the selected opening distance.

recipes.verification: The drawer is open to the intended distance, supported by its rails, with contents visible and not spilling or shifting.

recipes.title: open a ziploc bag
recipes.name: open-a-ziploc-bag
recipes.goal: The bag seal is separated along the track and the mouth is open enough to add or remove contents.

steps.action: **Support the bag.** Hold the body below the seal so contents stay low.
steps.expect: bag remains upright and stable.

steps.action: **Find the seam lips.** Feel for the two raised tracks at the top opening.
steps.expect: each hand contacts a different side of the seam.

steps.action: **Pinch both sides.** Grip the front lip with one hand and the back lip with the other.
steps.expect: the two plastic layers are controlled separately.

steps.action: **Start separation.** Pull the lips apart near one corner with steady outward force.
steps.expect: a small gap opens in the seal.

steps.action: **Open along the track.** Move the pull across the seam or slide fingers as the track separates.
steps.expect: the gap travels across the full width.

steps.action: **Check for missed sections.** Look and feel for any still-linked zipper ridges.
steps.expect: both lips are loose from corner to corner.

steps.action: **Hold the mouth open.** Roll or spread the top edges away from each other.
steps.expect: contents can pass without rubbing the seal.

steps.action: **Verify open state.** [BRANCH: add item | remove item] pass fingers or the target object through the mouth.
steps.expect: nothing catches on a closed segment.

recipes.verification: The seal track is separated across the full mouth and an object can enter or exit without pushing through a closed section.

recipes.title: open and close an umbrella
recipes.name: open-and-close-an-umbrella
recipes.goal: The umbrella opens to a locked canopy and closes back to a wrapped bundle without striking people or damaging ribs.

steps.action: **Clear the space.** Hold the umbrella tip down and scan a full arm length around the canopy path. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a rib tip can hit an eye, so pause if anyone is close.
steps.expect: no person or fragile item is inside the opening radius.

steps.action: **Hold the handle.** Grip the handle with the shaft pointed away from bodies.
steps.expect: umbrella is stable and aimed safely.

steps.action: **Release the strap.** Unfasten hook, snap, or sleeve around the folded canopy.
steps.expect: fabric loosens around the ribs.

steps.action: **Open the canopy.** Slide the runner upward or press the auto-open button.
steps.expect: ribs spread evenly.

steps.action: **Lock the runner.** Push until the runner clicks or rests above the catch.
steps.expect: canopy stays open without hand pressure on the runner.

steps.action: **Close by release.** Press the runner catch or close button while controlling the shaft.
steps.expect: runner begins moving down without snapping into fingers.

steps.action: **Fold the canopy.** Pull ribs and fabric downward along the shaft. [BRANCH: wet | dry] keep wet fabric pointed away from electronics.
steps.expect: ribs nest together.

steps.action: **Wrap the strap.** Smooth panels around the shaft and fasten the strap.
steps.expect: umbrella remains compact when released.

recipes.verification: The umbrella opens locked, closes under control, and finishes strapped with ribs aligned and no contact with people.

recipes.title: organize a bookshelf
recipes.name: organize-a-bookshelf
recipes.goal: Every book is shelved upright under a single stated sort scheme, rows are stable without leaning, and any given book can be found and removed with one hand.

steps.action: **Empty the shelf completely, one shelf at a time.** Stack books on the floor in the order removed. Working around books left in place produces a half-sorted mess.
steps.expect: bare shelves; floor stacks no taller than 5 or 6 books so they cannot topple.

steps.action: **Wipe the empty shelves.** Dust builds a gray felt at the back edge that transfers to page tops.
steps.expect: clean, dry shelf surfaces before anything goes back.

steps.action: **Commit to one sort scheme.** [BRANCH: by subject then author (reference-heavy collections) | by author surname (fiction-heavy) | by size or color (display shelves, harder to search)] Mixed schemes are the classic failure: pick one and note the rule.
steps.expect: a rule you can state in one sentence that assigns every book a unique region.

steps.action: **Pre-sort into labeled floor piles by the scheme.** Sort on the floor first; sorting directly onto shelves forces constant reshuffling.
steps.expect: piles matching the scheme, plus a "cull" pile for donations and a "misfit" pile for oversized items.

steps.action: **Assign heights to shelves before shelving.** Tall books (atlases, art books) to the bottom shelf, standard heights mid, small paperbacks up top. Heavy rows low also keeps the unit's center of gravity down.
steps.expect: each pile mapped to a shelf whose clearance fits its tallest spine.

steps.action: **Shelve upright, spines flush to the front edge.** Front-flush spines read better and leave the rear gap for airflow. Within a shelf, keep a size-graded row: tallest at the ends or one end, so no tall book stands isolated between short ones and warps.
steps.expect: an even front line of spines; every book fully vertical.

steps.action: **Do not overpack.** Leave a hand's width of slack per shelf: a book should slide out with a one-finger tilt at the headcap area top without dragging its neighbors. Overpacked rows tear headcaps and split spines.
steps.expect: any test book removable with one hand; row does not spring back shut.

steps.action: **Set bookends on partial rows.** A leaning row warps every book in it within weeks. Use real bookends or lay 2 or 3 heavy books horizontally as an end block.
steps.expect: all rows vertical with no lean anywhere on the unit.

steps.action: **Place misfits and finish.** Oversized books lie flat in short stacks (3 or 4 max) on the bottom shelf; box the cull pile and remove it from the room today, or it re-shelves itself.
steps.expect: no books left on the floor; cull box by the door.

recipes.verification: State the sort rule aloud and test it: pick 3 random titles from memory and locate each within 15 seconds. Every row stands vertical with no lean, each test book slides out one-handed, and the floor and staging area are empty.

recipes.title: pair and fold socks
recipes.name: pair-and-fold-socks
recipes.goal: Clean socks are matched by pattern and size, folded or rolled without overstretching cuffs, and unmatched socks are placed in an odd-sock bin.

steps.action: **Spread socks flat.** Place socks on the surface with toes pointing roughly the same direction and cuffs visible.
steps.expect: patterns, sizes, and wear marks can be compared.

steps.action: **Match by pattern first.** Pair socks with the same color, texture, logo, and stripe or knit pattern.
steps.expect: likely pairs form without needing to stretch them.

steps.action: **Confirm by size and wear.** Align toe to toe and heel to heel, checking cuff height and fabric thickness.
steps.expect: each pair has matching length and shape.

steps.action: **Set odd socks aside.** Place any unmatched sock in the odd-sock bin rather than forcing a weak match.
steps.expect: sorting area contains only confirmed pairs.

steps.action: **Choose fold or roll.** [BRANCH: fold-over cuff | roll] use fold-over for drawers and roll for travel or compact storage.
steps.expect: both socks in a pair are stacked evenly.

steps.action: **Fold-over method.** Lay one sock on the other, align toes and cuffs, then fold only the outer cuff over the pair with light tension.
steps.expect: cuff holds the pair without whitening or stretching.

steps.action: **Roll method.** Stack the pair, roll from toes toward cuffs using gentle pressure, then tuck the last cuff edge around the roll if needed.
steps.expect: roll stays together and the cuff is not strained.

steps.action: **Place the pair.** Put folded pairs in the drawer with cuffs visible for identification.
steps.expect: pairs remain together and are easy to select later.

recipes.verification: Every stored pair contains two matching socks held together without stretched cuffs, and every unmatched sock is in the odd-sock bin.

recipes.title: peel and apply a sticker
recipes.name: peel-and-apply-a-sticker
recipes.goal: Separate a sticker from its backing and attach it smoothly to a clean target surface in the intended position.

steps.action: **Clean the target spot.** Wipe dust or moisture away and let the area dry.
steps.expect: the surface looks dry and debris-free.

steps.action: **Plan alignment.** Hold the sticker over the target without peeling and note edges or marks for placement.
steps.expect: the final position is visually clear.

steps.action: **Peel one edge.** Bend the backing away from a sticker corner and lift only 1 to 2 cm of adhesive.
steps.expect: the sticker edge separates without curling into itself.

steps.action: **Anchor the exposed edge.** Place the exposed adhesive on the target at the planned line and press lightly.
steps.expect: the sticker is attached at one edge and still adjustable by the backing.

steps.action: **Remove backing while smoothing.** Pull the backing away slowly while pressing from the anchored edge outward with a finger or card.
steps.expect: the sticker lays down without trapped bubbles or wrinkles.

steps.action: **Seal the edges.** Press along the perimeter and across the center with even pressure.
steps.expect: all edges adhere flat and no corner lifts.

recipes.verification: The sticker is attached at the intended location with flat edges, no major bubbles, and no visible dust or moisture under the adhesive.

recipes.title: pick up a coin from a table
recipes.name: pick-up-a-coin-from-a-table
recipes.goal: A coin is lifted from a table and placed into a target hand, dish, or container.

steps.action: **Locate the coin edge.** View the coin from above and identify an accessible rim.
steps.expect: the coin boundary is visible against the table.

steps.action: **Place fingertips near the rim.** Bring thumb and index finger to opposite sides without pushing the coin away.
steps.expect: both fingertips contact the coin edge or table beside it.

steps.action: **Pinch lightly.** Apply inward pressure on the coin rim while keeping fingers vertical.
steps.expect: the coin resists sliding and is captured between fingertips.

steps.action: **Lift straight up.** Raise the coin 2-5 cm above the table with steady grip.
steps.expect: the coin clears the table and remains between fingertips.

steps.action: **Move over the target.** Translate the coin slowly above the hand, dish, or container opening.
steps.expect: the coin is centered over the intended drop area.

steps.action: **Release low.** Lower close to the target surface and relax the pinch.
steps.expect: the coin lands in the target with minimal bounce.

recipes.verification: The coin is no longer on the table and is resting in the specified target location.

recipes.title: pick up an object from the floor
recipes.name: pick-up-an-object-from-the-floor
recipes.goal: An object resting on the floor is lifted to a stable carried position without dropping it or losing balance.

steps.action: **Approach with a clear path.** Move toward the object until it is centered between the feet or directly in front of the base.
steps.expect: object is within comfortable arm reach and no obstacle blocks the stance.

steps.action: **Stop and classify the object.** Estimate size, weight, fragile surfaces, and best grip points before lowering.
steps.expect: a planned grip location and lifting direction are identified.

steps.action: **Set a stable stance.** Place feet shoulder-width apart, one foot slightly forward if needed, with knees unlocked.
steps.expect: body weight is balanced over the base of support.

steps.action: **Bend using knees and hips.** Squat or hinge down with the back neutral, keeping the object close to the centerline.
steps.expect: hand or gripper reaches the object without overextending.

steps.action: **Form the grip.** Close fingers or gripper around solid sides, under an edge, or through a handle. [BRANCH: handle available | no handle] use the handle if present; otherwise use opposing sides.
steps.expect: object resists a light upward test without slipping.

steps.action: **Lift with legs.** Press through the feet and extend knees and hips while keeping the object close to the torso or chassis.
steps.expect: object leaves the floor smoothly without twisting the spine or base.

steps.action: **Pause at knee height.** Hold for one beat and check grip, object orientation, and balance.
steps.expect: no wobble, sliding, or unexpected weight shift.

steps.action: **Bring to carry height.** Raise or tuck the object to a stable carried position that does not block vision or foot placement.
steps.expect: object is secure and the actor can stand upright.

steps.action: **Re-scan before moving.** Look at the floor path and nearby people before taking a step.
steps.expect: route is clear enough to continue.

recipes.verification: The object is off the floor, held securely at carry height, and the actor is upright with stable balance for at least two seconds.

recipes.title: pick up broken glass
recipes.name: pick-up-broken-glass
recipes.goal: Broken glass is collected from a floor or counter, including tiny shards, and disposed of in a puncture-resistant container.

steps.action: **Freeze traffic.** Tell nearby people to stop and step away from the break area.
steps.expect: no bare feet, hands, or paws enter the shard zone.

steps.action: **Put on protection.** Wear shoes and gloves before touching anything.
steps.expect: skin is covered where accidental contact is likely.

steps.action: **Mark the area.** Mentally include the obvious break zone plus at least 1 meter around it.
steps.expect: cleanup covers the scatter field, not just the center.

steps.action: **Pick up big pieces first.** Grasp large shards by dull edges if visible and place them in a rigid container.
steps.expect: large pieces are removed without squeezing sharp edges.

steps.action: **Sweep medium pieces.** Sweep slowly toward the dustpan using short strokes.
steps.expect: visible fragments collect in the pan without skittering away.

steps.action: **Use low-angle light.** Shine a flashlight or phone light across the surface from the side.
steps.expect: tiny shards sparkle against the floor or counter.

steps.action: **Press bread or tape for shards.** Dab soft bread or tape sticky-side down over the area.
steps.expect: fine glass specks stick to the bread or tape.

steps.action: **Wipe last residue.** Use a damp paper towel and fold it inward after each pass.
steps.expect: dust and remaining grit are captured inside the towel.

steps.action: **Package disposal.** Place glass, tape, bread, and towels into a rigid container or wrapped bundle. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* loose glass in a thin trash bag can cut handlers, so contain it before discarding.
steps.expect: sharp waste cannot poke through normal handling.

steps.action: **Final light check.** Re-scan the area from multiple angles before allowing traffic.
steps.expect: no reflections or gritty sounds remain.

recipes.verification: The area shows no visible reflections under low-angle light, no gritty sound under a protected shoe, and all glass is contained for disposal.

recipes.title: place an object on a shelf
recipes.name: place-an-object-on-a-shelf
recipes.goal: An object is placed fully on a shelf with clearance from the edge and enough stability to remain there unattended.

steps.action: **Approach the shelf squarely.** Move until the shelf is centered in front of the body or manipulator.
steps.expect: target shelf is within reach without leaning far forward.

steps.action: **Confirm shelf height.** Raise an empty hand or the object close to the shelf plane without contact.
steps.expect: the placement height is known and shoulder or actuator range is comfortable.

steps.action: **Inspect the landing area.** Look for obstacles, lips, loose papers, or nearby fragile items.
steps.expect: a flat landing zone larger than the object base is identified.

steps.action: **Raise the object near the body.** Lift to shelf height with elbows bent or manipulator joints inside normal range.
steps.expect: object remains level and controlled.

steps.action: **Clear the front edge.** Move the object forward until the entire base passes over the shelf edge.
steps.expect: no part of the object is hanging below or catching on the edge.

steps.action: **Lower onto the shelf.** Descend vertically until the base makes contact, keeping fingers clear of pinch points.
steps.expect: the shelf supports the object's weight.

steps.action: **Slide inward if needed.** Push gently away from the front edge until the object is fully inside the shelf footprint.
steps.expect: the object's center of mass is behind the shelf edge.

steps.action: **Release gradually.** Open fingers or gripper while maintaining a light guard nearby.
steps.expect: object stays in place without tilting or rolling.

steps.action: **Withdraw without contact.** Move the hand back along the entry path.
steps.expect: nearby shelf items remain undisturbed.

recipes.verification: The object rests fully on the shelf, at least one object depth from the front edge when space allows, and remains still after release.

recipes.title: place books upright on a shelf
recipes.name: place-books-upright-on-a-shelf
recipes.goal: Books stand upright on a shelf with their spines visible and the row supported.

steps.action: **Clear shelf space.** Move loose objects aside and make a gap slightly wider than the book group.
steps.expect: the shelf surface is visible and unobstructed.

steps.action: **Pick up the first book.** Grip both covers near the spine with the bottom edge facing downward.
steps.expect: the pages stay closed and aligned.

steps.action: **Set the book upright.** Lower the bottom edge onto the shelf with the spine facing outward.
steps.expect: the book stands vertical when supported by the hand.

steps.action: **Add adjacent books.** Place each next book with its bottom edge on the shelf and spine aligned to the row.
steps.expect: covers touch lightly without bending.

steps.action: **Compress the row gently.** Press the outer book toward the row with flat palm pressure.
steps.expect: gaps close and the row remains upright.

steps.action: **Add side support.** Slide a bookend or heavy book against the exposed side of the row.
steps.expect: the last book no longer leans when released.

steps.action: **Align fronts and spines.** Push the row backward or forward as a group until spines form an even line.
steps.expect: spines are readable and the row is straight.

recipes.verification: Books stand upright with bottom edges fully on the shelf, spines facing outward, and no unsupported book leaning more than a few degrees.

recipes.title: plug in a charger
recipes.name: plug-in-a-charger
recipes.goal: A compatible charger is safely plugged into power, connected to the device, and confirmed charging with the cord routed where it will not trip or strain anyone.

steps.action: **Inspect the charger.** Look over the block, plug blades, and cable for frays, exposed wire, scorch marks, or bent metal.
steps.expect: all parts are intact and dry.

steps.action: **Choose the outlet.** Use a firm wall outlet or grounded power strip that is not overloaded.
steps.expect: the outlet face is stable and has room for the plug.

steps.action: **Orient the plug.** Match the plug blade shape to the outlet slot shape before pushing.
steps.expect: the plug lines up without twisting.

steps.action: **Insert the plug firmly.** Push straight in while supporting the charger body, not the cable.
steps.expect: the plug sits fully seated with little or no metal blade visible.

steps.action: **Connect the device end.** Align the charging connector with the device port and insert gently.
steps.expect: the connector seats without scraping or force.

steps.action: **Confirm charging.** Look for the battery icon, charging light, sound, or lock-screen message.
steps.expect: the device reports charging within a few seconds.

steps.action: **Route the cord.** Lay the cable along an edge, behind furniture, or away from feet and chair wheels.
steps.expect: the cable has slack at both ends and does not cross a walking path.

steps.action: **Recheck heat later.** After several minutes, touch near the charger body lightly if safe.
steps.expect: it may be warm but not hot, buzzing, or smelling burnt.

recipes.verification: The charger is fully seated, the device shows a charging indicator, and the cord is routed with slack outside normal walking paths.

recipes.title: plug in a lamp
recipes.name: plug-in-a-lamp
recipes.goal: A lamp is plugged into a suitable outlet, the cord is routed safely, and the switch turns the light on and off.

steps.action: **Inspect the lamp cord.** Look for cuts, exposed wire, scorch marks, loose prongs, cracked plug body, or a crushed section.
steps.expect: the cord and plug look intact, or the lamp is not used.

steps.action: **Check the outlet area.** Confirm the outlet cover is secure, dry, and not already crowded with high-power devices.
steps.expect: the socket is accessible and safe to approach.

steps.action: **Place the lamp first.** Put the lamp where it will be used, with shade clear of curtains, paper, and bedding.
steps.expect: the lamp stands upright without wobbling.

steps.action: **Orient the plug.** Match the wide prong to the wide slot if the plug is polarized, and do not force a mismatch.
steps.expect: the plug lines up naturally with the outlet.

steps.action: **Insert firmly.** Hold the plug body, not the cord, and push straight in until seated. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* forcing a damaged plug or outlet can cause shock or fire, so stop if there is cracking, sparking, heat, or resistance.
steps.expect: no metal prong remains exposed.

steps.action: **Route the cord.** [BRANCH: along wall | across open path] tuck along the wall or furniture edge, or choose another outlet instead of crossing a walkway.
steps.expect: feet, chair legs, doors, and wheels will not snag it.

steps.action: **Switch test.** Turn the lamp switch on, then off, then on if light is desired.
steps.expect: the bulb responds without flicker, buzzing, sparks, or heat at the plug.

steps.action: **Final position check.** Adjust shade and lamp base after switching off if your hand needs to go near the bulb.
steps.expect: the shade is straight and the lamp illuminates the intended area.

recipes.verification: The lamp stands stable, the plug is fully seated in a safe outlet, the cord is out of traffic paths, and the switch controls the light normally.

recipes.title: put a cover on a duvet
recipes.name: put-a-cover-on-a-duvet
recipes.goal: The duvet fills the cover evenly, all far corners are seated, the opening is fastened, and the finished duvet lies smooth on the bed.

steps.action: **Turn the cover inside out.** Put both hands through the opening, grab the far inside corners, and pull them out so seams face outward.
steps.expect: cover is inside out with the opening near you.

steps.action: **Reach through to the far corners.** Insert both hands through the cover opening and hold the two far corners from inside.
steps.expect: each hand controls one far cover corner.

steps.action: **Grab the duvet corners.** With cover corners still in hand, pinch the matching duvet far corners through the fabric or tie them if loops exist.
steps.expect: duvet corners are locked to cover corners.

steps.action: **Flip the cover over the duvet.** Lift the paired far corners and shake downward so the cover starts sliding over the duvet body.
steps.expect: cover turns right side out around the upper half.

steps.action: **Shake down in pulses.** Hold both far corners high, snap the fabric downward in short controlled shakes, and let gravity pull the cover over the fill.
steps.expect: duvet moves deeper into the cover without bunching at the top.

steps.action: **Seat the near corners.** Lay the bundle down, reach into the opening, and pull each near duvet corner into its matching cover corner.
steps.expect: all four corners feel filled and square.

steps.action: **Fasten the opening.** Button, snap, or zip from one end to the other while keeping the duvet edge tucked inside.
steps.expect: closure lies flat and no fill protrudes.

steps.action: **Smooth the panels.** Spread the duvet on the bed and sweep palms from center to edges to distribute loft.
steps.expect: top surface is even with no empty corner pockets.

recipes.verification: All four cover corners contain the matching duvet corners, the opening is fastened, and the duvet lies flat without a central bunch.

recipes.title: put a key on a keyring
recipes.name: put-a-key-on-a-keyring
recipes.goal: Attach a key securely onto a split keyring without bending the key, dropping it, or injuring fingertips.

steps.action: **Place parts on the table.** Set the key and ring flat with the ring opening visible.
steps.expect: both parts are stable and easy to grasp.

steps.action: **Open the split ring slightly.** Lift the outer wire end with a fingernail, coin edge, or opener.
steps.expect: a small gap appears without overbending the ring.

steps.action: **Insert the key hole.** Slide the key hole onto the raised wire end, keeping the key flat.
steps.expect: the key is captured between the ring layers.

steps.action: **Rotate the key around the ring.** Push the key along the ring spiral until it passes the opening and reaches the main loop.
steps.expect: the key moves smoothly and does not pop off.

steps.action: **Release and inspect.** Let the ring close and tug the key lightly.
steps.expect: the key hangs inside the closed loop and cannot leave through the opening.

recipes.verification: The key is fully inside the split ring, the ring closes without a gap, and a light tug does not detach the key.

recipes.title: put a pillowcase on
recipes.name: put-a-pillowcase-on
recipes.goal: The pillow is fully seated inside the pillowcase, corners are squared, and the open end is tucked or aligned neatly.

steps.action: **Orient the case.** Hold the pillowcase with the opening facing your body and seams aligned left to right.
steps.expect: the far closed corners are visible or easy to feel.

steps.action: **Choose the method.** [BRANCH: tuck-corners method | flip method] use tuck-corners for standard cases and flip for tight or decorative cases.
steps.expect: opening is controlled and not twisted.

steps.action: **Tuck-corners method: compress the pillow.** Pinch both pillow corners at one short end and squeeze them slightly toward the center.
steps.expect: pillow end narrows enough to enter the case.

steps.action: **Insert and seat the far end.** Slide the compressed pillow end into the case until both pillow corners reach the closed corners.
steps.expect: far corners feel filled when pinched from outside.

steps.action: **Pull the case over the pillow.** Hold the seated corners with one hand and draw the case opening over the pillow body with the other.
steps.expect: fabric advances evenly without rolling into a band.

steps.action: **Flip method: grab through the case.** Turn the case inside out, grab the far case corners and pillow corners together, then flip the case over the pillow.
steps.expect: case rolls right side out around the pillow.

steps.action: **Square the corners.** Pinch each corner from outside and tug the pillow fill into it using small shakes, not hard pulls.
steps.expect: four corners are filled and angular.

steps.action: **Finish the open end.** Smooth the pillow flat, tuck any internal flap around the pillow, and align the opening seam.
steps.expect: pillow lies flat with no exposed inner pillow except at an intentional opening.

recipes.verification: The pillow fills the pillowcase from closed end to open end, all corners are seated, and the surface is smooth when laid flat.

recipes.title: put away groceries into cupboards
recipes.name: put-away-groceries-into-cupboards
recipes.goal: Move shelf-stable groceries from bags into cupboards so items are visible, stable, and grouped with similar goods.

steps.action: **Sort shelf-stable items.** Separate cans, jars, boxes, snacks, baking items, and cleaning products.
steps.expect: items with different storage needs are in groups.

steps.action: **Check for damage.** Inspect packages for leaks, broken seals, dents, or cracked glass.
steps.expect: unsafe items are set aside.

steps.action: **Open the target cupboard.** Choose the shelf where similar items already live.
steps.expect: the storage location is visible and reachable.

steps.action: **Place heavy items low.** Put cans, jars, and bulk goods on lower or sturdier shelves.
steps.expect: shelves do not bow and items sit flat.

steps.action: **Place fragile items securely.** Set glass jars and bottles away from shelf edges.
steps.expect: fragile containers cannot roll or fall when the door moves.

steps.action: **Group labels outward.** Arrange items so labels or contents can be seen without unstacking.
steps.expect: the next user can identify items quickly.

steps.action: **Keep food separate from chemicals.** Store cleaners away from edible goods.
steps.expect: no chemical container shares a spill path with food.

steps.action: **Close bags and cupboards.** Fold reusable bags, discard empty bags, and close doors.
steps.expect: the floor and counter are clear.

recipes.verification: All shelf-stable groceries are off counters and floors, stored in appropriate cupboards with heavy items stable, fragile items away from edges, and food separated from chemicals.

recipes.title: put on a backpack
recipes.name: put-on-a-backpack
recipes.goal: A backpack is worn with both straps on the shoulders, the load settled against the back, and balance checked before walking.

steps.action: **Place the backpack upright.** Hold or set it so the shoulder straps face the actor.
steps.expect: top handle and both straps are visible.

steps.action: **Check strap orientation.** Untwist straps and loosen tight adjusters if needed.
steps.expect: each strap forms an open loop.

steps.action: **Grip the top handle or one strap.** Lift the backpack close to the torso.
steps.expect: pack weight is controlled and not swinging.

steps.action: **Thread the first arm.** Insert one arm through the nearest strap until the strap rests on that shoulder.
steps.expect: one strap is seated and the pack hangs on one side.

steps.action: **Swing the pack onto the back.** Move the pack behind the torso while keeping the first shoulder engaged.
steps.expect: backpack panel contacts the back.

steps.action: **Thread the second arm.** Reach the free arm back and through the second strap. [BRANCH: standing | seated] standing actors lean slightly forward; seated actors keep the pack supported by the seat or lap.
steps.expect: both straps are over shoulders.

steps.action: **Settle the load.** Shrug shoulders and pull the lower pack down or back until it lies flat.
steps.expect: weight feels centered and the pack is not twisted.

steps.action: **Adjust straps.** Pull adjuster tails evenly or loosen if straps bite into shoulders.
steps.expect: pack sits close to the back without restricting arm motion.

steps.action: **Check balance before stepping.** Stand still for two seconds and shift weight gently left and right.
steps.expect: no backward pull, side sway, or loose dangling strap hazard.

recipes.verification: Both shoulder straps are worn, the backpack lies against the back, straps are adjusted, and the actor can stand steady without holding the pack.

recipes.title: put on a coat
recipes.name: put-on-a-coat
recipes.goal: The coat is worn with both arms through sleeves, shoulders seated, hem hanging evenly, and fasteners closed if desired.

steps.action: **Find the collar and sleeves.** Hold the coat by the collar or upper shoulders.
steps.expect: left and right sleeve openings are visible.

steps.action: **Insert the first arm.** Slide one hand into its sleeve while keeping the sleeve path open.
steps.expect: hand emerges at or near the cuff.

steps.action: **Lift behind the back.** Bring the coat around the shoulders without twisting the first sleeve.
steps.expect: empty sleeve hangs near the other hand.

steps.action: **Insert the second arm.** Guide the other hand into the second sleeve opening and push through.
steps.expect: both hands reach their cuffs.

steps.action: **Shrug over shoulders.** Raise and roll shoulders backward to seat the coat yoke.
steps.expect: collar rests at the back of the neck.

steps.action: **Settle the hem.** Pull front panels down and smooth sleeves from shoulder to cuff.
steps.expect: hem hangs evenly without bunching.

steps.action: **Fasten the front.** [BRANCH: zipper | buttons | open] close the chosen fastener without forcing.
steps.expect: front panels align.

steps.action: **Check mobility.** Move arms forward and down once.
steps.expect: coat stays seated and does not bind painfully.

recipes.verification: Both arms pass through sleeves, shoulders and collar are seated, hem is even, and any chosen front fastener is closed without strain.

recipes.title: replace a paper towel roll
recipes.name: replace-a-paper-towel-roll
recipes.goal: The empty tube is removed, a new roll is loaded in the intended feed direction, and sheets tear cleanly from the holder.

steps.action: **Remove the empty tube.** Pull the cardboard tube off the holder or rod.
steps.expect: holder is exposed and free of paper scraps.

steps.action: **Release the rod.** For a spring holder, compress one end and lift it out of its socket.
steps.expect: rod comes free without bending.

steps.action: **Check roll orientation.** Decide whether sheets should feed over the front or under from the back.
steps.expect: loose sheet points toward the normal pull direction.

steps.action: **Load the roll.** Slide the rod through the tube or place the roll over the post.
steps.expect: roll rotates around its center.

steps.action: **Reseat the rod.** Compress the spring end, place both ends into sockets, then release.
steps.expect: rod tips lock into both supports.

steps.action: **Center the roll.** Shift the roll so it does not rub either side.
steps.expect: roll spins with light resistance.

steps.action: **Start the sheet.** Pull the loose edge forward to the perforation.
steps.expect: one sheet presents beyond the roll.

steps.action: **Perform a tear test.** Hold the roll or use the holder edge and pull down at the perforation.
steps.expect: one sheet detaches cleanly.

recipes.verification: A new roll is secured on the holder, rotates freely, feeds in the chosen direction, and releases one sheet at a perforation.

recipes.title: replace a toilet roll
recipes.name: replace-a-toilet-roll
recipes.goal: Replace an empty toilet paper roll with a full roll seated on the holder and ready to dispense.

steps.action: **Locate the empty tube.** Look at the holder and identify whether a cardboard tube remains on the bar.
steps.expect: the empty tube or missing roll is visible.

steps.action: **Remove the spring bar.** Compress one end of the bar toward the other and pull it free from the holder sockets.
steps.expect: the bar releases without bending the holder.

steps.action: **Slide off the empty tube.** Pull the cardboard tube off the bar.
steps.expect: the bar is bare and the empty tube is in hand.

steps.action: **Dispose of the tube.** Put the tube in recycling or trash according to the room's setup.
steps.expect: the old tube is no longer on the floor or counter.

steps.action: **Choose orientation.** [BRANCH: over | under] place the new roll so paper feeds over the front or under the back based on household preference.
steps.expect: the loose sheet points in the chosen direction.

steps.action: **Load the roll on the bar.** Slide the bar through the cardboard core without crushing the roll.
steps.expect: the roll spins around the bar.

steps.action: **Compress and seat one end.** Put one bar tip into a holder socket, compress the spring, and align the other tip.
steps.expect: the first side stays in place while the second side approaches its socket.

steps.action: **Release into the second socket.** Let the spring expand gently into the opposite socket.
steps.expect: the bar clicks or settles into both sides.

steps.action: **Test the feed.** Pull one sheet down and forward.
steps.expect: paper unrolls smoothly and the bar remains seated.

steps.action: **Tidy the area.** Remove wrapper scraps or fallen sheets.
steps.expect: the holder area is clean and reachable for the next user.

recipes.verification: A full roll is mounted, spins freely, feeds in the chosen orientation, and the empty tube has been disposed of.

recipes.title: replace a trash bag
recipes.name: replace-a-trash-bag
recipes.goal: Remove a full trash bag and install a clean liner so the can is ready for new trash without leaks or exposed edges.

steps.action: **Open or remove the lid.** Lift the lid or swing it clear without touching the trash surface.
steps.expect: the liner rim is visible around the can.

steps.action: **Free the bag edge.** Pull the liner edge or drawstrings inward from the can rim.
steps.expect: the bag mouth can close above the trash.

steps.action: **Close the full bag.** Tie drawstrings or twist the neck and knot it above the waste level.
steps.expect: trash is enclosed and the bag can be lifted from the closed neck.

steps.action: **Lift straight up.** Pull the bag out without dragging against sharp can edges.
steps.expect: the bag clears the can without tearing or leaking.

steps.action: **Insert the new bag.** Open a clean liner, push its bottom to the can base, and fold the top edge over the rim.
steps.expect: the liner reaches the bottom and stays captured around the rim.

steps.action: **Reinstall the lid.** Set the lid back or close it, then place the full bag at the disposal point.
steps.expect: the can opens normally and the full bag remains closed.

recipes.verification: The full bag is closed and removed, and the trash can has a clean liner seated at the bottom with its edge secured over the rim.

recipes.title: roll up a rug
recipes.name: roll-up-a-rug
recipes.goal: Roll a rug into a compact cylinder for moving, storage, or cleaning access without trapping furniture or creating a trip hazard.

steps.action: **Clear the rug surface.** Remove objects, cords, and small furniture from the rug.
steps.expect: the rug surface is empty from edge to edge.

steps.action: **Straighten one short edge.** Lift and pull the edge until it lies square across the width.
steps.expect: the starting edge forms a straight line.

steps.action: **Make the first fold-over.** Curl the starting edge over itself by 5 to 10 cm and press it evenly across the width.
steps.expect: a straight roll core forms.

steps.action: **Roll forward with both hands.** Push the roll away while guiding both ends so they stay aligned.
steps.expect: the cylinder grows without diagonal drift.

steps.action: **Tuck loose fringe or corners.** Pause when fringe appears and fold it inward before continuing.
steps.expect: no fabric strings trail outside the roll.

steps.action: **Secure the roll.** Wrap a strap or loose tie around the middle and near each end if needed.
steps.expect: the rug remains rolled when released.

recipes.verification: The rug is a secure, aligned cylinder with no trapped objects, no loose fringe dragging, and no raised edge left as a trip hazard.

recipes.title: roll up a yoga mat
recipes.name: roll-up-a-yoga-mat
recipes.goal: The yoga mat is rolled tight and even according to its care preference, strapped if needed, and stored upright or flat without curled edges becoming damaged.

steps.action: **Identify the top side.** Look for texture, logo placement, or care instructions that indicate which surface should face in or out.
steps.expect: rolling orientation is chosen before folding.

steps.action: **Clear and align the mat.** Lay the mat flat, brush away grit, and square the long edges with both hands.
steps.expect: corners are visible and edges are parallel.

steps.action: **Set the first edge.** Fold or curl the starting short edge into a small straight roll using both thumbs.
steps.expect: first turn is even across the width.

steps.action: **Roll with even pressure.** Push the roll forward from the center while outer fingers guide both ends.
steps.expect: roll advances as a cylinder, not a cone.

steps.action: **Correct drifting edges.** If one end protrudes, pause and nudge that side inward before the next turn.
steps.expect: edges return to alignment.

steps.action: **Tighten without crushing.** Apply light downward pressure with palms as each turn closes, keeping the mat surface smooth.
steps.expect: roll feels firm but not creased.

steps.action: **Strap the roll.** Wrap the strap around the center or both ends and fasten with moderate tension.
steps.expect: roll stays closed when released.

steps.action: **Store upright or flat.** Place the roll upright in a rack or flat on a shelf away from direct heat.
steps.expect: mat does not unroll or lean into a sharp bend.

recipes.verification: The mat forms an even cylinder with aligned edges, remains closed under its strap, and is stored without dampness or sharp bends.

recipes.title: screw a cap onto a bottle
recipes.name: screw-a-cap-onto-a-bottle
recipes.goal: Thread a cap onto a bottle straight and tighten it enough to close the bottle without cross-threading or cracking it.

steps.action: **Stabilize the bottle.** Hold the bottle body upright near its shoulder or base.
steps.expect: the bottle does not tip when touched at the mouth.

steps.action: **Place the cap level.** Set the cap centered on the bottle mouth with its open side downward.
steps.expect: the cap sits flat rather than tilted.

steps.action: **Find the thread start.** Rotate the cap counterclockwise lightly until it drops or clicks into the thread start.
steps.expect: the cap settles level on the mouth.

steps.action: **Turn clockwise gently.** Rotate with light downward pressure for the first full turn.
steps.expect: the cap advances downward evenly without wobbling.

steps.action: **Tighten to seal.** Continue turning until resistance increases, then stop at snug hand-tight force.
steps.expect: the cap no longer spins freely and sits evenly against the bottle neck.

steps.action: **Check closure.** Lift or gently invert only if the contents allow it.
steps.expect: no liquid leaks and the cap remains straight.

recipes.verification: The cap is level, hand-tight, seated against the bottle neck, and the bottle does not leak during a gentle closure check.

recipes.title: set out bins for collection
recipes.name: set-out-bins-for-collection
recipes.goal: Place the correct waste bins at the collection point with lids closed, access clear, and no obstruction to pedestrians, vehicles, or collectors.

steps.action: **Confirm collection schedule.** Check which bins are due for pickup.
steps.expect: only the correct trash, recycling, compost, or yard bins are selected.

steps.action: **Check lids and contents.** Close lids and remove prohibited overflow or loose sharp items if visible.
steps.expect: bins can roll without spilling.

steps.action: **Grip handles securely.** Stand behind wheeled bins and keep feet clear of wheels.
steps.expect: the bin can be tipped slightly under control.

steps.action: **Roll along a clear route.** Move slowly over thresholds, slopes, gravel, or wet surfaces.
steps.expect: the bin remains upright.

steps.action: **Place at the collection point.** Set bins where local practice expects them, usually near curb edge but out of traffic lanes.
steps.expect: collection arms or workers can reach them.

steps.action: **Orient bins correctly.** Face arrows, handles, or lids according to local collection markings.
steps.expect: the bin opening and wheels match collection requirements.

steps.action: **Leave clearance.** Keep bins away from parked cars, mailboxes, hydrants, bike lanes, and sidewalks.
steps.expect: pedestrians, vehicles, and collectors have access.

steps.action: **Return safely.** Walk back along the route and close gates or doors.
steps.expect: the property is secure and paths remain clear.

recipes.verification: The scheduled bins are upright at the collection point, lids closed, correctly oriented, reachable by collectors, and not blocking pedestrians, traffic, hydrants, or driveways.

recipes.title: sharpen a pencil
recipes.name: sharpen-a-pencil
recipes.goal: The pencil is sharpened to a centered usable point, and shavings are contained or cleared.

steps.action: **Inspect the pencil end.** Check whether the core is centered and the wood is intact.
steps.expect: pencil can enter the sharpener without splinters catching.

steps.action: **Insert squarely.** Push the pencil straight into the sharpener hole along its axis.
steps.expect: pencil seats against the blade with no side angle.

steps.action: **Steady the sharpener.** Hold the sharpener body or place it flat on the table.
steps.expect: sharpener does not rotate with the pencil.

steps.action: **Turn steadily.** Rotate the pencil clockwise with light inward pressure.
steps.expect: continuous shavings form and resistance stays smooth.

steps.action: **Pause and check.** Remove the pencil after several turns and inspect the exposed graphite.
steps.expect: wood tapers evenly toward a point.

steps.action: **Continue if needed.** [BRANCH: dull point | sharp point] reinsert squarely for a few more turns or stop.
steps.expect: point reaches the needed length without breaking.

steps.action: **Clear shavings.** Empty the sharpener chamber or brush loose shavings into trash.
steps.expect: blade path and table are free of debris.

steps.action: **Test lightly.** Touch the point to scrap paper with normal writing pressure.
steps.expect: line appears without the point snapping.

recipes.verification: The pencil writes a clear line, the point is centered enough for use, and shavings are removed from the work area.

recipes.title: slide a book off a shelf
recipes.name: slide-a-book-off-a-shelf
recipes.goal: One selected book is removed from the shelf without pulling down neighboring books.

steps.action: **Locate the selected spine.** Read or match the spine and identify its left and right neighbors.
steps.expect: the target book boundaries are visible.

steps.action: **Create a small gap.** Press neighboring books slightly away from the target with flat finger pressure.
steps.expect: a narrow clearance appears on at least one side.

steps.action: **Grip the upper spine.** Pinch the target book near the top spine edge without hooking fragile paper.
steps.expect: the book moves slightly while neighbors stay in place.

steps.action: **Slide outward partway.** Pull the book straight forward 3-6 cm while keeping it vertical.
steps.expect: enough cover edge protrudes for a full grip.

steps.action: **Transfer to cover support.** Grip the protruding book with one hand on each side or one hand under the bottom edge.
steps.expect: the book weight is supported beyond the spine.

steps.action: **Remove fully.** Pull straight out until the back cover clears the shelf row.
steps.expect: the book is free and neighboring books remain upright.

steps.action: **Close the shelf gap.** Push neighboring books together or move a bookend inward.
steps.expect: the remaining row is upright and supported.

recipes.verification: The selected book is fully removed and the remaining books stand upright without falling or leaning unsupported.

recipes.title: sort laundry into lights and darks
recipes.name: sort-laundry-into-lights-and-darks
recipes.goal: Sort dirty laundry into light and dark loads while removing pocket hazards and separating items that need special handling.

steps.action: **Create sorting spaces.** Designate one area for lights and one for darks.
steps.expect: two clearly separate piles or baskets exist.

steps.action: **Inspect each item.** Pick up one garment at a time and check color, fabric, and care label if uncertain.
steps.expect: the item's load category is known.

steps.action: **Empty pockets.** Remove tissues, coins, keys, pens, and sharp objects.
steps.expect: pockets are flat and no hard items remain.

steps.action: **Place lights together.** Put white, pale, and light-gray washable items in the light pile.
steps.expect: light pile contains no saturated dark dyes.

steps.action: **Place darks together.** Put black, navy, red, denim, and strong colors in the dark pile.
steps.expect: dark pile contains items likely to bleed or shed dye.

steps.action: **Separate special items.** Set delicates, wool, dry-clean-only, heavily soiled, or new bright items aside.
steps.expect: special-care items are not mixed into standard loads.

steps.action: **Check pile size.** Keep each load loose enough for water and agitation.
steps.expect: no load is packed tight before washing.

recipes.verification: Laundry is divided into light, dark, and special-care groups, with pockets emptied and no sharp or hard objects left in standard wash piles.

recipes.title: spray and wipe a surface
recipes.name: spray-and-wipe-a-surface
recipes.goal: Apply cleaner to a compatible surface and wipe it dry or evenly damp without streaks, residue, or overspray damage.

steps.action: **Clear and inspect the surface.** Move objects aside and look for loose grit or liquid.
steps.expect: the wipe path is open and hazards are visible.

steps.action: **Aim the spray safely.** Hold the nozzle 15 to 25 cm from the surface, pointed away from faces and electronics.
steps.expect: the spray cone lands only on the intended area.

steps.action: **Apply a light mist.** Squeeze the trigger once or twice over the dirty area.
steps.expect: the surface is damp, not puddled.

steps.action: **Wipe in overlapping strokes.** Fold the cloth flat and press lightly from the far edge toward the near edge.
steps.expect: soil transfers to the cloth and the surface becomes clearer.

steps.action: **Turn the cloth to a clean face.** Refold or replace it when the wiping side looks dirty or wet.
steps.expect: later strokes do not smear residue back onto the surface.

steps.action: **Dry and inspect.** Make final dry passes along the grain or edge direction.
steps.expect: the surface has no wet streaks, visible debris, or cleaner pools.

recipes.verification: The cleaned surface is free of visible debris, has no standing liquid or streaks, and nearby objects are dry.

recipes.title: staple papers together
recipes.name: staple-papers-together
recipes.goal: Fasten a stack of papers with one staple in the intended corner or edge so pages stay aligned and turn easily.

steps.action: **Square the paper stack.** Tap the bottom and side edges on the desk until corners align.
steps.expect: page edges form one clean rectangle.

steps.action: **Choose staple location.** Usually use the upper-left corner, angled about 45 degrees across the corner.
steps.expect: the intended staple path crosses all pages away from text.

steps.action: **Insert the stack into the stapler.** Slide the corner between base and head until the staple mark is under the driver.
steps.expect: paper lies flat and reaches the target depth.

steps.action: **Press straight down.** Hold the stack still and compress the stapler in one firm motion.
steps.expect: a click or snap occurs and the stapler head returns up.

steps.action: **Remove and inspect.** Pull the papers out flat and look at both sides of the staple.
steps.expect: the staple crown is flush and both legs are folded through the stack.

recipes.verification: All intended pages are attached in order by a flush staple, and both staple legs are folded without sharp protrusions.

recipes.title: sweep a floor with a broom
recipes.name: sweep-a-floor-with-a-broom
recipes.goal: A hard floor is free of visible crumbs, dust, and debris, with everything collected into the dustpan and binned, and moved furniture returned to place.

steps.action: **Clear the floor first.** Lift chairs onto the table or shift them out, shake mats outside, pick up cables and large litter by hand.
steps.expect: open floor with only sweepable debris left on it.

steps.action: **Pick a collection spot and a direction.** Sweep from the far corner toward one open spot near the exit or bin, never toward already-cleaned floor.
steps.expect: a mental lane map: perimeter and corners first, open middle last.

steps.action: **Sweep with short, overlapping pull strokes.** Hold the broom like a canoe paddle (one hand on top, one mid-shaft), bristles at a low angle, and pull debris toward you in 30 to 50 cm strokes. Do not flick: long fast strokes launch fine dust airborne.
steps.expect: debris moves in a growing line ahead of the bristles; no dust cloud rising.

steps.action: **Work edges and corners with the broom's corner.** Use the bristle tip edge to rake debris out of corners and along baseboards into the open, then rejoin the main pattern.
steps.expect: baseboard lines free of the gray dust ribbon that collects there.

steps.action: **Merge into one pile per zone.** In large or multi-room spaces, build a small pile per zone rather than pushing one pile long distances; long pushes shed a trail.
steps.expect: one compact pile in each zone, floor behind you clean.

steps.action: **Hold the dustpan and load the pile.** Crouch, press the dustpan lip flat and firm against the floor, and sweep the pile in with short strokes.
steps.expect: bulk of the pile inside the pan on the first pass.

steps.action: **Beat the dustpan line.** A thin line of fine dust always remains at the pan lip. Back the pan up 20 cm and sweep the line in again at a shallower angle; repeat once or twice more.
steps.expect: the line shrinks each pass to nearly nothing. Line will not shrink → F2.

steps.action: **Empty the pan into the bin low and slowly.** Tip it deep inside the bin to avoid puffing dust back out.
steps.expect: pan empty, no dust plume.

steps.action: **Restore the room.** Return chairs, mats, and anything moved.
steps.expect: room in its original arrangement over clean floor.

recipes.verification: Sight down the floor at a low angle against the light: no crumbs, hair, or dust ribbons along baseboards or in corners, the dustpan is emptied and stowed, and the furniture is back in place.

recipes.title: switch off a power strip
recipes.name: switch-off-a-power-strip
recipes.goal: A power strip is switched off in a safe order and the off state is confirmed by the switch position or indicator light.

steps.action: **Identify the correct strip.** Trace or visually confirm the strip serving the intended devices.
steps.expect: target power strip is distinguished from nearby strips.

steps.action: **Check connected devices.** Look for computers, medical devices, chargers, lamps, or appliances attached to the strip.
steps.expect: no critical device requires continuous power.

steps.action: **Stop sensitive devices first.** Shut down or unplug devices that need an orderly power-off before using the strip switch.
steps.expect: devices that could lose data are already off or safe.

steps.action: **Stabilize the strip.** Hold the strip body or press it gently against the floor or desk without touching plug prongs.
steps.expect: strip does not slide when the switch is pressed.

steps.action: **Locate the main switch.** Find the rocker, toggle, or push button, usually near the cord entry.
steps.expect: switch actuator and current indicator state are known.

steps.action: **Press to off.** Move the switch to OFF or press the unlit side until it clicks. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* active device power may be cut; confirm step 2 before pressing.
steps.expect: switch rests in the off position.

steps.action: **Confirm indicator off.** Observe the lamp or LED on the strip and any powered devices.
steps.expect: strip indicator is dark and connected devices lose standby lights as expected.

steps.action: **Leave cords undisturbed.** Release the strip and route feet or wheels away from cords.
steps.expect: plugs remain seated and cords are not under tension.

recipes.verification: The intended power strip switch is in the off position and its power indicator or connected device indicators confirm no output power.

recipes.title: take out the trash
recipes.name: take-out-the-trash
recipes.goal: The kitchen bin's full bag is sealed, deposited in the correct outdoor/building collection bin, and the kitchen bin is relined and back in place.

steps.action: **Open the bin lid and check the contents' top layer.** No liquids pooling, no protruding sharp objects. If glass shards or skewers protrude, fold cardboard around them before proceeding.
steps.expect: the bag's contents are containable; nothing pierces the bag wall.

steps.action: **Lift the bag's edges off the bin rim and tie a secure knot.** Gather the liner's loose edges, twist, and double-knot; leave no open mouth.
steps.expect: bag sealed; nothing can fall out when inverted slightly.

steps.action: **Lift the bag straight up and out of the bin.** Lift from the knot with one hand, support the base with the other if heavy. If resistance (vacuum or snag), tilt the bin and break the seal — don't yank.
steps.expect: bag comes free intact; no tearing sound; bin stays upright.

steps.action: **Check the bag for leaks before crossing the home.** Hold over the bin for 3 s and watch for drips. [BRANCH: drips → double-bag before moving | dry → proceed]
steps.expect: no drips on the floor route.

steps.action: **Carry the bag to the outdoor/collection bin.** Hold away from your body/chassis and clear of walls; open doors fully before passing through; slow near people.
steps.expect: no contact between bag and walls, door frames, or people en route.

steps.action: **Deposit into the correct collection bin.** Open the outdoor bin lid, place (don't throw) the bag in, close the lid fully. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* retrieval from collection bins is not assumed possible — confirm this is the trash bag, not a similar bag of belongings, before depositing.
steps.expect: bag inside the correct bin; lid closed flat (animal-proof).

steps.action: **Return and reline the kitchen bin.** Pull a new liner over the rim, push it to conform, leaving overhang.
steps.expect: liner snug on the rim, no air pocket at the bottom.

steps.action: **Replace the bin in its position and wash/wipe hands or grippers.**
steps.expect: bin lid closes; workspace as found, minus the trash.

recipes.verification: The sealed bag sits in the correct collection bin with its lid fully closed, the kitchen bin is relined and repositioned, the carry route has no drips or debris, and hands/grippers have been cleaned.

recipes.title: thread a needle
recipes.name: thread-a-needle
recipes.goal: Thread passes through the needle eye with a usable tail, and the far end is knotted for sewing.

steps.action: **Trim the thread end.** Cut a fresh angled end if the tip is fuzzy.
steps.expect: thread narrows to one compact point.

steps.action: **Wet and flatten the tip.** Lightly moisten the last centimeter, then pinch it flat between thumb and index finger.
steps.expect: fibers cling into a stiff blade.

steps.action: **Steady both hands.** Rest wrists or little fingers on the table with needle in one hand and thread in the other.
steps.expect: the eye and tip move slowly relative to each other.

steps.action: **Orient the eye.** Rotate the needle until the eye opening faces the thread tip squarely.
steps.expect: a bright slot or hole is visible.

steps.action: **Push through the eye.** Advance the flattened tip through the center of the eye with minimal bend.
steps.expect: a small loop or thread point appears on the far side.

steps.action: **Pull the tail.** Pinch the appearing thread and draw 8 to 12 cm through the eye.
steps.expect: needle hangs on the thread without slipping off.

steps.action: **Equalize or leave a tail.** [BRANCH: single thread | doubled thread] set the working length required.
steps.expect: chosen tail length remains stable when lifted.

steps.action: **Tie the knot.** Wrap the long end around a fingertip, roll the loop, and pull it tight at the end.
steps.expect: a knot stops at the thread end.

recipes.verification: The needle carries thread through its eye, a usable tail remains, and the far end has a knot that resists a light pull.

recipes.title: tidy a room
recipes.name: tidy-a-room
recipes.goal: A cluttered room is returned to its baseline state: surfaces clear, every item in its home location or staged for its correct destination (trash, laundry, dishes, other rooms), nothing lost in the process.

steps.action: **Survey and set the four stations.** Walk the room once; place the trash bag, laundry basket, elsewhere-box, and don't-know tray at accessible spots.
steps.expect: a mental map of the mess density and four labeled destinations ready.

steps.action: **First pass — trash only.** Circle the room collecting unambiguous garbage: wrappers, empty cans, used tissues. One category per pass keeps decisions fast.
steps.expect: visible trash gone; bag filling; zero agonizing (ambiguous items stay put this pass).

steps.action: **Second pass — dishes and food items.** Cups, plates, bowls, snack remnants to a carried stack or directly to the kitchen sink (`embodied/carry-and-deliver-an-item` for stacks; liquids emptied into the sink first, never carried atop a stack).
steps.expect: no dishware or perishables remain in the room.

steps.action: **Third pass — laundry.** Clothes and textiles: worn → basket; clean-but-displaced → folded to their storage (`embodied/fold-a-tshirt`) or staged on the bed for the owner.
steps.expect: floor and furniture free of fabric; basket staged at the door.

steps.action: **Fourth pass — homeless items to homes.** Everything with a known home goes there now, batch-carried by destination room via the elsewhere-box. Unknown-home items → the don't-know tray, *not* a guessed drawer (hidden ≠ tidy; lost is the failure mode). ⚠️ *Irreversible:* discarding someone else's item — never trash anything ambiguous (papers, cables, small parts); the don't-know tray exists so nothing irreversible happens without its owner.
steps.expect: surfaces and floor holding only items that belong in this room, plus one honest tray of questions.

steps.action: **Surface pass.** Now-cleared surfaces get a wipe (damp cloth for desks/tables, dry for electronics); items lifted-wiped-under-replaced, back at right angles/owner's arrangement.
steps.expect: dust-free surfaces; the room's items back in their arrangement, squared.

steps.action: **Floor finish and exit with the stations.** Quick floor pass (`daily/sweep-and-mop-a-floor` or vacuum) now that it's reachable; carry out trash (`embodied/take-out-the-trash`), basket to laundry, elsewhere-box distributed, don't-know tray presented to the owner or left labeled in plain sight.
steps.expect: room at baseline; all four stations resolved or explicitly handed off.

recipes.verification: Surfaces and floor are clear and wiped, every item is at its home / correct destination room / trash / laundry, the don't-know tray is explicitly handed off or visibly staged, and nothing was irreversibly discarded or hidden that an owner couldn't locate by asking the system.

recipes.title: turn a light on and off
recipes.name: turn-a-light-on-and-off
recipes.goal: A light is changed to the intended on or off state and the result is confirmed from the room illumination or switch indicator.

steps.action: **Locate the control.** Find the wall switch, lamp switch, pull chain, or dimmer associated with the target light.
steps.expect: the control is identified and reachable.

steps.action: **Check current state.** Observe the fixture, room brightness, or switch indicator.
steps.expect: current on, off, or dim level is known.

steps.action: **Position for operation.** Stand or align the manipulator close enough to move the control without leaning.
steps.expect: finger or gripper reaches the control squarely.

steps.action: **Operate a toggle switch.** Flip the switch fully to the desired direction. [BRANCH: turn on | turn off] move to ON for light; move to OFF for dark.
steps.expect: the switch rests at its end position.

steps.action: **Operate a rocker or button.** Press the active side or center until the switch clicks.
steps.expect: tactile or audible click occurs.

steps.action: **Operate a dimmer variant.** Rotate, slide, or long-press to the target brightness when dimming is required.
steps.expect: brightness changes smoothly toward the target.

steps.action: **Confirm the light state.** Look at the fixture or the illuminated area for one second.
steps.expect: final state matches the intended on, off, or dim level.

steps.action: **Correct if the wrong light changed.** Return the first control to its prior state, then try the adjacent labeled control.
steps.expect: target light changes and unintended light is restored.

recipes.verification: The target light is in the requested state and the physical control is resting in a stable position after operation.

recipes.title: unplug a cable by the connector
recipes.name: unplug-a-cable-by-the-connector
recipes.goal: The cable is disconnected by pulling the connector body, leaving the cable and port undamaged.

steps.action: **Stabilize the device or socket.** Hold the device body or wall plate near the port.
steps.expect: the port does not move when lightly touched.

steps.action: **Grip the connector body.** Pinch or hold the rigid plug shell, not the flexible cable.
steps.expect: grip force is on the connector housing.

steps.action: **Align with the port axis.** Set the pull direction straight out from the port opening.
steps.expect: the connector is not angled up, down, or sideways.

steps.action: **Pull steadily.** Apply smooth outward force along the connector axis.
steps.expect: the connector slides out without bending.

steps.action: **Clear the port.** Continue pulling until the metal or plastic tip fully exits.
steps.expect: the plug is free and no part remains seated.

steps.action: **Inspect both ends.** Look at the connector and port for bent pins, cracks, or debris.
steps.expect: connector and port appear intact.

steps.action: **Place the cable safely.** Lay the cable end on the desk or coil it loosely away from walkways.
steps.expect: the connector is not dangling under strain.
