recipes.verification: The connector is fully removed, the port and plug are visibly undamaged, and the cable is stored without tension.

recipes.title: use a handheld vacuum
recipes.name: use-a-handheld-vacuum
recipes.goal: Remove small dry debris from a surface or floor using a handheld vacuum and return the vacuum ready for next use.

steps.action: **Inspect the intake and bin.** Look for clogs, a full bin, or missing filter before turning on.
steps.expect: the vacuum is assembled and airflow path is open.

steps.action: **Grip and power on.** Hold the handle with the intake angled toward the debris, then press the power button.
steps.expect: motor noise starts and suction is felt at the nozzle.

steps.action: **Vacuum from far edge inward.** Move the nozzle slowly over debris with the opening close to the surface.
steps.expect: visible crumbs or dust disappear into the intake.

steps.action: **Use short overlapping passes.** Sweep each area with slight overlap instead of fast waving.
steps.expect: no debris remains between passes.

steps.action: **Power off before lifting away.** Press the power button while the nozzle is still near the surface.
steps.expect: suction stops and debris does not fall back out.

steps.action: **Empty or dock if needed.** Empty the bin if it reached the fill line, then place the vacuum on its charger.
steps.expect: the vacuum is clean enough inside and seated on the base or stored safely.

recipes.verification: The target area has no visible dry debris, the vacuum bin is not overfilled, and the vacuum is powered off and stored or charging.

recipes.title: use a hole punch
recipes.name: use-a-hole-punch
recipes.goal: Punch clean holes in a paper stack at positions that fit the intended binder or fastener.

steps.action: **Square the papers.** Tap the stack edges on the desk to align pages.
steps.expect: all page corners line up.

steps.action: **Set the paper guide.** Slide the guide to the page size mark or center mark.
steps.expect: the stack will enter to the same depth across pages.

steps.action: **Insert the stack.** Push the edge into the slot until it contacts the back stop and side guide.
steps.expect: paper lies flat and hole positions are aligned.

steps.action: **Press the handle fully.** Apply downward force until the punch completes its travel.
steps.expect: a firm cut is felt and paper dots drop into the catch tray.

steps.action: **Release and remove.** Let the handle return before pulling the stack out.
steps.expect: the papers slide out without tearing.

steps.action: **Inspect and empty if needed.** Check hole edges and empty the catch tray if it is near full.
steps.expect: holes are clean and the punch is not packed with paper dots.

recipes.verification: The papers have clean holes in matching positions, fit onto the binder rings or fastener, and are not torn at the punched edge.

recipes.title: use a screwdriver
recipes.name: use-a-screwdriver
recipes.goal: The screw is tightened or loosened with the correct driver, without stripping the head or damaging the workpiece.

steps.action: **Identify the head.** Inspect for Phillips, flat, Torx, hex, or square drive.
steps.expect: matching bit type is selected.

steps.action: **Match the size.** Test the bit in the head without turning.
steps.expect: bit fills the recess with little wobble.

steps.action: **Seat the bit.** Place the tip straight into the screw head along the screw axis.
steps.expect: driver shaft aligns with the screw.

steps.action: **Brace the workpiece.** Hold the object or surface so it cannot spin or shift.
steps.expect: screw remains the only moving part.

steps.action: **Push while turning.** Apply inward pressure and rotate clockwise to tighten, counterclockwise to loosen.
steps.expect: screw turns without the bit climbing out.

steps.action: **Use short resets.** Lift and regrip the handle when wrist range ends.
steps.expect: pressure stays axial and the bit stays seated.

steps.action: **Stop at snug.** [BRANCH: tightening | loosening] stop when resistance rises sharply or the screw releases.
steps.expect: screw is secure or free without stripped edges.

steps.action: **Inspect the head.** Remove the driver straight out and check the recess.
steps.expect: head shape remains crisp.

recipes.verification: The screw reaches the intended tight or loose state, the head remains usable, and the workpiece surface is not gouged.

recipes.title: use a tape measure
recipes.name: use-a-tape-measure
recipes.goal: A distance is measured from a hooked or aligned edge, read at the correct mark, and the tape is retracted under control.

steps.action: **Choose the start point.** Place the hook on an outside edge or butt the case against an inside surface.
steps.expect: zero reference is physically anchored.

steps.action: **Extend the blade.** Pull the case away in line with the measurement path.
steps.expect: blade stays straight without twisting.

steps.action: **Hook the edge.** Let the hook catch fully over the edge, then add light tension.
steps.expect: hook seats squarely and does not slide.

steps.action: **Align to the end point.** Keep the blade parallel to the measured span.
steps.expect: markings cross the target point cleanly.

steps.action: **Lock if needed.** Press the lock before moving your reading hand away.
steps.expect: blade length holds without retracting.

steps.action: **Read the mark.** Look straight down at the end point and note the nearest printed mark.
steps.expect: measurement is read without parallax shift.

steps.action: **Release the hook.** [BRANCH: hooked edge | free measurement] unhook gently or keep the blade supported.
steps.expect: blade remains under hand control.

steps.action: **Retract controlled.** Press the lock open and feed the blade back slowly.
steps.expect: hook returns to the case without snapping.

recipes.verification: The measured value corresponds to a stable start reference and visible end mark, and the tape blade is fully retracted without injury.

recipes.title: water garden plants
recipes.name: water-garden-plants
recipes.goal: Every plant that actually needs water has been watered deeply at the root zone, pots drain freely, and the can and faucet are shut down and stowed.

steps.action: **Walk the route before filling anything.** Check each bed and pot for wilt, and note which containers dried out. Not everything needs water every day.
steps.expect: a short mental list of targets; obviously moist beds struck off.

steps.action: **Do the soil check on each candidate.** Push a finger 3 to 5 cm into the soil beside the stem (not against it). [BRANCH: dry at depth → water it | still moist at depth → skip it, surface dryness lies]
steps.expect: a clear wet/dry verdict per plant; skipped plants noted for tomorrow.

steps.action: **Fill the can at the faucet.** Fill to a weight you can carry with a straight back; two lighter trips beat one staggering one. Close the faucet fully after each fill.
steps.expect: can filled, faucet not dripping, path back to the beds unobstructed.

steps.action: **Water the root zone, not the leaves.** Remove or bypass the rose, lower the spout close to the soil at the base of each plant, and pour slowly around the stem's drip circle. Wet foliage is the main avoidable cause of leaf fungus.
steps.expect: water pooling briefly then soaking in around the base; leaves staying dry.

steps.action: **Water deeply, not often.** Give each plant a slow, generous dose so moisture reaches full root depth; a daily light sprinkle trains roots to stay shallow. If water runs off, pause, let it soak, and continue in a second pass.
steps.expect: soil dark and moist at finger depth on a re-probe, not just a wet surface film.

steps.action: **Handle pots to the drain point.** Water potted plants until water just emerges from the drainage holes, then stop.
steps.expect: first trickle at the holes; saucer catching it. Water races straight through instantly → F2.

steps.action: **Use the rose for seedlings and delicate plants.** Attach the rose head and water with a gentle sweeping pass; a hard pour from the spout flattens seedlings and blasts soil off roots.
steps.expect: seedlings upright after watering, soil surface intact.

steps.action: **Refill and repeat along the route.** Track roughly how many cans each zone took; that number becomes your calibration for the season.
steps.expect: all targets from step 1 watered; can count noted.

steps.action: **Shut down.** Empty the last part-can onto any plant rather than storing it (stored water breeds mosquitoes), close the faucet firmly, and store the can inverted.
steps.expect: faucet off and dry, can empty and upside down, path clear.

recipes.verification: Re-probe two or three watered plants: soil is moist at 3 to 5 cm depth, pots have drained into their saucers without standing water above the soil, foliage is dry, the faucet is off with no drip, and the can is empty and stowed inverted.

recipes.title: water houseplants
recipes.name: water-houseplants
recipes.goal: Every houseplant on the care list that needs water has been watered to drainage, without overwatering any plant or spilling on floors and furniture.

steps.action: **Fill the watering can at the faucet.** Room-temperature water, ~3/4 full for carrying stability.
steps.expect: can filled below the spill line; faucet fully closed after.

steps.action: **Go to the first plant and test soil moisture.** Probe a finger (or moisture sensor) ~3 cm into the soil. [BRANCH: dry at depth → water it | moist → skip, next plant]
steps.expect: a clear dry/moist reading; when in doubt, skip — underwatering recovers, overwatering kills.

steps.action: **Water slowly at the soil, around the base.** Pour in a slow spiral, avoiding leaves and the pot rim, until water just appears in the saucer.
steps.expect: soil darkens evenly; first drips reach the saucer; no overflow.

steps.action: **Pause and check the saucer.** If the saucer approaches full, stop — the pot has reached drainage capacity.
steps.expect: saucer holds a shallow layer, well below its rim.

steps.action: **Move to the next plant and repeat steps 2–4.** Refill the can at the faucet when empty.
steps.expect: each visited plant is either watered-to-drainage or skipped-as-moist.

steps.action: **Second pass: empty any saucer still full after ~20 minutes.** Carry it level to the sink, pour out, replace. Standing water rots roots.
steps.expect: no saucer holds deep standing water.

steps.action: **Return the can to storage and wipe any drips along the route.**
steps.expect: floors and furniture dry; can stored.

recipes.verification: Every plant on the list was visited; each is either watered (soil dark, saucer with shallow drainage) or logged as skipped-moist; no saucer has standing water at the 20-minute check; floors along the route are dry.

recipes.title: wind and store an extension cord
recipes.name: wind-and-store-an-extension-cord
recipes.goal: Unplug, wind, and store an extension cord without damaging insulation, creating trip hazards, or leaving it energized.

steps.action: **Turn off connected devices.** Switch off tools, lamps, or appliances before unplugging.
steps.expect: connected devices stop drawing power.

steps.action: **Unplug from the wall.** Pull by the plug body, not the cord.
steps.expect: metal prongs are out of the outlet.

steps.action: **Unplug attached devices.** Disconnect the far end and keep plugs off wet or dirty surfaces.
steps.expect: the cord is fully de-energized and free.

steps.action: **Inspect the cord.** Look for cuts, exposed wire, heat marks, crushed plugs, or loose sockets.
steps.expect: the cord is safe to store or set aside for disposal.

steps.action: **Straighten twists.** Walk the cord out or shake gentle loops loose.
steps.expect: the cord lies without tight kinks.

steps.action: **Wind in loose loops.** Coil using hand-to-elbow or over-under loops without forcing tight bends.
steps.expect: the coil is even and not twisted.

steps.action: **Secure the coil.** Use a cord strap, hook-and-loop tie, or loose tie around the coil, not around one tight spot.
steps.expect: the cord stays coiled without pinching.

steps.action: **Store dry and off walkways.** Hang or place the coil away from water, heat, doors, and foot traffic.
steps.expect: no trip hazard or strain on plugs remains.

recipes.verification: The cord is unplugged at both ends, inspected, loosely coiled, secured, and stored dry outside any walking path.

recipes.title: wipe a table
recipes.name: wipe-a-table
recipes.goal: The table surface is clear of items, free of crumbs and residue, wiped clean, and left dry, ready for the next meal or task.

steps.action: **Clear the table completely.** Move dishes to the sink, papers and objects to a counter or tray. Wiping around objects leaves a ring of grime at every base.
steps.expect: fully bare surface; fragile items (glassware) carried one or two at a time, not stacked.

steps.action: **Do a dry crumb sweep first.** Cup one hand at the table edge and sweep crumbs into it with the other hand or a dry cloth, working toward the edge, or sweep into a plate held under the edge lip. Wetting crumbs first turns them into smeared paste.
steps.expect: loose debris off the surface and in the hand, plate, or bin, not on the floor or chairs.

steps.action: **Prepare the cloth: damp, not wet.** Rinse and wring the cloth until it does not drip when held flat. For greasy residue, add a drop of dish soap or an all-purpose spray. Smell the cloth first: a sour cloth spreads the smell onto the table.
steps.expect: clean-smelling cloth, damp to the touch, no drips.

steps.action: **Wipe in overlapping S-strokes from the far edge toward you.** Cover the whole surface in one directional pass so no strip is skipped; fold the cloth to a fresh face when a face loads up.
steps.expect: visible sheen of moisture behind the stroke; residue lifting onto the cloth faces.

steps.action: **Spot-treat stuck spills.** Lay the damp cloth over dried spots for 30 to 60 seconds to soften, then rub in small circles. Scrape stubborn spots with a fingernail or plastic scraper through the cloth, never a knife blade.
steps.expect: fingertip glides over the spot with no ridge.

steps.action: **Wipe the edges and the edge underside lip.** The rim where hands and plates rest is the grimiest zone and the most skipped.
steps.expect: cloth shows pickup from the rim; edge feels smooth, not tacky.

steps.action: **Do the dry pass.** Go over the whole surface with the dry cloth in the same S-pattern. On wood this is not optional: standing moisture clouds the finish; on glass and stone it prevents streaks.
steps.expect: surface fully dry within a few seconds, uniform matte or gloss with no swirl marks.

steps.action: **Finish and reset.** Rinse and hang the wet cloth to dry, return any items that live on the table.
steps.expect: cloth hung open (not balled up damp), table in its resting state.

recipes.verification: Sight across the surface at a low angle against a light source: no crumbs, streaks, or damp patches anywhere including the rim. A palm swept across the middle and edges comes away clean and dry with no tacky spots.

recipes.title: wipe a whiteboard
recipes.name: wipe-a-whiteboard
recipes.goal: The whiteboard writing surface is visibly clean and ready for new marker writing.

steps.action: **Grip the eraser flat.** Hold the eraser with the wiping face parallel to the board.
steps.expect: the eraser face covers the writing area without edge-only contact.

steps.action: **Start at the upper left.** Press lightly against the board and wipe horizontally across the top band.
steps.expect: marker residue fades along the wiped path.

steps.action: **Overlap the next pass.** Move the eraser down by half its height and wipe back in the opposite direction.
steps.expect: no unwiped stripe remains between passes.

steps.action: **Continue downward.** Repeat overlapping horizontal passes until the written area is covered.
steps.expect: only light haze or small edge marks remain.

steps.action: **Detail stubborn marks.** Use a clean corner of the cloth or eraser with small circular motions and moderate pressure.
steps.expect: the mark lightens without scratching the surface.

steps.action: **Clean the tray edge.** Wipe loose dust from the lower board tray toward a collected corner.
steps.expect: residue gathers in one removable line or pile.

steps.action: **Inspect from an angle.** Step or tilt view to catch reflected light across the board.
steps.expect: the surface appears uniformly clean with no readable writing.

recipes.verification: No readable marker strokes remain on the main writing surface when viewed straight on and at a shallow angle.

recipes.title: wring out a sponge
recipes.name: wring-out-a-sponge
recipes.goal: Excess water is removed from the sponge over the sink until it no longer drips under normal handling.

steps.action: **Move over the sink.** Hold the sponge fully above the basin, not over the counter or floor.
steps.expect: any water falls into the sink.

steps.action: **Set the grip.** Wrap fingers around the sponge with thumbs opposed.
steps.expect: sponge is enclosed but not yet compressed.

steps.action: **Squeeze evenly.** Press both hands inward until water streams out.
steps.expect: flow exits downward into the basin.

steps.action: **Release slightly.** Let the sponge expand while keeping it over the sink.
steps.expect: sponge rebounds and draws in air.

steps.action: **Repeat compression.** Squeeze again with firmer pressure.
steps.expect: water output drops from stream to drips.

steps.action: **Add twist if needed.** [BRANCH: soft sponge | stiff sponge] twist opposite ends gently only if it will not tear.
steps.expect: remaining water expresses from the center.

steps.action: **Check drip rate.** Hold the sponge still for two seconds.
steps.expect: no steady drip forms.

steps.action: **Place or reuse.** Set the sponge on its holder or return it to cleaning.
steps.expect: no puddle forms under it.

recipes.verification: The sponge can be held over the counter for two seconds without releasing a steady drip.

recipes.title: zip up a jacket
recipes.name: zip-up-a-jacket
recipes.goal: The jacket zipper is started cleanly, pulled straight to the desired height, and closed without fabric caught in the teeth.

steps.action: **Lower the slider fully.** Pull the tab down until the slider rests against the zipper box.
steps.expect: the box opening is exposed and stationary.

steps.action: **Align the zipper halves.** Bring the insertion pin side to the box side with both hems at the same height.
steps.expect: zipper tapes lie parallel.

steps.action: **Seat the insertion pin.** Push the pin straight down into the box until it bottoms out.
steps.expect: no gap remains between pin tip and box floor.

steps.action: **Hold the hem.** Pinch both lower hems together below the slider to keep the pin seated.
steps.expect: the bottom stays aligned when the tab is touched.

steps.action: **Pull straight up.** Draw the tab upward along the centerline with steady light force.
steps.expect: teeth interlock immediately above the slider.

steps.action: **Guide fabric away.** Keep loose lining, scarf edges, or shirt fabric outside the slider path.
steps.expect: slider moves without scraping or bunching.

steps.action: **Continue to height.** [BRANCH: full close | partial vent] stop at the planned position without yanking.
steps.expect: zipper track is closed below the slider.

steps.action: **Settle the front.** Smooth both sides downward and release the hem grip.
steps.expect: jacket front hangs flat with the slider staying in place.

recipes.verification: The zipper is closed from the box to the chosen height, the bottom remains joined, and the slider moves no fabric other than the zipper tape.

recipes.title: clean up a liquid spill
recipes.name: clean-up-a-liquid-spill
recipes.goal: A liquid spill on counter or floor is contained, fully absorbed, degreased if needed, and the surface is verified dry and safe to walk on.

steps.action: **Stop the source first.** Right the tipped container, close the tap, kill the burner under a boil-over. Cleaning while the source still flows is mopping a river.
steps.expect: nothing more is being added to the puddle.

steps.action: **Guard the zone.** Warn anyone nearby ("spill here, don't walk through"), and put a chair, the mop bucket, or a wet-floor sign at the puddle's edge if you must step away even briefly.
steps.expect: no foot traffic path crosses the wet area unannounced.

steps.action: **Dam the spread.** Lay towels around the puddle's leading edge, especially the side toward cabinets, appliance gaps, and rugs. Liquid that gets under an appliance or cabinet toe-kick is the part you can never reach.
steps.expect: puddle edge stopped; nothing advancing toward gaps.

steps.action: **Absorb from the edges inward.** Press towels flat onto the liquid and let them wick; lift straight up when saturated. Blot, do not wipe outward: wiping spreads the spill thinner and wider. [BRANCH: small spill → paper towels to the bin | large spill → wring rags into the sink or a bucket, repeat]
steps.expect: puddle shrinking toward its center; used towels binned or wrung, not left sitting in the liquid.

steps.action: **Degrease if the spill was oily, milky, or sugary.** Water alone leaves an invisible film that stays slippery (oil) or turns sticky and sour (milk, juice). Wipe the whole affected area with a sponge or cloth and warm water plus a drop of dish soap, then rinse-wipe with a clean damp cloth.
steps.expect: no rainbow sheen, no squeak-drag stickiness under a clean fingertip.

steps.action: **Dry the surface completely.** Go over the area with a dry towel until a final pass picks up no moisture.
steps.expect: dry towel comes away dry.

steps.action: **Verify with a hand and a shoe.** Press a flat palm on the counter area, or test the floor patch with a shoe-sole twist. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* slip-and-fall injuries are the whole reason this step exists; a floor that merely looks dry is the trap, thin water films are near invisible on smooth flooring.
steps.expect: no moisture on the palm; sole grips without any glide.

steps.action: **Reset.** Bin the disposables, laundry-bin the rags (a milk rag left in the sink smells by evening), rinse the mop, remove the warning marker.
steps.expect: zone open again; no sour-smelling cloths left anywhere.

recipes.verification: Palm test and sole-twist test both pass on the affected area, no sheen or stickiness remains, no liquid sits in any adjacent gap or under any appliance edge, used absorbents are binned or in the laundry, and the warning marker is removed only after the tests pass.

recipes.title: clip a chip bag closed
recipes.name: clip-a-chip-bag-closed
recipes.goal: The chip bag opening is folded and clipped closed to reduce air exposure and spilling.

steps.action: **Stand the bag upright.** Hold both upper corners and settle chips below the opening.
steps.expect: loose chips drop away from the top edge.

steps.action: **Flatten the top air pocket.** Press the front and back panels together above the chips with light palm pressure.
steps.expect: the upper bag is flat and free of trapped chips.

steps.action: **Fold the top edge down.** Make a straight fold 2-4 cm below the opening.
steps.expect: the open edge is hidden inside the fold.

steps.action: **Add one more fold.** Roll or fold downward once more while keeping side edges aligned.
steps.expect: the folded band is firm and even.

steps.action: **Open the clip.** Squeeze the clip handles until the jaws separate wider than the folded band.
steps.expect: the clip jaws are fully open.

steps.action: **Place clip across the fold.** Center the clip over the folded band and release slowly.
steps.expect: the jaws clamp both layers across most of the bag width.

steps.action: **Test the seal.** Lift the bag by the body and tilt it slightly side to side.
steps.expect: the fold stays closed and no chips spill.

recipes.verification: The bag remains closed when tilted gently, with the clip centered over a folded band and no chips caught in the seal.

recipes.title: close a jar lid
recipes.name: close-a-jar-lid
recipes.goal: A jar lid is seated on matching threads, tightened until snug, and checked for a usable seal without cracking the jar or deforming the lid.

steps.action: **Place the jar upright.** Set the jar on a flat counter with the opening facing straight up.
steps.expect: the jar stands stable and does not rock.

steps.action: **Inspect the rim and lid.** Check the glass rim, lid threads, and gasket area for chips, crumbs, or residue.
steps.expect: the contact surfaces look clean and continuous.

steps.action: **Position the lid level.** Set the lid on the jar mouth without turning yet, centered and flat.
steps.expect: the lid rests evenly, not tipped to one side.

steps.action: **Find the thread start.** Turn the lid slightly counterclockwise until it drops or clicks into the thread start.
steps.expect: the lid sits lower and no longer skates across the rim.

steps.action: **Tighten clockwise.** Rotate the lid clockwise with light downward pressure, keeping it level.
steps.expect: the lid advances smoothly with no scraping or jump.

steps.action: **Stop at snug.** Tighten until resistance increases, then stop without forcing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* excess torque can crack fragile glass or deform the lid; confirm the lid is aligned before adding force.
steps.expect: the lid is secure and the jar is undamaged.

steps.action: **Check the seal.** Hold the jar upright and gently try to wiggle the lid without loosening it.
steps.expect: the lid does not wobble or lift.

steps.action: **Store upright.** Place the jar where it will not be knocked over.
steps.expect: the jar remains closed and stable.

recipes.verification: The lid is level, snug, not forced, and stays attached when the upright jar is gently wiggled by the lid.

recipes.title: crack an egg
recipes.name: crack-an-egg
recipes.goal: The egg's contents are in the bowl with the yolk intact (unless scrambling), zero shell fragments in the food, and the shell halves discarded.

steps.action: **Grasp the egg across its equator.** Fingers curled around the middle, firm enough not to drop it, loose enough not to dent it.
steps.expect: egg held securely without any shell flexing.

steps.action: **Tap the equator once against the flat counter, not the bowl's rim.** One confident medium tap; a rim's edge drives shell shards inward, while a flat surface makes a clean dent with the membrane intact behind it.
steps.expect: a single visible crack line or flattened dent at the equator, nothing leaking yet.

steps.action: **Assess the crack.** [BRANCH: clean crack across the equator → proceed | barely a mark → one slightly firmer tap in the same spot | crushed/wet patch → F2]
steps.expect: a crack you could split along, dry outer shell.

steps.action: **Split with two thumbs at the crack, low over the bowl.** Hold the egg horizontally an inch or two above the bowl, place both thumb tips into the dent, and pull the halves apart with a slight outward-and-down motion. Height matters: a high drop bursts the yolk.
steps.expect: contents slide out in one mass; yolk lands whole; two shell halves in your hands.

steps.action: **Drain the halves and inspect the bowl.** Let clinging white drip in for a second or two, then look for shell fragments and check the contents look and smell normal.
steps.expect: clear white, domed unbroken yolk, no gray-green tint, no sulfur smell, no visible shell bits.

steps.action: **Rescue any shell fragment immediately, before stirring.** Use one emptied half-shell as the scoop: its edge cuts through the white and the fragment clings to shell far better than to fingers or a spoon. A wetted fingertip also works for tiny flecks.
steps.expect: fragment out on the first or second scoop; bowl contents shell-free.

steps.action: **Discard shells away from the food path.** Halves into the compost or trash, not left dripping on the counter; wipe any drips now, since dried egg cements itself to surfaces. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* raw egg contact contaminates hands and surfaces; wash hands before touching anything else.
steps.expect: counter clean, shells gone, hands washed.

recipes.verification: The bowl holds the intended egg contents with an intact yolk (unless scrambling was the goal), a fragment check of the bowl comes up empty, shells are discarded, and the counter and hands are clean of raw egg.

recipes.title: dispense tape from a roll
recipes.name: dispense-tape-from-a-roll
recipes.goal: A controlled strip of tape is pulled, torn on the serrated edge, applied without folding onto itself, and the tape end remains findable.

steps.action: **Find the tape end.** Rotate the roll slowly and feel for the raised edge with a thumb pad or fingernail.
steps.expect: a small tab lifts from the roll.

steps.action: **Peel a starter tab.** Pinch the lifted edge between thumb and index finger and pull it free by a few centimeters.
steps.expect: tape separates as a flat ribbon, sticky side down.

steps.action: **Anchor the dispenser.** Hold the dispenser body or roll core with the opposite hand so only the roll turns.
steps.expect: dispenser stays in place under pulling force.

steps.action: **Pull the desired length.** Draw the tape straight out with steady tension, keeping the strip away from itself and the counter.
steps.expect: strip remains flat and does not twist.

steps.action: **Set against the serrated edge.** Angle the tape downward over the cutter with the planned cut line touching the teeth.
steps.expect: tape stretches tight across the full cutter width.

steps.action: **Tear with a snap.** Pull down and slightly forward in one short motion while keeping the dispenser anchored.
steps.expect: tape separates cleanly at the teeth.

steps.action: **Apply from one end.** Place one end on the target, then smooth along the strip with a fingertip using light pressure.
steps.expect: tape lies flat with no bubbles or folded sticky spots.

steps.action: **Stick the tab back.** Press the remaining tape end to the dispenser lip or fold a tiny nonsticky handle at the end.
steps.expect: next-use tab is visible and can be pinched.

recipes.verification: The tape strip is adhered flat to the intended surface and the remaining roll has a reachable tab on or near the dispenser edge.

recipes.title: drain a pot into a colander
recipes.name: drain-a-pot-into-a-colander
recipes.goal: Hot water is drained from a pot through a colander while food is retained and steam exposure is controlled.

steps.action: **Seat the colander.** Place the colander in the sink with feet down and handles clear of the pouring path.
steps.expect: the colander is stable and centered over the drain.

steps.action: **Clear the approach.** Remove dishes, soap bottles, and loose tools between stove and sink.
steps.expect: the carry path is open and dry.

steps.action: **Grip the hot pot.** Use dry potholders on both handles and keep wrists straight.
steps.expect: hands are insulated and the pot lifts level.

steps.action: **Move to the sink.** Carry the pot close to the body, then position its far rim over the colander.
steps.expect: the pot is above the colander with the pour direction away from the face.

steps.action: **Tilt away from face.** Rotate the pot slowly so water exits the far side first. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* steam burns can occur instantly, so keep face and forearms out of the plume.
steps.expect: hot water flows into the colander and steam rises away.

steps.action: **Control the last pour.** Lower the tilt angle as food reaches the rim, using the pot lip to hold solids back if needed.
steps.expect: water drains while food lands in or stays above the colander.

steps.action: **Shake to drain.** Set the pot down if empty, then lift the colander handles and shake gently up and down over the sink.
steps.expect: water droplets fall through and food remains contained.

steps.action: **Set safely.** Place the drained food or colander on a heat-safe surface.
steps.expect: the sink holds the drained water and all hot items are stable.

recipes.verification: Most water has passed through the colander, food remains contained, and the hot pot and colander are stable with no active steam exposure to the face.

recipes.title: fill a pot with water
recipes.name: fill-a-pot-with-water
recipes.goal: A pot is filled with the requested amount of water and carried without sloshing or strain.

steps.action: **Inspect the pot.** Check that the pot has no residue, loose handle, or obstruction inside.
steps.expect: the interior is clean and both handles are usable.

steps.action: **Place under the tap.** Set the pot flat in the sink with the faucet aimed near the center of the base.
steps.expect: the pot is stable and the stream will not hit the rim.

steps.action: **Start water gently.** Open the cold tap partway to avoid splashing from the empty base.
steps.expect: water enters the pot with limited splash.

steps.action: **Fill to target.** Watch the water level rise to the recipe amount, marked line, or no more than two-thirds full for carrying.
steps.expect: water stops below the safe carry line.

steps.action: **Shut off fully.** Close the tap before lifting the pot.
steps.expect: the stream stops and no new water enters the pot.

steps.action: **Test weight.** Grip both handles and lift one centimeter to assess load.
steps.expect: the pot feels controllable and level.

steps.action: **Carry with two hands.** Hold the pot close to the torso, elbows bent, and keep the rim level while moving.
steps.expect: the water surface stays below the rim without sloshing over.

steps.action: **Set down level.** Lower the pot onto the target burner or counter before releasing either handle.
steps.expect: the pot base contacts the surface evenly and the water settles.

recipes.verification: The pot contains the intended amount of water, remains below a safe carry line, and is placed level at the destination with no active spill.

recipes.title: fill an ice cube tray
recipes.name: fill-an-ice-cube-tray
recipes.goal: Fill an ice cube tray with water and place it level in the freezer without spilling into the freezer or onto the floor.

steps.action: **Inspect the tray.** Hold it level and check each cube pocket for dirt, old ice, or cracks.
steps.expect: all pockets are empty, clean, and able to hold water.

steps.action: **Position under water source.** Set the tray on the sink base or counter under the faucet, or hold a pitcher above one corner.
steps.expect: the tray is level and supported.

steps.action: **Fill slowly across pockets.** Run a thin stream and move it from pocket to pocket until each is nearly full.
steps.expect: water reaches just below the top edge of each pocket.

steps.action: **Correct the level.** Pour off excess from overfilled pockets or add water to low pockets.
steps.expect: no water sheet connects across the tray top.

steps.action: **Carry with two-hand support.** Hold both short ends level and move at low speed toward the freezer.
steps.expect: water surfaces stay inside the pockets.

steps.action: **Place flat in the freezer.** Slide the tray onto a level shelf without tilting it upward at the back.
steps.expect: the tray rests flat and water remains in the pockets.

recipes.verification: The tray is in the freezer on a flat surface, each pocket contains water below the rim, and no standing water remains on the floor or freezer shelf.

recipes.title: fill and run a kettle
recipes.name: fill-and-run-a-kettle
recipes.goal: The kettle is filled to a safe level, boiled, and has clicked itself off automatically, with hot water ready to pour and no water on the electrical base.

steps.action: **Inspect kettle and base.** Look into the kettle: no standing stale water, no loose scale flakes; base contacts dry.
steps.expect: clean interior, dry base plate, switch in the off position.

steps.action: **Lift the kettle off the base before filling.** Never fill it while seated: drips reach the electrical contacts.
steps.expect: kettle free in hand, base stays put on the counter.

steps.action: **Fill at the tap between the MIN and MAX lines.** Below MIN risks dry-boiling the element; above MAX makes the spout spit boiling water at the boil. Fill only what you need: a mug's worth boils in half the time of a full kettle.
steps.expect: water level visibly between the two marks on the gauge window.

steps.action: **Close the lid until it clicks and dry the outside.** A latched lid matters twice: it keeps steam on the auto-off sensor, and it keeps the lid shut during the pour. Wipe drips off the body and especially the underside.
steps.expect: lid latched, exterior and underside dry to the touch.

steps.action: **Seat the kettle on the base.** Lower it on and rotate slightly until it drops fully home; most bases are 360-degree so orientation is free.
steps.expect: kettle sits flush and does not rock; on some models a standby light appears.

steps.action: **Press the switch on.**
steps.expect: switch latches down and the indicator light comes on; heating hiss starts within about 30 seconds. No latch or no light → F1.

steps.action: **Wait nearby for the automatic click-off.** Sound builds from hiss to rumble, then quietens just before the boil.
steps.expect: the switch flips off by itself with an audible click and the light goes out, typically 2 to 5 minutes. Steaming hard with no click → F2.

steps.action: **Verify off, then pour.** Confirm the light is out before touching the handle. Bring the mug next to the kettle and pour slowly with the spout low. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* scald risk: steam exits the spout ahead of the water, so keep your holding hand behind the handle and never pour toward yourself.
steps.expect: mug filled without splash, kettle returned to the base, lid still shut.

recipes.verification: The switch has returned to off on its own (auto-off confirmed this run), the water gauge shows the expected drop after pouring, the base and counter are dry, and the kettle rests seated on its base with the lid latched.

recipes.title: flip food with a spatula
recipes.name: flip-food-with-a-spatula
recipes.goal: A piece of food is turned over in a pan using a spatula while keeping it intact and inside the pan.

steps.action: **Stabilize the pan.** Hold or brace the pan handle so the cooking surface does not slide.
steps.expect: the pan resists light spatula pressure.

steps.action: **Choose the entry edge.** Identify the thinnest or loosest food edge and approach from a low angle.
steps.expect: the spatula tip can touch under the edge without pushing the food away.

steps.action: **Slide under.** Push the spatula forward with shallow pressure, keeping the blade nearly parallel to the pan.
steps.expect: at least half the food is supported on the spatula.

steps.action: **Release stuck spots.** Wiggle or scrape with short strokes rather than prying upward.
steps.expect: the food separates without tearing.

steps.action: **Lift low.** Raise the spatula only a few centimeters above the pan.
steps.expect: the food stays balanced and close to the landing surface.

steps.action: **Commit the flip.** Rotate the wrist in one smooth motion toward the empty landing area.
steps.expect: the food turns over once without pausing on edge.

steps.action: **Catch and settle.** Lower the spatula as the food lands, then slide it out from underneath.
steps.expect: the food rests flat on its second side.

steps.action: **Correct placement.** [BRANCH: centered | near rim] Leave it if centered; nudge it inward if near the rim.
steps.expect: the food is fully inside the pan and away from the edge.

recipes.verification: The food is turned onto its opposite side, remains in the pan, and is stable enough to continue cooking without immediate correction.

recipes.title: get an item from the fridge
recipes.name: get-an-item-from-the-fridge
recipes.goal: The requested item is retrieved from the refrigerator and the door is closed promptly.

steps.action: **Approach and check clearance.** Stand beside the door swing path with feet stable.
steps.expect: the door can open without hitting body, cabinets, or people.

steps.action: **Open the door.** Pull the handle smoothly until shelves are visible, keeping the door under control.
steps.expect: interior light turns on and cold shelves are accessible.

steps.action: **Locate the item.** Scan shelves from top to bottom, then door bins, using label, shape, or parent-task cue.
steps.expect: the target item or a likely candidate is visible.

steps.action: **Clear access.** Move blocking items only as far as needed and keep them upright.
steps.expect: a direct hand path reaches the target.

steps.action: **Grasp securely.** Hold jars and bottles around the body, cartons at the sides, and open containers from below.
steps.expect: the item lifts without slipping or tilting.

steps.action: **Withdraw level.** Pull the item straight out, clearing shelf lips and nearby containers.
steps.expect: no neighboring item falls or drags forward.

steps.action: **Close the door.** Push the door shut with hand or hip after the item is clear.
steps.expect: gasket contacts the frame and interior light turns off.

steps.action: **Set or deliver.** Place the cold item on the counter or carry it level to the next task.
steps.expect: the item rests upright and condensation or cold surface is manageable.

recipes.verification: The requested item is outside the fridge, upright and under control, and the refrigerator door is fully closed.

recipes.title: grate on a box grater
recipes.name: grate-on-a-box-grater
recipes.goal: Reduce a firm food item into shreds using a box grater while keeping fingers clear of the cutting surface.

steps.action: **Set the grater upright.** Place the wide base flat on a board or inside a shallow bowl with the chosen grating face outward.
steps.expect: the grater stands vertical and does not rock.

steps.action: **Grip the handle and food.** Hold the grater handle from above and hold the food with fingertips curled away from the grating face.
steps.expect: both the grater and food are controlled before contact.

steps.action: **Start with light downward strokes.** Press the food against the upper part of the face and slide down in one straight motion.
steps.expect: shreds appear on the inside or below the grater.

steps.action: **Repeat with consistent pressure.** Lift the food off the teeth before moving it back upward, then grate downward again.
steps.expect: the food shortens gradually and the grater remains planted.

steps.action: **Stop before the unsafe nub.** When less than about 2 cm of food remains between fingers and teeth, stop grating.
steps.expect: fingers never cross the plane of the grater teeth.

steps.action: **Collect the shreds.** Lift the grater vertically, tap lightly over the bowl, and scrape loose shreds from the safe outside edges.
steps.expect: grated food is gathered and the sharp face is clear of hands.

recipes.verification: The requested amount of food is shredded into the collection area, the grater stayed stable, and no finger or gripper contacted the cutting teeth.

recipes.title: grease a baking pan
recipes.name: grease-a-baking-pan
recipes.goal: Coat a baking pan so batter or dough releases cleanly after baking, with corners, edges, and optional parchment handled correctly.

steps.action: **Read the recipe instruction.** Check whether it says grease, grease and flour, line with parchment, or leave ungreased.
steps.expect: the pan treatment matches the recipe.

steps.action: **Inspect the pan.** Remove crumbs, water, labels, or old oil.
steps.expect: the inside surface is clean and dry.

steps.action: **Choose the fat.** [BRANCH: butter | oil | spray] use softened butter for flavor, oil for neutral coating, or spray for speed.
steps.expect: the fat can cover the pan in a thin film.

steps.action: **Coat the bottom.** Rub or spray across the flat base from center to corners.
steps.expect: the bottom has a continuous shine with no dry patches.

steps.action: **Coat corners and edges.** Push fat into seams, corners, and up the sides to the expected batter height.
steps.expect: corner lines look glossy, not pale.

steps.action: **Remove puddles.** Wipe extra oil or thick butter lumps with a paper towel.
steps.expect: the coating is thin and even.

steps.action: **Dust with flour if needed.** Add a spoonful of flour, tilt and tap until it clings to all greased surfaces.
steps.expect: a light powder film covers bottom and sides.

steps.action: **Tap out excess.** Turn the pan over the sink or trash and tap gently.
steps.expect: loose flour falls out and no thick patches remain.

steps.action: **Add parchment option.** For cakes or bars, press parchment onto the greased bottom, leaving handles if useful.
steps.expect: parchment lies flat and sticks lightly.

steps.action: **Final check before batter.** Look along the corners and side walls.
steps.expect: every surface the batter touches is greased, lined, or deliberately bare.

recipes.verification: The pan has a continuous thin release layer on all recipe-specified surfaces, with optional flour or parchment evenly applied and no loose piles.

recipes.title: hang a mug on a rack
recipes.name: hang-a-mug-on-a-rack
recipes.goal: A mug is suspended by its handle on a rack hook without touching neighboring mugs.

steps.action: **Inspect the hook.** Confirm the hook is clear and points upward or outward enough to retain the handle.
steps.expect: the hook has open space at its tip.

steps.action: **Grasp the mug body.** Hold the mug around the side wall with the handle exposed.
steps.expect: the mug is stable and the handle opening is visible.

steps.action: **Orient the handle to the hook.** Rotate the mug so the handle loop is coaxial with the hook tip.
steps.expect: the hook can pass through the handle opening without hitting the rim.

steps.action: **Lift to hook height.** Raise the mug slowly until the lower edge of the handle is just above the hook tip.
steps.expect: the handle clears the hook by a small margin.

steps.action: **Slide handle onto hook.** Move the mug inward until the hook enters the handle loop, then lower gently.
steps.expect: the handle settles onto the hook and carries the mug weight.

steps.action: **Release gradually.** Reduce grip force while keeping a hand near the mug for one second.
steps.expect: the mug remains hanging and does not swing into neighbors.

steps.action: **Check spacing.** Observe the mug from front and side.
steps.expect: the mug hangs vertical with no contact against adjacent mugs or wall.

recipes.verification: The mug remains suspended by the handle for 5 seconds, hangs vertical, and has clearance from neighboring objects.

recipes.title: knock crumbs into the bin
recipes.name: knock-crumbs-into-the-bin
recipes.goal: Move loose crumbs from a plate, board, or counter into the correct bin without scattering them onto the floor.

steps.action: **Choose the bin.** [BRANCH: trash | compost] use compost for accepted food scraps and trash for contaminated or non-compostable crumbs.
steps.expect: the correct bin is open before lifting crumbs.

steps.action: **Lift the crumb surface.** Grasp the plate or board level with two stable contact points.
steps.expect: crumbs remain on the surface during the lift.

steps.action: **Move over the bin opening.** Hold the crumb side fully inside the bin perimeter.
steps.expect: falling crumbs would land inside the bin.

steps.action: **Tilt and tap.** Angle the surface downward and tap the far edge lightly with a hand or brush.
steps.expect: crumbs slide or fall into the bin.

steps.action: **Sweep remaining crumbs.** Use a brush, paper towel, or hand edge to push stuck crumbs toward the lowered side.
steps.expect: only tiny residue remains on the surface.

steps.action: **Return and inspect.** Bring the plate or board back level before moving away from the bin.
steps.expect: no visible crumb trail appears between bin and counter.

recipes.verification: The original surface has no loose crumbs, the crumbs are inside the correct bin, and the floor around the bin is clean.

recipes.title: ladle soup into a bowl
recipes.name: ladle-soup-into-a-bowl
recipes.goal: Transfer hot soup from a pot into a bowl using a ladle without splashing or overfilling.

steps.action: **Set the bowl near the pot.** Place it on a flat surface within one short ladle travel distance.
steps.expect: the bowl does not wobble and its opening is unobstructed.

steps.action: **Grip the ladle handle.** Hold near the end with the bowl of the ladle hanging level.
steps.expect: the ladle can rotate without hitting the pot rim.

steps.action: **Dip below the soup surface.** Lower the ladle bowl-first and draw it toward the center of the pot.
steps.expect: the ladle fills without scraping the pot hard.

steps.action: **Lift and pause over the pot.** Raise the ladle just above the soup and let excess drip back for one second.
steps.expect: the outside of the ladle is not streaming liquid.

steps.action: **Move over the serving bowl.** Keep the ladle level and low while crossing the gap.
steps.expect: the soup remains inside the ladle.

steps.action: **Pour against the bowl interior.** Tilt the ladle so soup runs down the inner side of the bowl, repeating until filled below the rim.
steps.expect: soup sits at least 2 cm below the bowl rim with no splash outside.

recipes.verification: The bowl contains soup below carry height, the pot remains stable, and no hot liquid is on the counter, floor, or outside of the bowl.

recipes.title: load a dishwasher
recipes.name: load-a-dishwasher
recipes.goal: All dirty dishes from the sink/counter are loaded into the dishwasher, detergent is dosed, and a wash cycle is running.

steps.action: **Open the dishwasher door fully and slide out the bottom rack.**
steps.expect: door rests horizontal; bottom rack glides out without obstruction.

steps.action: **Scrape food solids off each dish into the trash/compost.** No pre-rinsing needed beyond solids.
steps.expect: no bones, pits, or food chunks remain on any item.

steps.action: **Load the bottom rack, then spin the lower spray arm one full turn by hand.** Plates vertical in the tines, faces toward the center; pots and pans face-down at the sides/back. Nothing blocks the detergent dispenser's swing path or the spray arm's rotation.
steps.expect: the arm completes a full rotation without touching any item.

steps.action: **Slide out the top rack and load cups, glasses, and bowls face-down at an angle.** Glasses between tines, not over them; fragile glasses not touching each other.
steps.expect: no item rocks when the rack is jiggled; no two glasses in contact.

steps.action: **Load cutlery into the basket, handles down, except sharp knives: handles up** (or flat in a dedicated top tray). ⚠️ *Safety:* blade-up knives are a laceration hazard to whoever unloads; always handles-up for blades.
steps.expect: cutlery loosely mixed (not nested); knife blades all pointing down or lying flat.

steps.action: **Slide both racks in and check clearance.**
steps.expect: racks seat fully; tall items don't block the upper spray arm.

steps.action: **Open the detergent dispenser, insert one pod (or fill powder to the line), and snap it shut.**
steps.expect: dispenser clicks closed with the pod inside.

steps.action: **Close the door until it latches and select the normal cycle; press start.**
steps.expect: latch clicks; cycle indicator lights; water-fill sound begins within ~1 min. If a human opens the door area, pause motion until clear.

recipes.verification: Door latched, cycle running (indicator on, water audible), sink/counter clear of dishwasher-safe dirty dishes, hand-wash items staged separately, and no knife loaded blade-up.

recipes.title: make drip coffee
recipes.name: make-drip-coffee
recipes.goal: A carafe of brewed coffee sits on the coffee maker's warming plate, and one mug is filled and delivered to the counter.

steps.action: **Open the water reservoir lid and fill with water.** Pour to the marked line for the target number of cups (e.g., the "4" line for 4 cups).
steps.expect: water level gauge reads at the target line; no overflow.

steps.action: **Open the filter basket and insert a filter paper.** Splay the paper so it sits flush against the basket walls.
steps.expect: filter paper conforms to the basket; no folded-over edges.

steps.action: **Scoop ground coffee into the filter.** One level scoop (~7 g) per cup of water.
steps.expect: grounds sit level in the filter; basket closes without resistance.

steps.action: **Confirm the carafe is seated on the warming plate, lid aligned under the drip outlet.**
steps.expect: carafe clicks/rests fully back; anti-drip valve is engaged by the lid.

steps.action: **Press the brew button.**
steps.expect: indicator light turns on; within ~60 s, gurgling begins and coffee drips into the carafe. If nothing after 90 s, F1.

steps.action: **Wait for the brew cycle to finish.** Do not remove the carafe mid-brew unless the machine's pause-and-serve is confirmed.
steps.expect: dripping stops; the machine sputters, then quiets; carafe level matches the water volume from step 1.

steps.action: **Pour one mug.** Grasp the carafe handle, pour slowly into the mug to ~2 cm below the rim, return the carafe to the warming plate. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* hot-liquid spill — pour over the counter, never over the floor or near a person; pause pouring if a human enters arm's reach.
steps.expect: mug filled to target level; no spill on the counter.

steps.action: **Deliver the mug to the designated counter position.** Carry level, at slow speed.
steps.expect: mug at rest at the target position, contents not spilled.

recipes.verification: Carafe on the warming plate contains brewed coffee (level ≈ water volume minus one mug), the filled mug rests at the delivery position, warming plate area is dry, and the machine's indicator shows brew complete/keep-warm.

recipes.title: make toast
recipes.name: make-toast
recipes.goal: Bread is toasted to the target brownness, retrieved without burns, and (optionally) buttered and delivered on a plate.

steps.action: **Inspect the toaster.** Empty slots (no stuck remnants), lever up, dial legible.
steps.expect: clear slots; browning dial at a known setting (3 of 6 is the sane default on an unfamiliar machine).

steps.action: **Insert the bread.** One slice per slot, dropped vertically, not forced.
steps.expect: slices seated below the slot rim, standing free.

steps.action: **Set browning and start.** Dial to target (first run on any toaster: middle, then calibrate); press the lever fully down.
steps.expect: lever latches, elements glow orange within seconds. Lever won't latch → F1.

steps.action: **Stay in the room while it runs.** Toasters are a leading small-appliance fire source precisely because they're "quick".
steps.expect: ~1–3 minutes of glowing, then a pop.

steps.action: **Retrieve at the pop.** Slices usually present above the rim — grasp the *top corners* of the bread. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* burns — the slot rims and the bread's lower half are hot; **never insert a knife or any metal into the slots**, even "just to help it out". Shy slices: use the lever's lift boost, or unplug first if fingers must go anywhere near.
steps.expect: toast on the plate, fingers intact.

steps.action: **Assess brownness against target.** [BRANCH: pale → one short second round, watched, dial slightly lower than you think | on target → proceed]
steps.expect: the color you wanted; the second-round trap (going from pale to charcoal) avoided by watching.

steps.action: **Butter while hot, if buttering.** Thin shavings of butter spread edge-to-edge with the knife — hot toast melts it in; toppings after.
steps.expect: even melt, toast on the plate, knife to the sink.

steps.action: **After-cool housekeeping (periodically, not every run):** empty the crumb tray once cool — crumbs are the fuel of F3.
steps.expect: tray emptied and reseated on maintenance runs.

recipes.verification: Toast at the target brownness is on the plate (buttered if intended), the toaster is off/idle with nothing left inside, no metal ever entered a slot, and no burn on the hands that made it.

recipes.title: mash with a fork
recipes.name: mash-with-a-fork
recipes.goal: Soft food is mashed with a fork to the target texture while the bowl stays stable.

steps.action: **Stabilize the bowl.** Hold the rim with the support hand or set it on a damp towel.
steps.expect: the bowl does not slide under a test push.

steps.action: **Grip the fork.** Hold the handle with tines angled downward and wrist aligned over the food.
steps.expect: fork tines contact the food squarely.

steps.action: **Press down.** Push the tines into one piece of food with steady vertical pressure.
steps.expect: the food flattens or splits under the fork.

steps.action: **Drag through.** Pull the fork toward the near side while maintaining light downward force.
steps.expect: mashed food spreads into a rough paste or smaller pieces.

steps.action: **Rotate the bowl.** Turn the bowl a quarter turn or move to an unmashed section.
steps.expect: whole pieces are presented under the fork.

steps.action: **Repeat in passes.** Press and drag across the full surface, reducing force as pieces become smaller.
steps.expect: texture becomes more uniform with each pass.

steps.action: **Check texture.** [BRANCH: chunky target | smooth target] Stop when chunks match target; continue shorter strokes for smoother texture.
steps.expect: visible texture matches the parent recipe.

steps.action: **Scrape and gather.** Use the fork side to pull mash from the bowl wall back to the center.
steps.expect: mash is consolidated and ready for seasoning or serving.

recipes.verification: The food is mashed to the target chunk size or smoothness, gathered in the bowl, and the bowl remains stable and intact.

recipes.title: measure ingredients
recipes.name: measure-ingredients
recipes.goal: Measure dry, liquid, and weighed ingredients accurately enough for cooking or baking, then transfer them without spills or cross-contamination.

steps.action: **Identify the measurement type.** [BRANCH: dry volume | liquid volume | weight] match the tool to the recipe unit.
steps.expect: cup, spoon, liquid cup, or scale is selected before opening ingredients.

steps.action: **Stage the receiving bowl.** Place the bowl close to the measuring area.
steps.expect: measured ingredients travel only a short distance.

steps.action: **Use dry cups for dry volume.** Scoop flour, sugar, grains, or similar dry ingredients into the exact cup.
steps.expect: ingredient mounds slightly above the rim.

steps.action: **Level dry ingredients.** Sweep a straight edge across the rim without compacting unless instructed.
steps.expect: the surface is flat and flush with the cup edge.

steps.action: **Pack brown sugar when asked.** Press brown sugar firmly into the cup, then level it.
steps.expect: sugar holds the cup shape when tipped out.

steps.action: **Use liquid cups for liquids.** Set the cup on the counter and pour to the mark.
steps.expect: the meniscus sits at the target line when viewed at eye level.

steps.action: **Use spoons for small amounts.** Fill the spoon over the ingredient container or a scrap bowl, then level if dry.
steps.expect: the spoon is full to the rim, not heaped unless specified.

steps.action: **Weigh for baking precision.** Put the bowl on the scale, press tare, then add ingredient to the target grams.
steps.expect: scale reads the recipe weight with the container excluded.

steps.action: **Transfer cleanly.** Tip the measured ingredient into the mixing bowl and tap gently if needed.
steps.expect: nearly all measured material lands in the bowl.

steps.action: **Separate wet and dry tools.** Keep wet spoons out of dry containers unless the recipe is finished with them.
steps.expect: containers remain dry and unclumped.

recipes.verification: Each ingredient amount matches the recipe unit using the appropriate tool, and measured ingredients are in the bowl without visible spills or contaminated containers.

recipes.title: microwave a frozen meal
recipes.name: microwave-a-frozen-meal
recipes.goal: A packaged frozen meal is microwaved per its own instructions, actually hot in the center, and served without a steam burn, the task that looks trivial and stalls robots and teenagers alike on the package-reading step.

steps.action: **Read the package's microwave panel first, fully.** Wattage rows, piercing or lid instructions, the mid-cook stir, and the stand time. The instructions differ meaningfully per meal; the guess-and-nuke path produces lava edges around an ice core.
steps.expect: the times for your oven's wattage known (the wattage is on the microwave's door sticker or inside frame).

steps.action: **Prepare the package as instructed.** Typically: remove the outer sleeve, pierce the film lid several times (or peel a corner), leave the tray on. Metal-crisping sleeves stay in only when the panel explicitly says so.
steps.expect: film vented or peeled per the panel; no unvetted metal.

steps.action: **Center the tray and run the first heating stage.** Set the panel's first time; start.
steps.expect: rotation, rising steam through the vents; sauce bubbling at the edges by the stage's end.

steps.action: **Do the mid-cook stir or rotate, exactly as told.** ⚠️ hot film and escaping steam: peel away from your face and fingers (the `daily/food/use-a-microwave` steam rule at its sharpest). Stir from the edges inward for stirrable meals; rotate or re-cover the rest.
steps.expect: frozen center broken up and redistributed; film handled without a scald.

steps.action: **Run the second stage and the stand time.** The stand minutes on the panel are cooking, not waiting: the heat equalizes into the center then.
steps.expect: full time run, then the tray resting untouched for its stated stand.

steps.action: **Verify steaming-hot-throughout before serving.** Stir once more and check the center: visibly steaming, uncomfortably hot to a testing bite. Lukewarm centers in meat, rice, or fish meals re-run in 30-second bursts (`daily/food/use-a-microwave` step 7's standard; `daily/food/cook-rice`'s reheat rules agree).
steps.expect: steam from the center, not just the edges.

steps.action: **Serve with tray physics respected.** The tray is floppy and hot: carry on a plate, peel film fully away from yourself, and the tray recycles per its symbol once cool (`daily/home/sort-recycling`).
steps.expect: meal plated or eaten from the tray on a plate, no dropped-tray floor sauce.

recipes.verification: The panel's stages, stir, and stand were followed for your wattage, the center passes the steaming test, the film never met your face, and the tray traveled on a plate.

recipes.title: nest mixing bowls
recipes.name: nest-mixing-bowls
recipes.goal: Mixing bowls are nested largest-to-smallest in a compact, stable stack.

steps.action: **Sort bowls by size.** Place bowls in a row from largest rim diameter to smallest.
steps.expect: each bowl is visible and no bowl is hidden inside another.

steps.action: **Place the largest bowl.** Grasp both sides near the rim, keep the opening upward, and lower it onto the target surface.
steps.expect: the largest bowl sits flat and centered.

steps.action: **Lift the next smaller bowl.** Use two opposing side grasps and keep fingers clear of the lower rim.
steps.expect: the bowl is level with its open side facing upward.

steps.action: **Center it above the lower bowl.** Align the bowl axes and keep the rims parallel.
steps.expect: the lower bowl rim appears evenly around the lifted bowl.

steps.action: **Nest with light downward force.** Lower until the smaller bowl contacts the inside of the larger bowl and stops moving.
steps.expect: the smaller bowl rests inside without rocking.

steps.action: **Continue smallest last.** Repeat the same centered lowering for each remaining bowl.
steps.expect: each added bowl sits below the rim height of the bowl beneath it when possible.

steps.action: **Final stability check.** Release both hands and observe the nested set from the side.
steps.expect: the stack is compact, level, and does not tip.

recipes.verification: The nested bowls remain upright and compact after release, with the largest bowl on the bottom and no rim carrying an off-center load.

recipes.title: open a blister pack
recipes.name: open-a-blister-pack
recipes.goal: One pill or item is removed from the blister pack intact, caught on a clean surface or in a hand, and the remaining blisters stay sealed.

steps.action: **Select one cell.** Hold the pack flat and isolate the blister containing the intended pill.
steps.expect: the chosen dome is centered and adjacent doses remain untouched.

steps.action: **Inspect the backing.** Look for a peel tab, perforation, paper layer, or plain foil backing.
steps.expect: the opening method is visible.

steps.action: **Prepare to catch.** Cup one hand or place the pack over a clean tray, palm, or small dish.
steps.expect: there is a target directly below the pill path.

steps.action: **Peel from the corner if present.** [BRANCH: peel tab present → lift the corner and pull foil back | no tab → go to push-through] use fingernail pressure only on the foil corner.
steps.expect: foil separates without bending the pill.

steps.action: **Push through if needed.** Support the foil side with one hand and press the center of the plastic dome with the thumb pad, using steady pressure rather than a jab.
steps.expect: foil splits and the pill drops onto the catch surface.

steps.action: **Avoid crushing force.** If the pill resists, bend the pack slightly along the perforation or peel more foil before pressing again.
steps.expect: pill remains whole with no powder dust.

steps.action: **Collect the pill.** Pinch the pill gently at its edges or slide it from the tray into the intended container or hand.
steps.expect: pill is controlled and does not roll.

steps.action: **Inspect the pack.** Confirm only the chosen cell is opened and no loose foil fragments cling to the pill.
steps.expect: remaining cells are sealed and the removed item is clean.

recipes.verification: Exactly one intended pill is out of the blister, intact and accounted for, with the remaining blister cells sealed.

recipes.title: open a can with a can opener
recipes.name: open-a-can-with-a-can-opener
recipes.goal: A sealed food can is opened cleanly, with the lid controlled and sharp metal edges kept away from hands.

steps.action: **Inspect the can.** Check for bulging ends, deep dents on seams, leaks, rust holes, or sour smell.
steps.expect: the can appears safe to open, or it is discarded unopened.

steps.action: **Set the can on a stable surface.** Place it upright near the counter edge with the label facing out if helpful.
steps.expect: the can does not wobble when touched.

steps.action: **Open the can opener jaws.** Spread the handles so the cutting wheel and feed wheel can straddle the rim.
steps.expect: the opener mouth fits over the can lip.

steps.action: **Clamp the wheel on the rim.** Seat the cutting wheel on the top inside edge and squeeze the handles firmly.
steps.expect: the opener grips the rim without sliding.

steps.action: **Turn the knob forward.** Rotate the knob steadily while holding the handles closed.
steps.expect: the can rotates under the opener and a cut line appears around the lid.

steps.action: **Continue around the circle.** Keep turning until the cut nearly meets the start point. [BRANCH: leave a small hinge | cut fully free] leave 1 cm attached for control, or finish the circle if draining.
steps.expect: the lid is loose but not flying loose.

steps.action: **Lift the lid safely.** Use the opener tip, a spoon handle, or the uncut hinge to lift the lid away from your fingers. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the cut lid and can rim are sharp, so never slide a finger along the edge.
steps.expect: the can is open and fingers never touch the cut metal.

steps.action: **Pour or scoop contents.** Transfer food to a bowl or pot, then place the lid inside the empty can for disposal if local practice allows.
steps.expect: food is out, and sharp pieces are contained.

recipes.verification: The can is open, contents are usable, and the sharp lid and rim are controlled so no bare finger contacts cut metal.

recipes.title: open a childproof cap
recipes.name: open-a-childproof-cap
recipes.goal: The childproof cap is opened using its intended simultaneous motion, contents are accessed without spilling, and the cap is resealed so children cannot open it easily.

steps.action: **Read the cap cue.** Find text, arrows, squeeze pads, or alignment marks on the cap and neck.
steps.expect: the required action is identified before force is applied.

steps.action: **Brace the bottle.** Hold the bottle body upright in the non-turning hand, fingers around the label area and base on the counter.
steps.expect: bottle does not tip or flex.

steps.action: **Choose the mechanism.** [BRANCH: push-down-and-turn | squeeze-and-turn | align-arrows-then-turn] follow the visible cue on the cap.
steps.expect: grip points match the cap markings.

steps.action: **Apply simultaneous pressure.** For push-down caps, press the palm straight down while rotating counterclockwise; for squeeze caps, pinch both side pads inward while rotating.
steps.expect: cap clicks past the safety catches and begins to loosen.

steps.action: **Reduce force after release.** Once threads move freely, continue turning with lighter pressure so the bottle stays upright.
steps.expect: cap rises on the threads without jerking.

steps.action: **Lift the cap cleanly.** Remove the cap straight up and place it inner side up on a clean surface.
steps.expect: no tablets, liquid, or powder spill onto the counter.

steps.action: **Use or inspect the contents.** Keep the opening above the counter and close the bottle immediately after removing the needed item.
steps.expect: contents remain inside except the intended dose or item.

steps.action: **Reseal and test.** Set the cap on square, turn clockwise until tight, then try a light counterclockwise twist without pressing or squeezing.
steps.expect: cap resists casual turning and stays seated.

recipes.verification: After closing, the cap cannot be removed by a plain counterclockwise twist without the required push, squeeze, or alignment action.

recipes.title: open a milk carton
recipes.name: open-a-milk-carton
recipes.goal: The gable-top carton is opened into a clean pouring spout, a small pour test runs without side leaks, and the carton remains upright and resealable.

steps.action: **Orient the carton.** Place the carton upright with the printed opening side facing you and the top ridge centered under both thumbs.
steps.expect: the marked spout panel is visible and the base does not rock.

steps.action: **Brace the body.** Wrap one hand around the upper carton body using light inward pressure that does not dent the side walls.
steps.expect: carton stays vertical while the top can move.

steps.action: **Push the folded wings back.** Press both triangular side wings away from the spout panel until the gable opens into a shallow V.
steps.expect: the top ridge separates slightly and both wings stay folded back.

steps.action: **Pull the spout panel outward.** Pinch the front lip between thumb and index finger, then pull outward and slightly upward with steady force.
steps.expect: the sealed paper seam begins to peel without tearing down the carton wall.

steps.action: **Pinch the spout open.** Place thumbs behind the two spout cheeks and index fingers outside them, then squeeze the cheeks apart into a diamond opening.
steps.expect: an oval or diamond pour mouth stays open by itself.

steps.action: **Clear stuck inner layers.** [BRANCH: inner seam open → continue | inner seam stuck → insert a clean fingertip at the lip and tease the layers apart]
steps.expect: light is visible through the spout and no paper flap blocks the path.

steps.action: **Perform a pour test.** Tilt the carton a few degrees over a cup or sink, then return upright before flow becomes heavy.
steps.expect: a narrow stream exits only from the spout.

steps.action: **Reseat for storage.** Press the spout cheeks together and fold the wings back toward the ridge if storing.
steps.expect: top is mostly closed and carton can stand in the refrigerator without dripping.

recipes.verification: The carton has an open, stable spout and a brief tilt produces a controlled stream from the spout with no liquid escaping from other seams.

recipes.title: peel a hard boiled egg
recipes.name: peel-a-hard-boiled-egg
recipes.goal: The shell and membrane are removed from the hard-boiled egg while keeping the cooked white mostly intact.

steps.action: **Hold the egg gently.** Cup it in one hand with enough support to prevent dropping.
steps.expect: shell stays intact until tapped.

steps.action: **Crack all over.** Tap the egg against the counter, rotating to make many small cracks.
steps.expect: shell shows a network of cracks.

steps.action: **Roll under the palm.** Roll the egg with light downward pressure to loosen the membrane.
steps.expect: shell crackles and separates slightly from the white.

steps.action: **Find the fat end.** Locate the wider end where the air pocket usually sits.
steps.expect: shell feels slightly easier to lift there.

steps.action: **Start under the membrane.** Pick away shell at the fat end until the thin membrane lifts with it.
steps.expect: a flap of shell and membrane comes free.

steps.action: **Peel in sections.** Pull shell pieces away following the curve of the egg.
steps.expect: white surface appears with minimal gouging.

steps.action: **Use running water.** [BRANCH: shell loosens | shell sticks] rinse under a thin stream while peeling under the membrane.
steps.expect: water slips between shell and white.

steps.action: **Rinse and inspect.** Wash off fragments and place the peeled egg in a bowl.
steps.expect: no shell grit remains on the egg.

recipes.verification: The egg has no shell or membrane patches visible, no gritty fragments remain, and the cooked white is intact enough for the intended use.

recipes.title: peel a vegetable
recipes.name: peel-a-vegetable
recipes.goal: The vegetable has its outer skin removed with controlled peeler strokes, and peelings are contained for cleanup.

steps.action: **Stage the catch area.** Place the bowl or bin opening below the work path, close enough that peels drop into it without reaching across the blade.
steps.expect: the catch area sits below the vegetable and does not wobble.

steps.action: **Grip the vegetable.** Hold one end with the support hand, fingers curled back from the peel path, or stabilize it flat on the board if it rolls.
steps.expect: the vegetable resists light pulling without slipping.

steps.action: **Grip the peeler.** Wrap the dominant hand around the handle with the blade facing away from the body and away from the support hand.
steps.expect: the peeler edge is visible and the handle does not rotate in the hand.

steps.action: **Start a test stroke.** Touch the blade near the far end and draw it away from the body with light pressure.
steps.expect: a thin strip of peel separates without gouging deep flesh.

steps.action: **Peel in lanes.** Repeat long strokes from near to far, overlapping each lane slightly and keeping the wrist aligned with the blade.
steps.expect: exposed vegetable flesh forms clean parallel bands.

steps.action: **Rotate the vegetable.** Turn it a quarter turn after each exposed band set, moving the support hand before the blade moves again.
steps.expect: unpeeled skin faces the peeler and fingers remain outside the stroke path.

steps.action: **Trim ends carefully.** [BRANCH: flat end | rounded end] For a flat end, rest it on the board; for a rounded end, use short outward strokes only. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cuts from the peeler edge require stopping before skin contact.
steps.expect: end skin is removed or left as a small safe patch.

steps.action: **Set down and collect peels.** Place the peeled vegetable on the board, then move peelings into the trash or compost without touching the blade.
steps.expect: peeled vegetable is separate from waste and the peeler is at rest.

recipes.verification: The vegetable surface is mostly free of outer skin, remaining peel patches are intentional and small, the peeler is stationary, and loose peels are contained.

recipes.title: peel and slice a banana
recipes.name: peel-and-slice-a-banana
recipes.goal: A banana is peeled cleanly and cut into even slices on a board, delivered to a plate or bowl before browning sets in.

steps.action: **Orient the banana.** Identify the stem end (the thick, curved attachment point) and the blossom end (the small dark nub at the opposite tip).
steps.expect: both ends identified; fruit held in the non-dominant hand.

steps.action: **Open from the blossom end.** Pinch the dark nub between thumb and forefinger and squeeze; the peel splits cleanly. This is the reliable end: the stem end often bends without breaking and bruises the top of the fruit into mush. [BRANCH: blossom end opens → continue | banana is under-ripe and won't pinch open → nick the peel at the blossom end with the knife tip, on the board, blade away from the holding hand]
steps.expect: peel split at the tip with the fruit's top intact, not mashed.

steps.action: **Peel in thirds.** Pull each strip of peel down slowly toward the stem, one at a time, keeping the strips attached at the stem end.
steps.expect: naked fruit, peel strips hanging like a skirt from the stem end.

steps.action: **Strip the strings.** Run a thumb down the fruit to remove any flat white strings (phloem strands) still clinging.
steps.expect: smooth fruit surface; strings gone with the peel.

steps.action: **Detach and discard the peel.** Snap the peel off at the stem, and put it directly in the bin or compost, never left on the counter or floor.
steps.expect: peel in the bin; board clear.

steps.action: **Slice on the board with a claw grip.** Lay the banana on the board. Curl the fingertips of the holding hand so the knuckles (not fingertips) face the blade, and cut straight down in slow strokes, moving the claw back between cuts. Aim for uniform rounds, about 1 cm for cereal and snacking, thinner for topping toast.
steps.expect: even coins of consistent thickness; fingertips never in the blade's path.

steps.action: **Transfer at once.** Slide the slices off the board into the bowl or onto the plate with the back of the knife or a scooped hand.
steps.expect: slices in the serving vessel within a minute or two of cutting; knife set at the back of the board, edge away.

recipes.verification: Even slices sit in the serving vessel with no browning, the peel is in the bin (not on any surface someone could slip on), the knife is at the back of the board with the edge facing away, and all fingertips are intact.

recipes.title: place dishes in the sink
recipes.name: place-dishes-in-the-sink
recipes.goal: Dishes are placed in the sink without dropping, chipping, or creating an unstable stack.

steps.action: **Inspect the sink.** Look for knives, glass shards, or fragile items hidden under water.
steps.expect: the landing area is visible and safe.

steps.action: **Choose one load.** Carry only the number of dishes that can be held without shifting, usually one to three items.
steps.expect: each item is supported from below or by a secure rim grip.
