steps.action: **Grip the dish.** Hold plates by opposite edges, bowls under the base, and cups around the body near the bottom.
steps.expect: the item does not tilt when lifted.

steps.action: **Move to the basin.** Carry at waist height and keep the load close to the body.
steps.expect: dishes remain separated enough not to knock.

steps.action: **Lower, do not drop.** Bring the dish to within one centimeter of the sink surface or stack before release.
steps.expect: contact is quiet and controlled.

steps.action: **Stack by shape.** Put plates vertical or nested together, bowls nested, and cups upright or sideways where they cannot roll.
steps.expect: the stack sits stable without leaning.

steps.action: **Protect fragile rims.** [BRANCH: glassware present | no glassware] Place glassware away from heavy plates; continue normal stacking otherwise.
steps.expect: fragile items are not bearing heavy load.

steps.action: **Check clearance.** Remove hands slowly and nudge any unstable piece into a safer position.
steps.expect: no dish shifts after release.

recipes.verification: All carried dishes rest inside the sink or intended basin area, the stack is stable, and no fragile item is chipped or supporting excessive weight.

recipes.title: pour a glass of water
recipes.name: pour-a-glass-of-water
recipes.goal: A clean glass filled with drinking water to a sensible level and delivered into a hand or onto a surface without spill, the primitive that half the kitchen's fetch requests reduce to.

steps.action: **Select and inspect the glass.** Grasp by the body (or stem for stemware), quick look against the light.
steps.expect: a clean, intact glass; chips at the rim retire it (`daily/home/wash-dishes-by-hand` F4).

steps.action: **Position the glass at the source.** Under the tap without touching the faucet mouth; or on a stable counter surface next to the pitcher/bottle rather than held in the air, if your pouring control is developing (robots: counter-set is the default).
steps.expect: glass stable and centered under the incoming stream's path.

steps.action: **Start the flow gently.** Tap: cold lever opened partway (full blast into an empty glass splashes and overshoots). Pitcher/bottle: two-point grip (handle plus base for heavy pitchers), tilt slowly until the stream starts thin.
steps.expect: a controlled, narrow stream into the glass's center.

steps.action: **Fill to two to three centimeters below the rim.** The headroom is the anti-spill margin for carrying; watch the level, not the pour spout.
steps.expect: flow stopped at the target line; tap fully closed (drips off), pitcher returned upright before moving anything.

steps.action: **Deliver.** Carry at core height, watching the water's surface as live telemetry (`embodied/mobility/carry-and-deliver-an-item` step 3), and hand into a confirmed grip or set onto a coaster/table within the recipient's actual reach (`embodied/care/fetch-an-item-for-a-person` step 6).
steps.expect: glass at rest or in hand, surface calm, no trail of drops.

recipes.verification: The right-temperature water sits at a carryable level in a clean intact glass, delivered into a confirmed grip or within true reach, with the tap closed, the pitcher upright, and no drops marking the route.

recipes.title: pour batter into a pan
recipes.name: pour-batter-into-a-pan
recipes.goal: Move batter from a mixing bowl into a prepared pan with even distribution and minimal spill.

steps.action: **Set the pan close to the bowl.** Place the pan flat with its long side facing the pour path.
steps.expect: the pan is stable and reachable without stretching.

steps.action: **Grip the bowl securely.** Use two hands or one hand plus support under the base.
steps.expect: the bowl can tilt without slipping.

steps.action: **Start a slow pour.** Tilt the bowl lip over the center of the pan and let batter flow in a thick ribbon.
steps.expect: batter lands inside the pan and begins spreading outward.

steps.action: **Scrape remaining batter.** Hold the bowl tilted and draw the spatula along the inner wall toward the lip.
steps.expect: most batter leaves the bowl without dripping down the outside.

steps.action: **Distribute the batter.** Use the spatula to push batter into corners and level high ridges.
steps.expect: the batter covers the pan bottom at an even depth.

steps.action: **Clean the rim.** Wipe batter from the pan rim or outside wall before moving it.
steps.expect: the pan can be lifted without sticky trails or burnt-on drips.

recipes.verification: The batter is inside the prepared pan, spread to the required corners or shape, with the pan exterior clean enough to handle.

recipes.title: pour cereal and milk
recipes.name: pour-cereal-and-milk
recipes.goal: A bowl contains cereal and milk at a comfortable level, with no overflow, spills, or crushed packaging left open.

steps.action: **Place the bowl on a flat surface.** Center it away from the counter edge.
steps.expect: the bowl stays stable when lightly tapped.

steps.action: **Open the cereal carefully.** Open the box top and inner bag without tearing a giant side hole.
steps.expect: the bag opening forms a controlled spout.

steps.action: **Pour cereal first.** Tilt the box or bag slowly over the bowl until the bowl is about half to two-thirds full.
steps.expect: cereal lands in the bowl with headroom left.

steps.action: **Set the cereal down upright.** Close or fold the inner bag before returning attention to the bowl.
steps.expect: the cereal package does not keep spilling.

steps.action: **Open the milk container.** Remove cap or open spout and check smell if freshness is uncertain.
steps.expect: milk smells normal and the opening is clear.

steps.action: **Pour milk to the target level.** [BRANCH: light milk | milk-heavy] pour around the cereal edges until the lower cereal floats, or continue until milk sits just below the top cereal layer.
steps.expect: liquid stays below the bowl rim.

steps.action: **Stop before overflow.** Level the container upright when milk is 1 to 2 cm below the rim. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* spilled milk soaks cereal and surfaces quickly, so stop early rather than trying to fill to the brim.
steps.expect: the bowl can be lifted without sloshing.

steps.action: **Carry and set down smoothly.** Put spoon in the bowl, lift with one or two hands, and set it on the eating surface before releasing.
steps.expect: the bowl arrives level, with no trail of milk or cereal.

recipes.verification: The bowl contains cereal and milk below the rim, the spoon is present, packages are closed, and the counter or table is dry.

recipes.title: pour dry rice into a jar
recipes.name: pour-dry-rice-into-a-jar
recipes.goal: Dry rice is transferred from its bag into a jar and the jar is closed without spilling.

steps.action: **Place and stabilize the jar.** Set the jar upright on the counter and hold it near the base.
steps.expect: the jar does not slide when nudged.

steps.action: **Add a funnel if needed.** Insert the funnel tip into the jar mouth and center it.
steps.expect: the funnel rests upright without blocking the opening.

steps.action: **Grip the rice bag.** Hold the bag with one hand near the lower body and one hand near the open top.
steps.expect: the bag opening is controlled and points upward.

steps.action: **Move opening over the jar.** Position the bag mouth above the funnel or jar centerline.
steps.expect: any falling grains would land inside the opening.

steps.action: **Tilt gradually.** Rotate the bag slowly until rice begins to flow in a narrow stream.
steps.expect: grains enter the jar without hitting the counter.

steps.action: **Control the fill level.** Reduce tilt as rice approaches 2-3 cm below the jar rim.
steps.expect: the flow slows before the jar overfills.

steps.action: **Stop the pour.** Rotate the bag upright and hold it over the opening until the last grains fall.
steps.expect: rice flow stops and no grains spill from the bag mouth.

steps.action: **Remove funnel and close jar.** Lift the funnel vertically, place the lid on the jar, and tighten or press until sealed.
steps.expect: the lid seats fully and the jar can be moved without rice escaping.

recipes.verification: Rice is inside the jar below the rim, the lid is fully seated, and no active spill remains around the jar.

recipes.title: pour from a carton
recipes.name: pour-from-a-carton
recipes.goal: Liquid is poured from a carton into a target container at a controlled rate with enough headroom to prevent spill.

steps.action: **Inspect and orient.** Hold the carton upright and locate the spout, fill weight, and cap.
steps.expect: the spout faces the target side and the carton is not leaking.

steps.action: **Open the cap.** Twist or flip the cap fully open and keep it attached or set it in a clean visible place.
steps.expect: the pouring opening is unobstructed.

steps.action: **Position the target.** Place the target on the counter below the spout path rather than holding it in midair.
steps.expect: the target remains stable and has visible headroom.

steps.action: **Grip for control.** Use one hand around the carton body and the other under the base if it is heavy.
steps.expect: the carton can tilt without buckling.

steps.action: **Tip spout down.** Tilt slowly until the liquid just begins to flow from the lower edge of the spout.
steps.expect: a narrow stream enters the target.

steps.action: **Control rate.** Increase tilt only enough to maintain a steady stream, watching the rising fill level.
steps.expect: liquid level rises smoothly without splashing the rim.

steps.action: **Stop before full.** Return the carton upright when the target has required amount or at least two centimeters headroom.
steps.expect: flow stops before reaching the rim.

steps.action: **Prevent the drip.** Hold upright over the target for a beat, then move the carton away and close the cap.
steps.expect: final drops land in the target and the cap seals.

recipes.verification: The target contains the desired liquid below its rim, the carton is upright and closed, and no active drip remains on the spout.

recipes.title: prepare a simple breakfast tray
recipes.name: prepare-a-simple-breakfast-tray
recipes.goal: A loaded breakfast tray (plate, hot drink, juice, cutlery, extras) is carried from kitchen to the recipient and set down with nothing spilled, tipped, or dropped en route.

steps.action: **Line the tray.** Lay a cloth napkin or non-slip mat over the tray base. This one change stops most in-transit sliding.
steps.expect: liner flat, corners not folded up under where items will sit.

steps.action: **Load heavy and low in the center.** The plate goes in the middle; it is the mass anchor.
steps.expect: tray balances level when lifted a centimeter by both hands.

steps.action: **Place drinks inboard, filled to 80 percent.** Mug and juice glass go near the center-line of the tray, not at the edges, handles turned inward. The last 20 percent of a full cup is what ends up on the floor. [BRANCH: teapot or carafe → spout pointing inward over the tray, lid checked seated | no pot → skip]
steps.expect: no vessel within 3 cm of the tray rim; liquid levels below the sloshing line.

steps.action: **Add smalls in the gaps.** Cutlery parallel to the tray's long edge (rolls otherwise), napkin under the cutlery to pin it, jam and butter in remaining gaps.
steps.expect: nothing overlaps a plate rim or leans on another item; every item touches the liner.

steps.action: **Do the shake test.** Grip both ends and tilt the tray one or two degrees each way. Anything that slides now slides worse mid-hallway; re-seat it.
steps.expect: zero movement at small tilt.

steps.action: **Lift with two hands at the balance points, thumbs over the rim.** Elbows in, tray held slightly above waist height, back straight. Do not hug the tray against your chest; you need to see its surface.
steps.expect: level tray, both drink surfaces still, view of the route over the tray.

steps.action: **Walk the route slowly, eyes ahead not on the drinks.** Staring at the liquid causes over-correction; the liquid follows your gait. Announce yourself at blind corners ("coming through, hot drinks"). Anyone crossing your path → stop fully, let them pass.
steps.expect: smooth, even steps; no slosh rings climbing the mug walls.

steps.action: **Handle doors before or without hands.** [BRANCH: door already open or can be shouldered gently → pass through | latched door → set the tray down on a nearby stable surface, open and block the door, re-lift] Never balance the tray on one hand or a raised knee to work a handle.
steps.expect: both hands on the tray whenever it is airborne.

steps.action: **Set down back-edge first.** Land the tray's far edge on the destination surface, then lower the near edge, then release. Confirm the surface holds it (no overhang past half the tray depth) before letting go.
steps.expect: tray fully supported, drinks unspilled, recipient warned which item is hot.

recipes.verification: The tray sits fully supported at the destination, all liquid remains in its vessels at their original levels, nothing shifted from its loaded position, the recipient knows which items are hot, and the route behind you has no drips.

recipes.title: put away clean dishes
recipes.name: put-away-clean-dishes
recipes.goal: Every clean dish from the rack or dishwasher is dry and stored in its home location, cabinets and drawers are closed, and the rack or dishwasher is empty and ready for the next load.

steps.action: **Confirm dryness before anything moves.** Feel the undersides of a few plates and the recessed rims of upside-down mugs and bowls: these trap water even when tops look dry. [BRANCH: dry → proceed | wet spots → towel-dry each piece as you pick it up]
steps.expect: no piece goes into a closed cabinet wet; trapped water breeds smell and spots.

steps.action: **If unloading a dishwasher, do the bottom rack first.** The top rack's cupped items hold puddles that dump onto the bottom rack's dry dishes if you open top-first.
steps.expect: bottom rack cleared with its contents still dry.

steps.action: **Batch by category, not by grab order.** Gather all plates into one stack in hand (4 to 6 max), all glasses in a next pass, cutlery last. One cabinet trip per category instead of one trip per item.
steps.expect: each carry targets exactly one destination; total trips roughly equal to number of categories.

steps.action: **Carry stacks low and level with two hands.** Plates flat against the chest height, never balanced one-handed above shoulder height.
steps.expect: stack arrives at the cabinet without a wobble.

steps.action: **Place plates onto existing stacks, respecting stack limits.** Lower the new stack on top gently; keep any single stack to roughly 8 to 10 dinner plates, and never mix sizes in one stack (small on large slides).
steps.expect: stacks stable and straight; shelf not visibly bowing; a plate can be removed one-handed from the top.

steps.action: **Store glasses and mugs standing, not nested.** Same-shape glasses in rows, open side per house convention (up on closed shelves, down on open shelves that collect dust). Nested glasses stick and crack when separated.
steps.expect: each glass free-standing with a finger's clearance to its neighbors.

steps.action: **Sort cutlery into its tray slots, points down out of the basket.** Grab dishwasher-basket cutlery by the handles, never a fistful of blades. Knives that are sharp go in a block or blade-guard slot, not loose in the tray.
steps.expect: each slot single-category; nothing sharp pointing up where a reaching hand lands.

steps.action: **Big items last: pots, pans, boards.** Heavy pieces to low shelves, lids nested with their pots or in the lid rack.
steps.expect: nothing heavy stored above shoulder height.

steps.action: **Close every door and drawer, and reset the station.** Fold the towel to dry, leave the rack empty (or dishwasher open a crack to air out).
steps.expect: all cabinets flush shut; counters clear; nothing left orphaned on the counter.

recipes.verification: The rack or dishwasher is empty, every item sits dry in its home category (no mixed stacks, no nested glasses, no blade pointing up), all doors and drawers are closed, and the counter holds nothing but items awaiting a decision.

recipes.title: rinse a vegetable
recipes.name: rinse-a-vegetable
recipes.goal: A vegetable is rinsed under running water, loosened surface dirt is removed, and excess water is shaken off before use.

steps.action: **Inspect the vegetable.** Look for heavy dirt, damaged spots, or stickers.
steps.expect: visible debris and labels are identified before rinsing.

steps.action: **Start cool water.** Open the faucet to a gentle stream that will not splash out of the sink.
steps.expect: steady cool water falls into the basin.

steps.action: **Place under stream.** Hold the vegetable with fingers away from the drain and rotate it into the water.
steps.expect: the first surface is fully wetted.

steps.action: **Rub the surface.** Use fingertips to rub along the skin while water runs over the contact area.
steps.expect: dirt releases and flows away.

steps.action: **Rotate and repeat.** Turn the vegetable until all sides, ends, and creases pass under the stream.
steps.expect: no dry unwashed patch remains.

steps.action: **Check stubborn spots.** [BRANCH: dirt remains | surface clean] Rub remaining dirt with firmer fingertip pressure; proceed if clean.
steps.expect: stuck particles are removed or marked for trimming.

steps.action: **Shake off water.** Hold over the sink and shake with short downward motions.
steps.expect: loose drops fall into the basin.

steps.action: **Set down cleanly.** Place the vegetable on a clean towel, board, or colander away from dirty sink surfaces.
steps.expect: rinsed vegetable rests on a clean surface.

recipes.verification: All visible surfaces of the vegetable have been rinsed and rubbed, no loose dirt is visible, and the vegetable rests on a clean surface.

recipes.title: roll dough with a rolling pin
recipes.name: roll-dough-with-a-rolling-pin
recipes.goal: Flatten dough into an even sheet of the target thickness without sticking, tearing, or forcing it off the work surface.

steps.action: **Prepare the surface.** Dust the counter lightly with flour or place parchment flat.
steps.expect: the dough contact area has a thin nonstick layer with no flour piles.

steps.action: **Shape the dough disk.** Place dough in the center and press it by hand into a thick, even round or rectangle.
steps.expect: the dough has no tall mound in the middle.

steps.action: **Roll from center outward.** Hold both pin handles or ends and push forward with even downward pressure.
steps.expect: the dough lengthens in the stroke direction without sticking to the pin.

steps.action: **Rotate and repeat.** Lift or turn the dough a quarter turn between strokes, adding a light flour dusting if needed.
steps.expect: thickness spreads evenly in multiple directions.

steps.action: **Check thickness by sight and touch.** Compare edges and center, then roll only the thicker zones with lighter passes.
steps.expect: the sheet has a consistent thickness within the recipe tolerance.

steps.action: **Release the dough.** Slide a hand, scraper, or parchment under an edge to confirm it moves.
steps.expect: the dough lifts without tearing and is ready for cutting or transfer.

recipes.verification: The dough sheet is the intended shape and thickness, releases from the surface, and has no major tears or stuck areas.

recipes.title: scoop with a spoon
recipes.name: scoop-with-a-spoon
recipes.goal: A spoonful of food or liquid is gathered, transported level, and released at the intended target.

steps.action: **Grip the spoon.** Hold the handle near its middle with the bowl of the spoon facing up.
steps.expect: the spoon stays level when lifted empty.

steps.action: **Stabilize the source.** Hold the source container or confirm it will not slide.
steps.expect: the container resists a light spoon push.

steps.action: **Set angle of attack.** Lower the spoon bowl into the food at a shallow forward angle, about 20 to 45 degrees.
steps.expect: the front edge enters without pushing the food away.

steps.action: **Draw through the food.** Pull or push the spoon through the material until the bowl fills.
steps.expect: food collects inside the spoon bowl.

steps.action: **Level the fill.** Lift slightly and pause over the source so excess falls back.
steps.expect: the spoon holds a rounded but stable portion.

steps.action: **Transport level.** Move the spoon slowly to the destination, keeping the bowl horizontal and below chest height.
steps.expect: contents remain in the spoon.

steps.action: **Release.** Tip the spoon over the destination or touch it to the target surface and roll the wrist.
steps.expect: the scoop leaves the spoon and lands in the intended place.

steps.action: **Reset.** Return the spoon to level or set it on a clean rest.
steps.expect: no trailing drip crosses the work surface.

recipes.verification: One controlled spoonful has been transferred to the target, with no significant food left on the path between source and destination.

recipes.title: serve food onto plates
recipes.name: serve-food-onto-plates
recipes.goal: Cooked food is portioned evenly from its pot or pan onto individual plates, with clean rims, correct portions per eater, and every plate delivered to the table while still hot.

steps.action: **Warm the plates if the food is saucy or quick-cooling.** Hot tap water rinse and a towel-dry, or 30 seconds in the microwave in a stack. Cold plates kill hot food in two minutes.
steps.expect: plates warm to the touch, dry.

steps.action: **Do the portion math before the first scoop.** Eyeball the pot as N equal shares, and hold back roughly 10 percent as a reserve. The classic error is generous early plates and a scraped-thin last one. [BRANCH: seconds culture (family style) → plate slightly under, leave the rest in the pot | plated-and-done → divide fully, still reserve-last]
steps.expect: a stated plan ("about two ladles each") before serving starts.

steps.action: **Bring plates to the pan, not the pan to the plates.** Serve at the stove with the pan on its burner or on a trivet beside it. Carrying a hot full pan across the kitchen to a table of plates is the highest-risk move in home cooking.
steps.expect: the hot vessel moves zero or one short step, ever.

steps.action: **Handle the hot vessel with a dry barrier only.** Dry pot holder or folded dry towel on the handle; a damp towel conducts steam through instantly. Angle handles inward, and steady the pan by the handle while scooping, never with a bare hand on the rim.
steps.expect: firm grip, no bare skin near metal, pan stable while the utensil works.

steps.action: **Plate in rounds, not one plate at a time.** First component to every plate, then second component to every plate. Rounds average out portion drift and every plate finishes at the same temperature.
steps.expect: all plates visually level with each other after each round.

steps.action: **Place food, don't drop it.** Bring the spoon low over the plate before releasing; sauce ladled from a height splashes the rim and the counter. Wet foods first in the plate's center, drier sides beside, sauce over the item it belongs to.
steps.expect: food inside the plate's inner well; rim clean or nearly so.

steps.action: **Wipe the rims.** Fold a clean damp towel over one finger and run it around each rim. Thirty seconds total, and it is the difference between "dinner" and "mess".
steps.expect: every rim bare and clean; towel back on its hook, not on the counter in a puddle.

steps.action: **Deliver plates two at a time maximum, announced.** One plate per hand, thumbs on the rim edge only, no forearm-stacking with hot plates. Say "hot plate" as each lands, especially to children.
steps.expect: each plate set down flat in front of an eater without a tilt; recipients warned.

steps.action: **Park the pan safely.** Vessel back on the off burner or trivet, serving utensil resting in the pan (not flat on the counter), reserve portion covered.
steps.expect: no hot vessel at a counter edge; utensil contained; leftovers ready for seconds or storage.

recipes.verification: Every eater has a plate with a visually equal portion, all rims are clean, the hot vessel rests on a burner or trivet away from edges with its utensil inside, the reserve or leftovers are covered, and no one (server included) touched bare hot metal.

recipes.title: set a kitchen timer
recipes.name: set-a-kitchen-timer
recipes.goal: A kitchen timer is set to the requested duration, started, and confirmed to be counting down.

steps.action: **Read the current state.** Look at the display or dial before pressing buttons.
steps.expect: timer is idle, counting, or showing a previous value.

steps.action: **Clear if needed.** Press cancel, stop, or reset if an old value is active.
steps.expect: display returns to zero or idle.

steps.action: **Enter minutes.** Use minute buttons, number keys, or dial turns to reach the requested minutes.
steps.expect: displayed minutes match the target.

steps.action: **Enter seconds if needed.** Add seconds with the seconds control or number keys.
steps.expect: full displayed duration matches the requested time.

steps.action: **Start the timer.** Press start or twist the mechanical timer past the target and back if that model requires winding.
steps.expect: countdown begins or ticking starts.

steps.action: **Confirm counting.** Watch for at least one decrement, moving colon, or audible tick.
steps.expect: time is actively decreasing.

steps.action: **Place within hearing range.** Set the timer where it is visible or audible but away from burners, water, and edges.
steps.expect: timer rests stable and unobstructed.

steps.action: **Cancel when requested.** [BRANCH: timer needed | timer no longer needed] Leave it running if needed; press cancel or stop if the task is abandoned.
steps.expect: active timer state matches the cooking task.

recipes.verification: The timer shows the requested countdown actively decreasing, or it is canceled only because the parent task no longer needs timing.

recipes.title: set a table
recipes.name: set-a-table
recipes.goal: The dining table is set for N diners with a complete, consistently arranged place setting at each seat.

steps.action: **Confirm the seat positions.** One setting per chair, centered on the chair's position, ~2 cm from the table edge.
steps.expect: N positions identified, evenly spaced, no setting straddling a table leg or corner awkwardly.

steps.action: **Carry and place the plates.** Carry plates in a stable stack of ≤ N (both hands or against the chassis), then place one plate at each position's center.
steps.expect: one plate per seat, centered, ~2 cm from the edge; stack emptied without chips or clinks.

steps.action: **Place the forks.** Fork on the *left* of each plate, tines up, aligned with the plate's bottom edge.
steps.expect: each fork parallel to the plate, consistent spacing (~1 cm from plate rim).

steps.action: **Place the knives and spoons.** Knife on the *right* of the plate, blade facing *inward* toward the plate; spoon to the right of the knife. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* none, but blades outward read as careless and snag reaching hands — blade-in is the rule.
steps.expect: right side of each setting reads knife-then-spoon outward, blades in.

steps.action: **Place the glasses.** Above the knife tip (upper right of the plate), upright. Fragile — individual grasps, no stacking, reduced speed over the table.
steps.expect: one glass per setting, upper right, stable and not touching other items.

steps.action: **Place the napkins.** Folded napkin either on the plate's center or under the fork, consistently — pick one style for the whole table.
steps.expect: all N settings use the same napkin placement.

steps.action: **Add shared items to the table's center.** Water pitcher/bottle, salt and pepper, serving trivets if hot dishes are coming, within reach of all seats.
steps.expect: shared items centered, leaving clearance in front of every setting.

steps.action: **Final pass around the table.** Walk/scan the full circumference: every setting complete and aligned the same way; chair access unobstructed.
steps.expect: N identical complete settings; nothing missing or extra.

recipes.verification: Walking the table's full circumference: N settings, each with plate centered, fork left, knife (blade in) then spoon right, glass upper right, napkin in the chosen style; shared items reachable from every seat; no chips, water spots, or misalignments.

recipes.title: skewer food onto a stick
recipes.name: skewer-food-onto-a-stick
recipes.goal: Thread prepared food pieces onto a skewer in a stable order without puncturing hands or splitting the food.

steps.action: **Set the skewer orientation.** Hold the blunt end and point the tip down toward the board at a shallow angle.
steps.expect: the sharp tip is visible and aimed away from hands and people.

steps.action: **Pick a food piece.** Grip it at the sides, leaving the intended centerline exposed.
steps.expect: the piece is steady and fingers are not behind the puncture path.

steps.action: **Pierce through the center.** Press the skewer tip into the food and rotate slightly if resistance is high.
steps.expect: the tip emerges on the far side without tearing the piece apart.

steps.action: **Slide the food down.** Push the food along the skewer toward the blunt end, leaving a small gap from other pieces.
steps.expect: the piece stays on the skewer and can rotate only slightly.

steps.action: **Repeat with spacing.** Alternate pieces as desired and keep about 3 to 5 mm between dense pieces for cooking airflow.
steps.expect: the skewer is balanced and not overloaded.

steps.action: **Place on a tray.** Lay the finished skewer flat with the tip pointing inward or away from the tray edge.
steps.expect: the skewer rests without rolling off and the sharp tip is not exposed outward.

recipes.verification: Food pieces are threaded securely with safe spacing, the skewer remains straight, and the sharp tip is oriented away from hands and tray edges.

recipes.title: sort cutlery into a tray
recipes.name: sort-cutlery-into-a-tray
recipes.goal: Clean cutlery is grouped by type in the correct tray compartments with handles aligned.

steps.action: **Open or expose the tray.** Pull the drawer straight out or place the tray on the counter.
steps.expect: all compartments are visible and reachable.

steps.action: **Identify compartments.** Inspect existing labels or contents to map forks, spoons, knives, and small utensils.
steps.expect: each cutlery type has a chosen compartment.

steps.action: **Pick one utensil by the handle.** Grasp near the handle midpoint, keeping tips and blades pointed away.
steps.expect: the utensil is controlled without contacting the eating end.

steps.action: **Classify the utensil.** Observe its shape: tines, bowl, blade, or specialty profile.
steps.expect: the matching compartment is selected.

steps.action: **Place handle-aligned.** Lower the utensil into the compartment with handle ends facing the same direction as existing pieces.
steps.expect: it lies flat and does not bridge across dividers.

steps.action: **Repeat one utensil at a time.** Continue until the unsorted pile is empty, slowing near sharp knives.
steps.expect: each compartment accumulates only one utensil class.

steps.action: **Straighten each group.** Use light side pressure to align handles and tips within each compartment.
steps.expect: utensils are nested flat and drawer clearance is unobstructed.

recipes.verification: Forks, spoons, knives, and specialty utensils are separated by compartment, lie flat, and the drawer or tray can close without contact.

recipes.title: spread butter with a knife
recipes.name: spread-butter-with-a-knife
recipes.goal: Butter is spread in an even layer across bread or toast, including edges, without tearing the surface.

steps.action: **Stabilize the bread.** Place the bread flat and hold one corner lightly if it slides.
steps.expect: the bread does not move under light knife contact.

steps.action: **Load the knife.** Scrape a small curl of soft butter onto one side of the knife blade.
steps.expect: butter adheres near the middle third of the blade.

steps.action: **Deposit butter.** Touch the loaded blade to the bread center and press gently.
steps.expect: butter transfers from knife to bread without tearing.

steps.action: **Spread outward.** Use short, flat strokes from center toward the edges with low pressure.
steps.expect: a thin layer extends across the surface.

steps.action: **Reload as needed.** Add small amounts rather than one large lump.
steps.expect: butter coverage increases without thick ridges.

steps.action: **Cover the edges.** Angle the knife slightly and sweep along each edge while staying on the bread surface.
steps.expect: corners and edges have visible butter.

steps.action: **Smooth high spots.** Drag the knife lightly across ridges to even the layer.
steps.expect: thickness appears consistent across the bread.

steps.action: **Set knife down safely.** Place the knife on the plate edge or a clean rest with the blade not protruding.
steps.expect: knife is stable and buttered side faces up or inward.

recipes.verification: The bread has a continuous butter layer from center to edges, with no major torn area and the knife resting safely.

recipes.title: stack cups
recipes.name: stack-cups
recipes.goal: Cups are nested or stacked upright in a stable vertical group on the shelf or counter.

steps.action: **Clear the target surface.** Sweep the placement area with a light open-hand pass and remove loose items.
steps.expect: a flat area wider than the largest cup is unobstructed.

steps.action: **Place the base cup.** Grasp the largest cup around the side wall, keep the open rim facing upward, and lower it until the base contacts the surface.
steps.expect: the cup stands upright without wobble.

steps.action: **Select the next cup.** Choose a cup with an equal or smaller rim diameter and grip it near the upper side wall.
steps.expect: the cup is controlled with the open rim still facing upward.

steps.action: **Align over the base.** Center the next cup above the base cup with rims parallel and vertical axes aligned.
steps.expect: the lower cup rim is evenly visible around the upper cup.

steps.action: **Lower gently.** Descend with light force until the upper cup settles into or onto the lower cup.
steps.expect: contact is quiet and the stack height stops changing.

steps.action: **Repeat for remaining cups.** Add cups largest to smallest, re-centering after each placement.
steps.expect: the stack remains vertical and no cup edge catches.

steps.action: **Check stability.** Release the stack, then lightly tap the shelf beside it without touching the cups.
steps.expect: cups remain upright and do not slide.

recipes.verification: All cups are empty, upright, vertically aligned, and stable for 5 seconds after release with no cup contacting a fragile neighboring item.

recipes.title: stack plates in a cupboard
recipes.name: stack-plates-in-a-cupboard
recipes.goal: Plates are stacked flat in a cupboard with aligned edges and stable shelf clearance.

steps.action: **Clear the shelf.** Remove loose objects from the intended stack footprint.
steps.expect: a flat shelf area wider than the plate diameter is open.

steps.action: **Place the largest plate first.** Grip opposite rim edges with both hands and lower the plate flat onto the shelf.
steps.expect: the plate sits level with no rocking.

steps.action: **Lift the next plate level.** Hold opposite sides and keep the eating surface facing upward.
steps.expect: the plate remains horizontal during movement.

steps.action: **Align over the stack.** Center the plate above the lower plate with rims matching.
steps.expect: the lower rim is evenly visible around the top plate.

steps.action: **Lower with minimal impact.** Descend slowly until ceramic contacts ceramic.
steps.expect: the plate lands quietly and does not slide.

steps.action: **Repeat by size.** Continue largest to smallest, keeping each plate centered.
steps.expect: the stack remains vertical and edges form an even column.

steps.action: **Check clearance and weight.** Release the stack and observe shelf sag and door clearance.
steps.expect: the shelf stays level and the cupboard door can close.

recipes.verification: The plate stack is centered, flat, stable after release, and the cupboard door closes without touching it.

recipes.title: stir a pot safely
recipes.name: stir-a-pot-safely
recipes.goal: The pot's contents are stirred evenly (nothing sticking or scorching on the bottom) without steam burns, splatter, or a utensil left in the pot.

steps.action: **Rotate the pot handle inward.** Turn it so it points over the counter, not out over the floor or a walkway.
steps.expect: handle cannot be snagged by a passing hip or reaching child.

steps.action: **Choose the utensil for the pot and contents.** [BRANCH: nonstick pot → wood or silicone only | thick contents (risotto, oatmeal, sauce) → flat-edged spatula that can scrape the bottom | thin liquid (soup, stock) → any long spoon]
steps.expect: utensil handle long enough that your knuckles stay above the rim while the head reaches the bottom.

steps.action: **Take the grip.** Hold the utensil like a hammer, overhand near the handle's end, and steady the pot by its handle with your other hand (through a pot holder if the handle is metal).
steps.expect: pot cannot rotate or walk on the burner when you stir.

steps.action: **If lidded, vent before opening.** Lift the lid tilted away from your face and let the steam plume rise on the far side, then set the lid down wet-side up.
steps.expect: steam cloud vents away from you; no condensation dripped on the burner or floor.

steps.action: **Stand to the side of the steam column.** Position yourself so rising steam passes in front of you, not into your face and forearm.
steps.expect: you can see the surface of the contents without leaning over the pot.

steps.action: **Stir bottom-first, then in a slow figure-eight.** Drag the utensil edge flat across the bottom to lift anything settling, then sweep the walls and middle. Keep the speed low: splatter comes from fast stirring, not thorough stirring.
steps.expect: even color and texture; no dark flecks lifting off the bottom (dark flecks → F2); no drops leaving the pot.

steps.action: **Park the utensil on the spoon rest between stirs.** Never leave it standing in the pot (it heats up, tips the pot, or melts) and never flat on the counter (it glues sauce to the surface).
steps.expect: utensil on the rest, drips contained, handle cool for the next stir.

steps.action: **Re-lid if the recipe wants it, tilted vent-open for foamy contents.** Starches (pasta, oats, beans) boil over under a sealed lid.
steps.expect: lid seated (or cracked open for starches); simmer steady, not climbing.

recipes.verification: Contents are uniform in color and texture with nothing stuck to the bottom, the utensil rests on the spoon rest (not in the pot, not on the bare counter), the pot handle points inward, and no burns or splatter occurred.

recipes.title: store groceries
recipes.name: store-groceries
recipes.goal: All grocery bags are unpacked with every item stored in its correct zone — cold chain preserved, older stock rotated forward, fragile items intact, bags cleared.

steps.action: **Triage all bags by temperature class first.** One fast pass: frozen → chilled → everything else, grouped on the counter. Cold items have been warming since checkout — they get priority, not bag order.
steps.expect: three counter groups; frozen and chilled identified within the first minute.

steps.action: **Load the freezer.** Frozen group in first, flat items stacked, new stock *behind or below* existing (older gets used first).
steps.expect: freezer closed with everything frozen inside; nothing left sweating on the counter.

steps.action: **Load the fridge by zone.** Raw meat/fish: bottom shelf (drip containment — never above ready-to-eat). Dairy and eggs: middle/upper shelves, *not* the door (its temperature swings). Vegetables/fruit: crisper drawers. Condiments and juices: the door. Rotate: new milk behind old milk.
steps.expect: each chilled item in its zone; older duplicates in front of newer.

steps.action: **Handle the counter-dwellers correctly.** Bananas, tomatoes, onions, garlic, potatoes, and most whole melons prefer room temperature — bowl or pantry basket, with potatoes/onions dark and *separated from each other* (they spoil each other faster). Bread: breadbox/counter (fridge staling is real), or freezer for the long haul.
steps.expect: no cold-sensitive produce accidentally refrigerated.

steps.action: **Stock the pantry with rotation.** Cans, jars, dry goods to their shelves; new behind old (first-in-first-out); heavy items at waist height or lower, light on top. Fragile jars placed with clearance, not slid against neighbors.
steps.expect: shelves stocked, older stock at the front edge, nothing precarious above head height.

steps.action: **Close the loop.** Fold/store reusable bags at their spot (or by the door for the car); wipe any drips; discard anything expired that surfaced while making space.
steps.expect: empty counters, stored bags, and a fridge/pantry you got slightly *more* organized, not less.

recipes.verification: Counters and bags are empty, frozen/chilled items reached their zones promptly, meat sits below ready-to-eat food, cold-sensitive produce is out of the fridge, stock is rotated old-in-front, and nothing expired is hiding where the new stock went.

recipes.title: tear off plastic wrap
recipes.name: tear-off-plastic-wrap
recipes.goal: A clean sheet of plastic wrap is torn from the roll, stretched across the target without tangling, and the box edge is left ready for the next pull.

steps.action: **Find the film edge.** Rotate the roll until the loose edge or matte line is visible, then pinch both corners lightly.
steps.expect: a full-width leading edge lifts from the roll.

steps.action: **Pin the box and roll.** Place one forearm or hand on the box lid while fingertips restrain the roll ends.
steps.expect: the roll resists spinning freely.

steps.action: **Pull a measured length.** Draw the film straight out at counter height with even tension across both corners.
steps.expect: sheet advances without diagonal wrinkles.

steps.action: **Set the length against the cutter.** Lower the film onto the serrated edge with the desired tear line just beyond the teeth.
steps.expect: film is taut across the cutter from left to right.

steps.action: **Tear across the edge.** Pull down and slightly sideways from one corner, letting the teeth start the cut, then continue across the width.
steps.expect: sheet separates in a mostly straight line.

steps.action: **Prevent cling tangle.** Keep the free sheet stretched between both hands and avoid letting the middle touch itself.
steps.expect: sheet stays open and transparent, not roped or folded.

steps.action: **Cover the target.** Lay the near edge on the rim first, then smooth outward with flat fingertips and light tension.
steps.expect: wrap seals to the rim or surface without large trapped folds.

steps.action: **Leave a starter tab.** Press the remaining roll edge lightly to the box lip or fold a small corner back on itself.
steps.expect: next-use edge is visible and reachable.

recipes.verification: The target is covered by one intact sheet and the remaining roll has a visible starter edge at the box lip.

recipes.title: transfer food between containers
recipes.name: transfer-food-between-containers
recipes.goal: Food is moved from one container to another with minimal spill and without crushing or contaminating it.

steps.action: **Place the destination.** Set the destination container on a flat surface directly in front of the source container.
steps.expect: the destination does not slide when nudged.

steps.action: **Check capacity.** Compare the food volume with the destination headroom before lifting anything.
steps.expect: the destination has visible room above the expected fill level.

steps.action: **Align the rims.** Bring the source rim just above or slightly inside the destination rim without touching dirty outer surfaces to food.
steps.expect: a short transfer gap exists and both openings overlap.

steps.action: **Set the guiding tool.** Hold the spatula or spoon at the lower lip of the source container to guide food flow.
steps.expect: the tool blocks food from escaping sideways.

steps.action: **Tilt slowly.** Rotate the source container toward the destination until food begins moving.
steps.expect: food crosses the rim in a controlled stream or slide.

steps.action: **Scrape the trailing food.** Use the spatula with light pressure along the inner wall, pushing food toward the aligned rim.
steps.expect: remaining food gathers at the pour edge and drops into the destination.

steps.action: **Pause before overflow.** [BRANCH: destination still has headroom | destination nearly full] Continue if there is room; stop and choose a larger container if the level is within two centimeters of the rim.
steps.expect: no food reaches the outside rim.

steps.action: **Right and set down.** Return the source container upright before moving it away, then set it down on the work surface.
steps.expect: no trailing drip or falling piece follows the source container.

recipes.verification: The intended food is inside the destination container, the destination remains below its rim, and visible spills are absent or wiped.

recipes.title: turn a stove burner on and off
recipes.name: turn-a-stove-burner-on-and-off
recipes.goal: The intended stove burner is turned on to a controlled heat level and later fully turned off with the correct knob verified.

steps.action: **Identify the target burner.** Match the burner position to the printed knob diagram before touching the knob.
steps.expect: the selected knob corresponds to the intended front, rear, left, or right burner.

steps.action: **Clear the area.** Move flammable items and handles away from adjacent burners.
steps.expect: only heat-safe cookware is near the burner.

steps.action: **Prepare ignition.** [BRANCH: electric | gas] For electric, set hand on the knob; for gas, have the igniter, match, or built-in spark ready.
steps.expect: ignition method is available before gas flow starts.

steps.action: **Turn on gradually.** Press or turn the correct knob to the ignition or low setting, following the knob's required push-turn motion.
steps.expect: the target burner starts heating or gas clicks for ignition.

steps.action: **Verify active heat.** For gas, confirm a stable blue flame around the ring; for electric, confirm indicator light or visible coil glow.
steps.expect: only the intended burner is active.

steps.action: **Adjust to target.** Rotate the knob slowly to low, medium, or high while watching the flame size or heat indicator.
steps.expect: heat output changes smoothly and cookware remains centered.

steps.action: **Turn off deliberately.** Rotate the same knob back to OFF until it stops. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* leaving gas or heat on can cause fire, burns, or gas buildup, so verify before walking away.
steps.expect: the knob pointer aligns exactly with OFF.

steps.action: **Off-verify.** Look at the burner, indicator light, and flame area for five seconds.
steps.expect: flame is out, indicator is off or cooling, and no gas smell increases.

recipes.verification: The intended burner can be observed active when on, and after shutdown its matched knob is at OFF with no flame and no active heat indicator.

recipes.title: twist off a bottle cap
recipes.name: twist-off-a-bottle-cap
recipes.goal: The bottle cap is loosened counterclockwise, removed without spilling, and optionally tightened again to reseal.

steps.action: **Stabilize the bottle.** Hold the bottle body below the neck with the non-turning hand.
steps.expect: bottle stays upright.

steps.action: **Grip the cap.** Wrap fingers and thumb around the cap ridges with firm even pressure.
steps.expect: cap skin contact does not slip.

steps.action: **Brace the base.** Press the bottle lightly against the counter or hold it close to the body.
steps.expect: bottle resists rotation.

steps.action: **Twist counterclockwise.** Turn the cap left while the bottle hand holds steady.
steps.expect: cap begins to rotate relative to the bottle.

steps.action: **Feel the seal break.** Continue through the first pop, crack, or drop in resistance.
steps.expect: tamper ring separates or threads loosen.

steps.action: **Remove the cap.** Keep twisting until threads disengage, then lift the cap straight up.
steps.expect: bottle mouth is open and liquid remains below the rim.

steps.action: **Use the contents.** [BRANCH: pour | sip | inspect] keep the bottle upright between actions.
steps.expect: controlled access to the liquid.

steps.action: **Tighten to reseal.** Place cap squarely and twist clockwise until snug.
steps.expect: cap stops without cross-threading.

recipes.verification: The cap is removed or resealed as intended, the bottle remains upright, and no liquid is spilled outside the target area.

recipes.title: unload a dishwasher
recipes.name: unload-a-dishwasher
recipes.goal: A finished dishwasher is emptied with everything dry, intact, and stored in its home location, leaving the machine ready for the next load.

steps.action: **Open the door and pause for the steam.** Crack the door and wait a few seconds; a just-finished machine vents hot moist air at face height.
steps.expect: steam dispersed; contents hot-to-warm but touchable.

steps.action: **Check the cycle actually cleaned.** Glance at a few items: food residue or gritty film means the load re-runs (or the spray arm was blocked, `embodied/kitchen/load-a-dishwasher` F1), and unloading dirty dishes into cabinets is the failure to avoid at all costs.
steps.expect: clean, hot items throughout.

steps.action: **Unload the bottom rack first.** The reason is physics: cup hollows on the top rack pool water, and pulling the top rack first rains that water onto the dry plates below. Plates in carried stacks sized to your grip (four to six), pots by their handles, straight to their cabinets.
steps.expect: bottom rack empty; nothing dripped on.

steps.action: **Unload the top rack, tipping pooled water into the sink.** Glasses and cups get individual or two-at-a-time grasps, fragile rules in force: no glass-on-glass clinking, reduced speed, full control before release (`embodied/mobility/carry-and-deliver-an-item` step 6's release-is-commitment).
steps.expect: pooled water in the sink, not the floor; glasses shelved upright or rim-down per the cabinet's convention.

steps.action: **Unload cutlery by grasping handles, never blades.** Knives from the basket by their handles regardless of orientation (`load-a-dishwasher` step 5 put blades down; trust but verify by sight before reaching), sorted directly into the drawer's slots.
steps.expect: cutlery sorted, no blade grasped, drawer closed.

steps.action: **Wipe and close the machine.** A quick swipe of the door gasket's ledge where debris collects, filter checked if the machine's schedule calls for it, racks in, door closed, and the clean-indicator reset if the model has one.
steps.expect: machine empty, dry-ish, and unambiguously ready for dirty dishes, so the next person never plays the clean-or-dirty guessing game.

recipes.verification: The machine is empty with racks in and door closed, every item is dry, intact, and in its home (or staged-with-question), no blade was grasped, no water hit the floor, and the clean/dirty state of the machine is unambiguous to the next user.

recipes.title: use a pizza cutter
recipes.name: use-a-pizza-cutter
recipes.goal: Cut a pizza or flat baked item into portions using a rolling pizza cutter without dragging toppings or damaging the surface.

steps.action: **Grip the cutter handle.** Hold with the wheel vertical and fingers behind the guard or handle.
steps.expect: the wheel points down and away from hands.

steps.action: **Stabilize the pizza surface.** Hold the pan, board, or tray edge away from the cut line.
steps.expect: the pizza does not slide when touched by the wheel.

steps.action: **Place wheel at the crust edge.** Align the wheel with the intended diameter or cut path.
steps.expect: the cutter is perpendicular to the pizza surface.

steps.action: **Roll through with steady pressure.** Push from one edge to the opposite edge in a single line.
steps.expect: crust and toppings separate along the path.

steps.action: **Repeat for portions.** Rotate the board or change cutter angle for the next cut while keeping hands out of the wheel path.
steps.expect: slices have distinct boundaries.

steps.action: **Check and finish attached spots.** Re-roll only over connected cheese or crust, then lift the cutter clear.
steps.expect: each slice can separate without tearing adjacent slices.

recipes.verification: The pizza is divided into intended portions, each slice separates cleanly, and the cutter wheel has not contacted hands or an unsafe surface.

recipes.title: use kitchen tongs
recipes.name: use-kitchen-tongs
recipes.goal: Grip, lift, turn, or transfer a food item with kitchen tongs without dropping it or touching unsafe surfaces.

steps.action: **Pick up the tongs by the handles.** Grasp both handles near the hinge-facing half, keeping tips pointed away from faces and edges.
steps.expect: the tongs are held as one tool and the tips open and close when squeezed.

steps.action: **Test the closing force.** Squeeze until the tips meet, then relax until they open about 3 to 5 cm.
steps.expect: the spring action returns the tips open and the tool does not twist in the grip.

steps.action: **Approach the food from the sides.** Align the two tips around the widest stable part of the item, not under liquid or against the pan wall.
steps.expect: the food sits centered between the tong tips.

steps.action: **Clamp with just enough pressure.** Close until the food resists sliding, avoiding crushing soft items.
steps.expect: the food moves with the tongs during a 1 cm test lift.

steps.action: **Lift and move slowly.** Raise only high enough to clear the surface, keep the item over the pan or counter path, and rotate the wrist as needed.
steps.expect: the food stays captured and no drips or crumbs fall outside the work area.

steps.action: **Release at the destination.** Lower until the food touches the plate, bowl, or pan, then open the tips smoothly.
steps.expect: the food lands flat or in the intended orientation and the tongs come away cleanly.

recipes.verification: The food item is transferred, turned, or placed at the target location, and the tongs are still under control with no dropped item or unintended surface contact.

recipes.title: whisk eggs in a bowl
recipes.name: whisk-eggs-in-a-bowl
recipes.goal: Combine egg yolks and whites in a bowl into a uniform beaten mixture ready for cooking or baking.

steps.action: **Stabilize the bowl.** Place one hand or gripper on the bowl rim or side without touching the egg.
steps.expect: the bowl does not slide when lightly nudged.

steps.action: **Insert the whisk.** Hold the handle near its middle and lower the wires into the eggs at a shallow angle.
steps.expect: the whisk tip rests inside the liquid without scraping hard.

steps.action: **Break the yolks.** Press and drag the whisk through each yolk before fast motion.
steps.expect: yellow yolk begins spreading through the clear whites.

steps.action: **Whisk in small circles.** Move the wrist in tight circles while keeping the whisk tip below the liquid surface.
steps.expect: the mixture rotates in the bowl without splashing over the rim.

steps.action: **Scrape the bowl path.** Sweep around the inner wall and across the bottom to collect streaks of white.
steps.expect: no large transparent egg-white pockets remain along the sides.

steps.action: **Stop at uniform color.** Lift the whisk just above the surface and let liquid drip back into the bowl.
steps.expect: the eggs are evenly yellow and flow as one mixture.

recipes.verification: The bowl contains a shell-free egg mixture with uniform yellow color and no large clear streaks, and the counter is free of egg spills.

recipes.title: wipe a knife clean
recipes.name: wipe-a-knife-clean
recipes.goal: Residue is removed from both sides of a knife blade without contacting the cutting edge.

steps.action: **Set blade orientation.** Hold the knife by the handle with the cutting edge facing away from the wiping hand.
steps.expect: the edge is visible and points away from fingers and body.

steps.action: **Fold the cloth.** Fold the cloth into a thick pad wider than the blade height.
steps.expect: fingers can pinch cloth without protruding past its edge.

steps.action: **Place cloth on spine.** Lay the cloth over the dull spine side first, not over the cutting edge.
steps.expect: cloth covers the blade face while fingers remain above the spine.

steps.action: **Wipe first side.** Pinch lightly through the cloth near the spine and pull from handle toward tip.
steps.expect: residue transfers to the cloth in a straight pass.

steps.action: **Rotate safely.** Turn the knife so the opposite face is accessible while the edge still points away.
steps.expect: the cutting edge never faces the wiping hand.

steps.action: **Wipe second side.** Repeat handle-to-tip strokes with cloth pressure directed against the blade face, not across the edge.
steps.expect: visible residue leaves the second side.

steps.action: **Inspect without touch.** Hold the knife still and look along both faces for remaining food.
steps.expect: blade faces appear clean and dry enough for the next step.

steps.action: **Place the knife down.** Set it flat on the board or sink edge with blade fully supported. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* edge contact can cut skin or cloth, so never draw fingers along the edge.
steps.expect: knife is stationary with handle reachable.

recipes.verification: Both blade faces are visibly clean, the cutting edge was not touched, and the knife is resting flat with the handle accessible.

recipes.title: wipe down a countertop
recipes.name: wipe-down-a-countertop
recipes.goal: A kitchen counter cleared, wiped clean edge to edge including under the things that live on it, and left dry, the five-minute reset that keeps a kitchen trustworthy.

steps.action: **Clear the counter's working zones.** Dishes to the sink or machine, stray items to a temporary tray or their homes (`embodied/household/tidy-a-room`'s elsewhere-logic in miniature), small appliances slid aside or lifted.
steps.expect: bare surface in the zone being wiped; a tray of displaced items awaiting return.

steps.action: **Sweep the solids first, into a hand or straight off the edge into the bin held below.** Crumbs and chopping debris go to the bin, not onto the floor and not into the cloth's first stroke (a crumb under a wet cloth becomes a smear with grit). ⚠️ Check for blades before sweeping blind along cluttered counters: a knife under a towel is the kitchen's classic hand injury (`daily/home/wash-dishes-by-hand`'s soaking-blade rule, dry-land edition).
steps.expect: solids in the bin; no blade met by a sweeping palm.

steps.action: **Wipe systematically, back edge to front, in overlapping strokes.** Damp cloth or a light spray; work around the sink last (it is the dirtiest neighbor); include the backsplash's lower band and the counter's front lip, which catches drips invisibly.
steps.expect: uniform clean swath; the cloth visibly collecting rather than redistributing.

steps.action: **Lift, wipe under, replace.** The toaster, kettle (`daily/food/make-toast`'s crumb shadow lives here), jars, and boards each get their footprint wiped and go back; wiping around resident objects is the counter version of fake dusting (`daily/home/dust-a-room` step 2).
steps.expect: no crumb halos where appliances stand.

steps.action: **Deal with stuck spots by dwell, not force.** Dried sauce or syrup: park the wet cloth on it for a minute, then wipe; scraping with blades or green scourers wounds most surfaces.
steps.expect: fossils surrendering to patience; surface unscratched.

steps.action: **Dry pass and cloth exit.** A wrung cloth or dry towel pass leaves the counter dry (wet counters re-collect dust and spot stone); the cloth rinses, wrings, and hangs to dry, never balled wet in the sink.
steps.expect: dry counter, returned items, cloth drying open.

recipes.verification: The counter is dry, clean edge to edge including lips, backsplash band, and under residents; solids went to the bin; the cloth is rinsed and drying; and any raw-food zone got the disinfect upgrade with its cloth retired to the wash.

recipes.title: wring out a cloth
recipes.name: wring-out-a-cloth
recipes.goal: A wet cloth is wrung over the sink until damp rather than dripping, using opposing twists and a stable grip.

steps.action: **Move over the sink.** Hold the cloth fully above the basin before squeezing.
steps.expect: dripping water falls into the sink, not onto the floor.

steps.action: **Gather the cloth lengthwise.** Pull opposite corners or ends apart so the cloth forms a loose rope.
steps.expect: water collects along the twisted length.

steps.action: **Set hand positions.** Grip one end in each hand with thumbs wrapped around the cloth.
steps.expect: the cloth does not slip when lifted.

steps.action: **Twist opposite directions.** Rotate the right hand forward and the left hand backward, or the reverse.
steps.expect: the cloth tightens and water streams out.

steps.action: **Squeeze while twisting.** Maintain pressure for a few seconds at peak twist.
steps.expect: the water flow slows from stream to drops.

steps.action: **Relax and shift grip.** Release tension slightly, move hands closer to the wetter section, and twist again.
steps.expect: remaining water is driven from the middle.

steps.action: **Check drip level.** Hold the cloth above the sink without squeezing.
steps.expect: it drips slowly or not at all.

steps.action: **Repeat if needed.** For wiping, leave it damp; for storage, wring until only occasional drops fall.
steps.expect: the cloth matches the intended wetness.

steps.action: **Smooth or hang.** Shake the cloth open and place it where it can dry or be used.
steps.expect: it is not balled up and dripping.

recipes.verification: The cloth is damp to the intended level, does not leave a puddle when held still, and is placed for use or drying.

recipes.title: bag groceries at checkout
recipes.name: bag-groceries-at-checkout
recipes.goal: Groceries are packed into bags with heavy items low, fragile items protected, and each bag liftable.

steps.action: **Open one bag fully.** Grip opposite bag handles or edges and spread them apart on the bagging surface.
steps.expect: the bag mouth stays open and the base is flat.

steps.action: **Place heavy rigid items first.** Put cans, cartons, and jars upright at the bag bottom with close spacing.
steps.expect: the bag base is weighted evenly and does not tip.

steps.action: **Add medium items around gaps.** Place boxes and firm packages beside the heavy items without crushing soft items.
steps.expect: items support each other and remain below the bag rim.

steps.action: **Reserve fragile items.** Keep eggs, bread, chips, and soft produce out until the top layer.
steps.expect: fragile items remain outside the compression zone.

steps.action: **Place fragile items on top.** Lower them gently with broad support under the package.
steps.expect: fragile items sit above heavier items without deformation.

steps.action: **Check bag weight.** Lift the handles 2-5 cm with steady force, then set down if heavy.
steps.expect: the bag lifts without tearing and weight feels manageable.

steps.action: **Start another bag if needed.** Open a new bag before the current bag bulges or exceeds comfortable weight.
steps.expect: each bag remains upright and not overfilled.

steps.action: **Stage finished bags.** Move completed bags by handles and base support to the cart or pickup area.
steps.expect: bags stand upright and contents do not spill.

recipes.verification: Each bag can be lifted by its handles without tearing, heavy items are at the bottom, and fragile items are uncrushed at the top or in a separate bag.

recipes.title: board a bus with a mobility aid
recipes.name: board-a-bus-with-a-mobility-aid
recipes.goal: Board a bus while using a wheelchair, walker, scooter, cane, or similar mobility aid, then settle in a safe riding position.

steps.action: **Wait in the boarding zone.** Position where the driver can see the mobility aid without blocking exiting passengers.
steps.expect: the bus can stop with the front or accessible door near you.

steps.action: **Signal the driver.** Raise a hand, make eye contact, or move toward the marked accessible boarding point.
steps.expect: the driver stops and prepares the kneeling bus, ramp, or lift if needed.

steps.action: **Let passengers exit first.** Hold position until the doorway and ramp path are clear.
steps.expect: no one is crossing the threshold toward you.

steps.action: **Align with the ramp or step.** Face straight toward the entry path and keep wheels, cane tip, or walker feet centered.
steps.expect: the aid is square to the ramp or first step.

steps.action: **Board at controlled speed.** [BRANCH: ramp | no ramp] use the ramp slowly, or step up only if the aid and body can clear the step safely.
steps.expect: all wheels, feet, and carried items are inside the bus.

steps.action: **Pay or confirm fare.** Tap the card, show pass, or follow the driver's instruction before moving deeper into the bus.
steps.expect: fare reader or driver indicates acceptance.

steps.action: **Move to the secure area.** Take the shortest clear path to a priority seat, securement area, or open standing space.
steps.expect: the aid is out of the aisle as much as possible.

steps.action: **Stabilize for travel.** Lock brakes, hold a rail, sit if appropriate, and accept securement straps when required. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* bus motion can begin before balance is recovered; confirm the body and aid are stable before releasing support.
steps.expect: the bus can move without the aid rolling or tipping.

recipes.verification: The rider and mobility aid are fully inside the correct bus, fare is accepted or acknowledged, and the rider is seated, secured, or braced outside the doorway and main aisle.

recipes.title: carry a hot drink
recipes.name: carry-a-hot-drink
recipes.goal: Carry a hot drink from one surface to another without spilling, burning anyone, or dropping the cup.

steps.action: **Check fill level.** Leave headroom below the rim, especially for walking through people or over thresholds.
steps.expect: liquid sits below the rim and can slosh without immediately spilling.

steps.action: **Secure the lid if used.** Press around the lid edge and align the sip opening away from the carry hand.
steps.expect: the lid does not lift when lightly nudged.

steps.action: **Dry the outside.** Wipe drips from the cup, lid, and bottom.
steps.expect: the grip surface is dry enough not to slip.

steps.action: **Choose the grip.** Hold the handle if present, or wrap fingers around the insulated sleeve or cup body below the rim.
steps.expect: the cup feels balanced without squeezing hard.

steps.action: **Use a saucer or second hand if needed.** For a fragile mug or brimful drink, support from below with a saucer or second hand.
steps.expect: the cup is steadier before it leaves the table.

steps.action: **Lift vertically first.** Raise the cup a few centimeters and pause.
steps.expect: no drip, tilt, or lid shift appears.

steps.action: **Scan the path.** Look for rugs, cords, door thresholds, pets, children, and people turning unexpectedly.
steps.expect: you know where to slow or reroute.

steps.action: **Walk smoothly.** Keep the cup near torso height, elbow slightly bent, and eyes alternating between path and drink surface.
steps.expect: the liquid surface moves gently rather than sloshing up the sides.

steps.action: **Slow near people.** Give space, announce "hot drink" if someone may bump you, and pause for sudden crossings.
steps.expect: nearby humans have time to adjust.

steps.action: **Set down before release.** Place the cup fully on the destination surface, confirm it is stable, then let go.
steps.expect: the base is flat on the surface before fingers open.

recipes.verification: The hot drink reaches the destination surface upright, with no spill, no burn, and fingers released only after stable set-down.

recipes.title: carry a tray of drinks
recipes.name: carry-a-tray-of-drinks
recipes.goal: Carry multiple drinks on a tray to a destination without spilling, dropping glassware, or bumping people.

steps.action: **Arrange drinks near the tray center.** Place heavier or fuller cups closest to the middle and leave edges clear.
steps.expect: the tray does not tip when lightly nudged.

steps.action: **Wipe wet bases.** Dry cup bottoms and tray surface before lifting.
steps.expect: cups do not slide when the tray tilts slightly.

steps.action: **Choose the carry grip.** Use two hands under or at opposite sides of the tray.
steps.expect: wrists can keep the tray level.

steps.action: **Lift straight up and pause.** Raise the tray a few centimeters before walking.
steps.expect: no cup slides, tips, or leaks.

steps.action: **Scan the path.** Identify doors, people, pets, rugs, and tight turns before moving.
steps.expect: a clear route or waiting point is known.

steps.action: **Walk slowly with level tray.** Keep the tray near torso height and turn the body instead of twisting wrists.
steps.expect: drink surfaces ripple but do not reach rims.

steps.action: **Set the tray down fully.** Place it on the destination surface before removing any drink.
steps.expect: the tray is stable and supported.

steps.action: **Deliver drinks one at a time.** Move each cup by its safest grip point and confirm the recipient or table supports it before release.
steps.expect: each drink ends upright and controlled.

recipes.verification: All drinks arrive upright on the destination table or in recipients' hands, with no broken glass, burn, or active spill.

recipes.title: carry and deliver an item
recipes.name: carry-and-deliver-an-item
recipes.goal: A specified item is picked up from its source, transported along a route, and placed at its destination — intact, upright where required, and confirmed received where a person is the destination.

steps.action: **Inspect the item and plan the grasp.** Rigid box → side or underside grip; open container/liquid → upright two-point hold; bag → handles; plate → underhand palm. Note "this side up" implications.
steps.expect: a grasp plan matched to the item class and a route in mind including doors.

steps.action: **Lift correctly.** Close to the body/chassis, load over your base, knees not back (humans), both contact points engaged before full weight transfer.
steps.expect: item fully supported and stable before the first step; no slip at the interface.

steps.action: **Set the carry posture.** Load held close, sight line kept *over* the load (never carry what blinds you), liquids level, fragiles cushioned against the body not swinging free.
steps.expect: you can see the path; the item doesn't oscillate when you walk.

steps.action: **Navigate at load-appropriate speed.** Slow around corners and people (announce "behind you"/"excuse me" in shared spaces), wide berth from walls and furniture, extra caution at level changes (thresholds, ramps).
steps.expect: progress without contact; liquid surfaces staying calm is the live telemetry.

steps.action: **Handle doors per `embodied/open-a-door`'s loaded-carry branch.** Set down to operate if the door demands a hand you don't have.
steps.expect: through each door with item and door both controlled; nothing pinched in a closer.

steps.action: **Place, don't drop, at the destination.** Lower until the surface takes the weight, verify stability (no rocking, not overhanging the edge, clear of being knocked), *then* release the grasp. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* release is commitment — fragile items broken at placement break at exactly this instant; confirm support before letting go.
steps.expect: item at rest, stable, correctly oriented, at the agreed spot.

steps.action: **Person-destination variant: transfer or announce.** Hand over only into a ready grip ("got it?" → confirmed hold → release), or place nearby and announce: "Your coffee's on the desk."
steps.expect: recipient acknowledges; custody transferred unambiguously.

recipes.verification: The item sits stable and intact at the destination (or in the recipient's confirmed grip), oriented correctly, nothing was spilled or struck en route, and the recipient/requester knows delivery occurred.

recipes.title: climb stairs with a load
recipes.name: climb-stairs-with-a-load
recipes.goal: A carried load is moved up (or down) a staircase without a fall, a dropped item, or a strain, keeping one hand free for the rail and clear sight of each step.

steps.action: **Assess the load against the free-hand rule.** If you cannot hold the load and still free one hand for the rail, stop and rebalance: split the load, use a backpack, or get help.
steps.expect: one hand committed to the load, one hand available for the rail.

steps.action: **Shape the load for sightlines.** Carry it on the hip or to one side, not stacked in front of your face. You must see the tread edge of every step.
steps.expect: an unobstructed downward line of sight to the next two steps.

steps.action: **Set the load onto the rail side you will not use, or the opposite.** Hold the load on the side away from the rail so the free hand meets the rail cleanly.
steps.expect: rail-side hand empty and tracking the rail; load-side hand bearing the weight.

steps.action: **Establish the rail before the first step.** Grip the rail at the bottom newel before lifting a foot.
steps.expect: firm rail contact established while both feet are still on level ground.

steps.action: **Climb one step at a time, leading consistently.** Plant the full foot on each tread, not just the ball on the edge; slide the rail hand up in pace with each step rather than reaching ahead. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a missed edge with a load is how stair falls happen; never take two treads at once while loaded, and never let the load block your view of the next edge.
steps.expect: each foot lands flat and centered on its tread; rail contact never breaks.

steps.action: **Rest at landings, not mid-flight.** [BRANCH: single flight → climb through | multiple flights or heavy load → set the load down at each landing, breathe, regrip] On a long or heavy carry, use landings to reset grip and posture.
steps.expect: on multi-flight climbs, a controlled pause with the load set down on the flat landing, never balanced on a step.

steps.action: **Clear the top or bottom fully before releasing the rail.** Step onto the level surface with both feet before letting go and repositioning the load.
steps.expect: both feet on level ground, then rail released, then load set down or carried onward.

recipes.verification: The load reached the destination floor intact; at no point were both hands off the rail while loaded on the stairs; every step was taken one tread at a time with a flat footing; rests happened on flat landings, not on treads; no fall, drop, or strain occurred.

recipes.title: cross a street
recipes.name: cross-a-street
recipes.goal: You (or a sidewalk robot) get from one side of a street to the other at a legal crossing point, with every approaching-traffic check actually performed — the procedure everyone "knows" and fatalities keep proving isn't followed.

steps.action: **Position at the crossing point, on the curb, facing traffic-side first.** Stand back from the curb edge (mirrors and turning trucks overhang it); locate the signal or assess the street type.
steps.expect: you know which crossing regime applies: signal, zebra priority, or gap-judgment.

steps.action: **Signalized: press the button (where present) and wait for the walk signal — *and then still check*.** The green man grants right-of-way, not physics: turning vehicles cross the crosswalk on your green in most road systems.
steps.expect: walk signal lit *and* the turning lanes visibly yielding before your first step.

steps.action: **Look in the full sequence: near-lane direction, far-lane direction, near-lane again — plus the over-the-shoulder turn check.** (Left-right-left in right-driving countries; right-left-right in left-driving ones — see Variations for the tourist trap.) Listen between looks; electric vehicles defeat ears.
steps.expect: every lane you'll cross has been personally verified empty or stopping.

steps.action: **Make eye contact / confirm yielding with any near vehicle.** A slowing car with a visible driver looking at you is yielding; a car whose driver you can't see hasn't agreed to anything. At zebra crossings, priority is *taken by confirmation*, not assumed.
steps.expect: mutual acknowledgment with the nearest threat vehicle, or you wait.

steps.action: **Cross briskly and straight — no diagonal, no stopping, no phone.** Continue scanning the far lanes as you go; walk, don't run (running trades observation and footing for seconds).
steps.expect: steady progress; each lane re-checked as you enter it.

steps.action: **Handle the mid-crossing signal change without panic.** Flashing/countdown while you're in the road: continue at pace to the far side (or the refuge island where present) — the clearance interval is designed for exactly you. Never reverse mid-street on impulse.
steps.expect: far curb reached; done.

recipes.verification: You're on the far curb having crossed at a crossing point, with the walk signal (or confirmed yields) obtained, the full look-sequence performed including the turn check, and no step of it delegated to assumption, right-of-way, or headphones.

recipes.title: enter and exit a car
recipes.name: enter-and-exit-a-car
recipes.goal: You enter a parked car, seat yourself, and buckle in, then later exit safely onto a clear space, without a door strike, a fall, or stepping into traffic.

steps.action: **Check the door-swing zone before opening.** Glance for passing cyclists, cars, other opening doors, and low posts or curbs the door edge could hit. On the traffic side, this check is the difference between a routine exit and a dooring.
steps.expect: clear arc for the door swing; no approaching bike or vehicle in the lane beside the door.

steps.action: **Open the door only as far as needed.** Wide enough to enter, not flung to its stop where it can strike an adjacent car or spring back on a slope.
steps.expect: door held at a controlled opening; it stays where you put it.

steps.action: **Enter seat-first, not head-first.** Turn your back to the seat opening, lower onto the seat edge, then pivot both legs in together as a unit. Leading with the head or one leg is how people bang their skull on the frame or half-miss the seat.
steps.expect: you are seated on the cushion with both feet swinging in as a pair, head clearing the frame.

steps.action: **Settle and clear the door path.** Feet and clothing fully inside; check no coat hem, bag strap, or belt is in the door gap.
steps.expect: nothing crossing the door threshold.
