recipes.name: check-your-credit-report
recipes.goal: Review your credit report for accuracy, understand which items help or hurt credit, and start disputes for errors or signs of identity theft.

steps.action: **Use the official free source.** Go to the government-approved or bureau-approved free annual credit report site, not an ad or paid monitoring page.
steps.expect: you can request reports without buying a score or subscription.

steps.action: **Request the right bureau reports.** Choose one or all available credit bureaus depending on your review plan.
steps.expect: you know which bureau's file you are reading.

steps.action: **Verify identity carefully.** Answer identity questions and avoid guessing if a question appears unfamiliar.
steps.expect: the report opens or gives a clear next step for manual verification.

steps.action: **Save the report securely.** Download or print the report to a private location before leaving the session.
steps.expect: you can review it later without logging in again.

steps.action: **Read personal information.** Check name variations, addresses, employers, birth date, and identity numbers where shown.
steps.expect: old but accurate history is separated from wrong or suspicious identity data.

steps.action: **Review account sections.** Check each loan, card, balance, limit, payment status, open date, closed date, and ownership type.
steps.expect: every account is yours and reported accurately.

steps.action: **Review inquiries and public records.** Look for recent hard inquiries, collections, bankruptcies, judgments where applicable, or other negative items.
steps.expect: unfamiliar or outdated items are marked for action.

steps.action: **Classify what helps and hurts.** Identify on-time payments, low balances, long account history, and healthy account mix as helpful; late payments, high utilization, collections, defaults, and unnecessary hard inquiries as harmful.
steps.expect: you know which items affect creditworthiness.

steps.action: **Dispute errors.** [BRANCH: bureau error | creditor error] submit a bureau dispute for wrong report data; contact the creditor or collector when the source is reporting bad information.
steps.expect: you receive a confirmation number or written dispute record.

steps.action: **Set a review frequency.** Schedule periodic checks, commonly at least annually and more often after identity theft, denied credit, major loans, or disputes.
steps.expect: the next review date is on your calendar.

recipes.verification: Each available report has been saved, personal data and account sections have been reviewed, errors are either absent or disputed, and the next review date is scheduled.

recipes.title: choose a bank account
recipes.name: choose-a-bank-account
recipes.goal: Choose a bank account that fits your habits, minimizes avoidable fees, and provides the access and protections you need.

steps.action: **Define the account job.** Decide what the account must do, such as receive pay, pay bills, hold savings, use cash, or separate spending.
steps.expect: the required account type is clear.

steps.action: **List your habits.** Count expected monthly card purchases, ATM withdrawals, transfers, checks, cash deposits, and overseas transactions.
steps.expect: your likely usage pattern is written down.

steps.action: **Compare monthly fees.** Check maintenance fees, waiver rules, minimum balance, direct deposit requirements, and inactivity fees.
steps.expect: you know the realistic monthly cost.

steps.action: **Check access.** Compare branches, ATMs, cash deposit options, mobile check deposit, phone support, and app reliability.
steps.expect: the account can handle your normal access needs.

steps.action: **Review transaction fees.** Check ATM surcharges, foreign transaction fees, overdraft fees, wire fees, check fees, and transfer limits.
steps.expect: expensive mismatches are identified.

steps.action: **Assess interest and rewards.** Compare rate, balance caps, rewards conditions, and whether requirements fit your habits.
steps.expect: promotional benefits are separated from durable value.

steps.action: **Confirm deposit protection.** Verify the bank or credit union is covered by the relevant deposit protection scheme and note the limit.
steps.expect: you know what amount is protected.

steps.action: **Plan the switch.** List deposits, bill payments, subscriptions, linked wallets, and old account closure steps.
steps.expect: the move will not interrupt essential payments.

steps.action: **Open only after reviewing terms.** Submit the application through the official channel after checking fees, privacy terms, and eligibility.
steps.expect: you receive an approval, denial, or request for documents.

recipes.verification: The chosen account's fees, access, interest, protection limit, eligibility, and switching checklist are documented before opening or switching.

recipes.title: choose a credit card
recipes.name: choose-a-credit-card
recipes.goal: Choose a credit card whose fees, rewards, protections, and approval odds fit your spending habits and repayment plan.

steps.action: **Define the use case.** Choose one primary purpose: cash back, travel rewards, balance transfer, building credit, business spend, or low ongoing cost.
steps.expect: card comparisons are limited to one main goal.

steps.action: **Estimate monthly spending.** Use statements to total groceries, dining, gas, travel, online shopping, and other categories.
steps.expect: rewards can be estimated from real spending.

steps.action: **Screen fees and rates.** Compare annual fee, foreign transaction fee, late fee, balance transfer fee, cash advance fee, purchase APR, and penalty APR.
steps.expect: expensive cards are removed unless benefits justify the cost.

steps.action: **Read reward rules.** Check earning categories, caps, redemption value, expiration, transfer partners, and signup-bonus requirements.
steps.expect: expected rewards exceed fees under realistic spending.

steps.action: **Check protections and usability.** Review fraud protections, purchase protection, travel insurance, rental coverage, app controls, autopay, and accepted networks.
steps.expect: must-have features are present.

steps.action: **Check eligibility.** Use issuer prequalification if available and read credit-profile or banking-relationship requirements.
steps.expect: approval odds are reasonable before a hard application.

steps.action: **Apply only when ready.** Submit the official application with accurate identity, income, housing, and contact information. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a submitted application may create a hard credit inquiry, so confirm terms and eligibility first.
steps.expect: approval, denial, or pending review status is shown.

steps.action: **Set up controls.** If approved, enable autopay, alerts, app lock, and secure storage before using the card.
steps.expect: payment and fraud controls are active.

recipes.verification: The chosen card has documented fees, reward rules, protections, approval result, and autopay or payment reminder set before regular use.

recipes.title: choose a health insurance plan
recipes.name: choose-a-health-insurance-plan
recipes.goal: Compare health insurance plans using expected care, provider access, drug coverage, premiums, and total possible cost before enrolling.

steps.action: **List expected care.** Write down regular doctors, prescriptions, planned procedures, therapy, labs, urgent care needs, and dependents.
steps.expect: your comparison reflects actual use, not just premiums.

steps.action: **Gather plan documents.** Open each plan's summary of benefits, provider directory, formulary, premium, deductible, out-of-pocket maximum, copays, and coinsurance.
steps.expect: all plan inputs are visible side by side.

steps.action: **Check provider networks.** Search each doctor, facility, and pharmacy by exact name and location.
steps.expect: each important provider is marked in-network, out-of-network, or uncertain.

steps.action: **Check prescriptions.** Search drug name, dosage, quantity, tier, prior authorization, step therapy, and preferred pharmacy rules.
steps.expect: monthly medication cost and restrictions are known.

steps.action: **Estimate normal-year cost.** Add annual premiums plus expected copays, coinsurance, deductible spending, and prescription costs.
steps.expect: each plan has an estimated yearly cost.

steps.action: **Estimate bad-year cost.** Add annual premiums plus the in-network out-of-pocket maximum, and note separate out-of-network exposure.
steps.expect: worst-case affordable risk is visible.

steps.action: **Compare plan type rules.** [BRANCH: HMO | PPO | EPO | HDHP] note referrals, out-of-network coverage, network limits, and HSA eligibility.
steps.expect: tradeoffs are clear beyond price.

steps.action: **Verify subsidies and tax effects.** If using a marketplace or employer benefit, check premium credits, employer contribution, payroll deduction, and HSA or FSA options.
steps.expect: the net monthly cost is realistic.

steps.action: **Enroll before the deadline.** Select the plan only after confirming household members, start date, premium, doctors, drugs, and payment setup. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* after the enrollment window closes, changing plans usually requires a qualifying event.
steps.expect: you receive enrollment confirmation and plan ID or pending payment instructions.

recipes.verification: You have an enrollment confirmation for the selected plan and a comparison showing premium, deductible, out-of-pocket maximum, key providers, key drugs, and estimated annual cost.

recipes.title: choose renters insurance
recipes.name: choose-renters-insurance
recipes.goal: Choose renters insurance with suitable personal property, liability, loss-of-use coverage, deductible, and proof for a landlord if required.

steps.action: **Check lease requirements.** Read required liability limit, named interested party, address format, and coverage start date.
steps.expect: landlord requirements are recorded.

steps.action: **Estimate belongings.** Walk through rooms and estimate replacement cost for furniture, electronics, clothing, kitchen items, and valuables.
steps.expect: a personal property limit target is set.

steps.action: **Choose coverage basis.** Compare replacement cost against actual cash value for personal property.
steps.expect: depreciation treatment is understood.

steps.action: **Set liability and loss-of-use limits.** Choose liability, medical payments, and additional living expense coverage that meets lease and household needs.
steps.expect: major limits are selected.

steps.action: **Review exclusions and add-ons.** Check flood, earthquake, business property, jewelry, bikes, pets, water backup, and roommate treatment.
steps.expect: gaps are marked before purchase.

steps.action: **Compare quotes.** Compare premium, deductible, coverage limits, discounts, claims reputation, and bundling without lowering required coverage.
steps.expect: one quote is selected with reasons.

steps.action: **Buy the policy.** Submit the application and payment through the insurer or agent. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* coverage and payment start based on the submitted application, so confirm address, dates, limits, and interested party first.
steps.expect: declarations page and proof of insurance are available.

steps.action: **Send proof and save inventory.** Send required proof to the landlord and store the policy with photos or inventory of belongings.
steps.expect: landlord proof is sent and records are saved.

recipes.verification: The active policy declarations show the correct rental address, effective date, required liability limit, chosen property limit, deductible, and landlord proof if required.

recipes.title: compare savings accounts
recipes.name: compare-savings-accounts
recipes.goal: Compare savings accounts by rate, access, taxes, protection limits, and switching friction without treating the highest headline rate as automatically best.

steps.action: **Define access needs.** Decide whether the money is emergency cash, short-term savings, tax-reserved funds, or long-term cash reserve.
steps.expect: the acceptable withdrawal delay is clear.

steps.action: **Collect comparable rates.** Record annual rate, compounding basis, balance bands, and whether the rate is variable or fixed.
steps.expect: each account has a comparable rate entry.

steps.action: **Identify introductory rates.** Check bonus periods, end dates, qualifying deposits, and what rate applies afterward.
steps.expect: temporary rate boosts are marked.

steps.action: **Check withdrawal rules.** Review notice periods, limited withdrawals, penalties, minimum balance, and transfer limits.
steps.expect: access restrictions are visible before opening.

steps.action: **Calculate realistic earnings.** Estimate interest after fees and after any expected rate drop.
steps.expect: the likely annual benefit is stated in currency, not just percent.

steps.action: **Consider tax on interest.** Check whether interest is taxable, whether withholding applies, and whether tax-advantaged wrappers exist.
steps.expect: likely tax treatment is noted for your jurisdiction.

steps.action: **Confirm protection limits.** Verify deposit insurance or guarantee coverage, institution identity, and whether multiple brands share one license.
steps.expect: your planned balance is within or above the protected amount.

steps.action: **Plan the switch.** Check transfer method, linked account rules, account closure process, and time out of market.
steps.expect: the practical work to move funds is known.

steps.action: **Move a test amount first.** Transfer a small amount before moving larger cash.
steps.expect: the receiving account details and withdrawal path are confirmed.

recipes.verification: Each candidate account has documented rate, access rules, intro period, tax note, protection limit, fees, and switching steps.

recipes.title: contest a collections notice
recipes.name: contest-a-collections-notice
recipes.goal: Dispute or validate a collections notice before paying, while preserving deadlines, evidence, and consumer rights.

steps.action: **Do not admit or pay immediately.** Save the notice and avoid discussing payment until you identify the debt.
steps.expect: you have not restarted avoidable risk through rushed statements or payments.

steps.action: **Verify the collector.** Use the collector's official website, licensing lookup, or original creditor contact information instead of caller-provided pressure.
steps.expect: you know whether the contact appears legitimate.

steps.action: **Record notice details.** Write the date received, amount, original creditor, collector name, account number, and response deadline.
steps.expect: the timeline is clear.

steps.action: **Request validation in writing.** Send a debt validation or dispute letter through a trackable method, asking for creditor, amount, itemization, authority to collect, and judgment status.
steps.expect: you have proof of your dispute or validation request.

steps.action: **Compare records.** Check bills, EOBs, receipts, cancellation confirmations, return tracking, and bank statements against the claimed amount.
steps.expect: valid, invalid, paid, duplicate, or identity-theft issues are identified.

steps.action: **Check credit reports.** Look for the collection account and dispute inaccurate reporting with bureaus if needed.
steps.expect: credit-report impact is documented.

steps.action: **Choose a response.** [BRANCH: not yours | already paid | amount wrong | valid debt] dispute, send proof, request correction, negotiate, or plan payment.
steps.expect: your action matches the evidence.

steps.action: **Get any agreement in writing.** If settling or paying, require the collector's written terms, amount, due date, account release, and reporting treatment before sending money. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* payments or settlement admissions can affect legal and credit rights, so confirm the debt and terms first.
steps.expect: no money leaves until terms are documented.

steps.action: **Save final proof.** Keep validation, dispute letters, receipts, settlement letter, deletion or correction notices, and credit-report updates.
steps.expect: you can defend against duplicate collection.

recipes.verification: You have written validation, a written dispute record, correction confirmation, or a signed payment or settlement agreement that identifies the exact debt and outcome.

recipes.title: create a simple budget
recipes.name: create-a-simple-budget
recipes.goal: You have a written monthly budget where income minus fixed costs leaves a known amount, that amount is split into a few spending caps, and a short weekly check keeps you inside them.

steps.action: **Write down net monthly income.** Use what actually lands in the account, after tax and deductions. Irregular income: use the lowest of the last three months, not the average.
steps.expect: one income number you would bet on.

steps.action: **List fixed costs and total them.** Rent/mortgage, utilities, insurance, loan and phone payments, subscriptions. Pull them straight off statements so none are forgotten.
steps.expect: a fixed-cost total; every line traceable to a real transaction.

steps.action: **Compute the leftover.** Income minus fixed costs. This is what is genuinely yours to allocate.
steps.expect: a positive number. Zero or negative → F1.

steps.action: **Carve out savings first, before spending caps.** Move a fixed slice (even 5-10%) to the top, treated like a bill, not what happens to survive the month.
steps.expect: a savings figure subtracted from the leftover.

steps.action: **Split the rest into a few category caps.** Keep it to 4-6 buckets (groceries, transport, eating out, everyday/fun). Fewer buckets get followed; twenty do not.
steps.expect: caps summing to the post-savings leftover, no bucket left uncovered.

steps.action: **Set up the weekly check ritual.** Pick a fixed 10-minute slot (Sunday works). Open the app/statement, tally the week's spend per bucket, compare to a quarter of each cap.
steps.expect: a recurring calendar reminder and a first tally done.

steps.action: **Adjust caps after one real month, not mid-week.** If groceries always overrun and eating-out is always under, move the money between them. The budget serves you.
steps.expect: month-two caps that match how you actually live.

recipes.verification: A written budget exists where income minus fixed costs minus savings equals the sum of your category caps, and at least one weekly check has been completed with actual spend compared against the caps.

recipes.title: dispute a card charge
recipes.name: dispute-a-card-charge
recipes.goal: An incorrect, fraudulent, or undelivered-goods charge on your card is formally disputed, and the dispute is tracked to a credit or a justified rejection.

steps.action: **Classify the charge.** [BRANCH: fraud (you never transacted) → skip to step 3 | merchant error (wrong amount, duplicate, goods not delivered/not as described) → step 2] Decode the merchant string first — many "unknown" charges are legitimate with unfamiliar billing names; search the string before crying fraud.
steps.expect: a confident classification.

steps.action: **Attempt merchant resolution and document it.** Contact merchant support, state the problem, request a refund; save the ticket/emails and give them the stated response window.
steps.expect: either a refund (done once it posts on a statement; no dispute is filed) or a documented refusal/non-response, which the dispute will require.

steps.action: **For fraud: freeze the card immediately.** In the banking app: lock/freeze the card, then request a replacement.
steps.expect: card locked; further charges impossible.

steps.action: **Open the dispute with the issuer.** Banking app/site → the transaction → "Dispute charge", or call the number on the card. Provide the classification, the story, and upload the evidence from steps 1–2.
steps.expect: a dispute case number and a stated timeline.

steps.action: **Answer follow-up requests promptly.** Issuers may mail/message questionnaires; missing their deadlines forfeits the dispute.
steps.expect: every issuer request answered within its window; case shows "under review".

steps.action: **Track the provisional credit.** Many issuers credit the amount provisionally during investigation.
steps.expect: a provisional credit line on the statement (not guaranteed in all jurisdictions).

steps.action: **Receive the outcome.** *Note:* a first credit is not final. A resolved-in-your-favor dispute can still be reversed if the merchant provides counter-evidence, so keep your evidence until the written final-resolution notice.
steps.expect: written resolution: permanent credit, or rejection with reasons.

steps.action: **If rejected and you disagree: escalate.** Request the merchant's counter-evidence, rebut in writing, and if the issuer won't move, complain to the financial regulator/ombudsman for your jurisdiction.
steps.expect: an escalation case with its own timeline.

recipes.verification: Either the merchant's refund posted on a statement with no dispute needed, or the dispute case shows final resolution: a permanent credit for the full disputed amount (or a reasoned rejection you accepted). For fraud cases, the compromised card is dead and its recurring billers migrated.

recipes.title: dispute a credit report error
recipes.name: dispute-a-credit-report-error
recipes.goal: File a documented dispute for inaccurate credit report information and track the bureau or furnisher response to correction, deletion, or verified status.

steps.action: **Get the current report.** Download or save the report showing bureau name, report date, and disputed item.
steps.expect: the error is visible in a saved report.

steps.action: **Define the error.** Write the exact field that is wrong and the correction requested.
steps.expect: the dispute issue fits in one clear sentence.

steps.action: **Gather evidence.** Attach statements, payment records, identity documents, court records, fraud reports, or creditor letters that prove the correction.
steps.expect: each claim has supporting evidence.

steps.action: **Submit to the bureau.** Use the bureau's official dispute portal or mail address and include identifying information, report item, explanation, and evidence.
steps.expect: a dispute confirmation number or mailing proof is saved.

steps.action: **Notify the furnisher if useful.** Send the same dispute to the creditor, collector, or lender reporting the error.
steps.expect: the furnisher has written notice and evidence.

steps.action: **Track investigation timeline.** Calendar the bureau's expected response date and monitor mail, email, and portal messages.
steps.expect: follow-up requests are not missed.

steps.action: **Review the result.** Read whether the item was corrected, deleted, updated, or verified as accurate.
steps.expect: the bureau's decision and updated report are saved.

steps.action: **Escalate if unresolved.** If evidence was ignored, resubmit with clearer documents, add a consumer statement, or complain to the regulator for your jurisdiction.
steps.expect: a second dispute or complaint record exists.

recipes.verification: The bureau response and updated report show the inaccurate item corrected or deleted, or you have a written verified decision with next escalation documented.

recipes.title: dispute a medical bill
recipes.name: dispute-a-medical-bill
recipes.goal: Challenge an incorrect medical bill by comparing itemized charges, insurance records, and provider billing details.

steps.action: **Do not pay blindly.** Pause payment until you understand the charge and deadline.
steps.expect: the account remains unpaid or partially unpaid while under review.

steps.action: **Request an itemized bill.** Ask the provider for line-item charges, codes, dates, and payments already applied.
steps.expect: you receive more detail than a balance-only statement.

steps.action: **Get the insurance EOB.** Download the explanation of benefits for the same date of service.
steps.expect: the EOB shows billed amount, allowed amount, insurer paid, adjustments, and patient responsibility.

steps.action: **Match bill to EOB.** Compare provider, date, patient name, procedure codes, and patient responsibility.
steps.expect: mismatches or correct balances are visible.

steps.action: **Check common errors.** Look for duplicate charges, wrong date, canceled appointment, wrong insurance, out-of-network surprise, or services not received.
steps.expect: each suspected error is written down with evidence.

steps.action: **Call provider billing.** Use the phone number on the provider's official site or patient portal.
steps.expect: billing can see the account and explain the charge.

steps.action: **Ask for a hold.** Request that collections and late fees pause while the dispute is reviewed.
steps.expect: the representative notes the account as disputed or on hold.

steps.action: **Submit the dispute in writing.** Send the itemized error list, EOB, receipts, referral, authorization, or coverage proof through the portal or certified mail.
steps.expect: you receive confirmation or a ticket number.

steps.action: **Contact the insurer if needed.** Ask whether the claim was processed correctly and whether the provider must rebill.
steps.expect: the insurer explains approval, denial, appeal, or rebilling steps.

steps.action: **Negotiate valid balances.** If the corrected balance is real, ask for financial assistance, self-pay discount, prompt-pay discount, or a payment plan.
steps.expect: any discount or plan appears in writing.

steps.action: **Appeal before deadlines.** File provider or insurance appeals by the stated date.
steps.expect: the appeal confirmation includes date received and review timeline.

steps.action: **Pay only the resolved amount.** Pay through the official portal after corrections are posted. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* paying can make later corrections harder, so keep the dispute record and confirm the amount first.
steps.expect: the receipt matches the corrected balance or payment plan.

recipes.verification: The provider or insurer sends a corrected bill, written denial, approved appeal, or payment-plan agreement that matches your records and states the remaining balance.

recipes.title: do a no spend month
recipes.name: do-a-no-spend-month
recipes.goal: Run a one-month spending reset that pauses non-essential purchases, protects required expenses, and redirects saved money to a chosen goal.

steps.action: **Define the purpose.** Choose one reason such as emergency fund, debt payoff, overspending reset, or saving for a known expense.
steps.expect: the month has a measurable goal.

steps.action: **Write allowed spending.** List rent, utilities, groceries, medicine, fuel, transit, childcare, pet needs, minimum debt payments, and other true essentials.
steps.expect: necessary spending is protected.

steps.action: **Write paused spending.** List restaurants, clothing, decor, apps, entertainment, impulse shopping, delivery, and upgrades that will wait.
steps.expect: non-essential categories are clear.

steps.action: **Plan substitutes.** Use pantry meals, library resources, free activities, wish lists, repair, borrowing, or delayed purchases.
steps.expect: common temptations have alternatives.

steps.action: **Remove frictionless spending.** Pause shopping apps, unsubscribe from sale emails, remove saved cards where practical, and set alerts.
steps.expect: impulse purchases require extra effort.

steps.action: **Track every purchase.** Record amount, category, and whether it was allowed or paused.
steps.expect: spending is visible during the month.

steps.action: **Move saved money.** Transfer the avoided amount or a weekly target to the chosen savings or debt goal.
steps.expect: progress is captured instead of absorbed by other spending.

steps.action: **Close the month.** Review what worked, what was unrealistic, and which habits to keep.
steps.expect: final savings and lessons are documented.

recipes.verification: At month end, the spending log shows allowed and paused categories, the target account or debt received the planned saved amount, and any rule changes are documented.

recipes.title: exchange currency
recipes.name: exchange-currency
recipes.goal: You obtain foreign currency (as cash, or spending power on a card) at close to the real exchange rate, with the true cost of fees understood, and without being skinned at an airport desk.

steps.action: **Look up the mid-market rate.** Search the currency pair to get the real rate before anyone quotes you one. This is your yardstick.
steps.expect: a benchmark rate written down.

steps.action: **Understand the fee-versus-rate trick.** A "0% commission" desk still profits by giving you a worse rate; a fair-rate provider may charge a visible fee. Judge only the final amount of foreign currency per unit of yours.
steps.expect: you can compute the effective rate of any offer, ignoring the "no fee" label.

steps.action: **Check your card's foreign-transaction terms.** Many cards add 1-3% on foreign spend; some add nothing. A no-FX-fee card at the network rate usually beats cash exchange.
steps.expect: your card's foreign-spend fee known as a percentage.

steps.action: **Decline "pay in your home currency" prompts.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* at foreign terminals and ATMs, dynamic currency conversion offers to bill in your home currency at a padded rate. Always choose to be charged in the local currency.
steps.expect: the terminal charges in local currency; your bank does the conversion at the network rate.

steps.action: **Get cash the cheap way, not the airport way.** Avoid airport and hotel exchange desks; their rates are the worst you will see. Prefer a bank ATM at the destination (choosing local-currency billing) or a pre-ordered rate from home.
steps.expect: an effective rate within a small margin of mid-market, not 10%+ worse.

steps.action: **Split cash and card deliberately.** Carry enough local cash for small vendors, transit, and tips; put larger and card-friendly spending on the no-FX card.
steps.expect: a cash amount sized to genuine cash-only needs, not your whole trip.

steps.action: **Keep the receipt and check the posted amount.** For cash exchange keep the slip; for card spend, verify the converted amount when it posts.
steps.expect: posted amounts match the expected rate within the disclosed fee.

recipes.verification: You hold local currency and/or card spending power obtained at an effective rate within a few percent of the mid-market benchmark, you declined every home-currency conversion prompt, and no exchange happened at an airport or hotel desk.

recipes.title: file a home insurance claim
recipes.name: file-a-home-insurance-claim
recipes.goal: Report a covered home loss, document damage, prevent further damage, and track the claim through payment or written denial.

steps.action: **Make the property safe.** Stop active damage if safe, shut off water or power if appropriate, and avoid unsafe areas.
steps.expect: immediate hazards are controlled or emergency help is on site.

steps.action: **Document before cleanup.** Take photos and video of damage, affected rooms, damaged belongings, source of loss, and temporary repairs.
steps.expect: evidence exists before items are moved or discarded.

steps.action: **Review coverage and deductible.** Check policy limits, exclusions, claim duties, and deductible for the loss type.
steps.expect: you know whether filing is likely worth the deductible and record impact.

steps.action: **Prevent further damage.** Arrange tarping, drying, boarding, or emergency repairs and keep receipts.
steps.expect: mitigation actions and costs are documented.

steps.action: **Open the claim.** Use the insurer's official claim phone, app, or portal and provide date, cause, address, damage summary, and contact details.
steps.expect: claim number and adjuster or next-step timeline are recorded.

steps.action: **Submit evidence.** Upload photos, inventory, receipts, repair estimates, police or fire reports, and mitigation invoices.
steps.expect: claim file shows documents received.

steps.action: **Meet the adjuster.** Walk through damage, ask what is covered, and request the estimate in writing.
steps.expect: adjuster inspection or virtual review is completed.

steps.action: **Review settlement.** Compare insurer estimate with contractor estimates, deductible, depreciation, and recoverable amounts.
steps.expect: payment, supplemental request, or denial reason is understood.

steps.action: **Accept or dispute outcome.** Deposit payment only when you understand the settlement, or request reconsideration with evidence. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing a release or final settlement can limit later recovery, so read it before agreeing.
steps.expect: final payment, supplement, or appeal path is documented.

recipes.verification: The claim has a claim number, submitted evidence, mitigation receipts, adjuster estimate, written coverage decision, and either payment record or documented appeal next step.

recipes.title: file a simple tax return
recipes.name: file-a-simple-tax-return
recipes.goal: Prepare and file a simple tax return with the required income forms, basic deductions or credits, and records saved for future proof.

steps.action: **Confirm the filing deadline.** Check the official tax agency calendar for the tax year and your jurisdiction.
steps.expect: you know the due date and extension rules.

steps.action: **Gather tax documents.** Collect wage statements, interest forms, retirement forms, unemployment forms, tuition or childcare forms, and prior-year return if useful.
steps.expect: all expected documents are in one folder.

steps.action: **Choose filing method.** [BRANCH: reputable tax software | official free filing | paper forms | tax preparer] Pick the simplest method allowed for your situation.
steps.expect: you have a trusted filing path ready.

steps.action: **Enter personal information.** Add legal name, tax ID, address, filing status, dependents, and bank details carefully.
steps.expect: the software or form accepts identity fields without errors.

steps.action: **Enter income forms.** Copy employer, payer, income, withholding, and account numbers exactly from each form.
steps.expect: totals match the source forms.

steps.action: **Review deduction basics.** Compare standard deduction or default allowance against any simple itemized deductions the software supports.
steps.expect: the selected deduction method is shown and explained.

steps.action: **Check credits and payments.** Add withholding, estimated payments, education, child, retirement saver, or other simple credits only if you have support.
steps.expect: refund or balance due updates after each entry.

steps.action: **File and pay or request refund.** Review the return, then e-file or mail it. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once accepted, corrections usually require an amended return, so review names, IDs, income, and bank numbers first.
steps.expect: you receive an e-file acceptance, mailing proof, refund status, or payment confirmation.

steps.action: **Keep records.** Save the filed return, all forms, receipts, software confirmation, and payment proof.
steps.expect: a complete tax-year folder is stored securely.

recipes.verification: The tax agency or filing software shows the return was accepted or mailed with proof, and your saved folder contains the filed return plus source documents.

recipes.title: file a tax extension
recipes.name: file-a-tax-extension
recipes.goal: Request more time to file a tax return while estimating and paying any tax due by the original deadline.

steps.action: **Confirm what the extension covers.** Read the official rule for the tax year and jurisdiction.
steps.expect: you know whether it extends filing time only or also payment time.

steps.action: **Estimate income and tax.** Use pay forms, prior-year return, business records, investment income, withholding, and estimated payments.
steps.expect: you have a reasonable tax-due estimate.

steps.action: **Choose the filing method.** [BRANCH: official online payment | tax software | paper extension form | preparer] pick the method accepted by the agency.
steps.expect: the extension path is ready before the deadline.

steps.action: **Enter taxpayer details.** Provide legal name, tax ID, address, filing status, spouse details if applicable, and estimated liability.
steps.expect: the form identifies the correct taxpayer and tax year.

steps.action: **Schedule payment if due.** Pay estimated balance through the official portal, electronic withdrawal, card processor, or mailed voucher. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* payments and card processing fees may not be reversible, so confirm tax year, taxpayer ID, amount, and account details first.
steps.expect: you receive payment confirmation or mailing proof.

steps.action: **Submit the extension.** Send the extension request by the original filing deadline using the selected method.
steps.expect: you receive e-file acceptance, online confirmation, or proof of mailing.

steps.action: **Save records.** Store the extension confirmation, payment receipt, estimates, and source documents.
steps.expect: you can prove timely filing and payment.

steps.action: **Calendar the extended due date.** Add the new filing deadline and earlier prep reminders.
steps.expect: you have time to finish the return before penalties begin.

steps.action: **File the actual return.** Complete the return and apply extension payments correctly.
steps.expect: the final return shows the payment as already made.

recipes.verification: You have an accepted extension confirmation or mailing proof, and any estimated payment receipt shows the correct taxpayer, tax year, amount, and date.

recipes.title: file taxes with a side gig
recipes.name: file-taxes-with-a-side-gig
recipes.goal: Prepare and file a tax return that includes side-gig income, deductible business expenses, and any required estimated-payment records.

steps.action: **Separate side-gig records.** Put income, expenses, mileage, fees, refunds, and tax payments for the gig in one folder or spreadsheet.
steps.expect: side-gig records are separated from wage and household records.

steps.action: **Reconcile total income.** Compare payer forms, platform exports, invoices, payment-app records, and bank deposits, including income that has no form.
steps.expect: one gross-income total is documented with sources.

steps.action: **Classify expenses.** Group ordinary and necessary business costs such as supplies, platform fees, advertising, software, payment processing, phone use, or mileage.
steps.expect: each claimed expense has a category and supporting record.

steps.action: **Check vehicle and home-office rules.** Use the current official rules before claiming mileage, actual vehicle costs, or home office expenses.
steps.expect: only eligible deductions remain in the workpapers.

steps.action: **Enter side-gig forms.** In tax software or official forms, add business activity, gross receipts, returns, expense categories, and any self-employment tax screens.
steps.expect: the return shows side-gig profit or loss and related tax.

steps.action: **Apply payments and withholding.** Enter estimated payments, extension payments, backup withholding, and wage withholding from other jobs.
steps.expect: the balance due or refund reflects all payments already made.

steps.action: **Review before filing.** Compare totals against your spreadsheet and investigate large mismatches, negative profit, or unfamiliar forms.
steps.expect: income, expenses, and tax due match your records.

steps.action: **File and pay.** Submit the return and schedule any payment through the official agency, software, or preparer channel. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* accepted returns usually require an amendment to correct, so confirm legal name, tax ID, bank details, income, expenses, and payment amount first.
steps.expect: filing acceptance, mailing proof, or payment confirmation is saved.

steps.action: **Set next-year reminders.** Calendar estimated-tax dates, recordkeeping reviews, and document-download windows.
steps.expect: future side-gig tax tasks are scheduled.

recipes.verification: The filed return or draft workpaper includes side-gig gross income, categorized expenses, self-employment or equivalent tax treatment when applicable, all prior payments, and a saved filing or payment confirmation.

recipes.title: freeze a childs credit
recipes.name: freeze-a-childs-credit
recipes.goal: Freeze a child's credit file so identity thieves cannot easily open credit using the child's personal information.

steps.action: **Gather required documents.** Collect the child's identity proof, your government ID, proof of address, and proof of guardianship.
steps.expect: each document is current, readable, and shows matching names or addresses.

steps.action: **Make secure copies.** Scan or photocopy only what each bureau requires and store copies in a protected folder.
steps.expect: you have legible files or pages ready for submission.

steps.action: **Find official bureau instructions.** Navigate to each credit bureau's child security freeze page.
steps.expect: requirements and mailing or upload options are listed by the bureau.

steps.action: **Complete the first bureau request.** Fill out the minor freeze form with child and guardian details.
steps.expect: the form matches the documents you will send.

steps.action: **Submit documents securely.** Use the bureau's secure upload or mailed address from the official site.
steps.expect: you receive upload confirmation, tracking number, or mailing receipt.

steps.action: **Repeat for every major bureau.** Submit separate requests to all three major bureaus or all relevant bureaus in your country.
steps.expect: no bureau is skipped.

steps.action: **Save confirmation letters.** Keep bureau responses, freeze PINs, passwords, or reference numbers in a secure location.
steps.expect: you can later thaw or remove the freeze.

steps.action: **Check whether a file already existed.** Read bureau responses for signs that a credit file was found before the freeze.
steps.expect: either a new protected file was created or an existing file was frozen.

steps.action: **Investigate existing files.** If a bureau reports activity, request the child's credit report and review accounts.
steps.expect: any fraudulent accounts are identified for dispute.

steps.action: **Dispute fraud if found.** Send disputes with the child's documents and identity-theft report if needed.
steps.expect: each fraudulent entry receives an investigation case number.

steps.action: **Record thaw instructions.** Note how to temporarily lift the freeze when the child later needs credit, housing, student loans, or employment screening.
steps.expect: future thaw steps are available without hunting for old mail.

steps.action: **Review after major events.** Recheck if documents are stolen, mail arrives about credit, or the child approaches adulthood.
steps.expect: the freeze remains intentional and documented.

recipes.verification: Every major credit bureau confirms that the child's credit file is frozen or that a protected minor file was created and frozen, and all thaw credentials are stored securely.

recipes.title: freeze your credit
recipes.name: freeze-your-credit
recipes.goal: Your credit files are frozen at the three major credit bureaus so new creditors cannot access them without a thaw.

steps.action: **Open the first bureau's official freeze page.** Type the address directly or use a trusted government or bureau link.
steps.expect: the page describes a security freeze, not paid monitoring.

steps.action: **Create or access the bureau account.** Enter identity details and complete any verification questions.
steps.expect: the bureau recognizes your file or gives a manual verification path.

steps.action: **Place the freeze.** Choose freeze or security freeze and confirm the request.
steps.expect: the bureau shows the file is frozen.

steps.action: **Save recovery details.** Store the PIN, confirmation number, username, and password in a password manager or locked file.
steps.expect: you can find the details without exposing them.

steps.action: **Repeat for all bureaus.** Complete the same process for each major bureau, not just one. [BRANCH: online succeeds | phone or mail required]
steps.expect: every bureau has a freeze confirmation.

steps.action: **Record thaw instructions.** Note how to temporarily lift each freeze and how long it takes.
steps.expect: you know the steps before applying for credit.

steps.action: **Test account access.** Log out and confirm you can sign back in or have recovery methods saved.
steps.expect: you are not locked out of managing the freeze.

steps.action: **Tell household applicants.** If a joint application is coming, remind the other applicant to freeze or thaw their own credit too.
steps.expect: everyone involved understands each person has separate bureau files.

recipes.verification: Each major bureau account or confirmation page states that your credit file is frozen, and your recovery details are stored securely.

recipes.title: lower your car insurance
recipes.name: lower-your-car-insurance
recipes.goal: Reduce car insurance cost while keeping legally required and financially appropriate coverage in force.

steps.action: **Review current coverage.** Note liability limits, collision, comprehensive, deductibles, uninsured motorist, rental, roadside, discounts, and premium.
steps.expect: current cost and coverage are summarized.

steps.action: **Check required coverage.** Confirm state, lender, lease, rideshare, or employer requirements before changing anything.
steps.expect: non-negotiable coverage requirements are marked.

steps.action: **Update rating details.** Correct annual mileage, garaging address, drivers, vehicle use, anti-theft features, student status, and driving course eligibility.
steps.expect: quote inputs match reality.

steps.action: **Ask for discounts.** Request discounts for bundling, safe driving, telematics, low mileage, autopay, paperless billing, defensive driving, or good student status.
steps.expect: available discounts are applied or denied with reasons.

steps.action: **Compare quotes.** Get comparable quotes using the same limits, deductibles, vehicles, and drivers.
steps.expect: price differences reflect insurer pricing, not missing coverage.

steps.action: **Adjust deductibles carefully.** Compare premium savings against the cash you could pay after a claim.
steps.expect: deductible choices match available emergency cash.

steps.action: **Switch or renew.** Buy the new policy before canceling the old one, or accept the revised renewal. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* canceling before replacement coverage starts can create a lapse, so confirm effective dates first.
steps.expect: continuous coverage is confirmed.

steps.action: **Cancel duplicate coverage.** After the new policy is active, cancel the old policy and request refund confirmation if due.
steps.expect: no overlapping unpaid policy remains.

recipes.verification: The active policy has continuous effective dates, required coverage, documented discounts, affordable deductibles, and a lower premium or documented reason to keep the current policy.

recipes.title: make a debt payoff plan
recipes.name: make-a-debt-payoff-plan
recipes.goal: Create a realistic debt payoff plan that covers minimum payments, chooses a strategy, and prevents new missed-payment fees.

steps.action: **List every debt.** Record creditor, balance, interest rate, minimum payment, due date, account status, and any promo expiration.
steps.expect: no debt is hidden from the plan.

steps.action: **Protect minimum payments.** Add all minimums to a calendar or autopay from a funded account.
steps.expect: late fees and credit damage are less likely.

steps.action: **Calculate payoff cash.** Subtract rent, food, utilities, transport, insurance, minimum debt payments, and a small cash buffer from income.
steps.expect: you know the extra monthly amount available.

steps.action: **Pick a strategy.** [BRANCH: avalanche | snowball | urgent-default first] target highest interest, smallest balance, or accounts at risk of lawsuit/repossession first.
steps.expect: each extra dollar has a clear destination.

steps.action: **Check fee traps.** Note balance-transfer fees, origination fees, prepayment penalties, deferred-interest promotions, and hardship-plan credit reporting.
steps.expect: the plan does not accidentally increase cost.

steps.action: **Contact creditors if needed.** Ask about hardship plans, lower rates, due-date changes, fee waivers, or medical financial assistance.
steps.expect: any changed terms are confirmed in writing.

steps.action: **Build the monthly schedule.** Assign payment dates, minimum amounts, target extra payment, and payoff order for the next three months.
steps.expect: the plan fits actual paydays.

steps.action: **Make only confirmed payments.** Pay through official creditor portals or bill pay, starting with minimums and then the target extra payment. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* payments usually cannot be pulled back after processing, so confirm account, amount, and date before submitting.
steps.expect: receipts match the schedule.

steps.action: **Review monthly.** Update balances, interest rates, income changes, and emergency expenses.
steps.expect: the payoff date and next target stay current.

recipes.verification: Your plan lists every debt, covers every minimum payment, names one target debt, and shows receipts or scheduled payments for the current month.

recipes.title: name beneficiaries on your accounts
recipes.name: name-beneficiaries-on-your-accounts
recipes.goal: Add or update beneficiaries on financial accounts so assets pass to the intended people or organizations outside ordinary account access.

steps.action: **Inventory accounts.** List retirement plans, IRAs, life insurance, annuities, bank payable-on-death accounts, brokerage transfer-on-death accounts, HSAs, and employer benefits.
steps.expect: every account that can name a beneficiary is on one checklist.

steps.action: **Review current beneficiaries.** Log in or request beneficiary forms and note primary, contingent, percentages, and last update date.
steps.expect: you know what would happen today if you died.

steps.action: **Choose updated beneficiaries.** Decide primary and backup recipients, percentage splits, and whether any minors, trusts, charities, or estates are involved.
steps.expect: designations total 100% and include backups.

steps.action: **Check legal and tax complications.** Review spousal consent, divorce orders, community property, minor beneficiaries, special-needs benefits, and trust naming rules.
steps.expect: you know whether professional advice or notarized consent is needed.

steps.action: **Complete the institution's form.** Enter beneficiary details exactly, including full legal names, relationship, dates of birth, addresses, tax IDs if required, and percentages.
steps.expect: the form has no blanks or percentage errors.

steps.action: **Submit the beneficiary change.** [BRANCH: online | upload | mail | employer portal] Follow signature, notarization, medallion, or spousal-consent requirements. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* beneficiary designations can control assets at death and may override your will, so confirm names and shares before submission.
steps.expect: the institution accepts the change or shows pending review.

steps.action: **Save confirmation.** Download the confirmation page, updated beneficiary summary, or stamped form.
steps.expect: you have proof of current beneficiaries for each account.

steps.action: **Tell fiduciaries where records are.** Inform executor, trustee, or trusted person where the account inventory and confirmations are stored without sharing passwords.
steps.expect: someone responsible can find the records later.

steps.action: **Set a review schedule.** Recheck after marriage, divorce, birth, death, account rollover, job change, or every two years.
steps.expect: stale designations are less likely to survive unnoticed.

recipes.verification: Each account shows accepted primary and contingent beneficiaries with correct names and percentage shares, and confirmations are saved.

recipes.title: negotiate a bill
recipes.name: negotiate-a-bill
recipes.goal: You ask a provider to lower, credit, or restructure a bill and leave with a documented result.

steps.action: **Read the bill line by line.** Identify base rate, fees, taxes, equipment charges, and recent increases.
steps.expect: you know which charge you are challenging.

steps.action: **Research the market rate.** Check competitor offers, new-customer prices, and your provider's current posted plans.
steps.expect: you have a realistic target number.

steps.action: **Prepare a short script.** Write: "I want to keep service, but this bill is too high compared with X. What can you do?"
steps.expect: your ask is specific and calm.

steps.action: **Call the provider.** Use the number on the bill or official website and pass account verification.
steps.expect: the representative can view your account.

steps.action: **Ask for retention or loyalty.** If the first person cannot adjust price, ask for the cancellation, retention, or loyalty team.
steps.expect: you reach someone with discount authority.

steps.action: **Make the ask and wait.** State the target rate, mention competitor pricing, then stop talking while they check options. [BRANCH: discount offered | no discount offered]
steps.expect: you receive a concrete offer or reason.

steps.action: **Confirm total cost and terms.** Ask about taxes, fees, equipment, contract length, expiration date, and autopay requirements.
steps.expect: the monthly all-in amount and conditions are clear.

steps.action: **Get it in writing.** Request an email, chat transcript, confirmation number, or updated bill.
steps.expect: you have proof of the negotiated change.

recipes.verification: You have written confirmation showing the new bill amount, effective date, duration, and any contract or autopay conditions.

recipes.title: negotiate a medical bill
recipes.name: negotiate-a-medical-bill
recipes.goal: Reduce or restructure a valid medical bill by asking for corrections, financial assistance, discounts, or a manageable payment plan.

steps.action: **Confirm the balance is valid.** Compare the bill to the EOB, payments already made, and services received.
steps.expect: you know the amount eligible for negotiation.

steps.action: **Request an itemized bill.** Ask for procedure codes, dates, charges, adjustments, payments, and remaining balance.
steps.expect: duplicate or incorrect charges can be spotted.

steps.action: **Ask for financial assistance.** Request charity care, hardship assistance, income-based discounts, and the application form.
steps.expect: you know required documents such as pay stubs, tax return, ID, or bank statements.

steps.action: **Ask about discounts.** [BRANCH: insured balance | uninsured balance] request a prompt-pay discount, self-pay rate, cash price, or reduction to the insurer allowed amount.
steps.expect: the representative states available discount options.

steps.action: **Compare payment plans.** Ask whether plans are interest-free, whether late fees apply, and whether the account stays out of collections.
steps.expect: the monthly amount, length, and fees are clear.

steps.action: **Get terms in writing.** Request a letter, portal message, or revised statement showing discount, due date, payment plan, and collections hold.
steps.expect: verbal promises are backed by a document.

steps.action: **Submit documents.** Upload or mail only required assistance forms and proof of income or household size.
steps.expect: you receive confirmation that the application or request is under review.

steps.action: **Pay after agreement.** Make the agreed payment through the provider's official portal, phone line, or mailed check. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the revised balance and account number before paying because refunds can be slow.
steps.expect: the receipt matches the negotiated terms.

steps.action: **Monitor statements.** Check the next statement and portal balance for the discount, payment credit, and no collections activity.
steps.expect: the account follows the agreement.

recipes.verification: The provider sends a revised statement, assistance approval, discount confirmation, or payment-plan agreement showing the exact remaining balance and payment terms.

recipes.title: open a bank account
recipes.name: open-a-bank-account
recipes.goal: A current/checking account is open in your name at a bank you chose deliberately, with the card, online access, and any direct deposits or payments pointed at it.

steps.action: **Choose the bank on fees and fit, not proximity nostalgia.** Compare three candidates on: monthly fee and how to waive it, ATM network, foreign transaction fees if you travel, app quality, and branch access if you value it. Online-only banks win on fees; branch banks win when you need a human.
steps.expect: one chosen bank and a named account type, with its fee schedule actually read.

steps.action: **Gather the exact document list from the bank's site.** Newcomers: check which proofs of address are accepted before showing up; this is the step that fails immigrants and students most often, and some banks explicitly accept alternatives (employer letters, university letters).
steps.expect: every listed document in hand, originals where required.

steps.action: **Apply online or book a branch appointment.** Online flows verify identity by document photo and a selfie or video call; branch flows do it at the desk. Answer the regulatory questions (occupation, source of funds, tax residency) accurately. They are legally required, not curiosity.
steps.expect: an application submitted and an account number issued, sometimes instantly, sometimes after a review of days.

steps.action: **Complete the security setup the moment access arrives.** Set the online banking credentials from the bank's official app or site, enable the strongest offered 2FA, and store everything in your password manager (`accounts/enable-two-factor-authentication` applies in full).
steps.expect: you can log in, see the empty account, and the recovery paths point at you.

steps.action: **Activate the card when it arrives and set the PIN.** Follow the mailed or in-app activation; test with one small purchase or an ATM balance check (`daily/errands/use-an-atm`).
steps.expect: a working card with a PIN only you know.

steps.action: **Point your money at the account.** Salary: give the account details to payroll. Recurring payments: move them over deliberately, one list, one session (`finance/pay-a-bill-online` for each). Fund it with an initial transfer. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* typos in account numbers on inbound transfers are painful to unwind, so copy-paste details from the app rather than retyping.
steps.expect: a test deposit lands, and the payment list shows what moved and what remains.

steps.action: **If this replaces an old account, run both in parallel for one full billing cycle.** Watch what still hits the old account, migrate the stragglers, then close the old one properly rather than leaving it to rot (`accounts/delete-an-account` logic applied to banking: get written confirmation of closure).
steps.expect: a clean cutover with no bounced payment in the gap.

recipes.verification: You can log in with 2FA, the card works, a test deposit arrived, the fee waiver condition is understood and met, and either no old account exists or it survived a full parallel cycle and was closed with confirmation.

recipes.title: open a retirement account
recipes.name: open-a-retirement-account
recipes.goal: Open a retirement account, choose tax treatment and investments, name beneficiaries, and set up contributions.

steps.action: **Choose account type.** Compare employer plan, traditional IRA, Roth IRA, SEP IRA, solo 401(k), or rollover account based on income, employment, taxes, and access.
steps.expect: one account type is selected with contribution eligibility understood.

steps.action: **Choose provider or plan path.** Compare employer portal, brokerage, mutual fund company, robo-advisor, credit union, or bank on fees, investments, service, and transfer options.
steps.expect: you have a chosen provider and account application.

steps.action: **Gather identity and tax details.** Prepare legal name, address, tax ID, date of birth, employment, income range, bank information, and beneficiary names.
steps.expect: required fields can be completed without guessing.

steps.action: **Complete the application.** Enter personal, tax, employment, account type, communication, and beneficiary information. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* tax classification and beneficiary choices can have long-term consequences, so confirm account type and names before submitting.
steps.expect: the account is opened or pending approval.

steps.action: **Select investments.** Choose target-date fund, balanced fund, index funds, managed portfolio, or cash temporarily based on risk tolerance and retirement date.
steps.expect: contributions have an investment destination.

steps.action: **Set contributions.** Link payroll, bank ACH, or rollover instructions; choose amount and frequency within annual limits. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* market purchases and rollover elections can have tax effects, so confirm amount, year, and source before funding.
steps.expect: contribution or transfer is scheduled or posted.

steps.action: **Name beneficiaries.** Add primary and contingent beneficiaries with percentages totaling 100%.
steps.expect: beneficiary designations show accepted, not blank.

steps.action: **Save records.** Download account agreement, investment confirmation, beneficiary confirmation, contribution receipt, and rollover paperwork if any.
steps.expect: tax and estate records are stored.

steps.action: **Calendar review and tax tasks.** Record contribution deadlines, required tax forms, rebalancing dates, and required minimum distribution age if applicable.
steps.expect: future limits and paperwork are tracked.

recipes.verification: The retirement account is open, funded or scheduled for funding, invested according to your selection, and has accepted primary and contingent beneficiaries.

recipes.title: open a savings account
recipes.name: open-a-savings-account
recipes.goal: Open a savings account that fits your access needs, avoids avoidable fees, and receives an initial deposit.

steps.action: **Choose account type.** [BRANCH: high-yield online | branch bank or credit union] Pick online for rate and branch for in-person service.
steps.expect: you have a shortlist of providers.

steps.action: **Compare rates and fees.** Check annual yield, monthly fee, minimum balance, withdrawal rules, transfer limits, and deposit insurance.
steps.expect: the chosen account has clear costs and protections.

steps.action: **Check eligibility.** Confirm age, residency, membership, credit union field of membership, and required documents.
steps.expect: you meet the opening requirements.

steps.action: **Start the application.** Use the official bank website, app, or branch appointment.
steps.expect: the application asks for identity and contact information.

steps.action: **Provide identity details.** Enter legal name, address, date of birth, taxpayer number if required, and ID details.
steps.expect: the bank can verify your identity or asks for specific documents.

steps.action: **Link funding source.** Add a checking account by instant verification, trial deposits, debit card, check, or cash deposit.
steps.expect: the funding source is verified or pending.

steps.action: **Select opening deposit.** Choose an amount that meets the minimum while leaving enough in checking for bills.
steps.expect: the transfer amount and date are visible.

steps.action: **Submit application.** Review terms, fees, beneficiary options, and deposit insurance disclosure. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* submitting may start identity checks and transfers, so verify routing and account numbers first.
steps.expect: you receive an account approval, pending review notice, or application number.

steps.action: **Confirm funding and access.** Log in after opening and verify the deposit, routing or transfer details, and statement delivery preference.
steps.expect: the account shows an available or pending balance.

recipes.verification: The savings account is open, insured or protected as disclosed, accessible online or in branch, and funded with the intended opening deposit.

recipes.title: appeal a property tax assessment
recipes.name: appeal-a-property-tax-assessment
recipes.goal: You file a timely property-tax assessment appeal supported by comparable evidence and obtain a corrected assessed value if the assessment is too high.

steps.action: **Read the assessment notice completely.** Identify assessed value, taxable value, exemptions, appeal deadline, filing method, and required forms.
steps.expect: a deadline and submission checklist.

steps.action: **Verify the property record.** Check square footage, bedrooms, bathrooms, lot size, year built, condition, and exemptions.
steps.expect: any factual errors are listed with proof.

steps.action: **Build comparable-sales evidence.** Find similar properties sold near the valuation date, adjusting for size, condition, location, and features.
steps.expect: three to six relevant comparables with sale dates and prices.

steps.action: **Estimate a defensible value.** Use the best comparables and corrections rather than simply asking for a lower tax bill.
steps.expect: a requested assessed value supported by evidence.

steps.action: **Prepare the appeal package.** Complete the official form and attach assessment notice, comparables, photos, appraisals, repair estimates, and exemption proof.
steps.expect: a complete package that addresses the assessor's valuation basis.

steps.action: **File before the deadline.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm parcel number, tax year, requested value, and all attachments before submitting because late or incomplete appeals may be rejected.
steps.expect: a submission receipt, case number, or stamped copy.

steps.action: **Respond to assessor contact or settlement offers.** Review any proposed reduction against your evidence and tax impact.
steps.expect: either a signed agreement or a hearing date.

steps.action: **Attend the hearing if required.** Present facts concisely: record errors, best comparable sales, and requested value.
steps.expect: the board accepts evidence and tells you when a decision will issue.

steps.action: **Confirm the corrected tax record.** After a decision or settlement, check the parcel account and bill.
steps.expect: the assessed value and estimated tax reflect the decision.

recipes.verification: The appeal is accepted with a receipt or case number, and success is a written decision or updated parcel record reducing the assessed value or correcting the exemption for the target tax year.

recipes.title: ask for a retention offer
recipes.name: ask-for-a-retention-offer
recipes.goal: You ask a provider or card issuer for a retention offer and decide whether the credit, discount, bonus, or downgrade option is worth keeping the account.

steps.action: **Define your reason to leave.** Identify price increase, annual fee, underused service, competitor offer, or missing feature.
steps.expect: a concise and truthful cancellation rationale.

steps.action: **Calculate your walk-away point.** Decide the credit, discount, bonus, or downgrade that would make staying worthwhile.
steps.expect: a private minimum acceptable retention value.

steps.action: **Check existing offers online.** Review account offers, downgrade options, contract terms, and cancellation deadlines before calling.
steps.expect: you know what is already available without negotiation.

steps.action: **Call official customer service.** Verify identity and ask for the cancellation or retention department.
steps.expect: you reach a representative authorized to discuss retention.

steps.action: **State the cancellation intent clearly.** Explain that the account no longer makes sense at the current price and ask whether there are offers to keep it.
steps.expect: the representative checks retention offers.

steps.action: **Compare the offer to your walk-away point.** Include credits, bonus requirements, contract extensions, benefit changes, and taxes or fees.
steps.expect: the offer's net value is clear.

steps.action: **Negotiate or ask for alternatives.** [BRANCH: offer is close, ask if a stronger offer or downgrade exists | offer is poor, proceed with cancellation steps]
steps.expect: you have the best available option or a confirmed refusal.

steps.action: **Accept, downgrade, or cancel.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cancellations, point forfeiture, and contract changes can be hard to undo, so confirm benefits, fees, renewal date, and unused credits first.
steps.expect: the account status reflects the chosen action.

steps.action: **Save confirmation.** Record offer terms, confirmation number, effective date, and next billing date.
steps.expect: you can verify the account was credited, discounted, downgraded, or canceled.

recipes.verification: The account shows the accepted retention credit, discount, bonus, downgrade, or cancellation with confirmation number and effective date, and the net value meets the pre-set walk-away point.

recipes.title: avoid points expiration
recipes.name: avoid-points-expiration
recipes.goal: You prevent loyalty or reward points from expiring by creating qualifying account activity or redeeming them before the deadline.

steps.action: **Find the exact expiration rule.** Read the account page and program terms to see whether points expire on a fixed date or after inactivity.
steps.expect: a specific expiration date and extension method.

steps.action: **Verify the balance at risk.** Record the number of points expiring and whether all points or only some points are affected.
steps.expect: the at-risk amount is known.

steps.action: **Choose the lowest-cost qualifying activity.** [BRANCH: earn activity, make a small partner purchase | redeem activity, use a small redemption | transfer activity, move points only if it counts]
steps.expect: an action that should reset or reduce expiration without wasting value.

steps.action: **Check posting time.** Confirm whether the activity must occur or post before expiration.
steps.expect: the action can realistically post in time.

steps.action: **Complete the activity.** Make the qualifying purchase, redemption, survey, dining transaction, portal purchase, or transfer. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm fees and point value before spending money or redeeming points.
steps.expect: a receipt, transaction, or confirmation number.

steps.action: **Monitor account activity.** Refresh until the qualifying activity posts or the expiration date changes.
steps.expect: account history shows the activity.

steps.action: **Escalate before expiration if it does not post.** Contact program support with proof and ask whether they can manually protect the points.
steps.expect: a case number or manual extension decision.

steps.action: **Set future reminders.** Add reminders well before the next expiration date.
steps.expect: a calendar reminder or tracking note exists.

recipes.verification: The rewards account shows either an updated later expiration date, no points currently expiring, or a completed redemption that used the expiring points before the deadline.

recipes.title: bundle insurance for a discount
recipes.name: bundle-insurance-for-a-discount
recipes.goal: You evaluate whether combining insurance policies with one carrier lowers total cost without weakening coverage or creating cancellation penalties.

steps.action: **List every current policy and renewal date.** Include premium, term, coverage limits, deductibles, endorsements, and cancellation fees.
steps.expect: a complete baseline total cost and coverage inventory.

steps.action: **Choose the policies eligible to bundle.** [BRANCH: auto plus home | auto plus renters | home plus umbrella | multiple vehicles] Keep any specialized policy separate if a general carrier cannot match it.
steps.expect: a bundle candidate list.

steps.action: **Request bundled and unbundled quotes.** Ask each carrier for the bundle price and each standalone price using matching limits.
steps.expect: quotes that show the actual discount rather than only a marketing percentage.

steps.action: **Compare total cost after fees and timing.** Include prorated refunds, down payments, installment fees, and any early-cancellation penalties.
steps.expect: a net first-year savings or cost figure.

steps.action: **Check coverage quality policy by policy.** Confirm deductibles, replacement-cost terms, water or roof exclusions, liability limits, drivers, addresses, and named insureds.
steps.expect: no policy is worse than your coverage floor unless you intentionally accept it.

steps.action: **Bind the bundle only when all policies are ready.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before paying, confirm effective dates, total premium, discounts, and that all required coverages are included.
steps.expect: declarations pages or binders for each bundled policy.

steps.action: **Cancel replaced policies in the correct order.** Start new coverage first, then cancel old policies effective after the new start dates.
steps.expect: written confirmations and refund estimates for replaced policies.

steps.action: **Set a renewal review reminder.** Bundles can lose competitiveness after the first term.
steps.expect: a calendar reminder before the next renewal.

recipes.verification: All replacement policies are bound with coverage at or above your stated floor, old policies are canceled only after new effective dates, and the documented first-year net cost is below the previous combined premium by your target amount.

recipes.title: cancel and rebook for a lower price
recipes.name: cancel-and-rebook-for-a-lower-price
recipes.goal: You cancel and rebook a reservation or order only when the new total price is lower after all penalties, credits, and risks are accounted for.

steps.action: **Capture the current booking details.** Record confirmation number, dates, product/service, guests or passengers, inclusions, paid amount, taxes, fees, and cancellation deadline.
steps.expect: the original terms are saved before changes.

steps.action: **Read the cancellation policy.** Identify refundable amount, credit-only terms, cancellation fee, change fee, no-show penalty, and refund timing.
steps.expect: the cost to cancel is known.

steps.action: **Price the replacement.** Search the same dates and equivalent terms, including taxes, resort fees, baggage, seat fees, shipping, insurance, or service charges.
steps.expect: the replacement all-in price is comparable.

steps.action: **Check availability and lock timing.** Confirm the lower offer is actually bookable and whether you can hold it before canceling the original.
steps.expect: there is a realistic path to secure the cheaper option.

steps.action: **Calculate net savings.** Subtract cancellation fees, lost credits, nonrefundable extras, currency changes, and payment rewards lost from the price difference.
steps.expect: net savings exceed your minimum threshold.

steps.action: **Choose the order of operations.** [BRANCH: replacement can be held, hold/rebook first then cancel | no hold possible, cancel only if inventory and price risk are acceptable]
steps.expect: the risk of ending with no booking is explicit.

steps.action: **Rebook the lower option.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* payment or reservation terms may become binding, so confirm dates, names, refundability, and total price before purchase.
steps.expect: a new confirmation number is issued.

steps.action: **Cancel the original.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cancellation may permanently release inventory, so confirm the replacement is secured or the risk is acceptable.
steps.expect: the original booking shows canceled and refund or credit details.

steps.action: **Verify refund and final savings.** Track refund, credit, or statement adjustment and compare final totals.
steps.expect: the net savings are realized or a follow-up case is open.

recipes.verification: The replacement booking or order has a confirmed reference number, the original is canceled with documented refund or credit, and the final net cost is below the original by at least the chosen savings threshold.

recipes.title: claim a tax refund you missed
recipes.name: claim-a-tax-refund-you-missed
recipes.goal: You identify an unclaimed tax refund or credit, file the required original or amended return before the deadline, and track the refund until it posts.

steps.action: **Identify the missed refund source.** Determine whether the issue is an unfiled return, missed credit, incorrect income, excess withholding, or deductible expense.
steps.expect: a specific tax year and refund reason.

steps.action: **Check the refund-claim deadline.** Confirm the last date to file an original return or amended claim for that year.
steps.expect: the claim is still timely or you know it may be barred.

steps.action: **Gather source documents.** Download wage, interest, brokerage, tuition, mortgage, childcare, health, and prior filing records as relevant.
steps.expect: all numbers needed to support the claim are in one file.

steps.action: **Prepare the original or amended return.** [BRANCH: unfiled return, prepare the full return | already filed, prepare an amended return explaining the change]
steps.expect: the calculated refund amount and forms are ready for review.

steps.action: **Review for side effects.** Check whether the change affects state returns, credits, repayment obligations, or future carryovers.
steps.expect: no linked filing is left inconsistent.

steps.action: **File through the allowed channel.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm taxpayer identity, tax year, bank details, signature, and refund amount before submitting or mailing.
steps.expect: electronic acceptance, certified-mail proof, or tax-office receipt.

steps.action: **Track processing status.** Use the tax authority tool or account transcript and respond to notices promptly.
steps.expect: status changes to accepted, processing, adjusted, approved, or notice issued.

steps.action: **Confirm refund receipt and records.** Match the deposit or check to the claimed amount or notice-adjusted amount.
steps.expect: funds are received and the return package is archived.

recipes.verification: The tax authority has accepted the original or amended return for the target year, and the refund has posted to your account or been issued by check with no unresolved notice blocking it.

recipes.title: claim unclaimed property
recipes.name: claim-unclaimed-property
recipes.goal: You search official unclaimed-property databases, file a legitimate claim for money or assets that belong to you, and track payment to completion.

steps.action: **Use official government search portals.** Search the state, province, or national unclaimed-property site, not paid lead-generation ads.
steps.expect: search results tied to an official treasury or administrator domain.

steps.action: **Search name variations and old addresses.** Include maiden names, middle initials, business names, and common misspellings.
steps.expect: a list of possible matches with holder names and reported addresses.
