steps.expect: the portal accepts the partner account as linked or ready to link.

steps.action: **Check that transfers are irreversible.** Read the confirmation page for non-reversibility and expiration implications.
steps.expect: you understand points cannot usually return to the bank program.

steps.action: **Transfer only the needed amount.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm award space is still available, the loyalty number is correct, and the transfer amount is right before submitting.
steps.expect: a transfer confirmation number from the bank program.

steps.action: **Wait and refresh the partner account.** Monitor the partner balance until points arrive, using the stated transfer window.
steps.expect: partner account balance increases by the transferred points.

steps.action: **Book the award immediately.** Complete the award reservation and pay required taxes or fees. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm passenger names, dates, cancellation policy, and fee amount before final booking.
steps.expect: an airline ticket number or hotel confirmation number.

recipes.verification: The flexible points have posted to the correct travel partner account and have been used to issue the intended booking confirmation at or above the target redemption value.

recipes.title: organize tax documents
recipes.name: organize-tax-documents
recipes.goal: Collect and organize tax documents so a filer or tax preparer can complete a return with fewer missing forms, duplicated entries, or unsupported deductions.

steps.action: **Create the tax-year workspace.** Make one physical folder or digital folder named with the tax year and taxpayer name.
steps.expect: all documents have one obvious place to go.

steps.action: **Build the income checklist.** List wages, self-employment, interest, dividends, retirement income, unemployment, benefits, rental income, crypto or investment sales, and other taxable income.
steps.expect: each expected income source has a checkbox.

steps.action: **Build the deduction and credit checklist.** List mortgage interest, property tax, charitable gifts, education costs, medical costs, childcare, retirement contributions, business expenses, energy credits, and local deductions.
steps.expect: each possible deduction or credit has a place for proof.

steps.action: **Sort documents by type.** [BRANCH: income | deductions] place income forms in one group and deduction or credit proof in another group, then separate by payer or category.
steps.expect: a preparer can find each document without searching the whole folder.

steps.action: **Scan paper records.** Photograph or scan forms, receipts, letters, and year-end statements at readable quality.
steps.expect: every paper item has a legible backup file.

steps.action: **Name digital files consistently.** Use tax year, category, payer, and form or receipt name in the filename.
steps.expect: files sort predictably and duplicates stand out.

steps.action: **Track missing items.** Add a missing list for expected forms, corrected forms, passwords, charitable receipts, mileage logs, or identity documents.
steps.expect: unresolved items are visible before filing.

steps.action: **Record retention dates.** Note the default retention period you plan to use, commonly at least several years after filing, and longer for property, business, or unresolved tax matters.
steps.expect: you know what can be archived and what must be kept.

steps.action: **Prepare the hand-off packet.** For a preparer, add prior-year return, identification instructions, organizer questionnaire, contact information, direct deposit choice, and signed engagement documents if requested.
steps.expect: the preparer receives one complete packet instead of scattered files.

steps.action: **Review before delivery.** Remove irrelevant documents, mark originals, and list questions that need tax advice.
steps.expect: the folder is complete enough to file or to start the preparer's review.

recipes.verification: The tax-year folder contains income documents, deduction and credit proof, scanned backups, a missing-item list, retention notes, and a preparer hand-off packet when applicable.

recipes.title: pay a bill online
recipes.name: pay-a-bill-online
recipes.goal: A due bill (utility, phone, credit card, rent) is paid online before its due date, with a confirmation number saved.

steps.action: **Read the bill.** Note amount due, due date, account/customer number, and whether the amount looks normal for the season.
steps.expect: you can state amount, date, and account number; anomalies (double last month's?) get investigated before paying.

steps.action: **Choose the payment channel.** [BRANCH: biller's own portal | your bank's bill-pay | wallet/payment app] First time on a biller portal: reach it by typing the URL from the paper bill, never from an email link.
steps.expect: you are logged in at the correct channel (`accounts/log-in`).

steps.action: **Locate the bill in the portal.** Billing/Payments section → current statement.
steps.expect: portal's amount due and due date match the bill in hand; mismatch → F1.

steps.action: **Enter payment details.** Select or add the funding source; enter/confirm the amount — pay the statement balance unless intentionally paying partial.
steps.expect: a review screen: payee, amount, funding source, payment date.

steps.action: **Check the scheduled date lands on or before the due date.** Bank bill-pay may take 1–3 business days to deliver — schedule accordingly.
steps.expect: delivery/processing date ≤ due date.

steps.action: **Confirm the payment.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* online payments to billers are hard to recall once processed — verify payee and amount on the review screen now.
steps.expect: a confirmation screen with a confirmation/reference number.

steps.action: **Save the confirmation.** Screenshot or note the number with the date.
steps.expect: confirmation stored; an email receipt typically follows.

steps.action: **Verify settlement within a few days.** Bank statement shows the debit; biller portal shows balance cleared.
steps.expect: exactly one debit of the right amount; biller balance updated.

recipes.verification: The confirmation number is saved, the funding account shows exactly one debit for the intended amount, and the biller's portal shows the balance paid with no late flag by the due date.

recipes.title: pay a tax bill online
recipes.name: pay-a-tax-bill-online
recipes.goal: Pay a tax bill online through the official payment portal and keep records that prove the payment was made.

steps.action: **Confirm the bill source.** Compare the notice or balance to your filed return, official account, or tax preparer records.
steps.expect: the amount and tax year make sense.

steps.action: **Navigate to the official portal.** Type the tax agency address or follow links from the agency site, not ads or email buttons.
steps.expect: the browser shows the official government domain or approved processor named by it.

steps.action: **Choose payment type.** Select balance due, estimated tax, extension, installment agreement, notice payment, or other matching category.
steps.expect: the portal asks for the related tax year and form.

steps.action: **Enter taxpayer details.** Provide name, address, taxpayer ID, filing status, or notice number as required.
steps.expect: the portal accepts the identity fields without mismatch warnings.

steps.action: **Enter payment amount.** Use the exact bill amount or the amount you can pay if setting up a plan.
steps.expect: the review screen shows the intended amount and currency.

steps.action: **Consider payment plan options.** If you cannot pay in full, open the official installment or payment-plan page before making a partial payment.
steps.expect: you understand fees, interest, and due dates.

steps.action: **Select payment method.** [BRANCH: bank debit | card | digital wallet | payment plan] choose the option with acceptable fees and timing.
steps.expect: fee disclosures and processing date are visible.

steps.action: **Review tax year and form.** Check these fields carefully because misapplied tax payments can be slow to move.
steps.expect: year, form, taxpayer, and amount match the bill.

steps.action: **Submit the payment.** Confirm only after all details are correct. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* tax payments and card fees may not be cancelable once processed, so verify the official portal and tax year first.
steps.expect: the portal displays a confirmation number or receipt.

steps.action: **Save the receipt.** Download or print the confirmation with date, amount, tax year, and payment method last digits.
steps.expect: the receipt is stored with tax records.

steps.action: **Check bank or card posting.** Watch for the debit or charge over the stated processing window.
steps.expect: the posted amount matches the receipt.

steps.action: **Confirm agency credit.** Recheck the official tax account after processing time passes.
steps.expect: the balance is reduced or the payment is listed for the correct tax year.

recipes.verification: The official tax account or receipt shows the correct taxpayer, amount, tax year, payment type, confirmation number, and posted or scheduled payment status.

recipes.title: plan for an irregular income
recipes.name: plan-for-an-irregular-income
recipes.goal: Build a budgeting system for variable income that covers essentials first, saves during high-income periods, and plans for taxes or slow months.

steps.action: **Find the baseline month.** Total essential bills, minimum debt payments, food, transport, insurance, and required savings.
steps.expect: the minimum monthly survival number is known.

steps.action: **Estimate conservative income.** Use the lowest recent month, average of low months, or contracted minimum rather than the best month.
steps.expect: the budget is built on cautious income.

steps.action: **Create priority buckets.** Order money as taxes, essentials, debt minimums, emergency fund, sinking funds, long-term savings, and flexible spending.
steps.expect: each dollar has a priority before optional spending.

steps.action: **Build a holding account.** Deposit income into one account and pay yourself a steady monthly amount when possible.
steps.expect: high-income months can support low-income months.

steps.action: **Set tax aside.** If income arrives without withholding, reserve a percentage for estimated taxes using current official guidance or a tax professional.
steps.expect: tax money is separated from spending money.

steps.action: **Fund buffers in good months.** Put surplus into emergency fund and upcoming irregular bills before lifestyle upgrades.
steps.expect: slow-month protection grows after above-baseline income.

steps.action: **Use a low-income protocol.** When income falls below baseline, pause lower-priority categories and use the buffer according to the priority list.
steps.expect: essentials remain funded first.

steps.action: **Review monthly and quarterly.** Update income assumptions, tax set-aside, and minimum expenses based on actual results.
steps.expect: the plan adjusts before cash runs out.

recipes.verification: The plan shows a baseline monthly number, conservative income estimate, priority buckets, tax set-aside if needed, buffer balance, and low-income protocol.

recipes.title: read a 401k statement
recipes.name: read-a-401k-statement
recipes.goal: Read a 401k statement well enough to understand contributions, employer match, investments, fees, performance, loans, and vesting.

steps.action: **Confirm the statement period.** Check beginning date, ending date, participant name, and plan name.
steps.expect: you know which months or quarter the statement covers.

steps.action: **Review balance changes.** Compare beginning balance, contributions, employer match, rollovers, gains or losses, fees, loans, withdrawals, and ending balance.
steps.expect: the ending balance can be explained by listed activity.

steps.action: **Check contributions.** Match employee contributions to payroll deductions and note traditional pre-tax, Roth, after-tax, and catch-up categories.
steps.expect: contributions are going to the intended source.

steps.action: **Check employer match.** Compare employer contribution amount to the plan match formula if shown.
steps.expect: missing or unexpected match amounts are visible.

steps.action: **Read vesting.** Find vested balance versus total balance for employer contributions.
steps.expect: you know how much would be yours if you left now.

steps.action: **Review investments.** Note fund names, asset classes, allocation percentages, target-date fund year, and any concentrated company stock.
steps.expect: the portfolio mix is clear.

steps.action: **Review fees and expenses.** Find administrative fees, loan fees, advisory fees, and fund expense ratios if provided.
steps.expect: recurring costs are identified.

steps.action: **Look for loans or restrictions.** Check outstanding loan balance, payment schedule, blackout notices, required minimum distribution notices, or beneficiary warnings.
steps.expect: obligations and action items are visible.

steps.action: **Save or flag follow-up.** Download the statement and write questions for HR, plan administrator, or a financial professional.
steps.expect: you have a record and a short list of unresolved items.

recipes.verification: You can state the statement period, ending vested balance, contribution totals, employer match, investment allocation, fees, and any loan or action item.

recipes.title: read a brokerage statement
recipes.name: read-a-brokerage-statement
recipes.goal: Understand a brokerage statement well enough to identify holdings, activity, cost basis, gains or losses, fees, dividends, and mismatches.

steps.action: **Confirm statement identity.** Check account owner, account number ending, period dates, and brokerage name.
steps.expect: the statement belongs to the correct account and month or quarter.

steps.action: **Review account summary.** Compare beginning value, deposits, withdrawals, income, market change, fees, and ending value.
steps.expect: the summary arithmetic explains the change in account value.

steps.action: **List holdings.** Read each cash position, stock, fund, bond, option, or other security with quantity, price, and market value.
steps.expect: every holding has a current value and percentage or category.

steps.action: **Check cost basis.** For taxable accounts, review original cost, acquisition date, and covered or noncovered status.
steps.expect: you can see which positions have reliable tax basis information.

steps.action: **Review gains and losses.** Separate realized gains/losses from unrealized gains/losses.
steps.expect: sold positions are not confused with paper changes on holdings you still own.

steps.action: **Find income.** Look for dividends, interest, capital gain distributions, and reinvestments.
steps.expect: income entries match cash movements or added shares.

steps.action: **Identify fees.** Check advisory fees, fund expenses if listed, margin interest, transfer fees, and commissions.
steps.expect: any direct fees are visible and explainable.

steps.action: **Reconcile activity.** Compare deposits, withdrawals, trades, transfers, and dividends to your records.
steps.expect: no transaction is unfamiliar or duplicated.

steps.action: **Flag questions.** Mark unfamiliar securities, negative cash, margin balance, missing cost basis, or unexpected fees for brokerage support or an adviser.
steps.expect: you have a short list of items to resolve.

recipes.verification: For the statement period, beginning value plus net activity plus market change equals ending value, and every unfamiliar holding, fee, or transaction is either explained or flagged.

recipes.title: read a credit card statement
recipes.name: read-a-credit-card-statement
recipes.goal: Understand a credit card statement well enough to pay on time, avoid unnecessary interest, and spot unauthorized charges.

steps.action: **Find the statement period.** Note the opening date, closing date, and statement balance.
steps.expect: you know which transactions are included.

steps.action: **Separate statement date from due date.** Find the payment due date and minimum payment due.
steps.expect: you know the deadline for avoiding late fees.

steps.action: **Use the statement balance as the target.** Plan to pay the full statement balance by the due date when possible.
steps.expect: you know the amount that avoids new purchase interest on most cards.

steps.action: **Understand the minimum trap.** Read the minimum payment warning and payoff estimate.
steps.expect: you can see how paying only the minimum stretches debt and interest.

steps.action: **Review interest and fees.** Check purchase interest, cash advance interest, balance transfer interest, annual fees, late fees, and foreign transaction fees.
steps.expect: every finance charge or fee is explained by the statement.

steps.action: **Match transactions to reality.** Scan merchant names, dates, amounts, subscriptions, refunds, and tips against receipts or memory.
steps.expect: normal charges are recognized and suspicious ones are marked.

steps.action: **Check credits and payments.** Confirm returns, rewards credits, previous payments, and autopay posted correctly.
steps.expect: the balance reflects expected credits.

steps.action: **Dispute suspicious charges quickly.** [BRANCH: fraud | merchant error] report fraud to the issuer; for a merchant error, gather receipts and contact the merchant or issuer within the dispute window.
steps.expect: a case number or next action is recorded.

steps.action: **Schedule payment.** Pay or schedule at least the statement balance, or the best affordable amount above minimum.
steps.expect: the payment confirmation shows amount, date, and funding account.

recipes.verification: The due date, statement balance, minimum payment, interest or fee lines, suspicious charges, and payment plan are all identified from the statement.

recipes.title: read a fund fact sheet
recipes.name: read-a-fund-fact-sheet
recipes.goal: Read a mutual fund or ETF fact sheet well enough to understand objective, holdings, costs, risks, performance context, and fit within an existing plan.

steps.action: **Confirm fund identity.** Match name, ticker, share class, benchmark, and date of the fact sheet.
steps.expect: you are reading the intended current fund document.

steps.action: **Read the objective.** Identify whether the fund seeks growth, income, preservation, index tracking, target-date exposure, or another mandate.
steps.expect: the fund's purpose is clear in one sentence.

steps.action: **Check asset class and holdings.** Review stock, bond, cash, geography, sector, credit quality, duration, and top holdings.
steps.expect: you know what the fund actually owns.

steps.action: **Compare costs.** Find expense ratio, sales load, transaction fee, advisory fee, or plan-specific fee if listed.
steps.expect: ongoing and purchase costs are identified.

steps.action: **Review performance context.** Compare returns to benchmark over multiple periods and note that past performance is not a guarantee.
steps.expect: underperformance or outperformance is compared to the stated benchmark.

steps.action: **Read risk measures.** Check volatility, drawdown, duration, credit risk, concentration, turnover, or risk rating.
steps.expect: main risks are listed in plain language.

steps.action: **Check distributions and taxes.** Note dividend, capital-gain, yield, or tax-efficiency information when relevant.
steps.expect: expected taxable or income behavior is understood.

steps.action: **Decide the role.** Map the fund to your portfolio category and compare it with cheaper or simpler alternatives.
steps.expect: the fund is accepted, rejected, or flagged for more review with a reason.

recipes.verification: You can state the fund's objective, ticker or share class, benchmark, expense ratio, main holdings, main risks, and intended portfolio role from the latest fact sheet.

recipes.title: read a home insurance policy
recipes.name: read-a-home-insurance-policy
recipes.goal: Understand a home insurance policy's coverages, deductibles, exclusions, limits, and claim steps before a loss happens.

steps.action: **Confirm policy identity.** Check insurer, named insureds, property address, policy number, term dates, and premium.
steps.expect: the policy matches the home and coverage period.

steps.action: **Read dwelling coverage.** Find the limit for the structure and whether replacement cost, extended replacement cost, or actual cash value applies.
steps.expect: the main home coverage basis is known.

steps.action: **Review other coverages.** Check personal property, loss of use, other structures, personal liability, and medical payments limits.
steps.expect: each major coverage limit is listed.

steps.action: **Identify deductibles.** Note standard, wind, hail, hurricane, earthquake, flood, or percentage deductibles.
steps.expect: you know what you pay before insurance responds.

steps.action: **Find exclusions.** Read exclusions for flood, earth movement, wear and tear, vacancy, business use, mold, sewer backup, or high-value items.
steps.expect: uncovered risks are marked.

steps.action: **Check endorsements.** Review scheduled property, water backup, service line, equipment breakdown, identity theft, or ordinance coverage.
steps.expect: add-ons and missing add-ons are visible.

steps.action: **Compare to needs.** Match limits against rebuild estimate, possessions, mortgage requirements, and special risks.
steps.expect: gaps or questions for the agent are documented.

steps.action: **Save claim instructions.** Record emergency number, claim portal, mitigation duties, documentation rules, and contractor guidance.
steps.expect: claim steps are available without searching during a loss.

recipes.verification: You have a summary of current term dates, coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions, endorsements, claim contact method, and unresolved questions for the insurer or agent.

recipes.title: read a mortgage offer
recipes.name: read-a-mortgage-offer
recipes.goal: Read a mortgage offer well enough to identify the loan type, rate, fees, repayment obligations, and major risks before committing.

steps.action: **Confirm borrower and property details.** Check names, property address, loan amount, currency, occupancy type, and offer expiry.
steps.expect: the offer matches the intended transaction.

steps.action: **Identify rate and type.** Note fixed, variable, tracker, adjustable, interest-only, repayment, offset, or balloon features.
steps.expect: the interest structure and repayment model are clear.

steps.action: **Read the term and payment.** Check loan term, first payment date, monthly payment, escrow or tax amounts, and payment changes.
steps.expect: the regular payment obligation is stated.

steps.action: **List upfront fees.** Record arrangement, origination, valuation, appraisal, legal, broker, title, recording, and closing fees.
steps.expect: cash needed before or at completion is visible.

steps.action: **Check early-repayment charges.** Find prepayment penalties, early-repayment charges, lock-in periods, overpayment limits, and exit fees.
steps.expect: the cost of refinancing, selling, or overpaying is known.

steps.action: **Compare total cost.** Review APR, APRC, total amount payable, total interest, and assumptions used.
steps.expect: the long-term cost is visible beyond the monthly payment.

steps.action: **Review conditions.** Note required insurance, appraisal, survey, income verification, repairs, documents, or final credit checks.
steps.expect: unmet conditions are listed with owners and deadlines.

steps.action: **Ask advice before signing.** Consult a qualified mortgage adviser, housing counselor, solicitor, conveyancer, or attorney for anything unclear.
steps.expect: material questions are answered in writing.

steps.action: **Accept only when ready.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before signing or completing, confirm affordability, conditions, fees, repayment risk, and legal obligations.
steps.expect: acceptance reflects an informed commitment.

recipes.verification: The offer's rate type, term, payment, fees, early-repayment terms, total cost, conditions, expiry, and advice questions are documented before acceptance.

recipes.title: read a payslip
recipes.name: read-a-payslip
recipes.goal: You can walk your payslip from gross to net, name every deduction, confirm the figures are correct (including your tax code), and know how to escalate an error to payroll.

steps.action: **Confirm the identity and period header.** Your name, employee/tax ID, and the pay period dates. Wrong period or ID means you may be reading someone else's or a duplicate.
steps.expect: header matches you and the current period.

steps.action: **Read the gross pay.** This is total earnings before any deduction: base plus overtime, bonus, commission, allowances. Check it against your rate times hours, or salary divided by pay periods.
steps.expect: gross equals what your contract implies for this period.

steps.action: **Walk each deduction line by line.** Typically: income tax, social/national insurance or payroll tax, pension contribution, and any voluntary items (health cover, union, salary-sacrifice). Know which are mandatory and which you opted into.
steps.expect: every deduction line identified as tax, statutory, or elective.

steps.action: **Check the tax code or withholding setting.** A wrong tax code is the most common quiet error and silently over- or under-taxes you all year. Compare it to last period and to any code your tax authority issued.
steps.expect: the tax code matches your authority's notice; unchanged from last period unless you know why. Mismatch → F1.

steps.action: **Verify pre-tax versus post-tax ordering.** Pension and salary-sacrifice items usually come off before tax is calculated, lowering taxable pay; confirm they reduced the taxed amount rather than being taken after.
steps.expect: pre-tax deductions visibly reduce the figure that tax is charged on.

steps.action: **Arrive at net pay and match it to your bank.** Gross minus all deductions equals net (take-home). This number must equal the deposit that hits your account.
steps.expect: net on the slip equals the credit in your bank statement to the cent.

steps.action: **Read the year-to-date totals.** The YTD columns accumulate gross, tax, and deductions across the tax year; a lurching YTD figure signals a one-off error earlier.
steps.expect: YTD roughly equals this period times periods elapsed.

recipes.verification: You can state your gross, name every deduction and whether it is mandatory or elective, the tax code matches your authority's record, and the net figure equals the amount deposited in your bank account.

recipes.title: read a receipt
recipes.name: read-a-receipt
recipes.goal: Read a receipt well enough to confirm what you bought, what you paid, whether tax and discounts look right, and how long you have to return or support the purchase.

steps.action: **Identify the merchant and transaction.** Find the store name, location or website, date, time, register, transaction number, and payment method.
steps.expect: you can distinguish this receipt from similar purchases.

steps.action: **Scan every line item.** Match each product or service line to what you actually bought, including size, color, quantity, and unit price.
steps.expect: every item is recognized or marked for review.

steps.action: **Check discounts and coupons.** Confirm sale prices, coupon codes, loyalty discounts, and returns or exchanges were applied to the correct items.
steps.expect: reductions appear near the affected items or in a discount section.

steps.action: **Recalculate the subtotal.** Add the line items after discounts and before tax, shipping, tip, or fees.
steps.expect: your subtotal matches the receipt subtotal or differs by only a rounding cent.

steps.action: **Review tax, fees, tip, and total.** Compare taxable items, service fees, bag fees, delivery fees, and tip to the final total.
steps.expect: the amount charged matches the receipt total.

steps.action: **Find the return window.** Read the return policy, final sale labels, receipt date, and any deadline printed near the bottom or back.
steps.expect: you know the last practical return date and required condition.

steps.action: **Locate the barcode or receipt code.** Find the barcode, QR code, order number, or lookup code used for returns, pickup, warranty, or expense proof.
steps.expect: the merchant can use the receipt to retrieve the transaction.

steps.action: **Decide whether to keep it.** [BRANCH: routine purchase | warranty or expense] discard after return window for routine items; keep or scan receipts for warranties, reimbursements, tax records, or valuable goods.
steps.expect: the receipt is either safely stored or no longer needed.

steps.action: **Spot and document an error.** If any item, tax, coupon, tip, or total looks wrong, circle it and take a photo before contacting the merchant.
steps.expect: you have evidence that shows the exact disputed line.

steps.action: **Request a correction when needed.** Ask the cashier, service desk, or support channel to correct the receipt or refund the difference.
steps.expect: you receive a corrected receipt, refund confirmation, or case number.

recipes.verification: The receipt's merchant, date, line items, subtotal, tax or fees, total, return deadline, barcode or code, and any error action are identified.

recipes.title: read a utility bill
recipes.name: read-a-utility-bill
recipes.goal: Understand a utility bill well enough to confirm the meter reading, explain the charges, and challenge an unusual spike with evidence.

steps.action: **Confirm the account and period.** Check the customer name, service address, account number, billing dates, and due date.
steps.expect: the bill belongs to your service and covers a known time window.

steps.action: **Find the meter reading basis.** Look for actual, estimated, smart, customer, or final reading labels.
steps.expect: you know whether the usage was measured or estimated.

steps.action: **Compare opening and closing readings.** Subtract the prior reading from the latest reading and match the unit used, such as kWh, therms, gallons, or cubic feet.
steps.expect: the calculated usage agrees with the bill or the mismatch is marked.

steps.action: **Separate usage from fixed charges.** Identify variable usage charges, standing charge or service charge, delivery charges, taxes, fees, and credits.
steps.expect: you know which costs changed with use and which did not.

steps.action: **Check rate tiers and time bands.** Review tiered rates, peak periods, off-peak periods, fuel adjustments, or supplier charges.
steps.expect: the rate applied to each block of usage is visible.

steps.action: **Compare with recent history.** Compare usage, weather, household occupancy, appliance changes, and prior bills for the same season.
steps.expect: normal seasonal movement is separated from an unexplained spike.

steps.action: **Read payment status.** Check previous balance, payments received, late fees, credits, budget billing adjustment, and total due.
steps.expect: the amount due reconciles from prior balance plus current charges.

steps.action: **Record a current meter reading.** If safe and permitted, read the meter and take a dated photo.
steps.expect: you have evidence of current consumption.

steps.action: **Dispute a spike when evidence supports it.** Contact the supplier with account details, bill dates, reading photos, and the specific charge or reading you dispute.
steps.expect: you receive a case number, corrected bill, meter test option, or investigation timeline.

recipes.verification: The bill's period, reading type, usage calculation, fixed charges, variable charges, due date, and any dispute case number are recorded.

recipes.title: rebalance a portfolio
recipes.name: rebalance-a-portfolio
recipes.goal: Bring an investment portfolio back toward a chosen target allocation while considering taxes, fees, account types, and trading consequences.

steps.action: **List current holdings.** Export balances, tickers, asset classes, account types, and cash positions from each account.
steps.expect: one current portfolio view is available.

steps.action: **Compare against targets.** Calculate current percentages and differences from the target allocation.
steps.expect: overweight and underweight categories are visible.

steps.action: **Set rebalance bands.** Decide whether differences are large enough to act based on your written rule.
steps.expect: only categories outside the rule are marked for action.

steps.action: **Prefer new contributions.** Direct new deposits, dividends, or payroll contributions toward underweight categories first.
steps.expect: some or all imbalance can be corrected without selling.

steps.action: **Choose trade locations.** If trades are needed, prioritize tax-advantaged accounts when suitable and check taxable gains before selling.
steps.expect: proposed trades are mapped to accounts with tax impact noted.

steps.action: **Review costs and restrictions.** Check transaction fees, bid-ask spreads, short-term redemption fees, wash-sale issues, and employer-plan trading limits.
steps.expect: trade plan avoids avoidable costs and rule violations.

steps.action: **Place trades carefully.** Enter orders for the chosen funds or securities and confirm tickers, dollars or shares, account, and order type. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* submitted market orders may execute quickly and cannot always be canceled, so verify every order ticket first.
steps.expect: orders are accepted, filled, or waiting with status visible.

steps.action: **Record the new allocation.** Save confirmations and update the allocation spreadsheet after trades settle.
steps.expect: the portfolio is back inside the target bands or has a documented reason not to be.

recipes.verification: After settlement, the recorded portfolio allocation is within the chosen rebalance bands or the remaining deviation is documented with a tax, fee, or restriction reason.

recipes.title: recognize a fake invoice
recipes.name: recognize-a-fake-invoice
recipes.goal: Decide whether an invoice is legitimate before paying it, especially when details, pressure, or vendor identity look wrong.

steps.action: **Pause payment.** Do not click payment links or send money while checking the invoice.
steps.expect: no payment has been initiated.

steps.action: **Check the vendor identity.** Compare name, logo, address, tax ID, email domain, and phone number with past records.
steps.expect: differences are visible instead of hidden in the message.

steps.action: **Match the business reason.** Find the order, subscription, shipment, medical visit, repair, or contract tied to the charge.
steps.expect: there is a real event that explains the invoice.

steps.action: **Inspect payment details.** Look for new bank accounts, changed remit-to addresses, personal payment apps, gift cards, or crypto requests.
steps.expect: suspicious payment changes are flagged before payment.

steps.action: **Look for pressure tactics.** Note threats of immediate collection, legal action, account closure, or late fees that do not match normal terms.
steps.expect: urgency is treated as a risk signal.

steps.action: **Verify out-of-band.** Contact the vendor using a saved number, contract, prior invoice, or official portal, not the contact details on the suspect invoice.
steps.expect: a known contact confirms whether the invoice exists.

steps.action: **Confirm amount and due date.** Ask the known contact to verify invoice number, balance, due date, and payment instructions.
steps.expect: details match exactly or the invoice is rejected.

steps.action: **Check internal approvals.** For work invoices, match purchase order, receiving record, approver, and vendor master file.
steps.expect: normal approval evidence exists.

steps.action: **Reject fake invoices in writing.** If fake, mark it disputed or fraudulent and warn relevant accounting or household members.
steps.expect: nobody else pays the same invoice.

steps.action: **Pay only through verified channels.** Use the official portal or saved vendor payment profile. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* bank transfers, gift cards, crypto, and some instant payments may not be recoverable, so never pay blindly.
steps.expect: payment confirmation names the verified vendor and invoice.

steps.action: **Save the review trail.** Keep the invoice, verification notes, and payment confirmation or fraud report.
steps.expect: the decision can be audited later.

steps.action: **Block or report the sender.** Report phishing to your email provider, company security team, or the impersonated vendor.
steps.expect: the sender is blocked or the threat is documented.

recipes.verification: The invoice is either confirmed by a known vendor contact with matching amount and payment details, or it is marked fraudulent and no payment is made.

recipes.title: redeem credit card points
recipes.name: redeem-credit-card-points
recipes.goal: Redeem credit card points, miles, or cash-back rewards for an option that has clear value, correct account details, and saved confirmation.

steps.action: **Check the reward balance.** Open the issuer or loyalty rewards page and confirm available, pending, and expiring points.
steps.expect: redeemable balance and restrictions are visible.

steps.action: **List redemption options.** Compare cash back, statement credit, travel portal, point transfer, gift card, merchandise, or pay-with-points.
steps.expect: at least two available options are identified.

steps.action: **Calculate redemption value.** Divide cash price or credit amount by points required and compare fees or taxes.
steps.expect: each option has a value estimate.

steps.action: **Check restrictions.** Review cancellation rules, blackout dates, transfer ratios, minimum redemptions, and whether transfers are final.
steps.expect: limitations are understood before confirmation.

steps.action: **Enter redemption details.** Select amount, travel itinerary, loyalty account, bank account, statement credit, or gift card recipient.
steps.expect: preview page shows correct details and point cost.

steps.action: **Confirm redemption.** Submit only after reviewing value, recipient, dates, fees, and finality. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* many point transfers, gift cards, and travel bookings cannot be undone, so verify account numbers and dates first.
steps.expect: confirmation number or receipt appears.

steps.action: **Track completion.** Save the confirmation and monitor the statement, loyalty account, booking, or email delivery.
steps.expect: redeemed value posts or ticketing completes.

recipes.verification: The reward balance decreases by the expected amount and the cash, statement credit, booking, transfer, gift card, or merchandise redemption is confirmed in writing.

recipes.title: report identity theft
recipes.name: report-identity-theft
recipes.goal: Report identity theft, block new misuse, and create records needed to dispute fraudulent accounts or charges.

steps.action: **Secure core accounts first.** Change passwords for email, banking, and phone-carrier accounts, then sign out unknown sessions.
steps.expect: only your devices remain active.

steps.action: **Freeze your credit.** Place security freezes with the three major credit bureaus or the relevant bureaus in your locale.
steps.expect: each bureau gives a confirmation, PIN, or online account status showing frozen.

steps.action: **File the official identity-theft report.** Use the official government reporting portal for your country, such as IdentityTheft.gov in the United States.
steps.expect: you receive a report, recovery plan, or reference number.

steps.action: **Create an evidence folder.** Save the official report, bureau confirmations, collection letters, account statements, screenshots, and call notes.
steps.expect: every document has a date and source.

steps.action: **Contact affected financial institutions.** Call the number on the back of the card, statement, or official website, not a number from a suspicious message.
steps.expect: each institution opens a fraud case or closes the fraudulent account.

steps.action: **Dispute fraudulent credit entries.** Send disputes to credit bureaus with the identity-theft report and specific account names.
steps.expect: each bureau confirms receipt and investigation timing.

steps.action: **Dispute debts with collectors.** Request debt validation in writing and state that the debt is from identity theft.
steps.expect: the collector must pause or document the claim according to local rules.

steps.action: **Replace compromised cards and account numbers.** Ask issuers to close stolen credentials and issue new numbers.
steps.expect: old cards or account numbers no longer work.

steps.action: **Check tax and benefits exposure.** Review official tax, unemployment, health, or benefits accounts if your national ID was exposed.
steps.expect: no unfamiliar filings or claims appear, or a fraud case is opened.

steps.action: **Set a recovery schedule.** Calendar follow-ups for bureau investigations, bank provisional credits, police reports if needed, and statement reviews.
steps.expect: every open case has a next action date.

steps.action: **Send written confirmations.** Follow phone calls with secure messages or letters summarizing what was agreed.
steps.expect: you have written proof beyond call notes.

steps.action: **Keep monitoring after cleanup.** Review credit reports, statements, and mail for several months.
steps.expect: new suspicious activity is caught quickly.

recipes.verification: Credit freezes are active, the official identity-theft report is saved, each fraudulent account or charge has a dispute case number, and follow-up dates are recorded.

recipes.title: round up your savings
recipes.name: round-up-your-savings
recipes.goal: Use round-up savings so everyday purchases move small amounts into savings without overdrawing the source account.

steps.action: **Choose a trusted round-up provider.** Use your bank's feature when possible, or a reputable app with clear fees and insurance disclosures.
steps.expect: you know who holds the money and what it costs.

steps.action: **Read how round-ups work.** Most tools round purchases to the next whole currency unit and transfer the difference.
steps.expect: a 3.40 purchase would create a 0.60 round-up before multipliers.

steps.action: **Link the source account.** Connect checking or card data through the bank, app, or secure aggregator.
steps.expect: the app shows recent transactions or a linked account status.

steps.action: **Choose the savings destination.** Select an existing savings account or open the app's savings balance if appropriate.
steps.expect: round-ups have a clear place to land.

steps.action: **Set the multiplier conservatively.** [BRANCH: 1x | higher] start at 1x if cash flow is tight; use 2x or more only with a cushion.
steps.expect: estimated transfers fit your budget.

steps.action: **Set a balance guard if available.** Turn on minimum checking balance, transfer cap, or pause below threshold.
steps.expect: round-ups stop before the source account gets too low.

steps.action: **Confirm transfer timing.** Check whether money moves per purchase, daily, weekly, or after a threshold.
steps.expect: you know when the checking balance will drop.

steps.action: **Start the rule.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* transfers may be hard to cancel once processing starts; confirm linked accounts, multiplier, and fees first.
steps.expect: the app says round-ups are active.

steps.action: **Watch the source balance for two weeks.** Compare pending purchases, round-ups, bills, and payday timing.
steps.expect: the checking account stays above your safety buffer.

steps.action: **Review monthly.** Increase, decrease, pause, or withdraw based on real savings and cash flow.
steps.expect: the setup remains useful instead of forgotten.

recipes.verification: A recent purchase generated the expected round-up amount, and the source account remains above the chosen safety balance after transfer.

recipes.title: save for a big purchase
recipes.name: save-for-a-big-purchase
recipes.goal: A specific large purchase is funded on time by a deliberate plan: a target amount and date, an automatic transfer that siphons money before you can spend it, and the money parked somewhere separate and slightly hard to reach.

steps.action: **Pin the real target amount.** Add tax, delivery, and a 5 to 10 percent buffer to the sticker price.
steps.expect: one number you would actually hand over, not the advertised price.

steps.action: **Set the goal date and do the math.** Divide the target by the number of pay cycles until the date. That per-cycle figure is your contribution.
steps.expect: a per-paycheck amount; if it feels impossible, extend the date or cut the target now, not later.

steps.action: **Open a separate parking spot.** A named savings sub-account or a distinct high-yield account, not your checking account.
steps.expect: an empty account visibly labeled for this goal, separate from spending money.

steps.action: **Automate the siphon.** Schedule a transfer of the per-cycle amount, dated the day after payday, from checking into the goal account. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* automating means money leaves before you budget the rest, so set the amount you can truly spare, then live on what remains.
steps.expect: a recurring transfer confirmed; first run lands next cycle.

steps.action: **Make withdrawal deliberately slightly annoying.** Use an account without a linked debit card, or one with a 1 to 2 day transfer delay back to checking.
steps.expect: the money is reachable in an emergency but not tappable at a checkout.

steps.action: **Check progress monthly, adjust rarely.** Confirm the transfers ran and the balance tracks the plan line.
steps.expect: balance at or above (cycles elapsed × contribution); if behind, raise the contribution or move the date, do not just hope.

steps.action: **Spend from the parked money, then stop the siphon.** When the target is hit, buy, then cancel the recurring transfer.
steps.expect: purchase funded from savings, automatic transfer switched off so it does not silently continue.

recipes.verification: The goal account holds at least the target amount by the goal date, the money never got spent on anything else en route, and the automatic transfer is cancelled once the purchase is made.

recipes.title: send money to a friend
recipes.name: send-money-to-a-friend
recipes.goal: Money moves from you to a person you actually know, in the right amount, through a person-to-person channel — with the two dominant failure modes (wrong recipient, impersonation scam) structurally checked.

steps.action: **Confirm the recipient identifier live.** Have them show/send their handle or scan each other's QR in person; for bank transfers, have them paste their account details. Typing a phone number or handle from memory is the wrong-recipient generator.
steps.expect: the identifier arrived from the person, not from your recollection.

steps.action: **Start the payment and check the resolved name.** Enter the handle/number; the app resolves it to a display name and often a profile photo — *stop and read it*. [BRANCH: name matches your friend → continue | unfamiliar name/photo → halt, re-confirm the identifier]
steps.expect: the resolved identity is recognizably them.

steps.action: **Enter the amount and a note.** Decimal check (5.00 vs 500 is the classic), currency check where relevant, and a note ("dinner 7/20") — notes settle later ambiguity and mark the payment's purpose.
steps.expect: amount correct at the cents level; note attached.

steps.action: **Send a test round on first-time transfers of size.** New recipient + meaningful amount → send a trivial amount first, confirm they received it, then send the rest. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* instant P2P transfers (and many bank rails) cannot be recalled — the test-round habit is the only undo you get.
steps.expect: friend confirms the test landed; remainder sent to the now-verified recipient.

steps.action: **Verify completion on both ends.** Your app shows sent/completed; they confirm receipt (the payment can be "sent" into their unclaimed/pending state if their account isn't set up).
steps.expect: mutual confirmation; screenshots exist naturally in the app history.

recipes.verification: The intended person confirms receipt of the intended amount, your app history shows one completed payment with its note, no test-round remainder was forgotten, and nothing about the transaction involved a stranger, urgency, or goods.

recipes.title: set a monthly savings rate
recipes.name: set-a-monthly-savings-rate
recipes.goal: Set a monthly savings rate that fits income, essential spending, debt obligations, and priority goals.

steps.action: **Calculate take-home income.** Average recent paychecks or deposits after taxes and payroll deductions.
steps.expect: monthly spendable income is recorded.

steps.action: **List required expenses.** Total rent, utilities, food, insurance, transportation, minimum debt payments, childcare, and other non-optional costs.
steps.expect: baseline monthly obligations are known.

steps.action: **Choose priority goals.** Pick emergency fund, retirement, debt payoff, sinking funds, down payment, or another goal.
steps.expect: savings priorities are ranked.

steps.action: **Set a starting rate.** Choose a percentage or dollar amount that leaves bills covered and some buffer.
steps.expect: monthly savings target is realistic on paper.

steps.action: **Automate transfers.** Schedule payroll split or bank transfer shortly after income arrives.
steps.expect: the first automatic saving action is scheduled.

steps.action: **Protect bill cash.** Keep the transfer below the amount that would cause overdraft or late payment.
steps.expect: checking balance remains sufficient for upcoming bills.

steps.action: **Review after one cycle.** Compare actual spending, saved amount, and any shortfall after a full month.
steps.expect: the rate is confirmed or adjusted.

steps.action: **Increase gradually.** Raise the rate after raises, debt payoff, or spending reductions.
steps.expect: future increases are tied to specific triggers.

recipes.verification: After one full month, the chosen amount or percentage transferred successfully, bills were paid on time, and the savings balance increased by the planned amount.

recipes.title: set up a college savings plan
recipes.name: set-up-a-college-savings-plan
recipes.goal: Open a college savings plan, name the beneficiary, choose investments, and set contribution records for education funding.

steps.action: **Choose the plan type.** Compare 529 savings plans, prepaid tuition plans, custodial accounts, Coverdell accounts, and ordinary brokerage savings.
steps.expect: you know why the chosen plan fits the education goal.

steps.action: **Compare state and fee details.** Check in-state tax deductions/credits, annual fees, investment expenses, age-based portfolios, direct-sold vs advisor-sold options, and rollover rules.
steps.expect: one plan is selected with known costs and state benefits.

steps.action: **Gather owner and beneficiary details.** Prepare legal names, addresses, dates of birth, tax IDs, citizenship/residency questions, and successor owner information.
steps.expect: the application can be completed accurately.

steps.action: **Open the account.** Complete the official plan application and beneficiary designation. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* account ownership and beneficiary setup can affect taxes, aid, and control, so confirm details before submitting.
steps.expect: the plan issues an account number or pending application confirmation.

steps.action: **Choose investments.** Select age-based, static, bank, or custom portfolios based on time horizon and risk tolerance.
steps.expect: contributions have an investment allocation, not unassigned cash unless intentional.

steps.action: **Link funding source.** Add bank information or payroll/gift contribution instructions and verify microdeposits if required.
steps.expect: the funding source is confirmed or pending verification.

steps.action: **Make the first contribution.** Enter amount, contribution year if asked, and timing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* contributions may have tax and gift-tax reporting consequences, so confirm amount and source before transfer.
steps.expect: the plan shows a scheduled or posted contribution.

steps.action: **Save account documents.** Download the program disclosure, confirmation, investment selection, beneficiary details, and contribution receipt.
steps.expect: you have records for taxes and future account management.

steps.action: **Set review reminders.** Revisit contributions, investment age band, beneficiary, and qualified expense rules at least yearly.
steps.expect: the plan remains aligned with school timeline and family changes.

recipes.verification: The plan account is open, beneficiary and successor owner are correct, investment allocation is selected, and the first contribution is scheduled or posted.

recipes.title: set up a fraud alert
recipes.name: set-up-a-fraud-alert
recipes.goal: Place a fraud alert on your credit file so lenders are warned to verify identity before opening new credit.

steps.action: **Choose one credit bureau.** In systems like the United States, contact one major bureau because it must notify the others.
steps.expect: you have the official bureau website or phone number.

steps.action: **Open the fraud-alert request.** Use the bureau's official fraud alert, identity theft, or credit protection page.
steps.expect: the page describes alert types and duration.

steps.action: **Select the alert type.** [BRANCH: initial alert | extended alert | active-duty alert] choose the one that matches your situation and documentation.
steps.expect: the form shows the expected expiration period.

steps.action: **Enter identity details.** Provide name, address, date of birth, national ID digits if required, and contact phone.
steps.expect: the bureau can match your credit file.

steps.action: **Upload documents if required.** For extended alerts, provide the official identity-theft report or required proof.
steps.expect: the upload or mail instructions confirm the accepted document type.

steps.action: **Submit the alert request.** Review the phone number carefully before final submission.
steps.expect: the bureau accepts the request or gives a reference number.

steps.action: **Save confirmation.** Download or screenshot the alert confirmation, expiration date, and any case number.
steps.expect: you can prove when the alert was placed.

steps.action: **Check the other bureaus.** Wait the stated transfer time, then confirm alerts appear at the other major bureaus.
steps.expect: all relevant credit files show an active fraud alert.

steps.action: **Decide whether to freeze too.** If you want to block most new credit, set up freezes in addition to the alert.
steps.expect: you understand the alert warns lenders while a freeze blocks access until thawed.

steps.action: **Record renewal date.** Add a calendar reminder before the alert expires.
steps.expect: you will be prompted to renew if risk remains.

steps.action: **Answer verification calls carefully.** If a lender calls, verify the lender through a known number before sharing information.
steps.expect: you do not disclose data to an unknown caller.

steps.action: **Monitor reports.** Review credit reports or alerts for accounts opened despite the warning.
steps.expect: any suspicious application is found quickly.

recipes.verification: Each relevant credit bureau shows an active fraud alert with the correct contact phone number and an expiration date you have recorded.

recipes.title: set up a health savings account
recipes.name: set-up-a-health-savings-account
recipes.goal: Open and fund a health savings account only if you are eligible, then set it up for qualified medical expenses and recordkeeping.

steps.action: **Confirm eligibility.** Check your plan documents for HSA eligibility and confirm you are not enrolled in disqualifying coverage.
steps.expect: you know whether contributions are allowed.

steps.action: **Check contribution limits.** Look up the current annual limit, family or self-only status, employer contributions, catch-up eligibility, and partial-year rules.
steps.expect: your planned contribution will not exceed the limit.

steps.action: **Choose an HSA provider.** [BRANCH: employer HSA | outside HSA] compare payroll access, monthly fees, debit card, investment options, expense ratios, transfer fees, and minimum cash balance.
steps.expect: the account choice fits your use and cost needs.

steps.action: **Open the account.** Enter legal name, address, tax ID, date of birth, beneficiaries if available, and contact details through the official provider.
steps.expect: the HSA is opened or pending identity verification.

steps.action: **Set funding method.** Choose payroll deduction, bank transfer, rollover, or trustee transfer, and account for employer contributions.
steps.expect: the funding schedule and tax treatment are clear.

steps.action: **Keep receipts.** Create a folder for medical, dental, vision, prescription, and insurance documents tied to HSA withdrawals.
steps.expect: every future reimbursement can be supported.

steps.action: **Order and secure payment tools.** Activate debit card only if needed and set account alerts.
steps.expect: unauthorized charges are easier to catch.

steps.action: **Make contributions.** Transfer or elect the planned amount after confirming eligibility and limits. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* excess or ineligible contributions can create tax penalties, so confirm eligibility and annual limits first.
steps.expect: the contribution posts to the HSA.

steps.action: **Review periodically.** Check contributions, fees, investments, and qualified expense records at least quarterly.
steps.expect: the account remains within limits and documentation is current.

recipes.verification: The HSA is open, contribution limits are documented, the first contribution or payroll election is confirmed, and a receipt system exists for qualified expenses.

recipes.title: set up a recurring transfer
recipes.name: set-up-a-recurring-transfer
recipes.goal: Create a recurring transfer between accounts with the right amount, timing, and buffer so it runs without overdrafts or missed goals.

steps.action: **Open the official transfer page.** Sign in and choose transfers, move money, automatic transfer, or recurring transfer.
steps.expect: source and destination account selectors appear.

steps.action: **Choose the source account.** Pick the account money will leave from, such as checking or payroll-linked account.
steps.expect: the current or available balance is shown.

steps.action: **Choose the destination account.** Select savings, brokerage, loan, external bank, or another owned account.
steps.expect: the destination name and last digits match the intended account.

steps.action: **Set the amount.** Enter a number you can sustain after rent, utilities, debt payments, and minimum balance needs.
steps.expect: the form accepts the amount and shows currency.

steps.action: **Pick the first date.** Choose a date after predictable deposits clear, not the same morning payroll is expected.
steps.expect: the first run date gives the source account a buffer.

steps.action: **Set frequency.** [BRANCH: weekly | every paycheck | monthly | custom] choose the cadence that matches income or savings goals.
steps.expect: the schedule preview matches your intent.

steps.action: **Check end conditions.** Choose no end date, fixed number of transfers, or end date.
steps.expect: the transfer will not continue longer than intended.

steps.action: **Review fees and limits.** Look for external-transfer limits, brokerage settlement rules, minimum balances, and transfer fees.
steps.expect: no unexpected fee or limit blocks the schedule.

steps.action: **Submit the recurring transfer.** Confirm only after source, destination, amount, date, and frequency are correct. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some same-day transfers cannot be canceled after processing starts, so review before final confirmation.
steps.expect: a confirmation page shows the recurring schedule.

steps.action: **Save confirmation.** Record confirmation number, first date, amount, and destination.
steps.expect: you can find the setup details without relying on memory.

steps.action: **Confirm the first run.** Check both accounts after the first scheduled date and settlement window.
steps.expect: money left the source and arrived at the destination as scheduled.

steps.action: **Adjust if cash gets tight.** Lower, pause, or reschedule the transfer before the next run if the buffer is too small.
steps.expect: future transfers match the updated plan.

recipes.verification: The recurring-transfer page shows the intended source, destination, amount, frequency, next run date, and the first completed transfer posts correctly.

recipes.title: set up a roth ira
recipes.name: set-up-a-roth-ira
recipes.goal: Open a Roth IRA, fund it within current eligibility rules, select investments, and save the records needed for taxes and beneficiary tracking.

steps.action: **Confirm Roth eligibility.** Check current income limits, contribution limits, earned-income requirements, and filing-status rules.
steps.expect: you know whether you can contribute directly and how much.

steps.action: **Choose a provider.** Compare brokerages or fund companies on account fees, fund expenses, investment choices, automatic investing, and service.
steps.expect: one Roth IRA provider is selected.

steps.action: **Open the account.** Enter identity, tax, employment, address, communication, and regulatory information through the provider's official site.
steps.expect: the Roth IRA is open or pending identity review.

steps.action: **Name beneficiaries.** Add primary and contingent beneficiaries with percentages totaling 100%.
steps.expect: beneficiary designations show accepted.

steps.action: **Link funding source.** Add a bank account or transfer source and verify any microdeposits or login connection.
steps.expect: the provider shows an approved funding source.

steps.action: **Contribute for the correct year.** Enter amount, tax year, and frequency, staying within the current allowed limit. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* contributions and investment purchases can create tax corrections if ineligible, so confirm amount, tax year, and eligibility first.
steps.expect: the contribution is scheduled, pending, or posted for the intended year.

steps.action: **Select investments.** Choose a target-date fund, index funds, or another diversified option that fits your risk tolerance and timeline.
steps.expect: cash contributions have an investment allocation or order.

steps.action: **Save confirmations.** Download account opening, beneficiary, contribution, investment, and tax-form notices.
steps.expect: records are stored for the contribution year.

recipes.verification: The Roth IRA is open, beneficiary designations are accepted, the intended contribution is posted or scheduled for the correct year, and the balance is invested or has a documented investment order.

recipes.title: set up a standing order
recipes.name: set-up-a-standing-order
recipes.goal: Set up a standing order for a fixed amount on a fixed schedule, and confirm it runs as intended.

steps.action: **Confirm this is the right payment type.** Compare standing order with direct debit, bill pay, bank transfer, and card autopay.
steps.expect: you know that you, not the payee, control the amount and date.

steps.action: **Collect payee details.** Verify name, account number, routing or sort code, IBAN, reference, and address if required.
steps.expect: payee details match an official invoice or written instruction.

steps.action: **Choose amount and frequency.** Enter the fixed payment amount, start date, repeat interval, and end date or until-cancelled setting.
steps.expect: the schedule matches the obligation.

steps.action: **Check processing dates.** Note weekends, holidays, bank cutoff times, and whether the bank sends early or next business day.
steps.expect: the payee will receive funds by the expected deadline.

steps.action: **Review before submitting.** Confirm payee, amount, date, frequency, reference, and funding account.
steps.expect: every field matches your intended payment.

steps.action: **Create the standing order.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* sending a scheduled payment may be hard to recall after processing, so confirm details before final approval.
steps.expect: the bank shows the standing order as active or scheduled.

steps.action: **Save confirmation.** Record confirmation number, screenshot, or written acknowledgement.
steps.expect: you can prove the instruction was created.

steps.action: **Confirm the first run.** After the first payment date, check bank transaction history and payee balance if available.
steps.expect: the payment posted with the right amount and reference.

steps.action: **Edit or cancel when circumstances change.** Update or cancel through the bank before the cutoff for the next payment.
steps.expect: the bank confirms the revised instruction.

recipes.verification: The standing order appears as active with the correct payee, amount, frequency, reference, and next payment date, and the first payment is confirmed after it runs.

recipes.title: set up direct deposit
recipes.name: set-up-direct-deposit
recipes.goal: Your employer or payer has verified bank instructions and will send future payments directly to your account.

steps.action: **Get bank details from a trusted source.** Use your bank app, online banking, a void check, or bank letter.
steps.expect: routing and account numbers match the deposit account.

steps.action: **Confirm account type.** Decide checking or savings and whether deposits are allowed.
steps.expect: the account type is clear.

steps.action: **Open the payer's form.** [BRANCH: payroll portal | paper form | HR email process]
steps.expect: you have the official direct-deposit setup method.

steps.action: **Enter bank information carefully.** Type routing number, account number, bank name, and account type exactly.
steps.expect: no digit is missing or transposed.

steps.action: **Choose deposit allocation.** Select full net pay, fixed dollar amount, percentage, or remainder if splitting accounts.
steps.expect: the form shows where each portion will go.

steps.action: **Attach proof if required.** Upload a void check, bank letter, or direct-deposit form from the bank.
steps.expect: the payer has documentation to verify the account.

steps.action: **Submit and save confirmation.** Send the form and keep a screenshot, confirmation number, or copy. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* wrong account digits can send wages to the wrong place; verify every digit before submitting.
steps.expect: payroll marks the request received.

steps.action: **Watch the first deposit.** Expect a prenote or one payroll-cycle delay, then verify the first actual deposit amount.
steps.expect: money lands in the intended account on payday.

recipes.verification: The first real payment appears in the intended bank account for the expected amount, and the payroll portal or paystub lists the same direct-deposit account ending digits.

recipes.title: split a bill with an app
recipes.name: split-a-bill-with-an-app
recipes.goal: Split a shared bill with an app so everyone can see what they owe, pay securely, and settle without confusion.

steps.action: **Pick the app.** Choose a payment or bill-splitting app everyone can access and that supports your currency and country.
steps.expect: participants know where the split will be tracked.

steps.action: **Create the expense.** Enter merchant, date, total amount, currency, and who paid.
steps.expect: the app shows one shared expense.

steps.action: **Choose split method.** [BRANCH: even split | itemized split] divide equally for simple bills, or assign items, tax, tip, and discounts to specific people.
steps.expect: each person's share is calculated.

steps.action: **Review special adjustments.** Add shared appetizers, service charges, delivery fees, coupons, deposits, or cash contributions.
steps.expect: the app total matches the receipt total.

steps.action: **Verify recipients.** Confirm names, avatars, phone numbers, or emails before requesting or sending money.
steps.expect: no payment is addressed to the wrong person.

steps.action: **Send requests or payments.** Request money if you paid, or pay your share if someone else paid.
steps.expect: the app shows pending, paid, or settled status.

steps.action: **Add a clear note.** Include the event, date, and item if helpful.
steps.expect: recipients can recognize the charge.

steps.action: **Chase politely if needed.** Send one reminder after a reasonable interval and mention the exact amount and bill.
steps.expect: the recipient gets a clear reminder without a duplicate request.

steps.action: **Settle and archive.** Mark cash payments as paid and close the expense after everyone is settled.
steps.expect: the group balance returns to zero or agreed state.

recipes.verification: The app shows the expense total matching the receipt and each participant marked paid, pending, or intentionally settled another way.

recipes.title: split finances with a partner
recipes.name: split-finances-with-a-partner
recipes.goal: Create a clear, documented system for sharing expenses with a partner while preserving bill reliability, consent, and personal privacy.

steps.action: **List shared expenses.** Identify rent, utilities, groceries, insurance, household supplies, pets, subscriptions, travel, and shared debt if any.
steps.expect: shared and individual expenses are separated.

steps.action: **Choose a split rule.** Pick equal split, income-proportional split, category ownership, allowance method, or another explicit rule.
steps.expect: both partners can state the rule.

steps.action: **Set payment workflow.** Decide who pays each bill, when reimbursements happen, and which account or app tracks them.
steps.expect: every shared bill has an owner and due date.

steps.action: **Create a shared record.** Build a spreadsheet, budget app category, or shared note with amounts, due dates, and settlement status.
steps.expect: both partners can view the current state.

steps.action: **Decide account structure.** Choose separate accounts, one joint bill account, or partial pooling based on trust, legal status, and privacy needs.
steps.expect: account roles and access are documented.

steps.action: **Set boundaries.** Agree on spending thresholds, personal money, debt privacy, emergency support, and what requires prior discussion.
steps.expect: consent rules are written down.

steps.action: **Automate predictable transfers.** Schedule recurring transfers or reminders for fixed shared bills.
steps.expect: routine bills are funded before due dates.

steps.action: **Review monthly.** Compare actual expenses, settle differences, and update the rule when income or bills change.
steps.expect: balances are current and disagreements are recorded for discussion.

recipes.verification: Both partners can view a current shared-expense list showing split rule, bill owners, due dates, paid status, reimbursement status, and next review date.

recipes.title: split shared household costs
recipes.name: split-shared-household-costs
recipes.goal: Shared household expenses (rent, utilities, groceries) are tracked in one agreed system so that at any moment each person knows what they owe or are owed, and balances settle cleanly on a regular schedule.

steps.action: **Agree the split rule first.** Even split, income-weighted, or per-item (person X never uses the car).
steps.expect: every housemate can state the rule the same way without argument.

steps.action: **Choose the tracking system.** [BRANCH: shared ledger app (Splitwise, Tricount) for many small entries | one shared spreadsheet for full control | a joint account funded by equal standing orders for simple even splits]
steps.expect: one system named as the single source of truth; no parallel side-tallies.

steps.action: **Set up the group and members.** Invite everyone by the same identifier (phone or email) and confirm each person appears once.
steps.expect: member list matches the household exactly, no duplicates.

steps.action: **Log the first shared expense.** Enter amount, payer, date, and who it splits between.
steps.expect: the app shows the balance shifting; the payer is now owed their share of it.

steps.action: **Make logging a habit, not a reconciliation.** Enter each expense when it happens, from the receipt, before you forget the amount.
steps.expect: running balances stay believable week to week, never a mystery.

steps.action: **Settle on a fixed cadence.** Pick a monthly date. On it, read the net balances and each debtor pays their single net figure to each creditor. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a sent payment cannot be recalled. Confirm the recipient handle and amount before sending.
steps.expect: app "settle up" recorded; balances return to zero.

steps.action: **Close out when someone moves out.** Do a final settle, include the deposit split and any final utility bills that arrive later, then remove them from the group.
steps.expect: the leaving person's balance is zero and both sides agree in writing (a chat message counts).

recipes.verification: Every shared expense for the period is in the one system, the monthly settle has run, and each person's net balance reads zero (or a single agreed carried figure) that all parties can see and confirm.

recipes.title: spot a fake charity
recipes.name: spot-a-fake-charity
recipes.goal: A charity request is checked for legitimacy before you donate, and any gift is made only through the charity's official channel.

steps.action: **Pause the appeal.** Do not donate during the call, doorstep visit, message thread, or emotional pitch.
steps.expect: you have time to verify without pressure.

steps.action: **Record the claimed name.** Write down the exact charity name, website, phone number, and fundraiser name.
steps.expect: spelling and contact details are available for comparison.

steps.action: **Search official registration.** Check the charity regulator, tax-exempt database, or nonprofit registry for the exact name.
steps.expect: registration status, legal name, and identifier match or do not match.

steps.action: **Compare contact details.** Use the registry or official charity website to compare phone, domain, address, and donation page.
steps.expect: the solicitation details match trusted records.

steps.action: **Look for pressure tells.** Notice urgency, secrecy, vague programs, celebrity claims, or refusal to send written information.
steps.expect: any manipulation signs are identified before payment.

steps.action: **Reject unsafe payment methods.** Refuse gift cards, wire transfers, crypto, payment apps to individuals, or cash pickup.
steps.expect: only traceable donation channels remain.

steps.action: **Donate through the official site.** Type the official web address yourself or use the registry's link.
steps.expect: payment goes to the confirmed charity domain or mail address.

steps.action: **Save the receipt.** Keep confirmation, amount, date, and charity identifier for records.
steps.expect: proof of donation is stored.

recipes.verification: The charity registration and contact details match official records, and any donation is made through the verified official channel.

recipes.title: start investing with index funds
recipes.name: start-investing-with-index-funds
recipes.goal: Start investing through low-cost index funds using an appropriate account, target allocation, funding plan, and saved confirmations.

steps.action: **Define the goal and timeline.** Choose retirement, long-term wealth, education, or another goal and estimate when the money may be needed.
steps.expect: time horizon and purpose are written down.

steps.action: **Choose account type.** Select employer plan, IRA, taxable brokerage, education account, or another account based on goal and tax rules.
steps.expect: the account type matches the goal.

steps.action: **Set an allocation.** Choose a simple mix such as target-date fund, total stock index, total bond index, or global stock and bond indexes.
steps.expect: target percentages add to 100%.

steps.action: **Compare fund costs.** Check expense ratio, minimum investment, tracking index, diversification, and transaction fees.
steps.expect: chosen funds are broad and low cost relative to alternatives.

steps.action: **Open or access the account.** Complete identity, tax, funding, and beneficiary steps if the account is new.
steps.expect: the account is open and ready for funding.

steps.action: **Fund the account.** Link a bank or payroll source and transfer an amount that fits the budget and contribution limits.
steps.expect: cash is scheduled, pending, or posted.

steps.action: **Buy the fund.** Enter the ticker, dollar amount or shares, account, and order type, then submit after checking details. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* investment orders may execute and change value quickly, so confirm ticker, account, and amount first.
steps.expect: order is accepted, filled, or pending.

steps.action: **Set automation and review.** Schedule recurring investments and a periodic allocation review.
steps.expect: future contributions and review dates are set.

recipes.verification: The account is open, funded, invested in the selected index fund or funds, target allocation is recorded, and recurring contribution or review reminder is active.

recipes.title: track mileage for taxes
recipes.name: track-mileage-for-taxes
recipes.goal: Create a reliable mileage log that can support tax deductions or reimbursements for business, charitable, medical, or moving trips where allowed.

steps.action: **Choose a log method.** Pick one system for date, destination, purpose, starting mileage, ending mileage, and miles driven.
steps.expect: one log format is ready before trips begin.

steps.action: **Record the starting odometer.** Take a photo or write down the odometer at the beginning of the tax year, vehicle use, or reimbursement period.
steps.expect: the opening mileage is timestamped.

steps.action: **Log each eligible trip.** Immediately after each trip, record date, start, destination, business or allowed purpose, and miles.
steps.expect: the trip appears in the log with enough detail to explain it later.

steps.action: **Keep supporting evidence.** Save appointment notes, client visits, delivery records, invoices, or employer requests that match the trip.
steps.expect: each meaningful trip has a reason outside the mileage log.

steps.action: **Separate personal miles.** Mark commuting, errands, and personal detours as non-deductible or personal.
steps.expect: only eligible miles are included in the tax or reimbursement total.

steps.action: **Reconcile monthly.** Compare app totals, odometer changes, calendars, and receipts for gaps or duplicates.
steps.expect: monthly mileage totals are plausible and corrected.

steps.action: **Close the period.** Record the ending odometer and summarize eligible miles by category.
steps.expect: annual or period totals can be copied into tax or reimbursement forms.
