recipes.verification: The mileage log contains dated eligible trips, purposes, distances, opening and closing odometer readings, and a summarized total that matches the tax or reimbursement entry.

recipes.title: track your spending
recipes.name: track-your-spending
recipes.goal: Record and review spending clearly enough to see where money goes and choose specific changes.

steps.action: **Pick one method.** [BRANCH: app | spreadsheet | envelope] choose an app for automation, a spreadsheet for control, or envelopes for cash limits.
steps.expect: one system is selected before you start categorizing.

steps.action: **List all spending sources.** Include checking, credit cards, cash, payment apps, subscriptions, and shared bills.
steps.expect: no regular payment path is missing.

steps.action: **Create practical categories.** Use categories such as housing, groceries, transport, eating out, subscriptions, health, debt, gifts, and fun.
steps.expect: every transaction has an obvious place.

steps.action: **Enter the last 30 days.** Import or type transactions, then split mixed purchases only when the split changes decisions.
steps.expect: one month of spending is visible in the chosen system.

steps.action: **Mark fixed and flexible costs.** Separate rent, insurance, and debt from groceries, dining, rides, shopping, and subscriptions.
steps.expect: you can see which costs can change soon.

steps.action: **Find the leaks.** Sort categories from largest to smallest and look for repeated small charges, unused subscriptions, fees, and impulse purchases.
steps.expect: at least one specific spending leak is named.

steps.action: **Set a weekly review.** Put a recurring 15 minute calendar block to update transactions and compare against your target.
steps.expect: the next review has a date and time.

steps.action: **Choose one adjustment.** Pick a measurable change, such as canceling one subscription or setting a dining-out cap.
steps.expect: the tracking leads to an action, not just a report.

recipes.verification: At least 30 days of spending is categorized, a weekly review is scheduled, and one named spending leak has a concrete action assigned.

recipes.title: understand a deductible
recipes.name: understand-a-deductible
recipes.goal: Understand how an insurance deductible affects claim payments, premiums, and out-of-pocket planning.

steps.action: **Find the deductible amount.** Locate the deductible on the declarations page, benefit summary, quote, or claim estimate.
steps.expect: the deductible dollar amount or percentage is identified.

steps.action: **Identify what it applies to.** Check whether the deductible applies per claim, per person, per year, per coverage, or per event.
steps.expect: the trigger for paying it is clear.

steps.action: **Separate premiums from deductible.** Note that premiums are paid to keep coverage active, while deductible is paid when a covered claim or service occurs.
steps.expect: ongoing cost and claim cost are separated.

steps.action: **Check exceptions.** Look for services or coverages with no deductible, separate deductible, copay, coinsurance, or waived deductible.
steps.expect: exceptions are listed.

steps.action: **Estimate a claim payment.** Subtract the deductible from a covered loss or apply the policy formula shown by the insurer.
steps.expect: approximate insurer payment and your share are visible.

steps.action: **Compare deductible options.** If choosing a policy, compare premium savings against the cash needed after a loss.
steps.expect: the deductible choice is affordable under a realistic claim.

steps.action: **Save the example.** Write one example using your policy terms and keep it with the policy.
steps.expect: you can explain the deductible without rereading the whole policy.

recipes.verification: You can state the deductible amount, when it applies, whether exceptions exist, how it changes a sample claim payment, and whether you have cash to cover it.

recipes.title: understand a loan offer
recipes.name: understand-a-loan-offer
recipes.goal: Read a loan offer well enough to compare cost, repayment risk, fees, prepayment rules, and alternatives before accepting.

steps.action: **Identify the loan type.** Note whether it is personal, auto, mortgage, student, payday, buy-now-pay-later, or business debt.
steps.expect: you know which rules and risks apply.

steps.action: **Record principal and term.** Write down amount borrowed, repayment length, first payment date, and payment frequency.
steps.expect: the basic repayment schedule is clear.

steps.action: **Compare APR to interest rate.** Use APR for offer comparison because it includes many required finance charges.
steps.expect: you can see whether fees make APR higher than the stated rate.

steps.action: **Calculate total cost.** Multiply payment by number of payments and add upfront fees not financed.
steps.expect: you know the total repayment amount and total interest or finance charge.

steps.action: **List fees.** Find origination, application, late, processing, document, title, insurance, broker, and closing fees.
steps.expect: every mandatory fee is either included in APR or separately noted.

steps.action: **Check prepayment rules.** Look for penalties, minimum interest, refund rules, and whether extra payments go to principal.
steps.expect: you know the cost of paying early.

steps.action: **Stress-test payment.** Compare monthly payment with rent, food, utilities, insurance, taxes, and emergency savings.
steps.expect: the payment fits without relying on perfect conditions.

steps.action: **Compare offers.** [BRANCH: accept | negotiate | keep shopping] Compare APR, term, fees, total cost, collateral, and flexibility side by side.
steps.expect: one offer is clearly better or you know what to ask next.

steps.action: **Accept only after review.** Read final documents before signing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing can create a binding debt, so verify amount, APR, term, fees, and collateral first.
steps.expect: signed documents match the offer you intended to accept.

recipes.verification: You can state the loan amount, APR, term, monthly payment, total repayment cost, all required fees, and whether early payoff has a penalty.

recipes.title: understand a rental lease
recipes.name: understand-a-rental-lease
recipes.goal: Read a rental lease closely enough to understand obligations, costs, exit options, and negotiation points before signing.

steps.action: **Confirm the parties and premises.** Check names, address, unit, parking, storage, pets, and included areas.
steps.expect: the lease describes the exact place and people involved.

steps.action: **Read the term.** Note start date, end date, renewal type, notice period, and month-to-month conversion.
steps.expect: you know when the lease begins and how it ends.

steps.action: **Map the rent terms.** Find rent amount, due date, grace period, payment method, late fees, and rent increase language.
steps.expect: total monthly cost and increase rules are visible.

steps.action: **List deposits and move-in money.** Separate security deposit, last month's rent, application fee, pet fee, key fee, and prepaid rent.
steps.expect: refundable and non-refundable amounts are labeled.

steps.action: **Check utilities and services.** Identify who pays electricity, gas, water, trash, internet, parking, snow removal, lawn care, and pest control.
steps.expect: no recurring housing cost is hidden.

steps.action: **Study break clauses.** Look for early termination fees, subletting rules, job relocation clauses, military clauses, and notice requirements.
steps.expect: you know the cost and process of leaving early.

steps.action: **Review conduct and maintenance duties.** Note repair reporting, entry notice, quiet hours, guests, pets, smoking, alterations, and insurance requirements.
steps.expect: daily rules and repair responsibilities are clear.

steps.action: **Negotiate before signing.** [BRANCH: unclear term | unacceptable term] ask for written clarification or edits before signing; do not rely on spoken promises.
steps.expect: agreed changes appear in the lease or addendum.

steps.action: **Save the signed copy and evidence.** Keep the lease, move-in checklist, photos, payment receipts, and messages.
steps.expect: you can prove the agreed terms and property condition later.

recipes.verification: You can state the lease term, rent due date, increase rules, deposit refund rules, early exit cost, and top negotiation requests from the written lease.

recipes.title: understand an explanation of benefits
recipes.name: understand-an-explanation-of-benefits
recipes.goal: Understand what an insurance explanation of benefits says you owe, what the insurer paid, and whether the provider bill matches it.

steps.action: **Confirm it is not a bill.** Look for wording such as "explanation of benefits" and find the claim number.
steps.expect: you can separate the insurer notice from any provider bill.

steps.action: **Match the service.** Compare patient, provider, service date, and claim number to your appointment or bill.
steps.expect: the EOB is tied to the correct visit, test, prescription, or procedure.

steps.action: **Read the billed and allowed amounts.** Note the provider's billed charge, the insurer's allowed amount, and any contractual adjustment.
steps.expect: you can see the price the plan used instead of only the sticker charge.

steps.action: **Identify plan payments.** Find what the insurer paid and whether the claim was in-network, out-of-network, denied, or partly paid.
steps.expect: the insurer payment status is clear.

steps.action: **Break down your responsibility.** Add deductible, copay, coinsurance, noncovered amount, and any amount already paid.
steps.expect: your expected balance is written as a single number.

steps.action: **Compare the provider bill.** Check whether the provider's requested payment equals the EOB patient responsibility minus payments you already made.
steps.expect: the bill either matches or has a specific mismatch.

steps.action: **Save evidence.** Download or photograph the EOB and bill with dates, claim number, and balance visible.
steps.expect: you have records ready for billing calls or appeals.

steps.action: **Choose the next action.** [BRANCH: bill matches | bill does not match | claim denied] pay or schedule payment only if it matches, ask the provider to correct mismatches, or review appeal rights for denials. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* paying a disputed balance can reduce leverage, so confirm the EOB and bill agree before payment.
steps.expect: you know whether to pay, dispute, or appeal.

recipes.verification: Your notes show the EOB claim number, service date, allowed amount, insurer payment, and patient responsibility, and any provider bill matches that responsibility or is under dispute.

recipes.title: understand apr
recipes.name: understand-apr
recipes.goal: Understand annual percentage rate well enough to compare borrowing costs, avoid cash advance surprises, and see why minimum payments can keep debt expensive.

steps.action: **Identify the product.** Determine whether the APR is for a credit card, personal loan, auto loan, mortgage, overdraft, or promotional offer.
steps.expect: the APR is interpreted in the right product context.

steps.action: **Find what APR includes.** Read whether origination fees, broker fees, annual fees, points, or compulsory charges are included.
steps.expect: you know whether APR is broader than the simple interest rate.

steps.action: **Separate APR types.** Check purchase APR, cash advance APR, balance transfer APR, penalty APR, variable APR, and promotional APR.
steps.expect: each transaction type has its own rate if applicable.

steps.action: **Check the grace period.** For cards, find when purchases avoid interest and what cancels the grace period.
steps.expect: you know whether paying the statement balance by the due date avoids purchase interest.

steps.action: **Read promotional terms.** Note start date, end date, transfer fee, deferred-interest rule, and what happens after the promo.
steps.expect: the date and balance that must be paid before the promo ends are clear.

steps.action: **Estimate periodic interest.** Divide APR by the number of billing periods as an approximation, then compare with the issuer's stated daily or monthly method.
steps.expect: the interest calculation is understandable enough to check a statement.

steps.action: **Test minimum-payment math.** Use the statement warning or calculator to compare paying minimum only, a fixed higher amount, and full balance.
steps.expect: payoff time and interest cost differences are visible.

steps.action: **Compare offers using total cost.** Compare APR, fees, term length, monthly payment, and flexibility together.
steps.expect: the cheaper-looking payment is not confused with the cheaper loan.

steps.action: **Pause before accepting unaffordable terms.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before signing or drawing funds, confirm the payment fits your budget and the key rate terms are written.
steps.expect: acceptance happens only after cost and obligation are understood.

recipes.verification: The APR types, included fees, grace period rule, promotional expiration, and estimated cost under minimum versus higher payments are documented.

recipes.title: understand your credit score
recipes.name: understand-your-credit-score
recipes.goal: You know what your credit score is, which behaviors move it, where to check it for free without harming it, and the real steps that repair it over time (not the myths).

steps.action: **Get your score and report for free.** Use a bureau's statutory free report or a reputable free score service. Checking your own is a "soft" inquiry and never lowers your score.
steps.expect: a current score plus the full report behind it.

steps.action: **Read the report for errors first.** Wrong balances, accounts you never opened, a debt already paid still shown as owing, or an address that is not yours. Errors are common and drag the score.
steps.expect: every account and inquiry recognized, or an error list to dispute (F1).

steps.action: **Learn the levers that actually move it.** In rough order of weight: payment history (pay on time, always), amounts owed (keep balances low relative to limits), length of history, credit mix, and new applications.
steps.expect: you can name your weakest lever from your own report.

steps.action: **Fix utilization, the fastest legitimate lever.** Keep balances well under your limits (a common guideline is under 30%, lower is better). Paying a card down before its statement date lowers the reported balance.
steps.expect: reported balances that are a small fraction of limits.

steps.action: **Automate on-time payments.** One missed payment can dent a score for years; set autopay for at least the minimum on every account so a busy month never becomes a late mark.
steps.expect: autopay active on every credit account.

steps.action: **Space out new applications.** Each formal application is a "hard" inquiry that dips the score slightly; several in a short window reads as distress. Apply only when needed.
steps.expect: no unnecessary hard inquiries planned.

steps.action: **Discard the myths.** Checking your own score does not hurt it; carrying a balance to "build credit" is false and just costs interest; closing an old card can hurt by shortening history and cutting available credit.
steps.expect: you can refute each myth. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not close your oldest account to tidy up; the lost history and limit can drop the score for years.

steps.action: **Re-check periodically and after big steps.** Look again in a few months, and before any major application (mortgage, loan).
steps.expect: a trend line over time, not a single snapshot.

recipes.verification: You have retrieved your score and full report for free, every account and inquiry on it is recognized (or under dispute), you can name the levers moving your score and refute the common myths, and on-time autopay plus low utilization are in place.

recipes.title: what to do if your card is stolen
recipes.name: what-to-do-if-your-card-is-stolen
recipes.goal: Stop use of a stolen debit or credit card, dispute unauthorized charges, and restore payments with a replacement card.

steps.action: **Freeze or lock the card immediately.** Use the issuer app or website if available before calling.
steps.expect: the card status shows locked, frozen, or temporarily blocked.

steps.action: **Check recent activity.** Review pending and posted transactions since the last time you had the card.
steps.expect: you can identify known charges and suspicious ones.

steps.action: **Call the issuer from a trusted number.** Use the number in the official app, on a statement, or on the issuer website.
steps.expect: you reach card-loss or fraud support.

steps.action: **Report the card stolen.** State whether the physical card, wallet, phone wallet, or card number was stolen. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once a card is reported stolen, the old card number is usually canceled, so confirm the correct card.
steps.expect: the issuer blocks the card permanently.

steps.action: **Dispute unauthorized charges.** Give transaction dates, merchant names, and amounts you do not recognize.
steps.expect: each disputed charge receives a case number or provisional-credit status.

steps.action: **Request replacement delivery.** Confirm mailing address, shipping speed, and whether emergency digital card access is available.
steps.expect: a replacement card or digital card is issued.

steps.action: **Remove stolen digital wallets.** If a phone or wallet was stolen, remove the card from mobile wallets and merchant accounts.
steps.expect: the issuer or wallet shows old tokens revoked.

steps.action: **Change related passwords if needed.** Update issuer login and email passwords if the stolen item included a phone, wallet note, or password list.
steps.expect: account access is protected by a fresh password and two-factor method.

steps.action: **Update autopays.** List subscriptions, utilities, rent, insurance, and loan payments that used the card.
steps.expect: essential payments have the replacement card or alternate payment method.

steps.action: **Watch pending charges.** Check daily until all pending transactions settle or disappear.
steps.expect: no new unauthorized charges post after the stolen-card report time.

steps.action: **Save documentation.** Keep issuer messages, dispute numbers, police report if filed, and delivery tracking.
steps.expect: you can prove the report date and disputed amounts.

steps.action: **Destroy the old card if recovered.** Cut through chip, magnetic stripe, and numbers after the issuer confirms cancellation.
steps.expect: the recovered card cannot be used.

recipes.verification: The stolen card shows canceled or blocked, unauthorized charges have dispute case numbers, and essential autopays are moved to a replacement or alternate payment method.

recipes.title: write a simple will
recipes.name: write-a-simple-will
recipes.goal: Create a simple will that names beneficiaries, an executor, guardians if relevant, and is signed according to local formalities.

steps.action: **Confirm a simple will is appropriate.** Review whether blended families, disabled beneficiaries, business ownership, estate tax, foreign property, or likely disputes require a lawyer.
steps.expect: you know whether to proceed or get legal help.

steps.action: **List assets and transfers outside the will.** Note real estate, bank accounts, retirement accounts, insurance, vehicles, digital assets, and accounts with beneficiaries or joint owners.
steps.expect: you know what the will controls and what passes separately.

steps.action: **Choose beneficiaries and backups.** Decide who receives specific items, residue, and alternate gifts if someone dies first.
steps.expect: every major gift has a primary and backup plan.

steps.action: **Choose executor and guardian roles.** Pick a responsible executor, backup executor, and guardians for minor children if needed; ask them before naming them.
steps.expect: named people are willing and reachable.

steps.action: **Draft the will.** Use a jurisdiction-appropriate form, attorney, or reputable estate-planning service and include revocation of prior wills, gifts, executor powers, guardians, and residuary clause.
steps.expect: the draft reflects your current wishes in plain language.

steps.action: **Review for conflicts.** Compare the will against beneficiary designations, joint ownership, divorce orders, prenups, and payable-on-death accounts.
steps.expect: obvious contradictions are fixed before signing.

steps.action: **Sign with required formalities.** Arrange disinterested witnesses and notary/self-proving affidavit if applicable. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an incorrectly signed will may fail after death when it cannot be corrected, so follow local signing instructions exactly.
steps.expect: the will is signed, witnessed, dated, and notarized/self-proved if available.

steps.action: **Store the original safely.** Put the original where the executor can access it, and keep copies labeled as copies.
steps.expect: the executor knows where the original is and how to retrieve it.

steps.action: **Calendar review triggers.** Review after marriage, divorce, birth/adoption, death, major move, major asset change, or law change.
steps.expect: the will has a future review reminder.

recipes.verification: The original will is signed, dated, witnessed according to local law, stored safely, and the executor knows where it is.

recipes.title: appeal a parking ticket
recipes.name: appeal-a-parking-ticket
recipes.goal: Appeal a parking ticket with timely evidence and understand the risk of penalties if the appeal fails or deadlines are missed.

steps.action: **Read the ticket carefully.** Check violation code, location, date, time, vehicle details, fine amount, and deadline.
steps.expect: the alleged violation and response window are clear.

steps.action: **Check official appeal rules.** Use the city, council, campus, or parking authority site, not third-party promises.
steps.expect: the allowed appeal method and deadline are identified.

steps.action: **Identify valid grounds.** Match your situation to recognized grounds such as wrong vehicle, unclear sign, paid parking, valid permit, machine fault, emergency, or administrative error.
steps.expect: the appeal has a specific argument.

steps.action: **Gather evidence.** Take photos of signs, curb markings, meter, payment screen, permit, ticket placement, and surrounding context as soon as possible.
steps.expect: evidence shows conditions at the time or soon after.

steps.action: **Write a concise appeal.** State the facts, ticket number, requested cancellation, and evidence list without exaggeration.
steps.expect: the reviewer can understand the claim quickly.

steps.action: **Submit before the deadline.** [BRANCH: online | mail | in-person] use the official channel and keep confirmation or proof of mailing.
steps.expect: the appeal is recorded as received.

steps.action: **Pause payment if rules allow.** Check whether appeal pauses the discount period, penalty increase, or collection action.
steps.expect: you know the pay-or-appeal risk.

steps.action: **Respond to the decision.** If allowed, pay, escalate, request a hearing, or submit additional evidence by the next deadline.
steps.expect: the case status and next deadline are known.

steps.action: **Close the case.** Keep the cancellation notice, payment receipt, or final decision.
steps.expect: there is proof the ticket is resolved.

recipes.verification: The issuing authority shows the ticket as appealed, cancelled, paid, or otherwise resolved, with confirmation saved.

recipes.title: apply for a building permit
recipes.name: apply-for-a-building-permit
recipes.goal: Apply for a building permit with plans, contractor details, fees, and inspection requirements understood before work starts.

steps.action: **Confirm permit type.** Check the local building department site for whether the project needs building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, zoning, demolition, right-of-way, or historic approval.
steps.expect: you know every permit or review required.

steps.action: **Check zoning and property limits.** Review setbacks, height, lot coverage, easements, floodplain, HOA, historic district, and utility clearance rules.
steps.expect: the proposed work is allowed or needs a variance/extra approval.

steps.action: **Prepare plans and documents.** Gather site plan, floor plans, elevations, structural details, energy forms, product approvals, contractor licenses, insurance, and owner affidavit.
steps.expect: the submission packet matches the checklist.

steps.action: **Create the permit application.** Enter property, owner, contractor, scope, valuation, occupancy, and trade information in the official portal or form.
steps.expect: the draft permit shows the correct project address and permit category.

steps.action: **Upload plans and pay intake fees.** Attach files using required names, sheet sizes, seals, and formats. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* application and plan-review fees are often nonrefundable once review begins, so confirm scope and valuation first.
steps.expect: the portal issues an application number and fee receipt.

steps.action: **Respond to plan review comments.** Revise drawings, answer code comments, and resubmit with changes clouded or listed.
steps.expect: each review cycle shows approved, pending, or comments returned.

steps.action: **Receive and post the permit.** Download the approved permit card, stamped plans, conditions, and inspection list.
steps.expect: the permit is active and visible at the job site before work starts.

steps.action: **Schedule required inspections.** Call or use the portal for footing, framing, rough electrical/plumbing/mechanical, insulation, final, or specialty inspections at the required stages.
steps.expect: inspection results show passed, failed with corrections, or scheduled.

steps.action: **Close the permit.** Complete final inspection and obtain certificate of completion or occupancy if required.
steps.expect: the permit status is finaled/closed, not expired or open.

recipes.verification: The permit is issued, posted, inspected at required stages, and finaled with written closure or certificate of completion/occupancy.

recipes.title: apply for a child passport
recipes.name: apply-for-a-child-passport
recipes.goal: Submit a complete child passport application with proof of citizenship, parental relationship, consent, photo, and fees.

steps.action: **Read the official child passport instructions.** Check age category, in-person requirement, parental consent rules, fees, and current processing times.
steps.expect: you know whether to use routine, expedited, or urgent service.

steps.action: **Complete the application without signing.** Fill the official form online or in print, using the child's legal name, birth details, Social Security number if applicable, and parent information.
steps.expect: the form is complete but unsigned.

steps.action: **Gather citizenship and relationship proof.** Prepare original or certified birth certificate, prior passport, consular report, adoption decree, or court order as applicable.
steps.expect: the documents prove both citizenship and parental relationship or list the missing proof.

steps.action: **Prepare parent or guardian identification.** Bring government photo ID for each appearing parent/guardian and photocopies if required.
steps.expect: identity documents match the adults giving consent.

steps.action: **Handle consent.** [BRANCH: both parents appear | one parent appears with notarized consent | one parent has sole authority | special family circumstance] Prepare the required consent form, notarization, court order, or statement.
steps.expect: the acceptance agent can document lawful consent.

steps.action: **Get a compliant passport photo.** Use a recent color photo with correct size, background, face visibility, and no disallowed accessories.
steps.expect: the photo meets official requirements and is not visibly rejected.

steps.action: **Book or choose an acceptance facility.** Use a post office, clerk, library, or passport agency appointment if required.
steps.expect: you have the location, time, and accepted payment methods.

steps.action: **Submit in person.** The child and required parent/guardian appear, the agent witnesses the signature, reviews documents, and collects fees. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* fees are generally nonrefundable once accepted, so confirm documents, spelling, service speed, and mailing address first.
steps.expect: you receive an application receipt or tracking information.

steps.action: **Track and receive the passport.** Monitor status after the posted delay and watch for separate mailings of passport book/card and returned originals.
steps.expect: the passport arrives and original documents are returned.

recipes.verification: The application is accepted with a receipt, and later the child has a passport whose name, birth date, sex marker, expiration date, and photo are correct.

recipes.title: apply for a government benefit
recipes.name: apply-for-a-government-benefit
recipes.goal: Submit a complete application for the right government benefit program and know how to track, correct, or appeal the result.

steps.action: **Identify the right program.** Use an official benefit finder, agency website, or community benefits navigator.
steps.expect: you have the exact program name and administering agency.

steps.action: **Read eligibility rules.** Check income limits, residency, age, disability, work history, household size, and immigration or citizenship requirements.
steps.expect: you know which rules you appear to meet and which are uncertain.

steps.action: **Build a document pack.** Gather ID, proof of residence, recent pay stubs or benefit letters, bank statements if required, lease or utility bills, and medical or job records if relevant.
steps.expect: every required document is named and copied.

steps.action: **Choose the application path.** [BRANCH: online | phone | paper | in-person] Pick the fastest official path that you can complete accurately.
steps.expect: you have the form, portal account, appointment, or phone number.

steps.action: **Complete the application.** Answer every required question, using "0" or "none" only where true.
steps.expect: the form has no blank required fields or unexplained mismatches.

steps.action: **Upload or attach documents.** Label files with applicant name, document type, and date before upload.
steps.expect: the portal or worker confirms each document is received.

steps.action: **Submit and save proof.** Review the summary, then submit. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* false statements can trigger repayment, denial, or penalties, so correct estimates before submitting.
steps.expect: you receive a confirmation number, receipt, or stamped copy.

steps.action: **Track follow-up requests.** Check mail, email, texts, portal messages, and voicemail during the processing window.
steps.expect: every request has a due date and response plan.

steps.action: **Respond to the decision.** [BRANCH: approved | denied | more information needed] Follow the notice instructions for enrollment, correction, or appeal.
steps.expect: you know the next required action and deadline.

recipes.verification: The agency has issued a confirmation, case number, or stamped receipt for the benefit application, and you have the next deadline recorded.

recipes.title: apply for a library card
recipes.name: apply-for-a-library-card
recipes.goal: Apply for a library card and confirm what borrowing, digital, and in-person services it unlocks.

steps.action: **Find the correct library system.** Search by your home address or nearest branch, not just the closest building.
steps.expect: you know which system serves your residence.

steps.action: **Check eligibility.** Look for resident, worker, student, reciprocal, nonresident, or temporary card rules.
steps.expect: you know whether the card is free or has a fee.

steps.action: **Review ID requirements.** Identify accepted photo ID and proof of address before visiting or applying online.
steps.expect: you have documents the library says it accepts.

steps.action: **Choose the application path.** [BRANCH: online pre-registration | in-person application | school or institutional card] Use the fastest option available for your status.
steps.expect: chosen path matches the library's rules.

steps.action: **Complete the form.** Enter legal name, address, contact information, birth date if required, and preferred branch.
steps.expect: application has no blank required fields.

steps.action: **Create a PIN if asked.** Choose a PIN or password you can remember for catalog and e-book access.
steps.expect: login credential is accepted.

steps.action: **Verify identity.** Upload documents online if allowed, or bring them to the service desk.
steps.expect: staff or system confirms your identity and address.

steps.action: **Receive the card or number.** Save the card number and any temporary barcode.
steps.expect: you can sign in to the library catalog.

steps.action: **Check what the card unlocks.** Review borrowing limits, e-books, databases, museum passes, computers, printing, holds, and interlibrary loan.
steps.expect: you know the useful services and any limits.

recipes.verification: You can log in to the official library catalog with your card number and PIN, and the account shows active borrowing privileges.

recipes.title: apply for a marriage license
recipes.name: apply-for-a-marriage-license
recipes.goal: Apply for a marriage license through the correct local authority so the ceremony can be legally recorded.

steps.action: **Find the issuing office.** Use the official city, county, state, province, or national civil registry site for the ceremony location.
steps.expect: the correct licensing authority and application method are identified.

steps.action: **Check eligibility rules.** Review age, consent, relationship, residency, prior marriage, and witness requirements.
steps.expect: both parties know whether they can apply.

steps.action: **Gather identity documents.** Collect government ID, birth certificate, proof of address, divorce decree, death certificate, or translation if required.
steps.expect: required documents are ready.

steps.action: **Schedule or start the application.** [BRANCH: online pre-application | in-person application] complete the official form or book an office appointment.
steps.expect: the office confirms submission or appointment details.

steps.action: **Attend together if required.** Both parties appear, sign, swear or affirm information, and present documents as the authority requires.
steps.expect: the clerk accepts the application or lists missing items.

steps.action: **Pay the fee.** Pay only through accepted official methods and keep the receipt.
steps.expect: the payment is recorded by the issuing office.

steps.action: **Check waiting period and validity.** Note when the license becomes usable and when it expires.
steps.expect: the ceremony date falls inside the valid window.

steps.action: **Give instructions to the officiant.** Provide the license, return deadline, witness rules, and filing address to the officiant.
steps.expect: the officiant knows how to complete and return it.

steps.action: **Order certificates after filing.** Request certified marriage certificates once the completed license is recorded.
steps.expect: you know how and when to obtain proof of marriage.

recipes.verification: The license is issued or appointment is confirmed, the waiting period and expiration date are known, and the officiant has filing instructions.

recipes.title: apply for a social security card
recipes.name: apply-for-a-social-security-card
recipes.goal: Apply for an original or replacement Social Security card through the official agency while protecting the number from misuse.

steps.action: **Confirm eligibility.** Check official Social Security Administration rules for who may receive a number or replacement card.
steps.expect: the application type and eligibility are clear.

steps.action: **Identify required documents.** List documents proving identity, age, citizenship or lawful status, and legal name change if relevant.
steps.expect: every required evidence category has an acceptable document.

steps.action: **Check replacement limits.** Review annual and lifetime replacement-card limits and exceptions.
steps.expect: you know whether the request counts toward a limit.

steps.action: **Choose the submission path.** [BRANCH: online | in-person | mail] use the official online service if eligible, otherwise prepare for office visit or mail submission.
steps.expect: the correct channel is selected.

steps.action: **Complete the official form.** Enter name, date of birth, place of birth, parents' names if required, citizenship status, and contact details accurately.
steps.expect: the application matches supporting documents.

steps.action: **Submit original or certified documents only if required.** Use the agency's stated document rules and avoid sending irreplaceable records unless required.
steps.expect: documents meet the evidence standard.

steps.action: **Keep proof of submission.** Save confirmation, appointment details, mailing receipt, or office receipt.
steps.expect: you can track the application.

steps.action: **Watch for the card by mail.** Monitor the expected delivery window and secure the mailbox.
steps.expect: the card arrives or the agency gives a status update.

steps.action: **Store the card safely.** Put the card in a secure place and do not carry it daily unless specifically needed.
steps.expect: the number is protected from routine loss.

recipes.verification: The official application is submitted or appointment is booked, required documents are identified, and the Social Security card or status notice is received.

recipes.title: apply for disability benefits
recipes.name: apply-for-disability-benefits
recipes.goal: Submit a disability benefits application with medical, work, income, and daily-function evidence, then track decisions and appeals.

steps.action: **Identify the correct disability program.** Match the benefit to your work history, military service, injury source, income/resources, and state coverage.
steps.expect: you know the agency, form, and basic eligibility theory.

steps.action: **Read medical and nonmedical rules.** Check required duration, severity, work limits, insured status, income/resource limits, and application date rules.
steps.expect: you know what evidence must prove.

steps.action: **Build a medical timeline.** List diagnoses, onset date, symptoms, treatments, providers, tests, medications, side effects, hospitalizations, and assistive devices.
steps.expect: the application can identify every relevant source.

steps.action: **Document work and daily limitations.** Describe job duties, why work stopped or changed, lifting, standing, sitting, concentration, attendance, personal care, transportation, and household tasks.
steps.expect: limitations are concrete and tied to real activities.

steps.action: **Gather records and releases.** Collect medical records you have, provider addresses, patient portal downloads, therapy notes, imaging reports, and signed release forms if requested.
steps.expect: the agency can request or review the evidence.

steps.action: **Complete the application.** [BRANCH: online | phone | paper | in-person] Answer identity, work, medical, income, and household questions fully.
steps.expect: the application summary has no unexplained gaps.

steps.action: **Submit and save proof.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* statements about onset, work, income, and medical limitations shape the case, so correct errors before submitting.
steps.expect: you receive a confirmation, claim number, or stamped copy.

steps.action: **Attend consultative exams and respond to requests.** Keep appointments, update address/phone, and send new records by deadlines.
steps.expect: the claim remains active and evidence is current.

steps.action: **Act on the decision.** [BRANCH: approved | denied | partially approved | more evidence requested] Review benefit amount, onset date, back pay, continuing reviews, or appeal deadline.
steps.expect: you know whether to accept, correct, or appeal.

recipes.verification: You have a disability claim confirmation and later a written decision, payment notice, or appeal filing receipt tied to the correct program and claim number.

recipes.title: apply for food assistance
recipes.name: apply-for-food-assistance
recipes.goal: Apply for food assistance benefits and track the case through interview, verification, approval, denial, or appeal.

steps.action: **Find the official program portal.** Use the state or local benefits agency site and confirm it covers food assistance/SNAP or the local equivalent.
steps.expect: you have the official application, phone number, or office address.

steps.action: **Check household rules.** Identify everyone who must be included because they live together and buy or prepare food together, plus mandatory members such as spouses or children under local rules.
steps.expect: the application household matches program definitions.

steps.action: **Gather verification documents.** Prepare ID, proof of residence, income, job loss, rent or mortgage, utility bills, childcare costs, child support, and medical expenses if relevant.
steps.expect: documents are ready to upload or bring to an interview.

steps.action: **Submit the application quickly.** Complete required identity, address, household, income, expense, and signature fields. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the application date can affect benefits and false statements can cause repayment or penalties, so submit accurate information and corrections.
steps.expect: you receive a case number, confirmation page, or stamped receipt.

steps.action: **Ask about expedited processing.** If your household has very low income/resources or urgent need, answer the screening questions and upload proof.
steps.expect: the agency marks the case expedited or gives the normal processing timeline.

steps.action: **Complete the interview.** [BRANCH: phone | in-person | waived] Keep the appointment, answer household and income questions, and ask for a written list of missing proof.
steps.expect: the worker confirms whether anything remains due.

steps.action: **Submit missing documents.** Upload, mail, fax, or deliver only the documents requested, with the case number on every page.
steps.expect: each item has a receipt, upload timestamp, or worker confirmation.

steps.action: **Read the decision notice.** [BRANCH: approved | denied | pending] Check monthly amount, certification period, reporting rules, appeal deadline, and EBT card instructions.
steps.expect: you know the benefit amount or the reason no benefit was issued.

steps.action: **Set up and protect the EBT card.** Activate the card from official instructions, set a PIN, and save the customer-service number separately.
steps.expect: the card balance is available and usable at eligible retailers.

recipes.verification: You have a case number and either an active EBT benefit with amount and certification period, or a written denial/pending notice with next deadline recorded.

recipes.title: apply for unemployment benefits
recipes.name: apply-for-unemployment-benefits
recipes.goal: File an unemployment insurance claim, preserve the effective date, and know how to certify weekly while the agency decides eligibility.

steps.action: **Find the official state unemployment site.** Use the state labor department website for the state where wages were earned.
steps.expect: you are on the official claim portal or have the correct phone filing number.

steps.action: **Check basic eligibility rules.** Review wage base, reason for job separation, availability for work, waiting week, and weekly certification rules.
steps.expect: you know the issues the agency will evaluate.

steps.action: **Create or recover portal access.** Set up login, multifactor authentication, and identity proofing if required.
steps.expect: you can reach the initial claim form.

steps.action: **Enter personal and work history.** Provide legal name, contact details, citizenship/work authorization questions, employers, dates, wages, and separation reason.
steps.expect: the application summary accurately reflects your employment history.

steps.action: **Upload or prepare documents.** Attach layoff notice, separation letter, pay stubs, W-2/1099, union hiring-hall proof, or work authorization documents when requested.
steps.expect: required uploads show received or the portal lists what is still needed.

steps.action: **Choose payment method and tax withholding.** Enter direct deposit from a bank statement or choose the agency debit card; decide whether to withhold income tax.
steps.expect: the payment method is confirmed and bank numbers are correct.

steps.action: **Submit the initial claim.** Review all answers, especially separation reason and last day worked. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* false statements can cause denial, repayment, penalties, or fraud findings, so correct estimates before submitting.
steps.expect: you receive a claim confirmation number and effective date.

steps.action: **Complete weekly certifications.** File each weekly or biweekly certification on schedule, reporting work, earnings, refusals, job searches, and availability exactly as asked.
steps.expect: each week shows submitted or pending review.

steps.action: **Respond to fact-finding and decisions.** Answer employer-dispute questions, identity requests, and determinations by the stated deadline.
steps.expect: the claim has a payment, pending issue, denial, or appeal deadline.

recipes.verification: You have a claim confirmation number, effective date, payment method, and at least the next weekly certification deadline recorded.

recipes.title: book a government appointment
recipes.name: book-a-government-appointment
recipes.goal: You hold a confirmed appointment at the correct government office for your specific service, at a workable date and time, with a checklist of the exact documents that office requires so the visit succeeds in one trip.

steps.action: **Identify the exact office and service.** Confirm which agency and which branch handles your specific need and your catchment area; the right service at the wrong office is a wasted trip.
steps.expect: a named office and service that matches your goal and location.

steps.action: **Find the official booking channel.** Use the agency's own site or listed number; ignore paid intermediaries that resell free slots.
steps.expect: an official booking page or phone line for that service.

steps.action: **Read the document checklist before booking.** Most agencies publish exactly what to bring; note originals versus copies, photos, fees, and proof-of-address rules.
steps.expect: a written list of every required document for your service.

steps.action: **Choose the booking interface.** [BRANCH: online self-service portal | phone line (for services not bookable online, or if you need accommodations) | in-person queue ticket where no appointment system exists]
steps.expect: a booking method appropriate to the service.

steps.action: **Hunt for a slot, and widen the search if empty.** [BRANCH: slots available → book the best time | fully booked → check nearby branches, look for a released-slot refresh, or set an alert]
steps.expect: an offered date and time, or a concrete plan to catch a released slot.

steps.action: **Book a realistic time with travel and buffer.** Avoid the first slot if you cannot reliably arrive early; leave margin for security and check-in.
steps.expect: a held slot at a time you can actually make.

steps.action: **Confirm and capture the booking.** Save the confirmation number, QR code, or email, and add it to your calendar with the address and document checklist attached. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some agencies penalize no-shows with a cooldown before you can rebook, so cancel through the official channel if plans change rather than skipping.
steps.expect: a booking reference stored with all visit details.

steps.action: **Assemble documents the day before.** Work the checklist item by item, originals plus any required copies, in one folder.
steps.expect: every checklist item physically present and organized.

steps.action: **Attend with margin.** Arrive early, bring the confirmation and ID, and keep the reference number accessible.
steps.expect: you are checked in against your appointment and seen.

recipes.verification: You have a confirmation reference for the correct service at the correct office and a workable time, plus a complete document checklist for that service assembled before the visit.

recipes.title: check your voter registration status
recipes.name: check-your-voter-registration-status
recipes.goal: Confirm whether your voter registration is active and correct before the deadline for the next election.

steps.action: **Find the official lookup.** Start from your election office, secretary of state, electoral commission, or national voting portal and search "voter registration status".
steps.expect: the lookup page is on an official government domain or linked directly by one.

steps.action: **Check the page scope.** Confirm the lookup covers your current address and election jurisdiction.
steps.expect: the page names your state, province, county, municipality, or country.

steps.action: **Enter identifying information.** Type your name, birth date, address, and any requested ID exactly as they appear on your registration.
steps.expect: the form accepts the fields without format errors.

steps.action: **Review active status.** Look for "active", "registered", "inactive", "pending", or "not found".
steps.expect: you can record the exact status shown.

steps.action: **Verify personal details.** Compare name spelling, residential address, mailing address, party selection if applicable, and voting precinct.
steps.expect: each field is either correct or marked for correction.

steps.action: **Check upcoming deadlines.** Open the official election calendar for registration updates, absentee requests, and early voting.
steps.expect: you have the deadline dates for your next election.

steps.action: **Fix errors promptly.** [BRANCH: online update | paper form | election office contact] Use the correction method the official site lists.
steps.expect: you receive a submission confirmation or know where to deliver the form.

steps.action: **Save proof of the check.** Screenshot or print the status page without exposing it publicly.
steps.expect: you have a dated record for follow-up.

steps.action: **Recheck after processing.** Wait the stated processing time, then run the lookup again.
steps.expect: the corrected registration appears or you have a reason to contact the office.

recipes.verification: The official voter lookup shows your registration as active or accepted, with your current residential address and correct voting jurisdiction.

recipes.title: contact your elected representative
recipes.name: contact-your-elected-representative
recipes.goal: Contact the correct elected representative with a concise, specific request and create a record for follow-up.

steps.action: **Find who represents you.** Use an official election, legislature, parliament, council, or district lookup tool and enter your address if required.
steps.expect: you have the representative's name, office, district, and official contact page.

steps.action: **Choose the right level of government.** Match the issue to local, regional, national, school, or special-district authority.
steps.expect: you are contacting an office that can act on the matter.

steps.action: **Choose a channel.** [BRANCH: call | email or web form | letter | town hall] use a call for timely issues, written contact for detail, a letter for formal records, or a town hall for public questions.
steps.expect: the channel fits the urgency and complexity.

steps.action: **State your relationship to the district.** Give your name, city or neighborhood, and whether you are a constituent, business owner, student, worker, or affected person.
steps.expect: the office can route and count your message.

steps.action: **Be concise and specific.** Name the bill, policy, service request, agency case, budget item, or local problem, then state the action you want.
steps.expect: the staff can summarize your request in one sentence.

steps.action: **Add relevant facts.** Include dates, locations, case numbers, personal impact, and evidence links only when they support the request.
steps.expect: the message is persuasive without becoming hard to process.

steps.action: **Ask for a response or action.** Request a vote position, casework help, meeting, status update, or explanation of next steps.
steps.expect: the office knows what follow-up you expect.

steps.action: **Send or deliver the message.** Confirm spelling, contact details, attachment privacy, and office destination before submitting.
steps.expect: you receive a sent email, form confirmation, call note, postal receipt, or meeting record.

steps.action: **Record the follow-up date.** Save the message, staff name if known, confirmation number, and a date to follow up.
steps.expect: you have a usable contact log.

steps.action: **Follow up if needed.** If the office does not respond within a reasonable time, contact again with the prior date and confirmation details.
steps.expect: the second contact builds on the first instead of starting over.

recipes.verification: The correct representative and government level are identified, a concise request has been sent through an appropriate channel, and a follow-up record exists.

recipes.title: dispute a property tax assessment
recipes.name: dispute-a-property-tax-assessment
recipes.goal: Challenge a property tax assessment with evidence and preserve appeal rights before the local deadline.

steps.action: **Read the assessment notice.** Identify assessed market value, taxable value, exemptions, classification, deadline, and appeal office.
steps.expect: you know exactly what can be challenged and by when.

steps.action: **Review the property record card.** Check square footage, bedrooms, bathrooms, lot size, construction type, condition, year built, improvements, and exemptions.
steps.expect: you have a list of factual errors or know the dispute is about value.

steps.action: **Find comparable evidence.** Gather recent sales, appraisals, listings, photos of defects, repair bids, flood/fire damage records, or income data for rental property.
steps.expect: evidence supports a specific lower value or correction.

steps.action: **Calculate the requested value.** Write a clear proposed assessed value and explain the method, not just the desired tax bill.
steps.expect: the assessor can see the adjustment requested.

steps.action: **Try informal review if available.** Contact the assessor before the formal deadline and provide concise evidence.
steps.expect: the office either corrects the record or tells you to file a formal appeal.

steps.action: **File the formal appeal.** Complete the board, assessor, or tribunal form with parcel number, owner name, disputed value, grounds, and evidence list. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* missed appeal deadlines usually cannot be revived, so submit before attempting more negotiation.
steps.expect: you receive a filing receipt, case number, or hearing notice.

steps.action: **Pay required taxes or escrow amounts.** Follow local rules on whether payment is required to avoid penalties while appealing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* tax payments and late penalties affect liens and deadlines, so confirm payment rules before withholding anything.
steps.expect: taxes are current or a lawful appeal-payment arrangement is documented.

steps.action: **Prepare for hearing.** Organize evidence in the requested format, label comparable sales, and make copies for the board and assessor.
steps.expect: your packet proves factual error or overvaluation.

steps.action: **Attend and follow up.** Present facts briefly, answer questions, and wait for the written decision.
steps.expect: you receive a decision, revised notice, refund, credit, or further appeal deadline.

recipes.verification: You have a filed appeal receipt and later a written decision showing corrected assessment, denied appeal with reasons, or next-level appeal deadline.

recipes.title: file a noise complaint
recipes.name: file-a-noise-complaint
recipes.goal: File a noise complaint through the correct channel with enough detail for the city, landlord, or non-emergency responder to act.

steps.action: **Document the noise pattern.** Write down start time, stop time, address or landmark, type of sound, and how it affects you.
steps.expect: you have a dated log with at least one specific incident.

steps.action: **Check immediate danger.** If there is violence, threats, injury, fire, or suspected emergency, call emergency services instead.
steps.expect: the situation is classified as emergency or non-emergency.

steps.action: **Identify the right channel.** [BRANCH: non-emergency line | city service portal | landlord or building manager | council or code enforcement] Match the source to the listed enforcement channel.
steps.expect: you have the correct phone number, portal, or email.

steps.action: **Gather evidence carefully.** Record short audio or video only where lawful, capture decibel app readings as rough context, and keep witness notes.
steps.expect: evidence shows date, time, and location without trespassing.

steps.action: **Make the complaint.** Provide location, current status, duration, repeat history, and whether you want contact.
steps.expect: you receive a service request number, call log number, or written acknowledgment.

steps.action: **Avoid direct escalation during the incident.** Do not bang on doors or confront people if intoxication, anger, or crowds are involved.
steps.expect: you remain physically separated from the source.

steps.action: **Track the response.** Save the case number and note whether an officer, inspector, or manager responded.
steps.expect: your log includes response time and outcome.

steps.action: **Escalate repeated violations.** If the same source continues, attach the prior case numbers and request code enforcement or council review.
steps.expect: the agency sees the pattern rather than a single isolated complaint.

steps.action: **Close the loop.** If the noise stops, mark the incident resolved or tell the landlord/agency.
steps.expect: the record reflects the current condition.

recipes.verification: You have a complaint record number or written acknowledgment that names the noise location, date, time, and responsible handling channel.

recipes.title: file a police report online
recipes.name: file-a-police-report-online
recipes.goal: Submit a non-emergency police report through the correct official portal and keep proof that the agency received it.

steps.action: **Confirm online reporting is allowed.** Read the police department's online reporting rules for your incident type, location, dollar limits, suspect information, and evidence.
steps.expect: you know the incident can be reported online or that you must call/visit instead.

steps.action: **Identify the correct jurisdiction.** Match the incident location to city police, county sheriff, campus police, transit police, or state patrol.
steps.expect: the portal belongs to the agency responsible for that address.

steps.action: **Gather incident details.** Prepare names, phone numbers, addresses, dates, item descriptions, values, serial numbers, license plates, and a short factual timeline.
steps.expect: the report can be completed without guessing.

steps.action: **Open the official report form.** Use the agency website, not an ad or third-party form, and create an account only if required.
steps.expect: the page shows the agency name, online report categories, and privacy notice.

steps.action: **Complete the narrative.** State what happened, when, where, who was involved, and what evidence exists; avoid speculation or legal conclusions.
steps.expect: the narrative is clear enough for an officer to understand the event.

steps.action: **Upload supporting files.** Attach photos, screenshots, invoices, serial-number records, or identity-theft documents if the portal accepts them.
steps.expect: each upload shows as attached or queued.

steps.action: **Review and submit.** Verify spelling, contact details, incident address, dates, and dollar amounts before filing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* false police reports can carry criminal penalties, so correct uncertain statements before submitting.
steps.expect: the portal returns a temporary report number, confirmation page, or email receipt.

steps.action: **Save the confirmation.** Download or print the receipt, copy the report number, and save the submitted narrative and attachments.
steps.expect: you can prove when and where the report was filed.

steps.action: **Follow agency instructions.** Watch for approval, rejection, officer contact, or a request for an in-person statement.
steps.expect: you know the next status check date and response method.

recipes.verification: You have an official confirmation, temporary or final report number, incident summary, and saved copy of every file submitted.

recipes.title: find your polling place
recipes.name: find-your-polling-place
recipes.goal: Find the correct polling place for your address and election, then prepare the documents and access information needed to vote.

steps.action: **Use the official lookup.** Search the official election office, electoral commission, or local authority polling place tool.
steps.expect: the source is government-run or election-office-run.

steps.action: **Enter your address carefully.** Use residence address, apartment number, postal code, and name if requested.
steps.expect: the lookup returns your assigned polling place or voting district.

steps.action: **Confirm the election.** Make sure the result applies to the specific election, date, and voting method.
steps.expect: the polling place matches the election you plan to vote in.

steps.action: **Record hours.** Note opening time, closing time, early voting dates, and any holiday or runoff schedule.
steps.expect: you know when voting is available.

steps.action: **Check ID rules.** Review accepted identification, proof of address, voter card, or exception process.
steps.expect: you know what to bring and what to do if you lack it.

steps.action: **Check what else to bring.** Bring registration confirmation, sample ballot, required documents, and any allowed assistance forms.
steps.expect: your voting materials are ready.

steps.action: **Review accessibility.** Check accessible entrance, parking, language help, curbside voting, or assistance rights.
steps.expect: access needs have a plan.

steps.action: **Plan arrival.** Choose transport, parking, queue time, and backup timing before polls close.
steps.expect: the travel plan fits voting hours.

steps.action: **Verify before leaving.** Recheck the official source on voting day in case of location changes.
steps.expect: the latest polling place and hours are confirmed.

recipes.verification: The official election source confirms your polling place address, election date, voting hours, ID rules, and accessibility plan.

recipes.title: get a birth certificate copy
recipes.name: get-a-birth-certificate-copy
recipes.goal: You obtain an official copy of a birth certificate (certified or plain, as your purpose requires) from the correct issuing authority, with the right identity proof and fee, delivered in a form that will be accepted by whoever asked for it.

steps.action: **Identify the issuing authority.** Certificates are issued where the birth was registered (a vital-records office, civil registry, or the equivalent), regardless of where you live now.
steps.expect: a named registry office responsible for that place of birth.

steps.action: **Decide certified versus plain copy.** A certified (official, sealed) copy is required for passports, benefits, and legal use; a plain or informational copy is cheaper but not accepted for official purposes. Confirm what the requester actually needs.
steps.expect: a clear choice matching the purpose, since ordering the wrong type means ordering again.

steps.action: **Find the official ordering channel.** Use the registry's own site, an official mail form, or in-person counter; avoid third-party "expediter" sites that add large fees over the official price.
steps.expect: the official order page or address, with the real fee shown.

steps.action: **Confirm your eligibility and required ID.** Access is usually restricted to the person, close family, or a legal representative; you will typically need to prove your identity with a government ID and state your relationship.
steps.expect: your case matches the eligibility list and you have the accepted ID ready.

steps.action: **Complete the application with exact birth details.** Enter names, dates, and places precisely as registered; a mismatch stalls the search.
steps.expect: the form validates with no missing required field.

steps.action: **Choose delivery and processing speed.** [BRANCH: standard mail (cheapest, slowest) | expedited processing or shipping (extra fee) | in-person pickup where offered]
steps.expect: a delivery method and an estimated arrival date noted.

steps.action: **Pay the official fee.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* fees are generally non-refundable even if no record is found, so verify the birth details and issuing authority before paying.
steps.expect: a payment confirmation and an order/reference number saved.

steps.action: **Track the order and receive it.** Monitor status if tracking exists; on arrival, verify the seal, the spelling of every name, dates, and that it is the certified type if you ordered one.
steps.expect: a correct, sealed certificate (or the plain copy you chose) in hand.

steps.action: **Store it safely and note where it is.** A certified copy is a foundational identity document.
steps.expect: the certificate stored securely with its location known.

recipes.verification: You hold the correct type of birth certificate (certified and sealed if required) from the proper issuing authority, with every name, date, and place printed correctly, and it is accepted by the party that requested it.

recipes.title: get a business tax id
recipes.name: get-a-business-tax-id
recipes.goal: Obtain the correct business tax identification number and save the official confirmation for banking, payroll, tax filing, and licensing.

steps.action: **Determine which tax ID is needed.** Identify whether you need a federal employer identification number, state tax account, sales tax permit, payroll withholding account, or local tax number.
steps.expect: you know which agency issues the number.

steps.action: **Gather business details.** Prepare legal name, entity type, address, responsible party, formation jurisdiction, ownership date, employee plans, and business activity.
steps.expect: every required field can be answered accurately.

steps.action: **Open the official application.** Use the tax agency's direct site and avoid paid lookalike services unless you intentionally hire one.
steps.expect: the page belongs to the issuing government agency.

steps.action: **Complete the application.** Enter structure, reason, responsible party, addresses, industry, employee, excise, and sales questions as applicable.
steps.expect: the review screen matches formation documents and planned activity.

steps.action: **Submit the application.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* tax registrations create filing duties, so confirm the entity, responsible party, and tax types before submitting.
steps.expect: the agency issues a tax ID immediately or provides a pending confirmation.

steps.action: **Download the confirmation letter.** Save the EIN letter, state account notice, permit, or registration certificate in the business records folder.
steps.expect: you have a durable PDF or printed record.

steps.action: **Set portal access and notices.** Create login credentials, enable multifactor authentication, and choose mail/email notice preferences.
steps.expect: you can access the tax account and receive notices.

steps.action: **Use the tax ID consistently.** Provide it to the bank, payroll provider, vendors, licensing offices, and tax preparer only when needed.
steps.expect: business accounts use the official legal name and tax ID.

steps.action: **Calendar filing obligations.** Record sales tax, payroll, franchise, income, and annual report deadlines tied to the registration.
steps.expect: the business knows when the first filing is due, even if zero activity.

recipes.verification: You have an official tax ID confirmation showing the legal business name, number, issue date or registration date, and issuing agency.

recipes.title: get a copy of a police report
recipes.name: get-a-copy-of-a-police-report
recipes.goal: Request a copy of a police report from the correct agency for insurance, court, employment, or personal records.

steps.action: **Identify the reporting agency.** Match the incident location to city police, county sheriff, state patrol, campus police, transit police, or highway patrol.
steps.expect: you have the agency name that responded or took the report.

steps.action: **Find the records request page.** Use the official agency website and search for "police report request" or "records division".
steps.expect: you have the approved online form, email, mail address, or counter hours.

steps.action: **Check release rules.** Read who can request the report, what ID is required, whether juveniles or open investigations are restricted, and how long processing takes.
steps.expect: you know whether you can request the full report or only a summary.

steps.action: **Collect identifiers.** Write down report number, involved names, incident address, date, vehicle plate or crash number if relevant, and officer name if known.
steps.expect: the request can be matched without guessing.

steps.action: **Prepare ID and authorization.** Scan your ID and any insurance, attorney, employer, or victim authorization form if requested.
steps.expect: the records unit can verify your identity and relationship to the case.

steps.action: **Submit the request.** [BRANCH: portal | email | mail | records counter] Complete the official request with delivery preference.
steps.expect: the agency gives a receipt, request number, or staff confirmation.

steps.action: **Pay required fees.** Confirm copy, certification, mailing, and redaction fees before paying. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* paid records fees are often nonrefundable once staff begins processing.
steps.expect: you receive a fee receipt or invoice.

steps.action: **Wait the stated period.** Track the processing window and any notice that the report is unavailable or redacted.
steps.expect: you know the earliest reasonable follow-up date.

steps.action: **Receive and review the report.** Confirm the report number, incident date, parties, and redactions match the requested case.
steps.expect: the document can be used for the purpose you requested.

recipes.verification: You have a police report, crash report, incident summary, or official denial tied to the correct report number or incident details.

recipes.title: get a document apostilled
recipes.name: get-a-document-apostilled
recipes.goal: Get an apostille or the correct alternative authentication so a public document can be accepted in another country.

steps.action: **Confirm the destination country.** Check whether the destination is part of the Hague Apostille Convention with the issuing country.
steps.expect: you know whether apostille or legalization is required.

steps.action: **Identify the competent authority.** Find the official authority that apostilles this document type, such as state, national, court, or education authority.
steps.expect: the correct office is identified.

steps.action: **Check document condition.** Verify the document is certified, recently issued if required, signed by an eligible official, and not laminated or altered.
steps.expect: the document meets intake requirements.

steps.action: **Notarize first if needed.** For private documents, get notarization by an approved notary before requesting apostille.
steps.expect: the notarization is valid for the apostille office.

steps.action: **Prepare the request.** Complete the form, destination country field, return address, fee, and prepaid return method if required.
steps.expect: the submission packet is complete.

steps.action: **Submit to the authority.** [BRANCH: mail | counter service | online request] send or present the document through the official method.
steps.expect: the office accepts the request or provides a tracking reference.

steps.action: **Track the timeline.** Note processing time, mailing time, expedited options, and appointment availability.
steps.expect: you have a realistic completion date.

steps.action: **Check the apostille when returned.** Confirm name, document reference, seal, signature, country, and attachment are intact.
steps.expect: the apostille corresponds to your document.

steps.action: **Arrange translation if required.** Use a sworn, certified, or official translator only if the destination authority requires it.
steps.expect: the final packet matches the recipient's instructions.

recipes.verification: The document has an apostille or required authentication attached by the competent authority for the destination country.

recipes.title: pay a parking fine
recipes.name: pay-a-parking-fine
recipes.goal: A parking citation is resolved: either paid through the official channel with proof retained (ideally within any early-payment discount window), or formally appealed on valid grounds, with no escalation to late penalties or a vehicle hold.

steps.action: **Read the notice for the three dates that matter.** The discount deadline (many authorities halve the fine if you pay quickly), the standard due date, and the appeal deadline.
steps.expect: you know the amount owed today and how it rises after each date.

steps.action: **Verify the citation is real and yours.** Match the plate, date, time, and location to your own records; parking-fine phishing texts and fake QR stickers are common. Reach the authority through the number on the official notice or its official site, never a link in a text.
steps.expect: the citation appears in the authority's official lookup with matching details.

steps.action: **Decide pay or appeal.** [BRANCH: the ticket is valid and you will pay → go to payment | you have genuine grounds (wrong plate, valid permit shown, faded or missing signage, expired meter that was broken, already paid) → go to appeal]
steps.expect: a clear choice with the reasoning noted.

steps.action: **Appeal path: gather evidence and file before the deadline.** Photos of signage, meter receipts, permit, or a broken-meter report; submit through the official appeal form or hearing request.
steps.expect: an appeal reference number and a stated response timeline.

steps.action: **Pay path: use the official channel only.** Enter the citation number on the authority's portal, or pay by the listed mail or in-person method. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* paying a citation is generally treated as admitting liability and usually ends any right to appeal, so appeal first if you intend to contest.
steps.expect: the portal accepts payment and shows a paid/closed status.

steps.action: **Pay within the discount window if you are paying.** If the notice offers a reduced early amount, paying sooner is strictly cheaper.
steps.expect: the lower amount charged, confirmed on the receipt.

steps.action: **Capture proof of payment.** Save the confirmation number, screenshot, or emailed receipt, and note the date.
steps.expect: a durable record tying your payment to the citation number.

steps.action: **Confirm the citation shows closed.** Re-check the lookup a few days later.
steps.expect: status reads paid, closed, or dismissed, with no balance.

recipes.verification: The authority's official citation lookup shows the ticket as paid/closed or dismissed with a zero balance, and you hold a dated proof of payment or an appeal decision referencing the citation number.

recipes.title: register a change of address
recipes.name: register-a-change-of-address
recipes.goal: After a move, your new address is registered where the law requires it, your mail follows you, and the institutions that matter (bank, employer, insurance, subscriptions) all point at the new address, in the right order.

steps.action: **Establish your country's rule and deadline first.** Search the official municipal or government site for "change of address" or the local term (Anmeldung/Ummeldung, 転居届, verhuizing doorgeven). Note the deadline; several countries fine late registration.
steps.expect: you know whether you owe a formal registration, to whom, and by when.

steps.action: **Do the formal registration where required.** Book the municipal appointment (slots run out; book the moment the move date is known), bring the document set, and leave with the confirmation certificate. That certificate unlocks banks, contracts, and utilities in registration countries, so store it carefully.
steps.expect: registration completed within the deadline, certificate in hand or in the mail.

steps.action: **Set up postal forwarding before the move if possible.** The postal service's mail-forwarding product (USPS change of address, Royal Mail redirection, Nachsendeauftrag) buys you months of catching whatever you forgot. Pay for the longest sensible window.
steps.expect: mail addressed to the old place arrives at the new one, each piece a reminder of an institution still to update.

steps.action: **Update the money layer next.** Bank and cards, payroll or pension, tax authority, insurance policies. Copy the address exactly from the registration or lease; inconsistent formats across institutions cause verification failures later (`finance/open-a-bank-account` step 2's lesson in reverse).
steps.expect: the institutions that send legally important mail all show the new address.

steps.action: **Update the identity layer.** Driving licence and vehicle registration where required (often with its own deadline), voter registration, national ID where it carries an address.
steps.expect: every government-issued document that shows an address either updated or its update in progress.

steps.action: **Sweep the long tail with the forwarded mail as your checklist.** Doctor and dentist (`healthcare/book-a-doctors-appointment` records), phone and internet (`housing/set-up-utilities` step 8 closes the old, this step opens the new), online shopping default addresses (`shopping/buy-a-product-online` will otherwise ship to your past), subscriptions, loyalty programs, school or university. Each forwarded envelope names a laggard; update it and the stream dries up.
steps.expect: forwarded mail volume visibly declining month over month.

steps.action: **Tell the humans.** A short new-address message to family and friends, and neighbors at both ends where relevant (`daily/social/greet-a-neighbor` begins at the new place).
steps.expect: people who send you things know where you are.
