recipes.verification: Formal registration (where required) is done within deadline with the certificate stored, mail forwarding is active, the money and identity layers show the new address, forwarded mail has slowed to junk, and nothing that mails you codes, cards, or legal notices still believes in the old address.

recipes.title: register a small business
recipes.name: register-a-small-business
recipes.goal: Register a small business with the appropriate government office and keep proof of legal formation or trade-name registration.

steps.action: **Choose the legal structure.** Compare liability, tax, ownership, reporting, and cost for sole proprietor, LLC, corporation, partnership, or nonprofit.
steps.expect: one structure is chosen and documented.

steps.action: **Search the business name.** Check the state registry, local fictitious-name database, and obvious trademark/domain conflicts.
steps.expect: the name is available or you have a backup.

steps.action: **Identify required registrations.** Determine whether formation, DBA/trade name, local business license, sales tax permit, professional license, or zoning approval applies.
steps.expect: you have a checklist by agency.

steps.action: **Prepare filing information.** Gather organizer, owner/member, registered agent, principal office, mailing address, purpose, management, and duration details.
steps.expect: the online form can be completed in one session.

steps.action: **File with the official registry.** Submit articles, certificate, DBA, or local license application through the secretary of state, county clerk, or city portal. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* filing fees are usually nonrefundable and public records may reveal addresses, so review names and addresses first.
steps.expect: you receive a filing receipt, entity number, or pending status.

steps.action: **Save formation documents.** Download stamped articles, certificate of organization/incorporation, DBA certificate, and payment receipt.
steps.expect: you can prove the business exists or the filing is pending.

steps.action: **Apply for tax accounts if needed.** Register for employer withholding, sales tax, excise tax, or local gross receipts accounts after formation.
steps.expect: tax account numbers or portal access are issued.

steps.action: **Create internal records.** Prepare operating agreement, bylaws, initial resolutions, ownership ledger, and business record folder as appropriate.
steps.expect: ownership and authority are documented before banking or contracts.

steps.action: **Calendar renewals and reports.** Record annual report, franchise tax, DBA renewal, local license, and registered-agent deadlines.
steps.expect: compliance deadlines are on a calendar with reminders.

recipes.verification: You have a state or local confirmation showing the business name, registration/entity number, filing date, and current active or pending status.

recipes.title: register a vehicle
recipes.name: register-a-vehicle
recipes.goal: Register a vehicle with the correct government agency so it can be legally driven, identified by plates or a sticker, and documented for future renewals or sale.

steps.action: **Confirm the deadline.** Find how many days you have after purchase, move, import, or lease start to register the vehicle.
steps.expect: you know the latest date to avoid penalties.

steps.action: **Gather ownership proof.** Collect title, manufacturer certificate, bill of sale, lienholder information, odometer disclosure, and prior registration if required.
steps.expect: the agency can trace legal ownership.

steps.action: **Gather insurance and ID.** Bring valid insurance proof, government ID, address proof, and any residency or business documents required.
steps.expect: your identity and eligibility are ready for review.

steps.action: **Check inspection requirements.** Complete safety, emissions, VIN, weight, or roadworthiness inspection if the agency requires it before registration.
steps.expect: you have a passing certificate or exemption.

steps.action: **Complete the application.** Fill in owner names, vehicle identification number, make, model, year, fuel type, lienholder, address, and usage.
steps.expect: the form matches the ownership and insurance documents.

steps.action: **Calculate fees and taxes.** Review registration fee, title fee, plate fee, local tax, sales or use tax, inspection fee, and late penalty if any.
steps.expect: you know the amount and accepted payment methods.

steps.action: **Submit the packet.** [BRANCH: online | office | mail] upload, bring, or mail the application and supporting documents through the official channel.
steps.expect: the agency accepts the application or identifies a missing item.

steps.action: **Pay only after confirming details.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* verify VIN, owner name, address, taxes, and fee total before payment because some fees may be nonrefundable.
steps.expect: you receive a payment receipt or transaction number.

steps.action: **Receive plates, sticker, or temporary permit.** Install plates and registration sticker as instructed, or display the temporary permit until permanent items arrive.
steps.expect: the vehicle shows valid registration evidence.

steps.action: **Store the registration document.** Keep the registration card or certificate in the required place and save copies of the receipt and application.
steps.expect: you can prove registration during a traffic stop, renewal, or sale.

recipes.verification: The vehicle has active registration, valid plates or sticker or temporary permit, proof of payment, and a stored registration document matching the VIN and owner.

recipes.title: register to vote by mail
recipes.name: register-to-vote-by-mail
recipes.goal: Register to vote by mail using the correct official form, deadline, and identification rules for your election jurisdiction.

steps.action: **Find the official election office.** Use the national, state, local, or electoral commission site for your residence.
steps.expect: the correct registration authority is identified.

steps.action: **Check the deadline.** Note postmark, received-by, online, and in-person deadlines because they can differ.
steps.expect: the mail deadline is written with a date.

steps.action: **Download or request the form.** Use the official mail registration form for your jurisdiction.
steps.expect: you have the current form and instructions.

steps.action: **Confirm eligibility.** Read voter qualifications and penalties for false registration.
steps.expect: you know you are eligible before signing.

steps.action: **Enter identity details.** Provide legal name, residence address, mailing address, date of birth, ID number, and prior registration if required.
steps.expect: the form is complete and legible.

steps.action: **Attach ID only if required.** Follow instructions for copies or numbers and avoid sending original identity documents unless explicitly required.
steps.expect: ID evidence matches the rule.

steps.action: **Sign and date the form.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing may be a legal declaration, so confirm accuracy before mailing.
steps.expect: the form is validly signed.

steps.action: **Mail with proof.** Send to the listed election office, allowing time for delivery and using tracking if helpful.
steps.expect: you have a mailing date or receipt.

steps.action: **Confirm registration.** Check the official voter lookup or call the election office before the registration deadline if possible.
steps.expect: your registration status is active or a correction path is provided.

recipes.verification: The official voter registration lookup or election office confirms active registration at the current residence.

recipes.title: register to vote
recipes.name: register-to-vote
recipes.goal: Submit a voter registration or update an existing registration using an allowed method for your jurisdiction.

steps.action: **Check eligibility first.** Confirm age, citizenship or residency, address, and any disqualification rules for your jurisdiction.
steps.expect: you know whether you are eligible to register now.

steps.action: **Find the official election site.** Use the national, state, provincial, county, or municipal election office, not a random ad or petition site.
steps.expect: the page URL and branding match an official government source.

steps.action: **Check the deadline.** Look for registration cutoff dates for online, mail, and in-person methods.
steps.expect: you know the last safe date for your chosen method.

steps.action: **Choose the registration method.** [BRANCH: online | mail | in-person] Use online if available, mail if you need a paper form, or in-person for deadline or ID issues.
steps.expect: method is allowed for your address.

steps.action: **Enter identity and address information.** Use your legal name and residential address, plus mailing address if different.
steps.expect: the form matches your ID and current residence.

steps.action: **Provide ID details if required.** Enter the requested driver license, state ID, national ID, or last digits of a tax ID only on the official form.
steps.expect: required identity fields are complete.

steps.action: **Review before submitting.** Check spelling, date of birth, party selection if any, address, and signature requirement. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* submitting false eligibility information can have legal consequences, so confirm eligibility before submission.
steps.expect: all statements are accurate.

steps.action: **Submit or mail the form.** Submit online, mail with enough time for delivery, or hand it to the proper office.
steps.expect: you receive a confirmation screen, mailing proof, or receipt.

steps.action: **Confirm registration later.** Use the official lookup tool after processing time passes.
steps.expect: your name, address, and voting district appear correctly or you know what to fix.

recipes.verification: The official voter lookup shows an active registration at your current residential address, or you have a dated receipt for a submitted registration before the deadline.

recipes.title: renew a drivers license
recipes.name: renew-a-drivers-license
recipes.goal: Renew an existing driver's license before it expires and leave with proof you can keep driving legally.

steps.action: **Check renewal eligibility.** Look up the official motor vehicle agency for your state, province, or country and search "renew driver's license".
steps.expect: the page states whether your license type can renew now.

steps.action: **Choose the renewal channel.** [BRANCH: online | in-person] Use online if the site says you are eligible and your photo, address, and identity checks are accepted; otherwise book or visit an office.
steps.expect: you have either an online renewal form open or an appointment/walk-in plan.

steps.action: **Gather documents.** Set out your current license, renewal notice, proof of address if moved, lawful presence or identity documents if requested, and payment card or check.
steps.expect: every document named on the agency checklist is in one folder.

steps.action: **Resolve address or name changes first.** If your address or legal name changed, follow the agency's change process before paying.
steps.expect: the renewal form shows the correct mailing address and legal name.

steps.action: **Complete any vision requirement.** [BRANCH: self-certification | provider form | office test] Follow the exact method listed by the agency.
steps.expect: the system accepts the vision step or your test result is recorded.

steps.action: **Submit the renewal application.** Enter license details carefully, confirm restrictions and endorsements, and review spelling before final submission.
steps.expect: the application summary matches your current identity and driving privileges.

steps.action: **Pay the fee.** Confirm the amount, card processing fee, and mailing fee before paying. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* payment may be nonrefundable once submitted, so verify the license number and renewal term first.
steps.expect: a receipt, confirmation number, or transaction ID appears.

steps.action: **Save temporary proof.** Print or download the temporary license, receipt, or extension letter if offered.
steps.expect: you have a saved file or paper document showing permission to drive while the card is produced.

steps.action: **Track delivery.** Note the expected mailing window and set a calendar reminder for one week after that date.
steps.expect: you know when to follow up if the permanent license does not arrive.

recipes.verification: You have a renewal confirmation or temporary license with your name, license number, valid dates, and the agency's official identifier.

recipes.title: renew a passport
recipes.name: renew-a-passport
recipes.goal: Your passport is renewed: application submitted with compliant photo and payment, old passport handled per the rules, and the new one in your hands before you need it.

steps.action: **Confirm you're a renewal, not a first-time case.** Renewal usually requires: previous passport available, issued as an adult, within a validity window, name unchanged (or with proof of change). Fail any → the first-time/replacement process, different recipe.
steps.expect: your case matches the renewal criteria list on the official site.

steps.action: **Read the current requirements from the official source.** Form number/online portal, photo spec, fee, and whether your country renews by mail, online, or in-person appointment. Rules change; last year's knowledge is stale.
steps.expect: a checklist written from today's official page.

steps.action: **Get a compliant photo.** The spec is strict (size, background color, neutral expression, no glasses in many countries, recency ≤6 months). A photo service that knows passport specs beats DIY; if DIY, print at exact size and check against the template.
steps.expect: photos matching every line of the spec — photo rejection is the #1 processing delay.

steps.action: **Complete the application.** Online portal or the exact current form, fields matching your documents precisely (name as in the old passport, or with the name-change document attached).
steps.expect: application validated/printed with no blank required fields.

steps.action: **Pay the fee via the official channel.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* fees are typically non-refundable even for rejected applications — recheck the photo and fields once more before paying.
steps.expect: payment receipt/reference number saved.

steps.action: **Submit per your country's channel.** [BRANCH: mail → tracked envelope containing exactly the checklist items (old passport if required, photos, form, receipt) | in-person appointment → book the slot, bring originals | online → upload and confirm]
steps.expect: submission confirmation with a tracking/application number.

steps.action: **Track and receive.** Monitor the application status page; the new passport arrives by secure mail or pickup. **Sign it** and verify every printed detail (name spelling, birth date, sex, dates) on day one.
steps.expect: correct new passport signed and stored; old passport returned canceled (corner-cut) where that's the practice.

steps.action: **Update dependents of the passport number.** Travel bookings made with the old number, trusted-traveler programs, visa applications in flight.
steps.expect: no active booking still pointing at the dead number.

recipes.verification: The new passport is in hand, signed, every biographic detail verified correct, validity ~10 (or your country's) years out, the old one canceled-and-returned or accounted for, live visas preserved, and no upcoming booking references the old number.

recipes.title: report a lost passport
recipes.name: report-a-lost-passport
recipes.goal: Report a lost or stolen passport promptly, reduce fraud risk, and start the correct replacement process.

steps.action: **Act immediately.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* reporting usually cancels the passport, so confirm it is truly lost or stolen before filing.
steps.expect: you are ready for the old passport to become invalid.

steps.action: **Use the official reporting channel.** Find the issuing government's passport agency, embassy, consulate, or online lost-passport form.
steps.expect: you are on an official government site or phone line.

steps.action: **Complete the loss report.** Provide name, date of birth, passport details if known, where and when it was lost, and theft details if applicable.
steps.expect: the agency accepts the report or gives next steps.

steps.action: **Record the confirmation.** Save the report number, date, and agency contact details.
steps.expect: you can prove the passport was reported.

steps.action: **File a police report if needed.** For theft, local legal requirement, insurance, or embassy instructions, report to local police.
steps.expect: you have a police report number if required.

steps.action: **Assess travel impact.** Check airline, border, visa, and entry rules for any upcoming trip.
steps.expect: you know whether travel must be postponed or emergency documents are needed.

steps.action: **Apply for replacement.** [BRANCH: standard replacement | urgent travel document] submit the normal replacement application or contact an embassy for urgent travel.
steps.expect: the replacement route and timeline are clear.

steps.action: **Replace linked visas if necessary.** Contact relevant visa or residence permit authorities if the lost passport contained valid visas or permits.
steps.expect: affected documents are listed with replacement steps.

steps.action: **Monitor for misuse.** Watch identity accounts, credit files where relevant, and immigration notices after loss.
steps.expect: suspicious activity can be detected early.

recipes.verification: The lost or stolen passport report is accepted by the issuing authority, confirmation is saved, and the correct replacement or emergency travel process is started.

recipes.title: report a problem to the city
recipes.name: report-a-problem-to-the-city
recipes.goal: Report a local issue such as a pothole, broken streetlight, missed trash pickup, graffiti, or blocked sidewalk to the correct city service channel.

steps.action: **Make sure it belongs to the city.** Check whether the issue is on public property, a city street, park, sidewalk, or utility area.
steps.expect: you know the likely responsible agency.

steps.action: **Capture the location.** Note address, cross street, landmark, side of street, floor, or GPS pin.
steps.expect: someone who has never been there could find it.

steps.action: **Take a useful photo if safe.** Photograph the issue and nearby context without stepping into traffic or private property.
steps.expect: photo shows both the defect and where it is.

steps.action: **Choose the reporting channel.** [BRANCH: 311 phone | city app | web form] Use the channel your city supports for that issue type.
steps.expect: the channel offers a matching category.

steps.action: **Pick the closest category.** Select pothole, streetlight, sanitation, noise, tree, water leak, or other closest label.
steps.expect: form asks questions relevant to the problem.

steps.action: **Describe the problem plainly.** Include size, severity, when noticed, hazards, and whether access is blocked.
steps.expect: report can be triaged without a callback.

steps.action: **Submit contact details only if needed.** Provide email or phone if you want updates or the city requires it.
steps.expect: required fields are complete without extra personal information.

steps.action: **Save the reference number.** Copy or screenshot the ticket ID after submitting.
steps.expect: you can look up or cite the report later.

steps.action: **Follow up if unresolved.** Check status after the normal service window or report again with the reference number if conditions worsen.
steps.expect: follow-up includes the original ticket.

recipes.verification: You have a submitted city service request with a reference number, location, category, and description accurate enough for a crew to find the issue.

recipes.title: request your public records
recipes.name: request-your-public-records
recipes.goal: Submit a public records request to the correct government office and track it to production, denial, or appeal.

steps.action: **Define the records narrowly.** Write the subject, agency program, names, addresses, case numbers, dates, and document types you want.
steps.expect: the request can be understood without a records clerk guessing.

steps.action: **Find the custodian.** Search the official agency site for "public records", "FOIA", "open records", "records request", or "clerk".
steps.expect: you have the correct portal, email, mail address, or form.

steps.action: **Check exemptions and identity rules.** Read whether the records may be redacted for privacy, law enforcement, personnel, medical, juvenile, or trade-secret reasons.
steps.expect: you know what may be withheld and what proof is needed.

steps.action: **Draft the request.** Ask for existing records, not explanations, and request electronic delivery plus advance notice of fees over a set amount.
steps.expect: the text names the records, date range, format, and fee limit.

steps.action: **Submit through the official channel.** [BRANCH: portal | email | mail | in-person] Send the request and attach ID or authorization only if required.
steps.expect: you receive a tracking number, timestamp, email copy, or stamped receipt.

steps.action: **Calendar the response deadline.** Record the statutory or agency response date and any allowed extension.
steps.expect: you know when a late response becomes actionable.

steps.action: **Respond to fee or clarification notices.** Approve reasonable fees, narrow the request, or clarify search terms in writing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* paid search or copy fees may be nonrefundable once work begins, so approve only what you accept.
steps.expect: the agency confirms the request remains active.

steps.action: **Review the production.** Check that files open, dates match, redactions are labeled, and withheld records are explained.
steps.expect: you can tell whether the response satisfies the request.

steps.action: **Appeal or close the request.** [BRANCH: complete | incomplete | denied] Save the production if complete, or file the listed appeal/administrative review before the deadline.
steps.expect: the request has a final disposition or an active appeal.

recipes.verification: You have a tracking number and either the requested records, a written denial with appeal rights, or a documented clarification/fee decision still within deadline.

recipes.title: respond to jury duty
recipes.name: respond-to-jury-duty
recipes.goal: A jury summons is answered correctly and on time: you have either confirmed your service date, secured a lawful deferral or excusal, and you know exactly where and when to appear.

steps.action: **Read the summons top to bottom before doing anything.** Find four things: the response deadline, the report date, the court address, and the juror ID / badge number.
steps.expect: those four items located and written down; the deadline is usually days, not weeks, away.

steps.action: **Verify it is genuine.** Real courts summon by mail or official portal and never demand payment, gift cards, or a Social Security number by phone.
steps.expect: the summons matches the court named on the court's own official website; a phone caller "collecting a fine" is a scam, not the court.

steps.action: **Respond by the stated deadline, in the stated way.** [BRANCH: online portal with the juror ID | phone system | mail-back card] Complete the eligibility questionnaire honestly (residency, citizenship, age, language, prior felony where it disqualifies).
steps.expect: a confirmation number, stamped card, or portal receipt. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* ignoring the summons is a missed legal obligation and can lead to a fine or contempt order; never let the deadline pass silently.

steps.action: **Request a deferral or excusal if you cannot serve on the date.** Deferral moves you to a later date (usually one you propose within a set window); excusal removes you for this cycle. Use the same portal/form and attach any required proof.
steps.expect: a new date issued, or an excusal confirmation; unanswered requests default to the original date, so keep the receipt.

steps.action: **Set up the day-one logistics once your date is fixed.** Confirm the report time (often earlier than court opening), parking or transit, security screening rules, and the standby vs. in-person question. Many systems require a call-in or portal check the evening before.
steps.expect: you know whether you actually report, and by when, the night before.

steps.action: **Arrange work and care coverage.** Notify your employer in writing and keep the summons copy; most jurisdictions legally protect jury leave. Line up childcare or eldercare for a potentially full day.
steps.expect: employer acknowledgment in hand; no dependent left uncovered.

steps.action: **Report on the day with the right kit.** Bring the summons, photo ID, badge number, a book, chargers, and small cash. Leave prohibited items (large bags, some electronics, anything weapon-like) at home; security will turn you away with them.
steps.expect: you clear screening, check in with your juror number, and receive seating instructions.

recipes.verification: You hold a dated confirmation (number, stamped card, or portal receipt) of your response, you know your exact report date and time (or standby status), and your employer and dependents are covered for that day.

recipes.title: vote in an election
recipes.name: vote-in-an-election
recipes.goal: Your ballot is cast and counted in an election you are eligible to vote in, using the correct method (in-person, mail, or early), with informed choices on every contest you cared about.

steps.action: **Confirm you are registered, well before the deadline.** Use the official voter-lookup tool; check that your name, address, and precinct are current.
steps.expect: the tool shows you as registered at your current address for this election.

steps.action: **Register or update if needed, before the cutoff.** [BRANCH: not registered → complete registration by the deadline | moved → update your address | registered and current → skip] ⚠️ *Irreversible:* miss the registration deadline and you cannot vote in this election in most places; some offer same-day registration, verify whether yours does.
steps.expect: a registration confirmation, or confirmation you were already current.

steps.action: **Find your polling place and hours, or your ballot options.** The lookup tool gives your assigned location, early-voting sites, and mail-ballot eligibility. Assigned locations change between elections.
steps.expect: a specific address and open hours, or an early/mail path.

steps.action: **Choose your voting method.** [BRANCH: in-person on election day | early in-person during the early window | mail/absentee ballot requested by its deadline]
steps.expect: a method chosen with its own deadline noted on your calendar.

steps.action: **Research the full ballot in advance.** Pull your sample ballot from the official site; down-ballot races, judges, and measures are where unprepared voters stall or skip. Decide each contest before you go.
steps.expect: a marked sample ballot or notes covering every contest you will face.

steps.action: **Bring what your jurisdiction requires.** ID rules vary widely; check the exact accepted-document list, and bring your research notes (rules on notes in the booth vary, so confirm).
steps.expect: the required ID in hand and your choices decided.

steps.action: **Cast the ballot carefully.** Follow the marking instructions exactly; fill ovals completely, avoid stray marks, and review before submitting.
steps.expect: the machine accepts it, or a poll worker confirms your paper ballot is properly marked.

steps.action: **Mail path: sign and send with margin.** Sign the envelope where required (a missing signature is the top rejection cause), and return it early by the accepted method.
steps.expect: a tracking or drop-off confirmation, or a ballot-received status online.

steps.action: **Confirm it counted, if tracking exists.** Many jurisdictions offer ballot tracking.
steps.expect: status shows your ballot received and accepted.

recipes.verification: Your ballot was accepted by the voting machine or received-and-accepted per official tracking, covering every contest you intended to vote on, cast within your jurisdiction's deadline.

recipes.title: apply a cold compress
recipes.name: apply-a-cold-compress
recipes.goal: Cold is applied safely through a barrier to reduce early pain and swelling without causing skin injury.

steps.action: **Check the injury first.** Look for deformity, severe swelling, open wound, numbness, or inability to bear weight or move normally.
steps.expect: the injury appears minor enough for home care.

steps.action: **Wrap the cold source.** Put ice or a cold pack inside a towel; never place ice directly on skin.
steps.expect: cold passes through cloth without burning the skin.

steps.action: **Position comfortably.** Rest the injured area and elevate it if swelling is present.
steps.expect: the area is supported and not under strain.

steps.action: **Apply for 20 minutes.** Keep the compress on for up to 20 minutes, checking skin every few minutes.
steps.expect: pain or swelling feels reduced and skin stays normal colored.

steps.action: **Take 20 minutes off.** Remove the compress and let the skin return fully to normal temperature.
steps.expect: skin feels comfortable before another round.

steps.action: **Repeat early if useful.** Use 20 minutes on and 20 minutes off during the first day or two after minor injury.
steps.expect: swelling is managed without numbness or skin damage.

steps.action: **Switch strategy when stiffness dominates.** After the early swelling phase, gentle movement or heat may feel better for tight muscles.
steps.expect: treatment matches the symptom.

steps.action: **Protect the skin.** Stop cold immediately if skin turns white, blue, waxy, numb, or painful.
steps.expect: skin returns to normal after warming.

recipes.verification: Cold was applied through a barrier for no more than 20 minutes at a time, with equal warming breaks and no abnormal skin changes.

recipes.title: assist during an asthma attack
recipes.name: assist-during-an-asthma-attack
recipes.goal: A person having asthma symptoms uses their reliever inhaler or prescribed plan while emergency help is called for severe or worsening signs.

steps.action: **Move away from triggers.** Help the person leave smoke, fumes, cold air, allergens, or exercise if safe.
steps.expect: exposure stops getting worse.

steps.action: **Sit them upright.** Keep them sitting and leaning slightly forward if comfortable; do not make them lie down.
steps.expect: breathing mechanics are easier.

steps.action: **Reassure and slow activity.** Speak calmly and ask them to take steady breaths without forcing deep breaths.
steps.expect: panic and exertion decrease.

steps.action: **Find the reliever inhaler.** Look for the person's quick-relief inhaler and spacer if available.
steps.expect: the correct medication device is ready.

steps.action: **Help use the inhaler.** Follow the label or action plan, usually one puff at a time through a spacer with breaths between puffs.
steps.expect: medication reaches the lungs.

steps.action: **Start timing response.** Note when medication was taken and watch breathing, speech, color, and alertness.
steps.expect: changes are tracked clearly.

steps.action: **Call if severe or not improving.** [BRANCH: improving | severe or not improving] keep monitoring if improving; call emergency services if severe signs persist or worsen.
steps.expect: escalation is not delayed.

steps.action: **Repeat medication only as directed.** Use the action plan, label, or dispatcher instructions for additional puffs.
steps.expect: medication is not underused or wildly overused.

steps.action: **Prepare for responders.** Gather inhalers, spacer, medication list, allergies, and known triggers.
steps.expect: responders receive relevant information quickly.

steps.action: **Monitor until stable or help arrives.** Stay with the person and watch for exhaustion, confusion, blue color, or worsening breathing.
steps.expect: deterioration is recognized immediately.

recipes.verification: The person can speak comfortably, breathing and color are improving, emergency services were called for any severe or non-improving attack, and the person remains monitored until stable or professional care takes over.

recipes.title: book a doctors appointment
recipes.name: book-a-doctors-appointment
recipes.goal: An appointment with the right kind of clinician exists at a time you can make, with insurance/payment squared, and you arrive prepared so the visit's minutes count.

steps.action: **Match the need to the right door.** [BRANCH: routine/new symptoms → GP/primary care | known specialist need → check whether your system requires a GP referral first (many do) | minor-but-today (infections, sprains) → urgent care/walk-in clinic | medication-only → possibly a pharmacist or telehealth consult]
steps.expect: one chosen venue that matches both the need and the system's rules.

steps.action: **Book through the practice's real channel.** Phone at opening time, the practice's portal/app, or the national booking system — whichever *this practice* actually uses (their website/recording says).
steps.expect: a live booking interface or a human.

steps.action: **State the need in one useful sentence, and answer triage honestly.** "Persistent cough, three weeks, worsening" — the booker/triage uses this to size and route the slot (urgency, length, right clinician, phone-vs-in-person).
steps.expect: an offered slot; urgent-sounding descriptions may route you sooner or elsewhere — that's the system working.

steps.action: **Take the slot that works and capture the details.** Date, time, clinician name, location/room or telehealth link, any prep instructions (fasting for bloodwork, bring medication list).
steps.expect: appointment confirmed — in the calendar with the practice's phone number attached.

steps.action: **Square the money/coverage side.** Insurance systems: confirm the practice/clinician is in-network and referrals/authorizations are on file. Public systems: confirm registration is current. Private-pay: ask the price now.
steps.expect: no coverage surprise waiting at the front desk.

steps.action: **Prepare the visit's inputs.** A written symptom timeline (when it started, what changes it), current medication list with doses, your top 2–3 questions, relevant history.
steps.expect: a one-page (or phone-note) brief that survives the exam room's memory-erasing effect.

steps.action: **Show up right.** Arrive 10–15 min early (paperwork), or test the telehealth link 5 min prior; bring ID, insurance/health card, the brief, and the actual pill bottles if medications are on the agenda.
steps.expect: checked in on time; the visit spends its minutes on medicine, not admin.

recipes.verification: The appointment is on your calendar and in the practice's system (confirmed), coverage/referral requirements are satisfied, your prep brief exists, and you know exactly where to be (or which link to click) ten minutes before the time.

recipes.title: build a home first aid kit
recipes.name: build-a-home-first-aid-kit
recipes.goal: A stocked, organized, in-date home first-aid kit exists in a known location, and everyone in the household knows where it is and how to use the basics.

steps.action: **Choose the container and location.** Pick a box that closes fully and fits the shelf; store it somewhere cool and dry that adults reach easily but young children cannot. Avoid the bathroom, since heat and humidity degrade supplies.
steps.expect: a closable, labeled container in a spot every adult can name.

steps.action: **Stock wound care and dressings.** Assorted adhesive bandages, sterile gauze pads, a roll of gauze, medical tape, non-stick pads, adhesive wound-closure strips, and antiseptic wipes.
steps.expect: you can cover a range of cut and scrape sizes.

steps.action: **Add tools and barriers.** Tweezers, blunt-tip scissors, a digital thermometer, disposable gloves, a CPR face shield, safety pins, and an instant cold pack.
steps.expect: the tools to remove a splinter, cut tape, check a fever, and protect yourself while helping.

steps.action: **Add medicines and topicals, with a household check.** Antiseptic cream, hydrocortisone cream, antihistamine, pain and fever reducers (an adult one and a child dose if children live there), rehydration salts, and any prescribed emergency meds like an auto-injector or inhaler.
steps.expect: each medicine is appropriate for your household ages; child and adult doses are not confused. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never stock aspirin for children (Reye's syndrome risk) or mix up adult and pediatric dosing; label clearly.

steps.action: **Add reference and emergency information.** A first-aid instruction leaflet, a card with emergency numbers, poison-control, doctor and pharmacy numbers, and a list of each household member's allergies and key conditions.
steps.expect: a stranger or babysitter could act using only what is in the kit.

steps.action: **Label and date everything.** Write the earliest expiry on the outside, or keep a dated inventory card inside listing each item and its expiry.
steps.expect: you can see the next expiry at a glance without unpacking.

steps.action: **Run an expiry and restock audit on a schedule.** Twice a year (tie it to clock changes so you remember) open the kit, discard expired or used items, and replace them.
steps.expect: nothing expired remains; the inventory card is refreshed and dated.

steps.action: **Brief the household.** Show every capable member where the kit lives, how it is organized, and how to use the auto-injector or other emergency item if present.
steps.expect: each adult can find the kit and demonstrate the emergency-item steps unprompted.

recipes.verification: The kit contains in-date wound care, tools, barriers, household-appropriate medicines, and emergency info; the earliest expiry is visible on a dated inventory; and every capable household member can locate the kit and use its emergency items.

recipes.title: build a medication schedule
recipes.name: build-a-medication-schedule
recipes.goal: Create a clear medication schedule that shows what to take, when to take it, how to remember it, and when to refill it.

steps.action: **Gather every medicine.** Put prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, supplements, eye drops, inhalers, and as-needed medicines in one place.
steps.expect: nothing currently taken is left out of view.

steps.action: **Copy the label details.** For each item, write the name, strength, dose, route, timing instructions, prescribing clinician, and reason if known.
steps.expect: each medicine has a matching line in the schedule.

steps.action: **Mark special instructions.** Note food rules, empty-stomach rules, bedtime rules, missed-dose instructions, and medicines that should not be crushed.
steps.expect: timing constraints are visible next to the medicine name.

steps.action: **Choose daily time blocks.** [BRANCH: simple routine | complex routine] Use morning, midday, evening, and bedtime for simple plans; use exact clock times for complex plans.
steps.expect: every dose appears in one time block.

steps.action: **Check for conflicts.** Compare labels for duplicate ingredients, spacing rules, and warning stickers; ask a pharmacist or doctor to check interactions before using a new combined schedule.
steps.expect: unclear combinations are flagged for professional review.

steps.action: **Set up a pill organizer.** Fill only the medicines that are safe to pre-sort, keeping liquids, inhalers, refrigerated medicines, and original-package items separate.
steps.expect: compartments match the written schedule.

steps.action: **Add reminders.** Set phone alarms, calendar alerts, smart speaker reminders, or a paper checklist for each dose time.
steps.expect: each scheduled dose has a reminder or visible check box.

steps.action: **Add refill dates.** Count remaining doses and set refill reminders several days before running out, earlier for mail-order or controlled medicines.
steps.expect: each ongoing medicine has a refill-ahead date.

steps.action: **Confirm with the user.** Read the schedule aloud and compare it against the bottles before the first use. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* taking the wrong dose can cause harm; confirm medicine, dose, and time before swallowing.
steps.expect: the user or helper agrees the schedule matches the labels.

recipes.verification: Every current medicine appears once with dose, time, special instructions, reminder method, and refill date, and a pharmacist or doctor has been asked about any interaction concern.

recipes.title: call emergency services
recipes.name: call-emergency-services
recipes.goal: Emergency services are contacted quickly, given accurate location and problem details, and kept connected until help is arranged.

steps.action: **Get to relative safety.** Move away from traffic, fire, weapons, electrical hazards, or toxic fumes if you can do so without delaying urgent care.
steps.expect: you can speak and observe without becoming injured.

steps.action: **Call the local emergency number.** Dial the emergency number for the location, or use the phone's emergency-call function.
steps.expect: the call rings or connects to a dispatcher.

steps.action: **State the need first.** Say "medical emergency," "fire," "police," or "not sure" and describe the main problem in one sentence.
steps.expect: the dispatcher starts routing the right responders.

steps.action: **Give the exact location.** Provide address, business name, floor, room, entrance, cross streets, landmarks, or GPS/map information.
steps.expect: responders have a place they can find.

steps.action: **Give the callback number.** Say the number of the phone you are using, even if you think it appears automatically.
steps.expect: dispatch can reconnect if the call drops.

steps.action: **Answer focused questions.** Report age if known, breathing status, consciousness, severe bleeding, hazards, number of people hurt, and what first aid is happening.
steps.expect: dispatch has enough detail to prioritize and guide care.

steps.action: **Follow dispatcher instructions.** Put the phone on speaker if safe and do exactly what the dispatcher tells you.
steps.expect: care continues while help is being sent.

steps.action: **Assign bystanders.** Ask specific people to meet responders, control pets, bring an AED or naloxone if relevant, and keep the area clear.
steps.expect: useful tasks happen without crowding the person.

steps.action: **Stay on the line.** Do not hang up until the dispatcher says to, unless staying connected creates immediate danger.
steps.expect: dispatch can update instructions as the situation changes.

steps.action: **Flag responders when they arrive.** Send someone visible to the entrance or wave responders in from a safe place.
steps.expect: emergency crews reach the person faster.

recipes.verification: Emergency dispatch has the exact location, callback number, emergency type, current condition, known hazards, and the caller remains available until dispatch releases the call or responders arrive.

recipes.title: care for someone who drank too much
recipes.name: care-for-someone-who-drank-too-much
recipes.goal: A person who drank too much is kept safe, monitored continuously, and emergency help is called if alcohol poisoning is possible.

steps.action: **Move away from hazards.** Guide the person away from roads, water, balconies, kitchens, or crowds.
steps.expect: the immediate environment is safer.

steps.action: **Check responsiveness.** Speak clearly and gently tap a shoulder if they seem asleep.
steps.expect: you know whether they can wake and answer.

steps.action: **Call emergency help for danger signs.** Treat unconsciousness, slow breathing, repeated vomiting, seizure, or blue skin as an emergency.
steps.expect: emergency care is started when alcohol poisoning is possible.

steps.action: **Place in recovery position.** If drowsy or vomiting but breathing, roll them on their side with the top knee bent and head tilted slightly down.
steps.expect: vomit can drain away from the airway.

steps.action: **Monitor breathing.** Count breaths and watch chest movement every few minutes.
steps.expect: breathing remains regular and not dangerously slow.

steps.action: **Keep them warm.** Use a blanket or dry clothing without overheating.
steps.expect: shivering or cold skin is reduced.

steps.action: **Offer small sips only if alert.** Give water only if they are awake, sitting up, and able to swallow normally.
steps.expect: they can drink without coughing or choking.

steps.action: **Do not give more substances.** Avoid alcohol, sedatives, sleep medicine, or recreational drugs.
steps.expect: intoxication is not worsened.

steps.action: **Do not make them vomit.** Keep their airway protected instead.
steps.expect: choking risk is not increased.

steps.action: **Stay until sober care takes over.** Never leave them alone to sleep it off.
steps.expect: a sober person is continuously watching them.

recipes.verification: A sober adult is continuously monitoring the person, breathing is regular, and emergency services have been called for any alcohol-poisoning sign.

recipes.title: care for someone with the flu
recipes.name: care-for-someone-with-the-flu
recipes.goal: A person with flu-like illness is supported with rest, fluids, fever care, isolation, and timely medical escalation.

steps.action: **Set up a rest space.** Give the sick person a place to rest away from others when possible.
steps.expect: exposure to others is reduced.

steps.action: **Encourage fluids.** Offer water, oral rehydration solution, broth, or other tolerated fluids often.
steps.expect: urine is pale enough and the person can keep fluids down.

steps.action: **Manage fever and aches.** [BRANCH: adult | child] use age-appropriate acetaminophen or ibuprofen as labeled unless a clinician says not to.
steps.expect: fever discomfort and body aches are reduced. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not give aspirin to children or teenagers with viral illness unless a clinician specifically directs it.

steps.action: **Support breathing comfort.** Use humidified air, honey for cough only if over 1 year old, and upright positioning.
steps.expect: cough or throat irritation is easier to tolerate.

steps.action: **Isolate while contagious.** Keep the person home and away from others until fever is gone for at least 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine and symptoms are improving.
steps.expect: spread risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Use masks and ventilation.** Have the sick person mask around others if tolerated, improve airflow, and avoid visitors.
steps.expect: household exposure is lower.

steps.action: **Watch red flags twice daily.** Check breathing, hydration, alertness, fever pattern, chest pain, and symptom direction.
steps.expect: worsening is caught early.

steps.action: **Call for high-risk care.** Contact a clinician for high-risk people, symptoms lasting or worsening after several days, or fever that returns after improving.
steps.expect: complications are considered.

steps.action: **Clean hands and surfaces.** Wash hands often and clean high-touch surfaces.
steps.expect: shared spaces are less contaminated.

recipes.verification: The person is resting, drinking fluids, isolated from others, and has no emergency red flags or has been escalated for medical care.

recipes.title: change a wound dressing
recipes.name: change-a-wound-dressing
recipes.goal: A wound dressing is removed, the wound is checked, and a clean dressing is applied without contaminating the area.

steps.action: **Prepare a clean area.** Put supplies on a clean surface and place a trash bag nearby.
steps.expect: everything needed is reachable before the dressing is opened.

steps.action: **Wash your hands.** Scrub with soap and water, dry with a clean towel, and put on gloves if available.
steps.expect: hands are clean before touching the old dressing.

steps.action: **Loosen the old dressing.** [BRANCH: releases easily | stuck] peel tape toward the wound; if stuck, moisten with clean water or saline and wait.
steps.expect: the dressing lifts without tearing new tissue. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not pull out packing, drains, or anything embedded in the wound unless a clinician told you to.

steps.action: **Discard safely.** Fold the soiled side inward and place the old dressing in the trash bag.
steps.expect: drainage does not touch the clean supplies.

steps.action: **Assess the wound.** Look for bleeding, opening edges, swelling, spreading redness, warmth, pus, odor, or increased drainage.
steps.expect: infection or reopening signs are noticed before redressing.

steps.action: **Clean only as directed.** Rinse gently with clean water or saline if instructed, and wipe surrounding skin away from the wound.
steps.expect: the wound and nearby skin are clean without scrubbing the wound bed.

steps.action: **Dry surrounding skin.** Pat the skin around the wound dry with clean gauze.
steps.expect: tape will stick to dry skin and the wound is not rubbed.

steps.action: **Apply the new dressing.** Place a sterile nonstick pad or gauze over the wound, then secure it without tight pressure.
steps.expect: the wound is covered and circulation is not restricted.

steps.action: **Set the change cadence.** Change daily, when wet or dirty, or on the schedule from the clinician.
steps.expect: the next dressing change time is known.

steps.action: **Wash hands again.** Remove gloves if used, throw them away, and wash hands.
steps.expect: contamination does not spread after care.

recipes.verification: The wound is covered with a clean dry dressing, circulation is normal beyond the dressing, and infection signs have been checked.

recipes.title: check a mole
recipes.name: check-a-mole
recipes.goal: You inspect a mole using the ABCDE rule, document changes, and know what warrants a dermatologist instead of self-treatment.

steps.action: **Find the spot clearly.** Use bright light and expose the whole area of skin.
steps.expect: the entire mole border is visible.

steps.action: **Check A for asymmetry.** Imagine a line through the middle and compare both halves.
steps.expect: you know whether the halves roughly match.

steps.action: **Check B for border.** Look for ragged, blurred, notched, or uneven edges.
steps.expect: border is described as even or irregular.

steps.action: **Check C for color.** Note whether color is uniform or mixed tan, brown, black, red, white, or blue.
steps.expect: color pattern is recorded.

steps.action: **Check D for diameter.** Measure or compare with a pencil eraser, about 6 mm, while remembering smaller spots can still matter.
steps.expect: approximate size is known.

steps.action: **Check E for evolving.** Compare with memory, photos, or nearby moles for change in size, shape, color, elevation, bleeding, itching, or pain.
steps.expect: change is identified or ruled out.

steps.action: **Photograph and track.** Take a clear photo with a ruler or coin beside the mole and record the date.
steps.expect: future comparison is possible.

steps.action: **Do not self-remove.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* home removal can scar, infect, and destroy tissue needed for diagnosis.
steps.expect: the mole remains intact for medical assessment if needed.

recipes.verification: The mole has an ABCDE assessment, a dated size-reference photo when possible, and any suspicious or changing feature is scheduled for dermatologist review.

recipes.title: clean and dress a wound
recipes.name: clean-and-dress-a-wound
recipes.goal: A minor open wound is cleaned, covered, monitored, and escalated if it may need medical care.

steps.action: **Wash your hands.** Use soap and water for at least 20 seconds or hand sanitizer if water is unavailable.
steps.expect: hands are clean before touching the wound.

steps.action: **Control bleeding.** Press sterile gauze or a clean cloth directly on the wound.
steps.expect: bleeding slows or stops within several minutes.

steps.action: **Check whether stitches may be needed.** Look for separated edges, visible fat or muscle, deep puncture, loss of movement, or numbness.
steps.expect: serious features are identified before home care continues.

steps.action: **Rinse the wound.** Hold the wound under clean running water or pour clean water over it to irrigate debris.
steps.expect: loose dirt and visible grit wash away.

steps.action: **Clean around it.** Wash the surrounding skin with soap, keeping soap out of the open wound when possible.
steps.expect: nearby skin is clean without extra stinging inside the wound.

steps.action: **Remove loose debris only.** Use clean tweezers rinsed with alcohol for obvious surface particles.
steps.expect: only easy-to-lift debris is removed.

steps.action: **Apply a thin protective layer.** Use a small amount of petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment if tolerated.
steps.expect: the wound surface is lightly coated, not packed.

steps.action: **Cover the wound.** Place sterile gauze or an adhesive bandage over it.
steps.expect: the wound is covered without cutting off circulation.

steps.action: **Change the dressing.** Replace it daily, when wet, or when dirty.
steps.expect: each new dressing is clean and dry.

steps.action: **Watch for infection.** Check redness, warmth, swelling, pus, increasing pain, red streaks, fever, or delayed healing.
steps.expect: worsening signs trigger care instead of being ignored.

recipes.verification: The wound is visibly clean, bleeding is controlled, a clean dressing covers it, and no urgent-care warning sign is present.

recipes.title: decide er vs urgent care
recipes.name: decide-er-vs-urgent-care
recipes.goal: Choose emergency care, urgent care, a nurse line, or routine care based on clear danger signs.

steps.action: **Check immediate danger.** Look for chest pain, stroke signs, severe bleeding, trouble breathing, seizure, fainting, major trauma, poisoning, or severe allergic reaction.
steps.expect: any life-threatening sign is identified within seconds.

steps.action: **Call emergency services for red flags.** [BRANCH: red flag present | no red flag] call emergency services now if a red flag is present; continue triage only if none are present.
steps.expect: emergency help is activated when symptoms are dangerous. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not delay emergency care to compare prices, wait for a ride, or finish home treatment.

steps.action: **Screen for stroke.** Check face drooping, arm weakness, speech trouble, sudden confusion, sudden severe headache, sudden vision loss, or sudden balance trouble.
steps.expect: possible stroke goes to emergency services even if symptoms improve.

steps.action: **Screen breathing and circulation.** Treat severe shortness of breath, blue lips, choking, severe weakness, clammy skin, or new confusion as emergency signs.
steps.expect: unstable breathing or circulation is not sent to urgent care.

steps.action: **Screen bleeding and injury.** Treat spurting blood, bleeding that soaks dressings after 10 minutes of firm pressure, deep wounds, head injury with confusion, or possible broken neck, hip, or spine as emergency signs.
steps.expect: major trauma is routed to the ER.

steps.action: **Use urgent care for stable problems.** Consider urgent care for minor fractures or sprains, small cuts that may need stitches, mild asthma or flu symptoms, urinary symptoms, ear pain, rashes, or minor burns without danger signs.
steps.expect: the problem is uncomfortable but stable.

steps.action: **Call a nurse line when uncertain.** Use the number on an insurance card, clinic portal, local health system, or public health service.
steps.expect: a clinician or triage service gives next-step advice.

steps.action: **Choose routine care for non-urgent issues.** Use primary care for medication refills, chronic symptom follow-up, mild symptoms improving at home, or preventive questions.
steps.expect: care is scheduled without emergency delay.

steps.action: **Recheck during waiting.** If symptoms worsen, new red flags appear, or the person becomes hard to wake, change the plan to emergency services.
steps.expect: escalation happens immediately when risk changes.

recipes.verification: The person is routed to emergency services, urgent care, a nurse line, or routine care with all red-flag symptoms checked explicitly.

recipes.title: dispose of old medication
recipes.name: dispose-of-old-medication
recipes.goal: Expired, unused, or unwanted medication is disposed of safely while reducing poisoning, misuse, and privacy risks.

steps.action: **Gather only the target medications.** Place expired, stopped, unknown, or unwanted medicines on a clear surface.
steps.expect: active medicines you still take are separate.

steps.action: **Check labels and instructions.** Look for take-back, disposal, or flush instructions on the package or patient leaflet.
steps.expect: special disposal directions are identified.

steps.action: **Choose a take-back option first.** [BRANCH: take-back available | no take-back available] use a pharmacy, clinic, law enforcement drop box, or community event if available; use trash disposal only if not.
steps.expect: the safest disposal route is selected. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Once medication is dropped off, flushed when officially directed, or mixed with trash material, it cannot be recovered safely.

steps.action: **Prepare for take-back.** Keep pills, patches, liquids, and inhalers in their containers unless the site instructs otherwise.
steps.expect: the drop-off site can accept the medication.

steps.action: **Remove private details.** Scratch out or peel off name, address, prescription number, and prescriber information before recycling or trashing empty containers.
steps.expect: personal health details are not readable.

steps.action: **Use the trash method if allowed.** Mix medicine with used coffee grounds, dirt, or cat litter in a sealed bag without crushing tablets.
steps.expect: the medication is unappealing and contained.

steps.action: **Seal and discard.** Put the sealed mixture in household trash and discard the empty container separately after label removal.
steps.expect: children, pets, and others cannot easily access the medicine.

steps.action: **Handle sharps separately.** Put needles, syringes, and lancets in an approved sharps container, not loose trash.
steps.expect: puncture injury risk is controlled.

steps.action: **Wash hands and clean the surface.** Remove residue from the sorting area.
steps.expect: no medication dust or liquid remains.

recipes.verification: Unwanted medication has been taken to a take-back site or sealed in trash using the safe mixture method, and personal labels are unreadable.

recipes.title: do hands only cpr
recipes.name: do-hands-only-cpr
recipes.goal: A bystander starts hands-only CPR for an unresponsive person who is not breathing normally while emergency services are being called.

steps.action: **Check scene safety.** Look for traffic, electricity, fire, violence, or other immediate danger before approaching.
steps.expect: you can reach the person without becoming another casualty.

steps.action: **Check responsiveness.** Tap shoulders and shout to ask if they are okay.
steps.expect: no purposeful response means emergency action is needed.

steps.action: **Call emergency services immediately.** Tell a specific person to call, or call yourself on speaker.
steps.expect: dispatch is contacted and can guide you.

steps.action: **Send for an AED.** Point to someone and ask them to bring an AED if available.
steps.expect: a search starts without delaying compressions.

steps.action: **Check breathing quickly.** Look for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds; gasping is not normal breathing.
steps.expect: absent or abnormal breathing triggers CPR.

steps.action: **Position the person.** Lay them flat on their back on a firm surface if possible.
steps.expect: chest is accessible and not on a soft mattress.

steps.action: **Place hands correctly.** Put the heel of one hand in the center of the chest on the lower half of the breastbone, other hand on top.
steps.expect: shoulders stack over locked elbows.

steps.action: **Push hard and fast.** Compress at least 2 inches deep in adults at 100-120 compressions per minute, letting the chest recoil fully.
steps.expect: chest visibly moves down and springs back each compression.

steps.action: **Do not stop unnecessarily.** Continue until an AED is ready, trained help takes over, the person breathes normally, or you are physically unable.
steps.expect: interruptions stay very short.

steps.action: **Use the AED when it arrives.** Turn it on and follow voice prompts. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* shock delivery can harm someone touching the person; loudly clear everyone before shock.
steps.expect: AED prompts guide pads, analysis, and any shock.

recipes.verification: Emergency services have been called, chest compressions are ongoing at 100-120 per minute with full recoil, and interruptions occur only for AED prompts, responder takeover, normal breathing, or rescuer inability.

recipes.title: find a primary care doctor
recipes.name: find-a-primary-care-doctor
recipes.goal: Identify a primary care doctor or clinic that fits your insurance, location, care needs, and appointment timeline.

steps.action: **Define the type of clinician.** [BRANCH: family medicine | internal medicine | pediatrics | nurse practitioner or physician assistant] Choose based on age and care needs.
steps.expect: search is limited to suitable primary care clinicians.

steps.action: **Check the insurance network.** Use the insurer directory and the clinic website, then plan to confirm by phone.
steps.expect: candidate is listed as in network for your specific plan.

steps.action: **Filter for accepting new patients.** Look for online booking, directory status, or call the office.
steps.expect: clinic confirms new patient availability.

steps.action: **Check practical fit.** Compare location, transit, parking, hours, telehealth, language, accessibility, and lab availability.
steps.expect: the office is realistic for repeat visits.

steps.action: **Review credentials and scope.** Confirm board certification or clinic role, hospital affiliation if relevant, and whether they manage your conditions.
steps.expect: clinician can handle your routine care needs.

steps.action: **Call with specific questions.** Ask whether they take your plan, accept new patients, and how soon a new-patient visit is available.
steps.expect: staff gives a clear appointment option or wait time.

steps.action: **Ask about referrals.** If your insurance requires referrals, ask how the office handles specialist referrals and prior authorizations.
steps.expect: you know whether this doctor can coordinate needed care.

steps.action: **Book the first visit.** Schedule a new-patient physical, problem visit, or medication review depending on urgency.
steps.expect: you receive date, time, location, and check-in instructions.

steps.action: **Transfer records.** Request records from prior clinicians and prepare medication list before the visit.
steps.expect: the new office has or expects your history.

recipes.verification: You have a booked new-patient appointment with a clinician confirmed as accepting new patients and in network for your specific insurance plan, if applicable.

recipes.title: find urgent care near you
recipes.name: find-urgent-care-near-you
recipes.goal: You identify an appropriate nearby urgent care option, confirm it is open and suitable for your problem, and know when emergency care or primary care is the better choice.

steps.action: **Screen for emergency symptoms.** Check for chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, severe allergic reaction, severe bleeding, major trauma, or suicidal intent.
steps.expect: emergency symptoms are ruled out or you go to the ER.

steps.action: **Use finder tools.** Search your insurer directory, health system website, map app, or urgent care chain finder near your location.
steps.expect: you have a short list of nearby clinics.

steps.action: **Check hours and status.** Confirm today's hours, holiday changes, last check-in time, and whether walk-ins are accepted.
steps.expect: the clinic is actually open when you can arrive.

steps.action: **Confirm scope.** Look for services such as X-ray, stitches, labs, pediatric care, occupational health, or respiratory testing.
steps.expect: the clinic can handle your likely need.

steps.action: **Check insurance and cost.** Verify in-network status if possible and note copay, self-pay price, and required ID.
steps.expect: you know what to bring and likely pay.

steps.action: **Compare wait and travel time.** Use online wait estimates, call the clinic, or reserve a slot if available.
steps.expect: you choose the practical fastest appropriate option.

steps.action: **Bring essentials.** Take ID, insurance card, medication list, allergies, and relevant records or photos.
steps.expect: check-in can proceed smoothly.

recipes.verification: You have selected an open clinic that accepts your situation, know its location and costs as well as possible, and have ID, insurance, and medication information ready.

recipes.title: get a second opinion
recipes.name: get-a-second-opinion
recipes.goal: You obtain an independent medical opinion from an appropriate clinician using complete records, without damaging communication with your current care team.

steps.action: **Define the question.** Write the decision you need help with, such as diagnosis confirmation or treatment options.
steps.expect: the second opinion has a focused purpose.

steps.action: **Tell your current clinician plainly.** Say you would like another opinion before deciding, especially for major treatment.
steps.expect: the request is documented without accusation.

steps.action: **Gather records.** Request visit notes, labs, imaging reports, actual image files, pathology reports, medication lists, and procedure notes.
steps.expect: the second clinician can review the full case.

steps.action: **Choose a fresh specialist.** Look for someone in the relevant specialty who is not in the same immediate decision chain when possible.
steps.expect: the opinion is meaningfully independent.

steps.action: **Check coverage and logistics.** Confirm referral needs, insurance network status, costs, telehealth options, and wait time.
steps.expect: the appointment is financially and practically workable.

steps.action: **Send materials ahead.** Upload or deliver records before the visit and confirm they were received.
steps.expect: the clinician has time to review.

steps.action: **Compare recommendations.** Ask what they agree with, what differs, why, and what risks come with each option.
steps.expect: you have a clearer decision framework.

recipes.verification: You have an appointment or completed consultation with an independent clinician who received the relevant records and answered your written decision question.

recipes.title: get a vaccination
recipes.name: get-a-vaccination
recipes.goal: You receive the correct vaccine safely, tolerate the first 15 minutes without incident, manage any side effects, and have a durable record of the dose for future reference.

steps.action: **Confirm which vaccine and which dose you need.** Check with a pharmacist, GP, or an official immunization schedule. Some vaccines are single-shot, some are a timed series.
steps.expect: the exact vaccine name and, if a series, which dose number is due.

steps.action: **Book the appointment.** [BRANCH: pharmacy walk-in or app | GP clinic | public vaccination site | travel clinic for specialized vaccines] Note that some vaccines are stocked only at specific venues and travel vaccines may need days of lead time.
steps.expect: an appointment or a confirmed walk-in window; travel series scheduled with enough runway before departure.

steps.action: **Prepare on the day.** Eat and hydrate first (an empty stomach raises fainting risk), wear a short sleeve or a loose sleeve that rolls above the shoulder, and bring your ID, card, and any prior vaccine record.
steps.expect: you arrive fed, hydrated, and with an easily bared upper arm.

steps.action: **Disclose your history at check-in honestly.** Report pregnancy, immune-compromising conditions, allergies (especially to a previous dose or to eggs where relevant), blood thinners, and recent illness with fever.
steps.expect: the vaccinator confirms you are clear to proceed, or reschedules if you have an active fever.

steps.action: **Receive the injection.** Relax the arm, look away if that helps, and breathe out as it goes in. It is a few seconds.
steps.expect: a brief sting; a small bandage applied.

steps.action: **Wait the observation period before leaving.** Stay on-site 15 minutes (30 if you have an allergy history) so staff can treat the rare immediate reaction.
steps.expect: no lightheadedness, throat tightness, hives, or trouble breathing during the wait; then you are released. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not skip this wait and drive off; anaphylaxis is rare but time-critical and staff carry epinephrine.

steps.action: **Manage aftercare.** Expect a sore arm, and possibly mild fever, fatigue, or headache for a day or two. Move the arm normally, use a cool compress, and take an ordinary pain reliever if needed and allowed.
steps.expect: symptoms peak within 24 to 48 hours and fade; the injection site is not spreading redness or worsening after day three.

steps.action: **Record the dose.** Photograph the record card or confirm it landed in your digital immunization record, and note the date, vaccine name, lot number if shown, and any next-dose date.
steps.expect: a stored record you can produce for school, work, travel, or the next dose.

recipes.verification: The vaccine was administered, you completed the observation period without a reaction, and you hold a dated record (paper photo or digital registry entry) showing the vaccine name and any scheduled next dose.

recipes.title: get an eye test
recipes.name: get-an-eye-test
recipes.goal: You have a complete eye examination, understand your results, obtain a copy of your prescription, and can order glasses or contacts from the provider of your choice.

steps.action: **Book on the right cadence.** Book an eye exam (a "sight test") every 1 to 2 years for most adults, sooner if vision changed or you have diabetes or a family history of eye disease. Say if you also want a contact-lens fitting, which is a separate assessment.
steps.expect: an appointment booked with the exam types you need noted.

steps.action: **Confirm coverage and cost.** Ask whether your vision plan or public scheme covers the exam and how much glasses or contacts cost separately. Note that dilation or retinal imaging may be an add-on.
steps.expect: a clear picture of what the exam and any imaging cost.

steps.action: **Prepare and arrive.** Bring current glasses or contacts, your ID, plan details, and your symptom and history list. If you wear contacts, ask whether to remove them beforehand. Consider that dilating drops blur near vision for hours, so avoid driving yourself if dilation is likely.
steps.expect: you arrive with your current correction and a way home if dilated.

steps.action: **Complete the vision and health checks.** Expect a letter chart for acuity, a refraction ("which is clearer, one or two?"), a puff or contact test for eye pressure, and often a retinal look or imaging.
steps.expect: the optometrist measures each eye and describes what they see.

steps.action: **Get the results explained.** Ask what your acuity is, whether your prescription changed, and whether the health checks (pressure, retina, optic nerve) were normal.
steps.expect: plain-language answers, and a flag on anything needing monitoring or referral.

steps.action: **Obtain your prescription in writing.** Ask for a copy of the finalized prescription; you are generally entitled to it and are not required to buy glasses where you tested. It lists sphere, cylinder, axis, and any add or prism, plus a pupillary distance (PD) for glasses.
steps.expect: a written or emailed prescription with a validity date, PD included or measured on request. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm the numbers match what the optometrist told you before you leave; correcting a wrong prescription later means another visit.

steps.action: **Order glasses or contacts.** [BRANCH: buy in the same shop | take the prescription to another optician | order online using the prescription and PD] Choose lens options (single vision, progressive, coatings) to fit your needs and budget.
steps.expect: an order placed with the correct prescription and PD; a fitting date or delivery estimate given.

steps.action: **Check the finished eyewear.** On collection, confirm the lenses match the prescription, the frames sit level and comfortable, and vision is clear at the intended distance.
steps.expect: clear, comfortable vision with no distortion or persistent headache after a short adaptation.

recipes.verification: The exam is complete, you can state your acuity and whether your prescription changed and the health checks were normal, you hold a written prescription with PD, and any glasses or contacts you ordered match it and give clear, comfortable vision.

recipes.title: give childrens medicine safely
recipes.name: give-childrens-medicine-safely
recipes.goal: A child receives the correct medicine dose at the correct time using the proper measuring device, with overdose risks avoided.

steps.action: **Read the full label.** Check active ingredient, child age limits, warnings, dose chart, and maximum daily doses.
steps.expect: the medicine is appropriate for the child.

steps.action: **Confirm the child's weight.** Use weight-based dosing when the label or clinician provides it.
steps.expect: the dose matches weight rather than guesswork.

steps.action: **Check for duplicate ingredients.** Compare with other medicines, especially cough, cold, fever, allergy, and pain products.
steps.expect: the same active ingredient is not being doubled.

steps.action: **Use the right device.** Measure liquid medicine with the supplied syringe, dosing cup, or oral dispenser, not a kitchen spoon.
steps.expect: the marked dose can be read accurately.

steps.action: **Measure at eye level.** Draw or pour exactly to the correct line.
steps.expect: the dose line matches the intended amount.

steps.action: **Give the medicine safely.** Have the child upright and give liquid slowly toward the cheek.
steps.expect: the child swallows without choking.

steps.action: **Record the dose.** Write medicine name, amount, time, and who gave it.
steps.expect: another caregiver can see what was given.

steps.action: **Set the next allowed time.** Follow the label or prescription interval exactly.
steps.expect: the next dose is not too soon.

steps.action: **Store it securely.** Close the cap and put medicine out of sight and reach.
steps.expect: the child cannot access it.

steps.action: **Watch for side effects.** Monitor rash, vomiting, unusual sleepiness, agitation, breathing changes, or worsening illness.
steps.expect: concerning reactions trigger care.

recipes.verification: The child received only the intended child-appropriate dose, it was recorded with time, and the next safe dosing time is clear.

recipes.title: help a choking infant
recipes.name: help-a-choking-infant
recipes.goal: An infant under 1 year with a blocked airway receives age-appropriate choking first aid while emergency services are contacted.

steps.action: **Check for severe choking.** Look for weak or silent cough, inability to cry, noisy or absent breathing, blue or pale color, or panic.
steps.expect: severe airway obstruction is recognized.

steps.action: **Call or assign a caller.** Point to a specific person to call emergency services, or call on speaker if alone.
steps.expect: emergency help is being contacted.

steps.action: **Position face down.** Support the infant's head and jaw, place them face down along your forearm, and keep the head lower than the chest.
steps.expect: the airway points downward and the head is supported.

steps.action: **Give five back blows.** Use the heel of your hand to strike firmly between the shoulder blades, checking after each blow.
steps.expect: the object may come out or the infant may cry or cough strongly.

steps.action: **Turn face up safely.** Sandwich the infant between your forearms, support the head, and turn them face up with the head still lower than the chest.
steps.expect: the infant is controlled and supported.

steps.action: **Give five chest thrusts.** Place two fingers on the center of the chest just below the nipple line and press about one-third chest depth.
steps.expect: pressure may force air out and dislodge the object.

steps.action: **Repeat the cycle.** Continue five back blows and five chest thrusts until the object clears, help takes over, or the infant becomes unresponsive.
steps.expect: care continues without long pauses.

steps.action: **Remove only a visible object.** If you can clearly see and grasp the object, remove it gently.
steps.expect: the object is removed without pushing it deeper.

steps.action: **Start CPR if unresponsive.** Put the infant on a firm surface and begin infant CPR if trained or instructed by dispatch.
steps.expect: compressions and rescue guidance begin immediately.

steps.action: **Seek medical evaluation after clearing.** Keep watching breathing and have the infant evaluated after severe choking or chest thrusts.
steps.expect: delayed airway swelling or injury is not missed.

recipes.verification: The infant can cry, breathe, or cough effectively, emergency services were called for severe choking, and the infant is monitored until medical help or evaluation occurs.

recipes.title: help a diabetic having a hypo
recipes.name: help-a-diabetic-having-a-hypo
recipes.goal: A person with suspected low blood sugar receives fast sugar if awake and safe to swallow, or emergency help if severe.

steps.action: **Check responsiveness and swallowing.** Ask simple questions and confirm they can sit up and swallow safely.
steps.expect: you know whether oral sugar is safe.

steps.action: **Call emergency services for severe signs.** If unconscious, seizing, or unable to swallow, call immediately and use glucagon if available and trained.
steps.expect: severe hypoglycemia is escalated.

steps.action: **Check glucose if possible.** Use their meter or CGM if it does not delay treatment.
steps.expect: low or suspected low blood sugar is identified.

steps.action: **Give fast sugar if awake.** Provide glucose tablets, gel, juice, regular soda, candy, or sugar equivalent according to their plan.
steps.expect: quick carbohydrate is swallowed.

steps.action: **Wait 15 minutes.** Keep them seated and observe alertness, sweating, shaking, and behavior.
steps.expect: symptoms begin to improve if sugar is working.

steps.action: **Recheck or reassess.** Test glucose again if possible, or reassess symptoms.
steps.expect: improvement or persistent low signs are clear.

steps.action: **Repeat fast sugar if still low.** [BRANCH: improving | still low] repeat fast sugar if glucose remains low or symptoms persist and they can swallow.
