steps.expect: a second correction is given safely.

steps.action: **Give longer-acting food when better.** Once alert and improving, provide a snack or meal with carbohydrate and protein if the next meal is not soon.
steps.expect: blood sugar is less likely to drop again.

steps.action: **Avoid insulin correction.** Do not give insulin for the hypo unless a clinician or the person's plan explicitly directs it.
steps.expect: low blood sugar is not worsened.

steps.action: **Arrange follow-up or supervision.** Stay with them until normal, and contact a caregiver or clinician if cause is unclear.
steps.expect: recurrence risk is addressed.

recipes.verification: The person is awake, able to swallow, symptoms and glucose are improving after fast sugar, a longer-acting snack or meal is provided when appropriate, and emergency services were called for severe or non-improving signs.

recipes.title: help someone having a seizure
recipes.name: help-someone-having-a-seizure
recipes.goal: A person having a seizure is protected from injury, timed, and escalated to emergency services when warning signs are present.

steps.action: **Note the start time.** Check a clock or phone as soon as you recognize seizure activity.
steps.expect: the seizure duration can be reported accurately.

steps.action: **Clear nearby hazards.** Move chairs, sharp objects, hot items, or hard objects away from the person.
steps.expect: the area around the person is safer.

steps.action: **Protect the head.** Place a folded jacket or soft flat item under the head if available.
steps.expect: the head is cushioned without forcing movement.

steps.action: **Loosen tight neck items.** Loosen scarves, ties, or tight collars if you can do so safely.
steps.expect: breathing is not restricted by clothing.

steps.action: **Do not restrain.** Let the seizure run its course and keep others from holding the person down.
steps.expect: injury from forced restraint is avoided.

steps.action: **Keep the mouth clear from outside.** Do not insert fingers, spoons, wallets, or medicine into the mouth.
steps.expect: teeth, jaw, and airway are not endangered by objects.

steps.action: **Call when criteria are met.** [BRANCH: emergency criteria present | known brief seizure] call emergency services if any red flag is present; otherwise keep timing and monitoring.
steps.expect: urgent situations are escalated.

steps.action: **Turn after jerking stops.** If they are breathing but not fully awake, roll them onto their side in the recovery position.
steps.expect: saliva or vomit can drain and the airway stays open.

steps.action: **Reassure during recovery.** Speak calmly, explain what happened, and keep bystanders back.
steps.expect: confusion and embarrassment are reduced.

steps.action: **Monitor until fully alert.** Check breathing, injuries, and orientation until the person returns to their usual state or help arrives.
steps.expect: delayed problems are noticed.

recipes.verification: The seizure was timed, hazards were cleared, nothing was placed in the mouth, emergency services were called if criteria were met, and the person is monitored in recovery.

recipes.title: help someone in shock
recipes.name: help-someone-in-shock
recipes.goal: A person with possible shock is kept still, warm, and monitored while emergency services are called.

steps.action: **Check scene safety.** Look for traffic, violence, electricity, fire, or other hazards before approaching.
steps.expect: you can help without adding another casualty.

steps.action: **Call emergency services.** Say the person may be in shock and report the suspected cause.
steps.expect: dispatch is connected and can guide you.

steps.action: **Stop major bleeding.** Apply firm direct pressure with clean cloth or dressing if bleeding is present.
steps.expect: visible bleeding slows or stops.

steps.action: **Lay the person flat if tolerated.** Help them lie on their back unless breathing, injury, or comfort prevents it.
steps.expect: they are resting and not exerting themselves.

steps.action: **Avoid unsafe leg elevation.** [BRANCH: no injury and comfortable | trauma, pain, breathing trouble, pregnancy] raise legs slightly only if it does not cause pain or breathing trouble; otherwise keep flat or position of comfort.
steps.expect: positioning does not worsen injuries.

steps.action: **Keep warm.** Cover with a coat or blanket while avoiding overheating.
steps.expect: chills and heat loss are reduced.

steps.action: **Loosen tight clothing.** Loosen belts, collars, or restrictive clothing if easy and respectful.
steps.expect: breathing and circulation are not restricted.

steps.action: **Monitor breathing and alertness.** Watch for worsening confusion, blue color, vomiting, or loss of consciousness.
steps.expect: deterioration is detected quickly.

steps.action: **Use recovery position if needed.** If unconscious but breathing normally and no suspected spine injury prevents movement, roll them onto their side.
steps.expect: vomit or fluids can drain.

steps.action: **Prepare handoff.** Note symptoms, injuries, allergies, medications, and what changed over time.
steps.expect: responders get a clear summary.

recipes.verification: Emergency services have been called, life-threatening bleeding is controlled, the person is kept still and warm, and breathing plus alertness are monitored until responders arrive.

recipes.title: help someone who fainted
recipes.name: help-someone-who-fainted
recipes.goal: A person who fainted is protected from injury, checked for breathing, and escalated when fainting may signal a serious problem.

steps.action: **Check scene safety.** Make sure the area is safe from traffic, heat, electrical hazards, or crowd pressure.
steps.expect: you can assist safely.

steps.action: **Check responsiveness.** Tap shoulders and speak loudly to see if they wake.
steps.expect: you know whether this is fainting or ongoing unresponsiveness.

steps.action: **Check breathing.** Look for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
steps.expect: absent or abnormal breathing is recognized.

steps.action: **Call if not breathing normally.** [BRANCH: not breathing normally | breathing normally] start CPR if trained when breathing is absent or abnormal; continue fainting care if breathing is normal.
steps.expect: cardiac arrest is not mistaken for fainting.

steps.action: **Lay them flat.** If no injury prevents it, place them on their back.
steps.expect: blood flow to the brain is supported.

steps.action: **Raise the legs.** Lift legs about 12 inches if comfortable and no injury is suspected.
steps.expect: circulation may improve.

steps.action: **Loosen tight clothing.** Loosen collars, belts, or restrictive items.
steps.expect: breathing and comfort improve.

steps.action: **Use recovery position if needed.** If they are breathing but not fully awake, roll them onto their side.
steps.expect: the airway stays open and fluid can drain.

steps.action: **Keep them resting after waking.** Have them remain lying or seated for several minutes before standing.
steps.expect: repeat fainting risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Escalate serious features.** Call emergency services for red flags, injury, or failure to recover promptly.
steps.expect: dangerous causes are not dismissed.

recipes.verification: The person is breathing normally, lying safely or in recovery position, monitored until fully alert, and emergency services are called for any red flag.

recipes.title: help someone who is choking
recipes.name: help-someone-who-is-choking
recipes.goal: A responsive choking adult or child is helped while emergency services are called when the airway is blocked.

steps.action: **Check for severe choking.** Ask if they are choking and look for silent coughing, inability to speak, blue or pale color, panic, or hands at the throat.
steps.expect: you can distinguish mild choking from a blocked airway.

steps.action: **Encourage coughing if air is moving.** [BRANCH: effective cough | weak or silent cough] tell them to keep coughing if they can breathe or speak; act immediately if they cannot.
steps.expect: mild choking is not interrupted with forceful maneuvers.

steps.action: **Call emergency services for severe choking.** Point to a specific person to call, or call on speaker if alone.
steps.expect: dispatch is reached or being contacted while care begins.

steps.action: **Position for back blows.** Stand to the side and slightly behind, support the chest with one arm, and lean the person forward.
steps.expect: the airway points downward so the object can come out.

steps.action: **Give five back blows.** Strike firmly between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand, checking after each blow.
steps.expect: the object may dislodge or the person may begin coughing strongly.

steps.action: **Position for abdominal thrusts.** Stand behind, place a fist just above the navel and below the breastbone, and grasp it with the other hand.
steps.expect: your hands are on the abdomen, not the ribs or breastbone.

steps.action: **Give five abdominal thrusts.** Pull sharply inward and upward, checking after each thrust.
steps.expect: the pressure may force air out and expel the object.

steps.action: **Repeat cycles.** Alternate five back blows and five abdominal thrusts until the object clears, help takes over, or the person becomes unresponsive.
steps.expect: care continues without long pauses.

steps.action: **If they become unresponsive, lower them safely.** Place them on a firm, flat surface and start CPR if trained or instructed by dispatch.
steps.expect: compressions begin and emergency services are already involved.

steps.action: **After breathing returns, arrange medical evaluation.** Keep watching breathing and encourage evaluation, especially after thrusts, persistent coughing, or injury.
steps.expect: delayed airway or internal injury is not ignored.

recipes.verification: The person can breathe, speak, or cough effectively, emergency services have been called if severe choking occurred, and they are monitored until safe care takes over.

recipes.title: help someone with heat stroke
recipes.name: help-someone-with-heat-stroke
recipes.goal: A person with suspected heat stroke is cooled aggressively while emergency services are called.

steps.action: **Call emergency services.** Say suspected heat stroke and report mental status, exertion, and location.
steps.expect: urgent medical response is activated.

steps.action: **Move to a cooler place.** Get the person into shade, air conditioning, or a cool room if safe.
steps.expect: heat exposure decreases.

steps.action: **Remove excess clothing.** Loosen or remove outer layers, helmet, pads, or gear while preserving privacy.
steps.expect: skin is available for cooling.

steps.action: **Start rapid cooling.** Use cold water immersion if available, or soak with cold water and fan continuously.
steps.expect: body cooling begins immediately.

steps.action: **Cool key areas.** Place cold packs or wet cloths on neck, armpits, and groin while continuing whole-body cooling.
steps.expect: major blood-flow areas are cooled.

steps.action: **Monitor airway and breathing.** Watch for vomiting, seizure, or loss of consciousness.
steps.expect: airway danger is recognized.

steps.action: **Do not force drinks.** [BRANCH: fully alert | confused or vomiting] offer small sips only if fully alert and able to swallow; otherwise give nothing by mouth.
steps.expect: choking risk is avoided.

steps.action: **Continue cooling until help arrives.** Keep cooling unless shivering becomes severe or dispatch instructs otherwise.
steps.expect: cooling does not stop prematurely.

steps.action: **Prepare facts for responders.** Note exertion, heat exposure, medications, medical conditions, and cooling start time.
steps.expect: responders can judge severity.

steps.action: **Transfer care.** Tell responders what cooling was used and how the person changed.
steps.expect: emergency care continues without information loss.

recipes.verification: Emergency services have been called, active cooling is underway, the person is out of heat exposure, no unsafe fluids are given, and breathing plus mental status are monitored until responders arrive.

recipes.title: immobilize a suspected broken bone
recipes.name: immobilize-a-suspected-broken-bone
recipes.goal: A suspected fracture is kept still, circulation is monitored, and emergency care is obtained when needed.

steps.action: **Check scene and person.** Make sure the area is safe and check breathing, bleeding, and alertness first.
steps.expect: immediate life threats are recognized.

steps.action: **Call for emergency help if indicated.** Report suspected fracture, location, bleeding, deformity, and circulation changes.
steps.expect: urgent care is activated for serious injuries.

steps.action: **Tell them not to move.** Support the injured part in the position found.
steps.expect: pain and further tissue injury are reduced.

steps.action: **Check circulation beyond injury.** Look for color, warmth, sensation, movement, and pulse if you know how.
steps.expect: baseline circulation and nerve status are known.

steps.action: **Cover open wounds.** Place clean dressing over any wound without pushing exposed bone back in.
steps.expect: contamination is reduced.

steps.action: **Apply a splint if transport requires it.** [BRANCH: awaiting ambulance | must move] avoid unnecessary splinting if help is coming; splint only to prevent movement during necessary transport.
steps.expect: movement is minimized without extra manipulation.

steps.action: **Pad and secure above and below.** Use boards, rolled magazines, pillows, or clothing, tying above and below the injury without covering fingers or toes.
steps.expect: joints around the injury move less.

steps.action: **Recheck circulation after splinting.** Compare color, warmth, numbness, and movement beyond the splint.
steps.expect: the splint is not cutting off blood flow.

steps.action: **Use cold pack safely.** Apply wrapped cold pack for swelling if available and tolerated.
steps.expect: swelling and pain may decrease without skin freezing.

steps.action: **Monitor until care.** Watch pain, swelling, numbness, color, and shock signs while waiting or transporting.
steps.expect: worsening is caught and reported.

recipes.verification: The injured area is supported with minimal movement, emergency services are called for red flags, circulation beyond the injury is checked before and after splinting, and worsening symptoms are monitored.

recipes.title: manage a fever at home
recipes.name: manage-a-fever-at-home
recipes.goal: A fever in yourself or a household member is measured accurately, managed with rest and fluids, and escalated to a clinician the moment a red-flag threshold is crossed.

steps.action: **Pick the right thermometer for the person.** Oral for adults and cooperative children over 4; ear or axillary for younger; forehead scanners are fast but least accurate.
steps.expect: a device you can place correctly without a struggle.

steps.action: **Measure at rest, not right after activity or a hot drink.** Wait 15 minutes after eating/drinking/bathing for an oral reading.
steps.expect: a stable numeric reading, not one still climbing on the display.

steps.action: **Interpret the number by site.** Fever is roughly ≥38.0°C (100.4°F) core. Axillary reads ~0.5°C low; forehead/ear vary.
steps.expect: you know whether this crosses the fever line for the site you used.

steps.action: **Note the trend, not just one value.** Re-measure every 4 to 6 hours and write down time, value, and site.
steps.expect: a short log showing rising, plateau, or falling.

steps.action: **Treat the discomfort, not the number.** Give paracetamol or ibuprofen at the correct weight-based dose only if the person is uncomfortable; a well child at 38.5°C needs no drug. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never exceed the max daily dose and never combine two products containing the same drug (overdose is liver/kidney damage).
steps.expect: dose recorded with the clock time of the next allowed dose.

steps.action: **Push fluids and cool the environment.** Small frequent sips; light clothing; room comfortable, not cold. Do not sponge with cold water or alcohol (causes shivering, which raises temperature).
steps.expect: the person is drinking and passing urine; skin not clammy-cold.

steps.action: **Watch for red flags continuously.** [BRANCH: any red flag present → contact urgent care / emergency now | none, improving → continue home care and rest]
steps.expect: a clear decision each time you re-check.

recipes.verification: The person's temperature is logged with time and site, any medication is within safe dose and recorded, fluids are going in and urine is coming out, and no red-flag symptom is present. If any threshold was crossed, a clinician has been contacted.

recipes.title: manage an allergic reaction with antihistamines
recipes.name: manage-an-allergic-reaction-with-antihistamines
recipes.goal: A mild allergic reaction is managed with an appropriate antihistamine while anaphylaxis signs are recognized and escalated immediately.

steps.action: **Check for anaphylaxis first.** Look for breathing trouble, swelling of throat or tongue, faintness, severe vomiting, confusion, or rapid worsening.
steps.expect: emergency signs are ruled in or out.

steps.action: **Use epinephrine for emergency signs.** [BRANCH: anaphylaxis signs | mild symptoms only] help use prescribed epinephrine and call emergency services for anaphylaxis; continue antihistamine care only for mild symptoms.
steps.expect: life-threatening allergy is not treated with antihistamine alone.

steps.action: **Remove the trigger if safe.** Stop eating the food, move away from the allergen, remove the stinger by scraping, or wash skin exposure.
steps.expect: exposure is reduced.

steps.action: **Read the antihistamine label.** Confirm active ingredient, dose, age limits, warnings, and whether it causes drowsiness.
steps.expect: the medication is appropriate before use.

steps.action: **Check contraindications.** Ask about allergy to the medicine, interacting sedatives, alcohol, glaucoma, urinary retention, pregnancy, or clinician warnings.
steps.expect: obvious medication risks are screened.

steps.action: **Give the labeled dose.** Use the measuring device for liquids and do not combine multiple antihistamines unless directed by a clinician.
steps.expect: one appropriate dose is taken.

steps.action: **Record timing and dose.** Write down medication name, amount, and time.
steps.expect: caregivers or clinicians can avoid duplicate dosing.

steps.action: **Monitor closely.** Watch breathing, swelling, hives spread, vomiting, dizziness, and alertness for worsening.
steps.expect: escalation signs are detected.

steps.action: **Avoid driving if sedating.** Keep the person from driving or risky tasks if the medicine can cause drowsiness.
steps.expect: medication side-effect risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Seek medical advice if persistent.** Contact a clinician if symptoms last, recur, worsen, or the trigger was high risk.
steps.expect: unresolved reactions get follow-up.

recipes.verification: Anaphylaxis signs were checked, emergency services and epinephrine were used for red flags, any antihistamine dose followed the label, and symptoms are improving without breathing, swelling, faintness, or multi-system involvement.

recipes.title: measure your heart rate
recipes.name: measure-your-heart-rate
recipes.goal: You measure a pulse accurately, identify whether it is resting or active, and know when the number or symptoms need medical care.

steps.action: **Rest before a resting reading.** Sit quietly for 5 minutes if you want a resting heart rate.
steps.expect: breathing and movement settle.

steps.action: **Choose a pulse site.** [BRANCH: wrist | neck] use the wrist below the thumb, or the side of the neck beside the windpipe if the wrist is hard to feel.
steps.expect: a clear rhythmic beat under two fingertips.

steps.action: **Use two fingers.** Place index and middle fingers gently; do not use your thumb because it has its own pulse.
steps.expect: you feel the person's pulse, not your thumb's.

steps.action: **Count for 15 seconds.** Start at zero when the timer begins and count each beat for 15 seconds.
steps.expect: a beat count for the interval.

steps.action: **Multiply by four.** Convert the 15-second count to beats per minute.
steps.expect: a heart-rate number in bpm.

steps.action: **Use a longer count if irregular.** If beats skip or vary, count for 60 seconds instead.
steps.expect: a more accurate number for an irregular rhythm.

steps.action: **Label the context.** Record whether the reading was resting, after walking, during exercise, anxious, feverish, or after caffeine.
steps.expect: the number has useful context.

steps.action: **Compare to typical ranges.** Many adults rest around 60 to 100 bpm, while trained athletes may be lower and active heart rates rise with exertion.
steps.expect: you know whether the reading fits the situation.

recipes.verification: A beats-per-minute value is recorded with its context, and any urgent symptoms or repeated abnormal resting readings are escalated appropriately.

recipes.title: prepare for a blood test
recipes.name: prepare-for-a-blood-test
recipes.goal: You arrive for a blood draw correctly prepared (fasting or not, hydrated, medications handled), the sample is taken cleanly, and you know when and how to get the results.

steps.action: **Read the test order for prep requirements.** Look specifically for a fasting instruction and its duration. Common fasting tests: glucose, lipid panel, some metabolic panels. Many tests need no fasting at all.
steps.expect: you know whether fasting is required and for how many hours (often 8 to 12).

steps.action: **If fasting is required, plan the fast and the appointment time.** Stop eating and drinking everything except plain water at the start of the window, and book the earliest morning slot so you fast overnight through sleep.
steps.expect: a morning appointment that lets the fasting window fall mostly while you sleep. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* eating inside the fasting window invalidates fasting results; if you slip, reschedule rather than draw a spoiled sample.

steps.action: **Keep drinking plain water throughout.** Water is allowed during a fast and makes veins fuller and easier to find. Avoid coffee, tea, gum, and juice while fasting; they can alter results.
steps.expect: you are well hydrated but consuming only water before the draw.

steps.action: **Handle medications deliberately, not by guessing.** [BRANCH: routine daily meds usually continue with water | some tests require holding a specific drug or timing a dose (thyroid, certain diabetes meds, drug-level tests) | blood thinners are usually continued but tell the phlebotomist] Ask the ordering clinician if the order does not say.
steps.expect: a clear plan for each medication, confirmed rather than assumed.

steps.action: **Bring the right things and dress for access.** Order or requisition, ID, card, medication list, and a short or loose sleeve that rolls above the elbow.
steps.expect: the requisition matches your name and the phlebotomist can bare your arm easily.

steps.action: **At the draw, disclose and position well.** Tell the phlebotomist if you faint at needles, have a preferred arm, a lymphedema arm to avoid, or are on blood thinners. Sit back, relax the arm, and look away if needed.
steps.expect: a tourniquet, a brief sting, tubes filling; done in under two minutes.

steps.action: **Apply pressure and protect the site.** Press firmly on the puncture for a full 2 to 3 minutes (longer on blood thinners), then keep the bandage on for an hour and avoid heavy lifting with that arm.
steps.expect: bleeding stopped, only a small mark; no large bruise forming.

steps.action: **Confirm the results pathway before you leave.** Ask when results are expected, whether they post to a portal, and who contacts you about abnormal values.
steps.expect: a known turnaround (often 1 to 3 days) and a channel to see or discuss results.

recipes.verification: The sample was drawn from a correctly prepared state (fasting satisfied if required), bleeding has stopped with no growing hematoma, and you know when and where the results will appear and who follows up on abnormal values.

recipes.title: prepare for a doctor visit
recipes.name: prepare-for-a-doctor-visit
recipes.goal: Arrive at a doctor visit with the information, records, and questions needed to use the appointment well.

steps.action: **Confirm the appointment details.** Check date, time, location, parking, telehealth link, and arrival instructions.
steps.expect: you know when and where to check in.

steps.action: **Write the main concern.** Summarize the reason for the visit in one or two sentences.
steps.expect: you can explain the visit quickly at the start.

steps.action: **Build a symptom timeline.** Note when symptoms started, what changed, triggers, treatments tried, and what makes it better or worse.
steps.expect: timeline is specific enough to answer common questions.

steps.action: **Make a medication list.** Include prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, supplements, dose, and frequency.
steps.expect: list matches what you actually take.

steps.action: **List allergies and reactions.** Write the medicine or substance and what happened.
steps.expect: allergy information distinguishes rash, nausea, swelling, or other reaction.

steps.action: **Prepare questions.** Put the top 3 questions first so they are covered if time is short.
steps.expect: questions are visible during the appointment.

steps.action: **Gather records.** Bring recent test results, imaging reports, discharge papers, vaccine records, or prior visit notes if the office may not have them.
steps.expect: relevant records are saved, printed, or uploaded.

steps.action: **Bring ID and insurance.** Pack photo ID, insurance card, referral, copay method, and forms.
steps.expect: check-in documents are ready before leaving.

steps.action: **Plan the next step before leaving.** Ask about diagnosis, treatment, warning signs, follow-up, referrals, tests, and how results will arrive.
steps.expect: you leave with a clear action plan.

recipes.verification: Before the visit, you have appointment details, medication list, symptom timeline, top questions, relevant records, ID, insurance, and payment method ready.

recipes.title: prepare for a telehealth visit
recipes.name: prepare-for-a-telehealth-visit
recipes.goal: You enter a telehealth visit on time with working technology, useful health information, and a private setting that supports a focused medical conversation.

steps.action: **Confirm the appointment details.** Check date, time zone, link, clinician, and whether forms are due.
steps.expect: you know exactly when and where to join.

steps.action: **Test the technology.** Open the portal or video app, allow camera and microphone access, and check audio.
steps.expect: you can see and hear a test screen or preview.

steps.action: **Prepare the space.** Sit somewhere quiet, private, well lit, and close to power or strong battery.
steps.expect: your face is visible and background interruptions are reduced.

steps.action: **Gather health information.** Put medications, allergies, pharmacy, symptoms, photos, home readings, and questions within reach.
steps.expect: you can answer common intake questions quickly.

steps.action: **Measure if relevant.** Take temperature, blood pressure, pulse, weight, glucose, or oxygen level only if you have the device and it fits the visit.
steps.expect: readings are written with time and units.

steps.action: **Join early.** Enter the virtual waiting room 5 to 10 minutes before the appointment.
steps.expect: you are checked in before the clinician arrives.

steps.action: **Ask for next steps.** Before ending, confirm diagnosis impression, treatment, warning signs, prescriptions, work notes, and follow-up.
steps.expect: you know what to do after the call.

recipes.verification: You joined the visit with working audio and video, had your medication list and questions ready, and left with documented next steps.

recipes.title: prevent blisters on a hike
recipes.name: prevent-blisters-on-a-hike
recipes.goal: Your feet are prepared for hiking so friction, moisture, and pressure points are controlled before blisters form.

steps.action: **Fit boots with hiking socks.** Try footwear with the socks you will wear and enough room for toes on downhill steps.
steps.expect: toes do not jam and heel lift is minimal.

steps.action: **Break in footwear early.** Wear boots or shoes on short walks before the hike.
steps.expect: pressure points appear close to home, not on the trail.

steps.action: **Choose moisture-wicking socks.** Use wool or synthetic hiking socks and avoid cotton for long hikes.
steps.expect: feet stay drier under effort.

steps.action: **Reduce friction before starting.** Apply foot lubricant or pre-tape known hot spots such as heels, toes, or the ball of the foot.
steps.expect: high-rub areas are protected.

steps.action: **Pack quick-access supplies.** Keep tape, blister pads, spare socks, and a small wipe where you can reach them.
steps.expect: you can treat a hot spot without unpacking everything.

steps.action: **Stop at the first hot spot.** Pause as soon as you feel rubbing, heat, or a sharp sock wrinkle.
steps.expect: skin is still intact.

steps.action: **Dry and cover the hot spot.** Smooth the sock, dry the skin, then apply tape or moleskin without wrinkles.
steps.expect: rubbing stops when you resume walking.

steps.action: **Change wet socks.** Swap socks when feet are soaked from sweat, rain, or stream crossings.
steps.expect: moisture load drops.

steps.action: **Adjust lacing.** Tighten for downhill toe control or loosen pressure over the top of the foot.
steps.expect: foot movement is controlled without numbness.

recipes.verification: Footwear is broken in, socks manage moisture, hot spots are taped as soon as they appear, and no blister is ignored until skin breaks.

recipes.title: put someone in the recovery position
recipes.name: put-someone-in-the-recovery-position
recipes.goal: An unresponsive person who is breathing normally is placed on their side with an open airway while emergency services are called when appropriate.

steps.action: **Check safety and response.** Make sure the scene is safe, then tap shoulders and speak loudly.
steps.expect: you know the person is unresponsive or not fully responsive.

steps.action: **Call for help.** Ask a bystander to call emergency services and get an AED, or call on speaker if alone.
steps.expect: help is on the way or being contacted.

steps.action: **Check breathing.** Look, listen, and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
steps.expect: normal breathing is confirmed before rolling.

steps.action: **Decide whether to move.** [BRANCH: no spinal concern | spinal concern] roll if airway protection is needed and no spinal concern; avoid movement if spinal injury is suspected and breathing is clear.
steps.expect: movement risk is considered.

steps.action: **Position the near arm.** Place the arm nearest you at a right angle to the body with palm up.
steps.expect: the arm will help stop over-rolling.

steps.action: **Place the far hand.** Bring the far hand across the chest and hold the back of that hand against the cheek nearest you.
steps.expect: the hand supports the head during the roll.

steps.action: **Bend the far knee.** Lift the far knee so the foot stays flat on the ground.
steps.expect: the leg becomes a lever for rolling.

steps.action: **Roll toward you.** Pull the bent knee gently so the person rolls onto their side, keeping the hand against the cheek.
steps.expect: the person rests stably on their side.

steps.action: **Open the airway.** Tilt the head slightly back and lift the chin, checking that the mouth points downward for drainage.
steps.expect: the airway is open and fluids can drain.

steps.action: **Monitor continuously.** Recheck breathing and responsiveness until help arrives, and roll onto the other side after about 30 minutes if waiting long and no injury prevents it.
steps.expect: breathing changes are detected early.

recipes.verification: The person is on their side, breathing normally, airway open with the mouth draining downward, emergency services are called if indicated, and breathing is monitored.

recipes.title: read a prescription label
recipes.name: read-a-prescription-label
recipes.goal: Read a prescription label well enough to take the right medicine, dose, route, and schedule, and know when to ask a pharmacist for clarification.

steps.action: **Confirm the patient.** Check the name and date of birth or other identifier on the label.
steps.expect: the prescription belongs to the person who will take it.

steps.action: **Read the drug name and strength.** Identify brand or generic name and the amount per tablet, capsule, mL, patch, or inhalation.
steps.expect: you know exactly which medicine and strength you have.

steps.action: **Read the dose.** Find how much to take each time, such as 1 tablet, 5 mL, 2 puffs, or apply thin layer.
steps.expect: dose unit matches the medicine form.

steps.action: **Read frequency and timing.** Identify how often and when, such as once daily, every 8 hours, with food, or at bedtime.
steps.expect: you can place each dose on a daily schedule.

steps.action: **Read the route.** Confirm whether to take by mouth, inhale, inject, apply to skin, place in eye or ear, or use another route.
steps.expect: route is clear and matches the container.

steps.action: **Check warnings and stickers.** Read auxiliary stickers about drowsiness, alcohol, sun exposure, food, driving, shaking, refrigeration, or finishing the course.
steps.expect: special handling or activity limits are known.

steps.action: **Check quantity and refills.** Find how many doses were dispensed, number of refills, and refill expiration date if printed.
steps.expect: you know when to request more.

steps.action: **Check expiration and discard date.** Note the use-by date and any short expiration after mixing or opening.
steps.expect: medicine is current and storage rules are clear.

steps.action: **Ask before guessing.** If any instruction conflicts or is unclear, call the pharmacist or prescriber before taking it.
steps.expect: unclear directions are resolved by a professional.

recipes.verification: You can state the medicine name, strength, dose, frequency, route, key warnings, refill status, and expiration without guessing.

recipes.title: read your lab results
recipes.name: read-your-lab-results
recipes.goal: You understand what your lab report is showing, identify questions for your clinician, and avoid self-diagnosing from isolated flagged values.

steps.action: **Confirm the report belongs to you.** Check name, date of birth, collection date, and ordering clinician.
steps.expect: the identifying details match.

steps.action: **Read the test context.** Note why the test was ordered, whether you were fasting, and any medications or illness at the time.
steps.expect: the result has clinical context.

steps.action: **Compare result, unit, and reference range.** Read the number with its unit and the lab's own range.
steps.expect: you know whether this lab marked it low, normal, high, or critical.

steps.action: **Look for flags without panicking.** Treat H, L, abnormal, or out-of-range markers as prompts for interpretation, not diagnoses.
steps.expect: flagged values are listed for follow-up.

steps.action: **Check trends.** Compare with prior results from the same or similar test when available.
steps.expect: you can see whether the value is stable, improving, or changing.

steps.action: **Write clinician questions.** Ask what the result means for your situation, whether repeat testing is needed, and what action is recommended.
steps.expect: you have a short question list.

steps.action: **Follow the clinician's interpretation.** Use the ordering clinician's guidance before changing medicines, supplements, diet, or treatment.
steps.expect: no self-directed medical change is made from the report alone.

recipes.verification: You have confirmed the report identity, listed flagged or changing values with units and dates, and sent or prepared specific questions for the clinician without self-diagnosing.

recipes.title: recognize a heart attack
recipes.name: recognize-a-heart-attack
recipes.goal: Possible heart attack symptoms are recognized early, emergency services are called, and the person rests while waiting for medical care.

steps.action: **Look for chest discomfort.** Ask about pressure, squeezing, fullness, burning, or pain in the center or left chest.
steps.expect: chest symptoms are described in the person's own words.

steps.action: **Check related symptoms.** Ask about shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, lightheadedness, unusual fatigue, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.
steps.expect: non-chest warning signs are not missed.

steps.action: **Check spreading discomfort.** Ask about pain or pressure in one or both arms, back, neck, jaw, shoulder, or upper abdomen.
steps.expect: referred symptoms are recognized.

steps.action: **Consider atypical patterns.** [BRANCH: chest pain present | no chest pain but concerning symptoms] treat either pattern as possible heart attack, especially in women, older adults, and people with diabetes.
steps.expect: absence of classic chest pain does not delay action.

steps.action: **Call emergency services.** Call on speaker or assign one named bystander to call.
steps.expect: dispatch is connected and can guide care.

steps.action: **Keep the person resting.** Have them sit or lie in a comfortable position and loosen tight clothing.
steps.expect: exertion stops and breathing is easier.

steps.action: **Avoid self-transport.** Tell the person not to drive and arrange EMS transport unless dispatch says otherwise.
steps.expect: rapid medical transport is handled by professionals.

steps.action: **Ask about aspirin only if appropriate.** Follow dispatcher or clinician advice about chewing aspirin, and skip it for allergy, active bleeding, blood thinner concern, or prior instruction to avoid aspirin.
steps.expect: aspirin is not given blindly.

steps.action: **Watch for cardiac arrest.** Monitor responsiveness and normal breathing until help arrives.
steps.expect: collapse or abnormal breathing is detected immediately.

steps.action: **Start CPR if needed.** If unresponsive and not breathing normally, begin hands-only CPR and use an AED if available.
steps.expect: circulation support starts while EMS is on the way.

recipes.verification: Emergency services have been called, the person is resting, self-transport is avoided, and CPR or AED readiness is in place if they collapse.

recipes.title: recognize a severe allergic reaction
recipes.name: recognize-a-severe-allergic-reaction
recipes.goal: A severe allergic reaction is recognized early so epinephrine is used and emergency services are called without delay.

steps.action: **Identify possible exposure.** Ask about foods, stings, medicines, latex, exercise after food, or other known allergens.
steps.expect: a trigger may be identified without delaying care.

steps.action: **Check skin signs.** Look for hives, itching, flushing, swelling of lips, eyelids, face, or widespread rash.
steps.expect: allergic skin involvement is recognized.

steps.action: **Check airway signs.** Listen for hoarse voice, throat tightness, tongue swelling, trouble swallowing, or noisy breathing.
steps.expect: airway danger is identified.

steps.action: **Check breathing signs.** Look for wheeze, shortness of breath, persistent cough, or chest tightness.
steps.expect: lower airway involvement is recognized.

steps.action: **Check circulation and gut signs.** Ask about dizziness, faintness, collapse, severe vomiting, diarrhea, or cramping.
steps.expect: shock or multi-system symptoms are considered.

steps.action: **Decide if severe.** [BRANCH: airway or breathing or faintness | only mild local symptoms] treat airway, breathing, faintness, collapse, or multiple body systems as anaphylaxis.
steps.expect: severe allergy is not minimized.

steps.action: **Use epinephrine if available.** Give the prescribed auto-injector into the outer thigh or help the person use it.
steps.expect: first-line treatment is given promptly.

steps.action: **Call emergency services.** Call immediately after recognizing anaphylaxis or after injecting if injection had to come first.
steps.expect: EMS is responding.

steps.action: **Position and monitor.** Lay them flat with legs raised if tolerated, or sit upright for breathing difficulty, and monitor breathing.
steps.expect: collapse risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Watch for biphasic recurrence.** Keep monitoring because symptoms can return hours later.
steps.expect: improvement is not treated as the end of the emergency.

recipes.verification: Anaphylaxis warning signs have been checked, epinephrine is used when indicated, emergency services are called, and the person is monitored for recurrent symptoms.

recipes.title: recognize and respond to a concussion
recipes.name: recognize-and-respond-to-a-concussion
recipes.goal: A possible concussion is recognized, activity is stopped, red flags trigger emergency care, and safe monitoring is arranged.

steps.action: **Stop the activity.** Remove the person from play, work, cycling, driving, or the hazardous setting.
steps.expect: no second impact occurs.

steps.action: **Check immediate danger.** Look for airway issues, severe bleeding, neck pain, or unsafe surroundings.
steps.expect: life threats are recognized first.

steps.action: **Screen for red flags.** Ask about headache, vomiting, vision, weakness, numbness, confusion, memory gap, seizure, and loss of consciousness.
steps.expect: emergency warning signs are identified.

steps.action: **Call emergency services if red flags exist.** Report the injury mechanism and symptoms.
steps.expect: urgent care is activated for dangerous signs.

steps.action: **Keep them resting.** Have them sit or lie comfortably with supervision and minimal stimulation.
steps.expect: symptoms are not worsened by exertion.

steps.action: **Do not give risky medicines.** Avoid alcohol, sedatives, and blood-thinning pain relievers unless a clinician says otherwise.
steps.expect: bleeding or masking symptoms is avoided.

steps.action: **Arrange same-day medical advice.** Contact a clinician, urgent care, athletic trainer, or emergency department for evaluation guidance.
steps.expect: concussion care is not self-cleared.

steps.action: **Monitor for worsening.** Check alertness, headache, vomiting, behavior, balance, and speech over the next hours.
steps.expect: deterioration is caught quickly.

steps.action: **Prevent return to risk.** [BRANCH: wants to continue | agrees to rest] stop same-day return even if they feel better; arrange supervision and transport.
steps.expect: second-injury risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Document the event.** Note time, mechanism, symptoms, loss of consciousness, vomiting, and medicines.
steps.expect: clinicians get accurate history.

recipes.verification: The person has stopped risky activity, red flags were checked, emergency services were called for any warning sign, and medical evaluation plus supervised monitoring are arranged before return to normal activity.

recipes.title: recognize low blood sugar
recipes.name: recognize-low-blood-sugar
recipes.goal: Possible low blood sugar is recognized, treated promptly when safe, and escalated when it could be an emergency.

steps.action: **Check for severe symptoms.** Look for unconsciousness, seizure, inability to swallow, severe confusion, or collapse.
steps.expect: emergency signs are identified before giving anything by mouth.

steps.action: **Call emergency services if severe.** [BRANCH: severe symptoms | awake and can swallow] call emergency services and use prescribed glucagon if available for severe symptoms; continue oral treatment only if safe.
steps.expect: severe hypoglycemia is treated as an emergency. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not put food, drink, or fingers in the mouth of a person who is unconscious or seizing.

steps.action: **Check glucose if available.** Use a meter or CGM reading and note the time.
steps.expect: a low reading, often below 70 mg/dL or 3.9 mmol/L, supports treatment.

steps.action: **Give fast sugar.** Give 15 grams of fast-acting carbohydrate, such as glucose tablets, glucose gel, regular soda, juice, or hard candy that can be chewed safely.
steps.expect: sugar is swallowed without choking.

steps.action: **Wait 15 minutes.** Keep the person seated and recheck symptoms or glucose after 15 minutes.
steps.expect: symptoms start improving or the glucose can be remeasured.

steps.action: **Repeat the 15-15 rule.** If glucose is still low or symptoms persist, give another 15 grams and wait 15 minutes.
steps.expect: glucose rises or symptoms improve after repeat treatment.

steps.action: **Eat longer-acting food.** Once better, give a meal or snack with carbohydrate and protein if the next meal is not soon.
steps.expect: glucose is less likely to drop again.

steps.action: **Identify the cause.** Check for missed meal, extra insulin, more exercise than usual, alcohol, vomiting, or medication error.
steps.expect: the likely trigger is known for prevention.

steps.action: **Document and notify.** Record time, symptoms, glucose values, treatment, and tell the person's clinician if episodes recur.
steps.expect: follow-up information is available.

recipes.verification: The person is alert, able to swallow, symptoms are improving, and glucose is above the low threshold or emergency help has been activated.

recipes.title: recognize stroke signs
recipes.name: recognize-stroke-signs
recipes.goal: Possible stroke signs are recognized quickly, emergency services are called immediately, and the time symptoms began is recorded.

steps.action: **Check scene safety.** Make sure you can approach and speak with the person without danger.
steps.expect: you can focus on symptoms without creating another emergency.

steps.action: **Test face.** Ask the person to smile and look for one side drooping or not moving normally.
steps.expect: facial asymmetry is noticed quickly.

steps.action: **Test arms.** Ask them to raise both arms and watch for one arm drifting down or failing to lift.
steps.expect: one-sided weakness is identified if present.

steps.action: **Test speech.** Ask them to repeat a simple sentence and listen for slurring, wrong words, or inability to speak.
steps.expect: speech change is recognized without arguing about cause.

steps.action: **Act on time.** [BRANCH: any FAST sign | no FAST sign but sudden neurologic symptom] call emergency services now if any sign is present or symptoms are sudden and concerning.
steps.expect: EMS activation is not delayed.

steps.action: **Note symptom timing.** Ask when the person was last known well and when symptoms were first noticed.
steps.expect: a specific clock time or best estimate is available for responders.

steps.action: **Keep them resting.** Have the person sit or lie safely with the head and shoulders slightly raised if comfortable.
steps.expect: they are protected from falls while waiting.

steps.action: **Give nothing by mouth.** Do not offer food, drink, or pills because swallowing may be unsafe.
steps.expect: choking risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Monitor breathing and alertness.** Recheck responsiveness and breathing until help arrives.
steps.expect: any deterioration is noticed and reported.

steps.action: **Prepare information.** Gather medication list, allergies, known medical problems, and witness contact information if available.
steps.expect: responders receive useful context quickly.

recipes.verification: Emergency services have been called, the last-known-well time is recorded or estimated, and the person receives no food or drink while being monitored.

recipes.title: refill a prescription
recipes.name: refill-a-prescription
recipes.goal: An ongoing medication is refilled *before* the current supply runs out, picked up or delivered, and verified to be the right drug at the right dose.

steps.action: **Read the label for the two numbers that decide everything.** Refills remaining, and the prescription's validity/date. [BRANCH: refills > 0 and in-date → pharmacy path (step 2) | refills exhausted or expired → prescriber path (step 3)]
steps.expect: you know which path you're on before contacting anyone.

steps.action: **Pharmacy path: request the refill.** Pharmacy app/website with the Rx number, the phone line's refill option, or in person. State/enter the Rx number and confirm pickup vs delivery.
steps.expect: an acknowledged request with a ready-by time (hours to a day, typically). Skip to step 5.

steps.action: **Prescriber path: request a renewal.** Message the prescriber's practice (portal or phone): medication, dose, pharmacy on file, and a line on how it's going ("stable on this dose"). Many systems let the *pharmacy* initiate this request for you — asking them first can be the faster door.
steps.expect: renewal sent to the pharmacy within the practice's stated turnaround (often 1–3 working days — hence the 5–7 day buffer).

steps.action: **Confirm the renewal landed as a fillable prescription.** Pharmacy notifies, or you check the app after the turnaround.
steps.expect: the pharmacy now shows it fillable; you're on the step-2 path to a ready-by time.

steps.action: **Collect or receive.** Pickup: ID (and payment where applicable) at the counter — some medication classes require signature/ID by law. Delivery: someone present if signature-required.
steps.expect: a labeled bag/bottle handed over or delivered.

steps.action: **Verify before first dose.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* taking the wrong drug/dose — check the label against your last bottle: drug name, strength, dosing instructions, your name. Generic substitutions change the pill's *look* legitimately — the label, not the color, is the truth; ask the pharmacist to confirm any surprise.
steps.expect: label matches (or the pharmacist explained the substitution); questions about interactions/changes answered at the counter, which is free expertise.

steps.action: **Set the next-refill trigger.** Calendar note at supply-minus-a-week, or enroll in the pharmacy's auto-refill/reminder program for stable long-term meds.
steps.expect: future refills start themselves; this recipe stops requiring memory.

recipes.verification: The medication in hand matches your regimen (name, strength, instructions, your name on the label), supply runs past the next renewal horizon, refills-remaining is known, and a trigger (calendar or auto-refill) exists so the next cycle starts before the buffer.

recipes.title: remove a tick
recipes.name: remove-a-tick
recipes.goal: A tick is removed intact as soon as possible, the bite site is cleaned, and symptoms that need medical care are monitored.

steps.action: **Wash your hands.** Clean hands with soap and water before touching the bite area.
steps.expect: hands are clean before removal.

steps.action: **Expose the tick.** Move hair or clothing aside and steady the skin.
steps.expect: the tick and where it enters the skin are clearly visible.

steps.action: **Grip close to the skin.** Place fine tweezers around the tick as close to the skin surface as possible.
steps.expect: the tweezers hold the tick near the mouthparts, not the swollen body.

steps.action: **Pull steadily upward.** Use even pressure without twisting, jerking, squeezing, burning, or coating the tick.
steps.expect: the tick releases from the skin.

steps.action: **Check the bite site.** Look for any remaining dark mouthpart fragments at the surface.
steps.expect: no large attached tick body remains.

steps.action: **Clean the area.** Wash with soap and water, then apply antiseptic if available.
steps.expect: the bite site is clean.

steps.action: **Save the tick.** Put it in a sealed bag or container with the date and bite location.
steps.expect: the tick can be identified later if symptoms develop.

steps.action: **Record exposure.** Note where and when the bite likely happened and how long the tick may have been attached.
steps.expect: a clinician could assess risk if needed.

steps.action: **Monitor symptoms.** Watch for expanding rash, fever, chills, headache, muscle aches, joint pain, or unusual fatigue for several weeks.
steps.expect: concerning symptoms are noticed early.

steps.action: **Avoid unsafe methods.** Do not twist, crush, burn, use petroleum jelly, nail polish, or alcohol to make it detach.
steps.expect: removal is mechanical and prompt.

recipes.verification: The tick is removed or contained, the bite site is cleaned, and symptom monitoring details are recorded.

recipes.title: respond to an opioid overdose with naloxone
recipes.name: respond-to-an-opioid-overdose-with-naloxone
recipes.goal: A suspected opioid overdose is treated with naloxone, emergency services are called, and breathing is supported until help arrives.

steps.action: **Check responsiveness and breathing.** Shout their name if known, tap firmly, and look for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
steps.expect: overdose severity is recognized quickly.

steps.action: **Call emergency services.** Put the phone on speaker and say the person is unresponsive or may have overdosed.
steps.expect: dispatch is connected and guiding you.

steps.action: **Give naloxone.** Use nasal spray or injector exactly as labeled. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once given, naloxone cannot be retrieved; confirm suspected opioid overdose or unresponsiveness with poor breathing first.
steps.expect: a full dose is delivered.

steps.action: **Start rescue breathing or CPR as directed.** If not breathing normally, follow dispatcher instructions for rescue breaths and chest compressions.
steps.expect: oxygen support begins while naloxone takes effect.

steps.action: **Place in recovery position if breathing.** If they breathe normally but are not fully awake, roll them on their side.
steps.expect: the airway is more protected from vomit.

steps.action: **Watch for response.** Note the time naloxone was given and monitor breathing, color, and alertness.
steps.expect: any improvement or continued danger is tracked.

steps.action: **Give another dose if needed.** If there is no response in 2-3 minutes or breathing worsens again, give another naloxone dose if available.
steps.expect: additional reversal is attempted without stopping breathing support.

steps.action: **Keep them from using more opioids.** If they wake agitated or in withdrawal, explain naloxone may wear off and help is coming.
steps.expect: repeat overdose risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Collect information for responders.** Save empty naloxone packages, timing, substances if known, and medication details without handling dangerous items.
steps.expect: responders get useful facts.

steps.action: **Stay until responders arrive.** Continue monitoring because naloxone can wear off before opioids do.
steps.expect: recurrent breathing failure is noticed.

recipes.verification: Emergency services have been called, naloxone was administered with time noted, breathing is supported or normal, and the person remains monitored until professional responders take over.

recipes.title: see a dentist for a checkup
recipes.name: see-a-dentist-for-a-checkup
recipes.goal: You attend a routine dental checkup and cleaning, understand what the dentist found, and leave with a clear, prioritized plan for any follow-up treatment.

steps.action: **Book on the right cadence.** Call or use the practice's portal and ask for a checkup plus cleaning (a "recall" or "scale and polish"). If it has been well over a year, say so; they may allow extra time.
steps.expect: an appointment booked, with cleaning included in the same visit where the practice offers it.

steps.action: **Confirm coverage before the visit.** Ask whether the practice is in-network / accepts your plan, what the checkup and cleaning cost, and what your share is. Note any annual limit.
steps.expect: a clear price and coverage picture, no billing surprise at the desk.

steps.action: **Prepare and arrive.** Brush and floss beforehand (do not overbrush the gums raw), bring ID, plan details, and a list of symptoms and current medications. Arrive early for any new-patient paperwork.
steps.expect: checked in on time with your symptom list ready.

steps.action: **Have the examination.** The dentist checks teeth, gums, bite, and does an oral cancer soft-tissue check; X-rays may be taken periodically, not every visit.
steps.expect: the dentist describes findings out loud (cavities, gum health, wear); ask them to point to anything on the X-ray or a mirror.

steps.action: **Have the cleaning.** A hygienist or dentist scales tartar, polishes, and may floss and apply fluoride. Mild gum bleeding during scaling is normal, especially if flossing has been sparse.
steps.expect: teeth feel smooth; you are told where your brushing and flossing are missing.

steps.action: **Get the findings and any treatment plan explained.** Ask which items are urgent, which are watch-and-wait, and which are optional or cosmetic. Ask for the plan in writing with costs.
steps.expect: a written treatment plan sorted by priority, with each item's cost and whether it can wait.

steps.action: **Book follow-ups and set the next recall.** Schedule any needed treatment (filling, deeper cleaning) and book or note your next routine checkup before leaving.
steps.expect: follow-up treatment scheduled and the next recall date captured so it does not slip.

recipes.verification: The checkup and cleaning are done, you can state what the dentist found and which follow-up items are urgent vs. optional, you have the plan and costs in writing, and your next recall date is set.

recipes.title: spot dehydration
recipes.name: spot-dehydration
recipes.goal: Possible dehydration is recognized early, mild fluid loss is corrected, and severe signs are escalated.

steps.action: **Check recent losses.** Ask about vomiting, diarrhea, fever, sweating, heat exposure, alcohol, or hard exercise.
steps.expect: a likely fluid-loss trigger is known.

steps.action: **Look for early signs.** Notice thirst, dry mouth, headache, dizziness, fatigue, or reduced sweating.
steps.expect: mild dehydration signs are identified.

steps.action: **Check urine.** Look for dark yellow urine, strong smell, or fewer trips to urinate.
steps.expect: urine gives a hydration clue.

steps.action: **Assess high-risk people.** Treat infants, older adults, pregnant people, and people with chronic illness as higher risk.
steps.expect: vulnerable people are not managed casually.

steps.action: **Start rehydration.** Sip water or oral rehydration solution steadily rather than chugging.
steps.expect: fluids are tolerated.

steps.action: **Replace salts when needed.** Use oral rehydration solution, broth, or electrolyte drink after heavy sweating, vomiting, or diarrhea.
steps.expect: salt loss is addressed.

steps.action: **Rest and cool down.** Move to shade or a cool room and reduce activity.
steps.expect: sweating and heat stress decrease.

steps.action: **Avoid dehydrating choices.** Pause alcohol and limit very sugary drinks if they worsen stomach symptoms.
steps.expect: fluid loss is not aggravated.

steps.action: **Recheck after 30 to 60 minutes.** Look again at dizziness, thirst, urine, alertness, and ability to drink.
steps.expect: symptoms are improving or a care decision is clear.

steps.action: **Escalate severe signs.** Seek care for confusion, fainting, no urination, severe weakness, or inability to keep fluids down.
steps.expect: dangerous dehydration is not treated only at home.

recipes.verification: The person is drinking and keeping fluids down, urine and alertness are acceptable, and no severe dehydration sign is present.

recipes.title: stop severe bleeding
recipes.name: stop-severe-bleeding
recipes.goal: Life-threatening external bleeding is controlled with direct pressure while emergency services are called.

steps.action: **Check scene safety.** Look for traffic, weapons, electricity, glass, or other hazards before approaching.
steps.expect: you can help without becoming injured.

steps.action: **Call emergency services.** Assign a caller or call on speaker for severe bleeding.
steps.expect: EMS is activated early.

steps.action: **Expose the wound.** Move or cut clothing enough to see the bleeding source, leaving embedded objects in place.
steps.expect: pressure can be applied to the correct spot.

steps.action: **Apply direct pressure.** Press firmly on the wound with gloved hands, gauze, a clean cloth, or clothing.
steps.expect: bleeding slows under steady pressure.

steps.action: **Maintain pressure.** Keep constant firm pressure without peeking repeatedly.
steps.expect: clotting is not disrupted.

steps.action: **Add dressing if soaked.** Place more material on top if blood soaks through, but do not remove the original dressing.
steps.expect: pressure continues over the wound.

steps.action: **Elevate if practical.** Raise the injured limb above heart level only if it does not worsen pain or disturb pressure.
steps.expect: bleeding may slow while direct pressure remains primary.

steps.action: **Use tourniquet for uncontrolled limb bleeding.** Place a commercial tourniquet high and tight above the wound if direct pressure fails or bleeding is immediately life-threatening. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* prolonged tourniquet use can damage tissue; note the time and do not remove it once tightened.
steps.expect: limb bleeding stops or greatly decreases.

steps.action: **Treat for shock.** Have the person lie still, keep them warm, and avoid food or drink.
steps.expect: faintness and chilling are reduced while waiting.

steps.action: **Monitor breathing and responsiveness.** Continue pressure until EMS takes over or you are unable to continue.
steps.expect: changes are noticed and reported.

recipes.verification: Emergency services have been called, firm direct pressure is maintained, soaked dressings are left in place, and any tourniquet time is recorded.

recipes.title: take a temperature correctly
recipes.name: take-a-temperature-correctly
recipes.goal: You take a temperature with the right method for the person, avoid common timing errors, and know when fever needs medical advice.

steps.action: **Choose the method.** [BRANCH: oral | ear | forehead] use oral for cooperative older children and adults, ear with correct fit, or forehead with the device instructions.
steps.expect: the method matches the person and thermometer.

steps.action: **Wait after mouth changes.** For oral readings, wait 15 to 30 minutes after hot or cold drinks, eating, smoking, or chewing gum.
steps.expect: mouth temperature is not distorted.

steps.action: **Clean the thermometer.** Wash or wipe the probe as instructed and add a disposable cover if required.
steps.expect: clean device ready for use.

steps.action: **Take an oral reading.** Place the tip under the tongue, close lips, breathe through the nose, and wait for the beep or required time.
steps.expect: a stable oral temperature displays.

steps.action: **Take an ear reading.** Use the correct probe cover, aim as instructed toward the eardrum, and avoid an ear with pain, drainage, or heavy wax.
steps.expect: a stable ear temperature displays.

steps.action: **Take a forehead reading.** Sweep or hold the sensor exactly as the device directs on dry skin.
steps.expect: a stable forehead temperature displays.

steps.action: **Record method and number.** Write the temperature, time, method, and any fever medicine taken.
steps.expect: the reading can be interpreted later.

steps.action: **Interpret fever.** In many adults, 100.4 F or 38 C or higher is a fever, but method, age, baseline, and symptoms matter.
steps.expect: the number is not interpreted alone.

recipes.verification: A temperature is recorded with method and time, common timing errors were avoided, and age-specific or symptom-based red flags are escalated.

recipes.title: take blood pressure at home
recipes.name: take-blood-pressure-at-home
recipes.goal: A home blood pressure reading is taken under consistent resting conditions, logged accurately, and escalated when readings are concerning.

steps.action: **Prepare the setting.** Sit in a quiet place with the monitor on a table.
steps.expect: the cuff hose can reach the arm without pulling.

steps.action: **Rest first.** Sit quietly for 5 minutes before measuring.
steps.expect: breathing and heart rate feel settled.

steps.action: **Set posture.** Keep back supported, feet flat, legs uncrossed, and arm supported at heart level.
steps.expect: the body feels relaxed and symmetrical.

steps.action: **Place the cuff.** Wrap the cuff on bare upper arm, with the artery mark over the inner arm and lower edge about 2 cm above the elbow.
steps.expect: the cuff is snug enough for two fingertips under the edge.

steps.action: **Stay still and silent.** Press start and do not talk, text, or move during inflation.
steps.expect: the cuff inflates, pauses, and deflates automatically.

steps.action: **Read the numbers.** Note systolic, diastolic, pulse, arm used, date, time, and any symptoms.
steps.expect: the log has a complete entry.

steps.action: **Repeat correctly.** Wait 1 minute and take a second reading.
steps.expect: two readings are available under the same conditions.

steps.action: **Average routine readings.** If tracking for a clinician, average the two readings unless instructed otherwise.
steps.expect: the recorded value reflects repeated measurement, not a single spike.

steps.action: **Respond to concerning values.** [BRANCH: very high with symptoms | very high without symptoms | unusually low with symptoms] follow your clinician's plan or urgent guidance.
steps.expect: abnormal readings are not ignored.

steps.action: **Store the device.** Remove cuff, power off, and keep the log accessible for appointments.
steps.expect: readings can be reviewed later with context.

recipes.verification: Two seated, rested readings are logged with date, time, arm, systolic, diastolic, pulse, and symptom context.

recipes.title: take someones temperature
recipes.name: take-someones-temperature
recipes.goal: A temperature is measured with an age-appropriate digital thermometer method and documented with the site used.

steps.action: **Choose the method.** [BRANCH: infant | child or adult] use rectal for infants when appropriate, oral for cooperative older children and adults, temporal or ear when suitable, and armpit when a rough screen is acceptable.
steps.expect: the site matches age and cooperation.

steps.action: **Read device instructions.** Check how to turn on, place, and wait for the thermometer model.
steps.expect: the device is ready and understood.

steps.action: **Clean the probe.** Wipe with alcohol or wash with soap and lukewarm water, then dry.
steps.expect: the probe is clean before contact.

steps.action: **Prepare the person.** Wait after hot or cold drinks for oral readings, and keep the person still.
steps.expect: the reading is less likely to be distorted.

steps.action: **Take an oral reading.** Place the tip under the tongue toward the back, close lips, and wait for the beep.
steps.expect: the display shows a stable oral temperature.

steps.action: **Take a rectal reading when indicated.** Lubricate the tip, insert only about 1/2 to 1 inch for an infant or as directed, hold the thermometer, and wait for the beep.
steps.expect: the display shows a core temperature without letting go of the device.

steps.action: **Take a temporal or ear reading.** Position exactly as the device instructions say, with a clean forehead path or properly placed ear probe.
steps.expect: the sensor has a clear reading path.

steps.action: **Take an armpit reading.** Place the tip high in a dry armpit, hold the arm snugly against the body, and wait for the beep.
steps.expect: the display shows an axillary temperature.

steps.action: **Record the result.** Write the number, F or C, method, time, symptoms, and medicines given.
steps.expect: the reading can be interpreted later.

steps.action: **Decide on care.** Compare the result and symptoms with age-based medical guidance, and call a clinician or emergency services for red flags.
steps.expect: the number is not interpreted without context.

recipes.verification: The temperature is recorded with units, measurement site, time, symptoms, and escalation decision based on age and red flags.

recipes.title: transfer your medical records
recipes.name: transfer-your-medical-records
recipes.goal: Your medical records are requested from one healthcare organization and sent to the correct recipient, with a copy kept for your own files when possible.

steps.action: **Identify what to transfer.** List visit notes, labs, imaging reports, actual images, vaccine records, medication lists, or billing records.
steps.expect: the request is specific enough to process.

steps.action: **Find the release form.** Use the provider's medical records, health information management, or patient portal release process.
steps.expect: you have the correct authorization form or portal workflow.

steps.action: **Fill in identity details.** Enter your name, date of birth, contact information, and any patient identifier exactly.
steps.expect: the records office can match you.

steps.action: **Specify the recipient.** Add the clinician, organization, fax, mailing address, portal address, or pickup instructions.
steps.expect: the destination is unambiguous.

steps.action: **Choose record scope and dates.** Request only the records needed, and include imaging files separately if relevant.
steps.expect: the release covers the correct material.

steps.action: **Submit with required ID.** Send the signed form through the portal, fax, mail, or in person as instructed.
steps.expect: you receive confirmation or a reference point for follow-up.

steps.action: **Track and keep a copy.** Save the submitted form, confirmation, and any records you receive.
steps.expect: you can prove what was requested and when.

recipes.verification: The receiving office confirms the correct records arrived, and you have saved a copy or confirmation of the transfer request.

recipes.title: treat a bee or wasp sting
recipes.name: treat-a-bee-or-wasp-sting
recipes.goal: A bee or wasp sting is treated for local pain and swelling while severe allergy signs are recognized quickly.

steps.action: **Move away.** Leave the area calmly to avoid more stings.
steps.expect: no additional insects are nearby.

steps.action: **Check for anaphylaxis.** Look for breathing trouble, throat tightness, widespread hives, faintness, or facial swelling.
steps.expect: emergency symptoms are recognized before local care.

steps.action: **Scrape out a bee stinger.** Use a fingernail or card edge to scrape sideways across the skin.
steps.expect: a visible stinger is removed without squeezing the venom sac.

steps.action: **Clean the sting.** Wash the area with soap and water.
steps.expect: the skin is clean.

steps.action: **Apply cold.** Wrap ice or a cold pack in cloth and hold it on the area for 10 minutes at a time.
steps.expect: pain and swelling begin to ease.

steps.action: **Raise the area.** Elevate the limb if the sting is on an arm or leg.
steps.expect: swelling feels less tight.

steps.action: **Consider antihistamine.** Use an age-appropriate antihistamine only if the label allows it and the person can take it safely.
steps.expect: itching is addressed without unsafe dosing.

steps.action: **Use pain relief carefully.** Take an appropriate over-the-counter pain reliever if tolerated and allowed by the label.
steps.expect: pain is manageable.

steps.action: **Do not scratch.** Keep nails away and cover lightly if needed.
steps.expect: skin is not opened by scratching.

steps.action: **Monitor for delayed symptoms.** Watch for spreading swelling, infection signs, or allergic symptoms over the next several hours.
steps.expect: worsening symptoms lead to care.

recipes.verification: The stinger is removed if present, the site is clean and cooling, symptoms are localized, and no anaphylaxis sign is present.

recipes.title: treat a burn
recipes.name: treat-a-burn
recipes.goal: A minor burn is cooled, protected, and escalated for medical care when the burn may be serious.

steps.action: **Stop the burning.** Move the person away from the heat source, turn off power if electrical, or remove them from smoke if safe.
steps.expect: no ongoing heat or exposure is injuring the skin.

steps.action: **Call for serious burns.** [BRANCH: serious burn signs | small superficial burn] call emergency services now for serious signs; continue first aid while waiting.
steps.expect: urgent care is activated when needed.

steps.action: **Cool the burn.** Hold the burned area under cool running water for 20 minutes, starting as soon as possible.
steps.expect: pain and heat begin to reduce.

steps.action: **Protect from chilling.** Cool the burn area, not the whole body, and keep the rest of the person warm.
steps.expect: the person is not shivering or becoming cold.

steps.action: **Remove tight items.** Remove rings, watches, belts, or tight clothing near the burn unless stuck to skin.
steps.expect: swelling will not trap jewelry or fabric.

steps.action: **Leave stuck material alone.** Do not pull off clothing or objects attached to burned skin.
steps.expect: deeper tissue is not torn.

steps.action: **Cover loosely.** Use a sterile nonstick dressing, clean cloth, or clean plastic wrap laid loosely over the burn.
steps.expect: the burn is protected without pressure or sticking.

steps.action: **Avoid home substances.** Do not apply ice, butter, oils, toothpaste, or creams unless a clinician instructs you.
steps.expect: heat is not trapped and skin is not damaged further.

steps.action: **Reassess severity.** Look for blistering, white or charred skin, numbness, spreading redness, severe pain, or burns crossing joints.
steps.expect: the need for medical care is reconsidered.

steps.action: **Arrange follow-up.** Seek urgent care if pain is severe, the burn is worsening, tetanus status is uncertain, or infection signs appear.
steps.expect: the burn is not left unmanaged.

recipes.verification: The burn has been cooled for 20 minutes, covered loosely with a clean nonstick barrier, and serious burn criteria have been checked for escalation.

recipes.title: treat a chemical splash in the eye
recipes.name: treat-a-chemical-splash-in-the-eye
recipes.goal: A chemical eye exposure is flushed immediately and escalated to poison control or emergency services without delay.

steps.action: **Start irrigation immediately.** Hold the affected eye open under clean running water, shower, eyewash station, or poured saline.
steps.expect: water flows across the eye and away from the other eye when possible.

steps.action: **Remove contaminated items.** Take off contaminated gloves, glasses, or clothing near the face while flushing continues.
steps.expect: chemical transfer to the eye is reduced.

steps.action: **Hold eyelids open.** Use clean fingers to keep lids apart and ask the person to roll the eye around.
steps.expect: water reaches under both lids.

steps.action: **Remove contacts if easy.** Let contact lenses wash out or remove them gently only if they do not stick.
steps.expect: irrigation continues without scraping the eye.

steps.action: **Flush for at least 15 minutes.** Continue longer for strong acids, alkalis, unknown chemicals, or dispatcher instructions.
steps.expect: dilution is sustained long enough to reduce injury.

steps.action: **Call for expert help while flushing.** Ask someone to call poison control or emergency services and read the product label or safety data sheet.
steps.expect: guidance is obtained without stopping irrigation.

steps.action: **Avoid neutralizers or drops.** Do not put other chemicals, ointment, or medicated drops in the eye unless instructed by a professional.
steps.expect: no secondary reaction is created.

steps.action: **Cover lightly after flushing.** If transport is needed, place a clean loose shield or cloth over the eye without pressure.
steps.expect: the eye is protected but not compressed.

steps.action: **Bring chemical information.** Take the container, label, or photo if safe to do so.
steps.expect: clinicians can identify the exposure.

steps.action: **Get urgent evaluation.** Go to emergency care or follow poison control instructions after significant exposure.
steps.expect: corneal damage is assessed promptly.

recipes.verification: The eye was flushed continuously for at least 15 minutes, poison control or emergency services were contacted for significant exposure or red flags, and urgent evaluation is arranged when indicated.

recipes.title: treat a dog or animal bite
recipes.name: treat-a-dog-or-animal-bite
recipes.goal: An animal bite is cleaned, bleeding is controlled, and urgent care is arranged for infection, rabies, tetanus, or severe injury risk.

steps.action: **Get away from the animal.** Move to a secure area and prevent further bites without chasing or handling the animal.
steps.expect: the attack has stopped.

steps.action: **Control severe bleeding.** Apply firm direct pressure with clean cloth or dressing.
steps.expect: bleeding slows while help is contacted if severe.

steps.action: **Call emergency services for major injury.** Report bite location, bleeding, and animal danger if severe signs are present.
steps.expect: emergency response is activated when needed.

steps.action: **Wash the wound.** Rinse under running water with soap for several minutes if bleeding is controlled.
steps.expect: saliva and debris are reduced.

steps.action: **Remove loose debris.** Let water flush away dirt; do not dig deeply into the wound.
steps.expect: cleaning does not worsen tissue damage.

steps.action: **Cover with a clean dressing.** Pat around the wound dry and cover lightly.
steps.expect: the wound is protected while awaiting care.

steps.action: **Gather animal details.** Record animal type, owner contact, rabies vaccine status, location, and whether the animal can be observed.
steps.expect: rabies risk assessment has useful facts.

steps.action: **Check tetanus status.** Note when the injured person last had a tetanus shot if known.
steps.expect: clinicians can decide on booster needs.

steps.action: **Contact medical care.** [BRANCH: skin broken or high-risk bite | superficial no-break scratch] seek urgent care for broken skin or high-risk exposures; monitor superficial no-break scratches.
steps.expect: infection and rabies prevention are considered.

steps.action: **Watch for infection.** Monitor redness, swelling, pus, fever, red streaks, worsening pain, or reduced movement.
steps.expect: delayed infection is caught early.

recipes.verification: Bleeding is controlled, the wound is washed and covered, animal and tetanus details are recorded if available, and medical or emergency help is contacted for any broken-skin or high-risk bite.

recipes.title: treat a jellyfish sting
recipes.name: treat-a-jellyfish-sting
recipes.goal: A jellyfish sting is rinsed safely, tentacle material is removed, pain is reduced, and serious reactions are escalated.

steps.action: **Move to safety.** Help the person leave the water and sit or lie down away from surf.
