steps.expect: there is no continued exposure to jellyfish or drowning risk.

steps.action: **Assess urgent symptoms.** Check breathing, alertness, chest pain, severe weakness, and widespread swelling.
steps.expect: emergency symptoms are identified immediately.

steps.action: **Rinse with seawater.** Flush the sting with seawater to remove loose tentacle material.
steps.expect: sand and loose fragments wash away.

steps.action: **Use vinegar when appropriate.** [BRANCH: vinegar advised locally | vinegar not advised locally] apply vinegar if lifeguard or local guidance recommends it, otherwise continue seawater rinsing.
steps.expect: stinging cells are not triggered by fresh water.

steps.action: **Avoid fresh water.** Do not rinse with tap water, ice directly, urine, alcohol, or vigorous rubbing.
steps.expect: the sting is not aggravated by common irritants.

steps.action: **Remove tentacles.** Use tweezers, a gloved hand, or a plastic edge to lift visible tentacles from the skin.
steps.expect: no visible tentacle strands remain.

steps.action: **Soak in hot water.** Immerse or shower the area in hot but not scalding water for 20 to 45 minutes.
steps.expect: pain begins to ease without burning the skin.

steps.action: **Protect the skin.** Pat dry and cover lightly if clothing will rub the area.
steps.expect: the area is protected from friction.

steps.action: **Monitor the person.** Watch for worsening pain, spreading swelling, vomiting, dizziness, trouble breathing, or confusion.
steps.expect: serious progression triggers medical care.

steps.action: **Document the location.** Note beach, time, and any lifeguard advice.
steps.expect: details are available if symptoms require care.

recipes.verification: The person is out of danger, visible tentacles are removed, pain is improving, and no emergency symptom is present.

recipes.title: treat a knocked out tooth
recipes.name: treat-a-knocked-out-tooth
recipes.goal: A knocked-out permanent tooth is handled by the crown, kept moist, and taken to urgent dental care quickly.

steps.action: **Check for serious injury.** Look for airway trouble, heavy bleeding, confusion, vomiting, neck pain, or loss of consciousness.
steps.expect: life-threatening trauma is addressed first.

steps.action: **Find the tooth.** Pick it up by the white crown and avoid touching the root.
steps.expect: delicate root cells are protected.

steps.action: **Rinse only if dirty.** Briefly rinse with milk or clean water without scrubbing, soap, alcohol, or scraping.
steps.expect: visible dirt is removed while root tissue remains intact.

steps.action: **Decide if it is permanent.** [BRANCH: permanent tooth | baby tooth or unsure] reinsert only a permanent tooth if the person is alert and cooperative; store baby teeth or uncertain teeth moist.
steps.expect: a baby tooth is not forced into the socket.

steps.action: **Reinsert if appropriate.** Place the permanent tooth gently back into the socket facing the correct way.
steps.expect: the tooth sits near its normal position.

steps.action: **Hold in place.** Ask the person to bite gently on clean gauze or cloth.
steps.expect: the tooth stays seated without hard chewing.

steps.action: **Store moist if not reinserted.** Put the tooth in milk, tooth preservation solution, or inside the person's cheek if safe and they are old enough not to swallow it.
steps.expect: the tooth root stays wet.

steps.action: **Control mouth bleeding.** Apply gentle pressure with clean gauze or cloth.
steps.expect: bleeding slows without disturbing the tooth.

steps.action: **Call a dentist or emergency dental clinic.** Say a permanent tooth was avulsed and ask for immediate care.
steps.expect: urgent dental treatment is arranged.

steps.action: **Go promptly.** Bring the tooth, timing, and injury details to dental or emergency care.
steps.expect: reimplantation or stabilization can happen as soon as possible.

recipes.verification: Serious injuries have been screened, the tooth is reinserted or stored moist, bleeding is controlled, and urgent dental care is underway with the time of injury known.

recipes.title: treat a nosebleed
recipes.name: treat-a-nosebleed
recipes.goal: A typical nosebleed is slowed and stopped by leaning forward, pinching the soft part of the nose, and recognizing when medical care is needed.

steps.action: **Sit upright.** Keep the head above the heart and stay calm.
steps.expect: blood pressure in the nose is not increased by lying down.

steps.action: **Lean forward, not back.** Let blood drain out of the nose or mouth instead of swallowing it.
steps.expect: blood does not run down the throat.

steps.action: **Blow gently once if needed.** Clear large clots only at the start, then stop disturbing the nose.
steps.expect: nostrils are clear enough to pinch.

steps.action: **Pinch the soft part.** Use thumb and finger below the bony bridge, pressing both nostrils closed.
steps.expect: pressure is on the fleshy lower nose, not the hard bridge.

steps.action: **Hold for 10-15 minutes continuously.** Use a timer and do not peek.
steps.expect: steady pressure gives a clot time to form.

steps.action: **Breathe through the mouth.** Spit blood into a tissue if it reaches the mouth.
steps.expect: less blood is swallowed and nausea risk drops.

steps.action: **Check once when time ends.** Release pressure gently after the full interval.
steps.expect: bleeding has stopped or clearly slowed.

steps.action: **Repeat one more cycle if needed.** Pinch again for another 10-15 minutes.
steps.expect: most simple nosebleeds stop by the second cycle.

steps.action: **Avoid restarting the bleed.** Do not blow, pick, strain, or bend low for several hours.
steps.expect: clot remains undisturbed.

steps.action: **Seek care when warning signs appear.** Call emergency services for heavy bleeding, trouble breathing, fainting, major injury, or bleeding that will not stop.
steps.expect: dangerous cases are escalated promptly.

recipes.verification: Bleeding has stopped after continuous soft-nose pressure, the person is upright and breathing comfortably, and no warning sign requiring urgent care is present.

recipes.title: treat a scald or hot liquid burn
recipes.name: treat-a-scald-or-hot-liquid-burn
recipes.goal: A hot liquid burn is cooled promptly, protected cleanly, and escalated for medical care when severity or location requires it.

steps.action: **Move away from heat.** Get the person away from the hot liquid, steam, stove, kettle, or spill.
steps.expect: burning exposure has stopped.

steps.action: **Remove wet hot items.** Carefully remove hot wet clothing, jewelry, diapers, or watches unless stuck to skin.
steps.expect: retained heat and swelling risk are reduced.

steps.action: **Cool with running water.** Hold the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes as soon as possible.
steps.expect: pain and tissue heating decrease.

steps.action: **Protect from chilling.** Keep the rest of the person warm while cooling only the burn.
steps.expect: hypothermia risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Assess severity.** Look for size, location, blistering, white or charred skin, numbness, and breathing symptoms.
steps.expect: red flags are identified.

steps.action: **Call for help when indicated.** [BRANCH: red flags present | minor burn] call emergency services for severe burns; arrange medical advice for uncertain burns.
steps.expect: serious burns are escalated.

steps.action: **Cover loosely.** After cooling, cover with clean non-stick dressing or plastic wrap laid loosely, not wrapped tightly.
steps.expect: the burn is protected from contamination.

steps.action: **Do not burst blisters.** Leave blisters intact and avoid peeling skin.
steps.expect: infection protection remains intact.

steps.action: **Use simple pain relief if safe.** Offer age-appropriate over-the-counter pain medicine only if the person can take it safely.
steps.expect: pain is addressed without unsafe dosing.

steps.action: **Monitor for shock.** Watch for pale clammy skin, faintness, confusion, or worsening pain while awaiting care.
steps.expect: deterioration is caught early.

recipes.verification: The burn source is removed, the burn was cooled with running water for 20 minutes, severe-burn criteria were checked, medical help was called when indicated, and the burn is loosely covered.

recipes.title: treat a sprained ankle
recipes.name: treat-a-sprained-ankle
recipes.goal: A likely mild ankle sprain is protected, swelling is limited, and fracture red flags are identified for medical evaluation.

steps.action: **Stop activity.** Have the person sit or lie down and avoid putting weight on the injured ankle.
steps.expect: pain is not worsened by continued use.

steps.action: **Check for emergency signs.** Look for obvious deformity, open wound, numbness, blue or cold foot, or severe uncontrolled pain.
steps.expect: urgent injuries are separated from routine sprains.

steps.action: **Remove constricting items.** Loosen shoe laces and remove tight footwear or ankle jewelry if this can be done gently.
steps.expect: swelling will not trap tight material.

steps.action: **Rest the ankle.** Keep weight off the ankle and use support when moving.
steps.expect: the joint is protected from further injury.

steps.action: **Ice the area.** Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15 to 20 minutes at a time.
steps.expect: pain and swelling begin to settle without freezing the skin.

steps.action: **Compress lightly.** Wrap with an elastic bandage from toes upward, snug but not tight.
steps.expect: swelling is supported while toes stay warm and pink.

steps.action: **Elevate the ankle.** Raise the ankle above heart level when possible.
steps.expect: swelling drains away from the foot.

steps.action: **Check weight bearing.** [BRANCH: can take four steps | cannot take four steps] try only gentle standing if safe; stop if pain is sharp or unstable.
steps.expect: walking ability is assessed without forcing it.

steps.action: **Screen for x-ray red flags.** Check for bony tenderness at either ankle bone, the base of the fifth metatarsal, or the navicular area on top of the midfoot.
steps.expect: Ottawa-style warning signs are noted.

steps.action: **Plan recovery.** Arrange medical care for red flags, or begin gentle range of motion after pain allows and follow up if not improving in 5 to 7 days.
steps.expect: recovery has a safe next step.

recipes.verification: The ankle is rested, iced with a skin barrier, lightly compressed, elevated, and checked for inability to take four steps or focal bone tenderness.

recipes.title: treat frostbite
recipes.name: treat-frostbite
recipes.goal: Suspected frostbite is protected from refreezing, rewarmed safely when appropriate, and escalated for urgent medical care.

steps.action: **Move to warmth.** Get the person indoors, into a vehicle, tent, or sheltered place out of wind and cold.
steps.expect: ongoing freezing exposure stops.

steps.action: **Check for hypothermia.** Look for confusion, slurred speech, severe shivering, drowsiness, or clumsiness.
steps.expect: life-threatening cold illness is recognized.

steps.action: **Call emergency services for red flags.** Contact help if hypothermia, severe frostbite, blistering, or evacuation difficulty is present.
steps.expect: professional help is being arranged.

steps.action: **Remove constricting items.** Take off wet gloves, boots, socks, rings, watches, and tight clothing gently.
steps.expect: swelling will not be trapped by tight items.

steps.action: **Protect the area.** Cover loosely with clean dry cloth and separate fingers or toes with gauze if available.
steps.expect: skin is protected from pressure and rubbing.

steps.action: **Decide whether rewarming is safe.** [BRANCH: no refreezing risk | possible refreezing] rewarm only if the area can stay warm afterward; otherwise keep it protected.
steps.expect: tissue is not thawed and frozen again.

steps.action: **Rewarm in warm water.** Immerse the part in warm, not hot, water for 15-30 minutes if safe to rewarm.
steps.expect: skin softens and color may return while pain increases.

steps.action: **Avoid direct heat.** Keep the part away from fires, heaters, heating pads, stoves, and hot water.
steps.expect: numb skin is not burned.

steps.action: **Do not break blisters.** Leave blisters intact and cover loosely.
steps.expect: infection risk is reduced.

steps.action: **Keep warm during transport.** Elevate if practical, avoid walking on affected feet, and continue medical evaluation.
steps.expect: injury is protected until care takes over.

recipes.verification: The person is out of cold exposure, the affected area is protected from rubbing and refreezing, emergency services or urgent care is involved for red flags, and rewarming was done only when the area can stay warm.

recipes.title: treat heat exhaustion
recipes.name: treat-heat-exhaustion
recipes.goal: Heat exhaustion is treated early by cooling and hydration, and heat stroke warning signs trigger emergency services.

steps.action: **Stop heat exposure.** Move the person to shade, air conditioning, or the coolest available place.
steps.expect: heat gain from the environment decreases.

steps.action: **Have them rest.** Sit or lie them down and stop physical activity.
steps.expect: exertion no longer adds heat load.

steps.action: **Check mental status.** Ask simple questions and look for confusion, slurred speech, agitation, seizure, or loss of consciousness.
steps.expect: heat stroke signs are identified quickly.

steps.action: **Call for heat stroke signs.** [BRANCH: altered mental state | alert and sweating] call emergency services immediately if mental status is abnormal; continue cooling while waiting.
steps.expect: life-threatening heat illness is escalated.

steps.action: **Remove excess clothing.** Loosen or remove unnecessary layers, shoes, pads, or gear.
steps.expect: skin can release heat more effectively.

steps.action: **Cool the body.** Apply cool wet cloths, mist with water, fan the person, or use cool packs at neck, armpits, and groin.
steps.expect: skin temperature begins to drop.

steps.action: **Give small sips.** Offer cool water or an electrolyte drink if they are alert and can swallow.
steps.expect: fluid is taken without choking or vomiting.

steps.action: **Keep cooling for 15 minutes.** Continue active cooling and reassess symptoms.
steps.expect: dizziness, weakness, nausea, or cramps improve.

steps.action: **Escalate if not improving.** Seek urgent medical care if symptoms persist, worsen, or return after cooling.
steps.expect: heat exhaustion does not progress unnoticed.

steps.action: **Avoid return to heat.** Keep the person out of strenuous activity and heat for the rest of the day.
steps.expect: relapse risk is reduced.

recipes.verification: The person is in a cool place, activity has stopped, cooling is underway, fluids are given only if safe, and emergency services are called for any altered mental state.

recipes.title: treat mild hypothermia
recipes.name: treat-mild-hypothermia
recipes.goal: Mild hypothermia is recognized and treated with gentle warming while severe symptoms trigger emergency services.

steps.action: **Get out of cold exposure.** Move the person to shelter, a warm room, a vehicle, or a wind-protected area.
steps.expect: wind, wet, and cold exposure are reduced.

steps.action: **Call for severe signs.** [BRANCH: alert and shivering | confused or very drowsy] call emergency services if mental status is abnormal, shivering stops, or breathing is concerning.
steps.expect: severe hypothermia is escalated immediately.

steps.action: **Handle gently.** Keep movements slow and avoid unnecessary walking or jostling.
steps.expect: the person stays calm and stable.

steps.action: **Remove wet clothing.** Cut away clothing if needed to avoid rough movement, and dry the skin gently.
steps.expect: evaporative cooling stops.

steps.action: **Add dry insulation.** Wrap in blankets, coats, sleeping bags, or dry layers, including the head and neck.
steps.expect: body heat is retained.

steps.action: **Warm the core first.** Place warm packs wrapped in cloth on the chest, armpits, or groin if available.
steps.expect: warming targets major blood vessels without burning skin.

steps.action: **Share body heat if needed.** Use skin-to-skin core warming under dry blankets only when appropriate and privacy can be protected.
steps.expect: gentle warmth increases without direct heat injury.

steps.action: **Offer warm drinks if safe.** Give small sips of warm sweet nonalcoholic fluid only if fully alert.
steps.expect: the person swallows safely and receives warmth and energy.

steps.action: **Monitor breathing and alertness.** Recheck frequently and be ready for CPR if they stop breathing normally.
steps.expect: deterioration is noticed.

steps.action: **Continue gradual rewarming.** Keep the person dry, insulated, and resting until fully recovered or care arrives.
steps.expect: shivering and alertness improve without overheating.

recipes.verification: The person is dry, insulated, handled gently, warmed gradually, given fluids only if alert, and emergency services are called for severe signs.

recipes.title: treat swimmers ear
recipes.name: treat-swimmers-ear
recipes.goal: An irritated outer ear canal after water exposure is kept dry, protected from further trauma, and escalated when infection signs need a clinician.

steps.action: **Stop water exposure.** Stay out of swimming and keep shower water out of the ear until symptoms settle.
steps.expect: the ear is no longer being re-wetted.

steps.action: **Dry the outer ear.** Tilt the head, let water drain, and dry only the outside with a towel.
steps.expect: visible outer ear moisture is gone.

steps.action: **Do not insert cotton buds.** Keep cotton swabs, earbuds, hair pins, and fingers out of the canal.
steps.expect: no added scratches or packed wax.

steps.action: **Use drops only when appropriate.** [BRANCH: clinician-prescribed drops | no prescription] use prescribed ear drops as directed, or ask a pharmacist or clinician before using drying drops if you might have eardrum damage.
steps.expect: drops are used only when safe for your ear history.

steps.action: **Place drops correctly.** Lie with the affected ear up, add the directed number of drops, and stay there for a few minutes.
steps.expect: drops reach the canal instead of running out.

steps.action: **Manage mild pain.** Use an over-the-counter pain reliever you can take safely.
steps.expect: discomfort is reduced enough to rest.

steps.action: **Avoid ear devices.** Skip earbuds, earplugs, and hearing aids in that ear if they worsen pain, unless medically necessary.
steps.expect: less rubbing inside the canal.

steps.action: **Watch the next 24 to 48 hours.** Track pain, hearing, discharge, and fever.
steps.expect: mild irritation improves rather than worsens.

recipes.verification: The ear canal is kept dry, nothing is inserted into it, drops are used only when safe, and pain or discharge thresholds trigger medical care.

recipes.title: use a home blood glucose meter
recipes.name: use-a-home-blood-glucose-meter
recipes.goal: A home blood glucose reading is taken with clean technique, logged with context, and followed up according to the care plan or urgent thresholds.

steps.action: **Wash and dry hands.** Use soap and warm water, then dry fully.
steps.expect: sugar residue and moisture are removed.

steps.action: **Prepare the meter and strip.** Insert a compatible test strip and wait for the blood-drop prompt.
steps.expect: the meter is ready to accept blood.

steps.action: **Load a new lancet.** Place a fresh lancet in the lancing device and set depth as needed.
steps.expect: the device is ready and the needle was not reused.

steps.action: **Lance the side of a fingertip.** Press the device on the side, not the pad center, and trigger it.
steps.expect: a small blood drop forms with less tenderness.

steps.action: **Apply blood to the strip.** Touch the drop to the strip edge or target area as directed by the meter.
steps.expect: the meter begins counting or processing.

steps.action: **Read and log the result.** Record the number, unit, date, time, meal timing, medication, exercise, and symptoms.
steps.expect: the reading has enough context to interpret later.

steps.action: **Dispose safely.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* put the used lancet directly into a sharps container and do not recap by hand if unsafe.
steps.expect: the sharp cannot stick anyone.

recipes.verification: The meter displays a result, the value is logged with timing context, and the used lancet is secured in a sharps container.

recipes.title: use a pulse oximeter
recipes.name: use-a-pulse-oximeter
recipes.goal: You obtain a more reliable pulse oximeter reading, understand SpO2 and pulse, and know when low oxygen needs urgent care.

steps.action: **Warm the hand.** Rub hands together or warm them indoors before measuring.
steps.expect: fingers are warm and pink enough for blood flow.

steps.action: **Remove barriers.** Take off dark nail polish, artificial nails, or anything squeezing the finger if possible.
steps.expect: the sensor has a clear path through the nail bed.

steps.action: **Sit still.** Rest the hand at chest level and keep the finger still.
steps.expect: motion does not scramble the signal.

steps.action: **Clip the device on.** Insert the finger fully so the nail faces the display or as the device instructions show.
steps.expect: the oximeter turns on and begins detecting.

steps.action: **Wait for a stable reading.** Give it 30 to 60 seconds until numbers stop jumping.
steps.expect: SpO2 and pulse are steady for several seconds.

steps.action: **Read both numbers.** SpO2 is oxygen saturation percentage; pulse is beats per minute.
steps.expect: you record both values, not just one.

steps.action: **Repeat if surprising.** Try another warm finger and compare with how you feel.
steps.expect: a confirmed reading or a reason to distrust the device.

steps.action: **Interpret cautiously.** Many healthy people read 95% to 100% at sea level; 92% or lower, or a clear drop from your usual, deserves medical advice.
steps.expect: the number is judged with symptoms and baseline.

recipes.verification: A stable SpO2 and pulse are recorded after warm, still measurement, and any low oxygen threshold or serious symptom is escalated.

recipes.title: use a sling
recipes.name: use-a-sling
recipes.goal: An injured arm is supported in a sling while circulation and warning signs are monitored.

steps.action: **Support the arm.** Keep the elbow bent about 90 degrees and the hand slightly higher than the elbow.
steps.expect: the forearm rests comfortably across the chest.

steps.action: **Place the sling under the arm.** [BRANCH: commercial sling | cloth sling] slide the pouch or cloth under the forearm from elbow to hand.
steps.expect: the whole forearm is supported, not just the wrist.

steps.action: **Tie or fasten at the neck.** Bring the ends behind the neck and secure them so the wrist stays supported.
steps.expect: the arm does not sag and the neck is not pinched. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not force a deformed shoulder, elbow, or wrist back into place.

steps.action: **Secure the elbow.** Tuck or pin the sling so the elbow cannot slip backward.
steps.expect: the elbow stays inside the support.

steps.action: **Pad pressure points.** Add a small towel under the neck strap if it rubs or presses.
steps.expect: the neck and shoulder feel supported without sharp pressure.

steps.action: **Check circulation.** Look at finger color and warmth, then ask about numbness or tingling.
steps.expect: fingers are warm, pink, and normally sensitive.

steps.action: **Adjust if needed.** Loosen or retie the sling if fingers swell, turn blue, become cold, or tingle.
steps.expect: circulation symptoms improve after adjustment.

steps.action: **Elevate when resting.** Prop the hand higher than the elbow on pillows when sitting or lying down.
steps.expect: swelling and throbbing are reduced.

steps.action: **Limit use.** Avoid lifting, pushing, pulling, or driving until cleared.
steps.expect: the injured arm stays protected.

recipes.verification: The forearm is supported across the chest with the hand slightly elevated, and fingers remain warm, pink, and normally sensitive.

recipes.title: use a walking cane
recipes.name: use-a-walking-cane
recipes.goal: A walking cane is fitted and used on the correct side to improve balance and reduce strain on a weak or painful leg.

steps.action: **Set the cane height.** Stand tall with the cane tip near the outside of the foot.
steps.expect: the handle lines up with the wrist crease.

steps.action: **Check elbow bend.** Hold the handle with the arm relaxed.
steps.expect: the elbow bends slightly, about 15 to 30 degrees.

steps.action: **Hold it on the strong side.** [BRANCH: weak right leg | weak left leg] hold the cane in the hand opposite the weak or painful leg.
steps.expect: the cane supports the weak side during stepping.

steps.action: **Move cane and weak leg together.** Step the cane forward with the weak leg, then step through with the strong leg.
steps.expect: weight shifts smoothly through cane and strong leg. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not use a cane to avoid evaluation for sudden weakness or stroke symptoms.

steps.action: **Keep steps short.** Place the cane only a comfortable step ahead, not far out in front.
steps.expect: posture stays upright and balanced.

steps.action: **Turn slowly.** Take small steps instead of pivoting on the weak leg.
steps.expect: the cane stays planted during turns.

steps.action: **Use stairs with a rail.** Go up with the strong leg first, then cane and weak leg; go down with cane and weak leg first, then strong leg.
steps.expect: strong-leg-up and weak-leg-down remains consistent.

steps.action: **Inspect the tip.** Check the rubber tip for cracks, wear, or looseness.
steps.expect: the cane grips the floor.

steps.action: **Pause for unsafe symptoms.** Stop for dizziness, chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden weakness.
steps.expect: emergency symptoms are not treated as a balance problem.

recipes.verification: The cane handle reaches the wrist crease, it is held on the strong side, and cane plus weak leg move forward together.

recipes.title: use an epipen
recipes.name: use-an-epipen
recipes.goal: An epinephrine auto-injector is used promptly for suspected anaphylaxis while emergency services are called.

steps.action: **Recognize anaphylaxis.** Look for hives, swelling, breathing trouble, wheeze, throat tightness, hoarse voice, vomiting, dizziness, or collapse after a possible allergen.
steps.expect: a severe allergic reaction is treated as time-critical.

steps.action: **Call emergency services.** Assign a caller or call on speaker before or immediately after giving epinephrine.
steps.expect: EMS is on the way while care continues.

steps.action: **Position the person.** Have them lie flat with legs raised if tolerated; sit upright if breathing is difficult; do not let them stand or walk.
steps.expect: circulation and breathing are supported.

steps.action: **Prepare the EpiPen.** Hold it in your fist with blue safety cap up and orange tip down: blue to sky, orange to thigh.
steps.expect: fingers are away from both ends.

steps.action: **Remove the blue cap.** Pull the safety cap straight off only when ready to inject.
steps.expect: the device is armed and pointed at the outer thigh.

steps.action: **Inject into the thigh.** Press the orange tip firmly into the outer mid-thigh through clothing if needed until it clicks.
steps.expect: the dose starts delivering into the thigh muscle.

steps.action: **Hold in place.** Keep firm pressure for the time listed on the device label, commonly 3 seconds for current EpiPen devices.
steps.expect: the full dose has time to deliver.

steps.action: **Remove and protect.** Lift the device away and keep it for EMS, needle end covered by the device guard.
steps.expect: responders can identify what was given and when.

steps.action: **Monitor for return of symptoms.** If symptoms persist or return and a second prescribed auto-injector is available, give it after about 5 to 15 minutes or as instructed by dispatch.
steps.expect: worsening anaphylaxis is treated promptly.

steps.action: **Prepare for CPR.** If the person becomes unresponsive and is not breathing normally, begin CPR if trained and follow dispatch instructions.
steps.expect: life support starts if anaphylaxis causes collapse.

recipes.verification: Epinephrine has been given into the outer thigh, emergency services have been called, the injection time is noted, and the person is monitored for recurrent symptoms.

recipes.title: use an inhaler
recipes.name: use-an-inhaler
recipes.goal: A metered-dose inhaler is used with correct timing and breathing technique, and urgent help is sought when symptoms do not improve.

steps.action: **Identify the inhaler.** Confirm it is the prescribed medicine and whether it is a reliever or preventer.
steps.expect: the right inhaler is selected for the situation.

steps.action: **Sit upright.** Have the person sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed.
steps.expect: the chest can expand more easily.

steps.action: **Shake the inhaler.** Remove the cap, check the mouthpiece is clear, and shake the inhaler well.
steps.expect: medicine is mixed and the mouthpiece is unobstructed.

steps.action: **Attach spacer if available.** Insert the inhaler into the spacer and keep the spacer level.
steps.expect: medicine will be easier to inhale deeply.

steps.action: **Breathe out first.** Have the person exhale fully away from the inhaler or spacer.
steps.expect: lungs are ready for a slow deep breath in.

steps.action: **Seal lips.** Put lips tightly around the mouthpiece, or seal a mask spacer over the nose and mouth.
steps.expect: air does not leak around the device.

steps.action: **Press and inhale.** Press one puff while starting a slow deep breath in, continuing until the lungs feel full.
steps.expect: medicine is carried into the airways.

steps.action: **Hold breath.** Hold for up to 10 seconds if able, then breathe out slowly.
steps.expect: medicine has time to settle in the lungs.

steps.action: **Repeat only as directed.** Wait about 30 to 60 seconds between puffs if another puff is prescribed.
steps.expect: dosing follows the person's action plan or label.

steps.action: **Escalate if overused or ineffective.** [BRANCH: improves | does not improve] continue the action plan if improving; seek urgent help if repeated reliever doses are needed or symptoms worsen.
steps.expect: dangerous breathing trouble is not managed alone.

recipes.verification: The correct inhaler was used with an exhale, sealed mouthpiece or spacer, one puff during slow inhalation, breath hold, and escalation if symptoms did not improve.

recipes.title: use crutches
recipes.name: use-crutches
recipes.goal: Crutches are fitted and used safely for walking, sitting, and stairs without putting pressure on the armpits.

steps.action: **Fit the height.** Stand tall with crutch tips 6 inches ahead and to the side of each foot.
steps.expect: the top pads sit about 1 to 2 inches below the armpits.

steps.action: **Set the handgrips.** Adjust grips so elbows bend slightly when hands hold the grips.
steps.expect: weight can go through the hands, not the armpits.

steps.action: **Start in tripod position.** Place both crutches ahead with the injured leg between or slightly behind them.
steps.expect: your body feels balanced over three points.

steps.action: **Walk with the prescribed weight.** [BRANCH: non-weight-bearing | partial weight-bearing] move crutches first, then the injured leg as allowed, then step through with the good leg.
steps.expect: the injured leg does not take more weight than allowed. - ⚠️ *Irreversible:* Do not ignore a non-weight-bearing order because it can disrupt healing or a repair.

steps.action: **Keep pressure off armpits.** Push down through the handgrips and keep shoulders relaxed.
steps.expect: armpits are not carrying body weight.

steps.action: **Sit down safely.** Back up until the chair touches your good leg, hold both crutches on the injured side, and lower with the other hand on the chair.
steps.expect: you sit without falling backward.

steps.action: **Stand up safely.** Hold both crutches on the injured side, push from the chair, then place one crutch under each arm.
steps.expect: you regain balance before walking.

steps.action: **Use stairs correctly.** Go up with the good leg first, then crutches and injured leg; go down with crutches and injured leg first, then the good leg.
steps.expect: good-leg-up and bad-leg-down stays consistent.

steps.action: **Stop when unsafe.** Pause for dizziness, wet floors, fatigue, numb hands, or pain.
steps.expect: falls are prevented by stopping early.

recipes.verification: Crutches fit below the armpits, weight goes through the hands, and the person can walk several steps without breaking the clinician's weight-bearing limit.

recipes.title: board up a broken window
recipes.name: board-up-a-broken-window
recipes.goal: Temporarily secure a broken window against weather, injury, and entry until proper glass repair is arranged.

steps.action: **Make the scene safe.** Keep people and pets away, wear gloves and eye protection, and check for sharp hanging glass.
steps.expect: no one is moving through the glass hazard.

steps.action: **Photograph before cleanup.** Capture the broken window, frame, room, and outside view for landlord, police, or insurance.
steps.expect: evidence exists before anything is moved.

steps.action: **Remove loose glass carefully.** Lift large shards into a rigid container and vacuum small pieces only with suitable equipment.
steps.expect: loose glass is cleared without bare-hand contact.

steps.action: **Tape remaining cracked glass.** Use wide tape across cracked panes if glass is still held in place.
steps.expect: remaining glass is less likely to shed fragments while boarding.

steps.action: **Measure the opening.** Measure width and height beyond the damaged area, including frame surface for fastening.
steps.expect: the board will cover the whole vulnerable opening.

steps.action: **Cut the board.** Cut plywood or a rigid panel to overlap the frame enough for screws or braces.
steps.expect: the board covers the opening with usable fastening edges.

steps.action: **Fasten or brace it.** [BRANCH: screw to frame | brace from inside] screw into solid frame if allowed or brace with cross pieces from inside.
steps.expect: the board cannot be pushed in by wind or light force.

steps.action: **Seal as a stopgap.** Tape edges or add plastic sheeting to reduce drafts and rain entry.
steps.expect: weather exposure is reduced until repair.

steps.action: **Arrange permanent repair.** Contact a glazier, landlord, insurer, or emergency maintenance with measurements and photos.
steps.expect: a real repair appointment or claim is started.

recipes.verification: The broken glass hazard is contained, the opening is fully covered by a secure board or brace, weather entry is reduced, and permanent repair has been requested.

recipes.title: break a lease early
recipes.name: break-a-lease-early
recipes.goal: End a lease early with the least avoidable cost by using lease terms, legal rights, landlord agreement, or replacement tenant options.

steps.action: **Read the lease termination terms.** Identify notice period, early termination fee, reletting fee, sublet/assignment rules, mitigation language, and required delivery method.
steps.expect: you know the contractual cost and procedure.

steps.action: **Check legal rights and exceptions.** Review local rules for military orders, domestic violence, unsafe housing, landlord harassment, disability accommodation, or failure to repair.
steps.expect: you know whether a legal early-exit path may apply.

steps.action: **Calculate realistic cost.** Estimate rent through move-out, fees, deposit risk, utilities, advertising, and possible rent until replacement tenant starts.
steps.expect: you know the maximum exposure and negotiation target.

steps.action: **Choose an exit strategy.** [BRANCH: pay lease break fee | negotiate surrender | find replacement tenant | assert legal right | sublet/assign] Pick the path with evidence and lowest risk.
steps.expect: the plan matches the lease and local law.

steps.action: **Send written notice.** State move-out date, reason if helpful, forwarding address, and requested confirmation; attach proof only when needed.
steps.expect: the landlord has documented notice by the required method.

steps.action: **Get any agreement in writing.** Confirm release date, fees, deposit treatment, utility responsibilities, showing access, and whether future rent is waived. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing a lease-break agreement may waive rights or admit fees, so read every clause before signing.
steps.expect: both sides have a signed or clearly accepted written agreement.

steps.action: **Help mitigate if required.** Provide access for showings, propose qualified replacement tenants, and keep records of listings and landlord responses.
steps.expect: you can show reasonable efforts to reduce unpaid rent.

steps.action: **Move out cleanly.** Document condition, return keys with proof, transfer utilities, and request deposit accounting.
steps.expect: possession ends on a documented date.

steps.action: **Resolve final accounting.** Review charges for rent, fees, damages, utilities, and deposit deductions; dispute unsupported amounts promptly.
steps.expect: the account is paid, settled, or formally disputed.

recipes.verification: You have written confirmation of release, replacement tenancy, lawful termination, settlement, or a documented dispute of any claimed balance.

recipes.title: change a door lock
recipes.name: change-a-door-lock
recipes.goal: Replace a door lock or cylinder so the door latches, locks, unlocks, and closes securely with the new keys.

steps.action: **Identify and measure the lock.** Measure cylinder length, backset, latch size, door thickness, and screw spacing as applicable.
steps.expect: the replacement matches the door before removal begins.

steps.action: **Open the door and keep it open.** Work with the door open so a mistake does not lock you out.
steps.expect: both sides of the lock are reachable.

steps.action: **Remove the old hardware.** Unscrew the interior plate, knobs or handles, cylinder retaining screw, latch, and strike parts as needed.
steps.expect: the old lock comes out without damaging the door edge.

steps.action: **Fit the new latch or cylinder.** Insert the replacement in the same orientation and fasten it loosely at first.
steps.expect: parts sit flush without forcing.

steps.action: **Install handles, thumb turn, or deadbolt body.** Align spindles and screws, then tighten evenly.
steps.expect: the handle or bolt moves freely.

steps.action: **Fit or adjust the strike plate.** Close the door gently and align the latch or deadbolt with the frame opening.
steps.expect: the bolt enters the strike without scraping or lifting the door.

steps.action: **Test with every key.** Try lock, unlock, latch, and deadbolt operation from inside and outside while the door remains open.
steps.expect: all keys work smoothly.

steps.action: **Test closed operation.** Close the door and repeat locking and unlocking from both sides. [BRANCH: smooth | binding] keep or adjust the strike, screws, or latch position.
steps.expect: the door secures without slamming.

steps.action: **Store spare keys deliberately.** Label key copies without writing the address and give copies only to approved people.
steps.expect: access is controlled and documented.

recipes.verification: With the door open and then closed, every new key locks and unlocks the latch and deadbolt smoothly from the intended sides, and the bolt fully enters the strike.

recipes.title: childproof a kitchen
recipes.name: childproof-a-kitchen
recipes.goal: Reduce kitchen risks to children by controlling access to hazards, securing appliances, and making daily cooking safer.

steps.action: **Inspect from a child's height.** Crouch and look for handles, cords, knobs, cleaners, knives, glass, magnets, and small items.
steps.expect: hazards are visible from the child's perspective.

steps.action: **Lock chemical storage.** Move cleaners, dishwasher tablets, alcohol, medicines, and pest products to high locked cabinets.
steps.expect: poisons are not reachable through a low cabinet door.

steps.action: **Install cabinet and drawer latches.** Fit latches on low cabinets, utensil drawers, trash pullouts, and any drawer with sharp or heavy items.
steps.expect: a child cannot open them with normal pulling.

steps.action: **Move sharp and heavy items up high.** Store knives, graters, peelers, food processor blades, cast iron, glassware, and small appliances out of reach.
steps.expect: dangerous items are not available even if a latch fails.

steps.action: **Control the stove.** Add stove knob covers, use back burners, turn pot handles inward, and fit a stove guard if needed.
steps.expect: a child cannot easily turn on heat or pull hot cookware down.

steps.action: **Manage cords and appliances.** Push kettles, toasters, slow cookers, and coffee makers back from edges and shorten cords.
steps.expect: cords cannot be pulled from below.

steps.action: **Secure climb and tip hazards.** Anchor freestanding shelves, lock step stools away, and keep chairs away from counters when unsupervised.
steps.expect: the child has fewer ways to reach counters or pull furniture over.

steps.action: **Check choking and burn hazards.** Remove magnets, batteries, plastic bags, matches, lighters, and hot liquids from reach.
steps.expect: small and hot hazards are outside the child's access zone.

steps.action: **Test and maintain.** [BRANCH: latch holds | latch fails] keep working hardware or replace with stronger hardware.
steps.expect: controls survive normal household use.

recipes.verification: A child-height walkthrough finds no reachable cleaners, sharp tools, heavy pull-down items, stove controls, hot appliance cords, choking hazards, or unsecured climb and tip hazards.

recipes.title: deal with a burst pipe
recipes.name: deal-with-a-burst-pipe
recipes.goal: Stop water from a burst pipe, reduce electrical and structural hazards, and start repair and documentation.

steps.action: **Keep people out of the water.** Block access to the room if outlets, cords, or appliances may be wet.
steps.expect: no one is standing in potentially energized water.

steps.action: **Shut off the water main.** Close the main valve fully, or call building maintenance for an emergency shutoff.
steps.expect: spraying or flowing water slows.

steps.action: **Turn off power if water is near electrical systems.** Use the breaker only from a dry location; if the panel is wet or unsafe, call emergency services or an electrician.
steps.expect: affected circuits are de-energized without touching wet equipment.

steps.action: **Open low cold taps.** Open a tub, sink, or outdoor spigot below the burst to drain pressure.
steps.expect: remaining water drains away from the break.

steps.action: **Contain active water.** Use buckets, towels, plastic sheeting, or a temporary pipe wrap only after water and electrical hazards are controlled.
steps.expect: water is directed away from valuables and openings.

steps.action: **Call a plumber or emergency maintenance.** Describe the pipe location, material if known, and whether the main is off.
steps.expect: a repair visit is requested.

steps.action: **Document damage before moving items.** Photograph the pipe, standing water, walls, floors, and damaged belongings.
steps.expect: insurance evidence is captured.

steps.action: **Start drying what is safe to dry.** Remove wet rugs, run fans or dehumidifiers only on dry safe power, and ventilate if outdoor conditions allow.
steps.expect: moisture begins reducing.

steps.action: **Notify insurance or the landlord.** Report the event promptly with photos and repair details.
steps.expect: a claim or maintenance record is started.

recipes.verification: The water main is off, active flow has stopped or is contained, electrical hazards are avoided, a plumber or maintenance service is contacted, and damage photos are saved.

recipes.title: deal with a flooded room
recipes.name: deal-with-a-flooded-room
recipes.goal: Make a flooded room safe, stop the water source, remove water, and dry materials quickly enough to reduce damage and mold risk.

steps.action: **Assess electrical danger first.** Look for submerged outlets, cords, appliances, or water near the breaker panel.
steps.expect: you know whether the room is safe to enter.

steps.action: **Stay out if power may be live in water.** Shut power off only from a dry safe panel, or call emergency services or an electrician.
steps.expect: no one enters energized water.

steps.action: **Stop the water source.** Close the fixture valve, appliance valve, water main, or roof opening if safe.
steps.expect: new water stops entering or slows.

steps.action: **Photograph the room.** Capture water depth, source, damaged floors, walls, and belongings before moving them.
steps.expect: insurance evidence is recorded.

steps.action: **Remove standing water.** Use buckets, mop, squeegee, wet vacuum, or a pump rated for the conditions.
steps.expect: visible standing water decreases.

steps.action: **Move wet items out.** Remove rugs, cardboard, cushions, and low furniture to a dry ventilated area.
steps.expect: absorbent items stop feeding moisture into the room.

steps.action: **Dry the room fast.** Run dehumidifiers and fans only on dry safe power, and ventilate if outdoor humidity is lower.
steps.expect: surfaces feel progressively drier and humidity drops.

steps.action: **Remove wet porous materials when needed.** Pull baseboards, padding, or drywall only if you can do so safely, or hire mitigation.
steps.expect: trapped moisture is exposed for drying.

steps.action: **Call insurance, landlord, or mitigation for significant flooding.** Report water category, source, photos, and time discovered.
steps.expect: professional drying or claim guidance is arranged.

recipes.verification: The room is electrically safe or isolated, the water source is stopped, standing water is removed, drying equipment or professional mitigation is active, and damage photos are saved.

recipes.title: deal with a power outage
recipes.name: deal-with-a-power-outage
recipes.goal: When the power goes out you quickly determine whether the fault is yours or the grid's, report it if needed, keep your food and household safe, and light the home without creating a fire or carbon-monoxide hazard.

steps.action: **Check whether it is just you or the whole street.** Look at neighbours' lights and streetlights. [BRANCH: neighbours also dark → grid outage, go to step 4 | only your home dark → likely your circuit, go to step 2]
steps.expect: a clear yours-or-grid verdict.

steps.action: **Check the breaker panel.** Look for a tripped main or a single switch flipped to off/middle.
steps.expect: you can see which breaker, if any, has tripped.

steps.action: **Reset a tripped breaker once.** Push it fully off then back on. If it trips again immediately, leave it off. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a breaker that trips repeatedly is protecting you from a fault; do not tape or force it, unplug suspect appliances and call an electrician.
steps.expect: power restored, or the breaker holding off with the faulty circuit isolated.

steps.action: **Report a grid outage to the network operator, not just the supplier.** Use the outage hotline or app; give your address and ask for an estimated restoration time.
steps.expect: a logged report and, usually, an ETA.

steps.action: **Keep fridge and freezer doors shut.** A closed fridge holds safe temperature ~4 hours, a full freezer ~48 hours (24 if half full).
steps.expect: doors staying closed; no "just checking" openings.

steps.action: **Light the home safely.** Use battery lights or torches first. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never run a generator, barbecue, or fuel heater indoors or in a garage (carbon monoxide kills silently); candles are a fire risk near fabric and children.
steps.expect: rooms lit without an open flame or an indoor engine.

steps.action: **Turn off and unplug sensitive electronics.** Computers, TVs, and the boiler control can be hit by the surge when power returns. Leave one light switched on as a restoration indicator.
steps.expect: sensitive devices unplugged; one telltale light left on.

steps.action: **When power returns, restore gradually and check food.** Reconnect appliances one at a time; inspect fridge/freezer contents against the temperature rules.
steps.expect: everything powered, and any spoiled food identified.

recipes.verification: You have correctly identified the fault as yours or the grid's, reset a single tripped breaker or reported a grid outage with a reference, kept fridge/freezer closed, lit the home without any indoor flame or engine, and on restoration reconnected devices safely and discarded any unsafe food.

recipes.title: dispute a security deposit deduction
recipes.name: dispute-a-security-deposit-deduction
recipes.goal: Dispute an unsupported security deposit deduction with evidence and preserve the deadline for settlement, agency complaint, or court.

steps.action: **Read the deduction notice.** Identify each deduction, amount, claimed reason, invoice/receipt, date, and whether the landlord met the legal deadline.
steps.expect: disputed and undisputed amounts are separated.

steps.action: **Compare against lease and condition evidence.** Match each charge to move-in inventory, move-out photos, walkthrough notes, repair requests, and ordinary wear.
steps.expect: you know which charges lack support.

steps.action: **Calculate the refund requested.** Add unsupported charges, duplicate fees, late-return penalties, and any statutory interest or damages if applicable.
steps.expect: you have a specific dollar demand.

steps.action: **Draft a written dispute.** State the tenancy dates, deposit amount, deductions disputed, evidence, and requested refund deadline.
steps.expect: the letter is factual and organized by deduction.

steps.action: **Attach evidence.** Include photos, videos stills, inventories, receipts, emails, key return proof, and excerpts from the lease or law.
steps.expect: each claim has supporting proof.

steps.action: **Send the dispute.** [BRANCH: email | portal | certified mail | deposit scheme] Use the lease or legal notice address and keep delivery proof.
steps.expect: you have a sent timestamp, tracking receipt, or portal confirmation.

steps.action: **Negotiate in writing.** Accept only amounts you understand and request invoices or photos for vague charges.
steps.expect: the dispute narrows to documented issues.

steps.action: **Escalate if needed.** File with the deposit scheme, housing agency, small claims court, or mediation before the deadline. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* filing fees and settlement agreements can affect your rights, so confirm the amount and forum before filing or signing.
steps.expect: you receive a case number, hearing date, or settlement confirmation.

steps.action: **Close the record.** Save refund proof, settlement, judgment, or final denial with all evidence.
steps.expect: the outcome is documented for taxes, references, or future housing disputes.

recipes.verification: You have a written refund, settlement, agency case, court filing, or final decision for the disputed deposit amount.

recipes.title: do a move in inspection
recipes.name: do-a-move-in-inspection
recipes.goal: On move-in day you document the property's exact condition with dated photos, agree a signed inventory, record meter readings, and report every defect in writing so nothing is later deducted from your deposit.

steps.action: **Do a first walkthrough before you unload anything.** Empty rooms reveal scuffs, stains, and damage that furniture will hide for months.
steps.expect: a mental map of every room and problem area.

steps.action: **Photograph everything, systematically.** One wide shot per room, then close-ups of every mark, chip, appliance, and existing damage. Enable the timestamp or shoot a phone with the date visible.
steps.expect: a dated photo set covering all rooms, floors, walls, and appliances.

steps.action: **Test appliances and fixtures and film them working (or not).** Oven, hob, extractor, boiler, taps, toilet flush, window locks, smoke/CO alarms.
steps.expect: a short clip or note per item confirming function or fault.

steps.action: **Read every meter and photograph the dial.** Electricity, gas, and water, with the serial number visible in the shot.
steps.expect: meter type, serial, and reading captured for each utility.

steps.action: **Complete the inventory line by line.** Go through the landlord's list; mark each item's true condition and add anything missing or damaged that they omitted.
steps.expect: an inventory where your notes match your photos.

steps.action: **Report defects in writing the same day.** Email the landlord/agent the full list plus photos, keep a copy, and ask them to acknowledge.
steps.expect: a sent, timestamped message with the defect list attached.

steps.action: **Sign the inventory only when it is accurate.** [BRANCH: inventory matches reality → sign and keep your copy | discrepancies remain → annotate "signed subject to the attached corrections" and send both]
steps.expect: a signed document you and the landlord both hold. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* an unqualified signature on an inaccurate inventory becomes the agreed baseline against your deposit; correct it before signing.

steps.action: **Store the whole record safely.** Back up photos, meter shots, the signed inventory, and the sent email to cloud storage.
steps.expect: one dated, backed-up folder you can retrieve at move-out.

recipes.verification: You hold a dated photo/video set of every room and defect, meter readings with serials, and a signed inventory that matches those photos, and you have sent (and kept) a same-day defect report to the landlord with proof of delivery.

recipes.title: do a move out clean
recipes.name: do-a-move-out-clean
recipes.goal: Leave a rental empty, clean, photographed, and ready for inspection so ordinary dirt is not mistaken for damage.

steps.action: **Empty and sort each room.** Remove belongings, trash, food, and loose packaging before cleaning surfaces.
steps.expect: every room is accessible wall to wall.

steps.action: **Clean from high to low.** Dust ceiling corners, vents, light fittings, shelves, blinds, baseboards, then floors.
steps.expect: falling dust no longer lands on already-clean areas.

steps.action: **Deep-clean the kitchen appliances.** Degrease the hob, oven, racks, hood filters, fridge seals, freezer drawers, dishwasher filter, microwave, and sink.
steps.expect: appliances are odor-free, crumb-free, and visibly free of grease.

steps.action: **Reset bathrooms carefully.** Remove limescale, soap residue, hair, mildew, and stains from toilets, tubs, showers, tiles, mirrors, drains, and extractor fans.
steps.expect: fixtures look sanitary and drains are clear.

steps.action: **Hit the deposit-critical spots.** Clean inside cabinets, behind appliances, window tracks, skirting boards, door handles, switches, radiators, closets, and entry thresholds.
steps.expect: a slow inspection finds no obvious missed dirt.

steps.action: **Treat floors last.** Vacuum carpets, mop hard floors, spot-clean marks, and let floors dry before walking through. [BRANCH: carpet cleaning required by lease | ordinary vacuuming acceptable] follow the written standard.
steps.expect: floors are dry, clean, and free of loose debris.

steps.action: **Remove minor wall marks without damage.** Use a suitable eraser or mild cleaner, testing a hidden spot first.
steps.expect: marks are reduced without lifting paint.

steps.action: **Photograph the finished condition.** Take dated wide shots and close-ups of each room, appliances, meters, keys, and any pre-existing defects.
steps.expect: you have a complete photo record before handing over keys.

steps.action: **Dispose and hand over.** Remove final bags, return bins, close windows, turn off appliances, and return all keys as instructed.
steps.expect: the property is locked, empty, and documented.

recipes.verification: The property is empty, keys are ready to return, every room and appliance has dated after-clean photos, and no visible trash, loose dirt, grease, or bathroom residue remains.

recipes.title: file a renters insurance claim
recipes.name: file-a-renters-insurance-claim
recipes.goal: File a renters insurance claim for covered property loss, liability, or additional living expense and track it to payment or denial.

steps.action: **Protect people and property first.** Stop further damage if safe, call emergency services for fire/crime/injury, and notify the landlord about building issues.
steps.expect: immediate hazards and required notices are handled.

steps.action: **Review your policy basics.** Check covered perils, deductible, personal property limit, loss-of-use coverage, liability coverage, and claim reporting deadline.
steps.expect: you know what part of the policy may apply.

steps.action: **Document the loss.** Photograph rooms, damaged items, serial numbers, packaging, receipts, temporary housing costs, and any theft or police details.
steps.expect: evidence shows what was damaged, when, and approximate value.

steps.action: **Prevent additional loss.** Move undamaged items, dry wet property, board up if allowed, and keep receipts for emergency supplies or temporary lodging.
steps.expect: mitigation actions and costs are documented.

steps.action: **Start the claim.** [BRANCH: insurer app | website | phone] Provide policy number, date, location, cause, damage summary, and contact details.
steps.expect: you receive a claim number and adjuster or next-step instructions.

steps.action: **Submit inventory and proof.** List each item with age, cost, replacement cost, receipts, photos, and repair estimates; upload police/fire reports if required.
steps.expect: the claim file shows documents received.

steps.action: **Cooperate with inspection.** Schedule adjuster calls, video walkthroughs, sworn statements, or item inspections as requested.
steps.expect: the insurer has enough information to evaluate coverage and amount.

steps.action: **Review settlement or denial.** Check deductible, depreciation, replacement-cost holdback, coverage limits, exclusions, and additional living expense payments. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* accepting a final settlement or release may close the claim, so understand what remains unpaid before signing.
steps.expect: you know the payment, denial reason, or documents still needed.

steps.action: **Close and keep records.** Save claim number, payments, receipts for replacements, denial letters, and landlord correspondence.
steps.expect: the claim outcome is documented for renewal, taxes, or disputes.

recipes.verification: You have a claim number and either payment, written denial with reasons, or an active adjuster request with the next deadline recorded.

recipes.title: find your water shutoff
recipes.name: find-your-water-shutoff
recipes.goal: You locate, test, and label the main water shutoff and useful fixture shutoffs before an emergency.

steps.action: **Start where water enters.** Look along the wall facing the street, basement front wall, garage, utility closet, or near the water heater.
steps.expect: you find a pipe entering the building or a likely valve.

steps.action: **Identify the main valve.** Look for a wheel handle, lever handle, or stopcock on the cold water line before branches split.
steps.expect: one valve appears to control the whole home.

steps.action: **Check individual fixture valves.** Look under sinks, behind toilets, at washing machine hoses, and near the water heater.
steps.expect: you find smaller local shutoffs for common leak points.

steps.action: **Test the main gently.** Turn a wheel clockwise or move a lever perpendicular to the pipe, using moderate hand pressure only.
steps.expect: the valve moves without bending pipe.

steps.action: **Open a cold faucet.** Run a sink or tub after closing the suspected main valve.
steps.expect: flow slows and stops after pressure drains.

steps.action: **Reopen the valve fully.** Return the wheel or lever to open position, then run water until air clears.
steps.expect: normal flow returns.

steps.action: **Tag the valve.** Label "main water shutoff" with direction to close and date tested.
steps.expect: another person can identify it quickly.

steps.action: **Photograph and share location.** Save a photo and tell household members or landlord where it is.
steps.expect: the shutoff can be found during a leak.

recipes.verification: After the main valve is closed, a cold faucet slows to a stop; after reopening, normal flow returns and the valve is labeled.

recipes.title: forward your mail
recipes.name: forward-your-mail
recipes.goal: Set up temporary mail forwarding and directly update important senders so letters stop going to the old address.

steps.action: **List everyone covered.** Include each adult, common name variants, and dependents if the postal service permits.
steps.expect: the forwarding order will catch the names that actually receive mail.

steps.action: **Choose the postal redirect service.** Use the official postal service for the old address, not an ad or reseller.
steps.expect: you are on the legitimate forwarding or change-of-address page.

steps.action: **Set the start date.** Pick the move date or the first day mail should leave the old address. [BRANCH: already moved | moving in future] start immediately or schedule ahead.
steps.expect: forwarding starts when the old mailbox stops being safe to use.

steps.action: **Choose the duration.** Select the shortest duration that covers the transition, commonly months rather than weeks.
steps.expect: you have time to update senders directly before forwarding expires.

steps.action: **Submit and save confirmation.** Enter addresses exactly, pay if required, and save the confirmation number.
steps.expect: the redirect is active or scheduled.

steps.action: **Notify high-risk senders directly.** Update banks, tax agencies, employer, insurers, medical providers, schools, licenses, subscriptions, and legal contacts.
steps.expect: critical mail is addressed to the new home without relying on forwarding.

steps.action: **Notify ordinary senders next.** Update shopping accounts, memberships, charities, magazines, loyalty cards, and friends.
steps.expect: low-risk mail gradually shifts to the new address.

steps.action: **Monitor the first forwarded letters.** Check labels and dates to see which senders still need direct updates.
steps.expect: each forwarded item becomes an action item.

steps.action: **Close out the old mailbox.** Ask the landlord, buyer, or building manager not to discard stray mail during the first weeks.
steps.expect: accidental deliveries have a recovery path.

recipes.verification: The postal forwarding confirmation is saved, critical senders show the new address in their own systems, and no important mail is expected at the old address without a recovery plan.

recipes.title: get your rental deposit back
recipes.name: get-your-rental-deposit-back
recipes.goal: Recover the rental deposit by proving the handover condition, fixing fair minor issues, and disputing unsupported deductions.

steps.action: **Read the deposit rules.** Check the lease, inventory, local deposit scheme if any, and deadlines for claims.
steps.expect: you know what can be deducted and when disputes must be raised.

steps.action: **Compare against the move-in inventory.** Walk room by room and mark damage, wear, missing items, cleanliness, keys, meters, and furnishings.
steps.expect: you have a punch list tied to original condition.

steps.action: **Fix minor damage you caused.** Tighten loose screws, replace bulbs, patch tiny nail holes if allowed, remove adhesive, and clean marks with surface-safe products.
steps.expect: avoidable deductions are resolved without creating new damage.

steps.action: **Clean to the written standard.** Focus on appliances, bathrooms, floors, windowsills, cabinets, trash areas, and odor sources.
steps.expect: the home looks inspection-ready.

steps.action: **Photograph and video the final state.** Capture wide room shots, close-ups, appliances, inside drawers, meters, keys, and any pre-existing or disputed condition.
steps.expect: evidence is dated and organized by room.

steps.action: **Attend or request a walkthrough.** Ask the landlord or agent to identify concerns before keys are returned. [BRANCH: they attend | they refuse or are unavailable] document either result in writing.
steps.expect: inspection feedback is captured before you lose access.

steps.action: **Return keys with proof.** Use a signed receipt, email confirmation, lockbox photo, or tracked delivery.
steps.expect: the tenancy end and key return time are documented.

steps.action: **Request the deposit in writing.** Provide forwarding details and ask for an itemized list if any deduction is proposed.
steps.expect: the landlord must either return the deposit or explain deductions.

steps.action: **Dispute unsupported deductions.** Respond with photos, inventory excerpts, receipts, fair wear arguments, and a concise requested refund amount.
steps.expect: the dispute is narrowed to evidence, not opinion.

recipes.verification: The deposit is returned in full or every remaining deduction has an itemized written reason, evidence response, and active dispute path.

recipes.title: hide a spare key safely
recipes.name: hide-a-spare-key-safely
recipes.goal: Create an emergency entry option without leaving a spare key in an obvious place that compromises the home.

steps.action: **Reject obvious hiding places.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not leave a key under a mat, planter, fake rock, mailbox, door ledge, car, or nearby loose brick because discovery can compromise the home immediately.
steps.expect: no spare key is stored in a predictable spot.

steps.action: **Choose a safer method.** [BRANCH: lockbox | trusted person | digital alternative] pick the option that fits your access needs and risk.
steps.expect: the spare is protected by a person, code, or access system.

steps.action: **Use a rated lockbox if hiding on site.** Choose a weather-resistant, combination or keyed lockbox with mounting hardware.
steps.expect: the key is not loose or visible.

steps.action: **Mount the lockbox discreetly.** Place it away from the front door sightline and attach it to solid structure where allowed.
steps.expect: casual visitors do not notice it.

steps.action: **Set and protect the code.** Use a non-obvious code and share it only when needed.
steps.expect: access can be granted without permanent key exposure.

steps.action: **Use a trusted neighbor or contact.** Give one labeled-without-address key to someone reliable and nearby.
steps.expect: emergency access does not depend on a hidden object.

steps.action: **Consider digital access.** Use a smart lock guest code, garage keypad, or building-approved access method when appropriate.
steps.expect: access can be logged and revoked.

steps.action: **Test the recovery path.** Lock yourself out only in a controlled way with phone and backup contact available.
steps.expect: the spare method actually opens the door.

steps.action: **Review after changes.** Update or retrieve spares after roommate changes, contractor access, breakups, or lost-code events.
steps.expect: old access paths are closed.

recipes.verification: There is no spare in an obvious hiding place, and the chosen lockbox, trusted-person, or digital backup method has been tested and can be revoked or recovered.

recipes.title: install a door chain or guard
recipes.name: install-a-door-chain-or-guard
recipes.goal: Install a door chain or door guard that limits door opening while acknowledging that it is not a substitute for a proper lock.

steps.action: **Choose the correct side and height.** Position the guard where an adult can operate it and children cannot easily reach it.
steps.expect: the hardware is usable without bending or stretching.

steps.action: **Check for solid frame material.** Press, tap, or inspect trim to avoid thin decorative casing only.
steps.expect: screws will bite into solid frame or blocking.

steps.action: **Mark the frame piece.** Hold the fixed plate level on the frame and mark screw holes.
steps.expect: the plate sits flat and does not block weatherstripping.

steps.action: **Mark the door piece.** Align the chain receiver or guard arm with enough slack for limited opening.
steps.expect: the door can open slightly but not widely when engaged.

steps.action: **Drill pilot holes.** Use a bit smaller than the screws and stop before drilling through the door.
steps.expect: screws start straight and wood does not split.

steps.action: **Fasten into solid material.** Drive screws firmly into the frame and door, using longer screws where safe and appropriate.
steps.expect: plates do not wiggle under hand pressure.

steps.action: **Test the guard.** Engage it, open the door gently, then pull from inside with moderate force.
steps.expect: it holds normal limited opening without bending.

steps.action: **Test normal door use.** Disengage it and open, close, latch, and lock the door normally. [BRANCH: rubs | clears] adjust placement if it catches.
steps.expect: the main lock and latch still work.

steps.action: **Set household rules.** Use the guard only as a conversation barrier, not as primary security.
steps.expect: everyone understands its limits.

recipes.verification: The chain or guard is firmly screwed into solid door and frame material, limits opening when engaged, and does not interfere with the primary lock or emergency exit.

recipes.title: install a security light
recipes.name: install-a-security-light
recipes.goal: Install and aim a security light so it illuminates useful areas, avoids nuisance glare, and works reliably at night.

steps.action: **Choose the target area.** Pick entries, side paths, bins, garages, or dark corners, not neighbor windows or roads.
steps.expect: the light covers a security-relevant zone.

steps.action: **Select the power type.** [BRANCH: wired | solar | battery] choose permanent power, sun exposure, or easy installation based on the site.
steps.expect: the model can run reliably where mounted.

steps.action: **Set placement and angle.** Mount high enough to resist tampering, angled downward to reduce glare and false triggers.
steps.expect: light falls on ground and door areas, not faces or windows.

steps.action: **Make wiring safe.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* switch power off at the breaker before touching wiring, verify dead if you can, and stop for an electrician if wiring is unclear.
steps.expect: no live conductors are handled.

steps.action: **Mount the bracket.** Drill pilot holes, use exterior-rated screws or anchors, and seal penetrations if exposed to weather.
steps.expect: the bracket is solid and weather-resistant.

steps.action: **Connect or attach the fixture.** Wire per instructions or clip the solar or battery unit to its bracket.
steps.expect: the light is secured and the housing closes properly.

steps.action: **Set sensor controls.** Adjust range, sensitivity, dusk threshold, and timer.
steps.expect: movement in the intended area triggers the light for a useful duration.

steps.action: **Test at night.** Walk through approach paths after dark and observe from inside and outside.
steps.expect: the light triggers when needed without flooding neighbors.

steps.action: **Tune after false triggers.** Reduce sensitivity, angle away from roads, trim moving branches, or change timer.
steps.expect: nuisance activations drop while coverage remains.

recipes.verification: At night, the security light triggers from the intended approach paths, stays on for the set time, and does not shine directly into neighboring windows or traffic.

recipes.title: install a smart lock
recipes.name: install-a-smart-lock
recipes.goal: Install a smart lock that physically locks correctly, connects to the app, has working access codes, and has a battery-dead entry plan.

steps.action: **Check compatibility before removing anything.** Confirm deadbolt style, bore holes, door thickness, handedness, and Wi-Fi or hub requirements.
steps.expect: the lock kit matches the door and network setup.

steps.action: **Document the old lock.** Photograph the inside, outside, latch, strike, and screw positions.
steps.expect: you can restore the old hardware if needed.

steps.action: **Remove old hardware with the door open.** Take off the thumb turn, exterior cylinder or keypad area, and mounting plate while keeping the latch supported.
steps.expect: the deadbolt opening is exposed and undamaged.

steps.action: **Mount the smart lock hardware.** Install latch, exterior keypad, cable, mounting plate, and interior motor exactly as the guide specifies.
steps.expect: parts sit flush and cables are not pinched.

steps.action: **Calibrate bolt travel.** Run the app or lock calibration while the door is open, then again closed if required.
steps.expect: the motor learns full locked and unlocked positions.

steps.action: **Pair the app and update settings.** Add the lock to the account, apply firmware updates, set auto-lock carefully, and name the door.
steps.expect: the app shows the lock online or locally reachable.

steps.action: **Create access codes.** Add unique codes for household members and temporary codes for guests or workers.
steps.expect: each code opens the lock and can be revoked individually.

steps.action: **Test every entry method.** Try app, keypad, physical key, inside thumb turn, and voice or hub access if enabled. [BRANCH: works | jams] adjust before relying on it.
steps.expect: all intended methods operate reliably.

steps.action: **Plan for battery failure.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not throw away or seal away the backup key until you have tested it and stored it outside the locked area.
steps.expect: a battery-dead plan exists, using backup key, external battery contacts, or trusted access.

recipes.verification: The smart lock locks and unlocks from keypad, app, inside control, and backup key, reports correct status, and has a tested battery-dead access method.

recipes.title: install a stair gate
recipes.name: install-a-stair-gate
recipes.goal: Install a stair gate that fits snugly, latches reliably, and uses hardware mounting at the top of stairs.

steps.action: **Choose top or bottom treatment.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* use a hardware-mounted gate at the top of stairs; pressure-mounted gates can dislodge and should not be relied on there.
steps.expect: the top-of-stairs plan uses screwed brackets.

steps.action: **Measure the opening.** Measure width at top, middle, and bottom, plus baseboard or banister shape.
steps.expect: the gate fits the narrowest and widest points within its rated range.

steps.action: **Check swing direction.** Configure the gate so it does not swing out over the stairs if the model allows blocking that direction.
steps.expect: an opened gate does not create a fall path.

steps.action: **Mark bracket height.** Use the template and level on both sides, keeping the bottom gap within the manufacturer's limit.
steps.expect: bracket marks align and leave no child-sized gap.

steps.action: **Drill pilot holes.** Drill into studs, posts, banister kits, or solid mounting boards as specified.
steps.expect: screws will hold without splitting or stripping.

steps.action: **Fasten brackets firmly.** Drive screws fully and check each bracket for movement by hand.
steps.expect: brackets do not flex or pull away.

steps.action: **Hang and adjust the gate.** Set width, hinge tension, and latch alignment. [BRANCH: wall-to-wall | banister-to-wall] use the correct adapters.
steps.expect: the gate closes squarely.

steps.action: **Test latch and pressure.** Pull, push, lift, and shake at child force and adult force without climbing on it.
steps.expect: the latch stays closed and the gate stays mounted.

steps.action: **Teach household use.** Close it every time, avoid stepping over it, and remove it when the child outgrows the need.
steps.expect: adults use the gate consistently without creating trip hazards.

recipes.verification: The installed gate is hardware-mounted at the top of stairs, fits within its rated width, has no unsafe gaps, and remains latched and fixed when pushed, pulled, and lifted.

recipes.title: insulate a window for winter
recipes.name: insulate-a-window-for-winter
recipes.goal: A drafty window is sealed for winter with removable film, weatherstrip, or both so cold air leaks are reduced without damaging the frame.

steps.action: **Find the drafts.** On a windy or cold day, feel around sash edges, locks, trim, and meeting rails.
steps.expect: the leakiest spots are identified.

steps.action: **Choose the method.** [BRANCH: film kit | weatherstrip | both] use film for whole-window air leakage, weatherstrip for gaps where moving parts meet.
steps.expect: the product matches the draft path.

steps.action: **Clean the frame.** Wipe the tape or strip contact area and let it dry fully.
steps.expect: adhesive can bond to a clean surface.

steps.action: **Measure and cut.** Cut film larger than the window opening or weatherstrip to the exact gap length.
steps.expect: pieces cover the intended area with slight allowance.

steps.action: **Apply tape or strip.** Press double-sided tape around the frame, or press weatherstrip into the gap without blocking locks.
steps.expect: adhesive is continuous and secure.

steps.action: **Mount the film.** Press film onto the tape from top to bottom, keeping it lightly tensioned.
steps.expect: the film covers the opening with wrinkles but no large loose gaps.

steps.action: **Heat-shrink the film.** Use a hair dryer moving constantly, starting near the center and working outward.
steps.expect: wrinkles tighten and the film becomes clear.

steps.action: **Trim excess.** Cut extra film carefully without scoring the frame or glass.
steps.expect: edges look neat and tape remains sealed.

steps.action: **Check window operation.** Confirm locks are engaged and required exits remain usable.
steps.expect: the window is secure and safety access is preserved.

steps.action: **Plan spring removal.** Note the product removal instructions and expected residue cleanup.
steps.expect: the temporary insulation can be removed without surprise damage.

recipes.verification: After installation, the window area has no felt draft at the treated gaps, the film stays tight, locks still work, and required egress is not blocked.

recipes.title: move house
recipes.name: move-house
recipes.goal: You relocate your household to a new home on schedule, with belongings packed and labelled, transport arranged, utilities and address switched, and a first-night box that means you can eat and sleep the moment you arrive.

steps.action: **Build a backward timeline from move day.** Six weeks out: book transport. Three weeks: notify utilities, mail redirect, and change of address. One week: pack non-essentials. Move day: essentials only.
steps.expect: a dated checklist, not a vague intention.
