steps.action: **Decide movers versus friends honestly.** [BRANCH: professional movers (heavy/large home, tight schedule, insurance matters) | friends and a rented van (small home, budget, flexible timing)]
steps.expect: a booked mover with written quote, or a confirmed van and a headcount of helpers.

steps.action: **Declutter before you pack, not after.** Sell/donate/bin anything you would not pay to transport.
steps.expect: fewer boxes than you first estimated.

steps.action: **Pack room by room and label every box on the top and one side.** Write the destination room and contents, and mark fragile boxes clearly. Number boxes and keep a master list.
steps.expect: no unlabelled box; the count matches your list.

steps.action: **Pack a first-night box and keep it with you, not on the truck.** Phone chargers, medications, toiletries, a change of clothes, bedding, basic tools, snacks, kettle/mug, toilet paper, and important documents.
steps.expect: one clearly marked box that never leaves your side.

steps.action: **Protect fragiles and heavy items properly.** Plates on edge not flat, glasses wrapped individually, heavy items in small boxes so they stay liftable.
steps.expect: boxes you can carry without the bottom failing.

steps.action: **Take final meter readings and photos at the old home; do the same at the new one.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* leaving without readings can leave you billed for the next occupant's usage.
steps.expect: dated meter photos for both properties.

steps.action: **Do the load-out and a final sweep.** Load heavy first and low, check every cupboard and the loft, then hand back keys.
steps.expect: an empty old home and a full, secured vehicle.

steps.action: **At the new home, direct boxes to their labelled rooms and set up beds first.**
steps.expect: boxes in the right rooms and somewhere to sleep before nightfall.

recipes.verification: Your belongings are in the new home in their labelled rooms, the vehicle and helpers are released, meter readings for both properties are recorded, utilities and address are switched, and the first-night box gives you food, bedding, and documents without unpacking anything else.

recipes.title: prepare a home for vacation
recipes.name: prepare-a-home-for-vacation
recipes.goal: The home is left safe and low-cost for a multi-day absence: water and power hazards removed, food managed, mail handled, a spare key with someone trusted, and enough signs of life to not advertise an empty house.

steps.action: **Decide the water strategy by trip length and climate.** Short trip (2-4 days), mild weather: leave water on. Longer trip, or any freeze risk while away: shut the main valve.
steps.expect: a clear decision written down so nothing is half-done.

steps.action: **Shut off the main water valve if you chose to.** Turn the main clockwise until it stops, then open a low faucet to drain pressure. In freeze risk, also shut off and drain outdoor spigots.
steps.expect: faucets run to a trickle then stop; toilet tank refills once and goes quiet.

steps.action: **Turn off the water heater or set it to "vacation"/pilot.** Electric: flip its dedicated breaker or the vacation setting. Gas: turn the dial to "vac".
steps.expect: no reason for the heater to cycle while no one draws hot water.

steps.action: **Set the thermostat to a holding range, not off.** Summer: ~28-30 C (82-85 F). Winter: no lower than ~13 C (55 F) to protect pipes. Never fully off in freezing climates.
steps.expect: thermostat shows the hold setpoint, HVAC idle but armed.

steps.action: **Manage the fridge and perishables.** Eat, freeze, or bin anything that spoils before your return; check the produce drawer and any open dairy. Keep the fridge running (do not unplug for a normal trip).
steps.expect: nothing left that will rot; no science experiments waiting for you.

steps.action: **Take out all trash and run the disposal.** Empty every bin, especially kitchen and bathroom; a week-old bin is odor and pests.
steps.expect: bins empty, liners fresh, sink drain clear.

steps.action: **Unplug standby electronics and reduce phantom load.** TV, computers, chargers, coffee maker, toaster. Leave the fridge, and anything on a lived-in-look timer.
steps.expect: fewer glowing standby lights; only intended loads powered.

steps.action: **Set the lived-in look on timers.** Put one or two lamps on a mechanical or smart timer with slightly randomized evening hours; optionally a radio. Do NOT leave a porch light on 24/7 (that reads as away).
steps.expect: a lamp cycles on at dusk during a test.

steps.action: **Handle mail and deliveries.** Place a mail hold (post office site/app or in person), pause package deliveries and subscription boxes, and cancel or redirect the newspaper. A stuffed mailbox is the classic empty-house tell.
steps.expect: hold confirmation number saved; no scheduled deliveries in the window.

steps.action: **Give a spare key and info to your trusted contact.** Hand over a physical key (not hidden outside), your return date, a phone number, and which lamp is on a timer so they are not alarmed. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never hide a key under the mat or a fake rock. Burglars check there first.
steps.expect: contact has the key in hand and your dates.

steps.action: **Lock and arm on the way out.** All windows and doors locked, garage down, any alarm armed, sliding doors pinned.
steps.expect: every entry point checked and secured; a final walk-through done.

recipes.verification: Water is in its chosen state (off+drained, or on with heater on vacation), thermostat holds a safe setpoint, the fridge runs with no perishables left to spoil, all trash is out, a mail hold is confirmed, at least one lamp is on a working timer, a trusted person physically holds a spare key with your dates, and every door and window is locked. No key is hidden outdoors.

recipes.title: prevent frozen pipes
recipes.name: prevent-frozen-pipes
recipes.goal: Reduce the chance that water pipes freeze and burst during freezing weather or while you are away.

steps.action: **Identify vulnerable pipes.** Check exterior walls, crawlspaces, attics, garages, basements, and under-sink cabinets.
steps.expect: exposed or poorly heated pipe runs are listed.

steps.action: **Disconnect outdoor hoses.** Remove hoses and drain outdoor spigots if they have shutoffs.
steps.expect: trapped water is not held against the faucet.

steps.action: **Insulate exposed pipes.** Fit foam sleeves or approved heat tape according to manufacturer instructions.
steps.expect: vulnerable pipe sections are covered without gaps.

steps.action: **Seal cold air leaks.** Close vents, repair gaps, and block drafts near pipes without blocking required appliance combustion air.
steps.expect: cold air no longer blows directly on plumbing.

steps.action: **Keep heat on.** Set the thermostat to a safe minimum, commonly at least 55 °F or 13 °C unless local guidance differs.
steps.expect: interior areas with plumbing remain above freezing.

steps.action: **Open cabinet doors.** Open doors under sinks on exterior walls so room air reaches pipes.
steps.expect: warmer air circulates around supply lines.

steps.action: **Drip taps during severe freezes.** Let a vulnerable faucet drip cold water slowly, especially at the farthest fixture.
steps.expect: water movement and pressure relief reduce freezing risk.

steps.action: **Prepare before travel.** Leave heat on, open vulnerable cabinets, shut off and drain water if appropriate, and ask someone to check the home.
steps.expect: the home has active freeze protection while unoccupied.

steps.action: **Know the water main location.** Tag the shutoff so anyone checking the home can close it quickly.
steps.expect: emergency shutoff can be found in seconds.

recipes.verification: Vulnerable pipes are insulated or warmed, outdoor hoses are disconnected, heat remains on, selected taps drip during severe freezes, and the water main is identified.

recipes.title: prevent mold at home
recipes.name: prevent-mold-at-home
recipes.goal: You keep indoor humidity and surface condensation low enough that mold cannot establish, and you clean up any small patches early so they do not spread or damage health.

steps.action: **Find where moisture is produced and vent it at the source.** Cooking, showering, and drying clothes indoors are the big three. Run the extractor and open a window during and 15 minutes after.
steps.expect: steam clears quickly; mirror/tiles not left streaming.

steps.action: **Air the whole home briefly each day.** Open windows wide for 5 to 10 minutes (cross-ventilation) even in winter; short and full beats permanently ajar.
steps.expect: a noticeable freshening of stale, damp air.

steps.action: **Keep indoor humidity in range.** Aim for roughly 40 to 60 percent relative humidity; a hygrometer confirms it. If it sits high, run a dehumidifier or ventilate more.
steps.expect: readings settling into the 40 to 60 band.

steps.action: **Leave an air gap behind furniture on cold external walls.** Pull wardrobes and beds a few centimetres off north-facing/outside walls so air can circulate and the wall stays warmer than its dew point.
steps.expect: no trapped, cold, still air pocket behind large furniture.

steps.action: **Wipe condensation before it feeds mold.** Squeegee shower walls and wipe window sills each morning in cold weather; do not let pooled water sit.
steps.expect: dry sills and glass, not daily puddles.

steps.action: **Keep rooms gently and evenly warm.** Cold surfaces are where water condenses; a little constant background heat beats brief blasts in an otherwise cold flat.
steps.expect: no single room left much colder than the rest.

steps.action: **Deal with any patch early.** [BRANCH: small surface patch (< ~1 m², non-porous) → clean it yourself | large area, or on plaster/behind walls, or you have respiratory issues → get a professional and find the source]
steps.expect: a clear self-treat versus escalate decision.

steps.action: **Clean a small patch safely.** Wear gloves and a mask, ventilate, wipe with a mold cleaner or diluted solution, and dry fully. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not dry-brush or vacuum dry mold (it aerosolises spores through the room); wipe damp and bin the cloth.
steps.expect: the patch removed and the surface left dry.

recipes.verification: Indoor humidity reads in the 40 to 60 percent range, kitchen and bathroom are vented at the source, furniture on cold walls has an air gap, condensation is wiped rather than pooling, and any small patch has been wiped away damp (never dry-brushed) leaving a dry surface, with larger or recurring growth escalated.

recipes.title: program a thermostat
recipes.name: program-a-thermostat
recipes.goal: A programmable thermostat follows a realistic heating or cooling schedule that matches daily routines while preserving comfort and saving energy.

steps.action: **Identify system mode.** Set the thermostat to heat, cool, or auto according to the season and system.
steps.expect: the display shows the active mode.

steps.action: **Open schedule settings.** Press schedule, program, menu, or the equivalent control.
steps.expect: weekday and time periods are editable.

steps.action: **Choose schedule structure.** [BRANCH: 5-2 | 7-day | daily] use weekday-weekend, each-day, or identical daily scheduling based on routine.
steps.expect: the thermostat is ready for the right pattern.

steps.action: **Set wake time and temperature.** Program the comfort temperature shortly before people wake.
steps.expect: the first period reflects morning comfort.

steps.action: **Set away period.** Program a setback when the home is empty.
steps.expect: heating lowers or cooling rises during away hours.

steps.action: **Set return period.** Program comfort to resume before people arrive home.
steps.expect: the house will recover before normal use.

steps.action: **Set sleep period.** Program a nighttime temperature suitable for sleeping.
steps.expect: the overnight period is saved.

steps.action: **Review hold settings.** Learn temporary hold versus permanent hold so the schedule is not accidentally disabled.
steps.expect: the display indicates schedule, hold, or resume clearly.

steps.action: **Save and exit.** Confirm or done the schedule and return to the main screen.
steps.expect: the next scheduled period appears.

steps.action: **Test a small change.** Temporarily adjust the setpoint, then press resume schedule.
steps.expect: the thermostat returns to programmed control.

recipes.verification: The thermostat main screen shows schedule or run mode, the next period matches the intended time and temperature, and temporary hold can be cancelled back to the schedule.

recipes.title: read a utility meter
recipes.name: read-a-utility-meter
recipes.goal: You read a water, gas, or electric utility meter accurately enough to submit a reading or spot abnormal usage.

steps.action: **Match the meter to the utility.** Check the label, pipe, cable, or account meter number.
steps.expect: the meter number matches the bill or property.

steps.action: **Clean the view without opening seals.** Wipe dust or condensation from the outside of the display only.
steps.expect: digits or dials are readable.

steps.action: **Read digital or rolling numbers left to right.** Record the black or main digits and ignore red decimals unless your utility asks for them.
steps.expect: you have a whole-unit reading.

steps.action: **Read dial meters carefully.** For each dial, record the lower number when the pointer is between two numbers.
steps.expect: each dial has one chosen digit.

steps.action: **Handle opposite dial directions.** Notice that adjacent dials may rotate opposite ways, and read the printed numbers on each dial.
steps.expect: direction does not change the lower-number rule.

steps.action: **Photograph the meter.** Take a clear photo including meter number and reading.
steps.expect: you have evidence if a digit is questioned.

steps.action: **Submit the reading if needed.** [BRANCH: utility website | app | phone | postcard] enter digits exactly as requested.
steps.expect: the system accepts the reading or gives a confirmation.

steps.action: **Check for unusual movement.** With water or gas appliances off, watch whether the indicator still moves.
steps.expect: no unexplained usage appears during a short check.

recipes.verification: The submitted or recorded reading matches a clear meter photo, uses the correct meter number, and follows the utility's requested digit format.

recipes.title: relight a pilot light
recipes.name: relight-a-pilot-light
recipes.goal: A gas appliance pilot light is relit only when the appliance instructions allow it and no gas hazard is present.

steps.action: **Check for gas smell.** Smell near the appliance and the floor without kneeling into an enclosed space.
steps.expect: no gas odor is present.

steps.action: **Read the appliance label.** Find the exact pilot-light instructions on the appliance or manual.
steps.expect: the procedure matches the controls in front of you.

steps.action: **Turn control to off.** Rotate the gas control knob to OFF.
steps.expect: the appliance is not feeding pilot gas.

steps.action: **Wait.** Leave it off for at least five minutes, or longer if the label requires.
steps.expect: any small gas accumulation has time to dissipate.

steps.action: **Set to pilot.** Turn the knob to PILOT and press or hold it as directed.
steps.expect: pilot gas is available only while the control is held.

steps.action: **Ignite the pilot.** [BRANCH: built-in igniter | approved manual lighter] press the igniter button, or use a long lighter only if the label permits.
steps.expect: a small steady pilot flame appears.

steps.action: **Hold the valve.** Keep holding the pilot control for the label's time, often 30 to 60 seconds.
steps.expect: the flame stays lit while the safety sensor warms.

steps.action: **Release slowly.** Let go of the control knob gradually.
steps.expect: the pilot remains lit.

steps.action: **Turn to on.** Rotate the control from PILOT to ON and restore the thermostat or appliance call.
steps.expect: the main burner lights normally when called.

steps.action: **Observe briefly.** Watch for stable flame and normal operation without smell, rollout, or sputtering.
steps.expect: flame remains steady and contained.

recipes.verification: The pilot remains lit after the control is released, the appliance runs normally on demand, and no gas smell or abnormal flame appears during several minutes of observation.

recipes.title: report a housing code violation
recipes.name: report-a-housing-code-violation
recipes.goal: Report a serious housing code problem to the correct agency with evidence, while preserving repair notices and tenant protections.

steps.action: **Handle emergencies first.** For fire, gas smell, carbon monoxide, active flooding near electricity, collapse, or violence, call emergency services or the utility emergency line.
steps.expect: immediate danger is routed to emergency responders.

steps.action: **Document the condition.** Photograph and video the defect, date, location, affected rooms, temperature readings, leaks, pests, notices, and damaged belongings.
steps.expect: evidence shows severity and timeline.

steps.action: **Notify the landlord in writing.** Send a repair request describing the issue, access availability, and urgency unless doing so would create danger.
steps.expect: the landlord has a timestamped chance to repair.

steps.action: **Find the enforcement agency.** Identify city/county housing, building, code enforcement, health department, fire marshal, or tenant hotline.
steps.expect: you know who inspects this type of violation.

steps.action: **Submit the complaint.** [BRANCH: web | phone | 311 | in-person] Provide address, unit, issue, dates, landlord response, photos if accepted, and access details.
steps.expect: you receive a complaint, service request, or inspection number.

steps.action: **Prepare for inspection.** Keep the condition visible if safe, collect documents, and arrange access with other occupants as needed.
steps.expect: the inspector can verify the violation.

steps.action: **Attend or follow the inspection.** Show the issue, answer factual questions, and ask how to get the inspection report or violation notice.
steps.expect: you know whether a violation was found and what happens next.

steps.action: **Track orders and repairs.** Monitor deadlines for landlord correction, reinspection, fines, or emergency orders.
steps.expect: repair status and enforcement dates are documented.

steps.action: **Escalate retaliation or noncompliance.** If repairs are not made or retaliation occurs, contact tenant legal aid, housing agency, or court process before withholding rent or moving. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* rent withholding or lease termination can risk eviction if done incorrectly, so confirm local rules first.
steps.expect: any escalation follows a documented legal path.

recipes.verification: You have a complaint number and later an inspection result, violation notice, repair order, closure notice, or documented escalation for noncompliance.

recipes.title: report a repair to your landlord
recipes.name: report-a-repair-to-your-landlord
recipes.goal: A defect in your rental (leak, broken heating, faulty appliance, mold) is reported to the landlord/manager in a way that gets it fixed — documented well enough to protect your deposit and your rights if it doesn't.

steps.action: **Document before you report.** Photos/video of the defect with something for scale, timestamps; note when it started and what it affects ("bedroom window won't close → room at 12 °C at night").
steps.expect: evidence that shows the problem to someone who isn't standing in your flat.

steps.action: **Mitigate reasonable damage meanwhile.** Water: containment (bucket, towels, stop-tap if it's live flow — know where yours is *today*); electrical: stop using the circuit. Tenants have a duty to limit avoidable worsening.
steps.expect: the problem contained to its footprint; your mitigation noted (it's part of the story).

steps.action: **Report through the official channel, in writing.** Even after a phone call, follow up in writing (email/portal — the paper trail *is* the protection): what, where, since when, photos attached, impact, and access availability ("home after 17:00, or contractor may enter with notice").
steps.expect: a dated written report with evidence attached; ticket/reference number captured.

steps.action: **Ask for the timeline and log the response.** Reasonable timeframes scale with severity (heating in winter: days; a dripping tap: weeks). Note their committed date.
steps.expect: a stated plan, or a follow-up date you set yourself ("I'll check back Friday if I haven't heard").

steps.action: **Enable the fix.** Confirm access windows, secure pets, clear the work area (`embodied/household/tidy-a-room` around the defect); be present or explicitly authorize entry per your comfort and local law.
steps.expect: contractor access happens on the first attempt — failed-access loops are the most common self-inflicted delay.

steps.action: **Verify the repair before closing the loop.** Test the actual function (window latches, heater cycles, leak dry after a week — some fixes fail slow); photograph the after-state. Reply to the thread: fixed and confirmed, thanks — or *not* fixed, with the new evidence.
steps.expect: the written record ends in either verified-fixed or an escalated reopened ticket.

recipes.verification: The defect is fixed and function-tested, the written thread runs report → response → repair → your confirmation with photos at both ends, and your deposit-relevant record is stronger, not weaker, than before the defect.

recipes.title: reset a boiler
recipes.name: reset-a-boiler
recipes.goal: A boiler in lockout is checked once, reset according to its manual, and either returns to normal operation or is left safely for an engineer.

steps.action: **Check for immediate danger.** Look for gas smell, carbon monoxide alarm, scorch marks, leaks, or unusual noise.
steps.expect: no emergency signs are present before touching controls.

steps.action: **Confirm demand.** Set the thermostat to call for heat or hot water.
steps.expect: the boiler has a reason to run.

steps.action: **Read the display.** Note any lockout code, fault light pattern, or pressure reading before resetting.
steps.expect: you have information for the engineer if needed.

steps.action: **Check pressure.** Compare the gauge to the normal cold range in the manual, often around 1 to 1.5 bar for many sealed systems.
steps.expect: pressure is within the manual's safe range or clearly abnormal.

steps.action: **Do not refill blindly.** [BRANCH: pressure normal | pressure low] if normal, continue; if low, follow the manual only if you know the filling loop procedure, otherwise call an engineer.
steps.expect: no valve is opened without certainty.

steps.action: **Press reset once.** Hold or press the reset button exactly as the label or manual states.
steps.expect: the lockout light clears or the boiler begins an ignition sequence.

steps.action: **Observe ignition.** Stand nearby without opening sealed covers and listen for normal startup.
steps.expect: the boiler runs quietly or shows a new fault code.

steps.action: **Wait for heat.** Allow several minutes for radiators or hot water pipes to warm.
steps.expect: heat output begins if the reset succeeded.

steps.action: **Watch the pressure again.** Check that pressure stays in range while heating starts.
steps.expect: the gauge does not spike or fall rapidly.

steps.action: **Stop after one failed reset.** If lockout returns, record the code and leave the boiler off if the manual says to.
steps.expect: you avoid repeated unsafe ignition attempts.

recipes.verification: The boiler completes one reset, stays out of lockout, shows pressure within the manual's normal range, and supplies heat or hot water for at least ten minutes.

recipes.title: respond to a break in
recipes.name: respond-to-a-break-in
recipes.goal: Respond to a suspected break-in with personal safety first, preserve evidence, report the crime, document losses, and secure the home afterward.

steps.action: **Stay out if danger may be present.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not enter if the break-in may be in progress, if you hear movement, see an open door, or feel unsafe; leave and call emergency services.
steps.expect: you are in a safe place before taking any other action.

steps.action: **Call the police.** Report location, whether anyone may be inside, visible entry points, injuries, and immediate risks.
steps.expect: you receive instructions and an incident or report number when available.

steps.action: **Do not touch likely evidence.** Avoid handles, broken windows, disturbed drawers, footprints, tools, and dropped items unless needed for safety.
steps.expect: the scene remains useful for police or insurance review.

steps.action: **Check people and pets only when safe.** [BRANCH: police cleared entry | no sign of active threat] confirm occupants are safe or wait for responders.
steps.expect: life safety is handled before property inventory.

steps.action: **Document the scene.** Take photos and video of entry damage, rooms, missing-item locations, serial numbers, and security alerts.
steps.expect: evidence exists before cleanup or repairs.

steps.action: **Make an initial loss list.** List stolen or damaged items with make, model, serial, purchase date, value, and receipts if available.
steps.expect: police and insurer have a starting inventory.

steps.action: **Notify insurer and landlord.** Provide the police report number, photos, loss list, and urgent repair needs.
steps.expect: claim and repair responsibilities are opened.

steps.action: **Secure the home after evidence handling.** Change compromised locks, board broken windows, close damaged doors, and arrange emergency repairs.
steps.expect: the home is not left exposed.

steps.action: **Protect accounts and identity.** If devices, cards, documents, or keys were taken, freeze cards, change passwords, revoke sessions, and consider credit monitoring.
steps.expect: theft does not become wider identity or account compromise.

recipes.verification: You are safe, police have been contacted, evidence is documented before cleanup, insurance or landlord has been notified, and the home is physically secured or you have moved to safe temporary lodging.

recipes.title: set up broadband in a new home
recipes.name: set-up-broadband-in-a-new-home
recipes.goal: Order, install, and verify home broadband so the new home has usable internet with documented account and router details.

steps.action: **Check availability by exact address.** Use provider and independent coverage checkers, including unit number.
steps.expect: a short list of actual service types and speeds available at the home.

steps.action: **Compare plan terms.** Check speed, upload rate, data caps, contract length, install fees, equipment fees, and cancellation rules.
steps.expect: the chosen plan matches your usage and stay length.

steps.action: **Order ahead.** Book as soon as you have a move-in date because install appointments can have lead time.
steps.expect: an install or activation date near move-in.

steps.action: **Prepare the install location.** Find the existing coax, fiber, phone, or network point and clear access around it.
steps.expect: the technician or self-install kit can reach the entry point.

steps.action: **Install or receive the router.** [BRANCH: technician install | self-install kit] let the technician finish line activation or connect modem and router per labels.
steps.expect: router lights show service, internet, and Wi-Fi readiness.

steps.action: **Place the router sensibly.** Put it high, central, ventilated, and away from thick walls, metal cabinets, and electrical clutter.
steps.expect: main living and work areas get stronger signal.

steps.action: **Secure Wi-Fi.** Change the admin password if allowed, use WPA2 or WPA3, set a strong network password, and disable unsafe defaults.
steps.expect: unknown users cannot join or manage the router.

steps.action: **Test speed and latency.** Run tests near the router and in normal work areas, preferably wired and wireless.
steps.expect: speeds are close to the plan near the router and acceptable where you use devices.

steps.action: **Save account and equipment details.** Record account number, support contact, install date, router login method, Wi-Fi name, and return obligations.
steps.expect: support calls and future moves are easier.

recipes.verification: The broadband account is active, the router is secured, and a speed test near the router plus one normal-use room meets the practical needs for the home.

recipes.title: set up utilities
recipes.name: set-up-utilities
recipes.goal: A new home has working electricity, gas (if applicable), water, and internet — each in your name, on sane tariffs, with first meter readings recorded and billing running to you.

steps.action: **Inventory the property's connections before moving day.** Electricity always; gas maybe; water (often municipal and landlord-mediated in rentals); internet options at *this address* (checker tools on providers' sites — availability is address-specific). Ask the outgoing party which suppliers currently serve it.
steps.expect: a per-utility list: supplier-now, options, and who's responsible (you vs. landlord) per your lease.

steps.action: **Sequence by lead time, internet first.** Internet installation appointments run days-to-weeks out — book it first against your move date. Electricity/gas/water are usually switchable in days.
steps.expect: an internet install date near move-in; the rest scheduled around it.

steps.action: **Open each account (or transfer service) effective move-in date.** Supplier's website/phone: address, your details, start date, tariff choice. [BRANCH: regulated single-supplier region → registration is the whole task | competitive market → compare tariffs on a comparison site first: unit rate, standing charge, contract length, exit fees]
steps.expect: per utility: an account number, a start date, and a chosen tariff you can name the shape of.

steps.action: **On move-in day: read every meter and photograph it.** Electricity, gas, water meters — numbers + photo with the move-in date. This is the boundary between the previous occupant's consumption and yours.
steps.expect: dated photos of all meters; readings submitted to each supplier as opening readings.

steps.action: **Verify the physical services actually work.** Lights and sockets; gas appliances light (smell gas → stop, ventilate, no switches/flames, call the gas emergency line — this is the recipe's hard-stop); water runs clear after a few minutes; heating/hot water fire up.
steps.expect: every service functioning, or a fault reported to the right party (supplier vs. landlord per the lease).

steps.action: **Set billing to autopay + e-billing, and file the details.** ⚠️ *Irreversible-ish:* missed utility bills damage credit records and can end in disconnection — autopay converts the whole class of failure into a solved problem.
steps.expect: each account showing an active payment method and your contact details; account numbers stored where you store such things.

steps.action: **Confirm the internet install and test it.** Be present for the appointment; test speed against the contracted tier before the technician leaves.
steps.expect: live connection at roughly the promised speed; router details recorded.

steps.action: **Close the loop on the old place (if you moved from one).** Final readings + photos there, accounts closed or transferred, forwarding address given for final bills.
steps.expect: no zombie account billing you for a stranger's showers.

recipes.verification: Every utility serving the property has an account in your name with the right start date, opening meter readings are submitted and photo-archived, all services physically work, autopay + e-billing are live on each, internet performs to contract — and the old address (if any) is fully closed out.

recipes.title: shut off your gas
recipes.name: shut-off-your-gas
recipes.goal: Shut off gas at the meter only during a suspected gas emergency or when directed by the gas utility or emergency services.

steps.action: **Decide whether shutoff is appropriate.** Use the meter valve only for suspected gas release, damaged piping, earthquake response, or utility instruction.
steps.expect: you have a clear emergency reason.

steps.action: **Do not create ignition sources.** Avoid flames, smoking, phones near the odor, light switches, doorbells, plugs, and garage door openers.
steps.expect: nothing electrical or flame-producing is operated near the gas.

steps.action: **Evacuate people first if gas odor is strong.** Move everyone outside and upwind if possible before working near the meter.
steps.expect: people are away from the building.

steps.action: **Find the meter shutoff valve.** Look for the valve on the gas pipe feeding into the meter.
steps.expect: you see a valve tab or lever aligned with the pipe when open.

steps.action: **Turn the valve one quarter turn.** Use a wrench if needed and turn until the tab or lever is perpendicular to the pipe.
steps.expect: the valve is crosswise to the pipe, indicating closed.

steps.action: **Leave the area.** Do not re-enter to check appliances or open windows if the gas smell was inside.
steps.expect: you are outside at a safe distance.

steps.action: **Call the gas emergency line or fire service from outside.** Use a mobile phone only after leaving the suspected gas area, or call from a neighbor's phone.
steps.expect: trained responders are notified.

steps.action: **Do not turn gas back on yourself.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* restoring gas without leak checks and appliance relighting can cause explosion or carbon monoxide danger; only the utility or qualified professional should restore service.
steps.expect: the meter remains off until cleared.

recipes.verification: The meter valve is perpendicular to the pipe, everyone is outside, the gas emergency line or fire service has been called, and gas service is not restored by the occupant.

recipes.title: shut off your water main
recipes.name: shut-off-your-water-main
recipes.goal: Find and close the main water shutoff so uncontrolled water stops entering the home.

steps.action: **Look near where water enters the building.** Check basement front wall, crawlspace, garage, utility closet, water heater area, or meter box.
steps.expect: you find a main valve on the pipe before it branches through the home.

steps.action: **Identify the valve type.** [BRANCH: round gate handle | lever ball valve | curb or meter valve] choose the matching closing motion.
steps.expect: you know which part moves before applying force.

steps.action: **Close a round handle clockwise.** Turn gently until it stops without using excessive force.
steps.expect: the handle reaches a firm closed position.

steps.action: **Close a lever valve with a quarter turn.** Move the lever until it is perpendicular to the pipe.
steps.expect: the lever crosses the pipe at a right angle.

steps.action: **Use the curb valve only if allowed and equipped.** If the shutoff is at the street or meter pit, follow local utility rules or call the utility.
steps.expect: you do not damage a utility-owned valve.

steps.action: **Open a cold faucet at the lowest safe fixture.** Use a tub, laundry sink, or outdoor spigot away from electrical hazards.
steps.expect: pressure drops and flow slows to a trickle.

steps.action: **Tag the valve.** Add a durable label showing "water main shutoff" and the closing direction.
steps.expect: another person can identify it quickly later.

steps.action: **Test the valve yearly.** Close it briefly, confirm flow stops, then reopen slowly if there is no emergency.
steps.expect: the valve moves and still controls water.

steps.action: **After a leak, reopen carefully only when repairs are ready.** Open slowly while someone watches the repaired area.
steps.expect: pressure returns without renewed leakage.

recipes.verification: With faucets open and no fixtures running, water pressure drops to a trickle or stops, and the shutoff is labeled for future emergencies.

recipes.title: stop a draft
recipes.name: stop-a-draft
recipes.goal: Obvious air leaks around doors, windows, and outlets are found and reduced with low-cost fixes first.

steps.action: **Make a draft map.** Walk exterior walls, doors, windows, baseboards, outlets, and attic hatches with your hand.
steps.expect: cold or moving-air spots are marked with tape.

steps.action: **Confirm carefully.** Use a hand, tissue, incense, or candle flame held away from combustibles.
steps.expect: the indicator moves near real leaks.

steps.action: **Start with door bottoms.** Install or adjust a door sweep, or place a draft stopper at the threshold.
steps.expect: light and air under the door are reduced.

steps.action: **Seal door and window edges.** Apply adhesive weatherstripping where the sash or door closes against the frame.
steps.expect: the door or window closes snugly without forcing.

steps.action: **Lock windows fully.** Close and latch each window because locks often pull seals tight.
steps.expect: the gap at the meeting rail shrinks.

steps.action: **Treat outlet drafts.** Turn off power to the circuit if removing covers, then install foam gaskets behind exterior-wall outlet plates.
steps.expect: air movement at the plate decreases.

steps.action: **Use temporary cheap wins.** [BRANCH: renter-safe tape or film | permanent caulk or trim repair] cover seasonal leaks without blocking exits.
steps.expect: the room feels less drafty without damage.

steps.action: **Recheck the map.** Repeat the hand or tissue test and remove tape from fixed spots.
steps.expect: remaining drafts are fewer and easier to prioritize.

recipes.verification: Previously marked draft points show little or no tissue movement during the same conditions, and all doors and windows still open, close, and latch.

recipes.title: sublet your apartment
recipes.name: sublet-your-apartment
recipes.goal: Sublet an apartment lawfully by getting required approval, screening a subtenant, signing clear terms, and documenting condition and payments.

steps.action: **Read the lease and local rules.** Check whether subletting is allowed, requires consent, has fees, bans short-term rentals, or requires specific forms.
steps.expect: you know the approval path and restrictions.

steps.action: **Ask the landlord for written consent if required.** Provide proposed dates, reason, and process before advertising if the lease requires approval.
steps.expect: the landlord confirms the requirements or sends an application form.

steps.action: **Set sublet terms.** Decide rent, deposit, utilities, furniture, pets, parking, mail, move-in date, move-out date, and access to shared spaces.
steps.expect: the offer is clear and does not exceed lease limits.

steps.action: **Advertise and screen lawfully.** Use accurate listing details, apply the same criteria to applicants, and avoid discriminatory preferences.
steps.expect: you have a qualified candidate and screening records.

steps.action: **Submit the candidate for approval.** Send application, ID, income proof, references, and consent forms only as required by landlord or law.
steps.expect: approval, denial with reason, or request for more information is documented.

steps.action: **Sign a written sublease.** Include parties, premises, dates, rent, deposit, utilities, rules, furniture, maintenance reporting, no holdover, and lease attachment. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing can leave you liable to both landlord and subtenant, so confirm approval and dates before signing.
steps.expect: all parties have signed copies.

steps.action: **Collect permitted payments.** Take deposit and first rent using traceable payment methods and provide receipts. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* improper deposit handling can create penalties, so follow local deposit rules before accepting funds.
steps.expect: payments are recorded and stored correctly.

steps.action: **Document move-in condition and keys.** Photograph the unit, inventory furniture, record meter readings if relevant, and list keys/fobs/cards transferred.
steps.expect: condition and access items are agreed at handover.

steps.action: **Monitor and close the sublet.** Track rent, notices, repairs, rule compliance, move-out condition, key return, and deposit accounting.
steps.expect: the apartment returns to you or the landlord with documented condition and balances.

recipes.verification: You have landlord approval if required, a signed sublease, payment receipts, move-in condition evidence, and a tracked end date.

recipes.title: take meter readings when moving
recipes.name: take-meter-readings-when-moving
recipes.goal: Record accurate gas, electric, and water meter readings at move-in or move-out so billing responsibility starts and ends at the right point.

steps.action: **Find every meter.** Check cupboards, basements, exterior boxes, utility rooms, garages, hallways, or building meter banks.
steps.expect: each gas, electric, and water meter is located or marked inaccessible.

steps.action: **Match the meter to the home.** Compare unit labels, meter serial numbers, and supplier records if available.
steps.expect: you are reading your meter, not a neighbor's.

steps.action: **Wake or cycle displays.** Press the display button on smart or digital meters until the total import reading appears.
steps.expect: a stable number and unit are visible.

steps.action: **Photograph the reading.** Include the number, meter serial, and enough surroundings to identify the meter.
steps.expect: the image proves both reading and meter identity.

steps.action: **Add the date context.** Capture a phone timestamp, newspaper, key handover email, or written note in one photo if helpful.
steps.expect: the reading is tied to the move date.

steps.action: **Write the numbers down.** Record each reading exactly, including decimal treatment if the supplier instructs it.
steps.expect: you can submit values without re-opening the meter box.

steps.action: **Submit readings promptly.** [BRANCH: closing old account | opening new account] send final readings or opening readings to the relevant supplier.
steps.expect: the account shows an actual reading, not an estimate.

steps.action: **Save confirmations.** Store photos, submitted numbers, account references, and confirmation emails together.
steps.expect: future billing disputes have evidence.

recipes.verification: All meters serving the property have dated photos, written readings, and submitted opening or closing confirmations from the correct account.

recipes.title: test a carbon monoxide alarm
recipes.name: test-a-carbon-monoxide-alarm
recipes.goal: Confirm carbon monoxide alarms can sound and know what to do if a real alarm occurs.

steps.action: **Confirm placement.** Check that alarms are outside sleeping areas, on each level where recommended, and near fuel-burning appliances as allowed by the manual.
steps.expect: alarm locations match manufacturer and local guidance.

steps.action: **Check the date.** Look for manufacture, replace-by, or end-of-life markings.
steps.expect: the alarm is within its service life.

steps.action: **Press and hold the test button.** Follow the alarm label until the test sound starts.
steps.expect: the alarm emits a loud test pattern.

steps.action: **Confirm everyone can hear it.** Ask people in sleeping areas whether they heard the alarm.
steps.expect: the sound is audible where people sleep.

steps.action: **Replace batteries if needed.** Install the specified battery type when the alarm chirps, fails a test, or the schedule calls for it.
steps.expect: chirping stops and the test passes.

steps.action: **Clean the alarm lightly.** Dust vents with a vacuum brush or dry cloth without spraying cleaners.
steps.expect: vents are clear.

steps.action: **Record the monthly test.** Note the date on a calendar or maintenance log.
steps.expect: the next test date is easy to see.

steps.action: **Practice the real-alarm response.** If the alarm sounds outside a test, get everyone outside to fresh air and call emergency services or the fire service from outside.
steps.expect: no one stays inside to investigate.

recipes.verification: Each carbon monoxide alarm is within service life, sounds when tested, is audible near sleeping areas, and the household response to a real alarm is to get outside and call emergency services.

recipes.title: thaw a frozen pipe
recipes.name: thaw-a-frozen-pipe
recipes.goal: Thaw a frozen water pipe using gentle heat while reducing burst, fire, and electrical risks.

steps.action: **Check for a burst first.** Look for split pipe, spraying water, bulging walls, or ceiling leaks.
steps.expect: you know whether water must be shut off immediately.

steps.action: **Shut the water main if a pipe has burst.** Close the main and call a plumber for repair.
steps.expect: active water flow stops or slows.

steps.action: **Open the affected tap.** Open both hot and cold handles for that fixture, or the single mixer to a warm position.
steps.expect: steam and meltwater have a pressure-relief path.

steps.action: **Locate the frozen section.** Feel for very cold sections and check pipes near exterior walls, crawlspaces, cabinets, and unheated areas.
steps.expect: the likely frozen segment is identified.

steps.action: **Warm from the open faucet back toward the blockage.** Apply gentle heat starting near the faucet and moving along the pipe.
steps.expect: water begins to drip, then flow more steadily.

steps.action: **Use only safe heat.** Use a hair dryer, warm towels, or a listed space heater kept away from water and combustibles. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never use an open flame, torch, charcoal heater, or fuel-burning heater indoors to thaw a pipe, because it can start a fire or produce carbon monoxide.
steps.expect: pipe warms without scorching or flame.

steps.action: **Keep heating until full flow returns.** Continue after the first trickle so ice farther back can melt.
steps.expect: flow becomes normal at the open tap.

steps.action: **Inspect for leaks while pressure returns.** Watch the pipe, walls, and ceiling as water flow resumes.
steps.expect: no spraying, dripping, or new stains appear.

steps.action: **Prevent refreezing.** Insulate the area, open cabinets, keep heat on, and let the faucet drip during continued severe cold.
steps.expect: the pipe remains flowing.

recipes.verification: The affected faucet has normal flow, the pipe and nearby surfaces show no leaks, and freeze protection is in place before temperatures drop again.

recipes.title: transfer utilities when moving
recipes.name: transfer-utilities-when-moving
recipes.goal: Close or transfer utilities at the old home and open utilities at the new home with correct dates, readings, and billing.

steps.action: **Make a utility list for both homes.** Record supplier, account number, meter type, billing cycle, and whether the service transfers or closes.
steps.expect: no utility is handled from memory.

steps.action: **Schedule old-place closure.** Tell each supplier the move-out date, forwarding address, and final billing instructions.
steps.expect: each old account has a planned final date.

steps.action: **Open new-place accounts.** Contact current or chosen suppliers with the move-in date and address. [BRANCH: single required supplier | competitive supplier choice] register directly or compare tariffs first.
steps.expect: each new account has a start date and reference number.

steps.action: **Plan a small overlap.** Keep essential service active until the final day at the old place and starting the first day at the new place.
steps.expect: cleaning, handover, and move-in are not blocked by a shutoff.

steps.action: **Take final old readings.** Photograph gas, electric, and water meters on the day you leave, with meter serials if visible.
steps.expect: final usage is separated from the next occupant's use.

steps.action: **Take opening new readings.** Photograph the new meters before heavy use starts.
steps.expect: opening readings match the date you became responsible.

steps.action: **Submit every reading.** Enter readings online or by phone and save confirmations.
steps.expect: accounts show final or opening readings rather than estimates.

steps.action: **Confirm billing and payment.** Check autopay, tariff, paperless billing, deposits, and final bills.
steps.expect: no old account continues billing and no new account is on an unknown default.

steps.action: **Keep a utility folder.** Store confirmations, photos, account numbers, and final bills together.
steps.expect: any future dispute can be answered quickly.

recipes.verification: Each old utility has a closure confirmation or final bill, each new utility has an active account from the correct date, and all final and opening readings are saved with photos.

recipes.title: view and apply for a rental
recipes.name: view-and-apply-for-a-rental
recipes.goal: You inspect a rental property properly, spot dealbreakers before signing anything, and submit a complete application with your deposit protected under local rules.

steps.action: **Confirm the viewing and the person.** Verify the agent/landlord and that the address matches the listing before you travel; view in daylight if possible.
steps.expect: a confirmed time and a name that matches the listing contact.

steps.action: **Test everything that moves or flows during the viewing.** Run taps and flush, check water pressure and hot water, open every window, try light switches, look under sinks for leaks, and check phone signal.
steps.expect: working fixtures noted; any fault written down on the spot.

steps.action: **Inspect for the expensive hidden problems.** Look for damp/mold at wall bases and ceiling corners, sniff for musty air, check window seals and any black spotting, and note heating type and age.
steps.expect: a clear read on damp, heating, and insulation, not just cosmetics.

steps.action: **Ask the money and management questions.** Total monthly cost, what deposit scheme protects it, notice period, who handles repairs, and why the last tenant left.
steps.expect: straight answers; evasiveness is itself a data point.

steps.action: **Score against red flags before applying.** [BRANCH: red flags present (see Decision points) → walk away, keep looking | acceptable → proceed to apply]
steps.expect: a go/no-go decision you can justify.

steps.action: **Assemble the application pack.** ID, proof of income (payslips/bank statements), references, and a completed application form.
steps.expect: one folder/PDF with every document the landlord asked for.

steps.action: **Pay only a holding deposit, and get it in writing.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* never pay a full deposit or rent before viewing in person or before a written agreement; wire transfers to strangers are unrecoverable. Confirm what the holding fee reserves and whether it is refundable.
steps.expect: a dated receipt stating the amount, purpose, and refund conditions.

steps.action: **Confirm deposit protection before move-in.** Ask which government/registered scheme will hold the deposit and get the scheme reference.
steps.expect: written confirmation of where your deposit money sits.

recipes.verification: You have viewed the property in person, recorded its condition and faults, submitted a complete application, paid only a documented holding fee (if any), and hold written confirmation of the deposit-protection scheme before any money beyond the holding fee changes hands.

recipes.title: what to do if you smell gas
recipes.name: what-to-do-if-you-smell-gas
recipes.goal: Get people away from a possible gas leak and contact the proper emergency responders without creating an ignition source.

steps.action: **Stop what you are doing.** Do not light matches, smoke, use candles, or operate appliances.
steps.expect: no flame or spark source is introduced.

steps.action: **Avoid switches and electronics.** Do not flip lights, unplug cords, use a phone inside, ring doorbells, or use a garage door opener.
steps.expect: electrical contacts are not operated in the suspected gas area.

steps.action: **Leave immediately.** Walk out, bringing other people with you, and leave doors as they are unless closing one is effortless on the way out.
steps.expect: everyone is outside the building.

steps.action: **Move away from the odor.** Go to the sidewalk, neighbor, or upwind area away from the meter and vents.
steps.expect: you are no longer smelling strong gas.

steps.action: **Call from outside.** Contact the gas emergency line or fire service, and give the address and what you noticed.
steps.expect: emergency responders or the utility are dispatched.

steps.action: **Keep others away.** Warn arriving people not to enter, use switches, or start vehicles nearby.
steps.expect: the area remains clear.

steps.action: **Shut off the gas only if trained or instructed.** If the meter is outside and safely reachable, close the meter valve; otherwise wait for responders.
steps.expect: you do not re-enter or linger in the gas area.

steps.action: **Wait for clearance.** Do not return until the fire service, gas utility, or qualified professional says it is safe.
steps.expect: re-entry happens only after leak testing or official clearance.

recipes.verification: All people are outside, the gas emergency line or fire service has been called from a safe location, and no one returns until responders or the utility clear the building.

recipes.title: avoid fake listings online
recipes.name: avoid-fake-listings-online
recipes.goal: Screen an online listing for scam signs before sending money, personal information, or arranging pickup.

steps.action: **Compare market price.** Check several sold or current listings for the same model, condition, age, and accessories.
steps.expect: the price is plausible or suspiciously low.

steps.action: **Inspect seller history.** Review account age, ratings, completed sales, location consistency, and copied profile text.
steps.expect: seller trust level is clearer.

steps.action: **Check photos and description.** Look for stock photos, mismatched backgrounds, blurry serials, inconsistent specs, or copied wording.
steps.expect: listing originality is assessed.

steps.action: **Ask specific questions.** Request a new photo with date, serial or model label where safe, condition details, pickup area, and included items.
steps.expect: a real seller can answer concretely.

steps.action: **Keep communication on platform.** Refuse moves to text, email, payment apps, or external checkout unless the platform itself requires it.
steps.expect: platform protections remain available.

steps.action: **Review payment method.** [BRANCH: platform checkout | local pickup | shipped direct] prefer protected checkout, in-person inspection with safe payment, or decline unprotected shipping.
steps.expect: refund or dispute options are known.

steps.action: **Check pressure tactics.** Watch for urgency, overpayment, courier pickup, deposit demands, fake escrow, or requests for verification codes.
steps.expect: scam patterns are identified before payment.

steps.action: **Buy only if protections are adequate.** Submit payment only through the agreed protected method after confirming item and seller. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* wire, crypto, gift card, cash app friends payments, and deposits may be unrecoverable.
steps.expect: receipt or meetup plan preserves evidence and protection.

recipes.verification: Before payment, the listing has plausible price, consistent seller history, original proof, protected payment or safe pickup terms, and no unresolved scam signals.

recipes.title: avoid impulse buying
recipes.name: avoid-impulse-buying
recipes.goal: Reduce impulse purchases by using a list, waiting period, sale-email controls, cart delay, and a need-versus-want check.

steps.action: **Write the shopping list first.** Put planned items and maximum prices in a note before opening stores or apps.
steps.expect: there is a clear target list.

steps.action: **Set the spending boundary.** Decide the maximum total and payment method before browsing.
steps.expect: checkout has a hard limit.

steps.action: **Apply the 24-hour rule.** For any unplanned nonessential item, wait at least 24 hours before buying.
steps.expect: impulse items leave the immediate checkout flow.

steps.action: **Use cart-and-wait.** Add the item to cart or wish list, then close the store page or leave the shop area.
steps.expect: the item is saved without being purchased.

steps.action: **Run the need-versus-want check.** Ask what problem it solves, what happens if you do not buy it, and whether you already own a substitute.
steps.expect: the reason to buy or skip is explicit.

steps.action: **Unsubscribe from sale triggers.** [BRANCH: email | app | text] turn off promotional emails, push alerts, and marketing texts that create false urgency.
steps.expect: fewer sale prompts reach you.

steps.action: **Check real price and budget.** Compare price history, total cost, shipping, returns, and whether it fits this month's budget.
steps.expect: the purchase is evaluated beyond the sale tag.

steps.action: **Remove failed items.** If it is still a want, over budget, duplicate, or pressure-driven, delete it from cart.
steps.expect: checkout contains only approved items.

steps.action: **Buy deliberately if it passes.** Purchase only after the wait and checks are satisfied. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some clearance, digital, or final-sale purchases cannot be returned, so confirm return terms before paying.
steps.expect: the order matches the list and budget.

recipes.verification: Only planned or post-wait approved items remain in the cart, the total fits the budget, and promotional triggers have been reduced.

recipes.title: buy a gift card
recipes.name: buy-a-gift-card
recipes.goal: Buy a legitimate gift card that activates correctly and can be given without exposing the balance to theft.

steps.action: **Choose the card type.** Pick a store-specific card for a known preference, or a general prepaid card only if the fees are acceptable.
steps.expect: the card matches where the recipient can actually use it.

steps.action: **Inspect the rack card.** Check that packaging is sealed, the scratch-off PIN area is intact, and no sticker covers the barcode or number.
steps.expect: there are no cuts, glue marks, exposed numbers, or mismatched labels.

steps.action: **Prefer a front card from a staffed area.** Avoid cards hanging where anyone could tamper with them unnoticed.
steps.expect: the card came from a supervised rack or from behind the counter.

steps.action: **Take the card to checkout.** Ask the cashier to activate the exact amount you want. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once activated, many gift cards cannot be refunded, so confirm the brand and value before payment.
steps.expect: the register prints an activation receipt.

steps.action: **Check activation before leaving.** Compare the receipt brand, last digits if shown, and loaded amount with the card.
steps.expect: the activation receipt matches the card in your hand.

steps.action: **Keep the receipt separate.** Put the activation receipt in your wallet or a separate envelope, not inside the gift-card package if mailing.
steps.expect: you can prove purchase if the balance is missing.

steps.action: **Hide the code until gifting.** Do not scratch the PIN or photograph the number unless you are redeeming it yourself.
steps.expect: the card number and PIN remain covered.

steps.action: **Add a note with basics.** Tell the recipient to use the card promptly and keep it until the balance is zero.
steps.expect: the recipient knows not to throw it away after one partial purchase.

steps.action: **Walk away from suspicious demands.** If anyone says to buy gift cards to pay a debt, fine, bill, tax, tech support fee, or emergency, stop and verify independently.
steps.expect: no card is bought for a demand that behaves like a scam.

recipes.verification: The card is sealed, the activation receipt shows the correct brand and value, and no one except the recipient has seen the PIN.

recipes.title: buy a laptop that fits your needs
recipes.name: buy-a-laptop-that-fits-your-needs
recipes.goal: Buy a laptop that matches your workload, budget, portability needs, support expectations, and upgrade horizon.

steps.action: **List required work.** Note apps, browser tabs, video calls, coding, gaming, design, school testing software, or accessibility needs.
steps.expect: minimum performance needs are explicit.

steps.action: **Choose platform.** [BRANCH: Windows | macOS | ChromeOS | Linux] match required software, peripherals, IT support, and budget.
steps.expect: incompatible platforms are removed.

steps.action: **Set core specs.** Choose processor class, memory, storage, screen size, resolution, battery target, ports, webcam, and weight.
steps.expect: listings can be filtered consistently.

steps.action: **Compare real prices.** Add tax, shipping, warranty, adapters, dock, software, cloud storage, and financing cost.
steps.expect: total ownership cost is clear.

steps.action: **Check reviews and reliability.** Look for thermal throttling, keyboard issues, battery life tests, repairability, noise, and common defects.
steps.expect: weak models are flagged.

steps.action: **Review return and warranty terms.** Check return window, restocking fee, open-box policy, accidental coverage, repair turnaround, and support location.
steps.expect: recovery options are known before purchase.

steps.action: **Verify seller and condition.** For refurbished or used laptops, confirm grade, battery health, charger, serial status, warranty, and reset state.
steps.expect: condition and support risk are understood.

steps.action: **Buy the selected configuration.** Confirm exact model, CPU, RAM, storage, screen, keyboard language, and warranty before paying. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* custom builds, opened software, and financing agreements may be hard to unwind, so check configuration before checkout.
steps.expect: receipt lists the exact configuration.

steps.action: **Test during return window.** Run updates, battery test, webcam, keyboard, ports, Wi-Fi, screen, speakers, and required apps.
steps.expect: defects are found while return is still possible.

recipes.verification: The laptop receipt matches the chosen specs, required apps run acceptably, hardware tests pass, and the return deadline is saved.

recipes.title: buy a major appliance
recipes.name: buy-a-major-appliance
recipes.goal: Buy a refrigerator, washer, dryer, dishwasher, range, or similar appliance that fits the space, utilities, delivery path, budget, and service needs.

steps.action: **Measure the real space.** Record width, height, depth, ventilation clearance, door swing, hoses, plugs, gas line, water line, and drain location.
steps.expect: a model can be rejected before purchase if it will not fit.

steps.action: **Measure the delivery path.** Measure doorways, hallways, elevators, turns, stairs, and old appliance removal path.
steps.expect: delivery risk is known before scheduling.

steps.action: **Define required features.** List capacity, fuel type, voltage, finish, noise, efficiency rating, accessibility, and smart features you actually need.
steps.expect: comparison filters match the household use.

steps.action: **Compare total cost.** Add item price, sales tax, delivery, installation kit, haul-away, permit if needed, restocking fee, warranty, and financing cost.
steps.expect: the final cost is not just the shelf price.

steps.action: **Check reliability and service.** Read recent reviews for failure patterns, parts availability, local repair support, and warranty length.
steps.expect: weak models or hard-to-service brands are flagged.

steps.action: **Review policies.** Confirm return window, damage reporting deadline, installation exclusions, old-appliance disconnection rules, and cancellation fees.
steps.expect: you know what must be ready on delivery day.

steps.action: **Place the order.** Choose the exact model, accessories, delivery slot, installation, haul-away, and payment method. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* custom orders, installed appliances, and delivery fees may be hard to refund, so confirm measurements and policies before paying.
steps.expect: receipt shows model number, services, fees, and delivery date.

steps.action: **Inspect at delivery.** Check model number, visible damage, missing parts, and fit before signing or accepting installation.
steps.expect: defects are documented before the crew leaves.

steps.action: **Register and save records.** Save receipt, serial number, warranty, manuals, and installer notes.
steps.expect: warranty support can be started later without searching.

recipes.verification: The installed appliance matches the receipt model number, operates through a basic cycle or startup check, and all delivery, warranty, and payment records are saved.

recipes.title: buy a mattress
recipes.name: buy-a-mattress
recipes.goal: Buy a mattress that fits your body, bed frame, sleep preferences, return window, and total budget.

steps.action: **Measure bed and room.** Confirm mattress size, frame slat spacing, stairways, doorway clearance, and elevator limits.
steps.expect: the mattress and delivery method fit the home.

steps.action: **Define sleep needs.** Note sleep position, body support needs, partner motion, heat sensitivity, allergies, and edge support.
steps.expect: unsuitable materials and firmness levels are filtered out.

steps.action: **Compare mattress types.** [BRANCH: foam | innerspring | hybrid | latex | adjustable] compare feel, durability, heat, weight, and price.
steps.expect: you know which type best matches the need.

steps.action: **Check real total cost.** Add mattress, foundation, delivery, setup, removal, mattress protector, return fees, financing, and taxes.
steps.expect: the purchase fits the full budget.

steps.action: **Read return trial terms.** Check minimum break-in period, return window, pickup fee, exchange-only rules, stain requirements, and refund method.
steps.expect: you know how to return it if sleep quality is poor.

steps.action: **Read warranty terms.** Check sag depth threshold, required support, stain exclusions, shipping cost, and prorated coverage.
steps.expect: warranty promises are realistic.

steps.action: **Buy from a traceable seller.** Use the official brand, known retailer, or marketplace listing sold by an authorized seller. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* clearance, floor models, and final-sale mattresses may not be returnable, so confirm trial terms before payment.
steps.expect: receipt lists model, size, price, trial, and delivery details.

steps.action: **Inspect on delivery.** Check size, label, damage, odor, and packaging before discarding materials required for return.
steps.expect: any defect is documented immediately.

steps.action: **Test through the required period.** Use a protector and track comfort until the return or exchange decision date.
steps.expect: you can keep, exchange, or return before the window closes.

recipes.verification: The mattress is the correct model and size, fits the frame, has saved receipt and trial deadline, and either sleeps acceptably or is scheduled for return within the window.

recipes.title: buy a product online
recipes.name: buy-a-product-online
recipes.goal: A specific product is ordered from an online store, paid for, and confirmed, with a receipt and delivery estimate in hand.

steps.action: **Identify the exact product.** Search the store or a comparison engine; pin down model/size/variant.
steps.expect: a product page whose title, photos, and specs match what you intend to buy.

steps.action: **Vet the listing.** Check seller rating, review count and recency, return policy, and total price including shipping and tax. [BRANCH: marketplace third-party seller | first-party store] Third-party sellers need closer scrutiny.
steps.expect: no red flags — price far below market, stock photos only, or no return policy are exits.

steps.action: **Add to cart and open the cart.** Select variant (size/color) first.
steps.expect: cart shows the right item, variant, quantity, and unit price.

steps.action: **Proceed to checkout.** Sign in or use guest checkout.
steps.expect: an address form or your stored address.

steps.action: **Enter delivery address and choose shipping speed.**
steps.expect: an order summary showing item, address, shipping method, and a final total.

steps.action: **Enter payment and review the final total.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* the next click charges your payment method — confirm item, variant, quantity, address, and total now.
steps.expect: totals match step 2's expectation; no surprise fees.

steps.action: **Place the order.**
steps.expect: an on-screen confirmation with an order number.

steps.action: **Capture the receipt.** Save/screenshot the confirmation email with order number and delivery estimate.
steps.expect: the email arrives within minutes and matches the on-screen order.

recipes.verification: Order history shows the order as confirmed/processing with the correct item and address, a receipt email exists, and the pending charge equals the confirmed total.

recipes.title: buy a used car part
recipes.name: buy-a-used-car-part
recipes.goal: Buy a used car part that matches the vehicle, has acceptable condition and return terms, and avoids unsafe or incompatible components.

steps.action: **Identify the exact part.** Use VIN, OEM part number, casting number, trim, engine, and side or position.
steps.expect: compatibility requirements are specific.

steps.action: **Decide used is appropriate.** Avoid used safety-critical or wear-heavy parts when new or remanufactured is safer.
steps.expect: the part category is reasonable for used purchase.

steps.action: **Search reputable sources.** [BRANCH: local salvage yard | recycler database | marketplace | forum] compare sellers with ratings, warranty, and return terms.
steps.expect: candidates include price, condition, and seller identity.

steps.action: **Verify compatibility with seller.** Send VIN or exact specs and ask for confirmation in writing.
steps.expect: seller confirms fitment or explains uncertainty.

steps.action: **Inspect condition evidence.** Review photos, mileage, damage, rust, connector pins, broken tabs, fluid leaks, and included accessories.
steps.expect: condition risks are visible before payment.

steps.action: **Compare total cost.** Add part price, shipping, tax, core charge, return shipping, restocking fee, programming, gaskets, fluids, and labor.
steps.expect: used part savings survive full-cost comparison.

steps.action: **Confirm warranty and returns.** Check duration, start date, labor coverage, electrical exclusions, installation requirements, and return authorization process.
steps.expect: you know what happens if the part fails or does not fit.

steps.action: **Pay through a protected method.** Use a marketplace checkout, card, or invoiced payment with part number and condition listed. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cash, wire, or friends-and-family payments may remove dispute rights, so confirm part identity and seller terms first.
steps.expect: receipt includes part details and seller contact.

steps.action: **Inspect on arrival.** Compare markings, connectors, damage, and included pieces before installation.
steps.expect: mismatch or shipping damage is documented before labor begins.

recipes.verification: The received part matches the vehicle specs and receipt, passes visual inspection, and has saved warranty and return documentation before installation.

recipes.title: buy second hand
recipes.name: buy-second-hand
recipes.goal: A used item is bought from a marketplace, thrift store, or private seller at a fair price, inspected before money changes hands, and the transaction completed safely.

steps.action: **Search with variants and set a price ceiling.** Try synonyms, brand names, and common misspellings; sort by newest for local classifieds. Decide your maximum before messaging anyone, based on the new price and the condition tier you will accept.
steps.expect: a shortlist with asking prices you can compare against your ceiling.

steps.action: **Evaluate the listing before contact.** Photos of the actual item (not stock photos), specific defects mentioned, seller history and ratings where the platform has them. A price far below market is the main scam signal in either direction of the deal.
steps.expect: a listing where the age, condition, and reason for sale form a coherent story.

steps.action: **Ask the questions the listing dodges.** Age, usage history, defects, original packaging or receipts, and for electronics the specific model number. Request an extra photo of the weak point (laptop screen on, bike drivetrain close-up, garment label).
steps.expect: prompt, specific answers. Evasive answers end the deal at zero cost.

steps.action: **Negotiate briefly and in one round.** A fair counter with a reason ("going rate is X, I can do Y today") lands better than lowball ping-pong. Agree the price, the payment method, and the handover before meeting.
steps.expect: agreed terms in writing in the chat.

steps.action: **Meet safely and inspect before paying.** Daytime, public place (many police stations offer marketplace-exchange zones); bring a friend for high-value items. Test the item for real: power it on, ride it, zip it, check the serial against the listing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* private sales are almost always final. The inspection is your only warranty, so do not pay before it is done.
steps.expect: the item performs as described in your hands.

steps.action: **Pay by the agreed method and keep the trail.** Cash or an in-person-appropriate transfer (`finance/send-money-to-a-friend` rails, noting its stranger warning: for marketplace goods use the platform's protected payment where it exists, never friends-and-family mode). Save the chat, listing screenshot, and any receipt.
steps.expect: payment made once, records kept, both parties clear.

recipes.verification: The item you inspected is the item you took home, it works as described, the price stayed at or under your ceiling, payment went through a protected or in-person channel exactly once, and the chat history documents the terms.

recipes.title: audit your subscriptions
recipes.name: audit-your-subscriptions
recipes.goal: You identify all recurring paid subscriptions, cancel or downgrade waste, and document the expected monthly savings.

steps.action: **Collect recurring charges.** Review the last three to six months of card, bank, wallet, and app-store statements for repeating merchants.
steps.expect: a list of suspected subscriptions with amounts and dates.

steps.action: **Search email for billing terms.** Search for receipts, renewal notices, "subscription", "trial", and merchant names.
steps.expect: each charge has an account email or billing source when possible.

steps.action: **Classify each subscription.** Mark each as keep, cancel, downgrade, share, negotiate, or unknown based on usage and value.
steps.expect: every recurring charge has a next action.

steps.action: **Cancel unused subscriptions.** Use official account or app-store cancellation flows and save confirmation. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm whether cancellation deletes data or ends access immediately before finalizing.
steps.expect: unused plans show canceled or auto-renew off.

steps.action: **Downgrade underused plans.** Change tiers where a lower plan preserves needed features.
steps.expect: billing page shows the cheaper plan and effective date.

steps.action: **Investigate unknown charges.** Contact merchant or card issuer for charges you cannot identify; do not ignore them.
steps.expect: unknown charges are matched to an account or disputed if unauthorized.

steps.action: **Calculate savings and reminders.** Sum monthly savings and set reminders for annual renewals and discounted-plan expirations.
steps.expect: a savings total and future review dates.

recipes.verification: Every recurring charge found has a keep, downgrade, cancel, or dispute status; canceled services show confirmation; downgraded services show new billing terms; and expected monthly savings are documented.

recipes.title: avoid buying counterfeit goods
recipes.name: avoid-buying-counterfeit-goods
recipes.goal: You evaluate a product listing before purchase and reject counterfeit-risk listings before money changes hands.

steps.action: **Identify the exact authentic product.** Open the brand or authorized-retailer page and note the official name, SKU, materials, packaging, warranty terms, and retail price.
steps.expect: a reference record for what a genuine item should look like and cost.

steps.action: **Compare the seller's photos to the official reference.** Check logo placement, stitching, typography, serial-number format, packaging, labels, and included accessories.
steps.expect: either no visible mismatch or a list of specific authenticity concerns.

steps.action: **Check whether the photos are original.** Reverse-search images or look for watermark/crop artifacts that suggest copied catalog photos.
steps.expect: confidence that the seller photographed the actual item, or evidence the photos are reused.

steps.action: **Evaluate the price against the real market.** Compare sold listings and authorized sale prices; treat deep discounts on scarce or luxury goods as a warning sign.
steps.expect: a plausible market range and a decision whether the listing price is suspicious.

steps.action: **Read the seller's return and authenticity policy.** Confirm whether the platform permits returns for counterfeit goods and whether the seller accepts returns without restocking traps.
steps.expect: documented buyer protection before purchase.

steps.action: **Ask for proof only a real seller can provide.** Request a dated photo of the item, serial number if safe, purchase receipt with personal data redacted, or platform authenticity guarantee.
steps.expect: responsive, consistent evidence or a seller who refuses reasonable proof.

steps.action: **Choose the safer purchase path.** [BRANCH: high-value or commonly counterfeited item | ordinary low-risk item] For high-risk goods, buy only through an authorized retailer or a platform with authentication; for low-risk goods, proceed only if all checks are clean.
steps.expect: the chosen seller has acceptable authenticity protection for the item's risk.

steps.action: **Confirm before payment.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* before placing the order, confirm the item, seller, price, shipping address, return window, and buyer-protection method.
steps.expect: the checkout page matches the listing you vetted and uses a protected payment method.

recipes.verification: The listing is either rejected for documented counterfeit risk or purchased only after matching official references, seller evidence, buyer protection, and protected checkout terms.

recipes.title: buy a gift within a budget
recipes.name: buy-a-gift-within-a-budget
recipes.goal: You buy a suitable gift that arrives on time, respects the recipient's preferences, and stays within a fixed all-in budget.

steps.action: **Define constraints.** Write the budget, delivery deadline, recipient preferences, and items to avoid.
steps.expect: a clear shopping brief.

steps.action: **Generate a short candidate list.** Choose three to five gifts that fit the person's interests and practical constraints.
