recipes.goal: You know where an ordered package is, when it will arrive, and it ends up in your hands — including when tracking stalls or delivery fails.

steps.action: **Find the tracking number.** Order history → the order → "Track", or the shipping-confirmation email.
steps.expect: a carrier name and tracking number (or an in-portal tracking view).

steps.action: **Open the tracking page.** Use the order portal's link, or type the carrier's site and paste the number. Ignore "your package has a problem" texts/emails you didn't expect — that's the top smishing lure; only trust tracking you navigate to yourself.
steps.expect: a status timeline: label created → in transit → out for delivery → delivered.

steps.action: **Interpret the current status.** "Label created" for days = seller hasn't handed it over yet (seller's issue, not carrier's). "In transit" gaps of 24–48 h between scans are normal.
steps.expect: an estimated delivery date consistent with the seller's promise.

steps.action: **Prepare for the delivery day.** Ensure the address has a deliverable point (reachable mailbox/doorstep/locker); enable carrier notifications if offered; authorize a safe place or neighbor if you'll be out.
steps.expect: delivery-day instructions set where the carrier supports them.

steps.action: **On "out for delivery": be reachable.** Signature-required packages fail without a receiver.
steps.expect: delivery scan by end of day: "delivered" with a location note, or an attempted-delivery notice.

steps.action: **Verify receipt immediately after the delivered scan.** Check doorstep/mailbox/locker/reception. [BRANCH: package in hand → step 7 | "delivered" but nothing there → F2]
steps.expect: the physical package matches the order; packaging intact.

steps.action: **Inspect contents promptly.** Damage or wrong item → photograph everything as found (before discarding packaging) and go to `shopping/return-a-product`'s damaged-item path.
steps.expect: contents correct and intact; order can be marked complete.

recipes.verification: The package is physically in your possession, its contents verified against the order, and the tracking timeline shows delivered — or a seller-acknowledged trace/refund case exists.

recipes.title: use a price tracker
recipes.name: use-a-price-tracker
recipes.goal: Use a price tracker to monitor real price history, set alerts, spot fake sales, and choose a better time to buy.

steps.action: **Identify the exact listing.** Copy the product URL or model number, including size, color, storage, bundle, or seller.
steps.expect: the tracker follows the item you actually want.

steps.action: **Open a reputable tracker.** Use a known tracker or retailer alert that supports the store.
steps.expect: the tracker accepts the URL or finds the product.

steps.action: **Review price history.** Look at the last 3 to 12 months, not only the current discount label.
steps.expect: you know typical price, low price, and recent high price.

steps.action: **Detect fake-sale patterns.** Compare current price with historical lows and recent price hikes before a discount.
steps.expect: a "sale" is classified as real, weak, or fake.

steps.action: **Set a target price.** Choose an alert price based on history, budget, and urgency.
steps.expect: the alert threshold is lower than normal price and still realistic.

steps.action: **Create the alert.** [BRANCH: email | app | browser extension] save the alert with the exact variant and retailer.
steps.expect: the tracker confirms the alert is active.

steps.action: **Check total cost.** Include shipping, tax, coupons, membership fees, return fees, and warranty differences.
steps.expect: the tracked price reflects the buying decision.

steps.action: **Time the purchase.** Buy when the alert triggers and the total cost, seller, and return policy still look acceptable. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* final-sale or marketplace purchases can be hard to unwind, so confirm seller and return terms before paying.
steps.expect: purchase happens at or below the target price.

steps.action: **Disable stale alerts.** Remove alerts after buying or deciding against the item.
steps.expect: future notifications do not create new impulse buys.

recipes.verification: The tracker shows active alerts for the exact product variant, with a target based on real price history and a saved decision rule for when to buy.

recipes.title: use buy now pay later wisely
recipes.name: use-buy-now-pay-later-wisely
recipes.goal: Decide whether a buy-now-pay-later offer fits your budget, and use it without missed payments or surprise debt.

steps.action: **Read the offer type.** Identify whether it is pay-in-four, monthly financing, deferred interest, or a store-specific plan.
steps.expect: you know how many payments, when they are due, and whether interest applies.

steps.action: **Calculate the full commitment.** Add the down payment, installments, fees, and any interest.
steps.expect: the total cost is written down.

steps.action: **Place installments on your budget.** Put each due date into your budget or calendar before accepting.
steps.expect: each payment has money assigned on the date it will draft.

steps.action: **Check other active plans.** Count every existing installment plan, not just this purchase.
steps.expect: you know the total amount due across all plans this month.

steps.action: **Test affordability without the item.** Ask whether you would still buy it today if charged in full.
steps.expect: the plan is not hiding an unaffordable purchase.

steps.action: **Review missed-payment consequences.** Look for late fees, account lockouts, collections, credit reporting, or loss of promotions.
steps.expect: the penalty for one missed payment is clear.

steps.action: **Choose a payment method.** Use an account that will have funds before each due date, and avoid stacking it onto a near-limit credit card.
steps.expect: autopay will not overdraft or bounce.

steps.action: **Accept only if every date is covered.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* accepting creates a payment obligation, so confirm the schedule and amount before clicking agree.
steps.expect: confirmation shows the payment plan and first payment status.

steps.action: **Track delivery and returns.** Keep plan details until the item arrives and any refund posts back to the plan.
steps.expect: the BNPL account balance matches what you kept or returned.

recipes.verification: Every installment date and amount is recorded in your budget, and the total monthly BNPL payments fit within money already assigned.

recipes.title: use coupons and promo codes
recipes.name: use-coupons-and-promo-codes
recipes.goal: You apply the best available discount to your online order (a working promo code, plus any stacked cashback), confirm it reduced the total, and complete checkout without losing the saving.

steps.action: **Look for the promo-code field before you commit.** It is usually on the cart or payment page, labeled "promo code", "coupon", or "gift card".
steps.expect: an input box for a code exists at checkout.

steps.action: **Search for codes across a few sources.** Try the retailer's own homepage banner and email/first-order popup, a coupon aggregator, and the retailer's browser-extension deals. Note each candidate code.
steps.expect: a short list of candidate codes with their claimed terms.

steps.action: **Read each code's conditions.** Common gotchas: minimum spend, new-customers-only, specific categories, or "excludes sale items".
steps.expect: you know each code's minimum and exclusions before trying it.

steps.action: **Apply the most valuable eligible code first.** Enter it, apply, and watch the order summary.
steps.expect: the total drops by the expected amount and the code shows as accepted, not "invalid".

steps.action: **Test whether codes stack.** Most sites allow only one promo code per order; try adding a second only if the site permits it.
steps.expect: either a second discount applies, or the site replaces/rejects it (one-code sites do this).

steps.action: **Compare percentage vs fixed codes if you must choose one.** On a large order a percentage code usually wins; on a small order a fixed amount often wins.
steps.expect: the code that yields the lowest total is the one left applied.

steps.action: **Layer cashback outside the retailer.** Start your session by clicking through a cashback portal or card-linked offer before checkout, since cashback usually stacks on top of a promo code.
steps.expect: the cashback portal registered the click/visit for this session.

steps.action: **Verify the final total and place the order.** Confirm the discount survived to the last screen; some sites drop a code when you edit the cart.
steps.expect: the discounted total is what you are charged on the confirmation page.

recipes.verification: The order confirmation shows a total reduced by an accepted promo code, any cashback appears as pending in your portal within its stated window, and the amount charged matches the discounted total.

recipes.title: write a useful product review
recipes.name: write-a-useful-product-review
recipes.goal: You publish a review that actually helps the next buyer decide: specific about your use, honest about pros and cons, grounded in how long you have used the item, and supported by a photo where it matters.

steps.action: **Wait until you have real use behind you.** A review after one hour and a review after a month say different things; note which you are writing.
steps.expect: you can state roughly how long and how often you have used it.

steps.action: **Lead with your use case and context.** Who you are as a user and what you needed it for (e.g. "daily commuter backpack for a 15-inch laptop"). Context lets readers judge relevance.
steps.expect: the first lines say what you used it for and for how long.

steps.action: **Give a balanced pros and cons.** List concrete strengths and concrete weaknesses; a review with only praise or only complaints is less trusted and less useful.
steps.expect: at least one specific pro and one specific con.

steps.action: **Be specific, not vague.** Replace "great quality" with measurable detail: battery lasted two days, strap frayed after three weeks, runs true to size.
steps.expect: claims tied to observable facts, numbers, or timeframes.

steps.action: **Report failures and durability honestly.** If it broke, say when and how, and whether support helped. This is often the single most valuable part for the next buyer.
steps.expect: any defect or wear is described with its timing.

steps.action: **Add a photo or short video where it clarifies.** Show scale, color accuracy, a flaw, or the item in real use.
steps.expect: an attached image that shows something words cannot.

steps.action: **Rate consistently with your text.** Do not write a glowing paragraph and give two stars (or the reverse); the star count should match the words.
steps.expect: star rating and written sentiment agree.

steps.action: **Disclose anything that biases you.** Free/discounted unit, replacement, or gift. Skip fake-sounding superlatives and keep it in your own words.
steps.expect: any incentive is stated; tone reads as a real person.

steps.action: **Proofread and submit.**
steps.expect: the review posts and appears under the correct product.

recipes.verification: The published review states your use case and duration, contains at least one concrete pro and one concrete con with specific detail, carries a star rating consistent with the text, and discloses any incentive.

recipes.title: buy a monthly transit pass
recipes.name: buy-a-monthly-transit-pass
recipes.goal: Buy a monthly transit pass only when it costs less than your likely rides and activate it correctly.

steps.action: **List expected rides.** Count commute trips, regular errands, and likely weekend trips for the month.
steps.expect: you have a realistic ride count, not a best-case number.

steps.action: **Do break-even math.** Divide the monthly pass price by the single fare, or compare it with daily and weekly caps.
steps.expect: you know the number of rides needed to make the pass worth it.

steps.action: **Check zones and services.** Confirm whether the pass covers buses, subway, rail, express routes, airport trips, or only certain zones.
steps.expect: the pass covers the routes you actually ride.

steps.action: **Check rider eligibility.** Review student, senior, disability, low-income, employer, or resident requirements before choosing a discount pass.
steps.expect: you can prove eligibility if inspected.

steps.action: **Choose where to buy.** [BRANCH: app | fare card | vending machine | ticket office] pick the method that supports your pass type and payment method.
steps.expect: the purchase channel offers the correct monthly pass.

steps.action: **Confirm start and activation rules.** Some passes start immediately, some start on first tap, and some are calendar-month only.
steps.expect: you know when the pass begins and ends.

steps.action: **Buy the pass.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* many passes are nonrefundable after activation, so confirm zone, month, and rider type before payment.
steps.expect: the app, card, or receipt shows the monthly pass.

steps.action: **Activate as required.** Tap, validate, or wait for the start date according to the agency rules.
steps.expect: the fare gate, validator, or app shows the pass is active or ready.

steps.action: **Save proof.** Keep the receipt, confirmation email, or app account record until the month ends.
steps.expect: you can resolve a missing pass or inspection dispute.

recipes.verification: The active pass shown on your card, app, or receipt covers the correct rider type, zone, and date range, and expected rides exceed break-even.

recipes.title: catch a connecting train
recipes.name: catch-a-connecting-train
recipes.goal: Move from one train to a connecting train with enough time to board the correct service or recover from a missed connection.

steps.action: **Check the connection before boarding.** Look up arrival time, departure time, platform if known, and minimum transfer time.
steps.expect: the planned connection has enough minutes on paper.

steps.action: **Watch delay updates en route.** Check the app, conductor announcements, or onboard screen before the connection station.
steps.expect: you know whether the first train is on time.

steps.action: **Gather before arrival.** Pack bags, put the ticket where you can reach it, and move toward the exit if allowed.
steps.expect: you are ready to step off when doors open.

steps.action: **Read the station board first.** At the station, check destination, train number, departure time, and platform.
steps.expect: the connecting platform is confirmed from live information.

steps.action: **Follow platform signs.** Use stairs, elevators, or passageways marked for the platform, keeping to the walking side where local custom applies.
steps.expect: you are moving toward the correct track without blocking others.

steps.action: **Confirm at the platform.** Check the train number, destination, intermediate stops, and car restrictions before boarding.
steps.expect: the train at the platform matches your connection.

steps.action: **Board before door close.** Enter an open door with your party and bags, then move away from the doorway.
steps.expect: you and your bags are on the connecting train before departure.

steps.action: **Use the missed-connection plan if needed.** [BRANCH: protected connection | unprotected connection] ask staff for rebooking if protected, or search the next valid service if unprotected.
steps.expect: you have a next train, rebooked ticket, or support case.

steps.action: **Update anyone waiting.** Send the new arrival time if the connection changed.
steps.expect: pickup, hotel, or meeting plans reflect the latest arrival.

recipes.verification: You are on the connecting train that matches the live board's destination, train number, and departure time, or you have a confirmed replacement plan.

recipes.title: change lanes safely
recipes.name: change-lanes-safely
recipes.goal: Change lanes with a deliberate mirror-signal-blindspot-maneuver sequence and enough gap to avoid forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

steps.action: **Plan the lane change early.** Identify why you need the lane: exit, turn, passing, obstruction, or lane ending.
steps.expect: the maneuver is not a last-second reaction.

steps.action: **Check mirrors first.** Look at rearview and side mirror for vehicles approaching in the target lane.
steps.expect: you know the traffic pattern behind and beside you.

steps.action: **Signal before moving.** Turn on the signal for several blinks before crossing the lane line.
steps.expect: nearby drivers get clear notice of your intent.

steps.action: **Check the blind spot.** Turn your head briefly toward the target lane while keeping the vehicle straight.
steps.expect: motorcycles, small cars, and fast overtaking vehicles are not hidden beside you.

steps.action: **Judge the gap.** Confirm the target lane has space ahead and behind, and that your move will not make another driver brake hard.
steps.expect: the lane change can happen at traffic speed.

steps.action: **Move smoothly, not suddenly.** [BRANCH: accelerate slightly | hold speed | wait] match the target lane speed, steer gently across the line, or stay put if the gap is not real.
steps.expect: the vehicle crosses predictably.

steps.action: **Change one lane at a time.** Finish in the first target lane, straighten, cancel or reset the signal, then reassess before another lane change.
steps.expect: no diagonal sweep surprises other drivers.

steps.action: **Rebuild following distance.** Once in the lane, leave at least a three-second gap where speed allows.
steps.expect: you are not tailgating the vehicle you moved behind.

steps.action: **Cancel the signal and rescan.** Confirm the signal is off and mirrors show stable spacing.
steps.expect: the lane change is complete and traffic around you is steady.

recipes.verification: The vehicle moves one lane only after mirror, signal, blind-spot check, and gap confirmation, without causing nearby traffic to brake or swerve.

recipes.title: hail a rideshare
recipes.name: hail-a-rideshare
recipes.goal: A rideshare (Uber/Lyft/Didi/Grab-class) takes you from pickup to destination — the right car, the fare you agreed to, and the ride's safety checks actually performed.

steps.action: **Set the destination first, then the pickup point.** Type the destination; then check the app's guessed pickup pin — drag it to where a car can actually stop (not mid-block on a highway, not inside the pedestrian mall). Airports/malls: use the app's designated pickup zones.
steps.expect: fare estimate and ETA shown for a pickup point a car can legally reach.

steps.action: **Choose the tier and confirm the price.** Economy/shared/XL per group size and luggage; the up-front price is the agreement — surge pricing shows here, and "wait 10 minutes" is a legitimate response to a surge multiplier.
steps.expect: a booked ride with driver name, photo, car model, and **plate number** on screen.

steps.action: **Match the car before you touch the door.** Plate first (the unfakeable one), then model/color, then the driver's face. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* getting into an unverified car is the category's central risk — the plate check is non-negotiable, and asking "who are you here for?" (making *them* say your name) beats announcing yours.
steps.expect: plate, car, and driver all match the app; they said your name.

steps.action: **Ride with the app open.** Seatbelt on; the app's route trace runs; share-trip-status with a contact for night rides (one tap, built-in). A driver going firmly off-route without explanation → speak up, and the in-app safety button exists.
steps.expect: the blue dot follows roughly the app's proposed route to your destination.

steps.action: **End the ride and check out clean.** Confirm you're at the destination (or a sane drop point you approved), take your belongings — phone, wallet, the bag in the trunk — *before* the car leaves.
steps.expect: everything in hand; the ride auto-completes and charges the stored payment.

steps.action: **Verify the receipt.** The charged fare ≈ the quoted fare (tolls/wait fees legitimately add); rate/tip per the local norm.
steps.expect: receipt matches the agreement; anomalies → F3.

recipes.verification: Plate-matched car, route roughly as proposed, arrived at the intended destination with all belongings, charged what was quoted (± legitimate fees), and the receipt sits in trip history for any dispute window.

recipes.title: keep a safe following distance
recipes.name: keep-a-safe-following-distance
recipes.goal: Maintain enough following distance to stop or react safely as speed, weather, visibility, and vehicle size change.

steps.action: **Pick a fixed marker.** Choose a sign, shadow, bridge, lane stripe, or crack that the vehicle ahead will pass.
steps.expect: the marker is stationary and easy to count from.

steps.action: **Count when the vehicle ahead passes it.** Say "one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three" until your front bumper reaches the marker.
steps.expect: the count gives your following gap.

steps.action: **Keep at least three seconds in good conditions.** Ease off the accelerator until you have a full three-second gap.
steps.expect: you are not closing on the vehicle ahead during normal flow.

steps.action: **Add time for bad conditions.** Use four to six seconds or more in rain, darkness, glare, fog, snow, gravel, heavy traffic, or when tired.
steps.expect: stopping room grows with risk.

steps.action: **Add time behind big vehicles.** Stay farther back from trucks, buses, trailers, motorcycles, and vehicles carrying loads.
steps.expect: you can see around hazards and avoid debris or sudden stops.

steps.action: **Protect your escape space.** Avoid driving boxed in beside another vehicle when possible, and keep a lane or shoulder option visible.
steps.expect: you have somewhere to go if braking alone is not enough.

steps.action: **Respond to tailgaters calmly.** [BRANCH: maintain speed | change lanes | pull over] keep steady speed, move right when safe, or let them pass; do not brake-check.
steps.expect: pressure behind you decreases without creating a new hazard.

steps.action: **Reset after every merge.** When someone cuts into your gap, lift off and rebuild the space instead of defending it.
steps.expect: the three-second buffer returns.

steps.action: **Brake early and smoothly.** Signal slowing with brake lights before hard braking is needed.
steps.expect: drivers behind have more warning and the vehicle stays stable.

recipes.verification: You maintain at least a three-second following gap in good conditions and a longer gap whenever weather, visibility, load, fatigue, or vehicle type increases stopping risk.

recipes.title: lock a bike properly
recipes.name: lock-a-bike-properly
recipes.goal: Lock a bike so the frame and at least one wheel are secured to a fixed rack with minimal leverage for theft.

steps.action: **Choose a fixed rack.** Pull and shake the rack or post to confirm it is bolted down and not a removable signpost.
steps.expect: the anchor cannot be lifted, unscrewed, or carried away.

steps.action: **Avoid weak lock spots.** Skip trees, thin signs, scaffolding, fences, and anything the bike can be lifted over.
steps.expect: the anchor is stronger than the lock.

steps.action: **Position the bike close.** Put the frame triangle and rear wheel near the rack with little open space between them.
steps.expect: the lock can capture frame, wheel, and rack tightly.

steps.action: **Lock frame and rear wheel with the U-lock.** Pass the U-lock through the rear triangle, rear wheel, and fixed rack.
steps.expect: the most valuable removable parts are captured by the strongest lock.

steps.action: **Fill the gap.** Use the smallest lock space possible so a jack or pry bar cannot easily fit inside.
steps.expect: the lock sits snugly instead of floating in open air.

steps.action: **Secure the front wheel.** [BRANCH: cable | second U-lock | remove wheel] cable it to the U-lock, use a second lock, or remove it and lock it with the frame.
steps.expect: both wheels are either locked or intentionally protected.

steps.action: **Remove accessories.** Take lights, computer, bags, pump, phone mount, and quick-release seat if theft is likely.
steps.expect: easy-grab items are not left on the bike.

steps.action: **Keep the lock off the ground.** Rotate the keyway downward or sideways and keep the lock body suspended.
steps.expect: smashing or picking access is harder.

steps.action: **Do a final lift test.** Try to move the bike away from the rack without damaging it.
steps.expect: frame, wheel, and rack stay connected.

recipes.verification: The bike frame and at least one wheel are locked to a fixed object with a tight U-lock or chain, and removable accessories are taken with you.

recipes.title: navigate with a maps app
recipes.name: navigate-with-a-maps-app
recipes.goal: A maps app takes you from here to a named destination on foot or by transit/car — including the two skills the app can't do for you: picking the *right* destination entry, and getting your first hundred meters pointed correctly.

steps.action: **Search and pick the destination *carefully*.** Same-name traps: chains (which branch?), cities sharing street names, "Springfield" in the wrong state/country. Check the result's address and map position against what you know before routing.
steps.expect: the pin sits where the destination plausibly is — right city, right district.

steps.action: **Choose the mode and read the route candidates.** Walk/transit/drive/bike change everything. Glance at the 2–3 offered routes: time, arrival estimate, and their character (transfers for transit, tolls/highway for driving, stairs for walking).
steps.expect: a chosen route whose shape you could sketch: "blue line 4 stops, then a 5-minute walk."

steps.action: **Solve the first-100-meters problem before moving.** The classic failure is walking confidently the wrong way. Anchor the map: watch your dot move a few steps, or use the compass/AR-walking mode, or match one visible landmark ("the river should be on my left").
steps.expect: your first movement makes the dot travel *along* the route, not away from it.

steps.action: **Follow the route with the app as advisor, not autopilot.** Glance-and-walk (don't screen-stare into traffic and lampposts); at each decision point the app announces/vibrates. Transit mode: it names the stop to exit — cross-check with the vehicle's own announcements (`transit/take-a-city-bus` step 5).
steps.expect: progress ticking off; estimated arrival stable or improving.

steps.action: **Handle re-routing calmly.** Missed a turn → the app re-plans in seconds; keep moving safely rather than U-turning on impulse. Transit disruption → re-run the route; apps ingest live service data unevenly, so posted station notices outrank the app (`transit/ride-a-subway` decision points).
steps.expect: a new route absorbed without drama.

steps.action: **Land the last meters.** GPS is ±10–30 m in cities: at the pin, look up and find the actual entrance (often around the corner from the pin), building numbers, or the venue's sign. "You have arrived" is a suggestion; the door is the fact.
steps.expect: you at the door, not standing in the road where the pin says.

recipes.verification: You're at the destination's actual entrance, roughly on the estimated time, with battery surviving; and the route's shape matched what you sketched at step 2 — or diverged for reasons you understood at the time.

recipes.title: plan a commute
recipes.name: plan-a-commute
recipes.goal: You have a reliable everyday route between two fixed points (home and work or school), chosen by comparing modes, padded with a sensible time buffer, and backed by a known alternative for when the primary route fails.

steps.action: **Fix the hard arrival time.** Work back from when you must be there, not from when you like to leave.
steps.expect: a target arrival time written down.

steps.action: **Compare modes on the real timetable.** Check walk, bike, bus, train, and drive for your actual departure window, not an off-peak average.
steps.expect: a door-to-door time and cost for each viable mode at rush hour.

steps.action: **Choose the primary mode on total reliability, not raw speed.** A slightly slower option with predictable timing beats a fast one that swings wildly with traffic.
steps.expect: one primary route with a typical and a bad-day time.

steps.action: **Apply the buffer rule.** Add padding equal to the route's variability: roughly 15 percent for a steady rail run, more for traffic-dependent driving. Leave by (arrival time minus typical time minus buffer).
steps.expect: a fixed departure time that absorbs a normal bad day.

steps.action: **Pick a concrete backup route.** Identify one alternative that fails independently of the first: a different line, a bus parallel to the train, or a bike-plus-transit combo.
steps.expect: a named plan B you could start within minutes, not a vague idea.

steps.action: **Do a trial run at the real time.** Ride the full route on a normal weekday at your intended departure time before you depend on it.
steps.expect: the trial arrives with buffer to spare; note any surprise (a slow transfer, a crowded platform).

steps.action: **Adjust from the trial, then lock it in.** Fix the departure time and buffer from what you actually observed, not the app estimate.
steps.expect: a settled leave-time and route you can repeat daily.

steps.action: **Set up live disruption alerts.** Follow the line or road on the transit app so you learn of delays before you leave home.
steps.expect: you get notified of a disruption in time to switch to plan B.

recipes.verification: You have a written primary route with a fixed departure time and buffer, a genuinely independent backup route, and a trial run that arrived on time with margin to spare.

recipes.title: plan a multi leg journey
recipes.name: plan-a-multi-leg-journey
recipes.goal: Plan a journey with two or more legs so the timing, tickets, transfers, and backup option are clear before departure.

steps.action: **Enter the full door-to-door trip.** Use a journey planner with the exact date and time, including walking start and end points.
steps.expect: at least two candidate itineraries appear.

steps.action: **Inspect each leg.** Note mode, line, direction, platform or stop, departure time, and arrival time.
steps.expect: every leg has a concrete boarding point and time.

steps.action: **Check transfer buffers.** Compare each transfer time with walking distance, station complexity, crowds, and delay risk.
steps.expect: each handoff has a buffer you could actually make.

steps.action: **Compare ticket structure.** [BRANCH: single through ticket | separate tickets] check whether one fare protects the connection or each leg is independent.
steps.expect: you know who is responsible if an early leg is late.

steps.action: **Price the full trip.** Add fares, reservation fees, luggage fees, and any peak surcharges.
steps.expect: the total cost is known before purchase.

steps.action: **Choose the itinerary.** Prefer the option that meets arrival needs with realistic transfers, not only the shortest app estimate.
steps.expect: one primary journey is selected.

steps.action: **Pick a backup.** Identify a later connection, alternate route, taxi segment, or overnight fallback before leaving.
steps.expect: there is a named plan if one leg fails.

steps.action: **Buy or reserve carefully.** Purchase required tickets and reservations only after checking date, direction, passenger count, and transfer stations. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* nonrefundable tickets may lock the route, so confirm every leg before paying.
steps.expect: confirmations or tickets are saved.

steps.action: **Create a trip sheet.** Save offline screenshots with times, ticket references, station maps, and support contacts.
steps.expect: you can navigate even with weak signal.

recipes.verification: You have a primary itinerary with every leg, transfer buffer, fare or ticket rule, confirmation, and backup option saved offline.

recipes.title: read a bus schedule
recipes.name: read-a-bus-schedule
recipes.goal: Read a bus schedule well enough to choose the correct route, direction, stop, and departure time.

steps.action: **Find the route number.** Use a map, trip planner, or system map to identify the bus route serving both origin and destination.
steps.expect: you have a route number or letter to look up.

steps.action: **Choose the correct direction.** Read the endpoint or major destination shown for each direction, not just the route number.
steps.expect: the bus direction matches where you need to go.

steps.action: **Find your boarding stop.** Locate the stop name, stop ID, or nearest intersection in the schedule or app.
steps.expect: the stop appears on the route in the correct direction.

steps.action: **Select the right service day column.** [BRANCH: weekday | Saturday | Sunday/holiday] use the column or table for the actual day of travel.
steps.expect: times match today's service pattern.

steps.action: **Read across from a timepoint.** If your exact stop is not listed, use the nearest earlier timepoint and add walking or waiting buffer.
steps.expect: you have a conservative departure estimate.

steps.action: **Check frequency notes.** Look for "every 10 minutes," school-day notes, express-only stops, limited service, or footnotes.
steps.expect: you know whether every bus stops for you.

steps.action: **Confirm with live-time data.** Use the transit app, stop QR code, text number, or real-time board close to departure.
steps.expect: the next bus countdown agrees with the scheduled pattern or explains a delay.

steps.action: **Plan to arrive early.** Reach the stop 3-5 minutes before scheduled time, more for infrequent routes.
steps.expect: an early bus does not leave without you.

steps.action: **Match the headsign when boarding.** Check route number and destination on the bus before stepping on.
steps.expect: the vehicle matches the schedule you selected.

recipes.verification: You can state the route, direction, boarding stop, service-day table, and next usable departure time before going to the stop.

recipes.title: read a train timetable
recipes.name: read-a-train-timetable
recipes.goal: Find the correct train, direction, departure time, arrival time, transfers, service days, and timetable symbols before going to the station.

steps.action: **Identify the route line.** Match your origin and destination to a named line, route number, or corridor on the map.
steps.expect: one line or set of lines can serve the trip.

steps.action: **Choose the travel direction.** Use the line's endpoint names to pick the direction that passes your destination.
steps.expect: the destination appears after your origin in that direction.

steps.action: **Select the correct service day.** [BRANCH: weekday | Saturday | Sunday/holiday] open the schedule for the actual date, not the nearest normal day.
steps.expect: the heading or date range matches your travel day.

steps.action: **Decide departure or arrival search.** If you must be somewhere on time, search by arrival; otherwise search by departure.
steps.expect: the timetable rows are being read from the right time target.

steps.action: **Read across the station row or column.** Follow the same train row from origin time to destination time, keeping your finger or cursor on one row.
steps.expect: one departure time and one arrival time belong to the same train.

steps.action: **Check transfers.** If the destination is blank or requires a change, note the transfer station, platform if shown, and connecting train time.
steps.expect: every leg has a train number or departure time.

steps.action: **Decode symbols and footnotes.** Look up letters, icons, and marks for express service, request stops, no bicycles, seat reservations, or limited service.
steps.expect: no symbol beside your train is unexplained.

steps.action: **Add station time.** Include walking to the platform, ticket purchase, and any security or gate time.
steps.expect: you know when to arrive at the origin station.

steps.action: **Save the itinerary.** Screenshot or write the line, direction, times, transfer point, and platform notes.
steps.expect: the plan is usable without reloading the timetable.

recipes.verification: You can state the line, direction, origin departure time, destination arrival time, transfer details if any, service day, and meaning of every symbol on the chosen trip.

recipes.title: read a transit map
recipes.name: read-a-transit-map
recipes.goal: A rider reads a transit map well enough to identify lines, transfer points, direction, fare zones, and a practical route.

steps.action: **Find the legend.** Locate symbols for rail, bus, tram, accessible stations, airports, and fare zones.
steps.expect: map symbols have known meanings.

steps.action: **Locate your start.** Search by station name, neighborhood, route number, or nearby landmark.
steps.expect: starting point is marked on the map.

steps.action: **Locate your destination.** Find the closest station or stop to where you need to arrive.
steps.expect: destination point is marked separately.

steps.action: **Identify lines by color and label.** Trace colored lines while reading route letters, numbers, or names printed on them.
steps.expect: relevant lines between start and destination are visible.

steps.action: **Check direction by terminus.** Read the end station names at each end of the line, not just compass direction.
steps.expect: the correct platform direction matches the terminus beyond your destination.

steps.action: **Find interchange stations.** Look for stations where multiple colored lines meet or share a transfer symbol.
steps.expect: possible transfer points are identified.

steps.action: **Build the route.** Trace from start to destination with the fewest sensible transfers, considering walking distance.
steps.expect: route sequence is written or remembered.

steps.action: **Check fare zones.** Note whether the trip crosses zone boundaries or special fare areas.
steps.expect: required fare type or tap rule is known.

steps.action: **Check service pattern.** Confirm express, branch, peak-only, or weekend differences before committing.
steps.expect: the chosen train or bus actually serves every needed segment.

steps.action: **Use the map at the station.** Match the line color, route label, direction terminus, and platform signs.
steps.expect: boarding choice matches the planned route.

recipes.verification: The rider can state the start stop, destination stop, line or route labels, travel direction by terminus, transfer station if any, and fare zone requirement.

recipes.title: rent a shared bike
recipes.name: rent-a-shared-bike
recipes.goal: A shared bike (docked or dockless) is unlocked, ridden to your destination, and returned correctly, so the trip ends both physically and in the app.

steps.action: **Find a bike and give it a twenty-second check before unlocking.** Tires firm, brakes grab when squeezed, saddle clamp holds, chain seated, no obvious damage. Skip a bad bike; there is always another.
steps.expect: a bike that passes all four checks. Report clearly broken ones in the app, which usually also flags them for others.

steps.action: **Unlock through the app or kiosk.** Scan the QR code or enter the bike number; docked systems release with a click, dockless locks snap open.
steps.expect: the lock opens and the app shows an active trip with the meter running.

steps.action: **Adjust the saddle before riding off.** Correct height puts your leg nearly straight at the pedal's bottom. One lever, two seconds, and it changes the whole ride.
steps.expect: comfortable extension on a test pedal.

steps.action: **Ride by local rules, predictably.** Bike lanes where they exist, hand signals for turns, lights on at night (shared bikes have built-in lights that run automatically), and no phone in hand. `embodied/mobility/cross-a-street` logic applies at every junction, from the saddle.
steps.expect: steady progress; the app's map can wait for red lights.

steps.action: **End the trip correctly. This is where the money leaks.** Docked: push the bike firmly into a dock until the light confirms, and check the app shows the trip closed. Dockless: park within the service zone in a legal spot (not blocking sidewalks, ramps, or doorways), close the lock, and confirm the app ended the trip. ⚠️ *Irreversible in effect:* an unclosed trip keeps billing for hours and an out-of-zone drop incurs fines. The confirmation screen is the actual end of the ride, not the kickstand.
steps.expect: app shows trip ended with a final price that matches expectations.

steps.action: **Note the receipt.** Trip history keeps the record for any dispute.
steps.expect: one closed trip at the advertised rate.

recipes.verification: The trip shows as closed in the app at the expected price, the bike is docked or legally parked with the lock engaged, and you arrived where you intended without traffic incident.

recipes.title: ride a scooter share
recipes.name: ride-a-scooter-share
recipes.goal: A shared electric scooter is unlocked through the app, ridden safely by local road rules, and parked in a legal zone so the trip ends both physically and in the app with no lingering charge.

steps.action: **Open the app and check the scooter before unlocking.** Confirm battery range covers your trip, then squeeze the brake, wiggle the stem for looseness, and glance at the tires. A wobbly stem or dead battery is a different scooter's problem.
steps.expect: a scooter that brakes firmly with a stem that does not shift, and battery range comfortably above your distance.

steps.action: **Scan to unlock.** Point the camera at the QR code on the handlebar or deck, or type the scooter ID.
steps.expect: a beep or light, an audible motor arm, and the app showing an active trip with the meter running.

steps.action: **Fit a helmet if you have one.** Some operators clip a helmet to the scooter; many riders carry their own.
steps.expect: helmet on and strapped before you touch the throttle.

steps.action: **Start moving with one deliberate kick.** These scooters need a manual push before the throttle engages, a safety feature to prevent lurching. Keep both hands on the bars.
steps.expect: the motor picks up smoothly after your first kick; no sudden jolt.

steps.action: **Ride by local rules, predictably.** Use bike lanes or the road where the law directs (sidewalk riding is banned in most cities), signal turns, obey the speed cap the app enforces, and never carry a passenger. Slow zones on the map throttle you down automatically.
steps.expect: steady progress; the app may chime and cut speed in a geofenced slow zone.

steps.action: **End the trip only in a legal parking zone.** This is where money and fines leak. Park upright on its stand, off the pedestrian path, not blocking ramps or doorways, inside the app's permitted zone. Then end the trip and take the required parking photo. ⚠️ *Irreversible in effect:* an out-of-zone or blocked-path parking triggers a fine, and a trip you never end keeps billing.
steps.expect: the app confirms the trip ended, accepts the photo, and shows a final price matching the distance and time.

steps.action: **Confirm the receipt.** Check trip history for the closed ride and its charge.
steps.expect: one closed trip at the expected rate, no ongoing hold.

recipes.verification: The app shows the trip closed at the expected price with the parking photo accepted, the scooter stands upright in a legal zone off the pedestrian path, and you reached your destination without a traffic incident.

recipes.title: ride a subway
recipes.name: ride-a-subway
recipes.goal: You are at street level at your destination, having traveled there by the local subway/metro with the fare correctly paid.

steps.action: **Plan the route.** Use a maps app or the station's route map: identify boarding station, line, direction (by terminus), any transfers, and exit station.
steps.expect: a written/remembered plan: "Line X toward Terminus Y, change at Z, exit at W."

steps.action: **Find and enter the nearest station.** Look for the system's logo/signage at street level.
steps.expect: you are in a station hall with fare gates and a system map that shows your planned line.

steps.action: **Obtain or validate fare.** [BRANCH: tap-to-pay bank card | transit card with balance | ticket machine | transit app QR] At a machine: select destination or fare type, pay, take the ticket/card. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* multi-day passes and non-refundable tickets — confirm fare type before paying.
steps.expect: you hold a valid fare medium for this trip.

steps.action: **Pass the fare gate.** Tap or insert; walk through on green/open.
steps.expect: gate opens and (on card systems) displays balance or fare; if rejected, F1. ![Fare gate: tap the reader, wait for green, walk through](assets/ride-a-subway/fare-gate-flow.svg)

steps.action: **Navigate to the correct platform.** Follow signs for your line *and direction* (terminus name from step 1).
steps.expect: platform signage lists your destination or the correct terminus.

steps.action: **Board the train.** Let passengers exit first; move inside the car.
steps.expect: the in-car line map matches your line; next-station announcements begin.

steps.action: **Monitor stops and transfer if planned.** At a transfer, follow the connecting line's signs (repeat step 5).
steps.expect: each announced station matches your route plan in sequence.

steps.action: **Exit at the destination station.** Leave the train, follow Exit/Way Out signs, tap out where the system requires it.
steps.expect: fare gate opens on tap-out (distance-fare systems) and you reach street level near the target address.

recipes.verification: You are at street level at the destination station, the exit signage names the street/landmark you targeted, and (on tap-out systems) the fare was deducted exactly once.

recipes.title: take a city bus
recipes.name: take-a-city-bus
recipes.goal: Travel to a destination on a scheduled city bus, boarding the right route in the right direction and alighting at the right stop.

steps.action: **Plan route and stop.** Maps app or posted route map: route number, boarding stop, direction (by terminus/major street), alighting stop, and expected arrival time of the next bus.
steps.expect: "Route N toward T, board at S1, alight at S2, next bus ~M min."

steps.action: **Get to the boarding stop on the correct side of the street.** Direction of travel = side of the street; confirm the stop's sign lists your route number.
steps.expect: stop sign shows route N; the maps arrival estimate is counting down.

steps.action: **Identify and hail your bus.** Read the headsign (route number + terminus) as the bus approaches; signal with a raised arm where hailing is customary.
steps.expect: the bus with your route number pulls in and opens its doors.

steps.action: **Board and pay.** [BRANCH: tap card/phone at reader | coins in farebox | show driver a pass] Boarding door varies (front-door in most systems).
steps.expect: reader beeps/green light or driver nods; take a transfer slip if the system issues them.

steps.action: **Take a seat or hold on; track your position.** Follow stops on the in-bus display or your maps app blue dot.
steps.expect: announced/displayed stops match your planned sequence.

steps.action: **Request your stop.** One stop before yours, press the stop-request button or pull the cord.
steps.expect: "stop requested" light/chime turns on.

steps.action: **Alight at the destination stop.** Exit via the rear door where customary; tap out if the system requires it.
steps.expect: you are at S2; street signs match the planned alighting point.

recipes.verification: You are at the planned alighting stop (street signage matches), having paid exactly one fare, within roughly the planned travel time.

recipes.title: take a ferry
recipes.name: take-a-ferry
recipes.goal: You board the correct ferry with the right ticket class (foot passenger or vehicle), ride a comfortable stretch of the crossing, and disembark at your destination port with your belongings and, if applicable, your car.

steps.action: **Confirm the sailing and buy or collect the ticket.** Match the departure time, destination, and passenger-versus-vehicle class on the board or app.
steps.expect: a ticket (paper or mobile) showing today's date, this port, and the correct class.

steps.action: **Go to the correct queue.** Vehicles line up in numbered marshalling lanes by destination; foot passengers use a separate terminal entrance. Do not join the car lanes on foot.
steps.expect: you are in a lane whose sign matches your ticket class and destination.

steps.action: **Clear the ticket and any security check.** Scan or show the ticket; some international or high-security routes check ID and scan bags.
steps.expect: a green light, gate open, or a wave-through from staff.

steps.action: **Board when your class is called.** Vehicles drive on in lane order at crew direction; foot passengers walk the gangway or ramp. Note your deck and, for cars, your exact parking spot and lane. ⚠️ *Irreversible for this sailing:* once vehicle loading closes it does not reopen, and a missed vehicle boarding usually forfeits the fare.
steps.expect: you are aboard, engine off and in gear or parked handbrake-on for a vehicle, on the gangway for foot passengers.

steps.action: **Note where you left the car and lock it.** On vehicle decks you cannot usually return mid-crossing, so take everything you need up to the passenger decks.
steps.expect: car locked, valuables and jacket with you, deck and lane number remembered or photographed.

steps.action: **Choose a seat for the conditions.** For seasickness, sit low and central near the waterline where motion is least, facing forward, near a window with a view of the horizon. Avoid the top decks and the bow in rough weather.
steps.expect: a stable-feeling seat with horizon visibility; less pitching than the extremities.

steps.action: **Watch for the arrival announcement and return to your vehicle only when told.** Crew announce when drivers may go down to the car decks.
steps.expect: the announcement, then an orderly move to your deck; foot passengers gather near the exit.

steps.action: **Disembark at your port.** Vehicles drive off in crew-directed order; foot passengers follow the gangway. Confirm the port name before stepping off a multi-stop route.
steps.expect: you are ashore at your intended destination with all belongings and, if applicable, your car.

recipes.verification: You disembarked at the intended port with all your belongings, your vehicle (if any) drove off with you, and no fare was forfeited to a missed loading window.

recipes.title: take a licensed taxi
recipes.name: take-a-licensed-taxi
recipes.goal: You get into a genuinely licensed taxi, reach your destination by a fair route, pay a metered or pre-agreed fare, and leave with a receipt and all your belongings.

steps.action: **Pick a genuinely licensed taxi.** [BRANCH: taxi rank at a station or airport (safest, ordered queue) | flag a marked cab on the street | phone or app dispatch]
steps.expect: an official livery, visible license/medallion number, and a driver ID displayed inside.

steps.action: **Confirm it is real before getting in.** Licensed cabs have a company name, plate, and a working meter; be wary of unmarked cars touting for fares at airports.
steps.expect: a meter visible on the dash and identification on show.

steps.action: **State the destination and agree the basis.** Say the address or landmark; confirm "on the meter" or, where flat rates are normal (some airports), agree the fixed price first.
steps.expect: driver acknowledges the destination and either starts the meter or states the flat fare.

steps.action: **Watch the meter start correctly.** It should begin at the standard flag-fall, not a random high number, and run only while moving or per the local tariff.
steps.expect: meter reads the known starting fare and increments sensibly.

steps.action: **Keep light route awareness.** Glance at your maps app; a fair route is roughly the app's route. Traffic detours are normal, but a wildly longer path is not.
steps.expect: the cab broadly follows a sensible route toward your destination.

steps.action: **Arrive and read the final fare.** Note the meter total plus any legitimate surcharges (night, luggage, airport), which should be posted.
steps.expect: a total consistent with the meter and any posted extras.

steps.action: **Pay and get a receipt.** Pay by the agreed method; ask for a printed or written receipt showing fare, date, and the cab number. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* cash handed over is gone. Count your change before stepping out.
steps.expect: correct change or card charge, and a receipt in hand.

steps.action: **Do a seat sweep before closing the door.** Check the seat and footwell for phone, bag, and documents.
steps.expect: you are on the pavement with every item you arrived with.

recipes.verification: You reached your destination, paid a fare consistent with the meter or agreed price, hold a receipt with the cab number, and have all your belongings.

recipes.title: take a long distance bus
recipes.name: take-a-long-distance-bus
recipes.goal: You board the correct long-distance coach with a valid ticket, stow your large luggage in the hold, ride to your destination without missing a required transfer or over-staying a rest stop, and collect your bags at the end.

steps.action: **Get to the right terminal and gate.** Coach terminals have many bays; find your operator's desk or the departures board and note the bay number.
steps.expect: a bay/stand number matching your departure time and operator.

steps.action: **Have your ticket ready in the accepted form.** Mobile QR, printout, or a collected paper ticket; know which your operator wants.
steps.expect: ticket open and scannable, plus ID if the ticket is named.

steps.action: **Arrive at the bay early.** Be there 20 to 30 minutes before departure; coaches board and load luggage on a tight schedule and may pull away on time.
steps.expect: you are queuing at the correct bay before the coach doors open.

steps.action: **Hand large bags to the hold.** Give big luggage to the driver or handler for the underfloor hold; keep valuables, documents, and medication in your carry-on. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a bag in the hold is out of your reach until the destination. Do not pack anything you will need en route.
steps.expect: your hold bag is loaded, ideally with a tag or claim check.

steps.action: **Board and confirm your seat.** Take your reserved seat or any free one if unreserved; keep the carry-on at your feet or overhead in view.
steps.expect: seated, carry-on with you, ticket already scanned.

steps.action: **Note the schedule and any transfer.** Confirm whether the route is direct or has a connection, and where.
steps.expect: you know your arrival time and any change point.

steps.action: **Practice rest-stop discipline.** At breaks, note the exact departure time the driver gives and the coach's plate or bay; be back five minutes early.
steps.expect: you re-board the same coach before it leaves; nobody is left behind.

steps.action: **Alight and reclaim hold luggage.** At your stop, collect your bag from the hold before the coach moves on.
steps.expect: you have your carry-on and hold bag, and the claim check matches.

recipes.verification: You are at your destination stop with both your carry-on and your hold luggage, having made any required transfer, and your ticket was accepted on board.

recipes.title: take an intercity train
recipes.name: take-an-intercity-train
recipes.goal: You board the correct intercity train with a valid ticket and any required seat reservation, ride to your destination, and get off at the right stop with your luggage.

steps.action: **Book the ticket and class.** Choose date, time, and class (standard vs first is mostly space and quiet, not speed). Note whether the fare is flexible or a cheaper fixed-train ticket.
steps.expect: a ticket showing train number, date, class, and departure time.

steps.action: **Add a seat reservation if the service needs one.** On reserved trains, a ticket alone may not grant a seat.
steps.expect: a coach and seat number on the ticket, or explicit "unreserved" wording.

steps.action: **Arrive with a buffer, not a sprint.** Get to the station 20 to 30 minutes early; big stations are large and platforms are assigned late.
steps.expect: you are inside the station with time to read the board calmly.

steps.action: **Read the departure board for YOUR train.** Match by departure time and train number, not just destination; several trains may share a destination. Note the platform (track) when it appears. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a fixed-train ticket is void if you board the wrong departure. Confirm train number against your ticket before boarding.
steps.expect: your train's row shows a platform number and "on time" or a delay.

steps.action: **Go to the platform and find your coach.** Coach numbers are marked on the train side and often on platform floor markers; walk to your coach zone before the train fills.
steps.expect: you are standing at the marker for your coach number.

steps.action: **Board and stow luggage.** Large bags go on end-of-coach racks or overhead; keep valuables with you.
steps.expect: seated in your reserved seat (or any free seat if unreserved), bag stowed and in view or tagged.

steps.action: **Ride and track your stop.** Watch announcements and the moving map; intercity stops can be brief, one to two minutes.
steps.expect: you recognize your stop one station ahead and gather your bags before arrival.

steps.action: **Alight promptly with everything.** Step off at the door, mind the platform gap.
steps.expect: you are on the correct platform with all luggage, train doors closing behind you.

recipes.verification: You are at your destination station on the correct platform, your ticket was accepted by any check en route, and all your luggage is with you.

recipes.title: transport a bike on a car rack
recipes.name: transport-a-bike-on-a-car-rack
recipes.goal: Carry a bike on a car rack securely while keeping the vehicle, lights, plate, bike, and road users safe.

steps.action: **Pick the correct rack type.** Use a hitch, trunk, roof, or spare-tire rack only as designed for the vehicle and bike weight.
steps.expect: the rack manual permits this vehicle and bike combination.

steps.action: **Install the empty rack first.** Tighten hitch bolts, trunk straps, roof clamps, or spare-tire mounts according to the rack instructions.
steps.expect: the empty rack does not wobble beyond normal flex.

steps.action: **Prepare the bike.** Remove bottles, bags, computers, loose lights, child seats, and batteries if the e-bike manual allows removal.
steps.expect: nothing loose can fly off.

steps.action: **Load the bike in the intended position.** Lift with help if needed and place tires, frame, or fork exactly where the rack supports them.
steps.expect: the bike rests on the load-bearing parts, not on cables or fenders.

steps.action: **Secure frame and wheels.** [BRANCH: platform rack | hanging rack | roof rack] clamp the frame or tire, strap both wheels, and add anti-sway straps where provided.
steps.expect: the bike cannot roll, swing, or bounce free.

steps.action: **Protect contact points.** Pad frame rub areas and keep pedals, bars, and wheels from touching the vehicle or another bike.
steps.expect: normal vibration will not grind paint or bend parts.

steps.action: **Check plate and light visibility.** Confirm brake lights, turn signals, and license plate remain visible, or install an auxiliary light or plate board where required.
steps.expect: following drivers and enforcement can see required signals.

steps.action: **Do a shake and clearance test.** Push the bike and rack, then check garage height, hatch clearance, exhaust heat, and rear-camera obstruction.
steps.expect: movement is controlled and known clearances are safe.

steps.action: **Recheck after driving briefly.** Stop after 5-10 minutes, then retighten straps and clamps.
steps.expect: settling is corrected before highway speed or long distance.

recipes.verification: The rack is tight, each bike's frame and wheels are secured, lights and plate are visible or legally supplemented, and straps remain tight after a short recheck stop.

recipes.title: use a bike lane safely
recipes.name: use-a-bike-lane-safely
recipes.goal: Ride in a bike lane predictably while managing doors, junctions, turning vehicles, pedestrians, and other riders.

steps.action: **Enter in the legal direction.** Ride with traffic unless the lane is explicitly marked two-way.
steps.expect: signs, arrows, or lane markings match your direction.

steps.action: **Scan before merging in.** Check behind, signal, and merge into the bike lane when there is a safe gap.
steps.expect: nearby riders and drivers can predict your move.

steps.action: **Stay out of the door zone.** Keep distance from parked cars, especially where doors can open into the lane.
steps.expect: you have room to react if a door opens.

steps.action: **Signal turns and lane exits.** Use hand signals early, then return hands to brakes before turning or slowing.
steps.expect: other road users see your intention before you move.

steps.action: **Slow at junctions.** Watch for right-turning or left-turning vehicles crossing the bike lane, and make eye contact only as a bonus, not a guarantee.
steps.expect: you can stop if a driver turns across you.

steps.action: **Yield where required.** [BRANCH: pedestrians | buses | turning vehicles] obey signs, signals, and crosswalk rules even when the lane continues visually.
steps.expect: conflicts are resolved by law and caution, not speed.

steps.action: **Pass other riders carefully.** Call "passing left" or ring once, pass with space, and return smoothly.
steps.expect: the other rider does not swerve from surprise.

steps.action: **Be visible in low light.** Use front white and rear red lights, avoid blind spots, and do not ride beside large vehicles at intersections.
steps.expect: drivers and pedestrians have a better chance to detect you.

steps.action: **Leave the lane when it is unsafe.** Merge into the traffic lane if legally allowed and necessary to avoid debris, doors, construction, or blocked bike lanes.
steps.expect: you avoid hazards without sudden swerves.

recipes.verification: You complete the bike-lane segment in the correct direction with predictable signals, safe spacing from doors, and controlled behavior at every junction.

recipes.title: use contactless payment on transit
recipes.name: use-contactless-payment-on-transit
recipes.goal: Pay for a transit ride with a contactless card, phone wallet, or wearable while avoiding fare errors, duplicate charges, and penalty fares.

steps.action: **Choose one payment token.** Pick one physical card, phone wallet card, or wearable and use it for the whole trip.
steps.expect: you know exactly what will be tapped at every reader.

steps.action: **Confirm fare rules.** Check whether the system charges flat fare, distance fare, daily cap, weekly cap, or transfer discount.
steps.expect: you know whether a tap out or same-token transfer is required.

steps.action: **Check balance or credit.** Make sure the account can cover the maximum fare or preauthorization.
steps.expect: the payment method is unlikely to be declined at the gate.

steps.action: **Tap in deliberately.** Hold the chosen token flat on the reader until it confirms.
steps.expect: the reader shows accepted, green light, beep, or gate opens.

steps.action: **Keep the token separate.** Do not wave a wallet with multiple contactless cards near the reader.
steps.expect: only the intended card or device was charged.

steps.action: **Ride and transfer with the same token.** [BRANCH: transfer within system | exit and re-enter] tap the same token so caps and transfers connect.
steps.expect: the system treats the ride as one linked journey where eligible.

steps.action: **Tap out if required.** At the destination, use the same token at the exit reader before leaving the paid area. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* skipping a required tap out can charge the maximum fare, so confirm the exit reader accepted before walking away.
steps.expect: the reader confirms exit or fare completion.

steps.action: **Check charges later.** Review the transit account, bank feed, or wallet history after posting.
steps.expect: charges match the fare, cap, or maximum-fare correction rules.

steps.action: **Dispute errors promptly.** Use the agency fare account or support form with date, station, route, and token type.
steps.expect: a case number or correction request is recorded.

recipes.verification: The same accepted payment token was used for every required tap, the ride completed without fare inspection issue, and the posted charge or cap is explainable.

recipes.title: use cruise control
recipes.name: use-cruise-control
recipes.goal: Use cruise control on suitable roads while staying responsible for speed, steering, braking, and traffic conditions.

steps.action: **Choose the right road.** Use cruise control on open highways or steady roads, not in city traffic, heavy congestion, construction, rain, snow, ice, or winding roads.
steps.expect: the vehicle can hold speed without frequent braking.

steps.action: **Reach a legal steady speed.** Accelerate manually to a safe speed at or below the limit.
steps.expect: traffic flow and road conditions support that speed.

steps.action: **Turn cruise on.** Press the cruise or driver-assist power button without taking eyes off the road for long.
steps.expect: the dashboard shows cruise is available or armed.

steps.action: **Set the speed.** Press SET when the car is stable in the lane.
steps.expect: the vehicle maintains the current speed without your foot on the accelerator.

steps.action: **Keep your foot ready.** Rest your right foot where you can brake quickly, not tucked away or crossed.
steps.expect: you can cancel immediately if traffic changes.

steps.action: **Adjust in small increments.** Use plus or minus controls for 1 mph or 1 km/h changes, or hold only when you intentionally want larger changes.
steps.expect: speed changes smoothly.

steps.action: **Cancel before conflict.** [BRANCH: brake | cancel button | clutch] brake, press cancel, or depress clutch in a manual car before traffic, curves, exits, or poor traction.
steps.expect: you regain full manual speed control.

steps.action: **Use resume only when still safe.** Press RES only after confirming the saved speed is legal and appropriate for current traffic.
steps.expect: the car returns to the prior set speed without surprising you.

steps.action: **Stay engaged.** Scan mirrors, maintain lane position, and monitor speed downhill because some systems may exceed the set speed.
steps.expect: cruise assists speed, but you remain the driver.

recipes.verification: Cruise control is used only on a suitable road, maintains a legal set speed, and is canceled before traffic, weather, or road geometry requires manual control.

recipes.title: use park and ride
recipes.name: use-park-and-ride
recipes.goal: Park at a designated lot and transfer to transit without missing the trip, overpaying, or violating parking rules.

steps.action: **Find the official lot.** Use the transit agency page or station map, not just a map pin.
steps.expect: you know the lot entrance, transit stop, and operating hours.

steps.action: **Check parking rules.** Read fees, time limits, permit rules, overnight rules, height limits, and enforcement hours.
steps.expect: your planned stay is allowed.

steps.action: **Compare total cost.** Add parking fee, transit fare, and any fuel or toll savings.
steps.expect: park-and-ride is cheaper or easier than driving all the way.

steps.action: **Plan arrival time.** Add time for traffic near the lot, finding a space, paying, walking, and buying fare.
steps.expect: you arrive at least one departure before the last acceptable one.

steps.action: **Park legally.** Choose a marked space, avoid reserved areas, and note the level, row, or landmark.
steps.expect: the car is within lines and not in a restricted zone.

steps.action: **Pay for parking if required.** [BRANCH: meter | app | kiosk | included] enter plate or space number carefully and save proof.
steps.expect: the paid time covers your whole planned absence.

steps.action: **Secure the car.** Remove visible valuables, close windows, lock doors, and keep the parking proof with you or in the app.
steps.expect: nothing valuable is visible from outside.

steps.action: **Reach the platform or stop.** Follow signs from the lot to the correct route and direction.
steps.expect: you are waiting at the correct boarding point before departure.

steps.action: **Check return access.** Confirm the last return transit option and whether the lot gate closes.
steps.expect: you know how you will get back to the car.

recipes.verification: The car is legally parked and paid through the planned return time, and you are at the correct transit stop before the needed departure.

recipes.title: validate a transit ticket
recipes.name: validate-a-transit-ticket
recipes.goal: Activate a transit ticket correctly so it is valid for inspection until the trip is complete.

steps.action: **Read the ticket instructions.** Look for "validate before boarding," "tap in," "stamp," "activate," or "not valid until."
steps.expect: you know whether action is required before travel.

steps.action: **Find the validator.** [BRANCH: station | platform | onboard] look near entrances, platform ramps, bus doors, tram doors, or fare gates.
steps.expect: you can see a machine, gate reader, or app activation button.

steps.action: **Validate before the required point.** If the system requires pre-boarding validation, do it before stepping onto the vehicle.
steps.expect: the ticket is active before inspection can occur.

steps.action: **Insert, tap, scan, or activate.** Use the arrow direction for paper tickets, tap the card flat, scan the code, or press activate in the app.
steps.expect: the validator beeps, stamps, opens, or shows a green check.

steps.action: **Check the confirmation.** Read the timestamp, zone, remaining rides, or app countdown.
steps.expect: the visible proof matches this trip.

steps.action: **Handle transfer rules.** If transfers are included, note the expiration time or required tap-out.
steps.expect: you know whether another validation is needed later.

steps.action: **Keep the ticket until exit.** Store paper or card where you can reach it for inspectors and exit gates.
steps.expect: proof of payment is available throughout the ride.

steps.action: **Do not validate twice unless required.** Double stamping can consume another ride or start a new fare.
steps.expect: only the required ride or time window is used.

steps.action: **Tap out if the system requires it.** [BRANCH: tap-out required | no tap-out] use the exit validator for distance fares; skip if flat fare rules say no.
steps.expect: fare is closed correctly and overcharges are avoided.

steps.action: **Keep proof after leaving if needed.** Hold the receipt or used ticket until beyond the paid area.
steps.expect: a late inspection or exit check can still be answered.

recipes.verification: The ticket, card, or app shows a current validated ride or open paid journey, and you still possess it until exiting the system.

recipes.title: apply for a travel visa
recipes.name: apply-for-a-travel-visa
recipes.goal: Submit a travel visa application with the right documents early enough to reduce the risk of denial, delay, or wasted travel costs.

steps.action: **Check requirements early.** Use the official destination government site, not ads or third-party summaries, to confirm whether you need a visa.
steps.expect: visa type, eligibility, fee, and processing estimate are known.

steps.action: **Confirm passport validity.** Check blank page rules and how many months of validity are required after entry or departure.
steps.expect: your passport meets the stated rule or you know it must be renewed first.

steps.action: **Build the document pack.** Gather passport, photo, application form, itinerary, accommodation, funds proof, employment or school proof, invitation letter, and travel insurance if required.
steps.expect: every required item is present in the requested format.

steps.action: **Avoid non-refundable bookings when possible.** Use refundable reservations or hold off until the visa is issued if the rules allow.
steps.expect: a denial or delay would not waste major prepaid costs.

steps.action: **Complete the application carefully.** Match names, passport number, dates, addresses, and trip purpose exactly to documents.
steps.expect: the form has no mismatched identity or travel details.

steps.action: **Book the appointment or mailing slot.** [BRANCH: consulate appointment | visa center | mail-in] choose the required submission route and calendar it with travel time.
steps.expect: you have a confirmation number and deadline.

steps.action: **Attend or submit with copies.** Bring originals, copies, photos, payment proof, and appointment confirmation; keep tracking for mailed passports.
steps.expect: the application is accepted for processing or you receive a clear missing-item notice.

steps.action: **Monitor processing.** Track status only through official tools and avoid buying final tickets until the visa and passport are returned.
steps.expect: you know whether the application is pending, approved, refused, or needs more documents.

steps.action: **Verify the issued visa.** Check name, passport number, entries, validity dates, duration of stay, and work or study restrictions.
steps.expect: errors are caught before departure.

recipes.verification: The visa application is accepted or issued, the passport and visa details match your trip, and no non-refundable major booking depends on an unissued visa.

recipes.title: avoid a tourist scam
recipes.name: avoid-a-tourist-scam
recipes.goal: Recognize and avoid common tourist scams while keeping money, documents, and attention under your control.

steps.action: **Set a refusal script.** Use a calm "No, thank you" and keep walking without debate.
steps.expect: you have a default response before pressure starts.

steps.action: **Treat urgency as a warning.** Reject offers that require deciding now, following someone, or handing over money before seeing terms.
steps.expect: the too-good deal slows down or disappears.

steps.action: **Use official taxi and ride channels.** Choose marked taxi stands, app rides, hotel-called cars, or transit; confirm meter use or fixed fare before moving.
steps.expect: the fare method is agreed before the ride begins.

steps.action: **Keep documents out of casual hands.** Show ID only to legitimate officials, hotels, rental agencies, or ticket checks; do not let a stranger "inspect" a passport or wallet.
steps.expect: your critical documents remain physically controlled.

steps.action: **Watch the distraction setup.** If someone spills, bumps, asks for a photo, drops jewelry, ties a bracelet, or creates a crowd, protect pockets and bags first.
steps.expect: attention returns to valuables before a second person can act.

steps.action: **Verify tickets and tours at the source.** Buy through the venue, official app, licensed booth, or a reputable platform with reviews and cancellation terms.
steps.expect: ticket validity can be checked before payment.

steps.action: **Control payment exposure.** Count cash privately, cover PIN entry, keep the card in sight, and decline currency conversion at card terminals when your card offers a fair rate.
steps.expect: payment happens once, in the expected currency.

steps.action: **Walk away from forced gifts.** Bracelets, roses, CDs, petitions, tea invitations, and "free" photos can become demands for payment.
steps.expect: no object or obligation is accepted by accident.

steps.action: **Debrief after any strange contact.** Step into a shop, hotel, or busy safe area and check wallet, phone, passport, and bag zippers.
steps.expect: missing items are noticed quickly enough to act.

recipes.verification: You complete the outing with valuables, documents, and payment cards accounted for, and any paid service has a verifiable official source or agreed price.

recipes.title: avoid pickpockets
recipes.name: avoid-pickpockets
recipes.goal: Wallet, phone, passport, and cards are carried so they are harder to steal in crowded travel areas and easier to recover from if something goes missing.

steps.action: **Reduce what you carry.** Leave spare cards, excess cash, and nonessential documents locked at lodging if safe.
steps.expect: losing the day bag would not remove every resource.

steps.action: **Move valuables to controlled locations.** Put phone and wallet in zipped front pockets, inner jacket pockets, or a crossbody bag worn in front.
steps.expect: valuables are visible or touch-detectable by you.

steps.action: **Use a decoy wallet if useful.** Carry a small wallet with a little cash and expired or low-risk cards in an accessible pocket.
steps.expect: essential cards and passport remain elsewhere.

steps.action: **Secure the main bag.** Keep zippers closed, pulls forward, and the bag on the front of your body in crowds.
steps.expect: no pocket or zipper is open behind you.

steps.action: **Recognize crowded-risk zones.** Increase attention at train doors, escalators, markets, tourist viewpoints, street performances, and ticket machines.
steps.expect: your hand naturally checks the bag when bodies press close.

steps.action: **Watch for distraction plays.** [BRANCH: spill or bump | petition, photo, or commotion] step aside with your bag held, or keep walking and decline while checking valuables.
steps.expect: attention stays on possessions, not just the distraction.

steps.action: **Handle payments deliberately.** Take out only the card or cash needed, then close the pocket or bag before moving away.
steps.expect: money is not exposed in a crowd.

steps.action: **Respond quickly if something is missing.** Move to a safe spot, lock phone or cards, contact bank or lodging, and file a report if documents are gone. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* chasing a suspected thief can escalate danger, so prioritize account locks, location safety, and official help.
steps.expect: loss response starts without physical confrontation.

recipes.verification: Before entering a crowd, all essential valuables are zipped, front-carried, split across locations, and no phone or wallet is in a rear pocket or open bag.

recipes.title: board a cruise
recipes.name: board-a-cruise
recipes.goal: Board a cruise ship with documents accepted, luggage handed off correctly, onboard account active, and muster requirements completed.

steps.action: **Complete online check-in.** Upload required identity, payment, photo, emergency contact, and arrival-time information before embarkation day.
steps.expect: the cruise app or portal shows ready-to-board documents.

steps.action: **Tag checked luggage.** Attach cruise luggage tags with cabin number, ship, sailing date, and passenger name before reaching the port.
steps.expect: porters can route bags to the correct stateroom.
