steps.action: **Arrive inside the assigned window.** Use the correct terminal and keep documents out before dropping luggage.
steps.expect: staff accept your arrival time and direct you to security or check-in.

steps.action: **Hand bags only to official porters.** Confirm ship name and tip locally if appropriate, keeping documents, medication, valuables, and first-day essentials with you.
steps.expect: checked bags leave with tagged port staff and your carry-on stays with you.

steps.action: **Clear security and document check.** Present ID, boarding pass, health paperwork, and any minors' consent documents.
steps.expect: you receive a key card, wearable, or app status authorizing boarding.

steps.action: **Complete muster instructions.** Watch the safety briefing, visit the assigned muster station if required, and scan in.
steps.expect: the app, crew, or station scan marks muster complete.

steps.action: **Verify the cabin and onboard account.** Check key access, dining time, packages, shore excursions, and bag delivery status.
steps.expect: the cruise account and stateroom setup match your booking.

recipes.verification: You are physically aboard, your onboard account works, muster is marked complete, cabin access works, and checked luggage is delivered or formally tracked by guest services.

recipes.title: board a plane efficiently
recipes.name: board-a-plane-efficiently
recipes.goal: Board a plane smoothly, keep the aisle moving, and reach your seat with essentials accessible.

steps.action: **Check the boarding group system.** Read the boarding pass and gate screen for group, zone, row, or priority rules.
steps.expect: you know when to approach without blocking earlier groups.

steps.action: **Prepare before your group is called.** Put ID away if no longer needed, hold boarding pass ready, and move headphones, water, medicine, charger, and layers into the personal item.
steps.expect: you will not unpack in the aisle.

steps.action: **Decide on gate-checking early.** [BRANCH: keep carry-on | gate-check carry-on] if overhead space looks tight and the airline offers free gate-check, remove valuables and batteries first.
steps.expect: any checked bag contains nothing critical.

steps.action: **Join only when called.** Stand near the lane only for your group and keep the walkway clear.
steps.expect: the scanner line moves without crowding the gate.

steps.action: **Scan and clear the doorway.** Board pass-first, then walk onto the jet bridge without stopping to repack.
steps.expect: passengers behind you keep moving.

steps.action: **Move to your row with the bag in front.** Carry the roller low and controlled, backpack forward or in hand, and avoid hitting seated passengers.
steps.expect: you reach the row without snagging armrests or people.

steps.action: **Stow fast.** Place the roller wheels-first or as crew directs, use nearby space only if your row is full, and put the personal item under the seat.
steps.expect: bags are placed in one motion and the aisle opens.

steps.action: **Step into the row before organizing.** Let others pass, then settle seat belt, phone, book, and headphones.
steps.expect: the aisle is clear while you arrange yourself.

steps.action: **Sit down and stay aware.** Keep feet and straps out of the aisle and listen for crew instructions about bags or seats.
steps.expect: boarding continues around you with minimal friction.

recipes.verification: You are seated in the correct seat with required items accessible, carry-on safely stowed, and no critical item left in a gate-checked bag.

recipes.title: book a flight
recipes.name: book-a-flight
recipes.goal: A flight is booked for the right person, dates, and route, at an acceptable price, with the confirmation and ticket number in hand.

steps.action: **Search broad first.** A meta-search (flexible-dates view on) across the route: see the price landscape by day and carrier.
steps.expect: you know the cheap days, typical price, and which airlines fly it.

steps.action: **Select a candidate itinerary and scrutinize it.** Layover length (90 min+ for international connections; tight domestic connections fail on any delay), airport changes within a city (a trap), arrival time vs. your ground plans, and the *fare class's* baggage and change rules.
steps.expect: an itinerary you'd accept even on a mildly bad day, with known bag allowance.

steps.action: **Price the same itinerary on the airline's own site.** Often equal or near it — and booking direct makes every future change/cancellation far easier than through an intermediary.
steps.expect: a direct price within a few dollars of the meta-search; if the OTA is dramatically cheaper, read its change-policy fine print before being tempted.

steps.action: **Enter passenger details against the passport, character by character.** Name spelling, birth date, passport number where asked. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* name errors can mean denied boarding or paid correction — verify each field against the physical document, not memory.
steps.expect: details matching the document exactly.

steps.action: **Decline or accept extras deliberately.** Seats, bags, insurance — priced à la carte. Add checked bags *now* if you'll need them (airport prices are punitive); skip seat fees on couples-who-can-sit-apart; consider insurance only if you understand what it actually covers.
steps.expect: extras chosen on purpose, not by default checkbox.

steps.action: **Review the final screen fully, then pay.** Route, dates, times (AM/PM!), passengers, total. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* most cheap fares are nonrefundable past the cooling-off window — this screen is the commitment.
steps.expect: payment accepted; confirmation page with a booking reference (PNR).

steps.action: **Capture the confirmation.** Email with PNR and the 13-digit e-ticket number saved; add flights to your calendar with the airport and terminal.
steps.expect: booking retrievable on the airline's site with PNR + name (test it once now).

recipes.verification: The booking retrieves on the airline's own site showing correct names, route, and dates; the e-ticket number is saved; bags you'll need are attached to the fare; and the calendar holds the flights with times cross-checked AM/PM.

recipes.title: book a hotel
recipes.name: book-a-hotel
recipes.goal: A hotel room is booked for the right city, dates, and party — at a location that serves the trip — with cancellation terms you chose on purpose and the confirmation saved.

steps.action: **Fix the location target before the hotel.** Map your trip's anchor points (venue, office, station); the right hotel is *near your days*, not near the city's name.
steps.expect: a target area drawn on the map view of any booking engine.

steps.action: **Search with real filters.** Dates, party size, then the honest filters: your price band, review score ≥8-ish, and the needs from preconditions (breakfast, parking, twin beds).
steps.expect: a shortlist of 3–5 plausible properties inside the target area.

steps.action: **Read reviews for patterns, not verdicts.** Skim recent reviews for repeated specifics ("street noise", "great staff", "photos flatter the rooms") — one grump is noise, a chorus is signal. Check the photos' dates/room types against what you'd book.
steps.expect: a top choice whose weaknesses you know and accept.

steps.action: **Compare the booking channels for that hotel.** The OTA price vs. the hotel's own site (often matches, sometimes beats with perks; and direct bookings resolve problems far better). Watch the total: taxes, city fees, and "resort fees" land at checkout or at the desk.
steps.expect: the true total price known on your chosen channel.

steps.action: **Choose the cancellation class deliberately.** [BRANCH: refundable rate (costs a bit more, cancels free until a date) | nonrefundable (cheaper, locked)] Any trip with moving parts (flights, health, weather season) argues refundable.
steps.expect: the cancellation deadline and penalty stated and screenshot-worthy.

steps.action: **Book: enter guest name(s) matching ID, arrival time estimate, requests (high floor, quiet side) in the notes.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* nonrefundable rates commit at this click — recheck dates (check-*in* vs check-*out* off-by-one is the classic) and the room type.
steps.expect: confirmation screen + email with a confirmation number.

steps.action: **Save and integrate.** Confirmation number and address into your trip notes/calendar; note check-in/out times and the front desk's hours if arriving late (warn them for late arrivals — unclaimed rooms can be released).
steps.expect: the booking retrievable; late arrival flagged if relevant.

recipes.verification: The confirmation (number + email) shows correct dates, guest names, room type, and total; the cancellation deadline is in your calendar if refundable; and the hotel's location actually serves the trip's mapped anchors.

recipes.title: book a last minute trip
recipes.name: book-a-last-minute-trip
recipes.goal: Book a last-minute trip that is legal, affordable enough, logistically coherent, and not undone by missing documents or impossible timing.

steps.action: **Check document feasibility first.** Verify passport validity, visa needs, vaccination or entry forms, and ID rules before searching fares deeply.
steps.expect: only legal destinations remain on the list.

steps.action: **Set hard constraints.** Define latest departure, latest arrival, maximum price, minimum hotel standard, and cancellation tolerance.
steps.expect: search choices have clear stop rules.

steps.action: **Search bundled logistics.** Price flight or train, lodging, airport transfers, arrival time, and first meal together rather than as separate bargains.
steps.expect: the total trip cost and first-night plan are visible.

steps.action: **Prefer direct and refundable where possible.** Book direct with airlines, hotels, and major operators when disruption help matters.
steps.expect: changes can be handled by the provider responsible for the service.

steps.action: **Confirm location details before paying.** Check hotel address, late check-in, airport distance, local transit end times, and neighborhood safety at arrival hour.
steps.expect: the arrival path works after delays or after dark.

steps.action: **Pay after one final identity review.** Match names, dates, airports, baggage, and room dates, then complete the purchases.
steps.expect: confirmations arrive for transport and lodging with correct details.

steps.action: **Build the departure checklist.** Add check-in deadline, packing minimums, chargers, medication, documents, weather layer, and transport to the airport or station.
steps.expect: the trip can start without another planning session.

recipes.verification: You have valid entry documents, confirmed transport and lodging, a feasible arrival plan, correct traveler details, and a packed essentials list before leaving.

recipes.title: book a multi city trip
recipes.name: book-a-multi-city-trip
recipes.goal: Book a multi-city itinerary whose flights, ground transfers, dates, baggage rules, and connection protections work as one coherent trip.

steps.action: **Map the trip as segments.** Write each city pair, travel date, airport options, and must-arrive-by commitment in a list.
steps.expect: every movement between overnight cities has an assigned transport need.

steps.action: **Price the protected version first.** Search the airline or alliance multi-city tool for flights on one ticket where missed connections would be protected.
steps.expect: you know the price and schedule for the low-risk baseline.

steps.action: **Compare separate tickets deliberately.** Price one-ways, trains, and low-cost carriers, adding baggage, airport transfers, and overnight buffers.
steps.expect: any savings are visible after real fees and buffer costs.

steps.action: **Check airport and visa traps.** Confirm airport changes within cities, Schengen or transit visa implications, overnight layovers, and minimum connection times.
steps.expect: no segment depends on an impossible terminal change or illegal transit.

steps.action: **Build the calendar before paying.** Put each flight or train in local time with airport codes, hotel nights, and transfer windows.
steps.expect: date-line shifts, red-eyes, and missing hotel nights are visible.

steps.action: **Review and purchase segment by segment.** Match traveler names to passports, verify baggage, seat needs, and refund/change rules, then pay only after the full route still works.
steps.expect: confirmations exist for all paid segments and none conflict.

steps.action: **Store the master itinerary.** Save booking references, ticket numbers, train PNRs, hotel nights, and emergency alternates in one offline note.
steps.expect: the trip can be reconstructed without email search or data service.

recipes.verification: Every city-to-city movement has a confirmation, local-time calendar entry, baggage plan, and legal transit path, and all names and dates match the passport and intended route.

recipes.title: ask for a room upgrade
recipes.name: ask-for-a-room-upgrade
recipes.goal: You ask for a better hotel room politely and increase your chance of receiving a useful upgrade without paying unexpected fees.

steps.action: **Check availability before arrival.** Look at the hotel's same-night room inventory and price differences.
steps.expect: you know which room categories appear available and what paid upgrades cost.

steps.action: **Join or add loyalty details.** Attach your loyalty number and note any elite status or direct-booking benefits.
steps.expect: the reservation shows your membership.

steps.action: **Choose the right timing.** Ask through chat shortly before arrival or at check-in when staff can see actual inventory.
steps.expect: a staff member can evaluate available rooms.

steps.action: **Make a specific, courteous request.** Ask for a quiet room, higher floor, view, larger room, or early check-in rather than a vague "best room."
steps.expect: the agent understands the upgrade that matters to you.

steps.action: **Disclose your constraints.** If you cannot pay, say you would appreciate any complimentary option; if willing, ask the exact upgrade price before accepting.
steps.expect: the offer is clearly free or priced.

steps.action: **Confirm the final assignment.** Verify room type, bed count, fees, lounge/breakfast access, and checkout time.
steps.expect: key packet or app check-in shows the upgraded room without surprise charges.

steps.action: **Inspect the room promptly.** Check bed type, noise, cleanliness, and promised features before unpacking.
steps.expect: the room matches the accepted upgrade or you can return to the desk quickly.

recipes.verification: The hotel app, key packet, or folio shows the accepted room assignment and any upgrade charge is either zero or at or below your pre-set cap.

recipes.title: avoid hidden travel fees
recipes.name: avoid-hidden-travel-fees
recipes.goal: You identify and avoid avoidable travel fees before booking, so the trip's final cost matches your budget.

steps.action: **Define the services you actually need.** List bags, seats, meals, Wi-Fi, parking, resort amenities, insurance, child seats, tolls, and cancellation flexibility.
steps.expect: a fee checklist tailored to the trip.

steps.action: **Open the final checkout price.** Do not rely on search-result prices; proceed to the last review page before payment.
steps.expect: taxes, mandatory fees, and add-ons are visible.

steps.action: **Check airline extras.** Review carry-on, checked bag, seat assignment, boarding, change, and payment-card fees.
steps.expect: the flight cost includes every required passenger service.

steps.action: **Check lodging extras.** Look for resort/destination fees, cleaning fees, deposits, parking, breakfast, occupancy taxes, early/late fees, and local currency charges.
steps.expect: the stay cost reflects mandatory and likely optional fees.

steps.action: **Check ground transport extras.** For rental cars, inspect insurance, fuel, toll transponder, mileage, young-driver, additional-driver, and one-way fees.
steps.expect: the transport cost reflects pickup-counter charges.

steps.action: **Remove unwanted add-ons.** Decline duplicate insurance, charity donations, priority services, subscriptions, and preselected extras you do not need.
steps.expect: checkout shows only intentional purchases.

steps.action: **Use benefits that waive fees.** Apply loyalty status, eligible credit card, corporate code, or membership that legitimately covers bags, insurance, breakfast, or cancellation.
steps.expect: waived fees appear in the quote or benefit terms.

steps.action: **Confirm before payment.** Compare the final amount against your budget and save the fee breakdown. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* after payment, some fees and fares may be nonrefundable.
steps.expect: a final checkout total at or below your cap.

recipes.verification: Before purchase, the saved checkout pages show the final trip components at or below budget with all required fees included and unwanted add-ons removed.

recipes.title: book a cheaper connecting itinerary
recipes.name: book-a-cheaper-connecting-itinerary
recipes.goal: You book a connecting flight itinerary that saves money without creating an unrealistic transfer, missed-connection exposure, or baggage problem.

steps.action: **Search nonstop and connecting options.** Compare official airline sites and reputable search tools for the same dates and nearby airports.
steps.expect: a baseline nonstop price and several connecting alternatives.

steps.action: **Calculate the all-in cost.** Add bags, seat selection, overnight hotel, meals, airport transfers, and extra time value.
steps.expect: a true savings amount versus the nonstop or simpler itinerary.

steps.action: **Check connection quality.** Verify layover length, terminal changes, minimum connection time, customs or security rescreening, and on-time history.
steps.expect: only connections with realistic transfer buffers remain.

steps.action: **Prefer protected single-ticket itineraries.** Choose one ticket where the airline is responsible for rebooking missed protected connections.
steps.expect: checkout shows one confirmation covering all segments.

steps.action: **Avoid risky self-transfer unless deliberate.** [BRANCH: protected connection, proceed if timing is realistic | self-transfer, require long buffer, no checked bags, and backup plan]
steps.expect: missed-connection responsibility is clear.

steps.action: **Check visa and transit rules.** Confirm whether connecting countries require transit visas, passport validity, or COVID/health documents.
steps.expect: every passenger can legally transit.

steps.action: **Review baggage handling.** Confirm checked bags are through-checked or that you have enough time to reclaim and recheck them.
steps.expect: bag routing and fees are known.

steps.action: **Book the itinerary.** Confirm passenger names, dates, airports, layovers, total price, and refund/change rules before payment. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* many cheap fares become nonrefundable once ticketed.
steps.expect: a ticketed itinerary with e-ticket numbers and all segments visible.

steps.action: **Monitor schedule changes.** Set alerts for each segment and recheck connection time after airline schedule updates.
steps.expect: any later unsafe connection is caught while rebooking options remain.

recipes.verification: You hold a ticketed itinerary with all segments confirmed, total cost below your cap, legal transit confirmed, and each connection meeting your minimum buffer.

recipes.title: book a flight with points
recipes.name: book-a-flight-with-points
recipes.goal: You redeem points or miles for a flight that beats your cash-value threshold while confirming taxes, fees, availability, and ticketing.

steps.action: **Define the redemption target.** Set route, dates, cabin, acceptable stops, points budget, cash co-pay limit, and minimum cents-per-point value.
steps.expect: a measurable redemption threshold.

steps.action: **Search award availability.** Check the airline program and relevant partners for saver, standard, or dynamic awards.
steps.expect: a shortlist showing miles, taxes, fees, and itinerary details.

steps.action: **Compare against cash fares.** Calculate redemption value as cash fare minus taxes and fees divided by points used.
steps.expect: you know whether the award exceeds your threshold.

steps.action: **Check transfer requirements before moving points.** Confirm transfer ratio, minimum transfer, expected timing, and whether award seats can disappear.
steps.expect: you know if a transfer is necessary and risky.

steps.action: **Hold the award if possible.** Use an award hold or temporary reservation before transferring points when the program allows it.
steps.expect: seats are held with an expiration time, or you know no hold is available.

steps.action: **Transfer points only after final review.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm program, member number, passenger name, award availability, and transfer amount because most point transfers cannot be reversed.
steps.expect: points arrive or show pending in the airline account.

steps.action: **Book the award ticket.** Select flights, enter traveler details, pay taxes and fees, and apply points. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm dates, airports, cabin, cancellation fees, and co-pay before submitting.
steps.expect: a confirmation code and ticket receipt are issued.

steps.action: **Verify with the operating airline.** Use the record locator to confirm seats, ticket number, and baggage allowance.
steps.expect: the airline itinerary shows ticketed status for each traveler.

recipes.verification: The airline shows a ticketed award reservation for every traveler, points were deducted as expected, taxes and fees stayed within the co-pay cap, and redemption value meets or exceeds the preset threshold.

recipes.title: book a hotel with free cancellation
recipes.name: book-a-hotel-with-free-cancellation
recipes.goal: You reserve a hotel room that can be cancelled without penalty until a known deadline and still meets your location, price, and amenity needs.

steps.action: **Set the exact stay parameters.** Enter destination, dates, rooms, guests, bed needs, and accessibility requirements.
steps.expect: search results matching the actual trip.

steps.action: **Filter for free cancellation.** Apply refundable or free-cancellation filters, then open candidate rate details.
steps.expect: each remaining candidate advertises a no-penalty cancellation window.

steps.action: **Compare the total price.** Include taxes, resort/destination fees, cleaning fees, parking, breakfast, Wi-Fi, and currency conversion.
steps.expect: a ranked shortlist by all-in cost, not nightly teaser rate.

steps.action: **Read the cancellation deadline.** Confirm the local hotel time zone, cutoff date, and whether the first night or full stay becomes nonrefundable after the deadline.
steps.expect: a precise cancellation deadline such as date, time, and time zone.

steps.action: **Check booking source tradeoffs.** Compare direct hotel booking against online travel agencies for loyalty credit, price, support, and cancellation handling.
steps.expect: a chosen booking channel with known support path.

steps.action: **Review room type and occupancy.** Verify bed type, smoking status, refundable rate label, included meals, and guest names.
steps.expect: the checkout page matches the intended room and refundable terms.

steps.action: **Book the refundable rate.** Enter payment and contact details, then confirm only after the cancellation policy and total price are still correct. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* once confirmed, a guarantee or deposit may be authorized and later penalties apply after the deadline.
steps.expect: a hotel confirmation number and cancellation policy in writing.

steps.action: **Calendar the deadline.** Add a reminder at least 24 hours before free cancellation expires.
steps.expect: a calendar alert with the booking link and confirmation number.

recipes.verification: You have a written confirmation showing the correct hotel, dates, room type, total price, and a no-penalty cancellation deadline saved in your calendar.

recipes.title: book an award seat when it opens
recipes.name: book-an-award-seat-when-it-opens
recipes.goal: You secure scarce airline award space as soon as it appears while staying within your points, cash fee, and routing limits.

steps.action: **Define the acceptable award.** Set route, date range, cabin, number of seats, maximum points, and maximum cash surcharge.
steps.expect: a clear booking target and walk-away limits.

steps.action: **Learn release patterns.** Check the operating airline and partner programs for schedule-open timing, last-minute releases, and married-segment behavior.
steps.expect: likely search windows and programs are known.

steps.action: **Search multiple programs.** Compare airline sites, alliance partners, and award search tools for the same flight numbers.
steps.expect: a list of programs that can see or book the target space.

steps.action: **Prepare accounts and passenger data.** Save traveler names, birth dates, passport details if needed, and payment card in the booking program.
steps.expect: checkout can be completed quickly when space appears.

steps.action: **Set alerts and manual checks.** Use award alerts where allowed and schedule manual searches around release times.
steps.expect: you will be notified or searching when seats open.

steps.action: **Verify transfer risk before moving points.** Confirm space is visible, transfer ratio, transfer time, reversibility, and whether holds are possible.
steps.expect: a decision to transfer now, hold first, or use existing miles.

steps.action: **Book immediately when within limits.** Select the flights, apply miles, pay taxes/fees, and confirm names before ticketing. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* point transfers usually cannot be reversed and award space can disappear during checkout.
steps.expect: a ticketed award with confirmation and e-ticket numbers.

steps.action: **Confirm with operating carrier.** Use the airline record locator to verify seats, schedule, and meal or seat assignments.
steps.expect: the operating airline shows the reservation as ticketed.

steps.action: **Keep monitoring for better space.** If change/cancel rules allow, watch for nonstop, lower-fee, or better-cabin awards.
steps.expect: an improvement opportunity can be acted on before travel.

recipes.verification: The award itinerary is ticketed, all passengers have e-ticket numbers, taxes/fees are at or below the cap, and the operating carrier can see the reservation.

recipes.title: book the cheapest flight for dates
recipes.name: book-the-cheapest-flight-for-dates
recipes.goal: You book the lowest total-cost flight that meets fixed travel dates, passenger needs, and acceptable risk limits.

steps.action: **Define the trip constraints.** Set must-have dates, departure windows, airports, maximum stops, baggage needs, and refund or change requirements.
steps.expect: a written filter set and maximum all-in price.

steps.action: **Search broad flight-comparison tools.** Compare nearby airports, nonstop versus connecting, and airline-direct fares.
steps.expect: a shortlist of flights ranked by total cost and fit.

steps.action: **Calculate the true total price.** Add carry-on, checked bag, seat assignment, payment, and agency service fees.
steps.expect: each candidate has an all-in price, not just a base fare.

steps.action: **Check schedule and connection risk.** Avoid unrealistic layovers, separate-ticket connections, overnight airport waits, or self-transfer baggage unless intentionally accepted.
steps.expect: the cheapest acceptable itinerary remains viable.

steps.action: **Compare booking channel protections.** Prefer airline-direct booking when the price difference is small; use online travel agencies only when savings justify support complexity.
steps.expect: a chosen booking channel and known support path.

steps.action: **Enter passenger details exactly.** Match names to IDs or passports and include loyalty numbers if desired.
steps.expect: passenger information matches travel documents with no spelling errors.

steps.action: **Review fare rules and final price.** Confirm dates, airports, times, baggage, refundability, change fees, and total charged amount. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm every itinerary field before purchase because corrections may require fees or cancellation.
steps.expect: the checkout page matches the selected flight and price cap.

steps.action: **Purchase and save confirmation.** Submit payment once the final price is within your cap.
steps.expect: a ticket confirmation code, receipt, and email itinerary arrive.

steps.action: **Verify ticketing status with the airline.** Look up the record locator on the airline site.
steps.expect: the airline shows ticketed status for every passenger.

recipes.verification: The airline record shows every passenger as ticketed on the intended dates and airports, and the total charged amount including required bags and fees is at or below the preset maximum price.

recipes.title: choose refundable vs nonrefundable
recipes.name: choose-refundable-vs-nonrefundable
recipes.goal: You choose the refundable or nonrefundable travel rate that has the better expected value for your uncertainty and cash risk.

steps.action: **Write down both prices and terms.** Capture base price, taxes, fees, deposit, refund deadline, change fee, and credit expiration.
steps.expect: refundable and nonrefundable choices are comparable.

steps.action: **Estimate change probability honestly.** Consider work approvals, health, visas, weather, event tickets, and companion reliability.
steps.expect: a realistic low, medium, or high cancellation-risk rating.

steps.action: **Calculate break-even risk.** Divide the refundable premium by the amount you would lose if cancelling the nonrefundable option.
steps.expect: a percentage showing how often plans must change for refundable to pay off.

steps.action: **Check whether credits are usable.** If nonrefundable produces a credit, inspect expiration, name restrictions, fare differences, and rebooking fees.
steps.expect: credit value is discounted if hard to use.

steps.action: **Review external coverage.** Check card or travel insurance for covered reasons, documentation, exclusions, and claim limits.
steps.expect: you know whether insurance actually replaces refundability.

steps.action: **Choose based on risk and cash flow.** [BRANCH: uncertainty exceeds break-even or loss is unaffordable, pick refundable | plans are firm and loss is tolerable, pick nonrefundable]
steps.expect: a selected rate with a written rationale.

steps.action: **Confirm terms at checkout.** Re-read the cancellation policy immediately before payment. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* buying nonrefundable travel can lock in a loss if plans change.
steps.expect: final checkout terms match the selected risk choice.

steps.action: **Calendar any action deadline.** Add reminders for free cancellation, final payment, visa decision, or credit expiration.
steps.expect: the key deadline is visible before money becomes locked.

recipes.verification: The booked option matches the chosen refundable or nonrefundable strategy, the financial exposure is documented, and all refund or credit deadlines are saved.

recipes.title: compare total trip cost
recipes.name: compare-total-trip-cost
recipes.goal: You choose between travel options using total trip cost, not isolated flight, hotel, or car prices.

steps.action: **Create comparable options.** Define each option with the same traveler count, trip length, baggage needs, and lodging standard.
steps.expect: a like-for-like set of alternatives.

steps.action: **Price transportation door to door.** Include flights, trains, baggage, seats, transfers, parking, tolls, fuel, rideshares, and extra travel time.
steps.expect: transportation total for each option.

steps.action: **Price lodging all-in.** Include nightly rate, taxes, resort fees, cleaning fees, deposits, breakfast, parking, and location-related transit costs.
steps.expect: lodging total for each option.

steps.action: **Add activity and food differences.** Estimate mandatory tickets, local meal costs, groceries, childcare, pet care, and seasonal surcharges.
steps.expect: destination-specific daily cost estimate.

steps.action: **Account for points and credits conservatively.** Value points at realistic cash savings, include fees, and subtract expiring credits only if they would otherwise go unused.
steps.expect: net cash cost and separate points cost.

steps.action: **Score flexibility and risk.** Note refundable deadlines, change fees, weather risk, visa risk, and connection risk.
steps.expect: a non-price risk note for every option.

steps.action: **Compare against the cap.** Rank options by all-in cash cost, points used, time burden, and cancellation exposure.
steps.expect: one preferred option and at least one backup.

steps.action: **Save the evidence before booking.** Keep screenshots or a simple spreadsheet with final checkout totals.
steps.expect: a decision record that can be checked after purchase.

recipes.verification: A saved comparison shows each viable option's all-in cash cost, points cost, flexibility deadlines, and the selected option is within the stated budget cap.

recipes.title: find an error fare
recipes.name: find-an-error-fare
recipes.goal: You identify a likely error fare, book it quickly if it fits your constraints, and wait for ticketing confirmation before making nonrefundable plans.

steps.action: **Monitor reputable fare-alert sources.** Use deal sites, fare newsletters, airline searches, and flexible-date tools.
steps.expect: a candidate fare far below normal market price.

steps.action: **Validate the fare independently.** Search the same route and dates on the airline site and at least one comparison tool.
steps.expect: the low price appears on a bookable checkout path.

steps.action: **Check trip feasibility quickly.** Verify dates, airports, baggage, visa or entry needs, overnight layovers, and total trip cost.
steps.expect: no non-price constraint makes the trip unacceptable.

steps.action: **Book through the safest available channel.** Prefer airline-direct if the error fare is available there; otherwise use a reputable seller with clear cancellation terms.
steps.expect: checkout still shows the low all-in price.

steps.action: **Purchase only within your risk cap.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm passenger names, dates, airports, and total charge before submitting, and accept that the fare may later be voided.
steps.expect: a booking confirmation and payment receipt.

steps.action: **Wait for ticket numbers before planning further.** Do not book nonrefundable hotels, tours, or positioning flights until ticketed and stable.
steps.expect: the airline record shows ticket numbers or remains pending.

steps.action: **Monitor for cancellation or schedule changes.** Check email and airline reservation status for several days.
steps.expect: the ticket remains active or the airline cancels and refunds it.

steps.action: **Lock in dependent travel only after confirmation.** Once ticketed and not canceled, book lodging and related travel with compatible cancellation terms.
steps.expect: the broader trip plan no longer depends on an unconfirmed fare.

recipes.verification: The booking has an airline ticket number for each traveler at the error-fare price, or if canceled the full charge has been refunded and no nonrefundable dependent travel was purchased.

recipes.title: get a refund for a cancelled flight
recipes.name: get-a-refund-for-a-cancelled-flight
recipes.goal: You recover the refundable value of a cancelled flight when you choose not to travel on the airline's alternative.

steps.action: **Confirm who cancelled the flight.** Verify that the airline cancelled or significantly changed the itinerary, not that you voluntarily cancelled first.
steps.expect: a cancellation notice or changed itinerary showing the airline-initiated disruption.

steps.action: **Identify the merchant of record.** Check the receipt to see whether the airline, online travel agency, employer travel tool, or card portal sold the ticket.
steps.expect: the correct refund channel is known.

steps.action: **Calculate the refundable amount.** Include unused fare, taxes, carrier-imposed fees, paid seats, bags, and services not provided.
steps.expect: a target refund amount by passenger and add-on.

steps.action: **Reject unwanted alternatives clearly.** Do not click "accept voucher" or "confirm new flight" if you want cash.
steps.expect: the booking remains eligible for a refund request rather than a voluntary exchange.

steps.action: **Submit the official refund request.** Use the merchant's refund form, choose cancelled flight or schedule change, attach the notice, and request refund to original payment. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm you do not need the replacement itinerary before cancelling remaining segments.
steps.expect: a refund confirmation number or email.

steps.action: **Save the refund terms.** Screenshot the submitted amount, ticket numbers, and promised timeline.
steps.expect: evidence for follow-up or chargeback.

steps.action: **Track the payment method.** Check card, bank, wallet, or agency balance until the refund posts.
steps.expect: a posted credit or a missed deadline.

steps.action: **Escalate nonpayment.** Contact the seller with the case number; if still unresolved, complain to the aviation regulator and consider a card dispute for services not provided.
steps.expect: an escalation reference, dispute case, or refund release.

recipes.verification: The original payment method or agreed account shows a posted refund for the unused ticket value and eligible ancillary fees, with no replacement booking accepted.

recipes.title: get compensation for a delayed flight
recipes.name: get-compensation-for-a-delayed-flight
recipes.goal: You claim any delay compensation, reimbursement, or duty-of-care payment you are entitled to after arriving substantially late.

steps.action: **Confirm the actual arrival delay.** Compare scheduled arrival with the time the aircraft door opened or the airline's official arrival record.
steps.expect: a documented arrival delay in hours and minutes.

steps.action: **Identify the governing rule.** [BRANCH: EU/UK-covered flight, check EU261/UK261 compensation thresholds | other route, check the airline contract, local regulator, and travel insurance benefits]
steps.expect: a clear rule source for whether cash compensation, expenses, or only goodwill applies.

steps.action: **Collect disruption evidence.** Save boarding passes, delay notifications, screenshots of status pages, and written staff explanations.
steps.expect: a claim folder with proof of the flight, delay, and stated reason.

steps.action: **Separate compensation from expense reimbursement.** Compensation is a fixed statutory amount where eligible; reimbursement covers reasonable care costs with receipts.
steps.expect: two claim amounts: statutory compensation if applicable and itemized expenses.

steps.action: **Check for disqualifying causes.** Look for extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather, security closure, or air traffic restrictions; technical or crew issues may still qualify in many regimes.
steps.expect: a claim position that explains why the delay is eligible or why only expenses are claimed.

steps.action: **Submit the airline claim form.** Use the airline's official compensation/refund page, enter each passenger, flight, bank or payment details, and attach evidence. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm bank details and passenger names before submitting because wrong details can delay payment.
steps.expect: a submitted claim with reference number or confirmation email.

steps.action: **Calendar the response deadline.** Note the airline's promised response time and the regulator's complaint escalation window.
steps.expect: a follow-up date and saved claim reference.

steps.action: **Escalate if refused or ignored.** Reply with evidence and the specific rule; if unresolved, file with the relevant aviation regulator, ADR body, ombudsman, or card/travel-insurance channel.
steps.expect: an escalation case number or a revised airline decision.

steps.action: **Confirm payment.** Match the received payment against the claimed amount and passenger count.
steps.expect: funds posted to your account or a written final denial to use for further escalation.

recipes.verification: The airline or escalation body has issued a written decision and either cash compensation/reimbursement has posted to your account for the expected amount, or a final denial with case reference is saved.

recipes.title: join a hotel and airline loyalty program
recipes.name: join-a-hotel-and-airline-loyalty-program
recipes.goal: You create hotel and airline loyalty accounts, capture the member numbers, and attach them to future bookings so eligible trips earn points and benefits.

steps.action: **Choose programs based on real travel patterns.** Pick airlines, hotel chains, or alliances you actually use rather than every advertised program.
steps.expect: a short list of programs likely to earn usable points.

steps.action: **Open the official enrollment page.** Navigate from the airline or hotel website, not a third-party ad or email link.
steps.expect: the browser domain matches the brand.

steps.action: **Enter identity details exactly as used for travel.** Use legal name, date of birth when required, email, phone, and address consistent with booking documents.
steps.expect: the account profile can match reservations without name conflicts.

steps.action: **Set secure login and preferences.** Use a unique password, enable multi-factor authentication if available, and opt out of unnecessary marketing.
steps.expect: the account is protected and communication settings match your choice.

steps.action: **Submit enrollment.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm name and date-of-birth fields before submission because some programs require support to correct them.
steps.expect: the site issues a member number or account ID.

steps.action: **Save member details.** Store program name, member number, login URL, email used, and recovery options in a password manager or travel record.
steps.expect: you can retrieve the number when booking or checking in.

steps.action: **Attach numbers to upcoming travel.** Add the airline frequent-flyer number or hotel loyalty number to existing reservations and traveler profiles.
steps.expect: reservation details show the loyalty number accepted.

steps.action: **Verify earning after travel.** After a flight or stay, check that points posted and save receipts or boarding passes until they do.
steps.expect: points post or you have documents for a missing-credit request.

recipes.verification: Each selected hotel or airline program has an active account with a saved member number, secure login, and at least one upcoming reservation or traveler profile shows the correct loyalty number attached if applicable.

recipes.title: price match a hotel rate
recipes.name: price-match-a-hotel-rate
recipes.goal: You obtain a hotel price match or best-rate guarantee adjustment for the same room, dates, occupancy, and terms.

steps.action: **Confirm the guarantee rules.** Read the hotel's best-rate policy for eligible sites, timing, currency, taxes, membership rates, and claim deadline.
steps.expect: a checklist of exact eligibility requirements.

steps.action: **Find a truly comparable lower rate.** Match hotel, room name, bed type, meal plan, cancellation policy, payment timing, dates, guests, and taxes.
steps.expect: a lower all-in price for the same stay terms.

steps.action: **Capture evidence before it changes.** Screenshot the competitor page with timestamp, URL, full rate details, and final checkout total.
steps.expect: proof that a reviewer can reproduce or understand the lower rate.

steps.action: **Check whether booking first is required.** [BRANCH: claim requires existing booking, reserve the eligible direct rate | pre-booking claim allowed, submit before paying]
steps.expect: you are using the correct claim sequence.

steps.action: **Submit the price-match claim.** Enter confirmation number, competitor URL, lower rate, currency, screenshots, and requested adjustment. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* do not book a nonrefundable rate only to chase a match unless the unmatched price is still acceptable.
steps.expect: a claim case number or confirmation email.

steps.action: **Keep the lower rate live if possible.** Leave the competitor page open and note inventory details in case support asks for more proof.
steps.expect: backup evidence remains available during review.

steps.action: **Review the decision.** Verify that the approved adjustment applies to room rate, taxes, bonus discount, or points as promised.
steps.expect: an updated confirmation or written denial with reason.

steps.action: **Cancel or keep based on your floor.** If denied and still inside free cancellation, cancel and book the cheaper eligible option if it is trustworthy.
steps.expect: either a matched direct booking or a cheaper alternative booking.

recipes.verification: The hotel has issued an updated confirmation showing the matched or better total price for the same stay, or you cancelled within the free window and booked the lower eligible rate.

recipes.title: rebook a flight after a price drop
recipes.name: rebook-a-flight-after-a-price-drop
recipes.goal: You capture savings from a post-purchase fare drop by rebooking, changing, or canceling and repurchasing without losing the original trip.

steps.action: **Confirm the current lower fare is real.** Search the same route, date, cabin, passengers, bags, and booking channel.
steps.expect: a bookable replacement fare below your original net cost.

steps.action: **Read the original fare rules.** Check refundability, change fees, cancellation deadline, credit expiration, and whether basic economy is restricted.
steps.expect: you know the cost to change or cancel.

steps.action: **Calculate net savings.** Subtract change fees, lost seat or bag fees, agency fees, and credit restrictions from the fare difference.
steps.expect: a positive savings amount or a decision not to proceed.

steps.action: **Use the airline change/reprice tool first.** Try changing to the same flight or acceptable alternate at the lower price.
steps.expect: the tool displays refund, credit, or additional collection amount.

steps.action: **If needed, hold or book the replacement before canceling.** [BRANCH: refundable or 24-hour-free-cancel replacement, book first | no free-cancel replacement, use same-session change path]
steps.expect: you do not lose the trip while trying to save money.

steps.action: **Submit the change or cancellation only after review.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm passenger, flight, date, credit amount, refund method, and expiration before changing or canceling.
steps.expect: the airline issues a new confirmation, refund, or travel credit.

steps.action: **Verify the new itinerary and funds.** Check ticketed status, seat assignments, bags, and refund or credit balance.
steps.expect: the lower-cost itinerary is active and savings are recorded.

steps.action: **Cancel duplicate holds or alerts.** Remove any extra booking or price alert that could cause confusion.
steps.expect: only the intended itinerary remains active.

recipes.verification: The airline shows the intended active ticket, and the refund, credit, or lower reissued fare produces documented net savings after all fees and lost add-ons.

recipes.title: rent a car without extra fees
recipes.name: rent-a-car-without-extra-fees
recipes.goal: You reserve and pick up a rental car while avoiding unnecessary insurance, fuel, toll, upgrade, and penalty fees.

steps.action: **Price the rental all-in.** Search reputable rental companies and include taxes, facility fees, one-way fees, mileage, young-driver fees, and required extras.
steps.expect: a final estimated total, not just daily rate.

steps.action: **Choose a fuel plan intentionally.** Prefer full-to-full unless prepaid fuel is cheaper than your expected use.
steps.expect: the reservation states the fuel rule.

steps.action: **Decide insurance before the counter.** Review whether your card or policy covers collision, liability, country, vehicle type, and rental length.
steps.expect: a written coverage decision for each offered product.

steps.action: **Avoid unnecessary toll products.** Research local toll roads and whether pay-by-plate, cashless tolls, or your own transponder works.
steps.expect: a toll plan cheaper than the rental company's daily toll package if you do not need it.

steps.action: **Reserve the right class.** Book the smallest class that fits passengers and luggage; do not rely on a free upgrade for capacity.
steps.expect: reservation meets actual space needs.

steps.action: **Inspect the counter contract.** At pickup, review rate, return time, fuel, mileage, insurance declines/acceptances, toll device status, and extras. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* signing the rental agreement can authorize optional products and deposits.
steps.expect: signed contract contains only intended charges.

steps.action: **Document the car condition.** Photograph exterior, interior, fuel gauge, odometer, tires, windshield, and existing damage before leaving.
steps.expect: timestamped proof of condition and starting fuel/mileage.

steps.action: **Return on time and with required fuel.** Keep fuel receipt and return photos, then request a closing receipt.
steps.expect: final receipt matches expected charges or lists any disputed item.

recipes.verification: The final rental receipt matches the intended base rate plus known mandatory charges, with no unwanted insurance, fuel, toll, upgrade, damage, or late fees.

recipes.title: set a flight price alert
recipes.name: set-a-flight-price-alert
recipes.goal: You create a flight price alert that notifies you when an itinerary falls below a target price and gives enough context to book before the fare changes.

steps.action: **Define the alert route and flexibility.** Choose exact dates or a flexible window, nearby airports, nonstop preference, baggage needs, and cabin.
steps.expect: a clear search profile for the desired trip.

steps.action: **Check the current baseline price.** Run an initial search before setting the alert.
steps.expect: you know today's typical price and cheapest acceptable itinerary.

steps.action: **Create the alert in a reputable tool.** Enter route, dates, passengers, cabin, and notification method.
steps.expect: the tool shows an active price alert.

steps.action: **Set a target booking threshold.** Decide the fare at which you will buy, including expected bag and seat fees.
steps.expect: a written buy price that is below or equal to your maximum.

steps.action: **Enable fast notifications.** Confirm email, push, or browser alerts are turned on and not filtered to spam.
steps.expect: a test or confirmation notification can reach you.

steps.action: **Review alerts promptly.** When an alert fires, open the live fare and verify total price, schedule, and booking channel.
steps.expect: the fare is currently bookable or already gone.

steps.action: **Book only after final price review.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm dates, airports, passenger details, and total charge before buying.
steps.expect: a ticket confirmation if the fare still meets the threshold.

recipes.verification: An active alert exists for the intended route, date range, cabin, and passengers, notifications are enabled, and the target buy price is documented for a future booking decision.

recipes.title: split a trip into two tickets to save
recipes.name: split-a-trip-into-two-tickets-to-save
recipes.goal: You save money by booking two separate tickets only when the savings justify the added missed-connection, baggage, and support risk.

steps.action: **Price the through-ticket baseline.** Find the best single-ticket itinerary that protects connections and through-checks bags.
steps.expect: a baseline price and travel time.

steps.action: **Search split-ticket combinations.** Try nearby hub cities, low-cost carriers, trains, or separate outbound/inbound segments.
steps.expect: candidate split options with apparent savings.

steps.action: **Add all extra costs.** Include bags on both tickets, seats, transfers between airports, overnight hotel, meals, insurance, and backup fare.
steps.expect: true net savings after split-ticket friction.

steps.action: **Evaluate connection risk.** Require a long buffer for delays, immigration, baggage claim, terminal changes, and recheck cutoffs.
steps.expect: each split connection has a realistic protection buffer.

steps.action: **Check baggage and visa rules.** Confirm whether checked bags must be reclaimed and whether entering the connection country requires documents.
steps.expect: no hidden legal or baggage blocker.

steps.action: **Set a savings threshold.** Decide the minimum savings required to accept separate-ticket risk.
steps.expect: a private go/no-go number.

steps.action: **Book in the safest order.** Usually book the scarce or expensive segment first, then immediately book the feeder if prices still fit. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* separate nonrefundable tickets leave you responsible if one segment changes or fails.
steps.expect: both tickets are confirmed within the savings threshold.

steps.action: **Build a disruption plan.** Save later same-day alternatives, airline contacts, insurance details, and overnight options.
steps.expect: you know what to buy or call if the first ticket is delayed.

steps.action: **Monitor both reservations.** Track schedule changes separately and reassess buffer after any change.
steps.expect: unsafe changes are caught early enough to rebook.

recipes.verification: Both tickets are confirmed, the combined total including realistic extras is below the through-ticket baseline by at least your savings threshold, and every self-transfer buffer meets your minimum.

recipes.title: use a hotel free night award
recipes.name: use-a-hotel-free-night-award
recipes.goal: You redeem a hotel free-night certificate for a stay where its value exceeds the cash alternative and its restrictions are satisfied.

steps.action: **Open the certificate details.** Check expiration date, eligible brands, point cap, room type, blackout rules, and whether top-up points are allowed.
steps.expect: the award's usable value and constraints are known.

steps.action: **Search award availability.** Use "redeem points/certificates" search for exact dates and flexible nearby dates.
steps.expect: candidate hotels with standard-room award space.

steps.action: **Compare against cash rates.** Include taxes, resort fees, parking, breakfast, and points you would earn on a paid stay.
steps.expect: a redemption value that justifies using the certificate now.

steps.action: **Select the eligible room.** Choose a standard award room that the certificate can cover; avoid premium rooms unless top-up is explicitly allowed.
steps.expect: checkout shows the certificate applied to the intended night.

steps.action: **Handle multi-night stays carefully.** [BRANCH: one-night stay, apply certificate to the only night | multiple nights, apply certificate to the most expensive eligible night or make separate bookings if needed]
steps.expect: the award offsets the highest useful eligible night.

steps.action: **Review fees and cancellation.** Confirm whether the certificate returns if cancelled, the deadline, and which cash fees remain due.
steps.expect: a written cancellation rule and remaining cash total.

steps.action: **Complete the redemption.** Confirm only after the certificate, dates, hotel, and guest details are correct. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* after expiration or late cancellation, the certificate may not be restored.
steps.expect: a confirmation showing certificate redemption and any cash due.

steps.action: **Save proof and monitor the account.** Keep the confirmation and verify the certificate is deducted only once.
steps.expect: booking appears in account and certificate balance reflects the redemption.

recipes.verification: You have a hotel confirmation for the correct stay showing the free-night award applied, remaining cash charges disclosed, and the cancellation deadline saved.

recipes.title: use a travel credit before it expires
recipes.name: use-a-travel-credit-before-it-expires
recipes.goal: You redeem an expiring airline, hotel, agency, or card travel credit for useful travel before value is lost.

steps.action: **Read the credit rules.** Check expiration meaning, eligible traveler, merchant, route/property restrictions, cash residuals, and whether travel or booking must occur by the deadline.
steps.expect: the credit's usable window and limits are clear.

steps.action: **Verify the live balance.** Log in to the issuing airline, hotel, agency, or card portal rather than trusting old email amounts.
steps.expect: current credit value and identifier are visible.

steps.action: **Choose a use that beats losing value.** Search trips you would actually take; include taxes, fees, fare differences, and opportunity cost.
steps.expect: a candidate booking where the credit offsets real spending.

steps.action: **Test credit application before checkout.** Enter the credit on the payment page and confirm it reduces the total correctly.
steps.expect: checkout shows the credit amount applied.

steps.action: **Check residual handling.** Determine whether unused value remains, expires, or is forfeited.
steps.expect: you know whether to spend the full credit in one booking.

steps.action: **Book before the controlling deadline.** Confirm passenger names, dates, route, cancellation terms, and credit application. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* some credits are consumed or reissued with stricter terms after booking.
steps.expect: a confirmation showing credit redemption and remaining cash paid.

steps.action: **Save the new terms.** Store confirmation, ticket number, residual credit code, and any new expiration.
steps.expect: proof of redemption and remaining value.

steps.action: **Confirm ticketing or hotel confirmation.** Check that the booking is actually issued, not just held.
steps.expect: e-ticket number, hotel confirmation, or agency voucher is active.

recipes.verification: The travel credit balance has been applied to a confirmed booking before its controlling expiration deadline, with any residual value and new deadline documented.

recipes.title: use the 24 hour cancellation rule
recipes.name: use-the-24-hour-cancellation-rule
recipes.goal: You use an applicable 24-hour flight cancellation option to hold or correct a booking decision without losing money.

steps.action: **Confirm the policy before booking.** Check whether the airline or seller offers free cancellation or a free hold, and whether departure is far enough away.
steps.expect: the exact cancellation deadline and eligibility conditions are known.

steps.action: **Book only through an eligible channel.** Prefer airline-direct booking when relying on the 24-hour rule, because third-party policies can differ.
steps.expect: checkout or fare rules mention cancellation or hold rights.

steps.action: **Set an immediate deadline reminder.** Create a reminder several hours before the free-cancel window ends.
steps.expect: a calendar alert includes the booking reference and cancel link.

steps.action: **Review the booking after purchase.** Check passenger names, dates, airports, baggage, fare class, and total price.
steps.expect: you know whether to keep, correct, or cancel the ticket.

steps.action: **Compare alternatives during the window.** Search better fares, verify companion availability, and confirm time off or trip details.
steps.expect: a keep-or-cancel decision before the deadline.

steps.action: **Cancel through the official booking path if needed.** ⚠️ *Irreversible:* confirm you are canceling the correct record locator and all passengers before submitting.
steps.expect: the reservation status changes to canceled and a refund confirmation appears.

steps.action: **Verify refund timing and payment status.** Check the card or account after cancellation and save the confirmation.
steps.expect: the charge is voided, pending reversal, or refunded according to the stated timeline.

steps.action: **Keep the booking only after final confirmation.** If keeping it, remove the reminder and verify ticketed status.
steps.expect: the active itinerary remains ticketed and no accidental cancellation reminder remains.

recipes.verification: If canceled, the reservation shows canceled within the free-cancellation window and the full fare is voided or refunded; if kept, the ticket remains active after deliberate review before the deadline.

recipes.title: build a travel day bag
recipes.name: build-a-travel-day-bag
recipes.goal: Pack a compact day bag for transit or sightseeing with essentials accessible and valuables protected.

steps.action: **Choose the bag.** Pick a small backpack, crossbody, or tote that zips and fits under a seat or on your body.
steps.expect: the bag is comfortable and not overlarge.

steps.action: **Pack documents and money securely.** Put passport, ID, transit card, one payment card, and small cash in an inner pocket or pouch.
steps.expect: essentials are reachable but not exposed.

steps.action: **Add health and comfort basics.** Pack medications, hand sanitizer, tissues, sunscreen, lip balm, and any child or period supplies needed for the day.
steps.expect: predictable personal needs are covered.

steps.action: **Add power and navigation.** Bring phone, charging cable, power bank, offline map, and address of lodging.
steps.expect: you can navigate even with weak service.

steps.action: **Pack weather layers.** [BRANCH: heat | rain | cold] add water and hat for heat, shell or umbrella for rain, or warm layer for cold.
steps.expect: the bag matches the forecast.

steps.action: **Include food and water.** Add a refillable bottle and sturdy snack, especially for flights, trains, hikes, or children.
steps.expect: delays will not immediately cause hunger or dehydration.

steps.action: **Reduce theft and bulk.** Remove full wallets, extra keys, jewelry, and duplicate electronics; keep the bag closed and balanced.
steps.expect: the bag carries only what you need today.

steps.action: **Do a final access check.** Place high-use items near the top and emergency items in a consistent pocket.
steps.expect: you can find tickets, phone, medication, and water without unpacking everything.

recipes.verification: Before leaving lodging, the day bag contains documents, money, phone power, medication, weather protection, water, and a snack, with valuables minimized and secured.

recipes.title: check in for a flight
recipes.name: check-in-for-a-flight
recipes.goal: You are checked in for your flight with a boarding pass on your phone or in hand, bags handled, and you know your terminal, gate window, and boarding time.

steps.action: **Open check-in when the window opens.** Airline app/site → check-in → PNR + name. Doing it at window-open gets seat choice and kills the airport-queue dependency.
steps.expect: your itinerary loads and offers check-in.

steps.action: **Complete the document/health/customs questions honestly.** International: passport details (often scanned by the app), destination address, any required declarations.
steps.expect: documents accepted; no "see agent at airport" flag (flag → F1).

steps.action: **Confirm or change your seat.** Free options first; paid upgrades knowingly.
steps.expect: a seat assignment on the pass.

steps.action: **Declare bags.** [BRANCH: carry-on only → done | checked bags → confirm/pay for them now (cheaper than at the counter)]
steps.expect: bag allowance attached; the pass or email states it.

steps.action: **Obtain the boarding pass.** App wallet pass preferred (it updates gates live); screenshot it as backup; or print at home.
steps.expect: a scannable pass showing name, flight, seat, boarding *time*, and boarding group — gate may still say "TBD", that's normal.

steps.action: **At the airport: drop bags if any.** Bag-drop desk or self-service kiosk within the *bag-drop deadline* (earlier than the check-in deadline — usually 45–60 min international). ⚠️ *Irreversible:* missing the bag deadline can mean flying without your bag or not flying — build the buffer.
steps.expect: bag tagged to your final destination (read the tag's airport code) and a receipt sticker in your possession.

steps.action: **Clear security and verify the gate.** Pass + ID through security; then check the departure boards against your app — gates move.
steps.expect: through security with time to reach the gate by *boarding* time (not departure time), which is typically 30–45 min before departure.

recipes.verification: A live boarding pass (plus backup) shows your correct name, flight, and seat; bags (if any) are tagged to the right final airport code with receipts in hand; and you're through security tracking the gate with the boarding time — not the departure time — as your deadline.

recipes.title: check into a hotel
recipes.name: check-into-a-hotel
recipes.goal: You check into your reserved room at the front desk, understand the deposit hold placed on your card, verify the room matches what you booked, and know the wifi and breakfast details before you settle in.

steps.action: **Go to the front desk and give your name and reservation.** Have the confirmation number and ID ready.
steps.expect: the clerk finds your booking and confirms the room type, rate, and number of nights.

steps.action: **Present ID and a payment card.** Hotels take a card even on prepaid bookings, to cover a security or incidentals deposit.
steps.expect: the clerk takes an imprint or taps the card and returns your ID.

steps.action: **Understand the deposit hold before you agree.** Ask the amount and whether it is a hold (released at checkout) or a charge. A hold reduces your available balance for days after you leave. ⚠️ *Irreversible in the moment:* on a debit card the held funds are genuinely locked until the bank releases them, sometimes a week later, which can strand you on a tight balance.
steps.expect: a stated hold amount you have confirmed your card can absorb, ideally on a credit card rather than debit.

steps.action: **Confirm the practical details while you are still at the desk.** Ask the wifi network and password, breakfast hours and whether it is included in your rate, checkout time, and where to park.
steps.expect: wifi credentials, breakfast time and inclusion status, and checkout time noted.

steps.action: **Take the key and note the room number privately.** Clerks write the number rather than say it aloud for security; keep the key sleeve, which usually has it.
steps.expect: a working key card and your room number recorded discreetly.

steps.action: **Do a room-check ritual on entering.** Test that the key works, confirm the room type and bed configuration match the booking, check the lock and deadbolt, run the shower and toilet, test the AC or heat, look at the bed and bathroom for cleanliness and any pre-existing damage, and confirm wifi connects.
steps.expect: everything works and matches; note any pre-existing damage now so you are not blamed later.

steps.action: **Report any mismatch or fault immediately, from the room.** Call the desk while the evidence is fresh.
steps.expect: a fix, a room change, or a logged note; a same-day report is far stronger than one at checkout.

recipes.verification: You hold a working key to a room that matches your booking, you know the deposit hold amount and how it clears, and you have the wifi and breakfast details, with any pre-existing room faults already reported.

recipes.title: choose a good plane seat
recipes.name: choose-a-good-plane-seat
recipes.goal: Choose a plane seat that fits your priorities for comfort, sleep, speed, view, and restrictions before check-in or boarding.

steps.action: **Open the airline seat map.** Use the airline's booking page or app rather than a third-party guess if possible.
steps.expect: available seats and prices are visible.

steps.action: **Choose aisle or window first.** [BRANCH: aisle | window] pick aisle for easy movement, or window for sleep, view, and fewer interruptions.
steps.expect: your main comfort tradeoff is settled.

steps.action: **Avoid obvious problem rows.** Look for the last row, rows near toilets, galley areas, and seats that do not recline.
steps.expect: noisy or restricted seats are excluded.

steps.action: **Check exit-row rules.** Confirm age, mobility, language, pregnancy, pet, and carry-on restrictions before selecting an exit row.
steps.expect: you qualify and accept the responsibility if choosing it.

steps.action: **Check wing and engine position.** Seats over the wing often feel steadier, while seats behind engines may be louder.
steps.expect: motion and noise preferences are considered.

steps.action: **Confirm seat type and aircraft.** Watch for missing windows, bassinet rows, bulkheads with no under-seat storage, and aircraft swaps.
steps.expect: the seat matches what you think you selected.

steps.action: **Balance price against benefit.** Decide whether extra-legroom, preferred, or paid selection is worth the flight length.
steps.expect: you know the exact added cost before payment.

steps.action: **Select and save the seat.** Choose the seat, review passenger assignment, then confirm. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* paid seat fees may be nonrefundable, so check passenger, flight, and seat number before paying.
steps.expect: confirmation page or itinerary shows the assigned seat.

steps.action: **Recheck at check-in.** Look for aircraft changes, newly opened seats, or separated travelers.
steps.expect: the seat still appears on the boarding pass.

recipes.verification: Your itinerary or boarding pass shows a seat assignment that matches your aisle/window choice, avoids known problem rows, and complies with any exit-row rules.

recipes.title: clear immigration and customs
recipes.name: clear-immigration-and-customs
recipes.goal: You pass through passport control (immigration) and then customs at an international arrival, entering the country legally with your belongings, and exit into the arrivals hall without a secondary inspection or penalty.

steps.action: **Follow the arrivals signs and pick the right immigration queue.** Lanes split by passport type: citizens or residents, this-country nationals, all-passports or foreign nationals, and often e-gates for eligible passports. Joining the wrong lane costs you the whole wait.
steps.expect: you are queued in a lane your passport is eligible for.

steps.action: **Have documents ready before you reach the desk.** Passport open to the photo page, visa or authorization accessible, landing card and onward-ticket or address details in hand. Remove hat and sunglasses; silence the phone.
steps.expect: everything the officer will ask for is in your hand, not buried in a bag.

steps.action: **Approach the desk or e-gate only when signaled.** Wait behind the line until called or the light turns green.
steps.expect: the officer waves you forward or the e-gate opens.

steps.action: **Answer immigration questions plainly and honestly.** Purpose of visit, length of stay, where you are staying. Answer only what is asked, briefly and truthfully. Look up for the camera and fingerprint scan if requested. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* a false statement to an immigration officer can mean refused entry and a lasting record; never guess or embellish.
steps.expect: the passport is stamped or the entry recorded electronically, and you are released toward baggage.

steps.action: **Collect checked baggage.** Read the screen for your flight's carousel; wait for and grab your bags.
steps.expect: all your checked bags in hand before you approach customs.

steps.action: **Choose the correct customs channel.** Green "nothing to declare" only if you genuinely carry nothing over the limits; red "goods to declare" if you carry anything declarable, or the single channel where officers direct everyone.
steps.expect: you are in the channel that matches what you actually carry, ready to declare if needed.

steps.action: **Declare honestly if you have anything to declare.** Hand over your completed form, state the goods, pay any duty. Declaring is routine and cheap; hiding is the offense. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* smuggling or a false customs declaration risks seizure, fines, and prosecution far exceeding any duty owed.
steps.expect: the officer processes the declaration, you pay any duty, and you are cleared.

steps.action: **Walk through and keep any receipt or stamped form.** Some exits scan your form or ticket.
steps.expect: you exit into the public arrivals hall, clear of both checkpoints.

recipes.verification: Your passport shows an entry stamp or recorded electronic entry, you cleared customs through the correct channel with any duty paid, and you are standing in the public arrivals hall with all your baggage and no pending inspection.

recipes.title: cross a land border
recipes.name: cross-a-land-border
recipes.goal: Cross an international land border legally with documents, transport, customs declarations, money, and onward plans in order.

steps.action: **Confirm the official crossing.** Check government or operator sources for hours, closures, visa-on-arrival availability, and pedestrian or vehicle rules.
steps.expect: the crossing is open for your nationality and transport mode.

steps.action: **Stage documents before arrival.** Put passport, visa, entry forms, vehicle registration, rental permission, insurance, and onward proof in one reachable folder.
steps.expect: inspection can happen without unpacking luggage.

steps.action: **Exit the first country properly.** Get exit stamp, electronic exit confirmation, or vehicle export processing where required.
steps.expect: your departure is recorded before entering the next country.

steps.action: **Enter the next country at the official post.** Present documents, answer itinerary questions briefly, and pay only posted official fees at marked counters.
steps.expect: entry is stamped, electronically approved, or otherwise documented.

steps.action: **Clear customs and biosecurity.** Declare cash, goods, food, medication, equipment, or vehicle contents as required.
steps.expect: customs releases you without undeclared restricted items.

steps.action: **Reset practical basics after entry.** Get local cash or eSIM if needed, confirm onward transport, check time zone, and save emergency numbers.
steps.expect: the next leg works under the new country's rules.

recipes.verification: Your passport or electronic record shows legal exit and entry, customs has released you, luggage and transport are intact, and you know your allowed stay length.

recipes.title: deal with jet lag
recipes.name: deal-with-jet-lag
recipes.goal: Your body clock is realigned to the destination time zone within a few days of arrival, so you sleep at local night and function during local day.

steps.action: **Compute the shift and its direction.** Eastward (e.g. US to Europe) advances your clock and is the hard direction; westward delays it and is easier.
steps.expect: a number of hours and a label, "advance" or "delay".

steps.action: **Pre-shift 2 to 3 days before flying.** Eastward: go to bed and wake 1 hour earlier each day. Westward: 1 hour later each day.
steps.expect: by departure, your sleep window has moved 2 to 3 hours toward destination time.

steps.action: **Set your watch and phone to destination time as you board.** Then act on that time: decide "is it day or night there right now?"
steps.expect: every food/sleep decision now references local destination time, not origin.

steps.action: **Sleep on the plane only if it is night at the destination.** If it is destination-daytime, stay awake (screen, walk the aisle). Use an eye mask and earplugs for the sleep window.
steps.expect: your onboard rest aligns with destination night, not origin night.

steps.action: **On landing, get outdoor daylight if it is local morning or midday.** [BRANCH: arrive local morning/day → seek bright light and stay up until local evening | arrive local night → keep lights dim, go to bed even if not fully tired]
steps.expect: light exposure reinforces the correct new schedule.

steps.action: **Apply the first-day rule: no nap longer than 20 to 30 minutes.** Set an alarm. A long afternoon crash resets progress.
steps.expect: you reach local bedtime genuinely sleepy.

steps.action: **Use caffeine as a tool, not a habit.** Have it in the local morning to stay awake; stop 8+ hours before target bedtime so it does not block sleep.
steps.expect: alert during local day, able to fall asleep at local night.

steps.action: **Optional melatonin, low dose (0.5 to 1 mg), 30 to 60 min before target bedtime for eastward trips.** Small doses work better than large ones for timing.
steps.expect: easier sleep onset at the new bedtime; repeat 2 to 4 nights.

recipes.verification: By day 3 to 4 at the destination you fall asleep within ~30 minutes at local bedtime, sleep through most of the local night, and stay awake without a long nap through the local day.

recipes.title: drive abroad safely
recipes.name: drive-abroad-safely
recipes.goal: Drive in another country with legal documents, a suitable vehicle, local-road awareness, and a plan for navigation, fuel, tolls, and emergencies.

steps.action: **Confirm legal eligibility.** Check license validity, minimum age, IDP rules, border-crossing permission, and insurance before accepting the vehicle.
steps.expect: documents satisfy police, rental, and insurance requirements.

steps.action: **Inspect the car before leaving.** Photograph all sides, wheels, windshield, fuel level or battery charge, spare tire or repair kit, safety vest, warning triangle, and child seats.
steps.expect: existing damage and required equipment are documented.

steps.action: **Set navigation while parked.** Load offline maps, route, toll settings, fuel stops, and hotel parking destination before moving.
steps.expect: the first drive starts without phone handling at speed.

steps.action: **Rehearse local controls.** Find headlights, wipers, mirrors, gear selector, parking brake, fuel cap, and lane position cues.
steps.expect: basic controls are muscle-ready before traffic.

steps.action: **Drive defensively for the first hour.** Use slower lanes, avoid city centers at rush hour, keep longer following distance, and let locals pass.
steps.expect: you adapt to signage, lane discipline, and roundabouts without pressure.

steps.action: **Handle tolls, fuel, and parking early.** Learn the toll tag or ticket system, fuel type, pump payment flow, and legal parking signs before you are nearly empty or late.
steps.expect: no avoidable fines, wrong-fuel risk, or unpaid tolls.

steps.action: **Park and secure the car.** Remove visible luggage, lock the car, note the parking level or street rules, and save the rental emergency number.
steps.expect: the vehicle is legal, findable, and not advertising baggage.

recipes.verification: You are legally documented, the rental condition is photographed, route and controls are understood, and the first drive is completed without traffic violations, wrong-fuel incidents, or unsafe phone use.

recipes.title: exchange money abroad
recipes.name: exchange-money-abroad
