steps.expect: one plan matches the trip rather than only the first city.

steps.action: **Install while on stable Wi-Fi.** Scan the QR code or use the provider app before travel or at the hotel, following the phone's add-cellular-plan flow.
steps.expect: the eSIM appears in cellular settings as an installed plan.

steps.action: **Label lines clearly.** Name the home SIM and travel eSIM, keep the home line available for calls or SMS if needed, and set travel data to the eSIM.
steps.expect: cellular settings show which line handles data, calls, and messages.

steps.action: **Disable costly roaming.** Turn off data roaming on the home line unless you intentionally bought a roaming pass.
steps.expect: mobile data uses the eSIM and the home carrier is not silently roaming.

steps.action: **Test data on arrival.** Enable the eSIM, turn on data roaming for that eSIM if required, and open a map or browser.
steps.expect: local network bars and working data appear without home-line data charges.

steps.action: **Monitor usage.** Check provider app data balance and phone usage during navigation, video, hotspot, and upload-heavy days.
steps.expect: you know whether to top up before data runs out.

recipes.verification: The phone shows the travel eSIM installed and selected for mobile data, a local network connects, a web page loads off Wi-Fi, and the home line is not using data roaming unintentionally.

recipes.title: use public transit in a new city
recipes.name: use-public-transit-in-a-new-city
recipes.goal: Use buses, trains, trams, or metros in an unfamiliar city with the right map, fare, validation method, timing, and basic safety habits.

steps.action: **Get the official map or app.** Download the transit agency app or save the route map from the agency website.
steps.expect: you can identify nearby stops and major lines.

steps.action: **Locate your nearest stop.** Find the stop name, direction, and walking route from your lodging.
steps.expect: you can reach the correct platform or curb without guessing.

steps.action: **Choose a fare product.** [BRANCH: single ride | day pass | stored value] compare your planned rides with pass cost and transfer rules.
steps.expect: the chosen fare covers the expected trips.

steps.action: **Learn validation rules.** Check whether you must tap in, tap out, stamp a paper ticket, scan a code, or carry proof of payment.
steps.expect: you know what makes the fare valid before boarding.

steps.action: **Buy from an official source.** Use a station machine, staffed counter, agency app, or accepted contactless card.
steps.expect: ticket, pass, or payment method is ready before travel.

steps.action: **Plan around peak times.** Check whether rush hour crowding, limited luggage space, or reduced late-night service affects the trip.
steps.expect: departure time accounts for crowding and service frequency.

steps.action: **Board in the correct direction.** Match the platform or stop sign to the line endpoint and destination sequence.
steps.expect: the next vehicle is going toward your destination.

steps.action: **Validate before or at boarding.** Complete the required tap, stamp, or scan. ⚠️ *Irreversible:* inspectors may fine invalid tickets even if you paid, so validate before sitting down.
steps.expect: the reader, stamp, or app shows a valid ride.

steps.action: **Monitor your stop.** Follow the route on the map and move toward the exit one stop early.
steps.expect: you exit at the planned stop without rushing.

recipes.verification: You completed the ride on the intended line, with a valid fare, correct stop exit, and no fare inspection or safety issue.

journeys.goal:
Go from "I want to buy" to holding the keys and a recorded deed, without over-committing before
financing and inspection are certain. This is long-horizon: it is gated on a lender's underwriting
clock, an appraisal, an inspection contingency window, and a fixed closing date — and several steps
are irreversible (earnest money, the purchase agreement, closing).
journeys.outcome_state:
When done you hold: keys, a recorded deed in your name, a funded mortgage on terms you understood,
active utilities, and your address updated everywhere.

milestones.title: Get mortgage-ready
milestones.wait: credit improvement and saving take months — this is usually the longest node.
milestones.verify: you know your price ceiling, your down-payment target is saved, and your credit score band is documented.
milestones.replan: credit is too low or savings short → extend the timeline and prioritize building credit before touching M2.

milestones.title: Get pre-approved
milestones.wait: a pre-approval letter takes 1–5 days and is valid ~60–90 days.
milestones.verify: you hold a written pre-approval stating a maximum loan amount and rate estimate.
milestones.replan: the pre-approval is below what you need → return to M1 (save more or lower the price band).

milestones.title: Search and shortlist
milestones.gate: M2 (sellers expect a pre-approval before offers).
milestones.verify: a shortlisted property within budget that you want to offer on.
milestones.replan: nothing fits the budget → widen area or adjust the band (loop to M1).

milestones.title: Offer and go under contract
milestones.verify: a signed purchase agreement and earnest money deposited into escrow.
milestones.replan: you are outbid or the seller rejects → return to M3.

milestones.title: Inspection and due diligence
milestones.wait: the inspection contingency window is typically 7–14 days.
milestones.verify: the inspection is reviewed and issues are negotiated or accepted; all contingencies are satisfied or explicitly waived.
milestones.replan: major defects appear → renegotiate the price or exit under the contingency (return to M3).

milestones.title: Finalize financing and close
milestones.wait: underwriting takes 2–4 weeks; the closing date is fixed.
milestones.verify: ⚠ *Irreversible:* you sign at closing, funds transfer, and the deed is recorded in your name — you hold the keys.
milestones.replan: the appraisal comes in below price or the loan is denied in underwriting → renegotiate the price or restart financing at M2.

milestones.title: Move in and transfer your life
milestones.verify: utilities are on, mail is forwarded, and your address is updated across accounts and government records.
milestones.replan: none — this is the closeout.

journeys.replan_triggers:
- Interest rates move materially → re-run affordability (M1) and re-shop the loan (M2).
- Your income or credit changes during the process → tell the lender immediately; underwriting
  re-checks at closing.
- The appraisal or inspection changes the economics → renegotiate or exit via the matching contingency.

journeys.goal:
Go from carrying high-interest debt to a zero (or controlled) balance, on a plan you can actually
sustain. This is long-horizon and, until the end, a **control loop, not a one-shot**: you set a
policy, run it monthly for months to years, and re-plan as balances, rates, and income change.
journeys.outcome_state:
When done you hold: a written picture of every debt, an automated payoff that beats minimums, a
starter emergency fund so surprises don't create new debt, resolved collections/medical items, and
a monthly balance that trends to zero.

milestones.title: Face the numbers
milestones.verify: a written list of every debt (balance, APR, minimum payment) and your monthly surplus or shortfall figure.
milestones.replan: there is no surplus → do M2 (cut costs) before any payoff plan.

milestones.title: Free up cash flow
milestones.wait: cancellations are immediate; bill negotiations take days.
milestones.verify: your monthly surplus has increased by a measured amount you can direct at debt.
milestones.replan: cash flow is still negative → the problem is income, not spending → pursue more income or hardship options before payoff (branch).

milestones.title: Choose a strategy and automate
milestones.verify: avalanche (highest APR first) or snowball (smallest balance first) chosen, and an automatic extra payment is scheduled to the target debt.
milestones.replan: an interest rate changes or a new debt appears → re-rank the targets.

milestones.title: Build a starter safety net
milestones.wait: takes weeks to months to fund.
milestones.verify: a small starter emergency fund exists so a surprise expense doesn't create new debt.
milestones.replan: the fund is spent → pause extra payoff and refill it first.

milestones.title: Handle problem debts
milestones.gate: any collections or disputed medical items on the M1 list.
milestones.verify: each collections/medical item is resolved, reduced, or on a written payment plan.
milestones.replan: an item is re-sold or reappears → loop it back through M5.

milestones.title: Run the loop to zero
milestones.verify: balances fall every month; when one debt hits zero, its payment rolls onto the next target (the accelerating part of the plan).
milestones.replan: income drops or a new expense appears → rebuild the budget (M1) and adjust the plan.

journeys.replan_triggers:
- Income or expenses change → rebuild the budget (M1) and re-rank targets (M3).
- A rate rises (variable card/loan) → move it up the payoff order.
- A new debt or collections item appears → add it to M1's list and route to M5.
- A debt hits zero → roll its payment onto the next (M6 is where the plan accelerates).

journeys.goal:
Move from your current job to a better one without a gap and without burning bridges — materials
ready, a live pipeline, offers negotiated, and your resignation timed so it lands only *after* the
new offer is signed. This is long-horizon: it runs on other people's clocks (replies, multi-round
loops, ghosting) and re-plans constantly as feedback arrives.
journeys.outcome_state:
When done you hold: a signed offer you understand, a graceful exit from your old role with a notice
period and handover, references intact, and payroll/benefits set up at the new job.

milestones.title: Prep materials and positioning
milestones.verify: an updated resume, a tailorable cover-letter template, a current LinkedIn profile, and a one-line positioning statement for your target role.
milestones.replan: you can't name a target role → do informational interviews (M2) before applying.

milestones.title: Network and source leads
milestones.wait: replies take days to weeks; expect silence on most.
milestones.verify: a pipeline of several live leads and at least two references lined up.
milestones.replan: the pipeline is dry after weeks → broaden roles/geography and revise M1 positioning.

milestones.title: Apply and interview
milestones.wait: multi-round loops over weeks; ghosting is normal — keep applying in parallel.
milestones.verify: at least one final-round or offer in hand.
milestones.replan: consistent early-stage rejections → fix the resume/story (M1) or the targeting (M2).

milestones.title: Evaluate and negotiate the offer
milestones.wait: offer deadlines are days — ask for time if you need competing offers to land.
milestones.verify: ⚠ *Irreversible:* a signed offer whose comp, title, and start date you understand; other offers declined gracefully (you may want them later).
milestones.replan: the offer is withdrawn or a lowball won't move → return to M3.

milestones.title: Resign gracefully
milestones.gate: M4 — a *signed* offer with a firm start date. Never resign before this.
milestones.verify: ⚠ *Irreversible:* resignation delivered, notice period set, and a handover plan agreed.
milestones.replan: a counteroffer arrives → decide stay-or-go deliberately (it rarely fixes why you left); if the new offer is rescinded before you've resigned, pause M5 entirely.

milestones.title: Onboard and set up
milestones.gate: M5 complete and the start date reached.
milestones.verify: payroll and direct deposit are set, systems access works, and 30-day goals are agreed.
milestones.replan: a serious role mismatch surfaces → renegotiate scope early, while you have goodwill.

journeys.replan_triggers:
- Repeated rejection at the same stage → the problem is that stage's materials/prep; fix it (M1/M3).
- A better offer appears mid-process → renegotiate or switch targets before signing (M4).
- Your current job situation changes (layoff, new manager) → re-time M5 and adjust urgency.

journeys.goal:
Return from "someone is using my identity" to a fully secured, clean state: the fraud stopped,
your accounts locked down, an official record on file, every fraudulent item disputed and
removed, and monitoring in place so it does not silently resume. This is a long-horizon task —
it is gated on third-party clocks (card reissue, bureau responses, the ~30-day dispute window)
and it loops: new fraud surfacing weeks later reopens earlier milestones.

milestones.title: Stop the bleeding on the known-compromised account
milestones.gate: you have identified at least one specific compromised card or account.
milestones.verify: the compromised card is frozen/replaced and any hacked account is back under your sole control with a new password.
milestones.replan: more accounts show unauthorized access → add each to M2's scope before continuing.

milestones.title: Change credentials and lock the front door
milestones.gate: you control your primary email (it is the reset path for everything else).
milestones.verify: primary email and every financial login are on unique passwords with 2FA; the breach check is done and any exposed reused passwords are retired.
milestones.replan: the breached account *is* your email → do M2 for email FIRST, then redo every downstream reset, since prior resets may have gone to the attacker.

milestones.title: Freeze credit at all three bureaus
milestones.gate: none — do this immediately, in parallel with M1/M2.
milestones.wait: online freeze is instant; mailed confirmations arrive in 1–2 weeks.
milestones.verify: a freeze is active at Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion (three separate confirmations).
milestones.replan: you must apply for legitimate credit during recovery → schedule a temporary thaw for that one bureau/window, then re-freeze.

milestones.title: Enumerate the damage
milestones.gate: M3 started (so no new accounts open while you review).
milestones.verify: you have a written list of every fraudulent account, hard inquiry, and charge with dates and amounts — this list drives M5 and M6.
milestones.replan: new fraudulent tradelines appear later → reopen M4 and extend M6.

milestones.title: Create the official record
milestones.wait: a police report copy can take 1–2 weeks.
milestones.verify: you hold an FTC Identity Theft Report (IdentityTheft.gov recovery plan + affidavit) and a police report number — the documents creditors and bureaus require to block fraud.
milestones.replan: a creditor demands notarized or additional documentation → obtain it (branch) before that specific dispute in M6.

milestones.title: Dispute and remove each fraudulent item
milestones.gate: M4 (the item list) and M5 (the reports to attach).
milestones.wait: bureaus and creditors must respond within ~30 days under the FCRA; collections can be re-sold or re-aged.
milestones.verify: each fraudulent item is marked deleted or blocked *in writing*.
milestones.replan: a removed item reappears, or a new collections notice arrives → loop that item back through M6 with the FTC report attached.

milestones.title: Report residual scams and restore your contact surface
milestones.verify: the scam is reported and your real address/phone/email is restored on every account a fraudster may have altered.
milestones.replan: a fraudster-controlled address or phone is still on file anywhere → reopen until clean.

milestones.title: Monitor and close out
milestones.track: E (month 1–12, a maintenance loop, not a one-shot)
milestones.wait: ongoing; an extended fraud alert (with your FTC report) lasts 7 years.
milestones.verify: two consecutive monthly reviews are clean and all three freezes remain in place.
milestones.replan: any new unauthorized activity appears → restart from M1 for that account.

journeys.replan_triggers:
- A new unrecognized account, inquiry, charge, or bill appears → reopen M4, extend M6.
- A previously removed item returns → loop it back through M6.
- You learn the breach was broader (e.g. SSN exposed) → add an IRS Identity Protection PIN and a
  Social Security account lock as new milestones.
- Your email/phone turns out to have been compromised → M2-email becomes the new root; re-verify
  everything downstream.
